2611.01283.title: DriftingPlanner: Drifting Generative Models for One-Step Trajectory Planning in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
2611.01283.abstract: End-to-end planners decode the ego trajectory either by coordinate regression, which is fast but blends plausible maneuvers into one trajectory that may follow none of them, or by diffusion and flow matching, which model the trajectory distribution but need several inference steps. Drifting models move this iteration into training: a one-step generator learns to follow an attraction--repulsion field between generated and ground-truth samples. Drifting was developed for class-conditional image generation, where every class supplies many positive samples. In planning, every scene is its own condition. Pooling scenes would attract the generated trajectories of one scene to the ground truth of unrelated scenes, whereas computing the field per scene leaves a single positive, the expert trajectory. Mutual repulsion then holds the generated trajectories on a shell around it, so any single generated trajectory deviates from the ground truth. We present DriftingPlanner, a trajectory planner trained with the drifting loss alone, without any coordinate regression term. It computes the field per scene and removes the shell at inference: it decodes every noise vector together with its negation in one batched pass, and averaging each antithetic pair cancels the linear part of the displacement from the shell center. On NAVSIM navtest, DriftingPlanner reaches a state-of-the-art 93.75 PDMS, and with single-step inference its drifting decoder comes within 0.13 PDMS of the best diffusion or flow matching setting, which needs ten inference steps.

llm.title_ja: DriftingPlanner：エンドツーエンド自動運転における1ステップ軌跡計画のためのドリフト生成モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 座標回帰や拡散モデルの課題を克服するため、シーンごとの引力-斥力場を用いたドリフト損失のみで学習し、反対称ペアの平均化により1ステップで高品質な軌跡を生成するDriftingPlannerを提案した。
llm.problem: 座標回帰は複数の許容される軌跡をブレンドしてしまい、拡散モデルやフローマッチングは複数の推論ステップを必要とすること。
llm.method: シーンごとに引力-斥力場を計算するドリフト損失を用いた学習と、推論時にノイズベクトルとその否定をバッチ処理でデコードする手法。
llm.result: NAVSIM navtestにおいて状態最先端の93.75 PDMSを達成し、1ステップ推論で10ステップ必要な最良の拡散設定に匹敵する性能を示した。

2611.01283.tldr_en: DriftingPlanner is presented, a trajectory planner trained with the drifting loss alone, without any coordinate regression term, and reaches a state-of-the-art 93.75 PDMS with single-step inference.

2611.01277.title: Programmable Droplets as Active Matter in a Reconfigurable Environment
2611.01277.abstract: Exploring systems that bridge the gap between non living and living matter requires a reconfigurable environment coupled to synthetic systems capable of autonomous motion, adaptive behaviour and persistent dynamics. Self propelled droplets provide a minimal platform for such life like behaviour, but quantitative measures capturing both persistence and adaptability to enable closed loop reconfiguration remain lacking. Here we introduce an autonomous closed loop robotic platform to characterise and dynamically program the autonomous behaviour of multicomponent oil in water droplets. We explored two chemical composition spaces, with and without external pH perturbations, analysing droplet behaviour in real time and iteratively selecting formulations. To quantify this behaviour, we introduce two descriptors, persistence and diversity. Persistence is quantified by mapping temporal dynamics in a speed shape complexity space, where we identify a persistence domain that distinguishes active from inactive droplets. Diversity captures spontaneous or environmentally induced variation in motion and the propensity of droplets to reorient or adapt under perturbation. We show that persistence and diversity are constrained by a behavioural trade off: high persistence limits diversity, whereas high diversity reduces persistent activity. Our results provide a quantitative framework for navigating and programming life like behaviours in active droplets and show how closed-loop experimentation can uncover organising principles in complex active matter.

llm.title_ja: 再構成可能な環境におけるアクティブマターとしてのプログラマブル液滴
llm.tldr_ja: 多成分油中水滴の自律的挙動を特徴づけ動的にプログラムするため、持続性と多様性という2つの記述子を用いた自律型クローズドループロボットプラットフォームを提案した。
llm.problem: 非生物と生物の橋渡しをするシステムにおいて、閉ループ再構成を可能にする持続性と適応性の定量的尺度が欠如していること。
llm.method: 持続性と多様性を定量化する記述子を導入し、外部pH外乱の有無における化学組成空間を探索して配合を反復選択する自律型クローズドループロボットプラットフォームの構築。
llm.result: 持続性と多様性の間に行動上のトレードオフが存在することが示され、アクティブ液滴における生命様の挙動のプログラミングフレームワークを提供した。
keywords_ja: ロボットプラットフォーム

2611.01250.title: Shades of Success: Evaluating Manipulation Quality from Object-Centric Constraints
2611.01250.abstract: As learned manipulation policies become increasingly capable of solving practical manipulation tasks, assessing how well a task is performed becomes a fundamental challenge. While binary labels confirm task success, they cannot distinguish successful executions with different levels of geometric precision. To address this, we introduce SPECTRA, an object-centric framework for quantifying execution quality in manipulation of rigid objects. From a small set of oracle demonstrations generated in simulation, SPECTRA represents object interactions through progress-aligned relative poses. SPECTRA identifies which relative-pose directions are constrained and their admissible variations from demonstrations. These constraints establish a reference for evaluating robotic manipulation tasks. To score an unseen execution, deviations beyond the admissible variation are summarized by a Task Quality Index Q in [0,1]. Across seven simulated tasks, SPECTRA recovers constraints with 94% accuracy using 30 demonstrations per task. On rollouts from three learned policies, its scores achieve pooled Spearman correlations with human judgments of p=0.81 over all rollouts and p=0.61 among successful rollouts, exceeding all baselines in both subsets. Using the task reference learned in simulation, we use SPECTRA to select the highest-scoring demonstrations for training a diffusion policy on hardware. Exploratory results show higher success rate than training on randomly selected demonstrations.

llm.title_ja: 成功のグラデーション：オブジェクト中心の制約に基づくマニプレーション品質の評価
llm.tldr_ja: 剛体マニプレーションの実行品質を定量化するため、オブジェクト中心のフレームワークSPECTRAを提案し、シミュレーションで学習したタスク基準を用いて優れたデモの選択やポリシー評価を実現した。
llm.problem: バイナリの成功ラベルでは、異なる幾何学的精度を持つ成功した実行を区別できないこと。
llm.method: シミュレーション上の少数のオラクルデモから、進捗に整列した相対ポーズを通じてオブジェクト間の制約と許容変動を表現するSPECTRAフレームワークの構築。
llm.result: 7つのシミュレーションタスクで94%の精度で制約を復元し、人間の判断との間で高いスピアマン相関（p=0.81）を達成した。
keywords_ja: マニプレーション品質

2611.01250.tldr_en: SPECTRA, an object-centric framework for quantifying execution quality in manipulation of rigid objects, is introduced, which identifies which relative-pose directions are constrained and their admissible variations from demonstrations to establish a reference for evaluating robotic manipulation tasks.

2611.01220.title: Differentiable Iterative Learning Control for Black-Box Position-Commanded Manipulators
2611.01220.abstract: High-accuracy repetitive tracking is challenging for position-commanded manipulators whose low-level controllers are inaccessible, while constrained model-based iterative learning control (ILC) can require substantial manual parameter tuning. We present Differentiable Iterative Learning Control (Diff-ILC), an online bilevel framework that adapts the parameters of a constrained ILC update between physical robot executions. A closed-loop differential model is identified once from paired smooth perturbations and subsequently kept fixed. At each trial, a constrained quadratic program computes a feasible command correction, while a real-anchored next-trial prediction defines a task-level objective. Hypergradients are obtained by implicitly differentiating the locally active KKT system, enabling multiple computational parameter updates without additional robot executions. Experiments on a 6-DoF DOBOT CR3 across unseen planar and three-dimensional trajectories show substantially faster physical-trial convergence than fixed-parameter model-based ILC. Across the four primary trajectories, after only two trial-to-trial updates, Diff-ILC achieves 78.8% and 76.4% lower mean joint-vector and Cartesian RMSE, respectively, than fixed-parameter model-based ILC.

llm.title_ja: ブラックボックス位置指令型マニピュレータのための微分可能反復学習制御
llm.tldr_ja: 低レベルコントローラーにアクセスできない位置指令型マニピュレータの高精度な反復追従を実現するため、オンラインの2レベルフレームワークであるDiff-ILCを提案した。
llm.problem: 低レベルコントローラーにアクセスできない位置指令型マニピュレータにおいて、制約付きモデルベースILCが多大な手動パラメータ調整を必要とすること。
llm.method: 閉ループ差分モデルを一度同定し、局所的にアクティブなKKTシステムの暗黙的微分によりハイパーグラディエントを得るオンライン2レベルフレームワークDiff-ILCの開発。
llm.result: 6軸ロボットを用いた実験において、固定パラメータモデルベースILCと比較してわずか2回の試行更新で大幅に低いRMSEを達成した。

2611.01220.tldr_en: Differentiable Iterative Learning Control (Diff-ILC), an online bilevel framework that adapts the parameters of a constrained ILC update between physical robot executions, shows substantially faster physical-trial convergence than fixed-parameter model-based ILC.

2611.01215.title: Vision-Language Models Are Joint Denoisers in Robotic Action Generation
2611.01215.abstract: Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models cascade pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion action experts, but typically restrict the VLM to providing static conditioning. This separation limits how much pretrained perception and reasoning can guide action generation, especially in out-of-distribution settings. We introduce JADE, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions. Our key insight is that structured action latents allow the VLM to read the current noisy action together with visual observations and language instructions. At every denoising step, the VLM contextualizes the noisy action and guides the action expert through gated cross-attention, so that its guidance evolves with the action being generated. We further supervise the VLM to recover clean action latents from noisy ones, which gives it a direct action-learning signal and couples perception with control. Additionally, joint denoising enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation. An adaptive step-size schedule further balances task performance and inference latency. On RoboDojo, JADE achieves an average success rate of 12.67%, the highest among the evaluated $π_{0.5}$-based methods, and is competitive with recent VLA and WAM foundation models pretrained at scale. It also improves performance on RoboTwin 2.0 and raises the average success rate across four real-world bimanual tasks by 20.8 percentage points compared with $π_{0.5}$.

llm.title_ja: ビジョン言語モデルはロボット行動生成における共同デノイザーである
llm.tldr_ja: VLMと行動専門家を統合して行動を共同で洗練させるJoint Action DEnoiser（JADE）を提案し、少ないサンプリングステップで優れたタスク成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 拡散ベースのVLAモデルにおいてVLMが静的な条件付けに制限されており、事前の知覚や推論が行動生成を十分に導けないこと。
llm.method: 構造化された行動潜在表現を用いて、VLMがノイズの多い行動と視覚・言語観測を一緒に読み取り、ゲーテッドクロスアテンションを通じて行動専門家を導くJADEの導入。
llm.result: RoboDojoでπ0.5ベースの手法の中で最高平均成功率12.67%を達成し、4つの実世界両手タスクで成功率を20.8ポイント向上させた。

2611.01215.tldr_en: JADE is introduced, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions and enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation.

2611.01197.title: Learning Agile Humanoid Dodgeball with Onboard Monocular Vision
2611.01197.abstract: Humanoid robots operating in shared, dynamic environments must respond to rapidly approaching objects while maintaining balance. We study dodgeball as a controlled test of this capability, coupling visual threat assessment with whole-body evasion, recovery, and target reacquisition. We develop a system that integrates onboard monocular perception, temporal ball-state and threat-flag estimation, and learned whole-body control. A ball detector supplies bounding-box histories, and a temporal estimator predicts relative ball position and a binary threat flag. Separate dodge/recovery and search/track policies share this interface and are composed to support repeated encounters. A three-stage curriculum first trains control with privileged ball states, then starts estimator supervision from stable policy rollouts, and finally replaces the actor's privileged inputs with estimator outputs. Analytic projection and perception randomization provide detector-like training observations without image rendering. Across approach-angle bins in controlled simulation, dodge success ranges from 97.8--100.0% for 5.0 m launches at 6 m/s to 33.2--40.8% for 2.5 m launches at 10 m/s, with 1000 throws per speed--distance condition. On a physical Unitree G1, controlled single-throw success exceeds 85% over more than 15 trials. A hardware sequence demonstrates full-azimuth target reacquisition followed by another dodge. These results demonstrate an integrated onboard-monocular-vision system under highly dynamic motions.
2611.01197.comment: Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2027)

llm.title_ja: オンボード単眼ビジョンによる俊敏なヒューノイドのドッジボール学習
llm.tldr_ja: 動的環境でヒューマノイドロボットが急速に接近する物体に対処できるよう、オンボード単眼知覚、時間的ボール状態推定、学習済み全身制御を統合したシステムを開発した。
llm.problem: 共有された動的環境で動作するヒューマノイドロボットが、バランスを維持しながら急速に接近する物体に応答する必要があること。
llm.method: ボール検出器、時間的推定量、分離された回避/復帰ポリシーを組み合わせ、特権状態から訓練して推定器出力を利用するカリキュラム学習の採用。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの高い回避成功率に加え、実機のUnitree G1において単一スローで85%を超える成功率を実証した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.01197.tldr_en: A system that integrates onboard monocular perception, temporal ball-state and threat-flag estimation, and learned whole-body control is developed, demonstrating an integrated onboard-monocular-vision system under highly dynamic motions.

2611.01190.title: ClothDojo: Learned Data Generation and Benchmarking for Bimanual Garment Flattening and Folding
2611.01190.abstract: Garment flattening and folding require robots to identify garment structure during manipulation and adapt their actions as the cloth deforms. We present ClothDojo, a simulation platform that generates adaptive manipulation trajectories at scale across diverse garments and initial states and evaluates policies in closed loop. ClothDojo encodes each garment's canonical mesh coordinates as an NOCS texture, providing canonical surface-position cues through the visual interface of a pretrained vision-language-action model. We fine-tune the model on human demonstrations and corrections to obtain a data-generation policy. The policy autonomously generates simulated manipulation trajectories, and we retain rollouts that satisfy task-specific success criteria. Each retained trajectory is re-rendered under a randomly sampled appearance to provide RGB observations for downstream policies that do not receive NOCS. Across both tasks, the policy produces nearly 8,000 successful trajectories over hundreds of garments. RGB policies trained on these generated trajectories outperform those trained directly on the original human demonstrations and corrections across all evaluated garment splits and appearance settings. Evaluations across multiple policy models show that overall performance and appearance robustness vary across models and tasks, while generalization to unseen garments remains a common challenge.
2611.01190.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://clothdojo.github.io/

llm.title_ja: ClothDojo：衣服の平坦化と折り畳みのための学習済みデータ生成とベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 衣服の平坦化と折り畳みのために、多様な衣服と初期状態に対して適応的な操作軌跡を大規模に生成しポリシーを評価するシミュレーションプラットフォームClothDojoを提案した。
llm.problem: 衣服の操作において、ロボットが操作中に衣服の構造を識別し、布の変形に合わせて行動を適応させる必要があること。
llm.method: NOCSテクスチャを用いて衣服のメッシュ座標をコード化し、デモと修正から自動で成功軌跡を生成してダウンストリームポリシーの学習に利用するプラットフォームの構築。
llm.result: 生成された軌跡で学習したRGBポリシーは、元の人間のデモから直接学習したものよりも、すべての評価設定で優れた性能を示した。

2611.01190.tldr_en: ClothDojo is a simulation platform that generates adaptive manipulation trajectories at scale across diverse garments and initial states and evaluates policies in closed loop, showing that overall performance and appearance robustness vary across models and tasks, while generalization to unseen garments remains a common challenge.

2611.01112.title: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
2611.01112.abstract: Vision-language models can interpret instructions and plan manipulation tasks, yet struggle when acting directly as robot policies. On RoboDojo, a large planning-execution gap separates high-level task decisions from physical execution: removing arm execution raises GPT-6 Astra's success rate from 22.5% under the reference control interface to 76.2%. We present Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness that closes 68.3% of this gap in zero-shot manipulation without target-task trials or resets. In Auriga, the model makes all task decisions over an explicit task belief and acts through either direct tool calls or synthesized multi-step Python programs, while the harness supplies calibrated 3D measurements, finger-referenced dual-arm control, and a single admission gateway to the robot. Before motion, the model inspects a visual trajectory preview while simulation is paused; during execution, the harness checks declared stage tolerances and grasp bounds, stopping the robot on divergence and returning the measured discrepancy for in-place recovery. Developed across 13 cross-task capability iterations and frozen for evaluation, Auriga ranks first on the RoboDojo leaderboard with a 57.7% success rate (64.0 Score), more than doubling the reference harness on the same model, and remains first under scene randomization while learned policies drop by up to 33.9%. On RoboCasa365, the same frozen harness reaches a 73.2% success rate, outperforming VLA-assisted agents by up to 23.1% on composite tasks. Project page: https://auriga.stelledge.com/ Code: https://github.com/lose4578/Auriga
2611.01112.tldr_en: Developed across 13 cross-task capability iterations and frozen for evaluation, Auriga ranks first on the RoboDojo leaderboard with a 57.7% success rate (64.0 Score), more than doubling the reference harness on the same model, and remains first under scene randomization while learned policies drop by up to 33.9%.
2611.01112.hf_summary_en: Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness, closes most of the planning-execution gap in zero-shot robot manipulation by combining explicit task beliefs, calibrated 3D measurements, dual-arm control, and execution monitoring, achieving state-of-the-art results on RoboDojo and RoboCasa365.

2611.01081.title: Robust Safety Assurance for Robotic Swarms Using Decentralized Collision Verification
2611.01081.abstract: In this paper we present the methodologies, results, and analysis used to deploy a decentralized safety verification algorithm on a robotic swarm to prevent collisions at runtime in an outdoor environment. Typically, approaches toward verification of swarms of cyber-physical systems (CPS) are evaluated solely in numerical simulations or in highly controlled, noiseless indoor environments. Our efforts to implement collision avoidance on a real swarm system outdoors have revealed that the underlying algorithmic assumptions juxtaposed against the implementation details of the target system are critical factors in a method's efficacy in the real world. Here we modify, enhance, and analyze a decentralized reachability-based method for collision avoidance on a size, weight, and power-constrained uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm with the objective of illustrating the challenges of real-world CPS deployments as well as provide guidance for researchers in this space. Verification performance, resource utilization, and timing data were gathered over the course of 140 total outdoor vehicle flights, including 6 swarm flights composed of 8 UAVs, and used to improve collision-avoidance performance as experimentation progressed. Our extensive experiments show that the proposed decentralized runtime verification approach can efficiently verify the safety of multiple UAVs in real-time and help all agents take safe actions to avoid collisions. On average, each agent, using our open-source safety_checker library, takes approximately 500-520 ms to verify its safety for the next 4 s into the future, in which the reachable set broadcast time dominates the total verification time (~300-500 ms).
2611.01081.comment: Accepted version. Published in IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems, vol. 62, pp. 9706-9717, 2026. 13 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Video: https://youtu.be/Y-Z3IN--_Vc
2611.01081.journal_ref: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems, vol. 62, pp. 9706-9717, 2026

llm.title_ja: 分散型衝突検証を用いたロボット群のためのロバストな安全性保証
llm.tldr_ja: 屋外環境のロボット群において実行時衝突を防ぐため、到達可能性に基づく分散型安全性検証手法を改良・分析し、多数の屋外飛行実験を通じて検証した。
llm.problem: サイバー物理システムの群知能に対する検証手法が、数値シミュレーションや管理された屋内環境でのみ評価されがちであること。
llm.method: サイズ・重量・電力制約のあるUAV群向けに分散型到達可能性ベースの衝突回避手法を拡張し、open-sourceのsafety_checkerライブラリを用いて実装。
llm.result: 140回を超える屋外飛行実験を通じて、分散型実行時検証アプローチが複数のUAVの安全性をリアルタイムで効率的に検証できることを示した。

badges.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Elect 2026

2611.01081.tldr_en: This article presents the methodologies, results, and analysis used to deploy a decentralized safety verification algorithm on a robotic swarm to prevent collisions at runtime in an outdoor environment, with the objective of illustrating the challenges of real-world CPS deployments.
2611.01081.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems

2611.01071.title: Hi-CoLA: High Confidence Lower Bound Approximation Based Reinforcement Learning for Flex-Route Transit Operation Control
2611.01071.abstract: This paper studies safe policy improvement for real-time operation control of flex-route transit (FRT) systems, where robustness is critical and any performance decrease is undesirable. While reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong empirical success, its adoption remains limited in safety and cost critical applications, such as intelligent transportation, since learned policies lack statistically certified performance guarantees before deployment. In this paper, we propose the High Confidence Lower Bound Approximation (Hi-CoLA) RL framework, which combines importance sampling and concentration inequalities with a differentiable surrogate network to efficiently estimate the high-confidence performance lower bound and optimize it via policy gradient for robust performance improvement. On the FRT operation control problem, Hi-CoLA outperforms state-of-the-art offline and safe RL methods in both average and tail-risk performance. A case study on an actual route in Chicago, implemented in the SUMO simulator, serves as a proof of concept. Hi-CoLA enhances real-time FRT control with guaranteed performance and is broadly applicable to other safety critical decision-making scenarios.

llm.title_ja: Hi-CoLA：フレキシブルルート交通運行制御のための高信頼度下界近似に基づく強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: フレキシブルルート交通システムの安全なポリシー改善のため、重要度サンプリングと集中不等式を組み合わせた高信頼度パフォーマンス下界近似（Hi-CoLA）フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 強化学習の方策が展開前に統計的に証明された性能保証を欠いており、安全性やコストが重要な交通システムでの採用が制限されていること。
llm.method: 重要度サンプリング、集中不等式、微分可能なサロゲートネットワークを組み合わせて性能の下界を効率的に推定し、方策勾配で最適化するHi-CoLAフレームワークの構築。
llm.result: シミュレータを用いたケーススタディにおいて、平均およびテールリスクのパフォーマンスの両方で最先端のオフラインおよび安全強化学習手法を上回った。

2611.01071.tldr_en: The High Confidence Lower Bound Approximation (Hi-CoLA) RL framework is proposed, which combines importance sampling and concentration inequalities with a differentiable surrogate network to efficiently estimate the high-confidence performance lower bound and optimize it via policy gradient for robust performance improvement.

2611.01067.title: Ripple: Deadline-Aware CPU-GPU Sharing for Embodied Inference
2611.01067.abstract: Unified-memory edge devices increasingly run LLM/VLM inference alongside time-critical CPU tasks for perception and control. GPU memory traffic can overwhelm these tasks, yet platforms such as DGX Spark expose neither bandwidth counters nor direct bandwidth regulation. We present Ripple, a CPU-GPU co-scheduler that combines model-derived GPU memory volumes with CPU completion feedback to regulate interference. Ripple divides inference into pausable, layer-based units and translates each CPU job's deadline slack into a GPU-byte budget, admitting work within the budgets of all overlapping jobs. Online updates track changing interference, while deadline-aware pacing and judicious SM footprint narrowing preserve inference progress. Implemented with SGLang engine hooks and a central scheduler, we evaluate Ripple on DGX Spark with four robotic CPU task mixes and LLM/VLM inference. It is the only evaluated approach that consistently meets the 2% CPU deadline-miss target and VLM deadlines across the tested deadline settings while retaining best-effort LLM throughput.

llm.title_ja: Ripple：身体性推論のための期限を考慮したCPU-GPU共有
llm.tldr_ja: エッジデバイス上でLLM/VLM推論と時間的制約のあるCPUタスクを効率的に共存させるため、GPUメモリ量とCPU完了フィードバックを組み合わせて干渉を調整するCPU-GPU共同スケジューラRippleを提案した。
llm.problem: 統合メモリのエッジデバイスにおいて、GPUメモリトラフィックが知覚や制御のための時間的制約のあるCPUタスクを圧倒してしまうこと。
llm.method: 推論をレイヤーベースの単位に分割し、CPUジョブの期限スラックをGPUバイト予算に翻訳して割り込み作業を調整するCPU-GPU共同スケジューラRippleの実装。
llm.result: テストされたすべての期限設定において、ベストエフォートのLLMスループットを維持しつつ、CPUの期限ミス目標とVLMの期限を首尾一貫して満たす唯一の手法となった。

2611.01067.tldr_en: Ripple is presented, a CPU-GPU co-scheduler that combines model-derived GPU memory volumes with CPU completion feedback to regulate interference and is the only evaluated approach that consistently meets the 2% CPU deadline-miss target and VLM deadlines across the tested deadline settings while retaining best-effort LLM throughput.

2611.01039.title: pico-WAM: Evaluating Counterfactual Prediction and Planning Error in a Compact World Action Model
2611.01039.abstract: When a World Action Model fails at control, is the bottleneck proposal generation or trajectory scoring? We introduce pico-WAM, a compact model with supplied physical state for tracing policy-dynamics interactions. Using 206 Push-T demonstrations and 15 training seeds, we compare data regimes and search configurations. Counterfactual branch training improves short-horizon cost ranking and enlarges the coverage advantage of policy-restarted over warm-started search by 4.8 percentage points; restart wins under both data regimes. Replacing learned trajectory scores with simulator costs improves coverage by 12.2 points while retaining learned proposals. Substituting simulator states in proposal generation alone shows no detected gain. Component diagnostics and a separate door-opening study show why better ranking need not yield better control or outperform imitation. These controlled interventions identify scoring as an effective improvement target in the tested setting and provide a reproducible protocol for diagnosing compact world models.
2611.01039.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures. Code available at https://github.com/keivalya/pico-wam

llm.title_ja: pico-WAM：コンパクトなワールドアクションモデルにおける反事実的予測と計画エラーの評価
llm.tldr_ja: ワールドアクションモデルの制御失敗時のボトルネックを特定するため、物理状態を備えたコンパクトなモデルpico-WAMを導入し、データレジームと探索構成を比較評価した。
llm.problem: ワールドアクションモデルが制御に失敗した際、そのボトルネックが提案生成にあるのか軌跡スコアリングにあるのかが不明であること。
llm.method: 206件のPush-Tデモを用いて、反事実的分岐訓練やシミュレータコストの置換などを行い、方策とダイナミクスの相互作用を追跡するコンパクトモデルの検証。
llm.result: カウンターファクトラル分岐訓練が短期ホライズンのコストランキングを改善し、シミュレータコストによる置き換えがカバレッジを12.2ポイント向上させることを示した。

2611.01039.tldr_en: This work introduces pico-WAM, a compact model with supplied physical state for tracing policy-dynamics interactions and provides a reproducible protocol for diagnosing compact world models.

2611.01038.title: HALO-LP: A Homogeneous All-Shifted Non-Interior-Point Method for Linear Programming
2611.01038.abstract: This letter introduces HALO-LP, a novel homogeneous all-shifted non-interior-point method for linear programming (LP). The proposed method combines a homogeneous self-dual (HSD) embedding with all-shifted nonlinear complementarity (NCP) functions and proximal primal-dual regularization, enabling arbitrary primal-dual warm starts without requiring strictly interior iterates. The resulting Newton equations admit a condensation based on a positive-definite matrix that can be efficiently factorized using Cholesky decomposition, while the HSD embedding enables primal and dual infeasibility detection through Farkas certificates. Numerical evaluations on perturbed LP instances derived from the Netlib test set demonstrate state-of-the-art warm-starting performance, outperforming the competing solvers in the evaluated setting. We further validate optimality and infeasibility detection on analytically characterized LP problems. Finally, we demonstrate HALO-LP's applicability to robotic optimal control through sequential linear programming (SLP) for centroidal walking and trotting of quadrupedal robots.

llm.title_ja: HALO-LP：線形計画法のための同次型全シフト非内点法
llm.tldr_ja: 線形計画法（LP）に向けて、厳密な内点を必要とせずに任意の主・双対ウォームスタートを可能にする同次型全シフト非内点法（HALO-LP）を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の線形計画法ソルバーが厳密な内点を必要とし、ウォームスタートや非負制約の扱いに課題があること。
llm.method: 同次自己双対埋め込みと全シフト非線形相補関数、および近接主双対正則化を組み合わせた最適化アルゴリズムの開発。
llm.result: Netlibテストセットから派生したLPインスタンスにおいて最先端のウォームスタート性能を示し、四脚ロボットの歩行制御への応用を実証した。

2611.01038.tldr_en: HALO-LP is introduced, a novel homogeneous all-shifted non-interior-point method for linear programming (LP) that combines a homogeneous self-dual (HSD) embedding with all-shifted nonlinear complementarity (NCP) functions and proximal primal-dual regularization, enabling arbitrary primal-dual warm starts without requiring strictly interior iterates.

2611.01031.title: Trouble With Time: Compile Timestamps and First-Seen Date Regression in EMBER2024
2611.01031.abstract: Reliable first-seen dates are important for constructing temporal malware evaluation splits, but this information often comes from external services that are not equally accessible to all researchers. We investigate whether machine learning can instead estimate an executable's first-seen date or determine when its PE/COFF compilation timestamp is unreliable. Using EMBER2024, we evaluate feature-based and raw-byte models across classification, regression, ranking, and latent-reliability formulations. Direct first-seen regression produces errors comparable to a substantial portion of the dataset's collection window, and none of the evaluated scores provides a useful chronological ordering of files. Current models therefore cannot replace externally sourced first-seen metadata. In contrast, classifiers can identify timestamps that fall within specified tolerances of first seen and can detect clearly implausible timestamps with high discrimination. We also find substantial timestamp disagreement among both benign and malicious executables, indicating that unreliable timestamps are not exclusively a product of malicious manipulation. These results establish baselines and identify timestamp reliability as a distinct direction for future security-ML research.
2611.01031.comment: To appear in the Conference on Applied Machine Learning for Information Security (CAMLIS) 2026

llm.title_ja: 時間の問題：EMBER2024におけるコンパイルタイムスタンプと最初に観測された日付の回帰
llm.tldr_ja: 実行ファイルの最初の検出日を機械学習で推定できるかを調査し、直接的な回帰は困難である一方、分類器によって信頼性の低いタイムスタンプを高精度に検出できることを示した。
llm.problem: 一時的なマルウェア評価の分割に重要な最初の検出日情報が外部サービスに依存しており、信頼性の評価が必要であること。
llm.method: EMBER2024データセットを用い、特徴量ベースおよび生バイトモデルによる分類、回帰、ランキング、潜在的信頼性定式化の評価。
llm.result: 直接的な第一発見日回帰は困難だが、分類器により不正なタイムスタンプや不審なタイムスタンプを高精度に識別できることを確認した。

2611.01031.tldr_en: This work investigates whether machine learning can estimate an executable's first-seen date or determine when its PE/COFF compilation timestamp is unreliable, and establishes baselines and identifies timestamp reliability as a distinct direction for future security-ML research.

2611.01011.title: Leap-VLA: High-Rate Robot Control from a Low-Rate VLM Backbone
2611.01011.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models re-encode the full observation through a multi-billion-parameter vision-language model (VLM) at every control step, even though scene semantics evolve at roughly 1 Hz while reactive control requires 20-50 Hz. We present a VLA that decouples the two: a VLM runs as a low-frequency semantic anchor whose cached context is reused across control steps, while a flow-matching action expert operates at high frequency, consuming the cached semantics with a fresh, low-latency visual stream from a compact encoder pretrained on robot video with masked reconstruction, optical flow, and depth. The measured age $τ$ of the cache conditions the expert through adaptive layer normalization. Reusing the cache makes the policy a function of its age, and training covers that function explicitly: cache ages sampled from real episode history, plus an age-ramped pixel corruption that erases the stale snapshot the way deployed staleness corrupts content. On the asynchronous deployment stack, the recipe closes most of the staleness gap: on LIBERO-Spatial, 61.4% to 95.5% at a 2 s semantic refresh (95.9% at 1 s, within 1.6 points of the frequency-matched anchor); averaged over the four LIBERO suites, the deployed policy holds 95.2% at a 1 s refresh and 94.5% at 2 s against a 96.3% matched anchor. A forward-only chunk-boundary correction (soft-nudge), an autograd-free reformulation of real-time-chunking guidance, carries per-control-step re-planning without loss (97.1%) at zero added latency. The same lens exposes a second defect: under an instruction-scene mismatch the policy keeps manipulating the scene, and a chain-of-thought verdict gate trained on zero-cost negative episodes freezes execution exactly on mismatched instructions without hurting feasible success.
2611.01011.comment: 21 pages, 14 figures. Corresponding author: Lin Yang

llm.title_ja: Leap-VLA：低レートVLMバックボーンからの高レートロボット制御
llm.tldr_ja: セマンティクスの進化が低速である一方リアクティブ制御が高レートを要求する問題に対し、低周波VLMキャッシュと高周波フローマッチング行動専門家を分離したLeap-VLAを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルがすべての制御ステップで大規模VLMを通して全観測を再エンコードするため、シーンのセマンティクス変化と制御周波数の間でミスマッチが生じること。
llm.method: 低周波のセマンティックアンカーとして動作するVLMと、キャッシュされたセマンティクスとコンパクトなエンコーダからの高頻度視覚ストリームを消費するフローマッチング行動専門家への分離。
llm.result: LIBEROスイートにおいて、1〜2秒のセマンティックリフレッシュレートに対して、同期ベースラインに匹敵する95%以上の高い成功率を維持した。

2611.01011.tldr_en: A VLA that decouples the two: a VLM runs as a low-frequency semantic anchor whose cached context is reused across control steps, while a flow-matching action expert operates at high frequency, consuming the cached semantics with a fresh, low-latency visual stream from a compact encoder pretrained on robot video with masked reconstruction, optical flow, and depth.

2611.00957.title: Evaluating Tactile Foundation Models for End-to-End Imitation Learning in Contact-Rich Manipulation
2611.00957.abstract: Tactile sensing plays an important role in imitation learning for contact-rich manipulation by providing direct observations of physical contact with objects. Recently, several tactile foundation models (TFMs) have been proposed to learn general-purpose tactile representations through pretraining on large-scale tactile datasets. However, how these pretrained tactile representations should be leveraged for end-to-end imitation learning remains insufficiently explored. In this work, we integrate multiple TFMs into Diffusion Policy and systematically evaluate their effectiveness for contact-rich manipulation under common experimental settings. We further investigate adaptation strategies, including encoder fine-tuning and task-specific mid-training, to understand how pretrained tactile representations can be effectively used for downstream imitation learning. Through extensive evaluation across diverse manipulation tasks in both real-world and simulation environments, including more than 5,000 real-world policy rollouts, we provide empirical insights into the use of TFMs for end-to-end imitation learning. Project page: https://mmurooka.github.io/tfm4il-project-page/
2611.00957.comment: Accepted for the 2027 IEEE/SICE International Symposium on System Integration (SII 2027)

llm.title_ja: 接触リッチなマニプレーションのエンドツーエンド模倣学習における触覚基盤モデルの評価
llm.tldr_ja: 接触リッチなマニプレーションの模倣学習において複数の触覚基盤モデル（TFM）をDiffusion Policyに統合し、適応戦略を含めてその有効性を体系的に評価した。
llm.problem: 大規模な触覚データセットで事前学習された触覚表現を、エンドツーエンドの模倣学習にどのように活用すべきかが十分に探求されていないこと。
llm.method: 複数のTFMをDiffusion Policyに統合し、エンコーダの微調整やタスク固有の中間トレーニングなどの適応戦略を用いた実世界およびシミュレーションでの評価。
llm.result: 5,000回を超える実世界ポリシーロールアウトを通じた広範な評価により、エンドツーエンド模倣学習におけるTFMの活用に関する実証的知見を提供した。
keywords_ja: 接触リッチマニプレーション

2611.00957.tldr_en: This work integrates multiple TFMs into Diffusion Policy and systematically evaluates their effectiveness for contact-rich manipulation under common experimental settings, and provides empirical insights into the use of TFMs for end-to-end imitation learning.

2611.00955.title: Task-Specialized Language-Conditioned Models for Fine-Grained Robotic Manipulation
2611.00955.abstract: Fine-grained robotic manipulation requires instruction grounding, robust perception, and precise contact control. We describe our submission to the MetaFine Open Competition at CoRL 2026. Five independently trained models use a common architecture with frozen DINOv2 and CLIP encoders, trainable language-conditioned feature modulation, and task-specific action heads. We improve demonstrations through contact-aware grasp filtering, instruction-matched data, and expert correction of insertion failures. At inference, task-dependent strategies include photometric test-time augmentation, stochastic action averaging, and uncertainty-triggered replanning. Our submission achieves an official overall score of 0.914 and ranks third among 15 teams. We analyze the models and their task-specific behavior.
2611.00955.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Technical report for the MetaFine Open Competition at CoRL 2026

llm.title_ja: タスク特化型言語条件付けモデルによる微細なロボットマニプレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 微細なロボットマニプレーションに向けて、凍結されたDINOv2およびCLIPエンコーダとタスク特化型アクションヘッドを共通アーキテクチャに組み合わせたモデル群を構築し評価した。
llm.problem: 微細なロボットマニプレーションには、指示の接地、頑健な知覚、および正確な接触制御が要求されること。
llm.method: 接触を考慮した把持フィルタリング、指示に一致するデータの改良、およびテスト時拡張や不確実性駆動型再計画などのタスク依存戦略の採用。
llm.result: MetaFineオープンコンペティションにおいて公式総合スコア0.914を達成し、15チーム中3位にランクインした。
keywords_ja: ロボットコンペティション

2611.00955.tldr_en: This paper describes five independently trained models that use a common architecture with frozen DINOv2 and CLIP encoders, trainable language-conditioned feature modulation, and task-specific action heads to fine-grained robotic manipulation and analyzes the models and their task-specific behavior.

2611.00951.title: Why Koopman Structure Does Not Help Differentiable World Models for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking
2611.00951.abstract: We test whether Koopman structure, linear dynamics in a lifted state space, helps when a humanoid whole-body tracking policy is trained by backpropagating through a differentiable world model, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline for simulated Unitree G1 tracking. It does not: return is at best equal (0.823 versus 0.830), one-step error on identical data is 1.3 to 1.6 times the MLP's, and training is about 15% slower. Lifted rollouts diverge or fail to train a policy; of the schemes tested, re-lifting at every imagined step trains best. Re-lifting never uses the lifted linear dynamics and leaves a model affine in the action, with state-dependent offset and slope; an action-affine MLP also predicts worse, so the cost belongs to this class. At a fixed state, the curvature of the true dynamics in the action explains only part of it. Across states, the policy's actions span a curved region, so an affine model fits policy data only as the tangent at the policy's action, the operating point: on G1, the MLP's tangent there is as accurate as the MLP; at the mean action, 31 times worse. The offset must encode, from the state alone, where the policy acts, whereas an MLP reads the action. Supplying the policy's action removes most of the remaining gap on G1, Ant and Humanoid. The only online repair approaching the MLP feeds the action into the nonlinear lift, giving up the structure. The MLP world model thus remains the better choice here.
2611.00951.tldr_en: It is tested whether Koopman structure helps a differentiable world model used to train a simulated Unitree G1 whole-body tracking policy by backpropagation through imagined rollouts through imagined rollouts, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline.

llm.title_ja: クーパマン構造がヒューマノイド全身トラッキングの微分可能世界モデルに寄与しない理由
llm.tldr_ja: 微分可能世界モデルを用いたヒューマノイドのトラッキングにおいて、クーパマン構造の導入が性能向上につながらないことを検証した。
llm.problem: リフトされた状態空間における線形ダイナミクス（クーパマン構造）が、微分可能世界モデルの学習に有効かどうかは不明であった。
llm.method: Unitree G1のシミュレーション環境において、MLP世界モデルをクーパマン構造に基づくモデルに置き換えて性能を比較検証した。
llm.result: リフトされた線形ダイナミクスは性能を向上させず、MLPベースの世界モデルの方が優れた選択肢であることが示された。

2611.00898.title: Trading Transparency for Stability: Friction-Cone-Constrained Bilateral Teleoperation for Opening Doors of Unsecured Furniture
2611.00898.abstract: Opening the door of unsecured furniture loads the frictional contacts at its supports; too large a pull slides or tips the object. A friction-cone constraint on the commanded wrench removes this failure mode but costs haptic transparency. We quantify the trade-off: an admissible wrench set built from contact friction cones and support-polygon tipping margins is shrunk for robustness to bounded mass and friction errors, and any command in the shrunken set provably leaves the furniture static (Prop. 1). We call this map the robust friction cone projection (RFCP). RFCP and its haptic guard admit a bounded force transmission error (Prop. 2): transparency degrades only within a band near the constraint boundary, whose width is set by one scalar, the stability factor . A working condition controller handles the door: the operator commands a scalar swing amplitude, the slave orientation follows hinge kinematics, and the grasp wrench is regulated per phase. A pre task certificate decides whether a door can be opened without moving the furniture. Experiments on three cabinets and two supports with five operators (100 trials) measure the stability transparency trade-off and ablate the guard, RFCP and the position baseline. The mechanism is not door-specific: it applies to any body reacted by frictional contacts.
2611.00898.tldr_en: The trade-off is quantified: an admissible wrench set built from contact friction cones and support-polygon tipping margins is shrunk for robustness to bounded mass and friction errors, and any command in the shrunken set provably leaves the furniture static.

llm.title_ja: 透明性と安定性のトレードオフ：固定されていない家具の扉を開けるための摩擦円錐制約付き両側遠隔操作
llm.tldr_ja: 家具の転倒や滑りを防ぎつつ扉を開けるため、接触摩擦円錐と支持多角形に基づいた頑健な摩擦円錐射影（RFCP）を提案した。
llm.problem: 固定されていない家具の扉を開ける際、過度な引張り力は支持部の摩擦接点を滑らせたり転倒させたりする。
llm.method: 接触摩擦円錐と支持多角形の転倒マージンから許容されるレンチ集合を構築し、境界付近で透明性を犠牲にして頑健性を確保するRFCPを設計した。
llm.result: 3つのキャビネットと2つの支持台を用いた100回の実験により、安定性と触覚の透明性のトレードオフを定量化した。

2611.00896.title: Verifying Test-State Identity in Paired Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.00896.abstract: Simulation-based VLA evaluation often treats matching task, seed, and episode identifiers as sufficient evidence that two policies faced identical test conditions. Under specific vectorized reset and autoreset conditions, different termination timing can change subsequent initial-state assignment, so the same episode index need not mean the same test state. We present an evaluation-integrity framework for paired comparison - invariants I1-I5, provenance logging, optional scene fingerprints, and an automated checker - and a controlled LeRobot 0.6.1 LIBERO harness study with emulated controllers. Four evidence levels are kept separate: (A) mixed-horizon Sync wave-1 IDs [20, 5, 22, 7] vs [4, 5, 6, 7]; (B) homogeneous separate-job Sync control (16 cells, 0 ID/fingerprint mismatches); (C) Async+Freeze batch-size map differences (12 I3 mismatches; bs=8 incomplete; mechanism unisolated); (D) a synthetic McNemar illustration only. Controllers were emulated and no real-VLA shared-vector experiment was completed. We recommend checking declared/resolved init-state identity and provenance before paired statistics. We do not claim that published VLA leaderboards are generally invalid.
2611.00896.tldr_en: An evaluation-integrity framework for paired comparison - invariants I1-I5, provenance logging, optional scene fingerprints, and an automated checker - and a controlled LeRobot 0.6.1 LIBERO harness study with emulated controllers are presented.

llm.title_ja: 視覚言語行動モデルのペア評価におけるテスト状態同一性の検証
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーションベースのVLA評価において同一のテスト条件を保証するため、評価インテグリティフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: シミュレーションにおける終了タイミングの違いにより、同じエピソードインデックスでも異なる初期状態が割り当てられる問題がある。
llm.method: 不変条件I1-I5、プロベナンスロギング、シーンフィンガープリント、自動チェッカーからなる評価インテグリティフレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: 制御されたLeRobot 0.6.1 LIBEROハーネススタディを通じて、ペア統計の前に初期状態の同一性とプロベナンスを確認することの重要性を示した。

2611.00887.title: Multi-quadrotor systems interconnected via structurally unknown forces and moments
2611.00887.abstract: This work addresses the challenge of controlling multi-quadrotor systems subject to tight uncertain couplings. We consider interconnection forces and moments among the quadrotors to be state-dependent functions of the coordination errors, without assuming knowledge of their functional/parametric structures, e.g., no linear-in-parameters assumptions are made. We only rely on general state-dependent quadratic bounds valid for several Euler-Lagrange mechanical systems. We propose a coordination strategy embedding adaptive laws dedicated to compensating for the lack of structural knowledge. Unlike conventional decoupled position-attitude designs, we present a coupled stability analysis accounting for the position-attitude couplings induced by the interconnection forces and moments. The analysis, along with real experiments involving cooperative aerial transportation of rope-interconnected payloads, demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed solution in compensating for these complex interconnections. Comparative experiments show that, when a payload drop induces a disturbance propagating through the ropes across the whole formation, the proposed strategy reduces significantly post-disturbance transients.
2611.00887.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Video available at: https://tinyurl.com/4mzpb9rf

llm.title_ja: 構造的に未知の力とモーメントを介して相互接続されたマルチクアッドローターシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 厳密な不確実結合を持つマルチクアッドローターシステムの制御課題に対し、構造的知識を仮定しない協調戦略を提案した。
llm.problem: クアッドローター間の相互接続力やモーメントの関数的・パラメトリックな構造が未知である場合の制御が課題となる。
llm.method: 構造的知識の欠如を補償する適応則を組み込んだ協調戦略と、位置・姿勢の結合を考慮した統合的な安定性解析を提案した。
llm.result: ロープで接続されたペイロードの協調空輸実験を通じて、外乱伝播による過渡現象を大幅に軽減できることを実証した。

2611.00879.title: Flap like a bat: Soft pneumatic wings for biomimetic ornithopters
2611.00879.abstract: This paper describes the development of a bio-inspired ornithopter wing mechanism that uses soft pneumatic actuators, such as PneuNet structures, in place of revolute joints, inspired by the complicated kinematics of bat flight. The proposed design employs pneumatically driven air pockets within a flexible wing skeleton to achieve smooth, lifelike flapping motion. The actuation system is controlled by 3/2-way solenoid valves and an air pump, which manipulate airflow and actuator deformation. We demonstrate, using ANSYS FEA software, the bending behavior of the PneuNet actuators under varying pressures to inform the wing's structural design. The implementation of soft robotics in the flapping-wing system offers potential advantages over traditional mechanisms, such as reduced mechanical complexity, lower acoustic signatures, enhanced adaptability, and wing morphing. This work demonstrates the feasibility of replacing rigid revolute joints with compliant pneumatic actuators, enabling more agile, silent, and biomimetic aerial robots.
2611.00879.tldr_en: A bio-inspired ornithopter wing mechanism that uses soft pneumatic actuators, such as PneuNet structures, in place of revolute joints, inspired by the complicated kinematics of bat flight is developed.

llm.title_ja: コウモリのように羽ばたく：生体模倣オーニソプターのためのソフト空圧翼
llm.tldr_ja: コウモリの複雑な飛行運動に着目し、回転関節の代わりにソフト空圧アクチュエータを用いた生体模倣オーニソプターの翼機構を開発した。
llm.problem: 従来の剛体関節を用いた羽ばたき翼機構は、機械的複雑さや騒音などの課題を抱えている。
llm.method: PneuNet構造などのソフト空圧アクチュエータを柔軟な翼骨格内に配置し、ソレノイドバルブとポンプで気流と変形を制御する機構を設計した。
llm.result: ANSYSを用いたFEA解析および実証により、剛体関節を柔軟な空圧アクチュエータに置き換えることの有効性と機敏性を示した。
keywords_ja: 羽ばたき飛行ロボット

2611.00870.title: A Reproducible Reconstruction and Evaluation Framework for Photorealistic Lunar Analog Scene Reconstruction Toward Digital Twins
2611.00870.abstract: In this paper, we present a reconstruction pipeline that empirically quantifies the photorealistic scene reconstruction accuracy from both human-controlled and rover mast camera monocular feeds against physical ground truth as a function of Lunar traversal effects (e.g., motion blur, haze due to lofted regolith, trajectory bias, and sparse views). First, we benchmark six variants of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) across three Lunar analog scenes on held-out test sets using standard photometric metrics. We then establish how under traversal effects, this test-set-specific Novel View Synthesis (NVS) performance does not proportionally scale to the same photometric metrics in the reconstructed DTs. Our results quantify that splat training metrics alone are insufficient predictors of Cross-Reconstruction Photorealistic NVS Fidelity (CRPNVS), and that factors such as rover trajectory bias and geometric scene coverage play a critical role in determining the photorealistic quality of the reconstructed scenes targeting Lunar analog Digital Twins. Additionally, we pilot study Coverage Score ($S_c$), a geometry-based diagnostic derived from COLMAP poses and point cloud structure that provides a meaningful heuristic about the highest achievable CRPNVS structural fidelity, independently of splat training performance in the absence of a human-controlled reference. These findings establish a standardized, human control-referenced evaluation pipeline for photorealistic scene reconstruction for Lunar-analog Digital Twin development and future planetary exploration. Code and project page: https://rose-lab-admin.github.io/rose-lunar-dt-rec

llm.title_ja: デジタルツインに向けたフォトリアルな月面アナログシーン再構築のための再現可能な再構築および評価フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 月面走行効果を考慮した単眼カメラ映像からのフォトリアルなシーン再構築精度を評価するパイプラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 月面環境における運動ぼかしや塵などの影響下で、3Dガウススプラッティングのトレーニング指標が実際の再構築精度と一致しない。
llm.method: 3DGSの6つのバリアントをベンチマークし、地上真値と比較してクロス再構築フォトリアルNVS忠実度（CRPNVS）を評価するパイプラインを構築した。
llm.result: スプラットのトレーニング指標単体ではCRPNVSの十分な予測因子にならないこと、および幾何学的シーンカバレッジの重要性を定量化した。

2611.00756.title: SceneBound: How Much Should a Streaming 3D Reconstruction Model Remember?
2611.00756.abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction models keep past video frames in a recurrent state, fast weights from test-time training, or a key-value (KV) cache. Each written frame shifts the coordinate frame of later cameras or occupies GPU memory. Training-free rules decide what to write from a signal of the current frame. How much they write accounts for their mean accuracy: spending the update budget of a gate at uniformly spaced frames, with no signal, matches nine published gates, and the budget bounds the drift of the state wherever the writes fall. We propose SceneBound, a training-free rule that writes a frame only when its predicted camera pose lies at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe. Its keyframe count stays within a constant factor of the covering number of the visited poses, the fewest views that keep a keyframe near every camera, so the count grows with the places visited and stays flat when the camera returns. In large scenes, SceneBound closes a submap once decoding its first frame again reveals drift. SceneBound uses one radius across four released models and three memory types. In the recurrent state of CUT3R and the KV cache of StreamVGGT, it achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules we evaluate, in one pass and over nine passes of a scene, where its keyframes grow by 3% to 6%.
2611.00756.tldr_en: SceneBound is proposed, a training-free rule that writes a frame only when its predicted camera pose lies at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe, and achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules.

llm.title_ja: SceneBound：ストリーミング3D再構築モデルはどれくらい記憶すべきか？
llm.tldr_ja: 予測されたカメラポーズが既存のキーフレームから一定の距離離れた場合にのみフレームを書き込む学習不要のルールSceneBoundを提案した。
llm.problem: ストリーミング3D再構築モデルにおいて、過去のフレームをどの程度記憶し続けるかがメモリ消費とドリフトに影響する。
llm.method: カメラポーズが既存の保存済みキーフレームから固定半径以上離れているときにのみフレームを書き込むトレーニング不要のルールを設計した。
llm.result: 複数のモデルとメモリタイプにおいて、提案手法は公開されているトレーニング不要のルールの中で最も低い平均軌跡誤差を達成した。

2611.00734.title: MOST: Memory of Object States and Task Progress for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
2611.00734.abstract: Long-horizon embodied manipulation requires policies to act on information that is no longer visible. Modified objects may leave the field of view, while completed subtasks continue to constrain future actions. Existing approaches extend temporal context through recurrent state updates, test-time training, or storage and retrieval of past observations. As horizons grow, these mechanisms can still leave the policy to infer task state from long, redundant, and viewpoint-dependent visual experience. We argue that long-horizon agents benefit not merely from remembering more, but from remembering task-relevant state changes and progress. We propose Memory of Object States and Task Progress (MOST), a policy-internal memory framework that compresses multi-view observations into temporal tokens. Historical and predictive future tokens are explicitly supervised with object states and subtask progress, structuring memory around what has changed in the world and what has already been accomplished. The resulting memory directly conditions action generation within a single end-to-end policy, without an external planner or retrieval stage. We further introduce RoboCasa-Long, a benchmark of multi-minute, multi-stage mobile manipulation tasks. Across RoboCasa365, RoboCasa-Long, and real-world robot experiments, MOST consistently outperforms Xiaomi-Robotics-1 (XR-1), the previous state-of-the-art model. It raises average success from 65.9% to 72.1% on RoboCasa365, average maximum task progress from 20.83% to 42.22% on RoboCasa-Long, and real-world success from 6.66% to 43.33%. MOST also outperforms a matched visual-history memory variant, showing that effective long-horizon memory depends not only on how much experience is retained, but on whether it preserves decision-relevant progress and world-state changes.
2611.00734.tldr_en: Memory of Object States and Task Progress (MOST), a policy-internal memory framework that compresses multi-view observations into temporal tokens, is proposed, and RoboCasa-Long, a benchmark of multi-minute, multi-stage mobile manipulation tasks, is introduced, showing that effective long-horizon memory depends not only on how much experience is retained, but on whether it preserves decision-relevant progress and world-state changes.

llm.title_ja: MOST：長期モバイルマニピュレーションのためのオブジェクト状態とタスク進捗の記憶
llm.tldr_ja: マルチビュー観測を時間的トークンに圧縮するポリシー内メモリフレームワークMOSTを提案し、長期タスクの成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 長期にわたる具現化マニピュレーションでは、視野外のオブジェクトの状態や完了したサブタスクの情報をポリシーが保持する必要がある。
llm.method: オブジェクトの状態とサブタスクの進捗を明示的に教師あり学習させ、マルチビュー観測を時間的トークンに圧縮するポリシー内メモリフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: RoboCasa365や実ロボット実験において、従来モデルを上回る成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2610.42146.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
2610.42146.abstract: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io

llm.title_ja: 暗黙的ダイナミクスを持つ階層的世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 状態空間の到達可能性と局所制御を分離する階層的世界モデルID-WMを提案し、長期タスクにおいて最先端のプランナーや単一レベルのモデル予測制御を大きく上回る性能を実証した。
llm.problem: 長期タスクにおいて累積誤差と探索の複雑さが障害となり、既存の階層的手法は硬直したマクロアクションや潜在スキルにより制御が制限されること。
llm.method: 状態多様体上の実行可能な遷移をサンプリングする高レベルモデルと、逆ダイナミクスソルバーとして機能する低レベル世界モデルを組み合わせたID-WMを提案する。
llm.result: 3つのナビゲーションおよびマニピュレーションスイートで、最先端のポリシーや拡散ベースのプランナーを38.5%上回る改善を達成した。

2610.42146.tldr_en: This work introduces ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control and yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks.

2610.42145.title: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid
2610.42145.abstract: Representing 3D shapes using a set of primitives - known as shape abstraction - is an actively studied problem in computer graphics with wide applications in shape understanding, analysis, and simulation due to the compactness and computational efficiency of the primitive-based representation. Prior work has primarily focused on geometry-aware shape abstraction, where the objective is to approximate the input shape with a minimal set of primitives while preserving geometric fidelity. However, these methods often overlook semantic consistency, inevitably leading to primitives that span across multiple semantic parts. Such inconsistency can cause undesirable artifacts in downstream tasks such as part-level shape editing or manipulation. In this paper, we introduce a new task - semantic-aware shape abstraction, where the goal is to produce abstractions that are both geometrically faithful and semantically consistent, ensuring that each primitive adheres strictly to a single semantic part without crossing semantic boundaries. We propose SemEllipsoid, a novel method to address this problem using ellipsoidal primitives. The core idea is to inject semantic constraints into the primitive optimization process leveraging the availability of semantic cues from large-scale foundation models. We design a fully differentiable projection-blending-evaluation scheme to measure semantic divergence against input semantic masks, and formulate an alternating optimization strategy to iteratively solve for optimal semantic assignment and primitive configurations. Our method is non-learning-based, requiring no data collection or network training, and generalizes well to shapes from arbitrary categories. It also supports different levels of abstraction according to user demand. Extensive experiments and evaluations validate the effectiveness of our approach across several 3D shape collections.

llm.title_ja: SemEllipsoid：楕円体を用いた意味論を考慮した形状抽象化
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模基盤モデルからの意味論的手がかりを活用して形状抽象化プロセスに意味的制約を組み込む、SemEllipsoidという非学習型手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の幾何学を意識した形状抽象化手法は意味的一貫性を無視するため、パーツレベルの形状編集やマニピュレーションで望ましくないアーティファクトを引き起こすこと。
llm.method: 大規模基盤モデルのセマンティックキューを利用して最適化プロセスに意味的制約を注入し、微分可能な投影・ブレンド・評価スキームと交互最適化戦略を用いる。
llm.result: データ収集やネットワークのトレーニングを必要とせず、任意のカテゴリの形状によく汎化し、ユーザーの要求に応じた異なるレベルの抽象化をサポートする。

2610.42145.tldr_en: SemEllipsoid, a novel method to address this problem using ellipsoidal primitives, is proposed, to inject semantic constraints into the primitive optimization process leveraging the availability of semantic cues from large-scale foundation models.

2610.42141.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
2610.42141.abstract: Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup. In RoboArchitect, a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures, and iteratively revises the harness around the frozen policy. The harness evolves on a set of episodes for its optimization and is evaluated on held-out scenes and tasks. Without updating any model weights, RoboArchitect raises average success from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes (4.5x) and from 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks (3.2x), across multiple benchmarks and policies. The gains are largest where the benchmark is far from the policy's training data: wrapping a general-purpose policy, the evolved harness yields a specialist that often outperforms even the finetuned version. Intuitive control strategies are automatically designed, such as lifting a jammed arm clear or reaching in horizontally when an obstacle blocks the way from above. The harness also evolves its own persistent memory, carrying learned experience, such as effective grasp depths, into later decisions. These results suggest that substantial headroom in robotic manipulation lies in the agent harness, and its design can be effectively automated and optimized without weight updates.
2610.42141.hf_summary_en: RoboArchitect automates robot harness design by iteratively revising control code around a frozen policy, substantially improving success on unseen scenes and tasks without model updates.

llm.title_ja: RoboArchitect：永続的メモリを用いたロボットエージェントの設計自動化
llm.tldr_ja: コーディングモデルがロボットの実行結果を観察し、モデルの重みを更新することなく凍結されたポリシーの周囲の制御コードを反復的に修正してハーネス設計を自動化するRoboArchitectを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットポリシー用のエージェントハーネスは手動で構築され、新しいロボットやベンチマークごとに再設計する必要があること。
llm.method: コーディングモデルがロールアウトを観察して失敗を診断し、学習経験を運ぶ永続的メモリを持つハーネスを反復的に進化させる。
llm.result: モデルの重みを更新することなく、複数ベンチマークの未見のシーンで平均成功率を9.7%から43.3%へ、未見のタスクで12.7%から40.2%へと向上させた。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.42141.tldr_en: RoboArchitect shows that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup, and its design can be effectively automated and optimized without weight updates.

2610.42097.title: ROOF: Learning Humanoid Fall Recovery under Overhead Constraints
2610.42097.abstract: A fallen humanoid beneath an overhead obstacle faces a coupled recovery problem. It must create clearance while organizing support for a stable rise, since attempting to stand before making room can further increase obstruction. We introduce a reinforcement learning method with contact-supported geometric escape guidance, which rewards incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path. To achieve this, a learned motion prior, together with posture-dependent support and joint-stall costs, is proposed to shape a single policy that learns when to clear the obstacle, how to establish support, and when to complete the rise, all using proprioception alone. In simulation, it recovers in 88.5% of trials beneath plates that can only be lifted, compared with 18.9% without geometric guidance, and in 98.6% of trials beneath free plates with randomized size, mass and placement. On a Unitree G1, the deployed policy recovered in 95 of 150 attempts across seven real-world obstacle scenes, including furniture and multi-object arrangements absent from training. Project page: https://lu-yidan.github.io/ROOF/

llm.title_ja: ROOF：オーバーヘッド制約下でのヒューマノイド転倒からの復帰学習
llm.tldr_ja: 接触を伴う幾何学的エスケープガイダンスを備えた強化学習法により、プロプリオセプションのみを用いて頭上障害物のある状況下でのヒューマノイドの起き上がり動作学習を実現した。
llm.problem: 頭上に障害物がある状態で倒れたヒューマノイドは、障害物を避けるための空間を作りつつ安定して立ち上がるための支持を組織化しなければならないこと。
llm.method: 障害物とのオーバーラップの段階的な削減を報酬とし、学習された動作事前分布、姿勢依存の支持コスト、関節のストールコストを組み合わせた単一ポリシーを訓練する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいてランダムなプレートの下で98.6%の試行で復帰に成功し、Unitree G1を用いた実機実験でも多様な障害物シーンで高い成功率を達成した。

2610.42097.tldr_en: A reinforcement learning method with contact-supported geometric escape guidance, which rewards incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path, is introduced.

2610.42096.title: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models
2610.42096.abstract: World action models (WAMs) learn latent variables from observations and use these to both predict the evolution of the scene and to generate actions. The prediction has to be of the whole scene, whereas only a portion of the scene causes actions. WAMs fitted to demonstrations do not, in general, guarantee that they will generate actions solely from the latent causes of the demonstrated actions (the action-relevant latent variables), as the model could just as well learn to imitate in this way whilst entangling the action-relevant latent variables with the nuisance variables. We therefore separate out what causes action from what prediction depends on. We prove that under a sparsity constraint the latent variables used to generate actions are an invertible function of the action-relevant latent variables alone and the true structure is identified up to a permutation of the latent variables. This requires neither sufficient temporal dependence nor any assumptions on how the unobserved regimes evolve and holds even when the action-relevant latent variables are statistically dependent on the rest. We therefore propose CWAM (Causal WAM), which incorporates the constraint into a pretrained WAM by adding a sparse routing path to its action head, with the world modeling objective remaining unchanged. Experiments on both synthetic data and real-world robots validate the theory as well as showcase the improved efficiency in closed-loop success.
2610.42096.hf_summary_en: Causal World Action Models enforce sparse routing to isolate action-relevant latent variables, ensuring identifiable causal structure without requiring temporal independence assumptions.

llm.title_ja: CausalWAM：世界行動モデルにおける行動の原因の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの世界行動モデルにスパースなルーティングパスを追加し、行動関連の潜在変数を分離して因果構造を特定するCWAMを提案した。
llm.problem: デモンストレーションに適合させた世界行動モデルは、行動に関連する潜在変数を不要な変数と絡み合わせて学習してしまう可能性があること。
llm.method: スパース性制約の下で、行動の生成に使用される潜在変数が行動関連の潜在変数の可逆的な関数であることを証明し、モデルに行動ヘッドへのスパースルーティングパスを追加する。
llm.result: 合成データと実世界ロボットの両方の実験により理論が検証され、閉ループでの成功における効率の向上が示された。

2610.42096.tldr_en: CWAM (Causal WAM), which incorporates the sparsity constraint into a pretrained WAM by adding a sparse routing path to its action head, with the world modeling objective remaining unchanged, is proposed.

2610.42053.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
2610.42053.abstract: Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult. For example, an agent that calls the VLA in the agentic loop can stall the fast execution, while a VLA that calls the agent on errors tends to re-trigger fallbacks repeatedly or completely miss silent failures. To address this, we propose REA (Routed Embodied Agent), a unified runtime where a deliberative System 2, an embodied router System 1 and reactive System 0 policies cooperate under a single golden rule - no running policy waits on the brain. Instead of querying the brain at each failure, REA employs a route memory that stores each policy's measured success ahead of time, a boundary-triggered judge gate that consults the brain on policy execution, and a shared-budget escalation ladder for bounded recovery. Evaluated on 3,000 test episodes across 60 LIBERO-Pro tasks, REA reaches 95.9% success and beats the best single-agent baseline in its own policy pool (94.7%) while reducing control steps by 25% and control time by 17%. In a separate 100-episode RoboTwin 2.0 study, REA achieves 84% success with VLA policies and 86% with VLA+code, compared with 80% for the strongest single VLA baseline MEDex. These results demonstrate learned and programmatic policies operating within the same runtime. REA also transfers to BEHAVIOR-1K and a real Unitree G1 humanoid, achieving the highest observed success among the compared methods.

llm.title_ja: REA：非同期脳・小脳制御のためのルーテッド・エンボディド・エージェント・ランタイム
llm.tldr_ja: 高レベルな推論を行う脳と高速なポリシーを非同期で協調させ、実行中のポリシーが脳の処理を待つ必要のない統合ランタイムREAを提案した。
llm.problem: 基盤モデルは高レベル推論に優れるが低速かつ高コストであり、VLA等の高速ポリシーは汎化性能に劣る上、両者の非同期協調が困難であること。
llm.method: ルートメモリ、境界トリガー型ジャッジゲート、共有予算のエスカレーションラダーを備え、System 2、ルーター、System 0ポリシーを統合したランタイムを構築する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Proタスクの3,000エピソードの評価で95.9%の成功率を達成し、単一エージェントのベースラインを上回りつつ制御ステップと時間を削減した。

2610.42053.tldr_en: REA (Routed Embodied Agent) is proposed, a unified runtime where a deliberative System 2, an embodied router System 1 and reactive System 0 policies cooperate under a single golden rule - no running policy waits on the brain.
2610.42053.hf_summary_en: REA unifies deliberative and reactive policies in a single runtime with asynchronous coordination, achieving high success rates with reduced control overhead across simulated and real robot tasks.

2610.42049.title: A Hybrid Path Planning Framework for Assistive Wheelchair Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments
2610.42049.abstract: Autonomous wheelchairs can improve the quality of life for individuals with mobility impairments by providing greater independence. However, reliable navigation especially in human environments is a major challenge due to factors such as dynamic obstacles, unpredictable pedestrian behavior, and the users' need to complete multiple stops along the way before reaching their final destination. This paper presents a hybrid path planning framework for multi-goal navigation in dynamic environments. The framework integrates the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) for global task ordering with the Potential Field (PF) method and heuristic local planners such as Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) and A-star (A*) to achieve collision-free navigation. Within this hybrid framework, TSP determines the visiting order of intermediate stations, PF transfers global path information, and local planners avoid obstacles while guiding the robot to the stations. The local planners generate feasible paths that allow the robot to follow the global trajectory and reroute to avoid static and dynamic obstacles. For this purpose, two algorithms have been developed: (i) TSP-PF-RRT and (ii) TSP-PF-A*. The performance of the proposed algorithms are evaluated using Monte Carlo simulations in crowded and extra-crowded scenarios that contain heterogeneous dynamic and static obstacles. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework enables efficient multi-goal navigation while maintaining safe operation in dynamic environments with humans, with TSP-PF-RRT achieving fewer or no collisions and shorter travel distances.
2610.42049.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. Presented as a main-track paper at the International Conference of Social Robotics + ART'26, London, UK, 1-4 July 2026

llm.title_ja: 動的歩行環境における介助用車椅子ナビゲーションのためのハイブリッド経路計画フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 巡回セールス問題（TSP）とポテンシャル法、ヒューリスティックな局所プランナーを統合し、動的環境において衝突のない多目的ナビゲーションを実現するハイブリッドフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 動的障害物や予測不可能な歩行者の行動、複数の中継地点を経由する必要性などにより、人間の環境での信頼性の高いナビゲーションが大きな課題であること。
llm.method: TSPによる大域的タスク順序付けと、ポテンシャル法・RRT・A*などの局所プランナーを組み合わせて大域的軌道に沿った移動と障害物回避を行うTSP-PF-RRTおよびTSP-PF-A*アルゴリズムを開発する。
llm.result: 混雑したシミュレーション環境において、提案するハイブリッドフレームワークが効率的な多目的ナビゲーションと動的環境での安全な動作を可能にすることを示した。
keywords_ja: 車椅子ナビゲーション

2610.42049.tldr_en: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework enables efficient multi-goal navigation while maintaining safe operation in dynamic environments with humans, with TSP-PF-RRT achieving fewer or no collisions and shorter travel distances.

2610.42043.title: Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight
2610.42043.abstract: We study whether a language model can help design controllers whose behavior can be formally checked. In proof-carrying evolution (PCE), a search proposes controllers together with their certificates. Their mathematical forms are fixed; a proposer chooses their numerical parameters together. Certificate checks guide selection, and only a certified candidate can be returned. The deployed artifact is a control law and its certificate; the language model is used only during design. We compare four language models with classical search and synthesis on docking under a speed limit, pursuit of a maneuvering target, and attitude control on SO(3), using paired runs and shared proposal allowances. Certificates are checked in exact rational arithmetic during search on the linear problems. On SO(3), the search uses floating-point checks, followed by exact re-verification of every reported champion. The best run of each method also receives Lean 4 proofs of its stated control properties. On the linear problems, the strongest models beat the standard classical baselines on every run, but a classical optimizer that chooses certificates for the same objective closes most of that lead. Among the cited pursuit champions, the ranking does not survive a change from Euler to zero-order-hold dynamics. On SO(3), no model detectably outperforms CMA-ES when mixed with classical mutation. When models write every proposal, one tested model improves on CMA-ES and the other performs worse than its mixed variant. All search medians remain below the hand-tuned law. In a docking control with the objective and mutation operator held fixed, retaining certified candidates yields new certified designs in every run; removing this rule yields none.

llm.title_ja: 証明付き進化：ブラックボックス探索、ホワイトボックス飛行
llm.tldr_ja: 言語モデルを利用して数値パラメータや制御則の提案を行い、証明チェックによる選択を経て形式的に検証可能な制御器を設計する「証明付き進化（PCE）」を研究した。
llm.problem: 言語モデルを活用して、動作を形式的にチェックできる制御器を設計できるかという点について検証すること。
llm.method: サーチャーが制御器の数値パラメータと証明を同時に提案し、厳密な算術による証明チェックを通過した候補のみを採用するプロセスを用いる。
llm.result: 線形問題において強力なモデルは古典的なベースラインを上回ったが、SO(3)上の姿勢制御ではCMA-ESを明確に上回るモデルはなく、証明の保持が新しい設計の獲得に不可欠であることを示した。

2610.42043.tldr_en: Whether a language model can help design controllers whose behavior can be formally checked is studied, and four language models with classical search and synthesis on docking under a speed limit, pursuit of a maneuvering target, and attitude control on SO(3), are compared.

2610.42026.title: GhostPrefix: Synchronization-Free Universal Prefix Attacks for ASR Manipulation
2610.42026.abstract: We present GhostPrefix, the first synchronization-free universal adversarial prefix attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. Unlike prior audio attacks, which are typically crafted per utterance, require synchronization with the victim waveform, or target narrow objectives, GhostPrefix learns a short, reusable audio segment prepended to arbitrary live speech to exert real-time control over ASR outputs without knowledge of the future utterance or temporal alignment. A key challenge is maintaining stable adversarial effects across unknown, evolving speech contexts. GhostPrefix combines token-level losses with a novel representation-level objective for stable, input-agnostic effects. GhostPrefix supports three attack modes: (i) prompted prefix attacks for semantic steering, (ii) targeted prefix attacks for transcript hijacking, and (iii) untargeted prefix attacks for transcription degradation. To remain perceptually inconspicuous, we regularize prefixes toward benign environmental-sound distributions and improve robustness against over-the-air distortions. We evaluate GhostPrefix across 13 open-source ASR models from four families. In digital settings, it achieves average attack success rates of 97.6% for prompted steering and 93.4% for targeted hijacking, while driving word error rate to 1.18 under untargeted attacks. Over the air, it achieves success rates of 91.5% and 89.5% for prompted and targeted modes, respectively. These manipulations propagate into downstream AI-assisted pipelines, including voice assistants and AI note-taking tools, causing systematic semantic misinterpretations. GhostPrefix exposes synchronization-free universal prefixes as a practical, under-explored threat to real-world ASR and downstream applications. Artifacts and demos are available at https://ghostprefix.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: GhostPrefix：ASR操作のための同期不要の汎用プレフィックス攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: 音声認識システムに対して、将来の発話や時間的アライメントの知識なしにリアルタイムで制御を行える初の同期不要の汎用敵対的プレフィックス攻撃手法GhostPrefixを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の音声攻撃は通常、発話ごとに作成され、被害者の波形との同期が必要であるか、または限定的な目的に絞られていること。
llm.method: トークンレベルの損失と新しい表現レベルの目的関数を組み合わせ、環境音の分布に近づける正則化や空中歪みに対する頑健性を向上させた短い音声セグメントを学習する。
llm.result: 13のオープンソースASRモデルを用いたデジタル設定で、プロンプト誘導の平均攻撃成功率97.6%を達成し、音声アシスタント等の下流パイプラインへも深刻な影響を与えることを示した。

2610.42026.tldr_en: The first synchronization-free universal adversarial prefix attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems, GhostPrefix exposes synchronization-free universal prefixes as a practical, under-explored threat to real-world ASR and downstream applications.

2610.42021.title: Nexus-VLA: Bridging Human and Robot Experiences via a Shared Hierarchical Semantic Latent Space
2610.42021.abstract: Large-scale egocentric human videos provide rich and scalable manipulation experience for robot policy learning, yet substantial embodiment gaps in visual appearance, kinematic structure, and action spaces hinder effective knowledge transfer. Existing methods often decouple cross-embodiment knowledge alignment from robot policy learning, making it difficult for human manipulation knowledge to directly and fully contribute to robot action learning. To address this issue, we propose Nexus-VLA, a hybrid policy learning framework that enables cross-embodiment knowledge transfer through end-to-end human-robot joint training, allowing human manipulation experience to directly contribute to robot policy learning. We first introduce a hierarchical cross-embodiment semantic alignment paradigm that progressively establishes shared manipulation semantics from task intent to fine-grained interactions, enabling more complete use of the manipulation knowledge contained in human videos. Building on this hierarchy, we design a shared manipulation latent representation that jointly encodes multi-level shared knowledge into an internal representation directly used for continuous action generation, improving policy learning efficiency while effectively leveraging human knowledge. Across RoboCasa-GR1, OOD settings, and real-world robot experiments, Nexus-VLA achieves an 80.5% task success rate on RoboCasa-GR1 and demonstrates strong advantages in human-data utilization, learning efficiency, and cross-scenario generalization.

llm.title_ja: Nexus-VLA：共有階層型意味論的潜在空間を介した人間とロボットの経験の架け橋
llm.tldr_ja: 人間とロボットのエンドツーエンドの共同トレーニングを通じて、人間のマニピュレーション知識をロボットのポリシー学習に直接かつ最大限に活用できるNexus-VLAフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚的外観、運動学的構造、行動空間における大きな身体的ギャップが、人間動画からの効果的な知識転移を妨げていること。
llm.method: タスクの意図から細粒度の相互作用まで共有されるマニピュレーション意味論を段階的に確立する階層的クロス・エンボディメント意味アライメントパラダイムを導入する。
llm.result: RoboCasa-GR1、OOD設定、実ロボット実験において80.5%のタスク成功率を達成し、人間データの活用効率や汎化性能で優れた利点を示した。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント

2610.42021.tldr_en: Nexus-VLA is proposed, a hybrid policy learning framework that enables cross-embodiment knowledge transfer through end-to-end human-robot joint training, allowing human manipulation experience to directly contribute to robot policy learning.

2610.41998.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
