2610.41998.abstract: Recognized as a top threat to AI agents, prompt injection allows instructions from untrusted data (email, documents, websites) to manipulate the agent's operation. The existing best-defended LLM, Meta-SecAlign, is trained with the DPO loss but still suffers from attack success rates (ASRs) approaching 100% under adaptive prompt injections. One reason is that DPO anchors the model around the undefended reference model, which is insecure. We show an idealized reference model---an injection-invariant, utility-preserving oracle---can nevertheless be approximated, as its output distribution in training is interestingly accessible. This new observation motivates a theoretically principled SecPO loss. Another Meta-SecAlign shortcoming is that it trains on weak simulated attacks. We implement an efficient adversarial training (AT) pipeline that synthesizes strong injected inputs (best@240), and train the model on them. Our AT reduces ASRs by 1.5-14.5$\times$ across three SoTA adaptive attacks, compared with Meta-SecAlign; the SecPO loss reduces them by a further 2.4-4.6$\times$ compared with using DPO loss. In agentic workflows, our SecPO + AT Qwen3.6-27B is much more secure than Meta-SecAlign: 8.8% vs. 78.8% AgentDojo ASR@800 under the AttackerMovesSecond attack. Moreover, our defended model shows no noticeable reduction in benign utility in nine benchmarks covering agentic tool calling, instruction following, science, and math. We release our $\href{//github.com/Sizhe-Chen/SecPO}{\text{code}}$, $\href{//huggingface.co/datasets/Sizhe-Chen/Qwen3.6-27B-Instruct-SecPO-trainset}{\text{training data}}$ (with optimized injections from AT), and $\href{//huggingface.co/Sizhe-Chen/Qwen3.6-27B-Instruct-SecPO}{\text{model}}$.

llm.title_ja: SecPO：プロンプトインジェクションセキュリティのための原理に基づく敵対的訓練
llm.tldr_ja: 理想化された参照モデルの出力分布に近似可能な、理論的に裏付けられたSecPO損失関数と強力な敵対的訓練パイプラインを提案し、プロンプトインジェクションに対する防御性能を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 既存の最高性能の防御LLMであるMeta-SecAlignはDPO損失で訓練されているが、未定義の脆弱な参照モデルに依存しているため適応的プロンプトインジェクションに対して攻撃成功率が100%に近づくこと。
llm.method: インジェクション不変でユーティリティ保持型オラクルである理想的な参照モデルを近似するSecPO損失を導出し、強力なインジェクション入力を合成する効率的な敵対的訓練パイプラインを実装する。
llm.result: 3つのSoTA適応型攻撃に対して攻撃成功率を1.5〜14.5倍削減し、エージェントワークフローにおいてベンチマークの有用性を損なうことなく安全性を大幅に高めた。
keywords_ja: プロンプトインジェクション

2610.41998.tldr_en: An idealized reference model---an injection-invariant, utility-preserving oracle---can nevertheless be approximated, as its output distribution in training is interestingly accessible, which motivates a theoretically principled SecPO loss.

2610.41982.title: Suspended-Fabric Robotic Manipulation Surfaces: Modelling, Design Space, and Multimodular Extensio
2610.41982.abstract: Robotic Manipulation Surfaces (RMS) reposition objects by deforming the surface on which they rest. A recent class of RMS suspends a continuous fabric sheet from a sparse grid of vertical linear actuators lowering the actuator density of such surfaces but how to design such surfaces so that objects can be controlled everywhere on it, and how to extend it beyond a single module so that objects can pass between modules and achieve parallel, remain open. This paper presents a separable catenary model of the suspended sheet that is fast to compute and provides both the surface shape for given actuator heights and the actuator heights for a desired local slope. The closed form inverse lets a simple PID controller position objects on the sheet, and the model relates fabric length, module span and actuator stroke to the reachable workspace, yielding a minimum fabric length bound and design charts for these surfaces. The approach is then extended to a multimodular platform in which neighbouring modules share actuators. On a $2 \times 2$ prototype, we demonstrate that centimetre-scale objects are transferred between modules and positioned within 0.03 m over a $1 m^2$ workspace with only nine actuators, enabling multi-object manipulation and opening the way to parallel manipulation.

llm.title_ja: 吊り下げ式布製ロボットマニピュレーション表面：モデリング、設計空間、およびマルチモジュール拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 垂直リニアアクチュエータの疎なグリッドから連続的な布シートを吊り下げたロボットマニピュレーション表面（RMS）の分離カテナリーモデルを提案し、モジュール間での物体転送と位置決めを実証した。
llm.problem: アクチュエータ密度を下げつつ、表面上のどこでも物体を制御する方法や、複数のモジュールに拡張して並行処理を行う方法が未解決であったこと。
llm.method: アクチュエータの高さから表面形状を、また目的の局所傾斜から高さを計算できる分離カテナリーモデルを構築し、単純なPIDコントローラーと組み合わせて分析・拡張する。
llm.result: 2x2のプロトタイプにおいて、わずか9個のアクチュエータで1m²のワークスペースにわたり、センチメートルサイズの物体をモジュール間で転送し0.03m以内に位置決めできることを実証した。
keywords_ja: マニピュレーション表面
モジュール型ロボット

2610.41982.tldr_en: A separable catenary model of the suspended sheet is presented that is fast to compute and provides both the surface shape for given actuator heights and the actuator heights for a desired local slope, enabling multi-object manipulation and opening the way to parallel manipulation.

2610.41981.title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control
2610.41981.abstract: Data-driven controllers have enabled lower-limb robotic exoskeletons to adapt assistance to the user across many tasks. A leading example is biological torque control, which estimates the user's own joint moment from onboard sensors and assists in proportion to that estimate. However, its estimators are trained on data recorded with the target device, so deploying the controller on new hardware requires collecting new data. Existing open-source efforts release hardware, software, or controllers separately, so this data collection must still be repeated on the assembled device. Here, we present an open-source knee exoskeleton, built from off-the-shelf components and widely available fabrication tools, with a biological torque controller derived entirely from simulation. A muscle-driven imitation policy reproduces squatting motions from an open biomechanics dataset, and the resulting knee moments are distilled into an estimator that uses only onboard sensors, so no training data are recorded on the device. In seven able-bodied participants, assistance reduced peak biological knee extension moment by 21.5% and peak vastus medialis activation by 26.7% during squatting, relative to squatting without the exoskeleton (p<0.05). Our results demonstrate that a biological torque controller derived from simulation can transfer to physical hardware without device-specific data collection. Because the hardware and training pipeline are released together, research groups can train and compare knee exoskeleton controllers on shared hardware without additional data collection overhead.

llm.title_ja: 筋骨格シミュレーション由来の生物学的トルク制御を用いたロボット膝外骨格の設計と検証
llm.tldr_ja: オープンソースの膝外骨格を構築し、筋駆動模倣ポリシーを用いてデバイス固有のデータ収集を一切行わずにシミュレーションから生物学的トルクコントローラーを実機へ転移させた。
llm.problem: 生物学的トルクコントローラーの推定器はターゲットデバイスで記録されたデータで訓練されるため、新しいハードウェアにコントローラーをデプロイするには新しいデータの収集が必要になること。
llm.method: バイオメカニクスデータセットからのスクワット動作を模倣する筋肉駆動ポリシーを構築し、得られた膝関節モーメントをオンボードセンサーのみを使用する推定器に蒸留する。
llm.result: 7名の健常参加者を用いたスクワット実験において、外骨格なしと比較してピーク時の生物学的膝伸展モーメントを21.5%、外側広筋の活動を26.7%削減することに成功した。
keywords_ja: 筋骨格シミュレーション
ロボットハードウェア

2610.41981.tldr_en: This work presents an open-source knee exoskeleton, built from off-the-shelf components and widely available fabrication tools, with a biological torque controller derived entirely from simulation, demonstrating that a biological torque controller derived from simulation can transfer to physical hardware without device-specific data collection.

2610.41978.title: Language-Conditioned Behavioral Cloning for Autonomous Endoscope Guidance
2610.41978.abstract: Automated endoscope guidance reduces the need for continuous manual camera control during minimally invasive surgery. However, the desired camera motion depends on the surgeon's immediate intentions and cannot always be inferred from the visual operative scene alone. We propose to automate the task using language-conditioned behavioral cloning; we define 6 clinically relevant guidance behaviors and collect 235 subtask demonstrations. In preliminary phantom experiments, our policy achieves 100% success on focus, overview, and stop, 80% on search-tip and follow-tip behaviors, and 50% on horizon leveling. These results demonstrate the feasibility of learning heterogeneous surgeon-requested camera behaviors with a single visuomotor policy, while the observed failure modes motivate future work on adding temporal context for more demanding guidance tasks.
2610.41978.comment: The Evolving Landscape of Surgical Robotics: Surgical Autonomy for Today and Tomorrow @ IROS 2026

llm.title_ja: 自律型内視鏡ガイダンスのための言語条件付き行動クローン
llm.tldr_ja: 6つの臨床的に関連するガイダンス行動を定義し、単一の視覚運動ポリシーを用いて外科医が要求する多様なカメラ動作を学習できることをファントム実験で実証した。
llm.problem: 自動化された内視鏡ガイダンスにおいて、望ましいカメラの動きは外科医の即時の意図に依存し、視覚的な術野の映像だけから常に推論できるわけではないこと。
llm.method: 言語条件付き行動クローンを用いて、定義された6つの臨床的ガイダンス行動に関する235件のサブタスクデモンストレーションを収集しポリシーを訓練する。
llm.result: 予備的なファントム実験において、フォーカス、概要、停止の動作で100%、先端探索・追従で80%、水平合わせで50%の成功率を達成した。

2610.41978.tldr_en: The results demonstrate the feasibility of learning heterogeneous surgeon-requested camera behaviors with a single visuomotor policy, while the observed failure modes motivate future work on adding temporal context for more demanding guidance tasks.

2610.41946.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
2610.41946.abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.
2610.41946.comment: GenAI for Health Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026, Sydney

llm.title_ja: Sensorium：体感型外科AIのためのオープンソースマルチモーダルデータ収集・キュレーションライブラリ
llm.tldr_ja: ROS/ROS2ミドルウェアを用いて設定可能なロボットおよびセンサーからのマルチモーダルな外科データを記録、処理、アノテーション、キュレーションするためのオープンソースPythonライブラリSensoriumを提案した。
llm.problem: 体感型外科AIには信頼性の高いマルチモーダルデータが必要であるにもかかわらず、外科データの収集は依然としてコストがかかり、再現が難しく、ハードウェア設定に強く依存していること。
llm.method: オペレーター向けのデータ買収、設定可能な処理、意味論的アノテーション、およびエピソードデータセット生成を組み合わせたPythonライブラリを開発する。
llm.result: ファントム、ex vivo、in vivoの豚実験を含む1,516件の記録を通じてライブラリを評価し、有用性に関する予備的フィードバックを報告した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルデータ

2610.41936.title: Adaptive Coverage Algorithms for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks in Dynamic Worlds
2610.41936.abstract: This paper extends an existing framework for the coordination of mobile agents in unknown worlds, by considering the possibility of dynamic instability. In the original problem, known as the Partially Observable Cooperative Guard Art Gallery Problem (POCGAGP) (arXiv:2512.09495), the multi-agent system must establish a communication network which completely covers an initially unknown constrained space. However, the POCGAGP fails to account for the unpredictability often seen in real-world deployment. To address this, the dynamic case (DPOCGAGP) introduces two settings which can influence the mobile network during deployment: Agent Loss and World Change, which represent dynamic changes to the world. Within this study, we present advancements to two state-of-the-art algorithms, the Centralized Agent-Directed Exploration for Network Coverage (CADENCE), and its decentralized analogue, DADENCE, to provide solutions in these cases. We then compare their performance against another state-of-the-art benchmark algorithm, and show that the adapted algorithms outperform across our benchmark test set, which comprises over 4500 test cases of varied size and structure.
2610.41936.comment: 8 pages, 10 figures. Accepted to the 2026 IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference (URTC)

llm.title_ja: 動的世界におけるモバイルアドホックネットワークのための適応型カバレッジアルゴリズム
llm.tldr_ja: 動的不 instabilityの可能性を考慮してネットワークカバレッジ問題（POCGAGP）を拡張し、エージェントの損失や世界の変化に対応するCADENCEおよびDADENCEアルゴリズムの改良版を提案した。
llm.problem: 元のPOCGAGPフレームワークは、実世界の展開で見られる予測不可能性、すなわち動的な不安定性を考慮に入れていないこと。
llm.method: 動的設定（エージェントの損失と世界の変化）に対応するため、集中型アルゴリズムCADENCEとその分散型アナログであるDADENCEの最先端アルゴリズムを高度化する。
llm.result: 様々な規模と構造の4,500件以上のテストケースからなるベンチマークテストセットにおいて、適応型アルゴリズムが既存の最先端ベンチマークアルゴリズムを上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: モバイルアドホックネットワーク

2610.41936.tldr_en: Two state-of-the-art algorithms, the Centralized Agent-Directed Exploration for Network Coverage (CADENCE) and its decentralized analogue, DADENCE, are presented to provide solutions in dynamic instability cases, and are compared against another state-of-the-art benchmark algorithm.

2610.41903.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
2610.41903.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) embodies a foundational paradigm for sequential decision-making in the face of uncertainty. The rapid growth of model complexity in emerging applications has significantly amplified the challenges of achieving data-efficient RL, particularly in sample-starved scenarios where data collection may be costly, time-consuming, or even high-stakes. Consequently, understanding and improving the data efficiency of RL algorithms has become a central problem of both fundamental theoretical interest and practical importance. Despite decades of research, the statistical underpinnings of RL remained remarkably underdeveloped until relatively recently, particularly in the finite-sample regimes most relevant to modern practice. Over the past few years, there has been a surge of activity advancing the frontiers of non-asymptotic statistical RL theory, drawing on ideas from high-dimensional statistics and probability, information theory, and statistical learning theory. In this monograph, we present a non-asymptotic treatment for RL based on tabular Markov decision processes, focusing on three canonical sampling mechanisms --- RL with a generative model, online RL, and offline RL --- together with two algorithmic paradigms: model-based and model-free approaches. Centered around non-asymptotic sample complexity analysis, our treatment emphasizes minimax-optimal algorithm design, particularly methods that attain statistical optimality without significant burn-in costs, as well as sharp statistical characterizations of several widely used RL algorithms. Whenever possible, we provide largely self-contained analyses together with intuitive explanations. We also briefly discuss several extensions, such as robust RL, competitive multi-agent RL, federated RL, uncertainty quantification, and RL from human feedback.

llm.title_ja: 強化学習の統計的基礎：非漸近的視点
llm.tldr_ja: 表形式のマルコフ決定過程に基づき、3つのサンプリングメカニズムと2つのアルゴリズムパラダイムに焦点を当てた、強化学習の非漸近的統計理論についてのモノグラフを提示した。
llm.problem: 新興アプリケーションにおけるモデルの複雑さの急速な成長により、特にデータ収集が高コスト、時間のかかる、あるいは重大なリスクを伴うシナリオにおいて、データ効率の高い強化学習の達成が困難になっていること。
llm.method: 高次元統計、確率、情報論、統計学習理論からのアイデアを活用し、非漸近的サンプル複雑性解析を中心としたミニマックス最適アルゴリズム設計を提示する。
llm.result: 有意なバーンインコストなしで統計的最適性を達成する手法や、広く使用されている強化学習アルゴリズムの厳密な統計的特徴付けを行った。

2610.41903.tldr_en: This monograph presents a non-asymptotic treatment for RL based on tabular Markov decision processes, focusing on three canonical sampling mechanisms --- RL with a generative model, online RL, and offline RL --- together with two algorithmic paradigms: model-based and model-free approaches.

2610.41892.title: Online Learning of Heterogeneous Locomotion Dynamics under Reinforcement Learning Policies for Precise Loco-Manipulation
2610.41892.abstract: How to reuse a pretrained locomotion policy for precise loco-manipulation is still an open problem. We propose an online method to learn the closed-loop dynamics under a frozen locomotion policy. The learned model predicts floating-base motion and improves loco-manipulation accuracy. However, unobserved latent conditions of the policy introduce heterogeneous responses, meaning that the same observed state will lead to different motions. Direct learning without accounting for this heterogeneity introduces bias and fluctuations into dynamics estimates, degrading floating-base prediction and end-effector tracking. To address this problem, a contaminated Gaussian model is proposed to approximate the effects of latent conditions. The model uses two Gaussian components to approximate predictable and unpredictable responses under the same observed state. Then, the contaminated Gaussian model is combined with a Gaussian process to construct an online learner using random Fourier features (RFFs). The learner estimates each response's probability of belonging to the predictable component and uses it to weight online updates, capturing predictable responses while reducing bias and fluctuations caused by heterogeneous observations. With consistent and unbiased dynamics estimates, model predictive control (MPC) predicts floating-base motion accurately and enables precise loco-manipulation. A finite-sample error bound is established to ensure uniform convergence in online learning. Simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate consistent end-effector tracking across different manipulator configurations and tasks, with errors of 0.01 m.

llm.title_ja: 精密なロコ・マニピュレーションのための強化学習ポリシー下での異質移動ダイナミクスのオンライン学習
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された移動ポリシーの下で閉ループダイナミクスをオンライン学習する手法を提案し、汚染ガウスモデルを用いて未観測の潜在条件による異質な応答を近似・補正することで正確なモデル予測制御を実現した。
llm.problem: ポリシーの未観測の潜在条件が異質な応答を導入し、ダイナミクス推定にバイアスと変動を生じさせ、フローティングベースの予測とエンドエフェクタの追従精度を低下させること。
llm.method: 予測可能および予測不可能な応答を2つのガウス成分で近似する汚染ガウスモデルを提案し、ランダムフーリエ特徴を用いたガウス過程と組み合わせてオンライン学習器を構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよびハードウェア実験により、異なるマニピュレータの構成やタスクにわたって0.01mという小さな誤差で一貫したエンドエフェクタ追従を実現できることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロコ・マニピュレーション

2610.41892.tldr_en: An online method to learn the closed-loop dynamics under a frozen locomotion policy with consistent and unbiased dynamics estimates is proposed, and model predictive control (MPC) predicts floating-base motion accurately and enables precise loco-manipulation.

2610.41877.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
2610.41877.abstract: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. Building on this data, we introduce Movens-Zero, a scalable understanding-generation-execution architecture that supports joint learning across modalities and real-time closed-loop execution. Task-mixed flow-matching training jointly optimizes a single action expert across seven generation tasks, enabling direct motion generation from text, speech, music, and video. Multimodal Real-Time Chunking connects overlapping chunks under continuously updated instructions and robot states for continuous closed-loop execution. We further introduce Movens-Intent, a four-track benchmark with 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs across text, speech, music, and video. Experiments show consistent gains across all four modalities when scaling execution-verified data from 1% to 100% and action-expert capacity from 64M to 911M parameters, while demonstrating that data quality and cross-modal supervision improve generation and execution.
2610.41877.comment: Technical report. 86 pages, 31 figures, 15 tables. Project page: https://movens-zero.github.io

llm.title_ja: Movens-Zero：大規模な人間動画を用いたヒューマノイド動作基盤モデルのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 1,500万件の人間動作シーケンスと500万件の物理的実行可能なヒューマノイド動作シーケンスを含むMovens-5Mを構築し、多様なモダリティからの直接的な動作生成とリアルタイムの閉ループ実行を可能にするMovens-Zeroを提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイド動作基盤モデルのスケーリングは、多様でロボットが実行可能なデータの不足や、異質なマルチモーダル入力を同時に学習しながらリアルタイムの閉ループ制御をサポートする難しさによって制限されていること。
llm.method: タスク混合フローマッチング訓練により単一のアクションエキスパートを最適化し、マルチモーダルリアルタイムチャンキングによって連続的な閉ループ実行を実現する。
llm.result: 実行検証済みデータのスケールアップとアクションエキスパートの容量拡大により4つのモダリティすべてで一貫した性能向上が見られ、データ品質とクロスモーダルスーパービジョンの有効性が示された。

2610.41877.tldr_en: This work introduces Movens-Zero, a scalable understanding-generation-execution architecture that supports joint learning across modalities and real-time closed-loop execution, and introduces Movens-Intent, a four-track benchmark with 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs across text, speech, music, and video.

2610.41868.title: META-Robot: Self-Cognition and Capability Scaling in Agentic Robots
2610.41868.abstract: LLM-based robotic agent systems can generate programs for robot control, yet their generalization to new tasks often depends on elaborate scaffolding. Expanding their skill repertoires alone offers limited guidance on how to assess new capabilities or identify what remains beyond their reach. We introduce META-Robot, a framework that couples self cognition with capability scaling by expanding the criteria through which an agent evaluates and develops its skills. At its core, action-level predicates make execution outcomes explicit and available for LLM reasoning. The agent uses these assessments to identify its own limitations, extend relevant evaluation criteria, and guide the structured expansion of its skills. Proprioceptive feedback further grounds this process in the robot's physical state, enriching the evidence available for self-cognition. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate stronger overall task performance, generalization to new tasks, continued expansion of skills and evaluation criteria, and effective use of non-visual proprioceptive signals.

llm.title_ja: META-Robot：エージェントロボットにおける自己認識と能力のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 実行結果を明示的なアクションレベルの述語としてLLMの推論に利用可能にし、自己認識とプロプリオセプションを結合してスキルの構造的拡張を導出するMETA-Robotフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: LLMベースのロボットエージェントシステムは制御プログラムを生成できるが、新しいタスクへの汎化は複雑な足場に依存しがちであり、自身の限界を評価する基準の拡張方法が限られていること。
llm.method: アクションレベルの述語によって実行結果を明確化し、プロプリオセプションのフィードバックと組み合わせてエージェント自身が自身の限界を識別し評価基準を拡張する枠組みを構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機ロボットの実験により、優れたタスク性能、新タスクへの汎化、スキルと評価基準の継続的拡張、非視覚的固有受容信号の効果的な活用が示された。
keywords_ja: ロボットエージェント

2610.41868.tldr_en: This work introduces META-Robot, a framework that couples self cognition with capability scaling by expanding the criteria through which an agent evaluates and develops its skills, and demonstrates stronger overall task performance, generalization to new tasks, and continued expansion of skills and evaluation criteria.

2610.41857.title: When the Simulator Fails, Not the Policy: Auditing Contact Artifacts in Simulated Robot Benchmarks
2610.41857.abstract: Simulation benchmarks score robot policies by success rate, and every failed episode counts against the policy. Many of these failures are the simulator's fault, not the policy's; we find the cause and fix it. Testing a vision language action model and a world action model in simulation, we find that the policy often places the object and the simulator then ejects it, and that the benchmark's own scripted demonstrations fail the same way. We present SimuGuard, an auditing plugin for LIBERO, RoboTwin, RoboCasa and RoboDojo. It leaves the evaluation unchanged. At every physics step, it records the state and flags an object that starts moving at a contact faster than the robot's contact or gravity account for. It replays a recorded episode bit for bit, and it reruns the episode with one simulation parameter changed. With it we trace these episodes on RoboTwin to the collision detection of the physics engine: for geometry one to two centimeters apart, the engine reports a penetration of about two centimeters, and the solver throws the object out at several meters per second. The cause is one constant: the distance algorithm discards triangles below a fixed area threshold, which valid triangles fall below at the centimeter scale. With that constant changed and nothing else, episodes with an artifact fall from 12 in 100 to none, and the success rate on five container tasks rises from 89% to 98%. Success rates in simulation thus count failures that the simulator causes. Benchmarks on PhysX 5.3.1 or earlier should rerun in a repaired engine. Where the engine cannot change, they should report the success rate together with the range it spans when every flagged episode fails or passes: 75.8% to 98.5% around a reported 83.1% for LingBot-VA.

llm.title_ja: シミュレータが失敗するとき、ポリシーではない：シミュレートされたロボットベンチマークにおける接触アーティファクトの監査
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレータの衝突検出の不具合が原因でロボットポリシーの評価に誤った失敗やペナルティがカウントされていることを発見し、プラグインによる監査とエンジンの修正を提案した。
llm.problem: シミュレーションベンチマークにおける失敗の多くはポリシーではなくシミュレータの物理エンジンの不具合に起因している。
llm.method: 接触時の異常な挙動を検出し、シミュレーションパラメータを変更して追跡・監査するプラグイン「SimuGuard」を提案し、物理エンジンの定数を修正した。
llm.result: アーティファクトの発生率が12%から0%に低下し、5つのコンテナタスクの成功率が89%から98%に向上した。

2610.41857.tldr_en: Testing a vision language action model and a world action model in simulation, it is found that the policy often places the object and the simulator then ejects it, and that the benchmark's own scripted demonstrations fail the same way.

2610.41844.title: SketchMate: Agentic Geometric Reasoning for Zero-Shot Precision Insertion
2610.41844.abstract: Inserting an unseen part requires sub-millimetre precision and the correct orientation of keyed features. Current zero-shot agentic manipulation methods built on vision-language models (VLMs) produce spatial outputs that are far too coarse for this. We propose to let a VLM build a sketch model of the task, i.e., a few geometric primitives and two mate frames, which a VLM agent measures with geometric tools in multi-view depth and which a standard planner and compliant controller execute. Because a sketch describes the parts independently of their placement, the robot needs to build it only once per task. A sketch memory stores each agent run and transfers the stored sketch to later placements by point-cloud registration, so that the VLM is called only for unfamiliar parts. After grasping the part, the robot inspects both mating faces at close range and corrects the sketch by shape matching. On 69 simulated insertion episodes, our method inserts 88% of the parts at the assembled pose in a strict kinematic test, while ReKep and MOKA with the same VLM insert none. On new placements of eight tasks, reusing one stored run inserts as many parts as calling the agent in each episode, and it produces the sketch in 3.4 s instead of about 90 s.

llm.title_ja: SketchMate：ゼロショット高精度挿入のためのエージェント型幾何推論
llm.tldr_ja: VLMがタスクのスケッチモデルを構築し、幾何学的ツールや標準プランナーと連携することで、未知の部品のゼロショット高精度挿入を実現した。
llm.problem: VLMベースの既存の操作手法は空間出力が粗すぎるため、未知の部品のサブミリ単位の精密挿入に対応できない。
llm.method: VLMに幾何学的プリミティブとマイトフレームからなるタスクのスケッチモデルを作成させ、幾何ツールで測定し、プランナーとコントローラで実行する。
llm.result: 厳密な運動学的テストにおいて69のシミュレーション挿入エピソードのうち88%の部品を組み立て姿勢で挿入した。

2610.41844.tldr_en: This work proposes to let a VLM build a sketch model of the task, i.e., a few geometric primitives and two mate frames, which a VLM agent measures with geometric tools in multi-view depth and which a standard planner and compliant controller execute.

2610.41839.title: Integrating Low-Thrust Transfer Dynamics into POMDP Planning for On-Orbit Servicing
2610.41839.abstract: Recent developments in both high-thrust (HT) and low-thrust (LT) propulsion technologies broaden design options for on-orbit servicing (OOS) missions. However, incorporating LT transfers into OOS mission planning requires accounting for the trade-off between prescribed transfer duration and propellant consumption. Multi-servicing, multi-transfer OOS mission planning is inherently sequential and requires adaptive planning tools that account for propulsion-dependent transfer durations and mass-dependent propellant consumption. Thus, transfer dynamics must be integrated into mission planning and scheduling to increase flexibility and adaptability. In addition, the planning is often done with imperfect information about the system's state and stochastic service demands. This paper focuses on modeling orbital transfers, particularly LT transfers, within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework for OOS mission planning. To enable offline policy computation, the transfer model must provide explicit state transitions and rewards for all admissible actions. The state space is therefore augmented with the servicing vehicle's remaining propellant to enable consistent mass updates. HT transfers are modeled using a precomputed transfer matrix that maps each transfer to the time of flight and propellant consumed. LT transfers are represented using an analytical GEO phasing model with prescribed transfer-duration alternatives. For each alternative, the model calculates propellant consumption and maneuver feasibility as functions of the required phase change and the current servicing-vehicle mass. The proposed modeling approach is evaluated on simplified OOS planning scenarios using circular phasing with HT and LT propulsion. The resulting POMDPs are solved using the Successive Approximations of the Reachable Space under Optimal Policies (SARSOP) algorithm, and the policies obtained under HT and LT are compared. This comparison provides a quantitative assessment of the feasibility and operational impact of LT options, particularly regarding the potential role of advanced electric propulsion in future servicing architectures.
2610.41839.journal_ref: 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC), Oct 2026, Antalya (Turkey), Turkey

llm.title_ja: 軌道上サービスのためのPOMDP計画への低推力移行ダイナミクスの統合
llm.tldr_ja: 軌道上サービス（OOS）ミッション計画において、推進力依存の移行時間や質量依存の推進剤消費を考慮するため、低推力移行を部分観測マルコフ決定過程（POMDP）フレームワーク内にモデル化した。
llm.problem: OOS計画において、指定された移行時間と推進剤消費のトレードオフや不完全情報を考慮した適応型計画ツールが必要である点。
llm.method: 状態空間に残存推進剤を追加し、高推力は事前計算マトリクス、低推力は解析的GEO位相モデルを用いてPOMDPとしてモデル化する。
llm.result: 要旨に記載なし

2610.41833.title: PGGT-Loc: Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer for Feed-Forward Camera Localization
2610.41833.abstract: Camera localization methods are mostly multi-stage pipelines relying on dedicated and complex maps that are costly to construct, store, and maintain over time. Alternatively, well-structured maps that organize scenes with compact yet expressive primitives are often readily available, providing rich structural and semantic cues that humans can interpret. However, their potential for direct camera localization remains largely unexplored due to the significant modality gap between map primitives and visual observations. This motivates a new concept for localization, which estimates camera poses by grounding query observations to map primitives. In this paper, we instantiate the concept in the context of planar primitives with PGGT, the Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer network. Given a single query image and a set of planar map primitives, the network is trained to predict multiple localization targets for feed-forward 6-DoF camera localization that generalizes to unseen environments. With this straightforward and scalable architecture, our method pushes the state-of-the-art localization performance on both dense surface maps and minimal layout models. The code and models are available at https://github.com/3dv-casia/PGGT-Loc
2610.41833.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 24 pages, 14 figures, including appendices. Code and models: https://github.com/3dv-casia/PGGT-Loc

llm.title_ja: PGGT-Loc：フィードフォワードカメラローカライゼーションのためのプリミティブ接地ジオメトリートランスフォーマー
llm.tldr_ja: クエリ画像と平面マッププリミティブを対応付けて複数のローカライゼーションターゲットを予測する、新しいトランスフォーマーネットワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のカメラ位置合わせは複雑なマルチステージパイプラインとコストのかかるマップに依存しており、マップと視覚観測間のモダリティギャップが大きい。
llm.method: 単一のクエリ画像と平面マッププリミティブのセットを入力し、未知環境に汎化する6-DoFカメラ位置を予測するPGGTネットワークを構築する。
llm.result: 高密度サーフェスマップと最小限のレイアウトモデルの両方で、最先端のローカライゼーション性能を向上させた。
keywords_ja: カメラローカライゼーション
幾何学的プリミティブ

2610.41833.tldr_en: This paper instantiates a new concept for localization, which estimates camera poses by grounding query observations to map primitives with PGGT, the Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer network, and pushes the state-of-the-art localization performance on both dense surface maps and minimal layout models.

2610.41768.title: Visual-Inertial RGB-D SLAM with Encoders for a Differential Wheeled Robot
2610.41768.abstract: Recent years have seen multiple impressive results in visual-inertial odometry (VIO) techniques, by which accurate state estimation can be achieved via the extended Kalman filter (EKF) or nonlinear optimization. However, these approaches are rarely open source, and they tend to fail in real experiments due to the temporary lack of feature points and fast motion. Therefore, in this study, we used encoders to overcome the temporary failure of purely vision-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Here, we propose a generative measurement model for encoders and derive an expression for the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate and necessary Jacobians for optimization. We use our theory to present a novel tightly coupled visual-inertial encoder RGB-Depth (RGB-D) SLAM system. Tests on our system on an in-house dataset confirmed that our modeling effort led to accurate (with a root mean squared error (RMSE) of approximately 2-7 cm) and robust state estimation in real time. The source code and our dataset containing the encoder information have been published for verification.
2610.41768.comment: 11 pages. Author-accepted manuscript of the article published in IEEE Sensors Journal, 2022
2610.41768.journal_ref: IEEE Sensors Journal, vol. 22, no. 6, pp. 5360-5371, March 2022

llm.title_ja: 差動式車輪型ロボットのためのエンコーダ付き視覚慣性RGB-D SLAM
llm.tldr_ja: エンコーダの生成測定モデルを導入し、特徴点不足や急な動きに起因する視覚SLAMの失敗を克服する密結合型視覚慣性エンコーダRGB-D SLAMシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚慣性オドメトリは特徴点の一時的な欠如や急激な動きにより実機実験で失敗しやすい。
llm.method: エンコーダの生成測定モデルを設計し、MAP推定の表現と最適化のためのヤコビアンを導出してタイトカップリングなRGB-D SLAMシステムを構築する。
llm.result: 自社製データセットでのテストにより、実時間で2〜7cmのRMSEという高精度かつロバストな状態推定を確認した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

badges.venue: IEEE Sensors Journal, vol. 22, no. 6, pp 2022

2610.41768.tldr_en: A generative measurement model for encoders is proposed and an expression for the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate and necessary Jacobians for optimization is derived and used to present a novel tightly coupled visual-inertial encoder RGB-Depth (RGB-D) SLAM system.

2610.41752.title: Higher-Order Kinematic Derivatives for Aspect-Preserving Real-Time Numerical Inverse Kinematics
2610.41752.abstract: This paper leverages the higher-order kinematic derivatives of serial robots to achieve efficient, aspect-preserving real-time inverse kinematics. First, a family of higher-order solvers is derived, with a necessary orientation-error correction map, yielding the QuIK4 and QuIK5 methods with fourth- and fifth-order convergence. Second, an aspect-preserving step limiter extrapolates the Jacobian determinant along the step to predict and avoid singularities, shortening steps only when they head toward a singularity rather than when the current iterate is ill-conditioned. Third, a Hermite-interpolation certifier verifies the aspect of each answer, and a certified restart algorithm recovers failures from proven same-aspect seeds. The proposed methods are shown to outperform prior methods, reducing failures by up to four orders of magnitude and nearly eliminating aspect switching at tracking-level errors. A C++ library is released with ROS 2 integration.

llm.title_ja: アスペクトを保持するリアルタイム数値逆運動学のための高次運動学的導関数
llm.tldr_ja: シリアルロボットの高次運動学的導関数を活用し、特異点を回避して失敗を大幅に削減する効率的な高次逆運動学ソルバーを開発した。
llm.problem: 従来の数値逆運動学は特異点付近で失敗しやすく、特異点回避のための計算コストやアスペクト切替の問題がある。
llm.method: 4次および5次の収束を持つソルバーファミリを導出し、特異点を予測・回避するアスペクト保持ステップリミッターと、ヘルミット補間による認定器を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 従来手法と比較して失敗を最大4桁削減し、トラッキングレベルのエラーにおけるアスペクト切替をほぼ排除した。

2610.41752.tldr_en: This paper leverages the higher-order kinematic derivatives of serial robots to achieve efficient, aspect-preserving real-time inverse kinematics, and proposes methods to outperform prior methods.

2610.41724.title: When Architectural Spaces Start to Act
2610.41724.abstract: Architectural spaces are increasingly gaining robotic capabilities. Architectural robots such as robotic partitions, ceilings, furniture, facades, and other spatial components can autonomously move and reconfigure in response to occupants' needs and activities. Yet, when architectural robots start shaping the spatial conditions in which people continuously live, work, and interact, we may begin to experience the architectural space itself as robotic. What does this shift mean for how we inhabit such spaces? Drawing on our previous studies, I reflect on how architectural robots interact with people not only through their motions, but also through the spatial configurations that persist after those motions stop; how their actions may benefit some occupants while disadvantaging others; and how multiple robots may together make a whole architectural space appear to act. I argue that as computation gains the capacity to physically reconfigure our environments, interaction extends beyond the moment of computational action into the spatial conditions that people continue to inhabit. Understanding robotic architecture therefore requires us to look beyond short-term human-robot interaction and toward how people inhabit, negotiate, and maintain control over spaces that can autonomously reconfigure.

llm.title_ja: 建築空間が動き始めるとき
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的に再構成可能な建築ロボットが人々の空間居住やインタラクションに与える影響について、短期的な動作を超えた長期的な視点から考察した。
llm.problem: 建築ロボットが自律的に空間を再構成する際、短期的なHRIに終始しがちで、人々が静的な空間状態をどう維持・受容するかが見落とされている。
llm.method: 過去の調査に基づき、建築ロボットの動きそのものだけでなく、動作停止後の空間構成が人々に与える影響を多角的に分析・考察する。
llm.result: 要旨に結果の数値記載なし
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.41702.title: Flexibility-Aware Robotic Manipulation: Deformation Estimation, Kinematics, and Control via Distributed Inertial Measurement
2610.41702.abstract: Flexible robot links challenge the rigid-body assumption, making joint measurements alone insufficient for accurate manipulation. This paper introduces a flexibility-aware manipulation framework that connects structural dynamics directly to sensing, kinematics, and control. Instead of prescribing a dense inertial measurement unit (IMU) network, the dominant vibration modes of each flexible link are first identified from response-convergence and excitation-bandwidth criteria. Under a full-rank modal observability condition, $m$ retained modes require only $m$ independent slope measurements and one reference IMU, defining the minimum observable IMU configuration. The resulting measurements are used to reconstruct the continuous link deformation, which is then incorporated into flexibility-aware forward kinematics and a deformation-informed partial differential equation-based controller. Experiments on hydraulic single- and double-link manipulators evaluate the framework. On the long-reach double-link platform, the proposed kinematics achieves end-effector root mean square errors of $0.0107$~m, $0.0194$~m, and $0.0102$~rad while using fewer sensors than the piecewise-rigid method. Closed-loop reaching experiments further demonstrate real-time integration of IMU-estimated joint states and reconstructed deformation into the proposed controller. The results show that dominant modal information can determine sensing requirements and enable real-time flexibility-aware robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: 柔軟性を考慮したロボットマニピュレーション：分散型慣性測定による変形推定、運動学、制御
llm.tldr_ja: 柔軟なリンクを持つロボットアンプにおいて、最小限のIMUセンサー構成から連続的なリンク変形を再構成し、柔軟性を考慮した運動学と制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 柔軟なロボットリンクは剛体仮定を崩し、関節測定のみでは正確なマニピュレーションが困難である。
llm.method: 応答収束・励振帯域基準から優勢な振動モードを同定し、最小限のIMU配置でリンク変形を再構成した上で、順運動学とPDEベースのコントローラに統合する。
llm.result: 長尺の二重リンクプラットフォームにおいて、少数のセンサーでエンドエフェクタのRMSEを小さく抑え、リアルタイム制御に成功した。

2610.41702.tldr_en: A flexibility-aware manipulation framework that connects structural dynamics directly to sensing, kinematics, and control is introduced that can determine sensing requirements and enable real-time flexibility-aware robotic manipulation.

2610.41688.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
2610.41688.abstract: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state persistence, task progress, belief maintenance, and experiential learning; and eight architectural categories, including recurrent states, fast weights, visual and symbolic representations, spatial memory, and experience-based systems. We analyze their capabilities and limitations, and examine how existing benchmarks evaluate memory-dependent behavior, distinguishing genuine use of historical information from general task performance. Finally, we identify open challenges in selecting relevant experiences, maintaining consistent beliefs in changing environments, and consolidating knowledge across episodes. Our analysis provides a framework for understanding memory as an essential component of reliable, adaptive, and lifelong-horizon embodied intelligence.

llm.title_ja: 過去が行動を形成するとき：身体性記憶の理解
llm.tldr_ja: 動的環境での長期的なタスク実行やナビゲーションにおいて、過去の観測や行動、経験を保持・活用する「身体性記憶」の要件とアーキテクチャを体系的に調査した。
llm.problem: 生成基盤モデルの発展によりロボットの能力は向上したが、動的環境での柔軟な対応には過去の情報の保持・更新が不可欠である。
llm.method: 身体性記憶を6つの基本要件と8つのアーキテクチャカテゴリに分類し、既存のベンチマークやオープンな課題を分析・整理する。
llm.result: 要旨に結果の数値記載なし

2610.41688.tldr_en: This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation, and provides a framework for understanding memory as an essential component of reliable, adaptive, and lifelong-horizon embodied intelligence.

2610.41679.title: Biomechanics do not predict perceptual and cognitive consequences of force augmentation
2610.41679.abstract: Wearable force-augmentation technologies, including exoskeletons and soft exosuits, are being developed for occupational and rehabilitation settings to enhance performance by reducing the muscular demands of movements. Yet enhanced performance also requires users to perceive the environment accurately, adapt to changing conditions, and decide whether actions are worth their physical cost. We used an elbow-assisting exosuit to investigate the physiological, perceptual and cognitive consequences of force augmentation during lifting. We assessed weight perception, adaptation in a volatile environment, and effort-based decision-making with and without assistance. While assistance reduced muscle activity, its behavioural outcomes did not simply reflect this biomechanical change. Assistance reduced perceived weight, but this effect was strongly shaped by participants' initial experience. Assistance also selectively reduced adaptation to changing environmental contingencies. Finally, reducing the muscular demands of lifting did not translate straightforwardly into how demanding the action felt or whether participants chose to perform it: differences in effort-based decisions were shaped by initial experience rather than simply tracking reductions in muscle activity or perceived fatigue. Together, we show that the perceptual and cognitive consequences of force augmentation cannot be inferred from its biomechanical benefits alone. Effective augmentation therefore requires perceptual and cognitive outcomes to be evaluated alongside physical performance.
2610.41679.comment: 43 pages, 3 main figures, 3 supplementary figures, 3 supplementary tables, 3 supplementary movies. Supplementary movies available at https://osf.io/ft56y/files/osfstorage

llm.title_ja: 生体力学は力拡張の知覚的および認知的結果を予測しない
llm.tldr_ja: 肘補助用パワードスーツを用いた実験により、力拡張技術による筋活動の低減がそのまま知覚や認知的決定、疲労感の軽減に直結しないことを明らかにした。
llm.problem: パワーアシストスーツなどの力拡張技術において、生体力学的負荷の軽減がユーザーの知覚的・認知的適応にどう影響するか十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: 肘補助外骨格を用いて、重量知覚、変動環境への適応、努力ベースの意思決定を補助の有無で比較・評価する。
llm.result: 補助は筋活動と知覚重量を軽減したが、環境への適応や努力に基づく意思決定は生体力学的軽減とは単純に対応せず初期経験に大きく影響された。

2610.41679.tldr_en: It is shown that the perceptual and cognitive consequences of force augmentation cannot be inferred from its biomechanical benefits alone and therefore requires perceptual and cognitive outcomes to be evaluated alongside physical performance.

2610.41676.title: Interaction-Aware Sampling-Based Motion Planning for Autonomous Surface Vessels in Urban Waterways
2610.41676.abstract: Autonomous surface vessels operating in urban waterways must coordinate with other vessels in confined spaces while complying with traffic regulations, often without knowing their intentions. We present a decentralized motion planner based on model predictive path integral control, a sampling-based model predictive control scheme. The planner jointly computes a trajectory for the ego vessel and a prediction of the trajectories of the other vessels, and therefore accounts for their interaction. Traffic regulations are encoded as discontinuous costs, which the sampling-based formulation admits without a smooth approximation. We evaluate the method in maps taken from real sections of Amsterdam's canals, in encounters between two vessels and in scenarios with four interacting vessels. Across 780 randomized runs the method reaches every goal without collisions or deadlocks, and outperforms an optimization-based planner designed for the same domain, as well as a version of the proposed planner that does not account for the interaction. We further validate the planner on two scaled vessel prototypes in an outdoor environment, where planning and localization run onboard at 10 Hz, and head-on and crossing encounters are resolved without collisions or rule violations.
2610.41676.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

llm.title_ja: 都市水路における自律水上船のための相互作用を考慮したサンプリングベースのモーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 混雑した都市水路において、他船の意図や交通規則を考慮しながら安全かつデッドロックなしに航行できる分散型モーションプランナーを提案した。
llm.problem: 都市水路を航行する自律水上船は、狭い空間で他船の意図が不明なまま交通規則を守りながら協調する必要がある。
llm.method: モデル予測経路積分制御に基づく分散型モーションプランナーを構築し、交通規則を不連続コストとしてエンコードして自己と他船の軌道を共同予測する。
llm.result: アムステルダムの水路マップを用いた780回のランで衝突やデッドロックなくゴールに到達し、実機プロトタイプでも検証された。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.41676.tldr_en: This work presents a decentralized motion planner based on model predictive path integral control, a sampling-based model predictive control scheme that outperforms an optimization-based planner designed for the same domain, as well as a version of the proposed planner that does not account for the interaction.

2610.41671.title: OpenVIO: A Versatile Open-Source Visual-Inertial Odometry System
2610.41671.abstract: Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is a fundamental topic in robotics research. Beyond research, VIO has been adopted in a wide range of products. In this manuscript, we present OpenVIO, an open-source VIO system for research and practical applications. It is released under the MIT license. OpenVIO supports pinhole and fisheye cameras and extends this support to stitched 360° images. We describe each part of the system together with its design considerations. We also report benchmark results with other open-source VIO systems on public datasets. OpenVIO is available as open source at https://github.com/93won/openvio.

llm.title_ja: OpenVIO：汎用オープンソース視覚慣性オドメトリシステム
llm.tldr_ja: ピンホールカメラや魚眼カメラ、360度全天候画像に対応した汎用オープンソースの視覚慣性オドメトリ（VIO）システムを提案・公開した。
llm.problem: 高性能なVIO技術は広く製品化されているものの、オープンソースとして利用できる汎用的で信頼性の高いシステムが限られている。
llm.method: 設計上の考慮事項を伴う各システムのコンポーネントを詳細に記述し、パブリックデータセットで他のオープンソースVIOシステムと比較評価する。
llm.result: 要旨に詳細な数値結果の記載はないが、MITライセンスの下でオープンソースとして公開された。

2610.41671.tldr_en: OpenVIO is presented, an open-source VIO system for research and practical applications that supports pinhole and fisheye cameras and extends this support to stitched 360{\deg} images.

2610.41667.title: GPU-accelerated Incremental Euclidean Distance Transform for Online Motion Planning of Mobile Robots
2610.41667.abstract: In this letter, we present a volumetric mapping system that effectively calculates Occupancy Grid Maps (OGMs) and Euclidean Distance Transforms (EDTs) with parallel computing. Unlike these mappers for high-precision structural reconstruction, our system incrementally constructs global EDT and outputs high-frequency local distance information for online robot motion planning. The proposed system constructs OGM with massive amount of data from multiple types of sensor inputs. Using GPU programming techniques, the system quickly computes EDT in parallel within local volume. The new observation is continuously integrated into the global EDT using the parallel wavefront algorithm while preserving the historical observations. Experiments with datasets have shown that our proposed approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art robot mapping systems and is particularly suitable for mapping unexplored areas. In its actual implementations on aerial and ground vehicles, the proposed system achieves real-time performance with limited onboard computational resources.
2610.41667.comment: Published in RA-L 2022. Author-accepted manuscript. Code: https://github.com/JINXER000/GIE-mapping
2610.41667.journal_ref: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, vol. 7, no. 3, pp. 6894-6901, July 2022

llm.title_ja: モバイルロボットのオンラインモーションプランニングのためのGPUアクセラレーション型インクリメンタルユークリッド距離変換
llm.tldr_ja: GPUの並列計算を用いて占有格子地図とユークリッド距離変換を高速にインクリメンタル構築し、オンラインのロボットモーションプランニングを実現するマッピングシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: 高精度な構造再構築用のマッパーはオンラインのロボットモーションプランニングにおいて計算負荷が高すぎる。
llm.method: 複数のセンサー入力を統合して占有格子地図を作成し、GPUプログラミングと並列ウェーブフロントアルゴリズムを用いて局所空間でEDTを高速に並列計算する。
llm.result: 既存の最先端マッピングシステムを凌駕し、限られたオンボード計算リソースを持つ空中・地上車両でリアルタイム性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ユークリッド距離変換
モーションプランニング

2610.41667.tldr_en: A volumetric mapping system that effectively calculates Occupancy Grid Maps (OGMs) and Euclidean Distance Transforms (EDTs) with parallel computing with limited onboard computational resources is presented.

2610.41663.title: ResMerge: Residual Policy Learning and Merging for Continual Adaptation of Pre-trained Robot Policies
2610.41663.abstract: Continual adaptation to new tasks is essential for robots deployed in the real world, but adapting pre-trained policies remains challenging due to parameter growth and the need for continual demonstration collection. Parameter-Efficient Continual Fine-Tuning (PECFT) isolates task-specific updates, but adapter-per-task designs require demonstrations and grow with the task set. We propose ResMerge, a two-stage framework that learns mergeable residual policies atop a frozen pre-trained policy: residual reinforcement learning (RL) acquires task-specific corrections without additional expert demonstrations during adaptation, and parameter-space merging consolidates compatible residuals to reduce stored parameters. We introduce Residual-Field Consistency (RFC), a simple, bounded, and interpretable metric that assesses compatibility in residual action-field space by comparing correction direction and magnitude. Experiments on LIBERO across two backbones and on a real-world Franka robot show improved continual learning performance over strong PECFT baselines, while selective merging reduces the residual-parameter footprint. Project website: https://resmerge.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: ResMerge：事前学習済みロボットポリシーの継続的適応のための残差ポリシー学習とマージ
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みポリシーの上にマージ可能な残差ポリシーを学習・統合することで、追加の専門家デモンストレーションなしで効率的な継続的適応を実現した。
llm.problem: ロボットポリシーの継続的適応では、パラメータの増大やタスクごとの追加デモンストレーション収集が必要となり課題が多い。
llm.method: 残差強化学習により追加デモンストレーションなしでタスク固有の修正を学習し、パラメータ空間でのマージにより互換性のある残差を統合する。
llm.result: LIBEROおよび実機のFrankaロボットを用いた実験で、強力なPECFTベースラインを上回る継続的学習性能を示した。

2610.41663.tldr_en: ResMerge is proposed, a two-stage framework that learns mergeable residual policies atop a frozen pre-trained policy: residual reinforcement learning (RL) acquires task-specific corrections without additional expert demonstrations during adaptation, and parameter-space merging consolidates compatible residuals to reduce stored parameters.

2610.41654.title: $\nabla$Mimic: Ultra-Efficient Humanoid Control with Differentiable Simulation
2610.41654.abstract:
Robot policy learning is dominated by zeroth-order methods such as PPO, which treat the simulator as a black box and pay for it with enormous sample counts. First-order policy learning differentiates through the dynamics, but on contact-rich whole-body control it has rarely worked: its gradients explode. A recent world-model method showed that derivative information can make humanoid motion tracking far more efficient, using surrogate gradients of a learned model. We show that exact gradients of the simulator itself do better, once two obstacles are removed. Exact gradients contain rare unbounded samples, because contact dynamics is not differentiable everywhere and its derivative diverges near some events; and they are expensive, because the simulator's adjoint has to replay the contact solve. $
abla$Mimic bounds these samples with median-relative per-sample gradient clipping at every step of the backward pass, and reuses each costly simulated window by multistep regression onto gradient-derived action targets, which bounds every action target independently of the gradient scale. NablaEngine, a differentiable GPU simulation engine for the Unitree G1, removes the cost: it computes MuJoCo's full contact dynamics with fused per-world kernels and the adjoint of a whole control step as a single megakernel, with analytic gradients that match float64 finite differences, $11.5	imes$ faster than the available MuJoCo Warp adjoint. On whole-body tracking of all 40 LAFAN1 clips with one policy on one GPU, $
abla$Mimic reaches the score reported by the state-of-the-art world-model method, 0.82, in 20 minutes instead of 1.2 h, and 0.874 in 1.8 h. SHAC, the standard first-order baseline, stops on exploding gradients within minutes. We release NablaEngine and $
abla$Mimic as open-source infrastructure for first-order humanoid policy learning.

llm.title_ja: $\nabla$Mimic：微分可能シミュレーションによる超効率的ヒューノイド制御
llm.tldr_ja: 接触の不連続性による勾配爆発をクリッピングとマルチステップ回帰で克服し、解析的勾配を持つ微分可能シミュレータを用いて超効率的なヒューノイドの全身運動制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 接触を多く含むヒューノイドの全身制御において、従来のゼロ次手法はサンプル数が膨大であり、一次手法は接触ダイナミクスの勾配爆発により困難であった。
llm.method: メダリ安値の勾配クリッピングと勾配誘導型アクションターゲットへのマルチステップ回帰を行い、GPU対応の微分可能エンジンNablaEngineを構築する。
llm.result: 全身トラッキングにおいてスコア0.82を従来の1.2時間から20分で達成し、0.874のスコアを1.8時間で達成した。
keywords_ja: 微分可能シミュレーション
ヒューノイドロボット
モーションコントロール

2610.41654.tldr_en: NablaEngine and $\nabla$Mimic are released as open-source infrastructure for first-order humanoid policy learning and it is shown that exact gradients of the simulator itself do better, once two obstacles are removed.

2610.41643.title: Direct Action-Manifold Modeling for Efficient and Robust Bimanual Manipulation
2610.41643.abstract: Diffusion and flow matching visuomotor policies require iterative denoising or numerical integration for multimodal action generation, introducing latency and execution mismatch. We instead consider a different formulation: conditioned on vision and proprioception, demonstrated bimanual action chunks concentrate in a structured observation-dependent region of joint-action space, making the action target more direct to model than the generative process. Based on this view, we propose the Direct Manifold Action Transformer (DMAT), which reformulates action generation as the direct modeling of clean, observation-conditioned joint-space action chunks from stochastic interpolants, thereby enabling single-step inference without relying on iterative generative inference or auxiliary trajectory-straightening procedures. Within DMAT, local 3D geometry anchors predictions to spatial structure, while State-Consistent Spectral-Time Refinement (STR) reconciles predicted chunks with proprioception and suppresses high-frequency residuals. Across 567 standard and out-of-distribution (OOD) trials per method, DMAT outperformed Improved 3D Diffusion Policy (IDP3) and DiTFlow3D in aggregate success rate, achieving relative improvements of 129.1% and 95.7%, respectively, while generating action chunks 2.06x and 1.34x faster and remaining robust under repeated 50 N interventions. These results pave the way for a novel generative paradigm for efficient and robust bimanual manipulation.

llm.title_ja: 効率的でロバストな両腕マニピュレーションのための直接行動多様体モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 確率的補間からクリーンな関節空間の行動チャンクを直接モデル化することで、反復的な生成推論を回避し単一ステップでの高速かつロバストな両腕操作を実現した。
llm.problem: 拡散モデルやフローマッチング等の視覚運動ポリシーは反復的なノイズ除去や数値積分を必要とし、遅延や実行時の不整合を引き起こす。
llm.method: ビジョンと固有受容感覚を条件として、構造化された観測依存の関節行動チャンクを直接モデル化するDMATフレームワークを提案し、単一ステップ推論を行う。
llm.result: IDP3やDiTFlow3Dと比較して成功率を大幅に向上させ、2倍以上高速な行動チャンク生成と外乱に対するロバスト性を達成した。
keywords_ja: 両腕マニピュレーション

2610.41643.tldr_en: The Direct Manifold Action Transformer (DMAT) is proposed, which reformulates action generation as the direct modeling of clean, observation-conditioned joint-space action chunks from stochastic interpolants, thereby enabling single-step inference without relying on iterative generative inference or auxiliary trajectory-straightening procedures.

2610.41625.title: RTPolicy: Real-Time (32.9 Hz) Multi-View Visuomotor Policy for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices
2610.41625.abstract: Low inference latency is critical for closed-loop robotic manipulation, especially under asynchronous inference, where action chunks must be updated promptly to correct accumulated deviations. However, existing visuomotor policies rely on computationally expensive visual backbones, resulting in high inference latency and deployment overhead. In this paper, we propose RTPolicy, a multi-view visuomotor policy that attains accurate manipulation with high inference efficiency. Its core design combines view-aware feature fusion with visual compression to aggregate complementary information across camera views into a compact token representation. The representation conditions a flow-matching action generator with the robot state and flow time, reducing the cost of action generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this design reduces the computational cost of visual representation and action generation while preserving visual information required for manipulation. On the RoboTwin~2.0 single-task clean evaluation across 50 tasks, RTPolicy attains a mean success rate of 52.26\%, outperforming the strongest leaderboard baseline $π_0$ (46.4\%). We further evaluate RTPolicy under asynchronous streaming inference on a real bimanual platform, where RTPolicy attains a mean success rate of 72.0\% and sustains real-time inference at 30.35 ms (32.9 Hz) on the RDK S600 and 149.72 ms (6.7 Hz) on the RDK S100, both in INT16. Project Page: https://d-robotics-ai-lab.github.io/RTPolicy.project.

llm.title_ja: RTPolicy：エッジデバイス上のロボットマニピュレーションのためのリアルタイム（32.9 Hz）多視点視覚運動ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 多視点の視覚特徴融合と視覚圧縮を組み合わせることで、ビジュアル表現の計算コストを削減し、エッジデバイス上で高精度かつリアルタイムな動作生成を実現した。
llm.problem: 既存の視覚運動ポリシーは計算コストの高い視覚バックボーンに依存しており、推論遅延が高く非同期推論時の遅延が大きい。
llm.method: 視覚情報をコンパクトなトークン表現に集約するビューアウェア特徴融合と視覚圧縮を設計し、フローマッチングアクションジェネレータを条件付けする。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0の評価で平均成功率52.26%を記録してベースラインを上回り、実機環境で最大32.9 Hzのリアルタイム推論を達成した。

2610.41625.tldr_en: RTPolicy, a multi-view visuomotor policy that attains accurate manipulation with high inference efficiency, is proposed, which combines view-aware feature fusion with visual compression to aggregate complementary information across camera views into a compact token representation.

2610.41609.title: VLA Policies Do Not Know When Not to Act: Unintended Task Execution and Start Suppression
2610.41609.abstract: A robot should act only on an instruction from a person or on an intent that the robot explicitly represents and generates. Unintended actions taken without such an instruction can cause risk or inconvenience to people and the environment. We examine how recent vision-language-action (VLA) policies respond when the instruction is missing or meaningless. We apply a paired protocol with empty, neutral, nonsense, infeasible, and wrong-task instructions to six model checkpoints in LIBERO-Goal simulation. Holding the initial state fixed and varying only the instruction, we ask three questions: whether the robot starts to move, which task it completes, and what the instruction determines. Even when the instruction was empty, the robot started moving in every episode with all six checkpoints, and with five of them it often completed a task that the instruction had not specified. On two GR00T checkpoints, the instruction determined which task was executed but not whether the robot started moving; the robot moved even on infeasible instructions. We then tested three methods for suppressing the start: prepending "if no task is given do not move" to the instruction; a gate that holds the robot when the first action chunk for the given instruction nearly equals that for an empty instruction; and fine-tuning the policy to hold still on non-task inputs. The prefix stopped the robot in none of the six checkpoints, and the gate held it on non-task inputs in five of the six checkpoints. The fine-tuned policy never completed a task on non-task inputs, but it did not reliably keep the robot still, and it failed to suppress the start on infeasible instructions.
2610.41609.tldr_en: A paired protocol with empty, neutral, nonsense, infeasible, and wrong-task instructions is applied to six model checkpoints in LIBERO-Goal simulation and three methods for suppressing the start are tested.

2610.41602.title: DrawSplat: Atlanta World-Guided Implicit Gaussian SLAM for Indoor Reconstruction
2610.41602.abstract: RGB-D SLAM requires accurate online tracking, high-quality rendering, and geometrically consistent reconstruction. Existing Gaussian SLAM methods mainly optimize Gaussian primitives with photometric, depth, or local frame-to-model constraints, which are often insufficient in indoor scenes with weak textures, large planar structures, noisy depth, and long trajectories. The resulting maps may suffer from pose drift, surface thickness artifacts, noisy normals, and blurred structural boundaries. We propose DrawSplat, an Atlanta World-guided implicit Gaussian SLAM framework for indoor reconstruction. DrawSplat follows a drawing-like process: explicit point-line geometry first sketches the structural layout, and implicit neural Gaussians then fill in high-fidelity appearance and continuous geometric details. It estimates camera poses, sparse geometry, and gravity direction through point-line joint tracking, infers structural planes from tracked lines using the shared-gravity component of the Atlanta World prior, and converts them into differentiable regularization terms on Gaussian centers and normals. To improve compactness and efficiency, DrawSplat further combines an anchor-based implicit neural Gaussian representation with adaptive structural sampling, which allocates Gaussian capacity to structurally informative regions. Experiments on multiple datasets show that DrawSplat achieves robust tracking, high-fidelity rendering, and strong geometric reconstruction among Gaussian-based SLAM systems, while maintaining a practical balance among quality, efficiency, and model size.

llm.title_ja: DrawSplat：屋内再構成のためのアトランタワールド誘導暗黙的ガウスSLAM
llm.tldr_ja: アトランタワールドの事前知識と点線幾何学を活用して構造的レイアウトをスケッチし、暗黙的ニューラルガウスで詳細を補うことで、高精度な屋内再構成とロバストなトラッキングを実現した。
llm.problem: テクスチャの乏しい屋内シーンやノイズの多い深度画像では、既存のガウスSLAMは姿勢ドリフトや表面の厚みアーティファクト、境界のぼやけが生じやすい。
llm.method: 点線結合トラッキングでカメラ姿勢と重力方向を推定し、アトランタワールドの事前知識から構造面を推論してガウス中心・法線の正則化項に変換するドローイング風のフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 複数のデータセットにおいて、トラッキングのロバスト性、高品質なレンダリング、強力な幾何学的再構成を優れたバランスで達成した。
keywords_ja: ガウスプラッティング

2610.41602.tldr_en: Experiments show that DrawSplat achieves robust tracking, high-fidelity rendering, and strong geometric reconstruction among Gaussian-based SLAM systems, while maintaining a practical balance among quality, efficiency, and model size.

2610.41558.title: A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots
2610.41558.abstract: Collision-free motion planning for multi-agent robotic systems remains an active research area because of the complexity of coordinating robot trajectories, with applications ranging from coordinated drone shows to autonomous operations on land, in the air, and on water. Importantly, the analytical difficulty of nonconvex collision-avoidance constraints has so far driven the development of exclusively numerical methods. We derive a complete analytical characterization of the optimal trajectories for two robots that start and end at rest, under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective. We prove that these trajectories belong to eight distinct contact families and determine which family applies for each configuration of initial and final positions. We analyze the geometrical properties of the optimal trajectories, provide a numerical algorithm for computing them, and discuss how these insights may improve the performance of existing numerical trajectory optimizers.

llm.title_ja: 2台のロボットの最適な衝突フリーモーションの完全な解析的特徴付け
llm.tldr_ja: 二重積分器ダイナミクスと二乗加速度目的関数のもとで、静止状態から開始・終了する2台のロボットの最適軌道が属する8つの接触ファミリを完全に解析的に解明した。
llm.problem: 非凸な衝突回避制約の解析的困難さから、マルチエージェントの衝突フリーモーションプランニングはこれまで主に数値的手法に依存していた。
llm.method: 最適軌道が属する8つの接触ファミリを導出し、初期位置と最終位置の各構成に対してどのファミリが適用されるかを決定するアルゴリズムを構築する。
llm.result: 最適軌道の幾何学的特性を明らかにし、計算のための数値アルゴリズムを提供して既存の数値的軌道最適化器の性能向上の道筋を示した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.41558.tldr_en: A complete analytical characterization of the optimal trajectories for two robots with zero initial and final velocities, under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective is derived.

2610.41548.title: Contact-based optimization for collision-free motion planning for a million robots
2610.41548.abstract: Multi-agent robotic systems have attracted growing interest in recent years, with applications ranging from coordinated drone shows to autonomous operations on land, in the air, and on water. At the planning level, robot motion is often modeled using double-integrator dynamics (with low-level controllers handling the physical dynamics during execution) with a minimum-energy objective subject to collision-avoidance constraints and limits on position, velocity, and acceleration. The complexity of the problem resides in the constraints, which couple the trajectories and make the optimization problem nonconvex. Existing numerical approaches typically discretize and optimize entire trajectories, which becomes expensive for large fleets. We exploit the structure of optimal trajectories by organizing optimization around contacts, at which robots reach the minimum allowed separation. We formulate a coupled algebraic system in contact variables and reconstruct trajectories analytically between contacts. Our algorithm, sequential contact insertion (SCI), starts from unconstrained trajectories, inserts contacts at separation violations, and jointly adjusts their times and states. Numerical experiments demonstrate planning for one million robots in minutes and thousands of robots in fractions of a second. On problems feasible for a fixed-grid sequential convex programming baseline, SCI achieves median speedups of several orders of magnitude at matching solution accuracy.

llm.title_ja: 100万台のロボットのための衝突回避モーションプランニングに向けた接触ベースの最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 接触のタイミングと状態を中心に最適化を構築し、100万台のロボットのモーションプランニングを数分で実現する逐次接触挿入（SCI）アルゴリズムを提案した。
llm.problem: 多エージェントシステムの大規模化に伴い、非凸な衝突回避制約を満たす軌道最適化の計算コストが爆発的に増大する課題がある。
llm.method: 接触変数の結合代数系を定式化し、接触間で軌道を解析的に再構成する逐次接触挿入（SCI）アルゴリズムを提案した。
llm.result: 100万台規模のロボットプランニングを数分で、数千台規模を秒単位未満で達成し、従来法に比べて数桁の高速化を実現した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.41548.tldr_en: This work exploits the structure of optimal trajectories by organizing optimization around contacts, at which robots reach the minimum allowed separation, and forms a coupled algebraic system in contact variables and reconstruct trajectories analytically between contacts.

2610.41540.title: FOCUS: First-Order Control Using Optimal Transport Supervision for Imitation from Observations
2610.41540.abstract: Imitation learning from observations must recover behavior from state-only demonstrations without known temporal correspondence. Differentiable simulators provide pathwise policy gradients, but differentiating through long, contact-rich trajectories can make optimization unstable. We introduce FOCUS, which combines local optimal-transport alignment with short-horizon differentiable actor-critic learning. FOCUS matches agent rollout windows to multiple sampled expert segments using a soft best-of-$K$ objective that emphasizes locally compatible matches. The resulting transport-based costs provide differentiable imitation rewards, while a learned critic bootstraps value beyond the rollout horizon. FOCUS requires neither temporally aligned trajectories nor expert-aligned initialization or teacher forcing. Across contact-rich locomotion tasks in DFlex, including a musculoskeletal humanoid controlled by 152 muscle activations, FOCUS improves sample efficiency and training stability over adversarial imitation-from-observation methods and prior differentiable imitation baselines.
2610.41540.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Physical Understanding for Decision-Making

llm.title_ja: FOCUS: 観測からの模倣学習のための最適輸送スーパービジョンを用いた一次制御
llm.tldr_ja: 局所的な最適輸送アライメントと短ホライズンの微分可能アクター・クリティック学習を組み合わせ、安定した観測からの模倣学習を実現するFOCUSを提案した。
llm.problem: 状態のみのデモンストレーションから時間的対応関係なしに挙動を復元する際、接触を多く含む長い軌道での微分が最適化を不安定にする。
llm.method: 局所的に適合するマッチングを重視するソフトbest-of-K目的関数を用いて、エージェントのロールアウトウィンドウを複数のエキスパートセグメントに合わせるFOCUSを導入した。
llm.result: 152個の筋肉活動で制御される筋骨格ヒューマノイドを含む接触の多い歩行タスクにおいて、敵対的模倣学習や既存の微分可能模倣手法よりもサンプル効率と学習安定性を向上させた。
keywords_ja: アクタークリティック
筋骨格ヒューマノイド

2610.41540.tldr_en: FOCUS is introduced, which combines local optimal-transport alignment with short-horizon differentiable actor-critic learning and improves sample efficiency and training stability over adversarial imitation-from-observation methods and prior differentiable imitation baselines.

2610.41501.title: VoxLution: Evolving Voxels for High-Fidelity 3D Scene Generation
2610.41501.abstract: High-resolution 3D indoor scene generation is crucial for immersive applications such as virtual reality, spatial computing, and robotics simulation. We introduce VoxLution, a coarse-to-fine transformer-based approach that generates high-fidelity indoor scenes with rich details, overcoming the overly smooth geometry typical of existing generative models. First, we generate a low-resolution spatial layout; then, based on this structural information, we progressively refine the scene geometry locally in chunks. Key to our approach is formulating 3D super-resolution as a sequence modeling problem over multi-resolution sparse voxel grids. To achieve this, we introduce a training-free, resolution-invariant tokenization scheme that compactly encodes the geometric information of eight octants into a single decimal number. We formulate the transformer sequence to include multiple resolutions, allowing the coarse layout to guide the generation of fine local details. To ensure coherence across local chunks, we incorporate adjacent chunk boundary information directly into the transformer sequencing. VoxLution achieves scene generation at a finer voxel resolution than existing baselines, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks with 59.6% lower FPD and 51.1% lower FID on 3D-FRONT, and 70.5% lower FPD and 73.8% lower FID on Scannet++.

llm.title_ja: VoxLution: 高忠実度3Dシーン生成のためのボクセル進化手法
llm.tldr_ja: 粗いレイアウトから段階的にシーン形状を局所的に洗練させる、マルチ解像度スパースボクセルグリッドを用いたトランスフォーマーベースの3Dシーン生成手法VoxLutionを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の生成モデルは過度に滑らかなジオメトリになりがちで、没入型アプリケーションやロボットシミュレーション向けの高品質な3D屋内シーン生成が困難である。
llm.method: 3D超解像をマルチ解像度スパースボクセルグリッド上のシーケンスモデリングとして定式化し、学習不要な解像度不変トークン化スキームとチャンク境界情報を統合した。
llm.result: 3D-FRONTおよびScanNet++において、既存のベースラインと比較して大幅に低いFPDとFIDを達成し、最先端のパフォーマンスを示した。
keywords_ja: 空間コンピューティング

2610.41501.tldr_en: VoxLution is introduced, a coarse-to-fine transformer-based approach that generates high-fidelity indoor scenes with rich details, overcoming the overly smooth geometry typical of existing generative models.

2610.41477.title: AC-SMPC: Differentiable Actor--Critic MPC with State Constraints for Safe and Fast Robot Navigation
2610.41477.abstract: Achieving safe navigation in confined dynamic environments remains a challenging problem, as robots must balance navigation efficiency with safety. Existing actor--critic MPC architectures typically employ differentiable MPC layers, but this way cannot readily accommodate explicit state constraints, making it intractable to involve collision avoidance within learning-based planning. To address this issue, we propose an actor--critic model predictive control framework with state constraints. We first use vertices to represent the robot and obstacles, and half-spaces to represent the workspace. Based on these, the nonlinear robot dynamics is locally linearized and the hyperplane-based collision avoidance constraints are convexified into the differentiable MPC layer, and then the actor exploits closed-loop feedback to adjust the MPC objective parameters that shape local motion behavior, while the critic evaluates long-term task performance. We further relax the convexified constraints with bounded and penalized slack variables to form an elastic quadratic program, accommodating cases where the local constraint approximations cannot be satisfied simultaneously. Simulation tests and experiments, involving dynamic collision avoidance for multi-robot in narrow cases, illustrate the advantages of the proposed framework in adaptively adjusting the learned policy and improving navigation efficiency over existing approaches while maintaining the motion safety.

llm.title_ja: AC-SMPC: 安全で高速なロボットナビゲーションのための状態制約付き微分可能アクター・クリティックMPC
llm.tldr_ja: 超平面ベースの衝突回避制約を微分可能MPC層に組み込み、閉ループフィードバックで局所的な動作を調整する状態制約付きアクター・クリティックMPCフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 狭い動的環境での安全なナビゲーションにおいて、既存のアクター・クリティックMPCアーキテクチャは明示的な状態制約を容易に組み込めない課題がある。
llm.method: ロボットと障害物を頂点で、作業空間を半空間で表現し、非線形力学を局所線形化して超平面ベースの衝突回避制約を凸化し、弾性二次計画問題として定式化した。
llm.result: 狭い空間でのマルチロボットの動的衝突回避において、動的にポリシーを適応させ、運動の安全性を維持しながらナビゲーション効率を向上させた。
keywords_ja: アクタークリティック

2610.41477.tldr_en: Simulation tests and experiments, involving dynamic collision avoidance for multi-robot in narrow cases, illustrate the advantages of the proposed framework in adaptively adjusting the learned policy and improving navigation efficiency over existing approaches while maintaining the motion safety.

2610.41456.title: SAFARI: Semantic- And Frontier-driven Autonomous Risk Inspection
2610.41456.abstract: Robotic exploration can reduce human exposure to hazardous environments by autonomously searching unknown areas for objects of interest while constructing a complete, risk-aware map. However, existing autonomous exploration approaches typically prioritize geometric coverage or information gain, without explicitly coupling semantic object detection and the risk associated with operating near potentially hazardous objects. Moreover, many systems have been demonstrated primarily in simulation or controlled environments, leaving limited validation of risk-aware semantic exploration in complex, unstructured field settings. To address this gap, we propose SAFARI, a framework that treats object detection as a native channel of a unified probabilistic map, thereby jointly informing exploration and planning with both geometric and semantic evidence. We evaluated SAFARI in 11 missions across three field sites on a quadruped platform. The framework achieved an average coverage of 98.7% of the accessible mission area, without operator intervention for 97.6% of mission time, and detected objects with characteristic dimensions as small as 15cm. Lastly, through ablation studies and a detailed analysis of system behavior, we show that object-size awareness and safety-aware path planning are crucial for effective hazardous-object search.
2610.41456.comment: First two listed authors have equal contribution. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Field Robotics

llm.title_ja: SAFARI: セマンティクスとフロンティア駆動による自律的リスク検査
llm.tldr_ja: 物体検出を確率的マップのネイティブチャネルとして統合し、幾何学的・セマンティックな証拠の両方で探索と計画を共同で行うSAFARIフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の自律探索手法は、潜在的に危険な物体付近での作業に関連するリスクやセマンティックな物体検出を明示的に結合していない。
llm.method: 物体検出を統合確率マップのネイティブチャネルとして扱い、探索と計画に幾何学的・セマンティックな情報を同時に反映させる仕組みを導入した。
llm.result: 四足歩行ロボットプラットフォームを用いた3つのフィールドサイトでの11回のミッションにおいて、平均98.7%のエリアカバー率を達成し、小型物体を検出した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックマップ

2610.41456.tldr_en: This work proposes SAFARI, a framework that treats object detection as a native channel of a unified probabilistic map, thereby jointly informing exploration and planning with both geometric and semantic evidence, and shows that object-size awareness and safety-aware path planning are crucial for effective hazardous-object search.

2610.41429.title: Physically Constrained Kinematic Calibration for High-Precision Robotic Needle Guidance
2610.41429.abstract: Percutaneous needle insertion is a common practice in minimally invasive procedures whose clinical success depends on accurate needle placement. However, achieving the necessary precision is a challenge for manual operators. Robotic assistance can improve targeting accuracy and reduce operator dependence, but residual millimeter-scale errors persist because nominal kinematic models do not fully represent the physical manipulator. This paper presents a robust bound-constrained kinematic calibration method designed to improve positional accuracy for a 6-Degree-of-Freedom (6-DoF) robotic needle-guidance manipulator. The approach uses physically plausible parameter ranges to regularize a compact 19-parameter geometric identification model. By treating these bounds as active optimization constraints rather than mere numerical safeguards, the framework effectively mitigates parameter coupling and overfitting, ensuring highly stable parameter identification. In simulation, the proposed method reduced end-effector Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) from 3.422 mm to 0.690 mm (a 79.8% improvement). In benchtop hardware experiments, the calibrated model achieved sub-millimeter validation accuracy, including 0.865 mm RMSE in experimental trajectory validation and 0.610 mm RMSE in a coordinate-lattice verification task. These results demonstrate that physically constrained kinematic calibration can enhance robotic needle-targeting accuracy, establishing a high-precision foundation for future clinical applications.

llm.title_ja: 高精度ロボットニードルガイダンスのための物理制約付き運動学キャリブレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的に妥当なパラメータ範囲を能動的な最適化制約として利用し、6自由度ニードルガイダンスマニピュレータの位置精度を向上させる堅牢なキャリブレーション手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 公称運動学モデルが物理的マニピュレータを完全に表現していないため、経皮的針穿刺のロボット支援においてミリメートル単位の誤差が残る課題がある。
llm.method: 物理的に妥当なパラメータ範囲を数値的セーフガードではなく能動的な最適化制約として扱い、コンパクトな19パラメータの幾何学的識別モデルを正則化した。
llm.result: シミュレーションでエンドエフェクタのRMSEを79.8%削減し、実機実験では0.865mm未満のトラジェクトリ検証精度などのサブミリメートルの精度を達成した。
keywords_ja: 運動学キャリブレーション

2610.41429.tldr_en: It is demonstrated that physically constrained kinematic calibration can enhance robotic needle-targeting accuracy, establishing a high-precision foundation for future clinical applications.

2610.41408.title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.41408.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable capable robot behavior, but their large memory footprint limits deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Weight quantization is a natural remedy, yet post-training quantization (PTQ) recipes inherited from large language models degrade when applied to VLAs at ultra-low precision.
