Existing low-bit PTQ methods often fail to explicitly account for the structure of downstream operations and allocate precision without considering its effect on the policy actions. We introduce SACQ, an ultra- low-bit weight-only vector-codebook quantization framework for VLAs. SACQ combines (1) structure-aware codebook fitting with role-specific quadratic metrics that reflect input statistics and downstream sensitivity; (2) action-aware mixed-bit allocation based on the increase in final-action error as individual layers are compressed; and (3) two-stage post-quantization refinement that reassigns codeword indices with second-order error compensation and calibrates codebooks and row-group scales against the decoded action. Using GR00T N1.7, SACQ achieves 93.85% average success across four LIBERO suites at 1.5 bits per language/action weight while reducing model memory by 4.83x. With INT8 activation quantization and low-precision attention, it retains 93.55% success while running 1.51x faster than BF16. On SimplER, SACQ further achieves 63.76% and 52.27% success under Visual Matching and Variant Aggregation at 2 bits per language/action weight, compared to 58.90% and 53.45% for BF16, respectively.

llm.title_ja: SACQ: 超低ビットVision-Language-Actionモデルのための構造認識型コードブック量子化
llm.tldr_ja: 構造認識型コードブックフィッティング、アクション認識型混成ビット割り当て、および2段階の後量子化洗練を組み合わせたVLA向け超低ビット量子化フレームワークSACQを提案した。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルから継承された既存の事後量子化レシピを超低精度でVLAに適用すると、下流タスクのポリシーアクションに悪影響を及ぼし性能が劣化する。
llm.method: 入力統計と下流感度を反映した役割別二次メトリックを用いる構造認識型コードブックフィッティングと、アクション誤差に基づく混成ビット割り当てを導入した。
llm.result: GR00T N1.7を用いてLIBEROスイートで平均93.85%の成功率を維持しながらモデルメモリを4.83倍削減し、推論速度の高速化も実現した。

2610.41408.tldr_en: SACQ is introduced, an ultra- low-bit weight-only vector-codebook quantization framework for VLAs that combines structure-aware codebook fitting with role-specific quadratic metrics that reflect input statistics and downstream sensitivity.

2610.41383.title: BioAgent: Self-Directed Skill Acquisition and Capability Growth for Long-Horizon Laboratory Protocols
2610.41383.abstract: Executing an unfamiliar laboratory protocol requires a robot to identify missing capabilities and determine whether each operation remains valid as the experiment progresses. This letter presents BioAgent, an embodied agent that addresses these coupled challenges of capability sufficiency and experimental validity. It matches human-reviewed requirements to validated skills and task packages, selects tool-based implementations for missing behaviors, and requests human teaching when needed during learning. Learned skills undergo sequential task-package validation to check outcomes and compatibility between successive operations. During execution, precondition, outcome, and experimental-state checks govern progression, autonomous recovery, or termination. Execution evidence guides tool selection, while accepted experience supports offline policy updates and task packaging. On the second task, BioAgent reuses 17 skill types unchanged, revises two existing implementations, and acquires five new types. On two dual-arm laboratory tasks with 20 and 31 ordered skill invocations, BioAgent achieves complete-task success rates of 66\% and 58\% with autonomous recovery over 50 runs per task. Across 25 atomic skills evaluated over 50 autonomous trials each with recovery disabled, success rates range from 84\% to 100\%, with 17 skills achieving 50/50.

llm.title_ja: BioAgent: 長期的実験プロトコルに向けた自己主導型スキル獲得と能力拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のレビュー済み要件と検証済みスキルをマッチングさせ、欠損している機能を自動で補いながら長期的な実験プロトコルを遂行する具現化エージェントBioAgentを提案した。
llm.problem: 不慣れな実験プロトコルの実行において、ロボットは不足している能力を特定し、実験の進行に伴い各操作が有効であるかを判断する必要がある。
llm.method: 人間がレビューした要件を検証済みスキルにマッチさせ、欠損行動に対するツールベースの実装選択、順次タスクパッケージ検証、自動回復機能を統合した。
llm.result: 2つの双腕実験室タスクにおいて、50回の実行にわたり自動回復を伴う完全タスク成功率58%〜66%を達成し、新しいスキルの獲得と再利用に成功した。

2610.41383.tldr_en: BioAgent is presented, an embodied agent that addresses the coupled challenges of capability sufficiency and experimental validity and matches human-reviewed requirements to validated skills and task packages, selects tool-based implementations for missing behaviors, and requests human teaching when needed during learning.

2610.41377.title: MolmoSpaces-CommonSense: Evaluating Commonsense in Robotic Manipulation Policies
2610.41377.abstract: Real-world robotic manipulation requires reasoning about cluttered scenes, partially observable or hidden objects, and semantically appropriate actions, in addition to low-level execution within those scenes. However, existing simulation benchmarks primarily test the latter and remain dominated by comparatively clean environments with limited clutter and narrowly scoped task structure, leaving many forms of commonsense reasoning untested. We address this by introducing a taxonomy of reasoning processes for robotic manipulation grounded in developmental cognitive science. We operationalize this taxonomy through a new benchmark of robot tasks, MolmoSpaces-CommonSense, that requires reasoning about occlusion, containment, support relations, semantically correct grasp points, spatial affordances, and hidden objects. These evaluations require policies not only to recognize relevant scene structure but also to execute correct actions in them. We evaluate several zero-shot generalist manipulation policies. Across model types and architectures, we observe consistent failures in commonsense reasoning: success rates in cluttered scenes drop by over 50% as distractors increase, policies act on incorrect objects in cluttered settings 30% of the time, and affordance-sensitive grasping remains unreliable even with highly specific language prompts, with correct object part selection happening only about 50% of the time. Further, VLM-based success estimation struggles to reliably evaluate rollouts in these settings, suggesting that the challenge extends beyond control to the broader perception-reasoning-action stack. Our results suggest that existing benchmarks may substantially overestimate zero-shot real-world readiness. Code and policy leaderboard link at https://github.com/allenai/molmospaces.

llm.title_ja: MolmoSpaces-CommonSense: ロボットマニピュレーションポリシーにおける常識推論の評価
llm.tldr_ja: 遮蔽、包含、支持関係、意味的に正しい把持点などの常識推論を評価するための新しいロボットタスクベンチマークMolmoSpaces-CommonSenseを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のシミュレーションベンチマークは主に低レベルの実行をテストするものであり、現実世界の複雑な環境に必要な多くの形式の常識推論が未検証のままである。
llm.method: 発達認知科学に基づくロボットマニピュレーションの推論プロセスの分類群を構築し、遮蔽や空間アフォードなどを必要とするタスクのベンチマークとして運用化した。
llm.result: ゼロショット汎用マニピュレーションポリシーの評価により、散らかりが増すと成功率が50%以上低下するなど、既存ベンチマークがゼロショットでの実世界適性を過大評価していることを示した。

2610.41377.tldr_en: This work introduces a taxonomy of reasoning processes for robotic manipulation grounded in developmental cognitive science and operationalizes this taxonomy through a new benchmark of robot tasks, MolmoSpaces-CommonSense, that requires reasoning about occlusion, containment, support relations, semantically correct grasp points, spatial affordances, and hidden objects.

2610.40646.title: SwapBot: Tool-Centric Robot Manipulation via Interchangeable End-Effectors and Tactile Sensing
2610.40646.abstract: Robot manipulation in everyday environments inherently involves substantial tool usage. Seemingly simple household tasks, such as cooking pan-fried tofu, require forceful cutting, delicate brushing, and precise placement using different tools under contact-rich interaction. Thus, the ability to autonomously swap and use task-appropriate tools is important for tool-centric manipulation. We introduce SwapBot, a modular, tool-centric end effector system featuring low-cost adapters that quickly convert common household tools into robot end effectors. Rather than pursuing a single universal gripper, SwapBot adopts a unified design principle that combines a fixed robot-side coupling interface with low-cost, tool-side adapters, enabling compatibility with diverse tools, including articulated ones, and multiple robot platforms. Each adapter integrates compact tactile sensors, supports fast autonomous swapping, and interfaces with an intuitive teleoperation system for efficient demonstration collection. User studies show that, during teleoperation, SwapBot reduces task completion time and operator workload. Using collected demonstrations on the robot, we train imitation learning policies to successfully perform tool-centric tasks like cooking tofu, stirring salad, flipping meat. Our ablation study shows that using tactile-augmented demonstrations improves policy performance across contact-rich skills, increasing success rates by 15 to 25 percentage points over RGB-only policies. These results highlight modular, tactile-equipped tools as a practical and extensible pathway toward robust and capable robot manipulation. Project website https://personalrobotics.github.io/SwapBot.
2610.40646.tldr_en: The ablation study shows that using tactile-augmented demonstrations improves policy performance across contact-rich skills, increasing success rates by 15 to 25 percentage points over RGB-only policies, highlighting modular, tactile-equipped tools as a practical and extensible pathway toward robust and capable robot manipulation.

llm.title_ja: SwapBot: 交換可能なエンドエフェクターと触覚センシングを用いたツール中心のロボットマニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 触覚情報を付加したデモンストレーションを用いることで、RGB画像のみを用いた方針と比較して接触を伴うスキルにおけるポリシーの性能が向上し、成功率が15〜25パーセントポイント向上することがアブレーションスタディにより示され、モジュール式の触覚搭載型ツールが頑健で高性能なロボットマニピュレーションに向けた実用的かつ拡張可能なアプローチであることが強調されている。
llm.problem: 日常環境でのマニピュレーションには、接触を伴う様々なツールの自律的な交換と使用が不可欠であるが、従来は困難であった。
llm.method: 固定されたロボット側インターフェースと、コンパクトな触覚センサーや高速交換機能を備えた低コストなツール側アダプターを組み合わせた、モジュール式のSwapBotシステムを提案する。
llm.result: 実機実験において、SwapBotはタスク完了時間と作業者の負担を軽減し、触覚を組み合わせることでRGB画像のみの場合と比べて成功率が15〜25%向上した。

2610.40632.title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors
2610.40632.abstract: As robots and intelligent systems increasingly interact with humans, they must anticipate long sequences of future actions from only brief observations. While purely neural models typically require extensive observations to predict future actions and remain difficult to interpret and adjust, symbolic priors offer a structured alternative. To this end, we introduce SymAnt, a novel neuro-symbolic approach that unifies the expressiveness of neural networks with the structured reasoning of scene and knowledge graphs. Given a short video, SymAnt performs a joint-search over both graphs to construct a symbolic context, enabling unified reasoning over spatial relationships, object attributes, affordances, and associated actions. This symbolic context serves as a prior for an iterative refinement process that progressively generates and improves the sequence of future actions. By grounding predictions in symbolic context, SymAnt anticipates long-horizon actions from short observation windows in a parameter-efficient manner, while enabling users to directly edit the underlying knowledge to adjust predictions without further training. Through our experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of SymAnt, particularly when only short observation contexts are available, across five diverse datasets: Breakfast, 50 Salads, EPIC-KITCHENS, EGTEA Gaze+, and Assembly101.
2610.40632.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 18 pages (8-page main paper, references, and supplementary appendix), 6 figures, 9 tables. Project page: https://aryanmangal769.github.io/symant/
2610.40632.tldr_en: SymAnt is introduced, a novel neuro-symbolic approach that unifies the expressiveness of neural networks with the structured reasoning of scene and knowledge graphs, enabling unified reasoning over spatial relationships, object attributes, affordances, and associated actions.

llm.title_ja: SymAnt: 適応可能なシンボリック事前知識を用いた長期行動予測のグラウンディング
llm.tldr_ja: SymAntは、ニューラルネットワークの表現力とシーンおよび知識グラフの構造化された推論を統合する新しい神経記号アプローチとして導入され、空間関係、オブジェクトの属性、アフォーダンス、関連する行動にわたる統合された推論を可能にする。
llm.problem: 純粋なニューラルモデルは未来の行動を予測するために多くの観測を必要とし、解釈や調整が困難である。
llm.method: シーングラフと知識グラフを統合した神経記号アプローチ（SymAnt）を用い、空間関係やアフォーダンスに関する記号的コンテキストを事前知識として未来の行動列を反復的に洗練する。
llm.result: 5つの多様なデータセットにおいて、わずかな観測コンテキストからでも長期的な行動を高精度かつパラメータ効率良く予測できることを示した。

2610.40600.title: A Conveyor Belt Mechanism for Repositionable Magnetic Coupling Between Continuum Robots
2610.40600.abstract: This work proposes a novel conveyor belt mechanism enabling continuous, active repositioning of functional elements along the body of a tendon-driven continuum robot. Up to three conveyor belt mechanisms are integrated within a 9 mm diameter continuum robot. We demonstrate equivalent or reduced conveyor belt actuation forces compared to robot tendon actuation forces. As a case study, we mount permanent magnets along two conveyor belts, and demonstrate actively reconfigurable inter-robot coupling. Coupling point location and quantity can be adjusted during robot operation to actively tune the effective stiffness of the coupled multi-robot system. We show that effective stiffness follows a predictable inverse-cubic relationship with coupling location, and increases with the number of coupling points. These findings demonstrate that the conveyor belt mechanism enables active functional element repositioning for changing tasks requirements, with magnetic inter-robot coupling as one proof-of-concept.

llm.title_ja: 連続可動型磁気結合のためのコンベルト機構：連続体ロボット間における適用
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: テンディリブン連続体ロボットの本体に沿って機能要素を連続的かつアクティブに再配置することが困難である。
llm.method: 直径9mmの連続体ロボット内に最大3つのコンベルト機構を統合し、永久磁石を搭載することでロボット間の磁気結合を動的に再構成する。
llm.result: コンベルトの駆動力はロボットの腱駆動と同等以下であり、結合位置と数によって有効剛性を予測可能かつアクティブに調整できることを示した。

2610.40565.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
2610.40565.abstract: Realistic, fast robotics simulations could enable large-scale training of embodied AI models that transfer to the real world. However, despite decades of progress, available simulations cover only a narrow range of real-world tasks and physical phenomena. The core bottleneck is that creating better simulations requires significant expert effort and therefore does not scale. To address this, we introduce Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations. Our core insight is that simulation creation is a coding agent task, so improvements in coding agents translate directly into richer and more faithful simulations. We select simulations based on U.S. GDP data to cover economically valuable physical work, define what makes a good simulation and a good task, and develop an adversarial creation-audit loop that checks each simulation and task against these definitions. Using this pipeline, we build RoboWorld, a set of 25 simulations with 25 test and 175 training RL environments of varying difficulty. Even the best frontier models fail on every RoboWorld test task, achieving an average reward of only 0.06. Building on RoboWorld, we introduce several new ways for frontier models to improve, including in-context learning across repeated attempts, a privileged teacher that reads the simulator state and teaches a student in context, self-assisted learning from the model's own privileged experience, and code policies that generate demonstrations across varied scenes to train vision-language-action models (VLAs) such as $π_{0.5}$. Each of these substantially improves performance. We release our pipeline, RL environments, and benchmark to facilitate future research. Code and data are available at https://gym-anything.github.io/robotics
2610.40565.tldr_en: Gym-Anything for Robotics is introduced, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations and introduces several new ways for frontier models to improve, including in-context learning across repeated attempts, a privileged teacher that reads the simulator state and teaches a student in context, and self-assisted learning from the model's own privileged experience.

llm.title_ja: ロボットのためのGym-Anything: デジタルエージェントによる物理シミュレーションのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: Gym-Anything for Roboticsは、コーディングエージェントが現実的なロボットシミュレーションを作成するフレームワークとして導入され、フロンティアモデルが試行を通じた文脈内学習、シミュレータ状態を読み取る特権教師、自己支援学習などによって改善するためのいくつかの新しい方法を導入している。
llm.problem: 優れたシミュレーションの作成には多大な専門的努力が必要であり、多様な実世界のタスクへスケールしない。
llm.method: コーディングエージェントが経済的に価値のある物理的作業に基づくシミュレーションを自律生成し、敵対的な作成・監査ループで検証する「Gym-Anything for Robotics」を構築する。
llm.result: 25のシミュレーションと多数のRL環境（RoboWorld）を構築し、フロンティアモデルの文脈内学習やVLAモデル（$\pi_{0.5}$）の学習用デモンストレーション生成において性能の大幅な向上を確認した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション
コーディングエージェント

2610.40559.title: A Tutorial on Shape Servoing of Deformable Objects-Part I: Fundamentals
2610.40559.abstract: In robotics, shape control (or shape servoing) refers to the automatic manipulation of a deformable object to achieve a desired shape. It involves a feedback loop that exploits the relation between robot motion and changes in the measured shape. This relation, known as the interaction Jacobian or, in this context, the deformation Jacobian, depends on the object's mechanical properties, geometry, and boundary conditions (e.g., where the object is grasped). Because these factors are often difficult to model accurately, the deformation Jacobian can be estimated locally from observed shape changes produced by commanded robot motions, without requiring a fine-tuned mechanical model. This article is the first of a two-part tutorial on data-driven Jacobian-based shape control of deformable objects. It introduces the central elements of the approach: the formulation of the shape-control problem, shape representation, estimation and online update of the deformation Jacobian, and a standard control law from the literature. It then assembles these elements into a complete shape-servoing loop, derives a local stability condition for this loop, and illustrates why some target shapes cannot be reached. Part II covers more advanced topics. Throughout both parts, a simulated planar example in which two robot arms manipulate an elastic rod observed by a camera illustrates the concepts.
2610.40559.comment: Part I of a two-part tutorial. 9 pages, 5 figures. Code: https://github.com/nachocz/tutorial_on_shape_servoing_of_deformable_objects. Interactive demos: https://nachocz.github.io/tutorial_on_shape_servoing_of_deformable_objects/
2610.40559.tldr_en: This article introduces the central elements of the approach: the formulation of the shape-control problem, shape representation, estimation and online update of the deformation Jacobian, and a standard control law from the literature, and assembles these elements into a complete shape-servoing loop, derives a local stability condition for this loop, and illustrates why some target shapes cannot be reached.

llm.title_ja: 変形可能な物体のシェイプサーボイングに関するチュートリアル - パート1：基礎
llm.tldr_ja: 本論文では、形状制御問題の定式化、形状表現、変形ヤコビアンの推定とオンライン更新、および文献からの標準的な制御則というアプローチの中心的な要素を導入し、これらを完全なシェイプサーボイングのループに組み立て、このループの局所安定性条件を導出し、一部の目標形状に到達できない理由を説明している。
llm.problem: 変形可能な物体の機械的特性や境界条件はモデル化が難しいため、正確な形状制御が困難である。
llm.method: ファインチューニングされた機械モデルを必要とせず、ロボットの動作によって観測された形状の変化から変形ヤコビアンを局所的に推定するデータ駆動型アプローチを用いる。
llm.result: 完全なシェイプサーボイングのループを構築し、局所安定性条件の導出と、到達不可能な目標形状の理由をシミュレーションの例を通じて示した。
keywords_ja: シェイプサーボイング

2610.40539.title: PhysVLMM: Interaction-Conditioned Physical Belief Maps for Articulated Objects in Robot Scene Maps
2610.40539.abstract: Mobile robots must open doors and drawers, yet their scene maps record what each object is and whether it has moved, not how it will respond to a pull. This paper proposes PhysVLMM, a method that maintains a physical belief for every articulated part of a Vision-Language-Motion Map and answers a planner's queries about it, with two algorithms: a map update and a query. Watching a part move provably cannot identify its dynamics, and a measured pull identifies only the pulled part, up to one direction. PhysVLMM therefore (i) keeps that direction as a posterior instead of a point estimate, (ii) passes the evidence of each pull in closed form to the untouched look-alike parts of the map, and (iii) answers whether an action will succeed at a stated risk, or abstains. On real doors and drawers in 18 homes, it identifies the joint type in 86% of held-out pulls (48% for a learned single-view method) and predicts the response to a pull with 41% lower error than differentiable simulation (CRPS 0.323 vs. 0.544), four orders of magnitude faster (13 ms vs. 230 s per case). The posterior lowers the final-position error from 0.460 to 0.270, sharing lowers the force error of untouched parts from 56% to 42%, and at every stated risk from 0.02 to 0.30 the false-safe answers stay within it. Pooling all measured parts of a home does as well as the look-alike groups, and simpler variants predict where a pulled part stops at least as well.
2610.40539.tldr_en: PhysVLMM is a method that maintains a physical belief for every articulated part of a Vision-Language-Motion Map and answers a planner's queries about it, with two algorithms: a map update and a query.

llm.title_ja: PhysVLMM: ロボットシーンマップにおける関節オブジェクトのための相互作用条件付き物理信念マップ
llm.tldr_ja: PhysVLMMは、ビジョン・言語・モーションマップのすべての関節部分に対して物理的信念を維持し、プランナーからのクエリにマップの更新とクエリという2つのアルゴリズムで答える手法である。
llm.problem: モバイルロボットは把手や扉を開ける必要があるが、従来のシーンマップはオブジェクトの種類や移動履歴を記録するだけで、外力を加えた際の応答を予測できない。
llm.method: ビジョン・言語・モーションマップ内の各関節パーツに対して、物理的信念（事後確率としての関節方向など）を維持し、マップ更新とクエリを行う2つのアルゴリズム（PhysVLMM）を提案する。
llm.result: 18件の実際の家庭環境において、関節タイプの識別精度が86%に達し、差分シミュレーションと比較して予測誤差を41%低減しつつ、4桁高速な処理を実現した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2610.40537.title: DAWN: Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network
2610.40537.abstract: We present DAWN (Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network), a hierarchical robotic framework designed to perform real-world, unfastening tasks through multi-modal sensory integration. Autonomous robotic unfastening is crucial for improving recycling processes, enhancing safety, and reducing operational costs; yet, it remains predominantly manual due to inherent challenges in precise screwdriver engagement with fasteners, detailed force execution, and robustness to environmental variability. To address the complexity of learning long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation tasks, we subdivide the unfastening task procedure into two sequential stages: (1) alignment & insertion, and (2) unfastening. DAWN consists of three key components: AlignNet, a diffusion-based policy ensuring precise screwdriver tip engagement; LatchNet, a multi-modal classifier reliably detecting successful stage transitions; and UnfastNet, which achieves stable, force-controlled screw removal. Experimental validation on a Franka Emika robot demonstrates that DAWN achieves alignment & insertion success rates comparable to trained human operators, robustly transitions between stages, and attains an impressive success rate in unfastening across various unseen scenarios. Ablation studies further elucidate critical input modalities and effective training strategies, highlighting DAWN's scalability, robustness, and data efficiency.
2610.40537.tldr_en: DAWN (Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network) is presented, a hierarchical robotic framework designed to perform real-world, unfastening tasks through multi-modal sensory integration that achieves scalability, robustness, and data efficiency.

llm.title_ja: DAWN: 拡散ベースの位置合わせおよび取り外しワークフローネットワーク
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダル感覚統合を通じて現実世界でのスクリュー取り外し作業を行う階層型ロボットフレームワークDAWNを提案した。
llm.problem: 自律的なねじの取り外しはリサイクルなどに不可欠であるが、正確なドライバーの係合や詳細な力制御、環境変動への頑健性の課題から手動に依存している。
llm.method: 位置合わせと挿入を行う「AlignNet」、段階遷移を検出する「LatchNet」、力制御によるねじ外しを行う「UnfastNet」の3つのコンポーネントからなる階層型フレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: Franka Emikaロボットを用いた実験で、人間のオペレーターと同等の位置合わせ成功率を達成し、様々な未見のシナリオで高い取り外し成功率を記録した。

2610.40532.title: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing
2610.40532.abstract: How effectively can vision-language-action (VLA) models learn diverse language-conditioned behaviors as training data scales? Investigating this question requires large and varied robot datasets, whose collection on physical robots remains costly. We introduce BURGER, a language-conditioned robotic drawing benchmark with a scalable, prompt-driven pipeline for generating continuous drawing trajectories, both in simulation and the real world. In BURGER, an agent starts from the same blank canvas and controls a robot arm to draw the object or spatial composition specified by language, while each instruction allows an open-ended variety of valid drawings and stroke orders. Using 28,200 simulated demonstrations spanning 282 drawing tasks, we evaluate five representative VLA models across data scales, language grounding, and multimodal behavior. BURGER supports fine-grained analysis of language grounding, spatial composition, and action generation, revealing distinct failure patterns across VLA models. Our experiments suggest that some VLA models can benefit from greater task diversity and demonstration scale, capture multimodal drawing behaviors, and generalize to unseen compositions of familiar objects. Finally, we deploy a trained policy on a Franka Panda arm, demonstrating the ability to draw reactively under human intervention. Project homepage and code can be found at https://siyingzhao.github.io/BURGER/.
2610.40532.tldr_en: BURGER is introduced, a language-conditioned robotic drawing benchmark with a scalable, prompt-driven pipeline for generating continuous drawing trajectories, both in simulation and the real world, revealing distinct failure patterns across VLA models.

llm.title_ja: BURGER: 具現化描画を通じたロボット汎化性能のベンチマークと理解
llm.tldr_ja: 連続的な描画軌道を生成するためのスケーラブルなプロンプト駆動型パイプラインを備えた、言語条件付きロボット描画ベンチマークBURGERを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルがデータスケールに伴い多様な言語条件付き挙動をどの程度学習できるかを調査するには大規模なロボットデータが必要だが、実機収集には膨大なコストがかかる。
llm.method: シミュレーションと実世界の双方で、連続的な描画軌道を生成するプロンプト駆動型パイプラインを構築し、282の描画タスクにわたる28,200件のシミュレーションデモンストレーションで評価した。
llm.result: VLAモデルの異なる失敗パターンを明らかにし、一部のモデルがタスクの多様性やデモンストレーションの規模から恩恵を受け、未見の構成へ汎化できることを示した。

2610.40525.title: CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment
2610.40525.abstract: Cross-modal scene and instance retrieval aims to retrieve a corresponding 3D environment or object given query 2D images, serving as a foundational mechanism for spatial reasoning in robotics and AR/VR. Existing methods achieve this by learning alignment only at the level of whole scenes or objects, which provides no supervision for the fine-grained local structure within them. In this work, we show that supervision on a set of sparse 2D-3D correspondences, without scene- or instance-level contrastive objectives, is sufficient to train a single model for both scene- and instance-level retrieval. Specifically, we propose $\textbf{CrossWeave}$, a novel framework for cross-modal retrieval that learns sparse patch-point alignment, which alone outperforms existing methods. An optimal transport-based aggregator over the aligned features gives further gains by clustering structurally redundant regions, freeing descriptor capacity for semantically distinct local features. CrossWeave achieves state-of-the-art performance on both scene- and instance-level retrieval on ScanNet and 3RScan with a $\textit{single model}$, whereas existing methods require separate models for each task. Our results suggest that whole-scene encoding is unnecessary for cross-modal retrieval and that sparse local correspondence supervision is a more effective and flexible alternative.
2610.40525.tldr_en: It is shown that supervision on a set of sparse 2D-3D correspondences, without scene- or instance-level contrastive objectives, is sufficient to train a single model for both scene- and instance-level retrieval, and that whole-scene encoding is unnecessary for cross-modal retrieval and that sparse local correspondence supervision is a more effective and flexible alternative.

llm.title_ja: CrossWeave: スパースな2D-3Dアライメントからのクロスモーダルシーンおよびインスタンス検索
llm.tldr_ja: シーンレベルまたはインスタンスレベルの対照損失なしに、スパースな2D-3D対応のセットに対する教師付けが、シーンレベルとインスタンスレベルの両方の検索を行う単一モデルの訓練に十分であり、シーン全体のエコーディングはクロスモーダル検索にとって不要であり、スパースな局所対応の教師付けがより効果的かつ柔軟な代替手段であることが示されている。
llm.problem: 既存のクロスモーダル検索手法はシーンやオブジェクト全体レベルでのみアライメントを学習するため、細かな局所構造の教師信号が得られない。
llm.method: シーンやオブジェクト全体の対照学習を行わず、スパースなパッチ・ポイント間のアライメントを学習するフレームワーク「CrossWeave」を提案し、最適輸送ベースの集約器を用いる。
llm.result: ScanNetおよび3RScanにおいて、単一のモデルでシーンおよびインスタンスレベルの検索で従来手法を上回るstate-of-the-artの性能を達成した。

2610.40502.title: A Two-Wheeled Quadrotor with All-Clockwise Tilted Rotors for Level-Attitude Surface Locomotnion
2610.40502.abstract: Conventional wheel-equipped quadrotor UAVs must tilt their bodies to generate lateral forces, limiting their ability to maintain a desired attitude during lateral motion. This paper proposes a wheeled quadrotor with all-clockwise tilted rotors that uses surface contact as a constraint to generate propulsion along the contact surface without tilting the vehicle. We analyze feasible forces and system controllability under surface contact and optimize the vehicle design considering different rotor-spin configurations. The optimization results show that a configuration in which all four rotors spin clockwise can generate a larger tangential force than the conventional alternating-spin configuration. This approach enables both aerial and contact-based locomotion without additional rotor-tilting actuators or mechanisms. Simulation results demonstrate both hovering in free space and horizontal locomotion on a floor while maintaining a level attitude.

llm.title_ja: 全時計回りに傾斜したローターを持つ二輪クアッドロータ：水平姿勢での表面移動
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 従来の車輪付きクアッドローターUAVは、側方力を生成するために機体を傾ける必要があり、側方移動中の姿勢維持が制限される。
llm.method: 表面接触を制約として利用し、機体を傾けることなく接触面に沿った推進力を生成するため、すべてのローターが時計回りに傾斜した車輪付きクアッドローターを提案・最適化する。
llm.result: 全ローターを時計回りに回転させる設定が従来の交互回転設定よりも大きな接線力を生成可能であり、機体姿勢を水平に保ったまま空中ホバリングと床面上の水平移動が可能であることをシミュレーションで示した。

2610.40495.title: LucidLyra: Feed-Forward Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction and Joint Understanding via Multi-Task Distillation
2610.40495.abstract: We present LucidLyra, a framework that makes generatively reconstructed 3D scenes directly queryable for semantics and instances in a feed-forward manner from video latents. While generative 3D reconstruction can synthesize virtual environments from a single image, downstream applications in robotics and physical AI require not only visual realism but also access to scene semantics and object identities. Existing 3D understanding approaches, however, require captured multi-view scenes, have limited generalization capabilities, or rely on expensive per-scene processing and optimization. To bridge this gap, our method distills complementary knowledge from a camera-controlled video diffusion model and frozen 2D vision foundation models into a unified model to jointly infer 3D Gaussians encoding geometry, appearance, open-vocabulary semantics, and class-agnostic instance cues. The resulting scenes support novel-view rendering, open-vocabulary segmentation, and object grouping without per-scene optimization, while training requires neither manual 3D annotations nor captured multi-view data. Our method outperforms baselines combining state-of-the-art 3DGS segmentation approaches with generative 3D scene reconstruction on curated synthetic and real-image-conditioned benchmarks, while preserving reconstruction quality. Furthermore, our latent formulation naturally extends to monocular video, reconstructing structured dynamic 3D scenes across time. By turning renderable but unstructured outputs into queryable 3D worlds, LucidLyra enables downstream applications including 3D scene editing, 3D asset mining, and robotic simulation.
2610.40495.tldr_en: LucidLyra is a framework that makes generatively reconstructed 3D scenes directly queryable for semantics and instances in a feed-forward manner from video latents, and enables downstream applications including 3D scene editing, 3D asset mining, and robotic simulation.

llm.title_ja: LucidLyra: マルチタスク蒸留によるフィードフォワード生成型3Dシーン再構成と統合理解
llm.tldr_ja: LucidLyraは、ビデオ潜在変数からフィードフォワード方式で生成的に再構成された3Dシーンをセマンティクスとインスタンスに対して直接クエリ可能にするフレームワークであり、3Dシーン編集、3Dアセットマイニング、ロボットシミュレーションなどの下流アプリケーションを可能にする。
llm.problem: 既存の3D理解手法は、複数視点のシーンキャプチャが必要であったり、汎化性能が制限されたり、シーンごとの高価な最適化に依存している。
llm.method: カメラ制御されたビデオ拡散モデルと凍結された2Dビジョン基盤モデルの知識を単一モデルに蒸留し、幾何学、外観、オープンボキャブラリーセマンティクスなどをエンコードした3Dガウスを推論する。
llm.result: 手動の3Dアノテーションやマルチ視点データを必要とせず、新規視点レンダリングやオープンボキャブラリーセグメンテーションにおいてベースラインを上回る性能を示し、動的シーンにも拡張可能である。
keywords_ja: オープンボキャブラリー

2610.40473.title: Fundamental Limits of Sampling-Based Reachability: Geometry and Flow Distortion
2610.40473.abstract: Sampling-based reachability estimates reachable sets from finitely many simulated trajectory endpoints. Existing guarantees often control missed probability mass or approximation error relative to the convex hull of the reachable set, leaving the geometric error relative to the reachable set incompletely characterized. We study this error as a problem of support estimation under flow distortion. Our assumptions combine a uniform lower bound on the local volume density of the initial set, a lower bound on the sampling density, and a one-sided Lipschitz constant $μ$ for the vector field. These conditions admit initial sets with corners and dynamics that may expand or contract. In the fine-accuracy regime, $\tilde{\mathcal O}\bigl(2^ne^{nμT}(R/r)^n/(ρκ)\bigr)$ independent endpoint samples suffice for Hausdorff accuracy $r$ using the endpoint cloud. Here, $n$ is the state dimension, $T$ is the horizon, $R$ is the volume-equivalent radius, and $ρ$ and $κ$ quantify sampling density and local volume density. For $n\ge2$ and sufficiently small $κ$, a minimax lower bound over all estimators based only on independent endpoints matches these dependencies up to a dimension-dependent factor $2\cdot4^n$ and logarithmic factors, within the stated parameter range and when the state domain accommodates the construction. The exponential burden in dimension, and in the horizon for expanding systems, is therefore intrinsic to this observation model. Planar experiments illustrate the predicted effects of corners and contraction; robot-arm experiments show how empirical accuracy deteriorates with dimension.
2610.40473.comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables. Extended version of the CoRL 2026 paper; submitted to IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control. Code: https://github.com/JeanLew01/reachapprox

llm.title_ja: サンプリングベースの到達可能性の基本限界：幾何学とフロー歪み
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: サンプリングベースの到達可能集合推定において、凸包に対する近似誤差や見逃し確率の保証は議論されてきたが、真の到達可能集合に対する幾何学的な誤差は十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: 初期集合の局所体積密度の下限、サンプリング密度の下限、ベクトル場の片側リップシッツ定数を仮定し、終端点クラウドを用いたハウスドルフ精度に関するサンプル数の十分条件とミニマックス下限を解析する。
llm.result: 高次元やホライゾンに対する指数関数的な負荷がこの観測モデルの本質的な限界であることを示し、平面およびロボットアームの実験で検証した。
llm.limitation: 次元数およびホライゾンに対して指数関数的な計算負荷が増大するという本質的な限界がある

2610.40431.title: Adaptive search with path-constrained mobile sensors using multi-arm bandits
2610.40431.abstract: We study a constrained sequential decision problem for detecting regions of interest from noisy online measurements collected by a team of energy-constrained mobile sensors. The sensor motion is restricted to a precomputed set of feasible paths that satisfy mobility constraints, limited available energy by requiring return to charging stations, and avoidance of known obstacles. We cast the resulting active path selection as a multi-armed bandit problem and propose an iterative search algorithm that adaptively assigns paths using confidence bounds computed from the collected data. We also propose a graph-based method to construct low-cardinality path covers under the team's constraints. We establish finite-time and anytime probabilistic correctness guarantees for the proposed algorithm, derive non-asymptotic upper bounds on the times required to detect all regions of interest and to label all nodes, and show that these bounds match algorithm-independent lower bounds up to constant factors for a broad class of problem instances. Using numerical simulations, we illustrate the behavior of the proposed approach and the effect of path redundancy and team size on search performance.
2610.40431.tldr_en: This work establishes finite-time and anytime probabilistic correctness guarantees for the proposed algorithm, derive non-asymptotic upper bounds on the times required to detect all regions of interest and to label all nodes, and shows that these bounds match algorithm-independent lower bounds up to constant factors for a broad class of problem instances.

llm.title_ja: 多腕バンディットを用いたパス制約付きモバイルセンサーによる適応的探索
llm.tldr_ja: 本提案アルゴリズムの有限時間および常時における確率的正確性の保証が確立され、すべての関心領域の検出と全ノードのラベリングに要する時間に対する非漸近的上界が導出され、これらの上界が幅広い問題インスタンスに対して定数係数を除いてアルゴリズム非依存の下限と一致することが示されている。
llm.problem: エネルギー制約のあるモバイルセンサー群を用いて、ノイズの多いオンライン測定から関心領域を検出する際に、移動制約や充電ステーションへの帰還要件を満たす必要がある。
llm.method: アクティブなパス選択を多腕バンディット問題として定式化し、収集されたデータから計算された信頼区間を用いてパスを適応的に割り当てる反復探索アルゴリズムとグラフベースのパス被覆構築手法を提案する。
llm.result: 数値シミュレーションにより、提案手法の挙動や、パスの冗長性とチームサイズが探索性能に与える影響を示した。

2610.40430.title: Improving Fine-Grained Manipulation through Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design
2610.40430.abstract: Fine-grained manipulation requires a robot policy to follow instructions, remain robust to visual variations, and translate predicted actions into precise robot control. We present Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design (DEED), a framework for adapting a pretrained vision-language-action policy to the five MetaFine tasks through structured demonstration expansion and execution design. DEED generates demonstrations for different instructions from the same initial scene and renders each physical trajectory under different camera positions and lighting conditions while preserving its original states and action targets. A hierarchical sampling strategy balances instructions, trajectories, and visual conditions during supervised adaptation. At deployment, DEED converts predicted action chunks into robot commands using inverse kinematics, gripper mappings selected for each task, and closed-loop replanning. DEED achieves an official Overall score of 85.55%. Fixed-policy evaluations show that performance varies with execution horizon, denoising budget, and gripper mapping.
2610.40430.tldr_en: Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design (DEED), a framework for adapting a pretrained vision-language-action policy to the five MetaFine tasks through structured demonstration expansion and execution design, is presented.

llm.title_ja: デモンストレーション拡張と実行設計を通じた微細マニピュレーションの改善
llm.tldr_ja: 構造化されたデモンストレーション拡張と実行設計により、事前学習済みのVLAポリシーを適応させるフレームワークDEEDを提案した。
llm.problem: 微細なマニピュレーションには、指示に従い、視覚的変動に対して頑健であり、予測されたアクションを正確なロボット制御に変換するポリシーが求められる。
llm.method: 同一の初期シーンから異なる指示に対するデモンストレーションを生成し、カメラ位置や照明条件を変えてレンダリングする構造化デモンストレーション拡張と階層的サンプリングを導入した。
llm.result: MetaFineの5つのタスクにおいて公式総合スコア85.55%を達成し、実行ホライズンやデノイジングバジェットがパフォーマンスに与える影響を示した。

2610.40429.title: Optimal Path Planning with Localization constraints
2610.40429.abstract: This paper studies UAV path planning in areas where GPS signals are not present. Because these drones can easily get lost when they don't have GPS, they must rely on dead reckoning and occasionally pass near cellular towers, which act as landmarks to reset and fix their position. The goal is to find the shortest path from a start to a goal location while keeping the estimation uncertainty within a given bound. To solve this problem, we propose a localization-constrained A* planner that treats uncertainty as a hard constraint during search. The robot state and covariance are propagated using an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), and only paths that satisfy the covariance limit are considered. We also show that the proposed method does not affect heuristic used in A* and remains admissible and consistent, ensuring optimality among all feasible paths. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and PyBullet quadrotor test show that the proposed method finds shorter and more reliable paths compared to RRT* and PRM, while always satisfying the uncertainty constraint.
2610.40429.tldr_en: This paper proposes a localization-constrained A* planner that treats uncertainty as a hard constraint during search and finds shorter and more reliable paths compared to RRT* and PRM, while always satisfying the uncertainty constraint.

llm.title_ja: 測位制約を伴う最適パス計画
llm.tldr_ja: 本論文では、不確実性をハード制約として扱う測位制約付きA*プランナーを提案し、不確実性制約を常に満たしながら、RRT*やPRMと比較してより短く信頼性の高いパスを発見することを示している。
llm.problem: GPSのない環境においてUAVはデッドレコニングに依存し迷いやすいため、セルラー塔などのランドマーク付近を通過して位置をリセットする必要がある。
llm.method: 不確実性をハード制約として扱う測位制約付きA*プランナーを提案し、拡張カルマンフィルター（EKF）で状態と共分散を伝播させつつ、共分散限界を満たすパスのみを探索する。
llm.result: モンテカルロシミュレーションおよびPyBulletによるクアッドローターテストにおいて、RRT*やPRMよりも短く信頼性の高いパスを見つけることを示した。
keywords_ja: 拡張カルマンフィルター

2610.40427.title: socx: GPU-Accelerated Chance-Constrained Stochastic Optimal Control using JAX
2610.40427.abstract: In this article, we present socx, a GPU-accelerated solver for lifted convex reformulations of linear stochastic optimal control under chance constraints, implemented in JAX. We demonstrate that by exploiting the sparse and independent structure of the problem, distributed optimization can reduce it to simpler problems: independent linear-quadratic tracking (LQT) problems and Euclidean projections onto sets. These simpler problems can be solved in parallel and then coupled using the constraints. To validate our solver, we run it on a hover-linearized 3D quadrotor and show a speed-up of up to $98\times$ over MOSEK and up to $2224\times$ over SCS. socx also solves horizons up to $N=1120$, whereas MOSEK runs out of memory at $N=320$. We present ablations to isolate the key components that enable the speed-up.

llm.title_ja: socx: JAXを用いたGPU加速型確率的チャンス制約付き最適制御
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 線形確率的最適制御におけるチャンス制約付き問題の求解には高い計算コストがかかり、大規模なホライゾンでメモリ不足に陥る。
llm.method: JAXを用いて実装された、リフトされた凸再定式化のためのGPU加速型ソルバー「socx」を提案し、問題のスパース性と独立した構造を活用して分散最適化により効率的に解く。
llm.result: ホバリング線形化3Dクアッドローターにおいて、MOSEKと比較して最大98倍、SCSと比較して最大2224倍の高速化を達成し、長大なホライゾン（N=1120）の求解に成功した。

2610.40401.title: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors
2610.40401.abstract: We introduce Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework for learning cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors that support robot action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies. At its core is a shared latent function space that captures the spatial and temporal structure of robot actions. We learn this space through two stages. First, function pretraining brings trajectories from different embodiments and sampling frequencies into a common representation, learning shared dynamics priors through action reconstruction and consistency across temporal sampling views. By accommodating heterogeneous robot trajectories, this stage broadens the range of data sources available for pretraining and facilitates scaling to larger and more diverse datasets. Second, we connect the pretrained function space to a world-model backbone, enabling observations, language instructions, and the current robot state to condition the prediction of a latent action function. A single decoder takes any query time and returns the corresponding end-effector action. By separating shared dynamics priors from task-conditioned action selection and temporal sampling, our approach provides a unified foundation for transferring robot experience across embodiments and control frequencies.
2610.40401.tldr_en: This work introduces Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework for learning cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors that support robot action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies and provides a unified foundation for transferring robot experience across embodiments and control frequencies.

llm.title_ja: 連続行動ワールドモデル：クロスエンボディメント時空間ダイナミクス事前知識の学習
llm.tldr_ja: この研究では、異なるエンボディメントや実行周波数にわたるロボットの行動生成をサポートするクロスエンボディメント時空間ダイナミクス事前知識を学習するためのフレームワークである連続行動ワールドモデル（CoAWM）を導入し、ロボットの経験を異なるエンボディメントや制御周波数間で転移するための統一された基盤を提供する。
llm.problem: 異なるエンボディメントやサンプリング周波数を持つ多様なロボットデータを統合して行動生成モデルを学習することが困難である。
llm.method: ロボット行動の時空間構造を捉える共有潜在関数空間を構築し、異なるエンボディメントの軌跡を用いた事前学習と、ワールドモデルバックボーンへの接続を行うフレームワーク「CoAWM」を提案する。
llm.result: 多様なデータソースからの事前学習を可能にし、タスク条件付き行動選択と時空間サンプリングを分離することで、クロスエンボディメントなロボット経験の転移を実現した。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント

2610.40396.title: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs
2610.40396.abstract: Despite growing capabilities, LLMs remain susceptible to prompt injections: malicious inputs that can manipulate or hijack models. In particular, it has recently been observed that LLMs can exhibit role confusion (Ye et al., 2026), where models attribute the source of text based on its style instead of its labeled role. Malicious text in tool outputs (for instance, a malicious webpage accessed by an agent) can leverage role confusion to impersonate the user, an attack we call role spoofing}. In this work, we seek to understand and mitigate role spoofing. We study how models track "who said what" in a conversation, showing that they use cues from both content (e.g., semantics and writing style) and structure (e.g., control tokens and formatting). We show that LLMs are highly susceptible to role spoofing attacks that combine both fake structure and content. Additionally, in a toy setting, we show that adversarial training which teaches the model to ignore content-based injections does mitigate content-based attacks but leaves the model susceptible to structure-based attacks. This can explain why frontier models, with increased resistance to many injection attacks, can still be susceptible to role spoofing. Finally, we propose a new method for detecting role spoofing using linear probes trained to predict roles in a conversation, and show that it is effective across different settings.
2610.40396.tldr_en: It is shown that LLMs are highly susceptible to role spoofing attacks that combine both fake structure and content, and that adversarial training which teaches the model to ignore content-based injections does mitigate content-based attacks but leaves the model susceptible to structure-based attacks.

llm.title_ja: LLMにおけるロールスプーフィングの理解と軽減
llm.tldr_ja: LLMは、偽の構造とコンテンツを組み合わせたロールスプーフィング攻撃に対して非常に脆弱であり、コンテンツベースのインジェクションを無視するようにモデルに教える敵対的訓練はコンテンツベースの攻撃を軽減するが、構造ベースの攻撃に対してはモデルを脆弱なままにすることが示されている。
llm.problem: LLMはプロンプトインジェクションに対して脆弱であり、特にツール出力中の悪意あるテキストがユーザーになりすます「ロールスプーフィング」の危険性がある。
llm.method: 会話における「誰が何を発言したか」の追跡方法（コンテンツや構造の手がかり）を分析し、敵対的訓練の影響を評価するとともに、会話中の役割を予測する線形プローブを用いた検出手法を提案する。
llm.result: モデルは構造とコンテンツを組み合わせたスプーフィングに弱く、提案する線形プローブによる検出手法が様々な設定で有効であることを示した。
keywords_ja: プロンプトインジェクション
ロールスプーフィング

2610.40385.title: Securing the Robotics Supply Chain
2610.40385.abstract: This paper sets out what a sustained federal research and investment agenda would need to include to close that gap--not within a single budget cycle, but over the decade such an undertaking will realistically require. It identifies where the gap is most pronounced today: in the methods needed to verify and certify components of uncertain origin, in the foundational hardware research that has long been underfunded relative to software, in the physical infrastructure researchers need to test systems at scale, and in the workforce required to build and sustain all of it. Robotics should not be treated merely as a downstream beneficiary of a broader artificial intelligence investment strategy. It constitutes its own supply chain, with its own points of failure, and merits its own sustained federal commitment.
2610.40385.tldr_en: Where the gap is most pronounced today is identified: in the methods needed to verify and certify components of uncertain origin, in the foundational hardware research that has long been underfunded relative to software, in the physical infrastructure researchers need to test systems at scale, and in the workforce required to build and sustain all of it.

llm.title_ja: ロボット工学サプライチェーンの確保
llm.tldr_ja: 今日最もギャップが顕著な場所、すなわち出所不明の部品を検証・認証するために必要な方法、ソフトウェアと比較して長年にわたり資金不足であった基礎的なハードウェア研究、研究者がシステムを大規模にテストするために必要な物理インフラ、そしてそれらのすべてを構築・維持するために必要な労働力が特定されている。
llm.problem: ロボット工学のサプライチェーンにおいて、部品の検証、ハードウェア研究、テストインフラ、人材育成などの分野で大きなギャップが存在している。
llm.method: 単一の予算サイクルではなく、1十年単位にわたる持続的な連邦政府の研究・投資アジェンダを策定し、サプライチェーンの脆弱性に対処する方針を提示する。
llm.result: ロボット工学を単なるAIの下流受益者としてではなく、独自のサプライチェーンを持つ独立した領域として持続的なコミットメントが必要であることを明らかにした。

2610.40373.title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
2610.40373.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
2610.40373.tldr_en: Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons, and Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval.

llm.title_ja: HiFOR: ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのための行動誘導型ワールドグラウンディングを伴う階層型フォーサイト
llm.tldr_ja: 階層型フォーサイト予測は、階層的依存マスク（HDM）を通じて短期的な状態進化、セマンティックなマイルストーン、および最終的な目標状態を共同で予測し、時間的ホライゾンにわたる依存関係を確立し、構造化された潜在ワールドモデルはホライゾン、視点、空間の次元に沿って将来の潜在表現を整理してきめ細かい検索を容易にする。
llm.problem: 既存のVLAモデルは短期的なダイナミクスと長期的な目標を別々にモデル化しがちであり、予測された未来を行動ポリシーに直接組み込む際に現在の行動要件との関連性が十分に考慮されていない。
llm.method: 短期・長期の予測を行う階層的依存マスク、将来の潜在表現を整理する構造化潜在ワールドモデル、およびデノイジング中の行動表現に基づいて関連する将来情報を適応的に取得する行動誘導型因数分解ワールドリトリーバルからなるフレームワーク「HiFOR」を提案する。
llm.result: 2つのシミュレーションベンチマークと6つの実世界ロボットマニピュレーションタスクでの実験により、提案手法の有効性を実証した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2610.40373.hf_summary_en: HiFOR improves robotic manipulation by hierarchically predicting future states and retrieving relevant future information to guide action generation.

2610.40370.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables
2610.40370.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents for personal health read wearable data and recommend, but do not learn about the individual in a way that can be audited or falsified. We present EpiCoach, an agentic system that treats one athlete, a cross-country mountain biker, as the subject of accountable N-of-1 science. Claims about the athlete live in an evidence-gated hypothesis registry: each must issue a probabilistic prediction about a future session before it occurs, and its belief moves only through computed evidence from a logged statistical fit. Predictions come from a mechanistic digital twin inferred from heart rate, GPS and barometric altitude: a lagged heart-rate response model, a fitness-fatigue model with learned time constants, and a latent technical-descending skill state, measured on discovered trail segments. The agent prescribes the next training week as a constrained experiment maximizing information gain subject to load and safety constraints, around two instrument rides. We evaluate the system two ways over eighteen months of data. A rolling-origin replay benchmark shows the twin beats standard forecasters on heart rate but not segment time, and the agentic loop matches a static model. A live prospective phase runs the weekly cycle: in its first three weeks the ledger sealed 20 predictions, scored 14, the descent forecast calibrated after one correction, the climb forecast pessimistic as the athlete improved, and the safety officer vetoed the agent twice. Every correction is preserved in the registry, a template for auditable, falsifiable personalization in digital health. We release the registry, benchmark and protocol.
2610.40370.tldr_en: EpiCoach is presented, an agentic system that treats one athlete, a cross-country mountain biker, as the subject of accountable N-of-1 science, and a template for auditable, falsifiable personalization in digital health is released.

llm.title_ja: 1人の科学者としての競技者: コンシューマー向けウェアラブル機器を用いた個別化生理学のためのエージェント型ベイズ実験デザイン
llm.tldr_ja: ウェアラブルデータから説明可能で反証可能なN-of-1科学の枠組みで個人特有の生理学的予測とトレーニング処方を行うエージェントシステムEpiCoachを提案した。
llm.problem: 個人の健康状態を読み取るLLMエージェントは推奨を行うものの、監査や反証が可能な形で個人について学習する仕組みを持っていない。
llm.method: 心拍数、GPS、気圧高度から推論される機械論的デジタルツインと、エビデンスに基づく仮説レジストリを組み合わせ、情報利得を最大化するトレーニング週間計画を処方するエージェントシステムを構築した。
llm.result: 18ヶ月間にわたるデータ評価やライブでの前向き検証フェーズにおいて、安全オフィサーによる介入や予測のキャリブレーションを通じて、監査可能で反証可能な個別化のテンプレートとしての有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: エージェントシステム

2610.40364.title: Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds
2610.40364.abstract: Unsupervised environment design (UED) methods such as PLR, ACCEL, SFL and PAIRED are compared mostly on 2D mazes, grid worlds and BipedalWalker, while terrain curricula for legged robots are hand-designed and evaluated against a few baselines. We present a benchmark that runs fourteen UED, domain-randomisation and robotics curricula under one protocol on five 3D quadrupeds in MuJoCo MJX: the closed-chain W01-TEK and the open-chain Unitree Go1 and Go2, Google Barkour vB and Boston Dynamics Spot. Levels are vectors of eight interpretable terrain parameters, and all curricula drive the same PPO student at matched environment-step budgets. The evaluation reports success on random and held-out structured terrains, interquartile means with stratified bootstrap intervals, capability envelopes and a level-by-level domination comparison. We compare methods within each robot and report, per level set, the top group of methods not significantly below the best. No method is in the top group on every robot and level set. Methods with easy or low-difficulty training levels, curated or not, fill the top groups on in-distribution random levels of Go1 and Barkour, and of W01-TEK apart from PAIRED+BiBC. The success-driven terrain curriculum from legged-robot practice is in a top group most often, domain randomisation on uniform levels in none, and PAIRED in none outside Spot, where the fourteen methods lie within 3.8 points on random levels of difficulty 0.25. On three robots the leader on in-distribution random levels is not the leader on held-out terrain. We collect the results into a per-robot guide to choosing a curriculum.
2610.40364.comment: 22 pages, 10 figures. Code, level space and evaluation suite: https://github.com/Solvro/ml-wojtek-ued
2610.40364.tldr_en: A benchmark that runs fourteen UED, domain-randomisation and robotics curricula under one protocol on five 3D quadrupeds in MuJoCo MJX is presented and a per-robot guide to choosing a curriculum is collected.

llm.title_ja: カリキュラムか、それとも単なる簡単な開始か？四足歩行ロボットにおける教師なし環境設計のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: MuJoCo MJXを用いて14の教師なし環境設計（UED）・ドメインランダム化・ロボット工学カリキュラムを5種類の3D四足歩行ロボットで統一プロトコルにより評価するベンチマークを提案した。
llm.problem: UED手法は主に2D迷路などで比較され、脚ロボットの地形カリキュラムは手動設計されて少数のベースラインと比較されるに留まっている。
llm.method: MuJoCo MJX上で、閉鎖・開放リンク構造を持つ5種類の3D四足歩行ロボットに対し、同一の環境ステップ予算の下で14のカリキュラムとドメインランダム化手法を適用する統一プロトコルを構築した。
llm.result: すべてのロボットとレベルセットで常にトップグループに入る手法は存在せず、簡単な訓練レベルを持つ手法がインディストリビューションのランダムレベルで優れた性能を示すことなどを明らかにした。

2610.40356.title: JEDI: Joint-Embedding Demonstration Compression for In-Context Imitation Learning
2610.40356.abstract: In-context imitation learning (ICIL) adapts robot policies through test-time demonstrations, but long multimodal trajectories constrain how many examples fit in context. We ask what a compressed demonstration should preserve. We propose JEDI, which compresses demonstrations into latent slots trained to predict the query episode's next-stage keyframe in a frozen video-JEPA space. Task and process counterfactuals help the slots preserve execution details, while the predictor selects demonstrations from a bank. Post-training with keypoint tokens enables human-hand conditioning on robots. Experiments on LIBERO and real robots show that JEDI supports many-shot context; LIBERO objective controls show improved success and demonstration following over action-only compression. These findings support query-future prediction as a training objective for preserving execution-relevant information in compressed demonstrations.
2610.40356.tldr_en: JEDI, which compresses demonstrations into latent slots trained to predict the query episode's next-stage keyframe in a frozen video-JEPA space, supports query-future prediction as a training objective for preserving execution-relevant information in compressed demonstrations.

llm.title_ja: JEDI: 文脈内模倣学習のための結合埋め込みデモンストレーション圧縮
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結されたビデオJEPA空間内で次のステージのキーフレームを予測する潜在スロットにデモンストレーションを圧縮する文脈内模倣学習手法JEDIを提案した。
llm.problem: 文脈内模倣学習（ICIL）はテスト時のデモンストレーションでポリシーを適応させるが、長いマルチモーダル軌道ではコンテキストに収まる例の数が制限される。
llm.method: タスクおよびプロセスの反実仮想を用いて実行詳細を保持する潜在スロットにデモンストレーションを圧縮し、ビデオJEPA空間で予測を行うJEDIを開発した。
llm.result: LIBEROおよび実ロボットの実験において、多数ショットのコンテキストをサポートし、アクション単体の圧縮と比較して成功率とデモンストレーション追従性が向上することを示した。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーション

2610.40349.title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
2610.40349.abstract: Human demonstrations offer an efficient and scalable source of data for dexterous robot manipulation, but differences in sensing and hand morphology complicate the transfer of contact-rich interactions. We present TouchBridge, a hardware--software co-designed framework for human-to-robot data transformation. A wearable human demonstration interface and a corresponding robot interface establish cross-embodiment correspondence in visual and fingertip tactile sensing. We introduce Tac-Retarget, a tactile-conditioned retargeting method that uses measured contact to align fingertip contact patches and preserve their spatial relations within and across hands. Unlike object-aware or simulation-based transfer pipelines, Tac-Retarget requires no object mesh, object-pose estimate, or physics simulation for retargeting, enabling direct and scalable conversion of human demonstrations into robot-domain training data. Combined with visual synthesis and camera-anchored action conversion, TouchBridge produces robot-domain demonstrations for fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model. Across four real-world contact-rich tasks, policies fine-tuned solely on TouchBridge-converted human demonstrations achieve a 72.5% average success rate, compared with 77.5% using an equal number of teleoperated robot demonstrations, while human demonstration collection is 7.0x faster. Under the same policy and training setup, Tac-Retarget outperforms DexPilot and UniDex by 25.0 and 42.5 percentage points, respectively.
2610.40349.tldr_en: This work introduces Tac-Retarget, a tactile-conditioned retargeting method that uses measured contact to align fingertip contact patches and preserve their spatial relations within and across hands.

llm.title_ja: TouchBridge: 巧みなマニピュレーションのための触覚条件付き人間からロボットへのデータ変換
llm.tldr_ja: オブジェクトのメッシュやシミュレーションを使用せず、測定された接触を用いて指先の接触パッチを揃える触覚条件付きリターゲティング手法「Tac-Retarget」を提案した。
llm.problem: 人間のデモンストレーションは器用なロボットマニピュレーションに有用だが、感覚やハンドの形態の違いにより、接触の多い相互作用の転送が複雑になる。
llm.method: 視覚と指先触覚のクロスモーダルな対応関係を確立し、測定された接触情報に基づいて指先の接触パッチの位置関係を合わせるTac-Retarget手法とハードウェア・ソフトウェア協調設計を行った。
llm.result: 4つの実世界の接触を伴うタスクにおいて、TouchBridgeで変換された人間デモンストレーションのみで微調整されたポリシーは平均72.5%の成功率を達成した。

2610.40333.title: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories
2610.40333.abstract: High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. Agentic synthesis and procedural generation are therefore complementary: agents can construct reusable programs, while procedural execution reuses the resulting logic across many samples. We therefore present RFW-A, which combines the two in a new articulated-asset generation paradigm. Starting from existing articulated programs, RFW-A organizes reusable components and their dependencies into category-level generators. Agents test and refine these generators across sampled configurations and motion states. Once constructed and validated, the generators produce diverse assets through procedural execution with no further model calls or token charges. The estimated API cost of generator authoring averages $10.62, amortizing to $0.05 per asset over 200 assets, versus $1.24 for the sampled per-asset agentic synthesis baseline. Using RFW-A, we built RFW-A-400K, containing over 400K sim-ready articulated assets across more than 500 categories. Experiments show high structural and kinematic validity and stable execution across physics simulators. Beyond asset validity, training with RFW-A-400K improves part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, while policies trained in simulation with retrieved and program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.
2610.40333.tldr_en: RFW-A is presented, which combines the two in a new articulated-asset generation paradigm, starting from existing articulated programs and organizes reusable components and their dependencies into category-level generators that produce diverse assets through procedural execution with no further model calls or token charges.

llm.title_ja: RFW-A: 500以上のカテゴリにわたる40万の関節機構アセットのエージェント型手続き的生成
llm.tldr_ja: 既存の関節機構プログラムから再利用可能なコンポーネントを整理し、追加のモデル呼び出しなしで多様なアセットを生成するカテゴリレベルのジェネレータを構築するRFW-Aを提案した。
llm.problem: 具現化知覚やシミュレーションに必要な高品質な関節機構アセットを大規模に構築するには膨大な手動注釈や手続き的モデリングの労力がかかる。
llm.method: 既存の関節機構プログラムをベースに、エージェントがカテゴリレベルのジェネレータをテスト・洗練し、その後の手続き的実行で多様なアセットを生成する仕組みを開発した。
llm.result: 40万以上のシムレディな関節機構アセットを含むRFW-A-400Kを構築し、物理シミュレータでの安定した実行と、部分レベルの関節推論および実世界へのゼロショット転移の向上を示した。

2610.40285.title: MUSBRIC: LEGO-Compatible Pneumatic Muscle Bricks for Reconfigurable Musculoskeletal Robots
2610.40285.abstract: Musculoskeletal robots combine compliant actuators with articulated skeletons, but exploring alternative configurations often requires repeated fabrication. We present MUSBRIC, a modular hardware platform and accompanying MuJoCo-based simulator for reconfigurable musculoskeletal robots. LEGO-compatible endcaps turn fiber-reinforced extensile pneumatic artificial muscles into reusable, plug-and-play muscle bricks that connect directly to standard LEGO components. Experimentally identified actuator behavior supports corresponding musculoskeletal simulations. An elbow-joint prototype validates load-dependent flexion and extension, showing that pulley-guided routing enables reversible motion and a mechanical stop stabilizes the straight posture. A robotic hand demonstrates compliant grasping and multi-joint construction. Matched hardware and simulation sweeps across 15 leg configurations demonstrate systematic exploration of attachment geometry, while a quadruped assembled from four legs demonstrates walking. Together, these demonstrations span mechanism analysis, configuration exploration, and functional robot construction within a single reconfigurable system. The hardware designs and simulation code will be released as open source soon to facilitate reproduction and further development.
2610.40285.comment: 6 figures. Qiyao Wang and Yinglei Zhu contributed equally to this work
2610.40285.tldr_en: MUSBRIC, a modular hardware platform and accompanying MuJoCo-based simulator for reconfigurable musculoskeletal robots, and LEGO-compatible endcaps turn fiber-reinforced extensile pneumatic artificial muscles into reusable, plug-and-play muscle bricks that connect directly to standard LEGO components are presented.

llm.title_ja: MUSBRIC: 再構成可能な筋骨格ロボットのためのLEGO互換空気圧筋肉ブロック
llm.tldr_ja: LEGO互換のエンドキャップにより空気圧人工筋肉を再利用可能なプラグアンドプレイの筋肉ブロックとして接続できる、モジュール式ハードウェアプラットフォームMUSBRICを提案した。
llm.problem: 筋骨格ロボットは柔軟なアクチュエータと骨格を組み合わせるが、代替構成の探索にはしばしば繰り返しの試作が必要となる。
llm.method: 繊維強化拡張型空気圧人工筋肉を標準LEGOコンポーネントに直接接続するLEGO互換エンドキャップを開発し、MuJoCoベースの対応シミュレータと組み合わせた。
llm.result: 肘関節プロトタイプによる屈曲・伸展の検証、ロボットハンドによる把持、4つの脚を組み合わせて歩行する四足歩行ロボットの構築により、機構分析から機能的構築まで実証した。
keywords_ja: 空気圧アクチュエータ
モジュール式ハードウェア

2610.40271.title: Gaussian Distillation of Flow Policies
2610.40271.abstract: Flow policies are among the strongest robot controllers and are well suited to modelling multimodal action distributions. Our analysis shows that the continuous-action distributions of the studied flow policies are well approximated by Gaussians. We propose the Gaussian Action Readout (GAR), which replaces a flow policy's final layer with a Gaussian readout trained on just 0.02% of eligible states, while keeping the rest of the network frozen. It samples with one action-network pass, gives closed-form likelihoods, and achieves near-teacher task success at up to twice the inference speed.
2610.40271.tldr_en: The Gaussian Action Readout (GAR) is proposed, which replaces a flow policy's final layer with a Gaussian readout trained on just 0.02% of eligible states, while keeping the rest of the network frozen.

llm.title_ja: フローポリシーのガウス蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: フローポリシーの最終層をガウス読み出し層に置き換え、ネットワークの残りを固定したままわずかな状態で訓練することで高速な推論を実現するガウスアクション読み出し（GAR）を提案した。
llm.problem: フローポリシーは強力なロボットコントローラーであるが、連続アクション分布の推論において計算コストやモデル構造の最適化が求められる。
llm.method: フローポリシーの連続アクション分布がガウス分布で近似できることに着目し、適格な状態のわずか0.02%で訓練されたガウス読み出し（GAR）で最終層を置換する手法を提案した。
llm.result: 1つのアクションネットワークパスでのサンプリング、閉形式の尤度計算を可能にし、教師モデルに近いタスク成功率を最大2倍の推論速度で達成した。

2610.40257.title: Learned Terminal Costs for Short-Horizon Model Predictive Control of Autonomous Trucks in Interactive Highway Traffic
2610.40257.abstract: Autonomous highway driving for heavy-duty trucks is a challenging control problem. The greater mass, dimensions and intricate dynamics increase the requirements for cooperation from surrounding traffic in critical maneuvers, requiring a careful balance between safety constraints and efficient long-horizon decision making. Model Predictive Control (MPC) provides rigorous constraint satisfaction but relies on terminal cost which can limit its effectiveness at short, computationally affordable horizons. Reinforcement Learning (RL) captures long-term driving behavior but offers no constraint guarantees and tends toward overly conservative policies when trained under sparse collision penalties. In this paper, we propose a hybrid MPC and RL framework for highway driving in autonomous trucks, where a finite-horizon MPC, solved via dynamic programming, uses a pre-trained RL model for terminal cost estimation. We evaluate the framework in a simulation environment with reactive surrounding traffic and compare it against pure MPC with zero terminal cost, rollout with terminal cost estimation using a base policy, and pure RL. Results show that the hybrid approach achieves zero collisions with the lowest cost of any configuration.
2610.40257.tldr_en: This paper proposes a hybrid MPC and RL framework for highway driving in autonomous trucks, where a finite-horizon MPC, solved via dynamic programming, uses a pre-trained RL model for terminal cost estimation.

llm.title_ja: 対話型高速道路交通における自動トラックの短ホライズンモデル予測制御に向けた学習済み終端コスト
llm.tldr_ja: 動的計画法で解かれる有限ホライズンMPCが事前訓練された強化学習モデルを終端コスト推定に利用する、高速道路走行向けのハイブリッドMPCおよびRLフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 大型トラックの自動高速道路走行では、大きな質量や寸法、複雑なダイナミクスに対処するため、安全性制約と効率的な長期的意思決定の慎重なバランスが必要だが、短ホライズンMPCでは終端コストが性能を制限する。
llm.method: 有限ホライズンMPCの終端コスト推定に、事前訓練された強化学習（RL）モデルを組み込んだハイブリッドフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 反応的な周囲交通を持つシミュレーション環境において、ゼロ衝突を達成し、他のどの構成よりも低いコストを実現した。

2610.40248.title: LLM-guided Planar Loco-Manipulation for Quadruped Robots
2610.40248.abstract: Robotic navigation typically assumes a collision-free route to the goal exists; in cluttered environments with movable obstacles, however, reaching the goal may require physical interaction. Classical solutions encode these behaviors through geometric rules and task-specific logic, while learning-based approaches often constrain the decision space to low-dimensional motion commands or predefined action sets. We instead consider a broader decision space, jointly selecting the skill, relevant object, and geometric target. Our language-conditioned task planner, fine-tuned with LoRA on synthetic data, maps natural-language tasks and a structured scene representation to variable-length sequences of parameterized actions, executed by low-level reinforcement-learning policies. The planner learns the geometric relations underlying interactive navigation and outperforms a classical planner and a prompted frontier model on interactive navigation tasks. Comparisons with models trained from scratch indicate that composition does not require pretraining when the representation is structured, whereas pretraining yields more reliable geometric targets. At the low level, we introduce an end-to-end whole-body planar pushing policy that achieves a 93.3% success rate in simulation, versus 83.5% for a hierarchical baseline, while reducing completion time by more than 60%. On hardware, the hierarchy yields the correct skill composition in 44/45 trials and end-to-end success in 34/45. Project website: https://anonymousprojects-dev.github.io/LLM-guided-LocoManipulation-Quadrupeds/
2610.40248.tldr_en: This work introduces an end-to-end whole-body planar pushing policy that achieves a 93.3% success rate in simulation, versus 83.5% for a hierarchical baseline, while reducing completion time by more than 60%.

llm.title_ja: 四足歩行ロボットのためのLLM誘導型平面移動マニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: エンドツーエンドの全身平面押しポリシーを導入し、シミュレーションで93.3%の成功率を達成し、完了時間を60%以上短縮した。
llm.problem: 古典的解法は幾何学的ルールやタスク特異的ロジックに依存し、学習ベースの手法は決定空間を低次元のモーションや事前定義されたアクションに制限する。
llm.method: LoRAでファインチューニングされた言語条件付きタスクプランナーが、自然言語タスクと構造化されたシーン表現をパラメータ化されたアクション列にマッピングし、低レベル強化学習ポリシーで実行する。
llm.result: シミュレーションでベースラインの83.5%を上回る93.3%の成功率を達成し、完了時間を60%以上短縮した。実機では45試行中44試行で正しいスキル構成、34試行でエンドツーエンドの成功を収めた。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション

2610.40210.title: AcrossDEX 1.0: From Human Motion Pretraining to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation across Hand Embodiments
2610.40210.abstract: Bimanual dexterous manipulation requires continuous coordination of wrist motion, finger contact, and object motion. Human videos provide rich manipulation experience. Using this experience for robot control requires aligning human poses with robot commands and accounting for embodiment-specific kinematics and contact dynamics. We present AcrossDEX 1.0, a learning system that connects human motion pretraining, simulation-based expert learning, robot demonstration collection, and visual closed-loop execution. Pretraining on HOT3D Aria predicts one second of bimanual motion from five images and thirty annotated hand states over the preceding second. Robot adaptation preserves the visual encoder, temporal backbone, and wrist parameters. Shared wrist representations, separate finger fields, and validity masks support both six-channel Inspire hands and sixteen-joint Allegro hands. The robot policy predicts sixty control targets from frontal images, command history, and task conditions. It executes a prefix and replans from updated observations. We compare direct regression, diffusion, and flow matching on lid opening and return and closed-lid object reorientation. Direct regression achieves success rates of 40.6\% for opening and return, 100.0\% for Inspire reorientation, and 93.3\% for Allegro reorientation. Flow matching achieves 90.0\% on Allegro reorientation. Paired comparisons further show that constraining replanning with the previous plan improves the continuous execution of generative policies. These results demonstrate a common adaptation pipeline for two hand embodiments and highlight the roles of contact coordination and action-chunk continuity.
2610.40210.tldr_en: AcrossDEX 1.0 is presented, a learning system that connects human motion pretraining, simulation-based expert learning, robot demonstration collection, and visual closed-loop execution and demonstrates a common adaptation pipeline for two hand embodiments.

llm.title_ja: AcrossDEX 1.0：人間のモーション事前学習から多様なハンド形態にわたる両手器用マニピュレーションへ
llm.tldr_ja: AcrossDEX 1.0は、人間のモーション事前学習、シミュレーションベースの専門家学習、ロボット実演収集、ビジュアル閉ループ実行を接続する学習システムである。
llm.problem: 人間の動画は豊富なマニピュレーション経験を提供するが、ロボット制御に利用するには人間のポーズをロボットのコマンドに合わせ、形態固有の運動学と接触ダイナミクスを考慮する必要がある。
llm.method: 人間のモーション事前学習、シミュレーションベースの専門家学習、ロボット実演の収集、ビジュアル閉ループ実行を接続する学習システムを提案し、共有の手首表現と個別の指フィールドを用いる。
llm.result: 直接回帰、拡散モデル、フローマッチングを比較し、Inspireハンドの再方向付けで100.0%、Allegroハンドで93.3%および90.0%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.40207.title: RoboAtom: Large-scale Atomic-Action Supervision for Robot Learning
2610.40207.abstract: Fine-grained action annotations can support skill reuse and compositional generalization in robot policies. However, robot datasets typically provide task-level instructions without subtask annotations. Although some include subtask labels, inconsistent formats and conventions hinder cross-source joint training. We propose RoboAtom-Data, which adds unified, time-aligned atomic-action annotations to existing data from multiple sources, covering 1.45 million trajectories, 6.88 million skill-labeled segments, and 16,882.1 hours. Our pipeline combines a unified protocol, large-scale manual annotation, propagation across repeated executions with the same ordered skill sequence, and multi-stage quality control. We evaluate the dataset through automatic atomic-action annotation and robot control. We construct RoboAtom-Bench to standardize evaluation of skill recognition and temporal boundary localization. Trained on the annotated data, RoboAtom-Anno achieves better automatic annotation performance than all evaluated open- and closed-source models on both RoboAtom-Bench and the external WGO-Bench. For robot control, atomic-action supervision paired with hierarchical execution improves task success over task-level baselines on LIBERO-Long, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin. We will release the data, benchmark, model, and construction pipeline to support further research on skill-level robot learning.
2610.40207.comment: 31 pages, 12 figures, including references and appendices
2610.40207.tldr_en: This work proposes RoboAtom-Data, which adds unified, time-aligned atomic-action annotations to existing data from multiple sources, covering 1.45 million trajectories, 6.88 million skill-labeled segments, and 16,882.1 hours of data, and achieves better automatic annotation performance than all evaluated open- and closed-source models on both RoboAtom-Bench and the external WGO-Bench.

llm.title_ja: RoboAtom：ロボット学習のための大規模アトミックアクション監督
llm.tldr_ja: RoboAtom-Dataは複数のソースからの既存データに統合され時間合わせされたアトミックアクションアノテーションを追加し、自動アノテーション性能で既存モデルを凌駕した。
llm.problem: ロボットデータセットはタスクレベルの指示を提供するがサブタスクのアノテーションが欠けており、形式やルールの不一致がクロスソースの共同トレーニングを妨げている。
llm.method: 複数のソースからの145万の軌跡、688万のセグメント、16882.1時間のデータに対して、統合プロトコル、大規模手動アノテーション、反復実行間での伝播、多段階品質管理を組み合わせたパイプラインを構築する。
llm.result: RoboAtom-Annoは、RoboAtom-BenchおよびWGO-Benchにおいて、評価されたすべてのオープンおよびクローズドソースモデルを上回る自動アノテーション性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: アトミックアクション

2610.40199.title: Decision-Level Error Attribution and Depth-Aware Safety Evaluation of Monocular RGB Human Tracking for Autonomous Robot Navigation
2610.40199.abstract: Monocular RGB tracking is useful for robots operating near people, but perception errors affect binary stop/proceed decisions in ways that geometric accuracy metrics do not capture. We examine how much decision error arises from the safety rule versus perception. We prove that lateral-only distance is a lower bound on planar distance: with accurate positions, it cannot miss dangers identified by the planar rule, but it produces unnecessary stops. We introduce a two-factor Shapley attribution separating rule and perception contributions, and further distinguish missed detections from localization errors. Experiments use ETH and UCY pedestrian videos with simulated stationary robots, disjoint calibration and evaluation pedestrians, and time-block bootstrap intervals. Across 898 pedestrians in three scenes, the lateral rule missed no dangers on annotated positions but achieved only 5.6-31.9% stop precision. In two scenes with RGB perception, calibrated ground-plane localization achieved 0.59 m and 0.51 m planar RMSE, compared with 1.72 m and 1.39 m for a geometric baseline and 0.81 m and 0.68 m for calibrated Depth Anything V2. Detection recall of 0.43 and 0.26 made missed detections the leading source of missed danger. A two-standard-deviation safety margin with ground-plane localization matched or improved on the lateral rule's missed-danger rate in all eight scene-threshold settings and reduced unnecessary stops in seven. All robot interactions are simulated, and outcomes are offline decision classifications, not demonstrations of collision avoidance.
2610.40199.tldr_en: It is proved that lateral-only distance is a lower bound on planar distance: with accurate positions, it cannot miss dangers identified by the planar rule, but it produces unnecessary stops.

llm.title_ja: 自律移動ロボットの単眼RGB人物追跡における決定レベルの誤差帰属と深度を考慮した安全性評価
llm.tldr_ja: 横方向のみの距離が平面距離の下界であることを証明し、正確な位置情報があれば平面ルールで特定される危険を見逃さないが不要な停止を生むことを示した。
llm.problem: 単眼RGB追跡は人間の近くで動作するロボットに有用だが、知覚誤差がバイナリの停止／進行の決定に影響を与える。
llm.method: 2因子のShapley帰属を用いてルールと知覚の貢献を分離し、見逃し検出とローカライゼーション誤差を区別して評価する。
llm.result: 横方向ルールは注釈付き位置上の危険を見逃さないが停止の精度は5.6〜31.9%にとどまり、較正された地面平面ローカライゼーションは良好な平面RMSEを達成した。
llm.limitation: すべてのロボットインタラクションはシミュレーションであり、結果はオフラインの決定分類であって衝突回避の実演ではない。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2610.40109.title: Coupled Guidance for Flow Matching
2610.40109.abstract: Guidance methods are essential tools for steering the generation process in diffusion models, improving the generalizability of stochastic robotic controllers and enabling high-quality controlled image synthesis. Despite strong parallels between flow-matching and diffusion, integrating guidance into flow-matching models remains quite challenging. Recent work has proposed general guidance frameworks for flow-matching, however, they are direct adaptations of diffusion guidance methods and can prove unstable. In this work, we conduct a theoretical analysis of guidance in flow-matching and show that a naive translation of diffusion-based guidance to flow-matching breaks the coupling distribution used during training, resulting in weaker control over sampling accuracy. Building on this insight, we propose Coupled Guidance, a flow-matching-specific guidance mechanism derived from a geometric perspective that leverages the coupling structure inherent to flow-matching training. To validate the effectiveness of our approach, we conduct extensive experimentation on a custom robotic collision avoidance task using ManiSkill3, four robotic dexterous manipulation tasks from the Adroit benchmark, and three image generation tasks, namely inpainting, super-resolution, and deblurring, using the ImageNet-128 and CelebA-HQ-256 datasets.
