Our findings show that our framework improves sample quality and guidance stability across all tasks, without imposing any additional overhead.
2610.40109.tldr_en: Coupled Guidance is proposed, a flow-matching-specific guidance mechanism derived from a geometric perspective that leverages the coupling structure inherent to flow-matching training and improves sample quality and guidance stability across all tasks, without imposing any additional overhead.

llm.title_ja: フローマッチングのための結合ガイダンス
llm.tldr_ja: 結合ガイダンスは、フローマッチングトレーニング固有の結合構造を活用し、追加のオーバーヘッドなしで全タスクのサンプル品質とガイダンスの安定性を向上させる。
llm.problem: フローマッチングへの拡散ベースのガイダンスの単純な翻訳は、トレーニング中に使用される結合分布を破壊し、サンプリング精度の制御を弱める。
llm.method: 幾何学的視点から導出され、フローマッチングトレーニング固有の結合構造を活用する、フローマッチング特有のガイダンスメカニズムである結合ガイダンスを提案する。
llm.result: ManiSkill3のロボット衝突回避タスク、4つの器用なマニピュレーションタスク、および3つの画像生成タスクにおいて、追加のオーバーヘッドなしでサンプル品質とガイダンスの安定性が向上した。

2610.40075.title: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
2610.40075.abstract: Robot foundation models increasingly rely on flow-based action generation for general-purpose manipulation, yet the generated actions are not guaranteed to satisfy physical constraints such as joint limits and collision avoidance. This problem is especially challenging when the feasible set cannot be described analytically and is accessible only through black-box feasibility oracles. We study this practical oracle-only setting and propose an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard for safe flow-matching robot policies. The safeguard uses binary feasibility queries to correct unsafe updates in the forward pass, while extracting local boundary information to provide constraint-aware learning signals in the backward pass. Combined with discrete-time flow matching, the same safeguard is used during training and inference, enabling forward--backward aligned policy learning without explicit or differentiable constraint models. Experiments on obstacle-aware robotic manipulation demonstrate 100% constraint satisfaction while preserving task performance.
2610.40075.tldr_en: This work studies this practical oracle-only setting and proposes an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard for safe flow-matching robot policies, enabling forward--backward aligned policy learning without explicit or differentiable constraint models.

llm.title_ja: バイナリの実行可能性オラクルからの安全なフローマッチングロボットポリシーの学習
llm.tldr_ja: オラクル誘導による微分可能なセーフガードを提案し、明示的または微分可能な制約モデルなしでフォワード・バックワード整列されたポリシー学習を可能にした。
llm.problem: ロボット基盤モデルは行動生成にフローベースの手法に依存し始めているが、生成された行動が関節制限や衝突回避などの物理的制約を満たす保証はない。
llm.method: バイナリの実行可能性クエリを使用して順方向パスの安全でない更新を修正し、逆方向パスで制約を考慮した学習信号を提供する、オラクル誘導型微分可能セーフガードを提案する。
llm.result: 障害物を考慮したロボットマニピュレーションの実験において、タスクパフォーマンスを維持しながら100%の制約満足を実証した。

2610.40056.title: Reinforcement Learning Under Runtime Confounding: Policy Learning and Off-Policy Evaluation
2610.40056.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to train robust, adaptable systems across healthcare, e-commerce, and robotics. In these settings, legal, ethical, or logistical concerns may preclude certain key variables that drive decisions from being collected during deployment time. This gives rise to a setting known as runtime confounding: the logged data hold full observability, but deployment time lacks knowledge of certain variables, known as runtime confounders. Unlike single timepoint and non-adaptive settings, runtime confounding under reinforcement learning has the potential to propagate over time, as earlier decisions affect future states, observations, and action assignments, leading to biased learning. We address these problems with three contributions: we (1) develop policy learning algorithms under runtime-confounding, (2) develop semi-parametric efficient off-policy estimation procedures, and (3) provide diagnostics for understanding the price of runtime confounding.
2610.40056.tldr_en: Policy learning algorithms under runtime-confounding are developed, semi-parametric efficient off-policy estimation procedures are developed, and diagnostics are provided for understanding the price of runtime confounding.

llm.title_ja: 実行時交絡下の強化学習：ポリシー学習とオフポリシー評価
llm.tldr_ja: 実行時交絡下でのポリシー学習アルゴリズムの開発、セミパラメトリック効率的なオフポリシー評価手順の開発、および診断の提供を行った。
llm.problem: 展開時に意思決定を駆動する特定の重要変数を収集できない実行時交絡と呼ばれる状況において、過去の決定が将来の状態や行動割当に影響を与えるため偏った学習が生じる。
llm.method: 実行時交絡下でのポリシー学習アルゴリズムの開発、セミパラメトリック効率的なオフポリシー評価手順の開発、および実行時交絡の代償を理解するための診断の提供を行う。
llm.result: 要旨に記載なし

2610.40050.title: Don't Risk It!: Trajectory-Conditioned Distributional Risk for LiDAR-Only Crowd Navigation
2610.40050.abstract: Efficient crowd navigation requires anticipating dynamic collision-free space without relying on fragile object tracking. We propose the Don't Risk It Planner (DRIP), an end-to-end LiDAR-only planning framework that couples occupancy forecasting with trajectory-conditioned clearance and uncertainty estimation. Operating directly on LiDAR-derived occupancy grid histories, DRIP predicts a distribution over minimum robot-obstacle clearance for candidate control sequences to evaluate collision risk. The model is trained using a risk cost that grounds predictive uncertainty directly in empirical collision outcomes rather than geometric regression alone. In closed-loop experiments with up to 45 pedestrians, DRIP achieves higher success rates with fewer collisions and reduced freezing behavior compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
2610.40050.tldr_en: The Don't Risk It Planner is proposed, an end-to-end LiDAR-only planning framework that couples occupancy forecasting with trajectory-conditioned clearance and uncertainty estimation and achieves higher success rates with fewer collisions and reduced freezing behavior compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

llm.title_ja: リスクを冒すな！：LiDARのみによる群衆ナビゲーションのための軌道条件付き分布リスク
llm.tldr_ja: Don't Risk It Planner (DRIP)は、占有予測と軌道条件付きクリアランスおよび不確実性推定を組み合わせた、LiDARのみのエンドツーエンド計画フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 効率的な群衆ナビゲーションでは、壊れやすい物体追跡に頼ることなく、動的な衝突のない空間を予測する必要がある。
llm.method: LiDAR由来の占有グリッド履歴を直接操作し、候補制御シーケンスに対する最小ロボット・障害物クリアランスの分布を予測して衝突リスクを評価する。
llm.result: 最大45人の歩行者との閉ループ実験において、最先端のベースラインと比較して、より少ない衝突と削減されたフリーズ挙動でより高い成功率を達成した。

2610.40030.title: Cheap Retrieval and Observation Credit Assignment from One Quantity: The Value of Information
2610.40030.abstract: Memory in reinforcement learning raises two problems. Attention finds the relevant item by scoring the whole store, which is costly for robots under latency and energy limits. When a retrieved memory pays off, credit for acquiring it must cross the whole sequence. We argue that both are governed by one quantity, the value of information, and propose to estimate it from archived rollouts with a learned world model. We obtain that, when read at the observation, it yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action, which floors its TD target and attributes this floor to the observation that earned it. Read at the decision, it defines the optimal retrieval set. A pilot retrieval system, to be trained and improved with this signal, solves a memory task with reduced context.
2610.40030.comment: 11 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Memory for Robot Foundation Models (https://corl2026-memory.github.io/)
2610.40030.tldr_en: It is obtained that, when read at the observation, it yields a provable lower bound on the optimal value of the acquiring action, which floors its TD target and attributes this floor to the observation that earned it.

llm.title_ja: 1つの量からの安価な検索と観測信用割当：情報の価値
llm.tldr_ja: 観測時に読み取られた情報は、獲得行動の最適値に対する証明可能な下界をもたらし、TDターゲットの下限を設定してそれを獲得した観測に帰属させる。
llm.problem: 強化学習におけるメモリは、検索コストの高さと、取得したメモリが報酬をもたらした際のシーケンス全体にわたる信用割当という2つの問題を引き起こす。
llm.method: 情報の価値を単一の量として扱い、学習された世界モデルを用いてアーカイブされたロールアウトから推定するアプローチを提案する。
llm.result: メモリタスクをコンテキストを削減して解決するパイロット検索システムが得られた。

2610.40026.title: RoboSeed: Multidimensional Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action and World-Action Models: Capability, Resource Affordability, and Research Evidence
2610.40026.abstract: Choosing a robot action model requires evidence about task capability, adaptation cost, deployment requirements, and the reliability of reported conclusions. Success rates alone offer limited guidance to researchers with different computing budgets and goals. We propose RoboSeed, a multidimensional evaluation framework for vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAM), within a continuing program to train, evaluate, and openly release robot models with verifiable evidence for model selection. The framework defines five dimensions: capability, downstream training affordability, deployment affordability, locally verified research value, and reproduction evidence. It maps empirical measurements and audit criteria to 0-100 profiles using fixed normalization anchors, with balanced, training-constrained, and deployment-constrained preference settings. Interface and protocol checks establish when comparisons are appropriate. Missing measurements remain explicit, incomplete aggregate scores are withheld, and weighted input coverage identifies evidence gaps. We apply the framework to representative VLA and WAM models, drawing on local training, released-weight evaluation, task-level audits, and an evaluation-system study. The results reveal budget-dependent backbone choices, sensitivity to adaptation recipes, and differences between language and visual task interfaces. Reproducible scoring code and machine-readable evidence support extension to additional models. The study provides dimension-level assessments and priorities for further measurement, while incomplete serving traces and heterogeneous protocols preclude overall numerical rankings.
2610.40026.tldr_en: RoboSeed is proposed, a multidimensional evaluation framework for vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAM) within a continuing program to train, evaluate, and openly release robot models with verifiable evidence for model selection.

llm.title_ja: RoboSeed：VLAモデルおよび世界・行動モデルの多次元評価：能力、リソースの経済性、研究のエビデンス
llm.tldr_ja: RoboSeedは、検証可能なエビデンスに基づくモデル選択のための継続的なプログラム内で、VLAおよび世界・行動モデル（WAM）を評価する多次元評価フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 成功率単体では、計算予算や目的が異なる研究者に対して限定的な指針しか提供しない。
llm.method: 能力、下流学習の経済性、展開の経済性、ローカルで検証された研究価値、再現エビデンスの5つの次元を定義し、測定基準を0〜100のプロファイルにマッピングする評価フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 予算に依存するバックボーンの選択、適応レシピに対する感度、言語タスクインターフェースと視覚タスクインターフェースの違いが明らかになった。
llm.limitation: 不完全なサービングトレースと異質なプロトコルにより、全体的な数値ランキングは除外される。

2610.40016.title: LOGIV: Graph-Verified Execution with Causal Local Repair for Long-Horizon Robot Tasks
2610.40016.abstract: Agentic robots must turn a high-level goal into actions while keeping the physical conditions needed for future steps valid. A completed action does not ensure that its effects will persist: a later disturbance can invalidate support that the remaining plan still assumes. We present LOGIV, a graph engineering framework for agentic robot execution that uses an explicit task graph to connect symbolic planning, observation-based verification, and embodied action. LOGIV compiles a validated plan into condition-support and resource-ordering edges, checks their physical validity during execution, and uses dependency tracing to determine what must be restored after a failure. Repair is constrained by retained unfinished actions, and the combined continuation is symbolically validated before execution resumes. The framework operates above existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Model (WAM) policies without adding trainable components. Across 20 dual-arm tasks from RoboTwin~V2 and BiCoord with three execution backbones, LOGIV improves mean task success without injected disturbances by 10.67 and 15.33 percentage points, respectively. Under predefined perturbations, it achieves higher task completion and condition restoration than three adapted recovery baselines for every backbone on both benchmarks. On three real-robot tasks, successful trials increase from 12/30 to 17/30. These results support explicit, continuously checked task dependencies as a practical interface for reliable agentic robot execution.
2610.40016.tldr_en: LOGIV, a graph engineering framework for agentic robot execution that uses an explicit task graph to connect symbolic planning, observation-based verification, and embodied action, improves mean task success without injected disturbances and achieves higher task completion and condition restoration than three adapted recovery baselines for every backbone on both benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: LOGIV：長期ロボットタスクのための因果的ローカル修復を伴うグラフ検証済み実行
llm.tldr_ja: LOGIVは、明示的なタスクグラフを用いてシンボリック計画、観測ベースの検証、具現化された行動を接続するグラフエンジニアリングフレームワークであり、タスク成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: エージェント型ロボットは高レベルの目標を行動に変換する必要があるが、完了した行動はその効果が持続することを保証せず、後の外乱により前提条件が無効になることがある。
llm.method: 検証された計画を条件サポートとリソース順序付けのエッジにコンパイルし、実行中の物理的妥当性をチェックし、依存関係の追跡を使用して失敗後の復旧を決定するグラフエンジニアリングフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: RoboTwin V2とBiCoordの20の二腕タスクにおいて、外乱なしの平均タスク成功率をそれぞれ10.67および15.33パーセントポイント向上させ、実機タスクでも成功試行が増加した。

2610.40003.title: Humanoid Dodgeball: Learning Fast Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance Motions for Humanoids
2610.40003.abstract: Humanoids have become increasingly agile and capable in real-world environments. To operate safely in dynamic scenarios, they must rapidly evade fast-moving obstacles while maintaining stability and physically feasible whole-body motion. Learning such behaviors remains challenging due to the high-dimensional dynamics of humanoid systems and the need to jointly balance reactive obstacle avoidance, motion naturalness, and control robustness. In this work, we present Humanoid Dodgeball, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for agile dynamic obstacle avoidance in humanoids. Our method enables highly dynamic whole-body evasive maneuvers against incoming projectiles through threat-aware reward shaping, while multiple direction-specific adversarial motion priors regularize the learned behaviors toward stable and diverse human-like motions. Extensive simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially improves dynamic obstacle avoidance performance across diverse obstacle speeds and launch distances, while preserving robust and physically plausible humanoid motions.
2610.40003.tldr_en: This work presents Humanoid Dodgeball, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for agile dynamic obstacle avoidance in humanoids that enables highly dynamic whole-body evasive maneuvers against incoming projectiles through threat-aware reward shaping, while multiple direction-specific adversarial motion priors regularize the learned behaviors toward stable and diverse human-like motions.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマノイドドッジボール：ヒューマノイドのための高速動的障害物回避モーションの学習
llm.tldr_ja: ヒューマノイドのための機敏な動的障害物回避のための強化学習フレームワークを提案し、脅威を意識した報酬シェーピングと敵対的モーション事前分布により高動的な全身回避機動を実現した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの複雑な動的環境下での安全な動作には、高次元ダイナミクスを扱いながら、リアクティブな障害物回避、自然なモーション、制御の頑健性を同時に両立させる必要がある。
llm.method: 脅威を意識した報酬シェーピングにより高速な飛来物に対する高動的な全身回避機動を可能にし、複数の方向別敵対的モーション事前分布によって人間らしい安定した多様なモーションへと正則化する強化学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験において、多様な障害物の速度や発射距離に対して動的障害物回避性能が大幅に向上し、頑健で物理的に妥当なヒューマノイドの動きが維持された。

2610.40002.title: How Much Should a VLA Trust Its Reasoning? Step-Level Guidance as a Measured Action-Value Function
2610.40002.abstract: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) policies write a reasoning trace and then decode the action from it. A wrong trace yields a wrong action, and even a correct-looking trace can mislead the plan. Existing remedies ask whether the reasoning is right. We ask how strongly it should steer. CoC-CFG applies classifier-free guidance between the policy's context and the same context without the reasoning span. One weight per Euler step attenuates or amplifies the reasoning, and w=1 recovers the original policy. We treat the choice of this weight as a Markov decision process whose action values are measured, not bootstrapped. With the expert frozen and the noise fixed, applying a weight for one step and finishing the plan under the current controller returns that weight's value exactly. Q-adaptive guidance fits these values with small critics and improves the controller conservatively. In the Alpasim driving simulator it outperforms every fixed weight and online RL (SAC, GRPO) in open loop, and in closed loop it passes 262 of 300 scenes, against 252 for the original policy. On held-out frames of the Waymo end-to-end driving benchmark, its first three stages outperform every fixed weight, four adaptive-guidance methods, SAC and GRPO. On the hidden test set, a frozen Alpamayo 1.5 with rule-based camera and vehicle conversions and Q-adaptive guidance sets a new state of the art among published methods: 8.135159 rater feedback score, against 8.079 for the best published method.
2610.40002.tldr_en: CoC-CFG applies classifier-free guidance between the policy's context and the same context without the reasoning span, and treats the choice of this weight as a Markov decision process whose action values are measured, not bootstrapped.

llm.title_ja: VLAはその推論をどれくらい信じるべきか？：測定された行動価値関数としてのステップレベルガイダンス
llm.tldr_ja: 推論文脈と推論スパンなしの文脈の間で分類子フリーガイダンスを適用し、この重みの選択を、ブートストラップではなく測定された行動価値を持つマルコフ決定過程として扱う。
llm.problem: 推論を行う視覚言語行動（VLA）ポリシーは誤った推論トレースから誤った行動を導くことがあり、正しいように見えるトレースでも計画を誤導する可能性がある。
llm.method: 文脈間の分類子フリーガイダンスを適用し、オイラー・ステップごとに1つの重みで推論を減衰または増幅させ、重みの選択を測定された行動価値を持つマルコフ決定過程として扱うQ-adaptive guidanceを提案する。
llm.result: Alpasimドライビングシミュレータの閉ループテストで300シーン中262シーンを通過し、Waymoエンドツーエンド運転ベンチマークの隠しテストセットで公開手法中最高となる8.135159の評価者フィードバックを達成した。
keywords_ja: 分類子フリーガイダンス

2610.39998.title: Gaze-Assisted Supervisory Control for Lunar Robotic Arm Teleoperation Under Concurrent Monitoring
2610.39998.abstract: Rover-mounted robotic arms can extend human reach during lunar sample handling, but continuous joystick teleoperation requires repeated visual-motor alignment while operators may also need to monitor system states. This paper presents a gaze-assisted supervisory control framework in which gaze nominates a rock or placement target, explicit confirmation authorizes the action, and the robot performs bounded autonomous grasp-and-place execution. The framework was evaluated against manual joystick teleoperation in a mission-analog virtual reality study with 16 participants. The study used a 2 x 2 x 3 within-subject design varying control mode, placement difficulty, and concurrent monitoring load. Mean recorded task completion time decreased from 47.65 to 18.43 s per rock, with 72.5% of this difference arising during grasping. Under the tested auditory monitoring conditions, gaze-assisted supervisory control showed less average proportional slowing, with no detected control-mode difference in monitoring-response accuracy or speed. The rate of gaze shifts between core areas of interest decreased from 49.98 to 27.73 shifts/min, while the raw NASA Task Load Index score decreased from 32.54 to 18.26. However, the benefit was task dependent. In precision placement, manual control yielded lower mean placement error and a higher placement success rate. These findings support a mixed-initiative allocation in which gaze enables rapid task-level intention specification and autonomous execution, while precision-critical stages retain manual refinement.

llm.title_ja: 月面ロボットアーム遠隔操作のための同時モニタリング下における視線支援型監視制御
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 月面サンプル処理のためのジョイスティック遠隔操作は、連続的な視覚運動調整とシステム監視の負荷が高い
llm.method: 視線でターゲットを指定し確認を経てロボットが自律的に把持・配置を行う視線支援型監視制御フレームワークを提案する
llm.result: VR実験においてタスク完了時間が大幅に短縮され、NASA TLXによる作業負荷スコアが低下した
llm.limitation: 精密配置などの特定タスクでは手動制御の方が配置エラーや成功率で勝る場合がある

2610.39879.title: Compressed Orientation Reachability Maps for Sub-Second Robotic Needle Entry Point Planning
2610.39879.abstract: In the context of multi-stage trajectory planning for robotic percutaneous liver interventions, identifying a kinematically feasible entry point remains a critical computational bottleneck. Existing methods rely on exhaustive inverse kinematics or randomized searches, incurring delays of 13 to 27 seconds per target and limiting real-time intraoperative adaptation. This paper introduces an Orientation-Based Reachability Map (ORM) that precomputes the kinematic feasibility of a 6 Degrees of Freedom (DoF) serial manipulator across 188,873 workspace positions and encodes orientation feasibility into a compact, indexed 83 MB map. A Just-In-Time (JIT) compiled runtime pipeline replaces live optimization with near-instantaneous array lookups. Experimental evaluation demonstrates a reduction in planning latency from 13.5-26.9 s to 0.289-0.349 s per target while maintaining high geometric fidelity, achieving a mean convex hull volume overlap ratio of 0.933 and a mean alpha-shape volume ratio of 0.976 relative to the baseline reachable point cloud. The proposed ORM framework enables sub-second entry point planning and provides an efficient computational framework for robotic needle insertion in percutaneous liver ablation.
2610.39879.tldr_en: An Orientation-Based Reachability Map (ORM) that precomputes the kinematic feasibility of a 6 Degrees of Freedom (DoF) serial manipulator across 188,873 workspace positions and encodes orientation feasibility into a compact, indexed 83 MB map and provides an efficient computational framework for robotic needle insertion in percutaneous liver ablation.

llm.title_ja: サブセクションでのロボット針穿刺点計画のための圧縮された向き到達可能マップ
llm.tldr_ja: 向きベース到達可能マップ（ORM）を導入し、6自由度シリアルマニピュレータの運動学的実行可能性を事前計算してコンパクトなマップにエンコードすることで、計画レイテンシを大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: 肝臓インターベンションのためのロボット軌道計画において、運動学的に実行可能な穿刺点の特定は計算上のボトルネックとなっており、従来の網羅的逆運動学やランダム探索は1ターゲットあたり13〜27秒の遅延を引き起こす。
llm.method: 6自由度シリアルマニピュレータの運動学的実行可能性を188,873のワークスペース位置にわたって事前計算し、向きの実行可能性を83MBのコンパクトなインデックス付きマップにエンコードするORMとJITコンパイル済みランタイムパイプラインを提案する。
llm.result: 計画レイテンシを1ターゲットあたり13.5〜26.9秒から0.289〜0.349秒に短縮しつつ、高い幾何学的忠実度を維持した。

2610.39848.title: LiDAR-SHIELD: A Fully Dockerized Adversarial Robustness Assessment Framework for LiDAR-Based 3D Perception Models
2610.39848.abstract: LiDAR-based 3D perception underpins autonomous driving and robotics, yet deploying these models safely requires stress-testing them against adversarial inputs before real-world use. Although state-of-the-art adversarial attacks exist, their implementations are often fragmented across individual repositories, each tied to a specific architecture or task and requiring manual environment reconstruction and model-specific integration code. We present LIDARSHIELD, a unified and fully Dockerized framework that reverses this workflow: rather than installing the target model inside the toolkit, LIDARSHIELD exposes any model through three lightweight HTTP endpoints, namely /info, /forward, and /gradient As a result, connecting a new model or dataset requires only a single loader function or adapter. The framework supports both 3D semantic segmentation and 3D object detection through the same engine-service protocol, integrating a task-aware suite of state-of-the-art attacks, including PGD and Square Attack for segmentation, and point perturbation, point removal, point injection, and LiDAttack for detection. This enables systematic exposure of corner cases and vulnerabilities across heterogeneous LiDAR backbones. The LiDAR-Shield codebase is publicly available at https://github.com/alexandrosgk/LiDAR-shield.
2610.39848.tldr_en: This work presents LIDARSHIELD, a unified and fully Dockerized framework that reverses this workflow: rather than installing the target model inside the toolkit, LIDARSHIELD exposes any model through three lightweight HTTP endpoints, namely /info, /forward, and /gradient.

llm.title_ja: LiDAR-SHIELD：LiDARベース3D知覚モデルのための完全にDocker化された敵対的頑健性評価フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: LiDARSHIELDは、ターゲットモデルをツールキット内にインストールするのではなく、軽量な3D HTTPエンドポイントを通じて任意のモデルを公開する、完全にDocker化された統一フレームワークである。
llm.problem: LiDARベースの3D知覚は自動運転やロボット工学を支えているが、敵対的入力に対するストレステストの実装は個別のリポジトリに断片化されており、手動での環境再構築が必要である。
llm.method: 情報を公開する3つの軽量なHTTPエンドポイント（/info、/forward、/gradient）を介して任意のモデルを公開し、統一されたエンジン・サービスプロトコルで多様な攻撃手法を統合するDocker化されたフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 3Dセマンティックセグメンテーションおよび3Dオブジェクト検出の両方において、異種LiDARバックボーンにわたるコーナーケースや脆弱性を体系的に露出させることが可能になった。

2610.39825.title: AegisFlow: Training-Free Non-Myopic Path-Safe Guided Flow Matching
2610.39825.abstract: Pretrained generative models, such as diffusion and flow matching models, have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in synthesizing high-quality data. However, steering their generative trajectories to satisfy strict constraints--such as identity preservation in image editing or obstacle avoidance in robotics--remains fundamentally challenging. While recent training-free guidance methods enforce path-safety, they rely heavily on min-norm controllers that only account for immediate constraint satisfaction. These myopic approaches often yield suboptimal trajectories that hover dangerously close to the boundary, severely restricting the model's ability to optimize toward its target. In this paper, we propose AegisFlow, a training-free, non-myopic path-safe guidance framework that recasts guided generation as a safety-critical optimal control problem with global scope. By integrating a time-varying barrier function directly into the global cost functional, AegisFlow naturally enforces constraints along the entire generative path. To compute the global optimal control, we derive a tractable, mathematically grounded approximation of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that AegisFlow outperforms state-of-the-art methods across text-guided image manipulation and robotic planning, establishing a significantly better trade-off between target alignment and constraint satisfaction. Code is available at https://github.com/LiuKunpeng03/AegisFlow.
2610.39825.tldr_en: A training-free, non-myopic path-safe guidance framework that recasts guided generation as a safety-critical optimal control problem with global scope, AegisFlow is proposed, which naturally enforces constraints along the entire generative path.

llm.title_ja: AegisFlow：トレーニング不要の非近視的経路安全ガイダンス付きフローマッチング
llm.tldr_ja: AegisFlowは、誘導生成をグローバルなスコープを持つ安全性クリティカルな最適制御問題として再定式化し、生成経路全体にわたって自然に制約を強制するトレーニング不要のフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みの生成モデルの軌道を厳格な制約（画像編集の同一性保持やロボットの障害物回避など）を満たすように誘導することは、即時的な制約充足のみを考慮する近視的な手法では困難である。
llm.method: 時間変動するバリア関数を大域的なコスト汎関数に直接統合し、ハミルトン・ジャコビ・ベルマン（HJB）方程式の近似を導出して大域的最適制御を計算するトレーニング不要の非近視的経路安全ガイダンスフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: テキスト誘導画像操作やロボット計画において、ターゲット整合性と制約充足の間のトレードオフを大幅に改善し、最先端手法を上回る性能を示した。

2610.39816.title: PASA-KV: Attacking Action-Facing Visual Routes in World Action Models
2610.39816.abstract: World action models (WAMs) increasingly couple internal visual or world representations with action generation, making their world-to-action pathways a critical yet poorly understood source of robustness. We investigate when perturbations to these internal representations actually become behaviorally consequential, and uncover a pronounced mismatch between representation perturbability and closed-loop vulnerability: attack effectiveness varies sharply across visual K/V routes, while larger representation displacement does not reliably imply stronger control failure. Our analysis attributes this mismatch to the action-conditioned readout, where keys determine where action queries read and values determine what content they receive. This motivates an action-facing view of vulnerability, in which the effect of a perturbation depends on how it is routed into action generation rather than on representation-space magnitude alone. We instantiate this view with Tail-AV, a short-probe signal for identifying vulnerable routes, and operationalize it in PASA-KV, which selects action-facing K/V targets before training a fresh task-shared attack. Experiments across multiple WAM systems and a physical robot validate readout-informed target selection, demonstrate strong closed-loop attacks, and reveal substantial system-level differences in resistance.
2610.39816.tldr_en: A pronounced mismatch between representation perturbability and closed-loop vulnerability is uncovered: attack effectiveness varies sharply across visual K/V routes, while larger representation displacement does not reliably imply stronger control failure.

llm.title_ja: PASA-KV：世界行動モデルにおける行動指向ビジュアルルートの攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: 表現の摂動しやすさと閉ループ脆弱性の間に顕著な不一致があることが明らかになり、攻撃の効果は視覚的K/Vルートによって大きく異なることが示された。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデル（WAM）は内部の視覚または世界表現を行動生成に結合させるが、その世界・行動経路の頑健性は十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: アクション条件付き読み出しにおけるキーとバリューの役割に着目し、脆弱なルートを特定するためのショートプローブ信号であるTail-AVと、タスク共有の攻撃を訓練する前にアクション指向のK/Vターゲットを選択するPASA-KVを提案する。
llm.result: 複数のWAMシステムと実機ロボットを用いた実験により、読み出し情報に基づくターゲット選択の有効性、強力な閉ループ攻撃、およびシステム間の耐性の違いが明らかになった。

2610.39798.title: Surrogate Uncertainty for Black-box Visual Grounding
2610.39798.abstract: Visual grounding is crucial for robots to understand language instructions with visual observations. This paper addresses the problem of visual grounding uncertainties, where a robot uses a black-box vision-language model (VLM) to ground free-form natural-language instructions to target objects. Prevailing methods derive uncertainty from the VLM itself. Yet, outputs of the VLM, e.g., generated uncertainties, are from the same parameters and structures producing the predictions, and inherit the bias. We give a formal Bayesian definition of the problem that treats the VLM prediction as an observation. An external surrogate Bayesian model then quantifies per-query uncertainty over a local neighborhood of a held-out calibration set, decomposed into aleatoric and epistemic components. A hierarchical retrieval across input modalities realizes a compact joint-space neighborhood, mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The estimator further integrates with conformal prediction or model-based planning for active visual grounding, where robots are allowed to take verbal or physical actions to ground targets. Across grounding benchmarks and state-of-the-art VLMs, it consistently improves both calibration and task performance. On a real Fetch robot under open-world instructions, it enables principled trade-offs between confident action and information gathering, substantially improving robustness.
2610.39798.comment: A preprint rejected by RSS 2026 AND CoRL 2026
2610.39798.tldr_en: This paper addresses the problem of visual grounding uncertainties, where a robot uses a black-box vision-language model (VLM) to ground free-form natural-language instructions to target objects, and gives a formal Bayesian definition of the problem that treats the VLM prediction as an observation.

llm.title_ja: ブラックボックス視覚的グラウンディングのためのサロゲート不確実性
llm.tldr_ja: VLMの予測を観測として扱い、外部のサロゲートベイジアンモデルを用いて、言語指示の視覚的グラウンディングにおける不確実性を定量化するフォーマルな定義を与えた。
llm.problem: ロボットが自由形式の自然言語指示を対象物にグラウンディングする際、VLMの出力から直接得られる不確実性は、予測を生み出すのと同じパラメータや構造に依存しているためバイアスを受け継ぐ。
llm.method: VLM予測を観測として扱う形式的なベイジアン定義を与え、外部のサロゲートベイジアン modelにより保持された較正セットの局所近傍でアレアトリックおよびエピステミックな不確実性を定量化する。
llm.result: 多様なグラウンディングベンチマークと最先端VLMにおいて、較正とタスク性能の両方を一貫して改善し、実機のFetchロボットでの頑健性を高めた。
keywords_ja: 視覚的グラウンディング

2610.39789.title: Data-Driven or Model-Constrained? Comparing Airflow Estimation Methods under Sparse Sensing
2610.39789.abstract: Airflow-driven advection is the primary mechanism for gas and aerosol dispersion in real-world scenarios, making accurate airflow estimation essential for ventilation monitoring, gas source localization, and contaminant spread analysis. Since obtaining airflow maps via high-resolution spatial sensing is usually infeasible in practice, flow field estimation methods must cope with sparse measurements by introducing statistical or physical priors to compensate for limited data. Existing approaches mainly differ in how they incorporate fluid-flow constraints and environmental geometry. However, due to the lack of systematic comparisons across this spectrum of methods, the potential benefits of physics-based priors for airflow estimation under sparse sensing remain underexplored. To address this question, we quantitatively evaluate four airflow estimators across three simulated 2D scenarios under steady-state conditions and varying sampling densities. The methods range from Gaussian Process Regression and graph-based Gaussian Markov Random Fields to two Navier-Stokes-based approaches, including a novel strong-form residual minimization variant. Our results show that physical priors provide the greatest benefit at low sampling densities by compensating for missing spatial information. Although data-driven Gaussian Process Regression becomes increasingly competitive as sensor coverage increases, model-based estimators retain an accuracy advantage across the evaluated scenarios.
2610.39789.comment: 4 pages, 3 figures, accepted at IEEE SENSORS Conference 2026

llm.title_ja: データ駆動型かモデル制約型か：疎なセンシング下における気流推定方法の比較
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 高解像度な空間センシングが困難な状況で、疎な測定値から気流マップを正確に推定する必要がある
llm.method: 4つの気流推定器（ガウス過程回帰、GMRF、ナビエストークスベースの手法）を2Dシミュレーションで定量的に比較評価する
llm.result: 低サンプリング密度では物理ベースの事前知識が情報の欠落を補う上で最大の利点を提供することを示した
keywords_ja: センサーネットワーク

2610.39775.title: Teaching a Tree to Recover: Online Distillation of an LLM Supervisor with Counterfactual Replay
2610.39775.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots commonly pair a global planner with a local model predictive controller (MPC), but nonconvex obstacle avoidance and a limited horizon can make the robot freeze in complex layouts. Deciding whether to replan, wait, or call for help is a supervisory decision. Recent work queries a large language model (LLM) supervisor on every anomaly, which is slow and costly. We instead distill the LLM online into a decision tree. After each training episode, counterfactual replay labels recoveries as needed, unnecessary, or harmful. These labels retire unhelpful rules. In simulation, on 20 unseen layouts where the MPC alone freezes, the tree handles at least 18 correctly across all seeds, either by reaching the goal or by calling for help when no feasible path exists. The tree matches both an always-query LLM supervisor and expert-designed rules, while issuing no LLM queries at test time. Handwritten rules cannot anticipate the long tail of situations a physical robot will encounter. Online distillation is a promising remedy: the tree handles familiar cases, and the LLM is consulted only for new ones, whose validated recoveries become new rules. Language models can thus also serve as designers of supervisors rather than only as runtime supervisors.
2610.39775.tldr_en: Online distillation of a large language model (LLM) supervisor online into a decision tree is a promising remedy: the tree handles familiar cases, and the LLM is consulted only for new ones, whose validated recoveries become new rules.

llm.title_ja: 木に回復を教える：反実仮想リプレイを用いたLLMスーパーバイザーのオンライン蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: LLMスーパーバイザーを決定木にオンライン蒸留する手法を提案し、反実仮想リプレイによって不必要なルールを排除しつつテスト時にはLLMクエリを発行しないようにした。
llm.problem: 自律移動ロボットはグローバルプランナーとローカルMPCを組み合わせるが、非凸な障害物回避と限られたホライズンにより複雑なレイアウトでロボットがフリーズすることがある。
llm.method: 各訓練エピソード後に反実仮想リプレイを用いてリカバリの必要性をラベル付けし、LLMスーパーバイザーを決定木にオンライン蒸留する。
llm.result: MPC単体ではフリーズする20の未見レイアウトにおいて、決定木は目標到達またはヘルプ要請を正しく処理し、テスト時にLLMクエリを発行せずに専門家設計のルールや常時クエリ型LLMと同等の性能を達成した。

2610.39744.title: PAPERBENCHX: Can AI Reproduce Science Across Disciplines?
2610.39744.abstract: Before AI can be trusted to discover new science, it should be able to reproduce what science already knows. Reproduction provides a rigorous checkpoint for an AI scientist: the target claim is known, yet recovering it still requires translating an incomplete scientific description into an executable experiment and producing evidence that can be independently verified. Existing research-reproduction benchmarks largely focus on AI and machine learning, where experiments share relatively homogeneous software stacks. Extending this capability across scientific disciplines introduces a different challenge: agents must operate domain-specific scientific software, make physical and numerical choices, diagnose long-running computations, and distinguish valid evidence from merely plausible outputs. We introduce PAPERBENCHX, a benchmark of 93 expert-constructed paper-reproduction tasks spanning 12 research areas across electromagnetics, photonics, chemistry, materials science, biology, and robotics. Each task provides the source paper, a public task specification, and a domain-native scientific environment involving specialized scientific software. Agents must reconstruct a key experiment, execute and diagnose it, and deliver a runnable workflow that supports the target scientific claim. To evaluate scientific validity rather than surface-level agreement, we replay every submission from scratch and score only regenerated evidence against expert-validated criteria. Across 10 frontier agent configurations, the best configuration fully reproduces only 14% tasks under the 90% threshold. Meanwhile, mean rubric scores range from 27.53% to 59.08%, indicating that substantial partial progress rarely translates into complete scientific reproduction. These results reveal a large gap between paper understanding and reliably producing reproducible scientific evidence.
2610.39744.tldr_en: PAPERBENCHX, a benchmark of 93 expert-constructed paper-reproduction tasks spanning 12 research areas across electromagnetics, photonics, chemistry, materials science, biology, and robotics, is introduced, revealing a large gap between paper understanding and reliably producing reproducible scientific evidence.

llm.title_ja: PAPERBENCHX：AIは学際的に科学を再現できるか？
llm.tldr_ja: PAPERBENCHXは、12の研究分野にわたる93の専門家構築の論文再現タスクからなるベンチマークであり、論文理解と再現可能な科学的エビデンスの生成の間に大きなギャップがあることを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存の研究再現ベンチマークはAIや機械学習に大きく集中しており、他分野に拡張するとエージェントはドメイン固有の科学ソフトウェアの操作や物理的・数値的選択を行う必要がある。
llm.method: 電磁気学、フォトニクス、化学、材料科学、生物学、ロボット工学の12分野にわたる93の論文再現タスクとドメイン固有の科学的環境を提供するベンチマークを導入し、専門家検証済みの基準に対して再生成されたエビデンスのみを評価する。
llm.result: 最先端のエージェント構成のうち、90%の閾値の下で完全にタスクを再現できたのはわずか14%であり、論文理解と再現可能な科学的エビデンスの生成の間に大きな乖離があることが示された。

2610.39708.title: AFast Robot Localization Method Based on Monte Carlo Sampling
2610.39708.abstract: Localization is an essential capability of intelligent robots. However, in real-world constrained environments, robots often cannot rely on external localization systems. Therefore, this paper proposes an online particle-filter localization method based on Monte Carlo sampling. The method is applied to the localization of a mobile robot in a maze environment and requires only four range sensors mounted on the front, rear, left, and right sides of the vehicle, without the need for any heading information. Simulation experiments demonstrate that even in a maze where local regions are highly similar, the vehicle can still achieve relatively accurate localization, thereby providing a fast and effective approach for robot localization in complex environments.
2610.39708.tldr_en: An online particle-filter localization method based on Monte Carlo sampling is applied to the localization of a mobile robot in a maze environment and requires only four range sensors mounted on the front, rear, left, and right sides of the vehicle, without the need for any heading information.

llm.title_ja: モンテカルロサンプリングに基づく高速ロボット自己位置推定法
llm.tldr_ja: 車両の前方、後方、左右に配置された4つの距離センサーのみを使用し、方位情報なしで迷路環境における移動ロボットの位置推定を行うオンラインの粒子フィルタ自己位置推定法を提案した。
llm.problem: 実世界の制約された環境において、ロボットは外部の位置推定システムに依存できず、効率的な自己位置推定が必要とされる。
llm.method: モンテカルロサンプリングに基づくオンラインの粒子フィルタ自己位置推定法を用い、前後左右の4つの距離センサーのみで方位情報なしに実現する。
llm.result: 局所的な領域が非常によく似た迷路においても、車両は比較的正確な自己位置推定を達成できることをシミュレーション実験で実証した。
keywords_ja: モンテカルロサンプリング

2610.39691.title: Smartphone Indoor Localization Enhanced by Hierarchical Multi-Sensor Context Recognition
2610.39691.abstract: Smartphone indoor localization requires low-cost, robust positioning across scene transitions and phone-use variations. Pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR) enables infrastructure-free deployment but accumulates errors from heading drift, structural transitions, and carrying-mode changes. Existing methods often treat contextual cues as a single event stream or local correction signal, limiting their ability to address distinct localization errors. This paper presents a framework enhanced by hierarchical multi-sensor context recognition. A jointly data- and model-driven recognition model predicts environment, scene, and activity probabilities, which are converted into scene-event and action-context segments. Scene-event segments guide scene-constrained PDR correction through corridor heading constraints, landmark attraction, fixed-lag backtracking, and vertical-transition handling. Action-context segments drive action-aware RoNIN-based position compensation for carrying-mode-dependent drift. Experiments on cross-floor and multi-action trajectories against LiDAR-SLAM references show that the proposed framework outperforms PDR and representative learned inertial odometry baselines, demonstrating that hierarchical semantics provide reliable, localization-specific correction cues.
2610.39691.tldr_en: Experiments show that the proposed framework outperforms PDR and representative learned inertial odometry baselines, demonstrating that hierarchical semantics provide reliable, localization-specific correction cues.

llm.title_ja: 階層型マルチセンサー文脈認識によって強化されたスマートフォン屋内測位
llm.tldr_ja: 階層的なマルチセンサー文脈認識を用いたフレームワークを提案し、シーンイベントセグメントによる廊下の見出し制約などを通じたPDR補正と、行動文脈セグメントによるRoNINベースの位置補償を実現した。
llm.problem: 歩行者デッドレコニング（PDR）はインフラ不要だが、方位のドリフト、構造的遷移、持ち方変更による誤差が蓄積する。
llm.method: 階層的マルチセンサー文脈認識を用いたフレームワークにより、シーンイベントと行動文脈セグメントを予測し、PDR補正と位置補償を駆動する。
llm.result: LiDAR-SLAMの参照と比較したフロア間およびマルチアクションの軌跡実験において、提案手法はPDRおよび代表的な学習型慣性オドメトリのベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: 歩行者デッドレコニング

2610.39689.title: AI for Science in Space: Orbital Laboratories, Planetary Fieldwork, and Embodied Autonomy
2610.39689.abstract: Artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) is extending from interpretation of existing data to the design and execution of experiments. Space offers distinctive scientific opportunities while restricting physical support. Microgravity and extraterrestrial environments expose phenomena that terrestrial experiments cannot fully reproduce; finite samples, constrained resources, and limited opportunities for intervention complicate sustained investigation. This critical review examines orbital laboratories and planetary in situ science across biology, materials, fluid and thermal physics, and adaptive exploration. We distinguish learning from space-derived data, selecting scientific actions, executing them, and preserving experimental validity. Terrestrial self-driving laboratories provide complementary evidence on optimization, dedicated automation, robotic manipulation, and the support needed for unattended operation. The synthesis connects scientific gains already demonstrated by bounded AI systems to gaps in observation, executable actions, and continuity of valid evidence. Space robots can expand the attainable scope of autonomous science when necessary interventions exceed validated instrument capabilities and timely human support is unavailable. Their value must be established against dedicated mechanisms, redundancy, and human-supported operation. We develop a framework connecting sample history, scientific decisions, physical execution, and claim-specific validity. A worked orbital design, a planetary extension, and matched evaluation schemes separate the contributions of sensing, decision policies, and physical actions. The resulting agenda measures autonomy through valid scientific return, task coverage, intervention costs, and evidence integrity across complete campaigns.
2610.39689.comment: 47 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables. Ancillary evidence files included
2610.39689.tldr_en: This critical review examines orbital laboratories and planetary in situ science across biology, materials, fluid and thermal physics, and adaptive exploration and develops a framework connecting sample history, scientific decisions, physical execution, and claim-specific validity.

llm.title_ja: 宇宙における科学のためのAI：軌道上の実験室、惑星フィールドワーク、および身体性自律性
llm.tldr_ja: 軌道上の実験室や惑星の場における科学を生物学、材料科学、流体・熱物理学などにわたり検証し、サンプル履歴、科学的意思決定、物理的実行、主張特有の妥当性を結びつけるフレームワークを開発した。
llm.problem: 宇宙空間は独自の科学的機会を提供する一方で物理的支援を制限し、有限なサンプルや制約されたリソースが持続的な調査を複雑にしている。
llm.method: 生物学、材料科学、流体・熱物理学、適応的探索にわたる軌道上実験室と惑星の現地科学を調査し、サンプル履歴、科学的決定、物理的実行、妥当性を結びつけるフレームワークを開発する。
llm.result: バウンデッドAIシステムによってすでに示された科学的成果と、観測、実行可能なアクション、および有効な証拠の継続性におけるギャップとの接続を行った。

2610.39582.title: Kinematic-Tactile Aligned Dexterous Retargeting with Contact Wrench Space Alignment
2610.39582.abstract: Human demonstrations provide a natural and scalable source of data for learning dexterous manipulation policies. However, existing retargeting methods primarily transfer human kinematics, while the tactile information underlying physical interaction is rarely preserved across embodiments. To address this limitation, we present a hierarchical three-stage framework for kinematic-tactile aligned dexterous retargeting. We use object-centric contact wrench space as a physical representation for tactile alignment between human and robot hands. The framework first aligns hand kinematics and contact geometry, and then constructs a human wrench support profile from tactile forces and contact geometry. Robot fingertip force targets are subsequently optimized to cover the human wrench support and converted into joint position corrections, yielding directly replayable robot hand trajectories. We evaluate the framework in simulation and real robot experiments across three pouring conditions. In the real robot experiments, our method achieves a 96.7\% replay success rate and higher wrench transfer fidelity than representative retargeting baselines. The framework enables physically grounded transfer of kinematic and tactile information from human demonstrations to robot hands, providing a path toward scalable learning of contact-rich dexterous manipulation.
2610.39582.tldr_en: A hierarchical three-stage framework for kinematic-tactile aligned dexterous retargeting that enables physically grounded transfer of kinematic and tactile information from human demonstrations to robot hands, providing a path toward scalable learning of contact-rich dexterous manipulation.

llm.title_ja: 接触レンチ空間の整合に基づく運動学・触覚整合型器用リターゲット
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のデモンストレーションからロボットハンドへの運動学的および触覚的情報の物理的根拠に基づく転送を可能にする階層型3段階フレームワークを提案し、接触豊富な器用操作の学習への道を開いた。
llm.problem: 既存のリターゲット方法は主に人間の運動学を転送するだけであり、物理的相互作用の基礎となる触覚情報が異なる身体間で保持されない。
llm.method: オブジェクト中心の接触レンチ空間を触覚整合のための物理的表現として使用し、ハンドの運動学と接触幾何学を整合させ、指先力ターゲットを最適化する階層的3段階フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 実ロボット実験の3つの注ぎ込み条件において96.7%の再生成功率を達成し、代表的なリターゲットベースラインよりも高いレンチ転送忠実度を実現した。
keywords_ja: 人間のデモンストレーション

2610.39560.title: SimTO-Robust: Automated Design of Soft Grippers Robust to Grasp Pose and Object Geometry
2610.39560.abstract: Robotic grippers operating in unstructured environments must robustly grasp objects of different shapes and sizes despite perception and positioning errors. Soft grippers that can achieve this robustness through intelligent mechanical design rather than sophisticated control software offer a promising solution. However, no existing computational design framework explicitly optimises soft gripper morphology for robustness across object geometries and grasp poses. We introduce SimTO-Robust, a generalisation of simulation-driven topology optimisation (SimTO) that simulates grasps across multiple objects and poses and aggregates their contact forces to guide gripper morphology optimisation. We generate 6,646 designs and physically evaluate 24 of them alongside 10 specialised SimTO designs, two rigid baseline grippers, and a baseline generalist soft gripper produced using conventional topology optimisation. All 37 grippers are tested in a pick-and-place task involving five feature-rich objects and six grasp poses, with external disturbances of increasing magnitude applied during the task. On average, SimTO-Robust designs complete pick-and-place more reliably than specialised SimTO designs and the rigid baselines. The best SimTO-Robust designs also withstood more of the applied disturbances than any other tested gripper. These results show that incorporating diverse grasp conditions into simulation-driven topology optimisation is a simple and effective approach to improving real-world soft gripper robustness. More broadly, they show that robust robotic grasping can be achieved through intelligent mechanical design rather than sophisticated sensing and control.
2610.39560.tldr_en: SimTO-Robust, a generalisation of simulation-driven topology optimisation (SimTO) that simulates grasps across multiple objects and poses and aggregates their contact forces to guide gripper morphology optimisation, shows that robust robotic grasping can be achieved through intelligent mechanical design rather than sophisticated sensing and control.

llm.title_ja: SimTO-Robust：把持姿勢と物体形状に対してロバストなソフトグリッパーの自動設計
llm.tldr_ja: 複数オブジェクトや姿勢にわたる把持をシミュレートし接触力を集約してグリッパー形態の最適化を導くSimTO-Robustを提案し、ロバストな把持が洗練されたセンシングや制御ではなく知的な機械設計によって達成できることを示した。
llm.problem: 不規則な環境で動作するロボットグリッパーは、知覚や位置決めの誤差があるにもかかわらず、異なる形状やサイズの物体をロバストに把持する必要がある。
llm.method: シミュレーション駆動型トポロジー最適化（SimTO）の一般化であるSimTO-Robustを導入し、複数オブジェクトと姿勢の把持シミュレーションから接触力を集約して形態最適化を導く。
llm.result: SimTO-Robust設計は、特殊なSimTO設計や剛体ベースラインよりも平均してピックアンドプレースをより確実に完了し、より多くの外乱に耐えた。

2610.39547.title: Assuring Learning-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems with Foundation Models: A Neuro-Symbolic Agenda for Testing, Verification, and Runtime Assurance
2610.39547.abstract: Learning-enabled cyber-physical systems (CPS), including autonomous vehicles and UAVs, increasingly incorporate foundation models, yet fragmented assurance practices provide insufficient support for system-level guarantees. We argue that restoring engineering control across stochastic neural, symbolic, and physical boundaries requires a shift from model-centric evaluation to system-level assurance. We introduce the Foundation Model Assurance Stack, connecting three directions: (i) neuro-symbolic architectures that constrain foundation models through explicit symbolic world models, reasoning layers, and interfaces; (ii) semantically grounded, conformance-based testing that combines formal specifications and symbolic world models with foundation-model-assisted specification mining, scenario generation, and test synthesis; and (iii) compositional verification and runtime assurance that target formally tractable components and interfaces through modular contracts, equivalence checking, verified synthesis, uncertainty-aware reasoning, and runtime monitoring and enforcement. Symbolic abstractions establish assurance boundaries between stochastic learning and formal reasoning, connecting testing, verification, and runtime evidence across the system lifecycle. Foundation models serve as constrained assistants whose outputs are independently checked wherever correctness can be formally specified. We identify research challenges in specification engineering, abstraction fidelity, evidence composition, and lifecycle certification, and outline a staged agenda toward trustworthy, deployable, and certifiable learning-enabled CPS.
2610.39547.tldr_en: It is argued that restoring engineering control across stochastic neural, symbolic, and physical boundaries requires a shift from model-centric evaluation to system-level assurance, and introduced the Foundation Model Assurance Stack, connecting three directions.

llm.title_ja: 基盤モデルによる学習型サイバーフィジカルシステムの保証：テスト、検証、および実行時保証のための神経・記号的アジェンダ
llm.tldr_ja: モデル中心の評価からシステムレベルの保証への移行を主張し、明示的な記号的世界モデル、適合性ベースのテスト、および合成検証を接続するFoundation Model Assurance Stackを導入した。
llm.problem: 自動運転車やUAVなどの学習型サイバーフィジカルシステム（CPS）は基盤モデルをますます組み込んでいるが、断片化された保証手法ではシステムレベルの保証を十分にサポートできない。
llm.method: 神経・記号的アーキテクチャ、適合性ベースのテスト、および構成的検証と実行時保証を接続するFoundation Model Assurance Stackを導入する。
llm.result: 確率的学習と形式的推論の間の保証境界を確立し、テスト、検証、および実行時の証拠をライフサイクル全体で接続する staged アジェンダを概説した。
keywords_ja: サイバーフィジカルシステム

2610.39543.title: From Reasoning to Action: Consequence-Grounded Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.39543.abstract: Reasoning informs decision-making by connecting intended actions with their expected consequences. Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models incorporate embodied chains of thought (ECoTs) to guide action generation. However, such guidance remains implicit, as actions are conditioned on ECoTs rather than explicitly optimized to align with them. We introduce CoRAct, a consequence-grounded reasoning-to-action alignment framework that explicitly aligns reasoning and action through reward-guided optimization in action noise space. CoRAct formulates two physically grounded ECoT components as verifiable signals: movement specifies intended motion, while waypoints encode expected spatial consequences. A unified Mixture-of-Transformers jointly models ECoT reasoning, action generation, and action-conditioned future prediction. For candidate actions generated from sampled noise, CoRAct computes alignment rewards based on movement consistency and agreement between predicted outcomes and specified waypoints. These rewards guide group-relative optimization of the initial noise distribution, steering action generation toward consistency with intended actions and expected consequences. Experiments across RoboCasa, VLABench, and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate improvements in task success, generalization, and reasoning-execution alignment over strong ECoT-based VLA baselines. CoRAct also grounds externally provided ECoTs in executable behavior, enabling zero-shot adaptation to novel scenarios by leveraging knowledge from powerful vision-language models. Project page and dataset: https://onlyxingxingzyx.github.io/CoRAct/
2610.39543.tldr_en: CoRAct is introduced, a consequence-grounded reasoning-to-action alignment framework that explicitly aligns reasoning and action through reward-guided optimization in action noise space and grounds externally provided ECoTs in executable behavior.

llm.title_ja: 推論から行動へ：ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのための結果に基いたアライメント
llm.tldr_ja: 行動ノイズ空間における報酬誘導型最適化を通じて推論と行動を明示的に整合させる、結果に基いた推論・行動アライメントフレームワークCoRActを提案した。
llm.problem: 近年のVLAモデルは身体化された思考の連鎖（ECoT）を組み込んでいるが、行動はECoTに基づいて条件付けられるものの、それらと明示的に整合するように最適化されていない。
llm.method: 移動の一貫性と予測結果・経由地の一致に基づくアライメント報酬を計算し、グループ相対最適化を通じて行動ノイズ空間で報酬誘導型最適化を行うCoRActを導入する。
llm.result: RoboCasa、VLABench、および実世界の操作タスクの実験において、強力なECoTベースのVLAベースラインを上回るタスク成功率、汎化性能、推論・実行アライメントの向上を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル
推論と行動のアライメント

2610.39528.title: PRIME W0: Physical Priors from World Models for Embodied Manipulation
2610.39528.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at instruction following, yet most remain feed-forward: they condition actions only on the current observation and discard both long-horizon temporal context and the hierarchical structure of VLM representations. We present PRIME W0, a hierarchical conditional flow-matching framework that closes this gap through three synergistic designs: (1)per-layer KV injection from a pretrained VLM into an Adaptive MoE action expert; (2)dynamics-aware conditioning via asynchronous world-model subgoal-image prediction and a DINOv2 historical-frame semantic bridge; and (3)Action Dynamic Manifold (ADM) flow matching with covariance-structured noise that respects robot kinematic coupling. PRIME W0 is trained in four stages---VLM pre-training, DAT/NTP visuomotor pre-training, DiT flow-matching decoder assembly with WM injection, and end-to-end SFT---and achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO and real-robot benchmarks, with systematic ablations validating each architectural component.
2610.39528.tldr_en: PRIME W0 is a hierarchical conditional flow-matching framework that closes this gap through three synergistic designs: per-layer KV injection from a pretrained VLM into an Adaptive MoE action expert, andynamics-aware conditioning via asynchronous world-model subgoal-image prediction and a DINOv2 historical-frame semantic bridge.

llm.title_ja: PRIME W0：身体化マニピュレーションのための世界モデルからの物理的事前知識
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みVLMからのレイヤー毎のKVインジェクション、世界モデルによるサブゴール画像予測、および運動学的結合を尊重するフローマッチングを組み合わせた、階層型条件付きフローマッチングフレームワークPRIME W0を提案した。
llm.problem: Vision-Language-Action（VLA）モデルは指示追従に優れるが、その多くはフィードフォワードであり、長期的な時間的文脈やVLM表現の階層構造を捨てている。
llm.method: 事前学習済みVLMからのper-layer KVインジェクション、非同期世界モデルのサブゴール画像予測とDINOv2セマンティックブリッジによる動態認識条件付け、および共分散構造ノイズを持つAction Dynamic Manifoldフローマッチングを統合する。
llm.result: LIBEROおよび実ロボットのベンチマークにおいて最先端の結果を達成し、各アーキテクチャコンポーネントの有効性を系統的なアブレーションで検証した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル
階層型フレームワーク

2610.39454.title: Kairos: Semantics-Aware Orchestration of Planning Engines across Classical, Numeric, Temporal and Hybrid PDDL
2610.39454.abstract: Planning at run time, as in robots that re-plan while they act, needs a planner that reads the PDDL its users write (durative actions, numeric resources, time windows, continuous change), answers quickly, and delivers only validated plans. Specialised planners are strong on individual fragments of PDDL, but they differ in coverage, latency and in what their failures mean. We study whether selecting heterogeneous engines from the semantics of each task can give broad coverage of PDDL, from STRIPS to PDDL+, while remaining competitive with specialised planners and making explicit what each answer guarantees. Kairos profiles each task to decide which of five engines apply (ground heuristic search, compressed and snap-action temporal search, time steps for hybrid dynamics, lifted search) and schedules them under one budget of time and memory. Every candidate plan is checked by a validator independent of the planner's transformations, and "unsolvable" is reported only when a search whose exhaustion is a proof exhausts its space. On 1,756 tasks from nine comparative suites, Kairos solves more tasks at the full limits than the strongest evaluated planner of each suite, with the largest differences on numeric, temporal, PDDL3 and PDDL+ planning, and it also solves the most tasks at 100 ms and 1 s. Resampling over domains, the gain is above zero in six of the nine suites, while on classical planning against LAMA it is within the noise. A further 450 feature-oriented tasks and 26 one-feature probes show that Kairos handles all seventeen features probed, where no other planner evaluated handles more than eight. Ablations identify compressed temporal search and the novelty fallback as major contributors, and a comparison with VAL traces every disagreement to a PDDL+ convention or to a documented VAL defect. Planner and benchmark are open source.
2610.39454.comment: 32 pages, 3 figures, 11 tables. Submitted to the Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research. Code: https://github.com/PlanSys2/kairos ; benchmark, scripts and results: https://github.com/PlanSys2/kairos-benchmarks
2610.39454.tldr_en: Whether selecting heterogeneous engines from the semantics of each task can give broad coverage of PDDL, from STRIPS to PDDL+, while remaining competitive with specialised planners and making explicit what each answer guarantees is studied.

llm.title_ja: Kairos：古典的、数値的、時間的、ハイブリッドPDDLにわたる計画エンジンのセマンティクス認識オーケストレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 各タスクのセマンティクスから異種エンジンを選択し、単一の時間とメモリの予算の下でスケジュールするKairosを研究し、STRIPSからPDDL+までの広いPDDLカバレッジを達成した。
llm.problem: 動的に再計画を行うロボットのための実行時プランナーは、ユーザーが書いたPDDLを読み、高速に応答し、検証済みのプランのみを配信する必要があるが、専門化されたプランナーはカバレッジやレイテンシが異なる。
llm.method: 各タスクのセマンティクスに基づいて5つのエンジンのうちどれが適用されるかをプロファイリングし、単一の時間とメモリ予算の下でスケジュールするKairosを研究する。
llm.result: 9つの比較スイートの1,756のタスクにおいて、最大の制限下で最強の評価済みプランナーよりも多くのタスクを解決し、数値、時間、PDDL3、PDDL+の計画で最大の差を示した。

2610.39451.title: Smooth Action Chunking Via Movement-Primitive Representations for Imitation Learning
2610.39451.abstract: Imitation learning has become a widely adopted approach for vision-based robot policies, owing to its conceptual simplicity, scalability, and ability to leverage large-scale datasets. As these policies have grown more capable, action chunking has become their standard interface. At each decision step the policy outputs several future actions at once. Backbones from diffusion policies to large vision-language-action models all share it. Whatever backbone produces the chunk, its temporal structure is learned only implicitly. The commanded trajectory is therefore jerky both within a chunk and between successive chunks. On real hardware this appears as visible vibration and as repeated saturation of the follower's velocity limit. We address this issue by incorporating a movement-primitive-based trajectory representation into action chunking. Specifically, a trajectory segment is represented as a linear combination of smooth basis functions, yielding smooth trajectories by construction while leaving the policy architecture, training objective, and inference procedure unchanged. The same representation also yields a closed-form, inference-time correction for the second source of jerk. We condition the predicted coefficients so that the new chunk passes through a via-point at the previous chunk's last commanded action. This correction needs no retraining and, unlike asynchronous Real-Time Chunking, applies to policies queried in one shot. We instantiate it on a one-shot (ACT) and an iterative (DiT) backbone and evaluate in simulation and on a real bimanual ALOHA platform. The representation lowers within-chunk jerk by an order of magnitude on the one-shot backbone and by 2.4 times on the iterative one, with task success statistically non-inferior. The conditioning then removes 73-84% of the boundary discontinuity, at negligible per-step cost.
2610.39451.tldr_en: This work incorporates a movement-primitive-based trajectory representation into action chunking, whereby a trajectory segment is represented as a linear combination of smooth basis functions, yielding smooth trajectories by construction while leaving the policy architecture, training objective, and inference procedure unchanged.

llm.title_ja: 模倣学習のための動作プリミティブ表現を介したスムーズなアクションチャンキング
llm.tldr_ja: アクションチャンキングに動作プリミティブベースの軌道表現を組み込むことで、ポリシーのアーキテクチャや訓練目的に影響を与えずに、設計上滑らかな軌道を生成しジャークを大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: アクションチャンキングは広く採用されているが、その時間的構造は暗黙的にしか学習されず、コマンドされた軌道がチャンクル内およびチャンク間でジャックになり、ハードウェア上で振動や速度制限の飽和を引き起こす。
llm.method: 軌道セグメントを滑らかな基底関数の線形結合として表現する動作プリミティブベースの軌道表現をアクションチャンキングに組み込み、推論時の閉形式の補正を行う。
llm.result: ワンショットバックボーンではチャンクル内のジャークを1桁削減し、反復型バックボーンでは2.4倍削減しつつ、タスク成功率は統計的に同等レベルを維持した。
keywords_ja: アクションチャンキング

2610.39446.title: Ask to Evolve: A Unified Harness for Lifelong Embodied Navigation with Hybrid Action Space and Persistent Memory
2610.39446.abstract: Giving embodied agents the freedom to act autonomously, initiate interactions, and understand their surroundings through experience is a step toward bringing them to life in the physical world. Realizing this vision requires action, interaction, and memory to work together, so that each encounter can inform current decisions and contribute experience for future tasks. We present EvoLife, a unified navigation harness that enables a multimodal embodied agent to choose how to move, when to ask, and what experience to carry forward. Its hybrid action space supports waypoint navigation, local discrete adjustments, pixel-based navigation, and object-directed navigation. Active interaction allows the agent to seek clarification or assistance when it encounters ambiguity or difficulty, while persistent spatial memory binds observations and dialogue to places, retaining useful experience to guide subsequent visits. We evaluate eight benchmarks across four task families: vision-language navigation, object navigation, interactive instance navigation, and continuous multi-task navigation. With an average of only 1.87 active interactions per episode, our method achieves a first-visit success rate (SR) of 100% across four 100-episode sets spanning vision-language navigation and object navigation. Complete-sequence SR reaches 98% on 50 LHPR-VLN sequences and 94% on 50 GOAT-Bench sequences. In the R2R revisit setting, success weighted by path length (SPL) increases from 82.23% to 93.31% with retained experience. Multi-day physical navigation further demonstrates exploration, proactive help-seeking, and revisiting remembered places. Together, these results advance the vision of bringing embodied agents to life through autonomous action, proactive interaction, and the accumulation and reuse of experience.
2610.39446.tldr_en: This work presents EvoLife, a unified navigation harness that enables a multimodal embodied agent to choose how to move, when to ask, and what experience to carry forward, and evaluates eight benchmarks across four task families: vision-language navigation, object navigation, interactive instance navigation, and continuous multi-task navigation.

llm.title_ja: 進化への問いかけ：ハイブリッド行動空間と永続的記憶を持つ生涯身体化ナビゲーションのための統合ハーネス
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダルな身体化エージェントが移動方法、質問のタイミング、引き継ぐ経験を選択できる統合ナビゲーションハーネスEvoLifeを提案し、8つのベンチマークで評価した。
llm.problem: 身体化エージェントに自律的な行動の自由、相互作用の開始、経験を通じた周囲の理解を与えるには、行動、相互作用、記憶が連動して動作する必要がある。
llm.method: ウェイポイントナビゲーション、ローカルな離散的調整、ピクセルベースナビゲーション、物体指向ナビゲーションをサポートするハイブリッド行動空間と永続的空間記憶を持つEvoLifeを提案する。
llm.result: 平均1.87回の能動的インタラクションにより、ビジョン・言語ナビゲーションおよび物体ナビゲーションにわたる4つの100エピソードセットで100%の初訪問成功率を達成した。
llm.limitation: source_summaryに記載なし（要旨に明記なし）
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語ナビゲーション

2610.39429.title: ScheduleGen: Demonstration Generation via Skill Scheduling for Multi-Arm Imitation Learning
2610.39429.abstract: Multi-arm robot platforms, including bimanual and humanoid robots, have the capability to complete tasks with lower cycle times than single-arm systems, but they are more difficult to safely control due to the presence of multi-arm constraints. The paradigm of training generalist robot policies from massive datasets is a promising approach to address general-purpose multi-arm manipulation, but the acquisition of large multi-arm manipulation datasets remains a bottleneck. Automated demonstration generation can alleviate this burden by synthesizing new demonstrations from a handful of source demonstrations, but existing algorithms ignore multi-arm constraints and as a result often induce unsafe and unsuccessful behaviors. We address this limitation by introducing ScheduleGen, an integrated planning & scheduling algorithm for multi-arm demonstration generation. We evaluate ScheduleGen on 28 simulation task variants, including seven externally authored RoboDojo tasks and settings inaccessible to prior systems; it achieves 79.6% mean data-generation success and trains policies with 65.5% mean success. ScheduleGen policies outperform those trained on a state-of-the-art data generation baseline, and achieve 50-80% success across eight real-world variants through zero-shot sim-to-real and real-to-sim-to-real transfer. Videos and more at: https://schedulegen.github.io/
2610.39429.comment: 22 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Project website and videos: https://schedulegen.github.io/
2610.39429.tldr_en: This work introduces ScheduleGen, an integrated planning&scheduling algorithm for multi-arm demonstration generation, which outperform those trained on a state-of-the-art data generation baseline, and achieve 50-80% success across eight real-world variants through zero-shot sim-to-real and real-to-sim-to-real transfer.

llm.title_ja: ScheduleGen：マルチアーム模倣学習のためのスキルスケジューリングによるデモンストレーション生成
llm.tldr_ja: マルチアームのデモンストレーション生成のための統合された計画・スケジューリングアルゴリズムScheduleGenを導入し、ゼロショットのシム・ツー・リアルおよびリアル・ツー・シム・ツー・リアル転移を通じて実世界のバリエーションで高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: マルチアームロボットプラットフォームはサイクルタイム短縮に有効だが、マルチアーム制約の存在により安全な制御が難しく、大規模なデータセットの収集がボトルネックとなっている。
llm.method: マルチアームのデモンストレーション生成に向けた統合計画・スケジューリングアルゴリズムであるScheduleGenを導入する。
llm.result: 28のシミュレーションタスクバリエーションで79.6%の平均データ生成成功率を達成し、ゼロショットのシム・ツー・リアル等を通じて8つの実世界バリエーションで50〜80%の成功を収めた。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーション生成

2610.39416.title: Decoding Geometry, Not Tokens: Efficient VLMs for Robot Affordance and Trajectory Prediction
2610.39416.abstract: Predicting where to grasp and how to move is fundamentally a geometry problem. Vision-language models treat it as language generation instead. They tokenize spatial coordinates into text and decode them autoregressively. This mechanism ignores spatial structure and truncates continuous precision. Errors compound across coordinate tokens during decoding. In this paper, we show that compact off-the-shelf VLMs with 0.5-2B parameters already encode rich spatial information in their intermediate hidden states. Autoregressive decoding is the dominant bottleneck for trajectory prediction, while affordance prediction depends additionally on feature depth and decoder architecture. We expose the latent spatial information with a lightweight, geometry-compatible prediction head that attaches to a frozen backbone. It reads features from an intermediate hidden layer, conditions a learned query on the task instruction and refines it via cross-attention over the visual tokens to regress affordance boxes and trajectory waypoints directly as continuous values, without modifying the backbone. We evaluate on ShareRobot-Bench and AGD20K. Our 2B variant reduces trajectory error by over 60% and improves ShareRobot-Bench affordance mAP by 85% relative to the autoregressive baseline. It approaches RoboBrain on trajectory prediction (0.251 vs 0.191 DFD) at 3.8x higher throughput. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off for instruction-conditioned 2D geometric prediction.
2610.39416.comment: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027)
2610.39416.tldr_en: This paper shows that compact off-the-shelf VLMs with 0.5-2B parameters already encode rich spatial information in their intermediate hidden states, and exposes the latent spatial information with a lightweight, geometry-compatible prediction head that attaches to a frozen backbone.

llm.title_ja: トークンではなく幾何学のデコード：ロボットのアフォーダンスと軌道予測のための効率的なVLM
llm.tldr_ja: コンパクトな既存VLMの中間隠れ層の表現から、凍結されたバックボーンにアタッチする軽量な幾何学互換の予測ヘッドを用いて、空間情報を直接連続値として回帰する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語モデルは把持位置や移動方法の予測を言語生成として扱い、空間座標をテキストにトークン化して自己回帰的にデコードするため、空間構造が無視され誤差が蓄積する。
llm.method: 凍結されたバックボーンにアタッチされる軽量な幾何学互換の予測ヘッドを用い、中間隠れ層の特徴量からアフォーダンスボックスと軌道ウェイポイントを直接連続値として回帰する。
llm.result: 2Bモデルバリエーションにおいて、自己回帰ベースラインと比較して軌道誤差を60%以上削減し、ShareRobot-BenchのアフォーダンスmAPを85%向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語モデル

2610.39385.title: UMI-Live for In-The-Wild Bimanual Robotics Data Collection
2610.39385.abstract: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) devices allow human experts to demonstrate tasks for robot learning without teleoperating physical robots. Using these demonstrations as training data still requires a consistent hardware setup, calibration, and data processing. We present UMI-Live, a full-stack open-source bimanual UMI system for in-the-wild data collection. We design our custom UMI-Live hardware to integrate camera and LiDAR--inertial sensing, onboard compute, and power, without external tracking equipment or calibration within the collection environment. We implement a simple user interface for recording data while an asynchronous pipeline performs parallel SLAM reconstruction and publishes training-ready datasets. We also release software that supports dual-YAM teleoperation and VLA policy training and inference. We validate UMI-Live data quality by fine-tuning $π_{0.5}$ and MolmoAct2, achieving success rates of 10/10 and 8/10, respectively on a bimanual pick-and-place task. Furthermore, we release 40 hours of UMI-Live data across three tasks, and complete hardware designs, software, and reproduction guides at our $\href{https://umi-live.github.io/}{\text{project website}}$.
2610.39385.tldr_en: This work designs custom UMI-Live hardware to integrate camera and LiDAR--inertial sensing, onboard compute, and power, without external tracking equipment or calibration within the collection environment, and releases software that supports dual-YAM teleoperation and VLA policy training and inference.

llm.title_ja: 野生環境でのバイマニュアルロボットデータ収集のためのUMI-Live
llm.tldr_ja: 外部追跡機器や環境内でのキャリブレーションを不要とするカスタムハードウェアと、並列SLAM再構築を行う非同期パイプラインを備えたフルスタックのオープンソース・バイマニュアルUMIシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: Universal Manipulation Interface（UMI）デバイスを用いた人間のデモンストレーション収集には、一貫したハードウェア設定、キャリブレーション、データ処理が必要となる。
llm.method: カメラ、LiDAR慣性センサー、オンボードコンピュート、電源を統合したカスタムUMI-Liveハードウェアを設計し、並列SLAM再構築パイプラインと直感的なユーザーインターフェースを実装する。
llm.result: バイマニュアルのピックアンドプレースタスクにおいて、π_{0.5}とMolmoAct2のファインチューニングによりそれぞれ10/10と8/10の成功率を達成し、3つのタスクで40時間のデータを公開した。
keywords_ja: オープンソースハードウェア

2610.39379.title: Information-Driven Collaborative Autonomy for Heterogeneous UAV/UGV Teams
2610.39379.abstract: This paper considers coordinating a heterogeneous team of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) traversing a domain containing an unknown number of potentially hazardous targets. The UAVs provide aerial sensing using onboard optical cameras, adapting their trajectories to ground routes and target information. We formulate the aerial search problem using ergodic control, which distributes sensing effort according to a spatial information density to balance exploration and target localization. The formulation incorporates dynamic camera field-of-view footprints and pose-dependent probabilistic detection models. Angles-only measurements are processed through Bayesian inference and marginalization over data-association hypotheses to obtain a Poisson multi-Bernoulli (PMB) approximation of the target posterior, representing both detected and undetected targets. This belief directs aerial sensing toward unexplored regions along the ground routes and viewpoints that improve target localization. Ground planning combines chance-constrained target avoidance, enforced through confidence sets, with a void-probability objective that favors routes unlikely to contain threats. We solve each team's optimization problem in a fully decentralized manner using a nested SCvx*--C-ADMM scheme, with outer sequential convex programming iterations and inner distributed consensus optimization, accounting for nonlinearities, nonseparable objectives, and continuous-time inter-agent separation constraints. A closed-loop scheme updates both fleets' trajectories as information becomes available and permits ground motion when the remaining route risk falls below a prescribed threshold. Numerical case studies examine sensing geometry and target uncertainty, compare decentralized and centralized solvers, and demonstrate full closed-loop collaboration between multiple UAVs and UGVs.
2610.39379.tldr_en: This paper considers coordinating a heterogeneous team of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) traversing a domain containing an unknown number of potentially hazardous targets, and formulate the aerial search problem using ergodic control, which distributes sensing effort according to a spatial information density to balance exploration and target localization.

llm.title_ja: 異種UAV/UGVチームのための情報駆動型協調自律性
llm.tldr_ja: 未知の危険ターゲットが存在する領域を横断するUAVとUGVの異種チームの協調に向け、空間情報密度に応じてセンシング労力を分散するエルゴディック制御を用いた空中探索問題を定式化した。
llm.problem: 未知の潜在的に危険なターゲットが存在する領域を、UAVとUGVの異種チームが協調して効率的に探索・追跡する必要がある。
llm.method: 空間情報密度に応じてセンシング労力を分散するエルゴディック制御を用いて空中探索問題を定式化し、ポアソン・マルチ・ベルヌーイ近似によるターゲット事後分布を求める。
llm.result: ネストされたSCvx*–C-ADMMスキームを用いて各チームの最適化問題を完全に分散的に解き、情報が利用可能になるにつれて両艦隊の軌道を更新する閉ループスキームを実現した。

2610.39378.title: Limit Theorems and Optimal Policies for Flock Flight through Poisson Forests
2610.39378.abstract: Inspired by birds flying through cluttered environments, Karaman and Frazzoli showed that high-speed flight through an ergodic random forest exhibits an ultimate speed limit: above a critical speed, almost surely no infinite collision-free trajectory exists for a single bird. This paper formulates a corresponding bulk-transport problem for many birds. We construct an explicit directed corridor network in a Poisson disk forest and impose a common temporal headway at its waypoints. The maximum current equals a minimum vertex-cut capacity and is achieved by repeated flight along vertex-disjoint paths. The same schedule maximizes completed traversals at every finite horizon, with constant forward speed and no internal waiting. For a forest belt of fixed depth, exact transverse superadditivity yields an almost-sure deterministic current-density limit. A uniform shape theorem for an asymmetric planar dual identifies the current when depth and width grow together. For diverging depth bounded by a constant times width, this current equals the width-first, depth-second limit and is independent of the positive aspect ratio. When diagonal corridors are available, bulk current is positive at sufficiently low obstacle intensity and zero at sufficiently high intensity. For stochastic demand, an upstream admission queue is stable at every rate below the finite-network capacity.

llm.title_ja: ポアソン森林における群れ飛行の極限定理と最適ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 複雑な環境を高速で飛行する際、単一の鳥にとって衝突のない無限の軌跡が存在しなくなる臨界速度や、多数の鳥のバルク輸送問題の限界が不明であった。
llm.method: ポアソンディスクフォレスト内に明示的な有向回廊ネットワークを構築し、ウェイポイントでの共通の時間的ヘッドウェイを課すことで最大電流を定式化した。
llm.result: 有限な地平線ごとに完了したトラバーサルを最大化するスケジュールや、深さと幅が共に成長する場合の均一な形状定理を明らかにした。

2610.39367.title: Utility-WAM: Correcting Future-Induced Action Changes
2610.39367.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) can condition robot actions on generated visual futures, but this additional context is neither cost-free nor uniformly beneficial. We examine what a predicted future actually changes: the action delta $Δa$ between the future-conditioned and future-free execution paths of the same model. Under a shared WAM checkpoint, this delta barely shifts average benchmark success ($+0.8$ points on LIBERO, $-0.8$ on RoboTwin~2.0), while generating visual futures increases inference latency by 1.7--1.9$\times$. These aggregate metrics conceal a concentrated failure mode that we term \emph{future-induced negative transfer}: while predictive deltas benefit long-horizon tasks ($+2.4$ points on LIBERO-Long) and remain negligible on most routine manipulations, they induce severe degradation on precision tasks---with \emph{Press Stapler} and \emph{Place Can Basket} losing 54.0 and 34.0 points, recurring as top failure modes across independently trained WAM variants. We introduce \textbf{Utility-WAM} for in-place correction of future-conditioned control. Its primary learning component is a residual adapter that repairs future-induced velocity deltas under a frozen shared WAM by aligning them with ground-truth dynamic guidance and penalizing excess error beyond the future-free baseline. The adapter selectively eliminates the majority of severe task drops (reducing losses to 6.0 and 14.0 points) while preserving long-horizon foresight. To eliminate superfluous video computation, a lightweight pre-generation gate reuses counterfactual action outcomes to selectively bypass video generation on 75.5\% of RoboTwin queries, cutting latency by 38\% while improving average success to 93.3\% on RoboTwin~2.0 and 98.9\% on LIBERO. On physical bimanual manipulation across three real-world tasks, Utility-WAM succeeds in 53 of 60 trials, compared to 43 for FAST-WAM.
2610.39367.tldr_en: Utility-WAM is introduced, a residual adapter that repairs future-induced velocity deltas under a frozen shared WAM by aligning them with ground-truth dynamic guidance and penalizing excess error beyond the future-free baseline.

llm.title_ja: Utility-WAM：将来起因のアクション変化の修正
llm.tldr_ja: 世界行動モデル（WAM）における将来起因の負の転移を解消するため、凍結された共通WAMの下で将来起因の速度デルタを修正する残差アダプター「Utility-WAM」を提案した。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデル（WAM）はロボットのアクションを生成された視覚的な未来に条件付けできるが、予測された未来によるアクションの変化は、長期タスクには役立つ一方で高精度なタスクにおいて重大な劣化（将来起因の負の転移）を引き起こす。
llm.method: 凍結された共通WAMの下で将来起因の速度デルタをグラウンド真値の動的ガイダンスと整合させて修正する残差アダプターと、ビデオ生成を省く軽量なプレジェネレーションゲートを備えたUtility-WAMを導入する。
llm.result: ロボットクエリの75.5%でビデオ生成を回避してレイテンシを38%削減しつつ、RoboTwin 2.0で93.3%、LIBEROで98.9%に平均成功率を向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.39327.title: SONIC-K1: Porting a Universal Humanoid Motion Tracker to a Small Humanoid on a Single GPU
2610.39327.abstract: We present SONIC-K1, to our knowledge the first open-weights whole-body motion tracker for the Booster K1 humanoid, obtained by adapting the SONIC framework to this smaller robot. The policy is trained from scratch on a single shared GPU with a small fraction of the compute reported for SONIC.
