In MuJoCo simulation, it tracks nearly all held-out motion clips and performs well on external benchmarks under SONIC's success criterion. On the real K1, it tracks upper-body and slow motions, while stepping and turning remain less reliable, and simulation experiments show a sensitivity to action latency. These results show broad motion-tracking capability on a modest training budget and point to quantitative hardware evaluation as the main next step. Code, policy weights and evaluation tools are publicly available.

llm.title_ja: SONIC-K1：単一GPU上で小型ヒューマノイドへのユニバーサルヒューマノイドモーショントラッカーの移植
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 大規模な計算リソースを必要とする汎用ヒューマノイド用モーション追跡フレームワークを、単一のGPUと限られた計算量で小型ヒューマノイドへ適応させる必要がある。
llm.method: SONICフレームワークをBooster K1ヒューマノイド向けに適応させ、単一の共有GPU上でゼロからポリシーをトレーニングした。
llm.result: MuJoCoシミュレーションにおいてほぼすべての保持されたモーションクリップを追跡し、実機のK1において上半身や低速のモーション追跡を実証した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
モーショントラッキング

2610.39319.title: ProLoop: Progress-Aware Closed-Loop Framework via Structured State Relations for Long-Horizon Robotic Task Planning
2610.39319.abstract: Long-horizon robotic tasks are commonly decomposed into semantic subgoals to simplify planning. However, subgoal progress in LLM-based planning is typically inferred implicitly from interaction histories. Inaccurate estimates can misguide execution and allow local errors to propagate. To address this, we propose ProLoop, a Progress-Aware Closed-Loop framework that derives explicit subgoal progress from structured relations between desired and execution states. A learned State-Relation Monitor assesses these relations, which are then aggregated into subgoal progress as ongoing, deviated, or completed. The resulting progress guides execution adaptation, enabling reliable progress-aware control throughout execution. Experiments on AgentBoard ALFWorld and a real-world robotic platform show that ProLoop improves success rate by 12.94% overall and by 15.46% on Hard tasks, while reducing environment interactions by 32.3%.
2610.39319.tldr_en: ProLoop is proposed, a Progress-Aware Closed-Loop framework that derives explicit subgoal progress from structured relations between desired and execution states, and a learned State-Relation Monitor assesses these relations, which are aggregated into subgoal progress as ongoing, deviated, or completed.

llm.title_ja: ProLoop：長期ロボットタスク計画のための構造化状態関係に基づく進捗認識型閉ループフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 所望の状態と実行中の状態の構造化された関係から明示的なサブゴール進捗を導き出し、学習された状態関係モニターを通じて進捗を継続的に評価・適応させるフレームワークProLoopを提案した。
llm.problem: 長期的なロボットタスクは計画簡略化のために意味的サブゴールに分解されるが、LLMベースの計画ではサブゴールの進捗が暗黙的に推論されるため、不正確な推定が誤差の伝播を引き起こす。
llm.method: 所望の状態と実行中の状態の間の構造化された関係から明示的なサブゴール進捗を導き出し、学習されたState-Relation Monitorがこれを継続的に評価・集約して実行の適応を導くProLoopを提案する。
llm.result: AgentBoard ALFWorldおよび実世界のロボットプラットフォームでの実験において、成功率を全体で12.94%、困難なタスクで15.46%向上させ、環境とのインタラクションを32.3%削減した。

2610.39314.title: Language-Grounded Force/Torque Pretraining for Extrinsic Contact Perception
2610.39314.abstract: Fine manipulation requires robots to recognize when a grasped object makes or changes contact with its environment, yet such extrinsic contact is not always directly observable from vision or local contact geometry. Force and torque signals carry this information, but also vary with object weight, grasp configuration, and robot motion, leaving it unclear whether they can provide a reusable representation of physical state. Here we show that bilateral six-axis force/torque histories can be pretrained as a semantically structured physical representation by aligning them with a frozen language space using supervision generated from simulated pick-and-place interactions. On unseen objects in simulation, the learned representation supports text-prototype readout of robot action, object weight, and grasp interaction. In real-world placement, unlabeled calibration enables contact and support-state recognition without updating the encoder, outperforming a vertical-force sign-reversal rule baseline. For connector insertion, an event absent from pretraining, low-rank adaptation improves data-efficient learning over training from scratch. These results show that force/torque histories can support both direct readout of known physical states and efficient adaptation to new extrinsic-contact events.
2610.39314.tldr_en: Bilateral six-axis force/torque histories can be pretrained as a semantically structured physical representation by aligning them with a frozen language space using supervision generated from simulated pick-and-place interactions, and both direct readout of known physical states and efficient adaptation to new extrinsic-contact events are shown.

llm.title_ja: 外因性接触知覚のための言語基盤型力覚・トルク事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーション上のピックアンドプレース相互作用から生成された教師信号を用いて、双方向の6軸力・トルク履歴を凍結された言語空間と整合させることで、意味的に構造化された物理的表現として事前学習できることを示した。
llm.problem: 微細な操作においてロボットは把持物体の環境との接触変化を認識する必要があるが、外因性の接触は視覚や局所的な接触幾何学から直接観測できない場合が多く、力・トルク信号は物体重量や動作によって変動する。
llm.method: シミュレーション環境でのピックアンドプレース相互作用から得られた教師信号を用いて、双方向6軸力・トルク履歴を凍結された言語空間に整合させて事前学習する。
llm.result: 未見の物体に対するテキストプロトコル読み出しをサポートし、実世界のプレースメントでは、エンコーダーを更新することなく接触および支持状態の認識を達成した。

2610.39287.title: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation
2610.39287.abstract: Human cognition flexibly draws on a shared perceptual foundation to understand environments, attend to referenced entities, reason about spatial relationships, and act. Endowing aerial robots with an analogous functional organization remains challenging, as existing systems are often specialized for individual capabilities, dependent on offboard computation, or unable to sustain closed-loop operation on resource-constrained platforms. We present OpenFlyV2, a unified onboard vision-language-action architecture that uses a shared vision-language representation to support semantic understanding, language-grounded perception, spatial reasoning, and continuous aerial control within a single model. A compact action expert converts the shared multimodal context into short-horizon flight waypoints, while motion-aware temporal memory and action priors reduce the computational cost of closed-loop execution. We construct \dataset{}, a simulation-based dataset comprising approximately 70,000 navigation trajectories and 60,000 vision-language instruction--response pairs. OpenFlyV2 generates action chunks, each comprising 12 waypoints, entirely onboard at 10 Hz using an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX. It transfers zero-shot from simulation to physical quadrotor flight, achieving a 48\% navigation success rate across four real-world environments without real-world aerial training data. Extensive results demonstrate that broad vision-language competence and continuous closed-loop flight can coexist within a single model on a resource-constrained aerial platform. Code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Ideal-ljl/AeroBrain.
2610.39287.tldr_en: OpenFlyV2 is presented, a unified onboard vision-language-action architecture that uses a shared vision-language representation to support semantic understanding, language-grounded perception, spatial reasoning, and continuous aerial control within a single model on a resource-constrained aerial platform.
2610.39287.hf_summary_en: OpenFlyV2 is a unified onboard vision-language-action model that enables real-time aerial navigation and reasoning on resource-constrained hardware using shared multimodal representations.

llm.title_ja: OpenFlyV2：空中知覚とナビゲーションのためのオンボードVLAモデル
llm.tldr_ja: 共有のビジョン・言語表現を用いてセマンティック理解、言語基盤知覚、空間認識、連続的な空中制御を単一モデル内でサポートするオンボードVLAアーキテクチャOpenFlyV2を提案した。
llm.problem: 空中ロボットに人間の認知に似た柔軟な機能組織を持たせることは、既存のシステムが個別の機能に特化していたり、オフボード計算に依存していたり、リソースの限られたプラットフォームで閉ループ動作を維持できなかったりするため困難である。
llm.method: 共有ビジョン・言語表現を活用し、コンパクトなアクションエキスパートがマルチモーダル文脈を短時間の飛行ウェイポイントに変換する、オンボードVLAアーキテクチャOpenFlyV2を構築する。
llm.result: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX上で10 Hzの完全にオンボードな推論によりアクションチャンクを生成し、実世界での空中訓練データなしに4つの実環境で48%のナビゲーション成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.39283.title: PriorMaskMap: Robust Online Vectorized Map Construction with Biased Priors
2610.39283.abstract: Online vectorized map construction provides autonomous vehicles with essential, real-time semantic and geometric scene understanding. While leveraging prior maps presents an opportunity to improve accuracy, they are often biased due to outdated information or temporary road changes. Existing methods, which typically treat priors as fully reliable or only consider limited noise patterns, suffer severe performance degradation when these priors are imperfect. To address this, we propose PriorMaskMap, a robust framework for prior-guided vectorized map construction. Its first innovation is a Prior-Aware Confidence Estimator (PACE) that evaluates the input rasterized map against current visual observations. It assigns confidence scores to regions classified as reliable, erroneous, or blank, creating a foundational mask that guides two subsequent branches. In one branch, the Dual-Prior Query Generator (DPQG) selectively filters and embeds both rasterized and vectorized priors to initialize informative queries from trustworthy map structures. In the other, the Confidence-Guided Prior Fusion (CGPF) module spatially propagates and refines the mask, using the refined version to govern the fusion of BEV features with the prior map, thereby providing rich contextual representations for the map decoder. Evaluation on the nuScenes dataset shows that PriorMaskMap achieves superior mapping precision over existing approaches and exhibits marked robustness when provided with priors containing apparent errors. Our code is released at https://github.com/healenrens/PriorMaskMap.
2610.39283.tldr_en: Evaluation on the nuScenes dataset shows that PriorMaskMap achieves superior mapping precision over existing approaches and exhibits marked robustness when provided with priors containing apparent errors.

llm.title_ja: PriorMaskMap：偏った事前知識を持つ堅牢なオンラインベクトル地図構築
llm.tldr_ja: 入力されたラスタライズ地図の信頼性を評価して基盤マスクを作成し、信頼できる地図構造からクエリを初期化して特徴フュージョンを制御するPriorMaskMapフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: オンラインベクトル地図構築は自動運転車に重要だが、利用する事前地図は古い情報や一時的な道路変更により偏りがあり、従来の完全な信頼を置く手法は事前地図が不完全な場合に性能が著しく低下する。
llm.method: 事前対応型信頼度推定器（PACE）でラスタライズ地図を評価して信頼度スコアを割り当て、デュアル事前クエリジェネレータ（DPQG）と信頼度誘導型事前フュージョン（CGPF）を通じてマップデコーダーを制御するPriorMaskMapを提案する。
llm.result: nuScenesデータセットにおける評価により、PriorMaskMapは既存のアプローチを上回るマッピング精度を達成し、明らかなエラーを含む事前地図に対しても著しい堅牢性を示した。

2610.39280.title: Cross-Controller Transfer via In-Context Behavior Adaptation
2610.39280.abstract: Generalist robot policies increasingly learn from data collected across diverse tasks and embodiments, yet typically assume a single controller for each robot. This assumption limits transfer because different controllers can assign different physical meanings to the same action and may require different strategies to complete a task. We study how to transfer robot data across both embodiments and controllers without allowing conflicting action interpretations to interfere with learning. Our setting spans six controller types as well as variations in controller gains and compliance. We propose a framework that encodes behavioral interaction under a controller through examples of commanded actions and the resulting robot motions. A transformer context encoder summarizes these interactions, allowing a single policy to adapt in context. Across real-world experiments, our method improves average success by 33 percentage points over naive data pooling, achieves 50\% success on unseen controller modes and 52\% on unseen controller gains, and transfers to tasks with limited controller-specific data. On contact-rich tasks such as USB insertion and surface wiping, behavioral interaction context enables the policy to adapt not only its actions but also its strategy. Our results provide a path toward generalist robot policies that can leverage data collected across diverse action interpretations. For more information, visit \href{https://controller-transfer.github.io}{https://controller-transfer.github.io}.
2610.39280.tldr_en: This work proposes a framework that encodes behavioral interaction under a controller through examples of commanded actions and the resulting robot motions, allowing a single policy to adapt in context and provides a path toward generalist robot policies that can leverage data collected across diverse action interpretations.

llm.title_ja: 文脈内行動適応を通じたクロスコントローラー転移
llm.tldr_ja: コントローラー下の行動インタラクションを指令行動とロボット動作の例から符号化するフレームワークを提案し、多様な行動解釈から収集されたデータを汎用ロボットポリシーが活用できるようにする。
llm.problem: 異なるコントローラー間で同じ行動に異なる物理的意味が割り当てられるため、クロスembodiment・クロスコントローラーのデータ転移が制限される。
llm.method: コマンド行動と結果のロボット動作の例を通じてコントローラー下の行動インタラクションを符号化するフレームワークを提案し、Transformer文脈エンコーダーを用いる。
llm.result: 実世界実験において、ナイーブなデータプーリングと比較して平均成功率が33パーセントポイント向上し、未見のコントローラーモードで50%、未見のコントローラーゲインで52%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: クロスコントローラー

2610.39279.title: CuBot-STT: Simultaneously Transport and Tighten for Lattice-type Modular Reconfiguration Robot
2610.39279.abstract: Lattice-type modular reconfigurable robots rearrange standardized modules across tasks. Dedicated transport robots reduce module weight and cost by eliminating module level reconfiguration actuators. But existing systems use low capacity connections or internal fastening robots that occupy space for functional components. This paper presents CuBot-STT, which integrates module transport, interface locking, and release in one external robot. Cubic modules provide structural support and $24\,\mathrm{V}$ power distribution. On each face, a gear transmission converts one external input into motion of four helical locking points, preserving internal space. The robot uses alternating foot support, a gripper for module handling, and a tightening head for interface actuation. The controller coordinates two-foot support and module locking through continuous constraint transfers. The planner decomposes relocation costs into an analytical lower bound and a residual learned through expert-guided, goal conditioned Q-learning. Contact face $A^*$ search expands relocation sequences into robot primitives satisfying connectivity, asymmetric manipulation, and foot stance constraints. Experiments demonstrate normal and tangential interface capacities of $300\,\mathrm{N}$ and $490\,\mathrm{N}$, electrical continuity across six modules, and autonomous reconfiguration of an 11-module lattice. Planning benchmarks show superior search efficiency over analytical guidance and bidirectional heuristic search, with generalization beyond training lattice sizes without fine-tuning.
2610.39279.comment: 11 pages. Submitted to IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics

llm.title_ja: CuBot-STT：格子型モジュール再構成ロボットのための同時運搬・締結
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 既存の格子型モジュール再構成ロボットの専用運搬ロボットは、接続容量が低かったり、内部の締結用ロボットが機能部品のスペースを占有するという課題があった。
llm.method: モジュール運搬、インタフェースのロック、解放を1つの外部ロボットに統合したCuBot-STTを提案し、外部入力から4つの螺旋状ロックポイントの動きに変換するギア伝動機構を採用した。
llm.result: 300 Nおよび490 Nの法線・接線方向のインタフェース容量を実証し、11モジュールの格子を自律的に再構成することに成功した。

2610.39278.title: WorldFlow: Joint Video and 3D Motion Prediction via Large-Scale Pretraining
2610.39278.abstract: Predicting future physical states stands as a central challenge in embodied intelligence. Existing video world models leave 3D dynamics implicit, action-based formulations remain tied to specific robot configurations, and 3D motion prediction models use flow-only supervision, providing a limited learning signal for physical dynamics. To circumvent these limitations, we introduce \method{}, a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and query-based 3D trajectories. By parameterizing 3D motion as continuous displacement tokens aligned with the video grid, a unified Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone jointly denoises both modalities under a rectified-flow objective. This formulation couples explicit geometric dynamics with visual evolution, effectively unlocking the physical commonsense embedded within pretrained video models. To empirically scale and validate this unified architecture, we train \method{} on a heterogeneous mixture of 1.44 million object-level samples spanning simulated and real-world domains. We further introduce WorldFlowBench, comprising 1,678 evaluation samples from 11 data sources across simulated and real-world interactions, including spatial reasoning tasks. Across all three evaluation sets, WorldFlow achieves the lowest average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) among the evaluated learning-based methods. Notably, on the challenging SpatialCog set, WorldFlow achieves an ADE of 0.060 m, a 54.2\% reduction compared with the strongest external baseline. It also reduces ADE and FDE by 55.9\% and 68.5\%, respectively, compared with its flow-only variant. Project page: https://worldflow-rbs.github.io/.
2610.39278.tldr_en: WorldFlow achieves the lowest average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) among the evaluated learning-based methods, and is introduced as a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and query-based 3D trajectories.

llm.title_ja: WorldFlow: 大規模事前学習による動画と3Dモーションの共同予測
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の動画とクエリベースの3D軌跡を共同で予測する生成世界モデル「WorldFlow」を導入し、評価された学習ベースの手法の中で最も低い平均変位誤差（ADE）と最終変位誤差（FDE）を達成する。
llm.problem: 既存の動画世界モデルは3Dダイナミクスを暗黙のままにし、行動ベースの定式化は特定のロボット構成に縛られ、3Dモーション予測モデルはフローのみの教師信号に依存している。
llm.method: 連続変位トークンとして3Dモーションをパラメータ化し、統一されたMixture-of-Transformersバックボーンが整流フロー目的関数のもとで両方のモダリティを共同でノイズ除去する。
llm.result: SpatialCogセットにおいて、最強の外部ベースラインと比較して54.2%削減となる0.060 mのADEを達成し、フローのみのバリアントと比較してADEとFDEを大幅に削減した。

2610.39278.hf_summary_en: WorldFlow is a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and 3D trajectories using continuous displacement tokens and a Mixture-of-Transformers backbone, improving physical dynamics prediction across diverse benchmarks.

2610.39267.title: RAIBO-Wagon: Real-Time Navigation System for a Legged Robot Towing a Wagon
2610.39267.abstract: Legged robots have demonstrated advanced capabilities across a wide range of real-world tasks, yet much of this progress concerns the robot controlling only itself. Once the robot is coupled to an external object -- particularly an underactuated one -- the dynamics of the combined assembly become more complex. Towing a wagon is a common practical scenario, where coupled dynamics make reliable navigation challenging. This difficulty is amplified in confined spaces, where collision-free navigation requires finding a narrow set of feasible paths under strict real-time constraints. To address this, we propose a navigation framework that combines Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) with Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control over a learned Forward Dynamics Model (FDM). The CFM model mitigates the initialization problem of MPPI and accelerates its convergence, while MPPI with the FDM recovers feasible solutions beyond the CFM model's training distribution by iterative refinement. We integrate the framework into a full-stack navigation system for RAIBO-Wagon, a quadruped towing a custom wagon, and validate it in real-world outdoor experiments on 15 m-long courses through confined spaces, with all sensing and computation performed fully onboard. The system achieves an 85% success rate across 40 trials, towing a total load of up to 40 kg -- nearly 100% of RAIBO's body weight.
2610.39267.comment: 19 pages, 13 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://insungyang.github.io/raibo-wagon/
2610.39267.tldr_en: This work proposes a navigation framework that combines Conditional Flow Matching with Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control over a learned Forward Dynamics Model (FDM), and integrates the framework into a full-stack navigation system for RAIBO-Wagon, a quadruped towing a custom wagon.

llm.title_ja: RAIBO-Wagon：ワゴンを牽引する脚ロボットのためのリアルタイムナビゲーションシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 学習された順動力学モデルに対する条件付きフローマッチングとモデル予測パスインテグラル制御を組み合わせたナビゲーションフレームワークを提案し、カスタムワゴンを牽引する四足歩行ロボットのフルスタックシステムに統合する。
llm.problem: 外部の（特に低駆動の）オブジェクトに結合されたロボットは結合ダイナミクスが複雑化し、狭い空間での衝突回避ナビゲーションが困難になる。
llm.method: 条件付きフローマッチング（CFM）とモデル予測パスインテグラル（MPPI）制御を学習済み順動力学モデル（FDM）上で組み合わせたナビゲーションフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: RAIBOの体重のほぼ100%に達する最大40 kgの総負荷を牽引し、狭い空間を通る15mの屋外コースの試行において85%の成功率を達成した。

2610.39232.title: Seeing and Imagining as One: Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception for Embodied World Modeling
2610.39232.abstract: Embodied world models should not only imagine plausible futures, but also perceive the geometric, semantic, and motion structure of the evolving world. We present GenSight, a unified embodied world model that brings future video generation and dense perception into a single pretrained video diffusion transformer. GenSight uses a unified spatiotemporal representation for video, depth, embodiment segmentation, and first-frame-relative 2D flow. Built on a shared DiT backbone, GenSight uses lightweight task modulation to predict all modalities within the same architecture. All tasks are jointly optimized within a unified velocity prediction space. At inference, GenSight supports two complementary modes: multi-step future video generation with aligned dense predictions and single-step dense perception from an observed video. By unifying modality representation, model architecture, and prediction space, GenSight avoids separate modality-specific pipelines and couples appearance, geometry, semantics, and motion in a shared representation. It promotes cross-modal consistency and allows dense perception to benefit from the spatiotemporal priors learned through video generation. Trained on embodied manipulation data spanning multiple robot embodiments and human-hand interactions, GenSight demonstrates strong performance in both video generation and dense 4D perception, highlighting the effectiveness of unifying seeing and imagining for embodied world modeling.
2610.39232.tldr_en: GenSight is a unified embodied world model that brings future video generation and dense perception into a single pretrained video diffusion transformer and demonstrates strong performance in both video generation and dense 4D perception, highlighting the effectiveness of unifying seeing and imagining for embodied world modeling.

llm.title_ja: 見る事と想像する事の統合：具身世界モデリングのための統一動画生成と4D知覚
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の動画生成と高密度知覚を単一の事前学習済み動画拡散Transformerに統合した統一具身世界モデル「GenSight」を提案し、動画生成と4D知覚の両方で強力な性能を示す。
llm.problem: 具身世界モデルは、妥当な未来を想像するだけでなく、進化する世界の幾何学的、意味的、および運動学的構造を知覚する必要があるが、従来は別々のモダリティ特化型パイプラインを使用している。
llm.method: 動画、深度、具身セグメンテーション、および初フレーム相対2Dフローに統一された時空間表現を使用し、共有DiTバックボーンと軽量なタスク変調によって同じアーキテクチャ内で全モダリティを予測する。
llm.result: 複数のロボットembodimentと人間の手のインタラクションにわたる具身マニプリケーションデータで訓練され、動画生成と高密度4D知覚の両方で強力な性能を発揮した。

2610.39212.title: Event2Reward: Learning Robotic Rewards from Progress Relations
2610.39212.abstract: Learning task progress from robot demonstrations provides a practical way to construct dense shaping rewards for robotic reinforcement learning. A common approach uses normalized demonstration time as progress labels, implicitly assuming monotonically increasing task progress. During policy exploration, however, actual task progress can stall or even regress. Such models may mistake regressions for progress, assigning positive shaping rewards to actions that cause progress loss. Real suboptimal and failed executions offer corrective experience, but assigning absolute progress values to their states is difficult. Our key observation is that stalls, regressions, and recoveries establish local relative progress relations even when absolute progress is unknown. We introduce Event2Reward, which uses normalized temporal labels to anchor the progress scale and these within-trajectory relations to constrain local changes, combining absolute and relative progress supervision. Its progress predictions serve as potentials for reward shaping. We curate an event-annotated dataset from approximately 100K raw real-robot execution records, covering successful, suboptimal, and failed executions, without requiring framewise absolute progress labels. Under the same training budgets, Event2Reward improves average policy success by 18.16 percentage points over a baseline using only sparse task rewards across 40 tasks in four LIBERO suites. On real robots, average success after 30 minutes of wall-clock training reaches 60.0% on three precise insertion tasks and 90.0% on three object manipulation tasks, exceeding the sparse-reward baseline under the same budget by 36.7 and 23.3 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies further show that absolute progress supervision and relative progress relations are complementary, with joint supervision yielding better downstream policy learning.
2610.39212.tldr_en: This work curates an event-annotated dataset from approximately 100K raw real-robot execution records, covering successful, suboptimal, and failed executions, without requiring framewise absolute progress labels, to show that absolute progress supervision and relative progress relations are complementary, with joint supervision yielding better downstream policy learning.

llm.title_ja: Event2Reward：進展関係からのロボット報酬学習
llm.tldr_ja: 絶対的な進展ラベルを必要とせずに、成功、最適未満、および失敗の実行記録をカバーする約10万件の生の実機実行記録からイベント注釈付きデータセットを構築し、絶対的・相対的な進展の監視を組み合わせる。
llm.problem: ポリシー探索中、実際のタスク進展は停滞・後退することがあり、標準的な進展モデルは後退を進展と誤認して報酬を与えてしまう。
llm.method: 正規化された時間的ラベルで進展スケールを固定し、軌跡内の相対的関係で局所的変化を制約するEvent2Rewardを提案し、報酬シェーピングのポテンシャルとして活用する。
llm.result: LIBEROスイートの40タスクにおいて、スパース報酬のみのベースラインと比較して平均ポリシー成功率を18.16パーセントポイント向上させ、実機でも優れた成績を収めた。

2610.39180.title: EmbodiExp: Compositional Experience Transfer for Embodied Agents
2610.39180.abstract: Experience can help embodied agents turn high-level plans into grounded actions, but transferring it across tasks remains challenging: previously effective strategies may be inapplicable to the current state or fail to produce their intended outcomes. We present EmbodiExp, a framework for constructing transferable experiences and composing them online during embodied task execution. Our key observation is that tasks often share subgoals whose completion can be assessed independently of overall task success. We therefore introduce an outcome-grounded subgoal experience that specifies a subgoal, applicability conditions, an adaptable policy, and a verifiable outcome. During execution, applicable experiences guide action generation, while verified outcomes can establish the conditions required by subsequent experiences, enabling online composition. Subgoal-level outcome attribution further enables failure utilization: failed trajectories can still contribute verified local successes and condition-specific guidance on actions to avoid. Experiments on multiple embodied benchmarks under a fold-based protocol with frozen experience banks demonstrate the effectiveness of EmbodiExp.
2610.39180.tldr_en: EmbodiExp is presented, a framework for constructing transferable experiences and composing them online during embodied task execution that specifies a subgoal, applicability conditions, an adaptable policy, and a verifiable outcome.

llm.title_ja: EmbodiExp：具身エージェントのための構成的経験転移
llm.tldr_ja: サブゴール、適用条件、適応可能なポリシー、検証可能な成果を指定する、転移可能な経験の構築と実行中のオンライン構成のためのフレームワーク「EmbodiExp」を提案する。
llm.problem: 経験をタスク間で転移することは困難であり、以前有効だった戦略が現在の状態に適用できなかったり、意図した結果を生み出さないことがある。
llm.method: 成果に基づいたサブゴール経験を導入し、適用可能な経験が行動生成を導き、検証された成果が後続の経験に必要な条件を確立してオンライン構成を可能にする。
llm.result: 凍結された経験バンクを持つフォールドベースのプロトコル下で複数の具身ベンチマークにおける有効性を実証した。

2610.39167.title: EgoContact: Evaluating Physical Intelligence with Egocentric Video
2610.39167.abstract: Egocentric video has emerged as one of the most scalable sources of data for learning generalizable manipulation priors. Yet, despite its growing use in pretraining robotic policies, it has been underutilized as a validation tool for physical intelligence, a key component of which is understanding where to make contact with an object to achieve an intended interaction. We present EgoContact, a large-scale egocentric dataset for evaluating the generalizability and precision of learned manipulation priors through future contact-point prediction. EgoContact contains 22.5K manually verified interaction events, each with a pre-contact observation, semantic intent, and pixel-precise contact locations. We find that current methods often struggle to predict precise interaction contacts and sometimes fail to localize the target object in diverse, in-the-wild scenes, even when allowed multiple predictions. Furthermore, we demonstrate the usefulness of EgoContact's annotated interactions for robotic manipulation: simply using EgoContact as the memory bank of an existing affordance-transfer policy improves grasp success from 14.2% to 31.2% in simulation and from 16% to 58% on a real robot.
2610.39167.tldr_en: This work presents EgoContact, a large-scale egocentric dataset for evaluating the generalizability and precision of learned manipulation priors through future contact-point prediction, and demonstrates the usefulness of EgoContact's annotated interactions for robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: EgoContact：一人称視点動画による物理的知性の評価
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の接触点予測を通じて学習済みマニプリケーション事前学習の汎用性と精度を評価するための大規模一人称視点データセット「EgoContact」を提案し、ロボットマニプリケーションへの有用性を示す。
llm.problem: 一人称視点動画は汎用的なマニプリケーション事前学習のスケーラブルなデータ源として浮上しているが、意図したインタラクションのための接触点を理解する物理的知性の検証ツールとしては十分に活用されていない。
llm.method: 事前接触観測、意味的意図、ピクセル精度の接触位置を持つ22.5Kの手動検証済みインタラクションイベントを含むEgoContactデータセットを構築し、アフォーダンス転移ポリシーのメモリバンクとして利用する。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの把持成功率を14.2%から31.2%に、実機での成功率を16%から58%に向上させた。
llm.limitation: 要旨 in 記載なし

2610.39147.title: Kinematic Causal Attribution: Black-Box Explanations of Motion versus Geometry for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models
2610.39147.abstract: 4D perception models, which classify 3D point-cloud videos, are being built into robots, assistive monitoring and AR, yet before deploying one a practitioner cannot check which cue it relies on: how a body part moves, or what shape it has. 3D attribution is single-frame, video attribution is confined to RGB pixels, gradient maps need white-box access, attention is absent from state-space backbones, and point-level perturbations assume a point correspondence across frames that real depth and LiDAR data lack. We present Kinematic Causal Attribution (KCA), a black-box, interventional attribution method that queries only the model's outputs. Its freeze operator removes a region's motion while keeping its shape, and a shape-free proxy removes the shape while keeping the motion. Together they span a motion$\times$geometry cube for every tracked region, whose order-symmetric Shapley decomposition is complete and whose interaction is measured rather than assumed away. The operators rewrite per-frame point sets, so they need no correspondences, and a context-averaged estimator handles structures that span several regions. We validate KCA on the official PSTNet, P4Transformer and Mamba4D trained on MSR-Action3D. The decisive test is an audit: two binary tasks are built from real clips whose classes differ only in the motion or only in the shape of the same arm, and the motion share of the arm's importance follows the defining cue on all three backbones (0.83 vs. 0.60 on P4Transformer, 0.86 vs. 0.30 on PSTNet, 0.92 vs. 0.61 on Mamba4D), a distinction no single attribution map can make. The split costs no faithfulness: the necessity maps have the lowest deletion AUC on P4Transformer and PSTNet, tie with the best baseline on Mamba4D, and lose their correlation with the trained model's once the weights are randomised. Skeleton ground truth, re-sampling stability and cost complete the validation.
2610.39147.tldr_en: Kinematic Causal Attribution (KCA), a black-box, interventional attribution method that queries only the model's outputs, is presented and validated on the official PSTNet, P4Transformer and Mamba4D trained on MSR-Action3D.

llm.title_ja: 運動因果的アトリビューション：4D点群動画モデルのためのモーション対ジオメトリのブラックボックス説明
llm.tldr_ja: モデルの出力のみをクエリするブラックボックスな介入型アトリビューション手法であるKinematic Causal Attribution (KCA)を提案し、MSR-Action3Dで訓練された公式のPSTNet、P4Transformer、Mamba4Dで検証した。
llm.problem: 4D知覚モデルの予測根拠（動きか形状か）をデプロイ前に検証するブラックボックス手法が不足している。
llm.method: 形状を保持したまま動きを削除する操作と動きを保持したまま形状を削除する操作を組み合わせたKCAを提案する。
llm.result: 3つのバックボーンにおいて、腕の重要度の動きの割合が定義された手掛かりと一致することを示した。

2610.39126.title: Actuator-Aware Observer Inputs for Cascade ADRC of Quadrotors Under Rotor Lag, Measurement Delay and Sensor Noise
2610.39126.abstract: In sampled cascade linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) of quadrotors, the extended-state observer typically receives the instantaneous command, although the delayed measurement reflects an earlier, rotor-filtered acceleration. This paper proposes actuator-aware (AA) observer inputs: altitude and attitude observers use limited virtual inputs filtered by an assumed rotor model and aligned with the measurement delay, and horizontal observers use acceleration reconstructed from measured attitude. Fixed gains are selected on the discrete-time model under sensitivity and step-response requirements and stationary covariance ceilings on each channel's control variance and increment and on the noise-induced inner-loop increment of the full cascade. In paired set-point trials, PID-Budget, AA-Budget and AA-HalfGain reach mean RMSEs of 65.5, 19.2 and 16.9~mm; under a stricter common cascade ceiling, the AA designs reach 29.9 and 26.4~mm versus 72.3~mm for a PID that uses roughly double their rotor-command increment. PX4 software-in-the-loop runs reproduce these results. Behind EKF2, a noise model fitted to the estimation errors predicts the roll/pitch and yaw increments within 5\% on held-out and out-of-sample runs and the total rotor-command increment within 14\%. Redesigned for this stack under the same sensitivity and response specification and estimator-aware ceilings, AA-Budget-E reduces the set-point RMSE from 59.1~mm (PID-E) to 44.0~mm with a lower rotor-command increment in every paired set-point and lemniscate run (mean S6 rotor-command-increment reductions relative to PID-E: 45\% before and 15\% after output quantization); AA-HalfGain-E beats PID-E only on the lemniscate. The evidence is simulation-based, and the ceilings are nominal tuning constraints.
2610.39126.comment: 19 pages. MATLAB and PX4 SITL evaluation. Code, controller gains, random seeds, and per-seed results: https://github.com/Quang61123/actuator-aware-cascade-adrc

llm.title_ja: ロータ遅延、測定遅延、センサーノイズ下におけるクアッドローラのカスケードADRCのためのアクチュエータ認識型オブザーバ入力
llm.tldr_ja: クアッドローラのカスケードLADRCにおいて、測定遅延とロータフィルタに合わせたアクチュエータ認識型オブザーバ入力を提案し、シミュレーションで性能向上を示した。
llm.problem: サンプリングされたカスケード制御において、オブザーバが遅延した測定値に対して瞬時指令を受け取ることで性能が低下する。
llm.method: 仮定されたロータモデルでフィルタリングされ測定遅延に合わせた制限付き仮想入力をオブザーバに使用する。
llm.result: PID制御と比較して平均RMSEが大幅に削減され、追従性能が向上した。
llm.limitation: 証拠はシミュレーションベースであり、上限値は公称の同調制約である。

2610.39125.title: Tracking Task Progress Through Errors and Recovery:A Benchmark and Recurrent Distributional Model
2610.39125.abstract: Operational strategies for long-horizon robotic tasks require reliable evaluation to determine whether execution is progressing, stalling, regressing, or recovering from errors. Yet real- world robot datasets that capture error recovery and provide frame-level error annotations remain scarce. To address this gap, we introduce and open-source ReSTEP, a dataset of 3,156 episodes across two manipulation tasks with semantic stage labels and frame-level er- ror annotations. ReSTEP supports training and benchmarking progress monitors through successful execution, mistakes, and recovery. Existing progress estimators can struggle to distinguish visually similar task stages and maintain temporally consistent predictions while responding to genuine setbacks. We therefore propose REMORA, an online progress esti- mator that combines recurrent visual memory, distributional prediction, and causal peak selection. Memory retains execution history to help resolve visual ambiguity, while distribu- tional prediction represents alternative progress hypotheses and causal peak selection tracks a supported hypothesis over time. Together, these components enable consistent progress tracking that remains responsive to errors and recovery. Experiments on both ReSTEP tasks demonstrate that REMORA outperforms the state-of-the-art SARM baseline in progress ac- curacy and temporal consistency.
2610.39125.tldr_en: Recurrent visual memory retains execution history to help resolve visual ambiguity, while distributional prediction represents alternative progress hypotheses and causal peak selection tracks a supported hypothesis over time enable consistent progress tracking that remains responsive to errors and recovery.

llm.title_ja: エラーと回復を通じたタスク進捗の追跡：ベンチマークとリカレント分布モデル
llm.tldr_ja: リカレント視覚メモリ、分布予測、因果的ピーク選択を組み合わせ、エラーと回復に対応した一貫した進捗追跡を可能にするオンライン進捗推定器REMORAを提案する。
llm.problem: 実世界のロボットデータセットにおいてエラー回復やフレームレベルのエラーアノテーションが不足しており、既存手法は視覚的曖昧さに弱い。
llm.method: 実行履歴を保持する視覚メモリ、複数の進捗仮説を表す分布予測、因果的ピーク選択を組み合わせたREMORAを提案する。
llm.result: ReSTEPの2つのタスクにおいて、REMORAは進捗精度と時間的一貫性でSARMベースラインを上回った。

2610.39119.title: CAPTURER: A Dexterous Aerial Manipulator for Dynamic and Precise Grasping across Diverse Environments
2610.39119.abstract: As a representative form of embodied robotic interaction, aerial grasping requires close coordination between the aerial platform and manipulator. Most existing systems perform aerial grasping with static or slowly moving targets under fixed scenarios. Dynamic and precise grasping across different conditions introduces additional challenges, including target motion, localization drift, dynamic coupling, and external disturbances. In this work, we present CAPTURER, a dexterous aerial manipulator for centimeter-level grasping across diverse environments. To achieve the challenging goal, we first develop an onboard perception system for state estimation and target detection. Drift correction and global pose transformation are introduced to improve target localization during flight. A cooperative motion planner is proposed to coordinate the mobility of the aerial platform with the dexterity of the manipulator according to the relative target state. To maintain grasping accuracy under disturbances, we design a disturbance-rejection controller to compensate for dynamic coupling, model uncertainty, and external disturbances. The capability of CAPTURER is validated through indoor and outdoor experiments with both static and moving targets. The results demonstrate that CAPTURER achieves centimeter-level grasping accuracy for a marker pen measuring only 1.5 cm in diameter at flight speeds exceeding 1.5 m/s.
2610.39119.tldr_en: CATTURER, a dexterous aerial manipulator for centimeter-level grasping across diverse environments, is presented and a disturbance-rejection controller is designed to compensate for dynamic coupling, model uncertainty, and external disturbances.

llm.title_ja: CAPTURER：多様な環境における動的かつ精密な把持のための器用な空中マニピュレーター
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な環境でセンチメートル単位の把持を実現する器用な空中マニピュレーター「CAPTURER」を提案し、動的結合、モデルの不確かさ、外乱を補償する外乱除去コントローラーを設計する。
llm.problem: 空中把持は空中プラットフォームとマニピュレーターの密接な協調を必要とし、ターゲットの運動、局所化のドリフト、動的結合、外乱などの課題が存在する。
llm.method: オンボード知覚システムを開発し、ドリフト補正と大域的姿勢変換を導入し、空中プラットフォームの機動性とマニピュレーターの器用さを協調させる協調モーションプランナーと外乱除去コントローラーを設計する。
llm.result: わずか直径1.5cmマーカーペンに対して飛行速度1.5 m/s以上でセンチメートル単位の把持精度を達成した。
keywords_ja: 空中マニピュレーター

2610.39100.title: Generating Critic-Guided Synthetic Experience in Latent World Models
2610.39100.abstract: Learning from offline datasets is limited in scalability, as collecting new experience is often costly or unsafe in the real world. World models offer an alternative way to generate new experience through a learned dynamics model, yet learning policies in latent space is limited due to compounding errors in imagined rollouts. To this end, we propose using the world model as a local transition generator, leveraging critic guidance to choose actions inside that model to generate synthetic experiences. We study action refinement methodologies, introducing Critic-Guided Synthetic Experience (CGSE) generation in world models. Specifically, CGSE augments an existing offline dataset by sampling candidate actions using an offline policy and refining each to maximize a first-order approximation of the $Q$-function within a trust region. We then use a frozen latent world model to imagine the future state given each updated action, and use the critic to choose the best one, appending this synthetic transition to the replay buffer. Our method requires no additional real-environment interaction or test-time planner, as it generates synthetic experience offline using the world model. On three OGBench manipulation tasks, CGSE improves an offline policy by a relative improvement of $7.1\%$ on the average success rate.
2610.39100.tldr_en: This work introduces Critic-Guided Synthetic Experience (CGSE) generation in world models, using the world model as a local transition generator, leveraging critic guidance to choose actions inside that model to generate synthetic experiences offline.

llm.title_ja: 潜在世界モデルにおける批評家ガイダンス付き合成経験の生成
llm.tldr_ja: 世界モデルをローカル遷移ジェネレータとして使用し、オフラインで合成経験を生成するために批評家のガイダンスを活用するCritic-Guidence Synthetic Experience (CGSE)を導入した。
llm.problem: オフラインデータセットからの学習は拡張性が制限され、実世界での新しい経験の収集はコストがかかるか危険である。
llm.method: オフラインポリシーを用いて候補行動をサンプリングし、Q関数の一次近似を最大化するように洗練させて世界モデルで未来の状態を予測するCGSEを提案する。
llm.result: 3つのOGBenchマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、オフラインポリシーの平均成功率を相対的に7.1%改善した。

2610.39076.title: Tactus: Tactile & Pose Sensing Glove for Natural Dexterity Data Collection
2610.39076.abstract: Collecting naturalistic human manipulation demonstrations with accurate contact force and hand pose is essential for robot dexterous manipulation policy and foundational world model learning - yet no existing wearable platform provides both calibrated fingertip force sensing and occlusion-resilient hand tracking in a form factor that preserves natural manipulation behavior. We present Tactus, a textile-integrated sensing glove that co-optimizes three design pillars: (1) a thin, conformal 3D-knit form factor (1.5 mm fingertip stackup) designed to minimize interference with natural manipulation, (2) strategically placed capacitive tactile sensors at manipulation-relevant regions informed by empirical contact studies, and (3) IMU-fused pose tracking that maintains accuracy through the hand-object occlusions where manipulation data is most valuable. Tactus includes a documented calibration pipeline for cross-glove consistency and per-session calibration for subject-dependent correction. To enable objective comparison, we introduce standardized benchmarking protocols for tactile force regression and hand pose estimation, and apply them to Tactus and two commercially available tactile gloves - to our knowledge the first quantitative cross-platform evaluation of this kind. Tactus resolves a minimum detectable force of 0.59 N at 95% confidence, 1.6 - 2.7x lower than the commercial baselines, and with 0.87 cross-participant consistency, while our pose tracking sustains 11.0 mm fingertip keypoint relative error during manipulation, when occlusion is heaviest. We show that these combined signals support object property estimation, slip detection, and representative recording of hand-object interaction - yielding demonstration data with the fidelity required for contact-aware manipulation policies and world models.
2610.39076.tldr_en: Tactus is presented, a textile-integrated sensing glove that co-optimizes three design pillars: a thin, conformal 3D-knit form factor, strategically placed capacitive tactile sensors at manipulation-relevant regions informed by empirical contact studies, and IMU-fused pose tracking that maintains accuracy through the hand-object occlusions where manipulation data is most valuable.

llm.title_ja: Tactus：自然な器用さのデータ収集のための触覚・姿勢センシンググローブ
llm.tldr_ja: 薄型の3Dニット形状、戦略的に配置された容量性触覚センサー、オクルージョン耐性を持つIMU融合姿勢追跡を統合したテキスタイル統合型センシンググローブTactusを提案した。
llm.problem: 正確な接触力と手姿勢を捉える自然な人間の操作デプロイメントの収集が、ロボットの器用な操作ポリシーや世界モデルの学習に不可欠であるが存在しない。
llm.method: 薄型3Dニット形状、接触研究に基づく触覚センサー配置、IMU融合ポーズトラッキングを組み合わせたグローブを開発した。
llm.result: 0.59 Nの最小検出力と高精度なポーズトラッキングを実現し、接触認識マニピュレーションのための高品質なデモンストレーションデータを取得できることを示した。

2610.39055.title: Controlling Continuum Robot Shape in Enclosed Space with Embedded Sensing using IMU and Actuator Feedback
2610.39055.abstract: Controlling continuum robots' shape to operate in confined, enclosed environments is challenging, since it cannot rely on external observation. Existing embedded shape sensing methods, although they can provide shape reconstruction, are insufficient to enable real-time shape control due to limitations in reconstruction accuracy, computational speed, and compatibility with shape-state representation. In this work, we present an embedded shape-sensing framework that uses readily available IMU and actuator feedback to reconstruct the continuum-robot shape with a neural network, providing accurate shape feedback at $400~\mathrm{Hz}$ for physical closed-loop control. We systematically investigate four key reconstruction design choices: shape-state representation, network architecture, training objective, and sensing inputs, through more than $5{,}000$ trained models on one- and three-segment continuum robots. The selected framework achieves global shape errors of $0.9\%L$ and $1.7\%L$ (of the robot length) for the one- and three-segment systems, respectively. In closed-loop control, one-segment tip tracking achieves a $6.1\%L$ error and three-segment shape control achieves a $2.3\%L$ global shape error, whereas IMU--PCC reconstruction using the same uncompensated measurements fails. Enclosed-space experiments further demonstrate operation without external observation. These results provide a practical framework for translating readily available embedded sensing into high-rate feedback for continuum robot closed-loop control.
2610.39055.tldr_en: This work presents an embedded shape-sensing framework that uses readily available IMU and actuator feedback to reconstruct the continuum-robot shape with a neural network, providing accurate shape feedback at $400~\mathrm{Hz}$ for physical closed-loop control.

llm.title_ja: IMUとアクチュエータフィードバックを用いた埋め込みセンシングによる閉鎖空間内での連続体ロボット形状制御
llm.tldr_ja: 利用可能なIMUとアクチュエータフィードバックを用いてニューラルネットワークで連続体ロボットの形状を再構築し、400 Hzでの正確な形状フィードバックを提供する埋め込み形状センシングフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 外部観察に依存できない閉鎖空間内で連続体ロボットの形状を制御することは、再構築の精度や計算速度の限界から困難である。
llm.method: 形状状態表現、ネットワークアーキテクチャ、学習目的、センシング入力を最適化した埋め込み形状センシングフレームワークを開発した。
llm.result: 1セグメントおよび3セグメントシステムにおいて、それぞれ0.9%Lおよび1.7%Lのグローバル形状誤差を達成し、物理的閉鎖空間での閉ループ制御を実現した。
keywords_ja: ニューラルネットワーク

2610.39054.title: Robotic Data Inoculation
2610.39054.abstract: Modern robot learning systems feed on high-quality demonstration data, and their performance hinges on coverage. Without good coverage, small errors compound and the policy can quickly go into out-of-distribution states from which it cannot recover. Yet there is no principled way of collecting high-coverage data, and data collection often relies on heuristic instructions to human operators. Purely online reinforcement learning (RL) explores at the cost of safety and sample efficiency, while DAgger-style interventions require the policy to fail by chance before a human can correct it. In this paper, we ask instead whether we can modify how the robot behaves during data collection to collect more useful data. We propose Data Inoculation (DI), a shared-control framework in which a human provide closed-loop teleoperation commands while a residual policy perturbs these commands. The residual policy is trained online, on the growing dataset, with the same reward-maximizing objective later used for policy extraction, so its perturbations steer data collection toward the deviations a policy trained on the data would make. These perturbations expose the robot to a wider range of states, while the human's continuous corrections provide recovery demonstrations, "inoculating" the dataset against the learner's future mistakes while the human remains in control. On three challenging real-world robotic tasks, DI consistently improves or matches the success rate of policies trained with both behavioral cloning and offline RL, showing DI as an effective data collection strategy for improving downstream policy performance.
2610.39054.tldr_en: Data Inoculation (DI), a shared-control framework in which a human provide closed-loop teleoperation commands while a residual policy perturbs these commands, is proposed, showing DI as an effective data collection strategy for improving downstream policy performance.

llm.title_ja: ロボットデータ接種（Data Inoculation）
llm.tldr_ja: 人間が閉ループの遠隔操作コマンドを提供し、残余ポリシーがそれらを摂動させる共有制御フレームワークであるData Inoculation (DI)を提案し、下流ポリシーの性能向上を示す。
llm.problem: 高品質な網羅的データ収集に原則的な方法がなく、純粋なオンライン強化学習は安全性とサンプル効率を犠牲にし、DAggerスタイルは失敗に依存する。
llm.method: 成長するデータセット上で報酬最大化目的に従ってオンラインで訓練された残余ポリシーが人間の遠隔操作コマンドを摂動させる共有制御フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 3つの困難な実世界のロボットタスクにおいて、行動クローンおよびオフライン強化学習で訓練されたポリシーの成功率を継続的に改善または一致させた。

2610.39044.title: Catch It All!: Generalizable Dynamic Catching with a Dexterous Hand
2610.39044.abstract: Catching arbitrary objects requires generalization to novel projectiles and real-time adaptation to unpredictable contact dynamics under noisy visual observations. This paper presents Catch It All!, a sim-to-real catching framework for humanoid robots that generalizes and adapts to unseen objects with variable physical properties for underhand and overhand catches, using only one egocentric camera. We learn policies which generalize to unseen objects with varying geometry, deformability, elasticity, and physical properties. Effective grasps which adapt real-time to object poses and shapes are learned through careful grasp reward design. We provide safety-aware curricula which enable safe, high-frequency action execution near hardware limits, including wrist torque limits as low as 5 Nm. We validate our system by deploying zero-shot on a Unitree G1. With only one egocentric camera, Catch It All! successfully performs underhand and overhand catches on 9 unseen objects not seen during training, including low-rebound plushes, semi-deformable toys and chip bags, and rigid-elastic objects with high rebound on contact.
2610.39044.tldr_en: Catch It All!, a sim-to-real catching framework for humanoid robots that generalizes and adapts to unseen objects with variable physical properties for underhand and overhand catches, using only one egocentric camera is presented.

llm.title_ja: 全てをキャッチせよ！：器用な手を用いた汎化可能な動的キャッチング
llm.tldr_ja: 1台の視点カメラのみを使用し、多様な物理的性質を持つ未知の物体に対してアンダーハンドおよびオーバーハンドのキャッチングを行う、ヒューマノイドロボット向けのシム2リアルキャッチングフレームワークCatch It All!を提案する。
llm.problem: 任意の物体のキャッチングには、未知の飛翔体への汎化と、ノイズの多い視覚観測下での予測不可能な接触ダイナミクスへのリアルタイム適応が必要である。
llm.method: ジオメトリ、変形性、弾性などの多様な物理特性を持つ未知物体に汎化するポリシーを学習し、慎重に設計された把持報酬と安全性を考慮したカリキュラムを導入する。
llm.result: Unitree G1にゼロショットでデプロイし、訓練時に見ていない9つの未知の物体に対してアンダーハンドおよびオーバーハンドのキャッチングに成功した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.39005.title: Self-Supervised Doppler-Guided RF Odometry
2610.39005.abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) sensing enables robot ego-motion estimation in darkness, smoke, and fog, yet RF odometry remains challenging because multipath and moving reflectors make cross-frame matching highly ambiguous. Existing methods often rely on auxiliary inertial sensors or ground-truth pose supervision. We present RFWalk, a self-supervised, RF-only odometry framework that models dense correspondences across range-azimuth frames as random walks on a space-time graph and learns them from unlabeled sequences through temporal cycle consistency. To rule out correspondences that are cycle-consistent but physically implausible, we introduce a Doppler consistency loss that constrains correspondence-induced motion using radial velocity measured by the RF sensor itself. Ego-motion is then recovered through robust $\mathrm{SE}(2)$ registration that suppresses uncertain correspondences and those arising from independently moving objects. Without pose labels or auxiliary sensors, RFWalk remains competitive with supervised baselines in static scenes and reduces absolute trajectory error by 58% in dynamic scenes with moving pedestrians.
2610.39005.tldr_en: RFWalk is presented, a self-supervised, RF-only odometry framework that models dense correspondences across range-azimuth frames as random walks on a space-time graph and learns them from unlabeled sequences through temporal cycle consistency.

llm.title_ja: 自己教師ありドップラー誘導型RFオドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 範囲・方位フレーム間の高密度対応を時空グラフ上のランダムウォークとしてモデル化し、時間的サイクル一貫性を通じてラベルなしシーケンスから学習する自己教師ありRFオドメトリフレームワークRFWalkを提案する。
llm.problem: マルチパスや移動する反射物のためにクロスフレームマッチングが非常に曖昧になり、RFオドメトリの推定が困難である。
llm.method: 時間的サイクル一貫性を用いて対応関係を学習し、RFセンサー自体のラジアル速度を利用するドップラー一貫性損失を導入してロバストなSE(2)登録により自己モーションを復元する。
llm.result: 静的シーンで教師ありベースラインと同等の性能を維持し、動的シーンでの絶対軌跡誤差を58%削減した。

2610.38993.title: Open-World Object Motion Anticipation via Meta-Learned Semantic Adaptation
2610.38993.abstract: Anticipating the motion of nearby objects is critical for safe and efficient robot navigation. Without a proper understanding of what may move, a robot may plan overly conservative, inefficient trajectories to guarantee safety, or it may be overly risky, resulting in unacceptable collisions. While tracking and predicting the motion of known objects has seen significant progress, little research addresses how a robot should adapt online to novel objects, including anticipating how one object may move another (e.g., a person operating a forklift to move a pallet). To enable this capability, we propose a meta-learned graph neural network that leverages a semantic, geometric, and relational history of objects to accurately predict, from a few online observations, when objects will begin to move in new environments. We demonstrate that our method, which is trained only in simulation, accurately anticipates the motion of objects unseen at training time, transfers to hardware without any fine-tuning, and outperforms a vision-language model and a class-frequency baseline in both simulation and hardware experiments. Our method's accurate prediction enables collision-free traversals in a closed-loop navigation simulation, while remaining within four seconds of the fastest, collision-prone planner.
2610.38993.tldr_en: A meta-learned graph neural network is proposed that accurately anticipates the motion of objects unseen at training time, transfers to hardware without any fine-tuning, and outperforms a vision-language model and a class-frequency baseline in both simulation and hardware experiments.

llm.title_ja: メタ学習された意味的適応によるオープンワールドの物体運動予測
llm.tldr_ja: 数回のオンライン観測から新しい環境で物体がいつ動き始めるかを正確に予測するために、物体の意味的・幾何学的・関係的履歴を活用するメタ学習型グラフニューラルネットワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットが安全かつ効率的にナビゲーションを行うためには近くの物体の動きを予測することが重要だが、新規物体へのオンライン適応に関する研究は少ない。
llm.method: 物体の意味的、幾何学的、関係的履歴を活用し、数回のオンライン観測から新規環境での物体の動き開始を正確に予測するメタ学習型グラフニューラルネットワークを構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションのみで訓練されながら、訓練時に未見の物体の動きを正確に予測し、微調整なしでハードウェアに転移でき、シミュレーションおよび実機実験でベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: グラフニューラルネットワーク
ロボットナビゲーション

2610.38967.title: Learning Event-based Obstacle Avoidance via Differentiable Simulation
2610.38967.abstract: Reliable obstacle avoidance is essential for safe quadrotor flight in unknown environments, yet conventional frame-based cameras remain challenged by motion blur, limited dynamic range, and latency under fast motion. Event cameras, with sub-millisecond latency, high dynamic range, and negligible motion blur, offer a promising alternative, but leveraging them for closed-loop control remains difficult. Existing approaches either adopt cascaded architectures that first estimate depth and then map it to control commands, introducing error propagation, or achieve end-to-end control through costly offline pretraining before online fine-tuning can even begin. We address these challenges with a CUDA-based event simulator that exploits GPU parallelism to render events efficiently within the training loop, integrated into a differentiable simulation pipeline that enables direct gradient backpropagation through the differentiable physics model, improving sample efficiency. This allows us to train an end-to-end policy that maps event frames directly to control commands, without intermediate depth estimation. We validate our approach through zero-shot real-world deployment on a quadrotor, achieving robust obstacle avoidance in both odometry-assisted and odometry-free settings, including under low-light conditions where conventional cameras typically fail.
2610.38967.tldr_en: This work develops a CUDA-based event simulator that exploits GPU parallelism to render events efficiently within the training loop, integrated into a differentiable simulation pipeline that enables direct gradient backpropagation through the differentiable physics model, improving sample efficiency.

llm.title_ja: 微分可能シミュレーションを用いたイベントベース障害物回避の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 訓練ループ内でイベントを効率的にレンダリングするCUDAベースのイベントシミュレータを開発し、中間深度推定なしでイベントフレームを制御コマンドに直接マッピングするエンドツーエンドポリシーの訓練を実現した。
llm.problem: イベントカメラを用いた閉ループ制御において、従来のカスケーデッドアーキテクチャは誤差伝播を引き起こし、エンドツーエンド制御は多大な事前学習コストを要する。
llm.method: GPU並列処理を活用するCUDAベースのイベントシミュレータを微分可能なシミュレーションパイプラインに統合し、勾配逆伝播によるサンプル効率の向上を図る。
llm.result: クアッドローラのゼロショット実機展開を通じて、オドメトリ補助の有無に関わらず、低照度環境を含むロバストな障害物回避を達成した。
keywords_ja: 微分可能シミュレーション

2610.38930.title: Selective Sliding Mode Control Enhances Robustness of Aerial Robots Under Disturbances
2610.38930.abstract: Quadrotor control under disturbances such as wind gusts and payload variations remains challenging. First-order sliding mode control (SMC) and matched/unmatched uncertainty distinction are classical approaches; however, neither tells a practitioner which loops in a cascaded controller should be made robust to sustain disturbances, how to tune those loops, nor what the additional costs are on an embedded processor. Applying robust control uniformly across all axes addresses disturbances indiscriminately, adding tuning effort on axes where no disturbance acts. On inherently underactuated vehicles, disturbances along some axes cannot be opposed directly at all. We propose a principled methodology for deciding where robust control belongs in a cascaded architecture, with all control running onboard the vehicle. We recover the acting disturbance from PID hover flights under disturbance by inverting the equations of motion, use the recovered signal to identify and quantify the excited axes, and deploy robust control where it counts. Experiments on a Crazyflie 2.1 quadrotor under slung-payload and oblique-wind disturbances show tracking improvements concentrated on the axes the rule selects, and gain sweeps confirm that the switching gain reduces error on matched axes but has no effect on an excited unmatched axis, as the analysis predicts.

llm.title_ja: 選択的スライディングモード制御による外乱下での空中ロボットのロバスト性向上
llm.tldr_ja: PIDホバリングフライトから外乱を逆算して励起された軸を特定し、カスケード構造内のどこにロバスト制御を配置すべきかを決定する原則的手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 外乱に対する一様なロバスト制御の適用は不要な同調労力を生み、アンダーステアな車両ではすべての軸の外乱に直接対抗できない。
llm.method: 運動方程式の反転により外乱を復元し、励起された軸を定量化して選択的にロバスト制御を適用する。
llm.result: Crazyflie 2.1クアッドローラを用いた実験で、選択された軸に集中した追従性の向上を確認した。
keywords_ja: スライディングモード制御

2610.38901.title: Geometric Time Score Estimators: Bridging Self-Predictive Representations and Generative Occupancy Models For Reinforcement Learning
2610.38901.abstract: In reinforcement learning (RL), temporal reasoning is essential for estimating the density of future outcomes under a policy's occupancy measure. While self-predictive representations have been a dominant paradigm for occupancy density estimation, we find that they yield surprisingly poor estimates. On the other hand, generative occupancy models can produce remarkably accurate samples from the occupancy measure. Yet, they cannot easily recover occupancy densities, limiting their use for control despite their expressivity. In this paper, we propose Geometric Time Score Estimators (GTSE), a framework that bridges the two paradigms by learning occupancy density estimators along probability paths. We analyze how GTSE implicitly induces better occupancy estimators through improved representation learning and show how to directly extract self-predictive representations from this framework. Through experiments across several locomotion and manipulation tasks, we show that GTSE improves performance over state-of-the-art methods by $2\times$ to $6\times$ in goal-conditioned RL settings, and that the representations learned using our framework transfer effectively to downstream RL tasks. Website: https://aravindvenu7.github.io/website/gtse/
2610.38901.tldr_en: Geometric Time Score Estimators is proposed, a framework that bridges the two paradigms by learning occupancy density estimators along probability paths and improves performance over state-of-the-art methods by $2\times$ to $6\times$ in goal-conditioned RL settings, and that the representations learned using this framework transfer effectively to downstream RL tasks.

llm.title_ja: 幾何学的時間スコア推定量：強化学習における自己予測表現と生成型占有モデルの架け橋
llm.tldr_ja: 確率経路に沿って占有密度推定量子を学習することで2つのパラダイムを橋渡しするGeometric Time Score Estimators (GTSE)を提案し、ゴール条件付き強化学習タスクにおいて性能を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 強化学習において自己予測表現は占有密度推定に劣り、生成型占有モデルは正確なサンプルの生成はできるが占有密度を容易に復元できない。
llm.method: 確率経路に沿って占有密度推定器を学習し、表現学習を改善するGeometric Time Score Estimators (GTSE)を提案する。
llm.result: いくつかの移動および操作タスクにおいて、ゴール条件付きRL設定で最先端手法を2倍から6倍上回る性能改善を示した。

2610.38888.title: Inertial Steering and Motion Prediction of Tracked Vehicles on Low-Adherence Surfaces
2610.38888.abstract: Tracked vehicles are widely used in off-road applications, but their conventional motion models often rely on no-slip assumptions that become inaccurate on low-adherence surfaces. Rather than treating inertial effects arising from slip as a disturbance to be minimized, this work investigates how inertial effects arising from a moving mass can be deliberately exploited for steering on low-friction surfaces. A dynamic model for an articulated tracked vehicle with a passive trailer is developed, allowing inertial effects from trailer motion to be captured. The approach is experimentally evaluated on ice, where our dynamic model outperforms the kinematic baseline. We also propose a mixed dynamic-kinematic model to adapt predictions to both surface and situation by exploiting predictions from both methods. Finally, we demonstrate inertial steering on a mono-track vehicle without a conventional steering mechanism, showing that controlled movements of an internal mass can generate turning motion on ice. The resulting behavior can be predicted using the proposed dynamic model by representing the internal mass as a frictionless trailer, revealing the analogous dynamics between the two configurations. These results demonstrate the feasibility of inertial steering as an alternative steering mechanism for tracked vehicles operating in low-adherence environments.

llm.title_ja: 低付着表面におけるクローラ車両の慣性ステアリングとモーション予測
llm.tldr_ja: 受動的トレーラを持つ関節式クローラ車両の動的モデルを開発し、氷上の低摩擦表面において移動質量の慣性効果を意図的に利用したステアリング手法を実験的に評価した。
llm.problem: クローラ車両の従来のモーションモデルはスリップなしの仮定に依存しており、低付着表面では不正確になる。
llm.method: 移動質量からの慣性効果を捉える関節式クローラ車両の動的モデルを開発し、氷上での実験および混合動的・運動学的モデルを提案する。
llm.result: 動的モデルが従来の運動学的ベースラインを上回り、内部質量の制御された動きにより氷上で旋回運動を生成できることを示した。

2610.38867.title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
2610.38867.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly adopted in long-horizon tasks and interact with diverse external environments. Despite their growing capabilities, these agents remain vulnerable to real-world attacks such as indirect prompt injections, which manipulate agents through malicious instructions embedded in external environments. While existing risk assessment work has primarily focused on the injection content, the effect of where an injection appears has not been systematically characterized. Studying injection placement requires agents to operate over longer-horizon tasks and interact with diverse environmental surfaces. Thus, we build three agentic testbeds spanning tool use, coding, and daily workflow domains with diverse injection surfaces. Holding the injection content fixed, we find that agent susceptibility varies across injection placements. We refer to this phenomenon as the trust region effect: agents implicitly assign different levels of trust to different regions of their environments. For example, an agent powered by GPT-5.4 follows an unsafe injection instruction placed in a repository documentation file (i.e., a README or TODO file) 2.6 times more often on average than the same instruction placed in a code or data file. Building upon this observation, we develop learning-based attackers that generate injection content and select better injection placements. Our approach demonstrates that both where an injection is placed and what content it contains can affect the strength of indirect prompt injection attacks. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first systematic characterization for the effectiveness of different injection placements, spanning both coarse-grained environmental surfaces and fine-grained positions. The uneven trust that agents implicitly place across their environments provides important insights for future attack and defense design.
2610.38867.tldr_en: This work provides the first systematic characterization for the effectiveness of different injection placements, spanning both coarse-grained environmental surfaces and fine-grained positions, and develops learning-based attackers that generate injection content and select better injection placements.

llm.title_ja: 注入場所の重要性：LLMエージェントにおける信頼領域効果
llm.tldr_ja: LLMエージェントが環境内の異なる場所に対して暗黙的に異なるレベルの信頼を割り当てる「信頼領域効果」を体系的に明らかにし、学習ベースの攻撃者を開発した。
llm.problem: LLMエージェントは外部環境の悪意ある指示による間接的プロンプトインジェクションに脆弱であるが、注入位置の効果は体系的に特徴づけられていなかった。
llm.method: ツール使用、コーディング、日常ワークフローにまたがる3つのエージェントテストベッドを構築し、インジェクションの配置と内容の効果を分析した。
llm.result: エージェントの脆弱性がインジェクションの配置によって異なることを示し、不正な命令に従う頻度が配置場所によって大きく変わることを発見した。
keywords_ja: プロンプトインジェクション

2610.38793.title: Trustworthy Distributed Machine Learning in Cloud-Edge-IoT Systems: A Heterogeneity-Aware Survey of Security, Privacy, and Robustness
2610.38793.abstract: Distributed machine learning (DML), including conventional distributed training and federated learning (FL), enables collaborative model development across cloud-edge-IoT systems without fully centralizing raw data. However, distributing data, computation, updates, and orchestration increases the attack surface and introduces coupled challenges across privacy, robustness, reliability, fairness, and governance. This survey presents a security-centered, heterogeneity-aware roadmap for trustworthy DML, with FL treated as a prominent high-risk case. We first characterize the assets, adversaries, trust assumptions, and coordination patterns that define DML/FL security boundaries. We then analyze how statistical, system, and trust heterogeneity, including non-IID data, resource asymmetry, intermittent participation, and cross-silo/cross-device trust differences, affect convergence, fairness, attack detectability, and defense reliability. Next, we synthesize attack-defense interactions across poisoning, backdoors, Byzantine manipulation, privacy leakage, model extraction, network/orchestration attacks, Sybil behavior, and strategic participation. We further compare layered defenses, including robust aggregation, drift-aware optimization, differential privacy, secure aggregation, homomorphic encryption, secure multiparty computation, trusted execution environments, watermarking, provenance, authenticated communication, and monitoring. Finally, we discuss deployment, evaluation, governance, and open research guidelines, emphasizing reproducible, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) partitions, attack-aware benchmarks, privacy budgets, attack success rate, client-level disparity, latency, communication, memory, energy/carbon overhead, and auditable lifecycle artifacts.
2610.38793.tldr_en: This survey presents a security-centered, heterogeneity-aware roadmap for trustworthy DML, with FL treated as a prominent high-risk case and how statistical, system, and trust heterogeneity, including non-IID data, resource asymmetry, intermittent participation, and cross-silo/cross-device trust differences, affect convergence, fairness, attack detectability, and defense reliability.

llm.title_ja: クラウド・エッジ・IoTシステムにおける信頼性の高い分散機械学習：セキュリティ、プライバシー、ロバスト性の不均一性を考慮したサーベイ
llm.tldr_ja: クラウド・エッジ・IoTシステムにおける分散機械学習のセキュリティ、プライバシー、ロバスト性に関する課題と対策を、統計的・システム的・信頼性の不均一性を軸に体系的にサーベイした。
llm.problem: 分散機械学習におけるデータの分散や計算の非中央集権化により、攻撃対象領域が広がり、プライバシーやロバスト性の課題が生じる。
llm.method: アセット、攻撃者、信頼の仮定を定義し、統計的・システム的・信頼性の不均一性が及ぼす影響を分析した上で、各種の防御策を比較・統合する。
llm.result: 分散機械学習における信頼性向上のためのロードマップを提示し、攻撃耐性やプライバシー保護の手法を整理した。
keywords_ja: フェデレーテッドラーニング

2610.38744.title: AtomTree: A Hierarchical Framework for State-Aware Embodied Instruction Following with LLMs
2610.38744.abstract: Embodied instruction following in interactive environments requires agents to interpret natural language commands and complete long-horizon tasks. Existing planners either rely on large labeled trajectories, or use few-shot and zero-shot LLM prompting that produces a whole plan in a single serial reasoning process. These approaches depend on linguistic common sense, commit to a plan from the initial instruction, and only update after failures, which weakens robustness and state awareness. We present AtomTree, a hierarchical framework for state-aware task planning with LLMs. AtomTree incrementally builds a tree of subgoals and actions, where the LLM decides at each step, from the current symbolic state, whether to further decompose or to output a grounded low-level action. A lightweight memory module summarizes past outcomes for reuse in later decisions. When a low-level action stalls, AtomTree triggers hierarchical backtracking replanning to return to the parent node and regenerate the subtree plan from the latest state, preventing continued drift along an incorrect trajectory. In zero-shot evaluation on the ALFRED benchmark, AtomTree outperforms prior LLM-based planners. Project page: https://zhaihaotian.github.io/atomtree-website/.
2610.38744.tldr_en: AtomTree is presented, a hierarchical framework for state-aware task planning with LLMs that incrementally builds a tree of subgoals and actions, where the LLM decides at each step, from the current symbolic state, whether to further decompose or to output a grounded low-level action.

llm.title_ja: AtomTree：LLMを用いた状態認識型・身体性指示追従のための階層的フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: LLMを使用してサブゴールとアクションの木をインクリメンタルに構築し、階層的バックトラッキングにより誤った軌道からの逸脱を防ぐAtomTreeを提案する。
llm.problem: インタラクティブな環境での身体性指示追従において、既存の計画手法は単一の逐次推論プロセスに依存し、失敗するまで計画を更新しないため頑健性と状態認識が弱い。
llm.method: LLMが現在のシンボル状態からさらに分解するか低レベルアクションを出力するかを各ステップで決定し、階層的な木の構造を構築するAtomTreeを提案する。
llm.result: ALFREDベンチマークのゼロショット評価において、既存のLLMベースのプランナーを上回る性能を示した。

2610.38731.title: Value Function-Guided MPPI for Hierarchical Planning and Control in Off-Road Autonomous Navigation
2610.38731.abstract: Autonomous navigation in off-road terrain is commonly achieved using hierarchical control and planning architectures that rely on explicit cost maps and one-way information flow from a high-level planner to a low-level controller, decoupling planning from the true execution cost experienced during control. We propose a hierarchical planning and control framework in which information flows bidirectionally, allowing the low-level controller to guide trajectory selection at the planning level. The highest level of the hierarchy is a Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control-style planner that determines optimal trajectories and passes these waypoints to a pretrained low-level reinforcement learning (RL) controller. Rather than drawing from an explicit cost map, our MPPI planner leverages the value function of the RL controller as an implicit cost representation. In this formulation, MPPI serves as a trajectory exploration mechanism, while the low-level controller's value function guides the search. To account for the distribution shift seen by the value function between training and evaluation, we propose an online policy evaluation process that adapts the value function to unseen driving experiences, and we demonstrate this adaptation in unseen off-road simulation environments. We evaluate our approach in a high-fidelity off-road driving simulator across a range of challenging terrain conditions and compare its performance against a baseline MPPI controller. The results demonstrate that our method achieves safer and more effective navigation to goal locations while eliminating the need for explicit cost maps and enabling tighter coupling between planning and control.
2610.38731.tldr_en: This work proposes a hierarchical planning and control framework in which information flows bidirectionally, allowing the low-level controller to guide trajectory selection at the planning level, and proposes an online policy evaluation process that adapts the value function to unseen driving experiences.

llm.title_ja: オフロード自律ナビゲーションにおける階層的計画と制御のための価値関数誘導型MPPI
llm.tldr_ja: 低レベルの強化学習コントローラの価値関数を暗黙のコスト表現として利用し、計画レベルでの軌道選択を双方向の情報の流れで導く階層的計画・制御フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: オフロード地形での自律ナビゲーションは明示的なコストマップと一方向の情報流に依存しており、計画と制御の実行コストが切り離されている。
llm.method: MPPIプランナーが軌道探索メカニズムとして機能し、事前訓練されたコントローラの価値関数が探索を誘導する双方向階層型フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 高精度なオフロードシミュレータでの評価において、明示的なコストマップなしでより安全で効果的なナビゲーションを達成した。

2610.38661.title: Quantize by Doing: Task-Guided Mixed-Precision Quantization of Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.38661.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the memory footprint of vision-language-action (VLA) models, but lowering bit widths while maintaining task performance remains challenging. Existing work has used sensitivity estimates from calibration data to assign bit widths to different model components. However, using task success directly to guide mixed-precision allocation is underexplored because closed-loop evaluations are costly and the effect of quantizing one component depends on the precision of other components. To this end, we propose \textbf{QbD-VLA}, a task-guided mixed-precision quantization method that uses task success from short closed-loop evaluations to assign weight and activation bit widths while accounting for interactions between model components. Experiments covering four VLA models and all four LIBERO suites show strong task performance at average precisions of approximately 4 bits for weights and fewer than 6 bits for activations. On SIMPLER, the gain over uniform quantization is small. On a Franka Research 3 robot arm, simulation-selected allocations show no detected success-rate loss on X-VLA but fail on $π_{0.5}$. These findings support using task success to guide mixed-precision VLA quantization, while highlighting the need for real-world evaluation before deployment. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/jiuyixu25/QbD-VLA}{\texttt{github.com/jiuyixu25/QbD-VLA}}.
2610.38661.tldr_en: This work proposes QbD-VLA, a task-guided mixed-precision quantization method that uses task success from short closed-loop evaluations to assign weight and activation bit widths while accounting for interactions between model components.

llm.title_ja: 行動による量子化：ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのタスク誘導型混合精度量子化
llm.tldr_ja: 短時間の閉ループ評価におけるタスク成功率を利用して重みと活性化のビット幅を割り当てる、タスク誘導型の混合精度量子化手法QbD-VLAを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルのメモリフットプリントを削減するポストトレーニング量子化において、タスク性能を維持しつつ低ビット幅化することは困難である。
llm.method: モデルコンポーネント間の相互作用を考慮しつつ、短時間の閉ループ評価でのタスク成功率を基にビット幅を割り当てるQbD-VLAを提案する。
llm.result: 4つのVLAモデルとLIBEROスイートを用いた実験により、重み平均約4ビット、活性化6ビット未満で高いタスク性能を維持できることを示した。
llm.limitation: 実用化の前に実世界での評価が必要であることを示唆している。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.38657.title: Explore Where It Matters: Targeted Exploration for Efficient Rover Adaptation
2610.38657.abstract: Future planetary rovers will traverse steep, deformable terrain where slip, sinkage, and terrain deformation can threaten mobility. Although simulation can capture some wheel-soil effects, unmodeled deformable-terrain phenomena create sim-to-real gaps requiring deployment-time adaptation. Yet, rover operations leave little room for extensive trial-and-error. We introduce TERRA (Targeted Exploration for Reward-Relevant Adaptation), an online adaptation framework that efficiently seeks deployment data exposing task-relevant model errors and corrects them. TERRA adapts a simulation-trained world model with a reward-weighted prediction loss and trains a loss predictor to estimate where future performance-relevant errors are likely to occur, using this signal to guide exploration during MPC. In simulation, TERRA reaches approximately 90% slope-climbing success within five trials under severe out-of-distribution pretraining conditions, outperforming exploration baselines in reward, completion time, and energy to first success. On the ERNEST rover, TERRA recovers coordinated active-suspension locomotion on a deformable Mars-simulant slope within three to five real-world trials. Project website: https://terra-explore.github.io

llm.title_ja: Explore Where It Matters: Targeted Exploration for Efficient Rover Adaptation
llm.tldr_ja: 未知の変形地形における惑星ローバーの適応効率を向上させるため、報酬に関連するモデル誤差を予測し探索を誘導するオンライン適応フレームワークTERRAを提案する。
llm.problem: 変形地形における未モデル化な現象によるシム・トゥ・リアルギャップに対し、ローバーの広範な試行錯誤が許されないこと。
llm.method: 報酬加重予測損失を用いて世界モデルを適応させ、将来の誤差が生じやすい場所を予測する損失予測器でMPCの探索を誘導するTERRAフレームワーク。
llm.result: シミュレーションで約5回以内で約90%の登坂成功率を達成し、ERNESTローバーの実機でも3〜5回の試行で協調アクティブサスペンション移動を実現した。

2610.38628.title: The Reality Gap in Automated Driving Systems Testing: Landscape, Challenges, and Research Directions
2610.38628.abstract: Simulation is essential for testing automated driving systems (ADS), but discrepancies between simulation and reality can undermine testing conclusions. It remains unclear which discrepancies the literature addresses and what evidence supports correspondence claims. We present a systematic mapping of 235 primary studies that measure or mitigate the reality gap in ADS testing, selected from 4,195 publications. We characterise objectives, targets, approaches, experimental setups, and evaluation evidence. Our classification distinguishes simulated and real-world execution across six ADS test components, separately for each approach and its evaluation reference. This distinguishes real-world information used to construct an approach from evidence used to evaluate its claims. Of the included studies, 76% address mitigation, primarily targeting scenario and actor realism and perception, while 94% report validation or measurement procedures. Only 61 studies report metrics from multiple families covering sensor/perception correspondence, ADS behaviour, vehicle dynamics, or safety outcomes; this coverage does not establish causal links between discrepancies and test verdicts. The synthesis highlights that real-world content and physical execution must be interpreted against the claim evaluated. The findings motivate claim-specific evaluation and component-level reporting to establish which discrepancies affect testing conclusions and when simulation evidence supports conclusions about real-world ADS behaviour.
2610.38628.tldr_en: A systematic mapping of 235 primary studies that measure or mitigate the reality gap in ADS testing, selected from 4,195 publications, characterise objectives, targets, approaches, experimental setups, and evaluation evidence and highlights that real-world content and physical execution must be interpreted against the claim evaluated.

llm.title_ja: The Reality Gap in Automated Driving Systems Testing: Landscape, Challenges, and Research Directions
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転システムのテストにおける現実ギャップを測定または軽減する235件の一次研究のシステマティックマッピングを実施し、その現状と課題を整理した。
llm.problem: シミュレーションと現実の間の不一致がテストの結論を損なう恐れがあるが、どの不一致が文献で対処されているか不明確であること。
llm.method: 4,195件の出版物から選定された235件の一次研究を対象に、目的、対象、アプローチ、実験設定、評価の証拠を体系的に分類・マッピングした。
llm.result: 研究の76%が軽減策を扱い、94%が検証手順を報告しているが、複数のメトリクスを網羅して不一致とテスト判定の因果関係を示した研究はわずか61件であった。
keywords_ja: シム・トゥ・リアルギャップ
システマティックマッピング

2610.38613.title: TRIM: Temporal Run-Time Monitoring of 3D Object Detection via Activation Statistics
