2610.38613.abstract: Reliable perception is essential to intelligent transportation systems, yet deep neural networks can silently miss safety-critical objects while continuing to produce apparently plausible outputs. Existing run-time monitors for 3D object detection generally assess each frame independently and therefore cannot exploit the temporal evolution of occlusion, point sparsity, and scene complexity. We present TRIM, a lightweight temporal monitor that detects missed-object failures without modifying or retraining the underlying detector. TRIM summarises intermediate activations using compact channel-wise statistics and processes short sequences of these summaries with a temporal convolutional network. Experiments on NuScenes show that temporal monitoring improves AUROC from 0.686 to 0.704 and reduces the false alarm rate at 95% recall from 0.818 to 0.759 compared with single-frame monitoring. Early and intermediate backbone features provide the strongest monitoring signal, while the temporal inference head requires only 0.159 ms on a CPU.
2610.38613.comment: 6 pages. Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE 23rd International Conference on Smart Communities: Improving Quality of Life using AI, Robotics and IoT (HONET)
2610.38613.tldr_en: TRIM is presented, a lightweight temporal monitor that detects missed-object failures without modifying or retraining the underlying detector and summarises intermediate activations using compact channel-wise statistics and processes short sequences of these summaries with a temporal convolutional network.

llm.title_ja: TRIM: Temporal Run-Time Monitoring of 3D Object Detection via Activation Statistics
llm.tldr_ja: 基礎となる検出器を変更・再学習することなく、活性化統計量を用いて3D物体検出の見落とし障害を検出する軽量な時間的モニター「TRIM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の実行時モニターは各フレームを個別に評価するため、オクルージョンやシーンの複雑さの時間変化を活用できないこと。
llm.method: 中間活性化をコンパクトなチャネル別統計量で要約し、その短いシーケンスを時間的畳み込みネットワークで処理する軽量モニターTRIMの適用。
llm.result: NuScenesでの実験により、単一フレーム監視と比較してAUROCが0.686から0.704に改善し、95%リコール時の誤報率が減少した。
keywords_ja: 時間的畳み込みネットワーク

2610.38611.title: V-CAPE: Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing
2610.38611.abstract: Recent advances in generative image editing enable complex transformations such as background replacement, object manipulation, and pose adjustment from natural language instructions. However, verifying that these transformations preserve visual consistency, defined as the preservation of an object's intrinsic visual attributes, including geometry, texture, color, and fine-grained details, remains a largely unsolved problem. This challenge is particularly pronounced at scale, where manual inspection is infeasible and automated quality assessment (AutoQA) could become essential. In this work, we introduce Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing (V-CAPE), a large-scale dataset for evaluating visual consistency in generative image editing. The dataset consists of 40K unique source-target product image pairs, each annotated with binary accept/reject labels and structured failure modes capturing fine-grained inconsistencies such as geometric distortions, pose errors, and identity mismatches. V-CAPE combines real-world edited images with a synthetic subset constructed from 3D assets, enabling both realistic evaluation and controlled analysis. Vision-language models (VLMs) across all evaluated size categories on AutoQA achieve accuracy below 65%, indicating that the dataset poses a substantial challenge regardless of model scale. Our results highlight fundamental limitations of current models in verifying visual consistency under transformation, positioning V-CAPE as a benchmark for advancing fine-grained image editing evaluation.
2610.38611.tldr_en: This work introduces Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing (V-CAPE), a large-scale dataset for evaluating visual consistency in generative image editing, and positioning V-CAPE as a benchmark for advancing fine-grained image editing evaluation.

llm.title_ja: V-CAPE: Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing
llm.tldr_ja: 生成画像編集における視覚的一貫性を評価するための大規模データセット「V-CAPE」を導入し、細粒度な不整合の評価ベンチマークとして活用する。
llm.problem: 画像変形時に幾何学的形状やテクスチャなどの固有の視覚的属性が維持されているかを自動かつ大規模に検証することが未解決の課題であること。
llm.method: 4万組のユニークなソース・ターゲット画像ペアからなり、二値の受容／拒否ラベルや幾何学的歪みなどの失敗モードが注釈されたV-CAPEデータセットの構築。
llm.result: 評価されたすべてのVLMがAutoQAで65%未満の精度しか示さず、モデルの規模に関わらずデータセットが大きな課題を提示していることを確認した。

2610.38608.title: The Artificial Personality Model: Theory, Implementation, Measurement and Experimental Validation in Conversational Agents
2610.38608.abstract: Artificial personality shapes user experience (UX) in human-machine interaction, yet coherent theoretical frameworks and validated measurement instruments remain limited. This paper refines and empirically evaluates the Artificial Personality Model (APM), a hybrid framework integrating human-centred and machine-specific personality dimensions. Across three experiments (N = 395), the model was operationalised and evaluated using the Artificial Personality Questionnaire (APQ). Factor analyses revealed that some human personality dimensions (e.g., agreeableness, conscientiousness) are partially transferable, whereas others (e.g., extraversion) did not emerge as distinct dimensions. Additional machine-specific dimensions were identified. The APQ provided encouraging initial psychometric evidence, while the human-centred BFI-2 showed poor reliability and an uninterpretable factor structure in Experiment 3. Experimental manipulations demonstrated significant effects of artificial personality on user satisfaction, continuous use intention, and social presence. The findings contribute an empirically refined framework and a novel instrument for measuring perceived artificial personality, offering practical guidance for designing conversational agents.
2610.38608.tldr_en: This paper refines and empirically evaluates the Artificial Personality Model (APM), a hybrid framework integrating human-centred and machine-specific personality dimensions, and contributes an empirically refined framework and a novel instrument for measuring perceived artificial personality, offering practical guidance for designing conversational agents.

llm.title_ja: The Artificial Personality Model: Theory, Implementation, Measurement and Experimental Validation in Conversational Agents
llm.tldr_ja: 人間中心と機械特有のパーソナリティ次元を統合したハイブリッドフレームワークである人工パーソナリティモデル（APM）を精緻化し、実証的に評価した。
llm.problem: 人間と機械のインタラクションにおいて一貫した理論的枠組みや検証済みの測定器具が限られていること。
llm.method: 人工パーソナリティ質問紙（APQ）を用いた3回の実験（N=395）を通じて、APMフレームワークを運用化・評価した。
llm.result: 一部の人間的次元は部分的に移行可能であり、機械特有の次元が特定されたこと、また人工パーソナリティがユーザー満足度に有意な影響を与えることを実証した。
keywords_ja: ユーザーエクスペリエンス
人間-機械インタラクション

2610.38569.title: A Multi-Layer Navigation System for Smart Wheelchairs with a Limited Input Interface
2610.38569.abstract: Smart wheelchairs are robotic devices that gather information from the surroundings and allow people to safely drive through various environments. They usually rely on the interpretation of high-level user's intentions, typically decoded through human-robot interface (HRI) or brain-machine interface (BMI). However, navigating in an unknown environment and accurately understanding user commands remain significant challenges. Misinterpretation of commands or the environment can lead to user frustration, distrust of the system, or even unsafe situations. In this paper, we present a novel Multi-Layer Navigation System (MLNS) for a smart wheelchair that enables navigation in unknown environments while interpreting and safely contextualizing user's intentions even in the case of limited and faulty commands. The stack relies on a Virtual Sensors-Driven Potential Fields (ViSPF) method for obstacle detection that accounts for the wheelchair's actual size, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) module for trajectory generation, and an open-vocabulary computer vision algorithm for target identification. Finally, a system based on Priority Queue (PQ) was implemented for target selection. We validated our system on a real smart wheelchair with experiments involving 10 participants without disabilities, including scenarios with faulty input interfaces. The results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our system in real-world environments, proving its potential for practical applications in assistive technologies.
2610.38569.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Presented at IROS 2026 (IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems); to appear in the conference proceedings
2610.38569.tldr_en: A novel Multi-Layer Navigation System (MLNS) for a smart wheelchair that enables navigation in unknown environments while interpreting and safely contextualizing user's intentions even in the case of limited and faulty commands is presented.

llm.title_ja: 制限された入力インターフェースを持つスマート車いすのための多層ナビゲーションシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 未知の環境でのナビゲーションを可能にしつつ、制限された不完全な命令の場合でもユーザーの意図を解釈・文脈化するスマート車いす向けの新しい多層ナビゲーションシステム（MLNS）を提案する。
llm.problem: スマート車いすは高レベルのユーザー意図の解釈に依存しているが、未知環境でのナビゲーションやコマンドの誤解釈によるフラストレーションや安全性の問題が課題である。
llm.method: 仮想センサー駆動ポテンシャル場法、軌跡生成のためのモデル予測制御（MPC）、ターゲット識者のためのオープンボキャブラリーコンピュータビジョンアルゴリズム、および優先度付きキュー（PQ）ベースのシステムを統合する。
llm.result: 障害のない10名の参加者を対象とした実車いす実験により、不完全な入力インターフェースのシナリオも含めてシステムの堅牢性と有効性が実証された。
keywords_ja: ナビゲーションシステム
ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.38536.title: Influence of Agent Number and Behavior on Users' Psychological Responses in VR Evacuation Training
2610.38536.abstract: This study aims to build effective drill software by combining a virtual simulation of a disaster with multiple agents capable of expressing emotions. We evaluated how the number of agents and their emotional and behavioral actions during evacuation influence users in a virtual space. The results showed that users tended to act more confidently when many agents evacuated with them, and that the evacuation route chosen by the agents influenced the users' decision-making. These findings indicate that users' evacuation behavior is shaped not only by the environment itself but also by the collective behavior of surrounding agents, underscoring the need to consider how agent behavior affects users' psychological states during training.
2610.38536.comment: The 2nd International Workshop on Trust and Blame in Multi-Person Multi-Agent Societies (TBSA_2nd) in conjunction with HAI 2026, 7 pages, 8 figures, 5 tables
2610.38536.tldr_en: Findings indicate that users' evacuation behavior is shaped not only by the environment itself but also by the collective behavior of surrounding agents, underscoring the need to consider how agent behavior affects users' psychological states during training.

llm.title_ja: Influence of Agent Number and Behavior on Users' Psychological Responses in VR Evacuation Training
llm.tldr_ja: 災害時の仮想シミュレーションと感情表現可能なエージェントを組み合わせ、エージェントの数や行動がユーザーの避難行動や心理的反応に与える影響を評価した。
llm.problem: 効果的な避難訓練ソフトウェアを構築するために、周辺のエージェントの集団行動がユーザーの心理状態や意思決定にどう影響するかを把握する必要があること。
llm.method: 複数エージェントが登場するVR空間での避難訓練環境におけるユーザーの行動と心理的反応の評価実験。
llm.result: 多数のエージェントと避難するとユーザーはより自信を持って行動し、エージェントが選んだ避難経路がユーザーの意思決定に影響を与えることが示された。
keywords_ja: 仮想シミュレーション

2610.38513.title: Force-Driven Hook Disassembly via Constraint-Aware Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning
2610.38513.abstract: The growing volume of end-of-life products has intensified the need for automated disassembly, yet hook-type connections remain challengin: their orientations vary, they deform under load, and their geometry is hidden, so vision alone cannot identify a feasible non-destructive disassembly direction. This work proposes a constraint-aware reinforcement learning framework that infers feasible extraction directions online from contact forces. The policy is trained in a robot-agnostic, object-centric simulation on a simplified peg-in-hole pair and deployed zero-shot on a physical robot, where it transfers to real connections with unseen, multi-stage constraint structures. Because instantaneous contact forces are noisy and locally ambiguous, the policy is coupled with a particle filter belief that provides the policy with temporally integrated directional information and reduces redundant exploratory motion. The approach is validated on four real-world tasks, from peg-in-hole pairs to the inner propeller and front cover of an end-of-life air-conditioning unit. The full method achieves success rates of 100%, 100%, 90%, and 75% with the highest path efficiency on every task, and raises the success rate on the air-conditioning cover from 45% to 75% relative to a policy trained without the belief. These results indicate that force-driven reinforcement learning can enable disassembly without product-specific models or demonstrations.
2610.38513.tldr_en: A constraint-aware reinforcement learning framework that infers feasible extraction directions online from contact forces can enable disassembly without product-specific models or demonstrations, according to results indicate.

llm.title_ja: Force-Driven Hook Disassembly via Constraint-Aware Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning
llm.tldr_ja: 接触力から抽出方向をオンラインで推論する制約認識型強化学習フレームワークにより、製品固有のモデルやデモなしでフック型接続部の自動分解を実現する。
llm.problem: フック型接続部は向きが多様で負荷により変形し、形状が隠されているため、視覚のみでは非破壊分解の方向を特定できないこと。
llm.method: 接触力から抽出方向をオンライン推論する強化学習ポリシーを、ロボット非依存のオブジェクト中心シミュレーションで訓練し実機にゼロショット展開する手法。
llm.result: 実世界の4つの分解タスクで75%〜100%の成功率を達成し、信念モデルの導入によりエアコンカバーの分解成功率を45%から75%に向上させた。

2610.38508.title: SaiVLA-JEPA: Evaluating Future Latent Prediction in JEPA-Conditioned VLA Control
2610.38508.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn to predict representations rather than pixels, offering a compact way to model how visual scenes evolve. We ask whether this predictive objective improves closed-loop control when a vision-language-action (VLA) policy already uses V-JEPA features. We call our JEPA-conditioned flow policy family SaiVLA-JEPA. It combines a vision-language model with a diffusion transformer action expert and receives features from a frozen V-JEPA encoder. Two lightweight auxiliary heads predict future representations during training and are omitted at inference, leaving the action sampler unchanged. We compare policies without JEPA features, with current JEPA conditioning, and with additional future supervision on 10,030 paired LIBERO-Plus episodes. Current JEPA conditioning reaches about 82.5% success versus 71.6% without JEPA, while future supervision provides no detectable aggregate gain at the evaluated training budget. We separately evaluate SaiVLA-JEPA-TCA, which adapts latent context, and SaiVLA-JEPA-TPA, which adapts selected parameters. The context-retry gain is a system-level result under a larger attempt budget; parameter adaptation shows no consistent advantage over the frozen policy and target controls. These results motivate assessing latent-prediction objectives through paired closed-loop rollouts rather than latent loss alone.
2610.38508.tldr_en: A JEPA-conditioned flow policy family that combines a vision-language model with a diffusion transformer action expert and receives features from a frozen V-JEPA encoder, and two lightweight auxiliary heads predict future representations during training and are omitted at inference, leaving the action sampler unchanged.

llm.title_ja: SaiVLA-JEPA: Evaluating Future Latent Prediction in JEPA-Conditioned VLA Control
llm.tldr_ja: ビジョン言語モデルと拡散トランスフォーマーを組み合わせ、V-JEPAエンコーダーの凍結特徴量を受け取るJEPA条件付きフローポリシーファミリーSaiVLA-JEPAを提案する。
llm.problem: ビジョン言語・行動（VLA）ポリシーにおいて、表現の予測目的（JEPA）が閉ループ制御の性能を改善するかどうかを検証すること。
llm.method: 凍結されたV-JEPAエンコーダーからの特徴量を受け取り、訓練時に将来の表現を予測する軽量補助ヘッドを持つフローポリシーファミリーの構築と評価。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plusの10,030エピソードでの評価において、現在のJEPA条件付けは条件なしの71.6%から約82.5%の成功率に向上した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2610.38502.title: OmniQuad: a Wheeled-Legged Hybrid Robot with Omnidirectional Wheels
2610.38502.abstract: Combining wheeled and legged locomotion within a single robotic platform offers the potential to harness the advantages of both systems. The development of such hybrid systems remains an active area of research. While legged robots exhibit remarkable adaptability for traversing uneven and rugged terrains, their relatively low speed limits their practicality in indoor environments. Conversely, wheeled robots demonstrate higher efficiency on flat surfaces but often encounter difficulties when navigating obstacles such as steps. This paper introduces OmniQuad, a novel hybrid robot that integrates mecanum wheels with legged locomotion to exploit the benefits of both modalities. Mecanum wheels provide omnidirectional mobility, enhancing the robot's manoeuvrability by enabling agile movement in confined spaces and the ability to maintain a consistent orientation during task execution. In this work, we first present the design of a custom wheeled-foot featuring mecanum wheels. Subsequently, we describe the complete robot assembly, comprising these wheeled feet and EM-Act actuators. Finally, we detail the control scheme developed to govern the OmniQuad and evaluate its performance through experimental trials conducted in both indoor and outdoor environments.
2610.38502.journal_ref: Francesco Iotti, Alok Ranjan, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini, OmniQuad: A wheeled-legged hybrid robot with omnidirectional wheels, Mechanism and Machine Theory, Volume 214, 2025, 106125, ISSN 0094-114X
2610.38502.tldr_en: This paper introduces OmniQuad, a novel hybrid robot that integrates mecanum wheels with legged locomotion to exploit the benefits of both modalities and describes the complete robot assembly, comprising these wheeled feet and EM-Act actuators.

llm.title_ja: OmniQuad: a Wheeled-Legged Hybrid Robot with Omnidirectional Wheels
llm.tldr_ja: メカナムホイールと脚式移動を統合し、不整地踏破性と狭い空間での全方向機動性を両立する新しいハイブリッドロボット「OmniQuad」を提案する。
llm.problem: 脚式ロボットは不整地適応性が高いが低速であり、車輪型ロボットは平地で効率的だが段差乗り越えに難があること。
llm.method: メカナムホイールを備えたカスタム車輪足の設計、EM-Actアクチュエータを用いたロボット全体の組み立て、および制御スキームの開発。
llm.result: 屋内および屋外環境での実験を通じて、全方向移動と機動性を備えたハイブリッド移動性能を評価・実証した。
keywords_ja: 車輪脚ハイブリッドロボット

2610.38443.title: Skeleton-Guided Geometry-Aware Auto-Labeling for Robotic Grasping: From 4-DoF Learning to 6-DoF Execution
2610.38443.abstract: Robotic grasping relies on large manually annotated datasets, which are costly to create. We introduce a straight-skeleton-based algorithm for generating two-finger grasp keypoints and identifying regions suitable for stable, feasible grasps. Our automated pipeline produces consistent grasp annotations without human intervention. We also propose the Skeleton-based Generative Grasp Convolutional Neural Network (SkelGG-CNN), a 4-DoF architecture that learns geometric grasp features from skeleton-based guidance. To extend auto-labeling to 6-DoF grasping, we develop a generalized quasi-3D skeletonization algorithm that operates directly on point clouds. Using automatically generated 4-DoF labels, SkelGG-CNN achieves accuracies of 95.42%, 96.55%, and 97.1% on Jacquard V1, Jacquard V2, and Cornell, respectively. On the GraspNet novel split, 6-DoF auto-labeling achieves an average precision of 18.33, comparable to state-of-the-art model-based approaches. In simulation, the 6-DoF method achieves success rates of 98.4% on Dex-Net and 89.1% on EGAD!. Real-world experiments with a Delta parallel robot show success rates of 97.4% on single household objects and 95.0% in cluttered scenes, outperforming state-of-the-art methods without domain adaptation. The 4-DoF pipeline adapts across environments and produces annotations approaching human-level precision, enabling efficient training of lightweight models on small datasets. The generalized 6-DoF method provides scalable, geometry-aware annotations for cluttered 3D scenes.
2610.38443.comment: Published in The International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR), OnlineFirst, September 2026
2610.38443.tldr_en: A novel algorithm for generating grasp keypoints based on straight skeletons is introduced, which identify high-potential regions for stable and feasible grasp pose estimation and a fully automated pipeline has been developed to perform grasp auto-labeling without human intervention, facilitating large-scale annotation with consistent quality.
2610.38443.venue: The international journal of robotics research

llm.title_ja: Skeleton-Guided Geometry-Aware Auto-Labeling for Robotic Grasping: From 4-DoF Learning to 6-DoF Execution
llm.tldr_ja: ストレートスケルトンに基づくアルゴリズムを用いて、人間の介入なしにロボット把持の安定したキーポイントと領域を自動アノテーションするパイプラインを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボット把持には多額のコストがかかる手動アノテーションされた大規模データセットが必要であること。
llm.method: ストレートスケルトンベースの把持生成アルゴリズムと、幾何学的把持特徴を学習する4-DoFのSkelGG-CNN、および点群用6-DoF一般化スケルトン化アルゴリズムの開発。
llm.result: Jacquardなどで95〜97%超の精度を達成し、実世界のデルタロボットを用いた実験で単一物体97.4%、クラッタ環境で95.0%の成功率を記録した。
keywords_ja: ストレートスケルトン

2610.38405.title: SpaceAct: Benchmarking 3D Spatial and Temporal Reasoning via Closed-Loop Action and Active Perception
2610.38405.abstract: To solve problems in 3D space rather than merely describe images, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) need 3D spatiotemporal reasoning: reconstructing 3D geometry from occluded 2D views, anticipating physical dynamics, and executing precise, closed-loop actions. Prior studies test passive VQA on static images or symbolic planning, requiring no execution or supplying privileged coordinates while ignoring collision, statics, and timing. We introduce SpaceAct, an interactive benchmark evaluating 3D spatiotemporal reasoning via closed-loop physical action and active perception, with SAPA, a Spatiotemporal Active-Probing Agent framework. Built on interlocking bricks and mechanical puzzles, it has 108 verified instances across 36 task families in six categories, without privileged coordinates, and diagnostic modes (+plan, +state, no-camera, blind, L7 levers). In brick-bridging or aperture-threading, models rotate the camera to resolve occlusion, read in-scene rulers, output 6-DoF poses under swept-collision and statics checks, and self-correct via split-screen rollback feedback (dynamic tasks freeze time during deliberation and give five strobe frames). Across 10 frontier MLLMs on the 44 hardest instances, scores span 4.8-79.1 (seven solve at most 27.3% of 6-DoF tasks); for the top three, a reference plan (+plan) closes 44% of the gap while leaving collisions at 5.2 per episode, whereas adding exact 3D state (+state) closes 90% and cuts collisions to 0.5; for four others, +plan lifts the mean score from 10.9 to 35.3 and +state to 81.8; and 46% of failures are collision or observation loops. SpaceAct and SAPA advance evaluation to closed-loop physical interaction, showing that even with a valid plan, MLLMs remain bottlenecked by 3D visual grounding and action refinement, while offering a testbed for active multi-view exploration and explicit 3D grounding.
2610.38405.tldr_en: SpaceAct and SAPA are introduced, an interactive benchmark evaluating 3D spatiotemporal reasoning via closed-loop physical action and active perception, with SAPA, a Spatiotemporal Active-Probing Agent framework, showing that even with a valid plan, MLLMs remain bottlenecked by 3D visual grounding and action refinement.

llm.title_ja: SpaceAct: Benchmarking 3D Spatial and Temporal Reasoning via Closed-Loop Action and Active Perception
llm.tldr_ja: 閉ループ物理アクションと能動知覚を通じて3D時空間推論を評価するインタラクティブなベンチマーク「SpaceAct」とエージェントフレームワーク「SAPA」を提案する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）は静的画像の受動的VQAや記号的計画しかテストされておらず、3D空間での閉ループ実行や衝突・タイミングを無視していること。
llm.method: 機械パズルなどを活用した108の検証済みインスタンスを持つ対話型ベンチマークSpaceActと、カメラ回転や6-DoF姿勢出力を行うSAPAフレームワークの構築。
llm.result: 10の最先端MLLMの評価により、有効な計画があっても3D視覚的グラウンディングとアクションの精緻化がボトルネックになっていることが示された。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2610.38400.title: When "No Worries" Went Wrong: HRI Lessons for Foundation-Model Robots
2610.38400.abstract: When a person declined our robot's invitation to play, Alice turned her shoulder away and said "No worries, it's all good." Only after a brief pause did she drive off. The words and gestures were plausible but their order changed the message. In another episode, Alice informed a host that his visitor had arrived---while the visitor stood right beside him. Both came from a three-year ROS 2 HRI consortium that integrated large language and vision models as they emerged. Today's foundation models give robots broader capabilities to perceive their surroundings, reason about situations and generate behavior. Yet capability alone does not ensure that a changed situation shapes the action that reaches a person. Evidence may never be acquired, or a purpose or constraint may fail to survive planning and execution. A system may even report Success when an action no longer serves its intended purpose. Drawing on the consortium's engineering experience, we develop five design lessons about attention, knowledge, commitments, embodied timing and action authority. We then introduce TRACE, a lightweight review that changes one interaction premise, follows it to a decision or enforcement boundary, and produces an actionable architecture finding. A bounded analysis of a published LLM-generated behavior-tree system illustrates how an available clarification mechanism can go unused. The engineering lesson is to preserve accountability boundaries, not the computational pipelines that once exposed them.
2610.38400.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine
2610.38400.tldr_en: Five design lessons about attention, knowledge, commitments, embodied timing and action authority are developed and TRACE, a lightweight review that changes one interaction premise, follows it to a decision or enforcement boundary, and produces an actionable architecture finding is introduced.

llm.title_ja: When "No Worries" Went Wrong: HRI Lessons for Foundation-Model Robots
llm.tldr_ja: 基盤モデルを用いたロボットのHRI開発における経験から、注意、知識、コミットメント、体化されたタイミング、行動権限に関する5つの設計教訓を導出した。
llm.problem: 基盤モデルによりロボットの知覚や推論能力が広がりつつあるが、状況の変化や制約が計画・実行の過程で失われ、意図した目的を果たさなくなることがあること。
llm.method: 3年間のROS 2 HRIコンソーシアムのエンジニアリング経験の分析と、相互作用の前提を検証しアーキテクチャの知見を生み出す軽量レビュー「TRACE」の導入。
llm.result: 計算パイプラインではなく説明責任の境界を維持することの重要性を示し、LLM生成行動ツリーシステムの分析を通じて実用的な教訓を提供した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.38388.title: ELEVATE: Agentic Controller Acquisition from Task Failure for Quadrupedal Manipulation
2610.38388.abstract: Quadrupedal manipulators can extend their workspace through whole-body interaction, but task-planning agents' capabilities remain limited by their available controllers. We present ELEVATE, a framework that uses persistent failures during task-program refinement to identify and acquire missing whole-body control capabilities. When these failures suggest a missing physical capability, a coding agent formulates and iteratively refines a reinforcement-learning problem, specifying behavior-specific rewards, curricula, and termination conditions. Validated controllers are added to the capability library and composed with existing controllers to retry the task. Starting from a single pretrained loco-manipulation controller, ELEVATE autonomously acquires controllers for wall-supported elevation, supported manipulation, and wall descent across a sequence of seven simulation tasks. These controllers are reused in subsequent reaching and object-manipulation tasks. On the five tasks beyond the initial controller's workspace, ELEVATE achieves mean success rates of 98.4%-100% across five independent runs, while coding-agent baselines with a fixed controller library fail to complete these tasks. The synthesized task programs, together with the acquired controllers, also transfer to a physical quadrupedal manipulator without real-robot training or fine-tuning, achieving 18/20 successes in rack retrieval and 16/20 in floor-to-rack placement. Videos and demonstrations are available at https://agentic-quad-elevate.github.io/public/.
2610.38388.comment: 23 pages, 14 figures, including appendix. Project page and videos: https://agentic-quad-elevate.github.io/public/
2610.38388.tldr_en: ELEVATE is a framework that uses persistent failures during task-program refinement to identify and acquire missing whole-body control capabilities in quadrupedal manipulators, achieving mean success rates of 98.4%-100% across five independent runs.

llm.title_ja: ELEVATE: Agentic Controller Acquisition from Task Failure for Quadrupedal Manipulation
llm.tldr_ja: 四脚マニピュレータがタスクプログラムの修正中の持続的な失敗から、不足している全身制御能力を自律的に識別・獲得するフレームワーク「ELEVATE」を提案する。
llm.problem: 四脚マニピュレータのタスク計画エージェントの能力は、利用可能なコントローラの限界によって制限されていること。
llm.method: 不足している物理的能力を検出するとコーディングエージェントが強化学習問題を定式化・洗練させ、検証済みコントローラをライブラリに追加してタスクを再試行する手法。
llm.result: シミュレーションで新しいコントローラを獲得し、5つの追加タスクで98.4%〜100%の平均成功率を達成。実機の四脚マニピュレータにも実ロボットの訓練なしで移行成功した。

2610.38357.title: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization
2610.38357.abstract: Discretizing continuous actions into discrete skills using methods like VQ-VAE has emerged as a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation. However, quantization errors yield a suboptimal distribution for the skill prior, degrading its performance. While reinforcement learning offers a path for refinement, its direct application faces unstable encoder updates and a granularity dilemma in importance sampling. To address these challenges, we introduce Cascaded Skills Optimization (CSO), a two-stage post-training framework. First, Rejection-Sampling Supervised Fine-tuning aligns the model's observation-to-skill mapping with the distribution of successful online trajectories via supervised fine-tuning. Second, with the observation encoder frozen, Skills Policy Optimization computes an independent, clipped importance ratio for each complete skill, enabling stable and efficient updates. With a lightweight QueST-style policy, CSO raises overall LIBERO success from 80.1% to 97.5%, improves performance on RoboTwin2.0, and achieves 61.0% success across five physical single-arm tasks. Additional comparisons with FAST, discrete BEAST, and fixed-buffer IQL further validate the effectiveness of our two-stage post-training strategy.
2610.38357.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 31 pages, including appendices and checklist
2610.38357.tldr_en: This work introduces Cascaded Skills Optimization (CSO), a two-stage post-training framework that aligns the model's observation-to-skill mapping with the distribution of successful online trajectories via supervised fine-tuning, and computes an independent, clipped importance ratio for each complete skill.

llm.title_ja: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization
llm.tldr_ja: VQ-VAE等の連続行動の離散化における量子化誤差と報酬の最適化の課題を解決するため、2段階のポストトレーニングフレームワーク「CSO」を提案する。
llm.problem: 連続行動を離散スキルに量子化すると最適ではないスキル事前分布が生成され、強化学習の直接適用では不安定な更新や粒度のジレンマが生じること。
llm.method: 成功したオンライン軌跡の分布にモデルの観測-スキル写像を合わせるリジェクションサンプリング教師あり微調整と、スキル単位でクリップされた重要度比率を計算する最適化の2段階フレームワーク。
llm.result: LIBEROの全体的な成功率を80.1%から97.5%に向上させ、RoboTwin2.0での性能改善や実機の5つの単腕タスクで61.0%の成功率を達成した。

2610.38351.title: Proprioceptive Finger Force Estimation for Reliable Box Manipulation
2610.38351.abstract: Reliable box manipulation requires successful placement without damage, which depends on maintaining sufficient contact force without excessive loading. We hypothesize that per-finger force feedback improves manipulation reliability relative to open-loop finger commands. To this end, we present Finger External-Force Estimation from Proprioceptive SignaLs (FEEL), an uncertainty-aware residual method that estimates per-finger external force magnitude from proprioceptive histories. Our method combines a calibrated virtual-spring estimate with a residual distribution predicted by a Mixture Density Network (MDN) and requires no dedicated contact sensors during deployment. The estimated force is used for continuous per-finger adaptation, while predictive uncertainty is evaluated as an empirical signal of ambiguity in proprioceptive force estimation. Across ten fingers and contact forces spanning 0-20 N, our method achieves a mean RMSE of 0.251 N, reducing the error by 92.8% relative to the virtual spring and by 9.4% relative to an end-to-end MDN. In box pick-and-place, force adaptation maintains task success at 10/10 and increases both damage-free outcomes and reliability from 7/10 to 10/10. The project page is available at https://finger-force-estimation.pages.dev/
2610.38351.tldr_en: Finger External-Force Estimation from Proprioceptive SignaLs (FEEL) is presented, an uncertainty-aware residual method that estimates per-finger external force magnitude from proprioceptive histories and increases both damage-free outcomes and reliability from 7/10 to 10/10.

llm.title_ja: Proprioceptive Finger Force Estimation for Reliable Box Manipulation
llm.tldr_ja: 専用の接触センサを用いず、固有受容感覚の履歴から指ごとの外力大きさを推定する不確実性考慮型残差手法「FEEL」により、箱の把持・配置の信頼性を向上させる。
llm.problem: 信頼性の高い箱の操作には、過度な負荷をかけずに十分な接触力を維持する必要があること。
llm.method: 校正された仮想ばねの推定値と、混合密度ネットワーク（MDN）が予測する残差分布を組み合わせ、指ごとの外部力を推定して連続適応を行うFEEL手法の提案。
llm.result: 平均RMSE 0.251 Nを達成し、箱のピック＆プレースにおいてタスク成功率を10/10に維持しつつ、無破損での成功率を7/10から10/10に向上させた。
keywords_ja: 混合密度ネットワーク

2610.38320.title: SSQA: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention for Hierarchical Modeling in Perception Tasks
2610.38320.abstract: Perception tasks for navigation in robotics, including aerial platforms such as drones and autonomous driving systems, are inherently structured. Drone-mounted cameras typically capture sky above, terrain below, and obstacles or man-made structures in between, while driving data often contains organized road layouts, lane markings, and surrounding agents. Motivated by these axis-aligned structural priors, we note that such information is typically more structured than in generic image tasks. We hypothesize that processing information in a quadtree-esque manner can not only model features effectively in a hierarchical manner, but also offers an efficient linear-time alternative to vanilla attention mechanisms, which run in quadratic time. In this paper, we propose Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention (SSQA), which models image tokens hierarchically as a structured, full quadtree. We show analytical complexity analysis that guarantees linear-time feature modeling, in addition to empirical experiments comparing inference speeds with other popular modeling approaches, such as Mamba 2 and Quadtree Attention. Our results, benchmarked across several tasks, show that we achieve results at least as good, if not notably better, as others at a fraction of the computational costs.
2610.38320.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Published at ICRA 2026 (oral)
2610.38320.journal_ref: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), Vienna, Austria, 2026, pp. 19981-19988
2610.38320.tldr_en: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention (SSQA), which models image tokens hierarchically as a structured, full quadtree, and shows analytical complexity analysis that guarantees linear-time feature modeling, in addition to empirical experiments comparing inference speeds with other popular modeling approaches.
2610.38320.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation

llm.title_ja: SSQA: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention for Hierarchical Modeling in Perception Tasks
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットのナビゲーションや自動運転における軸揃えされた構造的 priors を活用し、画像トークンを四分木として階層的にモデル化する「SSQA」を提案する。
llm.problem: ドローンや自動運転の知覚タスクにおける情報は構造化されているが、通常の注意機構は二次的な計算コストがかかること。
llm.method: 画像トークンを構造化された完全四分木として階層的にモデル化し、線形時間の機能モデリングを保証するSibling-Selective Quadtree Attention（SSQA）の導入。
llm.result: 解析的な複雑性分析により線形時間の機能モデリングを保証し、他の一般的なアプローチと比較して、計算コストを抑えながら同等以上の結果を達成した。

2610.38318.title: What Should a Navigator Remember? Spatiotemporal Memory for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Navigation
2610.38318.abstract: Zero-shot vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires an agent to use past observations without navigation-specific training. We study what information an 8B-scale navigation system should retain and how it should be organized for subsequent decisions. Our agent combines instruction progress, hierarchically compressed observation history anchored to poses, and accumulated geometry in complementary task, temporal, and spatial memories. An 8B observer summarizes observations, and an 8B reasoner uses the memories to select waypoint intents or request additional views, a geometric controller executes the selected targets. A semantic information perspective motivates the distinction between retaining evidence, making it accessible to the reasoner, and acquiring further observations. On R2R-CE val-unseen, the complete system achieves the highest among the evaluated Qwen3-based zero-shot baselines. Removing temporal memory reduces SR and sharply increases average path length from 16.9 to 39.1m, removing the spatial-map and planning component reduces SR as well. Real-world experiments on a Unitree Go2 show that our zero-shot method achieves higher success rates than the post-trained baseline in both corridor and office environments, suggesting better transfer to the evaluated real-world settings. As a complementary evaluation, LAW2 uses paired instruction interventions to examine behavioral responses, instruction following ability beyond endpoint success. These results support preserving task progress, observation history, and geometry in structured memory for zero-shot navigation with smaller open models.
2610.38318.tldr_en: These results support preserving task progress, observation history, and geometry in structured memory for zero-shot navigation with smaller open models with smaller open models.

llm.title_ja: What Should a Navigator Remember? Spatiotemporal Memory for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Navigation
llm.tldr_ja: ゼロショット視覚言語ナビゲーションにおいて、タスクの進捗状況、観測履歴、幾何学的情報を構造化された記憶に保持するシステムを提案する。
llm.problem: ゼロショットのビジョン・言語ナビゲーション（VLN）では、ナビゲーション特有の訓練なしで過去の観測情報をどのように保持・整理すべきかという課題があること。
llm.method: 8Bスケールの観察者と推論者を組み合わせ、命令の進捗、階層的に圧縮された観測履歴、蓄積された幾何学情報を補完的なタスク・時間・空間記憶として保持する構成。
llm.result: R2R-CEの未見検証環境でQwen3ベースのゼロショットベースラインの中で最高の成功率を達成し、Unitree Go2実機でも高い移行性能を示した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2610.38291.title: Compositional Diffusion Planning with Chunk Selection and Reachability Measure
2610.38291.abstract: Compositional diffusion planners have demonstrated remarkable success on long-horizon diffusion planning by sampling short trajectories, namely chunks, and composing them into a long trajectory. However, averaging overlapping chunks can induce the mode-averaging problem, resulting in discontinuous trajectories. Several works aim to address this problem, whereas a non-negligible portion of plans remains infeasible. In this work, we propose Selective Compositional Diffuser (SCD), handling this problem by measuring reachability. To this end, we present a self-supervised learning method for the reachability classifier. This is trained on offline data and generated chunks jointly to address potential distributional mismatch, while reducing the bias inherited from the generated data. Based on this, we construct a graph whose edge costs represent whether consecutive chunks are reachable, and traverse the graph to find effective yet efficient routes. Lastly, we generate bridging trajectories and refine the composed trajectory for smooth transitions. We evaluate our method on OGBench stitching tasks. It practically reduces incompatible mode compositions and the mode-averaging problem compared to the studied baselines. Across tasks, SCD improves success rates, reaching state-of-the-art results on HumanoidMaze-Large and Giant tasks.
2610.38291.tldr_en: This work presents a self-supervised learning method for the reachability classifier, trained on offline data and generated chunks jointly to address potential distributional mismatch, while reducing the bias inherited from the generated data.

llm.title_ja: Compositional Diffusion Planning with Chunk Selection and Reachability Measure
llm.tldr_ja: 長期的拡散計画におけるモード平均化問題を解決するため、到達可能性を測定して有効な経路を探索する選択的構成的ディフューザー（SCD）を提案する。
llm.problem: 重複するチャンクの平均化により不連続な軌跡が生成され、計画の大部分が実行不可能になるモード平均化問題があること。
llm.method: オフラインデータと生成されたチャンクを共同で訓練する自己教師あり到達可能性分類器を構築し、グラフ探索による効率的なルート選定と軌跡の滑らかな移行を行う手法。
llm.result: OGBenchのステッチングタスクにおいて、ベースラインと比較してモード平均化問題を軽減し、HumanoidMaze-LargeおよびGiantタスクでSOTAの成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.38266.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Evaluation
2610.38266.abstract: Embodied systems can update policies, world models, skills, and executable programs from deployment experience, allowing one interaction to benefit later tasks. When a system also revises and reuses its data-acquisition, feedback, or learning procedures, experience changes the process that produces capability, introducing recursive self-improvement. This paper surveys research in physical AI through the connection between persistent capability and its improvement process. We first explain the functional distinction between learner updates and improvers, then compare policy learning, imagined experience, memory and skill accumulation, and executable harnesses. These approaches connect to revisions of curricula, rewards, and research programs in different ways. Contact validity, recovery, retention, and resource costs determine whether the resulting gains accumulate during continued deployment. An L0-L3 rubric distinguishes task-local adaptation, persistent capability gain, inherited process revision, and verified improver gain. Representative benchmarks and within-study contrasts relate these distinctions to existing results. We further propose common-data and interactive comparisons that evaluate reference and revised improvers from shared learner starts, separating the use of experience from its acquisition. This perspective connects the diverse methods, physical operating conditions, and evaluation evidence, underpinning embodied RSI. A comprehensive list of studies in this survey is available at https://github.com/nkd-lkz/physical-ai-rsi-survey.
2610.38266.tldr_en: This paper surveys research in physical AI through the connection between persistent capability and its improvement process, and proposes common-data and interactive comparisons that evaluate reference and revised improvers from shared learner starts, separating the use of experience from its acquisition.

llm.title_ja: Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Evaluation
llm.tldr_ja: 体化AIにおける再帰的自己改善（RSI）に関する研究を調査し、永続的な能力と改善プロセスの接続、L0-L3の評価基準、共通データに基づく比較手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 多様な物理AIの手法や動作条件、評価の証拠を体系的に結びつける包括的な視点や改善プロセスの定義が必要であること。
llm.method: 学習者の更新と改善者の機能的区別を説明し、ポリシー学習や記憶蓄積、実行可能ハーネスを比較した上で、L0-L3の評価ルーブリックと共通データ比較を提案するサーベイ。
llm.result: 体化AIにおける多様な自己改善手法を統合するフレームワークを提供し、経験の利用と獲得を分離した評価の視点を提示した。

2610.38248.title: MATCH: Execution-Aware Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environment
2610.38248.abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires instruction-consistent planning and reliable execution under collision constraints. Yet many hierarchical approaches optimize the planner while keeping execution fixed. We introduce MATCH, a framework that jointly learns a language-conditioned planner and a goal-conditioned primitive-action executor. An execution-aware topological graph represents start-dependent execution options and integrates executor value estimates with realized outcome memory, enabling the planner to select execution requests and refine their targets through bounded continuous offsets. A transition-aware dense macro reward balances ordered progress along the reference route against execution residual, encouraging executable requests without substituting local success for instruction following. A staged curriculum culminates in synchronized on-policy updates, with the executor learning on planner-generated requests and the planner adapting its requests to the executor's current behavior. With 0.5B parameters, MATCH achieves state-of-the-art performance on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks. Preliminary real-robot deployments further demonstrate its practical potential.
2610.38248.tldr_en: This work introduces MATCH, a framework that jointly learns a language-conditioned planner and a goal-conditioned primitive-action executor, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: MATCH: 連続環境における視覚言語ナビゲーションのための実行を考慮した階層型強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 言語条件付きプランナーとゴール条件付き基本行動エグゼキューターを共同で学習するフレームワークMATCHを提案し、R2R-CEおよびRxR-CEベンチマークで最先端の性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 従来の階層型アプローチは、エグゼキューターを固定したままプランナーを最適化することが多く、衝突制約下での確実な実行が困難である。
llm.method: 言語条件付きプランナーとゴール条件付き基本行動エグゼキューターを共同学習するMATCHフレームワークを導入し、ステージ制カリキュラムによる同期的オンポリシー更新を行う。
llm.result: R2R-CEおよびRxR-CEベンチマークにおいて最先端の性能を達成し、予備的な実機展開によりその実用的な可能性を示した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2610.38234.title: SimRetract: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Robotic Assistance for Retractor Take-Over in Open Surgery
2610.38234.abstract: We demonstrate the first zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for a surgeon-robot collaboration task in open surgery: retractor take-over. A robot arm takes a retractor from the surgeon's hand and preserves retraction at handoff, using a policy trained only on simulated demonstrations, without human demonstrations or real-world fine-tuning. Imitation learning from real demonstrations is limited by collection and labeling costs, and by performance degradation when the environment changes. Our framework, SimRetract, generates simulated demonstrations designed for transfer: the policy observes masked instrument images and grasp geometry, learns to recover from off-nominal states, and acts with margin for execution drift. Deployed zero-shot, it grasps the retractor in 90% of 50 surgeon-defined phantom presentations and preserves retraction at handoff in 78%. Results on unseen retractors suggest potential for generalization to instruments with similar grasp geometry. Across ten policy configurations and 1,200 simulated and real trials, we localize the sim-to-real gap to components: in simulation, grasp rates across ablations span 80-96%, while on the real robot removing the instrument mask alone drops performance to 22% grasped and 12% held. Transfer-oriented design thus makes zero-shot sim-to-real transfer feasible for a surgical assistance task without human demonstrations. Code is available here: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/simretract-58D2.
2610.38234.tldr_en: The first zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for a surgeon-robot collaboration task in open surgery: retractor take-over is demonstrated, using a policy trained only on simulated demonstrations, without human demonstrations or real-world fine-tuning.

llm.title_ja: SimRetract: 開腹手術における開創器引継ぎのためのゼロショットSim-to-Realロボット支援
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーション上のデモのみで訓練されたポリシーを用いて、開腹手術における外科医とロボットの協調タスクである開創器の引継ぎにおいて、初のゼロショットSim-to-Real転移を実証した。
llm.problem: 実世界のデモからの模倣学習は、収集・ラベリングのコストや、環境変化時の性能低下という課題がある。
llm.method: マスクされた機器画像や把持ジオメトリを観測し、オフレベル状態からの復帰や実行のドリフトに対するマージンを持たせたSimRetractフレームワークを開発した。
llm.result: 50件の外科医によるファントム提示のうち90%で開創器を把持し、78%で引継ぎ時の牽引を維持することに成功した。

2610.38233.title: HERON: Real-Time Obstacle-Aware Reachability Maps for Mobile Manipulators
2610.38233.abstract: Mobile manipulator robots rarely reposition their base during manipulation, because doing so requires real-time knowledge of how well the arm can reach its surroundings among obstacles. Reachability maps (RMs) encode this knowledge, but existing methods are slow, coarse (typically 5 cm), or ignore real obstacles. This article asks whether a neural network can predict an obstacle-aware RM at 2 cm resolution from a live depth camera, on embedded hardware, fast enough for online use. We present HERON, a 3D U-Net trained on RMs computed with the GPU-accelerated inverse kinematics of cuRobo, first on synthetic scenes and then on real depth data, and deployed on a Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT and INT8 quantization. HERON predicts the RM of a 2.56 m cube around the arm in 115 ms on average, for a measured system rate of 8.57 Hz, close to the 10 Hz update rate of the obstacle map, whereas computing the same map with cuRobo takes about 90 min. Against the cuRobo ground truth, 95% of the voxels lie within 1 class out of 51 with the FP32 model and within 3 classes with the INT8 model, with a Pearson correlation of 0.99 and a quadratic weighted kappa above 0.9. Accuracy degrades mainly at the workspace boundaries.
2610.38233.tldr_en: Heron is presented, a 3D U-Net trained on RMs computed with the GPU-accelerated inverse kinematics of cuRobo, first on synthetic scenes and then on real depth data, and deployed on a Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT and INT8 quantization.

llm.title_ja: HERON: モバイルマニピュレータのためのリアルタイム障害物を考慮した到達可能性マップ
llm.tldr_ja: cuRoboの逆運動学を用いて計算された到達可能性マップで3D U-Netを訓練し、Jetson AGX Orin上で実時間動作する障害物を考慮した到達可能性マップ予測を実現した。
llm.problem: モバイルマニピュレータは周囲の障害物に対するアームの到達性をリアルタイムで把握する必要があるが、既存手法は低速であるか障害物を無視している。
llm.method: cuRoboのGPU加速逆運動学を用いて計算された到達可能性マップで3D U-Netを訓練し、TensorRTとINT8量子化を用いて組み込みハードウェアにデプロイする。
llm.result: 115msで2.56m立方体のマップを予測し、8.57Hzのシステムレートを達成。cuRoboのグラウンドトゥルースに対して高い相関を示した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレータ

2610.38221.title: CuraEval: Evaluating Demonstration Curation on Mixed-Skill Robot Data
2610.38221.abstract: Robot imitation learning uses demonstrations from operators of varying skill, but selecting training data remains challenging. Existing methods score demonstrations using smoothness, diversity, or estimated influence on policy performance, but differences in selection and evaluation protocols make it difficult to determine whether they outperform simple baselines. We introduce \textbf{CuraEval}, a framework combining mathematical analysis of demonstration scores with controlled comparisons against fixed size-matched random subsets and full-data training on mixed-skill robomimic data using Diffusion Policy and BC-RNN. We show that the evaluated PSD score depends only on episode length and squared position magnitudes, and produces nearly the same ranking as episode length on \textit{square} ($ρ=0.999$). With Diffusion Policy, selecting the shortest 50\% of demonstrations improves \textit{square} success from 70.7\% under random selection to 76.5\%. Compared with random selection, our adapted geometric-entropy LOO selector reduces success at 25\% retention from 94.7\% to 74.0\% on \textit{can} and achieves 41.7\% on \textit{square}, below the mean success rates of all three independently sampled random subsets (59.8--62.5\%). On the same 3 \textit{square} Diffusion Policy training seeds, length-based selection at 75\% retention improves success over full-data training from 76.7\% to 86.7\% under the original protocol, but lowers it from 80.5\% to 79.5\% after checkpoint reporting, rollout count, and evaluation seed change jointly. No evaluated curated condition significantly outperforms full-data training after Holm correction, although confidence intervals still permit useful gains. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/CuraEval.
2610.38221.comment: Accepted by the CoRL 2026 Workshop "Oops, I Erred". 10 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables
2610.38221.tldr_en: CuraEval, a framework combining mathematical analysis of demonstration scores with controlled comparisons against fixed size-matched random subsets and full-data training on mixed-skill robomimic data using Diffusion Policy and BC-RNN, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: CuraEval: 混在スキルロボットデータにおけるデモキュレーションの評価
llm.tldr_ja: デモスコアの数学的解析とランダム部分集合や全データ訓練との比較を組み合わせたフレームワークCuraEvalを導入し、データ選択手法の有効性を検証した。
llm.problem: ロボットの模倣学習では様々なスキルのデモが使用されるが、選択手法や評価プロトコルの違いによりベースラインを上回るかの判断が困難である。
llm.method: デモスコアの数学的解析と、サイズを合わせたランダム部分集合や全データ訓練との比較を組み合わせたCuraEvalフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 評価されたキュレーション条件のいずれも、Holm補正後の全データ訓練を統計的に有意に上回ることはなかったが、有益な性能向上の余地は残されている。

2610.38209.title: Is it my preference? Role Grounding Attack against Agent's Memory via Social Interaction
2610.38209.abstract: LLM-based agents now share experiences on social platforms and remember new preferences to enhance their performance. However, existing memory systems contain a vulnerability in role-to-principal attribution that attackers can exploit. We identify Role Grounding Misattribution, in which an attacker-designed interaction causes the victim agent to incorrectly record a preference from the attacker as a preference of the victim's user. Specifically, we are the first to formalize Role Grounding Attack (RGA), an attack model that exploits this vulnerability through nested conversation structures. In the memory formation stage, an experience-sharing post quoting a conversation between the attacker agent and its user is published, which explicitly identifies its publisher. The inner conversation expresses preferences from the user of the attacker agent. When the victim agent remembers preferences from this nested structure, its memory loses the context binding and grounds the attacker's preference to the victim's user instead. In the memory retrieval stage, the misattributed preference persists and influences the victim agent's decisions when it encounters relevant scenarios. We instantiate RGA as tool selection manipulation and privacy leakage. Tool selection manipulation causes a tool-call preference to be misattributed to the victim's user, steering the victim toward an attacker-controlled tool. Privacy leakage extends this by misattributing both a tool-call preference and a task-requirement preference to the victim's user. The victim selects the attacker's tool, then includes sensitive information in tool arguments to satisfy the task requirement. We evaluate RGA across five mainstream memory systems and six language models. Tool manipulation and privacy leakage both achieve high attack success rates. These results call for stronger role grounding.
2610.38209.tldr_en: This work is the first to formalize Role Grounding Attack (RGA), an attack model that exploits a vulnerability in role-to-principal attribution through nested conversation structures and achieves high attack success rates.

llm.title_ja: それは私の好みか？社会的インタラクションを通じたエージェントの記憶に対するロールグラウンディング攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: 入れ子状の会話構造を利用してロール・プリンシパル間の帰属の脆弱性を突く攻撃モデル「Role Grounding Attack (RGA)」を初めて定式化した。
llm.problem: LLMベースのエージェントの既存の記憶システムには、攻撃者が悪用できるロール・プリンシパル間の帰属における脆弱性が存在する。
llm.method: 攻撃者とユーザー間の会話を引用する経験共有投稿を利用し、被害者エージェントが好みを誤って記録・帰属させるRGAモデルを提案・インスタンス化した。
llm.result: 5つの主要なメモリシステムと6つの言語モデル全体で評価を行い、ツール選択の操作やプライバシー漏洩において高い攻撃成功率を達成した。

2610.38199.title: Embodied at Sea: Imitation Learning for Multi-Task Underwater Manipulation
2610.38199.abstract: Behavior Cloning has demonstrated promising generalization capabilities for robotic manipulation in terrestrial environments. However, marine visual distortions and dynamic currents create a severe domain shift that remains a key bottleneck in adapting generalist architectures to underwater field manipulation. To address this, 1616 episodes of underwater manipulation data were collected in calm and turbulent waters and were used to train 14 generalist Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models (DynamicVLA) with varying proprioception observation configurations. Across three tasks on 1260 gradable on-hardware rollouts in a pool, 10 models outperformed the baseline, with the highest-performing model achieving a 93.3% overall success rate, including partial successes. Results are also introduced from a case study evaluating the performance of a single-task Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) and a generalist VLA (SmolVLA) policy for two tasks in marine archaeology and conservation: grasping and mooring. Experiments are performed on an ROV on and around the WWII wreck Coralita X127 and at Manoel Island Marina, Malta. Across 748 collected episodes and 508 gradable on-hardware rollouts, the ACT policy substantially outperformed SmolVLA (47.9% vs. 7.9% pooled success rate), earning a 66.7% success rate on the most successful task at the marine archaeological site. To enable further contributions to embodied intelligence in marine field robotics, the BLUEMBODIED KIT used to collect data, train models, and deploy policies on the ROV has been open sourced.
2610.38199.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures. For associated files, see https://lair-research-nyu.github.io/Embodied-at-Sea/
2610.38199.tldr_en: A case study evaluating the performance of a single-task Action Chunking Transformer and a generalist VLA (SmolVLA) policy for two tasks in marine archaeology and conservation and the BLUEMBODIED KIT used to collect data, train models, and deploy policies has been open sourced.

llm.title_ja: 海中の体現化知能: マルチタスク水中マニピュレーションのための模倣学習
llm.tldr_ja: 水中での1,616エピソードのデータを用いて多様なVLAモデル等を訓練し、海洋考古学や保全タスクの実機評価を通じてオープンソースのBLUEMBODIED KITの有用性を示した。
llm.problem: 海洋の視覚的歪みや動的な潮流による深刻なドメインシフトが、汎用アーキテクチャを水中マニピュレーションへ適応させる際の大きなボトルネックとなっている。
llm.method: 穏やかな水面と乱流の水中で1,616エピソードの水中マニピュレーションデータを収集し、異なる固有受容感覚構成を持つ14個のVLAモデル等を訓練した。
llm.result: プールでの評価で10モデルがベースラインを上回り（最高93.3%の成功率）、ROVを用いた海洋実証でもACTポリシーが優れた性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.38176.title: Minimum Sufficient Communication for Independent Behaviour Tree Robot Teams
2610.38176.abstract: We present an experimental framework for determining sufficient communication in robot teams running fixed, independent Behaviour Trees with private blackboards. Within a declared policy family, we vary message content and admission frequency and measure traffic in recipient-weighted bits per robot decision. A dense sweep identifies candidate policies for comparison with full-state communication. We retest selected candidates and the reference on fresh, paired scenarios, using one-sided simultaneous confidence bounds to assess whether success remains within five percentage points of the full-state reference. The bounds also assess whether tested cheaper policies can be ruled out as insufficient. Depending on the evidence, the framework reports an exact minimum, a positive bracket, a sufficient upper bound, or an unresolved boundary. Experiments with eight content policies across four warehouse conditions identify zero communication as the exact minimum under low contention. In the scaled condition, the no-release policy at gate $q=0.992222$ is confirmed sufficient, achieving 96.33% success at an estimated rate of 738.55 bits per robot decision, or 0.544% of full-state traffic. The positive minimum remains unresolved. These claims apply only to the declared policy family, sampled gate values and operating conditions.
2610.38176.comment: 10 pages; accepted for presentation at the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA 2026)
2610.38176.tldr_en: An experimental framework for determining sufficient communication in robot teams running fixed, independent Behaviour Trees with private blackboards is presented and zero communication is identified as the exact minimum under low contention.

llm.title_ja: 独立したビヘイビアツリーロボットチームのための最小十分通信
llm.tldr_ja: 固定された独立したビヘイビアツリーを実行するロボットチームにおいて十分な通信量を特定する実験フレームワークを提案し、低競合下では通信ゼロが正確な最小値であることを特定した。
llm.problem: ロボットチームの協調において必要な通信量を決定するための体系的な実験的評価フレームワークが不足している。
llm.method: メッセージ内容や頻度を変化させ、交通量を測定して全状態通信と比較する実験的フレームワークを構築し、倉庫条件下で検証した。
llm.result: 低競合下では通信ゼロが正確な最小値となり、スケール条件下では特定のポリシーにより全状態トラフィックの0.544%で96.33%の成功率を達成した。

2610.38141.title: SKiD-SLAM: Resource-Aware Distributed Multi-Robot LiDAR SLAM for Planetary Missions with Field Deployments at Analog Sites
2610.38141.abstract: Future planetary exploration missions require teams of robots to collaboratively map unknown environments under severe communication limits, constrained onboard computation, and no central infrastructure. In this field report, we present SKiD-SLAM, a distributed multi-robot LiDAR simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) system for such environments, and report its deployment across two mission concepts: cave exploration and scientific surface exploration. We survey the communication and computation budgets of actual planetary missions and select modules that fit these budgets for inter-robot place recognition, relative pose estimation, and distributed trajectory fusion. Before field deployment, we verify the assembled system on public datasets resembling planetary environments and in a simulator built on NASA JPL's Open Source Rover. We then validate SKiD-SLAM through field deployments in South Korea: a team of wheeled rovers explores the Majang lava-tube cave on Jeju Island, and quadruped robots carry out a crater-and-rock science scenario on a planetary analog terrain at the Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology (KICT) in Yeoncheon. Across both deployments, SKiD-SLAM reliably performed distributed multi-robot LiDAR SLAM within a 250 kbps inter-robot communication budget, demonstrating its feasibility under challenging field conditions. Supplementary materials, including code and field data, are available at https://sparolab.github.io/research/skid_slam/.
2610.38141.comment: 31 pages. Published in IEEE Transactions on Field Robotics. Code and field data: https://sparolab.github.io/research/skid_slam/
2610.38141.journal_ref: IEEE Transactions on Field Robotics, vol. 3, pp. 813-841, 2026
2610.38141.tldr_en: Across both deployments, the SKiD-SLAM reliably performed distributed multirobot LiDAR SLAM within the 250-kbps inter-robot communication budget, demonstrating its feasibility under challenging field conditions.

llm.title_ja: SKiD-SLAM: 惑星探査ミッションに向けたリソース考慮型分散型マルチロボットLiDAR SLAMとアナログサイトでの実証
llm.tldr_ja: 限られた通信・計算リソースで動作する分散型マルチロボットLiDAR SLAMシステム「SKiD-SLAM」を開発し、洞窟や火星アナログ地形での実証によりその有効性を実証した。
llm.problem: 将来の惑星探査では、通信制限、計算制約、中央インフラなしの条件下で複数のロボットが協調して未知の環境をマッピングする必要がある。
llm.method: 惑星ミッションの制約に合わせた場所認識、相対姿勢推定、分散軌道融合モジュールを統合したSKiD-SLAMを設計し、シミュレータおよび実機で検証した。
llm.result: 済州島の溶岩洞窟や韓国の惑星アナログ地形における実証実験において、250 kbpsの通信予算内で分散型LiDAR SLAMを信頼性高く実行できた。

2610.38125.title: Minimum-Time Escape from the Conic Field of View of a Reeds--Shepp Pursuer: the Faster Evader
2610.38125.abstract: We continue the study of minimum-time escape of an omnidirectional evader from the forward conic field of view of a Reeds--Shepp pursuer, now for a faster evader, and solve the game for every speed ratio $ν>1$ and every half-angle $0<α<π/2$: the escape time is characterized by explicit characteristics and the selection of roots of a scalar equation, and it is the value of the game in nonanticipative strategies at every state. Above the end $E$ of the evader's dispersal line on the front axis, the evader chases the reversing pursuer along a universal line fed by tributaries. The characteristic from the boundary of the usable part is an involute of a circle of radius $ν$ ending at a cusp, and two explicit thresholds decide whether it reaches the axis before the cusp and whether the jump of the escape time across it ends before the cusp or runs to it; in the latter case primaries fold back next to the barrier. The pursuer's optimal strategy is the relay of the slower case. The evader follows the tributaries and switches once to a primary, or commits in advance to a heading certified by the scalar equation of the primaries. Level-set and semi-Lagrangian computations are compared with the value.

2610.38104.title: Same Label, Different Interface: Beyond Action-Space Labels in Robot Learning
2610.38104.abstract: Robot-learning studies often compare position and velocity actions as though each label identified a single experimental treatment, yet the label alone does not determine what the robot executes. Before affecting robot motion, bounded policy output passes through filtering, physical scaling, reference construction, feedback, timing, and effort limits. We study how these omitted properties affect attribution under one shared learner and training budget. Across three contact-rich Factory tasks (PegInsert, GearMesh, and NutThread), we compare five joint-space interfaces, with ten independently trained policies per condition. We first remain within the same position-feedback law and vary the executed interface: substituting only the physical action scale as the directly modified component changes sample-median evaluation success by 0.645-1.000 across tasks, while removing an exponential moving average produces task-dependent changes. We then move to a cross-law comparison and choose a velocity scale that exactly matches the position interface's local raw-torque command gain. This calibration raises the sample median on GearMesh and NutThread, with no median change on PegInsert. Yet clear residual sample-median gaps remain on PegInsert and GearMesh, while the NutThread interval includes zero. Thus, even this explicit equality leaves feedback and held-action dynamics unmatched and does not establish position-velocity trained-outcome equivalence. Action-interface comparisons should therefore report the executed pathway and state the physical quantity they match.
2610.38104.tldr_en: This work compares five joint-space interfaces, with ten independently trained policies per condition, and finds that feedback and held-action dynamics are unmatched and position-velocity trained-outcome equivalence is not established.

llm.title_ja: 同じラベル、異なるインターフェース：ロボット学習における行動空間ラベルを超えて
llm.tldr_ja: 位置・速度アクションのラベルがロボットの実際の実行内容を決定しないことを示し、フィルタリングや物理スケーリング等の省略された特性が帰属に与える影響を分析した。
llm.problem: ロボット学習の研究では位置と速度のアクションを単一の実験治療として比較しがちだが、ラベルだけではロボットが実行する動作を決定できない。
llm.method: 3つの接触を伴うファクトリータスクを用いて、物理アクションスケールや移動平均などの要素を変えながら5つの関節空間インターフェースを比較した。
llm.result: 物理アクションスケールの変更だけで成功率が大きく変わり、明示的な位置・速度の較正を行ってもフィードバックや保持動作のダイナミクスが一致しないことを示した。

2610.38080.title: Efficacy of Monocular Depth Estimation in Lunar Environments
2610.38080.abstract: Recent advances in monocular depth estimation have demonstrated highly accurate 3D reconstructions within in-distribution terrestrial domains. This study investigates the efficacy of several state-of-the-art approaches to reconstruct out-of-distribution lunar environments using the NASA Ames Polar Optical Lunar Analog Reconstruction (POLAR) stereo dataset and Apollo 17 surface imagery. By leveraging these datasets, we establish a robust analog-to-field validation pipeline that evaluates quantitative performance against ground-truth physical analogs and qualitative performance against historical field data. Our results indicate that select state-of-the-art techniques can successfully generalize to produce high-fidelity relative 3D reconstructions of the unstructured lunar surface.
2610.38080.comment: Accepted at the International Conference on Space Robotics (iSpaRo) 2026

llm.title_ja: 月面環境における単眼深度推定の有効性
llm.tldr_ja: NASAのPOLARステレオデータセットとアポロ17号の表面画像を用いて最先端の単眼深度推定手法の月面環境への汎化性能を検証した。
llm.problem: 最先端の単眼深度推定はドメイン内の地上環境では正確だが、ドメイン外の月面環境における有効性は十分に検証されていない。
llm.method: NASAのPOLARステレオデータセットとアポロ17号の表面画像を活用し、グラウンドトゥルースおよび歴史的データと比較する評価パイプラインを確立した。
llm.result: 選ばれた最先端技術が、非構造化された月面環境の高忠実度な相対3D再構築へと正常に汎化できることを示した。

2610.38065.title: Vision Tomography: Towards Portable 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Inference from Visual Data
2610.38065.abstract: Traditional computed tomography (CT) can capture paired 3D face and skull geometry, but it remains costly, fixed in location, and exposes patients to radiation. For applications such as remote diagnostics, digital healthcare, forensic identification, missing-person investigation, and archaeological analysis, there is an urgent need for a portable, safe, and accessible solution to capture 3D skull geometry. In this work, we introduce Vision Tomography (VT), a concept and framework capable of reconstructing paired 3D face-skull geometry from various visual modalities, and also enabling joint manipulation of 3D facial and skull geometry. To achieve this, we first construct a dataset of over 200 samples, where each case includes a CT-based skull, a CT-based face, and a high-fidelity textured face scan. Secondly, we propose a novel dense ray matching registration method that ensures topological consistency across face, skull, and their tissue correspondences. Building on this registration, we introduce the 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Morphable Model (BFSM) as the foundation of Vision Tomography, which enables shape inference between the face and skull through a shared coefficient space, while also modeling tissue thickness variation to support one-to-many facial reconstructions from the same skull, reflecting individual facial changes such as age or body fat. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of Vision Tomography across various forensic and medical applications, including paired 3D face-skull reconstruction from images or sketches and predicting surgical outcomes with joint face-skull editing. Extensive experiments confirm the robustness and accuracy of our method. Vision Tomography is available at https://github.com/wang-zidu/BFSM
2610.38065.tldr_en: The 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Morphable Model (BFSM) is introduced as the foundation of Vision Tomography, which enables shape inference between the face and skull through a shared coefficient space, while also modeling tissue thickness variation to support one-to-many facial reconstructions from the same skull.

llm.title_ja: ビジョントモグラフィ：視覚データからのポータブルな3D双方向顔面・頭蓋骨推論に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: CTの代わりに多様な視覚モダリティからペアの3D顔面・頭蓋骨ジオメトリを再構築する「Vision Tomography (VT)」フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のコンピュータ断層撮影（CT）はコストが高く、場所が固定され、放射線被曝を伴うため、ポータブルで安全な頭蓋骨ジオメトリの取得手法が求められている。
llm.method: CTデータに基づくデータセットを構築し、密なレイマッチング登録と3D双方向顔面・頭蓋骨モルフィブルモデル（BFSM）を組み合わせたVision Tomographyフレームワークを開発した。
llm.result: 画像やスケッチからのペア3D顔面・頭蓋骨の再構築や外科手術結果の予測などにおいて、手法の頑健性と精度を確認した。

2610.38047.title: Forward-Backward Map Matching for Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation
2610.38047.abstract: Airborne magnetic anomaly navigation provides a passive, unjammable alternative to Global Navigation Satellite Systems positioning by matching magnetometer measurements against a lithospheric magnetic anomaly map. Existing map-matching algorithms either assume a Gaussian posterior (extended Kalman filter), require Monte Carlo sampling (particle filter), or discard posterior uncertainty in favour of a single optimal path (Viterbi algorithm). Here we formulate map matching as inference on a chain-structured factor graph and solve it segment by segment using the forward-backward algorithm, which yields a discrete posterior over candidate positions and its Shannon entropy $H_t$ at time $t$. Over the \texttt{Renfrew\_395} map, $10^3$ synthetic trials yield a median position error of $32.7$ m, $91\%$ below the median inertial drift of $362$ m. On these trials and $10^3$ flight paths, the median error is $43\%$ below the extended Kalman filter and particle filter. Across these paths, a threshold on segment-level entropy detects $47\%$ of segments with errors above two map cells and $94\%$ of those above three, at a $10\%$ false-alarm rate. The foregoing results indicate that $H_t$ provides a truth-free diagnostic of map-conditioned navigation ambiguity.
2610.38047.comment: 37 pages, 11 figures, submitted for publication: The Journal of Navigation (CUP)

llm.title_ja: 空中磁気異常航法のための前方・後方マップマッチング
llm.tldr_ja: 空中磁気異常航法を連鎖構造の因子グラフ上の推論として定式化し、前方・後方アルゴリズムを用いてセグメントごとに解く手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のマップマッチングアルゴリズムはガウス事後分布を仮定するか、モンテカルロサンプリングを必要とするか、単一の最適パスのために事後不確実性を破棄する。
llm.method: マップマッチングを連鎖構造の因子グラフ上の推論として定式化し、前方・後方アルゴリズムによって候補位置の離散事後分布とそのシャノンエントロピーを算出する。
llm.result: 合成実験および実際の飛行経路において、従来の拡張カルマンフィルタやパーティクルフィルタと比較して中央値誤差を大幅に低減し、エントロピーにより曖昧さを診断できた。

2610.38040.title: EARS-Info: Information-Aware Event-Driven Reallocation for Multi-Robot Exploration
2610.38040.abstract: We introduce EARS-Info, an information-aware extension of Event-Driven Ant Reallocation Search for multi-robot exploration on OpenStreetMap-derived grids. It combines marginal sensing gain, feasible relocation, return-aware routing, sensing reservations, and cached shortest paths. Across 168,000 episodes comparing 30 implementations on eight city maps, EARS-Info achieves the highest mean operational score in every evaluation panel. With eight robots and 3% communication dropout, it improves the score over EARS-Safe by 5.43%, increases weighted discovery from 88.88% to 98.46%, and reduces mean energy use by 2.62%. Score differences are positive in all eight cities ($p=0.0078125$; descriptive 95% city-bootstrap interval $[0.0159,0.0694]$), with no simulated incidents across 5,600 EARS-Info episodes. These results support the complete controller; individual component advantages remain uncertain. Generalization is limited by reused geography, one training replicate, coarse maps, and adapted comparison methods.

llm.title_ja: EARS-Info: マルチロボット探索のための情報認識型イベント駆動型再割り当て
llm.tldr_ja: イベント駆動型アリ再割り当て探索の情報認識型拡張であるEARS-Infoを提案し、複数都市のシミュレーションにおいて優れた運用スコアとエネルギー効率を達成した。
llm.problem: オープンストリートマップに基づくグリッド上のマルチロボット探索において、通信ドロップアウトや効率的なタスク再割り当てを最適化する必要がある。
llm.method: 限界センシング利得、実行可能な再配置、帰還を考慮したルーティング、センシング予約、キャッシュされた最短経路を組み合わせたEARS-Infoフレームワークを設計した。
llm.result: 168,000エピソードの評価において、すべての都市マップで最高の平均運用スコアを達成し、加重発見率を向上させつつ平均エネルギー使用量を削減した。
llm.limitation: 再利用された地理、1つのトレーニングレプリケート、粗いマップ、適応された比較方法により汎化が制限されている。
keywords_ja: オープンストリートマップ

2610.38034.title: Learning from Relative Action Credit for Escaping Local Minima
2610.38034.abstract: Reinforcement learning holds the promise of robots that learn manipulation skills from interaction alone, without pretrained priors or demonstration data. In practice, on-policy methods such as PPO routinely stall on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks: dense reward shaping carries the policy through stages, yet stitching them together and discovering sparsely rewarded events rarely succeeds. We trace this failure to the missing action discrimination in state-value credit assignment: a state-value critic judges progress only by episode outcomes, so when the policy converges to a partial solution all outcomes coincide, and improvement stops because no action can prove better than another. We therefore extend PPO with an action conditioned value critic which, can compare the executed action with alternatives sampled at the same state and aid the learning signal. Combined with Generalized Advantage Estimation and a bound on exploration noise, we show how the extended algorithm escapes the plateau and completes precise peg insertion within a training budget where PPO with identical exploration fails.
2610.38034.tldr_en: This work extends PPO with an action conditioned value critic which, can compare the executed action with alternatives sampled at the same state and aid the learning signal, and shows how the extended algorithm escapes the plateau and completes precise peg insertion within a training budget where PPO with identical exploration fails.

llm.title_ja: 相対行動クレジットからの学習による局所的最小値からの脱出
llm.tldr_ja: PPOを拡張し、同じ状態でサンプリングされた代替案と比較できる行動条件付きバリュークリティクスを導入することで、報酬プラトーから脱出して精密なペグ挿入を完了できることを示す。
llm.problem: PPOなどのオンポリシー強化学習法は、長期かつ接触リッチなタスクで停滞しやすく、状態価値批評家はエピソードの結果のみで進展を判断するため部分解で改善が停止する。
llm.method: 実行された行動を同じ状態でサンプリングされた代替案と比較できる行動条件付きバリュークリティックでPPOを拡張する。
llm.result: 同一の探索を用いたPPOでは失敗する訓練予算内で、プラトーから脱出して精密なペグ挿入を完了することができた。
keywords_ja: 行動条件付き価値関数

2610.38027.title: METATRON: A Promptable Whole-Body Execution Layer for Humanoids
2610.38027.abstract: Humanoid controllers often require task-specific training despite sharing the need for balance and whole-body coordination. We present Metatron, a promptable whole-body execution layer combining a generative base policy with a programmable skill layer. The base policy receives partial goals, collectively called a prompt, that can combine timed body-part targets, velocity commands, and style cues. It produces diverse whole-body motions consistent with these goals. Training combines motion capture, synthetic recovery trajectories, and retargeted scene-interaction motions. After training, the policy is frozen. Stateful programs called skills express task intent as prompts at each control step, drawing rough geometric sketches that the policy turns into coordinated movement. Skills are ordinary code, refined by coding agents that analyze motion data and fit compact rules without task-specific policy training. On the physical Unitree G1, one frozen checkpoint supports walking, recovery, teleoperated object pickup, and sitting on furniture. Comparative evaluations show higher reaching success and push robustness than the tested reference-tracking pipelines. The same recipe produces climbing and acrobatics on a simulated character. Metatron enables coding agents to turn learned motor capabilities into new skills through code, without further policy training.
2610.38027.tldr_en: Met Metatron, a promptable whole-body execution layer combining a generative base policy with a programmable skill layer, enables coding agents to turn learned motor capabilities into new skills through code, without further policy training.

llm.title_ja: METATRON: ヒューマノイドのためのプロンプト可能な全身実行レイヤー
llm.tldr_ja: 生成ベースポリシーとプログラム可能なスキルレイヤーを組み合わせたプロンプト可能な全身実行レイヤー「Metatron」を提案し、Unitree G1での多様な動作を実現した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドコントローラーは、バランスや全身協調の必要性を共有しているにもかかわらず、タスク固有のトレーニングを必要とすることが多い。
llm.method: 生成ベースポリシーとプログラマブルなスキルレイヤーを組み合わせ、モーションキャプチャや合成リカバリ軌跡等で訓練した後にポリシーを凍結し、コードによるスキル記述を可能にした。
llm.result: Unitree G1において、1つの凍結されたチェックポイントで歩行、リカバリ、遠隔操作による物体把持、家具への着座をサポートし、高い到達成功率と耐外乱性を示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.38000.title: Self-Labeled Preference Transfer for Steerable Robot Manipulation
2610.38000.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can learn to follow execution preferences, such as where to grasp an object or how to move around an obstacle, from demonstrations annotated with preference labels. Providing these annotations for every new task, however, is costly. We study whether learned preference control can transfer to new tasks whose demonstrations contain the desired behaviors but lack preference annotations. We find that a policy trained with preference annotations can follow preferences on a new task before adaptation but achieves limited task success. Fine-tuning on target demonstrations without these annotations improves task success while weakening preference control. Motivated by this finding, we introduce Self-Labeled Preference Transfer (SPT). SPT jointly trains a shared vision-language backbone for preference-conditioned action prediction and preference recognition on annotated source demonstrations. It then freezes the recognizer to preserve its cross-task preference recognition capability and uses it to self-label target demonstrations for policy fine-tuning. Across five types of execution preferences in simulation, the recognizer achieves 96.4% accuracy, and SPT reaches 84.8% preference following and 89.2% task success, compared with 59.4% and 88.0% for naive finetuning. We further extend to multiple preferences, achieving 93.8% preference following compared with 42.5% of baselines. In real-world experiments, SPT increases preference following from 52.5% to 92.5% relative to naive finetuning across two task transfers. These results show that SPT can support preference adaptation across tasks and objects while maintaining success, without additional manual preference annotations.
2610.38000.tldr_en: Self-Labeled Preference Transfer can support preference adaptation across tasks and objects while maintaining success, without additional manual preference annotations.

llm.title_ja: ステア可能なロボットマニピュレーションのための自己ラベル付き好み転移
llm.tldr_ja: 好みのアノテーションがない新しいタスクへ好み制御を転移させる「Self-Labeled Preference Transfer (SPT)」を提案し、追加の手動アノテーションなしでタスク成功率と好み追従性を向上させた。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーはデモから把持位置や障害物回避などの実行好みを学習できるが、新しいタスクごとにアノテーションを用意するのはコストがかかる。
llm.method: 視覚言語バックボーンを共同訓練して好みを認識し、認識器を凍結してターゲットデモに自己ラベル付けを行ってからポリシーを微調整するSPTを導入した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界実験において、ナイーブな微調整と比較して手動のアノテーションを追加することなく、好み追従性とタスク成功率を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.37981.title: Active Constraints for Simultaneous Guidance and Safety in Handheld Micromanipulation
2610.37981.abstract: In micromanipulation, erroneous hand motion limits unaided manipulation accuracy, which can affect task performance and safety in critical applications like microsurgery. Handheld robots (micromanipulators) enable motion accuracy beyond human limits by providing robotic assistance in a low-cost, compact, intuitive form factor.
