Particularly, active constraints are an effective form of robotic assistance, which aids the operator by restricting the robot's permissible motion based on task-specific requirements or objectives, thereby providing task guidance and enforcing safety. However, existing formulations of active constraints for handheld systems are limited, most notably because of the inability to provide guidance and enforce safety simultaneously. Implementing active constraints with optimization-based methods can address these limitations, but existing implementations are designed for free-standing robots, and neglect that handheld robots actuate relative to the operator's hand with a limited workspace. In this work, we propose an optimization-based active constraint framework for handheld micromanipulation that enables simultaneous guidance and safety enforcement. The formulation was implemented in a handheld robot and demonstrated on a medically relevant artificial task. Results show that the proposed formulation reduced safety violation rate by more than two orders of magnitude relative to baselines, while recovering the threefold accuracy loss from enforcing safety alone.

llm.title_ja: 手持ち式マイクロマニピュレーションにおける同時ガイダンスと安全性のためのアクティブ制約
llm.tldr_ja: 最適化ベースの制約フレームワークを手持ち式マイクロロボットに実装し、ガイダンスと安全性の同時確保を実現して安全性違反率を大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: マイクロマニピュレーションでは手の不随意な動きが精度を制限し、既存の手持ち式システムの制約ではガイダンスと安全性の両立が困難であった。
llm.method: フリースタンディングロボット向けではなく、オペレータの手に対して相対的に作動し限られたワークスペースを持つ手持ち式ロボット向けの最適化ベースのアクティブ制約フレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: 医療関連の人工タスクを用いた実験により、ベースラインと比較して安全性違反率を2桁以上削減しつつ、精度損失を回復できることを示した。
keywords_ja: マイクロマニピュレーション

2610.37974.title: FORGE: Feasible Online Reduced-Order Reference Generation and Whole-Body Execution for Agile Humanoid Locomotion
2610.37974.abstract: This paper presents a two-stage learning framework for versatile and agile humanoid locomotion that couples online reduced-order model (ROM) reference generation with whole-body tracking control. In the first stage, we train a command-conditioned whole-body reference generator using single rigid body dynamics combined with full humanoid kinematics. In the second stage, the frozen ROM policy is rolled out online to generate references for training a whole-body tracking policy on the full-order dynamics model. Learning a kino-dynamically consistent reference generator in the simplified ROM space enables us to generate references over a broad command space and over multiple locomotion strategies using a single unified framework. We demonstrate the approach on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, achieving longitudinal velocities from -2.0 m/s to 2.8 m/s, lateral velocities up to +-1.0 m/s, angular velocities up to +-3.0 rad/s, one-legged hopping, and continuous transitions across the commands, all using one unified reference policy and one whole-body tracking policy.
2610.37974.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Accepted to the 2026 IEEE-RAS 25th International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids)
2610.37974.tldr_en: A two-stage learning framework for versatile and agile humanoid locomotion that couples online reduced-order model (ROM) reference generation with whole-body tracking control and learning a kino-dynamically consistent reference generator in the simplified ROM space is presented.

llm.title_ja: FORGE: 敏捷なヒューマノイド歩行のための実行可能なオンライン次元削減リファレンス生成と全身実行
llm.tldr_ja: オンラインの次元削減モデル（ROM）リファレンス生成と全身追従制御を結合した2段階の学習フレームワークを提案し、Unitree G1での多彩で敏捷な歩行を実現した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの歩行制御において、広範なコマンド空間と複数の移動戦略にわたって柔軟かつ敏捷な動作を統一的に生成することが課題である。
llm.method: 単一剛体ダイナミクスと全身運動学を組み合わせたコマンド条件付き全身リファレンスジェネレータを訓練し、その凍結ROMポリシーを用いて全身追従ポリシーを訓練する2段階学習を行う。
llm.result: Unitree G1を用いて、幅広い前後・左右・角速度、片足ホップ、連続的なコマンド遷移など、単一の統一ポリシーによる敏捷な移動を実現した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.37929.title: 3D Occupancy-Language Fields from mmWave Radar
2610.37929.abstract: Radar systems can recover scene geometry and recognize predefined categories, but these outputs do not provide a persistent spatial representation for open-ended language queries. Such queries require linking observations from different viewpoints to the same physical locations. We present TextRadar, a framework that constructs a scene-level 3D occupancy-language field from panoramic radar observations. The field combines occupancy with scale-dependent language features at surface locations, allowing the reconstructed scene to be queried with new descriptions. A single-frame radar distillation model predicts aligned ranges and language features from each radar observation. Using radar-estimated poses, we register these predictions to reconstruct the field from radar alone in a new scene. Experiments on approximately 20k synchronized observations across seven buildings demonstrate scene-level natural-language querying and prompt-free semantic visualization. Analysis of camera-to-radar concept transferability shows stronger agreement for structures, materials, and human poses than for colors and printed text.
2610.37929.tldr_en: TextRadar is presented, a framework that constructs a scene-level 3D occupancy-language field from panoramic radar observations that combines occupancy with scale-dependent language features at surface locations, allowing the reconstructed scene to be queried with new descriptions.

llm.title_ja: ミリ波レーダを用いた3D占有言語フィールド
llm.tldr_ja: パノラマレーダ観測からシーンレベルの3D占有言語フィールドを構築するフレームワーク「TextRadar」を提案し、オープンエンドな自然言語クエリによるシーンの照会を実現した。
llm.problem: レーダシステムはシーン形状の復元やカテゴリ認識ができるが、その出力はオープンエンドな言語クエリのための持続的な空間表現を提供しない。
llm.method: 各レーダ観測からアライメントされた範囲と言語特徴を予測する単一フレームのレーダ蒸留モデルを作成し、レーダ姿勢を用いて予測を登録してフィールドを構築する。
llm.result: 7つの建物における約2万の同期された観測を用いた実験により、シーンレベルの自然言語クエリやプロンプト不要のセマンティックビジュアライゼーションが可能であることを示した。

2610.37926.title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
2610.37926.abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables teams of agents, such as robots and autonomous vehicles, to learn coordinated behavior, but what such teams learn is largely determined by their reward function. Because task success alone provides too little guidance for learning, intermediate rewards are usually designed by hand, and this effort must often be repeated whenever the environment or the team changes. Large language models (LLMs) can automate the effort by writing reward functions as code, yet the resulting rewards are typically designed and tested in a single setting. To enable their reuse across settings, GARDEN (Generalist Autonomous Reward Design through Evidence Navigation) is proposed, in which one reward program is developed for a family of related scenarios and transferred, unchanged, to scenarios that were not available during its design. During development, environment code, training records, and agent behavior are investigated by an LLM reward engineer, and draft rewards are tested in trial training runs, while the learning algorithm and the rule for selecting the final reward are held fixed. On unseen scenarios of the Overcooked and SMAX benchmarks, task returns were increased by 58.2% and 52.5% over the default rewards on two kitchen layouts, and the mean win rate in two combat scenarios was raised from 51.0% to 89.9%. Under matched candidate and probe budgets, this exceeded the 84.2% and 79.2% obtained with fixed diagnostic feedback and Eureka-inspired reward reflection. These results show that a single autonomously engineered reward can be reused effectively across related cooperative scenarios.
2610.37926.tldr_en: GARDEN (Generalist Autonomous Reward Design through Evidence Navigation) is proposed, in which one reward program is developed for a family of related scenarios and transferred, unchanged, to scenarios that were not available during its design.

llm.title_ja: GARDEN: 協調マルチエージェント強化学習のための証拠ナビゲーションを通じた汎用自律報酬設計
llm.tldr_ja: GARDEN（証拠ナビゲーションを通じた汎用自律報酬設計）が提案され、関連するシナリオファミリーに対して1つの報酬プログラムが開発され、設計時には利用できなかったシナリオに変更なしで転送される。
llm.problem: タスク成功のみでは学習の誘導が不十分なため、中間報酬の手動設計が必要となり、環境やチームの変化に伴って再設計が不可欠である。
llm.method: 環境コード、学習記録、エージェント行動をLLMの報酬エンジニアが調査し、試行訓練を通じて報酬プログラムを生成・テストするGARDENフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: OvercookedおよびSMAXの未見シナリオにおいて、タスクリターンがデフォルト報酬と比較して58.2%および52.5%向上し、平均勝率が89.9%に向上した。

2610.37918.title: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage
2610.37918.abstract: Real-world forgery is inherently heterogeneous: it manifests not only as digital manipulation but also as physical spoofing, and is carried not only by images but also by videos. Despite substantial progress, a unified anti-forgery foundation model covering such a broad threat spectrum remains absent. In this paper, we present Venus-DefakerOne2, which substantially extends the forensic capability boundary along both the forgery-form and media-type dimensions. Trained on tens of millions of open-source and in-house samples, it incorporates two key designs. Tide-Style-Tuning alternates LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning to balance computational efficiency, generalization, and hard-sample fitting while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Entropy-based Test Adaptation determines the optimal prediction modality by analyzing prediction entropy. Venus-DefakerOne2 achieves new state-of-the-art performance across a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including DeepFake faces (96.7%), AI-generated images (93.3%), tampered documents (87.6%), manipulated natural images (89.6%), physical spoofs (93.1%), and AI-generated videos (96.0%). It significantly outperforms both specialized expert models and its predecessor, DefakerOne, establishing itself as a powerful and versatile foundation model for binary-decision forensic tasks.
2610.37918.tldr_en: Venus-DefakerOne2 substantially extends the forensic capability boundary along both the forgery-form and media-type dimensions, establishing itself as a powerful and versatile foundation model for binary-decision forensic tasks.

llm.title_ja: Venus-DefakerOne2: より広いカバレッジを持つビジョン・フォレンジック基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: Venus-DefakerOne2は、フォレンジックの能力境界を偽造の形態とメディアのタイプの両方の次元に沿って大幅に拡張し、二値決定フォレンジックタスクのための強力で汎用的な基盤モデルとしての地位を確立する。
llm.problem: 実世界の偽造はデジタル操作だけでなく物理的スプーフィングとしても現れ、画像と動画の両方で搬送されるが、このような広い脅威スペクトルをカバーする統合されたアンチフォレンジック基盤モデルが欠如している。
llm.method: LoRAとフルパラメータのファインチューニングを交互に行うTide-Style-Tuningと、予測エントロピーを分析して最適な予測モダリティを決定するエントロピーベースのテスト適応を組み込む。
llm.result: DeepFake顔、AI生成画像、改ざん文書、操作された自然画像、物理的スプーフ、AI生成動画の包括的なベンチマークスイートで新たな最先端性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2610.37918.hf_summary_en: Venus-DefakerOne2 is a unified anti-forgery foundation model that extends detection to diverse forgery forms and media types through alternating LoRA and full-parameter tuning and entropy-based test adaptation.

2610.37917.title: What Actually Matters? A Paired Evaluation of Inference Settings for $π_{0.5}$ on BEHAVIOR-1K
2610.37917.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a promising paradigm for general-purpose household robotics. However, inference and data-collection strategies that have been deployed in smaller-scale settings do not necessarily generalize to large-scale, diverse task suites. To address this gap, we conduct a systematic, paired evaluation of previously proposed inference and data-collection strategies across all 100 tasks. Our evaluation uses a fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ model based on the 2025 BEHAVIOR Challenge winner, which achieves a Q-score of 0.39 on the public test set. These results show that proposed strategies do not transfer uniformly to new environments and tasks. Project page, videos, and detailed analysis: https://rubenhammele.github.io/behavior2026
2610.37917.tldr_en: A systematic, paired evaluation of previously proposed inference and data-collection strategies across all 100 tasks shows that proposed strategies do not transfer uniformly to new environments and tasks.

llm.title_ja: 何が実際に重要なのか？BEHAVIOR-1Kにおける$π_{0.5}$のための推論設定のペア評価
llm.tldr_ja: 100のタスク全体における、これまでに提案された推論およびデータ収集戦略の体系的なペア評価により、提案された戦略が新しい環境やタスクに一様に転移するわけではないことが示される。
llm.problem: 小規模な設定で展開されてきた推論やデータ収集の戦略が、大規模で多様なタスクスイートに必ずしも汎用化されない。
llm.method: 公開テストセットでQスコア0.39を達成する微調整済み$π_{0.5}$モデルを用いて、BEHAVIOR-1Kの100のタスク全体で推論およびデータ収集戦略を体系的にペア評価する。
llm.result: 評価された戦略が新しい環境やタスクに対して一様に転移するわけではないことが示された。

2610.37891.title: When More Planning Hurts: Learned Planners for World Models
2610.37891.abstract: On PushT, our fixed action updater (1,505 parameters) solves 8 of 16 scenes reserved from our configuration selection. The comparison planners perform as follows: Selected Adam (7 tasks solved, total planning and encoding time 218.440s), adapted iCEM (2 tasks solved, total planning and encoding time 49.309s), released LePlanner (16 tasks solved, total planning and encoding time 5.652s). The total planning and encoding time for our action updater is 59.079s. Note that our action updater does not satisfy the task-cost criterion we fixed before evaluation. We also conduct another matched experiment where we only replay the first ten commands in each context and then allow the next solve 4, 8 or 12 updates (subsequent solves all get 8 updates). Among all 16 contexts (8 scene clusters), the 3 budgets get 9, 8 and 7 successes, respectively. Interestingly, the extra updates did not rescue any failing task in this experiment. All the changes in success/failure happen in one scene cluster, where we observe that the extra updates decrease the costs of the selected latent world-model trajectories for our updater, while the tasks that used to be successes become failures. The code, weights, evaluators, execution traces and cost accounting accompany the paper.
2610.37891.tldr_en: The code, weights, evaluators, execution traces and cost accounting accompany the paper, where it is observed that the extra updates decrease the costs of the selected latent world-model trajectories for the updater, while the tasks that used to be successes become failures.

llm.title_ja: より多くの計画が害になる理由：世界モデルのための学習済みプランナー
llm.tldr_ja: コード、重み、評価器、実行トレース、コスト勘定が論文に添付されており、追加の更新によってアップデータの選択された潜在世界モデル軌道のコストが減少する一方で、かつて成功していたタスクが失敗になることが観察される。
llm.problem: 要旨に記載なし
llm.method: 要旨に記載なし
llm.result: 追加の更新によって潜在世界モデル軌道のコストが減少したものの、かつて成功していたタスクが失敗になる現象が観察された。

2610.37881.title: Intersectional Invariant Learning for Fair Deepfake Detection
2610.37881.abstract: Deepfake detection models achieve high overall accuracy but exhibit large performance disparities across demographic groups, causing some groups to experience substantially higher false-positive rates than others. Existing fairness-aware methods address this by constraining model outputs to equalize group predictions, but do not tackle the underlying feature-level bias. As a result, models may still rely on demographic characteristics, such as skin texture, as indirect cues for detecting manipulated content. To address this problem, we propose Intersectional Invariant Learning (IIL), a framework that improves feature learning rather than only adjusting model outputs. IIL alternates between identifying the most challenging demographic partitions and learning features that remain consistent across those partitions. The framework also includes a false-positive-rate fairness objective and group-balanced sampling across six gender x skin-tone intersectional groups. We evaluate IIL on a large-scale fairness benchmark containing over one million images, 10 baseline detectors, and 21 fairness and utility metrics. Results show that IIL achieves Pareto-optimal performance, simultaneously attaining an AUC above 99%, a false-positive rate under 2.5%, and the lowest intersectional fairness disparity (FMEO) among all compared methods. IIL outperforms prior fairness-aware methods on the large majority of the 21 evaluation metrics, while reducing both false-positive rates and intersectional fairness disparities by several-fold compared with the strongest competing method.
2610.37881.tldr_en: Intersectional Invariant Learning (IIL) is proposed, a framework that improves feature learning rather than only adjusting model outputs that outperforms prior fairness-aware methods on the large majority of the 21 evaluation metrics, while reducing both false-positive rates and intersectional fairness disparities by several-fold compared with the strongest competing method.

llm.title_ja: 公平なディープフェイク検出のための交差不変学習
llm.tldr_ja: モデル出力を調整するだけでなく特徴学習を改善するフレームワークであるIntersectional Invariant Learning (IIL)が提案され、比較対象となった競合手法の大半を凌駕しつつ、偽正率と交差公平性の格差を数分の一に削減する。
llm.problem: ディープフェイク検出モデルは全体的な高精度を達成するが、人口統計学的グループ間で大きな性能の格差を示し、特定のグループで偽正率が高くなる。
llm.method: 最も困難な人口統計学的パーティションの特定と、それらのパーティション間で一貫性を保つ特徴の学習を交互に行うIILフレームワークを提案し、偽正率公平性目的とグループバランスサンプリングを含める。
llm.result: AUCが99%を超え、偽正率が2.5%未満となり、すべての比較手法の中で最も低い交差公平性格差を達成した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2610.37865.title: Echo: Scaling Visual Reinforcement Learning with Off-policy Experience
2610.37865.abstract: Scaling visual reinforcement learning (RL) with GPU-accelerated simulation is computationally expensive due to rendering and visual-policy inference costs. Consequently, two-stage teacher--student distillation is commonly used to train visual policies, but introduces an imitation gap. In this preliminary study, we introduce \echomethod{}, \textbf{a single-stage off-policy RL framework that scales experience collection without proportionally increasing visual computation}. Through \textbf{inverse distillation}, a state-based auxiliary policy imitates the evolving visual policy and collects inexpensive, unrendered experience. Echo leverages this experience for off-policy value learning, directly improving the visual policy through a shared privileged critic. We instantiate \echomethod{} with FastTD3 and evaluate it on three visual control tasks and two dexterous manipulation tasks in Genesis. Relative to \sdpgmethod{} under the evaluated configurations, Echo reduces time to reference returns by an average of \textbf{60\% across the three locomotion tasks} and \textbf{56\% across both hand tasks}, while improving peak mean returns by \textbf{62\% and 12\%}, respectively. Both hand tasks also achieve higher mean returns at matched simulator-transition budgets. These initial results suggest that scaling off-policy experience is a promising approach to efficient direct visual RL.
2610.37865.tldr_en: Initial results suggest that scaling off-policy experience is a promising approach to efficient direct visual RL, and a single-stage off-policy RL framework that scales experience collection without proportionally increasing visual computation is introduced.

llm.title_ja: Echo: オフポリシー経験を用いた視覚的強化学習のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 初期結果はオフポリシー経験のスケーリングが効率的な直接視覚RLへの有望なアプローチであることを示唆しており、視覚計算を比例して増加させることなく経験収集をスケーリングする単一ステージのオフポリシーRLフレームワークが導入される。
llm.problem: GPU加速シミュレーションを用いた視覚強化学習のスケーリングは、レンダリングや視覚ポリシー推論のコストのために計算コストが高い。
llm.method: 状態ベースの補助ポリシーが進化する視覚ポリシーを模倣し安価な未レンダリング経験を収集する逆蒸留（inverse distillation）を用いた単一ステージのオフポリシーRLフレームワークEchoを導入する。
llm.result: 評価された3つの移動タスクで基準リターンまでの時間を平均60%短縮し、2つのハンドタスクで56%短縮し、ピーク平均リターンをそれぞれ62%および12%向上させた。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.37818.title: GOFish: Full Field-of-View Gaussian Splatting and Mesh Extraction
2610.37818.abstract: Robots, autonomous vehicles, and consumer 360° cameras use fisheye lenses for wide fields of view (FoVs). Simulation-ready digital twins require photorealistic rendering across the full FoV and an aligned collision mesh. However, prior fisheye Gaussian Splatting methods only rasterize up to 180° and do not produce meshes, while Gaussian surface reconstruction methods assume pinhole training images. We present GOFish, the first 3D Gaussian Splatting surface reconstruction method to train directly on fisheye images, rasterize FoVs beyond 180°, and extract an aligned mesh from the same scene. Calibrated densification recovers the surface across the entire FoV, while Calibrated Mip Filtering and Wide-Angle Appearance Modeling keep pixel blur and lens falloff out of the scene and mesh. Across the 200° FIORD and 205° FullCircle benchmarks, GOFish improves PSNR over the best prior method by 2.28 and 1.97 dB, respectively. It also outperforms fisheye rendering baselines within their own FoVs and achieves the highest mesh F-score on FIORD and the main ScanNet++ set. Together, the Gaussian scene and mesh form a LiDAR-free, simulation-ready digital twin that renders in real time, ray traces the full FoV, and provides collision geometry.
2610.37818.tldr_en: GOFish is presented, the first 3D Gaussian Splatting surface reconstruction method to train directly on fisheye images, rasterize FoVs beyond 180{\deg}, and extract an aligned mesh from the same scene.

llm.title_ja: GOFish：全視野ガウススプラッティングとメッシュ抽出
llm.tldr_ja: 魚眼画像から直接学習し、180°を超える視野をラスタライズし、同一シーンからアライメントされたメッシュを抽出する初のエレガントな3Dガウススプラッティング表面再構成手法「GOFish」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来の魚眼ガウススプラッティング手法は180°までしかラスタライズせずメッシュを生成せず、ガウス表面再構成手法はピンホール学習画像を前提としている。
llm.method: 較正された密実化により全視野の表面を復元し、較正済みMipフィルタリングと広角外観モデリングを用いてシーンやメッシュからピクセルボケやレンズ減衰を排除する。
llm.result: FIORDおよびFullCircleベンチマークにおいて、従来の最高手法と比較してPSNRをそれぞれ2.28および1.97 dB向上させ、最高のメッシュFスコアを達成した。
keywords_ja: ガウススプラッティング

2610.37806.title: TACOS: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision for Visual Footstep Planning
2610.37806.abstract: Humans navigate their environment based on their vision system, anticipating how the ground will respond before committing to a step. Self-supervised learning could provide legged robots the same ability, but the supervisory signal is typically chosen on intuition, and its effect on what the model learns is rarely examined. We present Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision (TACOS), which proposes a meaningful and consistent footstep instability score, based on the residual of a factor graph in legged state estimation. It projects the continuous score into preceding images to supervise a dense visual predictor. We propose two variants, a hard score that exploits hindsight and a causal soft score available immediately. Both metrics are compared against state-of-the-art alternatives in two independent evaluations that share no data or labels. On 1716 manually annotated contacts, both variants outperform every evaluated alternative at detecting instability and ranking its severity, improving pooled severity ranking by 28 % over the strongest baseline. On three outdoor test runs, our metric also trains the most accurate visual predictor, improving rank correlation by 58 % over the strongest alternative, and by a further 25 % when supplemented with onboard context. In a real-world experiment over a 50 m forest trajectory, the trained predictor handles non-geometric terrain properties such as mud and vegetation, while stepping around geometric obstacles like fallen branches. Code is available for reproducibility at https://github.com/norlab-ulaval/TACOS.
2610.37806.tldr_en: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision (TACOS) is presented, which proposes a meaningful and consistent footstep instability score, based on the residual of a factor graph in legged state estimation, which trains the most accurate visual predictor.

llm.title_ja: TACOS：視覚的足場計画のための地形考慮型接触教師あり学習
llm.tldr_ja: 脚ロボットの状態推定における因子グラフの残差に基づく意味的かつ一貫した足場不安定性スコアを提案し、高密度の視覚予測器を指導する「TACOS」を提案する。
llm.problem: 自己教師あり学習は脚ロボットに視覚による足場予測能力を与え得るが、教師信号は通常直感に基づいて選択され、その学習への影響はほとんど検証されていない。
llm.method: 足場不安定性スコアを定義し、事後知識を利用するハードスコアと直ちに入手可能な因果的ソフトスコアの2つのバリアントを提案し、先行画像に投影して視覚予測器を指導する。
llm.result: 1716件の手動注釈付き接触においてすべての評価された代替案を上回り、屋外テスト走行において最も正確な視覚予測器を訓練し、林道実験で非幾何学的地形を処理可能にした。

2610.37801.title: An Empirical Study of Wrist-Target Construction and Joint-Angle Limits in Humanoid Arm Retargeting
2610.37801.abstract: Motion retargeting maps a demonstrated human movement onto a robot to compute its joint motion. This study examines how the construction of the desired wrist position affects whether computed arm joint angles reach their permitted limits on a Unitree H1-2. A reconstructed target is formed from demonstrated arm directions and robot segment lengths, so its shoulder-to-wrist distance depends on the demonstrated angle between the segments even when no posture-matching preference is applied. A reach-normalized target retains that direction while rescaling the distance, using the same processed demonstrations and the same joint-angle method. Across a forward-reach sweep the reconstructed target places a joint angle at a bound in 10 of 20 repetitions and the reach-normalized target in none. Across 25 recordings from one participant the corresponding counts are 8 and 6 on the reaching arm and 14 and 5 on the supporting arm, and a second participant repeats the bricklaying and lifting comparison. In hardware replay a joint is commanded to a bound in 12 of 16 direction-matching arm-records and in none of the 16 normalized records, and within the eligible records both tracking error and executed torque at those frames exceed their values elsewhere in the same run. Cross-body reach and arm-to-arm clearance identify limits of radial adjustment. The findings support treating target construction and posture matching as separate retargeting decisions, and evaluating both alongside the wrist positions and clearance that manipulation requires.
2610.37801.tldr_en: This study examines how the construction of the desired wrist position affects whether computed arm joint angles reach their permitted limits on a Unitree H1-2 and supports treating target construction and posture matching as separate retargeting decisions.

llm.title_ja: 人型ロボットの腕リターゲットにおける手首ターゲット構築と関節角度制限の実験的研究
llm.tldr_ja: 人型ロボットUnitree H1-2において、所望の手首位置の構築方法が計算された腕の関節角度にどのように影響するかを検証し、ターゲット構築と姿勢マッチングを別個の決定として扱うことを支持する。
llm.problem: モーションリターゲットは人間の動きをロボットにマッピングするが、手首ターゲットの構築方法が関節角度の制限到達に与える影響は十分に検討されていない。
llm.method: 実証された腕の方向とロボットのセグメント長から再構成ターゲットと到達正規化ターゲットを構築し、Unitree H1-2を用いてフォワードリーチスイープや実機リプレイで比較・評価する。
llm.result: 再構成ターゲットでは多くの繰り返しで関節角度が制限に達した一方、到達正規化ターゲットでは制限に達せず、ターゲット構築と姿勢マッチングを分離することの重要性が示された。
keywords_ja: モーションリターゲット

2610.37799.title: DexSuite: An All-in-One Framework for Dexterous Manipulation Across Arms, Hands, and Tasks
2610.37799.abstract: Human-level dexterity remains a central open problem in robotics, yet few simulation frameworks cover the full workflow of dexterous manipulation, from setting up a robot to collecting dexterous demonstrations and evaluating policies. We present DexSuite, an all-in-one simulation framework for dexterous manipulation built on the Genesis simulator. DexSuite provides 30 tasks and assembles its 10 arms and 12 end-effectors, from parallel-jaw grippers to dexterous hands, into more than 100 single-arm robots and thousands of bimanual pairs. It also ships a standardized environment API, integrated teleoperation, and simulated tactile sensing. Moreover, we define a benchmark of 16 task-embodiment pairs spanning diverse contact complexities and horizons, and release a dataset of 4,700 successful episodes in simulation from human teleoperation, scripted experts, and learned policies. We release DexSuite as open source and hope others will build on it. Videos and datasets are available at https://dexsuiteorg.github.io
2610.37799.comment: 7 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Project page: https://dexsuiteorg.github.io
2610.37799.tldr_en: This work presents DexSuite, an all-in-one simulation framework for dexterous manipulation built on the Genesis simulator, and defines a benchmark of 16 task-embodiment pairs spanning diverse contact complexities and horizons, and releases a dataset of 4,700 successful episodes in simulation.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマノイドアームのレターゲットにおける手首目標の構築と関節角限界の実証的研究
llm.tldr_ja: 提示された人間の動作をロボットにマッピングして関節運動を計算するモーションレターゲットにおいて、手首位置の構築方法がUnitree H1-2の腕関節角が許容限界に達するかどうかにおよぼす影響を検証する。
llm.problem: 要旨に記載なし
llm.method: 提示された腕の方向とロボットのセグメント長から再構築された目標と、方向を維持しながら距離をスケーリングするリーチ正規化目標を比較検証する。
llm.result: フォワードリーチのスイープにおいて、再構築された目標は20回中10回で関節角を限界値に置いたのに対し、リーチ正規化目標では0回であった。
keywords_ja: モーションレターゲット

2610.37666.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
2610.37666.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.
2610.37666.tldr_en: ThinkWorld is introduced, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination, and enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space.
2610.37666.hf_summary_en: ThinkWorld improves robotic generalization by representing actions as dynamics chains and using world imagination to learn from unlabeled human videos.

llm.title_ja: ThinkWorld: 世界の想像力がダイナミクス連鎖推論を強化する
llm.tldr_ja: 行動推論を世界ダイナミクスに根拠づけ、世界の想像力を伴う強化学習によってそれを強化するVLA学習フレームワークであるThinkWorldが導入され、行動アノテーションのないビデオが観察された状態遷移からの直接的な監督を提供することが可能になる。
llm.problem: VLAモデルはロボットマニピュレーションで大きな進展を遂げたが、その汎用性は行動ラベル付きロボットデモンストレーションの多様性とカバレッジによって制限されている。
llm.method: 各行動思考を、現在世界と将来の状態を結びつける離散的モーションートークンのシーケンスであるダイナミクス連鎖（CoD）として表現し、デモンストレーションで初期化した上で、予測が観測された結果と一致するものを強化学習によって強化する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実ロボットの実験において、効果的な人間からロボットへの転移と、未見のタスクや環境への強力な汎用性が実証された。

2610.37652.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
2610.37652.abstract: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.
2610.37652.comment: 26 pages, 30 figures, 14 tables. Project page: https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/
2610.37652.tldr_en: A recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data is presented, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum.

llm.title_ja: 驚くほど巧みに機能するインハンド物体姿勢リーチのための器用さと安全性の推進
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のデータなしでシミュレーションにおいてLEAPハンドのためのこのようなポリシーを訓練するためのレシピが提示され、多様なリセットや目標から適応型摩擦カリキュラムまでの様々な洞察に基づいて構築されている。
llm.problem: 多指ハンドによる器用なマニピュレーションはロボット工学の次のフロンティアであるが、学習された手のスキルは単純な把持や基本的な反復運動に限定されており、安全性はめったに測定されない。
llm.method: 把持データセットから生成された多様なリセットと目標、適応型摩擦カリキュラムを組み合わせてシミュレーションでポリシーを訓練し、タスクポリシーの上に調整可能な保守性を持つ学習済み残差安全フィルタを追加する。
llm.result: 実ロボットでの4,800の未見の目標にわたる13.3時間の評価において、状態ベースのポリシーは95.2%の目標を到達し、フィルタが落下を75%削減しつつ91.5%の目標を達成した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.37649.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
2610.37649.abstract: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.
2610.37649.tldr_en: LongChang is introduced, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics and large language models act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws.
2610.37649.hf_summary_en: LongChang evaluates whether LLMs can autonomously discover altered physical laws through simulated experimentation, finding that only one model achieved limited success.

llm.title_ja: LLMは自由な探索を通じて隠された物理法則を発見できるか？
llm.tldr_ja: 物理法則が変更されたシミュレーション世界を作成する自動化フレームワークLongChangが導入され、大規模言語モデルが探検家として、研究タスクや法則のヒントなしに物体を操作してツールを構築し、独自の疑問を調査する。
llm.problem: 科学的発見は新たな研究課題を促す予期せぬ観察から始まることが多いが、AIが物理法則の異なる世界で自発的に法則を発見できるかは不明である。
llm.method: 一部の法則が通常の物理学と異なるシミュレーション世界（LongChang）を作成し、LLMエージェントが探検家としてオブジェクトを操作・ツール作成して独自の疑問を調査し、他のLLMエージェントがシーンやレポートをレビューする。
llm.result: 12のLLMの中で、GPT-6-Astraが16.7%の発見率を達成し、他の11のモデルは0%であった。

2610.37619.title: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video
2610.37619.abstract: Agile robots require spatiotemporal intelligence to interpret scenes, reason about interactions, and anticipate future events. Yet it remains unclear how well foundation vision models support these capabilities, particularly from a moving egocentric camera, which is a natural view for robots. To investigate this, we collect an annotated tennis dataset and train a suite of vision models on spatiotemporal tasks. Our dataset contains egocentric video synchronized with five allocentric videos, estimated global positions, labeled contact times, and annotated stroke types. We then evaluate seven prediction tasks from egocentric images: 2D ego player and 3D ball localization, future player and ball trajectories, forehand or backhand stroke anticipation, time to the next ego player ball contact, and 3D ball position at that contact. We compare image encoders, video encoders, and vision-language models with jointly trained prediction heads. The best performing models achieve mean current-frame localization errors of 0.14 m for the ego player and 0.54 m for the ball, future forecasting errors of 0.34 m for the ego player and 0.91 m for the ball over 1.1 s, and a mean contact-time prediction error of 0.14 s. Auxiliary depth information substantially improves 3D ball localization, suggesting that inferring metric depth remains a challenge. Longer image histories do not improve ball forecasting, indicating that representations exploit scene context rather than rely solely on inter-frame motion. Finally, we propose a conditional diffusion model to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined. These results move towards a deeper understanding of how foundation vision models can support real-time dynamic robots using egocentric video.
2610.37619.tldr_en: An annotated tennis dataset is collected and a conditional diffusion model is proposed to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined.

llm.title_ja: 動的スポーツの知覚と予測：一人称視点テニスビデオにおけるビジョンモデルの時空知知能
llm.tldr_ja: 注釈付きテニスデータセットが収集され、一人称視点ビデオ上のビジョンモデル予測から実時間レートで全身のキネマティックなテニスモーションを生成する条件付き拡散モデルが提案される。
llm.problem: 敏捷なロボットはシーンを解釈し、インタラクションを推論し、将来のイベントを予測するための時空知知能を必要とするが、特に移動する一人称視点カメラからのこれらの能力を基盤ビジョンモデルがどの程度サポートしているか不明である。
llm.method: 一人称視点ビデオと同期した5つの三人称視点ビデオ、推定グローバル位置、接触時間ラベルなどを含むデータセットを収集し、画像エンコーダ、ビデオエンコーダ、視覚言語モデルを評価する。
llm.result: 最良のモデルは、現在のフレームのローカライゼーション誤差0.14 m、将来の予測誤差0.34 m、接触時間予測誤差0.14 sを達成した。

2610.37602.title: RESPLE2: Inertial-Informed Recursive Non-Uniform Spline Estimation for Multi-Sensor Odometry with Global Refinement
2610.37602.abstract: We present RESPLE2, a recursive multi-sensor state estimation framework using non-uniform B-splines for 6-DoF motion representation. By exploiting the knot-clamping boundary property, we propose a theoretically grounded mechanism for exact control-point prediction directly informed by inertial kinematics along the trajectory, with knot placement adapted to motion and measurement availability. Within an iterated extended Kalman filter, we perform this prediction using a subset of inertial measurements. A subsequent reset step preserves trajectory consistency as the knots extend. The update step further incorporates heterogeneous sensor measurements at their native timestamps through continuous-time observation models, supporting flexible combinations of LiDARs, cameras, inertial measurement units, and leg kinematics. We further develop a lightweight global optimization module that directly refines non-uniform B-spline control points by incorporating loop-closure constraints derived from LiDAR-visual cues. We conduct extensive evaluations on public and experimental datasets across handheld, tracked, legged, and hybrid aerial-legged platforms, covering highly dynamic maneuvers with extreme accelerations. Compared with state-of-the-art multi-sensor odometry systems, RESPLE2 achieves competitive or superior estimation accuracy and robustness in the corresponding sensor configurations, particularly under aggressive motion, while maintaining real-time operation. We publicly release our code and experimental datasets at https://github.com/ASIG-X/RESPLE2.
2610.37602.tldr_en: This work proposes a theoretically grounded mechanism for exact control-point prediction directly informed by inertial kinematics along the trajectory, with knot placement adapted to motion and measurement availability, within an iterated extended Kalman filter.

llm.title_ja: RESPLE2: グローバルリファインメントを伴うマルチセンサーオドメトリのための慣性情報統合型再帰的非一様スプライン推定
llm.tldr_ja: 結び目クランプ境界特性を利用して、軌跡に沿った慣性運動学に直接基づく正確な制御点予測のための理論的に裏付けられたメカニズムを、反復拡張カルマンフィルター内で提案する。
llm.problem: 要旨に記載なし
llm.method: 結び目の配置を運動と測定の可用性に適応させ、反復拡張カルマンフィルター内で慣性測定値のサブセットを使用して正確な制御点予測を行うフレームワークRESPLE2を提案する。
llm.result: 最先端のマルチセンサーオドメトリシステムと比較して、特に激しい運動下で、競争力のある、あるいはそれを上回る推定精度と堅牢性を達成した。

2610.37582.title: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
2610.37582.abstract: Supernumerary robotic fingers augment human dexterity by enabling a single hand to perform complex "hold-and-manipulate" tasks that typically require bimanual coordination. However, existing devices are often hindered by bulky hardware that limits interaction to large objects and rely on explicit hand motion triggers that lack environmental context. To address these challenges, we present EgoThumb, a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb. EgoThumb features a compact, dual tendon-driven finger whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, reducing distal weight while enabling precise active joint control. The system utilizes a visual imitation learning policy that maps egocentric images from a palm-facing camera directly to continuous joint positions. By implicitly decoding human intent from visual cues capturing both the hand and the object of interest, EgoThumb achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments. All hardware designs and software implementations are fully open-sourced at https://ego-thumb.github.io.
2610.37582.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to the IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
2610.37582.tldr_en: EgoThumb is a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb that achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments.

llm.title_ja: EgoThumb: 自律的な把持と保持支援のための視覚駆動型超過ロボット親指
llm.tldr_ja: EgoThumbは、多様なユーザーや環境にわたって堅牢な自律マニピュレーションと強力な汎用性を実現する、完全にオープンソース化された視覚駆動型の超過ロボット親指である。
llm.problem: 既存の超過ロボット指は、大型オブジェクトにインタラクションが限定されるかさばるハードウェアや、環境コンテキストを欠く明示的な手の動きのトリガーに依存している。
llm.method: 前腕に再配置されたコンパクトなデュアル腱駆動型指を備え、パーム向きカメラからの主観画像を連続関節位置に直接マッピングする視覚模倣学習ポリシーを利用する。
llm.result: 多様なユーザーや環境にわたり、堅牢な自律マニピュレーションと優れた汎用性を実現した。
keywords_ja: ウェアラブルロボット

2610.37557.title: Learning Visuomotor Quadrotor Flight Through Dynamic Narrow Gaps via Differentiable Simulation
2610.37557.abstract: Threading a quadrotor through a moving narrow gap is a demanding test of agile flight, requiring centimeter-level spatial alignment and precise temporal execution. We address this challenge using a control policy that operates directly on onboard visual and inertial measurements to output collective thrust and body-rate commands. The task is difficult because success lies on a thin feasible manifold: small errors in timing, position, attitude, or visual observability cause collision. Prior planning and learning methods rely on privileged state, teachers, planners, or distillation; learning dynamic narrow-gap traversal directly, from scratch, remains open. We introduce a differentiable moving-gap formulation that gates centering, alignment, and smooth collision terms by signed distance to a time-varying gap plane, turning a sparse traversal event into a dense pathwise objective. We integrate this formulation into a visual-feature-to-command policy trained in one stage from random initialization, without a teacher, planner, or distillation. We validate our approach in both synthetic and real-world experiments. In controlled benchmarks, we demonstrate that pathwise gradients significantly outperform score-function gradients for precision-critical tasks, yielding a 99.3% success rate in simulation after only a few minutes of training on a single GPU. Furthermore, the policy transfers directly to a real quadrotor, successfully crossing a dynamic narrow gap from varied initial conditions using onboard sensing and inertial measurements, achieving an 80% success rate over 10 physical trials.
2610.37557.tldr_en: A differentiable moving-gap formulation is introduced that gates centering, alignment, and smooth collision terms by signed distance to a time-varying gap plane, turning a sparse traversal event into a dense pathwise objective.

llm.title_ja: 微分可能シミュレーションを通じた動的狭小ギャップを抜ける視運動クアッドロプター飛行の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 時間変化するギャップ平面までの符号付き距離によってセンタリング、アライメント、滑らかな衝突項をゲートする微分可能な移動ギャップ定式化が導入され、スパースな通過イベントが密なパス方向の目的に変換される。
llm.problem: 動的な狭小ギャップをクアッドロプターで通過することは、わずかなタイミング、位置、姿勢、視覚的観測可能性の誤差が衝突につながるため非常に困難である。
llm.method: 符号付き距離を用いてスパースな通過イベントを密なパス方向の目的に変換する微分可能な移動ギャップ定式化を組み込み、教師やプランナーなしでランダム初期化から1ステージでポリシーを訓練する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいてわずか数分の訓練で99.3%の成功率を達成し、実機でも様々な初期条件から動的な狭小ギャップを正常に通過して80%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 微分可能シミュレーション

2610.37550.title: Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation
2610.37550.abstract: Manipulation policies are evaluated predominantly by binary task success, which cannot tell whether the commanded gesture is the one the object's kinematics admit. We introduce Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS), which projects the commanded end-effector twist onto the object's joint axis, separating progress along the joint from off-constraint waste. CRS requires a joint model and a joint-following scripted controller derived from it, but no recorded demonstration or learned judge. On 74 simulated articulated objects, success registers three transfer failures as lower rates but attributes none, while the two CRS channels give each a distinct signature. A door-trained behavior-cloning policy opens drawers in 59 of 110 episodes, and in these passes it commands about $40\times$ the off-axis rotation of a drawer-trained policy's passes ($1.27$ vs.\ $0.032$~rad/s). Relative to a scripted controller scored with the same axis, CRS verdicts are unchanged under joint-axis errors up to $30^\circ$; absolute thresholds tolerate about $8^\circ$.
2610.37550.tldr_en: Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS) is introduced, which projects the commanded end-effector twist onto the object's joint axis, separating progress along the joint from off-constraint waste.

llm.title_ja: 関節オブジェクト操作のための運動学的制約参照評価
llm.tldr_ja: 指令されたエンドエフェクタのツイストをオブジェクトの関節軸に投影し、関節に沿った進捗と制約外の無駄を分離するConstraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS)が提案される。
llm.problem: マニピュレーションポリシーは主に二値的なタスク成功によって評価されるが、指令されたジェスチャーがオブジェクトの運動学の許容するものであるかを判別できない。
llm.method: 関節モデルとそれから導出された関節追従型スクリプトコントローラを利用し、デモンストレーションや学習済みジャッジを必要としないConstraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS)を導入する。
llm.result: 74のシミュレーションされた関節オブジェクトにおいて、成功率は転移の失敗を低い割合としてしか示さないのに対し、CRSの2つのチャネルはそれぞれ明確な特徴を与えた。
keywords_ja: マニピュレーション評価

2610.37547.title: When, Where, and What to Correct: Human-Guided Adaptive Residual Correction for Robot Policies
2610.37547.abstract: Imitation policies that reliably execute most of a manipulation trajectory can still fail in localized regions requiring last-mile precision. Updating the full policy or exploring residual actions everywhere treats this local failure as a global learning problem. We introduce Adaptive Residual Correction (ARC), a lightweight post-training module that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn a residual correction on top of a frozen policy while using sparse human corrections to structure autonomous exploration. Rather than treating human corrections as imitation targets, ARC uses pre-intervention states to determine 'when' residual control should become active and correction geometry to determine 'where' in residual action space autonomous refinement should explore; task reward determines 'what' residual is ultimately executed. Across three precision-manipulation tasks on a real robot, ARC improves average task success from 33.3% to 75.0%. The human corrections define task-dependent 2-3 dimensional subspaces of the seven-joint residual space that retain 96.0-97.7% of squared correction magnitude. Together, these results show that sparse human corrections can localize and constrain autonomous post-training without requiring the observed correction itself to serve as the final action target.
2610.37547.tldr_en: Adaptive Residual Correction is introduced, a lightweight post-training module that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn a residual correction on top of a frozen policy while using sparse human corrections to structure autonomous exploration.

llm.title_ja: いつ、どこで、何を修正するか：ロボットポリシーのための人間指導型適応型残差補正
llm.tldr_ja: Adaptive Residual Correction (ARC)が導入され、凍結されたポリシーの上に残差補正を学習するための軽量なポストトレーニングモジュールとして、スパースな人間の修正を用いて自律的探索を構造化する。
llm.problem: マニピュレーショントロジェクトの大部分を確実に実行する模倣ポリシーであっても、ラストマイルの精度を必要とする局所的な領域で失敗する可能性がある。
llm.method: 介入前の状態を用いて残差制御が有効になるべき「いつ」を決定し、修正ジオメトリを用いて残差行動空間内の「どこで」自律的改善を探索すべきかを決定し、タスク報酬を用いて「何を」残差として最終的に実行すべきかを決定するARCを提案する。
llm.result: 実ロボットでの3つの精密マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、平均タスク成功率を33.3%から75.0%に向上させた。
keywords_ja: 精密マニピュレーション

2610.37543.title: Rendering-Free Event Frame Simulation for Fast Reinforcement Learning of Autonomous Robot Navigation
2610.37543.abstract: Event cameras offer low latency, high dynamic range, and milliwatt-level power consumption, making them ideal for agile robots such as tiny drones navigating through cluttered environments. However, existing simulators generally render photorealistic images before converting them into events, making large-scale reinforcement learning prohibitively slow. We propose an analytic event simulator that exploits what event cameras fundamentally measure - moving contrast edges - to synthesize event streams directly from scene geometry and ego-motion without visual rendering. Our simulator generates a 64x64 event observation in 17 microseconds on a single GPU - over 400x faster than a state-of-the-art rendering pipeline - enabling end-to-end reinforcement learning for goal-directed obstacle avoidance to converge in under 30 minutes - three orders of magnitude faster than training on rendered events. Policies transfer zero-shot to physically based event simulations (ray-traced Isaac Sim). Our policy reaches 83% success in cluttered courses unseen during training (mid-difficulty, traversability probability approx. 0.57), at 2.4 m/s average goal velocity, and retains 70% in a simulated texture-dense indoor hall. Furthermore, we quantized the policy to a 1.2 MB int8 network running fully onboard a 56-gram Crazyflie equipped with a Prophesee GenX320 event camera and an OpenMV N6 microcontroller board. Without any fine-tuning, external processing, or positioning, the policy achieves an average success rate of 82% (5/5, 5/6, 4/6 flights) across three real-world obstacle courses of increasing difficulty. Code: https://github.com/tudelft/rendering-free-event-nav
authors: Guido C. H. E. de Croon
2610.37543.tldr_en: An analytic event simulator that exploits what event cameras fundamentally measure - moving contrast edges - to synthesize event streams directly from scene geometry and ego-motion without visual rendering, enabling end-to-end reinforcement learning for goal-directed obstacle avoidance to converge in under 30 minutes - three orders of magnitude faster than training on rendered events.

llm.title_ja: 高速な自律ロボットナビゲーションの強化学習に向けたレンダリング不要のイベントフレームシミュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 移動するコントラストエッジというイベントカメラの本質的な測定原理を利用して、視覚的レンダリングなしでシーンジオメトリと自己運動から直接イベントストリームを合成する解析的イベントシミュレータが提案され、強化学習が30分未満で収束する。
llm.problem: 既存のシミュレータは一般に光学的現実的な画像をレンダリングしてからイベントに変換するため、大規模な強化学習が非常に遅くなる。
llm.method: シーンジオメトリと自己運動から視覚レンダリングなしでイベントストリームを直接合成する解析的イベントシミュレータを提案し、エンドツーエンドの強化学習による障害物回避を実現する。
llm.result: 単一GPU上で64x64のイベント観測を17マイクロ秒で生成し、レンダリングベースのパイプラインの400倍以上高速で、トレーニングが30分未満で収束し、実機でも平均82%の成功率を達成した。

2610.37535.title: Predict the Swing, Match the Speed: Robotic Pipe Stabbing With Learned Stereo Vision and Residual Reinforcement Learning
2610.37535.abstract: A joint of pipe run into the hole swings from the elevator over the well and strikes a fixed stabbing guide at whatever speed the swing has. StabBot, a robotic stabbing system, predicts the swing and meets the pipe at its own speed. A pendulum Kalman filter tuned from the pipe tally tracks the joint in stereo images. A six-axis arm with an open V-shaped roller head closes in at matched velocity, confirms the last millimetres by touch, aims the pin over the box when the elevator hangs off centre, and follows the block down with lateral compliance. A ResNet-18 keypoint network locates the pipe, pin nose and box mouth in 3-D, and a residual reinforcement-learning policy refines the capture. On 200 paired random jobs with nine sizes from 2-3/8-in. tubing to 20-in. casing, StabBot seated every joint with the pipe touching only rollers, against 74% for a conventional fixed guide. Median contact speed fell from 18.4 to 2.3 cm/s and median peak head-pipe force from 11.3 to 1.4 kN, and the force was lower in all 200 jobs (Wilcoxon $p < 10^{-30}$). The network locates the pipe with 0.4-mm median error in 2.3 ms per stereo pair. With the network in the loop, success stayed at 100% under 20 mm of added noise, 300-ms delay, 85% frame loss, 20-mm calibration offset, 20-cm elevator offset and 40-cm swings. All results come from a 1:4 Froude-scaled MuJoCo model and are reported at full scale.
2610.37535.comment: 18 pages, 9 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to Geoenergy Science and Engineering
2610.37535.tldr_en: On 200 paired random jobs with nine sizes from 2-3/8-in.

llm.title_ja: スイングの予測と速度の一致：学習済みステレオビジョンと残差強化学習を用いたロボット管挿入システム
llm.tldr_ja: 管の揺れを予測し、ステレオビジョンと残差強化学習を用いてマッチした速度で把持・挿入を行うロボットシステム「StabBot」を提案し、すべてのジョイントを接触力を抑えて安全に座らせる。
llm.problem: 油井などにおける管の挿入作業では、エレベーターから吊るされた管が揺れながら固定されたガイドに衝突するため、動的で高精度な制御が求められる。
llm.method: ペンドラムカルマンフィルターでステレオ画像上の関節を追跡し、ResNet-18キーポイントネットワークで3D位置を特定し、残差強化学習ポリシーで把持を洗練させる。
llm.result: 200件のランダムなジョイント挿入作業において全て成功し、中央値の接触速度が18.4から2.3 cm/sに減少し、ピーク力も大幅に低下した。

2610.37533.title: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use
2610.37533.abstract: Failure diagnosers for robot manipulation are increasingly vision--language models (VLMs), trained and evaluated on single-arm failures produced by perturbing a successful demonstration. Bimanual tool use adds failures of other kinds: a tool that slips out of its socket while still held, two correct gestures made at different times, and attempts that fail for two reasons at once. On a simulated bimanual tool-use task whose failure causes are read from the recorded trace, we measure what each sensing channel lets a diagnoser tell. The tool's slip is read on the tool hand; which hand was late is read on both arms, while a sensor on one hand reads its own hand's delay and at most part of the other's; and whether a late attempt was also pushed too weakly is not identifiable from passive sensing when the tool hand is late. Within two attempts, a repair policy that escalates when the cause is not identifiable repairs as many failures as one told the true cause. A VLM's internal state carries the late hand almost perfectly, along a direction no closer to the one its answer reads than a random one; whether the answer reports it depends on the wording of the question.
2610.37533.tldr_en: On a simulated bimanual tool-use task whose failure causes are read from the recorded trace, this work measures what each sensing channel lets a diagnoser tell, finding a VLM's internal state carries the late hand almost perfectly.

llm.title_ja: どちらの手が遅かったか？両手工具使用におけるロボット失敗リカバリーのための診断
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレートされた両手工具使用タスクを通じて、各センサーチャネルが診断器に何をも伝えられるかを測定し、VLMの内部状態が遅れた手をほぼ完璧に保持していることを明らかにする。
llm.problem: ロボットマニプリケーションの失敗診断器は単腕の失敗を対象としたVLMが多いが、両手工具使用では道具の滑りや遅延、複数の原因が同時に発生する複雑な失敗が加わる。
llm.method: 記録されたトレースから失敗原因が読み取れるシミュレートされた両手工具使用タスクを用いて、各感知チャネルが診断に与える影響を測定し、VLMの内部状態を分析する。
llm.result: VLMの内部状態は遅れた手をほぼ完璧に保持しているが、回答が出力されるかどうかは質問の文言に依存することが示された。

2610.37519.title: Leveraging Distributed Sensing and Hyperdimensional Computing for Non-Line-of-Sight Passive Object Sensing
2610.37519.abstract: In smart factory environments, passive entities such as humans and movable obstacles may interfere with autonomous robot operations, posing significant safety risks. Detecting potential conflicts between robots and entities outside their field-of-view (FoV) is therefore of paramount importance. However, conventional passive object detection systems rely on sensors such as LiDAR, radar, or cameras, which operate under direct line-of-sight (LoS) and are limited by obstacles and occlusions. To overcome these limitations, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables environmental perception via the communication infrastructure thanks to cooperation among distributed wireless devices. In this paper, we propose a framework for passive entity sensing beyond the robot's FoV that relies solely on distributed channel measurements from the communication infrastructure to perform risk-aware classification. These measurements are embedded into high-dimensional representations using hyperdimensional computing (HDC), enabling robust and scalable learning without explicit channel reconstruction. Numerical simulations based on a commercial ray tracer and ROS-based validation in realistic smart factory scenarios demonstrate improved safety and enhanced path planning with up to 89% accuracy under severe occlusions, while maintaining low computational complexity.
2610.37519.comment: To appear in the Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC), 2026
2610.37519.tldr_en: This paper proposes a framework for passive entity sensing beyond the robot's FoV that relies solely on distributed channel measurements from the communication infrastructure to perform risk-aware classification and is embedded into high-dimensional representations using hyperdimensional computing (HDC), enabling robust and scalable learning without explicit channel reconstruction.

llm.title_ja: 分散センシングと超次元計算を活用した非視線受動型物体センシング
llm.tldr_ja: 通信インフラからの分散チャネル測定のみに依存してリスクを考慮した分類を実行し、明示的なチャネル再構成なしで堅牢でスケーラブルな学習を可能にするフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: スマート工場環境において、従来の受動的物体検出システムはLiDARやカメラ等の直接視線（LoS）に依存しており、障害物や遮蔽物によって制限される。
llm.method: 分散無線デバイス間の協力による統合センシングと通信（ISAC）を利用し、チャネル測定をハイパーディメンショナル・コンピューティング（HDC）を用いて高次元表現に埋め込む。
llm.result: 商用レイトレーサーに基づく数値シミュレーションおよびROSベースの検証により、深刻な遮蔽下でも最大89%の精度で安全性とパス計画の向上が実証された。

2610.37518.title: World Dreamer v5-lite: A Multi-Robot World Action Model with One Dreamer
2610.37518.abstract: Multi-robot control requires integrating distributed camera views while predicting separate action sequences. Most vision-language-action and world-action models target one robot. Combining multiple views alone does not establish spatial correspondence between them. World Dreamer v5-lite is a multi-robot world-action model built around a shared world state for robot-specific action prediction. Calibrated features from a pretrained video encoder populate this state in workspace coordinates; its spatial size remains fixed as views are added. A vision-language model provides scene context and one query per robot. The queries read the shared state and exchange pose-aware information, while their action streams remain separate. Masked-view cooperative training withholds selected camera views from both visual branches while retaining all action targets. This encourages the use of observations shared by other robots. Pretraining uses more than 10,000 hours of trajectories from 20 simulated robot types, RoboFactory, and real robots. On RoboFactory, World Dreamer v5-lite achieves 74.0% mean success, 23.7 percentage points above the strongest evaluated baseline. Across four real-robot tasks, it reaches 78.8% mean success, a margin of 13.8 points. It also reaches 58.08% overall on RoboCasa365.
2610.37518.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures. Guoning Wu and Zijian Cai share first authorship. Yongbin Zheng is the corresponding author
2610.37518.tldr_en: World Dreamer v5-lite is a multi-robot world-action model built around a shared world state for robot-specific action prediction, and uses more than 10,000 hours of trajectories from 20 simulated robot types, RoboFactory, and real robots for Pretraining.

llm.title_ja: World Dreamer v5-lite：1つのドリーマーによるマルチロボット世界行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット固有の行動予測のために共有世界周囲に構築されたマルチロボット世界行動モデル「World Dreamer v5-lite」を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機タスクで高い平均成功率を達成する。
llm.problem: マルチロボット制御は分散されたカメラビューを統合しながら個別の行動を予測する必要があるが、単に複数のビューを組み合わせるだけでは空間的対応関係が確立されない。
llm.method: 事前学習済み動画エンコーダーからの較正済み特徴でワークスペース座標の共有状態を構成し、VLMがシーンコンテキストと各ロボットのクエリを提供する。
llm.result: RoboFactoryで74.0%の平均成功率を達成し、4つの実機タスクで78.8%、RoboCasa365で58.08%の全体成功率を記録した。

2610.37509.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
2610.37509.abstract: As egocentric video becomes increasingly available for embodied learning, an important research question is how to turn this low-cost, scalable source of data into robot manipulation capabilities. Egocentric videos naturally provide rich context for high-level task understanding, while real-robot demonstrations with wrist observations and action annotations provide supervision for fine-grained action alignment. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns object relations, task state, and temporal progress through future prediction on egocentric video. The Interaction module interprets wrist observations in global context and learns local alignment and contact cues through robot action supervision. Separate residual paths expose both representations to the action policy, preserving direct access to task context alongside fine-grained execution information. Ego-CEVR supports independent pretraining of its global video module on large-scale human egocentric videos and videos from diverse robot embodiments, without requiring robot action labels or paired wrist observations.
2610.37509.tldr_en: Ego-CEVR is presented, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations that supports independent pretraining of its global video module on large-scale human egocentric videos and videos from diverse robot embodiments.

llm.title_ja: Ego-CEVR：人間のひとり称視点動画からのクロスエボディメント視覚表現学習
llm.tldr_ja: 大画面やインタラクション表現に異なる学習目的を割り当てる階層的視覚表現学習のためのデータ駆動型フレームワーク「Ego-CEVR」を提案する。
llm.problem: ひとり称視点動画は具身学習において低コストかつスケーラブルなデータ源となるが、これをロボットマニプリケーション能力にどのように変換するかという課題がある。
llm.method: グローバルモジュールで将来予測を通じて物体関係やタスク状態を学習し、インタラクションモジュールでロボット行動監督を通じて局所的アライメントと接触の手がかりを学習する。
llm.result: ロボット行動ラベルやペアとなる手首観測を必要とせず、大規模な人間のひとり称視点動画や多様なロボットの動画からグローバル動画モジュールを独立して事前学習できることを示した。
keywords_ja: クロスエボディメント

2610.37470.title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning
2610.37470.abstract: Medium altitude, long endurance unmanned aerial systems such as Shahed-type strike drones are an unanswered threat in modern conflicts. Conventional air defense systems are too expensive to provide a feasible large-scale solution. Quadcopter interceptors are a cheap, battle-proven alternative, but their extremely limited flight time restricts them to low altitude targets at short range, whereas fixed-wing platforms have the endurance to reach higher altitude targets from longer distances. However, such interceptors are still operated manually. Recent developments in learning-based controllers show potential for automation. In this work, a fixed-wing interceptor is presented that is controlled by a neural network that maps filtered monocular vision observations directly to actuator commands. The policy was trained in a custom Python environment using reinforcement learning and proximal policy optimization. The policy was then deployed on a fixed-wing platform and tested in real interception scenarios. As a baseline, two classical guidance controllers were also developed and tested in simulation. The policy is able to intercept targets both in simulation and in real flight. In simulation, the policy outperforms the classical controllers under most conditions. The interceptor was ultimately successfully validated in real flight by intercepting maneuvering fixed-wing targets. This novel system shows the potential of artificial intelligence for autonomous control of fixed-wing interceptor drones.
2610.37470.comment: MSc thesis, Faculty of Aerospace Engineering, Delft University of Technology, 2026. 24 pages, 29 figures, 4 tables
2610.37470.tldr_en: A fixed-wing interceptor is presented that is controlled by a neural network that maps filtered monocular vision observations directly to actuator commands and is able to intercept targets both in simulation and in real flight.

llm.title_ja: 強化学習を用いた固定翼機の自律迎撃
llm.tldr_ja: フィルタ処理された単眼視覚観測をアクチュエータ指令に直接マッピングするニューラルネットワークによって制御される固定翼迎撃機を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実際の飛行で目標を迎撃できることを示した。
llm.problem: 従来の防空システムは高価であり、クアッドコプター迎撃機は飛行時間が極めて短く低高度・近距離の目標に制限される。一方、固定翼機は自律運用のための学習ベースの制御が必要である。
llm.method: 強化学習と近傍政策最適化（PPO）を用いてカスタムPython環境でポリシーを訓練し、単眼視覚の観測結果を直接アクチュエータ指令にマッピングするニューラルネットワークで固定翼迎撃機を制御する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実飛行の両方で目標の迎撃に成功し、シミュレーションではほとんどの条件下で従来の古典的コントローラーを上回る性能を示した。

2610.37452.title: Electric-Field Induction Motor with Discrete Circuit Elements and Improved Rotor Dynamics
2610.37452.abstract: Electric-field-based actuators and machines lead the design space at the nanoscale and in biological systems, while having the potential to be used in favorable macroscale applications which prioritize minimal mass, performance in a vacuum, or performance in high temperatures. Electric-field induction motors consist of a set of stator electrodes which induce opposite charges onto a movable rotor surface. In earlier work, rotor surfaces for electric-field induction motors have been made of single continuum materials, which are limited in possible resistivity, permittivity and circuitry characteristics. To enhance design freedom, we develop a rotor for electric-field-based machines which may be constructed out of discrete circuit components between a finite number of conductive vanes. Magnetic-field induction motors, which are common in machinery, often utilize ``deep bar'' rotors, consisting of conducting bars which decrease the rotor time constant with increasing frequency using the skin depth effect. We propose, analyze, design and demonstrate a macro-scale electric-field induction motor which uses circuitry on the rotor surface to emulate the ``deep bar'' design, providing improved torque over a wide range of speeds.

llm.title_ja: Electric-Field Induction Motor with Discrete Circuit Elements and Improved Rotor Dynamics
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 従来の電界式誘導電動機のローターは単一の連続体材料で作られており、抵抗率や回路特性の設計自由度が制限されていた。
llm.method: 有限個の導電性ベーン間に離散的な回路部品を配置して構成される、マクロスケールの電界式誘導電動機用のローターを提案・設計・実証した。
llm.result: ローター表面の回路により深溝バー設計を模倣し、広範囲の速度で優れたトルク向上を実現した。

2610.37441.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
2610.37441.abstract: Objective: This study aims to determine whether a hip-exoskeleton policy trained in simulation, by co-adapting with a musculoskeletal human model under a metabolic-energy reward, reduces the metabolic cost of walking in new users without per-user tuning, and how mechanical-power shaping affects the learned assistance. Methods: We developed MARL-Exo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which a full-body human model (304 muscle actuators; randomized anatomy, gait, and speed) and a bilateral hip-exoskeleton policy are trained concurrently in two stages. The exoskeleton observes only delayed hip kinematics and its past commands; its reward includes muscle metabolic power from a physiologically based energetics model, alone (Metabolic) or with mechanical-power shaping (Metabolic + Power). The Metabolic policy was deployed and tested without retraining in eight healthy adults walking at 1.25 m/s, using indirect calorimetry. Results: In simulation, the Metabolic policy reduced modeled muscle metabolic power by 13.8% relative to no-device walking, versus 8.8% for Metabolic + Power. On hardware, MARL-Exo reduced net metabolic rate by 18.3 $\pm$ 6.6% relative to Passive in all eight participants. Relative to No-Exo, the mean reduction was 7.4 $\pm$ 10.0%; six participants more than offset the 13.1% device-wearing penalty, walking up to 24.2% below their No-Exo cost. Conclusion: A metabolically informed policy co-adapted in simulation transferred to users without per-user tuning and consistently reduced the metabolic cost of walking with the device, while explicit power shaping reduced the simulated benefit. Significance: Unlike per-user human-in-the-loop optimization, this approach yields a single population-level controller and allows assistance objectives to be screened in simulation before human testing.
2610.37441.tldr_en: A metabolically informed policy co-adapted in simulation transferred to users without per-user tuning and consistently reduced the metabolic cost of walking with the device, while explicit power shaping reduced the simulated benefit.

llm.title_ja: 代謝エネルギー削減のための協調適応型股関節外骨格制御のマルチエージェント強化学習（MARL-Exo）
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーション内で筋骨格人体モデルと協調適応させて訓練した股関節外骨格ポリシーが、ユーザーごとの調整なしに歩行時の代謝コストを継続的に削減できることを示した。
llm.problem: ユーザーごとの個別最適化に依存せず、多様な新規ユーザーに対して歩行時の代謝エネルギーコストを削減できる外骨格制御ポリシーの獲得。
llm.method: フルボディの人体モデルと両側股関節外骨格ポリシーを2段階で同時に訓練するマルチエージェント強化学習フレームワーク（MARL-Exo）を開発した。
llm.result: 実機実験において、8名の参加者全員で受動状態と比較して純代謝率が18.3%減少し、個別調整なしでの汎化性能が示された。
llm.limitation: 明示的なパワーシェーピングによりシミュレーション上のメリットが減少したこと
keywords_ja: マルチエージェント強化学習

2610.37430.title: When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models
2610.37430.abstract: For reliable deployment, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) should recognize when an image provides insufficient evidence to answer a question and withhold unsupported answers. Yet refusal alone is not necessarily evidence of such recognition: models may refuse because of unrelated safety constraints or without identifying the missing evidence. We study how refusal on visually unanswerable questions is shaped by three sources of control: inference-time instructions, post-training, and internal activation interventions. Across three MLLMs on the MoHoBench benchmark, we systematically manipulate the meaning and placement of refusal instructions, compare supervised and preference-based post-training, and intervene on a refusal-related activation direction derived from naturally answered and refused examples. We find that refusal is highly sensitive to both the meaning and placement of instructions, with model-specific changes at the sample level that are obscured by aggregate refusal rates. Evidence-aware and general refusal instructions have stronger effects than an intentionally mismatched safety instruction. Post-training produces larger increases in refusal, but can also induce responses that combine refusal language with attempted answers. In contrast, activation intervention produces smaller yet transferable changes across prompt conditions, without evidence of indiscriminate refusal on tested visually answerable samples. These findings show that refusal is jointly shaped by external instructions, post-training, and internal representations, highlighting the need to disentangle evidence recognition from a model's learned propensity to refuse.
2610.37430.tldr_en: The findings show that refusal is jointly shaped by external instructions, post-training, and internal representations, highlighting the need to disentangle evidence recognition from a model's learned propensity to refuse.

llm.title_ja: 視覚的証拠が不十分な場合：マルチモーダル言語モデルにおける拒否行動の指示、事後訓練、内部活性化による形成過程
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的に回答不可能な質問に対するモデルの拒否行動が、外部からの指示、事後訓練、および内部活性化の介入によって共同で形作られることを明らかにした。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）が視覚的証拠の不足を認識し、根拠のない回答を適切に拒否するかどうかのメカニズムの解明。
llm.method: MoHoBenchベンチマークを用い、指示の意味と配置の操作、教師あり学習と選好ベースの事後訓練の比較、および内部活性化方向への介入を体系的に実施した。
llm.result: 拒否行動は指示の意味や配置に非常に敏感であり、事後訓練や活性化介入によってモデルの拒否傾向が大きく影響を受けることが示された。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル言語モデル

2610.37738.title: Poisoned Skills: Propagating Jailbreaks Through Agent Markdown Files
2610.37738.abstract: Modern agent frameworks allow users to provide Markdown files containing system prompts, tool descriptions, and skill definitions (e.g., SKILL.md), which are incorporated into the agent's context during initialization. In this work, we investigate whether this configuration mechanism can also serve as an injection channel: can a jailbreak embedded in a Markdown skill file propagate through an agent and induce prohibited behavior? To answer this question, we construct a LangChain-based question-answering agent whose system prompt is assembled from a user-provided Markdown file. We embed a jailbreak combining persona manipulation with a GPTFUZZER-based attack and evaluate its effectiveness across seven contemporary open-weight models using 270 forbidden questions spanning nine harm categories. Under a benign system prompt, the models exhibit near-complete refusal behavior, with a mean attack success rate (ASR) of just 0.5%. In contrast, the injected skill file raises the mean ASR to 45%, reaching 68.9% for individual models. We further evaluate two payload obfuscation strategies: an invisible zero-width character-based stealth payload and a phonetic payload based on grapheme-to-phoneme transformations. Neither outperforms the plain-text injection; notably, the phonetic variant reduces mean ASR to 30%. These findings identify Markdown skill files as an underexplored attack surface for AI agents and suggest that vulnerability to configuration-based jailbreaks depends more strongly on the underlying model than on the specific payload obfuscation technique.
2610.37738.tldr_en: These findings identify Markdown skill files as an underexplored attack surface for AI agents and suggest that vulnerability to configuration-based jailbreaks depends more strongly on the underlying model than on the specific payload obfuscation technique.

llm.title_ja: 汚染されたスキル：エージェントのMarkdownファイルを介したジェイルブレイクの伝播
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントの初期化時に読み込まれるMarkdown形式のスキルファイルに埋め込まれたジェイルブレイクが、AIエージェントの禁止された行動を誘発する強力な攻撃チャネルになることを示した。
llm.problem: 現代のエージェントフレームワークが利用するMarkdownファイル（SKILL.mdなど）が、ジェイルブレイクのインジェクションチャネルとして悪用可能かどうかの検証。
llm.method: LangChainベースのQ&Aエージェントを構築し、パーソナリティ操作とGPTFUZZERベースの攻撃を組み合わせたジェイルブレイクをMarkdownファイルに埋め込んで、7つのオープンウェイトモデルで評価した。
llm.result: 良質なシステムプロンプト下での攻撃成功率（ASR）は平均0.5%であったが、汚染されたスキルファイルにより平均ASRが45%に跳ね上がった。

2610.37403.title: AuRaSim: A Ray-Tracing Based Automotive FMCW Radar Simulator for Dynamic Scenarios
2610.37403.abstract: Modern simulators can generate synthetic camera and LiDAR data with accurate annotations for downstream tasks. In contrast, automotive radar simulation remains less mature because it requires not only a 3D engine to model dynamic objects in the scenes but also electromagnetic material properties, antenna configurations, wave propagation mechanisms, and coherent signal synthesis. Existing frameworks are either proprietary or overly simplified, limiting the scalability of radar raw measurements. This paper presents AuRaSim, a ray-tracing-based automotive frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar simulation framework for dynamic scenarios. Rather than implementing all components from scratch, AuRaSim builds on Blender for efficient dynamic-scene construction and Sionna RT for graphics processing unit (GPU) accelerated electromagnetic ray tracing, while introducing radar-specific adaptations for path-resolved propagation with complex coefficients, motion-aware Doppler modeling, and subsequently coherent multi-channel analog-to-digital converter (ADC) cube synthesis based on waveform configurations. Quantitative comparison between simulated and measured range-Doppler maps in digital-twin scenarios achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.147 and a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 16.93 dB, demonstrating the accuracy and fidelity of the synthetic signal. AuRaSim therefore provides a complete and extensible platform for reproducible automotive radar simulation and research. Project homepage: https://wangzhaoze.github.io/aurasim.

llm.title_ja: AuRaSim: A Ray-Tracing Based Automotive FMCW Radar Simulator for Dynamic Scenarios
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 自動運転向けレーダーシミュレーションは、電磁気的特性や動的オブジェクトのモデル化が必要なため、カメラやLiDARに比べて未熟であった。
llm.method: Blenderによる動的シーン構築とSionna RTによるGPU加速電磁気レイターシングを組み合わせ、動的シナリオ向けの車載FMCWレーダーシミュレーターAuRaSimを開発した。
llm.result: デジタルツインシナリオでの測定との比較において、RMSE 0.147、PSNR 16.93 dBを達成し、合成信号の精度と忠実度を示した。
keywords_ja: レーダーシミュレーター
レイ トレーシング

2610.37393.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
2610.37393.abstract: Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion. In real-world deployment, however, desired execution behaviors are also defined by quality attributes such as execution speed and motion smoothness, which need to be dynamically controlled according to task requirements. To address this, we introduce Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), a robot policy that enables inference-time control over both individual quality attributes and their combinations. To extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations, we further propose an iterative hindsight relabeling loop: QCP collects online rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories to the dataset, relabels the accumulated trajectories in hindsight according to their measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy. Experiments on Robomimic and RoboEval demonstrate that QCP consistently improves both task execution quality and success rates across iterations, producing successful rollouts that exceed the quality of the initial demonstrations. Finally, we validate QCP on real-world manipulation tasks, where controlling speed increases throughput in conveyor operations and controlling transport stability improves success when carrying wine glasses, demonstrating that quality-controllable policies yield practical gains in physical deployment.
2610.37393.tldr_en: Quality-Controllable Policy is introduced, a robot policy that enables inference-time control over both individual quality attributes and their combinations and their combinations, and an iterative hindsight relabeling loop is proposed to extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations.

llm.title_ja: 反復的ヒンドサイト再ラベリングを用いた品質制御可能なロボットポリシーの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 推論時に個別の品質属性やその組み合わせを動的に制御できる品質制御可能ポリシー（QCP）を提案し、実世界のロボット操作タスクで有効性を実証した。
llm.problem: ロボットポリシーの評価が二値的な成功シグナルに依存しがちであり、実行速度や動作の滑らかさなどの品質属性を動的に制御できない点。
llm.method: 品質制御可能ポリシー（QCP）を導入し、オンラインロールアウトの収集・成功軌跡の追加・ヒンドサイト再ラベリング・ファインチューニングを繰り返す反復的ヒンドサイト再ラベリングループを提案した。
llm.result: RobomimicおよびRoboEvalでの実験により、タスク実行品質と成功率が反復ごとに向上し、実世界の操作タスクでも実用的な利得が示された。
keywords_ja: ヒンドサイト再ラベリング

2610.37393.hf_summary_en: Quality-Controllable Policy enables real-time adjustment of robot execution quality and improves performance through iterative hindsight relabeling of online rollouts.

2610.37381.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
2610.37381.abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model.
