Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.
2610.37381.tldr_en: PDRVLA is introduced, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation, andlations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.
2610.37381.hf_summary_en: PDRVLA improves robot action generation by integrating a lightweight physical dynamics module that predicts future visual features with world-model supervision, avoiding online video generation latency.

llm.title_ja: 物理ダイナミクス表現を持つVLAモデル：PDRVLA
llm.tldr_ja: オンラインでの動画生成を行わずに、視覚言語特徴から物理トークンを抽出してアクション生成を条件付けする軽量な物理ダイナミクスモジュールを備えたPDRVLAを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の視覚・言語・行動（VLA）モデルは物理ダイナミクスの理解が限定的であり、ビデオ世界モデルは将来の動画生成によって制御ループに高い遅延をもたらす点。
llm.method: 将来のRGB、深度、オプティカルフロー特徴の直接予測を通じて学習し、凍結された事前学習済みビデオ世界モデルによる補助的監督を受ける軽量な物理ダイナミクスモジュールを導入した。
llm.result: 4つのシミュレーションベンチマークにおいて、LIBEROで99.3%、LIBERO-Plusで89.9%、RoboTwin 2.0で93.6%、SimplerEnvで81.5%の成功率を達成した。

2610.37378.title: VLA-Stem: A Lightweight Safety Mechanism for Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforcement Learning
2610.37378.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate high-level reasoning with low-level action execution for end-to-end robotic control. However, most VLA models target static manipulation in unconstrained environments, overlooking spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. Fine-tuning VLAs on obstacle-avoidance data is a straightforward solution, but collecting such data is costly, especially for dynamic scenarios, and may degrade their original task capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose VLA-Stem, a lightweight, reinforcement-learning-based safety mechanism for VLA systems. Without fine-tuning the underlying VLA policy, VLA-Stem converts its action chunks into motion references and uses trajectory-level guidance to preserve their spatial intent while allowing flexible motion and timing adjustments. Conditioned on these references, robot proprioception, and local obstacle information, the Stem policy adaptively modifies execution at inference time, preserving the original task intent while enabling responsive adaptation to spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. For robust and sample-efficient training, we combine teacher-student distillation with curriculum learning. We evaluate VLA-Stem on reference following, static spatial constraints, and dynamic obstacle avoidance. Across six constrained simulation settings, VLA-Stem achieves 52.8% average collision-free task success versus 23.7% for the strongest safety baseline, while preserving base-policy performance in obstacle-free settings; real-world experiments further show consistent collision reductions under static and dynamic obstacles. These results demonstrate that VLA-Stem couples high-level VLA task intent with rapid, reflex-like responses to immediate physical risks, providing a brainstem-inspired mechanism for robust robot execution.
2610.37378.tldr_en: Results demonstrate that VLA-Stem couples high-level VLA task intent with rapid, reflex-like responses to immediate physical risks, providing a brainstem-inspired mechanism for robust robot execution.

llm.title_ja: 強化学習を用いたVLAモデルのための軽量安全機構：VLA-Stem
llm.tldr_ja: ベースとなるVLAポリシーをファインチューニングすることなく、即座の物理的リスクに対して迅速な反射的応答を可能にする脳幹に着想を得た安全機構VLA-Stemを提案した。
llm.problem: 大半のVLAモデルは静的な操作を対象としており、空間的制約や動的障害物を考慮しておらず、障害物回避データの収集が高コストである点。
llm.method: VLAのアクションチャンクをモーション参照に変換し、教師-生徒蒸留とカリキュラム学習を組み合わせて推論時に実行を適応的に修正する強化学習ベースの安全機構を構築した。
llm.result: 6つの制約付きシミュレーション設定で平均52.8%の衝突回避成功率を達成し、実世界実験でも静的・動的障害物に対する一貫した衝突削減を示した。

2610.37350.title: Generalizable Target-Less Joint Intrinsic-Extrinsic Camera-LiDAR Calibration using Deep Pixel-Point Correspondences
2610.37350.abstract: Accurate camera-LiDAR calibration is an essential prerequisite for robust multi-modal perception in robotics. Recent target-less methods based on learned pixel-point correspondences achieve high extrinsic calibration accuracy and generalize across environments. However, they operate on rectified images with known camera intrinsics, restricting their applicability to systems whose cameras have already been individually calibrated. We present a fully automatic, target-less framework that jointly estimates camera intrinsics, radial-tangential distortion, and camera-LiDAR extrinsics from raw images and LiDAR scans. Our method generalizes deep correspondence-based calibration from rectified images to raw cameras through intrinsic- and distortion-aware correspondence learning via synthetic augmentations. During calibration, we iteratively couple correspondence prediction and nonlinear optimization to jointly refine the camera parameters and relative sensor transformation. We evaluate our approach on an unseen camera-LiDAR configuration from the KITTI dataset and on three real robotic platforms in a zero-shot manner. The results demonstrate that joint calibration with our generalized pixel-point correspondence network improves extrinsic accuracy over correspondence-based methods using pre-calibrated cameras, while additionally recovering accurate intrinsics.
2610.37350.tldr_en: The results demonstrate that joint calibration with the generalized pixel-point correspondence network improves extrinsic accuracy over correspondence-based methods using pre-calibrated cameras, while additionally recovering accurate intrinsics.

llm.title_ja: 深層ピクセル・点対応を用いた汎用的なターゲットレス共同カメラ・LiDAR較正
llm.tldr_ja: 生画像とLiDARスキャンからカメラの内部パラメータ、動径・接線方向の歪み、およびカメラ-LiDAR間の外部パラメータを共同で推定する完全自動のターゲットレスフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のターゲットレス手法は個別に較正済みのカメラを前提とした整流画像に依存しており、適用範囲が制限される点。
llm.method: 合成拡張を用いた固有・歪み対応型対応学習により、ディープ対応ベースの較正を整流画像から生カメラへと拡張し、対応予測と非線形最適化を反復的に結合する。
llm.result: KITTIデータセットや3つの実ロボットプラットフォームにおけるゼロショット評価で、事前較正済みカメラを使用する手法よりも外部パラメータの精度が向上し、正確な内部パラメータも復元できた。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2610.37330.title: Tokens of Motion: Primitive Motion Learning for Human-Humanoid Skill Transfer
2610.37330.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models provide a promising paradigm for scalable robotic manipulation, yet their reliance on success-only behavioral cloning leaves them brittle; lacking corrective training signals, minor execution errors rapidly compound into unrecoverable, out-of-distribution failures. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL), an end-to-end framework that leverages failure trajectories as adaptive negative guidance for diffusion- and flow-based VLA policies. AFIL uses a pretrained VLA to generate failure rollouts online, avoiding the need for handcrafted failure-mode design or human-in-the-loop recovery. It then jointly trains Dual Action Generators (DAGs) for successful and failed behaviors while sharing a common vision-language backbone, enabling efficient failure-aware policy learning with limited parameter overhead. During sampling, the failure generator adaptively steers action generation away from failure-prone regions and toward more reliable success modes, with guidance strength determined by the per-diffusion-step distance between success and failure distributions. Experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain robotic manipulation tasks, covering both short- and long-horizon settings, show that AFIL consistently improves task success rates and robustness over existing VLA baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness, efficiency, and generality.
2610.37330.tldr_en: Experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain robotic manipulation tasks, covering both short- and long-horizon settings, show that AFIL consistently improves task success rates and robustness over existing VLA baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness, efficiency, and generality.

llm.title_ja: 運動のトークン：ヒューマン・ヒューマノイドスキル転移のためのプリミティブ運動学習
llm.tldr_ja: 成功のみの行動複製に依存するVLAポリシーの限界に対処するため、失敗軌跡を適応的な負のガイダンスとして活用する適応的失敗情報学習（AFIL）フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 成功データのみに基づく行動複製（BC）に依存するVLAポリシーは修正信号がなく、わずかな実行誤差が蓄積して回復不可能な分布外の失敗につながる点。
llm.method: 事前学習済みVLAを用いてオンラインで失敗ロールアウトを生成し、共通の視覚言語バックボーンを共有しながら成功・失敗の行動を共同で訓練するデュアルアクションジェネレータ（DAGs）を採用する。
llm.result: ドメイン内およびドメイン外のロボット操作タスクにおける実験により、既存のVLAベースラインと比較してタスク成功率と堅牢性が一貫して向上することが示された。

2610.37326.title: ScIntBench: Physical Interaction Plausibility in 3D Scene Generation
2610.37326.abstract: Existing evaluations of text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation largely emphasize semantic fidelity and physical validity at rest, leaving interaction-time physical reliability insufficiently assessed. To address this gap, we introduce ScIntBench, a unified benchmark centered on interaction readiness: it executes prescribed manipulation actions (e.g., pushing, opening, and surface probing) in physics simulation and measures task success, capability and progress, post-interaction integrity, and dynamic plausibility. Multi-view semantic and static physical evaluations complement these metrics and help explain interaction outcomes. We systematically evaluate 12 state-of-the-art scene generation systems across 10 room types. Our results reveal that strong semantic and static physical performance does not necessarily translate into interaction readiness: a system with near-perfect static plausibility completes only 11.54% of interactions, 7 of the 12 systems produce scenes that cannot support any interaction, and even the best system succeeds in only 36.92% of prescribed tasks. These findings highlight two fundamental challenges in generating interaction-ready scenes: providing the necessary physical interaction capabilities and ensuring reliable physical behavior under active manipulation.
2610.37326.tldr_en: ScIntBench is introduced, a unified benchmark centered on interaction readiness that executes prescribed manipulation actions in physics simulation and measures task success, capability and progress, post-interaction integrity, and dynamic plausibility.

llm.title_ja: ScIntBench：3Dシーン生成における物理的インタラクションの妥当性評価
llm.tldr_ja: 物理シミュレーション内で所定の操作アクションを実行し、タスク成功率や動的妥当性を測定する、インタラクション準備状況に焦点を当てた統合ベンチマークScIntBenchを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のテキスト条件付き3D屋内シーン生成の評価はセマンティックな忠実度や静的な物理的妥当性に偏っており、インタラクション時の物理的信頼性が十分に評価されていない点。
llm.method: 10種類の部屋タイプにわたり、12の最先端シーン生成システムに対して、物理シミュレーション内で押す、開く、表面をプローブするなどの操作アクションを実行して評価する。
llm.result: 強力な静的物理的性能を持つシステムであってもインタラクション準備が整っているとは限らず、半数以上のシステムがインタラクションを全くサポートできないシーンを生成することが判明した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション
インタラクション評価

2610.37310.title: Spiking Neuromorphic Control for Periodic Orbits Stabilization in Underactuated Robots: A Greedy Lyapunov-Based Approach
2610.37310.abstract: This work investigates the use of event-based spiking controllers, implemented as spiking neural networks, for trajectory tracking in underactuated robots. Specifically, we address the problem of stabilizing a prescribed periodic orbit. It is well known that, by applying the method of transverse linearization to the robot dynamics in a neighborhood of a periodic trajectory, the dynamics can be approximately described by a linear time-varying system with periodic coefficients (a periodic LTV system). The problem of orbital stabilization can therefore be reduced to stabilizing the trivial solution of this LTV system. We show that a previously proposed Lyapunov-based greedy design, originally developed for LTI systems, can also be extended to the corresponding linearized transverse dynamics, which take the form of a periodic LTV system. This enables the construction of a feedback controller for orbital stabilization of the robot. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated on the trajectory stabilization problem for the butterfly robot.
2610.37310.tldr_en: This work investigates the use of event-based spiking controllers, implemented as spiking neural networks, for trajectory tracking in underactuated robots and shows that a previously proposed Lyapunov-based greedy design can be extended to the corresponding linearized transverse dynamics, which take the form of a periodic LTV system.

llm.title_ja: アンダースチュアードロボットの周期軌道安定化に向けたスパイクニューロモルフィック制御：貪欲リヤプノフベースのアプローチ
llm.tldr_ja: スパイクニューラルネットワークとして実装されたイベントベースのスパイクコントローラーを用いて、アンダースチュアードロボットの軌道追従および周期軌道安定化の問題に取り組んだ。
llm.problem: アンダースチュアードロボットにおける所定の周期軌道の安定化およびイベントベース制御の実装。
llm.method: 周期軌道の近傍におけるロボットダイナミクスの横方向線形化を適用し、LTIシステム向けに開発されたリヤプノフベースの貪欲設計を周期LTVシステムに拡張してフィードバックコントローラーを構築した。
llm.result: 提案手法の有効性をバタフライロボットの軌道安定化問題によって実証した。
keywords_ja: スパイクニューラルネットワーク
ニューロモルフィック制御
アンダースチュアードロボット

2610.37298.title: Understanding Human-Robot Collaboration through Joint Action
2610.37298.abstract: Human-robot collaboration requires partners to coordinate interdependent contributions toward a shared goal. Joint Action theory provides concepts for understanding this coordination, but how these concepts are instantiated and combined across empirical research remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA 2020, identifying 83 empirical papers published between 2021 and 2026. Through theory-driven framework analysis, we organized the literature into nine constructs across three capacities: Representation, Prediction, and Integration. We analyze how these constructs are distributed and co-occur across studies, revealing where empirical evidence concentrates and where it is absent. By mapping empirical HRC research onto a unified Joint Action framework, this review offers a coherent overview of HRC studies, identifies gaps in current evidence, and provides guidelines for future research.
2610.37298.tldr_en: A systematic review of empirical HRC research following PRISMA 2020, identifying 83 empirical papers published between 2021 and 2026 and organized the literature into nine constructs across three capacities: Representation, Prediction, and Integration.

llm.title_ja: 共同行動を通じた人とロボットの協調の理解
llm.tldr_ja: PRISMA 2020に準拠した系統的レビューを実施し、2021年から2026年までに発表された83件の実証論文を分析して、表現、予測、統合の3つの能力にわたる9つの構成概念に整理した。
llm.problem: 人とロボットの協調（HRC）に関する共同行動理論の概念が、実証研究の間でどのように具体化・統合されているかの断片化。
llm.method: PRISMA 2020ガイドラインに従った系統的レビューを行い、理論主導のフレームワーク分析を用いて文献を整理・分類した。
llm.result: HRC研究を統一された共同行動フレームワークにマッピングし、現在の証拠におけるギャップを特定して将来の研究指針を提供した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.37239.title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning
2610.37239.abstract: Multi-relational graph detectors learn from clean data how much to trust each relation, but an adversary pays a different price to manipulate each relation and each action; taking such costs as given, we ask when using a relation is worse than ignoring it. Our first main result proves that degree gating strictly beats every selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, and that this window is sharp; on real graphs, validated gating gains exactly on the relations that meet these conditions and nowhere else. Our second shows that a per-node exposure bound, which extends to message passing, tells a platform which relation to harden: exposure per unit cost, computed without any attack, picks the relation whose hardening raises the exact trap threshold most in 15 of 16 cases, against at most 7 for informativeness, cheapness, or an analysis with equal edit costs. Supporting tools give exact worst cases for linear relational models, certified brackets for R-GCN and tree ensembles, and a finite-sample guarantee for adversarial validation, under which clean-trained graph detectors fall below their graph-free counterparts in 58 of 90 settings on six graphs. A selection protocol built on these results is never significantly worse than ignoring the graph; with at most four relations it mostly abstains, as validation alone would, and its cost-aware proposals help when relations are many, so far shown on synthetic graphs. Without cost information, the safe choice is to abstain.
2610.37239.tldr_en: This work proves that degree gating strictly beats every selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, and shows that a per-node exposure bound tells a platform which relation to harden.

llm.title_ja: 関係を信頼する価値はいつあるのか：マルチ関係グラフ学習における操作コスト、露出、およびトラップ
llm.tldr_ja: マルチ関係グラフ検出器において、攻撃者が関係を操作するためのコストを考慮した際、特定の条件下では関係の選択や再重み付けよりも次数ゲーティングが厳密に優れていることを証明した。
llm.problem: マルチ関係グラフ学習において、敵対者が各関係を操作するコストが異なる場合に、どの関係を使用し、どれを無視すべきかの判定基準の確立。
llm.method: 母集団の一部が関係上で孤立しており攻撃者がゲートを開けられない場合における次数ゲーティングの理論的証明、およびノードごとの露出バウンドを用いたプラットフォームの硬化対象選択プロトコルを提案した。
llm.result: 度数ゲーティングがすべての選択や再重み付けよりも厳密に優れていることを証明し、提案された選択プロトコルはグラフを無視するよりも有意に悪化しないことを示した。
keywords_ja: グラフニューラルネットワーク

2610.37219.title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
2610.37219.abstract: The vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action model (WAM) communities debate whether control policies should inherit pretrained knowledge from vision-language models or from visual generators. The debate, however, bundles three separable choices: backbone initialization, the objective applied to future observations, and whether the machinery for that future loss is kept at inference. A gap between a VLA and a WAM therefore cannot simply be attributed to any one of them. We show that decoupling these choices yields a common framework for both families, which we term Just Action Model (JAM): a pretrained visual backbone with an action expert, trained with an action loss and a foresight loss. The foresight loss trains current-observation features to predict frozen encodings of the recorded future through a prediction head discarded after training, so no visual generation is involved in either training or inference, and the backbone can be chosen freely. We first compare objectives within fixed policy architectures, then evaluate the foresight recipe across backbone families. The resulting JAM policies outperform their matched FastWAM and ImageWAM counterparts on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and achieve similar or slightly higher success rates on RoboTwin. Compared with FastWAM, JAM improves the success rates from 97.0%/55.3%/91.2% to 98.2%/64.5%/91.4%, respectively. With cached foresight targets, JAM reduces estimated online training FLOPs per sample per update by 73% relative to FastWAM. Our results show that future supervision improves control without visual generation or additional inference machinery, and strong foresight performance is attainable with either generator-initialized or vision-language backbones. Project Page: https://y0uroy.github.io/JAM
2610.37219.tldr_en: The results show that future supervision improves control without visual generation or additional inference machinery, and strong foresight performance is attainable with either generator-initialized or vision-language backbones.
2610.37219.hf_summary_en: Just Action Model decouples backbone initialization, future observation objectives, and inference machinery to improve robot control with foresight training and reduced computation.

llm.title_ja: Vision-Language-ActionまたはWorld-Action？単なる行動モデル（JAM）
llm.tldr_ja: 将来予測の監視を導入しつつ視覚生成や追加の推論機構を排除することで、事前学習済みバックボーンを活用しつつ制御性能を向上させる「Just Action Model（JAM）」フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAとWAMのコミュニティにおいて、制御ポリシーの事前知識の継承元や将来観測への損失適用の選択肢が混在し、性能差の要因が不明確であったこと。
llm.method: 将来の記録の凍結符号化を予測する予見損失と行動損失を用い、予測ヘッドを訓練後に破棄することで視覚生成を伴わずに学習・推論を行うJAMフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: LIBEROおよびLIBERO-Plusにおいて既存のFastWAMやImageWAMを上回り、RoboTwinでも同等以上の成功率を達成しつつ、オンライン訓練の計算量を大幅に削減した。

2610.37217.title: KEPT: Conformal Keepouts Kept in Planning for Enclosed-Space Navigation in Degraded Sensing
2610.37217.abstract: Autonomous vehicles in enclosed spaces such as tunnels and mines rely on range maps that smoke, dust and fog make inaccurate. Conformal prediction calibrates a keepout around the mapped walls that covers the true unsafe set at a chosen probability. Typically an unmodified planner treats the keepout as an inflated obstacle, and nothing ensures that the vehicle can stop before the keepout as it moves when sensing degrades. In narrow passages this margin and the planner's buffer close the route, and existing remedies recover reach by relaxing the coverage level. This paper conditions the conformal margin on a label-free severity estimate to hold coverage near its target as degradation varies. A planning and control layer enforces one braking-distance condition on the keepout at plan time and at every command, takes the measured tracking residual as its only margin and never alters the keepout. The keepout is validated on ground-robot smoke recordings and the closed loop in simulated quadrotor flights in a foggy tunnel against the standard deployment. In closed-loop simulation the proposed system substantially reduces entries into the calibrated keepout and reaches numerically more goals than the deployment pattern in both calibration regimes, an observed gain of 3.2 percentage points pooled whose per-regime confidence intervals include zero. The per-class keepout holds its coverage near the target on held-out recordings.
2610.37217.tldr_en: The proposed system substantially reduces entries into the calibrated keepout and reaches numerically more goals than the deployment pattern in both calibration regimes, and the per-class keepout holds its coverage near the target on held-out recordings.

llm.title_ja: KEPT：劣化センシング下の閉空間ナビゲーションにおける計画へのコンフォーマル・キープアウトの組込み
llm.tldr_ja: ラベルなしの劣化度推定に基づいてコンフォーマルマージンを条件付けし、計画時および制御時に制約を課すことで、煙や霧などの劣化センシング下でも安全性を維持して目標到達性を高めるシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: トンネルや鉱山などの閉空間において、煙や塵によりレンジマップが不正確になり、従来のプランナーでは安全な停止やルート確保が困難になること。
llm.method: ラベルなしの重大度推定に基づいてコンフォーマルマージンを調整し、計画時と全コマンド実行時にブレーキ距離条件を課す計画・制御層を導入した。
llm.result: 霧のトンネル内のシミュレーションおよびグラウンドロボットの記録を用いた検証において、キープアウト領域への侵入を大幅に削減し、目標到達数を向上させた。

2610.37215.title: Retrieve to Act: Motion Primitive Graph Retrieval for Robust VLA Execution
2610.37215.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies demonstrate remarkable semantic generalization, yet remain highly vulnerable to out-of-distribution (OOD) visual shifts during execution. While existing test-time methods attempt to suppress spurious visual cues, they fundamentally overlook the rich, uncorrupted kinematic priors embedded in the policy's own training experience. We introduce Retrieve to Act (R2A), a test-time scaling framework that formulates OOD robustness purely as a geometric motion primitive retrieval problem. R2A bypasses fragile visual features by structuring successful training demonstrations into an offline spatiotemporal motion primitive graph. During inference, a query-dependent Graph Neural Network dynamically localizes the robot's ongoing execution within this graph, retrieving structurally compatible future motion primitives. These retrieved geometric priors are then seamlessly harmonized with the frozen VLA's predicted actions via a learned, dimension-wise gating mechanism, adaptively rectifying erroneous spatial trajectories while preserving the policy's local reactivity. Extensive experiments across three state-of-the-art VLA architectures, GR00T N1.7, $π_{0.5}$, and StableVLA, demonstrate that R2A consistently and significantly enhances robustness against diverse contextual perturbations. R2A achieves absolute success rate improvements of up to +12% in simulation benchmarks (LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0-Plus) and +40% in real-world deployments, without requiring any finetuning of the base policies. Project page: https://retrieve2act.github.io/r2a/
2610.37215.tldr_en: Retrieve to Act is introduced, a test-time scaling framework that formulates OOD robustness purely as a geometric motion primitive retrieval problem that achieves absolute success rate improvements in simulation benchmarks and in real-world deployments, without requiring any finetuning of the base policies.

llm.title_ja: Retrieve to Act：ロバストなVLA実行のためのモーションプリミティブグラフ検索
llm.tldr_ja: VLAの実行時のOOD頑健性を高めるため、成功した訓練デモンストレーションをオフラインのモーションプリミティブグラフとして構造化し、テスト時に幾何学的な運動事前情報を検索して適応的に修正するR2Aフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーは優れた意味的汎化性能を示す一方で、実行時のドメイン外（OOD）の視覚的変動に対して非常に脆弱であること。
llm.method: 成功デモンストレーションからスパシオテポラルなモーションプリミティブグラフを構築し、GNNを用いて推論時に適切な未来の運動プリミティブを動的に検索・統合する。
llm.result: シミュレーションベンチマーク（LIBERO-Plus等）で最大+12%、実機展開で最大+40%の絶対成功率の向上をベースポリシーの微調整なしで達成した。
keywords_ja: モーションプリミティブ

2610.37203.title: Remember Where You Walk: Learning Spatial Memory for End-to-End Legged Robot Exploration
2610.37203.abstract: Humanoids and other legged robots operating in complex environments must remember information that leaves their field of view and only becomes relevant much later. Reinforcement learning policies address this using memory networks such as LSTMs that are trained end-to-end with the policy to memorize such task-relevant aspects. Yet, such architectures often fail to preserve sufficient information over long horizons. In this work, we propose a network architecture based on Hadamard memory that specifically targets robot navigation. Our Local Spatial Matrix Memory (LSMM) enables RL agents to store generic task-relevant information at specific, position-based memory cells, enabling flexible and spatially grounded memorization. We evaluate LSMM on the task of autonomous maze exploration, where it matches the maze coverage of strong recurrent and finite-history baselines while being the only architecture that remembers the maze layout, reducing the reconstruction error threefold.
2610.37203.tldr_en: This work proposes a network architecture based on Hadamard memory that specifically targets robot navigation and enables RL agents to store generic task-relevant information at specific, position-based memory cells, enabling flexible and spatially grounded memorization.

llm.title_ja: 歩いた場所を記憶する：エンド端脚ロボット探索のための空間メモリの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 位置ベースの特定メモリセルに汎用的なタスク関連情報を保存できるアダマールメモリに基づくネットワークアーキテクチャ（LSMM）を提案し、脚ロボットの自律的な迷路探索性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: リカレントニューラルネットワークなどの従来のメモリネットワークは、複雑な環境で視野外の重要な情報を長期間にわたって保持し続けることが困難である点。
llm.method: タスク関連情報を位置ベースのメモリセルに柔軟に保存できるアダマールメモリに基づくネットワークアーキテクチャ（Local Spatial Matrix Memory: LSMM）を提案し、強化学習エージェントに組み込んだ。
llm.result: 自律迷路探索タスクにおいて、強力なリカレントおよび過去履歴ベースのベースラインと同等の迷路カバー率を達成しつつ、迷路のレイアウトを記憶する唯一のアーキテクチャとして再構築誤差を3分の1に削減した。

2610.37199.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control
2610.37199.abstract: Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent. We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity ($1.625$ m/s$^2$) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization. The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima. We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

llm.title_ja: 2Dジャンプおよび着地制御を備えた月面単足ロボットのための二層協調設計フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 差動進化の外側ループと2種類のコントローラ評価を組み合わせた二層協調設計フレームワークを用いて、月面重力下における月面探査用単足ロボットのリンク長と制御手法の相互依存性を研究した。
llm.problem: 月面探査用の脚ロボットは低重力下で接触力が低下し飛行フェーズが長くなるため、脚の形態とコントローラの選択が相互依存的になること。
llm.method: 差動進化による外側ループでリンク長を探索し、各候補をQP-TSCまたは軌道最適化のいずれかで評価する二層協調設計フレームワークを構築し、2DジャンプとLQR制御に拡張した。
llm.result: 軌道最適化が設計空間の大部分でQP-TSCを上回り、輸送コスト（COT）を17%削減できることを示し、基準形態での安定したその場ジャンプおよび前方ジャンプを実証した。

2610.37196.title: How Much Can Best-of-N Help a World Action Model? Measuring Selectable Headroom and Realizing It in Closed Loop
2610.37196.abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict the visual consequences of the actions they generate, which makes test-time selection a natural way to improve a fixed policy: imagine the futures of candidate actions and execute the best one. The benefit of selection is bounded by the selectable headroom, how much better the best candidate truly is, but the standard estimate, which executes each candidate once and keeps the best outcome, conflates candidate quality with the randomness of everything that follows. We introduce a denoised counterfactual protocol, based on bitwise-reproducible branching, repeated continuations, held-out oracles, and common random numbers, that measures the headroom a selector can realize, and use its measurements to build a fail-gated selector. Across four WAMs, two benchmarks, over 100,000 branched rollouts, and pre-registered tests, we find that (i) the standard estimate overstates the selectable headroom of native samples: bounds from 17 continuations per candidate place its selectable share between 24% and 66% for three WAMs; (ii) structured action perturbations create up to 16 points of selectable headroom; and (iii) in both WAMs with action-conditioned imagination, imagined futures carry candidate-outcome information with no detectable loss relative to real futures, information that the value head of Cosmos Policy leaves unused. Deviating from the policy chunk only when a readout of the WAM predicts failure, the selector raises closed-loop task success from 76.9% to 81.6% on held-out episodes of training tasks, with the largest gain where the policy fails most often, and from 62.6% to 69.8% on unseen tasks.
2610.37196.tldr_en: A denoised counterfactual protocol is introduced, based on bitwise-reproducible branching, repeated continuations, held-out oracles, and common random numbers, that measures the headroom a selector can realize, and uses its measurements to build a fail-gated selector.

llm.title_ja: World Action Modelに対するBest-of-Nの効果：選択可能なヘッドルームの測定と閉ループでの実現
llm.tldr_ja: ビット単位で再現可能な分岐や反復継続に基づくノイズ除去カウンターファクトラルプロトコルを導入し、World Action Model（WAM）における選択可能なヘッドルームを測定して失敗ゲート付きセレクタを構築した。
llm.problem: WAMにおいてテスト時の選択によりポリシーを改善できるが、標準的な推定方法は候補の品質とそれに続くランダム性を混同してしまうこと。
llm.method: ビット単位で再現可能な分岐、保持されたオラクル、共通乱数を用いた「ノイズ除去カウンターファクトラルプロトコル」を提案し、ポリシーのチャンクから逸脱して失敗を予測した場合にのみ作動するセレクタを構築した。
llm.result: 4つのWAMと2つのベンチマークを用いた検証において、標準推定がネイティブサンプルのヘッドルームを過大評価していることを示し、提案するセレクタにより閉ループのタスク成功率を向上させた。

2610.37190.title: Acoustic Signature Optimisation for Bioinspired Flapping-Wing Micro Aerial Vehicles
2610.37190.abstract: Flapping-wing micro air vehicles are prized for quiet flight, yet the few existing measurements show engineered wings to be 15-30 dB louder than the animals they imitate. This paper investigates two passive geometric approaches to reduce the acoustic signature of a flapping membrane wing, and applies these to an exemplary wing. A significant sound source in flapping wings is the impulsive click radiated at stroke reversal, when a slack membrane snaps between two curvatures. Our first noise-reduction approach optimises the wing's venation layout, based on an analytical model of the reversal click as a dynamic snap-through of the membrane. The optimised venation pattern was manufactured and resulted in a reduction of up to 8 dB during the reversal snap in experiments. During testing, the venation was found to be sensitive to orientation rather than thickness. Secondly, an additive trailing-edge fringe inspired by hummingbird feathers was shown to further reduce the broadband swoosh by 3-4 dB at no lift cost, matching a cut serration wing without removing lifting area.

llm.title_ja: 生体模倣フラッピング翼型マイクロ飛行機の音響シグネチャ最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 膜の動的なスナップスルーとしての反転クリックの解析モデルに基づく脈絡レイアウトの最適化と、ハチドリの羽にインスパイアされたフリンジの追加により、揚力を損なわずにフラッピング翼の騒音を大幅に低減した。
llm.problem: フラッピング翼を持つマイクロ飛行機は静粛性で知られているが、既存の設計の翼は模倣対象の生物よりも15〜30 dB騒音が大きいこと。
llm.method: ストローク反転時のインパルス性クリックを抑制するための脈絡パターンの最適化と、ハチドリの羽にインスパイアされた付加的なトレーリングエッジフリンジの適用という2つの受動的幾何学アプローチを採用した。
llm.result: 最適化された脈絡により反転スナップ時の騒音を最大8 dB削減し、フリンジによって揚力を落とすことなくブロードバンドの音をさらに3〜4 dB低減することに成功した。

2610.37170.title: From 12 to 200 Demonstrations: How ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA and $π_{0.5}$ Scale on a Low-Cost Arm
2610.37170.abstract: We trained four widely used imitation-learning policies, ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA and $π_{0.5}$, on nested subsets of 12, 25, 50, 100 and 200 teleoperated demonstrations of one pick-and-place task with distractor objects, using one fixed training recipe per policy. Every trained model was then run on a physical SO-101 arm on a fixed set of object placements: 1,340 scored episodes in 126 blocks. ACT, trained from scratch, rose from 1 success in 40 episodes at 12 demonstrations to 37 in 40 at 100. $π_{0.5}$ with its action expert fine-tuned was the best policy when data was scarce (16 of 40 at 12 demonstrations, 28 of 40 at 25) and then stayed near 70%; from 100 demonstrations ACT was ahead, by a margin this study does not fully resolve. SmolVLA and Diffusion Policy peaked near 50%, and both were affected by a failure to start: SmolVLA's arm never started moving in 47% of episodes, and Diffusion Policy hardly ever started until an idle lead-in was trimmed from the demonstrations. For $π_{0.5}$ the fine-tuning recipe mattered more than the amount of data: low-rank adaptation succeeded in 4 of 110 episodes, against 130 of 200 for action-expert fine-tuning. From the joint and camera recordings we place every episode on a four-stage ladder (started, reached the ball, carried it, delivered it) and show that for ACT more data moves failures from reaching, to grasping, to none, while the failures $π_{0.5}$ retains are in grasping. We also measure how weak a ten-episode block is as a measurement (the same checkpoint tested twice differs by 2 successes in 10 on average), separate seed-to-seed variation from that noise, and audit the human scoring against the recordings. Training length was fixed within each recipe, so the amount of data and the number of times it was seen change together; we state which conclusions survive that confound and which do not.
2610.37170.tldr_en: Four widely used imitation-learning policies are trained on nested subsets of 12, 25, 50, 100 and 200 teleoperated demonstrations of one pick-and-place task with distractor objects using one fixed training recipe per policy, which states which conclusions survive that confound and which do not.

llm.title_ja: 12から200のデモンストレーションへ：ACT、Diffusion Policy、SmolVLA、π0.5の低コストアームにおけるスケーリング評価
llm.tldr_ja: 4つの広く使われている模倣学習ポリシーを、12から200のデモンストレーションを用いたピックアンドプレース課題で学習・評価し、データ量やファインチューニングレシピが性能に与える影響を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 低コストなロボットアームにおける模倣学習ポリシー（ACT、Diffusion Policy、SmolVLA、π0.5など）のデータスケーリング則や学習レシピの違いによる影響が十分に整理されていなかったこと。
llm.method: 12、25、50、100、200のデモンストレーションのネストされたサブセットを用いて4つのポリシーを学習させ、実機のSO-101アームで1,340エピソードの評価を実施した。
llm.result: データが少ない状況ではπ0.5が優れ、データが豊富になるとACTが優れるなど、ポリシーごとに異なるスケーリング特性や、ファインチューニングレシピ（LoRA vs アクションエキスパート）の重要性を明らかにした。

2610.37153.title: FastBEVFusion: Simple Multi-Modal Fusion for 3D Object Detection at 50 FPS
2610.37153.abstract: Reliable real-time 3D object detection based on LiDAR and camera data is critical for safety in autonomous driving, where systems must accurately perceive their surroundings with minimal latency. Many state-of-the-art systems achieve high-quality detection results but fail to meet real-time constraints, limiting their practical use. To address this challenge, we propose FastBEVFusion, a simple, fast, and robust fusion system for 3D object detection. Based on modality-specific features, FastBEVFusion projects these features into semi-aligned modality-specific BEV spaces, without relying on a computationally intensive and potentially error-prone depth estimation. Given these BEV spaces, we propose a light-weight, soft, and dynamic fusion module based on cross-attention, which adapts dynamically to the scene context and enables feature fusion across the entire BEV spaces. Experiments on the complex nuScenes dataset show that FastBEVFusion outperforms state-of-the-art real-time systems, and achieves over 50 FPS without deployment libraries. Additionally, our system shows strong robustness to calibration errors, making FastBEVFusion a powerful 3D object detection system for real-world applications.
2610.37153.tldr_en: This work proposes FastBEVFusion, a simple, fast, and robust fusion system for 3D object detection based on modality-specific features that outperforms state-of-the-art real-time systems, and achieves over 50 FPS without deployment libraries.

llm.title_ja: FastBEVFusion：50 FPSでの3D物体検出のためのシンプルなマルチモーダル融合
llm.tldr_ja: 計算コストの高い深度推定に依存せず、クロスアテンションに基づく軽量な動的融合モジュールにより、複雑なnuScenesデータセット上でデプロイメントライブラリなしで50 FPS以上を達成する3D物体検出システム「FastBEVFusion」を提案した。
llm.problem: LiDARとカメラデータに基づく信頼性の高いリアルタイム3D物体検出は自動運転の安全性に不可欠であるが、多くの最先端システムはリアルタイム制約を満たせないこと。
llm.method: モダリティ固有の特徴を明示的な深度推定なしで半整列したBEV空間に射影し、シーンの文脈に動的に適応するクロスアテンションを用いた軽量でソフトな動的融合モジュールを構築した。
llm.result: nuScenesデータセットにおいて最先端のリアルタイムシステムを凌駕し、専用ライブラリなしで50 FPS以上の処理速度と較正誤差に対する強い頑健性を実証した。

2610.37127.title: MCP-Net: Real-Time Coronary Perception Network and Topological Analysis for Robotic Guidewire Navigation
2610.37127.abstract: Coronary guidewire navigation during percutaneous coronary intervention requires continuous interpretation of vessel anatomy, guidewire position, and target stenosis under two-dimensional X-ray fluoroscopy. While existing approaches commonly address vessel segmentation or device localization as separate tasks, a robotic system requires a more structured perception of the coronary scene to support downstream navigation. In this work, we present a simulation-driven framework centered on a Multi-Task Coronary Perception Network (MCP-Net) for robotic guidewire navigation, integrating coronary vessel segmentation, vascular topology extraction, and roadmap generation. Starting from three-dimensional coronary CT angiography, we generate simulated fluoroscopy images containing vascular structures, simulated guidewires, stenotic lesions with varying severity, and diverse vascular geometries, together with simulation-derived ground truth. MCP-Net jointly performs coronary vessel segmentation, guidewire-tip localization, and stenosis localization from a single fluoroscopic frame. These predictions are subsequently converted into a structured vascular graph containing centerlines, bifurcations, endpoints, branch directions, and branch angles. By associating the predicted stenosis with this graph, the framework generates a roadmap from the automatically selected graph root toward the target lesion. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can jointly recover coronary perception targets and transform them into an interpretable vascular representation suitable for downstream robotic navigation.
2610.37127.tldr_en: The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can jointly recover coronary perception targets and transform them into an interpretable vascular representation suitable for downstream robotic navigation.

llm.title_ja: MCP-Net：ロボットガイドワイヤナビゲーションのためのリアルタイム冠動脈知覚ネットワークとトポロジカル解析
llm.tldr_ja: 3D冠動脈CTアンギオグラフィからシミュレーション画像を生成し、血管セグメンテーション、ガイドワイヤ先端・狭窄の局所化を単一のX線透視フレームから同時におこなう「MCP-Net」を提案した。
llm.problem: 経皮的冠動脈形成術におけるロボットガイドワイヤナビゲーションには、血管解剖、ガイドワイヤ位置、標的狭窄の構造化された知覚が必要であること。
llm.method: シミュレーション駆動型のフレームワークを構築し、Multi-Task Coronary Perception Network（MCP-Net）によりセグメンテーション、ガイドワイヤ先端局所化、狭窄局所化を同時予測して血管グラフを構築する。
llm.result: 冠動脈の知覚ターゲットを同時に復元し、下流のロボットナビゲーションに適した解釈可能な血管表現へと変換できることを示した。
keywords_ja: 冠動脈ナビゲーション
血管セグメンテーション

2610.37111.title: RAVEN: A Unified Active SLAM System for Rapid Autonomous Visual Exploration with Aerial Robots under Localization Uncertainty
2610.37111.abstract: Active simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) addresses the problem of planning robot motion to build complete and accurate maps of unknown environments through efficient exploration while maintaining high localization accuracy. This raises a dilemma between exploring unknown spaces to expand coverage and exploiting visited regions to perform active loop closures. Despite numerous prior works on ground robots, aerial robots with high agility and constrained sensor suites face more significant localization drift and thereby demand dedicated active SLAM planning. Moreover, a unified strategy that adapts performance based on task-specific priorities remains an open question. In this article, we introduce RAVEN, a unified active SLAM framework for Rapid Autonomous Visual ExploratioN using quadrotors, which systematically accounts for localization uncertainty. The framework starts with identifying frontiers and active loop closure candidates, from which global tour candidates are generated. These candidates are evaluated using a utility vector that separately quantifies exploration efficiency and localization accuracy, and the final tour is selected according to a prioritization parameter ranging from $[0,1]$. Finally, a perception-aware navigation planner generates smooth execution trajectories that minimize visual state estimation error based on the online Fisher information field that provides visual localization information in real-time. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate that RAVEN outperforms state-of-the-art active SLAM methods, highlighting its advantages in producing a spectrum of performance across prioritizations. Fully onboard field experiments with a customized stereo-inertial quadrotor further validate its practical applicability in challenging environments. The source code will be released to benefit the community.
2610.37111.comment: Conditionally accepted to the IEEE Transactions on Robotics
2610.37111.tldr_en: Benchmark evaluations demonstrate that RAVEN outperforms state-of-the-art active SLAM methods, highlighting its advantages in producing a spectrum of performance across prioritizations.

llm.title_ja: RAVEN：局所化不確実性下における空中ロボットのための迅速な自律型視覚探索統合型アクティブSLAMシステム
llm.tldr_ja: フロンティアとアクティブーループクロージャ候補を体系的に評価し、探索効率と局所化精度のバランスをとるユーティリティベクトルを用いて最適化するクワッドローター向けアクティブSLAMフレームワーク「RAVEN」を提案した。
llm.problem: 空中ロボットは高い機敏性と制約されたセンサー群により深刻な局所化ドリフトに直面し、未知空間の探索と訪問済み領域の利用（ループクロージャ）のジレンマがあること。
llm.method: フロンティアとループクロージャ候補からグローバルツアー候補を生成し、優先度パラメータに基づくユーティリティベクトルで評価、オンラインのフィッシャー情報場に基づく知覚認識型ナビゲーションプランナーで軌道を生成する。
llm.result: ベンチマーク評価で既存の最先端アクティブSLAM手法を上回る性能を示し、ステレオ慣性クワッドローターを用いたオンボード実飛行実験でその実用性を実証した。

2610.37091.title: GAWM: A Compact Latent World-Action Model for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation
2610.37091.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) incorporate the prediction of future observations into robot policy learning. However, most WAMs build on billion-parameter vision-language or video-generation backbones, which incur high training cost and inference latency. In this letter, we present GAWM (Geometry-Aware World Model), a compact multi-task WAM that predicts future observations in the latent space of a frozen DINOv3 encoder. GAWM compresses the features of each camera view into a small set of tokens. A lightweight predictor, conditioned on the task rather than on actions, forecasts these tokens at two future horizons. The forecast is supervised with the dense patch features of future frames, which requires it to encode the spatial layout of the future scene. An action decoder directly regresses a chunk of future actions from the current and predicted tokens. With fewer than 100M parameters and no robot or video pretraining, GAWM outperforms billion-parameter WAMs on RoboTwin 2.0 and performs comparably to billion-parameter VLAs on LIBERO. On a dual-arm robot, it achieves lower action-prediction error on held-out demonstrations than a fine-tuned billion-parameter VLA, with substantially lower inference latency. Ablation studies show that the latent world model substantially improves performance when training data or training time is limited. Code is available at https://github.com/gaoxiang12/ga-wm.
2610.37091.tldr_en: GAWM (Geometry-Aware World Model), a compact multi-task WAM that predicts future observations in the latent space of a frozen DINOv3 encoder, outperforms billion-parameter WAMs on RoboTwin 2.0 and performs comparably to billion-parameter VLAs on LIBERO.

llm.title_ja: GAWM：マルチタスク・ロボットマニピュレーションのためのコンパクトな潜在世界行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結されたDINOv3エンコーダの潜在空間内で将来の観測を予測するコンパクトなマルチタスク世界行動モデル「GAWM」を提案し、大規模な事前学習なしで高い性能と低い推論レイテンシを達成した。
llm.problem: 多くの世界行動モデル（WAM）が10億パラメータを超える大規模な視覚言語モデルや動画生成バックボーンを基盤としており、学習コストや推論レイテンシが高いこと。
llm.method: 各カメラビューの特徴を少数のトークンに圧縮し、タスク条件付けされた軽量な予測器を用いて将来のトークンを予測、行動デコーダにより直接将来の行動を回帰する。
llm.result: 100M未満のパラメータ数でありながら、RoboTwin 2.0で10億パラメータ級のWAMを上回り、LIBEROでも同等以上の性能を発揮し、推論レイテンシを大幅に削減した。

2610.37043.title: State estimation for a hybrid rigid-continuum space manipulator system
2610.37043.abstract: Spacecraft-mounted robotic manipulators can support long-term operability of orbiting assets by conducting tasks such as on-orbit assembly, repair, upgrade, and refueling. In this context, the integration of continuum/soft robotic mechanisms into space manipulator designs promises to reduce stowage volume and mass, as well as to improve operational safety through the inherent mechanical compliance of soft structures. This work presents a novel state reconstruction pipeline for a hybrid soft-rigid space manipulator, in which the distal link is a tendon-driven continuum robot. The estimation problem is formulated as a maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference problem over the hybrid manipulator's configuration, conditioned on discrete, noisy measurements from joint encoders and a vision-based sensing pipeline. The resulting soft-constrained optimization problem is transcribed as a factor graph, providing a compact representation for fusing heterogeneous measurements with the rigid-soft kinematic model. Furthermore, the adoption of the Geometric Variable Strain (GVS) approach yields a minimum-order parameterization of the configuration, a property expected to facilitate model-based feedback control design in future work. The proposed implementation is validated in simulation on a closed-loop trajectory where, for better realism, position measurements for the continuum link are obtained by means of a simulated visual pipeline leveraging synthetic photorealistic images. The state reconstruction accuracy and computational performance confirm the potential of the proposed framework for hybrid soft-rigid robotic applications in orbit.
2610.37043.comment: 10 pages, 9 figures. Version submitted to "Soft Robotics"

llm.title_ja: ハイブリッド剛体・連続体宇宙マニピュレータシステムの状態推定
llm.tldr_ja: 先端リンクがテンドン駆動の連続体ロボットであるハイブリッド柔軟・剛体宇宙マニピュレータを対象に、関節エンコーダと視覚センシングの測定値を因子グラフに統合して状態を再構築するMAP推論フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 宇宙空間での組立や修理を支える宇宙マニピュレータにおいて、柔軟構造の機械的コンプライアンスを活用しつつ正確な状態推定を行う必要があること。
llm.method: ハイブリッドマニピュレータの構成に関する最大事後確率は、関節エンコーダと視覚パイプラインからのノイズ測定値を条件とするMAP推論問題として定式化し、因子グラフを用いて表現した。
llm.result: シミュレーション上の閉ループ軌道において、合成フォトリアル画像を利用した視覚パイプラインを用いて状態再構築精度と計算性能を確認し、宇宙用途への有効性を示した。

2610.37037.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
2610.37037.abstract: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. In particular, spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding are two pivotal tasks that underpin embodied AI and multimodal agents. However, synthesizing targeted, high-quality training data for these tasks remains difficult and costly. Our key insight is that these tasks share an underlying capability, which we call connecting evidence: identifying relevant visual facts, binding them to the correct entities, recovering their relations, and composing them into an answer. Crucially, targeted training data are far easier to synthesize for this capability than for these tasks themselves. To strengthen this capability, we propose EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-implement data synthesis framework that uses zoomed views of related regions within a single image to generate questions requiring comparison, aggregation, or chaining of visual evidence. To ensure quality, a reference answer is retained only when independent VLMs agree on it, and region-ablation tests discard questions whose answer survives the removal of selected regions. We then train base VLMs on the resulting data with RLVR, obtaining Zooming without Zooming v2 (ZwZ2). Although the synthesized data are not tailored to any downstream benchmark, ZwZ2 improves fine-grained and spatial perception, with further gains on embodied spatial reasoning, multimodal long-context understanding, multimodal agent tasks, and general visual reasoning. These results establish EvidenceConnect as an effective framework for supervising evidence connection and suggest that strengthening this shared capability leads to more generalizable multimodal perception.
2610.37037.tldr_en: EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-implement data synthesis framework that uses zoomed views of related regions within a single image to generate questions requiring comparison, aggregation, or chaining of visual evidence, is established.
2610.37037.hf_summary_en: EvidenceConnect synthesizes training data to strengthen visual evidence connection, improving spatial perception and multimodal reasoning across diverse tasks.

llm.title_ja: ズームなしのズーム v2：詳細の把握から証拠の結合へ向けた汎化可能なマルチモーダル知覚
llm.tldr_ja: 画像内の関連領域のズームビューを利用して視覚的証拠の比較・集約・連鎖を要する質問を生成するデータ合成フレームワークEvidenceConnectを提案し、汎化性能の高いマルチモーダル知覚を実現した。
llm.problem: embodied AIやマルチモーダルエージェントの基礎となる空間知覚やマルチモーダル長期コンテキスト理解のためのターゲットを絞った高品質な訓練データの合成が困難かつ高コストであること。
llm.method: 同一画像内の関連領域の拡大図を用いて視覚的証拠を結合する質問を生成するEvidenceConnectフレームワークを構築し、複数のVLM合意と領域アブレーションにより品質を担保してRLVRで学習を行う。
llm.result: ファイングレインな空間知覚、身体化された空間推論、マルチモーダル長期コンテキスト理解などにおいて性能が向上し、証拠結合のスーパービジョンとしての有効性を示した。

2610.36999.title: Online gas classification at the edge
2610.36999.abstract: Field applications in chemical sensing, from portable safety monitors to mobile robots, require models that are lightweight, fast to respond, and can be recalibrated from limited labelled data. Current gas classification pipelines assume controlled sampling cycles and offline feature extraction, and rely on computationally expensive models. With a few thousand neurons and sub-milliwatt power consumption, insects reliably classify odours in open environments. Inspired by the insect olfactory system, we present a neural network architecture that classifies raw sensor array readings using a sparse, high-dimensional binary representation. We evaluate it on random sequences of single gases and binary mixtures, introducing new samples dynamically and classifying gas identity from the transient sensor response. In this setting, the architecture out-performs a linear \gls{svm} on gas mixtures and matches an optimised non-linear \gls{svm}, while maintaining online class-level frequency estimates that distinguish familiar from novel stimuli. It relies exclusively on binary weights and Hebbian-based local learning, remaining computationally lightweight and well suited to ultra-low-power neuromorphic processors. We demonstrated the network on-chip with a hazardous gas detection experiment running on the mixed-signal neuromorphic chip TEXEL. The on-chip classifier yielded an accuracy of 74.6\% while running at 482 $\unit{\nano\joule}$ per inference and 27 \unit{\micro\watt} of static-power.
2610.36999.tldr_en: A neural network architecture that classifies raw sensor array readings using a sparse, high-dimensional binary representation that relies exclusively on binary weights and Hebbian-based local learning, remaining computationally lightweight and well suited to ultra-low-power neuromorphic processors is presented.

llm.title_ja: エッジ上でのオンラインガス分類
llm.tldr_ja: 昆虫の嗅覚系にインスパイアされ、疎で高次元なバイナリ表現とヘブ則に基づく局所学習を用いて、超低消費電力のニューロモルフィックプロセッサ上で高速かつ軽量にガスを分類するニューラルネットワークアーキテクチャを提案した。
llm.problem: 化学センシングの現場応用において、従来のガス分類パイプラインは制御されたサンプリングサイクルやオフライン特徴抽出を前提とし、計算コストの高いモデルに依存していること。
llm.method: 生センサーアレイの読み値をバイナリ重みとヘブ則による局所学習のみで処理するスパースな高次元バイナリ表現を用いたニューラルネットワークを設計し、チップ上で実証した。
llm.result: 混合ガスに対して線形SVMを上回り、最適化された非線形SVMと同等の性能を維持しつつ、混成信号ニューロモルフィックチップ上での推論あたり482ナノジュールという超低電力で74.6%の精度を実現した。
keywords_ja: ニューロモルフィック

2610.36996.title: Structure-Actuation Co-Design of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators
2610.36996.abstract: This paper presents a mixed discrete-continuous multiobjective bilevel framework for the structure-actuation co-design of all-electric heavy-duty robotic manipulators. The upper level optimizes manipulator geometry and actuation topology, while joint-specific lower-level searches construct feasible archives of discrete motor, gearbox, and screw configurations. A system-level coordinator selects actuator packages according to hardware mass, co-design cost, and loss-aware supply energy, and the resulting actuator masses are fed back to the robot model until a mass-consistent fixed point is obtained. Evaluation on a full-pose SE(3) benchmark with a 100-kg tool payload yields eight feasible nondominated designs, all satisfying the 12 prescribed poses. Actuator-mass coupling converges in three iterations for every reported design. A fixed-design ablation shows that one-pass sequential sizing changes hardware mass by up to 2.13%, co-design cost by 10.20%, and supply energy by 9.40% in magnitude. Payload screening further reveals increasing mass-cost-energy demand and changes in competitive mechanism topology with carried load.
2610.36996.comment: 6 pages manuscript submitted to a conference (ICCMA 2026)

llm.title_ja: 全電動ヘビーデューティロボットマニピュレータの構造・駆動協調設計
llm.tldr_ja: マニピュレータの幾何学形状と駆動トポロジーを最適化する上位レベルと、モーター・減速機・ネジの構成を探索する下位レベルを組み合わせた混合離散・連続マルチオブジェクティブ二層フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 全電動ヘビーデューティロボットマニピュレータの設計において、構造と駆動システムの選択が複雑に絡み合うこと。
llm.method: 上位レベルで幾何学と駆動トポロジーを最適化し、下位レベルでモーター等の構成を探索、ハードウェア質量・協調設計コスト・損失考慮型供給エネルギーに基づいてシステムコーディネーターが選定し固定点を得る。
llm.result: 100kgのツールペイロードを持つSE(3)ベンチマークにおいて8つの実行可能な非支配設計を導出し、アクチュエータ質量の結合が3回の反復で収束することを確認した。

2610.36968.title: Omni-IGN: Onboard Image-Goal Navigation for Drones with Omnidirectional Vision
2610.36968.abstract: Image-goal navigation (ImageNav) requires an agent to reach a location specified by a goal image in an unknown environment. For drones, this task demands exploration, goal- directed navigation, and collision avoidance under limited onboard computing resources. Existing aerial ImageNav methods are built on single-view observations, requiring additional rotation and exploration to search for goal-relevant cues outside the field of view. In this paper, we present Omni-IGN, a fully onboard ImageNav system that integrates quad-fisheye perception, an attention-based reinforcement learning (RL) policy, and a collision-aware safety layer. The policy adaptively fuses goal-relevant features across multiple views to provide directional guidance for continuous navigation. The quad-fisheye RGB images support both ImageNav and obstacle avoidance without a dedicated depth sensor. On Habitat benchmarks, Omni-IGN achieves the best performance among continuous-action baselines. Moreover, flight tests in IsaacSim validate the effectiveness of integrating learning-based depth estimation with the action safety layer for collision avoidance. Finally, real-world experiments demonstrate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer without any fine-tuning or external localization. The code and model checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.
2610.36968.tldr_en: Omni-IGN is presented, a fully onboard ImageNav system that integrates quad-fisheye perception, an attention-based reinforcement learning (RL) policy, and a collision-aware safety layer that achieves the best performance among continuous-action baselines.

llm.title_ja: Omni-IGN：全方位ビジョンを備えたドローン向けオンボード画像ゴールナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: クワッド魚眼知覚、アテンションベースの強化学習ポリシー、衝突回避安全層を統合し、専用の深度センサなしでゴール画像への連続的なナビゲーションを実現するオンボードシステム「Omni-IGN」を提案した。
llm.problem: ドローンにおける画像ゴールナビゲーション（ImageNav）は、限られたオンボード計算リソースの中で、探索、ゴール指向ナビゲーション、衝突回避を同時に行う必要があること。
llm.method: クワッド魚眼RGB画像を入力とし、複数視点からゴール関連特徴を適応的に融合するアテンションベースのRLポリシーと、学習ベースの深度推定を組み合わせた安全層を統合した。
llm.result: Habitatベンチマークの連続アクションベースラインの中で最高の性能を達成し、IsaacSimでの飛行テストおよびファインチューニングなしのゼロショットSim2Real転送による実機実験で有効性を実証した。
keywords_ja: 画像ゴールナビゲーション

2610.36961.title: Keeping Contact: Task-Adaptive Friction Margins for Bimanual Non-Prehensile Manipulation
2610.36961.abstract: Maintaining contact in non-prehensile manipulation requires more than nominal friction cone feasibility: a force barely inside the cone and one well inside it are both feasible, but they provide different margins against slip and contact loss. This paper uses signed friction distance to measure friction margin in force space and derives a task-adaptive margin from the force correction needed to balance pivot moment deviations in bimanual tilting. The resulting contact margins are embedded in a sequence of second-order cone programs (SOCPs), each giving a globally optimal contact force solution at a tilt angle. The optimizer balances the object about an environmental pivot while keeping robot and pivot contact forces away from the nominal friction boundary. Optimizer-level results show interpretable force redistribution and adaptation to object property changes. Real-world experiments demonstrate successful execution under object property variations and model mismatch, while fixed margin and no-margin comparisons illustrate the importance of adapting the margin to task demand. These results support signed friction distance margins as a force planning mechanism for maintaining contact in bimanual non-prehensile manipulation. Project page: https://keeping-contact.github.io/
2610.36961.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
2610.36961.tldr_en: Signed friction distance is used to measure friction margin in force space and derives a task-adaptive margin from the force correction needed to balance pivot moment deviations in bimanual tilting and shows interpretable force redistribution and adaptation to object property changes.

llm.title_ja: 接触の維持：両手非把持マニピュレーションのためのタスク適応型摩擦マージン
llm.tldr_ja: 符号付き摩擦距離を用いて力空間における摩擦マージンを測定し、両手傾斜時のピボットモーメント偏差をバランスさせるために必要な力補正からタスク適応型マージンを導出して、接触を維持する最適化フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 非把持マニピュレーションにおいて接触を維持するには単なる摩擦円錐の実行可能性だけでなく、滑りや接触喪失に対する十分なマージンが必要であること。
llm.method: 符号付き摩擦距離によるマージンを二次計画問題（SOCP）のシーケンスに組み込み、環境ピボットの周りで物体をバランスさせながらロボットとピボットの接触力を摩擦境界から遠ざける。
llm.result: 物体の特性変化やモデル誤差がある状況下でも、解釈可能な力の再分配を行いながら安定して実行できることを実世界実験で実証した。

2610.36859.title: ActiveAlign: Aligning Egocentric Manipulation via Active Perception
2610.36859.abstract: Real-to-Sim-to-Real (Real2Sim2Real) enables structured world representations for planning, interpretability, and safe execution. Most existing approaches rely on passive perception, which creates real2sim gaps due to imperfect observation. Inspired by how humans perceive actively through actions, we propose ActiveAlign, a framework that leverages active perception to align the Real2Sim2Real gap from interactions. ActiveAlign introduces two complementary modules: (i) ActiveAlign-Waving, which performs hand-eye calibration by exploiting active hand motions and differentiable rendering, and (ii) ActiveAlign-Touching, which refines object alignment through tactile feedback to achieve millimeter-level precision. Together, these capabilities enable strong real2sim alignment. We demonstrate that ActiveAlign-Waving can be used to curate simulation environments for open-sourced uncalibrated robot manipulation datasets, and demonstrate on a real Unitree G1 robot that ActiveAlign enables fine manipulation of millimeter-scale objects such as pressing buttons and moving sliders.
2610.36859.tldr_en: ActiveAlign is proposed, a framework that leverages active perception to align the Real2Sim2Real gap from interactions and introduces two complementary modules: ActiveAlign-Waving, which performs hand-eye calibration by exploiting active hand motions and differentiable rendering, and ActiveAlign-Touching, which refines object alignment through tactile feedback to achieve millimeter-level precision.

llm.title_ja: ActiveAlign：能動的知覚を通じたエゴセントリックマニピュレーションの整合
llm.tldr_ja: 能動的な手の動きや触覚フィードバックを活用した能動的知覚により、不完全な観測に起因するReal2Sim2Realのギャップを解消してミリメートル単位の精密な操作を可能にするフレームワーク「ActiveAlign」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の多くの手法が受動的知覚に依存しているため、不完全な観測に起因するReal2Sim2Realのギャップが生じること。
llm.method: 能動的な手の動きと微分可能レンダリングを利用して手目キャリブレーションを行う「ActiveAlign-Waving」と、触覚フィードバックで物体位置を洗練する「ActiveAlign-Touching」の2つのモジュールを導入した。
llm.result: 未較正のロボットマニピュレーションデータセットのシミュレーション環境構築を可能にし、実機のUnitree G1ロボットにおいてボタン押しやスライダー移動などの微細な操作を実現した。

2610.36852.title: When Black-Box Robot Policies Fail: Online Sensor Diagnosis and Repair with a Transparent Surrogate
2610.36852.abstract: Robot foundation models may generalize across tasks and embodiments, but their actions still depend on sensors that can fail. When the policy is frozen or inaccessible, can an external monitor diagnose and repair corrupted inputs without access to its internals? We test a structured surrogate that separates periodic gait from sensor-dependent corrections to guide input repair around a frozen locomotion policy. On simulated Go2, offline diagnosis raises walking success from 259/640 to 429/640 episodes; online repair reaches 382/640, with no triggers in 64 held-out fault-free episodes. A matched boosted-tree surrogate predicts clean actions similarly well but yields no detected repair improvement over no repair. Separate fits improve walking on Go1 and ANYmal C, although phase-aware gradients perform better. Evidence remains limited to one policy and a partly screened simulated fault suite; robot foundation model and hardware validation remain open.
2610.36852.comment: Accepted at the Conference on Robot Learning 2026 Workshop on the Science of Physical AI Safety (SPAIS)
2610.36852.tldr_en: A structured surrogate is tested that separates periodic gait from sensor-dependent corrections to guide input repair around a frozen locomotion policy, and separate fits improve walking on Go1 and ANYmal C, although phase-aware gradients perform better.

llm.title_ja: ブラックボックス・ロボットポリシーが失敗するとき：透明なサロゲートを用いたオンラインセンサー診断と修復
llm.tldr_ja: 周期的な歩行とセンサー依存の補正を分離した構造化サロゲートを用いて、凍結されたロコモーションポリシー周辺の破損したセンサー入力を診断・修復する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボット基盤モデルは汎化性能が高い一方で、依存するセンサーが故障した際にブラックボックス化されたポリシーの内部にアクセスして入力を修復することが困難であること。
llm.method: 周期的な歩行とセンサー依存の補正を分離した構造化サロゲートを構築し、凍結されたロコモーションポリシーへの入力をガイドしてオンラインでの修復を行う。
llm.result: シミュレーション上のGo2においてオフラインおよびオンラインでの修復により歩行成功率が大幅に向上し、複数機種（Go1、ANYmal C）への適用可能性を確認した。
llm.limitation: 実証は1つのポリシーと一部のシミュレーション上の故障スイートに限定されており、基盤モデルや実機での検証は今後の課題である。

2610.36848.title: Evolving Agent Teams
2610.36848.abstract: The rapid progress of software engineering agents drives interest in applying them to open-ended problems such as GPU kernel optimization. However, we find that existing coding agents converge to local optima on real-world, expert-written kernels (e.g., FlashInfer). We introduce Evolving Agent Teams, a multi-agent framework that escapes such local optima. It features (1) a central supervisor that diagnoses each local optimum and restructures a team of agents; and (2) a persistent file system that comprises a learning document, an evolution history, and per-team artifacts, grounding restructuring with accumulated experience. Under a matched token budget, Evolving Agent Teams consistently outperforms strong coding-agent baselines. With an extended token budget, Evolving Agent Teams generates a CUDA kernel that reaches 1.2x mean speedup over the production FlashInfer MLA paged decode kernel from scratch and wins on 36 of 47 production workloads from FlashInfer-Bench (0.86-0.99x on the remaining 11). It also demonstrates superior performance on tasks such as KDA prefill on AMD MI350X (3.01x over vLLM) and NVIDIA B200 (3.44x over FlashKDA), MoE expert-offload serving on Apple silicon (30.3 tokens/s decode for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in MLX 4-bit on a 48 GB M4 Pro), and RoboDojo robot manipulation (62.1 on held-out seeds vs. 55.3 for the best leaderboard entry). Code is available at https://github.com/caoshiyi/EAT.
2610.36848.tldr_en: Evolving Agent Teams is introduced, a multi-agent framework that features a central supervisor that diagnoses each local optimum and restructures a team of agents; and a persistent file system that comprises a learning document, an evolution history, and per-team artifacts, grounding restructuring with accumulated experience.

llm.title_ja: 進化するエージェントチーム
llm.tldr_ja: 中央スーパーバイザーによるローカル最適解の診断とエージェントチームの再構築、および蓄積された経験に基づく永続的ファイルシステムを備えたマルチエージェントフレームワーク「Evolving Agent Teams」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のソフトウェアエンジニアリングエージェントが、実際の専門家が書いたコード（GPUカーネル最適化など）においてローカル最適解に収束してしまう点。
llm.method: 各ローカル最適解を診断してチーム構造を動的に再構築する中央スーパーバイザーと、学習ドキュメントや進化履歴を保持する永続的ファイルシステムを組み合わせたマルチエージェントフレームワークを導入した。
llm.result: 同等のトークン予算の下で既存の強力なコーディングエージェントベースラインを常に上回り、FlashInfer MLAページデコードカーネルなどで生産用ワークロードを凌駕する性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ソフトウェアエンジニアリング

2610.36840.title: Trace-WAM: Learning to Act via 3D Motion Prediction for World Action Models
2610.36840.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) learn representations for robot control by coupling future visual prediction with action generation. Successful manipulation depends primarily on how the robot and task-relevant objects evolve, whereas future-video prediction must also reconstruct the appearance and background of the entire scene. We therefore propose Trace-WAM, which augments video-action learning with future 3D motion prediction as an auxiliary objective. This objective supervises temporal point correspondence together with image-plane displacement and depth change, directly describing the interaction dynamics and spatial changes involved in manipulation. To this end, we adopt a three-branch Mixture-of-Transformer (Tri-MoT) architecture to jointly learn video prediction, motion prediction, and action generation. The motion expert predicts future trajectories from current visual features, allowing motion supervision to shape the representations used for action generation. Because the action expert does not consume predicted trajectories, inference retains the current-observation policy path: a single visual forward pass followed by action denoising. Experiments on RoboCasa-GR1, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus demonstrate strong in-distribution performance and out-of-distribution generalization, with particularly clear gains over Fast-WAM under limited demonstrations and distribution shifts.
2610.36840.tldr_en: Trace-WAM is proposed, which augments video-action learning with future 3D motion prediction as an auxiliary objective, and supervises temporal point correspondence together with image-plane displacement and depth change, directly describing the interaction dynamics and spatial changes involved in manipulation.

llm.title_ja: Trace-WAM：世界行動モデルのための3Dモーション予測を通じた行動学習
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ行動学習に将来の3Dモーション予測を補助目標として追加し、マニピュレーションに関わる相互作用ダイナミクスと空間的変化を直接記述するTrace-WAMを提案した。
llm.problem: 将来のビデオ予測がシーン全体の背景や外観の再構築まで行う必要がある一方、ロボットのマニピュレーションはロボット自身とタスクに関連するオブジェクトの進化に依存している点。
llm.method: ビデオ予測、モーション予測、行動生成を共同で学習するための3分岐Mixture-of-Transformer（Tri-MoT）アーキテクチャを採用し、将来の3Dモーション予測を補助目標として導入した。
llm.result: RoboCasa-GR1、LIBERO、LIBERO-Plusでの実験により、限られたデモンストレーションや分布のシフトの下でも、Fast-WAMと比較して優れた汎化性能と高い成功率が示された。

2610.36837.title: ExecDiffuser: Closing the Sample-to-Execution Gap in Diffusion Planning
2610.36837.abstract: Generative planners are often evaluated by the trajectories they can generate, although closed-loop driving ultimately depends on the single candidate committed to control. We identify this mismatch as the sample-to-execution gap and show that improving proposal quality alone can worsen the executed decision. Here, we introduce ExecDiffuser, a recurrent proposal-to-execution framework that couples candidate generation, trajectory selection, and subsequent replanning through shared execution semantics. Intent-Guided Diffusion Proposal (IGD) assigns hypothesis responsibility and shapes trajectories with execution-conditioned supervision. Execution-Grounded Selection (EGS) learns a candidate-conditioned publication utility, commits one trajectory to control, and returns it as context for the next planning cycle. Across nuPlan, InterPlan, and NAVSIM, ExecDiffuser achieves leading closed-loop performance against strong state-of-the-art baselines. Under a unified five-seed protocol, it obtains an average score of 85.62, improving over Diffusion Planner and FlowDrive by 4.02 and 1.31 points, respectively. On NAVSIM, it achieves 92.6 PDMS under the official evaluation pipeline. Matched counterfactual analysis further shows that ExecDiffuser more reliably converts strong candidates into committed decisions, while prefix interventions confirm that this advantage persists after physical execution and subsequent replanning.
2610.36837.tldr_en: ExecDiffuser is introduced, a recurrent proposal-to-execution framework that couples candidate generation, trajectory selection, and subsequent replanning through shared execution semantics and achieves leading closed-loop performance against strong state-of-the-art baselines.

llm.title_ja: ExecDiffuser：拡散計画におけるサンプルから実行へのギャップを埋める
llm.tldr_ja: 候補生成、軌道選択、後続の再計画を共有された実行セマンティクスで結びつける再帰的な提案・実行フレームワークExecDiffuserを提案し、優れた閉ループ駆動性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 生成プランナーが生成可能な軌道で評価される一方、自動運転の制御にコミットされるのは単一の候補であり、提案品質の向上が必ずしも実行された決定の改善につながらないギャップがある点。
llm.method: 実行条件付き監督で軌道を形成する意図誘導型拡散提案（IGD）と、候補条件付きの出版ユーティリティを学習して制御に1つの軌道を選択・コミットする実行基盤型選択（EGS）を組み合わせた。
llm.result: nuPlan、InterPlan、NAVSIMにおいて最先端のベースラインを上回る閉ループ性能を達成し、NAVSIMで92.6 PDMSを記録した。

2610.36825.title: HC2Robot: Hyper-Connection Transformers with Predicted Foresight for Multi-Terrain Humanoid Parkour
2610.36825.abstract: Humanoid parkour requires robots to reason about future footholds and whole-body motions over highly discontinuous terrain. We revisit the information asymmetry in asymmetric actor-critic learning for perceptive humanoid locomotion: the critic exploits privileged simulator signals during training, whereas the deployable actor operates solely from onboard perception. We argue that the key is not exposing privileged information to the actor, but learning a deployable approximation of it to narrow the information gap between training and deployment. We present HC2Robot, a deployable perceptive humanoid parkour framework consisting of a Predicted Foresight Module (PFM) and a Hyper-Connection (HC) Transformer. PFM predicts from deployable observations the policy-conditioned timing, location, and support quality of each foot's next touchdown event, converting privileged supervision into a deployable latent representation that provides the actor with predicted touchdown information without privileged runtime sensing. The HC Transformer further enhances temporal reasoning through learnable multi-stream routing, while a future motion prediction head provides short-horizon motion priors for regularization. Across stairs, gaps, high platforms, and slopes, HC2Robot achieves a mean simulated traversal success rate of 97.60% and consistently higher safe foothold rates than strong perceptive locomotion baselines, supporting improved traversal performance and geometric foothold support under deployable sensing.
2610.36825.tldr_en: It is argued that the key is not exposing privileged information to the actor, but learning a deployable approximation of it to narrow the information gap between training and deployment, and presented HC2Robot, a deployable perceptive humanoid parkour framework consisting of a Predicted Foresight Module and a Hyper-Connection Transformer.

llm.title_ja: HC2Robot：マルチ地形ヒューマノイドパルクールに向けた予測フォーサイト付きハイパーコネクション・トランスフォーマー
llm.tldr_ja: 非対称アクター・クリティック学習における情報非対称性に対処するため、予測フォーサイトモジュール（PFM）とハイパーコネクション・トランスフォーマーを組み合わせたヒューマノイドパルクールフレームワークHC2Robotを提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドパルクールにおいて、訓練時には特権的なシミュレータ信号を利用できるクリティックに対し、デプロイ可能なアクターはオンボード知覚のみに依存するという情報の非対称性がある点。
llm.method: デプロイ可能な観測から次の足のタッチダウンのタイミング、位置、支持品質を予測する予測フォーサイトモジュール（PFM）と、マルチストリームルーティングで時間的推論を強化するHCトランスフォーマーを導入した。
llm.result: 階段、段差、高プラットフォーム、傾斜地において、平均97.60%のシミュレーション通過成功率を達成し、強固な足場支持を実現した。

2610.36823.title: TAPESTRY: A Single Backbone for Video Generation and Robot Control
2610.36823.abstract: Pretrained video generation models encode rich priors about physical interactions, but leveraging them for robot control typically requires either resource-intensive video generation at test time or action heads trained from scratch that do not fully utilize the pretrained backbone. We introduce Tokenizing Actions as Video Patches in a Shared Transformer Policy (TAPESTRY), a world action model that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion transformer into a robotic policy without requiring video generation at inference. Our key idea is to treat robot actions as single-patch tokens in the video model's latent space. A lightweight linear projection maps each action timestep to the patch dimensions of the pretrained VAE, and the resulting tokens are processed by the same patchifying layers and transformer backbone used for video. The shared backbone is optimized through three diffusion objectives sampled per minibatch element: Video diffusion uses VAE latents from robot and human videos to establish dynamics priors. Joint video+action diffusion trains on robot demonstrations using a coupled diffusion timestep and an asymmetric attention mask. Action-only diffusion denoises actions conditioned on clean image latents. At test time, the model generates a compact action token sequence in a single DDIM step from pure noise, producing smooth action chunks at 84 ms per action chunk on consumer hardware and avoiding the cost of full video generation. Across simulation benchmarks and real-robot experiments, TAPESTRY achieves strong performance with substantially lower inference cost than comparable joint video--action policies. More information can be found at https://tapestry-wam.github.io.
2610.36823.comment: Accepted to Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2026
2610.36823.tldr_en: TAPESTRY is introduced, a world action model that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion transformer into a robotic policy without requiring video generation at inference, and achieves strong performance with substantially lower inference cost than comparable joint video--action policies.

llm.title_ja: TAPESTRY：ビデオ生成とロボット制御のための単一バックボーン
llm.tldr_ja: 推論時の動画生成コストを回避しつつ、事前学習済みビデオ拡散トランスフォーマーをロボットポリシーに転用する世界行動モデル「TAPESTRY」を提案した。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みビデオ生成モデルをロボット制御に活用するには、テスト時にリソース集約的な動画生成を行うか、ゼロから学習したアクションヘッドを使用する必要がありバックボーンを十分に活用できない点。
llm.method: ロボットのアクションをビデオモデルの潜在空間における単一パッチトークンとして扱い、軽量な線形射影でアクションタイムステップをVAEのパッチ寸法にマップして、ビデオと同じパッチ化レイヤーとバックボーンで処理する。
llm.result: シミュレーションベンチマークおよび実ロボット実験において、同等のジョイントビデオ・アクションポリシーと比較して大幅に低い推論コストで強力なパフォーマンスを達成した。

2610.36816.title: Integrated Design and Reproducible Feasibility Analysis of a Four-Wheel Rover with Packet-Commanded Imaging, LiDAR Ranging, and Learning-Assisted Target Recognition
2610.36816.abstract: This study develops an integrated, reproducible design assessment for a four-wheel educational rover intended for the high-school remote-control division of the 2027 NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge. The architecture combines commercial differential drive control, independently sprung wheel carriers, separate drive and task batteries, and a Raspberry Pi-based subsystem that executes received imaging and ranging commands. The analysis reconciles component lists with dimensioned computer-aided design views, derives mobility and electrical constraints, and connects sensor geometry to command execution. At the estimated mass of 10.919 kg, a 215 mm wheel rotating at 200 RPM produces a theoretical rolling speed of 8.105 km/h; consequently, the nominal motor label does not establish compliance with an 8 km/h design ceiling. A steady 20-degree climb requires at least 1.255 newton-meters per wheel under an assumed rolling-resistance coefficient of 0.10 and equal torque sharing. At 50 ft, an ideal 12-inch feature spans approximately 71 pixels across a full-resolution Camera Module 3 Standard image, while a 1-degree pointing error displaces the ranging ray by approximately 266 mm. An executed synthetic benchmark compares color-geometry rules and two linear support-vector classifiers on 2,400 generated board crops with scene-disjoint evaluation. A separate reference command executor is checked using mocked hardware. These software results and analytical sensitivities support a testable development plan; the study does not report physical rover trials. The principal contribution is a traceable connection between component choices, failure mechanisms, quantitative design limits, and reproducible verification tasks.

llm.title_ja: パケット指令型画像処理、LiDAR測距、学習支援型ターゲット認識を備えた4輪ローバーの統合設計と再現可能な実行可能性分析
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 2027年NASA Human Exploration Rover Challengeの高校生向けRC部門を対象とした4輪教育用ローバーの統合的で再現可能な設計評価が必要である。
llm.method: 商業的差動駆動制御、独立懸架ホイールキャリア、Raspberry Piベースのサブシステムを組み合わせたアーキテクチャを開発し、モビリティや電気的制約を導出する。
llm.result: 推計質量10.919kgにおいて、215mmホイールが200RPMで回転すると理論的な走行速度が8.105 km/hになることなどを分析し、テスト可能な開発計画を支える。
llm.limitation: 物理ローバーの試験は報告されていない。

2610.36812.title: Gradient flow of magnetic inclination and intensity as a GPS-free guidance mechanism
2610.36812.abstract: It is well established that some animals, such as sea turtles, sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it as a primary cue for long-distance navigation across the vast and featureless ocean. This remarkable ability has inspired the development of bio-inspired magnetic navigation (BIMN), which seeks to mimic these animals to develop robust and frugal navigation methods. BIMN exploits the Earth's magnetic field, sometimes described as ''Nature's GPS'', as a natural navigation infrastructure, providing a potential alternative to vulnerable satellite navigation systems. However, unlike geographic coordinates, magnetic coordinates extracted from the Earth's magnetic field do not provide a one-to-one mapping to geographic locations. Different locations can exhibit similar magnetic signatures, creating ambiguity and making BIMN inherently more challenging. Despite this fundamental challenge, we demonstrate that, within predefined regions of the Earth, magnetic inclination and intensity provide sufficient information to navigate to any destination. By formulating BIMN as a gradient flow control and guidance problem, we show that the resulting gradient flow act as current that carries the system and can be controlled to guide it through intermediate waypoints toward the desired destination. The resulting framework provides a GPS-free navigation mechanism with potential applications in both engineering and biology. In engineering, it can be used to establish a geomagnetic navigation infrastructure through which prescribed routes can be defined and followed, while in biology, it can be used to analyse the migration routes of animals known to rely on magnetoreception.

llm.title_ja: GPSフリーのガイダンス機構としての磁気伏角・強度の勾配流
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 生体模倣型磁気ナビゲーション（BIMN）において、地球の磁気から抽出される磁気座標は地理的位置と一対一対応せず、異なる場所で類似の磁気署名を示す曖昧さがある。
llm.method: BIMNを勾配流制御およびガイダンス問題として定式化し、磁気伏角と強度が中間ウェイポイントを通じた目的地への誘導に必要な情報を提供することを示す。
llm.result: 工学および生物学における応用可能性を持つGPSフリーのナビゲーション機構のためのフレームワークを提供した。

2610.36791.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
2610.36791.abstract: Learning controllable world dynamics from heterogeneous interaction videos is challenging because robot embodiments use incompatible action spaces, while human videos lack native control labels. We present RynnWorld-Latent, a cross-embodiment video world model that uses the 3D-grounded latent actions introduced by RynnLAM as a shared conditioning interface. This representation enables joint pretraining on human interaction videos, robot demonstrations, and simulation rollouts without requiring a common native action space.
