Built on a pretrained video transformer, RynnWorld-Latent combines global action tokens with an identity-initialized local pathway that aligns actions with future video latents. We pretrain on 23 datasets comprising approximately 553.5M frames and adapt the model to target robots through post-training. The framework supports two data-generation routes: digital teleoperation uses target robot commands to generate action-video demonstrations, while latent-action synthesis transfers source motion to an edited initial frame and pairs the resulting rollout with retargeted pseudo robot actions. Experiments show improved video prediction metrics on public benchmarks and two real-robot platforms, alongside qualitative action following when different action sequences share the same initial observation. Synthetic mid-training improves policy success rates on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and both generation routes improve real-world policy success rates over real-demonstration-only training in the evaluated settings. These results support universal latent actions as a scalable interface for learning controllable visual dynamics across heterogeneous embodiments.
2610.36791.tldr_en: RynnWorld-Latent is presented, a cross-embodiment video world model that uses the 3D-grounded latent actions introduced by RynnLAM as a shared conditioning interface that enables joint pretraining on human interaction videos, robot demonstrations, and simulation rollouts without requiring a common native action space.
2610.36791.hf_summary_en: RynnWorld-Latent learns cross-embodiment world dynamics via 3D-grounded latent actions, enabling joint pretraining on diverse video sources and synthetic data generation for improved robot policy performance.

llm.title_ja: RynnWorld-Latent：ユニバーサル潜在行動で条件付けられたクロスボディメント世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: RynnLAMが導入した3Dグラウンドされた潜在行動を共有の条件付けインターフェースとして使用し、共通のネイティブ行動空間を必要とせずに異種ロボットや人間の動画で共同事前学習を行うクロスボディメント世界モデルを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットのボディメントごとに互換性のない行動空間を持ち、人間の動画には固有の制御ラベルがないため、異種の相互作用動画から制御可能な世界ダイナミクスを学習することが困難である点。
llm.method: 事前学習済みビデオトランスフォーマーを基に、グローバルアクショントークンとアクションを将来のビデオ潜在変数に整列させるローカルパスウェイを組み合わせ、23のデータセット（約5億5,350万フレーム）で事前学習を実施した。
llm.result: 公開ベンチマークおよび2つの実ロボットプラットフォームでビデオ予測精度の向上が示され、合成ミッドトレーニングや生成ルートによりLIBEROおよび実世界のポリシー成功率が向上した。

2610.36789.title: A fully articulated humanoid dexterous hand with human-level joint structure enabled by linkage-based actuation
2610.36789.abstract: Humanoid dexterous hands are a core component of embodied intelligence, enabling robots to translate high-level intent into rich and adaptive physical interaction. However, existing designs remain constrained by a persistent trade-off among anthropomorphic kinematic complexity, mechanical robustness, load capacity and control simplicity, limiting dexterous manipulation in unstructured environments. Here we present Torch-Hand, a fully articulated humanoid dexterous hand that replicates the joint structure and motion hierarchy of the human hand with 21 degrees of freedom (DOF), comprising a highly articulated five-DOF thumb and four DOF in each of the remaining fingers. The differentiated thumb integrates multi-axis CMC motion to provide broad opposition and flexible contact orientation relative to the four fingers. Unlike tendon-driven or hybrid actuation approaches, Torch-Hand adopts an entirely linkage-based transmission architecture. By integrating screw-linkage actuation, the hand achieves high grasping force and substantial payload capacity while maintaining a compact anthropomorphic form. Its actuation architecture is optimized for control tractability, with all actuators integrated within the palm and arranged in a serial-robot-like configuration that establishes a direct correspondence between motor motion and joint kinematics. This architecture mechanically decouples functional DOF to reduce unintended inter-joint motion propagation, while allowing independently addressable DOF to be actively coordinated into coupled multi-joint motion patterns during complex manipulation. Comprehensive experiments assess reachable workspace, coordinated fingertip trajectories, thumb opposition, 33-grasp taxonomy coverage, grasping force, payload capacity and task-level manipulation. These results establish Torch-Hand as a robust hardware foundation for dexterous embodied manipulation.
2610.36789.tldr_en: Torch-Hand is presented, a fully articulated humanoid dexterous hand that replicates the joint structure and motion hierarchy of the human hand with 21 degrees of freedom (DOF), comprising a highly articulated five-DOF thumb and four DOF in each of the remaining fingers.

llm.title_ja: リンケージベースの駆動により人間レベルの関節構造を実現した完全多関節ヒューマノイド器用ハンド
llm.tldr_ja: Torch-Handは、21自由度を持ち人間の手の関節構造と運動階層を完全に再現した、リンケージ駆動によるヒューマノイド用器用ハンドである。
llm.problem: 既存のハンドは、人間のような運動学的複雑さ、機械的堅牢性、可搬重量、制御の容易さのトレードオフに制約されていた。
llm.method: すべての駆動装置を手の平に内蔵し、ねじ機構リンクを統合した完全なリンケージベースの伝動アーキテクチャを採用した。
llm.result: 把持力、可搬重量、把持の分類網羅性、器用なタスク性能に関する包括的な実験で評価を行い優れた性能を示した。

2610.36764.title: Beyond the Evidence Coherence Trap: Agent-Driven Evidence Selection for Temporally Disordered Fake News Detection
2610.36764.abstract: Fake news undermines public trust and the integrity of online information ecosystems. Temporally disordered fake news is especially elusive because it rearranges factual events into a false chronology. Individual events may remain factually valid even when their temporal relations are misrepresented. When similar events involving the same entity recur, retrieval may return semantically plausible evidence from the wrong period. Consequently, independent event verification may rely on locally coherent but temporally mismatched evidence and incorrectly validate the article. We call this the \textit{evidence coherence trap}. Because existing benchmarks rarely isolate this setting, we construct ChronoFake, a source-disjoint benchmark of 30,706 articles derived from temporally anchored real events. It distinguishes temporal manipulation from valid narration, including flashbacks. To address this, we propose DelSA, a \underline{D}ocument S\underline{el}ection \underline{S}elf-Updating \underline{A}gent that iteratively refines evidence selection during training and applies a frozen rulebook for one-pass evidence selection at inference. DelSA uses an LLM to characterize candidate evidence, while a verifier-trained reranker balances local relevance against timeline consistency. Finally, the classifier compares the article-implied chronology extracted by the LLM with the evidence-derived chronology to reveal global temporal conflicts. DelSA outperforms existing methods on ChronoFake, while remaining competitive on PolitiFact and GossipCop.
2610.36764.tldr_en: DelSA is proposed, a iteratively refines evidence selection during training and applies a frozen rulebook for one-pass evidence selection at inference that outperforms existing methods on ChronoFake, while remaining competitive on PolitiFact and GossipCop.

llm.title_ja: 証拠の整合性の罠を超えて：時間的に順序が狂ったフェイクニュース検出のためのエージェント駆動型証拠選択
llm.tldr_ja: DelSAは、訓練中に証拠選択を反復的に洗練し、推論時に一回のパスで証拠選択を行うエージェントであり、ChronoFakeで既存手法を上回る性能を示した。
llm.problem: 時間的に順序が狂ったフェイクニュースは事実関係の時系列が偽装されており、誤った証拠に依存して誤判定する「証拠の整合性の罠」が生じる。
llm.method: 候補となる証拠をLLMで特徴付け、検証器で訓練されたリランカーを用いてローカルな関連性とタイムラインの一貫性をバランスさせるDelSAを提案する。
llm.result: ChronoFakeベンチマークにおいて既存手法を凌駕し、PolitiFactやGossipCopでも競争力を維持した。
keywords_ja: フェイクニュース検出

2610.36761.title: Making Self-Driving Laboratories Auditable:A Unified Framework for Hybrid Actions,Measurements, and Safe Execution
2610.36761.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are laboratory systems that couple experimental planning, automated execution, and measurement feedback in a closed loop. Integrating flexible robot control with the typed application programming interfaces (APIs) and continuous measurements exposed by laboratory instruments remains an execution-interface challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a traceable framework comprising four components: LAM (Lab Action Model), OpenSDL, Safe-SDL, and L3-Bench. LAM is a proposed measurement-conditioned policy architecture that extends vision-language-action paradigms to generate both continuous robot trajectories and typed instrument API calls. OpenSDL is an execution substrate with an initial control implementation, designed to map role-level operations to heterogeneous devices, coordinate execution, and record timestamped causal events. The proposed Safe-SDL runtime gate combines pre-dispatch schema and resource checks with signal temporal logic monitoring during execution, including extended waiting periods. L3-Bench (Level-3 Laboratory Benchmark) specifies an episode-level evaluation protocol covering physical outcomes, timing, reproducibility, safety violations, and fault recovery. Together, these components provide an end-to-end design for linking hybrid action generation, monitored device execution, measurement feedback, and experimental evaluation, addressing coordination and traceability challenges in SDL workflows.
2610.36761.tldr_en: These components provide an end-to-end design for linking hybrid action generation, monitored device execution, measurement feedback, and experimental evaluation, addressing coordination and traceability challenges in SDL workflows.

llm.title_ja: セルフドライビング実験室の監査可能性向上：ハイブリッドな行動、測定、安全な実行のための統合フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: LAM、OpenSDL、Safe-SDL、L3-Benchからなる統合フレームワークにより、セルフドライビング実験室におけるハイブリッド行動生成と測定フィードバックの課題を解決する。
llm.problem: 柔軟なロボット制御と実験機器のAPIや連続的測定を統合する際、実行インターフェースの課題や調整・追跡可能性の困難が生じる。
llm.method: 測定条件付きポリシー構造（LAM）、実行基盤（OpenSDL）、安全実行ランタイム（Safe-SDL）、実験室ベンチマーク（L3-Bench）の4コンポーネントからなるトレーサブルなフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 実験室のワークフローにおける調整と追跡可能性の課題に対処するエンドツーエンドの設計を提供した。
keywords_ja: セルフドライビング実験室

2610.36726.title: Learning Side-by-Side Navigation for Personal Mobility Vehicles from Human Drivers
2610.36726.abstract: This paper presents an approach to achieve side-by-side autonomous motion with a pair of personal mobility vehicles (PMVs). Given a global path, two PMVs plan cooperatively so as to hold a social formation that lets the passengers hold a conversation, while keeping the ride safe and smooth. Each vehicle runs its own sampling-based model-predictive planner; the planners exchange nothing but the odometry each vehicle could observe of the other, and the joint decision is expressed as a pair of utility matrices over pairs of candidate trajectories, resolved by a common rule. The behavioural parameters are fitted by inverse reinforcement learning from 409 minutes of driving by ten pairs of people in human-driven PMVs in an indoor environment, and the lanes the pair can use are derived offline from the corridor itself rather than fixed by hand. A safety layer the cost cannot override executes a move only if the vehicle can still brake clear, measured from its whole body, and a vehicle that is stuck reverses along its own path and continues. In closed-loop simulation over 24 runs in the conditions the drivers were recorded in and 24 in four generated obstacle layouts, no vehicle entered a wall or a cone. The pair holds conversational formation for 60.5 and 68.9 percent of the time among obstacles (anticlockwise and clockwise) and 81.2 and 91.5 percent in a clear aisle, against the drivers' 34.0 and 36.0 percent, and 52.9 and 56.0 percent, and it matches their speed. It keeps one lateral formation where the drivers alternated between a close diagonal and a wide abreast one, and it varies far less. Experimental results are based on a differential drive kinematic simulator running on ROS 2.

llm.title_ja: 人間ドライバーからの個人用モビリティビークル向けサイドバイサイドナビゲーションの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 個人用モビリティビークル（PMV）のペアにおいて、安全でスムーズな走行を維持しながら、乗客が会話できる社会的隊形を保ちつつサイドバイサイドで協調的な自律移動を実現する必要がある。
llm.method: 各車両がサンプリングベースのモデル予測プランナーを実行し、逆強化学習によって行動パラメータをフィッティングするアプローチを提案する。
llm.result: 閉ループシミュレーションにおいて壁やコーンへの衝突はなく、障害物のある環境や開けた通路で高い割合で会話フォーテーションを維持できた。
llm.limitation: ROS 2上で動作する差動駆動キネマティックシミュレータに基づく実験結果である。
keywords_ja: パーソナルモビリティ

2610.36725.title: On Shaky Ground: Characterising Non-Rigid Base Effects in Mobile Manipulation
2610.36725.abstract: Mobile robot manipulators extend contact-task capability beyond the workspace of fixed robot installations, but their bases must also sustain the forces generated by the task. On lightweight platforms, base motion and support compliance can change the force and motion realised at the workpiece. How these non-rigid base effects manifest during sustained contact remains insufficiently characterised. This paper investigates non-rigid base effects in mobile robot manipulators through a sanding case study combining exploratory simulation with experiments on two lightweight, unactuated wheeled testbeds. Joint measurements of contact force, tool motion, and base vibration show that sustained contact coexisted with substantial task error: under low base-ground resistance, only 54-70% of a 100 N command was realised, with tool-centre-point errors reaching 100 mm. Increasing base-ground resistance during contact improved force realisation and arrested further tool displacement, while base vibration did not vary consistently with force-tracking error in the tested conditions. These observations illustrate how non-rigid base behaviour can affect contact-task execution and highlight the value of examining force, motion, and vibration together when characterising lightweight mobile manipulation.
2610.36725.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA 2026)

llm.title_ja: 揺れる足場：移動マニピュレーションにおける非剛性ベース効果の特性評価
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 軽量プラットフォーム上の移動ロボットマニピュレータにおいて、ベースの動きや支持コンプライアンスがワークピース上で実現される力や運動を変化させるが、持続的な接触中の影響は十分に特性評価されていない。
llm.method: サンディングのケーススタディを通じて、シミュレーションと2つの軽量な無動力車輪型テストベッドでの実験を組み合わせて非剛性ベース効果を調査する。
llm.result: 低ベース地上抵抗下では100N指令の54〜70%しか実現されず、ツール中心点エラーが最大100mmに達するなど、非剛性ベース挙動が接触タスク実行に影響することを示した。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション

2610.36694.title: TOPS: Reshaping Flow Source and Transport for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation
2610.36694.abstract: Flow-based policies for language-conditioned multi-task manipulation commonly share a single $\textit{Gaussian}$ source prior and a common linear transport path across tasks. However, reliably executing multiple tasks with distinct motion requirements remains challenging for a shared policy. We introduce $\textbf{TOPS}$ ($\textbf{T}$ask-$\textbf{O}$riented $\textbf{P}$riors and $\textbf{S}$chedules), which adapts the flow source prior and interpolation schedule to each task without modifying the network architecture. TOPS first constructs multimodal task sources from reverse-mapped expert action sequences, allowing language instructions to select where generation begins. Guided by source-target covariance mismatch, it then slows the transition toward expert actions early in denoising and accelerates it later along directions requiring expansion. Under a $\textit{Gaussian}$ endpoint model, our analysis shows that this schedule adjustment can lower an upper bound on velocity-prediction risk. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN demonstrate improved performance across in-distribution, perturbation and cross-environment settings, alongside better data efficiency. Using one integration step, TOPS raises LIBERO-10 success from $53.44\%$ to $69.67\%$ compared with ten-step Standard Flow Matching (FM), while reducing inference time to approximately one-sixth of the baseline. TOPS also yields consistent gains when transferred to the large-scale flow-based $π_{0.5}$ policy across all four evaluated settings. Real-world experiments further demonstrate improved task success, including an increase from $20\%$ with standard FM to $80\%$ with TOPS on the upper-drawer opening task.
2610.36694.tldr_en: This work introduces TOPS, which adapts the flow source prior and interpolation schedule to each task without modifying the network architecture, and shows that this schedule adjustment can lower an upper bound on velocity-prediction risk.

llm.title_ja: TOPS：マルチタスクロボットマニュピュレーションのためのフローソースとトランスポートの再構築
llm.tldr_ja: TOPSはネットワーク構造を変更せずにタスクごとにフローソース事前分布と補間スケジュールを適応させ、速度予測リスクの上界を低下させる。
llm.problem: 異なる動作要件を持つ複数のタスクを単一の共有ポリシーで信頼性高く実行することは困難である。
llm.method: 逆写像されたエキスパート行動からマルチモーダルなタスクソースを構築し、ノイズ除去過程のソース・ターゲット共分散のミスマッチに応じてスケジュールを調整するTOPSを導入する。
llm.result: LIBERO、LIBERO-Plus、CALVINでの実験および実機の引き出し開けタスクで成功率の向上と推論時間の短縮を実証した。
keywords_ja: マニュピュレーション

2610.36693.title: Quantifying and Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors
2610.36693.abstract: Security pipelines often fuse several data sources and protect a downstream model with a cross-source anomaly detector. Such detectors are usually judged by their clean false-positive rate and by how well they catch random corruption. Neither metric captures an adversary who controls some sources and targets a specific downstream decision. We propose a threat-quantification score, the \emph{task-conditioned visibility margin}, defined as the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm to the downstream task. The margin has a closed form, takes about $85\,μ$s per certificate, yields a minimum-evidence attack, and identifies task-relevant directions the detector cannot see. On a 17-channel industrial telemetry benchmark, a detector that flags 82.8\% of random single-channel corruptions is first-order blind on 64.7\% of task/subset pairs in an audit of one- to four-channel subsets. Task-conditioned manipulations cause more than twice as many falsely reassuring errors as generic stealthy ones, and more of them evade the alarm on four of five splits, mainly at small budgets. Used to prioritize audits on held-out subsets, the margin finds a median of four verified failures in ten checks, compared with none for random order and two for alarm-based ranking, and performs comparably to the task-gradient baseline. It also ranks vulnerable configurations of the learned GDN and TranAD detectors and of a five-source crop-yield panel.
2610.36693.comment: To be appeared at Workshop on AI for Cyber Threat Intelligence (WAITI) 2026 @ ACSAC 2026
2610.36693.tldr_en: A threat-quantification score is proposed, the task-conditioned visibility margin, defined as the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm to the downstream task, used to prioritize audits on held-out subsets and performs comparably to the task-gradient baseline.

llm.title_ja: マルチソース異常検知器に対するステルス性ソース操作脅威の定量化と優先順位付け
llm.tldr_ja: タスク条件付き可視性マージンという脅威定量化スコアを提案し、ダウンストリームタスクへの害あたりの最小検出証拠を定義して監査の優先順位付けを行う。
llm.problem: 既存の異常検知器の評価指標では、一部のソースを制御して特定の決定を標的とする攻撃者を捉えられない。
llm.method: 閉形式を持ち、最小証拠攻撃を生成し、検知器が検知できないタスク関連方向を特定するタスク条件付き可視性マージンを提案する。
llm.result: 産業用テレメトリーベンチマークにおいて、ランダム順序やアラームベースのランキングよりも効率的に検証済み障害を発見できることを示した。

2610.36685.title: RoboSTD: Zero-Shot Single-to-Dual Transfer via Sagittal Mirroring for Bimanual Learning
2610.36685.abstract: Bimanual robot manipulation plays an important role in real-world robotic applications, but the high cost of collecting bimanual demonstrations limits the scalable development of bimanual policy learning. Meanwhile, existing single-arm manipulation data are difficult to directly transfer to bimanual systems due to the Single-to-Dual gap in action spaces, coordination requirements, and arm-side spatial preference. To address this issue, we propose RoboSTD, a zero-shot Single-to-Dual data construction method for bimanual robot learning. RoboSTD first applies sagittal-plane mirroring to observations, proprioception, and actions to construct executable contralateral pseudo-demonstrations. It then uses an LLM to generate structured spatio-temporal coordination constraints that guide the reconstruction of pseudo-bimanual supervision across workspace regions and task stages. We evaluate RoboSTD on the AgileX ALOHA platform in both RoboTwin simulation and real-world settings. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RoboSTD for bimanual policy learning. Without requiring additional bimanual demonstrations, RoboSTD increases the average number of collected cups to 2.11x that of the single-arm baseline in the cup collection task. Project page: https://huahungy.github.io/RoboSTD/
2610.36685.tldr_en: RoboSTD first applies sagittal-plane mirroring to observations, proprioception, and actions to construct executable contralateral pseudo-demonstrations, and uses an LLM to generate structured spatio-temporal coordination constraints that guide the reconstruction of pseudo-bimanual supervision across workspace regions and task stages.

llm.title_ja: RoboSTD：矢状面鏡像反転を用いた両手学習のためのゼロショット単腕から両手への転移
llm.tldr_ja: RoboSTDは、矢状面ミラーリングとLLMによる構造化された協調制約を用いて、追加の両手デモンストレーションなしで単腕データから両手ポリシー学習を行う。
llm.problem: 両手デモンストレーションの収集コストが高く、単腕データの空間的・協調的ギャップのため両手システムへの直接転移が困難である。
llm.method: 観察・固有受容感覚・行動に矢状面ミラーリングを適用して疑似デモンストレーションを構築し、LLMで協調制約を生成して再構築を行う。
llm.result: AgileX ALOHAプラットフォームを用いたシミュレーションおよび実機実験において、カップ収集タスクなどで単腕ベースラインを上回る成果を実証した。
keywords_ja: 両手マニュピュレーション

2610.36681.title: From Biological Curves to Soft Modular Robots: Learning-Based Inverse Design with Uncertainty-Guided Refinement
2610.36681.abstract: Animals exhibit diverse shape-changing behaviors, from the undulatory swimming of eels to the arching movements of inchworms. Reproducing these biological shapes with modular soft robots offers a promising approach to developing versatile bioinspired robotic systems. However, translating a desired shape into a feasible robotic configuration remains challenging. Existing cable-driven modular soft robots rely on computationally expensive physics-based modeling and combinatorial search for inverse design, making it difficult to efficiently reproduce diverse target shapes. To address this challenge, we present a learning-based real-to-sim-to-real framework that translates biological curves into robotic configurations through surrogate-assisted inverse design and uncertainty-guided refinement. The proposed method combines learned inverse prediction with targeted candidate exploration, using a fast forward surrogate to evaluate and select suitable designs. The learned forward surrogate reduces deformation prediction time from $1.53 \times 10^5$ ms to 0.0008 ms, achieving approximately a $1.9 \times 10^8$-fold speedup. At the same time, the proposed inverse design method reduces design time from $1.99 \times 10^6$ ms to 4.18 ms. On 5,000 test samples generated from previously unseen threading patterns, the method achieves a 93% shape reconstruction success rate under surrogate-based evaluation. Physical demonstrations with four bioinspired robots further illustrate the translation of biological curves into realizable robotic shapes.
2610.36681.tldr_en: This work presents a learning-based real-to-sim-to-real framework that translates biological curves into robotic configurations through surrogate-assisted inverse design and uncertainty-guided refinement, and achieves a 93% shape reconstruction success rate under surrogate-based evaluation.

llm.title_ja: 生物学的曲線からソフトモジュラーロボットへ：不確実性ガイド付き洗練を伴う学習ベースの逆設計
llm.tldr_ja: 生物学的曲線をロボットの構成に変換する、サロゲート支援型逆設計と不確実性ガイド付き洗練を用いたreal-to-sim-to-realフレームワークを提案し、93%の形状再構成成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 目的の形状を、計算コストの高い物理モデルや組合せ探索に頼らずに実現可能なロボット構成へ効率的に変換することが困難である。
llm.method: 学習済みの順方向サロゲートを用いて迅速に評価・選択を行い、学習済み逆予測と候補探索を組み合わせたフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 変形予測時間を約1.9×10^8倍高速化し、未見の糸通しパターンを用いた5,000のテストサンプルで93%の形状再構成成功率を達成した。

2610.36662.title: SWIM: Learning What Matters from Behaviors for JEPA World Models
2610.36662.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) enable world models to plan from images by predicting future embeddings. However, their visual prediction objectives do not explicitly incorporate task-relevant state information, so the physical state that determines task progress may not be reliably captured in the latent space. Supervising world models with simulator state can make planning more informative, but it requires deciding which state features matter. Features are typically selected by hand or weighted uniformly, and a uniform weighting gives every standardized state feature equal influence, so redundant coordinates can overcount the same variation, while irrelevant ones can obscure task-relevant differences. To address this limitation, we propose SWIM (State Weighting with Inverse-Dynamics Model), which learns state weights from offline trajectories by predicting recorded actions from current states and observed future displacements. The learned weights quantify each feature's contribution to action prediction and define a weighted state metric for state-supervised training, which we demonstrate by aligning latent and state distances. The inverse-dynamics model is used only during training, so the resulting world model plans from images with no additional planning-time computation. Across five simulated robotic manipulation tasks, SWIM consistently improves planning success over uniform state weighting.
2610.36662.tldr_en: SWIM (State Weighting with Inverse-Dynamics Model), which learns state weights from offline trajectories by predicting recorded actions from current states and observed future displacements and consistently improves planning success over uniform state weighting.

llm.title_ja: SWIM：JEPA世界モデルのために行動から重要な学習を行う
llm.tldr_ja: SWIMは、現在状態と観測された将来変位から記録された行動を予測することでオフライン軌跡から状態ウェイトを学習し、計画成功率を一貫して向上させる。
llm.problem: JEPAの視覚予測目的にはタスク関連の状態情報が明示的に組み込まれておらず、一様な重み付けでは冗長な座標や無関係な座標が影響を与えてしまう。
llm.method: 現在状態と将来変位から行動を予測する逆ダイナミクスモデルにより状態ウェイトを学習し、状態教師あり訓練用の重み付き状態メトリックを定義する。
llm.result: 5つのシミュレーション化されたロボットマニュピュレーションタスクにおいて、一様な状態重み付けよりも計画成功率を一貫して向上させた。
keywords_ja: マニュピュレーション

2610.36658.title: SAGE: Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts for Point Cloud Registration
2610.36658.abstract: Point cloud registration is an essential task for scene reconstruction, requiring the alignment of partially overlapping point clouds. Under low-overlap conditions, this task remains challenging because existing geometry-only methods cannot distinguish geometrically similar but semantically distinct structures (e.g., TV corners vs. desk corners and chair legs vs. table legs), resulting in incorrect correspondences. To address this geometric ambiguity, we present Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts (SAGE), which integrates frozen pre-trained point cloud semantic representations into the registration pipeline without requiring additional sensors or fine-tuning the semantic encoder. To effectively leverage these semantic distinctions, SAGE employs a Semantic-Guided Mixture of Experts (SG-MoE) architecture. Through semantic-aware routing, SG-MoE enables each expert to specialize in distinct semantic-geometric patterns, reducing mismatches that confound geometry-only methods. With a structure-aware estimator, SAGE achieves the highest registration recall on 3DLoMatch while remaining competitive on 3DMatch. When evaluated with the same number of refinement iterations, SAGE further achieves the highest inlier ratio and registration recall on both benchmarks. These results indicate that frozen semantic representations provide effective cues for resolving geometric ambiguity in low-overlap registration.
2610.36658.tldr_en: Results indicate that frozen semantic representations provide effective cues for resolving geometric ambiguity in low-overlap registration.

llm.title_ja: SAGE：点群登録のための意味情報拡張型幾何学エキスパート
llm.tldr_ja: SAGEは、事前学習済みの点群セマンティック表現を統合し、Semantic-Guided Mixture of Experts (SG-MoE)を用いて低重なり条件下の幾何学的曖昧さを解決する。
llm.problem: 低重なり条件では、既存の幾何学のみの手法では幾何学的に類似し意味的に異なる構造を区別できず、誤った対応付けが生じる。
llm.method: セマンティック表現を統合し、意味認識型ルーティングを用いて各エキスパートが異なるパターンに特化するSG-MoEアーキテクチャを採用する。
llm.result: 3DLoMatchで最高の登録リコールを達成し、3DMatchでも競争力を維持して、固定されたセマンティック表現が幾何学的曖昧さの解決に有効であることを示した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックセグメンテーション

2610.36625.title: Polarity--Time Interaction and Multi-Level Reliability for Event-Based Spacecraft Pose Estimation
2610.36625.abstract: Sparse event responses produce uneven keypoint errors whose effects on spacecraft pose depend on correspondence geometry and the reliability of successive observations. We present a reliability-aware framework connecting polarity--time localization, geometric recovery, event--CAD refinement, and trajectory optimization. A three-branch representation combines positive events, negative events, and recent-event timing through cross-branch attention and gating, followed by spatiotemporal aggregation. An ordered semantic-point head estimates relative correspondence precision for geometrically constrained pose recovery. Event-edge and CAD-projection agreement then guide local pose refinement under keypoint-geometry safeguards. At the sequence level, a ten-dimensional descriptor combines heatmap shape, reprojection consistency, and geometric conditioning to set time-aligned observation scales. On the official SPADES challenge test set, the complete system achieves a combined pose score of 0.0474, approximately 5.4\% below PASAN+IRIS. Validation ablations reduce the score from 0.0772 for base localization with uniform PnP to 0.0514 for the complete cascade; on identical single-frame observations, quality weighting reduces the score from 0.0549 with constant-weight optimization to 0.0514.

llm.title_ja: イベントベースの宇宙船ポーズ推定における極性・時間相互作用とマルチレベル信頼性
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: スパースなイベント応答は、対応関係の幾何学や連続する観測の信頼性に依存して宇宙船のポーズに影響を与える不均一なキーポイント誤差を生成する。
llm.method: 極性・時間のローカライゼーション、幾何学的回復、イベント・CADの洗練、軌道最適化を接続する信頼性認識フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: SPADESチャレンジテストセットにおいて、ベースローカライゼーションから完全なカスケードへの改善によりポーズスコアを大幅に削減した。

2610.36624.title: Adapting Video Models for Robot Control via Motion-guided Asymmetric Prediction
2610.36624.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) leverage pretrained video generative models for robotic control by jointly predicting future visual observations and actions. The visual prediction objective plays a key role in adapting pretrained video representations to the target robot domain. Yet standard visual prediction inherited from video pretraining treats all visual regions uniformly, despite their differing relevance to robotic control. We therefore investigate the spatial allocation of visual supervision in WAMs and show that focusing supervision on dynamic regions can substantially improve policy performance. Building on this finding, we introduce Motion-Guided Asymmetric Prediction (MoGAP), which augments WAM training with motion-focused visual prediction. MoGAP allocates noise asymmetrically across regions, training the model to reconstruct more heavily corrupted dynamic regions using less corrupted static regions as context. MoGAP is trained alongside standard video-action prediction through a training-only auxiliary prediction path within the shared video diffusion backbone. It uses motion cues derived directly from training videos, requiring neither an external teacher nor additional modalities. Across robot manipulation benchmarks and WAM architectures, MoGAP consistently improves policy performance, increasing success rates on the GR-1 tabletop benchmark from 38.8% to 47.5% for Fast-WAM (Wan2.2-5B) and from 52.3% to 62.3% for Cosmos3-Nano.
2610.36624.tldr_en: Motion-Guided Asymmetric Prediction (MoGAP), which augments WAM training with motion-focused visual prediction, which consistently improves policy performance and uses motion cues derived directly from training videos, requiring neither an external teacher nor additional modalities.

llm.title_ja: モーション誘導非対称予測によるロボット制御のためのビデオモデル適応
llm.tldr_ja: MoGAPは、動的領域に視覚的監視を集中させるモーション誘導非対称予測を導入し、追加の教師なしでポリシー性能を向上させる。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みビデオモデルをロボット制御に適用する際、標準的な視覚予測はすべての視覚領域を均一に扱っており制御への関連性の違いを無視している。
llm.method: 動的領域と静的領域の間で非対称にノイズを割り当て、汚染された動的領域を復元するように訓練するMoGAPを導入する。
llm.result: GR-1などのタスクベンチマークにおいて、Fast-WAMやCosmos3-Nanoの成功率を向上させ、ポリシー性能の改善を一貫して示した。
keywords_ja: 世界アクションモデル

2610.36615.title: HumiMimic: Mimetic Embodiment Transfer of Human-Humanoid Interaction from In-the-Wild Videos
2610.36615.abstract: Enabling a humanoid to interact naturally with human partners requires preserving not only individual motions but also the spatial, semantic, and contact relationships underlying the interaction (i.e., hugging, dancing, hand-shaking, etc.). Furthermore, a practical solution should generalize across various humanoid embodiments with distinct morphologies and kinematic constraints. To tackle this challenge, we propose HumiTransfer, a mimetic embodiment transfer framework that converts in-the-wild human-human interaction videos into physically plausible human-humanoid interactions. HumiTransfer first reconstructs 3D human motion with consistent foot-ground contact, then transfers one participant to a target humanoid embodiment via interaction modeling, using weighted joint-relative directions and anatomical offsets to prioritize interaction-critical inter-body relationships, while post-retargeting optimization enforces balance, contact, and collision avoidance. Subsequently, we apply HumiTransfer to 1,200 in-the-wild videos, producing approximately 500,000 frames of diverse interactions for the 26-DoF Unitree R1 Edu and the 23-DoF HighTorque Mini-hi humanoid robot, resulting in our HumiMimic dataset. Across both robots, HumiTransfer achieves superior motion fidelity, preserves inter-body relationships, and maintains contact accuracy compared with existing baselines. Moreover, we demonstrate that HumiMimic supports motion generation methods for synthesizing interactive humanoid motions following a human partner. Finally, our real robot deployments confirm the physical executability of the transferred motions in real-world settings. Our project is available at https://aioznetwork.github.io/HumiMimic/
2610.36615.tldr_en: HumiTransfer is proposed, a mimetic embodiment transfer framework that converts in-the-wild human-human interaction videos into physically plausible human-humanoid interactions and demonstrates that HumiMimic supports motion generation methods for synthesizing interactive humanoid motions following a human partner.

llm.title_ja: HumiMimic：インザワイルド動画からのヒューマン・ヒューマノイド間インタラクションの模倣的身体転移
llm.tldr_ja: HumiTransferは、インザワイルドの人間同士のインタラクション動画を、物理的に妥当な人間とヒューマノイド間のインタラクションに変換する。
llm.problem: 自然なインタラクションを行うためには個々の動作だけでなく空間・意味・接触関係を保持する必要があり、異なる形態を持つヒューマノイドへの汎化が求められる。
llm.method: 3D人間の動きを再構築し、重み付けされた関節相対方向や解剖学的オフセットを用いてターゲットヒューマノイドの身体へインタラクション関係を転移する。
llm.result: 約50万フレームのHumiMimicデータセットを構築し、優れた動作忠実度と接触精度を確認するとともに実機での実行可能性を実証した。

2610.36610.title: 4D Reconstruction with Events & RGB
2610.36610.abstract: Reconstructing dynamic 3D scenes over time (4D reconstruction) from a single moving camera is central to robotics and AR/VR applications, yet state-of the-art feed-forward methods rely solely on RGB frames and therefore inherit the failure modes of conventional cameras, including motion blur and temporal aliasing under fast or non-uniform camera and object motion. Event cameras report per-pixel brightness changes asynchronously at microsecond resolution, offering a complementary signal that is largely immune to these artifacts, but whether this modality can be incorporated into existing RGB based 4D reconstruction pipelines without a full architectural redesign remains an open question. In this preliminary study, we investigate a minimal extension: we augment Monst3R, an existing RGB-only 4D reconstruction model, with an additional event-camera input branch, leaving the rest of the architecture unchanged. Across 3 benchmark datasets, this simple RGB-event fusion reduces Abs Rel by 3.4% on average relative to the RGB-only Monst3R baseline, and a sensitivity analysis shows that the improvement grows with the magnitude of camera and object motion, with the largest gains observed under high object motion conditions where RGB-only reconstruction degrades most. These early results suggest that even a lightweight, non-invasive fusion of event data can meaningfully improve 4D reconstruction robustness, motivating a more thorough architectural investigation in future work.
2610.36610.comment: Accepted at NeVi 2026 workshop at the 19th European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2026)
2610.36610.tldr_en: It is suggested that even a lightweight, non-invasive fusion of event data can meaningfully improve 4D reconstruction robustness, motivating a more thorough architectural investigation in future work.

llm.title_ja: イベントカメラとRGBを用いた4D再構成
llm.tldr_ja: 既存のRGBベースの4D再構成モデル（Monst3R）に軽量なイベントカメラ入力ブランチを追加することで、高速な動きに対する再構成の頑健性を高める。
llm.problem: RGBのみのフィードフォワード手法は高速または不規則なカメラや物体の動きによるモーションブラーや時間的エイリアシングの影響を受ける。
llm.method: Monst3Rに非侵襲的なイベントデータ用の追加入力ブランチを組み込む軽量な拡張を行い、RGB-event融合を実現する。
llm.result: 3つのベンチマークデータセットにおいてAbs Relを平均3.4%削減し、特に高速な動きの条件下で最大の改善効果を示した。
llm.limitation: 本研究は予備的検討であり、より詳細なアーキテクチャの調査が今後の課題である。

2610.36599.title: Camera-to-Quadruped Robot Pose Estimation from Sequential Images
2610.36599.abstract: Quadruped robots are increasingly deployed in hazardous environments such as disaster response and facility inspection, where external-camera monitoring is essential for safe operation. This setting is challenging because quadrupeds are articulated systems with time-varying leg joints, leg symmetry, and frequent self-occlusions, which make keypoint correspondence ambiguous. Moreover, no public benchmark exists, making quantitative comparison difficult. To address these challenges, we propose QuadPose, which estimates the full-body 18-DoF pose (6-DoF base pose + 12-DoF joint angles) from monocular video sequences, and introduce QuadSyn, the first camera-to-quadruped robot pose benchmark. On QuadSyn, QuadPose achieves 92.18% PCK@2.5px, 95.54% PCK-AUC, 85.94% ADD@20cm, 66.98% ADD-AUC, and 3.65 degree mean joint-angle error at approximately 33 FPS.
2610.36599.tldr_en: QuadPose is proposed, which estimates the full-body 18-DoF pose (6-DoF base pose + 12-DoF joint angles) from monocular video sequences, and QuadSyn is introduced, the first camera-to-quadruped robot pose benchmark.

llm.title_ja: シーケンシャル画像からのカメラから四足歩行ロボットの姿勢推定
llm.tldr_ja: QuadPoseは単眼ビデオシーケンスから四足歩行ロボットの18自由度全身姿勢を推定し、初のベンチマークであるQuadSynを導入した。
llm.problem: 四足歩行ロボットは関節が時変であり対称性や自己遮蔽が頻繁に起こるため、外部カメラからのキーポイント対応付けが曖昧で既存の公開ベンチマークもない。
llm.method: 単眼動画から6自由度のベース姿勢と12自由度の関節角度を推定するQuadPoseを提案し、新しい評価ベンチマークQuadSynを構築した。
llm.result: QuadSynにおいて92.18%のPCK@2.5pxや3.65度の平均関節角度誤差を約33 FPSで達成した。

2610.36598.title: OpenJaws: An Open Hardware UMI Framework with Stereo Localization for Generalist Manipulation
2610.36598.abstract: Handheld data-collection interfaces such as the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) allow manipulation demonstrations to be gathered in the wild without a robot in the loop, but the quality of the resulting action labels is bounded by the accuracy of vision-based localization. Existing systems recover end-effector pose from monocular visual-inertial odometry, which is subject to scale ambiguity and drift, or delegate tracking to closed-source modules and external infrastructure that reintroduce cost and setup burden. We present OpenJaws, a fully open hardware and software framework for sensorized UMI that improves localization and simplifies deployment across robot platforms. OpenJaws pairs a modular, 3D-printed gripper exposing a standardized ISO adapter with a low-cost stereo camera to recover metric camera trajectories. We further introduce UMI-Loc-Bench-v1, a benchmark quantifying real-world localization accuracy for handheld data-collection devices, and show that stereo localization substantially outperforms monocular alternatives. Finally, we demonstrate that policies trained on data collected with OpenJaws can be deployed on a real robot across multiple tasks. Hardware, software, and data are released under a commercially permissive license. Code, data, and videos are available at https://open-jaws.github.io/
2610.36598.tldr_en: OpenJaws is presented, a fully open hardware and software framework for sensorized UMI that improves localization and simplifies deployment across robot platforms and introduces UMI-Loc-Bench-v1, a benchmark quantifying real-world localization accuracy for handheld data-collection devices.

llm.title_ja: OpenJaws：汎用マニュピュレーションのためのステレオローカライゼーションを備えたオープンハードウェアUMIフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: OpenJawsは、モジュール式の3Dプリント製グリッパーと低コストステレオカメラを組み合わせることで測位精度を高めたオープンなハードウェア・ソフトウェアフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 従来のハンディキャップ型データ収集では、単眼視覚慣性オドメトリによるスケールの曖昧さやドリフト、または高コストな外部インフラに依存している。
llm.method: ISOアダプターを備えたグリッパーとステレオカメラをペアにし、実世界の測位精度を定量化するベンチマークUMI-Loc-Bench-v1を導入する。
llm.result: ステレオローカライゼーションが単眼手法よりも優れていることを示し、収集したデータを用いたポリシーが実機タスクで展開できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: オープンハードウェア
マニュピュレーション

2610.36592.title: LabWorld: Learning Interactive 4D Worlds for Scientific Experimentation
2610.36592.abstract: Autonomous scientific agents must not only reason about experiments but also interact with the physical environments in which they are executed. Existing laboratory simulators typically rely on manually constructed assets and predefined procedures, while laboratory videos capture real equipment, layouts, and interactions but leave this information implicit in pixels. We introduce LabWorld, an agent-driven Real2Sim framework for reconstructing interactive 4D laboratory worlds from monocular RGB video. LabWorld recovers reusable 3D assets, a metric scene, time-varying object states, and procedure events. Multi-frame observations provide complementary evidence for asset and scene reconstruction, while motion reconstruction combines visual and geometric observations with event constraints encoding the spatial and temporal requirements of laboratory interactions. We evaluate LabWorld on real pipetting and vortexing videos collected in our laboratory against general-purpose agentic and dedicated reconstruction baselines. For pipetting, LabWorld achieves a mean Mask IoU of 0.501, exceeding the strongest baseline by 0.033. For vortexing, it achieves a mean Tube-Length-Normalized PCK-AUC of 0.638, exceeding the strongest baseline by 0.035. On five pipetting videos, event-conditioned reconstruction increases the fraction of modeled physical constraints satisfied from 14.3% (5/35) to 100% (35/35). The resulting worlds expose geometry, motion, articulation, and events as explicit, editable state for replay, inspection, and future embodied scientific systems.
2610.36592.comment: 20 pages, 4 figures. Suozhi Huang and Kelsey Fu contributed equally
2610.36592.tldr_en: LabWorld, an agent-driven Real2Sim framework for reconstructing interactive 4D laboratory worlds from monocular RGB video, is introduced, an agent-driven Real2Sim framework for reconstructing interactive 4D laboratory worlds from monocular RGB video that recovers reusable 3D assets, a metric scene, time-varying object states, and procedure events.

llm.title_ja: LabWorld：科学実験のためのインタラクティブ4Dワールドの学習
llm.tldr_ja: LabWorldは、単眼RGBビデオから再利用可能な3Dアセットや時間変化するオブジェクト状態を復元するエージェント駆動型Real2Simフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存の実験室シミュレータは手動作成のアセットに依存し、実験室のビデオは実世界のレイアウトやインタラクションがピクセル内に埋め込まれている。
llm.method: 視覚的および幾何学的観察を、実験室の空間的・時間的要件をコード化したイベント制約と組み合わせたマルチフレーム再構成フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: ピペッティングやボルテックスのビデオにおいてベースラインを上回るマスクIoUやPCK-AUCを達成し、物理制約の充足率を大幅に向上させた。

2610.36546.title: REACH: An RL-based Hierarchical Humanoid Crawling Framework for Adaptable Confined Space Traversal
2610.36546.abstract: Humanoid locomotion in confined spaces requires continuous height adaptation across multiple locomotion modes, yet most existing approaches remain limited to height-adjustable bipedal walking. We present REACH, an RL-based hierarchical framework that enables a Unitree G1 humanoid to traverse height-constrained environments through variable-height bipedal walking and crawling. The learned policies regulate body height over complementary command ranges of 1.27--0.50m in bipedal locomotion and 0.50--0.20m in crawling, extending traversal beyond the clearance limits of crouched walking. To address contact-rich crawling dynamics, we employ a history-conditioned latent representation that captures terrain and interaction context from proprioceptive observations. A bidirectional transition policy further connects crouched bipedal locomotion and crawling across large kinematic and contact discontinuities. These skills are integrated with a LiDAR-based planner that converts point clouds into collision-free three-dimensional paths and locomotion commands, including proactive height targets. Real-world experiments demonstrate accurate height and velocity tracking, robust terrain traversal, reliable mode transitions and confined-space traversal with the proposed pipeline. Code and videos are available at https://aislab-sustech.github.io/REACH/.
2610.36546.comment: To appear at IEEE Humanoids 2026; Project page https://aislab-sustech.github.io/REACH/
2610.36546.tldr_en: REACH is presented, an RL-based hierarchical framework that enables a Unitree G1 humanoid to traverse height-constrained environments through variable-height bipedal walking and crawling through a LiDAR-based planner integrated with a LiDAR-based planner.

llm.title_ja: REACH：適応的な狭隘空間通行のための強化学習ベース階層型ヒューマノイド這行フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: REACHは、可変高さの二足歩行と這行動作を組み合わせてUnitree G1ヒューマノイドが狭隘空間を通過できるようにする強化学習ベースの階層型フレームワークである。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの狭隘空間での移動は連続的な高さ適応を必要とするが、既存の手法はしゃがみ歩行の高さ制限に留まっている。
llm.method: 固有受容感覚から地形やインタラクション文脈を捉える履歴条件付き潜在表現を用い、LiDARベースのプランナーと統合した階層型ポリシーを構築する。
llm.result: 実世界実験において正確な高さ・速度追従、頑健な地形走破、スムーズなモード移行と狭隘空間の通過を実現した。

2610.36539.title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
2610.36539.abstract: Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. Retargeting can avoid this. However, existing methods purely translate kinematics and ignore the real-world contact dynamics essential for task success. We present CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets. CARD unifies human data sources including video, motion capture, and tactile gloves via a shared hand--contact representation and generates explicit contact force targets in addition to kinematics. To maintain these contact targets during hardware open-loop replay, CARD also introduces a tactile tracking controller. For video which does not contain an explicit tactile source, we present Vid-HACO, our video-to-contact model that sets a new state of the art. Across our video, glove, motion-capture data and the GRAB dataset, CARD maintains contact on $43$--$78\%$ of contact frames, while kinematic and object-aware retargeting methods maintain contact on $<10\%$ and $22.5\%$ of the frames respectively. Further, integrating our formulation into physics-based retargeting improves strict task success from 12\% to 32\% on GRAB dataset. Finally, we show that our tactile tracker is critical to reproduce demonstrated forces during hardware replay. These results establish that contact preservation via CARD is a scalable interface for transferring human dexterity to robots.
2610.36539.tldr_en: CARD is presented, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets and it is established that contact preservation via CARD is a scalable interface for transferring human dexterity to robots.

llm.title_ja: CARD：器用なマニュピュレーションのための接触アンカー型リタイゲーティング
llm.tldr_ja: CARDは、接触力ターゲットを明示的に保持することで人間のデモンストレーションをロボットの行動に変換するシミュレータ・オブジェクトフリーなフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 従来のリタイゲーティングは運動学のみを翻訳し、タスク成功に不可欠な実世界の接触ダイナミクスを無視しているため人間の器用さを制限している。
llm.method: 共有されたハンド・接触表現を介して動画や触覚グローブなどの多様なデータを統合し、接触力ターゲットと触覚トラッキングコントローラを生成する。
llm.result: GRABデータセット等において高頻度での接触保持を維持し、ハードウェア再生時にデモンストレーションされた力を再現できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: マニュピュレーション

2610.36537.title: A Trainable CPG Framework for Quadruped Locomotion
2610.36537.abstract: We present CPG-ENN, a trainable quadruped locomotion framework that combines explicit neural coordination with learned motion realization. A symmetry-based eight-neuron central pattern generator (CPG) supplies gait rhythms, while a pretrained, leg-shared execution neural network (ENN) maps rhythmic signals and trajectory parameters to joint-angle references without online inverse kinematics. A single feedback policy modulates six physically interpretable trajectory variables. The controller tracks planar velocity and yaw-rate commands across walk, trot, pace, bound, and pronk without gait-specific learned controllers or transitionspecific rewards. Simulation yields 99.39% transition success across all 20 directed gait pairs and all source-target speed combinations from {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} m/s. Ablations show high cross-gait transition feasibility without transition exposure; exposure mainly refines gait acquisition and velocity transients. Comparisons with AllGaits and Walk These Ways demonstrate accurate gait-speed regulation, and Unitree Go2 experiments validate five gaits and their transitions.
2610.36537.tldr_en: A symmetry-based eight-neuron central pattern generator supplies gait rhythms, while a pretrained, leg-shared execution neural network maps rhythmic signals and trajectory parameters to joint-angle references without online inverse kinematics.

llm.title_ja: 四足歩行のための訓練可能なCPGフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: CPG-ENNは、対称性に基づく8ニューロンの中央パターンジェネレータと学習済み実行ニューラルネットワークを組み合わせ、オンライン逆運動学なしで多様な歩容を実現する。
llm.problem: 従来の制御では歩容ごとに学習されたコントローラや移行報酬が必要になり、多様な歩容と滑らかな移行を統一的に扱うのが難しい。
llm.method: 8ニューロンのCPGで歩容リズムを供給し、脚共有の実行ニューラルネットワークでリズム信号を関節角度参照にマップするフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーションで全ての歩容ペア間で高い移行成功率を示し、Unitree Go2実機実験により5種類の歩容とその移行を検証した。
keywords_ja: 中央パターンジェネレータ

2610.36535.title: A generalist policy for muscle-driven control across individual musculoskeletal models
2610.36535.abstract: Differences in musculoskeletal morphology challenge policy reuse across individual models. Here we present MyoAcross, a framework that combines individual musculoskeletal model construction, morphology-conditioned policy learning and virtual model augmentation to enable muscle-driven reference-motion tracking without individual fine-tuning. Across 31 held-out individual models, MyoAcross achieves 99.24% completion and reduces tracking error by 22.60% relative to an unconditioned multilayer perceptron. Policy reuse extends to models of 22 held-out individuals constructed from single-image shape estimates, measured height and body mass, and, with asymmetry augmentation, to models with unilateral lower-limb shortening. Comparisons with measurements from 120 additional individuals show agreement in vertical ground reaction force waveforms and channel-dependent agreement between simulated muscle activations and electromyography. These results establish a common control framework for comparative simulations of movement across individual musculoskeletal models.
2610.36535.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures. Project website: https://woodater-thu.github.io/MyoAcross/ Bozhao Wang and Yinglei Zhu contributed equally to this work
2610.36535.tldr_en: MyoAcross is presented, a framework that combines individual musculoskeletal model construction, morphology-conditioned policy learning and virtual model augmentation to enable muscle-driven reference-motion tracking without individual fine-tuning to establish a common control framework for comparative simulations of movement across individual musculoskeletal models.

llm.title_ja: 個別の筋骨格モデルに対する筋肉駆動制御のためのジェネラリストポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: MyoAcrossは、個別の筋骨格モデル構築、形態条件付きポリシー学習、仮想モデル augmentationを組み合わせ、個別ファインチューニングなしでの筋肉駆動追従を実現する。
llm.problem: 筋骨格の形態の違いにより、個別のモデル間でポリシーを再利用することが困難である。
llm.method: 個別モデルの構築と形態条件付きポリシー学習、および非対称性拡張を統合したMyoAcrossフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 31のホールドアウトモデルにおいて99.24%の完了率を達成し、筋電図データや地面反力波形との一致を確認した。

2610.36533.title: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding
2610.36533.abstract: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. In robotic manipulation, Code-as-Policy lets these agents search over modular and editable robot programs. However, effective program search requires physical understanding: agents must understand how objects can be manipulated, how scene geometry constrains actions, and why interactions succeed or fail. Existing methods rely mainly on execution feedback for program refinement, often leaving these physical questions unresolved. We introduce RoboAuto, a framework for robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels through three components. First, a hierarchical knowledge base combines executable skills with object-centric knowledge of affordances, spatial relations, and action effects, learned from embodied data and online task solving. Second, scene grounding connects this knowledge to the current environment by identifying relevant objects and resolving action-critical quantities. Third, multi-stage planning with self-designed experiments checks whether each stage produces its expected physical effects and actively tests competing hypotheses to resolve physical uncertainties. RoboAuto achieves superior performance across five benchmark families, attaining an 89.1% success rate on short-horizon LIBERO-PRO tasks and more than twice the mean success rate of ASPIRE on LIBERO-PRO Long and LIBERO-Plus. It also outperforms ASPIRE and $π_{0.5}$ on three challenging long-horizon real-robot tasks requiring precise manipulation. We further show that the knowledge base transfers across simulators and embodiments, and that program search performance scales with its size. Project page: https://roboauto-ai.github.io/
2610.36533.tldr_en: This work introduces RoboAuto, a framework for robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels through three components and shows that the knowledge base transfers across simulators and embodiments, and that program search performance scales with its size.

llm.title_ja: RoboAuto：マルチレベルの物理的理解を通じた自律型ロボットプログラム探索
llm.tldr_ja: RoboAutoは、オブジェクト、シーン、インタラクションレベルで物理的理解を組織化するロボットプログラム探索フレームワークであり、多様なベンチマークで高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 既存の手法はプログラムの洗練を実行フィードバックのみに依存しており、物理的理解（アフォーダンスや幾何学的制約）が不足している。
llm.method: 階層型知識ベース、シーン基盤付け、自己設計実験による多段階計画を組み合わせたRoboAutoフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROの短・長ホライゾンのタスクや高精度な実機マニュピュレーションタスクにおいて、既存手法を大きく上回る成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニュピュレーション

2610.36507.title: GRAFT: Geometry-Aware Residual Adaptation for Foundation Trackers
2610.36507.abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) provide reusable whole-body motion priors: given a kinematic reference, they generate coordinated joint commands for motion replay, teleoperation, and VLA control. However, trained primarily on flat-ground motion, BFMs lack an explicit mechanism to adapt foot placement, swing clearance, and contact timing to local terrain. Many terrain-aware BFM approaches address this limitation by retraining or fine-tuning the tracker together with perception, incurring substantial data and computation costs while coupling ordinary tracking to the perception pathway. To bridge this gap, we propose GRAFT, a geometry-aware residual adaptation framework for frozen behavior trackers. GRAFT preserves the BFM parameters and motion-reference interface, while a lightweight adapter adds terrain-conditioned corrections only to lower-body execution targets. The adapter is trained with task and foot-geometry rewards, regularized to suppress unnecessary corrections on flat ground, and distilled from privileged terrain observations to onboard depth. Because the frozen BFM already provides whole-body reference tracking and nominal locomotion, GRAFT reduces terrain learning to a focused execution-adaptation problem. We instantiate the framework on four frozen trackers and evaluate stairs, gaps, and platforms in simulation. We further validate it through real-world deployment on a Unitree G1, where the adapted SONIC tracker traverses terrain with onboard depth and unmodified references.
2610.36507.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Project page: https://graft-humanoid.github.io/
2610.36507.tldr_en: GRAFT is proposed, a geometry-aware residual adaptation framework for frozen behavior trackers that preserves the BFM parameters and motion-reference interface, while a lightweight adapter adds terrain-conditioned corrections only to lower-body execution targets.

llm.title_ja: GRAFT: 基礎トラッカーのための幾何学を考慮した残差適応フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: GRAFTは、凍結された振る舞いトラッカーのパラメータと動作基準インターフェースを維持しつつ、軽量なアダプターで下半身の実行目標に対してのみ地形に応じた補正を追加する、幾何学を考慮した残差適応フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 平地での動作訓練が主であるヒューマノイドの振る舞い基盤モデルは、局所的な地形への足場やクリアランスの適応機構を欠いている。
llm.method: 凍結したBFMのパラメータを維持し、軽量なアダプターで下半身の実行目標に地形条件付きの補正を追加する。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの階段、隙間、プラットフォームの踏破に加え、Unitree G1の実機デプロイでも車載深度を用いて地形を移動できることを実証した。

2610.36454.title: SVIn+: Multi-Modal Framework for Robust Underwater State Estimation using 3D Sonar, Visual-Inertial, Water-Pressure, and DVL
2610.36454.abstract: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. A fundamental challenge in any autonomous underwater operation, from control to safe navigation and mapping, is state estimation; a notorious hard problem to address, especially in low visibility conditions. In this paper, we tackle this problem, by presenting SVIn+, a multi-sensor framework for robust state estimation of AUVs equipped with an IMU, cameras, a water-pressure sensor, a Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), and a compact 3D sonar. This framework extends an established open-source state-of-the-art visual-inertial SLAM, SVIn, by integrating water-pressure and DVL measurements into a tightly-coupled nonlinear optimiza- tion formulation resulting in improved estimates. To leverage the structural information of recently available 3D acoustic sonars while maintaining computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical architecture that incorporates estimates from a decoupled front-end via KISS-ICP, treated as relative pose factors within the factor graph. The proposed framework is validated through field deployments in a shipwreck and coral reef, demonstrating drift mitigation and global consistency. To support further research in underwater multi-modal fusion, the code and the datasets can be found on project website https://cmburgul.github.io/projects/svin+/ https://dartmouthrobotics.github.io/svin-plus

llm.title_ja: SVIn+：3Dソナー、視覚慣性、水圧、DVLを用いたロバストな水中状態推定のためのマルチモーダルフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 低視認性環境における自律型水中車両（AUV）の状態推定は非常に困難な問題である点。
llm.method: IMU、カメラ、水圧計、DVL、3Dソナーを統合し、水圧とDVLを密結合の非線形最適化に組み込むとともに、KISS-ICPを用いた階層的アーキテクチャを導入する。
llm.result: 沈没船やサンゴ礁でのフィールド展開により、ドリフトの軽減と大域的整合性の維持が実証された。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2610.36453.title: Correction or Manipulation? Measuring Epistemic Vigilance in LLM Agents Under User Pressure
2610.36453.abstract: LLM agents that answer questions and act on behalf of users must decide when to yield to a user who disagrees. Disagreement may correct a genuine error or may be an attempt at manipulation. Prior work shows that models frequently abandon correct answers when challenged by users, yet it remains unclear whether they distinguish correction from manipulation or merely differ in their propensity to concede. We examine this question across seven LLMs from four vendors in two studies, one on the answers agents give and one on the actions they take as customer-support agents whose policy permits account changes only for verified users. Simulated users push toward correct and incorrect answers with graded pressure. Following research on epistemic vigilance, the pressure either appeals to the source, such as claimed authority, or offers content the agent cannot verify, namely a cited source. Drawing on signal detection theory, we measure on a set of benchmark questions how much more readily each agent concedes to correction than to manipulation, separately from its overall propensity to concede. Citations made five of seven models readier to concede and four worse at discriminating, while stronger wording added little. In the agentic study, five models never violated the verification policy, including models that readily abandoned correct answers, so concession on answers did not predict violations of policy. Ministral 3B violated the policy mainly under claimed authority, and Ministral 8B reported changes it had not made. An instruction to revise only on verifiable evidence chiefly shifted propensity to concede rather than improving discrimination. Concession rates alone are therefore misleading, and agents should be evaluated on both their discrimination and the actions they take.
2610.36453.comment: 20 pages, 7 figures, 11 tables. 8-page main paper with supplementary material included as an appendix. Under review
2610.36453.tldr_en: Drawing on signal detection theory, this work measures on a set of benchmark questions how much more readily each LLM concedes to correction than to manipulation, separately from its overall propensity to concede.

llm.title_ja: 修正か操作か：ユーザーからの圧力下におけるLLMエージェントの認識的警戒心の測定
llm.tldr_ja: 信号検出理論に基づき、各LLMが全体の譲歩性向とは別に、修正と操作に対してどれほど容易に譲歩するかをベンチマークの質問セットで測定した。
llm.problem: LLMエージェントが、意見の異なるユーザーに従うべきか（修正）否か（操作）をどのように識別しているか不明確である。
llm.method: 7つのLLMを対象に、検証ポリシーに関するカスタマーサポートエージェントの行動および質問への回答に関する2つの研究を実施し、信号検出理論を用いて分析した。
llm.result: 引用の提示により5つのモデルが譲歩しやすくなり、4つのモデルで識別能力が低下した一方、検証ポリシーの違反は見られないモデルも存在した。

2610.36452.title: Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Stochastic Motion Tokenization
2610.36452.abstract: While velocity-commanded RL policies are effective for controlling quadrupeds, they are a limited interface for humanoids that need to perform complex whole-body motions. Furthermore, RL tracking policies for whole-body motions typically have limited information about the desired future motion, preventing them from performing controlled deviations to achieve long-term task success; such information is particularly relevant when a controller must prepare for transitions between behaviors. We address these challenges using concise motion representations that can be generated by a high-level controller, given a behavior label or text command. These representations can be fed directly into a tracking policy to provide a detailed motion reference. Our method exhibits a high degree of flexibility in performing real-world robot motions such as dancing, fighting, or walking based on conditional information. At matched capacity, our adopted stochastic motion tokenizer reconstructs motions from the Unitree G1 at a level that exceeds state-of-the-art approaches such as finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and the vector-quantized autoencoder (VQ-VAE). The resulting discrete interface conditions whole-body tracking policies that execute generated dance, fight, and walk motions lasting 16.8 s each and a 35 s fight-to-dance sequence on a physical Unitree G1.
2610.36452.comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids 2026). (c) 2026 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses
2610.36452.tldr_en: The adopted stochastic motion tokenizer reconstructs motions from the Unitree G1 at a level that exceeds state-of-the-art approaches such as finite scalar quantization and the vector-quantized autoencoder and the VQ-VAE.

llm.title_ja: 確率的動作トークン化による全身ヒューマノイド制御
llm.tldr_ja: 採用された確率的動作トークナイザーは、Unitree G1の動作をFSQやVQ-VAEなどの最先端アプローチを超えるレベルで再構築し、離散インターフェースが全身追従ポリシーを条件付ける。
llm.problem: 速度指令型強化学習ポリシーは複雑な全身動作を行うヒューマノイドの制御インターフェースとして限定的であり、将来の動作情報も不足している。
llm.method: 高レベルコントローラーが生成できる簡潔な動作表現を用い、それをトラッキングポリシーに直接入力して詳細な動作基準を提供する。
llm.result: Unitree G1の実機上で、生成されたダンス、戦闘、歩行動作（各16.8秒）および35秒の戦闘からダンスへのシーケンスを実行した。

2610.36450.title: Ground Sample Distance Constrained k-Coverage Viewpoint Planning via Set Multi-Cover Formulation
2610.36450.abstract: Drone-based 3D reconstruction and inspection require viewpoints that satisfy image-quality constraints while observing each surface region multiple times, which overlap-based planning heuristics do not guarantee. We study ground sample distance (GSD)-constrained $k$-coverage viewpoint selection for structures represented by surface voxels. Candidate viewpoints are generated along outward surface directions, screened with distance, viewing-angle, field-of-view, and occlusion tests, and augmented for voxels with insufficient visibility. Selection is then posed as set multi-cover with per-voxel coverage demands. We propose a dynamically weighted greedy heuristic that prioritizes remaining coverage deficits and scarce viewing alternatives, and compare it with sequential overlap-based pruning and an integer linear programming (ILP) formulation on the same candidate pools. Across two structures, four voxel resolutions, and three coverage requirements, the proposed approach achieves full or near-full $k$-coverage with compact viewpoint sets, using only 3.00--16.39\% more viewpoints than ILP while offering an interpretable selection process based on coverage deficits and viewpoint availability.
2610.36450.tldr_en: This work proposes a dynamically weighted greedy heuristic that prioritizes remaining coverage deficits and scarce viewing alternatives, and compares it with sequential overlap-based pruning and an integer linear programming (ILP) formulation on the same candidate pools.

llm.title_ja: 地上サンプル距離制約付きkカバレッジ視点計画：集合マルチカバー定式化による手法
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は残りのカバレッジ不足と希少な視点選択肢を優先する動的重み付き貪欲ヒューリスティックを提案し、整数線形計画法と比較した。
llm.problem: ドローンによる3D再構築や検査では画質制約を満たしつつ表面領域を複数回観測する視点が必要だが、重複ベースの計画ヒューリスティックでは保証されない。
llm.method: 表面ボクセルで表現された構造体に対し、距離、視野角、遮蔽テスト等でスクリーニングした候補視点から、集合マルチカバー問題として定式化する。
llm.result: 2つの構造体、4つのボクセル解像度、3つのカバレッジ要件において、ILPよりもわずか3.00〜16.39%多い視点数で、完全またはほぼ完全なkカバレッジを達成した。

2610.36430.title: A Singularity Avoiding Track Model for Race Car Optimization
2610.36430.abstract: A track fitting pipeline is presented that converts a measured racetrack point cloud into a closed, $C^4$ differentiable, three-dimensional surface model suitable for high-fidelity Modelica race-car optimization. The surface is a Monge patch, parametrised by a curvilinear arc-length coordinate measured along the minimum-curvature line (MCL) and a signed lateral offset, with a height polynomial of user-selectable degree capturing the cross-sectional elevation profile. The choice of MCL as the reference line is deliberate since anchoring the same surface on the geometric centre-line can cause adjacent normals to cross inside the drivable region on tight corners. The resulting non-injective parametrisation assigns multiple curvilinear addresses to the same three-dimensional point and returns invalid road geometry. The MCL is obtained from a quadratic program that minimises integrated curvature subject to track-boundary, periodicity, and jerk-regularisation constraints. By reducing total curvature while remaining within the track bounds, the MCL moves the region of parametrisation breakdown outside the drivable strip on all circuits studied, keeps the normal map injective across the full track width, and yields a more linear time-to-arc-length transformation for minimum lap-time problems. The fitted surface and the associated track widths are exported as periodic piecewise-quintic $C^4$ B-splines, solved as a nonlinear program.

llm.title_ja: レースカー最適化のための特異点回避トラックモデル
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: サーキットの幾何学的中心線を基準にすると、急カーブで法線が交差し無効な道路ジオメトリやパラメータ化の破綻が生じる点。
llm.method: 最小曲率線（MCL）を基準線として採用し、積分曲率を最小化する二次計画法を用いてトラック表面モデルを構築するパイプラインを提案する。
llm.result: すべての調査サーキットにおいてパラメータ化の破綻領域を走行可能領域外に移動させ、全幅にわたって法線写像の単射性を維持することに成功した。

2610.36420.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
2610.36420.abstract: Low-cost arms such as the SO-101 have become the most common entry point to robot learning, yet no released policy performs spatially constrained, language-conditioned tasks on them out of the box, and existing SO-101 benchmarks run only on physical hardware with simple tasks and few held-out objects. We introduce SO-101 Bench, a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a real SO-101 setup. It has four tasks scored as five families, 138 objects in seen, unseen-instance and unseen-class splits, 916 evaluation episodes with subsets for held-out appearances, rotate-to-fit planning and occlusion memory, and 3,629 simulated demonstrations on which every learned policy is fine-tuned under an equal compute budget. The twin ranks policies as the real robot does: five policies trained without real data, four VLAs and an LLM agent, keep their exact ranking when the same weights run on the physical arm in an unseen environment with unseen objects (Spearman rho = 1.00, MMRV = 0.000), although simulation overestimates success. Across nine VLAs and world-action models, the best learned policies score near 61%, with spatial placement, unseen object classes and rotate-to-fit planning remaining open. An LLM agent that writes code and hands grasping to a learned policy scores 83.2%, and an ablation shows that this lead comes from the choice of harness and the choice of language model.
2610.36420.tldr_en: SO-101 Bench is introduced, a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a real SO-101 setup, and across nine VLAs and world-action models, the best learned policies score near 61%, with spatial placement, unseen object classes and rotate-to-fit planning remaining open.
2610.36420.hf_summary_en: A simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation on low-cost robot arms reveals that hybrid LLM agents outperform learned vision-language-action policies, with ranking consistency between simulation and real hardware.

llm.title_ja: SO-101 Bench：アクセシブルな空間マニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: SO-101 Benchは実際のSO-101セットアップのIsaac Labデジタルツイン上に構築された言語条件付き空間マニピュレーション用のシミュレーションベンチマークであり、最良の学習済みポリシーは61%近いスコアを記録した。
llm.problem: 低コストアームであるSO-101向けの既存ベンチマークは物理ハードウェア上でのみ動作し、空間制約や言語条件付きタスクをそのまま実行できるポリシーが存在しない。
llm.method: Isaac Labを用いたデジタルツイン上に、4つのタスクと138個のオブジェクトを含むシミュレーションベンチマークを構築し評価を行う。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの順位が実機環境と完全に一致し（Spearman rho = 1.00）、コードを記述するLLMエージェントは83.2%のスコアを達成した。
llm.limitation: シミュレーションは実機の成功率を過大評価する傾向がある

2610.36407.title: A 2-DOF MultiBody Track Joint for Race Car Optimization
2610.36407.abstract: TrackJoint is a Modelica MultiBody component that turns a three-dimensional road surface into a joint with two degrees of freedom. The two joint coordinates are the distance travelled along a reference line and the sideways offset from that line. Together they give the position, orientation and angular velocity of a single frame_b connector. All road geometry reaches the joint as a small set of periodic piecewise-quintic splines, so one component can represent any circuit whose splines have been fitted beforehand. The road constraint is closed with d'Alembert's principle. The two generalized forces that belong to the joint coordinates are set to zero, so no Lagrange multipliers are needed. The joint is connected to a multibody race car in Dymola and the pair is exported as one FMI~3.0 FMU. The same FMU is then used for time-domain simulation and for CasADi/IPOPT minimum lap-time optimization, with no change to the model in between. This works because the joint keeps the arc-length coordinate as a real state and publishes its time derivative, which is the quantity that lets the problem be rewritten with distance We report results for minimum lap time simulations on the Singapore Formula~1 circuit.

llm.title_ja: レースカー最適化のための2自由度マルチボディトラックジョイント
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 3次元道路表面をマルチボディシミュレーションや最適化において効率的かつラグランジュ乗数なしで表現することの難しさ。
llm.method: 基準線沿いの移動距離と側方オフセットを2自由度座標とするModelicaマルチボディコンポーネント「TrackJoint」を開発し、FMI 3.0 FMUとしてエクスポートする。
llm.result: シンガポールF1サーキットでの最小ラップタイムシミュレーションにおいて、時間領域シミュレーションと最適化に同じモデルをそのまま適用できることを示した。
keywords_ja: マルチボディダイナミクス

2610.36374.title: HIDRA: Hierarchical Dual-Routing Attention for Replay-Free Lifelong Imitation Learning
2610.36374.abstract: Robotic agents operating in real-world environments must adapt continuously from a stream of multimodal demonstrations, often under constraints that preclude storing or revisiting past data. In this replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning setting, sequential updates can progressively distort the representation space, making expert-based approaches particularly sensitive to routing interference, causing expert selection to degrade over time. We propose HIDRA, a structured routing framework that mitigates this issue through a hierarchical dual-attention mechanism, which decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement. To further stabilize routing under representation drift, HIDRA introduces a key-level geometric regularization that enforces both alignment within tasks and separation across tasks. The resulting approach enables reliable expert selection while supporting an expandable set of experts for continual adaptation. We evaluate HIDRA on several LIBERO benchmark suites, including more challenging variants with heterogeneous task sequences and paraphrased language instructions. Our approach consistently outperforms both replay-free and replay-based baselines, improving AUC and forward transfer while maintaining low forgetting, with stronger gains under high interference and language variation. The code is available at: https://github.com/yfqi/HIDRA.
2610.36374.comment: This is the authors' preprint, accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Conference. The final version is available in the NeurIPS 2026 proceedings
2610.36374.tldr_en: This work proposes HIDRA, a structured routing framework that mitigates this issue through a hierarchical dual-attention mechanism, which decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement, and introduces a key-level geometric regularization that enforces both alignment within tasks and separation across tasks.

llm.title_ja: HIDRA：リプレイを必要としない生涯模倣学習のための階層型デュアルルーティングアテンション
llm.tldr_ja: HIDRAは、命令レベルのエキスパート検索と文脈依存の精緻化を分離する階層型デュアルアテンション機構と、タスク内の整合性とタスク間の分離を強制する幾何学的正則化を導入する。
llm.problem: 過去のデータの保存や再訪問ができないリプレイフリーの生涯模倣学習では、逐次的な更新が表現空間を歪め、ルーティング干渉を引き起こす。
llm.method: 階層型デュアルアテンション機構とキーレベルの幾何学的正則化を組み合わせた構造化ルーティングフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: LIBEROベンチマークスイートにおいて、リプレイフリーおよびリプレイありのベースラインの双方を一貫して上回り、低い忘却率でAUCと前方転移を改善した。

2610.36341.title: Executable Archaeology of Programs That Model Programming: Reanimating the Heuristic Compiler (1961) and KBEmacs (1984)
2610.36341.abstract: Early AI programs were often also theories of how people think, and programs that wrote programs were, in part, theories of how people program. Here we report on the reanimation of two such programs that offer two seemingly different theories of programming and were developed for quite different purposes. The first, Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler (1961), was an experimental model of programming as problem-solving, applying the means-ends analysis methods of the General Problem Solver to investigate the nature of the programming task. The second, KBEmacs (1984), was a working prototype of an intelligent programming assistant developed by MIT's Programmer's Apprentice project, built on the view that expert programmers recognize and combine familiar patterns, or "cliches." It let a programmer build up programs by combining cliches through a stylized English command language. We approach both through the methodology of Executable Archaeology, the study of historical computational systems by running their original code, a process we call "reanimation." Our reanimation of the Heuristic Compiler reproduces the compiled code appearing in Simon's 1963 paper, and our reanimation of KBEmacs reproduces the SQRT sequence of its December 1984 self-test. Examined side by side, the two theories turn out to have much in common: the Heuristic Compiler also works by adapting existing routines, and Simon later argued that search alone requires a large body of programming knowledge. To highlight the reflexivity of this project, we deliberately used a modern AI-assisted programming tool, Anthropic's Claude Code (Opus 5.5), to carry out much of the detailed reanimation work, building on a significant base of existing software. The explicit, executable theories of programming that both systems embodied are largely absent from today's far more capable AI coding assistants.
2610.36341.tldr_en: The reanimation of the Heuristic Compiler reproduces the compiled code appearing in Simon's 1963 paper, and the reanimation of KBEmacs reproduces the SQRT sequence of its December 1984 self-test.

llm.title_ja: プログラムをモデル化するプログラムの実行可能考古学：発見的コンパイラ（1961）とKBEmacs（1984）の再アニメーション
llm.tldr_ja: ヒューリスティック・コンパイラの再アニメーションはサイモンの1963年の論文のコードを再現し、KBEmacsの再アニメーションは1984年の自己テストのSQRTシーケンスを再現した。
llm.problem: 初期のAIプログラムやプログラミング自動化プログラムが持つプログラミング理論や共通の側面を検証する必要がある。
llm.method: 歴史的な計算システムを実際のコードを実行して研究する「実行可能考古学（再アニメーション）」の methodology を適用した。
llm.result: ヒューリスティック・コンパイラとKBEmacsの双方を現代のAI支援ツールを用いて再アニメーション化し、既存ルーチンの適応という共通点を見出した。
keywords_ja: ヒューリスティック・コンパイラ

2610.36337.title: CRLoMTL: Conflict-Resolution through Low-rank matrices for Multi-Task Learning
2610.36337.abstract: Multi-task learning (MTL) improves model efficiency by sharing representations across related vision tasks, but it often suffers from negative transfer when task updates interfere with one another. Existing conflict-mitigation methods typically operate in gradient space, requiring explicit task-gradient manipulation and additional optimization steps. We propose Conflict-Resolution through Low-Rank Matrices for Multi-Task Learning (CRLoMTL), a parameter-efficient framework that mitigates task interference in the low-rank parameter-update space. CRLoMTL learns task-specific LoRA updates through task-specific passes, where each task updates its own low-rank matrices, and integrates these updates through global shared-subspace fusion. Specifically, we introduce a shared-subspace resolver based on singular value decomposition (SVD), referred to as the SVD resolver, which extracts a common low-dimensional orthonormal basis across task adapters and projects task updates into this shared space before merging them into a single deployment-time update. The resulting update can be folded into the backbone, preserving the inference structure of the original model without additional runtime branches. Experiments with Swin Transformer backbones on PASCAL-Context, NYUD-v2, and CelebA show that CRLoMTL achieves a favorable accuracy-parameter trade-off, improving over single-task baselines by up to 2.77% on PASCAL-Context, 5.03% on NYUD-v2, and 3.50% on CelebA, while training only a small fraction of the parameters used by single-task models.
2610.36337.comment: Accepted at the British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC 2026)
2610.36337.tldr_en: A shared-subspace resolver based on singular value decomposition (SVD), referred to as the SVD resolver, is introduced, which extracts a common low-dimensional orthonormal basis across task adapters and projects task updates into this shared space before merging them into a single deployment-time update.

llm.title_ja: CRLoMTL：マルチタスク学習のための低ランク行列を通じた競合解決
llm.tldr_ja: 特異値分解（SVD）に基づく共有部分空間リゾルバーを導入し、タスクアダプター間で共通の低次元基底を抽出してタスク更新を射影してから単一の更新に統合する。
llm.problem: マルチタスク学習は視覚タスク間で表現を共有することで効率を高めるが、タスクの更新が干渉し合うと負の転移を引き起こす。
llm.method: 低ランクパラメータ更新空間においてタスク干渉を軽減するパラメータ効率の良いフレームワーク（CRLoMTL）を提案し、SVDリゾルバーで統合する。
llm.result: Swin Transformerを用いたPASCAL-Contextなどの実験で、単一タスクベースラインを最大5.03%上回る精度とパラメータ効率を達成した。

2610.36312.title: SG^2SLAM: Spatial Geometry-Informed 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Monocular Outdoor Navigation
