2610.36312.abstract: Monocular outdoor navigation requires robust camera motion estimation and a dense, navigable map, where 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM serves this task through an explicit differentiable parameterization and closed-form projection. However, typically, the geometry is recovered by associating 2D pixels with 3D points, so a modular SLAM system absorbs tracking error into the map, leading to cascading degradation. To address these gaps, we present SG^2SLAM, which couples streaming spatial geometry with a ray-conditioned 3DGS kernel. Streaming spatial geometry replaces the per- frame cross-dimensional correspondence with a chunk-level metric prior that supervises tracking and mapping from one source. A ray-conditioned kernel extends each primitive with a viewing-direction subspace that senses the monocular camera viewpoints. The joint optimization over spatial geometry and poses ensures a globally consistent map and trajectory outcome. Experiments on the KITTI and Waymo Open datasets show that our SG^2SLAM surpasses the per-frame association baselines in the monocular outdoor navigation task. Code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.
2610.36312.tldr_en: SG^2SLAM is presented, which couples streaming spatial geometry with a ray-conditioned 3DGS kernel, which surpasses the per-frame association baselines in the monocular outdoor navigation task.

llm.title_ja: SG^2SLAM：単眼屋外ナビゲーションのための空間幾何学を考慮した3DガウススプラッティングSLAM
llm.tldr_ja: ストリーミング空間幾何学とレイ条件付き3DGSカーネルを結合したSG^2SLAMを提案し、単眼屋外ナビゲーションタスクにおいてフレームごとの対応付けベースラインを凌駕した。
llm.problem: モジュール式SLAMシステムは2Dピクセルと3D点の対応付けにより幾何学を復元するため、追跡誤差をマップに吸収してしまい、連鎖的な劣化を招く。
llm.method: フレームごとの対応付けをチャンクレベルのメートル法事前情報に置き換え、視線方向のサブスペースを持つレイ条件付きカーネルと結合して最適化する。
llm.result: KITTIおよびWaymoオープンデータセットを用いた実験において、単眼屋外ナビゲーションタスクで従来のフレーム単位の対応付けベースラインを上回った。

2610.36309.title: Bridging Exploration and Loss of Plasticity in On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
2610.36309.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms have been observed to lose the ability to adaptively learn from new data, a phenomenon termed Loss of Plasticity (LoP). While many metrics have been shown to correlate with it, the causal mechanisms and the geometric conditions from which it can arise have not been clearly identified. We analyze LoP in Proximal Policy Optimization with isotropic Gaussian policies, the state-of-the-art formulation for many continuous action spaces in RL. We report multiple metrics which characterize the effect that the policy standard deviation $σ$ has on LoP, and we also suggest related explanations for the effectiveness of widely adopted LoP mitigation techniques. We observe a significant effect of $σ$ on the extent of LoP, and accompany this with both theoretical and experimental supporting arguments. Our experimental validation consists of LoP benchmark evaluations against standard baselines as well as real-world policy deployment on a 7-DoF robotic arm.
2610.36309.tldr_en: This work reports multiple metrics which characterize the effect that the policy standard deviation $\sigma$ has on LoP, and suggests related explanations for the effectiveness of widely adopted LoP mitigation techniques.

llm.title_ja: オンポリシー強化学習における探索と可塑性喪失の架け橋
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシーの標準偏差σが可塑性喪失（LoP）に与える影響を特徴づける複数の指標を報告し、広く採用されているLoP緩和技術の有効性に関する説明を提案した。
llm.problem: ディープ強化学習アルゴリズムは新しいデータから適応的に学習する能力（可塑性喪失）を失うことが観測されているが、その因果メカニズムや幾何学的条件は明確になっていない。
llm.method: 連続行動空間のPPOにおける等方性ガウスポリシーを分析し、ポリシーの標準偏差σがLoPに与える影響について理論的・実験的議論を行う。
llm.result: LoPベンチマーク評価および7自由度ロボットアームを用いた実機ポリシー展開により実験的検証を行った。

2610.36289.title: Compatibility and future-proof testing for multi-agent systems
2610.36289.abstract: Independently developed autonomous agents, such as autonomous vehicles, must guarantee joint compatibility, such as safety and task-completion requirements, when they operate in a shared environment. Existing methods require a centrally designed specification, or interaction mechanism before any agent is deployed. However, such centralized design is unrealistic when agent designs are confidential to their developers, and it is not flexible enough to accommodate future agent designs. We study a bi-level structure in which a regulator coordinates developers by publishing seed agents, and each developer independently tests its agent to ensure that it is compatible with every seed-compatible agent, a property we call future-proofness. Under this structure, joint compatibility is guaranteed for any agents that are designed and tested independently, without any coordination with each other. In this work, we first formulate compatibility for general multi-agent systems and show why it is not trivially implied by seed-compatibility. We then characterize the future-proof agents as the closure of the seed and show that this closure is monotone in the seed. Finally, we study a class of executable tests that involve interaction with the seed alone, and we ask to what extent such tests can distinguish the future-proof agents.
2610.36289.tldr_en: This work forms compatibility for general multi-agent systems and shows why it is not trivially implied by seed-compatibility, and describes the future-proof agents as the closure of the seed and shows that this closure is monotone in the seed.

llm.title_ja: マルチエージェントシステムのための互換性と将来対応テスト
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は一般のマルチエージェントシステムにおける互換性を定式化し、将来対応エージェントをシードの閉包として特徴づけ、その閉包がシードに対して単調であることを示した。
llm.problem: 自動運転車などの自律エージェントが共有環境で動作する際、開発者間で設計が非公開である場合や将来の設計に対応する場合の中央集権的な事前仕様設計は現実的ではない。
llm.method: レギュレーターがシードエージェントを公開し、各開発者が独立して将来対応性をテストするという二層構造を研究する。
llm.result: シードとの相互作用を含む実行可能なテストのクラスを研究し、将来対応エージェントをどの程度区別できるかを明らかにした。

2610.36285.title: ASPEN: Adaptive Semantic Reasoning via Command Persistence Prediction for Efficient Navigation VLAs
2610.36285.abstract: Navigation vision-language-action (VLA) policies repeatedly invoke costly semantic reasoning even when the next command remains unchanged. Command reuse can reduce computation but risks missing instruction-dependent turns or stops. We introduce ASPEN, an event-triggered scheduler based on command persistence prediction: estimating whether the frozen base policy would reissue its previous command. A lightweight multimodal predictor combines temporal observations, language instructions, execution history, and cached VLA confidence. At eligible command boundaries, sufficient predicted persistence permits command reuse. Otherwise, ASPEN triggers fresh semantic reasoning from the VLA. Evaluated with frozen NaVILA on cross-dataset RxR-CE val-unseen, ASPEN reduces VLA calls by 9.5% and estimated inference time by 8.1%, including scheduling overhead. It maintains comparable navigation performance and preserves identical baseline action sequences on 92.1% of episodes.
2610.36285.tldr_en: ASEN, an event-triggered scheduler based on command persistence prediction: estimating whether the frozen base policy would reissue its previous command, is introduced, an event-triggered scheduler based on command persistence prediction that maintains comparable navigation performance and preserves identical baseline action sequences.

llm.title_ja: ASPEN：効率的なナビゲーションVLAのためのコマンド持続性予測による適応的意味推論
llm.tldr_ja: コマンド持続性予測に基づくイベント駆動型スケジューラーであるASPENを導入し、ナビゲーション性能を維持しつつベースラインの行動シーケンスを保存することを示した。
llm.problem: ナビゲーション用VLAポリシーは次の指令が変わらない場合でもコストのかかる意味推論を繰り返し実行してしまう。
llm.method: 前回のコマンドが再発行されるかを予測する軽量なマルチモーダル予測器を導入し、十分な持続性が予測された場合にコマンドを再利用する。
llm.result: RxR-CE検証セットの評価において、VLA呼び出しを9.5%、推定推論時間を8.1%削減しつつ、同等のナビゲーション性能を維持した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.36270.title: Learning Multi-Phase Robot Loco-Manipulation via Phase-Conditioned Policy Optimization
2610.36270.abstract: Complex whole-body loco-manipulation requires executing diverse maneuvers, such as crouching, grasping, and locomotion, within a single long-horizon task. While performing simple pick-and-place behaviors is well-established, scaling to complex, long-horizon tasks remains difficult. Currently, this challenge is addressed by relying on human motion data and correspondingly humanoid platforms, which limits platform independence and introduces substantial data processing overhead. Instead, we extend proximal policy optimization (PPO) to train a single policy for multi-phase tasks across diverse robotic hardware, leveraging prior task structure to shape behavior. Our method adapts PPO using a phase-conditioned critic, phase-gated reward functions, and a multi-phase reset curriculum to guide exploration. To support varied hardware, we employ a decoupled hierarchical control architecture that separates lower-level balancing dynamics from high-level phase execution. We demonstrate multi-stage loco-manipulation skills on hardware on both the Unitree G1 and a Boston Dynamics Spot equipped with a manipulator arm, and validate our design choices through ablations. Our approach enables the acquisition of complex loco-manipulation behaviors purely through environment interaction while directly incorporating high-level task structure into policy learning.
2610.36270.tldr_en: This work extends proximal policy optimization (PPO) to train a single policy for multi-phase tasks across diverse robotic hardware, leveraging prior task structure to shape behavior and directly incorporating high-level task structure into policy learning.

llm.title_ja: フェーズ条件付きポリシー最適化による多段階ロボット移動・マニピュレーションの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究はPPOを拡張して多様なロボットハードウェア向けの多段階タスク用単一ポリシーを訓練し、高レベルのタスク構造をポリシー学習に直接組み込んだ。
llm.problem: 複雑な全身の移動・マニピュレーションは人間のモーションデータや特定のヒューマノイドプラットフォームに依存しており、プラットフォームの独立性が制限される。
llm.method: フェーズ条件付きクリティカル、フェーズゲート報酬関数、多段階リセットカリキュラムを用いてPPOを適応させ、低レベルの動力学と高レベルのフェーズ実行を分離する。
llm.result: Unitree G1とマニピュレーター付きBoston Dynamics Spotの実機上で多段階の移動・マニピュレーションスキルを実証した。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション

2610.36250.title: cuArms: GPU-Accelerated Conflict-Based Planning for Multi-Arm Manipulation
2610.36250.abstract: Multi-arm manipulation has the potential to dramatically improve the throughput, efficiency, and dexterity of many manipulation tasks. Recent work coordinates multiple robot arms in a shared workcell by allocating and scheduling tasks for greater parallelism, jointly planning multi-arm motions, or directly learning multi-arm policies. So far, these approaches are either too slow, rely on domain-specific assumptions, or scale poorly with the number of robots and task horizon. Thus, we introduce cuArms, a conflict-based planner co-designed with GPU parallelism that efficiently decomposes the search space using reusable multi-modal roadmaps for individual robots and resolves conflicts and deadlocks through a lazy search. To jointly optimize task assignment, schedules, motions, and manipulation skills, we integrate a high-level scheduler that proposes candidate skeletons for cuArms to ground into coordinated manipulation plans. Experimental results show that our method establishes a new state of the art, with real-time initial solutions and anytime improvements in both motion quality and scheduling, without days of domain-specific training required by learning approaches. Videos of both simulated and real-world industrial tasks are available on https://cuarms.github.io/.
2610.36250.tldr_en: This work introduces cuArms, a conflict-based planner co-designed with GPU parallelism that efficiently decomposes the search space using reusable multi-modal roadmaps for individual robots and resolves conflicts and deadlocks through a lazy search.

llm.title_ja: cuArms：マルチアームマニピュレーションのためのGPU加速競合ベース計画
llm.tldr_ja: GPU並列処理と共同設計された競合ベースのプランナーであるcuArmsを導入し、再利用可能なマルチモーダルロードマップで探索空間を効率的に分解して競合やデッドロックを解決する。
llm.problem: マルチアームマニピュレーションの既存手法は処理が遅すぎるか、ドメイン固有の仮定に依存しているか、ロボットの数やタスクホライズンに対してスケーラブルではない。
llm.method: 個別のロボット用ロードマップによる探索空間の分解と、遅延探索による競合・デッドロック解決をGPU並列処理で行うプランナーを導入する。
llm.result: ドメイン固有の数日間の訓練を必要とせず、リアルタイムな初期解とモーション品質・スケジューリングの双方で新たな状態を確立した。
keywords_ja: マルチアームマニピュレーション
モーションプランニング

2610.36143.title: Program-Level Adversarial Co-Adaptive Self-Play for Robotic Security
2610.36143.abstract: Coding agents can adapt robotic software by revising executable programs, but successful responses to an evolving opponent may not remain effective. We present a framework for program-level adversarial co-adaptive self-play in which coding agents generate attacks and defenses from tested opponent code and mission feedback, without model fine-tuning. Environment-specific interfaces support external programs for autonomous driving and SDK-level defenses for humanoid locomotion. Two eight-generation case studies reveal concrete software responses: a driving defender introduces direct-actuation recovery, while a humanoid defender revises incoming-state validation. These responses provide local task recovery but do not establish sustained robustness. The framework makes such adaptation and limitations observable through executable artifacts and task-level evidence.
2610.36143.tldr_en: A framework for program-level adversarial co-adaptive self-play in which coding agents generate attacks and defenses from tested opponent code and mission feedback, without model fine-tuning is presented.

llm.title_ja: ロボットセキュリティのためのプログラムレベル敵対的共同適応セルフプレー
llm.tldr_ja: モデルの微調整なしで、コーディングエージェントがテストされた対戦相手のコードとミッションのフィードバックから攻撃と防御を生成するフレームワークを提示した。
llm.problem: コーディングエージェントはプログラムを修正してロボットソフトウェアに適応できるが、進化する対戦相手への成功した応答が有効であり続けるとは限らない。
llm.method: 自動運転用の外部プログラムやヒューマノイド移動用のSDKレベルの防御をサポートする環境固有のインターフェースを用いたセルフプレーフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 2つの8世代にわたるケーススタディを通じて、駆動側ディフェンダーの直接作動回復やヒューマノイド側の入力状態検証などの具体的なソフトウェア応答を明らかにした。
llm.limitation: 局所的なタスク回復は提供するが、持続的な堅牢性は確立しない
keywords_ja: コーディングエージェント
ロボットセキュリティ

2610.36079.title: Closed-Loop Aware Planning via Imitation-Free Speed Scoring for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
2610.36079.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. We realize this paradigm as Closed-Loop Aware Planning for Autonomous Driving (CLAP-AD), a plug-in planning head that integrates with existing end-to-end driving models and, to our knowledge, is the first to enable explicit test-time control over their speed selection without speed-conditioned training. On Bench2Drive-Speed, CLAP-AD sets a new state of the art Speed-Adherence Score of 82.53, topping TFv6, the strongest baseline on this metric, by 12.9 points while retaining strong closed-loop driving performance. On Bench2Drive, it improves driving score by +28.5 and +32.7 over UniAD and VAD, and on NAVSIM v2, built on real-world driving data, EPDMS by +6.1 over its backbone. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io
2610.36079.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. 17 pages (8-page main paper, references, and supplementary material), 5 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io. \c{opyright} 2027 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses, in any current or future media
2610.36079.tldr_en: Closed-Loop Aware Planning for Autonomous Driving (CLAP-AD), a plug-in planning head that integrates with existing end-to-end driving models and is the first to enable explicit test-time control over their speed selection without speed-conditioned training, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: エンドツーエンド自動運転のための模倣フリー速度スコアリングを用いた閉ループ考慮型計画
llm.tldr_ja: 既存のエンドツーエンドの運転モデルと統合し、速度条件付き訓練なしで速度選択に対するテスト時の明示的制御を可能にする最初のプラグイン計画ヘッドであるCLAP-ADを導入した。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンド自動運転はオープンループの模倣学習に依存しており、単一の行動しか示さないためテスト時にユーザーの好みに適応できず、デモのノイズにより信頼性の低い監督となる。
llm.method: 物理的に接地された安全制約によって監督された学習済み関数を用いて複数基準にわたる候補速度をスコアリングしつつ、模倣によって経路を学習する計画パラダイム（CLAP-AD）を導入する。
llm.result: Bench2Drive-Speedで82.53の速度遵守スコアを記録して新記録を打ち立て、Bench2DriveやNAVSIM v2でも駆動性能を向上させた。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.36077.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
2610.36077.abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.
2610.36077.tldr_en: The Trinity is introduced, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver, which introduces Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer.
2610.36077.hf_summary_en: The Trinity framework recursively improves multimodal agents by organizing tasks into a capability tree, generating simulated training worlds, and routing specialized harness modules to boost performance on diverse benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: The Trinity：マルチモーダルエージェントのための能力駆動型再帰的自己改善
llm.tldr_ja: Creator、Explorer、Evolverの3つの役割を通じて世界生成とHarness進化を結合する再帰的自己改善フレームワークであるThe Trinityを導入した。
llm.problem: 異種で検証可能な環境の構築にはコストがかかり、手動でのHarnessイテレーションはタスクの多様性と複雑さの増大に追いつかない。
llm.method: 共通の要件に基づいてタスクツリーを階層的能力ツリーに再編成し、簡素化されたシミュレーション環境での能力学習と検証を行うCapability-Driven Real2Sim2Realを導入する。
llm.result: 進化したHarnessesにより、28の訓練用ベンチマークで平均34ポイント、18の未訓練ベンチマークで26ポイントの性能向上の達成を示した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルエージェント

2610.36068.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
2610.36068.abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. We build a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement. We term the world-model side of this cycle test-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweight LoRA pipeline. Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show that Rollback improves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training. Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level, Rollback surpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.
2610.36068.tldr_en: This work introduces Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines, and builds a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle.
2610.36068.hf_summary_en: Rollback improves robot policies by using world models to rewind to past decisions, explore counterfactual actions, and generate fine-grained supervision, while continuously refining dynamics via real-world feedback.

llm.title_ja: Rollback：ポリシー改善のための世界モデルにおける経験バックトラッキング
llm.tldr_ja: 世界モデルを受動的なシミュレーターから反事実的エンジンへと転換するポリシー改善パラダイムであるRollbackを導入し、分散型世界モデル探索と非同期実機実行を統合した。
llm.problem: 既存の世界モデルベースの手法は世界モデルを物理環境の順方向の代用品としてのみ扱い、過去の決定ポイントへの巻き戻しによる反事実的未来の探索を活用していない。
llm.method: 重要な決定ポイントへロールバックして代替行動に分岐し、その結果を対比して個々の決定に成功を帰属させる。また、軽量なLoRAパイプラインでダイナミクスを補正する。
llm.result: ブロック抽出、ボール投げ、テーブルトップカーリングの実機タスクにおいて、最強のベースラインを絶対値で10.67%、11.11%、11.85%上回る成功率の向上を達成した。

2610.35862.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2610.35862.abstract: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.
2610.35862.tldr_en: FLORE is presented, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation, and across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller.

llm.title_ja: 力反応型ヒューマノイド移動・マニピュレーションの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 力反応型ヒューマノイドの移動・マニピュレーションを学習するフレームワークFLOREを提示し、力反応型ポリシーは3つの接触を伴う実機タスクにおいて80%の成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 日常の多くのタスクでは運動だけでなく接触力の制御が必要だが、ヒューマノイドでは手と全身に跨る力を協調させる必要があり、運動軌跡だけでは指定できない。
llm.method: 力センサー付きのハンドヘルドグリッパーやウェアラブルトラッカーでデモを収集し、視覚・固有受容感覚・測定されたレンチを入力に受けて行動と力指令を予測する力反応型拡散ポリシーを用いる。
llm.result: ロボット上の3つの接触を伴うタスクにおいて、同じデモで訓練された位置のみのポリシーの26.7%に対し、力反応型ポリシーは80%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション

2610.35852.title: Differentiable Contact Dynamics for Legged Locomotion: Policy Learning and Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization
2610.35852.abstract: This paper proposes a smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact and applies it to policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization for legged locomotion. The exact contact sensitivity is available in closed form but describes changes within the current contact mode, providing no first-order information toward neighboring contact modes. The proposed gradient replaces this sensitivity only in the backward pass, leaving the hard-contact forward solve unchanged and the realized rollout feasible. A central-path relaxation of the de Saxcé-corrected second-order-cone complementarity problem for Coulomb friction smooths the conditions defining the separating, clamping, and sliding modes. The relaxed sensitivity is evaluated at a point on the central path obtained by a Newton iteration initialized from the hard-contact solution. The sensitivity remains continuous through contact-mode transitions and converges to the exact sensitivity as the relaxation vanishes. Using 100,000 samples and less than 2 min of training on a desktop PC, policy learning with the proposed gradient produces a policy that transfers to hardware without fine-tuning. On hardware, the robot under a trotting policy withstands pushes and traverses debris and slippery ground. In trajectory optimization, the proposed gradient reaches contact-rich solutions missed by exact and Signorini-relaxed gradients. Project page: https://diffcontact.github.io
2610.35852.tldr_en: This paper proposes DiffContact, a smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact, and applies it to policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization for legged locomotion and reaches contact-rich solutions missed by exact and Signorini-relaxed gradients.

llm.title_ja: 脚式移動のための微分可能な接触ダイナミクス：ポリシー学習と接触暗黙的軌道最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 摩擦接触に対する滑らかな解析的勾配を提案し、それを脚式移動のポリシー学習および接触暗黙的軌道最適化に応用した。
llm.problem: 厳密な接触感度は現在の接触モード内の変化しか記述せず、隣接する接触モードへの一階情報を提供しない。
llm.method: クーロン摩擦に関する二重円錐相補性問題のセントラルパス緩和を用いて、分離、クランプ、滑りモードを定義する条件を滑らかにし、逆伝播でのみ感度を置き換える。
llm.result: 10万サンプルと2分未満の訓練により、微調整なしでハードウェアに転移可能なポリシーを生成し、トロッティングポリシーで外力に耐え、破片や滑りやすい地面を移動した。

2610.35851.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints
2610.35851.abstract: The problem of nonprehensile robotic catching is addressed using virtual nonholonomic constraints (VNHCs); the motion of the robot end-effector is designed and controlled directly in terms of the states of the object before it is caught on the surface of the end-effector. In contrast to contemporary approaches, our approach avoids the need for object trajectory prediction, and consequent time-varying robot trajectory generation. With a focus on the planar case, we demonstrate that our VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant. Moreover, the VNHC function depends only on the desired catching height, and the same VNHC can be used for a range of initial conditions. We use model predictive control (MPC) to bring the object and end-effector to rest at a desired location after contact is made. The approach is validated in simulation.
2610.35851.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures; an abridged version of this article has been submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference (ACC)
2610.35851.tldr_en: It is demonstrated that the VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant.

llm.title_ja: 仮想拘束を用いた非把持型ロボットキャッチング
llm.tldr_ja: 仮想非ホロノミック拘束（VNHC）アプローチを使い、対象物の軌道予測を行わずに、接触瞬間の相対法線速度を最小限に抑えて所望の高さでオブジェクトをキャッチできることがシミュレーションで実証された。
llm.problem: 従来のロボットキャッチング手法は対象物の軌道予測や時間変化する軌道生成が必要であること。
llm.method: 仮想非ホロノミック拘束（VNHC）を用いてエンドエフェクターの動きをオブジェクトの状態から直接設計・制御し、接触後はモデル予測制御（MPC）を使用する。
llm.result: 所望の高さでオブジェクトを最小の相対法線速度でキャッチでき、同じVNHCを多様な初期条件に適用可能であることをシミュレーションで実証した。
llm.limitation: シミュレーションでの検証にとどまっている点。

2610.35850.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
2610.35850.abstract: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. To reduce the denoising steps while enabling real-time action generation, we present an effective world action model with one-step action generation, namely OSWAM, for autonomous driving and embodied control. We argue that it is the absence of structured action priors in random noise initialization that forces direct-policy WAMs to recover coherent action sequences through iterative denoising. Hence, we construct imagination tokens to initialize the diffusion process, providing physical priors and action-conditioned representations. We further introduce privileged information distillation with future conditioning to enhance future-aware action generation. As a result, OSWAM can efficiently and effectively generate high quality actions in just one diffusion step. Our experiments demonstrate that OSWAM achieves comparable or even better results in both autonomous driving and embodied control than direct-policy WAM and Joint-WAM that require tens of steps. It obtains approximately $3\times$ speedup over direct-policy WAM baselines and supports real-time compiled inference with latency as low as 40ms on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU. The project page is available at https://gwenzhang.github.io/OSWAM/
2610.35850.tldr_en: This work argues that it is the absence of structured action priors in random noise initialization that forces direct-policy WAMs to recover coherent action sequences through iterative denoising, and constructs imagination tokens to initialize the diffusion process, providing physical priors and action-conditioned representations.

llm.title_ja: OSWAM：1ステップアクション生成による効果的なワールドアクションモデル
llm.tldr_ja: 拡散プロセスの初期化にイマジネーション・トークンを使用し、将来条件付きの特権情報蒸留を導入することで、わずか1ステップの拡散で高品質なアクションを効率的に生成するOSWAMを提案した。
llm.problem: 直接方策型ワールドアクションモデル（WAM）は競合するアクション品質を達成するために数十回のデノイズステップを必要とし、大きな遅延を生じさせてリアルタイム展開を妨げていること。
llm.method: ランダムノイズ初期化における構造化されたアクション事前分布の欠如に対処するため、イマジネーション・トークンを用いて拡散プロセスを初期化し、将来条件付きの特権情報蒸留を導入する。
llm.result: 自動運転や身体性制御において従来の手法と同等以上の結果を約3倍の高速化で達成し、NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU上で40msという低遅延のリアルタイム推論をサポートする。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル

2610.35850.hf_summary_en: OSWAM enables real-time, high-quality action generation in autonomous driving and embodied control by initializing diffusion with structured imagination tokens and distilling future-conditioned privileged information into a single denoising step.

2610.35832.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
2610.35832.abstract: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can control robots without robot-specific training, but how their capabilities compare and interact with post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across manipulation demands remains to be thoroughly evaluated. In this report, we evaluate GPT-6-Astra on EBench as the core of an agent that controls a robot through an agent harness under the same visual and proprioceptive observation protocol as post-trained policies. We study two agent configurations: direct control, in which the agent generates waypoint commands directly, and harness with policy, in which it can also invoke a post-trained VLA or WAM policy for action execution. Under direct control, the agent achieves competitive overall performance relative to post-trained policies. It leads on short-horizon tasks and exhibits the least performance variation across generalization dimensions, whereas it underperforms post-trained policies on long-horizon tasks, tabletop manipulation, and high-precision contact-rich tasks. In the harness with policy, invoking a post-trained VLA or WAM combines the complementary strengths of both components, raising overall task success to the level of the strongest compared post-trained policies while substantially reducing token cost. However, performance remains below the per-task upper bound of the standalone components due to suboptimal policy invocation, fixed-instruction execution without subgoals, and grasp disruption when the agent resumes control. Overall, our study characterizes the capability boundary of a frontier MLLM agent and suggests directions for improving future agent harness design. Project page: https://internrobotics.github.io/EBench-Astra-Tech-Report/
2610.35832.tldr_en: This study characterizes the capability boundary of a frontier MLLM agent and suggests directions for improving future agent harness design.

2610.35817.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
2610.35817.abstract: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness. We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning, followed by supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach it how to move the robot. Without observing real-world robot data during training, ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness and outperforming the MolmoAct2 VLA (33.3%), while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Furthermore, ZAP also generalizes to an unseen embodiment as well as new objects, goals and strategies never seen during training. On a single-arm Franka, ZAP reaches 55.9% on RoboLab-120, 4.9 percentage points ahead of the leading VLA/WAM baseline.
2610.35817.tldr_en: This work introduces Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches this missing motion skill, entirely in simulation on simple primitive tasks and from the model's own successes, with no frontier teacher or distillation and no real-world robot data.

llm.title_ja: 事前学習は「何を」を知り、シミュレーションは「どのように」を教える：シミュレーション学習型ロボットエージェントにおける構成的汎化
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの視覚言語モデルにシンプルなツールハーネスを組み合わせ、シミュレーション環境での教師あり微調整とGRPOを行うことで、実世界データなしでロボットを制御するZAPを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットポリシーはシーン内のタスク要求（何を）とタスクを達成するためのロボットの動かし方（どのように）の両方を理解する必要があること。
llm.method: 27Bパラメータの事前学習済みモデルで世界理解と推論をブートストラップし、シンプルなシミュレーションタスクでの教師あり微調整（SFT）とGRPOを適用する。
llm.result: 実世界のロボットデータなしで実世界タスクにおいて96.7%の成功率を達成し、既存のVLAを上回りつつ、高速かつ低コストでの動作を実現した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション学習

2610.36013.title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence
2610.36013.abstract: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.
2610.36013.comment: Technical Report; 40 pages, 27 figures, 8 tables; Project Page at https://public-bots.github.io/OmniBrain-0/
2610.36013.tldr_en: OmniBrain-0 is introduced, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery.

llm.title_ja: OmniBrain-0：身体性知能のための統合型エージェントモデル
llm.tldr_ja: マニピュレーションとナビゲーションを共有の高レベル決定モデルで調整し、タスク理解や計画、進捗追跡、フィードバック駆動型のリカバリを統合する軽量な統合型身体性エージェント「OmniBrain-0」を提案した。
llm.problem: 汎用的な身体性知能には多様なスキルの長期的調整や失敗からの回復が必要だが、専門特化ポリシーや既存のマルチモーダルエージェントは信頼性や推論コストの面で課題があること。
llm.method: 身体性事前学習、ドメイン特化エージェント蒸留、マルチティーチャー方策内蒸留（MOPD）を組み合わせ、再帰的自己改善（RSI）のデータ飛輪を活用するプログレッシブトレーニングフレームワークを用いる。
llm.result: クロスドメインの高いタスク性能を、クローズドソースの教師モデルよりも大幅に低い推論・実行オーバーヘッドで達成した。

2610.36011.title: E0.5: From Reconstructive to Future-Predictive 3D Foundations for Robotic World-Action Modeling
2610.36011.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models. Even when geometric features extracted by 3D models such as VGGT are incorporated, they are typically passed into a video model or VLM that serves as the primary backbone, leaving 3D geometry as an auxiliary input or prediction target rather than the native foundation for world modeling. We present E0.5, a geometry-native world-action model built directly on 3D foundation models. E0.5 introduces two key innovations. First, it adopts a 3D foundation model as the primary backbone, making 3D geometry the native representation for both world modeling and action prediction. Second, it explicitly predicts future 3D states together with actions, enabling the model to capture geometric world dynamics beyond action-only modeling or future video prediction. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 first demonstrate the effectiveness of E0.5 without embodied-data pretraining, achieving success rates of 89.90\% and 50.09\% under clean and randomized settings, respectively. Building on these results, we further pretrain E0.5 on more than 160k robot trajectories from AgiBotWorld-Beta, jointly learning robot actions and future geometry within the pretrained 3D foundation. This embodied pretraining improves mean real-world manipulation success rates by approximately 15 and 7 percentage points on AgileX Piper and Zerith H1, respectively. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of geometry-native foundations to acquire robot interaction knowledge and transfer it to physical manipulation. E0.5 embodies this geometry-native approach as a member of the VWA family of world-action models.
2610.36011.tldr_en: E0.5 is presented, a geometry-native world-action model built directly on 3D foundation models that explicitly predicts future 3D states together with actions, enabling the model to capture geometric world dynamics beyond action-only modeling or future video prediction.

llm.title_ja: E0.5：ロボットワールドアクションモデリングに向けた再構成型から将来予測型3D基盤への展開
llm.tldr_ja: 3D基盤モデルを直接のバックボーンとし、アクションと将来の3D状態を明示的に予測することで幾何学的世界ダイナミクスを捉えるジオメトリネイティブなワールドアクションモデル「E0.5」を提案した。
llm.problem: 主流のワールドアクションモデルは依然としてビデオ基盤モデルや視覚言語モデルを中心としており、3D幾何学は補助的な入力や予測ターゲットとして扱われていること。
llm.method: 3D基盤モデルをプライマリバックボーンとして採用し、ワールドモデリングとアクション予測の双方のネイティブ表現として3D幾何学を利用し、将来の3D状態をアクションと共に予測する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0での優れた性能を示し、さらに大規模なロボット軌道データを用いた身体性事前学習により実世界マニピュレーションの成功率を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル

2610.35733.title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
2610.35733.abstract: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-conflict coefficients and derive near-optimal regret bounds for online settings using this measure, thereby quantifying the impact of misalignment on learning efficiency. Then, we design routed ensemble policy learning, an algorithm that maintains a small set of basis policies and dynamically routes trajectories to the policy with the highest potential reward. Finally, we consider trajectory selection as another approach to mitigate objective conflict, and design a kernel surrogate trajectory attribution algorithm that estimates how feedback signals from a set of trajectories influence policy learning on other trajectories. The kernel can capture nonlinear interactions such as synergy and antagonism between trajectories. We evaluate our approach across diverse environments and benchmarks: routed ensembles improve average performance by 4.3% over baselines for online environments from Meta-World and MO-Gymnasium, and kernel surrogate attribution improves correlation with leave-one-out analysis over existing baselines by 50%. When applied to trajectory selection, kernel-based attribution yields a 27% improvement in reward over baseline attribution methods.
2610.35733.comment: 30 pages. To appear at NeurIPS 2026 (extended version)
2610.35733.tldr_en: This paper introduces objective-conflict coefficients and derive near-optimal regret bounds for online settings using this measure, thereby quantifying the impact of misalignment on learning efficiency, and designs routed ensemble policy learning, an algorithm that maintains a small set of basis policies and dynamically routes trajectories to the policy with the highest potential reward.

llm.title_ja: ルーテッドアンサンブルと軌道アトリビューションを用いた多目的強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 目的間の一致度を定量化する目的競合係数を導入し、少数のベース方策を維持して軌道を動的に割り当てるルーテッドアンサンブル方策学習を設計することで多目的強化学習の学習効率を改善した。
llm.problem: 多目的強化学習において競合する目的にバランスを取る方策の学習は、目的間の競合度に依存してサンプル効率が著しく低下すること。
llm.method: 目的競合係数を定義してオンライン設定での近最適後悔境界を導出し、ベース方策の小さな集合を維持して最高報酬の方策に動的に割り当てるルーテッドアンサンブルと、軌道からのフィードバック影響を推定するカーネルサロゲートアトリビューションを設計する。
llm.result: Meta-Worldなどのオンライン環境でベースラインを上回る平均性能の向上を達成し、軌道選択における報酬を大きく改善した。

2610.35730.title: SPECOLA: A Tool for Specification Driven Robot Evaluation
2610.35730.abstract: Simulation benchmarks are a useful way to measure progress in robotics; typically they provide success rate as the dominant measure of performance. However, success rate reports only whether a rollout completed the task, hiding by what margin it succeeded, how sensitive the success is to goal parameter changes, requirements it may have violated, and whether success persisted. Signal Temporal Logic (STL) provides a formal language for capturing specifications; it can be used to define requirements, and measure how close a robot behavior is to satisfying or violating them. Using STL monitors in a simulator, however, requires exposing simulator state and mapping it to specification-relevant signals. We present Specola, a tool for evaluating robot behaviors in simulation with respect to STL specifications. Specola provides an interface for writing specifications over simulator signals, and creates and manages the relevant monitors while a policy executes. We provide a Python API and command-line interface for integrating monitoring into existing policy execution loops. We provide an adapter interface for connecting new simulators, and provide adapters for nine simulation environments and benchmarks, including LIBERO, RoboCasa, Isaac Lab, and RoboDojo. We provide case studies that illustrate the nuanced evaluation that Specola enables. Code and adapters are available at https://github.com/specola-eval/specola.
2610.35730.tldr_en: Specola is presented, a tool for evaluating robot behaviors in simulation with respect to STL specifications, and Specola provides an interface for writing specifications over simulator signals, and creates and manages the relevant monitors while a policy executes.

llm.title_ja: SPECOLA: 仕様駆動型ロボット評価のためのツール
llm.tldr_ja: Specolaを提案した。これはSTL仕様に関してシミュレーション内のロボットの振る舞いを評価するツールであり、シミュレータ信号に対する仕様の記述インターフェースを提供し、ポリシーの実行中に該当するモニターを作成および管理する。
llm.problem: シミュレーションベンチマークにおける成功率は、タスク完了の有無を示すのみで、マージンやゴールパラメータの変化に対する感度などを隠してしまうこと。
llm.method: シミュレータ信号に対する仕様の記述を可能にし、ポリシー実行中にシグナル監視を行う Specola ツールの開発。
llm.result: LIBERO、RoboCasa、Isaac Labを含む9つのシミュレーション環境向けのアダプターとPython APIを実装し、きめ細かな評価を実現した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション評価

2610.35687.title: TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains
2610.35687.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities in high-level reasoning and task planning for robots. However, specialized domains remain a challenge for VLMs' image interpretation and grounding abilities. We introduce TrySee, a modular closed-loop robot task planning pipeline integrating general-purpose VLM reasoning with domain-specific perception and established robotics components. The system consists of an inherently reactive cyclic planning pipeline, augmented with domain-specific modular vision preprocessing, to provide online grounding. Finally, a dynamic preprocessing selection mechanism contributes to the scalability of the pipeline. The system requires neither VLM fine-tuning nor end-to-end demonstrations and adapts through replaceable perception modules and motion planning. The approach is evaluated on planning tasks across 5 widely different domains, including a real-world robot disassembly task. The field tests in a brownfield environment demonstrate the approach's practicality in integrating VLM planning into specialized robotic systems with limited domain-specific training data.
2610.35687.comment: To be published in the proceedings of the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics (ROBIO)
2610.35687.tldr_en: TrySee is introduced, a modular closed-loop robot task planning pipeline integrating general-purpose VLM reasoning with domain-specific perception and established robotics components, which demonstrates the approach's practicality in integrating VLM planning into specialized robotic systems with limited domain-specific training data.

llm.title_ja: TrySee：専門ドメインにおけるクローズドループ型ロボットタスク計画のためのモジュール式知覚拡張VLMグランディング
llm.tldr_ja: 汎用VLMの推論とドメイン固有の知覚・ロボティクスコンポーネントを統合し、モジュール式のビジョン前処理を備えたクローズドループ型タスク計画パイプライン「TrySee」を提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚言語モデル（VLM）は高次元推論に優れるものの、専門ドメインにおける画像解釈やグランディング能力には課題があること。
llm.method: 動的プレプロセッシング選択メカニズムとドメイン固有のモジュール式ビジョン前処理を組み込んだ、本質的に反応的な循環型計画パイプラインを構築する。
llm.result: ドメイン固有の訓練データが限られた専門的ロボットシステムへのVLM計画の統合における実用性を、実世界の分解タスクを含む5つのドメインで実証した。

2610.35686.title: FISRF: Flexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework for Robotics Task Planning with Large Language Model
2610.35686.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely adopted for reflective error correction in task planning; however, existing approaches primarily rely on autonomous exploration, rendering them prone to accumulating erroneous experiences during early interactions with new environments. To address this limitation, we propose the Flexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework (FISRF), an agent--mentor architecture that estimates the robot's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) in task planning and adaptively selects reflection strategies and mentor guidance, thereby facilitating the accumulation of effective error-correction experience. Experiments in ALFWorld and on real-world robotic platforms demonstrate that FISRF reduces the average number of error-correction rounds by 37% and redundant reasoning by 25.1%, while improving the overall task success rate by 8%. Project webpage : https://fisrfplanning.github.io/
2610.35686.tldr_en: The Flexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework is proposed, an agent--mentor architecture that estimates the robot's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) in task planning and adaptively selects reflection strategies and mentor guidance, thereby facilitating the accumulation of effective error-correction experience.

llm.title_ja: FISRF: ロボットタスク計画のための大規模言語モデルを用いた柔軟な教育的足場架け橋反射フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: エージェント・メンター構造を持つFlexible Instructional Scaffolding Reflection Framework（FISRF）を提案した。これはタスク計画におけるロボットの「発達の近接領域（ZPD）」を推定し、反射戦略とメンター指導を適応的に選択することで効果的な誤り訂正経験の蓄積を促進する。
llm.problem: 既存のLLMを用いた反射的誤り訂正は自律的な探索に依存するため、新しい環境との初期のインタラクションにおいて誤った経験を蓄積しやすいこと。
llm.method: 発達の近接領域（ZPD）を推定し、反射戦略とメンター指導を適応的に選択するエージェント・メンター構造の導入。
llm.result: ALFWorldおよび実世界のロボットプラットフォームにおいて、平均誤り訂正ラウンド数を37%、冗長な推論を25.1%削減し、タスク成功率を8%向上させた。
keywords_ja: エージェント・メンター

2610.35670.title: Continuous-Time Safe Planning and Control for Agile Quadrupeds
2610.35670.abstract: Agile quadruped navigation in dynamic environments demands trajectories that are both dynamically feasible and provably collision-free. Most real-time planners achieve tractability through a convex reduction that requires simplified kinematic models, discarding motion that the robot can readily execute, and certify safety only at discretization points, leaving open possible inter-sample collisions with moving obstacles. We present a real-time motion planning framework that retains the fully-actuated $SE(2)$ model of a quadruped, with its anisotropic, heading-coupled velocity bounds, and accepts the resulting nonconvexity. By parameterizing trajectories as composite Bernstein polynomials, we exploit the convex hull property to certify collision avoidance and the input bounds over the entirety of each planning horizon. Solved at online replanning rates, the optimization runs in closed loop, commanding body velocities to the locomotion controller. We validate the approach in simulation against ablations and external baselines, and in hardware experiments on a quadruped navigating among unknown moving obstacles, recovering both lateral and heading-coupled motion that simplified models exclude.
2610.35670.tldr_en: This work presents a real-time motion planning framework that retains the fully-actuated $SE(2)$ model of a quadruped, with its anisotropic, heading-coupled velocity bounds, and accepts the resulting nonconvexity by parameterizing trajectories as composite Bernstein polynomials.

llm.title_ja: 高機動四足歩行ロボットのための連続時間安全計画と制御
llm.tldr_ja: 四足歩行ロボットの全駆動SE(2)モデルを維持し、複合バーンズ多項式として軌道をパラメータ化することで、計画ホライズン全体にわたる衝突回避と入力境界を証明するリアルタイム動作計画フレームワークを提示した。
llm.problem: リアルタイムプランナーの多くは、簡略化された運動学モデルを必要とする凸縮約を用いており、移動障害物とのサンプル間衝突の可能性を残すこと。
llm.method: 異方性のヘディング結合速度境界を持つ全駆動SE(2)モデルを維持し、複合バーンズ多項式を用いて軌道をパラメータ化するリアルタイム動作計画の構築。
llm.result: シミュレーションによるベースラインとの比較検証に加え、未知の移動障害物の中をナビゲートする四足歩行ロボットを用いたハードウェア実験で有効性を検証した。

2610.35659.title: Environment Edits as a Corrective Signal for Reward Learning
2610.35659.abstract: Robot corrections allow people to adjust a robot's behavior, but a single correction changes many features. Also, preferences about object attributes and relationships between objects cannot be expressed by moving the robot. We propose environment edits as a complementary form of feedback. The robot's motion is held constant as the human edits the scene, so the only explanation for the edit is the moved object. We introduce Feature Learning from Environmental and Robot-Relational Edit Traces (FERRET), which learns preferences from both robot and environment corrections. We show that environment edits are able to disambiguate features and learn preferences that robot corrections alone cannot.
2610.35659.comment: Accepted to CoRL 2026 Workshop on Learning from Corrections
2610.35659.tldr_en: It is shown that environment edits are able to disambiguate features and learn preferences that robot corrections alone cannot, andFERRET, which learns preferences from both robot and environment corrections is introduced.

llm.title_ja: 報酬学習のための補正信号としての環境編集
llm.tldr_ja: 環境編集がロボットの補正単体では学習できない特徴を明確化し、好み学習できることを示し、ロボットと環境の双方の補正から好みを学習するFERRETを導入した。
llm.problem: 1つの補正で多くの特徴が変更されてしまうことや、オブジェクトの属性や関係に関する好みがロボットを動かすだけでは表現できないこと。
llm.method: ロボットの動きを固定した状態で人間がシーンを編集し、移動したオブジェクトから特徴と好みを学習するフレームワーク（FERRET）の提案。
llm.result: 環境編集により、ロボットの補正単体では不可能な特徴の曖昧さ解消や好みの学習が可能であることを示した。

2610.35656.title: Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning
2610.35656.abstract: Standard reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms based on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) are vulnerable to sim-to-real gaps. To address this issue, distributionally robust RL algorithms based on robust MDPs (RMDPs) have been proposed, for ensuring that agents can perform reliably to unpredictable conditions in real-world environments. Despite of the rich literature, \revision{an efficient model-free method is still lacking} for robust RL, particularly for Markovian data, which is more relevant in practical applications. In this work, we take a step towards settling this problem by proposing a sample efficient (asynchronous Q-learning) algorithm for robust RL. In particular, consider a $γ$-discounted infinite-horizon RMDP with state space $\mathcal{S}$ and action space $\mathcal{A}$, where the uncertainty set is specified by the total variation (TV) distance with uncertainty level $σ$. Assuming access to a single trajectory of Markovian samples induced by a behavior policy and the nominal transition kernel, the sample complexity of the proposed Q-learning algorithm --- to achieve an entrywise $\varepsilon$-approximation of the optimal Q-function --- is bounded by $$ \frac{1}{μ_{\mathsf{min}}\varepsilon^2(1-γ)^3\max\{1-γ,σ\}} + \frac{t_{\mathsf{mix}}}{μ_{\mathsf{min}}(1-γ)} $$ up to logarithmic factors. Here, $t_{\mathsf{mix}}$ and $μ_{\mathsf{min}}$ denote the mixing time and the minimum state-action occupancy probability of the sample trajectory, respectively. This result is nearly minimax optimal, with an additional factor of $\frac{1}{1-γ}$. Moreover, it achieves a significant improvement over existing bounds.
2610.35656.tldr_en: This work takes a step towards settling the problem of model-free Q-learning for robust RL by proposing a sample efficient (asynchronous Q-learning) algorithm for robust RL.

llm.title_ja: ロバスト強化学習のための証明可能な効率的Q学習
llm.tldr_ja: ロバスト強化学習のためのサンプル効率の高い（非同期Q学習）アルゴリズムを提案し、マルコフデータに関するモデルフリー手法の課題解決に向けた一歩を踏み出した。
llm.problem: 標準的な強化学習アルゴリズムはシム・トゥ・リアルギャップに対して脆弱であり、特に実用的な応用において重要となるマルコフデータに対するロバストRLのための効率的なモデルフリー手法が不足していること。
llm.method: 全変動距離を用いて不確実性集合を特定し、単一のマルコフサンプル軌道にアクセスするサンプル効率の高い非同期Q学習アルゴリズムの提案。
llm.result: 既存のバウンドに比べて大幅な改善を達成し、ほぼミニマックス最適なサンプル複雑度を実現した。
keywords_ja: マルコフ決定プロセス

2610.35642.title: VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains
2610.35642.abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While state-of-the-art VPR and SLAM approaches excel in urban and feature-rich natural environments, the vast and feature-poor environments of extraterrestrial surfaces like on the Moon or Mars pose severe challenges for existing approaches. This paper presents a novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces. There are three contributions: (1) We collected sixteen VPR database-query datasets based on existing data from Space Analog Domains (SAD), terrestrial environments that resemble properties of the Moon or Mars. The collection includes a range of challenges regarding environment, viewpoint change, and illumination conditions. (2) To address the ill-posed nature of VPR, we propose a novel approach to generate the ground-truth information in VPR benchmarks. Instead of defining that a query and datbase image show the same place if and only if their camera poses are within fixed position and viewing direction thresholds, we propose to make the decision dependent on whether the match would be valuable in the downstream SLAM task. To avoid the overhead and restrictions of evaluating VPR in-the-loop within SLAM systems, we provide VPR ground-truth (GT) matrices based on the performance of an ensemble of state-of-the-art Relative Pose Estimators (RPE). Under this GT we require a VPR method to identify exactly those image pairs for which a subsequently applied RPE is expected to provide a valuable pose estimate in a SLAM context. (3) We evaluated nine state-of-the-art VPR approaches. The results show considerable room for improvement and indicate directions for future research. We provide a pre-release version of the dataset on github: $\texttt{https://github.com/rfechner/VPR-Space}$
2610.35642.tldr_en: A novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces is presented and VPR ground-truth matrices based on the performance of an ensemble of state-of-the-art Relative Pose Estimators (RPE) are provided.

llm.title_ja: VPR-Space: 宇宙アナログドメインにおける視覚的場所認識のためのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 宇宙アナログドメインのデータに基づく16のVPRデータベース・クエリデータセットを収集し、最先端の相対姿勢推定器のアンサンブルの性能に基づくVPRグラウンド真値行列を提供する新たなベンチマーク VPR-Space を提示した。
llm.problem: 月や火星などの地球外表面における広大で特徴の乏しい環境が、既存の視覚的場所認識（VPR）およびSLAMアプローチにとって深刻な課題となっていること。
llm.method: 宇宙アナログドメイン（SAD）からのデータに基づく16のデータセットの収集と、下流のSLAMタスクにおける有用性に基づくグラウンド真値生成のためのRPEアンサンブル手法の提案。
llm.result: 9つの最先端VPRアプローチを評価し、将来の研究に向けた改善の余地と方向性を示した。

2610.35636.title: Adapt for Planning, Not just Prediction: Optimistic Test-Time World Model Adaptation
2610.35636.abstract: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this degradation by updating the model during deployment. Unlike pre-training on fixed data, TTA for planning is closed-loop: the planner uses model rollouts to select actions, and the resulting transitions drive the next update. This raises the question: which objective should guide TTA for planning? Under a prediction-only objective, the model is fit only to the outcomes of its own actions, so it can remain wrong about the actions that would reach the goal, and low prediction error need not translate into better planning. Inspired by reward-biased maximum likelihood from adaptive control, we introduce Optimistic Test-Time Adaptation (OpTTA). Its objective has two terms, the prediction loss on observed transitions and the planner's goal-reaching cost on its candidate rollouts, both minimized over the model parameters. The planning term biases adaptation toward models that are optimistic about reaching the goal, without any additional environment interaction. Across visual and environment shifts on manipulation, reaching and navigation tasks, OpTTA raises final planning success over the frozen model by 13.5 percentage points on average, compared with 6.9 for the prediction-only objective (AdaJEPA), when only the predictor is adapted. When the encoder is adapted as well, the gains are 13.5 and 7.5 points. These experiments span three JEPA world models with different encoders and training objectives and, for temporal straightening, both CEM and gradient-based planners. Our results suggest that test-time adaptation of world models for planning benefits from an optimistic, task-aware term in addition to the prediction loss.
2610.35636.comment: Accepted at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Pretrain to Adapt
2610.35636.tldr_en: Optimistic Test-time adaptation of world models for planning benefits from an optimistic, task-aware term in addition to the prediction loss, which is inspired by reward-biased maximum likelihood from adaptive control.

llm.title_ja: 予測だけでなく計画のための適応：楽観的なテスト時世界モデル適応
llm.tldr_ja: 適応制御における報酬バイアス付き最尤法にインスパイアされ、予測損失と計画のゴール到達コストを組み合わせた楽観的テスト時適応（OpTTA）を導入した。
llm.problem: 潜在世界モデルは通常オフラインで事前学習されテスト時は固定されるため、分布のシフトによって計画性能が劣化すること。
llm.method: 観測された遷移に対する予測損失と、候補ロールアウトに対する計画のゴール到達コストの2つの項を最小化する楽観的テスト時適応（OpTTA）の導入。
llm.result: 視覚および環境のシフトを伴うタスクにおいて、予測のみの損失を用いた場合と比較して、凍結モデルに対する最終的な計画成功率を平均で大幅に向上させた。

2610.35630.title: Revisiting Direct Control: A Field Evaluation of Sensor Fusion Efficacy in Teleoperating Full-Scale Autonomous Vehicles via Bird's Eye View
2610.35630.abstract: In autonomous driving, robot teleoperation serves as a critical safety fallback mechanism, requiring operators to assume direct control in the event of system failure. While recent research has pivoted toward high-level supervisory control or simulation-based studies, these approaches often fail to capture the physical dynamics and sensory demands of driving a full-scale vehicle. To address this gap, we evaluated the impact of spatial data representation on operator performance using a real car-sized vehicle in a field experiment with $N = 18$ participants. We compared three visualization interfaces: (i) a standard camera feed baseline, with two bird's-eye views (BEV) from (ii) a raw LiDAR point cloud, and (iii) a sensor fusion of LiDAR and camera data streams. Contrary to prior passive observation studies suggesting that sensor-fusion BEV may hinder awareness, our active-control results demonstrate that such representation significantly outperforms the standard LiDAR BEV in perceived usability ($p \leq 0.0001$) and cognitive task load ($p = 0.01$, NASA-TLX score: 34.58/100) while also being significantly better than the Camera-only view ($p = 0.043$). The fused interface also led to statistically significant reductions in task completion time ($p = 0.0461$) and superior usability (SUS: 77.9/100) compared to those of the Camera-only and LiDAR-only views. By synthesizing objective performance data with comprehensive subjective assessments, we demonstrate that BEV fusion maximizes safety margins while minimizing the operator's mental demand. These findings challenge existing teleoperation conventions and provide an empirically validated approach for designing robust remote piloting systems.
2610.35630.comment: Accepted at 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
2610.35630.tldr_en: By synthesizing objective performance data with comprehensive subjective assessments, it is demonstrated that BEV fusion maximizes safety margins while minimizing the operator's mental demand and provides an empirically validated approach for designing robust remote piloting systems.

llm.title_ja: 直接制御の再検討：鳥瞰図を通じた実規模自動運転車の遠隔操作におけるセンサーフュージョンの有効性の現場評価
llm.tldr_ja: 客観的なパフォーマンスデータと主観的な評価を統合することにより、BEVフュージョンが安全マージンを最大化しつつオペレーターの精神的負担を最小限に抑えることを実証し、頑健な遠隔操縦システム設計のための検証済みアプローチを提供した。
llm.problem: 近年の研究は高レベルな監視制御やシミュレーションベースの研究に移行しているが、実車を運転する際の物理的ダイナミクスや感覚的要求を捉えきれていないこと。
llm.method: 標準カメラ、LiDAR点群の鳥瞰図（BEV）、およびLiDARとカメラのセンサーフュージョンによる3つの視覚化インターフェースを、実車を用いた18人の参加者による野外実験で比較評価する。
llm.result: フュージョンインターフェースは、ユーザビリティの向上や認知タスク負荷の軽減、タスク完了時間の有意な削減を実現した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン
ヒューマンファクター

2610.35629.title: From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes
2610.35629.abstract: This work explores a multimodal approach to the alignment of the behavior of open-ended learning autonomous robots with human purposes through the use of large language models as cultural enablers. While autonomous robots can generate their own skills and goals through interaction with the environment, they often lack mechanisms to ensure that these remain relevant and aligned to those of human users. The proposed approach makes use of the general and cultural knowledge contained in LLMs and VLMs to establish a multimodal interactive alignment process in which human purposes, expressed in natural language, are transformed into motivational components of a robot architecture in the form of robot missions and drives that guide the behavior of the robot. The system is structured into three layers for semantic alignment, mission generation, and drive modeling. This design enables a bidirectional interaction loop: human inputs define high-level purposes, robots expand them into executable missions making use of multimodal information relayed by LLMs and VLMs, and feedback maintains alignment with human intent. Experiments in simulation and with a physical robot demonstrate that the process produces valid missions and behaviors, supporting effective human-agent alignment in interactive scenarios with autonomous robots.
2610.35629.tldr_en: This work explores a multimodal approach to the alignment of the behavior of open-ended learning autonomous robots with human purposes through the use of large language models as cultural enablers, supporting effective human-agent alignment in interactive scenarios with autonomous robots.

llm.title_ja: 言語から駆動へ：自律型ロボットを人間の目的に合致させるためのマルチモーダルフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデルを文化的仲介者として利用し、自律学習型ロボットの振る舞いを人間の目目に合致させるマルチモーダルアプローチを模索し、インタラクティブなシナリオにおける効果的なヒューマン・エージェントの調和を実証した。
llm.problem: 自律ロボットは環境との相互作用を通じて独自のスキルやゴールを生成できるが、それらが人間のユーザーの目的に関連し、合致していることを保証するメカニズムを欠いていること。
llm.method: LLMおよびVLMに含まれる汎用的・文化的知識を利用し、自然言語で表現された人間の目的をロボットのミッションや駆動に変換する、意味的アライメント、ミッション生成、駆動モデリングの3層構造の構築。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機ロボットを用いた実験により、有効なミッションと振る舞いを生成し、効果的なヒューマン・エージェント調和をサポートすることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットアライメント
ヒューマン・ロボット協調

2610.35626.title: Robot-Aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Precise Reaching with Wrist-Camera VLA Policies
2610.35626.abstract: Efficient robotic data collection remains a major bottleneck for vision-language-action (VLA) policy learning, especially for tasks requiring accurate end-effector positioning and camera-action alignment. This challenge is particularly severe in electronic-waste disassembly, where robots operate in cluttered assemblies of densely packed, visually similar components. Full digital-twin simulation is difficult because many parts are thin, reflective, or mechanically complex, making accurate object-level meshes and contact models difficult to obtain. In this work, we focus on pre-contact reaching and propose a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based data generation pipeline for wrist-camera VLA adaptation. Our method reconstructs the real workspace with 3DGS and renders diverse wrist-camera observations from robot-aligned poses. These observations are paired with smooth, structured reaching trajectories to provide robot-aligned visual-action supervision for VLA fine-tuning. We further augment the VLA policy with an instruction-conditioned reach verifier that estimates target proximity and provides reliable termination before physical interaction. Experiments in motherboard disassembly demonstrate precise VLA-based reaching using wrist-camera observations alone, without an external side-view camera. With $π$0.5, 1,500 generated trajectories achieve 80.0\% precise-reaching success across three targets, compared with 58.7\% using 150 teleoperated demonstrations, while requiring less than 10 minutes of active human capture. Project website: https://001-wang.github.io/PrecisionReach-GS/
2610.35626.tldr_en: This work focuses on pre-contact reaching and proposes a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based data generation pipeline for wrist-camera VLA adaptation and augments the VLA policy with an instruction-conditioned reach verifier that estimates target proximity and provides reliable termination before physical interaction.

llm.title_ja: 手首カメラVLAポリシーによる精密把持のためのロボットアライメント済み3Dガウシアン・スプラッティング
llm.tldr_ja: プレコンタクトなリーチングに焦点を当て、3DGSベースのデータ生成パイプラインを提案するとともに、ターゲット近接度を推定して安全な停止を提供する指示条件付きリーチ検証器でVLAポリシーを拡張した。
llm.problem: 高精度なエンドエフェクタの位置決めやカメラと動作のアライメントを必要とするタスク、特に電子廃棄物の分解などにおいて、効率的なロボットデータ収集が大きなボトルネックとなっていること。
llm.method: 3Dガウシアン・スプラッティング（3DGS）を用いて現実の作業スペースを再構築し、ロボットアライメントされたポーズから多様な手首カメラの観測をレンダリングしてVLA微調整用の教師データとする手法の提案。
llm.result: マザーボード分解実験において、π0.5を用いて、わずか10分未満の能動的人間によるキャプチャで1,500の生成軌道により80.0%の精密リーチ成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 3Dガウシアン・スプラッティング

2610.35615.title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models
2610.35615.abstract: Expressive robot motion positively impacts human-robot interaction by improving user engagement, likability, or task performance. We present a novel approach to automatically generate and modulate complex, expressive full-body gesture sequences from a multimodal (text, audio, video) context description. Based on a unified mathematical implementation of the Principles of Animation using Dynamic Movement Primitives, we use multimodal foundation models to generate such sequences along with parametric motion variations that are highly context-aware. This method extends the state of the art in terms of flexibility and generality by being interpretable, composable, and working across different robot morphologies. Moreover, we integrate the system into a continuous control framework and leverage knowledge distillation to learn a much smaller model, significantly improving token efficiency and system latency. Results from a user study with a human-like platform indicate that participants judged our system's motions to be better aligned with the interaction context than motions produced under a non-modulated or API-level condition. We also demonstrate how the system generates expressive motion for robots with different kinematics, showcasing its versatility. Paper webpage: https://gen-mod-expressive-motion-behavior.github.io/.
2610.35615.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 21st ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction, 2026, pp. 438-446
2610.35615.tldr_en: A novel approach to automatically generate and modulate complex, expressive full-body gesture sequences from a multimodal (text, audio, video) context description based on a unified mathematical implementation of the Principles of Animation using Dynamic Movement Primitives.
2610.35615.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction

llm.title_ja: マルチモーダル基盤モデルを用いた表現力豊かな動作行動の文脈認識型生成とモジュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 動的移動プリミティブを用いたアニメーション原則の数学的実装に基づき、マルチモーダルな文脈記述から複雑で表現力豊かな全身ジェスチャー配列を自動生成・モジュレーションする新規アプローチを提示した。
llm.problem: 表現力豊かなロボットの動きはHRIを向上させるが、多様な文脈や異なるロボットの形態に適応する柔軟性や一般性が不足していること。
llm.method: マルチモーダル基盤モデルを用いて、動的移動プリミティブ（DMP）に基づきコンテキストに応じたパラメータ変動を含む動作配列を生成・モジュレーションし、知識蒸留によって軽量化する手法の提案。
llm.result: ヒューマノイドプラットフォームを用いたユーザー実験により、システムが生成した動きが非モジュレーション条件よりも相互作用の文脈によく一致していると評価された。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル基盤モデル
動的移動プリミティブ
ヒューマン・ロボット相互作用

2610.35607.title: VaLoP: Value Gradient Lookahead and Pullback for Reward-Guided Diffusion
2610.35607.abstract: Reward guidance steers a pretrained diffusion or flow model toward images or actions that a reward model prefers, at sampling time and without retraining the model for each reward. It follows the gradient of a value function, the expected reward given the noisy state. The two common estimates of this gradient, gradients through a one-step denoised estimate and learned value models, are least accurate at high noise, where the coarse structure of the sample is decided. Interestingly, we find that both errors are posterior covariances, which grow with the uncertainty about the clean sample, and hence at higher noise. To reduce them, we evaluate the value at a less noisy state, one sampler step ahead, where this uncertainty is smaller, and pull its gradient back to the current state. This lookahead places both estimators at the two ends of one family and reveals that an intermediate lookahead requires one additional term, a correction through the generator. We therefore propose Value Gradient Lookahead and Pullback (VaLoP), which computes this correction with one vector-Jacobian product, and VaLoP-Fast, which amortizes it with a small head that, for text-to-image models, is trained with a single reward and reused for the others. Across various models, rewards, and benchmark datasets, both robustly outperform existing value-gradient guidance on the target reward, VaLoP-Fast at about the cost of learned-value guidance. Both extend to critic-guided robot policies, where VaLoP-Fast attains the highest success rates on LIBERO and RoboCasa.
2610.35607.tldr_en: Value Gradient Lookahead and Pullback (VaLoP), which computes this correction with one vector-Jacobian product, and VaLoP-Fast, which amortizes it with a small head that, for text-to-image models, is trained with a single reward and reused for the others, robustly outperform existing value-gradient guidance on the target reward.

llm.title_ja: VaLoP：報酬誘導型拡散のためのバリュー勾配ルックアヘッドとプルバック
llm.tldr_ja: サンプラーの1ステップ先で価値を評価しその勾配を現在に引き戻すことで推論時の不確実性から生じる誤差を軽減する「VaLoP」および「VaLoP-Fast」を提案し、報酬誘導型拡散の性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 事前学習済み拡散モデルを報酬モデルの嗜好に合わせる従来の報酬誘導では、高ノイズ時において価値勾配の推計誤差が大きくなること。
llm.method: ルックアヘッドによる状態先での価値評価とジェネレータを通じた補正項を1つのベクトル-ヤコビアン積で計算する「VaLoP」および軽量ヘッドでそれを近似する「VaLoP-Fast」を提案する。
llm.result: 多様なモデルやベンチマークにおいて既存の価値勾配誘導を一貫して上回り、ロボットポリシーの誘導においてLIBEROやRoboCasaで最高の成功率を達成した。

2610.35604.title: RoboDoctor: Training-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Robot Policies
2610.35604.abstract: Generalist robot policies and language-model agents provide complementary capabilities, but completing a task also requires adapting their use to the consequences of physical interaction. We study execution as a locus of adaptation: feedback guides the current action and supplies evidence for revising subsequent decisions under fixed model weights. We introduce RoboDoctor, a training-free framework that connects diagnosis, grounded action, and persistent experience across three revision targets. The harness allocates control between policy and agent; intervention determines when to assist while preserving useful policy behavior; and operation refines physical methods through observed effects. Linked experience records retain the reason for a decision, the attempted method, its outcome, and conditions for reuse. On a curated archive of 54 RoboDojo-Sim task entries, RoboDoctor achieves a five-dimension mean score of 57.10, with a native success rate of 49.44%. Recorded interactions illustrate strategy changes, selective correction, and grasp revision. These findings characterize execution-time adaptation in the evaluated system; controlled trials remain necessary to isolate the contribution of cross-episode experience.
2610.35604.tldr_en: This work introduces RoboDoctor, a training-free framework that connects diagnosis, grounded action, and persistent experience across three revision targets, and characterize execution-time adaptation in the evaluated system.

llm.title_ja: RoboDoctor: ロボットポリシーのためのトレーニング不要の再帰的自己改善
llm.tldr_ja: 診断、接地された行動、永続的な経験を3つの修正ターゲットで結びつけるトレーニング不要のフレームワーク RoboDoctor を導入し、評価されたシステムにおける実行時適応の特徴を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 汎用ロボットポリシーと言語モデルエージェントは相補的な能力を提供するか、タスク完了には物理的インタラクションの結果への適応が必要であること。
llm.method: ポリシーとエージェント間で制御を割り当て、介入のタイミングを決定し、観測された効果を通じて物理的手法を洗練させる、トレーニング不要のフレームワーク RoboDoctor の構築。
llm.result: RoboDojo-Simの54のタスクエントリにおいて、5次元の平均スコア57.10、ネイティブ成功率49.44%を達成し、戦略の変更や選択的修正を実証した。

2610.35582.title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
2610.35582.abstract: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics. As the swarm grows denser, collision avoidance becomes the limiting factor, and the number of safely coexisting robots depends on the formulation of the inter-robot safety constraint. We present a distributed predictive flocking controller in which each robot solves its own nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) problem, optimizing swarm cohesion and alignment costs, inter-robot and obstacle safety, and a task objective, while exchanging only predicted trajectories with local neighbors. Within this generalized controller architecture, solved in real time, we compare six barrier and control-barrier-function (CBF) safety formulations on a digital twin of an open-source vibration-driven bristlebot in a $0.64\,\mathrm{m^2}$ arena. A look-ahead discrete-time CBF performs best overall, with the fewest collisions and the widest inter-robot margins across nearly every swarm size tested. We deploy it on phototaxis, phototactic orbiting, and cohesion without a stimulus tasks, using swarm sizes starting from ten robots and up to the geometric packing limit. The swarm holds well: collisions stay low in small swarms, rising steeply as the packing limit approaches, while coordination and cohesion degrade gently rather than collapsing. The swarm is found not to trade safety for order, keeping both across the confined arena, with local alignment high at every swarm size.
2610.35582.comment: Submitted to Robotics and Autonomous Systems
2610.35582.tldr_en: A distributed predictive flocking controller in which each robot solves its own nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) problem, optimizing swarm cohesion and alignment costs, inter-robot and obstacle safety, and a task objective, while exchanging only predicted trajectories with local neighbors is presented.

llm.title_ja: 限られたアリーナにおける小型振動駆動ロボットの群れのための分散予測フロッキング
llm.tldr_ja: 各ロボットが自身の非線形モデル予測制御（NMPC）問題を解き、近隣の仲間と予測された軌道のみを交換しながら、群れの結束や障害物回避などを最適化する分散予測フロッキングコントローラーを提示した。
llm.problem: リーダーや中央プランナー、グローバルマップを持たずに、限られたアリーナ内で多数の小型ロボットを協調させる際、衝突回避が制限要因になること。
llm.method: 各ロボットがNMPC問題を解き、予測軌道のみを近隣と交換する分散予測フロッキングコントローラーの設計と、6つのバリアおよび制御バリア関数（CBF）安全定式化の比較。
llm.result: 先読み離散時間CBFが全体として最も優れた性能を発揮し、最小限の衝突と広いロボット間マージンを実現した。

2610.35576.title: Preemptive Instruction Following with Resumption
2610.35576.abstract: Long-horizon embodied navigation may be interrupted by a higher-priority instruction before the current task sequence is complete. The agent must finish its current atomic task, execute the inserted task, and resume the remaining sequence from the updated environment state, where its viewpoint and available navigation candidates may have changed. To evaluate this capability, we introduce PIFR benchmark, a novel task for runtime task preemption and resumption in embodied navigation. PIFR includes single, repeated, and nested interruption settings,with stage-specific metrics for inserted-task completion, resumption of the original task, and completion of the full sequence. Evaluations show that recovery performance varies across interruption conditions, while aggregate success can obscure differences in interruption handling and resumption. We further propose a lightweight candidate-ranking baseline to improve target re-grounding after interruption. Together, PIFR and the baseline provide a systematic framework for studying interruption handling and task recovery in long-horizon embodied navigation.
2610.35576.tldr_en: PIFR benchmark, a novel task for runtime task preemption and resumption in embodied navigation, and a lightweight candidate-ranking baseline to improve target re-grounding after interruption provide a systematic framework for studying interruption handling and task recovery in long-horizon embodied navigation.

llm.title_ja: 再開機能を備えたプリエンプティブな指示追従
