llm.tldr_ja: 定常ナビゲーションにおける実行時タスクプリエンプションと再開のための新規タスクであるPIFRベンチマークを導入し、中断後のターゲット再グランディングを改善するための軽量な候補ランキングベースラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 長期的な身体的ナビゲーションは、現在のタスクシーケンスが完了する前に、より優先度の高い指示によって中断される場合があること。
llm.method: 単一、繰り返し、ネストされた中断設定を含む新しいベンチマーク（PIFR）の構築と、中断後のターゲット再グランディングを改善する軽量な候補ランキングベースラインの提案。
llm.result: 中断条件によって回復パフォーマンスが異なることを示し、提案ベースラインとともに長期ナビゲーションにおける中断処理とタスク回復の体系的なフレームワークを提供した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2610.35566.title: Copying As Defense: Protecting Images from Editing By Eliciting Model Copying
2610.35566.abstract: Image editors built on diffusion transformers (DiTs), such as Flux Kontext, make it possible to turn a single photograph into a convincing manipulated image, including harmful and non-consensual edits. Proactive defenses aim to prevent such manipulations by adding an imperceptible perturbation before an image is shared. Existing defenses for DiT-based in-context editors make the output attend less to the protected reference image. But this leaves the model free to follow the edit instruction using the text and its own generated tokens, often producing a new, weakly grounded image rather than preventing the edit. We find that the opposite strategy is more effective: instead of leading the model to ignore the reference, we encourage it to copy it. Through controlled attention interventions, we show that concentrating target-token attention on the reference image in only a few early blocks is sufficient to collapse the editing behavior, causing the model to reproduce its input, often as a lossy copy, rather than execute the requested transformation. Based on this insight, we introduce Copying-as-Defense (CaD), which maximizes per-token target-to-reference attention mass in early transformer blocks. Since attention rows are normalized, increasing reference attention suppresses the attention allocated to the text and generated canvas. Restricting the objective to early blocks also lets us truncate the backpropagation path, keeping optimization cheap. Across editors and benchmarks, CaD reduces average edit success from 81.4% on unprotected images to 24.0%, a 70.6% relative reduction, and by a further 44.3% relative to DeContext, the strongest baseline (43.0%). CaD is also roughly 1.8-2.0x faster per optimization step than comparable methods.
2610.35566.tldr_en: Copying-as-Defense (CaD) is introduced, which maximizes per-token target-to-reference attention mass in early transformer blocks in early transformer blocks, and shows that concentrating target-token attention on the reference image in only a few early blocks is sufficient to collapse the editing behavior.

llm.title_ja: 防御としてのコピー：モデルコピーを誘発することによる編集からの画像の保護
llm.tldr_ja: 初期のトランスフォーマーブロックにおけるトークンごとのターゲットからリファレンスへのアテンション質量を最大化する Copying-as-Defense (CaD) を導入し、少数の初期ブロックでターゲットトークンアテンションを集中させるだけで編集動作を崩壊させるのに十分であることを示した。
llm.problem: 拡散トランスフォーマー（DiT）ベースの画像エディタにより、有害で同意のない編集を含む写真の改変が可能になっており、既存の防御策は編集指示に従うモデルの自由度を残してしまうこと。
llm.method: 初期のトランスフォーマーブロックでターゲットからリファレンスへのアテンションを最大化し、入力を（ロスのあるコピーとして）再現させる Copying-as-Defense (CaD) の導入。
llm.result: 保護されていない画像の平均編集成功率を81.4%から24.0%へと70.6%相対的に削減し、既存の最強ベースラインと比較しても大幅な削減を達成した。

2610.35563.title: High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable
2610.35563.abstract: Experts can master fine hand-object manipulation skills, yet limited conscious perception of rapid tactile interactions hinders their ability to articulate the underlying control mechanisms. Badminton racket control requires rapid, fine hand-force coordination, providing a demanding testbed for uncovering these mechanisms. An 864-node tactile-inertial glove with synchronized 100-Hz acquisition recorded over 14,000 strokes from more than 70 participants across five skills. Inspired by sensorimotor control, our mechanics-grounded two-layer framework inferred object-driving and grip-stabilizing control from tactile history, while resolving their spatiotemporal force realization. We found that higher proficiency was associated with selective rather than extensive control: greater skill specificity, anticipatory regulation, focal distal modulation and lower geometric torque cancellation, while spatiotemporal coordination showed a non-monotonic acquire-refine pattern. We translated these mechanisms into personalized guidance targeting force control and force-motion coordination. In a randomized cohort, mechanism-guided learners gained 0.72 expert-rated skill levels versus 0.05 with level-only feedback, making control mechanisms actionable.
2610.35563.comment: 58 pages, including 14 pages of main text and 44 pages of supplementary information. 5 main figures and 19 supplementary figures

llm.title_ja: 高解像度触覚観測による隠れたラケット制御メカニズムの学習可能性
llm.tldr_ja: 864ノードの触覚慣性グローブを用いてバドミントンラケット制御時の触覚データを収集し、メカニズムに基づいた2層フレームワークにより把持安定化およびオブジェクト駆動制御を推論した。
llm.problem: 急激な触覚相互作用に対する限られた意識的知覚が、熟練者の持つ細かい手と物体の操作スキルの根底にある制御メカニズムの言語化を妨げていること。
llm.method: 触覚履歴からオブジェクト駆動制御と把持安定化制御を推論するメカニズムに基づいた2層フレームワークを構築し、時空間的力の実現を解析する。
llm.result: 熟練者は広範な制御ではなく選択的な制御（スキルの特異性や予測的制御など）を行う傾向があることを発見し、そのメカニズムに基づく指導を受けた学習者のスキルレベルが向上した。

2610.35494.title: Enhancing Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Motion Planning via Task Decomposition
2610.35494.abstract: Obstacle-aware robotic manipulation can require substantial interaction data when deep reinforcement learning policies are trained from scratch. We study a task decomposition framework combining first-layer critic transfer with staged reward redesign (RR) on a Truncated Quantile Critics (TQC) backbone. Transfer reuses an input representation across tasks, while RR supplies intermediate feedback for Pick-and-Place. Experiments cover Push, Pick-and-Place, and Slide in obstacle-free and single-obstacle PyBullet environments, with three random seeds per setting. On obstacle-aware Push, transfer achieves $0.83\pm0.05$ success against $0.77\pm0.06$ for TQC. On obstacle-aware Slide, it achieves $0.95\pm0.02$ against $0.84\pm0.06$ for SAC, the strongest baseline in that setting. These are gains of $6$ and $11$ percentage points, respectively. RR reduces the target-training steps needed for obstacle-free Pick-and-Place from roughly $0.75$M to $0.20$M. Transfer benefits depend on the route: obstacle-aware Pick-and-Place shows a lower mean than training from scratch. A selected simulated trajectory is executed open-loop on a Franka Emika FR3 as a feasibility demonstration. The study characterizes when a lightweight combination of established transfer and reward-design components helps learning.
2610.35494.tldr_en: A task decomposition framework combining first-layer critic transfer with staged reward redesign (RR) on a Truncated Quantile Critics (TQC) backbone is studied, characterizes when a lightweight combination of established transfer and reward-design components helps learning.

llm.title_ja: タスク分解を通じたロボット動作計画のための深層強化学習の強化
llm.tldr_ja: 切り捨て分位数批判（TQC）バックボーン上で、第一層の批判的転移と段階的報酬再設計（RR）を組み合わせたタスク分解フレームワークを研究し、軽量なコンポーネントの組み合わせが学習を助ける条件を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 障害物を考慮したロボットマニピュレーションを深層強化学習ポリシーでスクラッチから訓練する場合、大量のインタラクションデータが必要になること。
llm.method: 第一層の批判的転移（transfer）と段階的報酬再設計（RR）をTQCバックボーンに組み合わせたタスク分解フレームワークの検討。
llm.result: 障害物ありのPushタスクおよびSlideタスクにおいて、ベースラインと比較してそれぞれ6%および11%の成功率向上を達成した。

2610.35489.title: TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration
2610.35489.abstract: Deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) on resource-constrained embodied agents for 3D visual question answering necessitates cloud-edge collaboration. However, offloading massive visual data to the cloud over bandwidth-limited and noisy channels introduces severe latency and transmission distortion. To address this, we propose TP-JSCC, an efficient token pruning and joint source-channel coding method for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration. First, we develop a Local and Global Semantics-based Hybrid Token Pruning (LGS-HTP) module to significantly reduce the visual token count. By decoupling foreground-background tokens and jointly selecting local and global semantics, LGS-HTP effectively reduces redundancy while preserving reasoning-critical tokens. Second, we introduce a lightweight Token Joint Source-Channel Coding (T-JSCC) module to further compress the pruned tokens and ensure their robust transmission over error-prone channels. By employing lightweight cascaded linear layers and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-adaptive mechanism, this module adapts to fluctuating channel conditions while maintaining minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on ScanQA and SQA3D datasets indicate the exceptional efficiency and robustness of our approach. Specifically, on ScanQA validation set, the LGS-HTP module could achieve 90% pruning ratio while incurring less than a 1% CIDEr loss. Building on this, the T-JSCC further compresses the tokens by 18 times, resulting in an overall 180 times data volume reduction for robust transmission, while saving 90% in computational complexity for LVLM deployment. Our code is available at https://github.com/yuanhui0325/TP-JSCC.
2610.35489.tldr_en: TP-JSCC, an efficient token pruning and joint source-channel coding method for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration, and a lightweight Token Joint Source-Channel Coding module to further compress the pruned tokens and ensure their robust transmission over error-prone channels.

llm.title_ja: TP-JSCC：クラウド・エッジ協調におけるLVLMベース3D-VQAのための効率的なトークンプルーニングと結合ソース・チャネル符号化
llm.tldr_ja: 前景・背景トークンの分離と局所・大域意味情報の選択により視覚トークンを削減するLGS-HTPモジュールと、雑音環境下での堅牢な送信を確保するT-JSCCモジュールを組み合わせた「TP-JSCC」を提案した。
llm.problem: リソース制約のある身体性エージェント上でLVLMを用いた3D視覚質問応答（3D-VQA）を行う際、帯域制限と雑音のあるチャネルを介した大量の視覚データオフロードが重大な遅延と歪みをもたらすこと。
llm.method: 局所・大域的意味に基づくハイブリッドトークンプルーニング（LGS-HTP）と、軽量なカスケード線形層とSNR適応型メカニズムを用いたトークン結合ソース・チャネル符号化（T-JSCC）を統合する。
llm.result: ScanQAデータセット等での実験により、CIDEr損失を1%未満に抑えながら90%のプルーニング率を達成し、全体として180倍のデータ量削減と90%の計算量削減を実現した。
keywords_ja: クラウド・エッジ協調
トークンプルーニング

2610.35462.title: DEX-PHD: A Dexterous Portable Handheld Device for Multimodal Data Collection
2610.35462.abstract: Existing manipulation data collection methods typically offer either accurate robot-state acquisition through kinematic-chain-based teleoperation or convenient, portable operation through vision-based approaches. We present DEX-PHD, a portable handheld device that combines these advantages for dexterous manipulation by integrating a dexterous robot hand, continuous per-finger control, and multimodal logging. The system records proprioceptive information, fingertip contact data, and wrist-camera video, while the operator directly controls the robot hand through joint-level mapping. Its untethered design enables data collection across diverse environments. We demonstrate DEX-PHD on contact-rich tasks requiring coordinated multi-finger manipulation and deploy the collected demonstrations through open-loop replay on a physical humanoid robot. The results show that open-loop replay preserves the main temporal patterns of finger motion and task-relevant contact. Therefore, DEX-PHD provides a practical platform for portable, multimodal dexterous manipulation data collection.
2610.35462.tldr_en: DEX-PHD is a portable handheld device that combines a dexterous robot hand, continuous per-finger control, and multimodal logging by integrating a dexterous robot hand, continuous per-finger control, and multimodal logging to provide a practical platform for dexterous manipulation data collection.

llm.title_ja: DEX-PHD：マルチモーダルデータ収集のための器用なポータブルハンドヘルドデバイス
llm.tldr_ja: 器用なロボットハンド、指ごとの連続制御、マルチモーダルな記録機能を統合し、関節レベルのマッピングを通じて現場で器用な操作データを収集できるポータブルデバイス「DEX-PHD」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のマニピュレーションデータ収集方法は、正確なロボット状態の取得か、持ち運びやすさのどちらかしか提供できないこと。
llm.method: 器用なロボットハンド、指ごとの連続制御、固有受容情報や接触データ、手首カメラ映像を記録するマルチモーダルロギングを組み合わせた、テザーレスな携帯型デバイスを開発する。
llm.result: 接触を伴う多指協調タスクで実証され、収集したデモを物理的なヒューマノイドロボットでオープンループ再生し、手指の動作や接触の主要な時間的パターンが維持されることを確認した。

2610.35458.title: RoKON: Efficient and Adaptive Data-Enabled Predictive Control for Robotic Manipulation
2610.35458.abstract: Data-enabled predictive control has recently emerged as a promising control paradigm, enabling a transparent optimal-control formulation without the need to learn an explicit dynamics model. This paper presents a number of extensions paving the path towards its use in real-time robotics tasks. Following recent work, we utilize a nonlinear predictor based on Gaussian kernels to represent the relationship between input and output data. We propose a damped Gauss-Newton method that enables real-time control by efficiently exploiting the least-squares structure of the control problem. In addition, we introduce a hybrid buffer management strategy that incorporates informative online data while retaining relevant offline data, allowing the predictor to account for changes in the dynamics. We demonstrate the tracking performance and computational suitability of the proposed method in MuJoCo using a Franka Research 3 arm pushing a block across surface, without prior knowledge of its changing friction values.
2610.35458.tldr_en: A damped Gauss-Newton method that enables real-time control by efficiently exploiting the least-squares structure of the control problem is proposed and a hybrid buffer management strategy that incorporates informative online data while retaining relevant offline data is introduced, allowing the predictor to account for changes in the dynamics.

llm.title_ja: RoKON：ロボットマニピュレーションのための効率的かつ適応的なデータ駆動型予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: ガウスカーネルに基づく非線形予測器と、最小二乗構造を活用するダンピングガウス・ニュートン法、およびオンラインデータを統合するハイブリッドバッファ管理を組み合わせたデータ駆動型予測制御手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 明示的なダイナミクスモデルの学習を必要としないデータ駆動型予測制御を、リアルタイムのロボットタスクに適用するための拡張が求められていること。
llm.method: 入力と出力データの関係を表現するガウスカーネルベースの非線形予測器を採用し、リアルタイム制御を可能にするダンピングガウス・ニュートン法とハイブリッドバッファ管理を導入する。
llm.result: 摩擦変化の事前知識なしで、Franka Research 3アームを用いたMuJoCo上のブロック押しタスクにおいてトラッキング性能と計算上の適合性を実証した。

2610.35448.title: Model-Aware Generation of Safety-Critical Scenes for Robust End-to-End Driving via Distilled Planner Surrogates
2610.35448.abstract: End-to-end driving models perform well on standard benchmarks but collide frequently in safety-critical scenarios. We present a failure-mode analysis on NeuroNCAP which shows that 95.9% of DiffusionDrive's collisions are planning failures despite reliable detection, pinpointing the bottleneck in planning rather than perception. We attribute this to a fundamental data imbalance, as safety-critical interactions are rare in real driving logs, so planners are hardly ever trained on them. We close this gap with a novel model-aware framework that generates safety-critical training scenes against a specific planner. Each planner is attacked at the bird's-eye-view (BEV) level through a differentiable surrogate distilled from its own planning head. This keeps the expensive video renderer out of the attack loop. We extract 50 scenes per planner, each pairing an attack with a safe escape trajectory that serves as the fine-tuning label. A fully automated quality-diversity search generates both the attacks and the escapes, so that their variety is not specified by hand. Only these scenes are rendered to fine-tune the planner, which reduces the computational cost significantly. Fine-tuning on these scenes roughly halves the closed-loop collision rate of two planners on NeuroNCAP (SparseDrive 28.0% to 12.2%, DiffusionDrive 37.5% to 19.2%) while largely preserving normal driving. A cross-planner transfer experiment shows that the gain comes from targeting the specific planner. Each planner improves most on the scenes generated against itself, and DiffusionDrive fine-tuned on SparseDrive's scenes retains only 6.7 of its 18.3-point collision-rate reduction.
2610.35448.tldr_en: A novel model-aware framework that generates safety-critical training scenes against a specific planner with a fundamental data imbalance, as safety-critical interactions are rare in real driving logs, so planners are hardly ever trained on them.

llm.title_ja: 蒸留プランナーサロゲートを用いた頑健なエンドツーエンド自動運転のための安全性クリティカルなシーンのモデル認識型生成
llm.tldr_ja: 高価なビデオレンダラーを攻撃ループから外すため、プランナーの計画ヘッドから微分可能なサロゲートを蒸留して鳥瞰図（BEV）レベルで安全クリティカルな学習シーンを生成するモデル認識型フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンド自動運転モデルは標準ベンチマークで高性能である一方、安全クリティカルな相互作用が実運転ログに少ないため衝突が頻発すること。
llm.method: プランナー自身の計画ヘッドから微分可能なサロゲートを構築してBEVレベルで攻撃を行い、自動品質多様性探索により攻撃と安全なエスケープ軌道を生成して微調整用ラベルとする。
llm.result: 生成されたシーンでの微調整により、NeuroNCAP上での2つのプランナー（SparseDriveやDiffusionDrive）のクローズドループ衝突率を約半分に削減した。

2610.35429.title: MATE-BT: A Behavior-Tree-Based Framework for Hierarchically Decentralized Mission Autonomy in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Teams
2610.35429.abstract: Multi-robot teams executing predefined missions must adapt to runtime changes and sustain mission management despite robot failures. This paper proposes MATE-BT (Mission, Allocation, and Task Execution with Behavior Trees), a hierarchically decentralized framework that separates mission execution, allocation, and task execution. An active onboard leader manages mission progression and team-level task assignment, with authority transferable to another leader-capable robot after failure. Interchangeable decentralized methods resolve target assignments, while each robot adapts its local behavior through planning and acting with behavior trees. Webots simulations and real-robot experiments demonstrate mission continuity despite new targets and robot failures, including active-leader failure. In the physical experiments, all MATE-BT computation runs onboard. Hardware-in-the-loop resource measurements further support onboard execution on Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 5. By updating only the affected layers without full-plan regeneration, MATE-BT maintained a response time of approximately 130 ms with 30 robots and 120 targets. Comparisons of four target-assignment plugins reveal scenario-dependent trade-offs between mission completion time and total travel distance.
2610.35429.tldr_en: This paper proposes MATE-BT (Mission, Allocation, and Task Execution with Behavior Trees), a hierarchically decentralized framework that separates mission execution, allocation, and task execution, and an active onboard leader manages mission progression and team-level task assignment.

llm.title_ja: MATE-BT：異種マルチロボットチームにおける階層的分散型ミッション自律性のためのビヘイビアツリーベースのフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ミッションの進行管理、割り当て、タスク実行を分離し、オンボードリーダーによる動的なタスク割り当てとビヘイビアツリーによる局所行動適応を可能にする階層的分散型フレームワーク「MATE-BT」を提案した。
llm.problem: 定義済みのミッションを実行するマルチロボットチームは、実行時の変化に適応し、ロボットの故障にもかかわらずミッション管理を維持する必要があること。
llm.method: ミッション実行、割り当て、タスク実行を分離し、アクティブなオンボードリーダーがミッション進行やタスク割り当てを管理しつつ、故障時にはリーダー権限を移行する階層的分散型構造を用いる。
llm.result: Webotsシミュレーションおよび実機実験により、新しいターゲットやロボットの故障、リーダーの故障に対してミッション継続性を維持できることを示した。

2610.35385.title: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
2610.35385.abstract: Embodied agents are expected to accomplish real-world goals by deciding for themselves how and when to interact with their surroundings. For many such goals, changing the physical state of the world is the means rather than the end: the agent changes the state of a system through interaction, observes the feedback, and explores until it either achieves the goal itself (e.g., discovering physical laws) or learns what the goal requires; it acts to know. Manipulation benchmarks stop at acting to change, with the target state given; scientific discovery benchmarks evaluate knowing but replace physical experimentation with symbolic actions or numerical queries. We introduce EmbodiedLab, a benchmark in which a robot must act to know. Quantitative science experiments make this setting controllable: the parameters of the system are resampled for every instance, so the result cannot be known in advance, yet it can be scored exactly. Across 30 experiments in five disciplines on 14 apparatus platforms, the agent receives an objective and the apparatus, chooses its own procedure, and operates a physics-based simulated laboratory, reading the instruments through its cameras. Evaluation checks what the agent came to know, grounded in readings recorded during the episode, as well as the physical state the task requires; every experiment is verified to be solvable. We evaluate six frontier models in their developers' coding agents with native observation and control, with added perception and motion planning, and with manipulation skills distilled from the strongest agents. With native control, even the strongest agent succeeds less than half the time; for every agent, most failures arise in interacting with the apparatus, and manipulation skills help weaker agents more than perception and planning. The benchmark and its evaluation code are available at https://github.com/HexaFuture/EmbodiedLab.
2610.35385.comment: Technical report. 19 pages, 10 figures, 9 tables. Project page: https://hexafuture.ai/benchmarks/embodiedlab/
2610.35385.tldr_en: This work introduces EmbodiedLab, a benchmark in which a robot must act to know, and evaluates six frontier models in their developers' coding agents with native observation and control, with added perception and motion planning, and with manipulation skills distilled from the strongest agents.
2610.35385.hf_summary_en: EmbodiedLab evaluates embodied agents that must physically interact with simulated laboratory apparatus to discover scientific principles through self-directed experimentation.

llm.title_ja: EmbodiedLab：知るために行動する身体性エージェントのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 物理法則の発見やシステムの状態を調査するためにロボットが試行錯誤して環境と相互作用し「知るために行動する」必要がある課題を評価するベンチマーク「EmbodiedLab」を提案した。
llm.problem: マニピュレーションのベンチマークは目標状態を与えられた変更にとどまり、科学的発見のベンチマークは物理的実験を記号的アクションに置き換えていること。
llm.method: パラメータが毎回再サンプリングされる定量的な科学実験環境において、エージェント自身が手順を選択し、カメラを介して機器を操作して物理ベースのシミュレーション実験室を動かすベンチマークを構築する。
llm.result: 6つのフロンティアモデルを評価した結果、最強のエージェントでも成功率は半分未満であり、失敗の大部分は機器との相互作用におけるものであったことを明らかにした。

2610.35342.title: VisGeo-PipeTrack: A Visual Geometric Servo Control Framework with MPC-RCAPID Control for UAV-Based Dynamic Pipes Tracking
2610.35342.abstract: While unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed for pipeline inspection, prevailing research predominantly assumes static pipes. In real-world industrial environments, pipes often exhibit dynamic movements, such as vibrations. This imposes more stringent requirements on UAVs' adaptive control and computational efficiency than in static scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes a servo control framework named VisGeo-PipeTrack, which utilizes geometric constraints to enable UAV tracking of dynamic pipes. To achieve efficient UAV positioning, YOLOv5 is employed to detect labels on the pipe. The positions are derived from visual geometric constraints based on these detected labels to enable precise localization. To address tracking control challenges, a model predictive control based real-time corrected adaptive PID (MPC-RCAPID) controller is proposed. This controller employs the Recursive Least Squares method for real-time model estimation and integrates rolling horizon optimization to dynamically adjust PID parameters. Experiments conducted on both the AirSim simulator and the Tello UAV platform validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Simulation comparisons with standard PID, fractional-order PID, adaptive PID, and fuzzy PID demonstrate that MPC-RCAPID achieves the shortest settling time (3.26 s) and the lowest average tracking error (3.52%). In physical experiments on the Tello platform, compared with standard PID control, MPC-RCAPID reduces the average tracking error by 55.52%, 26.72%, and 26.52% across the three test dimensions. These results demonstrate that VisGeo-PipeTrack facilitates efficient autonomous tracking in dynamic pipe environments.
2610.35342.comment: Submit to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems IEEE TITS
2610.35342.tldr_en: A servo control framework named VisGeo-PipeTrack, which utilizes geometric constraints to enable UAV tracking of dynamic pipes and facilitates efficient autonomous tracking in dynamic pipe environments is proposed.

llm.title_ja: VisGeo-PipeTrack：UAVベースの動的パイプ追従のためのMPC-RCAPID制御を伴う視覚幾何学的サーボ制御フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 幾何学的制約とYOLOv5による検出、および再帰的最小二乗法でモデルを推定しながらPIDパラメータを動的に調整するMPC-RCAPIDコントローラを統合したサーボ制御フレームワーク「VisGeo-PipeTrack」を提案した。
llm.problem: UAVによるパイプ点検において、実環境のパイプは振動などの動的移動を伴うため、従来の静止前提の手法よりも高度な適応制御と計算効率が求められること。
llm.method: 検出ラベルに基づく視覚的幾何学的制約から位置を導出し、実時間モデル推定とローリングホライゾン最適化を統合したMPC-RCAPIDコントローラを用いる。
llm.result: AirSimシミュレータおよびTello UAVプラットフォームを用いた実験により、標準PID等と比較して追従誤差と整定時間を大幅に削減できることを実証した。

2610.35289.title: Reward-Guided RRT* for Budgeted Task and Motion Planning
2610.35289.abstract: Robotic missions involving spatially distributed tasks often require jointly selecting rewarding locations and planning feasible motions under limited travel budgets. This paper proposes Reward-Guided RRT*, a new sampling-based framework that constructs a budget-feasible mission through a sequence of locally joint task-selection-and-motion-planning stages, evaluated directly in the continuous state space, without requiring a precomputed task-transition graph. The method incrementally builds a mission using reward-guided RRT* searches, while a return-feasibility procedure ensures that each selected task can be visited without violating the mission budget. Experiments with increasing obstacle complexity and number of tasks show solutions comparable to VNS-PRM* while requiring substantially fewer sampled states. We also extend the framework to Dubins steering and evaluate it in CoppeliaSim with a scaled car-like robotic platform, demonstrating its ability to incorporate vehicle kinematic constraints.
2610.35289.tldr_en: Reward-Guided RRT*, a new sampling-based framework that constructs a budget-feasible mission through a sequence of locally joint task-selection-and-motion-planning stages, evaluated directly in the continuous state space, without requiring a precomputed task-transition graph is proposed.

llm.title_ja: 予算制約付きタスク・モーションプランニングのための報酬誘導型RRT*
llm.tldr_ja: 事前計算されたタスク遷移グラフを必要とせず、連続状態空間上で局所的なタスク選択とモーションプランニングを組み合わせて予算内でミッションを構築するサンプリングベースのフレームワーク「Reward-Guided RRT*」を提案した。
llm.problem: 空間的に分散したタスクを伴うロボットミッションでは、限られた移動予算内で報酬の高い場所の選択と実行可能なモーションの計画を同時に行う必要があること。
llm.method: 報酬誘導型RRT*探索を用いてミッションをインクリメンタルに構築し、各タスクを予算違反なく訪問可能にする帰還可能性手続きを組み合わせる。
llm.result: 障害物の複雑さが増す環境において、状態のサンプル数を大幅に削減しつつVNS-PRM*と同等のソリューションを生成し、車両の運動学的制約にも対応できることを実証した。

2610.35252.title: Labference: Benchmarking the Reasoning-Action Connection in Robotic Laboratories
2610.35252.abstract: Realizing Embodied AI for Science requires robots to translate experimental goals into reliable physical procedures, reducing hazardous and repetitive human work while generating evidence for scientific discovery. Although language-based planning and learned manipulation provide complementary capabilities, their integration requires robots to adapt subsequent operations to actual execution outcomes. For example, an unsuccessful placement changes what must be done next, even when the experimental goal remains unchanged. Existing benchmarks assess planning, manipulation, and laboratory workflows through task completion and reasoning or execution metrics; however, aggregate performance leaves the connection between outcome-dependent choices and physical execution unresolved. To address this evaluation gap, we introduce Labference, a benchmark for evaluating how observed physical outcomes guide subsequent choices and how those choices translate into robotic laboratory actions. Its evaluation protocol is designed to test outcome-dependent behavioral adaptation through controlled evidence variations, while independently measuring operation selection, physical execution, and task completion. Matched Oracle-assisted continuations from shared checkpoints then assess which forms of support improve subsequent choices and task completion. Initial weighing evaluations reveal target-selection errors in the tested VLA policies despite successful object transfers, whereas GPT-driven control achieves correct selection but encounters execution failures and substantial computation costs. Together, these findings highlight the need to connect task-appropriate reasoning with reliable, timely action. By making this connection measurable and diagnosable, Labference supports targeted improvements toward autonomous experimentation for Embodied AI for Science.
2610.35252.tldr_en: Labference, a benchmark for evaluating how observed physical outcomes guide subsequent choices and how those choices translate into robotic laboratory actions, is introduced, highlighting the need to connect task-appropriate reasoning with reliable, timely action.

llm.title_ja: Labference：ロボット実験室における推論と行動の接続のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 観察された物理的結果が後続の選択をどのように導き、それがロボットの実験室での行動にどう翻訳されるかを評価するベンチマーク「Labference」を提案した。
llm.problem: 言語ベースの計画と学習されたマニピュレーションは相補的な能力を持つが、その統合には失敗したプレースメントなど実際の実行結果に応じて後続の操作を適応させることが求められること。
llm.method: 制御された証拠の変動を通じて結果依存の行動適応をテストし、操作選択、物理的実行、タスク完了を独立して測定する評価プロトコルを設計する。
llm.result: VLAポリシーではオブジェクト転送に成功しても目標選択エラーが発生する一方、GPT駆動型制御では正しい選択を行いつつも実行失敗や計算コストが発生することを明らかにした。

2610.35231.title: Thermal-Headroom Routing for Efficient Robot Perception in Extreme Heat
2610.35231.abstract: Adaptive robot perception systems must balance detector accuracy, inference latency, and energy consumption, particularly when high ambient temperatures cause processors to thermally throttle. We propose Thermal-Headroom Routing (THR), a lightweight model-selection policy that forecasts processor temperature using a closed-form RC thermal model and excludes detector configurations predicted to cross a throttling threshold. We evaluate THR with four YOLO11 configurations across seven real-world perception traces, eight ambient temperatures, and 20 randomized seeds, comparing it with latency-aware routing, fixed-threshold thermostats, duty caps, and a matched-compute-budget control. At ambient temperatures of 45-55 degrees C and a tight inference deadline, THR eliminates throttling in simulation, reduces deadline misses by 3.9-7.5 percentage points, and reduces energy per on-time frame by approximately 12-13% relative to a latency-belief router. A separate experiment using deadline-paced, nonoverlapping frame execution yields miss-rate reductions of 6.2-9.5 percentage points. A tuned thermostat or duty cap can match THR at a fixed operating point; predictive routing is most useful when ambient conditions or calibrated thermal parameters differ from those used to tune static policies. Measurements on an Apple M5 support the single-node heating approximation but do not validate hardware throttling. The results characterize the conditions under which thermal forecasting improves the efficiency and timeliness of resource-constrained robot perception.
2610.35231.comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 11 tables. Code and experimental outputs: https://github.com/ImSpxrsh/thermal-headroom-routing {Submitted IEEE Big Data}
2610.35231.tldr_en: Thermal-Headroom Routing is proposed, a lightweight model-selection policy that forecasts processor temperature using a closed-form RC thermal model and excludes detector configurations predicted to cross a throttling threshold, and the results characterize the conditions under which thermal forecasting improves the efficiency and timeliness of resource-constrained robot perception.

llm.title_ja: 極端な高温下での効率的なロボット知覚のためのサーマルヘッドルーム・ルーティング
llm.tldr_ja: 閉形式のRC熱モデルを用いてプロセッサ温度を予測し、サーマルスロットリングの閾値を超える検出器構成を除外する軽量なモデル選択ポリシー「Thermal-Headroom Routing（THR）」を提案した。
llm.problem: 適応型ロボット知覚システムは、周囲温度が高いときにプロセッサがサーマルスロットリングを起こすため、検出器の精度、推論遅延、エネルギー消費のバランスを取る必要があること。
llm.method: 閉形式のRC熱モデルによるプロセッサ温度予測に基づき、スロットリング閾値を超えると予測される検出器設定を動的に除外する軽量なルーティングポリシーを用いる。
llm.result: 45〜55℃の周囲温度および厳しい推論期限の下で、スロットリングを排除し、期限超過の削減とフレームあたりのエネルギー削減を実現できることを示した。
llm.limitation: Apple M5での測定は単一ノードの発熱近似をサポートするものの、ハードウェアスロットリング自体の検証には至っていないこと。

2610.35172.title: RetroNav: Scene-Grounded Retrospection and Retry for Self-Evolving Lifelong Navigation
2610.35172.abstract: Existing robot navigation methods primarily focus on isolated tasks, overlooking the need to accumulate knowledge and experience across repeated navigation episodes. Although recent lifelong navigation methods have explored cross-task knowledge accumulation, they mainly focus on scene knowledge while neglecting historical navigation experience and its connection to scene evidence, limiting the ability to reflect on past mistakes and improve future decisions. To address this limitation, this paper presents RetroNav, a training-free self-evolving navigation framework that integrates navigation, memory accumulation, and failure reflection. Specifically, we develop a unified memory system that connects geometric and semantic scene knowledge with historical navigation experience, distinguishing objective observations from task-dependent interpretations. After each navigation attempt, an independent evaluator determines whether a retry is necessary. If so, a Retrospection Agent revisits historical decisions using accumulated scene knowledge and navigation records, generating an evidence-grounded retry brief to guide the next attempt. RetroNav achieves state-of-the-art performance across five navigation benchmarks. Our method will be open-sourced at https://github.com/3dv-casia/RetroNav .
2610.35172.tldr_en: This paper develops a unified memory system that connects geometric and semantic scene knowledge with historical navigation experience, distinguishing objective observations from task-dependent interpretations and achieves state-of-the-art performance across five navigation benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: RetroNav: 自己進化型かつ生涯にわたるナビゲーションのためのシーン基盤型回想と再試行
llm.tldr_ja: 幾何学的・意味的シーン知識を過去のナビゲーション経験と結びつける統合メモリシステムを開発し、5つのナビゲーションベンチマークで最高性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 既存の生涯ナビゲーション手法はシーン知識に注目する一方で過去の経験やシーンの証拠とのつながりを軽視しており、過去の失敗を反省して決定を改善する能力が制限されていた。
llm.method: 幾何学的および意味的なシーン知識を過去のナビゲーション経験と結びつけ、客観的観察と解釈を区別する統合メモリシステムと、証拠に基づくリトライ指示を生成する回想エージェントを統合する。
llm.result: 5つのナビゲーションベンチマークにおいて、最先端の性能を達成した。

2610.35165.title: How Tuning, Reference Preview, Actuator Modeling, and Fallback Policies Change Quadrotor Controller Comparisons: A Reproducible Simulation Study
2610.35165.abstract: Quadrotor controller comparisons commonly report a single tracking error, although the resulting ranking also depends on tuning effort, reference information, actuator prediction, optimizer fallback, and command timing. We quantify these effects for cascade PID, hover LQR, boundary-layer sliding-mode control (BL-SMC), linear MPC with LQR fallback (LMPC-F), a preview-enabled LMPC-F, and a geometric $SO(3)$ controller on a common nonlinear plant with rotor gyroscopic coupling, motor lag, and saturation. A primary study (556 episodes at 50~Hz) combines matched twelve-candidate tuning, 400 paired evaluation episodes, and a 48-cell MPC factorial; a confirmation study (1462 episodes) repeats the evaluation on 50 fresh realizations with tuning budgets of 12, 24, and 48 candidates. A matched twelve-candidate tuning protocol changed the mean-RMSE ordering obtained with the fixed baseline settings, moving BL-SMC from last to first; the new ordering recurred on the fresh realizations, and a 48-candidate budget left it unchanged. Reference preview substantially reduced MPC tracking error and, on the figure-eight task, removed fallback activity. On an abrupt step, the outcome depended on the interplay between fallback policy, predictor, and actuator authority. Command timing also changed the outcome: replaying measured command-call delays terminated three of four nominal MPC configurations on a desktop computer and all four on a Raspberry Pi~5, whereas capping the solver at 100 iterations removed every deadline miss in the tested nominal timing profiles. Controller rankings therefore depend not only on tracking accuracy but also on the tuning protocol, reference information, fallback behavior, and implementation timing. We propose a reporting checklist covering tracking accuracy, tuning effort, completion and failure rates, fallback activity, applied-input variation, and command timing.
2610.35165.comment: 20 pages, 5 figures, 11 tables. Reproducible simulation study of quadrotor controller benchmarking

llm.title_ja: チューニング、リファレンスプレビュー、アクチュエータモデリング、フォールバックポリシーがクアッドコプターコントローラーの比較をどのように変えるか：再現可能なシミュレーション研究
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: クアッドコプターコントローラーの比較は単一の追跡誤差を報告することが多いが、ランキングはチューニングやリファレンス情報などにも依存する。
llm.method: 回転子のジャイロ結合やモータの遅延を持つ共通の非線形プラント上で、12候補のチューニングやMPCのファクター分析などを通じて効果を定量化する。
llm.result: コントローラーのランキングは追跡精度だけでなく、チューニングプロトコルやリファレンス情報、フォールバック動作、実装タイミングに依存することを示した。

2610.35151.title: SoK: Timestamps Are Not a Time Model: Rethinking Temporal Reasoning in Host-Based Intrusion Detection
2610.35151.abstract: Host-based intrusion detectors order events, window audit streams and sequence attack stages by their timestamps. Every conclusion they draw therefore rests on assumptions about clocks, delivery, entity identity and the integrity of the evidence, and most of these assumptions go unstated. This Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) makes them explicit. Drawing on temporal databases, stream processing and runtime verification, we distill five components of a time model, together with a checklist of evidence assumptions and four levels of guarantee, and walk through a running campaign with them. A documented search yields fifteen families of detection and investigation. For papers selected by screening role and period, plus named systems and landmarks, we check the stated assumptions in the full texts, and we assess eleven temporal knowledge representation and reasoning (KRR) formalisms and a learned baseline on nine attack patterns. Some early alert correlators stated clock and delivery assumptions, and forensics measures clock error. Current provenance-based detectors state no clock bound. Four audited papers describe input-ordering conditions or conventions, but none specifies conditions for conclusion validity across a stated class of delivery failures. In the selected provenance-based systems, campaign composition uses system-specific procedures or objectives, learned state, causal graph queries or language models, and beyond CEP-based query systems, we found no temporal rule language or stream reasoner from KRR applied to host audit data. In 28 of 38 audited provenance-era detector papers, capture or stored evidence is trusted or its manipulation is placed out of scope, and none says which conclusions survive deleted, delayed or forged records. Five open challenges follow from these gaps.
2610.35151.comment: Extended version with full appendices (search method, KRR domain analysis, rating evidence, formalizations). 51 pages, 1 figure, 16 tables. Artifacts: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23530002
2610.35151.tldr_en: Drawing on temporal databases, stream processing and runtime verification, this work distill five components of a time model, together with a checklist of evidence assumptions and four levels of guarantee, and walks through a running campaign with them.

llm.title_ja: SoK: タイムスタンプは時刻モデルではない：ホスト型侵入検知における時間的推論の再考
llm.tldr_ja: 時間データベース、ストリーム処理、実行時検証を活用して時間モデルの5つの構成要素を抽出し、証拠の前提条件のチェックリストと4つの保証レベルを提示した。
llm.problem: ホスト型侵入検知器はイベントの順序付けなどをタイムスタンプで行っており、時計や配信に関する暗黙の前提に依存しているが、それらが明示されていない。
llm.method: 時間データベース、ストリーム処理、実行時検証を活用して時間モデルの5つの構成要素を抽出し、証拠の前提条件のチェックリストと4つの保証レベルを提示して実例を検証した。
llm.result: 15の検出・調査ファミリに関する文書化された検索と、既存研究の前提条件の体系的な評価を実施した。

2610.35103.title: The Language of Deformation: Semantic Failure Analysis as a Prerequisite for Dexterous Manipulation of Deformable Objects
2610.35103.abstract: Dexterous manipulation of rigid objects has reached a level of maturity where grasp stability, control, and planning strategies are successfully applied in industry and logistics. In contrast, manipulating deformable objects (cables, plastic pieces, cloth) remains far more challenging, as rigid-object methods do not account for their additional complexity. This paper identifies semantic failure analysis as a key step toward mature deformable-object manipulation and supports this claim with proof-of-concept experiments. Unlike rigid-object manipulation, where goals are well-defined in terms of criteria such as force balance and slippage, deformable-object manipulation involves a broader variety of failure modes arising from differences in materials, geometry, and behaviour. Typical failures include buckling, plastic deformation, pressure variations, and tearing. These diverse and often hard-to-detect events require distinct corrective strategies, making semantic failure analysis necessary. We define its key components and challenges and present experimental results supporting its potential as a research direction.
2610.35103.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the European Robotics Forum (ERF) 2026
2610.35103.tldr_en: This paper identifies semantic failure analysis as a key step toward mature deformable-object manipulation and supports this claim with proof-of-concept experiments and presents experimental results supporting its potential as a research direction.

llm.title_ja: 変形の言語：変形物体の器用な操作の前提条件としての意味的失敗分析
llm.tldr_ja: 変形物体操作の成熟に向けた主要なステップとして意味的失敗分析を特定し、概念実証実験を通じてその有効性を示した。
llm.problem: 剛体操作手法では追加の複雑性に対応できないため、ケーブルや布などの変形物体の操作は依然として非常に困難である。
llm.method: 変形物体の操作における失敗モード（座屈、塑性変形、圧力変動、破れなど）の違いに対処するための意味的失敗分析の主要コンポーネントと課題を定義し、概念実証実験を行った。
llm.result: 変形物体操作の新しい研究方向性としての可能性を支持する実験結果を示した。

2610.35092.title: Uncertainty Evaluation to Support Safety of the Intended Functionality Analysis for Determining the Applicability of Performance Targets Across Triggering Conditions in ML-Based LiDAR Object Detection
2610.35092.abstract: For safety of the intended functionality (SOTIF) analysis according to ISO 21448, a machine learning object detector for light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point clouds can meet a performance target, a limit on the mean per-frame share of wrong detections among accepted detections, by rejecting detections above an uncertainty threshold. A threshold selected on data of one condition carries a statistical guarantee only for data distributed like its selection data, whereas SOTIF analysis covers every triggering condition. This paper presents an uncertainty evaluation in which the threshold is transferred into a triggering condition, a test decides at a stated error probability whether the target is applicable there, not applicable or not determined, and a lower bound counts the independent units an applicable outcome requires. For PointPillars ensembles on KITTI and nuScenes, counted in recorded sequences, as the dependence between frames requires, neither dataset held enough independent units for any target limit, and no transfer had a not applicable outcome. Counted in frames, the same data gave not applicable outcomes at limits fixed in advance after transfers into far distance, into rain and between two separately trained detectors, thresholds that met the target limit after a transfer rejected most correct detections, and in rain the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve did not decrease. A performance target met under one condition therefore counts as evidence under a triggering condition only after a test there, reported with its share of accepted correct detections and its number of independent recorded sequences.
2610.35092.comment: 24 pages, 6 figures. Extended version of the VEHITS 2026 conference paper (doi:10.5220/0014967200004030). Submitted for journal publication. Code and recorded results: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23495356
2610.35092.tldr_en: An uncertainty evaluation in which the threshold is transferred into a triggering condition, a test decides at a stated error probability whether the target is applicable there, not applicable or not determined, and a lower bound counts the independent units an applicable outcome requires.

llm.title_ja: MLベースのLiDAR物体検出におけるトリガー条件間の性能ターゲットの適用性を決定するための意図された機能の安全性のための不確実性評価
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実性閾値を用いた不確実性評価を提案し、指定された誤り確率のもとでターゲットが適用可能か否かをテストで判定できるようにした。
llm.problem: 単一の条件のデータで選択された閾値は、その選択データと同様に分布するデータに対してのみ統計的保証を持ち、SOTIF分析はすべてのトリガー条件をカバーする必要がある。
llm.method: 閾値をトリガー条件に転送し、指定された誤り確率でターゲットの適用性をテストで判定する不確実性評価を提案し、KITTIやnuScenesのPointPillarsアンサンブルで検証した。
llm.result: 前提条件を満たした性能ターゲットがトリガー条件下での証拠として機能するための条件を明らかにし、データセットやフレームごとの適用性を評価した。

2610.35075.title: Zero-HLM: Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation without Real Robot Data
2610.35075.abstract: Learning generalizable humanoid loco-manipulation remains bottlenecked by costly real-world demonstrations. Simulation provides a scalable alternative, but requires visually faithful, physics-ready scenes and executable whole-body motions. We present Zero-HLM, a real-to-sim-to-real framework that transforms smartphone captures and simulated source demonstrations into scalable training data for humanoid loco-manipulation. Gaussian-guided agentic real-to-sim reconstruction aligns visual and physical scenes; motion-environment co-adaptation uses rollout feedback to correct whole-body references and interaction geometry. We generate 4,800 physically validated demonstrations for zero-shot transfer across three Unitree G1 tasks. Simulation-trained GR00T N1.7 achieves 66.7% mean full-task success, versus 46.7% with real-data training. On generalized configurations, expanded simulation training raises pooled success from 23% for base-trained real-data policies to 69%, without additional real demonstrations. Project page: https://young-bit.github.io/zero-hlm/
2610.35075.tldr_en: Zero-HLM is presented, a real-to-sim-to-real framework that transforms smartphone captures and simulated source demonstrations into scalable training data for humanoid loco-manipulation and raises pooled success from 23% for base-trained real-data policies to 69%, without additional real demonstrations.

llm.title_ja: Zero-HLM: 実ロボットデータなしでの汎化可能なヒューマノイドの歩行・操作統合
llm.tldr_ja: スマートフォン撮影とシミュレーションデモをスケーラブルな学習データに変換するreal-to-sim-to-realフレームワーク「Zero-HLM」を提案し、実デモなしでのゼロショット転移を実現した。
llm.problem: 汎化可能なヒューマノイドの歩行・操作統合（loco-manipulation）の学習は、コストのかかる現実世界のデモンストレーションによってボトルネックとなっている。
llm.method: Gaussian-guided agenticなreal-to-sim再構築とモーション・環境の共適応を用いて、スマートフォン撮影やシミュレーションデモを学習データに変換するフレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: Unitree G1の3つのタスクにおいて4,800個の物理的検証済みデモを生成し、追加の実デモなしで統合成功率を23%から69%に向上させた。

2610.35066.title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
2610.35066.abstract: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.
2610.35066.tldr_en: MEMVLN is presented, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention.

llm.title_ja: MemVLN: 視覚言語ナビゲーションのためのストリーミング型エピソード記憶
llm.tldr_ja: 時間ステップと相対ポーズで注釈付けされた圧縮された知覚特徴のバウンドバンクを維持するストリーミング型エピソード記憶フレームワーク「MemVLN」を提案し、優れた性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 長期的なナビゲーションにおいて、VLMベースのストリーミングエージェントにとって永続的なエピソード記憶を維持することが課題となっている。
llm.method: タイムステップと相対ポーズで注釈付けされた圧縮知覚特徴のバウンドバンクを維持し、クロスアテンションを介してコンパクトなメモリトークンを生成するストリーミングエピソード記憶フレームワークを設計した。
llm.result: 標準的なVLN-CEベンチマークのほとんどの報告指標で最先端のパフォーマンスを達成し、物理評価でも成功率を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2610.35062.title: PushAround: Collaborative Path Clearing via Physics-Informed Hybrid Search
2610.35062.abstract: Large vehicles in cluttered environments are often blocked by movable obstacles, motivating mobile robot teams to clear traversable corridors. Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) approaches often abstract obstacle displacements while neglecting robot dimensions, obstacle mass, contact geometry and forces, yielding physically infeasible plans. PushAround is a physics-informed hybrid search that couples geometric connectivity reasoning with short-horizon simulation to construct executable clearing plans. Repeated W-clearance connectivity graph (WCCG) queries expose frontier gaps requiring widening and rank them by estimated downstream costs. The search generates direct or recursive pushing candidates, selecting obstacles, directions, contacts and forces, and admits physics-evaluated candidates. Numerical experiments validate WCCG against standard connectivity checks and demonstrate scaling to denser clutter and teams of up to four robots, with robustness to simulated execution-side physical-parameter mismatch.
2610.35062.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). 8 pages, 11 figures. Supplementary video and evaluation records are included as ancillary files. Video: https://youtu.be/HkQIcVWiIuQ
2610.35062.tldr_en: PushAround is a physics-informed hybrid search that couples geometric connectivity reasoning with short-horizon simulation to construct executable clearing plans and demonstrates robustness to simulated execution-side physical-parameter mismatch.

llm.title_ja: PushAround: 物理情報に基づくハイブリッド探索による協調的経路クリアリング
llm.tldr_ja: 幾何学的連結性推論と短時間シミュレーションを組み合わせた物理情報に基づくハイブリッド探索手法「PushAround」を提案し、実行可能なクリアリング計画を構築した。
llm.problem: 混雑した環境内の大型車両は動的な障害物によって遮られることが多く、移動ロボットチームによる通行可能回廊の確保が必要となるが、既存手法はロボットの寸法や物理的制約を無視しているため物理的に不可能な計画になる。
llm.method: 幾何学的連結性推論と短時間シミュレーションをカップリングし、WCCGクエリを用いてフロンティアギャップを検出し、直接的または再帰的な押し出し候補を生成する物理情報に基づくハイブリッド探索を行う。
llm.result: 標準的な連結性チェックに対するWCCGの検証に成功し、より高密度な障害物環境や最大4台のロボットチームへのスケーリング、および物理パラメータの不一致に対する頑健性を示した。

2610.35058.title: 3D-Force Estimation for Dual-arm Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects via Factor Graphs
2610.35058.abstract: Estimating forces acting on Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is challenging due to their underactuated nature. However, reliable contact estimation is crucial to precisely control them and enable safe manipulation tasks. Differently from the various approaches presented in the literature, this work adopts a probabilistic formulation where the DLO state and sensor data are related through conditional distributions. In particular, factor graphs are used to determine the magnitude, direction, and location of a 3D force acting on a DLO, while simultaneously reconstructing its shape. Since DLOs are not actuated and are typically thin, like cables and wires, strain gauges and actuation readings are usually impractical. Therefore, to overcome this issue, this work is tested using one type of sensing information only, thus developing a generic technique suited for a wider variety of tasks. Realistic tests are performed by introducing noise into the measurements while the DLO follows a prescribed path in the presence of external forces that are accurately estimated.
2610.35058.tldr_en: This work adopts a probabilistic formulation where the DLO state and sensor data are related through conditional distributions, and factor graphs are used to determine the magnitude, direction, and location of a 3D force acting on a DLO, while simultaneously reconstructing its shape.

llm.title_ja: 因子グラフを用いた変形可能な線状物体のデュアルアーム操作における3D力推定
llm.tldr_ja: 確率的定式化と因子グラフを採用し、ひずみゲージ等を使わずに変形可能な線状物体（DLO）に働く3D力の大きさと方向、位置を形状復元と同時に推定する手法を開発した。
llm.problem: 変形可能な線状物体（DLO）は未駆動であり過小駆動であるため、それに働く力の推定や正確な制御、安全な操作が困難である。
llm.method: DLOの状態とセンサーデータを条件付分布に関連付ける確率的定式化を採用し、因子グラフを用いてDLOに働く3D力の大きさ・方向・位置を推定すると同時に形状を再構築する。
llm.result: 外部力が正確に推定される中で、測定にノイズを導入した現実的なテストを通じて検証を行った。

2610.35051.title: VISTA: Active Exploration for Self-Improvement in Embodied Agents
2610.35051.abstract: Agentic embodied intelligence plays a foundational role in open-ended, dynamic physical environments. Rather than treating policy learning as an end-to-end mapping from instructions to actions, recent studies reveal that embodied systems depend not only on pre-trained foundation models, but also on harness. Prior approaches largely treat rollouts as static logs for post-hoc reflection, producing harness updates without autonomously testing and refining them through subsequent embodied interaction. To address this challenge, we propose VISTA, a meta-agent framework that transforms post-hoc rollout reflection into active self-exploration for embodied harness improvement. Specifically, VISTA maintains a harness graph that records the lineage of proposed harnesses, which enables the meta-agent to retrieve prior hypotheses, build on effective mechanisms, and avoid repeatedly exploring failed directions. Each iteration begins from a retained harness version and its execution evidence. Rather than directly committing an update from these historical trajectories, the meta-agent actively explores in the environment. It autonomously generates new rollouts, probes execution failures and recovery behaviors, and iteratively modifies the harness based on the resulting evidence. The refined harness is then evaluated afresh and added to the harness graph. We evaluate VISTA on the LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that VISTA progressively improves task success and is more rollout-efficient than static reflection, achieving higher success rates with fewer simulator rollouts.
2610.35051.tldr_en: Experimental results demonstrate that VISTA progressively improves task success and is more rollout-efficient than static reflection, achieving higher success rates with fewer simulator rollouts and is more rollout-efficient than static reflection.

llm.title_ja: VISTA: 具現化エージェントの自己改善のための能動的探索
llm.tldr_ja: 事後的なロールアウトの反省を能動的自己探索へと変換するメタエージェントフレームワーク「VISTA」を提案し、シミュレータのロールアウト効率を高めながらタスク成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 従来のアプローチはロールアウトを静的なログとして扱い、環境を通じた自律的なテストと洗練を行わずにハーネス（制御・評価システム）の更新を行っていた。
llm.method: ハーネスの系統を記録するハーネスグラフを維持し、過去の仮説を再利用しつつ、環境内で能動的に探索して新しいロールアウトを生成し、失敗と回復行動を調査してハーネスを反復的に修正するメタエージェントフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Pro、RoboCasa、RoboTwinベンチマークにおいて、静的な反省よりもロールアウト効率よくタスク成功率を向上させることが実証された。

2610.35044.title: DriveUniTok: A Unified Multimodal Tokenizer for Driving World-Action Models
2610.35044.abstract: World models are emerging as a fundamental component of policy learning for real-world agents, enabling agents to predict future world states and plan actions within a learned representation of the dynamic environment. Existing approaches, however, often model appearance, metric geometry represented by projected LiDAR depth, and ego motion either partially or independently, overlooking the fact that these modalities are different projections of a shared underlying world state. This separation can lead to information loss and cross-modal inconsistency, ultimately limiting downstream performance. Motivated by this unified view of the world, we propose DriveUniTok, a unified multimodal tokenizer for driving world-action models (WAMs) that encodes these modalities in a single decodable continuous latent. We freeze DriveUniTok and adapt a pretrained diffusion model, DriveUniWAM, to predict future unified latents; the tokenizer then decodes them into future appearance, projected LiDAR depth, and ego trajectories. Experiments on NAVSIM demonstrate that our unified design achieves better future prediction and planning performance at lower downstream computational cost than separate-stream alternatives. With reinforcement learning post-training, DriveUniWAM achieves a PDMS of 91.54, reaching state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated WAM-based planners.
2610.35044.tldr_en: DriveUniTok is proposed, a unified multimodal tokenizer for driving world-action models (WAMs) that encodes these modalities in a single decodable continuous latent that achieves better future prediction and planning performance at lower downstream computational cost than separate-stream alternatives.

llm.title_ja: DriveUniTok: 自動運転ワールド・アクションモデルのための統合マルチモーダル・トークナイザー
llm.tldr_ja: 外観、距離深度、エゴモーションを単一の連続潜在表現にエンコードする統合マルチモーダル・トークナイザー「DriveUniTok」を提案し、優れた将来予測と計画性能を実現した。
llm.problem: 既存のワールドモデルは外観、測距幾何学、エゴモーションを部分的にまたは独立してモデル化しており、情報の損失やクロスモーダルな不整合を引き起こす。
llm.method: 外観、投影されたLiDAR深度、エゴ軌道を単一のデコード可能な連続潜在表現にエンコードする統合マルチモーダル・トークナイザーを提案し、事前学習済みの拡散モデルを適応させる。
llm.result: NAVSIMでの実験により、分離ストリーム型の手法と比較して、より低いダウンストリーム計算コストで優れた将来予測と計画性能を実現し、SOTAを達成した。

2610.35040.title: Context-dependent Runtime Construction of Safe Regions of Attraction from Design-Time Identification for Multi-Candidate Simplex Architectures
2610.35040.abstract: Deploying safety-critical cyber-physical systems requires control strategies that reconcile high performance and adaptability with rigorous safety guarantees. Classical control strategies offer stability proofs but are conservative, while advanced optimization- and learning-based controllers achieve high performance but lack formal verification. Runtime Assurance (RTA) architectures bridge this gap by introducing their own (dis-)advantages. Safety filters use online optimization and introduce chattering, while Simplex permissiveness is bounded by the tightness of the certified Region of Attraction (RoA) of its High-Assurance (HA) controller. Targeting this conservatism, we present a two-stage RoA certification procedure leveraging contraction-based stability to establish a target set for Taylor-model-based reachability analysis. We then treat the closed-loop system under HA control as a switched system, enabling: (a) runtime construction of context-dependent safe RoA and (b) safe switching between HA candidates to optimize recovery and maximize the operating envelope of the uncertified High-Performance (HP) controller. We validate this framework on a robotic path-tracking task using a three-stage evaluation: Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) simulation for theoretical verification, high-fidelity Gazebo simulation under unmodeled dynamics, and experiments on physical hardware. Results show that the Simplex architecture maintains safety under fault injection and successfully shields a behavioral-cloning-trained HP controller. Crucially, the decision module introduces negligible overhead (0.028 ms average, 4.13 ms worst-case), consuming under 10 % of the control period.
2610.35040.tldr_en: This work presents a two-stage RoA certification procedure leveraging contraction-based stability to establish a target set for Taylor-model-based reachability analysis and shows that the Simplex architecture maintains safety under fault injection and successfully shields a behavioral-cloning-trained HP controller.

llm.title_ja: マルチ候補Simplexアーキテクチャのための設計時同定からの安全なアトラクション領域のコンテキスト依存型実行時構築
llm.tldr_ja: 収縮に基づく安定性を活用して到達可能性解析のターゲットセットを確立し、Simplexアーキテクチャによる安全性の維持と高性能コントローラーの保護を実現した。
llm.problem: 古典的な制御戦略は保守的であり、最適化や学習ベースのコントローラーは高性能だが形式検証が欠如しているため、安全性と適応性の両立が困難である。
llm.method: 収縮に基づく安定性を用いてテイラーモデルベースの到達可能性解析のためのターゲットセットを確立する2段階のRoA認証手順を提案し、文脈に応じた安全なRoAの実行時構築と安全な切り替えを実現する。
llm.result: ロボットの経路追従タスクにおいて、シミュレーションおよび実機実験により、故障注入下でも安全性を維持し行動クローン学習されたHPコントローラーを保護できることを示した。

2610.35010.title: JevVLA: Jev-Inspired Energy-Based Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Policies
2610.35010.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can select among discrete candidates for pick-and-place manipulation or generate continuous action chunks for motion control. Improving both forms of decision making through a common mechanism while retaining the capabilities of a pretrained policy is an important adaptation problem. Inspired by Jev's structured, probabilistic decision interface, we propose JevVLA, a lightweight energy-based adaptation framework for VLA policies. JevVLA instantiates this inspiration by modeling the relative quality of action proposals: with the base policy frozen, it learns a differentiable scalar energy conditioned on observations, task context, and actions, using execution feedback, expert corrections, or demonstration-derived preferences. JevVLA uses this single learned action preference function in two ways: its values compare discrete candidates, while its action gradients correct continuous actions or guide their generation. Candidate selection and continuous control thus share one trainable decision core. Each benchmark uses independently trained weights and fixed input/output encodings, while retaining the same core network with approximately 80,000 trainable parameters. On the held-out test sets, JevVLA improves task success over the respective matched base-policy controls by 1.28, 2.31, 1.60, 1.52, and 1.28 percentage points on MetaWorld MT50, VIMA, LanguageTable, LIBERO Plus, and CLIPort, respectively. These results support the feasibility of a lightweight, Jev-inspired energy model for adapting both discrete action selection and continuous action guidance. The JevVLA implementation will be open-sourced at https://github.com/ZJU4EmbodiedAI/JevVLA.
2610.35010.tldr_en: The feasibility of a lightweight, Jev-inspired energy model for adapting both discrete action selection and continuous action guidance is supported and the JevVLA implementation will be open-sourced.

llm.title_ja: JevVLA: Jevにインスパイアされた視覚言語行動ポリシー向けエネルギーベース適応
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みVLAポリシーの離散的な候補選択と連続的な行動生成の両方を単一の学習可能な決定コアで適応させる軽量なエネルギーベースのフレームワーク「JevVLA」を提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚言語行動（VLA）ポリシーにおいて、離散的な候補選択と連続的な行動生成の両方を共通のメカニズムで改善しつつ、事前学習済みポリシーの能力を維持することが課題である。
llm.method: ベースポリシーを固定したまま、観測・タスクコンテキスト・行動に条件付けられた微分可能なスカラーエネルギーを学習し、離散候補の比較と連続行動の修正を共通の決定コアで行うフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: MetaWorldやVIMAなどの複数のベンチマークにおいて、一致するベースポリシー制御と比較してタスク成功率の向上が確認された。
keywords_ja: エネルギーベースモデル

2610.35005.title: Shifted Window Temporal Transformer for YOLO-Guided Phase Recognition in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Surgery
2610.35005.abstract: Intelligent operating rooms require accurate awareness of surgical workflow for better intra-operative decisions, teamwork, and surgical documentation. Therefore, accurately recognizing surgical phase during surgery is crucial. However, previous artificial intelligence-based methods provide fluctuating predictions for the transitions, restricting their clinical use. To address this challenge, we propose a clinically meaningful framework that integrates a Swin Transformer and Temporal Transformer Encoder (TTE) for effective surgical phase recognition and a parallel YOLOv11s network for real-time surgical instrument localization. To avoid phase flickering and to produce stable workflow predictions, a causal temporal smoothing is applied. The proposed framework is tested on the Cholec80 dataset for the simultaneous recognition of the surgical phases and instruments. The overall phase recognition accuracy of this model was 92%, and the macro average F1-score was 0.86. This performance surpasses CNN based methods such as EndoNet (81.7%) and SV-RCNet (85.3%), as well as temporal convolutional and transformer-based approaches including TeCNO (88.6%), Trans-SVNet (90.9%), and LoViT (91.5%). Besides, the module of instrument detection achieved mAP@0.5 = 0.863. The reliability of the results is confirmed, obtaining a high recognition rate of the workflows, and a high accuracy of the localization of the instruments. The proposed framework can serve as a foundation for intelligent surgical assistance, enriching situation awareness, and potential robotic surgery applications. Code will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/ac005sheekar/LapChol-Surgery-Swin-Cholec80
2610.35005.tldr_en: A clinically meaningful framework that integrates a Swin Transformer and Temporal Transformer Encoder for effective surgical phase recognition and a parallel YOLOv11s network for real-time surgical instrument localization and a causal temporal smoothing is applied.

llm.title_ja: 腹腔鏡下胆嚢摘出術におけるYOLO誘導フェーズ認識のためのシフトウィンドウ時間的トランスフォーマー
llm.tldr_ja: Swin Transformerと時間的トランスフォーマーエンコーダー、並列YOLOv11sネットワークを統合した臨床的に有意義なフレームワークを提案し、優れた認識精度を達成した。
llm.problem: 従来のAIベースの手法は遷移部分で変動する予測を生成するため、臨床での使用が制限されるという課題があった。
llm.method: Swin Transformerと時間的トランスフォーマーエンコーダーを統合して効果的な手術フェーズ認識を行い、並列のYOLOv11sネットワークでリアルタイムの手術器具局所化を行い、因果的時間平滑化を適用する。
llm.result: Cholec80データセットにおいて、全体的なフェーズ認識精度92%を達成し、既存のCNNやトランスフォーマーベースの手法を上回る性能を示した。

2610.34934.title: A Certified Robustness Framework for Backdoor Poisoning Attacks using $f$-Divergences
2610.34934.abstract: Machine learning systems trained on untrusted data are vulnerable to data and backdoor poisoning attacks, in which an adversary corrupts training and test samples to manipulate predictions at inference time. Randomized smoothing yields provable defenses against such attacks, but existing applications to train-time robustness are limited to specific threat models and smoothing mechanisms. We propose a general framework that allows expressing complex adversary constraints on the number of corrupted training examples, feature and label perturbation magnitudes, and test-time corruptions. Our framework randomizes inputs by combining data subsampling with feature, label and test-sample noising. We develop a composable certification procedure based on $f$-divergences that handles arbitrary combinations of threat models and noising strategies, and recovers several prior certification regimes exactly as special cases. We demonstrate our framework experimentally by certifying, for the first time, robustness under general $\ell_p$-constrained poisoning adversaries under bagging with additive Laplace, Gaussian, and Uniform noises.
2610.34934.tldr_en: A composable certification procedure based on $f$-divergences that handles arbitrary combinations of threat models and noising strategies, and recovers several prior certification regimes exactly as special cases is developed.

llm.title_ja: f-ダイバージェンスを用いたバックドアポイズニング攻撃に対する公認頑健性フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: データサブサンプリングとノイズ付加を組み合わせ、f-ダイバージェンスに基づく構成可能な認証手順を開発することで、任意の脅威モデルや戦略に対する頑健性を証明した。
llm.problem: 信頼できないデータで訓練された機械学習システムは、推論時の予測を操作するデータおよびバックドアポイズニング攻撃に対して脆弱であり、既存の訓練時頑健性に対する防御は特定の脅威モデルに限定されている。
llm.method: データサブサンプリングと特徴・ラベル・テストサンプルのノイズ付加を組み合わせ、f-ダイバージェンスに基づく構成可能な認証手順を開発して任意の脅威モデルとノイズ戦略の組み合わせに対応する。
llm.result: 一般化されたl_p制約付きポイズニング攻撃に対するバギング下での頑健性を初めて証明した。
keywords_ja: 機械学習セキュリティ

2610.34929.title: Learning Direct Control from Optimization for Dynamic Target Tracking
2610.34929.abstract: Dynamic target tracking requires a mobile robot to maintain target visibility while navigating obstacles with smooth, feasible controls. Online trajectory optimization explicitly encodes these objectives but requires repeated numerical solving, whereas waypoint-based neural policies separate geometric prediction from control execution. We introduce LECO, a framework that transfers tracking optimization into offline learning of a direct-control policy. LECO predicts control sequences and maps them to trajectories through a differentiable kinematic model, allowing trajectory-level objectives to directly guide control learning. A decaying expert-guidance curriculum initializes effective tracking behavior and progressively shifts learning toward these task objectives. At deployment, a predictive safety lock checks short-horizon obstacle clearance and invokes a classical planning and control fallback when the predicted motion is unsafe or the target prediction is invalid. Across three simulated obstacle densities, LECO reduces root-mean-square linear jerk by 14.1--31.2\% relative to the best competing method for this metric and achieves the highest tracking success rate, with per-cycle computation times of 4.25--5.63\,ms. Experiments on two robot platforms further demonstrate tracking through indoor narrow passages and outdoor forest environments. These results demonstrate that learning direct control from optimization enables smooth and robust dynamic target tracking.
2610.34929.tldr_en: It is demonstrated that learning direct control from optimization enables smooth and robust dynamic target tracking, and LECO, a framework that transfers tracking optimization into offline learning of a direct-control policy, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: 動的ターゲット追従のための最適化からの直接制御学習
llm.tldr_ja: 追従最適化をオフラインでの直接制御ポリシーの学習に変換するフレームワーク「LECO」を導入し、スムーズで頑健な動的ターゲット追従を実現した。
llm.problem: 動的ターゲット追従ではオンラインの軌道最適化が必要だが反復的な数値解決が求められ、ウェイポイントベースの神経ポリシーでは幾何学的予測と制御実行が分離されている。
llm.method: 制御シーケンスを予測し微分可能なキネマティックモデルを通じて軌道にマッピングすることで軌道レベルの目的に直接制御学習を導かせるLECOフレームワークを提案し、安全ロック機構を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 従来の競合手法と比較して線形ジャーキを大幅に削減し、最高水準の追従成功率を達成したほか、屋内・屋外環境での実機での追従を実証した。

2610.34921.title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds
2610.34921.abstract: Physical reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality. Progress is critically constrained by the scarcity of grounded counterfactual training data, as observational videos capture only the factual trajectory that occurred. The self-evolving paradigm offers a route beyond fixed datasets by enabling models to construct their own training problems. Extending this paradigm to physics, however, requires an external source of truth that can both validate model-proposed environments and verify alternative physical outcomes under intervention. We introduce \physevolve{}, a verifier-grounded self-evolving framework that trains VLMs for causal physical reasoning from model-proposed executable worlds and simulation-authored tasks. At each round, a shared VLM proposes executable world programs and evidence schemas; a deterministic physics engine freezes each valid world, simulates matched baseline and body-elided counterfactual branches, and synthesizes discrete, answer-bound visual tasks. Exact verifier feedback from task solving updates both the shared policy via GRPO and an adaptive curriculum over physical intents. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, \physevolve{} achieves targeted gains across PhysBench, CausalPhys, and ContPhy without human intervention data, improving PhysBench Throwing by $8.8$ points and ContPhy Counterfactual Removal and Goal-Pit by $7.4$ and $24.4$ points. These gains concentrate on interaction-sensitive and altered-world questions, demonstrating zero-shot transfer of causal principles to unseen complex dynamics (cloth, fluid, soft bodies) and real-world video.
2610.34921.tldr_en: physevolve, a verifier-grounded self-evolving framework that trains VLMs for causal physical reasoning from model-proposed executable worlds and simulation-authored tasks, achieves targeted gains across PhysBench, CausalPhys, and ContPhy without human intervention data.
2610.34921.hf_summary_en: Physevolve trains vision-language models in causal physical reasoning by using a physics engine to validate self-generated executable worlds and counterfactual simulations, improving performance on dynamics benchmarks without human data.

llm.title_ja: PhysEvolve: 実行可能な世界を用いた物理的推論のための検証者基盤型自己進化
llm.tldr_ja: モデルが提案した実行可能な世界プログラムとシミュレーションタスクから因果的物理的推論のためのVLMを訓練する検証者基盤型の自己進化フレームワーク「PhysEvolve」を提案し、優れた性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 視覚言語モデル（VLM）は動力学や物理的因果関係に関する質問において信頼性が低く、観察ビデオは事実上の軌跡しか捉えないため反実仮想の訓練データが不足している。
llm.method: 共有VLMが実行可能な世界プログラムと証拠スキーマを提案し、決定論的物理エンジンがシミュレーションを行って正確な検証者フィードバックによりポリシーを更新するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 人間の介入データなしでPhysBench、CausalPhys、ContPhyにおいてターゲットとなる向上を達成し、複雑な動力学へのゼロショット転移を示した。

2610.34913.title: Quantile-Based Command-Reserve MPC for Current-Command Gimbal Pointing
2610.34913.abstract: This paper studies the constrained line-of-sight pointing control problem of a two-axis current-command gimbal subjected to mismatched mechanical disturbances. Friction, torque ripple, current-response lag, model mismatch, and limited drive commands make accurate pointing more challenging yet interesting. A quantile disturbance predictor is proposed to compensate predictable acceleration residuals and describe their remaining uncertainty, with the aid of learning median and outer quantiles from state, command, and reference histories. A tube-inspired model predictive controller is proposed to reserve command headroom according to prediction uncertainty, with the aid of calibrated radii and stage-dependent input margins. The median improves the nominal prediction, while the radius adapts the command reserve without adding optimization variables. A finite-horizon tube inclusion result is established for a specified linear error model and fixed ancillary policy; its conditions are distinguished from the approximations used in hardware. Native command bounds and a final command limiter keep the sent commands within their prescribed range. On a two-axis embedded platform, four controller configurations are compared in seven repeated trials each. The proposed configuration achieves a two-dimensional pointing root-mean-square error of $3.94 \pm 0.10$ mrad with no command-limit samples in the evaluation windows. Its performance supports the combined use of residual prediction and adaptive command margins in the tested operating condition. Solver times and logged loop overruns are reported separately for the nominal 100 Hz implementation.
2610.34913.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary hardware trial data and recomputation scripts included as ancillary files. Submitted to Journal of the Franklin Institute
2610.34913.tldr_en: A tube-inspired model predictive controller is proposed to reserve command headroom according to prediction uncertainty, with the aid of calibrated radii and stage-dependent input margins, which supports the combined use of residual prediction and adaptive command margins in the tested operating condition.

llm.title_ja: 電流指令ジンバルポインティングのための分位数ベースのコマンド予備付MPC
llm.tldr_ja: 予測不確実性に応じてコマンドの余裕を確保するチューブインスパイア型モデル予測制御を提案し、優れたポインティング精度を達成した。
llm.problem: 2軸電流指令ジンバルにおいて、摩擦、トルクのリップル、電流応答の遅れ、モデルの不一致、限られた駆動コマンドにより、正確なポインティングが困難となっている。
llm.method: 状態・指令・参照の履歴から中央値と外側分位数を学習し、予測不確実性の残差を補償する分位数外乱予測器と、予測不確実性に応じてコマンドの余裕を確保するチューブ型MPCを提案する。
llm.result: 2軸埋め込みプラットフォームを用いた評価において、コマンド制限サンプルなしで優れた2次元ポインティングの二乗平均平方根誤差を達成した。

2610.34893.title: MMGNet: Multi-Modal 6-DoF Grasp Synthesis for Cluttered Scenes
2610.34893.abstract: Grasping is a foundational capability in robotic manipulation. Scene-level 6-DoF grasp synthesis relies on point clouds for metric geometry, yet real-world point observations are often noisy, incomplete, and over-smoothed. RGB images provide object-region, boundary, and appearance cues, yet two bottlenecks limit their effective use in scene representation and local grasp reasoning. We present MMGNet, a Multi-Modal Grasp Synthesis Network that addresses these bottlenecks through hierarchical image-to-3D feature injection and rotational graspness modeling. Hierarchical injection integrates multi-scale image features throughout 3D representation formation, while the rotational graspness jointly predicts the grasp approach direction and in-plane rotation before organizing local image-informed features through grasp-shaded grouping. Ablation studies show that these two modules provide complementary gains. MMGNet achieves a mean AP of 60.34 on GraspNet-1Billion with RealSense, surpassing all compared methods. In real-world experiments with adversarial grasp objects, MMGNet improves the grasp success rate over AnyGrasp by 8.46 percentage points. \emph{Code, models, and data will be released upon publication.}
2610.34893.tldr_en: MMGNet is a Multi-Modal Grasp Synthesis Network that addresses bottlenecks through hierarchical image-to-3D feature injection and rotational graspness modeling and ablation studies show that these two modules provide complementary gains.

llm.title_ja: MMGNet: 雑然としたシーンのためのマルチモーダル6自由度grasp合成
llm.tldr_ja: 階層的な画像から3Dへの特徴注入と回転graspnessモデリングを通じてボトルネックに対処するマルチモーダルgrasp合成ネットワーク「MMGNet」を提案し、優れた成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 実世界の点群観察はノイズが多く不完全であり、RGB画像は外観の手がかりを提供するが、シーン表現や局所的把持推論での効果的利用にはボトルネックがあった。
llm.method: 3D表現形成全体にマルチスケール画像特徴を統合する階層的画像-3D特徴注入と、把持アプローチ方向と面内回転を共同予測する回転graspnessモデリングを組み合わせたネットワークを提案する。
llm.result: GraspNet-1Billionで最高性能を達成し、敵対的な把持物体を用いた実世界実験においてAnyGraspよりも把持成功率を向上させた。

2610.34873.title: Localization-Uncertainty-Aware UAV Swarm Search for GNSS-Denied Maritime Surveillance
2610.34873.abstract: This paper studies UAV swarm search in GNSS-denied maritime environments, where inter-UAV ranging drives cooperative localization and uncertainty propagates along the multi-hop reference chain, affecting connectivity, collision avoidance, and search effectiveness. We propose an uncertainty-aware control barrier function (CBF) framework approximating cascading localization covariance through Fisher information matrices. First, the cascading covariance model captures how ranging noise and neighbor uncertainty accumulate along the localization chain. Second, uncertainty-tightened CBFs incorporate the covariance model and its rate into margins for connectivity maintenance and collision avoidance, with conditional invariance and graceful-degradation bounds. Third, a hierarchical Voronoi-target strategy with formation keeping supports efficient forward-looking coverage. The distributed controller is validated with a standard unbiased extended Kalman filter in the loop. The framework is demonstrated on several polygon shapes and swarm sizes from 6 to 30 sUAVs. An estimator-in-the-loop run completes the search in 302.5 s, 20 Monte Carlo deployments confirm repeatable completion with all local QPs feasible and containment in at least 98.97% of UAV-frames, and six MBZIRC runs provide estimator-in-the-loop evidence. The source code is publicly available.
2610.34873.tldr_en: An uncertainty-aware control barrier function (CBF) framework approximating cascading localization covariance through Fisher information matrices is proposed, which captures how ranging noise and neighbor uncertainty accumulate along the localization chain.

llm.title_ja: GNSSの届かない海上監視のためのローカライゼーション不確実性を考慮したUAVスウォーム探索
llm.tldr_ja: フィッシャー情報行列を用いてカスケード状の測位共分散を近似する不確実性考慮型コントロールバリア関数（CBF）フレームワークを提案し、スウォーム探索の有効性を示した。
llm.problem: GNSSの届かない海上環境におけるUAVスウォーム探索では、UAV間の測距が協調測位を駆動する一方で不確実性がマルチホップの参照チェーンに沿って伝播し、接続性や衝突回避に悪影響を及ぼす。
llm.method: フィッシャー情報行列を通じてカスケード状の測位共分散を近似し、接続性維持と衝突回避のマージンに共分散モデルを組み込んだ不確実性考慮型CBFフレームワークと階層的ボロノイ目標戦略を提案する。
llm.result: 6〜30機のsUAVを用いたシミュレーションおよびMBZIRCの実行により、全てのローカルQPが実行可能であり信頼性の高い探索完了が確認された。
keywords_ja: コントロールバリア関数

2610.34849.title: Physics-Informed and Data-Driven Composite Disturbance Separation and Predictive Control for Airborne Electro-Optical Gimbals with Multiple Constraints
2610.34849.abstract: This paper studies the constrained pointing control problem of airborne electro-optical gimbals subjected to composite periodic and aperiodic disturbances. Under carrier vibration, input delay, and actuator constraints, achieving line-of-sight stabilization and tracking is challenging. A disturbance-separated model predictive control (MPC) scheme is proposed to compensate these heterogeneous disturbances according to their physical characteristics. An adaptive periodic observer predicts multi-harmonic vibrations over the MPC horizon using linear-regression frequency estimation. A linear observer estimates the aperiodic disturbance, and a bounded long short-term memory (LSTM) network predicts its change over the input delay. Embedding periodic predictions into the MPC model while applying aperiodic compensation outside the optimizer limits amplification of aperiodic estimation errors and improves pointing accuracy under frequency changes and parameter mismatch.
