On the stated headroom envelope, input-set tightening provides feasible commands within the prescribed limits, and a regional practical tracking bound is established under explicit input-sequence and predicted-state margin conditions. A UAV-mounted two-axis gimbal platform is assembled for comparative indoor hovering experiments, complemented by simulations under frequency changes and parameter mismatch. In the reported trials, the proposed method achieves yaw and pitch relative-angle root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 0.770 degrees and 0.350 degrees, reducing tracking errors by 25.1% and 45.9% compared with linear active disturbance rejection control.
2610.34849.comment: 20 pages, 8 figures. Includes supplementary derivations and proofs. Demonstration video included as an ancillary file

llm.title_ja: 複数制約を持つ空中電気光学ジンバル向けの物理情報およびデータ駆動型複合外乱分離・予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: 物理特性に応じて異種外乱を補償する外乱分離型モデル予測制御スキームを提案し、従来のリニア外アクティブ外乱拒絶制御と比較して追従誤差を大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: キャリアの振動、入力遅延、アクチュエータ制約の下で、空中電気光学ジンの視線安定化と追従制御を達成することは困難である。
llm.method: 適応型周期オブザーバと線形オブザーバ、および境界付きLSTMネットワークを組み合わせて周期外乱と非周期外乱を分離・予測し、MPCモデルに組み込んで入力セットの引き締めを行う。
llm.result: UAV搭載の2軸ジンバルプラットフォームを用いた実験において、追従エラーを大幅に削減し、優れたポインティング性能を実証した。

2610.34839.title: Behavioural Quality Is Not Learning Utility: Objective Mismatch in Human Behaviour Models for Robot Learning
2610.34839.abstract: Human behaviour models are increasingly used to provide simulated human interactions for training robots via reinforcement learning (RL). Existing approaches primarily evaluate these models according to how closely their generated behaviours resemble real human data, while their usefulness as training partners is less commonly assessed. This creates a potential objective mismatch: a model that performs well according to behavioural evaluation metrics may not necessarily provide useful training experiences for downstream robot policy learning. Across two human-robot interaction (HRI) domains, highway driving and object handover, we evaluate different types of human behaviour models using common generative-model evaluation metrics. We consider multiple human trajectory representations and compare the resulting evaluations with the downstream performance of RL policies trained using the corresponding models. We find that existing behavioural evaluation metrics do not consistently predict downstream policy performance across domains and trajectory representations, while their evaluations are sensitive to the choice of trajectory representation. We also show that even when the true testing behaviour distribution is known, training against a different distribution may yield better downstream performance than training directly against the true distribution.
2610.34839.tldr_en: It is found that existing behavioural evaluation metrics do not consistently predict downstream policy performance across domains and trajectory representations, while their evaluations are sensitive to the choice of trajectory representation.

llm.title_ja: 行動の品質は学習の有用性ではない：ロボット学習のための人間行動モデルにおける目的のミスマッチ
llm.tldr_ja: 既存の行動評価指標は、ドメインや軌道表現をまたいで下流の方策性能を一貫して予測するわけではないことが分かった。
llm.problem: 人間行動モデルの評価指標と下流のロボット方策における学習有用性の間にミスマッチが存在する。
llm.method: 2つのHRIドメインにおいて、複数の軌道表現を用いた人間行動モデルの評価と強化学習方策の下流性能を比較した。
llm.result: 既存の行動評価指標は、ドメインや軌道表現をまたいで下流の方策性能を一貫して予測せず、表現の選択に敏感であった。

2610.34837.title: Beyond Behaviour: A Stimulus-Response Safety Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.34837.abstract: Humans exhibit biological sensitivity to safety-critical stimuli that can trigger defensive action. Across three models and two video benchmarks, we investigate whether similar responses emerge in vision-language-action models by examining their internal representations and action tendencies in response to visible hazards and harmful consequences. Our findings suggest that task execution may remain the default response even when danger is internally registered.
2610.34837.journal_ref: The Science of Physical AI Safety workshop at CoRL 2026

llm.title_ja: 行動を超えて：ビジョン・言語・行動モデルの刺激-反応安全性評価
llm.tldr_ja: 危険が内部で認識されている場合でも、タスク実行がデフォルトの応答であり続けることが示唆された。
llm.problem: VLAモデルが可視的な危険や有害な結果に対して防御的行動のトリガーとなる生物学的感応を示すかどうかは不明である。
llm.method: 3つのモデルと2つのビデオベンチマークを対象に、目に見える危険や有害な結果に対する内部表現と行動傾向を調査した。
llm.result: 危険が内部で認識されている場合であっても、タスクの実行がデフォルトの応答のままであることが示唆された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.34789.title: ISB-NMPC: Interception-Oriented Spherical-Bearing Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors
2610.34789.abstract: Quadrotor interceptors equipped with strapdown cameras offer a low-cost solution for physically countering unauthorized UAVs. However, this configuration inherently couples vehicle maneuvering and camera pointing, creating a conflict between rapid closing and maintaining target visibility. We present interception-oriented spherical-bearing nonlinear model predictive control (ISB-NMPC), which couples spherical-bearing prediction with nonlinear quadrotor dynamics to jointly optimize target-directed closing motion and visibility. An attitude-compensated extended Kalman filter on S^2 estimates target bearing motion, compensates for perception delay, and predicts target bearings to guide scale-adaptive detection. Across 30 paired simulation trials, ISB-NMPC achieves an interception success rate of 86.7%, the highest among the evaluated controllers, with a mean per-trial target-visible time of 99.11%. Outdoor flights demonstrate acquisition of a 30 cm target at approximately 150 m, with interceptor speed reaching 17 m/s in the long-range flight and approximately 14 m/s while pursuing a quadrotor-towed maneuvering target. The software and hardware are open source at https://github.com/HOLYNOTBAD/ISB-NMPC and https://github.com/HOLYNOTBAD/holydrone, respectively.
2610.34789.comment: 9 pages, 10 figures, and 1 table. Submitted to IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics

llm.title_ja: ISB-NMPC：クアッドローター向け迎撃指向型球面ベアリング非線形モデル予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: 球面ベアリング予測と非線形ダイナミクスを結合し、目標への接近動作と視認性を共同で最適化するISB-NMPCを提案した。
llm.problem: 機体の機動とカメラの向く方向が結合するため、迅速な接近と目標視認性の維持の間で競合が発生する。
llm.method: 球面ベアリング予測と非線形クアッドローターダイナミクスを結合し、接近と視認性を共同最適化するISB-NMPCを提案した。
llm.result: シミュレーションで86.7%の迎撃成功率を達成し、屋外飛行において30cmの目標捕捉と最高17m/sの速度を確認した。

2610.34745.title: SceneAgent: An Agentic Pipeline from 3D and 4D Captures to Simulation Environments
2610.34745.abstract: Visual captures provide detailed scene appearance, but converting them into interactive simulation environments requires object reconstruction, physical modeling, and correction of intermediate errors. We present SceneAgent, an agentic pipeline that coordinates these steps through simulator-based visual inspection and repair. The pipeline processes 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), photogrammetry, LiDAR captures, AI-generated 3DGS scenes, and 4D videos of dynamic scenes, and combines object segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation, and deformable simulation. To support policy learning, SceneAgent generates diverse object variants ("digital sisters") and scripted demonstrations. On a cluttered bin scene from GraspClutter6D, SceneAgent raises F1 at 1 cm for every coding agent with scorable outputs both with and without its skills, and its reconstructions are better than SimFoundry: all agent configurations exceed SimFoundry's F1 score, with a best of 60.75% versus 6.9%. On three dynamic scenes from 4DCodeBench, SceneAgent raises the mean dynamic IoU of Gemini 4 Argon from 0.86% to 99.09%. We further demonstrate diverse simulated interactions and preliminary policy transfer to a real robot.
2610.34745.tldr_en: SceneAgent is presented, an agentic pipeline that coordinates these steps through simulator-based visual inspection and repair and combines object segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation, and deformable simulation and demonstrates diverse simulated interactions and preliminary policy transfer to a real robot.

llm.title_ja: SceneAgent：3Dおよび4Dキャプチャからシミュレーション環境へのエージェント型パイプライン
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレータベースの視覚的検査と修復を通じてオブジェクト再構築などを調整するエージェント型パイプラインSceneAgentを提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚的キャプチャをインタラクティブなシミュレーション環境に変換するには、オブジェクト再構築や物理モデリング、エラー修正が必要である。
llm.method: シミュレータベースの視覚的検査と修復を通じて各ステップを調整するエージェント型パイプラインSceneAgentを構築した。
llm.result: GraspClutter6Dの散らかったシーンにおいてF1スコアが大幅に向上し、動的シーンのIoUも大きく改善した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション環境
エージェント型パイプライン

2610.34740.title: Networked Humanoid Intelligence: Communication, Coordination, Collaboration, and Social Interaction
2610.34740.abstract: Humanoid robots are moving from laboratory platforms toward connected fleets that share workspaces, infrastructure, tasks, and knowledge with other robots and humans. As deployments grow, the operation and improvement of each humanoid depend on information exchanged across the network. However, existing research has largely studied humanoids as individual systems. This survey examines networked humanoid intelligence through four functions of information exchange: communication, coordination, collaboration, and social intelligence with human interaction. We first establish the foundations of networked humanoid systems, define the question addressed by each function, and connect them through a common factory scenario. We review the literature along six dimensions: interaction architecture, exchanged information, physical coupling, operating timescale, system scale, and embodiment. We separate results obtained with physical and simulated humanoids from those based on other robotic platforms or disembodied agents, because the latter do not fully capture humanoid-specific constraints such as balance, whole-body motion, contact, and physical interaction. We examine hardware, datasets, and benchmarks, and distinguish risks handled locally from those networking introduces, such as stale information or unsafe knowledge propagation. Finally, we identify open problems in control-aware networking, compact body-centric messages, physically grounded coordination, network- and embodiment-aware knowledge sharing, fleet-level social consistency, and accountable human oversight.
2610.34740.tldr_en: This survey examines networked humanoid intelligence through four functions of information exchange: communication, coordination, collaboration, and social intelligence with human interaction, and identifies open problems in control-aware networking, compact body-centric messages, physically grounded coordination, and network- and embodiment-aware knowledge sharing.

llm.title_ja: ネットワーク化されたヒューマノイド知能：通信、協調、協力、および社会的相互作用
llm.tldr_ja: 情報交換の4つの機能を通じてネットワーク化されたヒューマノイド知能を調査し、未解決の課題を特定した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの導入が増加する一方で、既存の研究は主に個別のシステムとして研究してきた。
llm.method: 通信、協調、協力、人間との社会的相互作用という4つの情報交換機能を通じて文献を調査した。
llm.result: ネットワーク化されたヒューマノイドシステムの基礎を確立し、制御対応型ネットワーキングなどの未解決問題を特定した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.34717.title: VLA-HWBench: Where the Time Goes When VLA Models Run on Edge Hardware
2610.34717.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly run on edge devices aboard robots, where inference latency constrains closed-loop robot control. However, it remains unclear how to design VLA models, their inference software and edge hardware so that robots can run VLA inference in real time. Most VLA models report only task success, while prior studies cover limited action-generation strategies, divide inference into at most three stages, and lack comparisons of inference optimizations on the same models. Therefore, we introduce VLA-HWBench, a benchmark that measures 18 open VLA models on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395, with a seven-stage inference breakdown. Our study reveals three insights. First, action-generation strategy matters more than model size. It dominates 14 of 19 Jetson configurations, latency varies by $82\times$ on Jetson and $157\times$ on AMD, and parameter count explains at most 15% of latency variance. Models that generate long action chunks in a few flow-matching steps keep up with control, whereas token-by-token decoding does not. Second, kernel fusion with 4-bit weights helps most, running $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 2.6-2.9$\times$ faster than PyTorch with torch.compile, but it exists for only these two models and only on the Jetson. Optimization also moves the time to the stages it shortens least, as CPU preprocessing grows from 12% to 39% of the GR00T N1.7 call. Third, after optimization, memory bandwidth limits only the stages that process few tokens on the Jetson, such as the denoising steps, whereas software limits all other stages, from unfused kernels to serial preprocessing on the host CPU. Overall, low-latency edge VLAs should use few action-generation iterations, inference software should extend kernel fusion and low-bit weights to more models and platforms, and edge hardware needs high memory bandwidth and a fast host CPU.
2610.34717.tldr_en: VLA-HWBench is introduced, a benchmark that measures 18 open VLA models on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395, with a seven-stage inference breakdown, and reveals three insights that suggest low-latency edge VLAs should use few action-generation iterations, inference software should extend kernel fusion and low-bit weights to more models and platforms, and edge hardware needs high memory bandwidth and a fast host CPU.

llm.title_ja: VLA-HWBench：VLAモデルがエッジハードウェアで実行される際の時間の行方
llm.tldr_ja: 18のオープンVLAモデルを測定するベンチマークを導入し、低遅延エッジVLAに関する3つの洞察を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 推論遅延がロボットの閉ループ制御を制約する中で、リアルタイム実行のための設計方法は不明確である。
llm.method: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor等で18のオープンVLAモデルを7段階の推論内訳で測定するベンチマークを導入した。
llm.result: アクション生成戦略がモデルサイズよりも重要であり、カーネル融合や低ビット量子化が有効であることを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.34708.title: Resource-Performance Trade-offs in Intra-Aisle Robotic Picking: A Discrete-Event Simulation Comparison of Shuttle Configurations With and Without an Onboard Tote Lift
2610.34708.abstract: This study compares two implemented intra-aisle robotic-picking configurations through discrete-event simulation. Without an onboard tote lift, two level-captive shuttles serve the two tested levels; with the lift, one shuttle remains on its horizontal level and its onboard mechanism moves the order tote to allow picks from the adjacent upper level. Thirty configuration-task-size experiments (n = 1-15 locations; ten replications each) yield 300 replication-level cycle-time observations. Two-sided Welch tests are applied to the replication means, with Holm adjustment across the 15 comparisons. The onboard-tote-lift configuration has longer mean cycle time at all tested task sizes. At n = 15, the means are 299.477 and 333.231 s/cycle, respectively: a 33.753 s increase (11.27%). The corresponding cycle-time-derived item rates are 180.314 and 162.050 items/h (-10.13%). These rates are calculated as 3600n divided by the scenario-mean cycle time; they are not measurements of the combined concurrent capacity of two level-captive shuttles. Importantly, task locations are sampled from different eligible-level sets in the two configurations, so the result concerns the implemented configuration-and-task-generation packages, not the isolated effect of a five-second tote-lift operation under identical picked locations. The study quantifies a cycle-performance difference alongside a reduction from two dedicated shuttles to one within the tested two-level block; it does not quantify system-level maximum throughput, investment cost, or reliability.

llm.title_ja: 通路内ロボットピッキングにおけるリソースと性能のトレードオフ：オンボードトートリフト有無のシャトル構成の離散事象シミュレーション比較
llm.tldr_ja: 離散事象シミュレーションを用いて、オンボードトートリフトの有無による2つの通路内ロボットピッキング構成を比較した。
llm.problem: 異なるシャトル構成間におけるリソースと性能のトレードオフが十分に定量化されていない。
llm.method: 離散事象シミュレーションを用いて30の構成・タスクサイズ実験を実施し、サイクルトップを比較した。
llm.result: オンボードトートリフト構成はすべてのテスト済みタスクサイズにおいて平均サイクルタイムが長くなった。
keywords_ja: 離散事象シミュレーション

2610.34674.title: Benchmarking Obstacle-Conditioned Safety in Household Robot Navigation
2610.34674.abstract: Safe household navigation requires robots to regulate clearance and speed according to what an obstacle is and how close it is, without unnecessary conservatism. Yet existing evaluations do not test whether semantic safety distinctions are reflected in continuous motion. To that end, we introduce OSMA-Bench, an Obstacle-Conditioned Safe Motion Adaptation Benchmark built on spatially matched scenario sets that differ only in obstacle type. We also propose the \emph{Semantic Sensitivity Index} (SSI), which measures whether clearance and distance-dependent speed and smoothness follow the caution ordering of obstacles. Evaluating VLM-based and vision-language-action (VLA) policies on the benchmark, we find that neither consistently adapts its motion to obstacle safety, even with explicit safety prompts. Our analysis shows that the policies can correctly distinguish obstacles by safety relevance but fail to reflect this distinction in the motion parameters or actions they produce. For VLM-based policies, which recognize the obstacle and then generate a navigation program, adding an explicit parameter-inference step between these two stages improves adaptation. These findings expose a gap in \emph{semantic-to-motion grounding}, highlighting the need to translate semantic caution into appropriately safe motion.
2610.34674.tldr_en: OSMA-Bench is introduced, an Obstacle-Conditioned Safe Motion Adaptation Benchmark built on spatially matched scenario sets that differ only in obstacle type, and the SSI is proposed, which measures whether clearance and distance-dependent speed and smoothness follow the caution ordering of obstacles.
2610.34674.hf_summary_en: The study introduces a benchmark and metric to evaluate whether robot navigation policies adapt continuous motion to obstacle safety semantics, revealing a gap in translating semantic caution into safe movement.

llm.title_ja: 家庭用ロボットナビゲーションにおける障害物条件付き安全性のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 障害物タイプが異なるシナリオセットに基づいたベンチマークを導入し、ポリシーのセマンティック・モーション接地における課題を暴露した。
llm.problem: 既存の評価では、意味的な安全性の違いが連続的な動作に反映されているかどうかがテストされていない。
llm.method: 障害物タイプのみが異なるシナリオからなるOSMA-Benchを導入し、セマンティック感度インデックス（SSI）を提案した。
llm.result: ポリシーは障害物を正しく区別できるものの、動作パラメータや行動にその区別を反映させることができていないことが判明した。

2610.34663.title: Video World Models Need Predictable Latents
2610.34663.abstract: Video world models trained on large-scale robot data promise a safe and scalable approach for learning and evaluating policies that act in the physical world. However, they still struggle with long-horizon rollouts and out-of-distribution generalization, and they remain computationally demanding at inference time. Typically, video world models make predictions in the latent space of a reconstruction-trained autoencoder, which however is not directly optimized for dynamics modeling. On the other hand, world models designed for latent planning usually optimize latents to be predictable, but they forgo accurate prediction of observations in pixel space. In this paper, we show that it is possible to achieve the best of both worlds: a latent geometry optimized to make future prediction as simple as possible without sacrificing accurate prediction of future observations. More precisely, we find that temporal objectives for representation learning, paired with a past-conditioned decoder architecture, lead to consistent improvements in generative video world models at the same training budget. The gains include up to 5x cheaper inference, over 7x faster training, and 15-24% lower pixel and perceptual errors out of distribution and over long horizons. Our world models also agree more closely with real-world policy evaluation when using a vision-language model to judge task success from their pixel-space predictions. Overall, our study indicates that temporal predictability is an important design criterion for the latent space of video world models, and provides concrete guidance on how to incorporate it into the training of autoencoders.
2610.34663.tldr_en: This study indicates that temporal predictability is an important design criterion for the latent space of video world models, and provides concrete guidance on how to incorporate it into the training of autoencoders.

llm.title_ja: ビデオ世界モデルには予測可能な潜在空間が必要である
llm.tldr_ja: 表現学習の目的関数と過去条件付きデコーダアーキテクチャの組み合わせにより、生成ビデオ世界モデルが継続的に改善されることを示した。
llm.problem: ビデオ世界モデルは長期ロールアウトやOOD一般化に苦労し、推論時に計算負荷が高い。
llm.method: 時間的予測可能性を重視した表現学習の目的関数と過去条件付きデコーダを組み合わせた訓練手法を提案した。
llm.result: 推論コストの最大5倍削減、学習の7倍以上の高速化、OODおよび長期でのピクセル誤差の削減を達成した。

2610.34650.title: Dream to Assist: Intent-Conditioned World Models for Shared Vehicle Control
2610.34650.abstract: Assistive agents in shared-control settings face a dual challenge: acting proactively to align with the human's intentions while remaining legible enough for the human to comprehend and fluently respond in real time. We present Dream2Assist, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for tightly-coupled shared decision making that addresses both sides of this challenge. Our approach extends a recurrent state-space world model with intent inference, enabling an assistive policy trained via fictitious co-play to anticipate and support discrete human objectives without overriding human agency. Beyond the computational framework, we describe the full deployment pipeline needed to translate a world-model-based policy into a safe, human-centered system in a resource-efficient way. Crucially, we address the sim-to-real-human gap via policy down-selection and reward restructuring within an iterative human-machine interface design. We validate the framework through three human-subjects studies and a preliminary on-vehicle deployment spanning two qualitatively distinct domains: high-speed racing (N=30) and urban driving with richer intent structure (N=10). Our results demonstrate that intent conditioning yields measurable improvements in torque alignment and collision rate. We surface key design insights and practices for deploying learning-based assistive agents in safety-critical, real-time human-robot teaming.
2610.34650.tldr_en: This work presents Dream2Assist, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for tightly-coupled shared decision making that addresses both sides of this challenge, and extends a recurrent state-space world model with intent inference, enabling an assistive policy trained via fictitious co-play to anticipate and support discrete human objectives without overriding human agency.

llm.title_ja: Dream to Assist: Intent-Conditioned World Models for Shared Vehicle Control
llm.tldr_ja: 人間との緊密な協調意思決定に向け、意図推論と仮想共同プレイを組み込んだモデルベース強化学習フレームワーク「Dream2Assist」を提案する。
llm.problem: 人間の意図に先回りしつつリアルタイムで理解・応答しやすい協調エージェントの構築は、人間の主体性を損なわないという課題がある。
llm.method: 再帰型状態空間世界モデルに意図推論を拡張し、仮想共同プレイで訓練された補助ポリシーを用いて人間の目的を予測・支援する。
llm.result: 意図条件付けにより、トルクの整合性と衝突率が測定可能に改善されることを実証した。
keywords_ja: 人間機械インターフェース

2610.34649.title: RobotAgentBench: Towards Open-world Robot Autonomy
2610.34649.abstract: Recent advances in vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) have significantly improved robotic manipulation, yet deploying robots in the open world demands a higher level of autonomy beyond executing predefined tasks. Robot agents offer a promising paradigm for this transition, integrating task discovery, contextual reasoning, physical execution, and adaptive recovery into a closed interaction loop. However, existing benchmarks largely evaluate isolated capabilities, failing to capture the complexity of open-world robot autonomy. We introduce RobotAgentBench (RAB), a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating robot agents in realistic, open-world household environments. Through an agent-assisted, human-in-the-loop real-to-sim pipeline, RAB constructs 50 diverse household layouts with interactive objects and physically grounded tasks, encompassing 90 atomic tasks, 18 short-horizon tasks, 8 long-horizon tasks, and 4 open-ended scenarios. RAB provides a multi-level evaluation of robot agent capabilities: (1) task-level assessments systematically examine five complementary dimensions: task discovery, context reasoning, manipulation, failure recovery, and robustness; (2) scenario-level evaluation assesses how agents integrate these capabilities to autonomously fulfill high-level user needs. Furthermore, RAB enables systematic comparisons of standalone VLA/WAM models and diverse robot agent architectures under a unified planning-execution-verification framework. Extensive experiments reveal substantial gaps between manipulation and autonomy, demonstrate the advantages of agentic architectures and recursive self-improvement, and highlight the remaining challenges toward open-world robot autonomy.
2610.34649.tldr_en: This work introduces RobotAgentBench (RAB), a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating robot agents in realistic, open-world household environments and enables systematic comparisons of standalone VLA/WAM models and diverse robot agent architectures under a unified planning-execution-verification framework.

llm.title_ja: RobotAgentBench: Towards Open-world Robot Autonomy
llm.tldr_ja: 現実的なオープンワールドの家庭環境でロボットエージェントを評価するための包括的ベンチマーク「RobotAgentBench (RAB)」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは孤立した能力の評価が主であり、オープンワールドでのロボット自律性の複雑さを捉えきれていない。
llm.method: エージェント支援によるヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループのリアル・ツー・シムパイプラインを用いて、多様な家庭環境レイアウトとグラウンディングされたタスクを構築する。
llm.result: マニピュレーションと自律性の間に大きな乖離があることを明らかにし、エージェント型アーキテクチャの利点を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットエージェント

2610.34638.title: Intrinsic Goals for Autonomous Agents: Hierarchical Exploration Captures Future Volitional Action in Drosophila
2610.34638.abstract: Animals have a remarkable capacity for autonomy---driven by intrinsic motivation---without external sensory cues or extrinsic objectives, yet the computational mechanisms behind this ability largely remain a mystery. We combine whole-brain recordings in the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster), which reveal neural representations of spontaneous exploratory decisions more than 10 seconds in advance, with a neuromechanical digital twin to test whether optimizing intrinsic goals yields realistically embodied artificial agents that quantitatively match fly behavior and internal representations of future volitional action during exploration. Our hierarchical policy selects from a discrete library of low-level motor primitives, consistent with ethological theories of behavioral syllables. We train agents without external reward using 20 intrinsic motivation algorithms spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency methods. The agents are evaluated in a virtual tethered-ball assay modeled on the fly experiment, comparing spontaneous locomotor statistics and internal representations and decoding future turn direction from kinematics and neural activity on the same timescales observed in flies. DIAYN, a hierarchical competency algorithm learning discrete policies that maximize behavioral entropy and the separability of induced sensory observations, achieves the strongest joint behavioral and neural prospective coding performance relative to flies. Its learned policies closely capture individual variability in fly exploration strategies, suggesting that this diversity serves to maximize state-space coverage at the population level. DIAYN's latent activity also closely captures the sum-difference rule for interhemispheric encoding of kinematics in biological flies. These results establish hierarchical, intrinsically motivated agents as a powerful framework for reverse-engineering animal autonomy.
2610.34638.tldr_en: It is found that DIAYN—a hierarchical competency algorithm that learns a discrete set of policies maximizing behavioral entropy and the separability of their induced sensory observations—achieves the strongest joint behavioral and neural prospective coding performance with the fruit fly.
2610.34638.hf_summary_en: Hierarchical intrinsically motivated agents trained with competency-based objectives replicate fruit fly exploratory behavior and neural representations of future actions, supporting reverse-engineering of autonomous decision-making.

llm.title_ja: Intrinsic Goals for Autonomous Agents: Hierarchical Exploration Captures Future Volitional Action in Drosophila
llm.tldr_ja: 行動エントロピーを最大化する階層的コンペテンシーアルゴリズム「DIAYN」が、キイロショウジョウバエの行動および神経の予測的コーディング性能と最もよく一致することを示す。
llm.problem: 外部の手がかりや目的がない状態での自律性の裏にある計算メカニズムは、依然として謎に包まれている。
llm.method: ショウジョウバエの全脳記録と神経力学的デジタルツインを組み合わせ、外発的報酬なしで20種の動機付けアルゴリズムを訓練・評価する。
llm.result: DIAYNはハエの探索戦略における個体差や神経の半球間エンコーディングの法則を密に捉えることができた。

2610.34593.title: What Does World Modeling Actually Improve in Robot Action Learning?
2610.34593.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) combine future-video prediction with robot action learning, yet improvements in task success alone do not reveal how predictive supervision manifests in execution behavior or whether its benefits persist under task and environmental shifts. We conduct controlled future-video prediction loss ablations within FastWAM and OpenWAM, keeping model architecture, initialization, robot training data, and training steps fixed within each model family. Under clean conditions on seen tasks, predictive supervision increases success rates by 24.38 and 72.91 percentage points, respectively. Trajectory clustering further reveals higher success rates within several coarse trajectory clusters, including cases where cluster frequencies change little, indicating that the gains are not solely reflected in changes in the prevalence of trajectory patterns. However, these benefits do not consistently persist under distribution shifts: improvements on unseen tasks vary across models and tasks, while both models exhibit low success rates under the evaluated environmental randomizations, without a consistent advantage from predictive supervision. We further introduce future-video prediction as an auxiliary training objective for $π_{0.5}$, where a lightweight Transformer predictor used only during training increases success from 82.94% to 89.19%. These findings support future-video prediction as effective auxiliary supervision for action learning, while distinguishing improved execution on familiar tasks from reliable transfer and showing that such gains need not rely on a large pretrained video diffusion transformer (DiT) in the evaluated setting.
2610.34593.tldr_en: These findings support future-video prediction as effective auxiliary supervision for action learning, while distinguishing improved execution on familiar tasks from reliable transfer and showing that such gains need not rely on a large pretrained video diffusion transformer (DiT) in the evaluated setting.

llm.title_ja: What Does World Modeling Actually Improve in Robot Action Learning?
llm.tldr_ja: 将来映像予測による教師あり学習がロボットの行動学習に果たす役割を検証し、見慣れたタスクでの実行を改善する一方で、分布シフトに対する頑健性への寄与はモデルによって異なることを示す。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデル（WAM）におけるタスク成功率の向上だけでは、予測的教師あり学習が実行挙動にどう現れるかや汎用性が不明である。
llm.method: FastWAMとOpenWAMを用いて、モデルアーキテクチャ等を固定した上で将来映像予測損失の厳密なアブレーション評価を実施する。
llm.result: クリーンな条件下の既知タスクでは成功率が大幅に向上するが、環境のランダム化などの分布シフトに対しては一貫した優位性を示さないことを発見した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.34590.title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
2610.34590.abstract: A central limitation of modern machine learning systems is the lack of formal certificates guaranteeing their behavior beyond empirical, sample-based evaluation. Sum-of-squares (SOS) methods provide such guarantees by certifying polynomial inequalities over continuous domains via semidefinite programming (SDP). While prior work has introduced SDP layers as differentiable components in neural networks, repeated learning calls can lose the computational benefit of the forward program's sparse representation. We propose Sparse SOS Layers, differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the local coordinates of the forward solve. Under a fixed template and learned objective coefficients, each layer avoids building dense certificates and reuses its sparse structure across training steps. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves up to 2.7 times speedup in total warm-call time, with nearly 100 times lower memory usage (1.7 vs. 160 GiB) for relatively large problem sizes for the tested dense parameterization. Experiments cover sparse polynomial certification, pendulum control, combinatorial relaxations, robotics projection, oscillator chains, and pose graph synchronization. A design study achieves zero certified violations across unseen problem instances and sizes, while requiring roughly 7 times fewer optimization solves than estimating gradients by perturbing the objective coefficients and re-solving the problem (finite differences). These results show that sparse certificate values can be effectively integrated into learning pipelines when the backward pass respects the verifier's structure.
2610.34590.tldr_en: These results show that sparse certificate values can be effectively integrated into learning pipelines when the backward pass respects the verifier's structure, and propose Sparse SOS Layers, differentiable value layers whose backward passes reuse the local coordinates of the forward solve.

llm.title_ja: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
llm.tldr_ja: 順伝播の解の局所座標を逆伝播で再利用することで、密な証明書の構築を避けて計算効率を高める微分可能な値レイヤー「Sparse SOS Layers」を提案する。
llm.problem: 現代の機械学習システムにおける中心的な限界は、経験的な評価を超えた動作を保証する形式的証明の欠如にある。
llm.method: 固定テンプレートと学習された目的係数のもとで、順伝播のスパース構造をトレーニングステップ間で再利用する微分可能なSOSレイヤーを設計する。
llm.result: 既存手法と比較して最大2.7倍の速度向上と、約100倍低いメモリ使用量を大きな問題サイズにおいて達成した。

2610.34583.title: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent
2610.34583.abstract: A robot searching for the source of an odor must eventually answer a notably hard question: have I arrived? Near the source, concentration gradients homogenize, turbulence corrupts the signal, and a small robot often lacks the positional accuracy to map the plume. Here, we describe a lightweight remedy inspired by a World War II statistics conundrum: the German tank problem. To approximate German armament production, Allied analysts developed an estimator based on serial numbers from captured tanks. Analogously, we use the same procedure over sampled chemical sensor readings from a robot to create estimates for the peak concentration of an odor plume, and therefore the odor's source. Treating each sensor reading as an observation, our unbiased estimator needs only a running maximum and a sample counter. A confidence bound turns both numbers into a principled rule that the robot or UAV can use to determine whether it should keep searching for the odor source. We derive the estimator and its bound, demonstrate its sample efficiency, and examine its robustness even when its assumptions fail. Finally, we summarize the estimator's role as the termination criterion for olfactory navigation.

llm.title_ja: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent
llm.tldr_ja: 第二次世界大戦のドイツ戦車問題に着想を得て、化学センサーの読み取り値から臭気源のピーク濃度を推定し探索終了を判断する軽量な推定手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 臭気源の探索において、発生源近傍では濃度勾配が均質化し、ロボット自身の位置精度も不足するため到着の判定が困難である。
llm.method: 各センサーの読み取り値を観測値とし、実行中の最大値とサンプルカウンターのみを必要とする不偏推定量とその信頼区間を導出する。
llm.result: サンプルの効率性を示し、前提が崩れた場合でも頑健性を維持できることを検証した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2610.34538.title: Dual Gradient Consensus for Adaptive Learning to Transient Out-of-Distribution Disturbances in Quadrotor Control
2610.34538.abstract: Quadrotor trajectory tracking under unmodeled disturbances often relies on online residual adaptation, but short out-domain residuals can corrupt the learned disturbance model when constant-step updates treat every residual gradient uniformly. We propose Dual Gradient Consensus (DGC), an adaptive-learning method for mixed in-domain/out-domain disturbances that retains the random Fourier feature model, offline BPTT policy, and least-squares adaptation of a prior domain-adaptive residual policy (DAPL) while modifying the online update step size. DGC compares each residual gradient with long- and short-term gradient memories, classifies the current adaptation regime, and uses a confidence map to suppress unreliable updates while recovering adaptation after persistent domain shifts. We evaluate DGC in numerical quadrotor trajectory tracking under four residuals that mix an in-domain component with short out-domain events. Compared with $L_1$-augmented MPC, RFF-based MPC, constant-step DAPL, and a frozen-parameter baseline, DGC achieves the lowest mean position RMSE in all four cases.
2610.34538.tldr_en: Dual Gradient Consensus is proposed, an adaptive-learning method for mixed in-domain/out-domain disturbances that retains the random Fourier feature model, offline BPTT policy, and least-squares adaptation of a prior domain-adaptive residual policy (DAPL) while modifying the online update step size.

llm.title_ja: クアッドローター制御における過渡的なドメイン外外乱に対する適応学習のための二重勾配コンセンサス
llm.tldr_ja: オンライン更新のステップサイズを変更することで混合外乱に対応する適応学習手法DGCを提案した。
llm.problem: 未モデル化外乱下でのトラジェクトリ追従において、定数ステップ更新がすべての残差勾配を均一に扱い、学習済みモデルを破損させる。
llm.method: 残差勾配を勾配メモリと比較し、適応レジームを分類して信頼度マップで信頼性の低い更新を抑制するDGCを提案した。
llm.result: 4つのケースすべてにおいて、ベースラインと比較して最も低い平均位置RMSEを達成した。

2610.34534.title: Multimodal Socially Aware Framework for Human-Robot Interaction in Virtual Reality
2610.34534.abstract: Social robots must coordinate speech and movement while interpreting multimodal human input. We present a multimodal framework that integrates speech, vision, and touch to generate contextually appropriate robot speech and movement. We evaluated the framework in virtual reality with 18 participants across five social interaction scenarios, comparing its performance against a human-teleoperated baseline. Although participants rated the autonomous system above the neutral midpoint for both naturalness and social appropriateness, the teleoperated baseline received significantly higher ratings on both measures. Behavioral coding and qualitative feedback revealed that conversational timing, clarification of ambiguous requests, and spatial coordination were important factors contributing to this performance gap. These findings highlight key challenges in developing autonomous robots capable of natural, multimodal social interaction.
2610.34534.tldr_en: A multimodal framework that integrates speech, vision, and touch to generate contextually appropriate robot speech and movement is presented to highlight key challenges in developing autonomous robots capable of natural, multimodal social interaction.

llm.title_ja: Multimodal Socially Aware Framework for Human-Robot Interaction in Virtual Reality
llm.tldr_ja: 音声、視覚、触覚を統合して文脈に適したロボットの言語と動きを生成するマルチモーダルフレームワークを提案し、VR環境で評価する。
llm.problem: 社会的なロボットは、マルチモーダルな人間の入力を解釈しつつ、音声と動きを適切に調整する必要がある。
llm.method: 音声・視覚・触覚を統合するフレームワークを構築し、18名の参加者を対象に仮想現実（VR）環境下で5つの社会的インタラクションシナリオを用いて評価する。
llm.result: 参加者は自律システムの自然さと社会的妥当性を中立点より高く評価したが、遠隔操作ベースラインはさらに有意に高い評価を受けた。

2610.34527.title: How High Can GPT-6 Astra Climb in Contact-Rich Manipulation? PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
2610.34527.abstract: We introduce PhysLadder, a hierarchical Sim-Real benchmark for evaluating physical interaction capabilities in contact-rich manipulation. Its 16 household tasks span three cumulative levels: contact selection and geometric alignment (L1), force regulation within sustained contact (L2), and coordinated contact reconfiguration and force regulation (L3). Each task is instantiated in physically and visually matched simulated and real-world environments, with shared task definitions and success criteria. We evaluate GPT-6 Astra zero-shot with three trials per task in each environment. Real-world success rates decline from 80.0% at L1 to 47.6% at L2 and 0.0% at L3, with corresponding simulation rates of 66.7%, 47.6%, and 0.0%. Ten of the 16 tasks have identical success counts across environments; the remaining six differ by one success out of three trials. Across both environments, recurring difficulties in spatial reasoning, contact selection, force regulation, and coordination often prevent local physical progress from accumulating into task completion. These findings characterize Astra's observed capability boundary across increasing interaction demands and, for this model, support matched simulation as a repeatable, scalable testbed for studying the sustained, coordinated physical interactions that limit reliable manipulation.
2610.34527.tldr_en: LLM4Robot-Bench is introduced, a hierarchical, paired Sim-Real benchmark for evaluating physical interaction capabilities in contact-rich manipulation, and GPT-6 Astra's observed capability boundary is characterized across increasing interaction demands.

llm.title_ja: How High Can GPT-6 Astra Climb in Contact-Rich Manipulation? PhysLadder: A hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
llm.tldr_ja: 接触を伴うマニピュレーションにおける物理インタラクション能力を評価するための階層的なシム・リアルベンチマーク「PhysLadder」を提案する。
llm.problem: 信頼性の高いマニピュレーションを制限する持続的かつ協調的な物理的インタラクションの評価基準が不足している。
llm.method: 接触選択・幾力学的位置合わせ、力制御など16の家庭用タスクを含む、シミュレーションと実世界で一致した階層的ベンチマークPhysLadderを構築する。
llm.result: GPT-6 Astraを評価したところ、実世界の成功率はL1の80.0%からL3の0.0%まで低下し、空間推論や力制御における共通の課題が明らかになった。
keywords_ja: 接触マニピュレーション
物理インタラクション

2610.34519.title: TRIAGE: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference Needs Both Reuse and Pruning
2610.34519.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are increasingly used for robot manipulation because they map camera images and a language instruction directly to actions. Robots that cannot be tethered to a workstation, such as mobile manipulators and humanoids, must run them on onboard embedded boards, where the prefill latency of the language backbone grows with the hundreds of visual tokens processed at every control step. To meet real-time limits, training-free accelerators recompute only a subset of the visual tokens and skip the rest, either by pruning them or by reusing their cached key-value (KV) states. The two options save nearly the same computation, yet existing methods apply only one of them to every skipped token. Through a token-level diagnostic, we show that which option keeps the action closer to full recomputation depends on the token's drift, the change in its shallow-layer value since its cache was computed. On both backbones tested, reusing tokens below a drift threshold was no worse than pruning them, whereas beyond it, reuse yields up to 4.4x the action error of pruning; the same diagnostic calibrates this threshold per backbone. Building on this finding, we propose TRIAGE, which deems a cache valid when its drift is below this threshold and it is not too old. TRIAGE recomputes a fixed budget of tokens, prioritizing important tokens with invalid caches, reuses every other token with a valid cache, and prunes the rest; prune-only and reuse-only methods are the two extremes of this partition. Because the budget fixes the number of recomputed tokens, it directly sets the prefill latency. On LIBERO and SimplerEnv, TRIAGE stays within 3 pp of full recomputation in average success rate while cutting prefill latency on a Jetson AGX Orin by up to 48%, and with only 7% of visual tokens recomputed, it beats the strongest baseline by 24.4 pp on LIBERO-Object.
2610.34519.tldr_en: TRIAGE is proposed, which deems a cache valid when its drift is below this threshold and it is not too old, and TRIAGE recomputes a fixed budget of tokens, prioritizing important tokens with invalid caches, reuses every other token with a valid cache, and prunes the rest.

llm.title_ja: TRIAGE: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference Needs Both Reuse and Pruning
llm.tldr_ja: トークンのドリフト状態に基づいてKVキャッシュの再利用とプルーニングを適切に組み合わせ、推論レイテンシを削減するフレームワーク「TRIAGE」を提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルをモバイルロボットやヒューマノイドの車載ボードで動作させる際、視覚トークンの増加に伴う言語バックボーンのプレフィルレイテンシが大きくなる。
llm.method: トークンの浅い層の値の変化（ドリフト）を診断し、閾値未満のキャッシュを再利用し、古いものをプルーニングする予算制約型のアプローチを設計する。
llm.result: LIBEROやSimplerEnvにおいて、フル再計算と同等の平均成功率を維持しながら、Jetson AGX Orin上でのプレフィルレイテンシを最大48%削減した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.34488.title: Models Verify Sufficiency, Not Validity: Usable Falsehoods Evade the Checks that Gaps Trigger
2610.34488.abstract: Ask a model "how many settlements did the Normans control?" and it answers that the passage does not say. Tell it "given that the Normans controlled 12 settlements of 400 inhabitants, what is the total?" and it computes 4,800. Nothing was added to the passage; the unsupported fact merely became usable. Benchmarks for unanswerable questions are built almost entirely by omission, deleting the fact a question needs and scoring refusal, so they never probe this. Holding source support fixed and varying only whether an unsupported premise is usable, flagging drops 8-30 points and commitment to an answer rises 1.5-2.3x on GSM8K across four models spanning two families and 2B-26B; all 16 paired contrasts remain significant after Holm correction. Two further manipulations reproduce it, one also on SQuAD: a fact asserted rather than asked about, and a corrupted intermediate value rather than a removed one. Models articulate the exact gap they then ignore, stating that "there is no financial information provided" for an inert premise and silently adopting a fabricated price for the same item. We read these as one behaviour: whether a model checks depends substantially on whether usable material is present, even when source support is held fixed. Because the main design never instructs models to reject premises introduced in the question, adopting such a premise can also be read as conditional reasoning, and we delimit what the design does and does not show. In the judging seat the pattern differs: asked whether the answer follows, judges pass solutions with a required step deleted 78-99% of the time at every scale tested. A natural prompt-level mitigation lowers accuracy by 22 points without improving detection.
2610.34488.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Self-Evolving Diversity-Driven Search for Robust AI Systems (EvoRobust). 5 pages plus references, 3 tables

llm.title_ja: Models Verify Sufficiency, Not Validity: Usable Falsehoods Evade the Checks that Gaps Trigger
llm.tldr_ja: 質問内に利用可能な材料が存在する場合、情報の正当性ではなく充足性のみを確認し、根拠のない偽情報でも受け入れて回答してしまうモデルの挙動を実証する。
llm.problem: 不適切な質問に対するベンチマークは情報の削除による拒否評価に偏っており、サポートされていない前提が使用可能になった際の挙動を検証できていない。
llm.method: GSM8Kなどのタスクにおいて、ソースのサポートを固定したまま、根拠のない前提が使用可能であるかどうかを変えてモデルの回答へのコミットメントを比較する。
llm.result: モデルは欠落している情報に自分で気づきつつも、同じアイテムに対する捏造された価格を無言で受け入れて回答してしまう現象を確認した。

2610.34466.title: IntNet: A Communication-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
2610.34466.abstract: Achieving safety in autonomous driving through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is a critical yet challenging task due to non-stationarity, partial observability, and the need for effective coordination among agents. Although earlier cooperative MARL methods have aimed to improve coordination by sharing encoded state observations, we find these strategies are insufficient in safety-critical scenarios. To address this gap, we present IntNet, a novel MARL framework that enhances safety by incorporating the transmission of vehicle intent and adaptive communication scheduling into a unified end-to-end learning paradigm, jointly optimising all components for safe coordination. Central to our approach is an observation prediction module that enables agents to forecast subsequent policy outputs, which they can then share across a vehicle-to-vehicle network. Our model-free architecture employs a Graph Attention Network to process incoming messages and a scheduler component to dynamically optimise the communication graph for bandwidth efficiency. We compare IntNet against state-of-the-art communicative MARL methods in complex urban environments with both autonomous and human-operated vehicles, achieving improved coordination, lower collision rates, and reducing communication efforts by up to 60\%. Through extensive experiments, we assess the framework's learning efficiency, scalability, and the balance between information sharing and bandwidth usage for collision-free trajectories.
2610.34466.journal_ref: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters ( Volume: 10, Issue: 3, March 2025)
2610.34466.tldr_en: IntNet is presented, a novel MARL framework that enhances safety by incorporating the transmission of vehicle intent and adaptive communication scheduling into a unified end-to-end learning paradigm, jointly optimising all components for safe coordination.

llm.title_ja: IntNet: A Communication-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
llm.tldr_ja: 車両の意図の送信と適応的な通信スケジューリングを統合し、安全な協調をエンドツーエンドで学習するMARLフレームワーク「IntNet」を提案する。
llm.problem: 自律走行におけるマルチエージェント強化学習（MARL）は、非定常性、部分観測性、および効果的な協調の必要性から安全性の確保が困難である。
llm.method: 車両間ネットワークでポリシー出力を予測・共有する観測予測モジュールと、グラフ注意ネットワークを用いた動的な通信スケジューラを組み込む。
llm.result: 都市環境において最先端の手法と比較して、協調の向上、衝突率の低減、通信負荷の最大60%削減を達成した。
keywords_ja: マルチエージェント強化学習

2610.34456.title: Trajectory Generation and Control for Quadrotors
2610.34456.abstract: In this project, I explored controller design and trajectory generation for a quadrotor. Differential flatness was used for trajectory generation based on one of the references. A minimum snap trajectory is generated from the given algorithm based on waypoint navigation, and a simple proportional plus derivative (PD) controller is used to track the trajectories. Simulation results are presented which generate smooth trajectories for position and velocity of the quadrotor.

llm.title_ja: Trajectory Generation and Control for Quadrotors
llm.tldr_ja: 微分平坦性と最小スナップ軌道生成を用いてクアッドローターの滑らかな位置・速度軌道を生成し、PDコントローラで追従させる。
llm.problem: クアッドローターの自律飛行において、ウェイポイントナビゲーションに適した滑らかな軌道生成とコントローラ設計が必要とされる。
llm.method: 微分平坦性に基づくアルゴリズムで最小スナップ軌道を生成し、シンプルな比例・微分（PD）コントローラを用いて制御する。
llm.result: クアッドローターの位置と速度の滑らかな軌道を生成するシミュレーション結果を示した。

2610.34454.title: Nonlinear Control of Aerial Manipulator
2610.34454.abstract: This paper presents two controllers for a quadrotor equipped with a two-DOF robot manipulator that physically interacts with the environment. Cartesian impedance and adaptive sliding mode controllers are implemented and compared for a simple hovering task in the presence of some bounded disturbance. A full dynamic model is developed, and the two above controllers are implemented with the same initial conditions and desired position.

llm.title_ja: Nonlinear Control of Aerial Manipulator
llm.tldr_ja: 2自由度マニピュレータを搭載したクアッドローターのホバリングタスクを対象に、カルテシアンインピーダンス制御と適応スライディングモード制御を実装・比較する。
llm.problem: 外乱が存在する環境下で、環境と物理的に相互作用する空中マニピュレータの安定した制御が求められる。
llm.method: 完全な動的モデルを構築し、カルテシアンインピーダンス制御と適応スライディングモード制御を同一の初期条件と目標位置で実装する。
llm.result: 境界付き外乱が存在する状況下でのホバリングタスクにおける制御性能を比較・検証した。

2610.34453.title: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation via Action Representation Pretraining
2610.34453.abstract: Large-scale vision, language, and video pretraining has substantially improved the perception and generalization capabilities of robotic manipulation models, but action generation for complex dexterous manipulation remains constrained by the scarcity of robot demonstrations. Limited robot demonstrations must be used to learn both action representations and task-conditioned action distributions, making it difficult to adequately learn action representations and, in turn, limiting the ability of downstream generative models to generate complex dexterous actions. To address this limitation, we propose ARPG (Action Representation Pretraining and Generation), which explicitly separates action representation learning from action generation: we first pretrain an action representation encoder on large-scale human manipulation data. We then freeze the encoder and train a compact generative backbone (130M parameters) to learn task-conditioned action distributions in the encoder's representation space. Experimental results show that ARPG achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DexJoCo benchmark and improves the average success rate on bimanual dexterous manipulation from 10.1% for $π_{0.5}$ to 44.7%. Scaling experiments further show that broader coverage of human manipulation behaviors effectively improves downstream performance. These results indicate that action representation pretraining provides an independent scaling dimension for improving complex dexterous manipulation capabilities.
2610.34453.tldr_en: The proposed ARPG (Action Representation Pretraining and Generation), which explicitly separates action representation learning from action generation, achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DexJoCo benchmark and improves the average success rate on bimanual dexterous manipulation.

llm.title_ja: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation via Action Representation Pretraining
llm.tldr_ja: 行動表現の学習とアクション生成を明示的に分離し、大規模な人間マニピュレーションデータから事前学習を行う「ARPG」を提案する。
llm.problem: 複雑な器用なマニピュレーションのための行動生成は、ロボットデモデータの不足によって大きく制限されている。
llm.method: 人間のデータで行動表現エンコーダを事前学習したのち凍結し、コンパクトな生成バックボーンをその空間で訓練する（ARPG）。
llm.result: DexJoCoベンチマークで最先端の性能を達成し、両手器用マニピュレーションの平均成功率をπ0.5の10.1%から44.7%へと向上させた。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.34452.title: AuRA: From Atoms to Bits through Autonomous Robot Interaction
2610.34452.abstract: Simulation enables robot-learning experiments at scale, but acquiring physics-informed digital twins often requires human manipulation and manual annotation of recorded interactions. To reduce this reliance on human effort, we present AuRA, a system that automates robot interaction and data preparation for digital-twin reconstruction. AuRA combines execution-aware grasp selection, gripper-motion measurements derived from robot states, and registered pre-interaction geometry and appearance priors. These choices enable autonomous collection, avoid reliance on visual gripper tracking, and recover object information obscured by the robot. Across 13 deformable objects, AuRA reduces active human labor and wall-clock collection time per successfully reconstructed asset by 88.5% and 55.4%, respectively. Relative to the human-collected PhysTwin baseline, AuRA improves seven of nine metrics for future prediction under known gripper motion, including a 28.1% reduction in one-way $L_1$ Chamfer distance. It also achieves similar mean silhouette IoU and Chamfer distance under the evaluated unseen interactions. These results highlight the potential of autonomous robot interaction to support more efficient digital-twin acquisition with comparable reconstruction quality.
2610.34452.tldr_en: A system that automates robot interaction and data preparation for digital-twin reconstruction with comparable reconstruction quality, AuRA combines execution-aware grasp selection, gripper-motion measurements derived from robot states, and registered pre-interaction geometry and appearance priors to enable autonomous collection and avoid reliance on visual gripper tracking.

llm.title_ja: AuRA: From Atoms to Bits through Autonomous Robot Interaction
llm.tldr_ja: 実行を考慮した把持選択やグリッパ運動計測を組み合わせることで、デジタルツイン再構築のためのロボットインタラクションとデータ準備を自動化するシステム「AuRA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 物理情報に基づくデジタルツインの取得には、人間の手動操作やインタラクションの注釈付けが必要となり多大な労力がかかる。
llm.method: 実行を考慮した把持選択、ロボット状態から得られるグリッパ運動計測、事前の幾何・外観事前分布を統合して自動収集を実現する。
llm.result: 13種の変形可能なオブジェクトにおいて、再構築されたアセットあたりの人間の労力と収集時間を大幅に削減しつつ、同等の再構築品質を達成した。
keywords_ja: 自律ロボットインタラクション

2610.34393.title: On Distributed Sensing and Adversarial Localization of Narrowband Acoustic Sources for Offshore Data Center Monitoring
2610.34393.abstract: This report investigates an acoustic surveillance framework for localizing and tracking narrowband adversarial acoustic sources that threaten offshore data centers. Unlike conventional sound source localization (SSL) methods that rely on broadband signals and compact receiver arrays, the considered scenario involves narrowband emissions and sparse sensors. In such scenarios, the observed time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) measurements are aliased and produce an ambiguous solution space, rendering conventional localization methods ineffective. To address this challenge, we integrate a mobile receiver that temporarily forms anchor pairs with selected fixed receivers, constraining the feasible solution space. The proposed two-stage pipeline first estimates the initial source position using anchor constraints, then initializes a particle filter that jointly tracks source position and velocity using one live anchor measurement and quality-adaptive fixed-pair measurements. We evaluate the proposed method through Monte Carlo acoustic simulations, ROS-Gazebo robotic demonstrations, and open-water field experiments. Our framework achieves a localization success rate of 91% in simulation, while 9 of 10 field trials show tracking error below 2m under receiver-position uncertainty and noisy sensing conditions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of passive acoustic surveillance for protecting large-scale infrastructure against acoustic threats.
2610.34393.tldr_en: The proposed acoustic surveillance framework achieves a localization success rate of 91% in simulation, while 9 of 10 field trials show tracking error below 2m under receiver-position uncertainty and noisy sensing conditions, demonstrating the feasibility of passive acoustic surveillance for protecting large-scale infrastructure against acoustic threats.

llm.title_ja: On Distributed Sensing and Adversarial Localization of Narrowband Acoustic Sources for Offshore Data Center Monitoring
llm.tldr_ja: 移動型受信機と固定型受信機を一時的に組み合わせる2段階のパイプラインにより、海洋データセンターを脅かす狭帯域音源のローカライゼーションと追跡を行うフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 狭帯域エミッションとスパースなセンサーを用いる状況では、到達時間差（TDOA）の測定値がエイリアシングを起こし従来の音源局所化が無効になる。
llm.method: アンカー制約を用いて初期位置を推定し、単一のライブアンカー測定と品質適応型固定ペア測定を用いて位置と速度を追跡するパーティクルフィルタを初期化する。
llm.result: シミュレーションで91%のローカライゼーション成功率を達成し、野外実験でも2m未満の追跡誤差を確認した。
keywords_ja: パーティクルフィルタ

2610.34370.title: ThinkLocoManip: A Whole-Body Control Agentic Harness for Legged Loco-Manipulation
2610.34370.abstract: In this paper, we propose ThinkLocoManip, an agentic harness for legged loco-manipulation designed to tackle complex, long-horizon tasks in large-scale environments. Existing approaches typically follow either direct action generation or a plan-then-act paradigm, both of which can struggle with the generalization and error-recovery capabilities required for extended task execution. In contrast, ThinkLocoManip adopts an interleaved reasoning-and-acting paradigm, allowing the agent to continuously reason about its current state, execute actions, observe their outcomes, and adapt its strategy accordingly. Building on this paradigm, our agentic harness orchestrates a suite of specialized tools for perception, navigation, manipulation, and locomotion, enabling flexible composition of heterogeneous capabilities. Unlike existing robotic agentic harnesses, ThinkLocoManip explicitly incorporates locomotion as a tool domain for agent reasoning and execution. We further design a set of skills that explicitly account for both tool usage within each functional domain and coordination across domains, supporting effective execution of complex behaviors over long horizons. To tackle task failure during long-horizon interactions, we develop keyframe thinking mechanism to preserve critical execution context and support efficient error recovery. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that ThinkLocoManip substantially outperforms representative methods based on both direct action generation and plan-then-act paradigms across challenging long-horizon legged loco-manipulation tasks. Notably, ThinkLocoManip achieves a success rate of 77%, more than twice that of the strongest plan-then-act baseline (37.1%). Our experiments further validate the effectiveness of interleaved reasoning and acting, tool orchestration, and coordinated skill execution.
2610.34370.tldr_en: ThinkLocoManip substantially outperforms representative methods based on both direct action generation and plan-then-act paradigms across challenging long-horizon legged loco-manipulation tasks and develops keyframe thinking mechanism to preserve critical execution context and support efficient error recovery.

llm.title_ja: ThinkLocoManip: A Whole-Body Control Agentic Harness for Legged Loco-Manipulation
llm.tldr_ja: 推論と行動をインタリーブさせるパラダイムを採用し、知覚・ナビゲーション・マニピュレーション・移動のツールを統合する四足歩行ロボット向けエージェントハーネス「ThinkLocoManip」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の手法は直接的な行動生成や計画・実行分離パラダイムに依存しており、長時間のタスク実行に必要な汎化やエラー回復に苦労する。
llm.method: 現在の状態を継続的に推論し、行動し、結果を観察・適応する仕組みに加え、重要な実行コンテキストを維持するキーフレーム思考メカニズムを開発する。
llm.result: 困難な長時間の四足ロコ・マニピュレーションタスクにおいて77%の成功率を達成し、既存のベースラインを大幅に上回った。
keywords_ja: ロコ・マニピュレーション
エージェントハーネス

2610.34358.title: EAST: Embodied AI Safety Testing via Systematic Fault Injection in Digital Twins
2610.34358.abstract: Task success is not a sufficient measure of safety for embodied artificial intelligence (AI), because robots may complete objectives while violating safety requirements. Existing evaluations often emphasize performance and robustness, but lack a systematic route from documented safety hazards to executable, verifiable tests. We present EAST (Embodied AI Safety Testing), a digital-twin framework that converts literature-grounded safety evidence into fault-injection tests across perception, instructions, environments, actions, and timing. EAST combines an expert-reviewed safety-fault taxonomy and eight executable operators with applicability and validity constraints. Its three-stage workflow generates test specifications, verifies fault realization during simulated execution, and independently assesses safety challenges, violations, task outcomes, and behavioral signatures using simulator-state evidence. The framework preserves execution traces and replayable records, supporting attribution and reproducibility across experiments. We evaluate EAST on six RoboTwin manipulation tasks and two policy architectures, ACT and RDT, against alternative testing strategies under matched budgets. Across five comparative campaigns, EAST targets all 74 admissible task-policy-operator combinations and obtains valid evidence for 63, while achieving safety-challenge exposure rates close to Random-Legal and Rule-Based. Moreover, 82 valid EAST executions complete their tasks despite safety violations, revealing risks concealed by success-oriented evaluation. These findings support systematic, validity-aware, reproducible safety testing beyond task-completion metrics.
2610.34358.tldr_en: EAST (Embodied AI Safety Testing), a digital-twin framework that converts literature-grounded safety evidence into fault-injection tests across perception, instructions, environments, actions, and timing, supports systematic, validity-aware, reproducible safety testing beyond task-completion metrics.

llm.title_ja: EAST: Embodied AI Safety Testing via Systematic Fault Injection in Digital Twins
llm.tldr_ja: 文献に基づく安全上のハザードを、知覚・指示・環境・行動・タイミング全体にわたる故障注入テストに変換するデジタルツインフレームワーク「EAST」を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットが安全要件に違反しながら目的を達成する可能性があるため、タスク成功率は具現型AIの十分な安全性指標ではない。
llm.method: 専門家がレビューした安全性故障分類と実行可能なオペレータを組み合わせ、テスト仕様の生成、シミュレーション実行時の検証、安全性評価を行う3段階のワークフローを構築する。
llm.result: 安全違反にもかかわらずタスクを完了する有効な実行例を多数検出し、成功重視の評価では隠蔽されるリスクを明らかにした。

2610.34356.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
2610.34356.abstract: Scaling vision-language-action (VLA) models is constrained by scarce action-labeled demonstrations and incompatible control spaces across robot embodiments. We present RynnVLA-Latent, a framework that turns heterogeneous interaction videos into scalable supervision for robot policy pretraining. At its core, RynnLAM learns continuous, 3D-grounded latent actions from visual transitions without requiring native robot controls. By combining residual future-feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision, and camera-motion decoupling, RynnLAM encourages representations that capture control-relevant motion rather than appearance changes alone. We apply RynnLAM to 30.1K hours of human, robot, and simulation videos, producing 745.52M latent-action descriptors. RynnVLA-Latent then learns to predict latent-action chunks from visual observations and language through flow matching, before adapting its pretrained backbone and action expert to embodiment-specific robot actions. The resulting 4B policy achieves 98.8% success on LIBERO, 84.7% on LIBERO-Plus without benchmark-specific adaptation, 51.9% average success across five VLABench tracks, and 88.6% average success on the RoboTwin 2.0 bimanual benchmark. It also achieves the highest observed success rates among the compared methods on six real-world manipulation tasks across dexterous-hand and mobile-gripper platforms. Together with representation ablations and data-scaling results, these findings demonstrate the potential of latent-action supervision for scaling robot policy learning beyond native action-labeled data.
2610.34356.tldr_en: RynnVLA-Latent is presented, a framework that turns heterogeneous interaction videos into scalable supervision for robot policy pretraining and demonstrates the potential of latent-action supervision for scaling robot policy learning beyond native action-labeled data.
2610.34356.hf_summary_en: RynnVLA-Latent leverages latent actions derived from diverse video to pretrain large vision-language-action policies, achieving high success across simulated and real-world robot benchmarks without embodiment-specific tuning.

llm.title_ja: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
llm.tldr_ja: 異種のインタラクション動画から3Dグラウンディングされた連続的潜在アクションを学習し、ロボットポリシーの事前学習に活用する「RynnVLA-Latent」を提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルのスケーリングは、アクションのラベル付けされたデモデータの不足やロボットの制御空間の互換性のなさによって制限されている。
llm.method: 残差将来特徴予測、カメラ補正3Dフロー教師あり学習、カメラ運動の分離を組み合わせ、ネイティブ制御なしの視覚遷移から潜在アクションを学習する。
llm.result: LIBEROで98.8%、LIBERO-Plusで84.7%の成功率を達成し、器用なハンドやモバイルグリッパを用いた実世界の6つのマニピュレーションタスクでも優れた成果を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.34286.title: ScheNav: Schematic-Guided Object Goal Navigation
2610.34286.abstract: Object goal navigation requires an embodied agent to locate and reach target objects in complex environments. Humans often rely on low-cost yet informative schematic maps, such as rough sketches or directional annotations. We develop a workflow for schematic-guided embodied navigation with two components: a training-data generation pipeline and ScheNav, a closed-loop navigation framework. Our lightweight data-generation pipeline turns 2D floorplans into navigation training environments, yielding Furnished-RPLAN, a dataset of over 33k furnished layouts with paired navigation episodes and noise-controllable schematic maps. ScheNav turns rough schematic guidance into exploration and stopping decisions by using SchemaField, a learned spatial module that fuses the guidance with accumulated observations and predicts spatial value fields. The framework updates these fields as exploration proceeds, with trajectory-based training and a cross-frame consistency objective supporting coherent guidance across changing viewpoints. ScheNav learns to use schematic guidance entirely from simulated floorplans and transfers this ability to unseen embodied environments. Experiments show improved navigation success and path efficiency across schematic maps, goal ellipses, and pointed directions, together with tolerance to the tested schematic perturbations and omissions. Together, these results demonstrate that rough schematic guidance offers a practical way to improve embodied navigation.
2610.34286.tldr_en: This work develops a workflow for schematic-guided embodied navigation with two components: a training-data generation pipeline and ScheNav, a closed-loop navigation framework that learns to use schematic guidance entirely from simulated floorplans and transfers this ability to unseen embodied environments.

llm.title_ja: ScheNav：模式図誘導型オブジェクト目標ナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレートされたフロアプランから模式図誘導の利用を学習し、未見の環境へ転移する閉ループナビゲーションフレームワークScheNavを開発した。
llm.problem: オブジェクト目標ナビゲーションにおいて、複雑な環境内で目標を見つけて到達する能力が求められる。
llm.method: 2Dフロアプランから訓練データを生成するパイプラインと、空間値フィールドを予測するScheNavフレームワークを開発した。
llm.result: 模式図、目標楕円、指し示された方向全体でナビゲーション成功率と経路効率の向上が示された。
keywords_ja: オブジェクト目標ナビゲーション

2610.34280.title: AdaPolicy: Action-Driven Anticipatory Robot Policies via Next-Chunk Prediction
2610.34280.abstract: Endowing robot policies with anticipatory capabilities has proven effective in improving control performance. However, existing methods predominantly rely on explicit supervision derived from future observations, in either pixel or latent space, at the cost of additional architectural and computational complexity. Departing from explicit future supervision, we ask whether such foresight can be elicited directly from the action signal. To this end, we propose \textbf{AdaPolicy}, an \textbf{A}ction-\textbf{d}riven \textbf{a}nticipatory policy framework that shapes future-aware representations via cascaded next-chunk prediction. Specifically, an Online Action Head jointly produces the current action chunk and an evolved latent state. Building on this state, a cascaded Unrolled Action Head forecasts the next chunk, and the resulting loss flows back through the evolved state to instill implicit foresight into the online policy. Importantly, this training-only unroll requires no future-observation encoding, keeping AdaPolicy lightweight to train with zero inference-time overhead. Experiments on MetaWorld, RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and real-world deployments demonstrate consistent gains across diverse settings, including up to $14$ percentage points on millimeter-precision tasks such as earphone assembly and shoelace threading. More details and visualizations are available at \href{https://teee111.github.io/AdaPolicy/}{https://teee111.github.io/AdaPolicy/}.
2610.34280.tldr_en: This work proposes AdaPolicy, an anticipatory policy framework that shapes future-aware representations via cascaded next-chunk prediction via cascaded next-chunk prediction, and proposes a training-only unroll that requires no future-observation encoding.

llm.title_ja: AdaPolicy：次チャンク予測による行動駆動型の先読みロボット方策
llm.tldr_ja: 明示的な将来観測の符号化を必要とせず、カスケードされた次チャンク予測を通じて暗黙的な先読みを方策に植え付けるAdaPolicyを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボット方策の先読み能力向上には将来観測に基づく明示的な指導が必要とされ、計算複雑性が増す。
llm.method: オンライン行動ヘッドとカスケードされた展開行動ヘッドを組み合わせ、次チャンク予測を通じて将来対応表現を形成するAdaPolicyを提案した。
llm.result: MetaWorldなどの多様な設定で一貫した改善を示し、ミリメートル精度のタスクで最大14ポイント向上した。

2610.34271.title: Robust Single-Parameter Point Cloud Registration using Truncated Lp Functions
2610.34271.abstract: We propose a novel method for robust point cloud registration with only one tunable parameter. Our method, dubbed TLP, uses truncated $L_p$ functions with different values of $p$ to assign priority scores to correspondences, select the hypothesis, and refine the final model. By leveraging the robustness of truncated functions, TLP effectively handles the high outlier rates commonly encountered in real-world 3D feature matching. We also exploit GPU parallelization to evaluate hypotheses efficiently, enabling registration from thousands of correspondences in under a second on average. With only one tunable parameter, our method offers greater practicality than multi-parameter methods that require dataset-specific tuning of several parameters. Evaluations on public benchmark datasets demonstrate that TLP achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art single-parameter methods. Furthermore, it outperforms two widely used multi-parameter methods on three of the four evaluated datasets while maintaining competitive runtime.
2610.34271.tldr_en: This work proposes a novel method for robust point cloud registration with only one tunable parameter, dubbed TLP, which outperforms two widely used multi-parameter methods on three of the four evaluated datasets while maintaining competitive runtime.

llm.title_ja: 切断されたLp関数を用いた堅牢な単一パラメータ点群登録
llm.tldr_ja: 切断されたLp関数を用いて対応関係に優先順位をつけ、高外れ値率を効果的に処理する単一パラメータの点群登録手法TLPを提案した。
llm.problem: 現実世界の3D特徴量マッチングでは高外れ値率に直面し、複数パラメータの調整が必要となる。
llm.method: 異なるp値を持つ切断されたLp関数を利用して対応関係の優先順位付けや仮説選択、モデル洗練を行うTLPを提案した。
llm.result: 公開ベンチマークにおいて既存の単一パラメータ手法よりも高い精度を達成し、複数パラメータ手法とも競合する実行時間を維持した。

2610.34253.title: NameTrap: Steering AI Coding Agents Toward Security Vulnerabilities via Variable Names
2610.34253.abstract: AI coding agents routinely clone repositories, install packages, and read source code obtained from the Web, so publicly hosted code becomes part of the context that shapes the code they write. We show that this Web-borne context can be weaponized without any explicit instruction. We present NameTrap, a source-code poisoning attack that only renames identifiers in third-party Python files to steer AI coding agents toward attacker-targeted Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) vulnerabilities. An attacker-side coding agent iteratively aligns identifiers with a CWE-specific naming convention and confirms through local probe completions that the renamed file elicits the target weakness, while the released bait contains neither instructions nor vulnerable statements. We evaluate NameTrap across six AI coding agents, ten underlying language models, and four vulnerability categories: CWE-78, CWE-79, CWE-327, and CWE-502. Starting from files whose clean versions never yield the targeted CWE, identifier-level manipulation achieves overall attack success rates of 22.5\% to 56.0\% across the six agents, reaching 75.0\% for certain agent--model configurations, and substantially outperforms random renaming, neutral renaming, and the prior identifier-poisoning attack XOXO. The attack remains effective under Traditional Chinese prompts and transfers across models, while a security-reminder defense fails to consistently prevent vulnerability introduction. Moreover, three AI-based security analyzers and four static analyzers report none of the targeted weaknesses in the poisoned files. These findings expose an overlooked attack surface of agents that consume Web content: seemingly harmless variable names in untrusted, Web-hosted code can compromise the security of downstream software.
2610.34253.tldr_en: NameTrap, a source-code poisoning attack that only renames identifiers in third-party Python files to steer AI coding agents toward attacker-targeted Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) vulnerabilities, is presented.

llm.title_ja: NameTrap：変数名を介してAIコーディングエージェントをセキュリティ脆弱性へ誘導する攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: 識別子をリネームしてAIコーディングエージェントを脆弱性に誘導するソースコードポイズニング攻撃NameTrapを提案した。
llm.problem: AIコーディングエージェントがWeb上のコードを取り込むことで、意図しない文脈がコード記述に影響を与える。
llm.method: サードパーティ製Pythonファイルの識別子を変更し、ターゲットのCWE脆弱性にAIコーディングエージェントを誘導するNameTrapを提案した。
llm.result: 識別子レベルの操作により、6つのエージェント全体で22.5%から56.0%の攻撃成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: AIコーディングエージェント
ソースコードポイズニング

2610.34251.title: Variational Cognitive Memory Abstraction for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.34251.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown remarkable success in robotic manipulation, yet their ability to execute long-horizon tasks remains limited by insufficient long- term memory modeling. Existing methods either rely on implicit temporal representations within policy networks, where historical information can be gradually diluted, or maintain explicit memory buffers that suffer from redundancy, noise accumulation, and inefficient retrieval. In this paper, we propose CogMemory, a novel variational cognitive memory framework that enables VLA systems to selectively preserve and reuse task-relevant historical information. Our approach encodes multimodal trajectories into compact latent memory representations through a selective state- space memory encoder, multi-slot temporal abstraction, and variational information compression. During action generation, dynamic cross-attention retrieval with gated fusion adaptively incorporates relevant memories into policy prediction. With merely 3.45M additional parameters, CogMemory stays lightweight and seamlessly fits both early- and intermediate-fusion VLA backbones. Extensive experiments on long-horizon robotic manipulation benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse VLA backbones.
2610.34251.tldr_en: This work proposes CogMemory, a novel variational cognitive memory framework that enables VLA systems to selectively preserve and reuse task-relevant historical information and stays lightweight and seamlessly fits both early- and intermediate-fusion VLA backbones.

llm.title_ja: 長期ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのための変分認知的メモリ抽象化
llm.tldr_ja: タスクに関連する履歴情報を選択的に保持・再利用できる軽量な変分認知的メモリフレームワークCogMemoryを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルの長期タスク実行能力は、不十分な長期メモリモデル化によって制限されている。
llm.method: マルチモーダル軌道をコンパクトな潜在メモリにエンコードする選択的状態空間メモリエンコーダ等のCogMemoryを提案した。
llm.result: わずか345万個の追加パラメータで軽量に動作し、長期ロボットマニピュレーションベンチマークで一貫した改善を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル
ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.34186.title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience
2610.34186.abstract: Extending Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) to humanoid robots requires coordinated whole-body control and diverse demonstrations that are costly to collect in real-world scenarios. Although egocentric human demonstrations provide a complementary source of task experience, differences in visual embodiment and missing robot proprioception complicate transfer to humanoid policies. To address these challenges, we introduce HuGe, a family of Humanoid Generalist VLAs pre-trained on over 2,000 hours of egocentric human and robot data. Specifically, HuGe employs three existing representative VLA architectures to predict latent motion tokens for a pretrained whole-body controller, together with hand-control signals. Based on this, we introduce a three-stage training pipeline that combines egocentric pre-training, humanoid adaptation, and downstream fine-tuning. To facilitate transfer across embodiments, we construct pseudo-proprioceptive states through simulation playback during pre-training and modify arm appearance in egocentric observations through re-rendering during downstream fine-tuning. With this pipeline, HuGe achieves the state-of-the-art on simulation benchmark HumanoidArena. Furthermore, real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 indicate that augmenting robot demonstrations with visually adapted egocentric demonstrations significantly increases success on a pick-and-drop task.
2610.34186.tldr_en: HuGe, a family of Humanoid Generalist VLAs pre-trained on over 2,000 hours of egocentric human and robot data, is introduced, a three-stage training pipeline that combines egocentric pre-training, humanoid adaptation, and downstream fine-tuning that achieves the state-of-the-art on simulation benchmark HumanoidArena.
2610.34186.hf_summary_en: HuGe pre-trains vision-language-action models on egocentric human and robot data with pseudo-proprioception and visual adaptation to enable whole-body humanoid control.

llm.title_ja: HuGe：一人称視点経験を活用したヒューマノイド汎用ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 2,000時間以上の一人称視点人間・ロボットデータで事前学習されたヒューマノイド汎用VLA「HuGe」を導入した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットへのVLAの拡張には、実世界での収集コストが高い多様なデモンストレーションが必要となる。
llm.method: 一人称視点データの事前学習、ヒューマノイド適応、下流ファインチューニングを組み合わせた3段階の学習パイプラインを提案した。
llm.result: シミュレーションベンチマークHumanoidArenaで最先端の性能を達成し、実世界のUnitree G1でのタスク成功率を向上させた。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.34151.title: Execution Logs Sway VLM Judges of Robot Progress
2610.34151.abstract: Vision-language models now grade robot videos, and text placed beside the frames can change their verdicts. On clips where the robot is losing progress, we add one log line saying the robot is making progress. Across Gemini, Qwen and GPT judges, this flips correct verdicts to progress 10 to 35 percentage points more often than a neutral line does. A one-line warning that the log may be wrong removes most of this effect. Selected fake "task complete" claims flip half of Qwen's correct verdicts, against a tenth for unrelated log lines. They have no detectable effect on Gemini.
2610.34151.tldr_en: On clips where the robot is losing progress, the authors add one log line saying the robot is making progress, and across Gemini, Qwen and GPT judges, this flips correct verdicts to progress more often than a neutral line does.

llm.title_ja: 実行ログがロボットの進捗に関するVLM判定を左右する
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットが失速しているクリップにおいて、進捗しているというログ行を追加すると、Gemini等の判定が正しい判定から進捗へ反転することが分かった。
llm.problem: VLMがロボットの動画を評価する際、フレーム横に置かれたテキストがその判定結果を変えてしまう可能性がある。
