llm.method: ロボットが進捗を失っているクリップに「ロボットが進捗している」というログ行を追加し、各種VLMの判定の変化を調査した。
llm.result: 中立的な行と比較して、正しい判定を「進捗している」へと反転させる割合が大幅に増加した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語モデル

2610.34147.title: PS-DLO: Property- and Spatially Aware Deformable Linear Object Manipulation Policy
2610.34147.abstract: Deformable linear objects (DLO) pose a coupled perception and control challenge: their slender geometry makes precise localization difficult, while their deformations depend on object-specific physical properties. To address this challenge, we propose PS-DLO, a property- and spatially aware DLO manipulation policy. First, contrastive image-text learning maps the initial observation to categorical descriptions of DLO properties, providing explicit physical and structural priors for action generation. Second, SAM3 extracts mask-guided features from future observations, which are distilled into the policy's action expert to encode task-relevant DLO regions and their subsequent configurations. We evaluate PS-DLO on nine real-world tasks across single-arm and bimanual platforms, training a shared multi-task policy for each embodiment. PS-DLO achieves an average success rate of 68.9%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.0 percentage points. In generalization experiments, PS-DLO achieves higher success rates than the baseline in six of seven visual-shift conditions on butterfly-knot untying. These results demonstrate that combining object-property priors with future spatial supervision improves multi-task DLO manipulation and robustness to visual variation.
2610.34147.tldr_en: Results demonstrate that combining object-property priors with future spatial supervision improves multi-task DLO manipulation and robustness to visual variation.

llm.title_ja: PS-DLO：性質および空間を考慮した変形可能線状物体の操作方策
llm.tldr_ja: オブジェクトの性質の事前知識と将来の空間的監視を組み合わせることで、マルチタスクDLO操作と視覚変化に対する頑健性を向上させた。
llm.problem: 変形可能線状物体（DLO）は、細い幾何学形状による位置特定の難しさと、物体固有の物理特性に応じた変形の問題を抱えている。
llm.method: 初期観測をDLO特性の記述にマッピングする対照学習と、将来の観測からマスクガイド付き特徴を抽出するPS-DLOを提案した。
llm.result: 9つの実世界タスクにおいて平均成功率68.9%を達成し、最強のベースラインを20.0ポイント上回った。

2610.34128.title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
2610.34128.abstract: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Experiments on benchmark datasets evaluate the proposed framework in surgical phase recognition and target tracking, including scenarios involving occlusion and entity overlap. Phantom experiments further demonstrate the feasibility of autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution performance compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.
2610.34128.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) for possible publication
2610.34128.tldr_en: A closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control.

llm.title_ja: 自律型腹腔鏡制御のためのセマンティック結合知覚フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: リアルタイムの外科的フェーズ認識とカメラ運動補償型知覚を結合した閉ループフレームワークにより、挑戦的な視覚条件下でのターゲット状態推定を改善した。
llm.problem: 従来の自律型腹腔鏡制御は視覚追跡と外科的フェーズ認識を独立して扱うため、オクルージョン等に対する頑健性が制限される。
llm.method: フェーズ依存関係を利用してターゲット状態推定を改善する、セマンティック結合型の閉ループ自律型腹腔鏡制御フレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: ベンチマークデータセットでの評価およびファントム実験において、ターゲットの視認性とタスク実行性能の向上が示された。

2610.34126.title: HumanoidNDM: Closing the Training-Deployment Gap of Motion Tracking via Humanoid Neural Dynamics Model
2610.34126.abstract: Humanoid robots have recently achieved remarkable success in motion tracking. However, during real-world deployment, robots inevitably encounter dynamics gaps arising from either extra physical disturbances or inaccurate simulation modeling, resulting in a significant training-deployment gap. Therefore, effectively leveraging real-world data to fine-tune policies represents the crucial last mile for robust deployment. To bridge this gap, we propose HumanoidNDM, an online fine-tuning framework for humanoid motion tracking driven by a real-world-trained neural dynamics model. First, in the data collection stage, we introduce a low-frequency reference perturbation method with an adaptive intensity mechanism, balancing deployment feasibility and exploration efficiency. Second, for the model training stage, we train a robust history-based, proprioceptive neural dynamics model in Euclidean space by incorporating differentiable forward kinematics, eliminating the reliance on costly motion capture systems. Finally, in the policy fine-tuning stage, we directly fine-tune the policy via backpropagated model gradients, achieving high data efficiency. Through physical validation on the Unitree G1 robot, we demonstrate that HumanoidNDM enables rapid real-world adaptation to various perturbations, representing the first online, MoCap-free fine-tuning framework for humanoid tracking policies.
2610.34126.tldr_en: Through physical validation on the Unitree G1 robot, it is demonstrated that HumanoidNDM enables rapid real-world adaptation to various perturbations, representing the first online, MoCap-free fine-tuning framework for humanoid tracking policies.

llm.title_ja: HumanoidNDM：ヒューマノイド神経力学モデルによるモーション追従の訓練・展開ギャップの解消
llm.tldr_ja: 実世界訓練された神経力学モデルによって駆動されるオンラインファインチューニングフレームワークHumanoidNDMを提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットの実世界展開において、物理的外乱や不正確なシミュレーションモデリングに起因するダイナミクスギャップが存在する。
llm.method: 適応型低周波リファレンス外乱手法を用いたデータ収集と、微分可能な順運動学を組み込んだ力学モデルの訓練、および方策の直接ファインチューニングを行うフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: Unitree G1ロボットでの実証により、多様な外乱に対する迅速な実世界適応が可能であることを示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.34108.title: RoboDuo: Attempt, Check and Atomic Recovery through Code for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.34108.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map a language instruction and the current observation directly to actions, without checking whether the instruction has been completed. For long-horizon tasks, a single failed step therefore goes unnoticed and leaves the whole task unfinished. Such failed episodes, however, often end with the task partially complete. Moreover, the unfinished steps are reusable atomic skills that recur across demonstrations. A failed attempt can thus be recovered by composing with atomic skills. We propose RoboDuo, a closed-loop dual-system framework that uses code as the interface between a coding agent and two VLAs. The agent writes a program that lets a full-task VLA attempt the whole task and checks whether it is complete; on failure, an atomic VLA finishes the remaining steps. Since the agent emits no actions and only decides which VLA for execution, RoboDuo wraps an existing full-task VLA without updating its weights. To train the atomic VLA and the coding agent with the completion-checking ability, we build LIBERO-Atomic, LIBERO-Code, and LIBERO-Judge from a single set of LIBERO demonstrations. RoboDuo consistently improves X-VLA and $π_{0.5}$ on LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO, with the largest gains on long-horizon tasks, and recovers failed rollouts of a frozen full-task VLA on a real robot.
2610.34108.tldr_en: RoboDuo, a closed-loop dual-system framework that uses code as the interface between a coding agent and two VLAs, consistently improves X-VLA and $\pi_{0.5}$ on LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO, and recovers failed rollouts of a frozen full-task VLA on a real robot.

llm.title_ja: RoboDuo：コードを介した視覚言語行動モデルのための試行、確認、およびアトミックリカバリー
llm.tldr_ja: 失敗した長期タスクを自動的に回復するため、コーディングエージェントと2つのVLAをコードで結合した閉ループフレームワークRoboDuoを提案した。
llm.problem: 長期タスクにおいて単一のステップが失敗すると、VLAはそれに気づかずタスク全体が未完了のまま終わってしまう。
llm.method: コーディングエージェントがプログラムを記述してフルタスクVLAの完了を確認し、失敗時にはアトミックVLAで残りのステップを完了する閉ループフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: LIBEROおよびLIBERO-PROにおいてX-VLAと$\pi_{0.5}$の性能を継続的に向上させ、実ロボットでのリカバリーに成功した。

2610.34105.title: X-World: Transferring Video Priors to Variable-View Robot Control
2610.34105.abstract: Video diffusion models provide a source of interaction representations for robot control, but transferring these representations requires reconciling variable camera inputs with heterogeneous action interfaces and closed-loop execution. We present X-World, a framework that transfers a video prior through a fixed-length token sequence to a shared action expert. A residual cross-view attention branch extends a pretrained video backbone to one, two, or three views while retaining its original self-attention path. A layer-aligned Q-Former aggregates backbone features, and dataset-specific modules map between native state and action interfaces and the shared action expert. Training separates video adaptation from action-only pretraining by freezing the video backbone in the latter stage, followed by joint target-domain post-training. The policy extracts video features with a single backbone pass and uses asynchronous action chunking for execution. On LIBERO, X-World reaches 98.5\% mean success; its LIBERO-trained checkpoint obtains 76.5\% on LIBERO-Plus without further adaptation. The seven-shift breakdown reveals gains in robot, language, lighting, and layout perturbations, alongside weaknesses under camera, background, and noise shifts relative to OpenVLA-OFT. On six dual-arm real-world tasks, it achieves 81.7\% mean success over 20 trials per task. Removing video adaptation or cross-view fusion produces the largest observed success drops among the tested removals.
2610.34105.tldr_en: X-World, a framework that transfers a video prior through a fixed-length token sequence to a shared action expert through a layer-aligned Q-Former aggregates backbone features, and dataset-specific modules map between native state and action interfaces and the shared action expert.

llm.title_ja: X-World：ビデオ事前学習を可変視点ロボット制御へ転移する
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ拡散モデルの表現をロボット制御へ転移するため、残差クロスビューアテンションとQ-Formerを用いたフレームワークX-Worldを提案した。
llm.problem: ビデオモデルの表現をロボット制御に転移するには、可変のカメラ入力、異種の行動インターフェース、および閉ループ実行を調和させる必要がある。
llm.method: 事前学習済みビデオバックボーンを拡張する残差クロスビューアテンションブランチと、特徴を統合するレイヤー整列Q-Formerを設計した。
llm.result: LIBEROで98.5%の平均成功率を達成し、6つの両腕実世界タスクにおいても優れた性能を示した。

2610.34093.title: LegoOcc++: Towards Consistent Open-Vocabulary 3D Occupancy Prediction
2610.34093.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction is important for embodied agents operating in complex environments whose semantic categories extend beyond fixed taxonomies. While recent studies have explored open-vocabulary occupancy in outdoor driving scenarios, indoor environments remain challenging due to dense occlusions, complex geometry, and fine-grained long-tailed semantics. To reduce the need for expensive voxel-level semantic annotations, we study a geometry-only supervision setting requiring only binary occupancy labels. We build upon Language-Embedded Gaussians as a unified representation coupling 3D geometry with language-aligned semantics. For geometry learning, we introduce an opacity-aware Poisson-based Gaussian-to-Occupancy formulation that enables stable volumetric aggregation under binary occupancy supervision. For semantic learning, we render Gaussian features into images and align them with a frozen open-vocabulary model, together with Progressive Temperature Decay to reduce feature mixing during Gaussian splatting. Building on this framework, we further introduce Instance-Level Semantic Consistency to alleviate fragmented object predictions, and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to provide informative and less redundant multi-view semantic supervision. We also extend our framework to outdoor driving scenarios to evaluate its generality across substantially different environments. Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves strong open-vocabulary occupancy performance, validating the effectiveness and generality of our framework. Code will be available at https://github.com/JuIvyy/LegoOcc.
2610.34093.tldr_en: Instance-Level Semantic Consistency is introduced to alleviate fragmented object predictions, and Covisibility-Aware Support-View Selection to provide informative and less redundant multi-view semantic supervision, and the framework is extended to outdoor driving scenarios to evaluate its generality across substantially different environments.

llm.title_ja: LegoOcc++：一貫性のあるオープンボキャブラリー3D占有予測に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: バイナリ占有ラベルのみを用いて高精度なオープンボキャブラリー3D占有予測を行う、不透明度を考慮したフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 屋内環境のオープンボキャブラリー3D占有予測は、高密度なオクルージョン、複雑な幾何学形状、および高価なアノテーションの必要性から困難である。
llm.method: 言語埋め込み型ガウス表現をベースに、不透明度を考慮したPoissonベースのガウス占有定式化と、インスタンスレベルの意味的一貫性を導入した。
llm.result: 屋内および屋外のベンチマークにおいて強力なオープンボキャブラリー占有予測性能を達成し、汎用性を実証した。
keywords_ja: オープンボキャブラリー
ガウススプラッティング
セマンティックセグメンテーション

2610.34085.title: Doppler-aided Position-Velocity Tracking of Hidden Objects using mmWave Radar
2610.34085.abstract: Safe indoor operation requires autonomous tracking of objects that are not directly visible to the robot. Optical non-line-of-sight (NLoS) methods depend on ambient lighting and scene geometry or on weak multi-bounce returns that need long acquisitions. Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers an attractive alternative: walls act as reflectors for mmWave signals, and frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radars enable fast, practical measurement of range, angle, and velocity. However, the low resolution of these radars leads to spatially ambiguous observations. The Doppler information, although particularly sensitive to target motion, remains underexplored in indoor NLoS localization: existing methods emphasize spatial representations and either collapse or discard the Doppler dimension before learning. To leverage the complete Range-Azimuth-Doppler (RAD) information, we acquire the first indoor NLoS radar dataset that pairs sequential RAD measurements with synchronized position and velocity ground truth under controlled variations in motion: 576 sequences totaling 720,856 frames across 12 trajectories of a mobile robot moving along varying speeds, starting positions, and material configurations. We then formulate NLoS tracking as sequential position-velocity estimation rather than frame-wise localization: a shared 3-D encoder processes the full RAD representation of consecutive frames, separate recurrent branches estimate position and velocity, and post-inference refinement combines the two into a motion-consistent trajectory. Our method achieves 8.95cm position and 1.75cm/s velocity errors on held-out trajectories and generalizes to unseen scenarios involving a moving human target. Together, our dataset and tracker establish a benchmark for tracking hidden moving targets with a low-cost radar.

llm.title_ja: ミリ波レーダーを用いたドップラー支援による隠蔽オブジェクトの位置・速度追跡
llm.tldr_ja: 隠蔽された動的オブジェクトを追跡するため、ミリ波レーダーの全Range-Azimuth-Doppler情報を活用する新しいデータセットと追跡手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の光学式非視距（NLoS）手法は照明や幾何学的条件に依存し、ミリ波レーダーのドップラー情報は十分に活用されていなかった。
llm.method: 連続フレームの全RAD表現を3Dエンコーダーで処理し、位置と速度を推定するリカバリー分岐と統合するトラッカーを構築した。
llm.result: 保持された軌跡において位置誤差8.95cm、速度誤差1.75cm/sを達成し、移動する人間を対象とした未見のシナリオにも汎化することを示した。

2610.34084.title: DSGN: A Dual-Stream Gated Network for Scalable Simultaneous Surveillance and Containment
2610.34084.abstract: The simultaneous surveillance and containment (SSC) problem arises in multi-robot applications such as perimeter security and environmental monitoring, where robots must survey a region of interest and coordinate to enclose targets once they are detected. Surveillance favors spatial dispersion for coverage, whereas containment requires target-centric cohesion for enclosure. This conflict makes heuristic switching unstable, and the instability becomes more pronounced as larger robotic networks introduce more inter-agent and agent-target relations. End-to-end DRL reduces reliance on hand-crafted switching, but conventional single-stream policies often mix surveillance and containment cues in one shared feature space that could entangle dispersion-oriented and target-centric signals and weaken task transitions. In this paper, we propose the Dual-Stream Gated Network (DSGN), an architecture designed to address scale-amplified task-transition difficulties by separating surveillance and containment into specialized representation streams and coordinating them through a context-aware gating mechanism. A probabilistic prior further regularizes the gating process, reducing ambiguous intermediate decisions and supporting clearer behavioral transitions under large-scale interaction complexity. Evaluations show that DSGN maintains strong task efficacy and scalability under constant-density cross-scale settings. Additional ablation and phase-specific evaluations show that the proposed dynamic gating mechanism and probabilistic prior support effective task arbitration and reliable mode switching in both pure surveillance and task-switching scenarios. The source code is available at https://github.com/zuozysama/DSGN.
2610.34084.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. Full version of the paper accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), October 2026
2610.34084.tldr_en: The Dual-Stream Gated Network (DSGN), an architecture designed to address scale-amplified task-transition difficulties by separating surveillance and containment into specialized representation streams and coordinating them through a context-aware gating mechanism, is proposed.

llm.title_ja: DSGN：スケーラブルな同時監視と包囲のためのデュアルストリームゲートネットワーク
llm.tldr_ja: マルチロボットによる監視と包囲の相反する目的を効果的に切り替えるため、文脈に応じたゲート機構を持つDSGNを提案した。
llm.problem: 監視には空間的分散が必要である一方、包囲にはターゲット中心の凝集が必要であり、この矛盾がヒューリスティックな切り替えを不安定にする。
llm.method: 監視と包囲を専門の表現ストリームに分離し、文脈に応じたゲート機構と確率的事前分布で調整するDSGNアーキテクチャを提案した。
llm.result: 定常密度およびクロススケールの設定において、強力なタスク効率とスケーラビリティ、および信頼性の高いモード切り替えを維持することを示した。

2610.34060.title: Learning Interaction-Aware Path Corrections from Unlabeled Trajectories: A LiDAR-Based Sim-to-Real GNN Framework for Construction Robots
2610.34060.abstract: Construction robots operating near workers require navigation that can anticipate human motion while remaining robust to dynamic and unstructured site conditions. However, existing social navigation methods depend on hand-crafted interaction rules, labeled demonstrations, or robot-specific control policies, limiting their scalability and transferability in construction environments. We propose a real-time, LiDAR-only framework that learns interaction-aware path corrections from unlabeled demonstrations. Constant-velocity extrapolation generates residual learning targets, while a GNN models relationships among the robot, pedestrians, and goal context. During deployment, an extended Kalman filter tracks LiDAR detections to construct dynamic graphs, and the GNN offsets planner-generated waypoints through a planner-agnostic interface. Within the bricklaying trial, the GNN reduced path irregularity by 39.2\% and increased minimum TTC. Across Dynablox sequences, it increased minimum TTC by 38.3\% while producing shorter, smoother paths than the baselines. Ablation studies supported a 1.0-s prediction interval and confirmed the benefits of target context, reflection augmentation, and feature normalization.
2610.34060.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, submitted to Automation in Construction
2610.34060.tldr_en: A real-time, LiDAR-only framework that learns interaction-aware path corrections from unlabeled demonstrations, while a GNN models relationships among the robot, pedestrians, and goal context is proposed.

llm.title_ja: ラベルなし軌道からのインタラクションを考慮した経路修正の学習：建設ロボット向けのLiDARベースSim-to-Real GNNフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ラベルなしデモンストレーションからインタラクションを考慮した経路修正を学習する、リアルタイムなLiDAR専用フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のソーシャルナビゲーション手法は手動のルールやラベル付きデモンストレーションに依存し、建設環境でのスケーラビリティが低い。
llm.method: GNNを用いてロボット、歩行者、ゴールの関係をモデル化し、LiDAR検出を追跡してプランナー非依存のインターフェースでウェイポイントを修正する。
llm.result: レンガ積み試行で経路の不規則性を39.2%削減し、Dynabloxシーケンスで最小TTCを38.3%増加させ、より短く滑らかな経路を生成した。
keywords_ja: ソーシャルナビゲーション

2610.34059.title: Lightweight Change Detection for Adaptive Collective Perception in Dynamic Environments
2610.34059.abstract: Swarm robotics enables scalable inspection through collective perception, where robots infer environmental properties from distributed observations. A common benchmark considers robots exploring black-white tiled environments and determining the majority tile type. While most work studies static environments, dynamic environments remain underexplored. We study collective perception in dynamic environments where the tile proportion and the spatial correlation of surface patterns may change over time. To enable implementation on resource-constrained robots, we integrate a lightweight change detection mechanism into a Bayesian collective decision-making framework that resets robot beliefs when distribution shifts are detected. The proposed detector requires constant memory and constant per-sample computation, unlike two recent competitive approaches that store the full sample stream, making it suitable for memory-constrained robots. We further introduce a method that detects spatially correlated sampling and adapts sampling intervals online to mitigate correlation effects. Our simulation results in Webots show competitive change detection delays, more consistent precision across communication settings, and improved decision accuracy under changing spatial correlations.
2610.34059.tldr_en: This work integrates a lightweight change detection mechanism into a Bayesian collective decision-making framework that resets robot beliefs when distribution shifts are detected, and introduces a method that detects spatially correlated sampling and adapts sampling intervals online to mitigate correlation effects.

llm.title_ja: 動的環境における適応型集合知覚のための軽量な変化検知
llm.tldr_ja: 分布のシフトが検出されたときにロボットの信念をリセットする軽量な変化検知メカニズムを、ベイジアン集合意思決定フレームワークに統合した。
llm.problem: 静的環境の研究が多い一方、タイル比率や空間相関が変化する動的環境における集合知覚は十分に探求されていない。
llm.method: 定数メモリと定数のサンプル毎計算量を必要とする軽量な変化検知器をベイジアン集合意思決定フレームワークに統合した。
llm.result: Webotsのシミュレーションにおいて、競争力のある変化検知遅延、一貫した精度、変化する空間相関下での精度向上の改善を示した。

2610.34054.title: Extended LASMP: Language Aided Subset Sampling Based Motion Planner for Drone Navigation
2610.34054.abstract: This paper proposes a command-aligned sampling distribution that incorporates navigation commands directly into the exploration process to improve the efficiency of sampling-based motion planning for quadcopters in three-dimensional environments. Inspired by the Language-Aided Subset Sampling Motion Planner, this paper extends command-aware subset sampling to aerial systems. Subset sampling is generalized to command-aligned regions, enabling structured 3D exploration while preserving probabilistic completeness. Natural language instructions are grounded into yaw-conditioned and altitude-aware geometric constraints using a prompt-based large language model for entity extraction and instruction validation. Extensive simulations in complex environments demonstrate that the proposed method generates collision-free, consistent trajectories while significantly reducing sampling effort compared to uniform RRT-based planners.

llm.title_ja: Extended LASMP：ドローンナビゲーションのための言語支援型サブセットサンプリングベースモーションプランナー
llm.tldr_ja: 3次元環境におけるクアッドコプターのサンプリングベースモーションプランニングの効率を向上させるため、ナビゲーションコマンドを探索プロセスに直接組み込むコマンド整合サンプリング分布を提案する。
llm.problem: 3次元環境でのクアッドコプターのサンプリングベースモーションプランニングにおいて、効率的な探索が求められている。
llm.method: コマンド整合領域へのサブセットサンプリングの一般化を行い、大規模言語モデルを用いたプロンプトベースのエンティティ抽出と命令検証によって自然言語指示を幾何学的制約に接地する。
llm.result: 複雑な環境での広範なシミュレーションにおいて、一様なRRTベースのプランナーと比較してサンプリング労力を大幅に削減しつつ、衝突のない一貫した軌道を生成した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.34051.title: BEHAVIOR-Spatial Benchmark: Evaluating Spatial Understanding for Robotics
2610.34051.abstract: Robot tasks require grounding spatial language in physical scenes, but task success alone cannot establish whether spatial instructions are followed. We present BEHAVIOR-Spatial, a benchmark built on BEHAVIOR-1K that measures spatial question answering, point-based target grounding, and robot action to examine how VLM spatial understanding relates to VLA behavior. It comprises 3,256 spatial questions across 49 activities, 1,240 grounding queries across 14 manipulation tasks, and action evaluations covering those 14 tasks and 10 navigation tasks. Our manipulation protocol evaluates held-out configurations and instruction following when the requested target changes within a fixed training layout. The baseline achieves 41.6% on held-out configurations but only 16.1% under changed instructions. VLM adaptation and robot-data pretraining provide limited improvements, whereas oracle visual target cues raise these rates to 60.3% and 38.0%, respectively. Perception evaluations reveal policy-dependent correlations between VLM question-answering and grounding accuracy and VLA manipulation performance. Together, these findings motivate evaluating spatial instruction following alongside task completion and examining when spatial perception performance translates into robot behavior. Project website: https://arielchen07.github.io/behavior-spatial/.
2610.34051.tldr_en: BEHAVIOR-Spatial is presented, a benchmark built on BEHAVIOR-1K that measures spatial question answering, point-based target grounding, and robot action to examine how VLM spatial understanding relates to VLA behavior.

2610.34041.title: T-ConSG: A LiDAR-Based Real-Time Temporal Construction Scene Graph for Dynamic and Evolving Environments
2610.34041.abstract: Dynamic and continuously evolving environments present significant challenges for robotic mapping and scene understanding, particularly on construction sites where moving agents, temporary obstacles, and persistent structural changes coexist. While dynamic and long-term SLAM methods can detect motion and environmental changes, their outputs are predominantly metric representations that provide limited structure for higher-level spatial and temporal reasoning. This paper presents a LiDAR-based real-time temporal construction scene graph (T-ConSG) that jointly represents free-space regions, static objects, dynamic objects, and environmental events with spatial-relational and event-participation edges. The proposed framework incrementally constructs the graph from LiDAR-derived geometric evidence, maintaining persistent free-space and static-object information while tracking dynamic objects. Changes in accumulated spatial evidence are further represented as explicit installation and removal events, allowing the graph to capture both transient dynamics and persistent environmental evolution. We demonstrate the proposed representation through three complementary application studies: dynamics-aware navigation in a bricklaying testbed, construction progress monitoring on the ConSLAM dataset, and online change detection in a simulated construction environment. The results demonstrate that the proposed T-ConSG provides a unified representation for organizing spatial and temporal information and supports robotic reasoning across environments containing both short-term dynamics and persistent changes.
2610.34041.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
2610.34041.tldr_en: A LiDAR-based real-time temporal construction scene graph (T-ConSG) that jointly represents free-space regions, static objects, dynamic objects, and environmental events with spatial-relational and event-participation edges is presented.

llm.title_ja: T-ConSG：動的および発展する環境のためのLiDARベースのリアルタイム時空間建設シーングラフ
llm.tldr_ja: LiDARベースのリアルタイム時空間建設シーングラフ（T-ConSG）を提案し、自由空間、静的・動的物体、環境イベントを空間関係およびイベント参加エッジで統合的に表現する。
llm.problem: 動的で変化する建設現場において、従来のSLAM手法は高レベルな推論に必要な構造を提供しない指標表現にとどまっている点。
llm.method: LiDARの幾何学的証拠からグラフをインクリメンタルに構築し、自由空間や静的物体を維持しつつ動的物体を追跡する。
llm.result: れんが積みのナビゲーション、建設進捗モニタリング、オンライン変化検知の3つの応用研究を通じて、空間・時間情報を統合的に整理できることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2610.34040.title: Cut a Wall, See a Wall: Identity Substitution in Occluded Point-Cloud Perception for Construction Robots
2610.34040.abstract: Construction robots must label building elements they can only partly see. We show that when occlusion at test time removes whole regions of a scene, rather than parts of an object as in training, point-cloud segmentation networks do not simply miss the hidden elements: they relabel them, and the errors collapse onto a single sink class. With fixed synthetic layouts the column absorbs up to 70% of all test points; with randomized layouts the sink moves to the stair, predicted at 4.5-5.4x its true share across three training seeds. Baseline mIoU falls to 0.15-0.27 (fixed) and 0.36-0.72 (randomized), and up to 269 whole objects vanish in a single test set. Appending 14 hand-computed geometric features per point (GPE) restores mIoU to 0.54-0.92 and removes 64-100% of whole-object losses in every run, for PointNet++ and a PTv3-style transformer in both layout regimes; on real S3DIS scans it removes every whole-wall loss (10 to 0). In an as-built column check computed from the predictions, GPE raises the share of correctly checked views from 17-58% to 71-92%. Feature permutation on fixed, randomized and real scenes explains the pattern: each class relies on whichever cue is stable in its training data, position for height-banded slabs and beams, intrinsic shape for walls and stairs once their position varies. Occlusion augmentation is a strong alternative on mIoU, but in every setting it loses more whole objects than GPE (e.g., 25-35 vs. 0).
2610.34040.tldr_en: It is shown that when occlusion at test time removes whole regions of a scene, rather than parts of an object as in training, point-cloud segmentation networks do not simply miss the hidden elements: they relabel them, and the errors collapse onto a single sink class.

llm.title_ja: 壁を切断して壁を見る：建設ロボットのための隠蔽点群認識におけるアイデンティティ置換
llm.tldr_ja: テスト時に隠蔽によってシーン全体が消失すると、点群セグメンテーションネットワークは隠れた要素を見落とすだけでなく再ラベル付けし、単一のシンククラスにエラーが集中することを示す。
llm.problem: テスト時の隠蔽により点群セグメンテーションネットワークが隠れた要素を誤って再ラベル付けし、特定のクラスにエラーが集中してしまう点。
llm.method: 点ごとに14個の手動計算による幾何学的特徴（GPE）を追加し、PointNet++やPTv3スタイルTransformerに適用する。
llm.result: GPEの追加によりmIoUが大幅に改善され、合成データおよび実際のS3DISスキャンにおいてオブジェクト全体の消失が効果的に削減された。
keywords_ja: 点群セグメンテーション

2610.34034.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework
2610.34034.abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) enables fine-grained sensing of spatial relationships between wireless devices. The WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) toolbox demonstrated that WiFi-CSI measurements collected during robot motion, combined with odometry, can be used to synthesize virtual antenna arrays, enabling motion-induced bearing estimation in multi-robot experiments. However, deploying the WSR approach has remained challenging due to its limited integration with standard robotics tools and reliance on deprecated WiFi-CSI acquisition hardware. This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo. The framework generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization. It further supports processing both simulated and real WiFi-CSI data for direct comparison and validation. Our aim is to make WSR-style sensing accessible as a modular sensing modality for robotic research. We validate our framework by comparing simulated and real-world experiments using TurtleBot3 robots, and demonstrate its use for bearing estimation and robot localization. This work lowers the barrier to entry for WiFi-CSI-based sensing in multi-robot systems and provides a foundation for integrating WiFi-CSI sensing with multi-modal perception for localization and coordination. All code and experimental details are publicly available at https://github.com/baharhaghighat/DARS_2026_Dijkstra_et_al
2610.34034.tldr_en: This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo and generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization.

llm.title_ja: マルチロボットシステムにおけるモーション誘起WiFi-CSIセンシングの実現：シミュレーションフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットシミュレータGazebo内にWSRセンシングパイプラインを統合し、現実的な物理信号特性を持つ合成WiFi-CSI測定値を生成するオープンソースのシミュレーションフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: WSRアプローチの展開は、標準的なロボットツールとの統合の欠如や、推奨されないハードウェアへの依存により困難であった点。
llm.method: Gazeboシミュレータ内でWSRセンシングパイプラインを統合し、ロボットの動きを利用して仮想アンテナアレイを合成する。
llm.result: TurtleBot3ロボットを用いたシミュレーションと実世界実験の比較により、方位推定やロボットの自己位置推定に利用できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーションフレームワーク

2610.34031.title: ElevateHead: Decide Once, Then Commit: When the Action Head Matters for Multimodal Imitation
2610.34031.abstract: Robots that learn from people often see several valid ways to do the same task: pass an obstacle on the left or on the right, open the microwave or move the kettle first. A policy that re-decides at every step can waver between these ways mid-task. We ask when the action head (the part of a policy that turns the state into actions) matters, and how it should make this choice. On a controlled task, heads that sample one way succeed far more often than a head that averages the ways when the demonstrations contain several ways and the state gives no hint which to take (+0.72 success with two ways); this trend was not reproduced on the other tasks we ran. We then present ElevateHead, a head that decides once at a learned decision point, commits to that choice for the episode, and exposes the choice as an input a user can set. We designed it by diagnosis: each version was frozen and tested on tasks it had not seen, and the next version changed only what a measured failure pointed to; predictions were registered before each run. The first four versions each fell below BeT on at least one held-out task. The fifth completed all four subtasks of the held-out Franka Kitchen task in 45.2% of episodes against 29.3% for BeT, the strongest baseline across our tasks (+0.160, 95% CI [+0.129, +0.188]); when a mode was forced, the first completed subtask matched it in 95% of successful episodes. Diagnosis also located where commitment breaks: varied start positions (repaired on the controlled task: commitment 0.22 to 0.81, success 0.74 to 0.91) and varied object placement (partly repaired: in an exploratory variant, commitment 0.03 to 0.59 on aligning with no detectable change in success). On held-out block stacking, version 4 was comparable to BeT and did not exceed it. A real-robot test with predictions fixed in advance is planned for a follow-up version of this paper.
2610.34031.tldr_en: ElevateHead is presented, a head that decides once at a learned decision point, commits to that choice for the episode, and exposes the choice as an input a user can set.

llm.title_ja: ElevateHead：一度決定し、それに従う：マルチモーダル模倣学習においてアクションヘッドが重要となる理由
llm.tldr_ja: 学習された決定ポイントで一度だけ決定を下し、その選択をエピソード全体にわたって維持するアクションヘッド「ElevateHead」を提案する。
llm.problem: 毎ステップで再決定を行うポリシーは、タスク中に複数の有効な方法の間で揺らぎが生じる点。
llm.method: 学習された決定ポイントで一度だけ意思決定を行い、その選択をエピソード全体で固定し、ユーザーが入力として設定できるようにする。
llm.result: Franka Kitchenタスクのホールドアウト評価において、ベースラインであるBeTを上回る完了率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.34028.title: Explaining Navigation Decisions: Stage-Aware Visual Attribution for Vision-Language Navigation
2610.34028.abstract: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly enable robots to follow language instructions, understanding their navigation decisions becomes important for reliable deployment. Existing explainability methods overlook a key challenge in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN): evidence for the current action may be distributed across historical and current observations and associated with different instruction stages. We identify instruction-stage insensitivity, where existing methods produce similar explanations despite changes across different navigation stages. To address this issue, we propose a stage-aware attribution framework for VLN. We first construct action-conditioned temporal instruction--visual attributions across observations. These attributions are projected into instruction space to estimate stage associations, which guide the aggregation of relevant historical evidence for refining the current explanation. An instruction-guided spatial filter further suppresses isolated responses while preserving compact, instruction-relevant regions. Experiments across multiple VLN policies and benchmarks show improved attribution quality over existing methods. We further demonstrate that our method acts as a diagnostic tool for analyzing failure cases, and validate its applicability to real-world navigation on a Unitree G1 robot.
2610.34028.tldr_en: A stage-aware attribution framework for VLN that identifies instruction-stage insensitivity, where existing methods produce similar explanations despite changes across different navigation stages, and demonstrates its applicability to real-world navigation on a Unitree G1 robot.

llm.title_ja: ナビゲーション決定の説明：視覚言語ナビゲーションのためのステージ認識型視覚アトリビューション
llm.tldr_ja: 既存手法の指示ステージ感度の低さを解決するため、視覚言語ナビゲーション（VLN）に向けたステージ認識型アトリビューションフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の解釈可能性手法は、現在の行動の根拠が過去および現在の観測に分散しているというVLNの課題を見落としている点。
llm.method: 行動条件付きの時間的指示・視覚アトリビューションを構築し、指示空間に射影してステージとの関連性を推定することで関連履歴を統合する。
llm.result: 複数のVLNポリシーとベンチマークにおいて既存手法を上回るアトリビューション品質を示し、Unitree G1ロボットでの実世界ナビゲーションに適用できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2610.33966.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
2610.33966.abstract: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), egocentric AI assistants on wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we propose InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction between human and AI assistant. Unlike existing robot-centric simulators, InteractiveWorld lets the assistant guide a human agent who observes the scene, understands instructions, and acts independently. It thus realistically simulates how AI assistant collaborates with human: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment executes actions and updates what they see next. Building on it, we introduce InteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories. In each task, the assistant guides the human in real time, and every instruction shapes the outcome, which is scored by verifiable, state-based rewards. Experiments with 12 frontier MLLMs show they are still far from reliable assistants. Even the strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, achieves at most 20% and 25% on long-horizon Guidance and Planning tasks, respectively. Overall, our work offers a verifiable platform and a rigorous evaluation set, laying a solid foundation for research on interactive MLLM assistants that truly help people in the physical world.
2610.33966.tldr_en: This work proposes InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction between human and AI assistant, and introduces InteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories.
2610.33966.hf_summary_en: InteractiveWorld provides a verifiable simulation environment and benchmark to evaluate whether multimodal language models can reliably guide humans through physical tasks.

llm.title_ja: InteractiveWorld：より優れたインタラクティブなMLLMアシスタント構築のための検証可能な人間中心環境
llm.tldr_ja: 人間とAIアシスタントの間で閉ループ対話を行うための初の検証可能な環境「InteractiveWorld」と、120のマルチタスクからなるベンチマーク「InteractiveBench」を提案する。
llm.problem: AIアシスタントの物理世界での支援能力をテストするには通常本物の人間が必要であり、費用がかかりデータが稀少である点。
llm.method: AIアシスタントがシーンを観測し指示を出す人間エージェントを誘導し、人間が自律的に行動して環境がそれを実行・更新するシミュレーション環境を構築する。
llm.result: 12の最先端MLLMを評価した結果、最良のモデルでも長期的なタスクにおいて不十分であり、信頼性の高いアシスタントにはまだ遠いことが示された。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル
シミュレーション環境
インタラクティブアシスタント

2610.33959.title: I Won't Know Until I Try: Interactive Information Gathering for Long-Horizon Manipulation
2610.33959.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation often depends on object properties that cannot be reliably inferred from appearance alone. Physical interaction can reveal these properties, but it can also change the world in ways that invalidate subsequent actions. We present a task and motion planning (TAMP) framework that integrates task-directed interactive information-gathering with interleaved planning and execution. Building on PDDLStream, our framework plans optimistically with these interactive actions, verifies their outcomes during execution, and adapts the remaining plan by retaining still-applicable actions and replanning only the connections needed to continue execution. We evaluate the framework in simulation and on a real robot across tasks that require determining whether an object is movable, a pen has ink, a drawer can be opened, or a container is empty. These experiments demonstrate how interaction-driven state updates and recovery replanning support continued execution under uncertain outcomes and external disturbances.
2610.33959.tldr_en: A task and motion planning (TAMP) framework that integrates task-directed interactive information-gathering with interleaved planning and execution and demonstrates how interaction-driven state updates and recovery replanning support continued execution under uncertain outcomes and external disturbances.

llm.title_ja: 試してみるまで分からない：長期マニピュレーションのためのインタラクティブ情報収集
llm.tldr_ja: タスク指向のインタラクティブな情報収集と計画・実行のインターリーブを統合したタスク・モーションプランニング（TAMP）フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 長期マニピュレーションは見た目から推論できない物体特性に依存することが多く、物理的インタラクションは後続の行動を無効化する可能性がある点。
llm.method: PDDLStreamをベースに、インタラクティブな行動を楽観的に計画し、実行中に結果を検証しながら、残りの計画を再利用して必要な部分だけ再計画する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実ロボットによる実験を通じて、不確実な結果や外乱の下での継続的な実行をサポートできることを実証した。
keywords_ja: タスク・モーションプランニング

2610.33947.title: Learning Functional Specialisation for Bimanual Robotic Control
2610.33947.abstract: Bimanual robotic control requires simultaneous management of distinct functional demands under motor noise, energetic costs, and communication delays. We investigate how learning responsibility should be organised across modular controllers and the two arms in a simulated musculoskeletal system with two communicating recurrent controllers. Using a 2 x 2 design, we compare differential versus shared controller objectives and fixed versus balanced hand-task assignments. Task-aligned functional specialisation was strongest when differential objectives were combined with a fixed assignment aligned with contralateral control routing. This condition achieved the highest canonical-task performance and control efficiency, reaching 81.33% bimanual success. Its advantage over shared objectives increased with motor noise but narrowed under stronger energy penalties. Stronger specialisation also reduced hand-role flexibility: reversing the hand roles decreased bimanual success by 80.46 percentage points under Differential-Fixed training, compared with 1.51 percentage points under Shared-Balanced training. These results show that controller objectives and hand-task experience jointly determine functional organisation. Stronger role-specific specialisation favours performance and efficiency when roles remain stable, whereas more distributed training favours interchangeability when roles change.

llm.title_ja: 両手型ロボット制御における機能特化の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 両手型ロボット制御では、運動ノイズ、エネルギーコスト、通信遅延の下で異なる機能的要求を同時に管理する必要がある。
llm.method: 2つの通信するリカレントコントローラーを持つシミュレーション上の筋骨格系において、異なるコントローラー目的と固定対等な手のタスク割り当ての2x2デザインを用いて学習責任の組織化を比較する。
llm.result: 微分目的と対側制御ルーティングに合わせた固定割り当てを組み合わせた場合に、機能的特化が最も強くなり、81.33%の両手成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: モジュール型コントローラー

2610.33941.title: TurboWAM: Learning What Matters for Fast World Action Models
2610.33941.abstract: World action models have demonstrated promising performance in robot policy learning, yet their high inference latency remains a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment. Recent approaches have sought to improve inference efficiency by reducing test-time future-frame imagination or accelerating action prediction. However, these methods often leverage representations from all video world model layers without explicitly considering their varying relevance to action prediction, leading to redundant computation and suboptimal representation utilization. In this work, we propose TurboWAM, a fast world action model that efficiently aggregates structured world representations conditioned on action predictions. Specifically, TurboWAM introduces a structured world representation aggregation module that adaptively fuses representations from different world model layers according to their relevance to the evolving action denoising state. Furthermore, TurboWAM employs a structured action supervision mechanism that adaptively modulates gradients from action supervision across different world model layers during backward propagation, facilitating world representation learning. During inference, by reducing the number of world model layers executed and caching relevant representations across action denoising steps, TurboWAM substantially reduces computational overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that TurboWAM achieves low inference latency while maintaining competitive task success rates compared with state-of-the-art methods.
2610.33941.tldr_en: This work proposes TurboWAM, a fast world action model that learns to efficiently aggregate and optimize world representations for action prediction and employs a world model gradient modulation mechanism that decomposes action-supervision gradients into a layer-shared component and layer-specific residual components, enabling more balanced gradient propagation across world model layers.

llm.title_ja: TurboWAM：高速な世界行動モデルのために重要な要素を学習する
llm.tldr_ja: 行動予測に関連する構造化された世界表現を効率的に統合し、競争力のある成功率を維持しながら低い推論レイテンシを実現する高速世界行動モデル「TurboWAM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルにおける高い推論レイテンシが、実世界への展開における重要なボトルネックとなっている点。
llm.method: アクションデノイジング状態との関連性に応じて異なる世界モデル層からの表現を適応的に融合する構造化世界表現集約モジュールを導入する。
llm.result: 複数のロボットマニピュレーションベンチマークにおいて、最先端手法と同等の成功率を維持しつつ低い推論レイテンシを達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.33929.title: WebViSE: Scaling Visual Design Intelligence from the Open Web for LLM Website Generation
2610.33929.abstract: Large language models have made remarkable strides in website development, enabling complete and interactive web experiences to be built from natural-language instructions with far less effort. Yet, non-expert users often struggle to articulate sophisticated visual and interaction designs in natural language. Meanwhile, the open web already contains a vast reservoir of such design knowledge, embodied in mature website implementations. To this end, we introduce Website-derived Visual Skill Extraction (WebViSE), a framework that automatically abstracts these implementations into reusable Visual Skills and builds a structured Skill library. To scale the library, WebViSE organizes its Skills in a multi-parent DAG and jointly evolves Skill descriptions and DAG structure using Skill-conditioned Potential Queries, enabling efficient matching between diverse user instructions and relevant Skills. The auto-evolved structure outperforms non-hierarchical LLM retrieval baselines at only 39.09% of the estimated retrieval cost with Qwen3.8-Max. For any models, WebViSE can be directly injected as plug-and-play guidance, enabling diverse models to produce more visually compelling and aesthetically refined web pages. For open-source models, WebViSE can be used to build a data-synthesis pipeline that internalizes visual design intelligence into model weights. Experiments across multiple web development benchmarks and human evaluation consistently show that WebViSE improves the visual quality and interaction fidelity of artifacts. Overall, our work establishes an automated path for extracting, organizing, and transferring design intelligence from the open web to website-building models. We release all extracted Visual Skills, the associated Skill DAG, and our code at https://github.com/YifeiSun-0710/WebViSE.
2610.33929.tldr_en: This work establishes an automated path for extracting, organizing, and transferring design intelligence from the open web to website-building models and introduces Website-derived Visual Skill Extraction (WebViSE), a framework that automatically abstracts these implementations into reusable Visual Skills and builds a structured Skill library.

llm.title_ja: WebViSE：LLMによるウェブサイト生成に向けたオープンウェブからの視覚デザイン知能のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: オープンウェブのウェブサイト実装から再利用可能な視覚的スキルを自動的に抽出し、構造化されたスキルライブラリを構築するフレームワーク「WebViSE」を提案する。
llm.problem: 非専門家ユーザーが洗練された視覚的・インタラクションデザインを自然言語で明確に表現することが困難である点。
llm.method: マルチ親DAGにスキルを組織化し、スキル条件付きポテンシャルクエリを使用してスキル記述とDAG構造を共同で進化させる。
llm.result: 複数のウェブ開発ベンチマークおよび人間評価において、アーティファクトの視覚的品質とインタラクションの忠実度が向上することが示された。

2610.33916.title: Real-Time Human Trajectory Prediction from RGB-D for Mobile Robots Using Bi-Mamba
2610.33916.abstract: Predicting the short-term future trajectory of a person from RGB-D cameras is a key capability for mobile robots navigating in dynamic and human populated environment. The key challenge to deploying learned predictors on real robots is the train-deploy pipeline gap. Training data are often prepared with an idealized, smoothed ground truth, whereas at inference, the model is fed noisy estimates from pose detectors and depth sensors. The model is therefore evaluated on an input distribution it never encountered during training. Most existing models rely on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or transformers, which either struggle to capture short-term temporal dependencies or suffer from computational cost. We present TrajMamba, a lightweight, bidirectional state space model for short-term human trajectory prediction using an RGB-D camera. The model uses a single shared processing path for both training and deployment, aligning human pose extraction, depth back projection, and smoothing processes. It encodes a short window of persons's hip center velocities with stacked bidirectional Mamba blocks and decodes future velocities with a GRU head. On the ETH/UCY benchmark, TrajMamba reaches an average ADE of 0.29 m FDE of 0.51 m. With 262K parameters, it runs in real time on modest hardware and is deployed on a TIAGo robot with an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin.
2610.33916.comment: Accepted at the 14th International Conference on Control, Mechatronics and Automation (ICCMA 2026), Bari, Italy, November 3-5, 2026. 7 pages, 6 figures
2610.33916.tldr_en: TrajMamba is presented, a lightweight, bidirectional state space model for short-term human trajectory prediction using an RGB-D camera that runs in real time on modest hardware and is deployed on a TIAGo robot with an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin.

llm.title_ja: Bi-Mambaを用いたRGB-Dカメラによるモバイルロボットのためのリアルタイム人間軌跡予測
llm.tldr_ja: 軽量な双方向状態空間モデル「TrajMamba」を用い、RGB-Dカメラを使用して短期間の人間軌跡をリアルタイムで予測する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 学習済み予測器を実ロボットに展開する際のトレーニング・デプロイパイプラインのギャップと、既存モデルの計算コストの高さや短期的依存関係のキャプチャの難しさ。
llm.method: トレーニングとデプロイで単一の共有処理パスを使用し、スタックされた双方向Mambaブロックで速度をエンコードしGRUヘッドで未来の速度をデコードする。
llm.result: ETH/UCYベンチマークで優れたADE/FDEを達成し、控えめなハードウェア上でリアルタイム動作しTIAGoロボットに搭載して実証された。

2610.33906.title: Sybil-Resilient Multi-Drone Exploration of Indoor and Confined Spaces
2610.33906.abstract: When a team of drones explores a building together, each drone tells the others which frontier it is going to and shares the map it has built. This avoids duplicated effort, but it also means that the team trusts every identity from which it receives messages. In a Sybil attack, one compromised drone creates fake identities, and these fake teammates claim frontiers and send fabricated scans, so the real drones leave parts of the building unexplored and end up with walls in their maps that do not exist. We study five such attackers, including one that seals off the openings between floors, and five levels of defence that need no security infrastructure, only the drones' own sensors and maps: an audit of received map data against what a drone sees itself, a check that a body is present where an identity claims to be, trust only for identities whose body has been seen, a quarantine for identities that no drone has observed, and a rule that binds each observed body to one identity. Tests in simulation cover 70 maps of seven kinds, from offices and tunnels to three-storey buildings and caves. Without a defence, one compromised drone leaves on average up to 25% of a map unexplored (45% in offices), and the floor-sealing attacker cuts the explored part of a three-storey building to 82.3%, or 34.6% on the worst map. The quarantine brings exploration back to the level of an unattacked team in every setting, and in most settings it also brings the false data back to that level. The exceptions are two colluding attackers, fakes placed next to real drones, three of the ten caves and a team of 16 drones, and binding bodies to identities fixes the last three. Over 2,350 missions, an honest drone was revoked by a teammate only twice.
2610.33906.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, and 8 tables. Code, worlds and mission results: https://github.com/IDZTPHKKKS/Sybil4Drones
2610.33906.tldr_en: Five attackers are studied, including one that seals off the openings between floors, and five levels of defence that need no security infrastructure, only the drones'own sensors and maps: an audit of received map data against what a drone sees itself, a check that a body is present where an identity claims to be, trust only for identities whose body has been seen, a quarantine for identities that no drone has observed, and a rule that binds each observed body to one identity.

llm.title_ja: シビル攻撃耐性を持つ室内・閉鎖空間のマルチドローン探索
llm.tldr_ja: セキュリティインフラを必要とせず、ドローン自身のセンサーとマップのみを用いてシビル攻撃に対処する5つの防御レベルを提案する。
llm.problem: シビル攻撃により、妥協したドローンが偽のアイデンティティを作成して虚偽の情報を共有することで、実機ドローンが空間を未探索のまま残してしまう点。
llm.method: 受信したマップデータの監査、アイデンティティの存在確認、未観測のアイデンティティの検疫、観測された身体とアイデンティティの結合などの5段階の防御ルールを導入する。
llm.result: シミュレーションテストにおいて、検疫などの防御手法により攻撃を受けた場合でも攻撃を受けていないチームと同等の探索レベルを回復できることを示した。

2610.33894.title: WMEval: Evaluating Interactive World Models Grounded on Physical Simulations
2610.33894.abstract: Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility. We introduce WMEval, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates interactive world models against Unity-based physical simulations. By leveraging Unity as a high-fidelity ground-truth oracle, we shift evaluation beyond perceptual visual assessment toward the objective state-based verification required for downstream applications. Spanning 9 diverse scenes, WMEval assesses action controllability, scene and character consistency, prompt adherence, kinematics, fluid mechanics, physical causality, and lighting. By executing matched action sequences in both the simulator and the world model, WMEval enables evaluation at both the perceptual level and the physical-causal level, using simulator-derived states as reference. Experiments on state-of-the-art models reveal significant room for improvement in dimensions that remain hidden by standard perceptual metrics but are vital for real-world deployments. Our code is available at: https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/WMEval.
2610.33894.tldr_en: WMEval is introduced, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates interactive world models against Unity-based physical simulations against Unity as a high-fidelity ground-truth oracle, to shift evaluation beyond perceptual visual assessment toward the objective state-based verification required for downstream applications.

llm.title_ja: WMEval：物理シミュレーションに基づくインタラクティブ世界モデルの評価
llm.tldr_ja: Unityベースの物理シミュレーションを用いてインタラクティブな世界モデルを評価し、知覚的類似性から客観的な状態ベースの検証へとシフトさせる包括的ベンチマークWMEvalを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは物理的・因果的な一貫性よりも知覚的類似性に主に着目している。
llm.method: Unityを信頼できる正解オラクルとして利用し、一致する行動シーケンスを実行して知覚レベルおよび物理・因果レベルで評価を行う。
llm.result: 最先端モデルにおいて、標準的な知覚指標では隠れたままの、現実世界の展開に不可欠な次元において大幅な改善の余地があることが明らかになった。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2610.33866.title: Late Breaking Results: Audio-Language-Action Models with Direct Speech Conditioning for Robotic Manipulation
2610.33866.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to follow instructions in typed text, limiting broader deployment in natural speech. The traditional solution by prepending a speech recognition before VLA to convert speech into texts would incur additional latency and propagate errors. To address this, we present Speech-$π_{0.5}$, which maps raw speech directly to motor commands without explicit textual transcriptions. Specifically, built on $π_{0.5}$, we use a cross-modal projection to convert voice frames directly into audio tokens with significant response latency reduction. To further improve the accuracy, we adopt split LoRA adaptation with dedicated audio and task adapters, under a two-stage training. Speech-$π_{0.5}$ achieves $3\times$ lower response latency than ASR pipeline while maintaining competitive task success on LIBERO, and generalizes robustly to unseen accents where a single adapter degrades significantly.
2610.33866.comment: 2 pages, 1 figure. Accepted to DAC 2026 Late Breaking Results
2610.33866.tldr_en: Speech-ϕ0.5 achieves 3× lower response latency than ASR pipeline while maintaining competitive task success on LIBERO, and generalizes robustly to unseen accents where a single adapter degrades significantly.

llm.title_ja: 最新の成果：ロボットマニピュレーションのための直接音声条件付けを持つ音声・言語・行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: Speech-π0.5は、明示的なテキスト書き起こしを行わずに生の音声を直接モーターコマンドにマッピングし、ASRパイプラインと比較して3倍低い応答レイテンシを達成する。
llm.problem: 従来のVLAモデルはテキスト入力に限定されており、従来の音声認識の追加はレイテンシの増加とエラーの伝播を引き起こす。
llm.method: クロスモーダルプロジェクションを用いて音声フレームを直接音声トークンに変換し、分割LoRA適応と2段階トレーニングを採用する。
llm.result: ASRパイプラインと比較して3倍低い応答レイテンシを達成しつつLIBEROで同等のタスク成功率を維持し、未知のアクセントに対しても頑健に汎化する。

2610.33863.title: RoboLongR: Causally Consistent Rewards Teach Robots to Progressively Master Long-Horizon Manipulation
2610.33863.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation requires actions whose validity depends on earlier interactions, yet visual progress can conceal missing task prerequisites. We propose RoboLongR, an offline-to-online framework that learns history-dependent rewards to guide policy adaptation to new tasks. Its central objective is causal consistency: aligning rewarded progress with prerequisites supported by execution history. Stage-shuffle supervision encourages execution-order sensitivity, recurrent memory preserves evidence of earlier interactions, and two-round training refines trajectory segments using predicted progress. The resulting rewards guide stage-conditioned policy refinement from behavior cloning to online reinforcement learning. Sparse terminal feedback connects policy experience to reward learning by triggering correction for repeated high-scoring failures. Pretrained on demonstrations from 88 RLBench tasks and Open-X data, RoboLongR achieves 31.8% average success on 18 long-horizon tasks excluded from reward pretraining, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 9.2 percentage points. Across four real-robot tasks, it achieves 57.5% success, a 32.5-percentage-point improvement over the comparison method. Reward-level controls probe sensitivity to synthetic order perturbations, while ablations examine the contributions of individual components to policy improvement.
2610.33863.comment: 11 pages including appendices, 8 figures, 6 tables. Project website: https://chenzixuan99.github.io/RoboLongR-public/
2610.33863.tldr_en: RoboLongR is proposed, an offline-to-online framework that learns history-dependent rewards to guide policy adaptation to new tasks, and its central objective is causal consistency: aligning rewarded progress with prerequisites supported by execution history.

llm.title_ja: RoboLongR：因果的に一貫した報酬がロボットに長期マニピュレーションの段階的なマスターを教える
llm.tldr_ja: RoboLongRは、因果的一貫性を中心目的に据えた履歴依存報酬を学習し、振る舞いクローンからオンライン強化学習へのポリシー適応をガイドするオフライン・ツー・オンラインフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 長期マニピュレーションでは初期の相互作用に依存する行動が必要だが、視覚的な進捗だけではタスクの前提条件の欠落を隠してしまうことがある。
llm.method: 実行履歴によってサポートされる前提条件と報酬による進捗を合わせる因果的一貫性を目的とし、段階シャッフル監視やリカレントメモリ、2ラウンドトレーニングを導入する。
llm.result: 報酬事前学習から除外された18の長期タスクにおいて平均31.8%の成功率を達成し、実ロボットの4タスクでは57.5%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 長期マニピュレーション

2610.33862.title: Securing Edge & Physical AI: Post-Quantum IoT Blockchain for Mission-Critical Cyber-Physical Agents
2610.33862.abstract: Distributed Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Edge AI networks increasingly depend on public-key authentication and key-establishment mechanisms that are vulnerable to cryptographically relevant Quantum Computers (QC). Shor's algorithm threatens widely deployed asymmetric primitives, while Grover's algorithm reduces the effective security margins of symmetric and hash-based mechanisms. Although Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) provides a migration path, its larger public keys, ciphertexts, and signatures introduce additional computation, memory, communication, storage, and packet-fragmentation costs that can constrain dynamic multi-agent systems. In this article, we introduce rotational secrecy, an architectural objective that limits temporal key exposure through authenticated transitions between cryptographic epochs. We present Private Authentication for Rotational Secrecy (PARS), a reference mechanism that coordinates policy-triggered key establishment, rotation, and reconciliation among authorized Physical AI agents. For deployments that need distributed agreement on security state, we further develop the PARS-Enabled Edge Security Ledger (PARS-ESL), an optional permissioned architecture maintained by authorized validators or capable edge gateways. PARS-ESL does not store high-volume operational transactions. Instead, it records authenticated state for key epochs, group membership, revocation, algorithm-suite policies, challenge validation, and recovery checkpoints. As a result, resource-constrained agents can take part as lightweight clients, and low-latency operational traffic stays outside the ledger consensus path, protected by the currently active symmetric epoch keys. Our results show that ledger-assisted post-quantum key-epoch management is feasible for selected Edge AI and CPS security-control workloads under the stated trust, compromise, connectivity, and resource assumptions.
2610.33862.comment: 47 pages, 39 figures, 10 tables, 5 algorithms, to be published in IEEE IoTJ, Science Directy (Elseiver IoTJ, Embodied Intelligence in Physical Systems)
2610.33862.tldr_en: This article introduces rotational secrecy, an architectural objective that limits temporal key exposure through authenticated transitions between cryptographic epochs and shows that ledger-assisted post-quantum key-epoch management is feasible for selected Edge AI and CPS security-control workloads under the stated trust, compromise, connectivity, and resource assumptions.

llm.title_ja: エッジおよび物理AIの保護：ミッションクリティカルなサイバー物理エージェントのための耐量子IoTブロックチェーン
llm.tldr_ja: 本書では、暗号学的エポック間の認証された遷移を通じて一時的な鍵の露出を制限する「回転秘密性」というアーキテクチャ上の目的を導入し、PARSなどの参照メカニズムを提案する。
llm.problem: 分散サイバー物理システムは量子コンピュータの攻撃に対して脆弱な公開鍵認証や鍵確立メカニズムに依存しており、PQCの導入は計算や通信のコストを増加させる。
llm.method: ポリシー主導の鍵確立・ローテーション・調整を調整する参照メカニズムPARSと、オプションの許可型アーキテクチャPARS-ESLを開発する。
llm.result: 元帳支援型の耐量子鍵エポック管理が、指定された前提条件の下で特定のエッジAIおよびCPSセキュリティ制御ワークロードに対して実行可能であることを示した。
keywords_ja: サイバー物理システム

2610.33852.title: AdaDexTrack: Dynamic Modulation for Adaptive and Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation Tracking
2610.33852.abstract: Language is a natural way to command robots, but converting a single instruction into a long-horizon, contact-rich hand-object interaction remains challenging: synthesized references are noisy, human-to-robot retargeting introduces embodiment bias, and fixed-reference tracking lets small errors snowball. We address this with AdaDexTrack, a modulator-in-the-loop framework for language-conditioned manipulation tracking. A distilled generalist tracker serves as the skill carrier, while a tightly aligned modulator performs three feedback corrections: reference modulation (continual adjustment of what to track), object-latent modulation (online adaptation of the object representation to recruit suitable skills), and positional-target modulation (small state-dependent refinements for execution). The tracker is learned via large-scale specialist to generalist distillation on a corpus of language-conditioned hand-object trajectories; the modulator is trained with RL under the same task objective, ensuring tight coupling. Across large-scale evaluations, AdaDexTrack consistently outperforms prior SOTA on unseen-trajectory and unseen-object sets in both average tracking error and success rate, demonstrating robustness and generalization. We further show zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on real hardware, where adding the modulator yields substantial gains over a tracker-only variant. AdaDexTrack reframes language-conditioned dexterous manipulation as modulated tracking, replacing the open-loop, fixed-reference tracking with in-loop modulation that adjusts the reference, object latent, and positional target, yielding drift-resistant execution from noisy text references.
2610.33852.comment: CVPR 2026. 18 pages, 14 figures, including supplementary material. Project page: https://janebek.github.io/AdaDexTrack/
2610.33852.journal_ref: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 28021-28031, 2026
2610.33852.tldr_en: AdaDexTrack reframes language-conditioned dexterous manipulation as modulated tracking, replacing the open-loop, fixed-reference tracking with in-loop modulation that adjusts the reference, object latent, and positional target, yielding drift-resistant execution from noisy text references.

llm.title_ja: AdaDexTrack：適応的で汎用的な器用なマニピュレーション追跡のための動的変調
llm.tldr_ja: AdaDexTrackは、言語条件付きマニピュレーション追跡において、オープンループで固定参照の追跡をインループ変調に置き換えることでドリフト耐性のある実行を実現する modulator-in-the-loop フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 単一の指示を長期の接触を伴う手と物体のインタラクションに変換することは難しく、固定参照の追跡では小さな誤差が雪だるま式に膨れ上がる。
llm.method: 蒸留された汎用トラッカーをスキルキャリアとして使用し、参照・物体潜在・位置ターゲットの3つのフィードバック補正を同時に行う変調器を強化学習で訓練する。
llm.result: 未知の軌跡や未知の物体セットにおいて従来の最先端手法を一貫して上回り、実際のハードウェアでのゼロショットSim-to-Real転移を実現した。

2610.33807.title: RoboWorM: Evaluating Movement Realism, Consistency and Acceleration Affects in Embodied Video World Models
2610.33807.abstract: Video world models (VWMs) are rapidly emerging as scalable neural simulators for robotic manipulation. However, most benchmarks only evaluate them as open-world video generators, using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that lack strict 3D spatial and kinematic reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboWorM, a comprehensive, deployment-aware benchmark that leverages known hardware priors such as robot kinematic trees and fixed camera configurations, to systematically examine structural and spatiotemporal fidelity. RoboWorM curates 1,605 episodes across single-arm, bimanual, and humanoid morphologies, spanning both Markovian and long-horizon non-Markovian tasks under single- and multi-view setups. To explicitly measure physical consistency, we propose two deterministic, VLM-free metrics: KIVA for intra-view kinematic stability, and RIGIS for multi-view geometric consistency. By exploiting intrinsic robotic invariants, KIVA improves hallucination detection alignment with human annotations by 25.8% relative to the strongest frontier VLMs, while RIGIS achieves a 130% higher Spearman correlation with human preferences. Furthermore, since real-world deployment requires low inference latency, we utilize RoboWorM to conduct the first large-scale audit of the quality-efficiency trade-off. Evaluating 9 state-of-the-art acceleration techniques across 3 leading world models (over 29,000 generated rollouts), we demonstrate how these acceleration methods can retain superficial visual quality while silently compromising deployment-critical physical constraints. Using our metrics, we achieve 2.3$\times$ maximum inference speed-up with minimal quality loss.
2610.33807.tldr_en: This work introduces RoboWorM, a comprehensive, deployment-aware benchmark that leverages known hardware priors such as robot kinematic trees and fixed camera configurations, to systematically examine structural and spatiotemporal fidelity, and conducts the first large-scale audit of the quality-efficiency trade-off.

llm.title_ja: RoboWorM：具現化ビデオ世界モデルにおける運動の現実主義、一貫性、加速度の影響の評価
llm.tldr_ja: RoboWorMは、ロボットの運動学ツリーや固定カメラ構成などのハードウェア事前知識を活用して構造的および時空的な忠実度を体系的に検証する、包括的で展開を意識したベンチマークである。
llm.problem: ほとんどのビデオ世界モデルのベンチマークは、厳密な3D空間的・運動学的推論を欠くVLMを使い、オープンワールドの動画ジェネレーターとしてのみ評価している。
llm.method: 単一ビューの運動学的安定性のためのKIVAと、複数ビューの幾何学的一貫性のためのRIGISという、決定論的でVLM不要の2つの指標を提案する。
llm.result: KIVAは人間の注釈との hallucination 検出の一致度を25.8%改善し、RIGISは人間の好みと130%高い相関を達成するとともに、品質と効率のトレードオフの大規模な監査を行った。

2610.33794.title: One Scan is Enough: Demonstration-Free Adaptation for Language-Guided Navigation
2610.33794.abstract: Deploying a language-guided navigation policy in a new building usually means watching it fail. Public-benchmark VLAs degrade scene by scene as layout, appearance, and language drift, and the standard fix of teleoperating fresh trajectories on site does not scale. We replace human demonstration with a single brief iPhone scan. Scan2Instruction compiles that scan into a complete training environment, automatically synthesizing executable navigation episodes with grounded instructions. PRPT-KS then adapts the policy through a closed-form Pareto utility read directly off the reconstructed scene, with no learned critic and no human labels. Across five real environments, the two designs together drive our RealNav to an 85% real-robot success rate, compared with 49% for a RealNav baseline post-trained on human demonstrations, and still achieve 82% in unscanned regions of the same buildings, compared with 41% for the same baseline. Our work turns demonstration-free scene adaptation for language-guided navigation from an aspiration into a working reality.
2610.33794.tldr_en: This work turns demonstration-free scene adaptation for language-guided navigation from an aspiration into a working reality, and replaces human demonstration with a single brief iPhone scan.

llm.title_ja: 1回のスキャンで十分：言語誘導型ナビゲーションのためのデモンストレーション不要な適応
llm.tldr_ja: Scan2InstructionとPRPT-KSの組み合わせにより、人間のデモンストレーションの代わりに1回の簡単なiPhoneスキャンを用いて言語誘導型ナビゲーションポリシーの訓練環境を構築し適応させる。
llm.problem: 新しい建物への言語誘導型ナビゲーションポリシーの導入は、シーンの変化によるドリフトで失敗し、現地での新たな手動デモンストレーションはスケーラブルではない。
llm.method: 1回のiPhoneスキャンから訓練環境を構築し、グラウンドされた指示付きの実行可能なナビゲーションエピソードを合成、学習済み批評家なしでポリシーを適応させる。
llm.result: 5つの実環境において、実ロボットの成功率85%を達成し、デモンストレーションで追加訓練したベースラインの49%を大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: 言語誘導型ナビゲーション
デモンストレーション不要

2610.33789.title: Segmentation of Moving Objects During Camera Motion Using the OWL Function
2610.33789.abstract: We present a principled, analytical framework for segmenting multiple independently moving rigid objects during single camera motion, built directly upon the OWL perception function. OWL encodes two fundamental visual motion cues, perceived looming $L$ and perceived rotation $ω$, into a single closed-form representation of relative 3D structure. A key consequence of this structure is that the unit direction of relative translation $\hat{t}$ is analytically recoverable per image point from $L$ and $ω$ alone. All points belonging to a non-rotating rigid body share the same $\hat{t}$, whereas points on different rigid bodies generally yield distinct values. This furnishes a natural segmentation criterion: clustering per-point $\hat{t}$ estimates partitions the visible scene into independently moving rigid bodies. Building on the 2D complex form of OWL, we derive the framework in 3D using quaternions, for a single moving camera. The approach is parallel, camera rotation-invariant, and requires no training data, no depth information, and no semantic priors.
2610.33789.tldr_en: A principled, analytical framework for segmenting multiple independently moving rigid objects during single camera motion, built directly upon the OWL perception function, derived in 3D using quaternions for a single moving camera.

llm.title_ja: OWL関数を用いたカメラ移動中の移動物体のセグメンテーション
llm.tldr_ja: OWL知覚関数に直接基づいて、単一カメラの移動中に独立して移動する複数の剛体をセグメンテーションするための原理的かつ解析的なフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 単一のカメラ移動中における独立した複数移動剛体のセグメンテーションを、訓練データや深度情報、事前知識なしで行う必要がある。
llm.method: 知覚されるルーミングと回転の2つの視覚的動きの手がかりを表現に組み込み、相対並進の単位方向のクラスタリングによってシーンを分割する。
llm.result: 学習データや深度情報、セマンティックな事前知識を一切必要とせず、カメラの回転に不変で並列処理可能なセグメンテーションを実現した。

2610.33778.title: RoboReason: Boosting Robotics-Relevant VLM Reasoning Through Scalable Data Generation
2610.33778.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance when integrated into robot manipulation pipelines, but real-world evaluation of VLM capabilities on downstream robotics tasks is both difficult and expensive to scale. We propose that spatial and temporal ordering tasks using images from stereo and wrist cameras attached to real-world robots are particularly well-suited for evaluating visual reasoning capabilities, as they assess skills directly applicable to robots. We evaluate VLM reasoning abilities on three questions: ordering shuffled frames conditioned on a language description of the task, ordering objects depthwise based on distance from the camera, and ordering objects from left-to-right in pixel coordinates. The complexity of these tasks can also be modulated by changing the size of the set to sort. Our experiments show that several state-of-the-art vision-language models struggle on ordering tasks. To fix this, we propose a scalable autonomous training data generation pipeline, and show that both supervised finetuning and reinforcement-learning on the generated data can significantly improve VLM reasoning performance both on spatiotemporal ordering tasks as well as downstream robotics and visual reasoning tasks.
2610.33778.tldr_en: A scalable autonomous training data generation pipeline is proposed, and it is shown that both supervised finetuning and reinforcement-learning on the generated data can significantly improve VLM reasoning performance both on spatiotemporal ordering tasks as well as downstream robotics and visual reasoning tasks.
2610.33778.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

badges.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Em

llm.title_ja: RoboReason：スケーラブルなデータ生成によるロボット関連VLM推論の強化
llm.tldr_ja: スケーラブルな自律訓練データ生成パイプラインを提案し、生成されたデータを用いたファインチューニングと強化学習がVLMの推論性能を大幅に向上させることを示した。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーションにVLMを統合する際のロボットのタスクにおける実世界評価は困難かつコストがかかる。
llm.method: ステレオおよび手首カメラの画像を用いたシャッフルされたフレームの順序付け、深度方向の順序付け、画素座標での左から右への順序付けの3つの質問でVLMの推論能力を評価し、自動データ生成パイプラインを構築する。
llm.result: 最先端のVLMが順序付けタスクに苦戦していることを示し、提案手法によって時空の順序付けタスクおよび下流のロボット・視覚推論タスクの性能が大幅に向上した。

2610.33760.title: C-DFF: Concept-Level Diagnostics for Mechanism Parity in Simulation-Based Validation of Autonomous Driving Perception
2610.33760.abstract: Simulation is widely used in autonomous-driving validation, but matching task outputs between real and synthetic images does not guarantee that a system relies on the same visual evidence. This creates a validation gap for transfer, especially in safety-critical perception functions. We present Concept-Decisive Feature Fidelity (C-DFF), a concept-level mechanism-parity diagnostic for paired real-synthetic evaluation. Starting from decisive evidence extracted from a frozen system-under-test (SUT), C-DFF projects that evidence into a shared semantic concept space using off-the-shelf segmentation and compares real and synthetic concept-importance vectors. The result is not only a scalar mechanism-parity score, but also a concept-shift diagnostic that identifies which scene concepts become more or less decisive in simulation. We evaluate C-DFF on KITTI $\leftrightarrow$ Virtual KITTI 2 with 2126 matched pairs across three frozen SUTs (steering regression, YOLOP drivable-area, YOLOP lane-line). Across these tasks, C-DFF is SUT-discriminative and yields interpretable concept-level summaries that support validation triage and simulator debugging. When reported alongside task-specific output-value context metrics, C-DFF shows that output agreement does not by itself establish mechanism parity. These results position C-DFF as a practical semantic diagnostic layer for validation and verification workflows in simulation-based AV testing.
2610.33760.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Accepted and presented at the 2026 IEEE 29th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC), Naples, Italy, September 15-18, 2026
2610.33760.tldr_en: Concept-Decisive Feature Fidelity (C-DFF), a concept-level mechanism-parity diagnostic for paired real-synthetic evaluation, and results position C-DFF as a practical semantic diagnostic layer for validation and verification workflows in simulation-based AV testing.

llm.title_ja: C-DFF：自動運転知覚のシミュレーションベース検証におけるメカニズムパリティのための概念レベル診断
llm.tldr_ja: C-DFF（Concept-Decisive Feature Fidelity）は、ペアとなる実世界と合成データの評価において、モデルが同じ視覚的証拠に依存しているかを概念レベルで診断するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 実画像と合成画像の間でタスク出力が一致しても、システムが同じ視覚的証拠に依存しているとは限らず、安全性が重要な知覚機能で検証のギャップが生じる。
llm.method: 凍結されたテスト対象システムから抽出された決定的な証拠を共有セマンティック概念空間に投影し、実世界と合成の概念重要度ベクトルを比較する。
llm.result: スカラーのメカニズムパリティスコアと、シミュレーション内でどのシーン概念がより決定的になるかを特定する概念シフト診断を提供し、実用的な診断層として機能することを示した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション検証

2610.33745.title: POD-RoPE: Rotary Position Encoding over Physical Observation Distributions for Embodied AI
2610.33745.abstract: Embodied perception requires positional representations that capture both physical geometry and the spatial and temporal extent of observations. We introduce POD-RoPE (Physical Observation Distribution RoPE), which represents token observation footprints as distributions over camera centers, viewing directions, and sampling times. Under independent sampling, expected rotations encode relative relationships between distributions; when each distribution collapses to a single address, the construction recovers pointwise RoPE. The same rotation statistics support Q/K matching and coherence-dependent V/O transformations, allowing observation geometry to guide both information selection and content aggregation. Per-token pre-aggregation avoids increasing sequence length or processing pairs of observation nodes. We evaluate POD-RoPE across four robot policy architectures, simulation and real-world manipulation, and complementary reconstruction, depth-estimation, and novel-view-synthesis tasks. Integrating POD-RoPE into Fast-WAM improves mean success from 91.83% to 92.88% across all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and from 32.5% to 52.5% on two real-robot tasks on Sharpa North. Controlled reconstruction ablations support the contributions of distribution encoding and V/O transformations.
