In H20 model-block benchmarks, POD-RoPE achieves median forward-plus-backward speedups of $1.91\times$ over P-RoPE and $5.34\times$ over RayRoPE, with a median latency overhead of 17.4% over Standard RoPE. These results support physical observation distributions as an effective and computationally efficient basis for geometry-aware attention.
2610.33745.tldr_en: The introduction of POD-RoPE (Physical Observation Distribution RoPE), which represents token observation footprints as distributions over camera centers, viewing directions, and sampling times, supports physical observation distributions as an effective and computationally efficient basis for geometry-aware attention.

llm.title_ja: POD-RoPE：具現化AIのための物理的観測分布に基づく回転位置エンコーディング
llm.tldr_ja: POD-RoPEは、トークンの観測フットプリントをカメラ中心・視線方向・サンプリング時間の分布として表現し、幾何学的認識アテンションのための効率的な基盤を提供する。
llm.problem: 具現化された知覚には、物理的ジオメトリと観測の空間的・時間的広がりの両方を捉える位置表現が必要である。
llm.method: 独立サンプリングの下で期待回転が分布間の相対関係をエンコードし、観測ジオメトリが情報選択とコンテンツ集約をガイドするPOD-RoPEを統合する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0の全50タスクで平均成功率を91.83%から92.88%に向上させ、標準的なRoPEに対して顕著な高速化を達成した。
keywords_ja: 回転位置エンコーディング
幾何学的アテンション

2610.33735.title: Floor Friction Assessment from Robot Tire-Surface Interaction
2610.33735.abstract: Floor traction influences wheel-slip behavior, dead-reckoning accuracy, and the navigation performance of wheeled mobile robots that rely on wheel odometry. As these robots become increasingly common in GNSS-denied indoor environments, including automated manufacturing and retail facilities, their onboard measurements could also be used to characterize floor conditions and improve localization. In this study, a skid-steer robot was driven over five floor surfaces with distinct traction characteristics using commanded velocity profiles designed to induce wheel slip through repeated acceleration and direction reversal. Differences between the body velocity estimated from inertial sensing and the velocity obtained from wheel odometry were evaluated using the integrated relative-velocity error, phase-derived wheel-to-body response delay, and velocity-reversal response delay. Welch power spectral density analysis was additionally applied to characterize the frequency distribution of the velocity mismatch during positive and negative acceleration. Band-integrated spectral power, spectral centroid, and spectral decay rate were extracted from each recording and evaluated using linear discriminant analysis and multiclass classification. The response-delay measurements produced consistent surface-dependent trends, with the longest delays observed on soap and the shortest delays observed on carpet. The spectral features also provided clear separation among the tested surfaces, achieving a balanced classification accuracy of 97.1% under recording-level cross-validation. These results demonstrate that both the magnitude and frequency domain characteristics of wheel-to-body velocity mismatch contain useful information about tire-surface interactions. Such information could support surface recognition and the development of slip-aware wheel-odometry weighting within robot state-estimation frameworks.
2610.33735.comment: 11 pages and 14 figures; Extended abstract submitted to IEEE/ION PLANS 2027, under review

llm.title_ja: ロボットのタイヤと路面の相互作用からの床面摩擦評価
llm.tldr_ja: 床面摩擦評価に関する抽象的な要約はソースサマリーに記載されていませんが、本論文では車輪型移動ロボットの車輪オドメトリと慣性計測の比較から床面状態を推定する手法を提案しています。
llm.problem: GNSSの使えない屋内環境において、車輪の滑り挙動がナビゲーション性能やデッドレコニングの精度に影響を与える。
llm.method: 慣性センシングによる速度と車輪オドメトリの速度の差異を評価し、応答遅延やパワースペクトル密度解析を用いて分類する。
llm.result: 応答遅延測定により表面依存の傾向が一貫して示され、スペクトル特徴量を用いて97.1%のバランスの取れた分類精度を達成した。

2610.33718.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
2610.33718.abstract: Many robot manipulation videos do not indicate whether the task was successfully completed. RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that takes a task instruction, 10 frames of a manipulation attempt, and (if available) final frames from auxiliary cameras and predicts whether the robot accomplished the task. RoboJev-27B is a variant of JEV-27B-VL, trained with a rank-32 LoRA adapter on the language model only (keeping the vision encoder frozen) using 52,598 episode records. It also uses a source-specific KL penalty that applies only to research data, anchoring predictions closer to the original model on those sources. It uses a calibrated two-token readout that outputs success/failure probabilities in a single forward pass. On 268 held-out episodes of the same robot model (SO-101), RoboJev-27B attains 95.2% balanced accuracy and 0.993 AUROC. It also generalises to episodes collected by unseen labs/robots (AUROC = 0.890 over 459 episodes) as well as to clearly labelled community-collected episodes (accuracy = 93.3% over 135 episodes), where the base model attains an AUROC = 0.900 on the unseen-lab/robot subset with the same inputs. It takes 0.26 seconds per episode (median, serial) to infer on a single H100, which is about \$0.19 per 1,000 success predictions at \$2.69 per GPU-hour (not including media processing and serving costs). RoboJev-27B is released together with its inference code, along with a transparent evaluation: 20,628 predictions organized into 29 model/protocol entries are made available to facilitate browsing and to enable reproducible benchmarking of success detection. We also compare against strong API-based frontier VLMs, which take in fewer input frames (4 images from the primary camera only); note that this comparison is not strictly like-for-like because RoboJev-27B is given more frames at inference.
2610.33718.tldr_en: RoboJev-27B is released together with its inference code, along with a transparent evaluation: 20,628 predictions organized into 29 model/protocol entries are made available to facilitate browsing and to enable reproducible benchmarking of success detection.
2610.33718.hf_summary_en: RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that predicts robot manipulation success from video frames using LoRA fine-tuning, calibrated token readouts, and source-specific regularization, achieving high accuracy and generalization across labs and robots.

llm.title_ja: RoboJev：ロボットの成功検出のためのオープンな視覚言語ジャッジ
llm.tldr_ja: RoboJev-27Bは、タスク指示とマニピュレーション試行のフレームを入力として受け取り、ロボットがタスクを達成したかどうかを予測するオープン重みの視覚言語モデルである。
llm.problem: 多くのロボットマニピュレーション動画は、タスクが正常に完了したかどうかを示しておらず、成功の自動検出が必要である。
llm.method: JEV-27B-VLをベースに、言語モデル部分にランク32のLoRAアダプターを適用し、ソース固有のKLペナルティを用いて52,598件のエピソード記録で訓練する。
llm.result: 保持された268エピソードで95.2%のバランス精度と0.993のAUROCを達成し、未知のラボやロボットが収集したエピソードにも一般化した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.33715.title: Quantum Closed Loop Inverse Kinematics Through Hilbert-Space Encoding of Robot Kinematics
2610.33715.abstract: The integration of quantum computing into robotics requires mathematical representations that preserve the geometric structure and configuration dependence of robot motion. This paper introduces a structure-preserving quantum representation of rigid-body transformations and serial-manipulator kinematics, establishing a correspondence between classical kinematic models and parameterized quantum circuits. Building on the Bloch-sphere representation, spatial directions are encoded into single-qubit states, while quantum rotations reproduce the ordered composition of reference-frame transformations. Translational contributions are combined through quantum-state aggregation, with their metric scales retained classically, enabling the reconstruction of end-effector position and orientation from Pauli expectation values. The formulation preserves the original joint variables and accommodates different kinematic conventions and joint types. Beyond forward kinematics, we establish that the manipulator geometric Jacobian can be reconstructed from quantum-observable derivatives using the parameter-shift rule, with analytical equivalence to its classical counterpart under ideal readout. To demonstrate the applicability of this representation to robot-level algorithms, we introduce Quantum Closed Loop Inverse Kinematics, a hybrid closed-loop method that exploits quantum-derived pose and Jacobian information. The proposed framework provides a geometrically interpretable foundation for developing and investigating quantum and hybrid computational methods for robotic kinematics and motion.
2610.33715.tldr_en: A structure-preserving quantum representation of rigid-body transformations and serial-manipulator kinematics is introduced, establishing a correspondence between classical kinematic models and parameterized quantum circuits.

llm.title_ja: ロボット運動学のヒルベルト空間エンコーディングを通じた量子閉ループ逆運動学
llm.tldr_ja: 剛体変換と直列マニピュレータの運動学に対する構造保存型の量子表現を導入し、古典的な運動学モデルとパラメータ化された量子回路との対応関係を確立する。
llm.problem: ロボット工学への量子計算の統合には、ロボットの運動学的幾何学構造と構成依存性を保持する数学的表現が必要である。
llm.method: ブロッホ球表現に基づき、空間方向を単一量子ビット状態にエンコードし、量子回転によって基準フレーム変換の合成を再現する。
llm.result: パウリ期待値からエンドエフェクタの位置と姿勢を再構築可能にし、量子閉ループ逆運動学のための幾何学的に解釈可能な基盤を提供した。

2610.33705.title: Open-World Law-to-Action: Vision-Language Priors and Touch for Parts with Hidden Physics
2610.33705.abstract: A robot in a home it has never seen must open doors, drawers, lids and taps whose physics a picture does not show. Instructions such as "open the drawer halfway, gently" depend on that physics: how far a part travels, how it resists, and what locks it. We present Open-World Law-to-Action (L2A). A vision-language model (VLM) proposes, for each movable part, its motions, the terms of its law of motion, and what may lock it. Each proposal becomes a prior with a floor, so that touch can always overturn it. The robot identifies each part's law online by Bayesian linear regression with closed-form evidence, for parts that move in one way or in two, and keeps a hypothesis that an unseen part or motion locks the target. We prove that touch alone cannot rule this hypothesis out, derive when another look is worth its cost, and show that a constant load and friction cannot be told apart while a part moves one way. All experiments are in simulation, developed on some scenes and run once on held-out ones. In new kitchens the robot completes 80% of tasks from the VLM's proposals, against 98% when every part is known. Proposed physics raises success on objects that need new terms from 353 to 378-383 of 400 episodes, and a second look raises success in mixed scenes from 284 to 329 of 366 tasks. A mobile robot that takes nothing from the simulator completes 70 of 100 requests in new scenes, against 62 when the simulator says which part each box is (after one change made between two held-out tests).
2610.33705.tldr_en: It is proved that touch alone cannot rule this hypothesis out, derive when another look is worth its cost, and show that a constant load and friction cannot be told apart while a part moves one way.

llm.title_ja: オープンワールドの法から行動へ：隠れた物理特性を持つ部品のための視覚言語の事前知識と触覚
llm.tldr_ja: 未知の家庭環境におけるロボットが、画像からは分からない物理法則を持つドアや引き出しを開けるためのオープンワールド法から行動へ（L2A）フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 未知の環境の可動部品において、移動距離、抵抗、ロック機構などの物理特性は画像だけでは分からない。
llm.method: VLMが各可動部品の動きや運動法則を提案し、触覚によってそれを覆すことができる事前知識とし、ベイズ線形回帰を用いてオンラインで法則を特定する。
llm.result: 新しいキッチンのシミュレーション環境において、VLMの提案からタスクの80%を完了し、物理法則の提案や2度目の確認によって成功率が大幅に向上した。
llm.limitation: すべての実験がシミュレーション内で実施されている点

2610.33685.title: EXE: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Pretraining via Factorized Latent Actions for VLA Models
2610.33685.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are bottlenecked by the scarcity of robot data. Egocentric human manipulation videos offer an abundant, diverse, and semantically-rich alternative that inherently captures manipulation intent. However, the embodiment gap makes it difficult to extract action-relevant representations from these videos. From the perspective of action execution, human hands and robots share analogous manipulation primitives---reaching, grasping, placing---yet exhibit distinct kinematics tied to their embodiments. This might motivate our key approach: egocentric video pretraining can yield shared action representations capturing transferable manipulation skills, while human-specific motion patterns should be disentangled to avoid interfering with robot policy learning. To this end, we propose EXE, an Egocentric Cross(X)-Embodiment pretraining framework that learns a factorized latent action representation from egocentric human videos, separating shared manipulation priors from embodiment-specific signals. By leveraging the shared action space, the robot policy acquires generalizable manipulation semantics from diverse human demonstrations without being biased by human-specific kinematics. This shared knowledge transfers across embodiments with different kinematic structures, enabling the same pretraining to benefit both parallel grippers and dexterous hands. EXE yields consistent gains over baseline without pretraining on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa GR1, and real-world manipulation tasks.
2610.33685.tldr_en: ExE, an Egocentric Cross(X)-Embodiment pretraining framework that learns a factorized latent action representation from egocentric human videos, separating shared manipulation priors from embodiment-specific signals, and yields consistent gains over baseline without pretraining on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa GR1, and real-world manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: EXE：因数分解された潜在的行動を通じたVLAモデルのための自己中心型クロスエンボディメント事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: EXEは、自己中心型の人間による動画から共有操作事前知識とエンボディメント固有信号を分離する因数分解された潜在的行動表現を学習する自己中心型クロスエンボディメント事前学習フレームワークである。
llm.problem: VLAモデルはロボットデータの不足に直面しており、自己中心型の人間のマニピュレーション動画を活用したいが、エンボディメントギャップが行動表現の抽出を困難にしている。
llm.method: 共有行動空間を利用して、人間の運動学的偏りを受けずに多様な人間のデモンストレーションから一般化可能な操作セマンティクスを獲得する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0、RoboCasa GR1、および実世界の操作タスクにおいて、事前学習なしのベースラインに対して一貫した性能向上を達成した。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント

2610.33679.title: Energy-Based Fault Detection and Isolation Framework for Flat Port-Hamiltonian Mechanical Systems
2610.33679.abstract: Fault diagnosis during regulated motion requires informative signals even when feedback attenuates tracking deviations. This paper develops an energy-based diagnostic framework that constructs mechanical port-power residuals without a dedicated dynamic observer. Spectral Hamiltonian Algebraic Power Evaluation (SHAPE) combines port-Hamiltonian variables and differential flatness to generate nominal power references from planned motion for fully actuated mechanical systems with collocated actuation. Subtracting these references from commanded effort multiplied by measured flow yields residuals whose final evaluation requires neither recursive observer updates nor measured-state dynamics calculations. Continuous wavelet transform (CWT) scalograms and a shared-encoder convolutional neural network are used to distinguish nominal operation, actuator loss of effectiveness, anomalous friction, and vibration from complete trajectories. Evaluation uses a simulated six degree of freedom Kinova manipulator under model predictive control and fixed plant-model mismatch, with single faults at a specified joint. Across five training seeds and 3000 held-out test runs, SHAPE-CWT achieves a mean accuracy of 84.69 percent, versus 81.67 percent for torque residuals and 97.17 percent for the generalized momentum observer under common CWT processing. The respective sample standard deviations are 0.70, 0.70, and 0.37 percentage points. These results demonstrate useful fault-type discrimination from algebraic power residuals, while severity-excitation profiles and offline velocity perturbations reveal limits to their diagnostic capability.

llm.title_ja: 平面ポート・ハミルトニアン機械系のためのエネルギーベースの故障検出・分離フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: エネルギーベースの診断フレームワークにより、専用の動的オブザーバなしで機械的ポートパワー残差を構築し、シミュレーションによる故障診断を行った。
llm.problem: 規制された運動中の故障診断は、フィードバックが追従偏差を減衰させる場合でも有益な信号を必要とする。
llm.method: SHAPE法を用いてポート・ハミルトニアン変数と微分平坦性を組み合わせ、計画された運動から公称電力基準を生成する。
llm.result: SHAPE-CWTは平均精度84.69%を達成し、代数パワー残差からの有用な故障タイプ識別を示した。
keywords_ja: ポート・ハミルトニアン系

2610.33658.title: Power-of-Two Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neurons for Event-Driven Vision-Language-Action Inference
2610.33658.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong capabilities in robotic manipulation, yet their reliance on dense, continuous-valued computation presents a fundamental challenge for energy-constrained deployment. Inspired by the sparse, event-driven signaling and temporal integration mechanisms of biological neurons, a promising alternative is to introduce spiking computation into VLA models. However, enabling such computation without restructuring pretrained policies or compromising closed-loop control remains an open challenge. To address this challenge, we introduce the Power-of-Two Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (PoT-LIF) neuron, which emits signed spikes with power-of-two amplitudes. By combining magnitude-coded spike events with residual-preserving membrane dynamics, PoT-LIF enables continuous information to be progressively represented through discrete spikes. The Heartbeat formulation further localizes this process within weighted projections, bridging biologically inspired spiking computation and pretrained VLA architectures without modifying their external inference interfaces. We integrate PoT-LIF into the vision projection, vision-language projection, and action projection of $π_{0.5}$ and evaluate both operating modes over 2,000 paired closed-loop LIBERO episodes per configuration. Standard-mode PoT-LIF VLA achieves success rates of 96.90% and 96.35% at $T = 1$ and $T = 2$, respectively, while Heartbeat mode achieves 97.25% and 96.90% at $T = 2$ and $T = 4$, compared with 96.70% for the original continuous-activation $π_{0.5}$ baseline. At $T = 1$ with a 60.01% firing rate, PoT-LIF uses approximately 1/7.67 of the dense-reference arithmetic energy, corresponding to a modeled reduction of 86.95%.
2610.33658.tldr_en: The Power-of-Two Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (PoT-LIF) neuron is introduced, which emits signed spikes with power-of-two amplitudes and enables continuous information to be progressively represented through discrete spikes, and the Heartbeat formulation further localizes this process within weighted projections, bridging biologically inspired spiking computation and pretrained VLA architectures without modifying their external inference interfaces.

llm.title_ja: イベント駆動型視覚言語行動推論のための2のべき乗リーク型integrate-and-fireニューロン
llm.tldr_ja: 2のべき乗の振幅を持つ符号付きスパイクを発火するPoT-LIFニューロンを導入し、事前学習済みVLAアーキテクチャを変更することなくバイオ触発型スパイク計算をブリッジする。
llm.problem: VLAモデルはロボットマニピュレーションで強力な性能を示すが、高密度で連続値の計算への依存はエネルギー制約のある展開における課題である。
llm.method: 大きさでコード化されたスパイクイベントと残差保存膜ダイナミクスを組み合わせ、重み付き投影内でこれをローカライズするHeartbeat定式化を導入する。
llm.result: LIBEROのエピソード評価において元の連続活性化ベースラインと同等の成功率を維持しつつ、元の密なリファレンスの算術エネルギーの約1/7.67（86.95%削減）を達成した。
keywords_ja: スパイクニューラルネットワーク
ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.33650.title: TAD: Distilling Vision-Language-Action Policies from Teacher Trajectories Alone
2610.33650.abstract: Online distillation of vision-language-action (VLA) policies commonly relies on teacher action scores that an inference-only interface may not expose. Trajectory-only Adversarial Distillation (\gad{}) instead turns a fixed bank of teacher joint-position features into adaptive feedback: a discriminator compares feature marginals from teacher and student rollouts and supplies rewards for on-policy learning. The student interacts with the environment without online teacher queries or environment task rewards. On ManiSkill \texttt{PutOnPlateInScene25Main}, \gad{} improves OpenVLA-OFT (7B) from $26.2\%$ to $76.6\%$ \successonce{} ($+50.4$ percentage points) and from $20.3\%$ to $58.6\%$ \successend{}. It trails white-box on-policy distillation (OPD) at $81.6\%$ / $59.4\%$ by $5.0$ / $0.8$ percentage points ($n{=}256$ evaluation trajectories per checkpoint). The tested four-epoch continuation achieves the highest \gad{} result without additional teacher data. This best run uses $5\times$ OPD's student interaction budget and $12.5\times$ its complete-rollout batch-passes. The comparison demonstrates online VLA improvement without teacher scoring while quantifying unequal interaction and optimization budgets.
2610.33650.tldr_en: A comparison demonstrates online VLA improvement without teacher scoring while quantifying unequal interaction and optimization budgets while quantifying unequal interaction and optimization budgets.

llm.title_ja: TAD：教師軌跡のみからの視覚言語行動ポリシーの蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: Trajectory-only Adversarial Distillation（TAD）は、教師の関節位置特徴の固定バンクを適応的フィードバックに変え、オンラインの教師クエリやタスク報酬なしでポリシーのオンライン学習を可能にする。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーのオンライン蒸留は、推論専用インターフェースでは露出しない可能性のある教師の行動スコアに依存することが多い。
llm.method: 識別器が教師と学生のロールアウトからの特徴周辺分布を比較し、オンポリシー学習のための報酬を供給する敵対的蒸留を用いる。
llm.result: ManiSkillにおいてOpenVLA-OFT（7B）の成功率を大幅に向上させ、教師のスコアリングなしでのVLAのオンライン改善を示した。

2610.33640.title: HARP: Handoff-Aware Recovery Planning for Active Target Acquisition in Multi-UAV Handoff
2610.33640.abstract: Continuous aerial tracking often requires multiple drones to maintain target coverage over long periods. During handoff, the receiving UAV may lack prior target observations and must actively acquire a usable view without disrupting the sender's ongoing coverage. This work introduces HARP, a handoff-aware recovery planner that registers bounded sender predictions in the receiver's local map, distinguishes field-of-view failure from physical occlusion, and generates failure-specific yaw, translation, and parallax viewpoints. Candidate motions are checked for receiver clearance, sender-fiducial observability, protected sender--target visibility, temporal validity, and deadline compliance. When a complete trajectory cannot be admitted, HARP may execute a sampled admissible nonzero prefix and replan from updated evidence. In simulation, HARP acquired the target in all 49 standard trials and in 15 of 16 stress trials. Field trials validated HARP's recovery geometry under field-of-view limitation and environmental occlusions.
2610.33640.tldr_en: HARP is introduced, a handoff-aware recovery planner that registers bounded sender predictions in the receiver's local map, distinguishes field-of-view failure from physical occlusion, and generates failure-specific yaw, translation, and parallax viewpoints.

llm.title_ja: HARP：マルチUAVハンドオフにおける能動的目標獲得のためのハンドオフ認識型リカバリプランナー
llm.tldr_ja: HARPは、境界づけられた送信側予測を受信側のローカルマップに登録し、失敗特有の視点やヨー、並進を生成するハンドオフ認識型リカバリプランナーである。
llm.problem: 連続的な空中追跡において、ハンドオフ中の受信側UAVは事前の目標観測を欠いており、送信側のカバレッジを妨げずに利用可能な視点を能動的に獲得する必要がある。
llm.method: 受信側のクリアランス、送信側の観測可能性、保護された送信側と目標の可視性、時間的妥当性について候補運動をチェックし、到達不能な場合は再計画を行う。
llm.result: シミュレーションの49の標準試行すべてと16のストレストレス試行のうち15で目標を獲得し、実飛行試験でもリカバリジオメトリを検証した。
keywords_ja: リカバリプランニング

2610.33584.title: HA-DiPO: Diffusion Policy Optimization for Heterogeneous Cooperative Transport
2610.33584.abstract: Cooperative transport with heterogeneous legged robots requires coordinating different motion capabilities while supporting an unfixed shared payload. We present HA-DiPO (Heterogeneous-Agent Diffusion Policy Optimization), a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE). The framework decouples team-level coordination from embodiment-specific motion control: at the high level, a centralized critic uses team-value estimates to jointly train independent coordination policies, aligning robot-specific action responses with a shared transport objective; at the low level, embodiment-specific robust motion policies track the coordination commands. The high-level diffusion policies offer more flexible action distributions than single-Gaussian parameterizations, allowing potentially multimodal coordination responses to be represented. The coordination policies learn from scratch through reward-driven simulator interaction without demonstrations. At execution, each robot generates coordination commands using only local robot and payload observations, without partner-state inputs or inter-robot messages. Simulation comparisons show that HA-DiPO achieves higher final mean returns and velocity-tracking success rates, as well as lower velocity errors, than the evaluated baselines. Real-world experiments further demonstrate quadrupedal-wheeled-legged and human-robot cooperative transport.
2610.33584.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Project website: https://ha-dipo.github.io/
2610.33584.tldr_en: HA-DiPO (Heterogeneous-Agent Diffusion Policy Optimization), a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework under centralized training with decentralized execution, is presented and real-world experiments demonstrate quadrupedal-wheeled-legged and human-robot cooperative transport.

llm.title_ja: HA-DiPO：異種協調輸送のための拡散ポリシー最適化
llm.tldr_ja: HA-DiPOは、チームレベルのコーディネーションとエンボディメント固有の運動制御を分離し、報酬駆動型のシミュレータ相互作用を通じて学習する階層型マルチエージェント強化学習フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 異種脚ロボットによる協調輸送では、固定されていない共有ペイロードを支えながら異なる運動能力を調整する必要がある。
llm.method: 集中学習分散実行（CTDE）の下で、高レベルの集中批評家がチーム価値推定を用いて協調ポリシーを共同訓練し、低レベルが頑健な運動ポリシーでコマンドを追従する。
llm.result: ベースラインと比較して、より高い最終平均報酬、速度追跡成功率、および低い速度誤差を達成し、四足・車輪・脚およびヒューマノイドの協調輸送を実証した。

2610.33582.title: Replicate What Varies: Resource Sharing for Domain-Randomized Embodied Simulation
2610.33582.abstract: Simulation provides a low-cost sandbox where embodied agents can attempt tasks, observe outcomes, and learn from experience. Running many diverse simulation environments concurrently can consume substantial CPU and GPU memory because independently constructed scenes duplicate resources that remain unchanged across instances. We present Patchwork, a resource-sharing system for domain-randomized simulation, built around the representation $E=T+Δ$: a shared template contains common resources, and a patch records the mutations needed to construct a target environment. Patchwork separates randomization sampling from replay and selects reusable templates together with patches that preserve each target environment's intended configuration. Its layered runtime shares compiled model structure and immutable assets while keeping mutable parameters and simulation state private to each instance. We implement Patchwork on robosuite and MuJoCo and evaluate it on LIBERO-plus and RoboCasa365 workloads. At 32 replicas, shared-template execution reduces CPU RSS by 88-92% relative to process-per-environment execution. Controlled experiments show how sharing shifts memory growth toward template diversity and unique asset content rather than instance count, within the supported sharing boundaries.
2610.33582.tldr_en: This work presents Patchwork, a resource-sharing system for domain-randomized simulation, built around the representation $E=T+\Delta$: a shared template contains common resources, and a patch records the mutations needed to construct a target environment.

llm.title_ja: 変化するものを複製する：ドメインランダム化された具現化シミュレーションのためのリソース共有
llm.tldr_ja: Patchworkは、共通リソースを含む共有テンプレートとターゲット環境の構築に必要な変異を記録するパッチ表現に基づき、ドメインランダム化シミュレーションにおけるメモリ消費を削減するリソース共有システムである。
llm.problem: 多くの多様なシミュレーション環境を並行して実行すると、独立して構築されたシーンが不変のリソースを複製するため、CPUおよびGPUメモリを大量に消費する。
llm.method: ランダム化サンプリングをリプレイから分離し、コンパイルされたモデル構造や不変のアセットを共有しつつ、可変パラメータとシミュレーション状態をインスタンスごとにプライベートに保つ。
llm.result: 32レプリカにおいて、共有テンプレートの実行により、プロセスごとの実行と比較してCPUのRSSを88〜92%削減した。

2610.33574.title: Memory-Aware Keyframe Management for Dense Maps on Memory-Constrained Robots
2610.33574.abstract: Running a language model and a dense 3D map on one device means the two share one memory, and exceeding its limit is an out-of-memory failure. Map systems that keep a bounded working set bound it by a count of keyframes, but the memory one keyframe occupies varies widely with what it carries, so a count does not control what the working set occupies. The unit of admission is as poorly matched, since a radius around the pose, a fixed cell, or the graph neighbors of the last matched keyframe all move parts of the map that are not needed. We therefore propose two decisions. First, the memory the resident map uses is bounded directly, and the cost of every admission is known before any data is read, from per-keyframe resident sizes computed offline and carried with the map. Second, keyframes are admitted and released at a semantic spatial unit, the rooms and corridors of the building, so that the robot holds the zone it occupies together with the zone it is about to enter while the zones it has passed are released. Every admission measures the resident total, makes room, and only then reads, so the budget is never overshot. On two NVIDIA Jetson boards the budget holds in every run and the model gives up at most 0.8 percent of its throughput, whereas without it the operating system kills the model or the map. Under that budget, and over the environments evaluated, admission by semantic zone localizes 6-9 points more of the query frames than a geometric partition of matched zone count and about twice as much as the retrieval of RTAB-Map, at a lower ATE. Bounding memory lets the map and the model coexist, and moving the map in semantic zones makes the bounded map usable.
2610.33574.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to ICRA 2027
2610.33574.tldr_en: Bounding memory lets the map and the model coexist, and moving the map in semantic zones makes the bounded map usable.

llm.title_ja: メモリ制限のあるロボットにおける高密度マップのためのメモリを考慮したキーフレーム管理
llm.tldr_ja: メモリ制限のあるデバイス上で言語モデルと高密度3Dマップを共存させるため、メモリ使用量を直接制限し、建物内の部屋や廊下などの意味的空間単位でキーフレームの出し入れを行う手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 言語モデルと高密度の3Dマップを1つのデバイスで実行するとメモリ上限を超えてOOMエラーが発生するが、従来のキーフレーム数や幾何学的領域に基づく管理ではメモリ量を適切に制御できない。
llm.method: メモリ使用量を直接バジェット化し、オフラインで計算されたキーフレームごとの常駐サイズを用いて、部屋や廊下といった意味的空間単位でキーフレームの追加と解放を行う。
llm.result: NVIDIA Jetsonボード上で動作し、システムがモデルやマップを強制終了させることなく予算を維持し、従来の幾何学的分割やRTAB-Mapと比較してより高いクエリフレームのローカライズ率を低いATEで達成した。
keywords_ja: ローカライゼーション

2610.33565.title: WorldFailBench: Do World Models Understand Policy Failures?
2610.33565.abstract: Robot policy evaluation informs deployment decisions and policy improvement, but physical testing and simulator preparation require substantial effort. World models offer a complementary route through closed-loop interaction in generated environments. Recent benchmarks have demonstrated their potential as policy evaluators through outcome-based evaluation (i.e., assessing task success or failure). However, such evaluation does not establish whether world models faithfully simulate how policies fail. Misrepresenting failures can lead to incorrect diagnoses of policy weaknesses and make policies appear ready for deployment even when small scene changes cause them to fail. We therefore ask: do world models faithfully simulate how and at which stages policies fail, and under what conditions they transition from success to failure? To answer this question, we introduce WorldFailBench with three evaluation tasks. Failure reason tests whether models reproduce the observable errors policies make. Failure stage assesses whether failures concentrate at the same stages of full-task execution. Failure boundary examines whether models reproduce the conditions under which policies transition from success to failure under controlled scene changes in simulation. The benchmark covers manipulation tasks in the LIBERO and RoboTwin simulation environments and real-world manipulation tasks performed by the G1 humanoid robot. Experiments across seven world models reveal substantial gaps in their understanding of policy failures, providing guidance for developing more reliable world models for policy evaluation.
2610.33565.tldr_en: Experiments across seven world models reveal substantial gaps in their understanding of policy failures, providing guidance for developing more reliable world models for policy evaluation.

llm.title_ja: WorldFailBench：ワールドモデルは方針の失敗を理解しているか？
llm.tldr_ja: ワールドモデルがロボットポリシーの失敗理由、失敗ステージ、失敗境界を忠実にシミュレートできるかを評価するためのベンチマーク「WorldFailBench」を提案し、7つのワールドモデルを評価した。
llm.problem: ワールドモデルを用いたポリシー評価において、モデルがポリシーの失敗をどのように引き起こすかを忠実にシミュレートしているかが不明であり、失敗の誤認やデバッグミスにつながる。
llm.method: 失敗理由（observable errors）、失敗ステージ（failure concentration）、失敗境界（transition under controlled scene changes）の3つの評価タスクからなるベンチマーク「WorldFailBench」を導入する。
llm.result: 7つのワールドモデルの実験により、ポリシーの失敗に対する理解に大きなギャップがあることが明らかになり、ポリシー評価用により信頼性の高いワールドモデルを開発するための指針が得られた。

2610.33562.title: Hybrid-time PINNs: Discontinuity-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Learning Hybrid Dynamical Systems
2610.33562.abstract: Hybrid dynamical systems flow continuously but jump at discrete events. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) fit data while enforcing known dynamics, but a single network is smooth in time and cannot model these jumps. We show that the more closely a PINN follows a jump, the larger its physics loss must be. We propose hybrid-time PINNs (HT-PINNs), which assign one network to each flow interval of the hybrid time domain and train the networks jointly with the jump times and the unknown parameters. The number of jumps and the sequence of modes are found by enumeration. HT-PINNs recover the number of jumps and the restitution coefficient of a bouncing ball. In a MuJoCo simulation of robotic disassembly, where a robot pulls a press-fitted pin out of a housing through a spring, HT-PINNs find the number of jumps and the sequence of modes, and estimate the static and kinetic friction coefficients with small errors of 0.1% and 1.7%.
2610.33562.tldr_en: It is shown that the more closely a PINN follows a jump, the larger its physics loss must be, and proposed hybrid-time PINNs (HT-PINNs), which assign one network to each flow interval of the hybrid time domain and train the networks jointly with the jump times and the unknown parameters.

llm.title_ja: ハイブリッド時間PINN：ハイブリッド力学系学習のための不連続性を考慮した物理情報ニューラルネットワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 連続的なフローと離散的なジャンプを持つハイブリッド力学系をモデル化するため、ハイブリッド時間ドメインの各フロー区間にネットワークを割り当て、ジャンプ時間と未知パラメータと共同で訓練する「HT-PINN」を提案する。
llm.problem: 通常の物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）は時間に関して滑らかであるため、離散的なイベント（ジャンプ）を持つハイブリッド力学系をモデル化できない。
llm.method: ハイブリッド時間ドメインの各フロー区間に1つのネットワークを割り当て、ジャンプの回数とモードのシーケンスを列挙によって求めつつ、ネットワークをジャンプ時間や未知パラメータとともに共同で訓練する。
llm.result: 跳ねるボールのジャンプ数や反発係数を復元し、ロボットの分解組立のMuJoCoシミュレーションにおいてジャンプ数やモードの特定、静摩擦・動摩擦係数の推定を小さな誤差で実現した。
keywords_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク

2610.33546.title: MOON: Learning When to Forget and How to Move On in Vision-and-Language Navigation
2610.33546.abstract: Recent vision-and-language navigation (VLN) policies act on their visual history, and an incorrect action can take them off the instructed route. Paired interventions on four VLN policies show that clearing the history doubles pooled success at the onset of a deviation but lowers it on route, while later in a deviation, removing only the off-route frames helps much less. After a deviation, the retained history keeps the policy from turning where a turn is needed, which we call behavioral inertia. We propose MOON, a framework that equips a frozen VLN policy with two lightweight modules, adding less than 1% of its parameters. A deviation judge decides when to forget, raising an alarm that clears the history when it predicts that the agent is off route. A recovery policy, trained with GRPO from alarm states, learns how to move on, turning more of the successes found only by sampling into a single greedy rollout. Experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE show that MOON reaches the highest R2R-CE success rate among the compared methods and raises the success rate of its frozen base by 5.2 and 6.0 points, and an ablation with a random trigger indicates that this gain depends on when the history is cleared. Without retraining, MOON also improves zero-shot object-goal navigation on HM3D-OVON. Together, these results suggest that deviation recovery depends on knowing when to forget, not only how to act. Code is available at https://github.com/AutoLab-SAI-SJTU/MOON.
2610.33546.tldr_en: The proposed MOON framework, a framework that equips a frozen VLN policy with two lightweight modules, adding less than 1% of its parameters, improves zero-shot object-goal navigation on HM3D-OVON and suggests that deviation recovery depends on knowing when to forget, not only how to act.

llm.title_ja: MOON：視覚言語ナビゲーションにおいて「忘れるべき時」と「進むべき方法」を学ぶ
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された視覚言語ナビゲーションポリシーに軽量なモジュールを追加し、逸脱時に履歴をクリアするタイミングを判断してリカバリーポリシーで軌道を修正するフレームワーク「MOON」を提案する。
llm.problem: 視覚言語ナビゲーション（VLN）ポリシーにおいて、誤った行動がルートからの逸脱を招き、過去の履歴（行動的慣性）が新しい方向への旋回を妨げる。
llm.method: 凍結されたVLNポリシーにパラメータの1%未満の軽量モジュールを追加し、逸脱を判断して履歴をクリアする「deviation judge」と、アラーム状態からGRPOで訓練された「recovery policy」を組み合わせる。
llm.result: R2R-CEおよびRxR-CEにおいてベースラインを大きく上回る成功率を達成し、追加の再訓練なしでゼロショットの物体目標ナビゲーションも改善した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション
ロボットナビゲーション

2610.33508.title: MimicAll: Structured Embodiment Conditioning for Cross-Humanoid Whole-Body Motion Tracking
2610.33508.abstract: Humanoid motion trackers reproduce diverse behaviors, but sharing a policy across bodies requires accounting for differences in structure, morphology and dynamics. We present MimicAll, a reinforcement-learning framework for shared whole-body motion tracking across heterogeneous humanoids. A structured embodiment descriptor is encoded into global and joint-aligned conditions, which are combined with observation history and body-matched motion references to predict joint-target offsets. Physics-consistent embodiment randomization, body-calibrated retargeting and heterogeneous simulation support training across 4,096 variants from 16 humanoid families. We introduce a benchmark of 464 bodies across five distribution strata to evaluate motion generalization, within-family embodiment shifts and unseen-family transfer. Controlled ablations show that embodiment information improves motion completion with simple concatenation, while self-attention yields the lowest global position errors. With equal training transitions, shared training achieves 99.4% 30-second success on randomized G1 bodies in 100STYLE, versus 42.9% for a single-body specialist. With Flat-MLP encoding and concatenation, continued training on a motion subset excluding obstacle categories achieves 98.3% and 93.5% 30-second success on 100STYLE for sampled training bodies and out-of-distribution variants within seen families, respectively. On an eight-motion LAFAN1 subset excluding ground and get-up sequences across 464 bodies, mismatched body conditions reduce self-attention's 30-second success from 61.7% to 47.0%, demonstrating a closed-loop benefit from embodiment information.
2610.33508.tldr_en: Control ablations show that embodiment information improves motion completion with simple concatenation, while self-attention yields the lowest global position errors, in MimicAll, a reinforcement-learning framework for shared whole-body motion tracking across heterogeneous humanoids.

llm.title_ja: MimicAll：異種ヒューマノイドの全身モーション追従に向けた構造化身体条件付け
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な構造や形態を持つ異種ヒューマノイド間での共有全身モーション追従を実現するため、構造化された身体記述子を用いた強化学習フレームワーク「MimicAll」を提案する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドのモーション追従ポリシーを異なる身体間で共有する際、構造、形態、ダイナミクスの違いを考慮する必要がある。
llm.method: 構造化された身体記述子をグローバルおよび関節整合条件にエンコードし、観測履歴や身体適合モーション参照と組み合わせて関節ターゲットオフセットを予測する強化学習フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 16ファミリー4,096種のバリエーションにわたる訓練をサポートし、ランダム化されたG1ボディ等において単身体のスペシャリストを大きく上回る成功率を達成した。

2610.33494.title: RBGA: Residual-Budget Guide Arbitration for Offline-to-Online Safe Reinforcement Learning in Dexterous Manipulation
2610.33494.abstract: Dexterous manipulation requires robots to leverage existing datasets for rapid skill acquisition while maintaining safety during real-world deployment to prevent damage to the robot or its surroundings. Offline-to-online safe reinforcement learning (O2O safe RL) provides a promising solution for this problem by leveraging prior experience for online improvement under safety constraints, thereby mitigating the sample inefficiency and exploration risk of learning safe policies from scratch. However, existing O2O safe RL approaches do not explicitly account for the safety budget already consumed when making decisions within an episode. Excessive cost incurred early can therefore leave little room for subsequent exploration and policy improvement. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{R}esidual-\textbf{B}udget \textbf{G}uide \textbf{A}rbitration (RBGA), an algorithm that explicitly tracks the remaining episode safety budget and uses it to adaptively select between offline guidance and the evolving online policy. At each step, RBGA compares the cost-to-go estimates of the guide and online actions against the remaining budget, enabling step-wise action arbitration throughout the episode. We provide theoretical analysis characterizing the safety implications of residual-budget-based selection and its effect on guide-assisted exploration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RBGA enables effective online policy improvement while maintaining strong safety performance. Our code is available at this \href{https://github.com/sii-pilab}{link}.
2610.33494.tldr_en: An algorithm that explicitly tracks the remaining episode safety budget and uses it to adaptively select between offline guidance and the evolving online policy, enabling step-wise action arbitration throughout the episode and theoretical analysis characterizing the safety implications of residual-budget-based selection and its effect on guide-assisted exploration.

llm.title_ja: RBGA：器用なマニピュレーションにおけるオフライン・ツー・オンライン安全強化学習のための残余予算ガイド調停
llm.tldr_ja: エピソード内の残余安全予算を明示的に追跡し、オフラインガイダンスとオンラインポリシーを適応的に選択して安全な方策改善を実現するアルゴリズム「RBGA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のオフライン・ツー・オンライン安全強化学習ではエピソード内で消費された安全予算が考慮されないため、初期の過剰なコストがその後の探索と方策改善を妨げる。
llm.method: 残余エピソード安全予算を追跡し、ガイドとオンラインアクションの残余コスト推定量と予算を比較して、ステップごとにアクション調停を行うアルゴリズム「RBGA」を構築する。
llm.result: 安全性能を強く維持しながら、効果的なオンライン方策の改善が可能であることを広範な実験により実証した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.33487.title: ReSight: Task-Driven Self-Improving Memory for Embodied Agents
2610.33487.abstract: Robots can use historical observations to answer spatiotemporal queries in familiar environments, but the presence of relevant evidence does not imply that existing tools support the operations a task requires. We introduce ReSight, a task-driven self-improving memory system for embodied agents that expands the capabilities for processing and accessing historical observations as task demands arise. ReSight retains keyframes and their spatiotemporal associations, separating observation evidence from extensible derived fields so that stored observations can be reprocessed for new needs. An execution agent and a coding agent share this memory through different interfaces: the former calls registered tools within a bounded online budget, while the latter uses a programmable workspace and a larger exploration budget to inspect evidence, write programs, and acquire models as needed. To realize capability expansion in ReSight, we develop Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM), which identifies capability gaps from execution and exploration records without task reference answers and converts exploration-derived solutions into reusable memory builders, query tools, and skills, extending memory representations and access capabilities as needed. Experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate effective base memory access and capability expansion. With the execution model and online budget held fixed within each benchmark, EDM reduces mean position error on OC-NaVQA from 33.10 m to 24.72 m and improves high-level success on FindingDory from 38.3% to 63.8%. With the tools and skill frozen, success still improves by 28.3 percentage points on FindingDory episodes excluded from exploration and distillation. Experiments on real robot patrol memories further demonstrate reuse of these capabilities for subsequent queries and new memories, with fewer online tool calls on average.
2610.33487.tldr_en: This work introduces ReSight, a task-driven self-improving memory system for embodied agents that expands the capabilities for processing and accessing historical observations as task demands arise, and develops Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM), which identifies capability gaps from execution and exploration records without task reference answers.

llm.title_ja: ReSight：身体性エージェントのためのタスク駆動型自己改善メモリ
llm.tldr_ja: タスクの要求に応じて過去の観察履歴の処理・アクセス能力を拡張する、身体性エージェント向けのタスク駆動型自己改善メモリシステム「ReSight」を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットが過去の観察データを使ってクエリに答える際、既存のツールだけではタスクが必要とする操作を十分にサポートできない。
llm.method: キーフレームとその時空間的関連性を保持し、実行エージェントとコーディングエージェントでメモリを共有。探索・蒸留・マウント（EDM）により機能ギャップを特定し、再利用可能なツールやスキルを自動構築する。
llm.result: 複数のパブリックベンチマークにおいてベースメモリへのアクセスと機能拡張が効果的であることを示し、OC-NaVQAやFindingDoryでの位置誤差削減や成功率向上を達成した。

2610.33486.title: Learning Dexterous Manipulation: Hands, Simulators, Training, and Evaluation
2610.33486.abstract: A dexterous hand can change an object's pose without setting it down. This survey covers 113 learning-based methods that attempt it, the hands they run on, the simulators they train in, and how they report results. The field has largely converged on one recipe: reinforcement learning on privileged state in a GPU simulator, distilled into a vision-only student for transfer to hardware. Almost half the corpus trains that way, nearly all of it in one simulator, whose own successors are barely used. A second and faster-growing branch learns from teleoperated demonstration instead, through vision-language-action models, diffusion policies, and systems whose contribution is the collection rig itself. Published work has tripled since 2022. Grasping remains the largest task family and bimanual coordination the fastest-rising, and almost every experiment runs on one of four hands. What the survey adds comes from reading released code and vendor specifications beside the papers. Eight hands that can be bought or built from published designs appear in no method paper here. Where the depth a hand sinks into the object it holds is reported at all, it is not measured in the physics that produced the motion. Section VII proposes a protocol for the unreported quantities; the body gives the counts behind every claim above.
2610.33486.comment: 36 pages, 14 figures, 7 tables. Survey of 113 learning-based dexterous manipulation methods, with a comparison of each paper's stated reward against its released code
2610.33486.tldr_en: This survey covers 113 learning-based methods that attempt reinforcement learning on privileged state in a GPU simulator, the hands they run on, the simulators they train in, and how they report results.

llm.title_ja: 器用なマニピュレーションの学習：ハンド、シミュレータ、訓練、評価
llm.tldr_ja: GPUシミュレータでの強化学習やテレオペレーションによるデモンストレーション学習を用いた、113件の学習ベースの器用なマニピュレーション手法に関する調査を行う。
llm.problem: 学習ベースの器用なマニピュレーション分野において、使用されるハンド、シミュレータ、訓練手法、結果の報告方法が多岐にわたるが、その実態の全体像が体系的に整理されていない。
llm.method: 113件の学習ベースの手法、それらが使用するハンド、シミュレータ、評価方法について、公開コードやベンダー仕様を読み比べながら詳細な調査と分析を行う。
llm.result: GPUシミュレータでの強化学習からビジョンベースの学生モデルへの蒸留が主流であることや、把持が最大のタスクファミリーであり、双腕協調が急速に増加していることなどを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.33480.title: MDPO: Multi-constraint Dexterous Policy Optimization with Reinforcement Learning
2610.33480.abstract: Dexterous manipulation requires high-dimensional control policies to accomplish complex contact-rich tasks while simultaneously satisfying multiple safety requirements, such as joint limits, unsafe finger configurations, arm collisions, and unstable object interactions. Constrained reinforcement learning (RL) provides a principled framework for incorporating these requirements into dexterous manipulation policy learning. However, existing constrained RL methods for dexterous manipulation primarily focus on cumulative cost constraints and struggle to simultaneously handle multiple heterogeneous constraints during dexterous policy learning. In this work, we propose Multi-constraint Dexterous Policy Optimization (MDPO) for safe dexterous manipulation. We first formulate dexterous manipulation as a multi-constraint policy optimization problem involving both cumulative cost constraints and state-wise cost constraints. Based on this formulation, we integrate multi-constraint projection into the dexterous manipulation policy optimization process. Specifically, we employ constraint-specific policy projections to map the intermediate policy that maximizes task performance onto the feasible regions defined by the cumulative cost constraint and the state-wise cost constraint. Extensive experiments on ReDMan, including safe joint control, finger safety, and grasping tasks, demonstrate that MDPO achieves superior constraint satisfaction while maintaining competitive task performance compared with the baselines. Our code is available at this link.
2610.33480.tldr_en: This work first formulate dexterous manipulation as a multi-constraint policy optimization problem involving both cumulative cost constraints and state-wise cost constraints, and integrates multi-constraint projection into the dexterous manipulation policy optimization process.

llm.title_ja: MDPO：強化学習を用いた複数制約器用方策最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 累積コスト制約と状態ごとのコスト制約を同時に満たす安全な器用マニピュレーションを実現するため、制約固有の方策投影を組み込んだ「MDPO」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の制約付き強化学習は主に累積コスト制約に焦点を当てており、器用なマニピュレーションにおける複数の異種制約（関節制限、不安全な指の構成、腕の衝突など）を同時に扱うことが困難である。
llm.method: 器用なマニピュレーションを累積コスト制約と状態ごとのコスト制約を持つ多制約方策最適化問題として定式化し、タスク性能を最大化する中間方策を許容領域にマッピングする制約固有の方策投影を統合する。
llm.result: ReDManを用いた安全な関節制御、指の安全性、把持タスクの実験において、ベースラインと比較して優れた制約充足性と競争力のあるタスク性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.33476.title: A Differentiable Chassis Safety Layer for Intelligent Vehicle Motion Control
2610.33476.abstract: Learning-based vehicle motion control requires coordination between diverse task objectives and state-dependent chassis safety constraints. Conventional cascaded architectures may compromise task performance when safety filters modify nominal commands independently of policy learning. This article proposes a differentiable chassis safety layer that modularly integrates task-oriented control with explicit physical constraints. Actuator limits, individual-tire force constraints, and vehicle handling envelopes are incorporated into sequential quadratic programs. Each projected command propagates the predicted vehicle dynamics and updates subsequent constraints, enabling temporal gradient coupling through implicit differentiation. A two-stage learning strategy combines expert imitation with risk-guided supervision and conditional intervention guidance to coordinate nominal control decisions with chassis safety constraints. Closed-loop evaluations under unseen scenarios, emergency maneuvers, and ablation studies demonstrate that the proposed method improves safety-performance coordination and exploits vehicle dynamic potential while maintaining handling stability.
2610.33476.tldr_en: Closed-loop evaluations under unseen scenarios, emergency maneuvers, and ablation studies demonstrate that the proposed method improves safety-performance coordination and exploits vehicle dynamic potential while maintaining handling stability.

llm.title_ja: インテリジェント車両運動制御のための微分可能なシャシー安全層
llm.tldr_ja: タスク指向の制御と明示的な物理的制約をモジュール式に統合し、陰関数微分を通じて時間的勾配結合を可能にする微分可能なシャシー安全層を提案する。
llm.problem: 学習ベースの車両運動制御において、従来の階層型アーキテクチャでは安全フィルタが方策学習とは独立にコマンドを修正するため、タスク性能が損なわれる可能性がある。
llm.method: アクチュエータ限界、タイヤ力制約、車両ハンドリングエンベロープを逐次二次計画法（QP）に組み込み、投影された各コマンドを通じて予測車両ダイナミクスを伝播させ、陰関数微分で勾配を結合する。
llm.result: 未見のシナリオや緊急時機動の評価において、ハンドリングの安定性を維持しながら、安全性とパフォーマンスの協調を改善し、車両の動的潜在能力を引き出すことを実証した。

2610.33471.title: SCET-CBF: Speed-Calibrated Soft Guidance for One-Step Dynamic Navigation
2610.33471.abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) support collision avoidance, yet dense dynamic encounters can leave a vehicle with no feasible command. Geometric refinements and soft constraints help preserve motion choices. Using these choices also requires accounting for the vehicle's changing turning response. For a steering-limited bicycle, braking can lower closing speed while slowing the lateral motion needed before an obstacle arrives. We propose SCET-CBF, a speed-calibrated soft guidance law for one-step dynamic navigation. A short lateral escape maneuver gives an allowable approach speed. Its speed derivative allows a quadratic program to weigh both effects of braking when choosing acceleration and steering. Soft penalties accommodate competing obstacle preferences within the input set permitted by segment and braking constraints. We derive the guidance and establish protection over each accepted motion segment, together with conditional braking invariance for a single obstacle. On 2500 paired tasks with a 60 s deadline, SCET achieves 72.8% completion, compared with 49.8% for CBF/velocity-obstacle control and 69.8% for an enhanced 1 s CBF-MPC. At 100 obstacles, SCET and the enhanced MPC complete 52.4% and 33.6% of tasks. Paired studies identify the contributions of speed feedback and early activation. Further evaluations examine the operating range under lateral acceleration limits and bounded motion and execution errors.
2610.33471.tldr_en: This work proposes SCET-CBF, a speed-calibrated soft guidance law for one-step dynamic navigation that derives the guidance and establish protection over each accepted motion segment, together with conditional braking invariance for a single obstacle.

llm.title_ja: SCET-CBF：1ステップ動的ナビゲーションのための速度較正ソフトガイダンス
llm.tldr_ja: 車両の旋回応答の変化を考慮し、障害物回避のための許容接近速度とブレーキ効果を二次計画法で適切に重み付けする速度較正ソフトガイダンス法「SCET-CBF」を提案する。
llm.problem: 高密度な動的遭遇環境において制御バリア関数（CBF）を用いると、車両に実行可能なコマンドが残らない状況が生じる。
llm.method: 短い側方逃避機動から許容接近速度を導出し、その速度導関数を利用して、加速度とステアリングを選択する際にブレーキの両方の効果を二次計画法で重み付けするソフトガイダンス法を構築する。
llm.result: 2500件のペアタスクにおいて、従来のCBF/速度障害物制御や強化された1秒CBF-MPCを上回る完了率を達成した。

2610.33446.title: MOTIO: Agentic Skill Engineering for Reality-Grounded Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2610.33446.abstract: We present MOTIO, an agentic skill-engineering system that turns ordinary human-action videos, reality-grounded 3D assets, motion references, and reusable robot skills into executable humanoid loco-manipulation programs. Through in-context task and contact reasoning, an agent constructs staged robot-native interactions and improves them using physics execution, multi-frame feedback, and human validation---without task-specific teleoperation or robot demonstration collection. Agentic 3D supplies metric product and environment assets, while existing whole-body, inverse-kinematics, and dexterous-hand interfaces realize the programs. Across 33 timestamped first approvals, the median recorded agent-turn time is 97.0 minutes and request-to-approval duration is 2.80 hours. Simulation-side layout and object variation prepare a long-horizon bottle-disposal skill for a continuous 101.75-second physical G1 execution in a scanned office; physical refinement reduces screw-tightening thread residual by 76.0%. Agent-generated skills additionally supervise BC/DAgger distillation into one shared reference policy, completing 18 simulated tasks under the same checkpoint without inference-time expert intervention. Project page: https://iiiiqiiii.github.io/motio/
2610.33446.comment: 24 pages, including 11 pages of supplementary material
2610.33446.tldr_en: MOTIO is presented, an agentic skill-engineering system that turns ordinary human-action videos, reality-grounded 3D assets, motion references, and reusable robot skills into executable humanoid loco-manipulation programs without task-specific teleoperation or robot demonstration collection.

llm.title_ja: MOTIO：現実に基づくヒューマノイドの移動・操作のためのエージェント型スキルエンジニアリング
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の動作動画や3Dアセットから、タスク固有のテレオペレーションなしで実行可能なヒューマノイドの移動・操作プログラムを構築するエージェント型システム「MOTIO」を提案する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドに複雑な移動・操作（loco-manipulation）のスキルを教えるには、膨大なテレオペレーションや実機デモンストレーション収集の労力が必要となる。
llm.method: コンテキスト内のタスク・接触推論を通じて、エージェントが物理実行やマルチフレームフィードバックを用いて段階的なロボット向けインタラクションプログラムを構築・改善する。
llm.result: オフィスのスキャン環境でのG1ロボットによる101.75秒間の連続実行や、ネジ締めのスレッド残差の削減、共通参照ポリシーへの蒸留などにおいて有効性を実証した。
keywords_ja: スキルエンジニアリング

2610.33445.title: From Intelligence to Autonomy: Foundations and Construction of Autonomous Agents for Future Intelligent Systems
2610.33445.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from one-off perception and generation tasks toward long-term planning, tool use, and interaction with real environments. Greater task competence, however, does not automatically yield autonomy: an external actor may still have to set goals, sustain operating conditions, detect failures, and approve updates. We define an autonomous agent as a system that, within explicit identity and authority boundaries, maintains both task goals and viability conditions, acts continuously using models of the world and itself, and adjusts its control mechanisms and long-term capabilities through feedback. We trace the conceptual path from homeostasis and feedback control to autopoiesis and biological autonomy. We then distinguish six lines of operationalization: computational autopoiesis, behavior-based robotics, agent formalization, adaptive software, embodied adaptation, and robotic self-modeling. On this basis, we propose a one-boundary, four-loop framework in which Operational, Viability, Reflexive, and Learning loops organize task execution, self-maintenance, metacontrol, and governed learning. Five paired simulation experiments test permission constraints, road-closure response, health maintenance, capability re-estimation, and cross-task learning. Their results provide preliminary evidence for the feasibility of these mechanisms, while broader environments and physical systems remain to be tested.
2610.33445.tldr_en: This work traces the conceptual path from homeostasis and feedback control to autopoiesis and biological autonomy and proposes a one-boundary, four-loop framework in which Operational, Viability, Reflexive, and Learning loops organize task execution, self-maintenance, metacontrol, and governed learning.

llm.title_ja: 知性から自律性へ：未来のインテリジェントシステムのための自律エージェントの基礎と構築
llm.tldr_ja: 恒常性やフィードバック制御から生物学的自律性への概念的道筋をたどり、運用・生存・再帰・学習の4つのループで構成される自律エージェントのためのフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 人工知能のタスク能力が向上しても、外部のアクターが目標設定、稼働条件の維持、障害検知、アップデート承認を行う必要があり、自動的に自律性が得られるわけではない。
llm.method: 恒常性からオートポイエーシスに至る概念的道筋をトレースし、Operational、Viability、Reflexive、Learningの4つのループからなる1境界4ループフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 5つのペアシミュレーション実験を通じて、提案メカニズムの実行可能性に関する予備的証拠を示した。
llm.limitation: 広範な環境や物理システムでの検証は今後の課題として残されている

2610.33413.title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
2610.33413.abstract: Localized AI manipulations in long-form videos often affect brief events within otherwise authentic content, making video-level classification insufficient for forensic analysis. Existing audio-visual deepfake benchmarks largely focus on short talking-head clips, while long-form temporal forensics remains predominantly visual. We introduce AV-FABLE, a dual-timeline benchmark for sparse manipulations in open-scene long-form audio-visual videos. AV-FABLE contains 16,650 pristine--manipulated twin pairs (998 hours) created with 27 editing configurations, with separate audio and visual timelines that enable modality-specific temporal localization and expose errors hidden by joint-timeline evaluation. On AV-FABLE, zero-shot prompting of audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) yields near-chance detection and poor temporal localization. In contrast, supervised readouts of their frozen perception features recover strong forensic signals, suggesting manipulation evidence is encoded in these representations but not effectively exposed through language outputs. Motivated by this observation, we propose NFSR(Native Forensics via Separated Readouts), which reads frozen AV-LLM features with separate audio and visual temporal decoders. NFSR achieves the best audio-visual localization performance in-domain and across all three out-of-distribution settings, including transfer to held-out videos from an external long-video forensic benchmark. AV-FABLE, code, and model weights will be publicly released.
2610.33413.tldr_en: NFSR(Native Forensics via Separated Readouts), which reads frozen AV-LLM features with separate audio and visual temporal decoders achieves the best audio-visual localization performance in-domain and across all three out-of-distribution settings, including transfer to held-out videos from an external long-video forensic benchmark.
2610.33413.hf_summary_en: AV-FABLE introduces a long-form audio-visual benchmark for sparse manipulations, showing that frozen perception features of audio-visual large language models contain forensic evidence best recovered via separate temporal decoders rather than language outputs.

llm.title_ja: AV-FABLE：長尺動画における音声・視覚的改変のフォレンジック
llm.tldr_ja: 長尺動画内の局所的な改変をモダリティごとに時間的ローカライズして検出するため、音声と視覚のデュアルタイムラインを持つベンチマーク「AV-FABLE」と「NFSR」手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の音声・視覚ディープフェイクベンチマークは短いクリップに偏っており、長尺動画内の局所的な改変に対する時間的フォレンジック分析が不十分である。
llm.method: 16,650対のペア（998時間）からなるデュアルタイムラインベンチマーク「AV-FABLE」を構築し、音声と視覚の凍結された知覚特徴を別々の時間デコーダで読み取る「NFSR」を提案する。
llm.result: AV-FABLEおよびドメイン外の外部ベンチマークへの転移において、最高の音声・視覚ローカライズ性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出
音声・視覚フォレンジック

2610.33351.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
2610.33351.abstract: Motion perception is fundamental to computer vision and physical AI, and plays a central role in robotics, autonomous vehicles, human-computer interaction, and video compression. Traditional approaches such as background subtraction, frame-differencing and optical flow algorithms often struggle in complex or dynamic scenes, typically sacrificing spatial resolution for computational tractability. Here we introduce MoViD (Motion estimation via Virtual dispersion and phase Detection), a physics-inspired algorithm grounded in the principles that govern photonic time stretch - a highly successful ultrafast realtime data acquisition platform. Drawing inspiration from the optical physics therein, MoViD treats video as a collection of optical time series waveforms associated with pixels. Motion of an object through a pixel broadens the time series spectrum and, after group delay dispersion, induces a temporal phase that exists only if there is motion. Spatiotemporal group delay dispersion templates, corresponding to dielectric functions, classify specific motion trajectories. Unlike conventional empirical phase-based motion-analysis pipelines that require narrow-band spatial channelization and pyramid reconstruction, the physics-based MoViD operates directly on the broadband video signal, vastly increasing its computational speed. The resulting algorithm achieves unprecedented performance in both motion characterization and motion magnification, providing full-resolution motion mapping in real time at nearly 200 frames per second at 4K resolution and 70 frames per second for 8K video - orders of magnitude faster than classical optical flow approaches or learning-based methods. Notably, such extreme performance enables real time motion analysis at ultrahigh resolution for motion detection and compensation in robotics and other autonomous devices.
2610.33351.tldr_en: The resulting algorithm achieves unprecedented performance in both motion characterization and motion magnification, providing full-resolution motion mapping in real time at nearly 200 frames per second at 4K resolution and 70 frames per second for 8K video - orders of magnitude faster than classical optical flow approaches or learning-based methods.

llm.title_ja: フォトニックタイムストレッチにインスパイアされた動画内のリアルタイムモーション検出
llm.tldr_ja: フォトニックタイムストレッチの原理に基づき、動画を光時系列波形として処理することで、4K解像度で200 fps、8Kで70 fpsのリアルタイム・フル解像度モーションマッピングを実現する「MoViD」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来の背景差分やオプティカルフロー等の手法は、複雑なシーンにおいて計算処理能力を確保するために空間解像度を犠牲にすることが多い。
llm.method: 動画を画素に関連付けられた光時系列波形とみなし、オブジェクトの移動によるスペクトルの広がりと時間的位相を物理ベースのグループ遅延分散テンプレートで解析する「MoViD」を開発する。
llm.result: 従来のオプティカルフロー手法や学習ベースの手法よりも数桁高速に、4Kで約200 fps、8Kで70 fpsというリアルタイムでのフル解像度モーションマッピングを達成した。
keywords_ja: コンピュータビジョン

2610.33349.title: Contract-Based Agentic Systems Engineering: Delegation as Quotient for Assured System Design
2610.33349.abstract: A component an agent builds from a prompt can satisfy it and still break the system it joins, because the prompt omits what its neighbours assume of it. The artifact to hand over is computed, not written. A SysML v2 requirement with assumed and required constraints is an assume/guarantee contract, so when a system requirement is decomposed over fixed neighbours, the open component's requirement is the contract quotient, the weakest sound one, and again a SysML v2 requirement. Its required constraints carry the neighbours' assumptions, which a requirement for the mission alone drops and unit tests with mocked neighbours cannot reach. Signal Temporal Logic is closed under the quotient. We build the requirements, with derivation, allocation, satisfaction and verification, as a SysML~v2 model and compute the quotient from it. A case study delegates the local controller of a simulated warehouse robot, whose route crosses a worker's path and ends at a dock, to one language model under the quotient requirement, a mission-only requirement and a natural-language task, and scores the deliveries on live episodes against the system requirement from ground truth.
2610.33349.tldr_en: A case study delegates the local controller of a simulated warehouse robot to one language model under the quotient requirement, a mission-only requirement and a natural-language task, and scores the deliveries on live episodes against the system requirement from ground truth.

llm.title_ja: 契約ベースのエージェントシステム設計：保証されたシステム設計のための商としての委譲
llm.tldr_ja: SysML v2モデルから前提/保証コントラクトの商（quotient）を計算し、シミュレートされた倉庫ロボットのローカルコントローラーを言語モデルに安全に委譲するケーススタディを実施した。
llm.problem: エージェントがプロンプトから構築したコンポーネントは単体で満足しても、周囲のコンポーネントの前提条件を無視するためシステム全体を壊してしまう。
llm.method: SysML v2の要求モデルから前提/保証契約の商（quotient、最も弱い健全な条件）を計算し、シミュレートされた倉庫ロボットのローカルコントローラーの委譲に適用して検証する。
llm.result: シミュレートされた倉庫ロボットのタスクにおいて、商に基づく要求事項を用いることで正しく動作し、ライブエピソードで評価できることをケーススタディで示した。

2610.33338.title: TinyFlow: Breaking the Warping Bottleneck for Edge Optical Flow
2610.33338.abstract: High-performance optical flow networks are difficult to deploy on resource-constrained edge accelerators because their iterative refinement warps features by the current flow, which relies on flow-dependent resampling and data-dependent memory access. We present TinyFlow, a 1.26M-parameter warp-free optical flow network that preserves iterative coarse-to-fine refinement by replacing the warp with a fixed-window correlation over constant offsets, so the whole network compiles as a single static INT8 graph. Quantization-aware fine-tuning, warp-teacher distillation, and model souping reduce the Float32-to-INT8 penalty to below 0.2 end-point error (EPE) on MPI-Sintel. TinyFlow outperforms EdgeFlowNet and NanoFlowNet on Sintel Clean, Sintel Final, and FlyingChairs in both Float32 and INT8, while using 54% fewer parameters than EdgeFlowNet, and our INT8 model achieves 6.29/7.13 EPE on Sintel Clean/Final. In flow-only monocular visual odometry on TartanAir and UZH-FPV, the same INT8 model yields the lowest trajectory error on seven of eleven sequences.
2610.33338.tldr_en: TinyFlow is presented, a 1.26M-parameter warp-free optical flow network that preserves iterative coarse-to-fine refinement by replacing the warp with a fixed-window correlation over constant offsets, so the whole network compiles as a single static INT8 graph.

llm.title_ja: TinyFlow：エッジ向けオプティカルフローにおけるワーピングのボトルネックの打破
llm.tldr_ja: ワーピング処理を固定ウィンドウ相関に置き換えることで単一の静的INT8グラフとしてコンパイル可能にし、軽量かつ高精度な推論を実現した1.26Mパラメータのオプティカルフローネットワーク「TinyFlow」を提案する。
llm.problem: 高性能なオプティカルフローネットワークは、反復的な洗練プロセスにおけるフロー依存のリスリングとデータ依存のメモリアクセスのため、リソースの限られたエッジアクセラレータへのデプロイが困難である。
llm.method: ワーピング処理を固定オフセットに対する固定ウィンドウ相関に置き換え、量子化認識ファインチューニング、ワーピング教師蒸留、モデルスーピングを適用して1.26Mパラメータの軽量ネットワークを構築する。
llm.result: MPI-Sintel等において従来のEdgeFlowNetやNanoFlowNetを上回る精度を達成し、INT8モデルでSintel Clean/Finalにおいて優れたEPEを記録するとともに、オドメトリでも低誤差を達成した。

2610.33317.title: Active Reachability Learning for Humanoid Recoverability Monitoring
2610.33317.abstract: Deploying humanoid task policies requires reliable runtime monitors that anticipate unrecoverable falls in time to trigger a fallback. We formulate this task as learning the stochastic, finite-horizon recoverability envelope of a given fallback policy. Synthesizing this monitor is challenging: existing methods assume training data naturally covers the recoverability envelope, yet acquiring such data remains a major bottleneck for contact-rich systems. Consequently, they recover only a fraction of the true envelope, leaving them prone to optimistic hallucinations for out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. We resolve this via a unified framework that iterates between value learning and active exploration. Data exploration is reframed as a reach-avoid problem, where an uncertainty-guided explorer systematically uncovers unseen states while avoiding confidently unrecoverable regions. This loop is further supported by a combined Temporal Difference and Monte Carlo objective for accurate in-distribution value prediction and reliable uncertainty estimation. By explicitly treating the remaining high-uncertainty regions as unrecoverable, the monitor mitigates optimistic OOD hallucinations. Evaluated on stochastic benchmarks and a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid, our approach drastically improves monitor coverage and accuracy and successfully transfers zero-shot to real-world hardware.
2610.33317.tldr_en: This task is formulated as learning the stochastic, finite-horizon recoverability envelope of a given fallback policy, and the approach drastically improves monitor coverage and accuracy and successfully transfers zero-shot to real-world hardware.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマノイドの復旧可能性モニタリングのためのアクティブ到達可能性学習
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実性ガイド付きの探索と到達回避問題を組み合わせたフレームワークにより、ヒューマノイドの確率的・有限ホライゾン復旧可能性エンベロープを学習する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドタスクポリシーの展開において、未回収の転倒を事前に予測する信頼性の高いランタイムモニタが必要だが、接触の多いシステムで網羅的な訓練データを集めるのが困難である。
llm.method: データ探索を到達回避問題として再定式化し、不確実性ガイド付きエクスプローラーで未知の状態を体系的に発見しつつ不確実に回復不能な領域を避け、TDとモンテカルロを組み合わせた目的関数で価値を予測する。
llm.result: 29自由度のUnitree G1ヒューマノイドを用いたベンチマークにおいてモニタの網羅性と精度を大幅に改善し、実機へのゼロショット転移に成功した。

2610.33288.title: Tiny Recursive Policy: Recursive Latent Refinement for Visuomotor Control
2610.33288.abstract: Behaviour cloning has become a powerful approach for robotic manipulation, but many modern policies reconstruct their internal representation from a fixed observation window at each prediction and do not maintain persistent latent context throughout execution. We introduce Tiny Recursive Policy (TRP), a parameter-efficient behaviour-cloning policy that combines persistent temporal state with recursive latent refinement. At each control step, TRP repeatedly updates high- and low-level latent states using a shared computation module before decoding an action sequence, and propagates the resulting state to subsequent predictions. We evaluate TRP across LIBERO-100, MetaWorld ML45, and the LIBERO-Mem benchmarks. TRP performs competitively across multi-task and few-shot settings and shows substantial gains on long-horizon and context-dependent tasks, while using significantly fewer parameters than large generative baselines. Execution-time perturbations show that reliance on the persistent carry increases with temporal-context demand, while training with carry perturbations substantially improves robustness to both carry and visual corruptions. Ablations reveal a strong interaction between persistent state and recursive refinement: the benefit of carry depends strongly on the amount of within-step computation, and the resulting performance cannot be explained by parameter count alone.
2610.33288.tldr_en: Tiny Recursive Policy is introduced, a parameter-efficient behaviour-cloning policy that combines persistent temporal state with recursive latent refinement and shows substantial gains on long-horizon and context-dependent tasks, while using significantly fewer parameters than large generative baselines.

llm.title_ja: Tiny Recursive Policy：ビソモータ制御のための再帰的潜在表現洗練
llm.tldr_ja: 持続的な一時状態と共有モジュールによる再帰的な潜在表現の洗練を組み合わせることで、大規模な生成ベースラインよりも少ないパラメータで長期・文脈依存タスクをこなす「TRP」を提案する。
llm.problem: 多くの現代的な行動クローンポリシーは、各予測時に固定の観察ウィンドウから内部表現を再構築し、実行全体を通じて持続的な潜在コンテキストを維持しない。
llm.method: 共有計算モジュールを用いて高・低レベルの潜在状態を繰り返し更新してからアクションシーケンスをデコードし、その状態を次の予測へと伝播させるパラメータ効率の高い行動クローンポリシー「TRP」を構築する。
llm.result: LIBERO-100やMetaWorld ML45などのベンチマークにおいて、大規模な生成ベースラインよりも大幅に少ないパラメータ数で競争力のある性能と長期タスクでの高いゲインを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.33271.title: Neuromorphic Decision Dynamics for Deadlock-free Safe Navigation in Congested Environments
2610.33271.abstract: Safe navigation in congested environments requires both collision avoidance and coordinated passage. We introduce neuromorphic decision dynamics (NDD), a decentralized, event-based controller, that provides navigation in congested spaces with guarantees on safety, liveness, robustness, and scalability. NDD makes safe-and-live deconfliction a controllable, locally tunable emergent property of local agent interactions, without requiring communication, preassigned priorities, models of neighbors' objectives or future actions, or estimates of group size or global network properties. By design, NDD couples the dynamics of internal decision and attention states with changing physical states and locally observed relative motion. Each agent continuously modulates its speed along its prescribed path, responding as soon and as much as conflict resolution requires. Agents self-organize into disjoint, locally engaged groups that resolve conflicts concurrently. When any group's conflict becomes safety-critical, decision-action feedback destabilizes collective indecision, and coordinated conflict-resolution emerges that stabilizes a safe traversal order within the group. Order persists as conflicts clear, but groups may split or merge as agents autonomously adapt to new conflicts and those with resolved conflicts resume their nominal motion. We derive explicit conditions on sensing range, feedback gains, response time scales, and actuation limits that guarantee collision avoidance and traversal-order formation in finite time with no deadlock or livelock for finite, heterogeneous agent populations of arbitrary, changing size. Computational cost scales with the number of local interactions sensed by each agent. Large-scale simulations, comparisons with existing approaches, and hardware experiments demonstrate NDD in complex congested scenarios and validate its scalability.
2610.33271.tldr_en: NDD makes safe-and-live deconfliction a controllable, locally tunable emergent property of local agent interactions, without requiring communication, preassigned priorities, models of neighbors'objectives or future actions, or estimates of group size or global network properties.

llm.title_ja: 混雑環境におけるデッドロックフリーな安全ナビゲーションのためのニューロモルフィック意思決定ダイナミクス
llm.tldr_ja: 通信や事前割り当てられた優先順位を必要とせず、内部の意思決定・注意状態と物理状態の結合により安全かつ協調的な通過を実現する分散型イベント駆動コントローラ「NDD」を提案する。
llm.problem: 混雑した環境での安全なナビゲーションには衝突回避と協調的な通過の両方が必要だが、既存の手法は通信や事前の優先順位付け、近傍の目的モデルなどを前提としていることが多い。
llm.method: 内部の意思決定・注意状態のダイナミクスを、変化する物理状態や局所的に観測される相対運動と結合させ、競合解決が必要になった瞬間に各エージェントが速度を自己調整する分散型コントローラ「NDD」を構築する。
llm.result: 大規模なシミュレーション等を通じて、異種混雑環境におけるデッドロックやライブロックのない有限時間での衝突回避と通過順序の形成を実証した。
keywords_ja: ニューロモルフィック

2610.33241.title: ORBIT: A Modular Multi-finger Robotic Hand Platform with Rotational Finger Reconfiguration
2610.33241.abstract: Despite the popularity of multi-fingered robotic hands for dexterous manipulation, there is no systematic platform to compare different hand morphologies against one another. We present ORBIT (Orbital Reconfigurable Base-actuated Integrated Theta-motion Hand), a modular platform designed to enable principled exploration of multi-fingered hand morphology. The core contribution of ORBIT is a rotating knuckle mechanism, where independent fingers travel around a cylindrical palm via a belt drive. This enables ORBIT to perform quick recon- figuration (< 1 s) of finger layout without hand disassembly. ORBITs a robust system, with finger average angular velocity of 1.57 rad / s1 and a root finger force resistance of 50 N. Using a three fingers instantiation of ORBIT, we demonstrate an initial pilot grasping study, comparing anthropomorphic, isometric, and Barrett-style finger layouts across eleven objects of varied size, shape, and texture. We further demonstrate how ORBITs nonanthropomorphic orbital DOF enables the achievement of tasks that would be difficult to perform with fixed-knuckle designs, such as cube face reorientation, lid threading, and precision pinching of sub-centimeter objects. These results establish ORBIT as a viable platform for direct apples to apples comparison of multi-fingered hand morphologies for specific manipulation tasks

llm.title_ja: ORBIT：回転式指再構成を備えたモジュール式多指ロボットハンドプラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 多指ハンドのモルホロジーを体系的に比較するためのモジュール式プラットフォーム「ORBIT」を提案し、ハンドを分解せずに1秒未満で指のレイアウトを迅速に変更できることを実証した。
llm.problem: 多指ハンドの異なる形態を体系的に比較するためのプラットフォームが存在しないこと。
llm.method: 独立した指がベルト駆動により円筒状の掌の周囲を移動する回転ナックル機構を持つORBITプラットフォームの提案。
llm.result: 1秒未満での迅速なレイアウト再構成が可能となり、非人間型の軌道自由度により立方体の面再方向付けや糸通しなどのタスクが実行できることを示した。

2610.33227.title: Causal-based approaches to explain and learn from self-extension - A review
2610.33227.abstract: The last decades have seen a revolution in autonomous robotics. Deep learning approaches and their hardware implementations have made it possible to endow robots with extraordinary perceptual capabilities. In addition, they can also benefit from advances in Automated Planning, allowing them to autonomously solve complex tasks. However, on many occasions, the robot still acts without internalising and understanding the reasons behind a perception or an action, beyond an immediate response to a current state of the context. This gap results in limitations that affect its performance, reliability and trustworthiness. Deep learning alone cannot bridge this gap, because the reasons behind behaviour, when it emanates from a model in which the world is a black-box, are not accessible. What is really needed is an underlying architecture based on deeper reasoning. Among other issues, this architecture should enable the robot to generate explanations, allowing people to know why the robot is performing, or has performed, a certain action, or the reasons that may have caused a certain plan failure or perceptual anomaly. Furthermore, when these explanations arise from a cognitive process and are shared, and thus validated, with people, the robot should be able to incorporate these explanations into its knowledge base, and thus use this understanding to improve future behaviour. Our article looks at recent advances in the development of self-aware, self-evolving robots. These robots are designed to provide the necessary explanations to their human counterparts, thereby enhancing their functional capabilities, in the quest to gain their trust.
2610.33227.tldr_en: This article looks at recent advances in the development of self-aware, self-evolving robots, designed to provide the necessary explanations to their human counterparts, thereby enhancing their functional capabilities in the quest to gain their trust.

llm.title_ja: 自己拡張からの説明と学習に対する因果ベースのアプローチ - レビュー
llm.tldr_ja: 自律型ロボットの自己認識や自己進化に関する最近の進歩をレビューし、人間に対する説明生成や知識ベースへの統合を通じて信頼性と機能性を向上させる手法を論じた。
llm.problem: ロボットが現状に対する即時応答を超えて知覚や行動の理由を内面化・理解していないというギャップ。
llm.method: 自己認識型・自己進化型ロボットの開発における最近の進歩についてのレビューと、より深い推論に基づく基盤アーキテクチャの考察。
llm.result: 人間と説明を共有・検証することでロボットが将来の行動を改善できるような、自己認識型・自己進化型ロボットに関する知見を整理した。

2610.33191.title: Whale You Go Green? Immediate and Longitudinal Effects of Embodied Conversational AI Avatars on Sustainable Behavioral Tendencies and Pro-Environmental Attitudes
2610.33191.abstract: Embodied conversational AI can be persuasive, but can it motivate people to develop sustainable behavioral tendencies and increase pro-environmental attitudes? We conducted a randomized experiment (N = 576) comparing four embodied avatars--a beluga whale, Greta Thunberg, Emma Watson, and a generic human--with a text chatbot and no-intervention control. All embodied conditions increased immediate sustainable product selection relative to the control (beta = .401-.609, all q <= .0126) and chatbot (beta = .398-.604, all q <= .007), without differing significantly from one another. Only the Beluga condition increased immediate pro-environmental attitudes relative to the control after correction.
