Among 287 returners assessed two months later, following an intermediate assigned-condition session, Beluga also showed significantly higher pre-booster sustainable product choice compared to the control (beta = .657, q = .0176). Although it did not significantly outperform other embodied agents, these findings establish the immediate potential of nonhuman embodied avatar interfaces as a promising direction for memorable environmental interventions.
2610.33191.tldr_en: Although it did not significantly outperform other embodied agents, these findings establish the immediate potential of nonhuman embodied avatar interfaces as a promising direction for memorable environmental interventions.

llm.title_ja: クジラになって環境に優しく？持続可能な行動傾向と環境配慮型態度に対する具現化された会話型AIアバターの直接的および長期的効果
llm.tldr_ja: 4種類の具現化されたアバターを用いたランダム化実験を行い、非人間の具現化されたアバターインターフェースが記憶に残る環境介入の有望な方向性であることを示した。
llm.problem: 具現化された会話型AIが説得力を持つ一方で、人々の持続可能な行動傾向や環境配慮型態度を動機づけられるかという疑問。
llm.method: シロイルカ、グレタ・トゥンベリ、エマ・ワトソン、一般的な人間の4つのアバターとテキストチャットボット・対照群を比較するランダム化実験（N=576）の実施。
llm.result: すべての具現化された条件において、対照群やチャットボットと比較して持続可能な製品の即時選択が増加し、特にシロイルカ条件では環境配慮型態度や長期的選択への効果が確認された。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.33186.title: Interpretable Collision Avoidance and Feasibility Guarantees through an Uncertainty Aware Pipeline
2610.33186.abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) operating in dynamic, challenging conditions such as intersections and roundabouts must guarantee collision avoidance under uncertainty while maintaining real-time feasibility. Most existing planners struggle to simultaneously guarantee both requirements. Chance-constrained formulations embed safety constraints directly in the optimization but become infeasible as uncertainty compounds; deterministic planners provide feasible solutions but fail to address the uncertainty that causes collisions; end-to-end learned policies provide neither guarantee in an interpretable form. We present a modular perception-prediction-planning pipeline that closes this gap by propagating uncertainty as structured, interpretable quantities across module boundaries. Rather than embedding probabilistic risk directly in the optimization, our pipeline resolves collision probabilities upstream and constructs convex safe sets within which the planner provides a guaranteed feasible solution at every cycle -- decoupling the safety guarantee from solver feasibility. Across Monte Carlo trials in a four-way unsignalized intersection, our pipeline achieves 0% collisions and 0% solver infeasibility at 12.7ms per cycle, compared to 36% and 10% collision rates for deterministic and chance-constrained baselines respectively. The ablation study confirms the necessity of each uncertainty source and the hardware deployment on Clearpath Jackal UGVs validates the pipeline's real-time viability on physical platforms.
2610.33186.tldr_en: A modular perception-prediction-planning pipeline that closes this gap by propagating uncertainty as structured, interpretable quantities across module boundaries by resolving collision probabilities upstream and constructs convex safe sets within which the planner provides a guaranteed feasible solution at every cycle -- decoupling the safety guarantee from solver feasibility.

llm.title_ja: 不確実性を考慮したパイプラインによる解釈可能な衝突回避と実行可能性の保証
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実性を構造化された解釈可能な量としてモジュール間で伝播させることで、衝突回避とリアルタイムの実行可能性を同時に保証するモジュール式知覚・予測・計画パイプラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のほとんどのプランナーが、動的な環境下での不確実性下での衝突回避とリアルタイムでの実行可能性を同時に保証するのに苦労していること。
llm.method: 確率的リスクを最適化に直接組み込むのではなく、上流で衝突確率を解決し、プランナーが常に保証された実行可能解を提供する凸安全集合を構築するモジュール式パイプラインの構築。
llm.result: 交差点でのモンテカルロ試行において0%の衝突率と0%のソルバー実行不能率をサイクルあたり12.7msで達成し、実機（Clearpath Jackal UGV）でのリアルタイム性を検証した。

2610.33174.title: Bracketing Shows the Way: Adaptive Multi-Exposure Policy as Input for Robust Visual SLAM
2610.33174.abstract: Rapid illumination transitions can disturb Visual SLAM (VSLAM) by saturating images before the Automatic Exposure (AE) policy adapts, removing the visual correspondences needed to maintain tracking. Our proposed methods mitigate this disturbance at two levels: B-Adapt acquires adaptive exposure brackets to cover the scene dynamic range while promoting photometric overlap, and BVSLAM directly uses the multi-exposure sequence as constraints in a factor graph state estimator without relying on High Dynamic Range (HDR) merging. We evaluate both methods against state-of-the-art approaches in nominal environments and during a repeated tunnel-exit transition at an emulated vehicle speed of 32 m s-1. In the tunnel, combining our B-Adapt with BVSLAM reduces the state estimation error by 78 % compared with AE images. These results suggest that bracketing efficiently improves visual pose estimation robustness to rapid illumination disturbances while retaining low error under nominal conditions. Our code is available at https://github.com/norlab-ulaval/bracketing-shows-the-way.
2610.33174.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, submitted to 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2027)
2610.33174.tldr_en: B-Adapt and BVSLAM efficiently improves visual pose estimation robustness to rapid illumination disturbances while retaining low error under nominal conditions, and bracketing efficiently improves visual pose estimation robustness to rapid illumination disturbances while retaining low error under nominal conditions.

llm.title_ja: ブラケティングが道を示す：ロバストなVisual SLAMの入力としての適応型多露光ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 画像が飽和するような急速な照明変化に対して、適応型露光ブラケットとマルチ露光シーケンスを因子グラフ状態推定器に直接利用することでVisual SLAMのロバスト性を向上させる手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 自動露光ポリシーが適応する前に画像が飽和し、トラッキングに必要な視覚的対応関係が失われることで、急速な照明変化がVisual SLAMを妨害すること。
llm.method: シーンの動的範囲をカバーする適応型露光ブラケットを取得するB-Adaptと、HDRマージに頼らずにマルチ露光シーケンスを因子グラフの状態推定の制約として直接使用するBVSLAMの提案。
llm.result: トンネル出口の遷移実験において、B-AdaptとBVSLAMの組み合わせにより、自動露光画像と比較して状態推定誤差を78%削減できることを示した。

2610.33172.title: RAIWAY: A Large-Wheeled Bipedal Robot with Contact-Informed Blind Locomotion
2610.33172.abstract: We present RAIWAY, an in-house wheeled bipedal robot with 20-inch wheels, together with a contact-informed control approach for rolling locomotion across irregular and discontinuous terrain. Such locomotion is fundamentally contact-dominated, governed by local wheel--terrain interaction that is impractical to instrument directly and depends on more than terrain geometry alone. The proposed framework exploits the contact information available in simulation, distilling multi-contact events into a latent representation. At deployment, the controller infers this representation online from proprioception, requiring no contact sensing. In real-world experiments, the proposed system traverses diverse environments including steep slopes, gravel beds, studded surfaces, and rocky terrain, and demonstrates continuous ascent on the tested outdoor staircases with riser heights up to 15~cm. On our platform, the proposed controller further outperforms baselines without the contact-informed mechanism across challenging indoor and outdoor settings. The video can be found at https://youtu.be/Ch0divLg64w.
2610.33172.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
2610.33172.tldr_en: RAIWAY, an in-house wheeled bipedal robot with 20-inch wheels, together with a contact-informed control approach for rolling locomotion across irregular and discontinuous terrain is presented, together with a contact-informed control approach for rolling locomotion across irregular and discontinuous terrain.

llm.title_ja: RAIWAY：接触情報を活用した不整地・不連続地形向けブラインドロコモーションを持つ大径車輪二足歩行ロボット
llm.tldr_ja: 20インチ車輪を持つ車輪付き二足歩行ロボット「RAIWAY」を開発し、接触情報をシミュレーションから蒸留して固有受容感覚のみからオンラインで推論することで、不整地でのロコモーションを実現した。
llm.problem: 不規則・不連続な地形でのローリングロコモーションが局所的な車輪・地形間の相互作用に支配され、直接計装することが現実的ではないこと。
llm.method: シミュレーションで利用可能な接触情報を潜在表現に蒸留し、デプロイ時には接触センシングなしで固有受容感覚からオンラインでその表現を推論する接触情報活用型制御アプローチ。
llm.result: 急斜面、砂利、岩場などの多様な環境を走破し、最大15cmの階段を連続登坂できることを実証し、ベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2610.33158.title: Gaussian Episodic Memory for Long-Term Spatiotemporal Reasoning
2610.33158.abstract: Real-world environments undergo continual semi-static changes, requiring a memory representation that captures both the spatial and temporal evolution of a scene. Existing spatio-temporal memories for robots typically rely either on structured representations, which are limited to the entities and attributes captured during construction, or on image-based memories, which are constrained to previously observed viewpoints. We introduce GEMS, a framework that combines a persistent spatio-temporal 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) map with an agentic reasoning pipeline. The 3DGS map is reconstructed once and subsequently updated only in regions where the scene changes, storing only these modifications while preserving visual detail across time. The agentic pipeline leverages this map to render novel views on demand, iteratively accumulating evidence to answer spatio-temporal questions and ground objects from natural-language queries. To advance future research, we introduce GEMS-Bench, a spatiotemporal question-answering benchmark focused on semi-static environments. It comprises 3 real-world and 12 synthetic environments, spanning 473 question-answer pairs. We evaluate GEMS on novel-view synthesis quality across scene updates, 3D object grounding, spatiotemporal question answering, and storage efficiency. GEMS outperforms recent baselines in 3D object grounding and spatiotemporal question answering, while achieving rendering quality on par with dedicated scene-update methods. Code and data: https://abwerby.github.io/GEMS/
2610.33158.tldr_en: This work introduces GEMS, a framework that combines a persistent spatio-temporal 3D Gaussian Splatting map with an agentic reasoning pipeline, and introduces GEMS-Bench, a spatiotemporal question-answering benchmark focused on semi-static environments.

llm.title_ja: 長期的な時空間推論のためのガウス型エピソード記憶
llm.tldr_ja: 持続的な時空間3Dガウススプラッティング（3DGS）マップとエージェント型推論パイプラインを組み合わせることで、シーンの継続的な変化を捉えつつ時空間的な質問に答えるフレームワーク「GEMS」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の時空間記憶は、構築時に捉えられたエンティティに限定されるか、以前観測された視点に制約されるという課題があること。
llm.method: 変化した領域のみを更新して視覚的詳細を保持する持続的な3DGSマップと、オンデマンドで新規視点をレンダリングして時空間的質問に答えるエージェント型パイプラインの統合。
llm.result: 新規視点合成品質、3Dオブジェクトグラウンディング、時空間質問応答において最近のベースラインを上回る性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2610.32978.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
2610.32978.abstract: Training generalizable embodied agents requires realistic, varied, and simulation-ready indoor environments. Language-guided methods support semantic planning and object-level reasoning, but precise spatial grounding remains difficult. Visual generative models offer rich priors over plausible arrangements, yet their outputs require geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes. We introduce SceneBloom, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects. Its layouts are also closer to the distribution of real rooms than those of all compared baselines. Object navigation policies trained in these realistic scenes achieve a higher success rate in held-out real scans than those trained on an equal number of real training scans. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom.
2610.32978.tldr_en: SceneBloom is introduced, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation that attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects.

llm.title_ja: SceneBloom：具現化学習に向けた現実的かつ多様なレイアウトを持つエージェント型屋内環境生成
llm.tldr_ja: ビジュアルレイアウトサンプリングと契約誘導型3Dコンパイルを組み合わせたエージェント型フレームワーク「SceneBloom」を提案し、物理的に安定した多様な屋内環境の生成を実現した。
llm.problem: 汎用的な具現化エージェントの訓練には現実的で多様なシミュレーション対応の屋内環境が必要だが、視覚的生成モデルの出力には幾何学的推論が必要であり空間的グラウンディングが難しいこと。
llm.method: 拡散事前分布を用いて機能ゾーン内の家具配置を生成する階層的サンプラーと、幾何学的フィッティングや局所的な姿勢修正をガイドするコンパイラの統合。
llm.result: 5種類の部屋タイプにおいて最高の視覚品質と物理的安定性を達成し、メッシュの衝突や領域外のオブジェクトが検出されない唯一の手法であり、実機スキャンでのナビゲーション成功率も向上させた。

2610.32977.title: UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models
2610.32977.abstract: Actions that condition world models are highly heterogeneous, and thus existing action-conditioned world models are typically built for individual action types, fragmenting already limited action-annotated data across separate models. We introduce UniAction, a unified action-conditioning framework that represents any action as a sparse set of action elements, each with a discrete semantic identity and a continuous spatiotemporal grounding coordinate. By mapping these coordinates directly into the pretrained video model's native positional space, UniAction allows heterogeneous actions to condition a shared world model within the same spatiotemporal structure. We further introduce cardinality-calibrated attention to address the bias from differing action representation granularities. We evaluate UniAction on four representative action forms: force, camera control, hand pose, and robot pose. UniAction outperforms conditioning alternatives in action following, and a single jointly trained model surpasses the action-specific experts, showing that heterogeneous action data benefit from unified model and joint training.
2610.32977.tldr_en: UniAction is introduced, a unified action-conditioning framework that represents any action as a sparse set of action elements, each with a discrete semantic identity and a continuous spatiotemporal grounding coordinate, that allows heterogeneous actions to condition a shared world model within the same spatiotemporal structure.

llm.title_ja: UniAction：世界モデルのための統合アクション条件付け
llm.tldr_ja: あらゆるアクションをスパースなアクション要素のセットとして表現し、事前学習済みビデオモデルの空間位置に直接マッピングすることで、異種のアクションデータを共有世界モデルで統合するフレームワーク「UniAction」を提案した。
llm.problem: アクションの種類が異なると既存のアクション条件付き世界モデルも個別に構築され、限られたアクション注釈付きデータが断片化していること。
llm.method: 各アクションを離散的な意味的アイデンティティと連続的な時空間グラウンディング座標を持つスパースな要素として表現し、カーディナリティ較正注意機構を導入した統合アクション条件付けフレームワークの構築。
llm.result: 4つの代表的なアクション形式においてアクション追従性で代替手法を凌駕し、単一の共同訓練モデルがアクション固有のエキスパートを上回ることを示した。

2610.32971.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
2610.32971.abstract: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.
2610.32971.comment: Project page, code, and tutorial: https://robustrl-lib.github.io/
2610.32971.tldr_en: Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist.

llm.title_ja: RobustRLlib：ロバスト強化学習アルゴリズムのための統合ライブラリとベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 17の代表的なロバスト強化学習アルゴリズムを統合インターフェースの下にまとめ、多様な現実の変動や高度なヒューマノイド・VLAタスクにわたる評価プラットフォームを提供する「RobustRLlib」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のロバスト強化学習アルゴリズムの再利用性が限られており、その実証的な能力境界が不明確であるという2つの大きな障壁があること。
llm.method: オンライン、オフライン、安全な強化学習の17アルゴリズムを単一のインターフェースで統合し、273の摂動設定にわたる体系的な評価プラットフォームの構築。
llm.result: 273の摂動設定にわたる体系的評価により、現在のロバスト強化学習アルゴリズムの能力マップを明らかにし、有効な領域とロバスト性のギャップを特定した。

2610.32969.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
2610.32969.abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.

llm.title_ja: DexPort：器用なハンドのデータ収集のための手持ち式スキルインターフェース
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットアームを必要とせずに器用なマニポレーションのデモンストレーションを収集できるポータブルな手持ち式データ収集インターフェース「DexPort」を提案した。
llm.problem: 高品質なデモンストレーションの収集が器用なマニポレーション学習における中心的なボトルネックとなっており、従来の遠隔操作では完全なロボットセットアップと多くの指関節の協調が必要になること。
llm.method: データ収集とデプロイで同じハンドハードウェアを使用し、手持ち式インターフェースで手首の動きを指定しつつ指の動きを調整するスキルを選択・調整するポータブルなデータ収集システムの構築。
llm.result: 2,500件以上のデモンストレーションを収集し、行動クローンにより視覚運動ポリシーを訓練した結果、記録されたロボットコマンドを使用することでタスク成功率が大幅に向上した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニポレーション

2610.32967.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
2610.32967.abstract: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. We study this problem using DGM4+, a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies. We propose a multimodal model that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA. The model jointly predicts whether an image-caption pair is authentic, identifies the manipulation type, and grounds the misleading caption tokens. On the DGM4+ validation split, the model achieves an F1 score of $0.9679$ for binary authenticity classification. These results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies, while also motivating further work on precise token-level grounding.
2610.32967.tldr_en: A multimodal model is proposed that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA, suggesting that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies.

llm.title_ja: MiD-VLM：画像・キャプションペアにおけるグローバルな意味的偽情報の検出とグラウンディング
llm.tldr_ja: SigLIPの画像テキスト表現とDINOv2の視覚シーン特徴を組み合わせ、Qwen2-VL-7BをLoRAで適応させたマルチモーダルモデルにより、意味的偽情報の検出とトークンレベルのグラウンディングを実現した。
llm.problem: 画像自体には目に見える改ざんの兆候がない場合があり、画素レベルのアーティファクト検出手法では物語を歪める誤解を招く画像・キャプションペアを見逃してしまうこと。
llm.method: SigLIP表現とDINOv2特徴を射影MLPで結合し、LoRAを用いてQwen2-VL-7Bを適応させたマルチモーダルモデルの構築。
llm.result: DGM4+の検証データにおいてバイナリの真偽分類で0.9679のF1スコアを達成し、意味的不整合の検出におけるビジョン言語モデルの有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルモデル

2610.32966.title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
2610.32966.abstract: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback. We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization. We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability. We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.
2610.32966.comment: The first four authors contributed equally. Project website: https://awfuact.github.io/vit-h/
2610.32966.tldr_en: ViT-H is presented, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm that outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability and introduces an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency.

llm.title_ja: ViT-H：モーション追跡フィードバックを用いた生成型ビデオ・ツー・ヒューノイド制御
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の単眼ビデオから拡散モデルを用いてヒューマノイドの参照モーションを直接生成し、モーション追跡結果を用いた直接選好最適化により実行可能性を向上させるフレームワーク「ViT-H」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の再構築・リターゲット・トラッキングパイプラインは中間段階が個別に最適化されているためシステム全体の拡張性が制限され、ダウンストリームの追跡フィードバックを直接最適化できないこと。
llm.method: 人間のモーション再構築やリターゲットをバイパスしてビデオから拡散モデルで直接ヒューマノイドの参照モーションを生成し、追跡フィードバックで後訓練するアプローチの導入。
llm.result: Unitree G1を用いた実験において、モーション品質と実行可能性の両方で最先端のパイプラインを凌駕し、400ms未満のレイテンシでの実時間ビデオテレオペレーションを実現した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.32965.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
2610.32965.abstract: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano. Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks. Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.
2610.32965.tldr_en: RynnUnify is introduced, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning and develops an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes.
2610.32965.hf_summary_en: RynnUnify is a 16B unified embodied model that integrates visual planning, physical reasoning, and robot control, achieving state-of-the-art results on long-horizon embodied tasks.

llm.title_ja: RynnUnify：統合された具現化された脳に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: インターリーブされたビデオ・言語推論を通じて強力な具現化理解と長期的な視覚的計画を結合した16Bの統合具現化モデル「RynnUnify」を提案し、ロボット制御や視覚的計画の性能向上を実証した。
llm.problem: 従来のマルチモーダルモデルにおける具現化された理解、視覚的計画、ロボット制御の断片化。
llm.method: ビデオ・言語推論をインターリーブさせ、強化学習によるエージェント的拡張とワールド・アクション拡張を組み込んだ16Bパラメータの統合具現化モデルの開発。
llm.result: 具現化理解スコアで最高平均を達成し、 RoboCasa365の複合タスクで51.5%、実ロボットタスクで46.7%の平均成功率を達成した。

2610.32961.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
2610.32961.abstract: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions. This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, but target-conditioned control requires effective representations of both observed and desired tissue states. In this work, we introduce an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback. We study full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud representations, with or without residual conditioning, using deterministic (Explicit) and generative diffusion (Diffusion) policies. Across 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, OCT-derived 3D representations support both Explicit and Diffusion policies, with performance depending on representation and residual conditioning. Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion, while voxelized point-cloud Explicit with residuals achieves 0.534 mm for depth and 0.443 mm for directional control, with comparable accuracy at intermediate unseen targets and consistent performance across deployments. We further evaluate the framework in 60 ex vivo porcine rollouts, extending to biological tissue with final geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. These results establish volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.
2610.32961.tldr_en: This work introduces an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback, and establishes volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.

llm.title_ja: ロボット光干渉断層撮影（OCT）誘導による軟組織の幾何学的モデリング：データ駆動型閉ループ形状制御のための3D表現
llm.tldr_ja: OCTによる高解像度な体積知覚とユーザーによるデモンストレーションから学習したデータ駆動型フレームワークを用いて、決定論的および生成的ポリシーによる軟組織の閉ループ形状制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 微小領域での局所変形は観測・表現・制御が難しく、物理ベースモデルは計算コストが高く現実の環境に適応させにくいこと。
llm.method: OCTによる高解像度ボumetric知覚を用い、フルボリューム、スパースボリューム、ボクセル化点群表現と、残差条件付けの有無による決定論的・拡散ポリシーの検討。
llm.result: 576回のシミュレーションおよび60回の生体外ブタ組織を用いた実験において、決定論的および生成的アクションモデル全体で学習された閉ループ形状制御にボumetric OCTが有効であることを示した。

2610.32941.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
2610.32941.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.
2610.32941.tldr_en: Backtrack is introduced, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these mechanisms to be introduced, and reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points.

llm.title_ja: 最初からうまくいかないなら、バックトラックする：凍結されたVLAのための軽量なリカバリー機構
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結されたビジョン・言語・アクション（VLA）モデルの内部表現を読み取って失敗を予測し、自動で巻き戻して再試行を行う軽量なリカバリー機構「Backtrack」を提案した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルが自らの行動によって訓練データの分布外の状態に陥ると、容易に失敗し脆くなってしまうこと。
llm.method: VLAの既存の内部表現から失敗確率を推定する小さな失敗予測ヘッドを追加し、失敗予測時にアームの直近の動きを巻き戻してポリシーに制御を戻す仕組みの導入。
llm.result: LIBERO-Longにおいて各ポリシーの失敗率を19〜48%削減し、成功率を最大7.4パーセントポイント向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2610.32909.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
2610.32909.abstract: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution. A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control. This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run. This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.
2610.32909.tldr_en: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller, which keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration.
2610.32909.hf_summary_en: HoloBoxing learns humanoid boxing by combining a frozen whole-body controller with a compact planner that predicts body-point targets, using imitation initialization and reinforcement learning to refine interaction behavior with minimal additional training.

llm.title_ja: HoloBoxing：単一GPUで7分間訓練するヒューマノイドボクシングのシンプルなレシピ
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの全身コントローラーを活用し、再利用可能なモータースキルとタスク決定を分離することで、わずか7分でヒューマノイドのボクシング行動を学習するシンプルなレシピ「HoloBoxing」を提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの複雑な全身制御を維持しながら新しいインタラクティブなタスク行動を効率的に学習することの難しさ。
llm.method: コンパクトなプランナーが未来の身体目標を要求し、凍結されたコントローラーが関節レベルの実行を担当し、測定状態による模倣でプランナーを初期化するアプローチ。
llm.result: コントローラーの事前学習を除き、表現フィッティングと単一GPUでのタスク実行を含めて約7分の追加訓練でシミュレーション上のボクシング行動の学習を実現した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.32888.title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation
2610.32888.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments. Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot. We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. Immediate, legible defensive behavior remains necessary during human interaction. We offer counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.
2610.32888.comment: Accepted for presentation at SPAIS workshop in CoRL 2026
2610.32888.tldr_en: This work argues for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence.

llm.title_ja: 人間の修正が伝播するとき：連合VLA適応における安全性
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な人間による修正から得られた適応を、タスク、環境、人間、ロボットの形態を越えて共有する際の課題を分析し、安全性と文脈の保持に関する3つの要件を主張した。
llm.problem: あるロボットのタスク成功率を向上させる共有アップデートが、別のロボットではレアな安全介入を抑制したり安全でない応答を引き起こしたりする可能性があること。
llm.method: マルチモーダルな修正の文脈と不確実性の保存、デプロイ前の各ロボットの閉ループでの候補アップデートの評価、安全クリティカルな証拠の保持と漏洩の評価という3要件の提案。
llm.result: 実験結果は含まれておらず、カウンター例と反証可能な評価アジェンダの提示を通じて連合VLA適応における安全性の理論的要件を議論した。
llm.limitation: 実験結果は含まれず、理論的考察と評価アジェンダの提示にとどまる
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル
ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.32855.title: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
2610.32855.abstract: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.
2610.32855.comment: 9 pages of main-body content, with supporting details in the appendices. Under submission
2610.32855.tldr_en: Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees, is derived and demonstrated that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.

llm.title_ja: 正則化強化学習はシム・ツー・リアル転移を改善する
llm.tldr_ja: 強いロバスト性保証を持つ新しい正則化強化学習アルゴリズム「SMM-AC」を導出し、正則化がシム・ツー・リアルギャップや変化する環境条件に対するロバスト性を高めることで実機展開を改善することを示した。
llm.problem: シム・ツー・リアル転移の容易な正則化強化学習のプロわばすな保証があるにもかかわらず、弱い正則化を持つPPOなどが依然として主流であり、正則化の実用的な利点が十分に特徴づけられていないこと。
llm.method: ソフトメローマックス価値関数に基づき、強いロバスト性保証を持つ新しい正則化RLアルゴリズム「Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC)」の導出と評価。
llm.result: MuJoCoベンチマークでSAC等と競合しつつ、実機ロボットにおいてより高いリターンを達成し、観測・環境・ダイナミクスの摂動に対して優れたロバスト性を示した。

2610.35363.title: Resilient Decentralized Radar-LiDAR-Inertial Odometry in Challenging Subterranean Environments
2610.35363.abstract: Accurate localization in GPS-denied and visually degraded environments affected by smoke, dust, or fog remains a critical challenge for autonomous systems. While LiDAR provides high-resolution spatial perception, its performance deteriorates under particulate occlusion. In contrast, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar offers robustness under such conditions but suffers from sparse measurements and outliers. This article presents a resilient decentralized LiDAR Radar Inertial Odometry (LRIO) framework that fuses the complementary strengths of LiDAR, radar, and inertial sensing to achieve robust pose estimation in challenging subterranean environments. At the core of the framework is an Adaptive Residual Thresholding (ART) mechanism that autonomously detects temporal sensor degradation and selectively adjusts the fusion process to minimize unreliable measurements. Building on this, a Robust Error-Tolerant Optimal Information Filter (RETOIF) is employed within a decentralized fusion architecture to integrate LiDAR-inertial and multiple radar-inertial odometry estimates in a fault-aware manner, enhancing resilience to environmental disturbances and intermittent sensor failures. The proposed framework is evaluated using real-world sensor data collected in GPS-denied subterranean tunnels under smoke-free and smoke-degraded conditions. In the smoke-free experiment, the proposed RETOIF framework achieves a root mean square localization error (RMSE) of 2.1733, compared with 2.9929 for the conventional centralized LRIO approach, corresponding to a 27.4\% reduction in RMSE. Experimental results further demonstrate the framework's ability to maintain pose estimation under smoke-induced sensor degradation, highlighting its potential for resilient autonomous navigation and mapping in challenging subterranean environments.

llm.title_ja: 困難な地下環境におけるレジリエントな分散型レーダー・LiDAR・慣性オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: LiDAR、レーダー、慣性センシングを融合させ、適応型残差閾値機構（ART）とロバスト情報フィルター（RETOIF）を用いて煙や粉塵のある地下環境でも高精度な位置推定を実現する分散型オドメトリフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: GPSが届かず煙や粉塵、霧のある視覚的に劣化した環境において、LiDARの性能低下やレーダーのまばらな測定値と外れ値に対処しながら正確な位置推定を行うこと。
llm.method: 時間的なセンサー劣化を自動検出し統合プロセスを調整する適応型残差閾値（ART）機構と、故障耐性を持つ分散型融合アーキテクチャ内のロバスト情報フィルター（RETOIF）の活用。
llm.result: 煙のない実験でRMSEを27.4%削減し、煙によるセンサー劣化下でもポーズ推定を維持できることを実証した。

2610.32776.title: Predictive Long-Horizon Progress Modeling with Action-Aware Quantification
2610.32776.abstract: Quantitative and dense task progress feedback is essential for robotic manipulation across data curation, policy evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Existing progress annotations often rely on sparse keyframe markings derived from subjective manual judgments, limiting their scalability and cross-task consistency, particularly in long-horizon manipulation. To overcome these challenges, we propose action-aware quantification, a unified progress specification that decomposes long-horizon trajectories into object-level subtasks via a vision-language model (VLM) and assigns weighted action credits to capture fine-grained execution dynamics. Using VLM auto-labeling and human calibration, we construct an 800+ hour training video dataset and LOOM, a long-horizon progress benchmark containing 19,618 human-calibrated evaluation frames. To model these dense progress dynamics, we introduce NimCritic, a predictive progress critic trained via Joint Video-Progress Learning. We further incorporate Historical Progress Perturbation to mitigate sequential drift, and design a contrastive Video-Progress Alignment objective that bridges asymmetric expert streams by mutually grounding intermediate visual dynamics and denoised progress trajectories. NimCritic matches or outperforms state-of-the-art process reward models (PRMs) on the established Video Progress Benchmark (VPB) and LOOM, surpassing GVL (GPT-6-Sol) on VPB by about 65% in terminal success accuracy (TSA). On the large-scale RoboArena policy evaluation benchmark, it also retrieves human-selected successful rollouts with about 97% overall recall. These results establish action-aware quantification as a scalable foundation for dense progress feedback in robotic manipulation.
2610.32776.tldr_en: NimCritic, a predictive progress critic trained via Joint Video-Progress Learning, is introduced and action-aware quantification is proposed, a unified progress specification that decomposes long-horizon trajectories into object-level subtasks via a vision-language model and assigns weighted action credits to capture fine-grained execution dynamics.

llm.title_ja: 行動認識型量子化を用いた予測的長期タスク進捗モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 長期タスクをオブジェクト単位のサブタスクに分解し、重み付けされた行動クレジットを割り当てて詳細な実行ダイナミクスを捉える統合された進捗仕様である行動認識型量子化を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の進捗アノテーションは主観的な手動判断によるまばらなキーフレームに依存しており、特に長期マニピュレーションにおいて拡張性やタスク間の整合性が制限されている。
llm.method: ビジョン言語モデルを用いたVLM自動ラベル付けと人間の校正により、長期タスクの進捗ベンチマークを構築し、共同ビデオ進捗学習を通じて予測型進捗クリティックを訓練した。
llm.result: 確立されたVideo Progress BenchmarkやLOOMにおいて既存のプロセス報酬モデルと同等以上の性能を示し、ロボットアリーナのポリシー評価では高い再現率で成功したロールアウトを抽出した。

2610.32755.title: Semantic Representation for Agentic Self-Play in Automated Laboratories
2610.32755.abstract: Navigating complex, high-dimensional biological search spaces necessitates scalable physical and computational intelligence to explore beyond local optima through iterative self-play across ideation, experimentation, and automation. Translating experimental designs into reliable physical execution remains bottlenecked by static laboratory automation and unmodeled physical variability. To address this, we introduce VERified Infrastructure for Discovery Laboratories, or VERID, a foundational infrastructure designed to bridge the gap between the high-level reasoning of artificial intelligence (AI) agents and complex, error-prone physical realities of wet labs. VERID is a persistent, high-fidelity semantic digital twin of the laboratory workcell that provides four core services: queryable introspection for agentic reasoning, time-compressed simulation for protocol validation, comprehensive trace persistence for a complete scientific record, and a framework for safe execution. We present three case studies using aqueous dye and deionized water mixtures to validate the optical and fluidic foundations of VERID. These studies demonstrate how VERID enables pre-emptive detection of critical errors in experimental protocols, stateful mid-run error recovery and post-hoc identification of subtle physical failures. The simulation functions as a discrete accounting engine, allowing agents to safely and inexpensively explore experimental designs in silico and refine experimental strategies through iterative self-play. VERID also captures structured multimodal experimental data for downstream analysis, knowledge mining and agent training. We argue that this semantic layer is an essential prerequisite for deploying autonomous agents in the biochemical and biomedical sciences, ensuring data integrity, operational safety, and paving the way for tackling previously intractable grand challenges in biology.
2610.32755.tldr_en: It is argued that this semantic layer is an essential prerequisite for deploying autonomous agents in the biochemical and biomedical sciences, ensuring data integrity, operational safety, and paving the way for tackling previously intractable grand challenges in biology.

llm.title_ja: 自動化実験室における自律型セルフプレーのためのセマンティック表現
llm.tldr_ja: 人工知能エージェントの高水準な推論とウェットラボのエラーが起こりやすい物理的現実とのギャップを埋めるための基礎インフラストラクチャを提案した。
llm.problem: 実験デザインを信頼性の高い物理的実行へ翻訳することは、静的な実験室の自動化やモデル化されていない物理的変動によってボトルネックとなっている。
llm.method: 人工知能エージェント向けの高忠実度セマンティックデジタルツインとして機能するVERIDを導入し、クエリ可能な内省や時間圧縮シミュレーションなどの4つのコアサービスを提供する。
llm.result: 水溶液の混合を用いたケーススタディにより、実験プロトコルの重大なエラーの事前検知や状態に応じた中断時のエラー回復が可能であることを実証した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックデジタルツイン
物理シミュレーション

2610.32742.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection
2610.32742.abstract: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states. However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction. Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation. Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.
2610.32742.tldr_en: AWARE is a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction, and demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over the strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation.

llm.title_ja: 異常認識のための適応型世界モデル：ロボットダイナミクス予測と内省のためのフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: システムダイナミクスの推定と状態予測を介して外部カメラ監視のみを用いた異常検知が可能な世界モデルフレームワークを提案し、ノイズの多い環境で分類性能の向上を実証した。
llm.problem: 現在の異常検知アプローチは、オンボードセンサーへの直接アクセスに依存することが多いが、レガシーハードウェアにはセンサーが不足しているかセキュリティプロトコルで禁止されている。
llm.method: 外部カメラ監視のみを利用し、システムダイナミクスの推定と状態予測を通じて異常検知を行う世界モデルフレームワーク「AWARE」を提案する。
llm.result: 240の実世界ロボットクレーンの軌道を用いた評価において、ノイズの多いカメラのみの状態推定のもとで、ベースラインと比較して異常分類が26%向上した。

2610.32688.title: Conditional Neural Processes for Self-Supervised Goal Discovery in Action Imitation
2610.32688.abstract: Inspired by infants' ability to learn novel tasks by imitating others, in this work we evaluate to what extent Conditional Neural Processes can autonomously learn representations of actions that are informative about their underlying goal. We show that the addition of an attention mechanism in the hidden space fosters the emergence of robust goal representations early on in the observation of an action sequence, making it a promising model for a robotic self-supervised general learner.
2610.32688.comment: Presented at the poster session of the Workshop on World Models and Predictive Coding in Cognitive Robotics @ IROS2023 (https://world-model.emergent-symbol.systems/)
2610.32688.tldr_en: It is shown that the addition of an attention mechanism in the hidden space fosters the emergence of robust goal representations early on in the observation of an action sequence, making it a promising model for a robotic self-supervised general learner.

llm.title_ja: 行動模倣における自己教師ありゴール発見のための条件付きニューラルプロセス
llm.tldr_ja: 隠れ空間へのアテンション機構の追加が行動シーケンスの観察初期におけるロバストなゴール表現の創発を促進し、ロボットの自己教師あり汎用学習器としての有望なモデルであることを示した。
llm.problem: 乳児が他者の模倣によって新しいタスクを学ぶ能力にインスパイアされ、条件付きニューラルプロセスがどの程度自律的にゴールの情報を含む行動表現を学習できるかを評価する必要があった。
llm.method: 隠れ空間にアテンション機構を追加した条件付きニューラルプロセスを用い、行動シーケンスの観察から背後にあるゴール表現を自己教師ありで学習する。
llm.result: 隠れ空間へのアテンション機構の追加により、行動シーケンスの初期段階でロバストなゴール表現が創発し、ロボットの自己教師あり学習器として有望であることが示された。
keywords_ja: 条件付きニューラルプロセス

2610.32676.title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
2610.32676.abstract: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior. We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration. Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. A single trained speed prior instead covers every task in a corpus. We fit a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and use it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy. For execution, we pair the policy with a real-time optimal-control layer that tracks predicted action chunks under robot constraints using the predicted pace. On 120 RoboLab tasks, policies fine-tuned on our learned clocks succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with policies fine-tuned on the original demonstration timing and uniformly accelerated to the same speed. On a real robot, our policy stacks cups in 3.50s, 1.72$\times$ faster than the default policy's 6.02s while succeeding as often, in 29 of 30 trials. Videos and further material are available at https://mllab.snu.ac.kr/projects/learned_speed_prior.
2610.32676.tldr_en: This work fits a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and uses it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy.

llm.title_ja: 学習された速度事前分布を用いたロボットデモンストレーションの再タイミング
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模なデモンストレーションデータから速度事前分布を直接学習し、それを用いてロボットデモンストレーションのタイミングを人間のペースに再調整した上でVLAポリシーを微調整する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットデモンストレーションのペースはタスク自体ではなくオペレーターによって決定されるため、ポリシーがタスク動作とともにオペレーター固有のタイミングを引き継いでしまう。
llm.method: 大規模なデータから実行速度の分布を予測する速度事前分布を学習し、それを利用してロボットのデモンストレーションを手動デモのペースに再タイミングした上でポリシーを微調整する。
llm.result: 120のタスクにおいて、提案手法で微調整されたポリシーは従来のタイミングと比較して成功率が高く、ジャークが最大半分に低減された。実機ではカップのスタッキングを高速に成功させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションポリシー
モーション再タイミング

2610.32666.title: Robust Offset-Free Lane-Keeping Control Framework for Vision-Only Automated Vehicles
2610.32666.abstract: Achieving accurate, real-time lane-keeping control during high-speed cornering on large-curvature roads while ensuring robust vehicle stability is a critical challenge in autonomous driving. To address this challenge, this study developed a robust offset-free model predictive control (OF-MPC) framework for vision-based autonomous vehicle lane-keeping. The regulation problem in this framework is solved using several algorithms. Numerical simulation results indicated that the interpolation-tube-based constrained iterative linear quadratic regulator (itube-CILQR) algorithm outperformed solvers based on the standard Interior Point Optimizer (IPOPT) and Operator Splitting Quadratic Program (OSQP), achieving a mean computation time of less than 5 ms. The itube-CILQR algorithm was then used for vehicle control in vision-based lane-keeping experiments in a simulation environment to quantify the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception model (multitask UNet). This quantification was performed using the OF-MPC framework for traffic scenes that were not encountered during model training. Overall, the developed OF-MPC framework and the proposed method for characterizing the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception system in unseen environments can contribute to the future development of advanced autonomous driving systems.
2610.32666.tldr_en: The developed robust offset-free model predictive control framework and the proposed method for characterizing the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception system in unseen environments can contribute to the future development of advanced autonomous driving systems.

llm.title_ja: 視覚のみを用いた自動運転車のためのロバストなオフセットフリー車線維持制御フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 大曲率道路での高速コーナリング時に正確な車線維持制御とロバストな車両安定性を実現するため、ロバストなオフセットフリーモデル予測制御フレームワークを開発した。
llm.problem: 大曲率道路での高速コーナリングにおいて正確なリアルタイムの車線維持制御を実現しつつ、ロバストな車両安定性を確保することが自動運転における重要な課題である。
llm.method: 補間チューブベースの制約付き反復線形二次レギュレーターアルゴリズムを用いたロバストなオフセットフリーモデル予測制御フレームワークを開発した。
llm.result: 数値シミュレーションにより、提案するアルゴリズムは5ミリ秒未満の平均計算時間を達成し、視覚的知覚モデルの知覚的不確実性を定量化することができた。

2610.32645.title: Monte Carlo-Based Indoor UAV Localization in Dynamic Environments Using Only Four Onboard Range Sensors
2610.32645.abstract: Indoor UAV localization with minimal onboard sensing remains challenging, particularly in dynamic environments. We propose augmented filtered Monte Carlo localization (AF-MCL) for 2D localization using only four single-point range sensors and measured heading. AF-MCL rejects range measurements inconsistent with the known static map and adaptively injects particles to recover from localization divergence and kidnapping. Beam classification is performed only at the previous position estimate, making its ray-casting cost independent of the particle count. The particle distribution additionally provides an online measure of localization uncertainty. Real-world experiments in a 2.10x1.63 m environment yield mean position errors of 6.4-7.7 cm under static and dynamic conditions. Simulations in 6x6 m and 10x10 m environments yield 4.5-5.2 cm mean errors; under dynamic obstacles, standard MCL reaches 12.3 cm and reliable MCL 7.7 cm. The results show that robust indoor localization under dynamic obstacles is achievable with only four single-point range measurements and heading.

llm.title_ja: わずか4つのオンボード距離センサーを用いた動的環境におけるモンテカルロベースの屋内UAV自己位置推定
llm.tldr_ja: わずか4つの単一点距離センサーと方位計測のみを使用し、既知の静的地図と不一致な測定値を棄却してパーティクルを適応的に注入する拡張フィルタリングモンテカルロ自己位置推定手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 最小限のオンボードセンシングによる屋内のUAV自己位置推定は、特に動的環境において依然として挑戦的な課題である。
llm.method: 既知の静的地図と一致しない範囲測定値を棄却し、自己位置推定の破綻から回復するためにパーティクルを適応的に注入する拡張フィルタリングモンテカルロ自己位置推定を提案する。
llm.result: 実世界実験において、静的および動的条件下で6.4〜7.7 cmの平均位置誤差を達成し、動的障害物のある環境でもロバストな屋内自己位置推定が可能であることを示した。

2610.32636.title: Can AI Agents Help Robotic Engineers? Lessons from Two Focus Days in Industry
2610.32636.abstract: Software developers increasingly use AI agents that execute multi-step programming tasks on their own. However, it is unclear if and how this transfers to robotic engineering, where engineers program industrial robots in niche, vendor-specific languages and rely on visual feedback from simulation tools. Within this paper, we report a case study on the use of AI agents by an SME that programs industrial robots. Our results show that the agent did not make the engineers more productive, with the exception of a task that required the generation of highly repetitive code. However, the results with the agent improved over time, as the engineers learned how to use it and the agent was adapted to the domain. Moreover, the experience with AI mattered more for the success with the agent than the experience with robotic engineering. This shows that AI agents are not a plug-and-play solution. Instead, companies must train their engineers on the usage of agents, plan time for a learning curve, and ensure that agent configurations match the domain and developer requirements. The strong learning curve we observed further implies that studies on productivity gains with AI should be longitudinal, as they otherwise miss how engineers adopt agents in practice.
2610.32636.tldr_en: The results show that the agent did not make the engineers more productive, with the exception of a task that required the generation of highly repetitive code, and the strong learning curve implies that studies on productivity gains with AI should be longitudinal, as they otherwise miss how engineers adopt agents in practice.

llm.title_ja: AIエージェントはロボットエンジニアの助けになるか？産業界における2日間のフォーカスデイからの教訓
llm.tldr_ja: 産業用ロボットをプログラミングする中小企業においてAIエージェントの活用事例を報告し、高度に反復的なコード生成のタスクを除いてエージェントが直ちに生産性を向上させるわけではないことを示した。
llm.problem: ソフトウェア開発者向けAIエージェントが、ニッチでベンダー固有の言語で産業用ロボットをプログラムしシミュレーションツールに依存するロボットエンジニアリングにどのように移行できるかは不明確である。
llm.method: 産業用ロボットをプログラムする中小企業におけるAIエージェントの使用に関するケーススタディを実施し、エージェントの適応プロセスと生産性への影響を調査した。
llm.result: 高度に反復的なコード生成を除き、エージェントは直ちに生産性を向上させなかったが、エンジニアの習熟やドメインへの適応に伴い結果が改善される強い学習曲線が観察された。
keywords_ja: ロボットエンジニアリング

2610.32633.title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
2610.32633.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots support material transport in warehouses and industrial facilities, where navigation must adapt to changing operating conditions. Sensor observations reveal physical obstacles, but do not by themselves specify temporary access rules, route preferences, or exceptions known to operators. This paper presents a natural-language policy interface that brings this knowledge into ROS 2 Nav2. A local large language model converts instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions. Deterministic checks govern mission acceptance, and three costmap adapters project accepted policies into the existing navigation stack without changing its planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local models produce 107-142 correct accepted policies, compared with 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3-20 incorrect acceptances per model. Fault injection records rejection of eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults. Navigation experiments use correct task policies to evaluate keepouts, zone costs, person-dependent regions, and event-conditioned passage in simulation and on a TurtleBot3. For Tasks 1-3, mean travel times are 18.4-24.5% lower in simulation and 23.1-35.0% lower on the physical testbed than with the baseline lacking those policies. A native KeepoutFilter comparison and two-robot demonstrations examine basic keepout behavior and shared policy projection. The interface connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components.
2610.32633.comment: 23 pages, 16 figures, including supplementary material. Jiyeong Chae and Hyunkyo Seo contributed equally. Project page: https://a56239637-dot.github.io/Natural-Language-to-Nav2-Project-Page/
2610.32633.tldr_en: A natural-language policy interface that connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components is presented.

llm.title_ja: 自然言語からNav2へ：コストマップベースナビゲーションのための操作ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: ローカルな大規模言語モデルを使用して自然言語の指示をJSONポリシーに変換し、既存のプランナーやコントローラーを変更することなくROS 2 Nav2のナビゲーションスタックに統合する自然言語ポリシーインターフェースを提案した。
llm.problem: 自律移動ロボットのセンサー観測は物理的障害物を明らかにすることはできるが、オペレータだけが知っている一時的なアクセス規則やルートの選好をそれ単体では指定できない。
llm.method: ローカル大規模言語モデルを用いて指示を宛先や空間制約を含むJSONポリシーに変換し、決定論的なチェックを経てコストマップアダプターにより既存のナビゲーションスタックに投影する。
llm.result: 150件の英語コマンドを用いた評価において、提案手法はルールベースのパーサよりも多くの正しいポリシーを生成し、シミュレーションおよび実機のTurtleBot3で平均移動時間を大幅に短縮した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2610.33130.title: Ampe-DB: A Dataset for Human Activity and Interaction Analysis Using the Ghanaian Game Ampe
2610.33130.abstract: Human activity recognition benchmarks underrepresent culturally situated forms of movement and interaction. We introduce Ampe-DB, a multimodal dataset based on Ampe, a traditional Ghanaian game involving coordinated jumping, leg movements, and two-person interaction. It contains 637 canonical clips from 15 participants, with RGB video, two-person pose representations, participant and pair metadata, four-class movement labels, and derived binary movement-relation labels. We evaluate four-class movement recognition and binary movement-relation classification using three protocols: a duplicate-safe fixed benchmark, four-fold pair-held-out evaluation, and participant-held-out diagnostics for participants with complete class coverage. Baselines comprise a frozen Kinetics-400-pretrained R(2+1)D-18 RGB encoder, a two-layer bidirectional GRU for pose sequences, and validation-selected RGB-pose late fusion. For four-class recognition, RGB macro-F1 falls from 0.955 on the fixed benchmark to 0.418 under pair-held-out evaluation and 0.384 under participant-held-out evaluation. Pose is more robust, achieving 0.957, 0.811, and 0.839 across the same protocols. Fusion reaches 0.976 on the fixed benchmark and 0.824 under pair-held-out evaluation, but does not consistently improve on pose under participant shift. Binary movement-relation recognition also becomes substantially harder under held-out evaluation, especially for different-leg configurations. These findings show that strong fixed-benchmark scores can mask failures to generalize across people and pairings. Ampe-DB supports research on fine-grained movement recognition, human-human interaction, multimodal learning, and identity-aware generalization.
2610.33130.comment: 74 pages, 9 figures, 7 numbered tables. Ampe-DB V1 dataset (637 interaction clips) available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/RuthBiney/Ampe-DB
2610.33130.tldr_en: Findings show that strong fixed-benchmark scores can mask failures to generalize across people and pairings, and Ampe-DB supports research on fine-grained movement recognition, human-human interaction, multimodal learning, and identity-aware generalization.

llm.title_ja: Ampe-DB：ガーデンのゲーム「Ampe」を用いた人間行動・相互作用分析のための多次元データセット
llm.tldr_ja: 文化的に特異な動きや相互作用を捉えるため、ガーデンの伝統的なゲームであるAmpeをベースにしたマルチモーダルデータセット「Ampe-DB」を構築し、汎化性能の評価を行った。
llm.problem: 従来の人間行動認識のベンチマークは、文化的に偏った動作や相互作用の形態を十分に表現できていない。
llm.method: ガーデンの伝統的なゲーム「Ampe」に基づき、RGBビデオ、2人用の姿勢表現、メタデータ、動作ラベルを含むマルチモーダルデータセット「Ampe-DB」を構築し、複数の評価プロトコルでベースラインを評価した。
llm.result: 固定ベンチマークでは高い認識精度が得られるものの、参加者やペアを切り替えた評価においては精度が大幅に低下し、固定ベンチマークのスコアが汎化の失敗を隠蔽してしまうことを示した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルデータセット

2610.32596.title: OWLS: Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields for Zero-Shot Rover Navigation
2610.32596.abstract: Semantics can provide a proxy for physical traversability. Terrain that looks like loose sand or a rock field is likely to have similar physical properties. Open-vocabulary vision-language models (VLMs) enable this physical reasoning over terrain outside any fixed label set. We present Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields (OWLS), which plans directly over the dense feature map of a VLM. Prompted with a description of traversable terrain, the VLM scores every pixel of a single camera image; OWLS projects these scores onto the ground, adapts them to the platform with two morphological operations, and uses the result as the speed field of a minimum-time planner, so terrain appearance and obstacle clearance shape one trajectory. OWLS needs no task-specific training, no terrain annotation, no persistent map, and no exteroceptive sensor beyond the camera. We evaluate it on a physical rover indoors and off-road, on simulated Mars and Moon rovers over 200 procedurally generated terrains, and on real planetary imagery. Project page: https://chahyon-ku.github.io/owls/
2610.32596.tldr_en: Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields (OWLS), which plans directly over the dense feature map of a VLM, which scores every pixel of a single camera image and uses the result as the speed field of a minimum-time planner, so terrain appearance and obstacle clearance shape one trajectory.

llm.title_ja: OWLS: ゼロショットのローバーナビゲーションに向けたオープンワールド言語条件付き速度場
llm.tldr_ja: VLMの密な特徴マップを活用してカメラ画像から直接速度場を構築し、タスク特化型の訓練なしで効率的な軌道計画を実現する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 固定されたラベルセットに依存せず、未知の地形の外観から物理的通行性を推論してナビゲーションを行う必要があること。
llm.method: VLMのピクセルごとのスコアを地表に投影し、形態学的処理を適用して最小時間プランナーの速度場として利用する。
llm.result: 実機のローバー、シミュレーション上の火星・月ローバー、実際の惑星画像による評価で有効性を示した。

2610.32559.title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
2610.32559.abstract: Supervising a multi-UAV reconnaissance mission usually means plotting waypoints and watching every drone. We present UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes. The agent grounds inspection targets in an aerial map with a vision-language model, splits them among N UAVs by balancing route length, and dispatches worker agents that verify incidents with a compact onboard decision model. In simulation over 4 incident types and 3 foundation models, the swarm located the incident in 244 of 255 missions (95.7%). A paired scaling study with one to 5 UAVs shows that flight time follows an Amdahl-type law. The second UAV delivers half of the attainable saving and the speedup is bounded at 1.52x. We discuss what this predictability, and the false alarms we observed, imply for an operator who supervises the swarm, and outline the user study needed to test it.
2610.32559.tldr_en: UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes, is presented.

llm.title_ja: UAV-SwarmAgent：コード生成とビジョン言語推論を用いたスケーラブルなマルチUAV偵察とタスク割り当て
llm.tldr_ja: オペレーターが自然言語の1文でミッションを指定すると、地上ステーションのエージェントがコードを記述・実行して各UAVのルートを生成する階層型マルチエージェントシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: マルチUAVの偵察ミッションの監督には、通常、ウェイポイントのプロットやすべてのドローンの監視が必要であり、運用者の負担が大きい。
llm.method: ビジョン言語モデルを用いて空中マップ上の検査目標をグランドし、ルート長をバランスさせながらN台のUAVに分割し、オンボードの決定モデルで検証する階層型マルチエージェントシステムを構築した。
llm.result: 4種類のインシデントと3つの基盤モデルを用いたシミュレーションにおいて、95.7%のミッションでインシデントの位置を特定し、飛行時間がアムダールの法則に従うことを示した。
llm.limitation: 要旨 in 記載なし
keywords_ja: マルチエージェントシステム

2610.32554.title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
2610.32554.abstract: Zero-shot object navigation requires an agent to reason about where a target may be found while retaining evidence from previous observations. We present HGWM, a hierarchical graph-guided world model that combines a category-conditioned room--anchor prior with persistent spatial-semantic memory. A coarse stage uses a vision-language model to score candidate headings, while a fine stage explicitly compares observed objects and relations with the goal prior. Phase-dependent fusion integrates these signals with a language-model recommendation to guide local navigation. HGWM achieves 62.6\% success rate (SR) and 31.5\% success weighted by path length (SPL) on HM3D v0.1, improving over WMNav by 4.5 and 0.3 percentage points, respectively. On MP3D, it achieves 46.8\% SR and 17.9\% SPL, with gains of 1.4 and 0.7 points. On HM3D v0.2, the full model reaches 74.4\% SR and 31.9\% SPL; removing individual components reduces SR by 0.9--2.3 points and SPL by 0.6--1.5 points. These results support the use of relational priors and persistent graph memory for target-directed search.
2610.32554.tldr_en: The results support the use of relational priors and persistent graph memory for target-directed search in zero-shot object navigation and support the use of relational priors and persistent graph memory for target-directed search in relational memory.

llm.title_ja: HGWM：グラフマッチングによるゼロショット物体ナビゲーションのための階層的グラフ誘導世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: カテゴリ条件付きの部屋アンカー事前分布と持続的な空間セマンティックメモリを組み合わせた階層的グラフ誘導世界モデルを提案し、ゼロショット物体ナビゲーションにおける成功率の向上を実証した。
llm.problem: ゼロショット物体ナビゲーションでは、エージェントが過去の観察からの証拠を保持しながら、ターゲットがどこにあるかを推論する必要がある。
llm.method: ビジョン言語モデルを使用して候補の見出しをスコアリングする粗いステージと、観測された物体や関係をゴール事前分布と明示的に比較する細かいステージを組み合わせた階層的世界モデルを提案する。
llm.result: HM3DやMP3Dなどのベンチマークにおいて、既存モデルを上回る成功率を達成し、関係的事前分布と持続的なグラフメモリの有効性を実証した。

2610.32538.title: Optimization, Optimal Control, and Reinforcement Learning for Robotics
2610.32538.abstract: These lecture notes provide an introduction to optimization, optimal control, and reinforcement learning for robotics, emphasizing their mathematical connections and practical relevance. They present established material compiled and edited by Yonghyeon Lee, rather than new research results. The notes were developed through a human and AI collaborative writing process, with AI assistance in drafting, organizing, and refining the exposition. This first version is a preliminary collection of notes, not yet a fully developed textbook, and currently contains no figures or graphs. The notes may be revised, corrected, and expanded in future versions.
2610.32538.comment: Preliminary lecture notes, version 1. Compiled and edited by Yonghyeon Lee through a human and AI collaborative writing process. No figures; revisions and expansions are planned

llm.title_ja: ロボット工学のための最適化、最適制御、強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット工学における最適化、最適制御、強化学習の数学的つながりと実用的な関連性を強調した講義ノートを提供し、人間とAIの協調的な執筆プロセスを通じて作成された。
llm.problem: ロボット工学における最適化、最適制御、強化学習の数学的なつながりと実用的な関連性を体系的に学ぶための統合された教材が求められている。
llm.method: 人間とAIの協調的な執筆プロセス（AIによるドラフト作成、構成、洗練の補助）を通じて、確立された資料を編集・コンパイルした講義ノートを作成した。
llm.result: 将来のバージョンでの改訂や拡張が予定されている、予備的な講義ノートの初版をまとめた。

2610.32526.title: Facultative Swarming: A Capability, Not a Category, for Multi-Robot Systems
2610.32526.abstract: Collective robotics is split by a long-standing but increasingly artificial boundary between centralised multi-robot systems that prioritise optimality and decentralised swarms that prioritise robustness and adaptivity. We propose a unified control framework, shifting from `obligate' swarms---systems constrained to pure self-organisation---to facultatively swarming systems: hybrid architectures that operate as centrally planned systems under permissive conditions yet degrade gracefully into decentralised swarming under environmental stress. By reframing swarming as a dynamic capability, rather than a rigid system category, we outline a pathway towards collective robotic systems that benefit from centralised optimality when conditions permit and from the flexibility of self-organisation when they do not.
2610.32526.tldr_en: This work reframes swarming as a dynamic capability, rather than a rigid system category, and outlines a pathway towards collective robotic systems that benefit from centralised optimality when conditions permit and from the flexibility of self-organisation when they do not.

llm.title_ja: 条件付きスワーミング：マルチロボットシステムにおけるカテゴリではなく能力
llm.tldr_ja: スワーミングを厳格なシステムカテゴリではなく動的な能力として再定義し、中央集権的な最適性と自己組織化の柔軟性を両立するハイブリッドな制御フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 集合ロボット工学は、最適性を優先する中央集権型マルチロボットシステムと、ロバスト性と適応性を優先する分散型スウォームとの間の長年の境界によって分断されている。
llm.method: 純粋な自己組織化に制約されたシステムから、好ましい条件下では中央集権的に動作しつつ環境ストレス下では分散型スワーミングに優雅に移行するハイブリッドアーキテクチャへと移行する統一制御フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: スワーミングを動的な能力として再定義することで、条件が許す場合は中央集権的な最適性の恩恵を受け、そうでない場合は自己組織化の柔軟性を活かせる経路を示した。
keywords_ja: マルチロボットシステム
ハイブリッドアーキテクチャ

2610.32525.title: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework
2610.32525.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating robotic systems that reproduce expert scanning skills consistently. These skills involve coordinated interpretation of anatomical landmarks, ultrasound images, and probe-tissue interactions that are difficult to encode in hand-designed control strategies. Imitation learning offers an alternative, but its observation and action representations should reflect the anatomically structured nature of scanning. We propose an anatomy-anchored imitation-learning framework that combines anatomy-guided probe placement with learned ultrasound navigation. The placement module identifies a task-specific anatomical starting point from external visual observations and establishes the initial probe pose as the reference frame for scanning. A flow-based policy then generates scanning motions from anchor-relative probe poses, ultrasound images, probe-mounted camera views, and contact forces, while a termination head predicts task completion. This avoids continuous reliance on third-person vision and reduces dependence on the robot-patient configuration. A handheld acquisition platform enables multimodal demonstrations to be collected during natural freehand scanning without a robot. On 16 unseen participants, task success reaches 96%, 94%, 88%, and 94% for kidney, gallbladder, and liver standard-plane acquisition and radial artery sweeping, respectively. Compared with a fine-tuned pi_0 model, success on the abdominal tasks improves by 10-42 percentage points, with lower time-to-target, peak contact force, and trajectory jerk. Ablations support the complementary roles of anatomical anchoring, egocentric vision, and force feedback. End-to-end trials with automatic placement achieve 90-100% success, and the policies transfer without retraining to a second robot with 83-100% success.
2610.32525.tldr_en: An anatomy-anchored imitation-learning framework that combines anatomy-guided probe placement with learned ultrasound navigation is proposed, which avoids continuous reliance on third-person vision and reduces dependence on the robot-patient configuration.

llm.title_ja: フリーハンドデモンストレーションから自律型ロボット超音波へ：解剖学にアンカーされた学習フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 解剖学的にガイドされたプローブ配置と学習された超音波ナビゲーションを組み合わせ、第三者視点のビジョンへの依存を避ける解剖学アンカー型の模倣学習フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 超音波検査スキルはオペレーター依存が高く、解剖学的ランドマーク、超音波画像、プローブと組織の相互作用の協調的解釈をハンドメイドの制御戦略でエンコードすることは困難である。
llm.method: 外部視覚観測から解剖学的開始点を特定して初期プローブ姿勢を確立する配置モジュールと、フローベースのポリシーを用いてスキャン動作を生成するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 16名の未知の被験者を対象とした実験で、腎臓、胆嚢、肝臓等の標準面取得や橈骨動脈のスイーピングにおいて高い成功率を達成し、既存のπ0モデルと比較して性能が大幅に向上した。

2610.33125.title: Investigating the trackability of landmarks in NBI and WLI
2610.33125.abstract: Reliable visual tracking of anatomical landmarks in endoscopic video is a key prerequisite for computer-assisted interventions in laryngeal surgery. While Narrow Band Imaging (NBI) is clinically established for enhancing vascular contrast, its effect on automated tracking relative to conventional White Light Imaging (WLI) remains unexplored. We present a quantitative comparison of landmark trackability in NBI and WLI using a forward-backward error framework applied to 61 endoscopic videos from 39 patients. Two regions of interest are evaluated: the vocal folds (VF) and mucosa with a prominent vascular pattern (MPVP). We compare a classical feature-based tracker (CSRT) against learning-based point trackers (CoTracker3-Online and TrackOnR) across both modalities. NBI consistently reduced the forward-backward error in both regions, reaching statistical significance for the vocal folds, while failure rates stayed low. These findings indicate that NBI can improve tracking robustness in laryngeal endoscopy, with implications for motion analysis, navigation, and robotic assistance.
2610.33125.tldr_en: Findings indicate that NBI can improve tracking robustness in laryngeal endoscopy, with implications for motion analysis, navigation, and robotic assistance.

llm.title_ja: NBIおよびWLIにおけるランドマークの追跡可能性の調査
llm.tldr_ja: 狭帯域光観察（NBI）が従来の白色光観察（WLI）と比較して、喉頭手術の内視鏡ビデオにおける解剖学的ランドマークの自動追跡のロバスト性を向上させることを定量的に示した。
llm.problem: 狭帯域光観察（NBI）は血管コントラストの強調に臨床的確立されているが、従来の白色光観察（WLI）と比較した自動追跡への影響は未解明であった。
llm.method: 39患者の61件の内視鏡ビデオに前向き・後ろ向きのエラーフレームワークを適用し、従来の特徴ベースのトラッカーと学習ベースのポイントトラッカーを比較評価した。
llm.result: NBIは両方の関心領域において前向き・後ろ向きのエラーを首尾一貫して減少させ、特に声帯において統計的有意性に達し、追跡のロバスト性が向上することを示した。

2610.32460.title: CoCarry: Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting for Dual-Humanoid Cooperative Carrying
2610.32460.abstract: Recent advances in large-scale human motion data, motion retargeting, and motion imitation have enabled increasingly capable whole-body control for individual humanoids. Cooperative carrying is more challenging because successful coordination requires not only plausible individual motions, but also consistent cross-agent and agent-object relations, including shared grasp, relative configuration, and whole-body support. We introduce CoCarry, a cooperative-carrying dataset containing 220 synchronized two-person sequences across 21 task schemes, five shared-object geometries, four terrain types, and approximately 61 minutes of motion. We further propose Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting, which starts from nominal individual motions and jointly refines both humanoids around the same prescribed object trajectory. Cooperation-aware object-local hand anchors preserve compatible four-hand grasp relations, while complementary upper object-interaction and lower support structures retain object-relative geometry and coordinated support. Across all 220 CoCarry sequences retargeted to two A3 humanoids, our method achieves 0.9995 contact preservation, reduces penetration duration by 67.0% and 71.0% relative to GMR and OmniRetarget, respectively, and maintains a 100% retargeting success rate. On CORE4D with Unitree G1 humanoids, it achieves 0.9906 contact preservation with zero measured sliding. We further validate the generated references through physics simulation and multiple real-world cooperative carrying experiments on two physical A3 humanoids, demonstrating their usability for downstream dual-humanoid control.
2610.32460.tldr_en: This work introduces CoCarry, a cooperative-carrying dataset containing 220 synchronized two-person sequences across 21 task schemes, five shared-object geometries, four terrain types, and approximately 61 minutes of motion, and proposes Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting, which starts from nominal individual motions and jointly refines both humanoids around the same prescribed object trajectory.

llm.title_ja: CoCarry：デュアルヒューマノイドの協調搬送に向けた接触・支持構造化リタイジェーティング
llm.tldr_ja: 220件の同期された2人組の協調搬送データセットを構築し、個別の動作を共通のオブジェクト軌道に沿って共同で洗練させる接触・支持構造化リタイジェーティング手法を提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの協調搬送では、個別の自然な動作だけでなく、共有の把持や相対的姿勢、全身の支持を含む一貫したエージェント間・エージェント・物体間の関係の維持が課題となる。
llm.method: 220の同期されたシーケンスからなるデータセット「CoCarry」を構築し、協力認識型の物体ローカルハンドアンカーや上下の支持構造を用いて個別の動作を共同で洗練させる手法を提案する。
llm.result: 2体のA3ヒューマノイドへのリタイジェーティングにおいて、高い接触維持率を達成し、既存手法と比較して貫通時間を大幅に削減し、実機での協調搬送実験で有効性を検証した。
keywords_ja: モーションリタイジェーティング

2610.32459.title: MDMR-Bench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Multi-Reference Image Generation
2610.32459.abstract: Image generation models have rapidly advanced, with many models now supporting generation conditioned on multiple reference images and textual instructions. Such models enable a wide range of applications, including entity fusion and attribute transfer across images. However, existing benchmarks for multi-reference image generation rely on limited evaluation dimensions and fail to capture the diverse challenges of the task. To address this limitation, we propose MDMR-Bench, a Multi-Dimensional benchmark for Multi-Reference image generation. MDMR-Bench is organized around representative capability settings and consists of multiple evaluation subsets spanning diverse dimensions of multi-reference image generation, including (1) common entity fusion and attribute transfer, (2) multi-element extraction from a single image, (3) infographic manipulation, and (4) visual reasoning-intensive generation. This design enables systematic analysis of model capabilities and failure modes across different challenge dimensions. Furthermore, to achieve more reliable and interpretable evaluation, we introduce a checklist-based evaluation protocol that decomposes generation quality into fine-grained evaluation aspects.
