Instead of relying solely on holistic scoring, our framework uses structured checklists composed of both global-level and atomic-level queries, enabling more diagnostic assessment of model performance. By benchmarking both open-source and proprietary models, we demonstrate that MDMR-Bench provides fine-grained insights into model performance across different dimensions. The dataset and code are publicly available.
2610.32459.comment: Bowen Zheng and Jintao Lin contributed equally to this work. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track
2610.32459.tldr_en: This work proposes MDMR-Bench, a Multi-Dimensional benchmark for Multi-Reference image generation and introduces a checklist-based evaluation protocol that decomposes generation quality into fine-grained evaluation aspects, enabling more diagnostic assessment of model performance.

llm.title_ja: MDMR-Bench：マルチリファレンス画像生成のための多次元ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な課題次元をカバーするマルチリファレンス画像生成のための多次元ベンチマーク「MDMR-Bench」を提案し、生成品質を細粒度の評価項目に分解するチェックリストベースの評価プロトコルを導入した。
llm.problem: 既存のマルチリファレンス画像生成のベンチマークは評価次元が限られており、タスクの多様な課題を捉えきれていない。
llm.method: エンティティ融合や属性転写、マルチ要素抽出などの代表的なケイパビリティ設定に基づくマルチリファレンス画像生成ベンチマーク「MDMR-Bench」を構築し、チェックリストベースの評価プロトコルを導入した。
llm.result: オープンソースおよびプロプライエタリなモデルのベンチマークを通じて、モデルの性能や失敗モードについて細粒度な洞察が得られることを示した。

2610.32439.title: $R^2E:$ A Role-driven Reward Evolutionary Framework for Automated Reward Function Design
2610.32439.abstract: Designing effective reward functions is a critical challenge in Reinforcement Learning (RL), which traditionally requires costly manual trial-and-error. While Large Language Model (LLM)-based methods have shown promise in reward design, undifferentiated sampling and limited use of historical feedback often lead to insufficient exploration of the reward space and optimization instability. To address these challenges, we propose $R^2E$, a Role-driven Reward Evolutionary framework for automated reward function design that structures the process through explicit role specialization. $R^2E$ employs multiple LLM roles with complementary objectives: an Explorer that promotes novelty to expand the search space, a Guardian that performs conservative refinements to improve training stability, and an Evolver that recombines high-performing rewards via crossover and mutation to integrate effective structures. A dynamic scheduling strategy coordinates these roles, progressively shifting the search from broad exploration to focused exploitation. To mitigate optimization instability and provide a medium for cross-role collaboration, $R^2E$ incorporates a Global Elite Pool that retains the best-performing rewards to guide subsequent generations, thereby enabling coordinated interaction among roles and ensuring a reliable and consistent refinement process. Extensive experiments on multiple robotic tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.
2610.32439.tldr_en: A Role-driven Reward Evolutionary framework for automated reward function design that structures the process through explicit role specialization, thereby enabling coordinated interaction among roles and ensuring a reliable and consistent refinement process is proposed.

llm.title_ja: R^2E：自動報酬関数設計のための役割駆動型報酬進化フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 明確な役割特異化を通じてプロセスを構造化する自動報酬関数設計のための役割駆動型報酬進化フレームワーク「R^2E」を提案し、報酬空間の十分な探索と最適化の安定性を実現した。
llm.problem: 強化学習における効果的な報酬関数の設計は従来コストの高い手動の試行錯誤を必要とし、大規模言語モデルベースの手法でも非差別的なサンプリングや歴史的フィードバックの利用不足により最適化が不安定になりがちである。
llm.method: 新規性を促進するExplorer、保守的な洗練を行うGuardian、高パフォーマンスの報酬を組み換えるEvolverという明確な役割を持つ複数のLLMを用いた役割駆動型の進化フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 複数のロボットタスクに対する広範な実験により、提案手法の有効性が実証され、役割間の協調的相互作用を通じて信頼性の高い一貫した洗練プロセスが確保された。

2610.32431.title: When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning
2610.32431.abstract: A failed vision-language-action (VLA) rollout does not imply that every action contributed to failure. Yet in group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), a single trajectory-level advantage is assigned to all actions in a rollout. Potentially useful recovery attempts can thus be penalized alongside the errors they aim to correct. Ideal stopping conditions for failure feedback are characterized using success-probability and policy-score martingales. At these stops, the removed gradient contribution has zero conditional expectation given the retained information. Truncation therefore preserves the expectation of a reference GRPO group-gradient estimator and can reduce its covariance. One such stop occurs when the conditional probability of success is zero, motivating error and recovery cues for selecting candidate feedback boundaries. Martingale GRPO (MART-GRPO) is introduced with a vision-language model (VLM) for event-guided truncation. The VLM is fine-tuned on our annotated training set using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The last visible error without observed recovery is localized by the frozen VLM in complete rollout videos. Failure feedback is retained through the selected error interval and removed afterward, while successful-rollout loss terms and original loss normalization are preserved. For retrospective boundaries, changes in expectation and variance are analyzed to assess departures from ideal stopping. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on RoboTwin 2.0 show that MART-GRPO improves success rates over full-trajectory GRPO across multiple tasks.
2610.32431.tldr_en: Martingale GRPO (MART-GRPO) is introduced with a vision-language model (VLM) for event-guided truncation, and experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on RoboTwin 2.0 show that MART-GRPO improves success rates over full-trajectory GRPO across multiple tasks.

llm.title_ja: 行動にペナルティを与えるのはいつか？VLA強化学習のためのマルチンゲールGRPO
llm.tldr_ja: MART-GRPOは、イベントガイド付き打ち切りのための視覚言語モデルを導入し、RoboTwin 2.0上のOpenVLA-OFTを用いた実験により、複数タスクで全軌道GRPOよりも成功率を向上させることを示した。
llm.problem: グループ相対方策最適化（GRPO）では単一の軌道レベルの利得がすべての行動に割り当てられるため、有用なリカバリー試行も誤りとともにペナルティを受ける。
llm.method: 成功確率と方策スコアのマルチンゲールを用いて理想的な停止条件を特徴づけ、イベントガイド付き打ち切りのためにVLMを導入したMartingale GRPO（MART-GRPO）を提案する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0上のOpenVLA-OFTを用いた実験により、MART-GRPOは複数タスクにおいて全軌道GRPOよりも成功率を向上させることが示された。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.32390.title: PASTA: Prompt-Aware Annealed Diffusion Sampling
2610.32390.abstract: While Diffusion models produce high-quality images, real-world visual design requires intentionally preserving clean regions for headlines, logos, or UI elements. Existing layout-aware text-to-image methods struggle to strictly preserve reserved regions, often introducing unwanted content that complicates downstream editing. Existing approaches either manipulate attention to displace content or suppress conditioning via noise-level interventions. However, these methods sacrifice visual coherence, producing flat regions or noticeable style inconsistencies between reserved and non-reserved areas. To address this limitation, we propose a Prompt-Aware Shared-Latent Training-Free Annealed Diffusion Sampling (PASTA), a training-free framework that enforces reserved-region constraints by selectively applying semantic guidance to object-allowed regions during sampling. PASTA operates on a shared latent trajectory, where full-prompt and context-prompt guidance are fused through mask-guided sampling. An annealed schedule suppresses semantic leakage during early denoising stages while gradually restoring visual consistency in later stages. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PASTA improves reserved-region fidelity while preserving overall image realism and perceptual consistency.
2610.32390.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to ICONIP2026
2610.32390.tldr_en: A Prompt-Aware Shared-Latent Training-Free Annealed Diffusion Sampling (PASTA), a training-free framework that enforces reserved-region constraints by selectively applying semantic guidance to object-allowed regions during sampling to improve reserved-region fidelity and overall image realism and perceptual consistency.

llm.title_ja: PASTA: プロンプト認識型アニーリング拡散サンプリング
llm.tldr_ja: PASTAは、サンプリング中にオブジェクト許可領域に意味論的ガイダンスを選択的に適用することで、予約領域の忠実度、全体的な画像リアリズム、および知覚的一貫性を向上させる、学習不要のフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存のレイアウト認識型テキスト画像生成手法は、予約された領域を厳密に保持するのに苦労し、視覚的コヒーレンスを犠牲にして望ましくないコンテンツを導入してしまう。
llm.method: 共有された潜在軌道上で動作し、マスク誘導サンプリングによってフルプロンプトとコンテキストプロンプトのガイダンスを融合させる、学習不要のアニーリング拡散サンプリングフレームワーク（PASTA）を提案する。
llm.result: 大規模な実験により、PASTAは全体的な画像のリアリズムと知覚的一貫性を維持しながら、予約領域の忠実度を向上させることが実証された。
keywords_ja: コンピュータビジョン

2610.32365.title: Graphs of Trajectory Bundles for Nonlinear Motion Planning
2610.32365.abstract: We present the Graphs of Trajectory Bundles (GTB) method for motion planning of systems with nonlinear and black-box dynamics, combining sampling-based motion planning with trajectory optimization and graph search. Based on a graph-of-convex-sets decomposition of the workspace, GTB iteratively constructs a graph of trajectory bundles that captures the local dynamics of the system at any vertex. By solving a shortest-path problem on this graph, we find maximally dynamically feasible iterates that satisfy the system's dynamics in the limit and any constraints such as collision avoidance or additional safety or specification constraints by construction of the underlying graph. As a result, GTB can handle highly nonlinear, unstable, and even black-box dynamics with complex collision and specification constraints, making it a powerful tool for motion planning of complex systems.
2610.32365.tldr_en: The Graphs of Trajectory Bundles method is presented, combining sampling-based motion planning with trajectory optimization and graph search, and can handle highly nonlinear, unstable, and even black-box dynamics with complex collision and specification constraints.

llm.title_ja: 非線形モーションプランニングのための軌道バンドルグラフ
llm.tldr_ja: サンプリングベースのモーションプランニングと軌道最適化およびグラフ探索を組み合わせた「Graphs of Trajectory Bundles (GTB)」手法が提案され、複雑な衝突制約や仕様制約を持つ高度に非線形、不安定、ブラックボックスなダイナミクスを処理できる。
llm.problem: 複雑なシステムにおいて、高度に非線形、不安定、またはブラックボックスなダイナミクスを持ち、衝突回避や安全性などの複雑な制約を満たすモーションプランニングは困難である。
llm.method: 作業空間の凸集合グラフ分解に基づき、システムの局所ダイナミクスを捉える軌道バンドルグラフを反復的に構築し、最短経路問題を解くことで動的に実行可能な反復解を見つけるGTB手法を提案する。
llm.result: GTBは、複雑な衝突回避や安全性・仕様制約を伴う、高度に非線형、不安定、さらにはブラックボックスなダイナミクスを処理できる強力なツールであることが示された。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.32348.title: LogLook: Execution-Grounded Memory for Frontier-Model Robot Planners
2610.32348.abstract: Many manipulation tasks require a robot to remember what it has done and what it has seen. Frontier vision-language models can plan such tasks without task-specific training, but how such a planner should remember an episode is an open question. We argue that its memory must keep track of what the planner has done and learned, and must let the planner choose what to look at, since every frame costs tokens; a note rewritten at every step meets both poorly. We propose LogLook, whose execution-grounded memory lets the system keep the record, an execution log and the model's earlier notes, while the model decides where to look: frames are returned only where it expects a change, and demonstrations are skimmed before it inspects the parts it chooses. Measured with the benchmark's motion planner, LogLook matches the success of a note-only memory with 43% fewer tokens and less than half the images, and fails far fewer episodes through what it remembered or saw. With direct control, LogLook solves 93.5% of the RoboMME test set.
2610.32348.tldr_en: This work proposes LogLook, whose execution-grounded memory lets the system keep the record, an execution log and the model's earlier notes, while the model decides where to look: frames are returned only where it expects a change, and demonstrations are skimmed before it inspects the parts it chooses.

llm.title_ja: LogLook: フロンティアモデルロボットプランナーのための実行グラウンデッドメモリ
llm.tldr_ja: この研究では、システムが実行ログとモデルの以前のメモを保持しつつ、モデル自身がどこを見るべきかを決定する実行グラウンデッドメモリを持つLogLookを提案している。
llm.problem: フロンティア視覚言語モデルはタスク固有の訓練なしで計画を立てることができるが、エピソードの記憶をどのように保持すべきか（すべてのフレームにコストがかかる点など）は未解決の問いである。
llm.method: システムが実行ログと以前のメモを保持し、モデルが変化を期待するフレームのみを返すことでどこを見るべきかを決定する実行グラウンデッドメモリ「LogLook」を提案する。
llm.result: RoboMMEテストセットにおいて、LogLookは直接制御により93.5%のタスクを解決し、メモのみのメモリと同等の成功率を43%少ないトークン数と半分未満の画像で達成した。

2610.32330.title: DynaSlots: Slot-Centric 3D Dynamics Pretraining for Robot Manipulation
2610.32330.abstract: Robot manipulation involves localized changes: picking up a cup moves the cup while leaving the surrounding scene largely unchanged. Yet existing 3D visual pretraining methods, including recent dynamics-aware variants, model state transitions at the scene level, compressing the motion of everything in a scene into a single global latent action. This conflates semantically distinct transitions in scenes with multiple moving parts, obscures dependencies between changing regions, and leaves the learned representation vulnerable to task-irrelevant scene content. We introduce DynaSlots, an action-free, label-free pretraining framework that decomposes each point cloud frame into a small set of temporally consistent slots and models dynamics at this per-slot level rather than the scene level. A temporal slot propagation module promotes consistent slot assignments across frames; an inverse dynamics model then extracts one latent action per slot from feature differences, and a diffusion-based forward dynamics model, paired with a self-supervised interaction head, predicts each slot's future state while learning pairwise proximity-and-motion relations. Experiments on Meta-World, Adroit, and a RealMan RM65-B robot demonstrate that DynaSlots outperforms prior scene-level baselines. It achieves superior success rates in simulation and exhibits strong robustness to scene clutter and unseen objects in real-world manipulation. Code is available at \href{https://zhucezhanghao12345-source.github.io/DynaSlots-Anonymous/}{https://zhucezhanghao12345-source.github.io/DynaSlots-Anonymous/}.
2610.32330.tldr_en: DynaSlots is introduced, an action-free, label-free pretraining framework that decomposes each point cloud frame into a small set of temporally consistent slots and models dynamics at this per-slot level rather than the scene level and achieves superior success rates in simulation and exhibits strong robustness to scene clutter and unseen objects in real-world manipulation.

llm.title_ja: DynaSlots: ロボットマニピュレーションのためのスロット中心3D動的プレトレーニング
llm.tldr_ja: DynaSlotsが導入され、アクション不要かつラベルフリーのプレトレーニングフレームワークであり、ポイントクラウドフレームをテンポラルに一貫したスロットに分解し、シーンレベルではなくスロットレベルでダイナミクスをモデル化し、シミュレーションで優れた成功率を達成し実世界の複雑なシーンや未知のオブジェクトに対する強力なロバスト性を示す。
llm.problem: 既存の3D視覚プレトレーニング手法はシーンレベルで状態遷移をモデル化するため、複数の動く部分を持つシーンにおいて意味的に異なる遷移が混同され、タスクに無関係なシーン内容に脆弱になる。
llm.method: 各ポイントクラウドフレームをテンポラルに一貫したスロットの小セットに分解し、シーンレベルではなくスロットレベルでダイナミクスをモデル化するアクション不要・ラベルフリーのプレトレーニングフレームワーク「DynaSlots」を導入する。
llm.result: Meta-World、Adroit、およびRealManロボットでの実験により、DynaSlotsは従来のシーンレベルのベースラインを上回り、シミュレーションで優れた成功率を達成し、実世界のマニピュレーションにおいて強いロバスト性を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.32314.title: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains
2610.32314.abstract: This paper presents the engineering implementation methods of the SKG inference framework and provides complete case studies across four domains. Case 1, 2D Dissipative Mechanical System: OOD MSE is 1.69 to 4.12 times lower than the best neural baseline; the state-dependent metric yields a 10^8-order improvement under controlled conditions. Case 2, Target Detection Sim-to-Real: Real-machine mAP increases from 0.2564 to 0.4964 (+24.00 points, single-run experiment, 32 images, point estimate), and AP75 increases from 0.1736 to 0.5765 (+40.29 points), with no real-machine retraining required. Case 3, Sequence Modeling sine to square: OOD MSE is 0.0296 versus Transformer 0.0641 (mean of 5 seeds, p=0.024). Case 4, Molecular Dynamics MD17: ID@100 ADE is 0.0285 versus ESTAG 0.1467; OOD@100 is 0.0316 versus 0.1411 (single seed). For each case, we present the objective, applied SKG theory, parameter settings, baseline comparison protocol, data results, and sources of advantage. Following the cases, we provide the complete methodology: pre-validation, task invariant construction, three-stage training, residual training, and the four theorems and one proposition supporting these methods. This paper not only demonstrates effective configurations of SKG across four domains but also honestly reports the variance of single-run experiments, limitations of single-seed results, negative updates caused by parameterization mismatch, and practical experience of using engineering thresholds as diagnostic signals rather than hard constraints.
2610.32314.tldr_en: This paper not only demonstrates effective configurations of SKG across four domains but also honestly reports the variance of single-run experiments, limitations of single-seed results, negative updates caused by parameterization mismatch, and practical experience of using engineering thresholds as diagnostic signals rather than hard constraints.

llm.title_ja: 実践におけるSKG: 4つのドメインにわたるOOD汎化の事例
llm.tldr_ja: この論文では、SKG推論フレームワークのエンジニアリング実装方法を提示し、4つのドメインにわたる完全なケーススタディを提供するとともに、単一実行実験の分散やエンジニアリングしきい値の診断信号としての活用などの実用的な経験を正直に報告している。
llm.problem: パラメータ化のミスマッチによる負の更新や、単一シード結果の限界など、機械学習モデルのOOD汎化における実装上の課題への対処が必要である。
llm.method: SKG推論フレームワークのエンジニアリング実装方法を提示し、事前検証、タスク不変量構築、3段階トレーニング、残差トレーニングなどの完全な方法論と4つの定理を適用して4つのドメインで評価する。
llm.result: 4つのドメイン（2D散逸機械システム、ターゲット検出Sim-to-Sim、時系列モデリング、分子動力学）において有効な設定を示し、OOD MSEの大幅な低減やmAPの向上などの優れた結果を達成した。
llm.limitation: 単一実行実験の分散や単一シード結果の限界、パラメータ化のミスマッチによる負の更新が存在する。
keywords_ja: エンジニアリング実装

2610.32312.title: MAST-VLA: Skill-Conditioned Adaptation with Trajectory-Affordance Priors for Multi-Skill Robot Manipulation
2610.32312.abstract: Generalist robot manipulation requires a single vision-language-action (VLA) policy to execute diverse skills across scenes and instructions. However, current multi-skill VLA policies often leave two aspects of an instruction insufficiently modeled: which primitive skill to execute and where/how to contact and move objects. We propose MAST-VLA (Multi-skill Adaptation with Skill-conditioned experts and Trajectory-affordance priors), a dual-conditioning framework for robot manipulation. MAST-VLA introduces skill-conditioned LoRA Mixture-of-Experts (LoRA-MoE) adapters in the LLM backbone, where skill-query tokens and routing biases guide low-rank expert specialization, and converts a predicted affordance heatmap into a patch-level trajectory-affordance spatial prior for the action head. On the CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D long-horizon multi-skill cross-scene generalization setting, MAST-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching an Avg. Len of 4.65 over five-subtask evaluation sequences. Real-robot multi-skill sequence experiments further validate its deployability under real perception and control noise.
2610.32312.tldr_en: MAST-VLA introduces skill-conditioned LoRA Mixture-of-Experts (LoRA-MoE) adapters in the LLM backbone, where skill-query tokens and routing biases guide low-rank expert specialization, and converts a predicted affordance heatmap into a patch-level trajectory-affordance spatial prior for the action head.

llm.title_ja: MAST-VLA: マルチスキルロボットマニピュレーションのための軌道アフォーダンス事前分布を用いたスキル条件付き適応
llm.tldr_ja: MAST-VLAは、LLMバックボーンにスキル条件付きLoRA Mixture-of-Expertsアダプターを導入し、予測されたアフォーダンスヒートマップをパッチレベルの軌道アフォーダンス空間事前分布に変換するデュアル条件付けフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 現在のマルチスキルVLAポリシーは、どのプリミティブスキルを実行すべきか、そしてオブジェクトにどこでどのように接触して動かすべきかという命令の2つの側面のモデル化が不十分である。
llm.method: LLMバックボーンにスキル条件付きLoRA Mixture-of-Experts（LoRA-MoE）アダプターを導入し、予測されたアフォーダンスヒートマップをアクションヘッドのための空間事前分布に変換する「MAST-VLA」を提案する。
llm.result: CALVIN ABC→Dの長期マルチスキルクロスシーン汎化設定において、MAST-VLAは最先端のパフォーマンスを達成し、実ロボット実験により実世界での展開可能性が検証された。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.32295.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning
2610.32295.abstract: Lifelong LLM agents must learn from an expanding history of interactions while making each decision within a bounded context window. Memory makes past experience available, but the agent may still need to infer how to solve each new task from the retrieved records. Skills provide reusable procedures, yet may omit the task-specific facts needed to apply them. Because retrieved memory and skills shape the agent's behavior, they also influence the experience available for future learning. We introduce MemCryst, a framework for lifelong context adaptation through bidirectional learning of memory and skills with a frozen language model. Recurring episodes stored in memory support skill creation and revision, and the interactions guided by those skills supply new memory for subsequent learning. Facts retrieved from memory and learned skills jointly form the agent's context, while task outcomes adjust the future retrieval influence of the records actually served without rewriting their content. Across ten settings spanning embodied control, long-document reading, conversation, mathematics, and code, MemCryst leads seven reported comparisons. On ALFWorld, joint serving achieves 63.17% success, compared with 59.83% for memory-only and 50.50% for skill-only serving. Code is available at https://github.com/tianyi0216/Memcryst.git
2610.32295.comment: 42 pages, including references and appendices. 18 figures, 13 tables
2610.32295.tldr_en: This work introduces MemCryst, a framework for lifelong context adaptation through bidirectional learning of memory and skills with a frozen language model that leads seven reported comparisons.

llm.title_ja: 双方向の記憶・スキル学習を通じた生涯コンテキスト適応
llm.tldr_ja: MemCrystは、凍結された言語モデルを用いた記憶とスキルの双方向学習を通じて生涯コンテキスト適応を行うフレームワークであり、複数の比較対象を上回る性能を示した。
llm.problem: 生涯LLMエージェントは限られたコンテキストウィンドウ内で決定を下しながら拡大するインタラクション履歴から学習する必要があるが、記憶とスキルの管理と活用が課題となっている。
llm.method: 記憶とスキルの双方向学習を通じて生涯コンテキスト適応を行うフレームワーク「MemCryst」を導入する。記憶されたエピソードがスキル作成を支援し、スキルが新しい記憶を提供する。
llm.result: embodied controlや長文書読解など10の設定において、MemCrystは報告された7つの比較対象を上回り、ALFWorldでは63.17%の成功率を達成した。

2610.32277.title: Delay Randomization Widens the Delay Margin of Learned Humanoid Motion Trackers
2610.32277.abstract: Learned humanoid controllers are usually trained in one simulator and then checked in a second one before they go near hardware. We ask what that check says about command delay. We train motion-tracking policies for a 24-joint humanoid on five motions taken from monocular video and test them in an independent CPU MuJoCo harness, which we first verify against the training model. Every policy completes its motion in at least 26 of 30 episodes under the training randomization. With 40 ms of constant command delay, however, survival drops to 15% on average (0% - 45%), and the delay margin is only 20 - 30 ms. Randomizing the delay during training (0 - 50 ms) lifts survival at 40 ms to 95% on average (75% - 100%) and moves the margin to 50 - 70 ms. A control arm trained for the same number of extra iterations without delay does not improve, so the gain comes from the randomization itself. This holds for all five motions with three training seeds each, and a policy trained in PhysX behaves the same way. The price is slightly looser tracking (0.02 - 0.06 rad on four motions) and, for the most dynamic motion, less robustness to other perturbations. We also show that the first sim-to-sim gap we saw came from the harness, a missing floor and a wrong timestep, and not from the physics engines. The 0 - 20 ms delay ranges common in locomotion training lie inside the margin an unrandomized tracker already has. The benefit comes from randomizing beyond it, so the range should be set from the robot's measured latency, and delay margin belongs next to other sim-to-sim metrics.
2610.32277.tldr_en: The first sim-to-sim gap the authors saw came from the harness, a missing floor and a wrong timestep, and not from the physics engines, and it is shown that the first sim-to-sim gap belongs next to other sim-to-sim metrics.

llm.title_ja: 遅延ランダム化が学習済みヒューマノイド動作トラッカーの遅延マージンを拡大する
llm.tldr_ja: 学習済みヒューマノイドコントローラーの遅延マージンを調査し、トレーニング中に遅延をランダム化することで40ms遅延時の生存率が大幅に向上することを示した。
llm.problem: 学習済みヒューマノイドコントローラーはシミュレータで訓練されてハードウェアに展開されるが、コマンド遅延に対するロバスト性の評価と向上が必要である。
llm.method: 24関節のヒューマノイド向け動作追従ポリシーをトレーニングし、トレーニング中に0〜50msの遅延をランダム化する手法を検証した。
llm.result: トレーニング中の遅延ランダム化により、40ms遅延時の生存率が平均15%から95%に向上し、遅延マージンが50〜70msに拡大することが示された。
llm.limitation: わずかな追跡精度の低下（0.02〜0.06 rad）や、最も動的な動作に対する他の外乱に対するロバスト性の低下という代償がある。

2610.32271.title: From Tabletop to Walking Bot: Deploying a VLA Model on a Legged Manipulator Robot
2610.32271.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are typically pretrained on broad, diverse datasets and subsequently fine-tuned on a comparatively small dataset tailored to a specific target robot. Such adaptation recipe is now widely established, achieving its most mature results on fixed-base arms due to their static base dynamics and consistent reference frame. Mounting the same arm on a quadruped extends the workspace to the entire floor, but fundamentally changes the embodiment: rather than controlling the arm in isolation, the policy must jointly coordinate base navigation, body posture, and end-effector motion. In this work, we study the practical demands of this embodiment change across data collection, model adaptation, and inference design to achieve closed-loop loco-manipulation on a Unitree Go2 with an AgileX Piper arm. We report the choices that made this real-robot deployment feasible, namely model variant, action horizon, and demonstration conventions, together with a study tailored to a pick-and-place task, separating data coverage from model capacity. We show that expanding demonstration coverage reduces held-out end-effector error by 30%, and incorporating secondary skills (such as pushing rather than grasping) introduces new behavioral modes without degrading baseline performance. Finally, closed-loop real-world experiments show how dataset composition shapes success and failure, validating the pipeline for more complex loco-manipulation.
2610.32271.tldr_en: This work studies the practical demands of this embodiment change across data collection, model adaptation, and inference design to achieve closed-loop loco-manipulation on a Unitree Go2 with an AgileX Piper arm, and reports the choices that made this real-robot deployment feasible.

llm.title_ja: 卓上から歩行ロボットへ: 脚式マニピュレータロボットへのVLAモデルの展開
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究では、Unitree Go2とAgileX Piperアームを搭載した脚式マニピュレータにおいて、データ収集、モデル適応、推論設計にわたる実践的な要求事項を調査し、実ロボットでのクローズドループなロコ・マニピュレーションを実現した。
llm.problem: 固定ベースアーム用に最適化されたVLAモデルを四足歩行ロボットに搭載する場合、ベースのナビゲーション、姿勢、エンドエフェクタの動きを協調させる必要があり、身体性の変化に伴う課題が生じる。
llm.method: モデルバリアント、アクションホライゾン、デモンストレーションの規約など、実ロボット展開を可能にする選択事項を調査し、ピック＆プレースタスクを通じてデータカバレッジとモデル容量を分離して評価する。
llm.result: デモンストレーションのカバレッジ拡大により保持されたエンドエフェクタ誤差が30%削減され、閉ループ実世界実験により複雑なロコ・マニピュレーションのためのパイプラインが検証された。
keywords_ja: ロコ・マニピュレーション

2610.32259.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons
2610.32259.abstract: Protection levels (PLs) bound position errors under specified fault hypotheses and risk budgets, but advanced receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) is formulated for snapshot GNSS estimation rather than the correlated posterior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization (FGO). This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior. Because current-epoch pseudorange factors enter only the current-state block of the fixed-lag information matrix, the fault-excluded position covariance, solution separation, and nominal-bias propagation follow exactly from the linearized current-state marginal, which re-tains correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states and with historical information. Woodbury updates with selected-output evaluation compute these quantities for fault-free, single-satellite, constellation-wide, and second-order hypotheses with-out repeated full-state inversion or graph reoptimization. Surrounding monitoring layers screen measurements, handle post-fit outliers, and determine PL validity and availability. In two road experiments, both nominal sequences achieve 100% horizontal and vertical empirical bounding over PL-valid epochs, with a maximum error-to-PL ratio of 0.96. Normalized errors show that the posterior covariance alone does not capture slowly varying ranging biases: a covariance-only bound computed from the same posteriors retains no resolvable margin, and strong temporal correlation limits the empirical evidence to consistency checks rather than validation of the integrity budget. On identical Experiment A posteriors, the proposed method reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% relative to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity decisions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.
2610.32259.tldr_en: The proposed ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% relative to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity decisions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.

llm.title_ja: 都市キャニオンにおける強結合GNSS/IMU統合のための増分平滑化ベースARAIM保護レベル
llm.tldr_ja: FGO事後分布に基づくARAIM解分離と保護レベル計算を定式化し、直接的な全状態 inversion と比較して障害仮説評価とPL求解時間を65.2%削減することを示した。
llm.problem: 高度受信機自律完全性モニタリング（ARAIM）は、強結合GNSS/IMU因子グラフ最適化（FGO）の相関する事後分布ではなく、スナップショットGNSS推定用に定式化されている。
llm.method: FGO事後分布におけるARAIM解分離と保護レベル（PL）計算を定式化し、Woodbury更新を用いて複数仮説の量を繰り返し全状態 inversion なしで計算する。
llm.result: 2つの道路実験において、提案手法は直接的な全状態 inversion と比較して障害仮説評価とPL求解時間を65.2%削減し、100%の水平および垂直的実証的境界付けを達成した。
llm.limitation: 事後共分散単体では緩やかに変動する測距バイアスを捉えられないことや、強い時間的相関により実証的証拠が整合性チェックに限定されるという限界がある。

2610.32225.title: RoboCode: Learning Reusable Action Primitives for Robot Manipulation
2610.32225.abstract: Recent robot manipulation policies commonly predict continuous action chunks directly from observations, without explicitly modeling reusable structure in the action space. However, manipulation demonstrations often contain recurring short-horizon motion patterns that are shared across tasks. We introduce \textsc{RoboCode}, which learns these patterns through a shared soft-gated primitive action interface. Rather than assigning each action chunk to a single discrete code, \textsc{RoboCode} represents it as a soft composition of multiple learned primitives, providing a flexible intermediate representation of short-horizon actions. The primitive interface is learned from action chunks pooled across multiple tasks and then frozen while task-specific state encoders are trained to map current state inputs into the shared latent space. Experiments on five ManiSkill manipulation tasks address three questions. First, the learned primitive interface reconstructs action chunks with an average reconstruction MSE of 0.0187. Second, analysis of code activations reveals structured code reuse across tasks. Third, \textsc{RoboCode} achieves the highest or tied closed-loop success rate on all evaluated tasks, with an average success rate of 75.6%, compared with 68.8% for ACT and 41.6% for the larger Diffusion Policy baseline. These results suggest that soft-gated primitive codebooks provide an effective and interpretable intermediate action representation for robot manipulation.
2610.32225.tldr_en: Results suggest that soft-gated primitive codebooks provide an effective and interpretable intermediate action representation for robot manipulation, and suggest that structured code reuse across tasks is revealed.

llm.title_ja: RoboCode: ロボットマニピュレーションのための再利用可能な行動プリミティブの学習
llm.tldr_ja: RoboCodeは、共有されたソフトゲート・プリミティブ行動インターフェースを介して行動パターンを学習し、複数のマニピュレーションタスクにおいてACTや拡散ポリシーを上回る平均75.6%の成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーションポリシーは連続的なアクションチャンクを直接予測することが多いが、行動空間における再利用可能な構造を明示的にモデル化していない。
llm.method: 複数のタスク間でプールされたアクションチャンクから学習される共有のソフトゲート・プリミティブ行動インターフェース「RoboCode」を導入し、タスク固有の状態エンコーダーを訓練する。
llm.result: 5つのManiSkillタスクにおいて、RoboCodeは平均75.6%の成功率を達成し、ACT（68.8%）や大規模なDiffusion Policy（41.6%）を上回る閉ループ成功率を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.32208.title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
2610.32208.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful general-purpose robot policies, but their successes and failures remain difficult to diagnose and understand. In this work, we show that sparse autoencoder (SAE) representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can be used to predict task failure before the robot reaches an unrecoverable state. Moreover, to provide insights into what common behaviors may contribute to these outcomes, we identify individual SAE features whose strong activations are associated with specific stages of success or failure, and uncover recurring behavioral patterns by localizing temporal intervals where these features exhibit significant activation changes. We further develop a VLM-based interpretation pipeline to generate behavioral descriptions of these patterns and validate their correspondence to feature activations on held-out intervals.
2610.32208.comment: 12 pages (4 main pages + 8 pages appendix), 4 figures. Accepted at the Science of Physical AI Safety Workshop at the 2026 Conference on Robotic Learning (CoRL 2026, non-archival)
2610.32208.tldr_en: It is shown that sparse autoencoder representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can be used to predict task failure before the robot reaches an unrecoverable state.

llm.title_ja: VLAは失敗することを予知できるか？物理AIシステムにおける解釈可能な成功および失敗パターン
llm.tldr_ja: OpenVLAの活性化のスパースオートエンコーダー（SAE）表現が結果予測情報を含み、ロボットが回復不可能な状態に達する前にタスクの失敗を予測するために使用できることを示した。
llm.problem: 視覚言語モデル（VLA）は汎用ロボットポリシーとして強力であるが、その成功と失敗の診断や理解が困難である。
llm.method: OpenVLAの活性化のスパースオートエンコーダー（SAE）表現を用いて結果予測情報を抽出し、特定の成功・失敗ステージに関連するSAE特徴を特定してVLMベースの解釈パイプラインを開発する。
llm.result: SAE表現を利用して、ロボットが回復不可能な状態に陥る前にタスクの失敗を予測できること、および反復的な行動パターンをローカライズできることが示された。
keywords_ja: スパースオートエンコーダー

2610.32188.title: RAISE-Vision: An Automated Contact Angle Measurement Platform for Contact Lens Wettability Characterization
2610.32188.abstract: Contact angle (CA) is a common parameter measured in the development of novel contact lens materials and surface coating technologies. Existing literature on in vitro CA of contact lenses via the sessile drop method is hindered in repeatability, reliability, and comparability due to inter-laboratory and inter-operator protocol variation. In this work, the Robotic Autonomous Imaging Surface Evaluator for vision applications (RAISE-Vision) is introduced as an automated platform for CA measurement on curved hydrogel surfaces, with specific application to in vitro contact lens wettability analysis throughout air exposure. Customized 3D printed hardware, such as lens mounts, camera holders and drying apparatuses, was designed to facilitate an automated repeated sessile drop workflow within a liquid handler. Collected images were directly fed to a custom open-source image processing script for CA determination on a curved surface that combines the elliptical fit and tangent methods to allow for variations in droplet shape. The CA of senofilcon A contact lenses measured using the RAISE-Vision platform increased from $62.6 \pm 5.5^\circ$ to $83.4 \pm 2.1^\circ$ over 10 sequential measurements in air and was able to replicate results obtained using an analogous manual protocol ($p = 0.470$). The custom image processing script was also separately demonstrated to generate comparable results to a commercially available CA determination software ($p = 0.343$). Aside from minimizing operator variability for CA measurement, RAISE-Vision provides a platform for standardized in vitro contact lens wettability analysis and understanding of surface wetting behaviour during air exposure.

llm.title_ja: RAISE-Vision: コンタクトレンズの濡れ性特性評価のための自動接触角測定プラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: RAISE-Visionは、曲線状のハイドロゲル表面における接触角測定のための自動プラットフォームとして導入され、空気曝露中のコンタクトレンズのin vitro濡れ性解析を実現した。
llm.problem: sessile drop法によるコンタクトレンズのin vitro接触角測定に関する既存の文献は、実験室間やオペレーター間のプロトコルの違いにより、再現性、信頼性、比較可能性が妨げられている。
llm.method: 液体ハンドラー内での自動反復sessile dropワークフローを容易にするため、レンズマウント、カメラホルダー、乾燥装置などのカスタマイズされた3Dプリントハードウェアとカスタム画像処理スクリプトを組み合わせた「RAISE-Vision」プラットフォームを導入する。
llm.result: senofilcon Aコンタクトレンズの接触角が10回の連続測定で増加することを測定し、手動プロトコルや市販ソフトウェアと同等の結果を再現できることが示された。
keywords_ja: 自動プラットフォーム

2610.32182.title: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control
2610.32182.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are widely deployed, yet the internal mechanisms behind their safety behavior remain poorly understood. We present a lightweight inference-time framework for localizing and manipulating safety-sensitive representations in frozen VLMs, without retraining or modifying parameters. On Qwen3-VL-4B, layer-wise activation divergence analysis reveals non-uniform safety geometry across depth. Causal interventions show that early vision layers support strong bidirectional refusal control through activation steering along a learned safety direction, with unsafe rejection spanning 6%-96%, whereas later layers respond more to activation magnitude scaling and exhibit a substantial safety-selectivity trade-off. Deeper layers remain well separated along the safety direction yet are largely insensitive to steering, distinguishing representational separability from causal controllability. InternVL2.5-4B shows qualitatively similar depth-dependent activation geometry despite differences in layer location and magnitude. Our results expose a white-box, representation-level refusal-bypass attack surface in VLM vision encoders and motivate inference-time stabilization of safety-sensitive representations.
2610.32182.tldr_en: This work presents a lightweight inference-time framework for localizing and manipulating safety-sensitive representations in frozen VLMs, without retraining or modifying parameters, and exposes a white-box, representation-level refusal-bypass attack surface in VLM vision encoders to motivate inference-time stabilization of safety-sensitive representations.

llm.title_ja: 視覚言語モデルにおける深さ依存の安全性ジオメトリ: 層ごとの局所化と双方向拒否制御
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究では、再訓練やパラメータ変更を行わずに凍結されたVLM内の安全性に敏感な表現を局所化・操作するための軽量な推論時フレームワークを提案し、VLM視覚エンコーダーにおける拒否バイパス攻撃表面を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 視覚言語モデル（VLM）は広く配備されているが、その安全性の背景にある内部メカニズムはいまだに解明されていない。
llm.method: Qwen3-VL-4Bなどの凍結されたVLMにおいて、層ごとの活性化ダイバージェンス分析を用いて安全性ジオメトリを調査し、学習された安全方向に沿った活性化ステアリングによる軽量な推論時フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 初期の視覚層が強力な双方向拒否制御をサポートし、深層では表現の分離可能性と因果的制御可能性の間に違いがあることが示され、VLM視覚エンコーダーの脆弱性が露わになった。
keywords_ja: 推論時フレームワーク

2610.32143.title: Geometry-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Close-Fitting Wearable Insertion
2610.32143.abstract: Robot-assisted dressing is particularly challenging due to narrow openings and articulated body parts. Even small errors in the relative pose between the body part and garment opening can cause snagging, missed insertion, or incomplete dressing. To address these challenges, we formulate dressing as a geometry-aware insertion problem that represents task-relevant spatial relationships between the body part and object opening, rather than relying on the full deformable-object state. Based on this formulation, we propose a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework combining a staged curriculum, which progressively guides the policy from coarse alignment to insertion and final placement, with a finger-wise insertion soft gate that provides continuous feedback on individual finger insertion progress and helps suppress premature insertion. We evaluate the framework on rigid and deformable bracelet dressing tasks through component ablations, systematic variations in the initial hand pose, and closed-loop execution of the learned policies on a real robotic system. On the post-training deformable evaluation, the full method reaches 84.7 +- 1.2% success. The insertion gate accounts for the largest gain, and adding the curriculum on top of that gate reaches the top score. On a mannequin hand the same full policy succeeds on 15/20 real-robot trials.
2610.32143.tldr_en: A Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework combining a staged curriculum, which progressively guides the policy from coarse alignment to insertion and final placement, with a finger-wise insertion soft gate that provides continuous feedback on individual finger insertion progress and helps suppress premature insertion is proposed.

llm.title_ja: 密着型ウェアラブル挿入のためのジオメトリ認識強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 粗いアライメントから最終配置へポリシーを導く段階的カリキュラムと指ごとの挿入ソフトゲートを組み合わせた強化学習フレームワークを提案し、変形可能なブレスレット装着タスクで高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: ロボット支援による衣服の着用は、狭い開口部や関節のある身体部分のため非常に困難であり、相対姿勢の小さな誤差が引っかかりや挿入失敗を引き起こす。
llm.method: 身体部分とオブジェクト開口部のタスク関連の空間関係を表現するジオメトリ認識挿入問題として定式化し、段階的カリキュラムと指ごとの挿入ソフトゲートを組み合わせた強化学習（RL）フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 変形可能なブレスレット装着タスクの評価において、提案手法全体で84.7±1.2%の成功率を達成し、マネキンハンドを用いた実ロボット実験でも15/20の試行に成功した。

2610.32130.title: TravSUITE: Traversability via Self-Supervised, Uncertainty-Aware IRL and Terrain Estimation
2610.32130.abstract: Traversability analysis in off-road settings remains a fundamental challenge for mobile robots. Key difficulties include constructing an accurate and expressive local map from multimodal sensor data, and using the map to design traversability rules that yield desirable navigation behavior. Importantly, this system must be resilient to the limited sensing regime brought about by complex environments and high speeds. In this paper, we present TravSUITE, a traversability system suitable for high-speed navigation in off-road environments. TravSUITE consists of two major components: 1) an efficient voxel mapper that leverages visual foundation models (VFMs) to build a rich geometric-semantic local map from streams of on-board sensor data, and 2) a unified neural network that jointly predicts traversability-relevant quantities in bird's eye view (BEV), including geometry, semantics, speed and cost. Our training strategy is entirely annotation-free and self-supervised, leveraging tasks such as map inpainting and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) to learn both map representations and traversability. We perform a thorough ablation study and comparison to state-of-the-art approaches, and the results indicate that cost learning and auxiliary inpainting each contribute significantly to planning quality, and their combination is critical for achieving state-of-the-art performance in off-road path planning. We also design a simple risk adaptation mechanism to leverage our method's uncertainty estimates at deploy-time, and demonstrate that a combination of inpainting and risk estimation can result in 80% fewer navigation errors and 5% faster autonomous traversal speeds in real-world hardware experiments.
2610.32130.journal_ref: S. Triest, A. Shaban, D. Fan, W. Wang, and S. Scherer, "TravSUITE: Traversability via Self-Supervised, Uncertainty-Aware IRL and Terrain Estimation," in Proceedings of Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS), 2026
2610.32130.tldr_en: A thorough ablation study and comparison to state-of-the-art approaches are performed, and the results indicate that cost learning and auxiliary inpainting each contribute significantly to planning quality, and their combination is critical for achieving state-of-the-art performance in off-road path planning.

llm.title_ja: TravSUITE: 自己教師あり・不確実性認識型IRLと地形推定による走行可能性分析
llm.tldr_ja: TravSUITEは、視覚基盤モデルを活用した効率的なボクセルマッパーと、鳥瞰図上で走行可能性関連量を共同予測する統一ニューラルネットワークからなり、オフロードのパスプランニングで最先端の性能を実現する。
llm.problem: オフロード環境における走行可能性分析は、マルチモーダルセンサーデータから正確で表現力豊かなローカルマップを構築し、それを用いて望ましいナビゲーション動作を設計することが困難である。
llm.method: 視覚基盤モデルを活用して幾何学的・意味的ローカルマップを構築する効率的なボクセルマッパーと、マップ内省や逆強化学習（IRL）を用いて走行可能性を学習する統一ニューラルネットワーク「TravSUITE」を提案する。
llm.result: 実世界の実機実験において、マップ内省とリスク推定の組み合わせにより、ナビゲーションエラーを80%削減し、自動走行速度を5%向上させることが実証された。
keywords_ja: オフロードナビゲーション

2610.32102.title: Coupling Execution Horizon and Sampling Depth in Flow-Matching VLA Policies
2610.32102.abstract: Flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate expressive continuous trajectories for robotic manipulation, yet balancing real-time responsiveness with execution stability remains a persistent challenge. Standard deployment workflows typically treat numerical solver depth and execution horizon as decoupled choices. The horizon amortizes inference latency, while solver depth is kept high to preserve integration fidelity. In this paper, we reveal a fundamental compute-execution coupling in flow-matching VLAs governed by a systematic sign reversal. While coarse numerical integration degrades precision under rapid replanning, it markedly improves task performance under extended open-loop commitment. Geometrically, numerical truncation contracts lateral action dispersion around an invariant trajectory centroid, serving as an implicit regularizer that suppresses compounding open-loop drift. Across LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world Franka manipulation on representative VLA backbones including $π_0$, $π_{0.5}$, and GR00T, exploiting this joint coupling consistently achieves superior task success while drastically lowering inference latency, entirely training-free and without architectural modifications. These findings establish numerical sampling depth as an operational variance regulator, shifting its role from a static precision budget to an active deployment knob in robot learning. Project page: https://jiabingyang01.github.io/Horizon-Depth-VLA/
2610.32102.tldr_en: Numerical sampling depth is established as an operational variance regulator in flow-matching VLA models, shifting its role from a static precision budget to an active deployment knob in robot learning.

llm.title_ja: フローマッチングVLAポリシーにおける実行ホライゾンとサンプリング深度の結合
llm.tldr_ja: 数値的サンプリング深度を静的な精度予算からロボット学習におけるアクティブなデプロイメントノブへと移行させ、タスク成功率を向上させつつ推論レイテンシを大幅に削減する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: フローマッチング視覚言語モデル（VLA）は連続的な軌道を生成するが、リアルタイムの応答性と実行の安定性のバランスを取ることが課題である。
llm.method: 数値積分の粗さがオープンループコミットメント下でタスク性能を向上させる符号反転メカニズムを解明し、推論レイテンシを削減しつつタスク成功率を高める手法を検証する。
llm.result: LIBERO、RoboTwin 2.0、および実世界のFrankaマニピュレーションを用いた実験により、この結合を活用することでタスク成功率が向上し、推論レイテンシが大幅に削減されることが示された。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.32094.title: TTT in VLA Models: Exploring Training with Human Demonstrations
2610.32094.abstract: Long-horizon robot tasks require retaining and using past information. We integrate Test-Time Training (TTT), which stores context in fast weights, into InternVLA-A1 and Pi0.5 to study action generation conditioned on human demonstrations through training on paired demonstrations and robot trajectories. We implement memory transfer between the two phases and truncated backpropagation, and examine training objectives, gradient coverage, and contrastive regularization across video, short-video, and single-frame cue tasks. In our experiments, adding TTT and training on paired data at the current scale did not lead to consistent target selection based on demonstrations. Under the tested settings, shorter sequences, full trajectory gradient connectivity, and contrastive regularization did not clearly improve responsiveness to demonstrations. When demonstrations were reduced to single-frame cues, real-robot execution still showed a preference for cups at fixed positions. We document the implementation, training configurations, and observations to support further inspection and replication.
2610.32094.comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, a techreport form standard-robots company
2610.32094.tldr_en: In these experiments, adding TTT and training on paired data at the current scale did not lead to consistent target selection based on demonstrations, and under the tested settings, shorter sequences, full trajectory gradient connectivity, and contrastive regularization did not clearly improve responsiveness to demonstrations.

2610.32093.title: DiscoDemo: Discovering Efficient and Diverse Robot Demonstrations for Imitation Learning
2610.32093.abstract: Behavior cloning for robotic manipulation is highly sensitive to the coverage of its training data, yet collecting diverse successful demonstrations remains costly. We study reinforcement learning (RL) not as a deployable controller, but as a data generator for downstream visuomotor imitation learning. Our key premise is that multiple successful solution modes cover a broader range of successful trajectories than repeatedly collecting a single narrow solution. We introduce DiscoDemo, which trains a privileged latent-conditioned RL generator with a parallel reverse curriculum and a success-gated diversity objective to discover diverse solutions while preserving task success. The trained generator produces multiple successful closed-loop behaviors, which are safety-filtered and exported as a static dataset for downstream imitation learning. Across four manipulation tasks, DiscoDemo produces broader successful-state coverage and improves downstream visuomotor policies in both simulation and the real world. Averaged across tasks, downstream success increases to 62% from 40% for the strongest baseline in simulation, and to 78% from 39% on the real robot, respectively. These results suggest that successful solution diversity improves imitation learning for a pretrained flow-matching VLA and remains complementary to corrective data collection. Project page: https://davian-robotics.github.io/DiscoDemo
2610.32093.tldr_en: DiscoDemo is introduced, which trains a privileged latent-conditioned RL generator with a parallel reverse curriculum and a success-gated diversity objective to discover diverse solutions while preserving task success and suggests that successful solution diversity improves imitation learning for a pretrained flow-matching VLA and remains complementary to corrective data collection.
2610.32093.hf_summary_en: DiscoDemo uses reinforcement learning to generate diverse successful robot manipulation trajectories for training more robust visuomotor imitation policies.

llm.title_ja: DiscoDemo: 模倣学習のための効率的で多様なロボットデモンストレーションの発見
llm.tldr_ja: DiscoDemoは、並行リバースカリキュラムと成功ゲート付き多様性目的を持つ特権付き潜在条件付きRLジェネレーターを訓練し、タスクの成功を維持しながら多様な解決策を発見することで下流の模倣学習を改善する。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーションのための行動クローンは訓練データのカバレッジに敏感であるが、多様で成功したデモンストレーションの収集には多大なコストがかかる。
llm.method: 並行リバースカリキュラムと成功ゲート付き多様性目的を持つ特権付き潜在条件付きRLジェネレーターを訓練し、安全フィルタリングを経て静的データセットとして下流の模倣学習にエクスポートする「DiscoDemo」を導入する。
llm.result: 4つのマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、シミュレーションでは成功率が40%から62%に、実ロボットでは39%から78%に向上し、解決策の多様性が事前学習済みフローマッチングVLAの模倣学習を改善することが示された。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーション
ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.32060.title: Understanding Communication Failures in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
2610.32060.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems aim to improve reasoning through debate, evidence sharing, and mutual correction, but interaction can also introduce failures that final accuracy alone cannot explain. Agents may converge too early, ignore dissent, suppress correct minority answers, or preserve a wrong framing across rounds. We present a corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures, built from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across medical QA, coding, finance, multi-hop reasoning, ethics, and embodied text tasks. Using this taxonomy, we analyze failure distributions across datasets and system designs, round-level error dynamics, recovery hardness, majority transitions, minority-signal suppression, and self-reported confidence. We find that failures are dominated by recovery/correction and consensus/decision problems rather than isolated first-round mistakes, with many emerging after agents first observe peer responses. Based on these findings, we recommend stronger disagreement handling, evidence verification, minority-signal preservation, and recovery checks before finalization.
2610.32060.tldr_en: A corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures, built from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across medical QA, coding, finance, multi-hop reasoning, ethics, and embodied text tasks, finds that failures are dominated by recovery/correction and consensus/decision problems rather than isolated first-round mistakes.

llm.title_ja: マルチエージェントLLMシステムにおける通信障害の理解
llm.tldr_ja: 多様なタスクにわたる3,211件の失敗したマルチラウンド軌跡から構築されたコーパスベースの通信障害の分類法を示し、障害の大部分が修復や合意形成の問題に起因することを明らかにする。
llm.problem: マルチエージェントLLMシステムは推論を改善するが、対話によって最終的な精度だけでは説明できない障害が引き起こされる点。
llm.method: 医療QA、コーディング、金融など多様なタスクの失敗したマルチラウンド軌跡を分析し、コーパスベースの障害分類法を構築する。
llm.result: 初期の単発の過ちよりも、エージェントが他者の応答を観測した後に発生する修復・訂正および合意・決定の問題が失敗の大部分を占めることを発見した。

2610.32059.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2610.32059.abstract: Diffusion-based image generation models produce high-quality images but may generate harmful or policy-violating content, motivating machine unlearning (MU) to selectively remove target concepts while preserving general capabilities. However, existing MU approaches often struggle with the distributed and entangled nature of concept representations, leading to inefficient optimization and imprecise edits when applied through large-scale fine-tuning over full diffusion trajectories. To bridge this gap, we propose Concept Acupuncturist (ConceptACP), a novel MU framework that integrates interpretability-guided analysis with inference-free fine-tuning for efficient and precise concept removal. By establishing mappings between semantic concepts and cross-attention blocks in the U-Net denoiser and localizing the most concept-relevant block for targeted optimization, ConceptACP avoids full diffusion trajectory optimization, thereby improving fine-tuning efficiency. To mitigate concept entanglement, we propose a feature-level correction mechanism based on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), where SAE-derived sparse, semantically meaningful feature activations are manipulated to construct targeted correction signals, which are then projected back to the output space of the corresponding block and used as supervision for precise concept removal. Consequently, ConceptACP eliminates the need for external inference-time modules while achieving efficient and fine-grained unlearning. Instantiated on SDXL-Turbo, ConceptACP improves the forgetting success rate by 36.34 percentage points in the standard one-step generation setting on average over the best-performing baseline, while preserving image quality and prompt fidelity, and generalizes effectively across other Stable Diffusion backbones. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eran-Xia/ConceptACP.
2610.32059.tldr_en: This work proposes Concept Acupuncturist (ConceptACP), a novel MU framework that integrates interpretability-guided analysis with inference-free fine-tuning for efficient and precise concept removal, and eliminates the need for external inference-time modules while achieving efficient and fine-grained unlearning.

llm.title_ja: Concept Acupuncturist：スパースオートエンコーダを用いた拡散モデルのための効率的かつ精密な概念消去法
llm.tldr_ja: 解釈可能性に基づく分析と推論不要のファインチューニングを統合した新しいマシンアンレッスンフレームワーク「ConceptACP」を提案し、効率的かつ精密な概念削除を実現する。
llm.problem: 既存のマシンアンレッスン手法は概念表現の分散・絡み合いに苦しみ、非効率な最適化と不正確な編集につながる点。
llm.method: U-Netデノイザーのクロスアテンションブロックとのマッピングを確立し、スパースオートエンコーダ（SAE）に基づく特徴レベルの修正メカニズムを利用して対象を修正する。
llm.result: SDXL-Turboにおいて、画像品質やプロンプトの忠実度を維持しながら、標準的な生成設定での忘却成功率を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: スパースオートエンコーダ

2610.32034.title: PPO vs. SAC: A Comparative Study for Cooperative Motion Control of Dual-Arm Space Robots
2610.32034.abstract: The growing population of orbital debris has intensified interest in active debris removal and on-orbit servicing, for which dual-arm space manipulators offer improved grasping stability and load distribution relative to single-arm systems. However, coordinating two manipulators under inter-arm collision avoidance, orientation alignment, and sensing uncertainty remains challenging. This paper develops a coordinated reinforcement learning framework for cooperative motion planning of a dual-arm space manipulator in a target-reaching task with inter-arm collision-avoidance constraints. A centralized state representation combines joint-space, end-effector, and target-relative information, while a multi-objective reward function promotes target-reaching accuracy, orientation alignment, motion smoothness, synchronized task completion, and collision avoidance. Within this framework, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) are compared as representative on-policy and off-policy algorithms, and the learned policies are further evaluated for generalization to previously unseen target configurations. Across five random seeds, SAC substantially outperforms PPO within the considered fixed-base simulation scenarios: it reaches an 80% success threshold in every seed (median 1.6M environment steps) whereas PPO does not reach it within a 4M-step budget, and it attains a higher mean success rate (78.6% versus 7.4%) with lower position and orientation errors and tighter bimanual synchronization. Both algorithms degrade on unseen boundary targets, but SAC retains most of its performance while PPO's collapses. The results also expose a failure mode of PPO: under the two-phase shaped reward, it tends to converge to a reward-loitering local optimum rather than committing to the precision task. This behavior highlights the sensitivity of on-policy learning to reward shaping.
2610.32034.comment: Presented at the 2026 AAS/AIAA Astrodynamics Specialist Conference, Whistler, British Columbia, Canada, July 26-30, 2026. Paper AAS 26-740

2610.32022.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
2610.32022.abstract: Intent recognition in human-robot interaction requires agents to resolve ambiguous natural language instructions by inferring the speaker's underlying goals. Research has increasingly focused on two notable paradigms for addressing this task: structured symbolic reasoning and multimodal input enrichment. However, it remains unclear whether enrichment-based methods provide benefit in settings where the ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing observable scene information. In this paper, we present a comparative and diagnostic study benchmarking FISER - a framework utilizing structured social and embodied reasoning - against CEMIR (Context-Enriched Multimodal Intent Recognition), a method that performs multimodal enrichment by synthesizing narratives and photorealistic images from textual prompts. By evaluating both approaches across four Large Language Models (LLMs), ranging from Qwen2.5-Omni-3B to GPT-5, on the HandMeThat v2 benchmark, we analyze their capability to resolve pragmatic ambiguities. Our statistical analysis, employing multiple-comparison correction, reveals no statistically significant difference in performance between FISER and CEMIR across any model or difficulty level. This pattern holds across all sixteen model-by-difficulty comparisons, as well as in a targeted ablation isolating CEMIR's narrative and visual components. Instead, performance is primarily associated with backbone capability and the inherent difficulty of the ambiguity. These findings suggest a boundary condition for text-derived multimodal enrichment: when the relevant task constraints are already available in the textual instruction, synthetic multimodal augmentation may not provide measurable benefit over structured reasoning on the same text.
2610.32022.tldr_en: A boundary condition for text-derived multimodal enrichment is suggested: when the relevant task constraints are already available in the textual instruction, synthetic multimodal augmentation may not provide measurable benefit over structured reasoning on the same text.

2610.31979.title: Spectra: Multi-Scale Implicit Decomposition for Deepfake Detection
2610.31979.abstract: Deepfakes increasingly undermine trust in digital media, yet existing detectors often struggle to generalize across unseen manipulation techniques, compression levels, and dataset shifts. Most approaches rely on RGB appearance, frequency-domain artifacts, or their combination, learning cues present in the final synthesized image. While effective in-distribution, such cues are frequently generator-specific and can diminish as synthesis models evolve. We argue that a complementary perspective can be obtained through implicit neural representations (INRs), which expose how an image is reconstructed rather than merely how it appears. By fitting an INR to an image and analyzing its internal activations, one can reveal reconstruction dynamics that are difficult to observe in the image domain alone and may capture more intrinsic differences between genuine and synthetic content. To this end, we propose Spectra, a deepfake detection framework that combines semantic visual representations with artifact-aware cues derived from INR reconstruction. Spectra extracts multi-level reconstruction heatmaps from image-specific INRs and jointly models them with semantic features through a bidirectional fusion mechanism. This enables direct interaction between image semantics and reconstruction artifacts, allowing the model to identify forgery cues that are less dependent on specific generation pipelines. Extensive experiments on multiple deepfake benchmarks demonstrate improved robustness and cross-dataset generalization, consistently outperforming detectors based solely on RGB appearance or semantic representations. Furthermore, we show that the proposed representation extends beyond deepfake detection to face presentation attack detection, highlighting its potential as a unified framework for facial attack detection.
2610.31979.tldr_en: It is argued that a complementary perspective can be obtained through implicit neural representations (INRs), which expose how an image is reconstructed rather than merely how it appears, and extended beyond deepfake detection to face presentation attack detection, highlighting its potential as a unified framework for facial attack detection.

llm.title_ja: Spectra：ディープフェイク検出のためのマルチスケール陰的分解
llm.tldr_ja: 暗黙的ニューラル表現（INR）を用いて画像の再構築ダイナミクスを分析し、セマンティック視覚表現と組み合わせたディープフェイク検出フレームワーク「Spectra」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の検出器は、RGBの外観や周波数ドメインのartifactsに依存しており、未見の操作技術やデータセットのシフトに対する汎化に苦しんでいる点。
llm.method: 画像固有のINRからマルチレベル再構築ヒートマップを抽出し、双方向融合メカニズムを通じてセマンティック特徴と共同でモデリングする。
llm.result: 複数のディープフェイクベンチマークにおいて堅牢性とクロスデータセット汎化の向上が実証され、顔プレゼンテーション攻撃検出にも拡張可能であることを示した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出
暗黙的ニューラル表現

2610.31971.title: Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation
2610.31971.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in negotiations on behalf of individuals and organizations, yet they remain vulnerable to manipulation, particularly in repeated multi-party interactions. Classical multi-agent systems address this challenge through explicit trust and reputation models, whereas existing work on LLM negotiation largely treats trust as an emergent phenomenon. We investigate whether LLM agents can form useful trust estimates from prior interactions and leverage them to improve future negotiation outcomes. We introduce a repeated, multi-party, multi-issue negotiation framework in which recurring agents participate in a sequence of negotiation games while one participant covertly attempts to prevent agreement. After each game, agents assess their counterparts and maintain pairwise trust estimates that carry over to subsequent negotiations. We compare trust-aware and trust-agnostic agents and analyze how explicit trust influences negotiation outcomes. Our results reveal a \emph{trust--agreement gap}: trust-aware agents can identify the adversary within a few games, but accurate trust estimates do not consistently translate into better agreements. Trust increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points, but only when agents are explicitly guided to use it in their decisions. Explicit trust can therefore improve repeated LLM negotiations, but its value depends critically on how trust is assessed and incorporated into agents' reasoning.
2610.31971.tldr_en: This work introduces a repeated, multi-party, multi-issue negotiation framework in which recurring agents participate in a sequence of negotiation games while one participant covertly attempts to prevent agreement.

llm.title_ja: 信用すべき相手を知るだけでは不十分：反復型マルチパーティLLM交渉における信用・合意ギャップ
llm.tldr_ja: 反復的なマルチパーティ交渉ゲームにおいて、エージェントが過去の相互作用から有用な信用推定値を形成し、それを将来の交渉成果に活用できるかを調査する。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルエージェントは交渉に参加するが、特に反復的なマルチパーティインタラクションにおいて操作に対して脆弱である点。
llm.method: 参加者が合意を隠れて妨害しようとする中、定期的なエージェントが交渉ゲームのシーケンスに参加し、ペアごとの信用推定値を維持するフレームワークを導入する。
llm.result: 信用を意思決定に明示的に使用するよう誘導された場合にのみ合意率が向上するという「信用・合意ギャップ」が存在することを明らかにした。

2610.31929.title: Robotic Budding: From Homogeneous Cells to Diverse Morphologies in Physical Self-Reproduction
2610.31929.abstract: Physical self-reproduction in modular robots remains difficult because a robot must not only move, but also collect, align, dock, and separate modules reliably in hardware. Taking inspiration from how genetically identical cells form the varied tissues of an organism, we introduce a single standardized robotic module that combines a magnetic docking interface with two actuated joints and folds from a flat, two-dimensional configuration into three-dimensional structures. Modules of this single design can be assembled into two morphologies: a three-module "trilobite" and a five-module "seal". Using a small set of discrete motion commands, a human operator steers an assembled parent robot to dock magnetically with a sequence of spare modules, which are assembled into a second, structurally identical individual that then separates from the parent. Because the parent retains all of its original modules, this is a budding-style form of physical reproduction. Here, we report preliminary hardware demonstrations of this full process on both morphologies. We discuss the current scope of the system, including its present reliance on direct human teleoperation rather than autonomous control, and outline directions toward autonomous execution of this process and repeated validation across a larger number of independent trials.

llm.title_ja: ロボットの出芽：物理的自己複製における同質細胞から多様な形態へ
llm.tldr_ja: 磁気ドッキングインターフェースと2つの駆動ジョイントを組み合わせ、平らな2次元構成から3次元構造へと折り畳まれる単一の標準化されたロボットモジュールを提案する。
llm.problem: モジュール型ロボットの物理的自己複製は、ロボットが移動するだけでなく、ハードウェア上でモジュールを収集、位置合わせ、ドッキング、分離を確実に実行する必要があるため困難である点。
llm.method: 遺伝的に同一の細胞が生物の多様な組織を形成することに着想を得て、少数の動的コマンドを使用して親ロボットがスペアモジュールをドッキングして複製を作る。
llm.result: トリロバイトとアザラシの2つの形態を用いた全プロセスの予備的なハードウェア実証を報告し、自律制御に向けた課題と方向性を概説した。
llm.limitation: 現時点では自律制御ではなく直接的な人間の遠隔操作に依存している点。
keywords_ja: モジュール型ロボット

2610.31923.title: Not an Accident: Exploiting Safety Filter Inadequacy in Humanoid Robots
2610.31923.abstract: As humanoid robots move from research laboratories toward deployment in human-centered environments such as homes, hospitals, and warehouses, safe operation around nearby people and objects becomes a fundamental requirement. Safety filters have emerged as a promising technique to address this challenge by providing mathematical guarantees that generated control actions do not result in collisions. This paper shows that these guarantees hold only when the safety parameters are configured correctly. However, correct parameter configurations are task- and environment-specific, and no general method exists to determine them across diverse deployments. As a result, safety filters shipped with humanoid robots can fail after deployment in specific scenarios. We show that attackers can exploit these failures through only normal user interactions without any additional privileges or capabilities. To demonstrate this risk, we present goal insertion attacks and develop SIREN, an automated tool that identifies vulnerable inserting goals for a given task and environment. Experimental results show that SIREN identifies attacks in all vulnerable scenarios in the SPARK dataset. Compared with a baseline approach, SIREN discovers three times as many attacks. We also show that SIREN is able to generate attacks against a real humanoid and cause it to collide while executing tasks. These results demonstrate that current safety filters introduce exploitable vulnerabilities that can cause safety violations, which reveals that existing safety mechanisms can themselves become a source of safety risk for humanoid robots.
2610.31923.tldr_en: It is demonstrated that current safety filters introduce exploitable vulnerabilities that can cause safety violations, which reveals that existing safety mechanisms can themselves become a source of safety risk for humanoid robots.

llm.title_ja: 事故ではない：ヒューマノイドロボットにおける安全性フィルターの不十分さの悪用
llm.tldr_ja: 安全性フィルターが正しく設定されていない場合に脆弱性を生じさせ、通常のユーザーインタラクションを通じてヒューマノイドロボットに衝突を引き起こす可能性があることを示す。
llm.problem: 安全性フィルターのパラメータ設定がタスクや環境固有であり、展開後に失敗して安全上のリスクを引き起こす可能性がある点。
llm.method: 目標挿入攻撃を実証し、特定のタスクと環境に対して脆弱な挿入目標を特定する自動化ツール「SIREN」を開発する。
llm.result: SPARKデータセットのすべての脆弱なシナリオにおいて攻撃を特定し、実際のヒューマノイドロボットに対して衝突を引き起こすことに成功した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.31920.title: Input Bias Correction in Gaussian Process Regression
2610.31920.abstract: In traditional Gaussian process (GP) regression, the inputs are typically assumed to be known, and uncertainty enters only through the measurements. When scalar fields are mapped using GP regression with measurements obtained from a mobile sensor, the inputs correspond to the estimated pose of the mobile sensor. The goal in this letter is to understand how a recorded GP, trained on erroneous inputs (e.g., pose estimates from dead-reckoning), can be corrected in a numerically efficient way when better estimates of the inputs become available. In the developed bias-aware GP (Ba-GP) framework, the recorded GP posterior-mean gradient is used to propagate estimated input bias and noise into mean and covariance corrections. The resulting additive covariance structure is then exploited to develop numerically efficient first-order correction algorithms. A simulation study and an indoor light-intensity mapping experiment show that Ba-GP improves predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration relative to noisy-input GP baselines, with an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost relative to full GP retraining.
2610.31920.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) (Oct, 2026)
2610.31920.tldr_en: Ba-GP improves predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration relative to noisy-input GP baselines, with an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost relative to full GP retraining.

llm.title_ja: ガウス過程回帰における入力バイアス補正
llm.tldr_ja: バイアスを考慮したガウス過程（Ba-GP）フレームワークを開発し、予測精度と不確実性較正を改善するとともに、計算コストを大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: モバイルセンサーのデッドレコニング等の誤った入力で訓練された記録済みGPを、より良い入力推定値が得られた際に効率的に修正する方法が求められている。
llm.method: 記録済みGPの事後平均勾配を利用して推定された入力バイアスとノイズを平均および共分散の補正に伝播させ、数値的に効率的な1次補正アルゴリズムを開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび屋内の光強度マッピング実験により、Ba-GPはノイズの多い入力を用いたGPベースラインと比較して、予測精度と不確実性較正を改善し、計算コストを桁違いに削減することを示した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2610.31900.title: Distributed Swarm Morphogenesis with Neural Cellular Automata
2610.31900.abstract: Swarm morphogenesis requires robots to assemble desired shapes through local interactions. We present a modular framework integrating neural cellular automata (NCA) with existing site assignment and collision-aware control. Within this framework, we introduce a decentralized attachment-site discovery mechanism. Robots already in the formation update and share local NCA states to identify new attachment sites, enabling progressive growth without a predefined list of sites during deployment. To bridge the mismatch between conventional NCA growth and gradual physical assembly, we additionally propose offline sparse-retention fine-tuning that simulates partial attachment, together with a false-positive loss that penalizes invalid site activations. Simulations demonstrate formation of diverse lattice morphologies, scaling to several hundred robots, and substantial improvements in morphology accuracy from the proposed fine-tuning. Experiments with Crazyflie quadrotors validate the integrated execution pipeline using robot-relative observations reconstructed from external tracking.
2610.31900.tldr_en: A modular framework integrating neural cellular automata (NCA) with existing site assignment and collision-aware control is presented and a decentralized attachment-site discovery mechanism is introduced, enabling progressive growth without a predefined list of sites during deployment.

llm.title_ja: ニューラルセルオートマトンを用いた分散型群モルホジェネシス
llm.tldr_ja: ニューラルセルオートマトン（NCA）と既存のサイト割り当て・衝突回避制御を統合したモジュラーフレームワークを提案し、分散型の付着サイト発見メカニズムを導入した。
llm.problem: 群モルホジェネシスでは、ロボットが局所的な相互作用を通じて望ましい形を組み立てる必要があるが、展開時に事前定義されたサイトリストなしでの成長が課題となる。
llm.method: NCAとサイト割り当て制御を統合し、ロボットが局所的なNCA状態を共有して新たな付着サイトを特定する分散型メカニズムを提案し、オフラインのファインチューニングを行った。
llm.result: シミュレーションにより多様な格子形態の形成と数百機へのスケーリングを確認し、Crazyflieクアドロトルを用いた実機実験で実行パイプラインを検証した。

2610.31899.title: Silence Is Not Assurance: When Production Lane Keeping Assist Does Not Warn, and What It Costs
2610.31899.abstract: Production lane keeping assist (LKA) systems tell the driver whether they detect the lane markings, but whether this displayed status reflects what the system perceives, and what happens when it does not, has not been examined in real-world driving. This study introduces CANDID-LKA, a CAN-based Diagnosis of the Indicated Detection status in LKA. It evaluates a proprietary driver-facing status using three signals: the displayed status and the steering torque of the driver, both recorded from the controller area network (CAN) bus of the vehicle, and the lane perception confidence of a third-party vision system observing the same road. The framework examines how the status responds to driving conditions and estimates how completely it reports degraded lane perception by comparing it with the other two signals in a latent-class model. We apply it to 39,800 seconds of real-world driving from 13 vehicle models of three manufacturers. The results show that the status does not respond consistently to the conditions that make markings harder to see, and that the three makes differ widely in how often they report not detected. The latent-class model shows that the displayed status is incomplete: it reports only 47% of degraded seconds as not detected, compared with 80% for the third-party low perception confidence, and in half of the low-confidence episodes it never reports not detected. In the silent seconds in which the status reads detected while the perception confidence is low and the driver is not in control, the standard deviation of lateral position over the next 3 s is about 60% larger than when the status and the perception confidence agree. A detected status thus does not guarantee reliable lane perception, and silence with the driver not in control is the case that most needs attention.
2610.31899.tldr_en: CANDID-LKA is introduced, a CAN-based Diagnosis of the Indicated Detection status in LKA that evaluates a proprietary driver-facing status using three signals: the displayed status and the steering torque of the driver, both recorded from the controller area network of the vehicle, and the lane perception confidence of a third-party vision system observing the same road.

llm.title_ja: 沈黙は保証ではない：量産の車線維持支援（LKA）が警告を発しないとき、その代償とは何か
llm.tldr_ja: 車線維持支援（LKA）の表示状態が認識状態をどの程度反映しているかを評価するCANベースの診断フレームワーク「CANDID-LKA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 量産のLKAシステムが車線マーキングの検知状態をドライバーに表示する際、その表示状態が実際のシステム認識を反映しているか、認識していない場合にどうなるかが実世界で検証されていない。
llm.method: 車両のCANバスから得られる表示状態とステアリングトルク、およびサードパーティ製視覚システムの車線認識信頼度の3つの信号を用いて、ドライバー向けの状態を評価する潜在クラスモデルを構築した。
llm.result: 表示状態は劣化した車線認識のわずか47%しか「未検知」として報告せず、検知状態が緑であっても信頼度が低くドライバーが制御していない場合の横方向位置の標準偏差は約60%大きいことを示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンマシンインターフェース

2610.31891.title: Move, don't think: sample-efficient collision avoidance with lossy proximity sensors
2610.31891.abstract: Data-driven robots must learn to avoid collisions with as few demonstrations as possible to avoid collecting large datasets of destructive collision examples. We explore whole-body proximity sensors as inductive biases for learning reflexive collision-dodging behavior and find that lossy sensors with low resolution were stronger biases than high-resolution coverage. We also found that, perhaps unintuitively, anticipating when and where contact happens on the body of a robot reduced its learning sample efficiency. We investigated eight candidate representations in a reinforcement learning environment, which included latent compression, future contact anticipation, lossy corruption, and privileged state estimation. The candidate representations were tested by training over 200 humanoid robots to play a simplified version of dodgeball end-to-end under an intentionally constrained sample and compute budget.
2610.31891.tldr_en: This work explores whole-body proximity sensors as inductive biases for learning reflexive collision-dodging behavior and finds that lossy sensors with low resolution were stronger biases than high-resolution coverage.

llm.title_ja: 考えるな、動け：損失のある近接センサーによるサンプル効率の高い衝突回避
llm.tldr_ja: 全身の近接センサーを反射型衝突回避学習の帰納バイアスとして探索し、低解像度の損失のあるセンサーが強力なバイアスとなることを発見した。
llm.problem: データ駆動型ロボットは、破壊的な衝突例の巨大なデータセット収集を避けるため、極めて少ないデモンストレーションで衝突回避を学習する必要がある。
llm.method: 強化学習環境において、潜在圧縮、将来接触の予測、損失のある破損、特権状態推定を含む8つの候補表現をテストし、200機以上のヒューノイドロボットの学習で検証した。
llm.result: 低解像度の損失のあるセンサーが高解像度のカバレッジよりも強力なバイアスであること、および接触の予測が学習のサンプル効率を低下させることを発見した。
keywords_ja: ヒューノイドロボット

2610.31868.title: Emergent Cooperative Thermoregulation in Lunar Swarm Robotics
2610.31868.abstract: Swarms of small robots are an attractive way to survey lunar caves and lava tubes. Missions such as NASA's CADRE will fly cooperating rovers for distributed mapping, but only in daylight. The 354 h lunar night drops the surface towards 95 K, and the radioisotope heaters that let single rovers survive it cannot be supplied at swarm scale. In this study we investigate whether a swarm can instead use its own members as thermal shielding. We train one policy, shared by all twenty robots, by reinforcement learning with an evolution-strategies estimator. The policy receives a single reward, once, at the end of the night: the mean temperature of the five coldest robots. Nothing in that reward refers to position, spacing, exposure or motion. Two behaviors nonetheless emerge. The swarm aggregates, and robots circulate between the sheltered core and the exposed rim, the same pair of behaviors with which emperor penguins survive the Antarctic winter. We measure the survival threshold, the smallest stored energy per robot at which every robot is still alive at sunrise. Across ten runs it is 155.6 +/- 1.3 pcm-h, where one pcm-h is 7.2 kJ of stored heat. That is 37% below a motionless huddle and within 13% of a physics-based lower bound, and at a budget where the motionless huddle loses six robots, every robot survives. The behavior needs no shared spatial reference and no robot-robot contact, and transfers from twenty robots to forty without retraining.
2610.31868.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters. Video in ancillary files

llm.title_ja: 月面群ロボットにおける創発的協調温度調節
llm.tldr_ja: 強化学習を用いて20機のロボットが共有する単一のポリシーを訓練し、位置や運動に関する報酬を一切与えずに、群が集合してコアとリムの間を循環する適応的温度調節行動が創発することを示した。
llm.problem: 月面の過酷な夜間（95 K）を少数の放射性同位元素ヒーターなしで生存するために、ロボット群がメンバー自身を熱的遮蔽として利用できるかを検証する必要がある。
llm.method: 進化戦略推定量を用いた強化学習により、夜の終わりの最も冷たい5台のロボットの平均温度を報酬として単一のポリシーを訓練した。
llm.result: 群れが集合し、皇帝ペンギンのように保護されたコアと露出したリムの間をロボットが循環する行動が創発し、静止した群れと比較して生存率が大幅に向上し40機への転移も成功した。

2610.31859.title: Full-Weight VLA Fine-Tuning Without an fp32 Master Copy Silently Erases Most Updates
2610.31859.abstract: When a vision-language-action (VLA) model is fine-tuned with its trainable weights in bfloat16 (bf16) and no fp32 master copy, AdamW writes each update straight into bf16, silently rounding away any update smaller than 1/512 of a weight. In 9 of 12 open VLA codebases a default or documented recipe trains this way, 4 on full weight matrices, including LeRobot's SmolVLA default and its $π_0$/$π_{0.5}$ guides. In our LIBERO runs without the copy, a probe every 100 steps finds at least 79% of updates to bf16 weights erased.
