On the Hugging Face Hub, 99% of sampled full-weight SmolVLA fine-tunes store the action expert in bf16, and 84% of recent $π_{0.5}$ fine-tunes with a training configuration set the bf16 flag. On LIBERO-Object, with rules fixed in advance, an fp32 copy raises success over LeRobot's storage from 4.3% to 49.3% for SmolVLA and from 5.1% to 80.9% for $π_{0.5}$ at a ten-times lower learning rate, where both models are undertrained, and from 89.0% to 97.7% for $π_{0.5}$ at its default rate. For SmolVLA at its default rate it adds 10.2 points with open-loop 50-action chunks but only 4.2 when re-planning every 10 actions. In these five comparisons and two more against SmolVLA with every trainable weight in bf16, every run with the copy beats every run without it (p < 0.05); all gaps but the 8.7- and 4.2-point ones clear our 10-point threshold. The fix is to keep the trainable weights in fp32 during training, a one-line change for SmolVLA in LeRobot.
2610.31859.tldr_en: In these five comparisons and two more against SmolVLA with every trainable weight in bf16, every run with the copy beats every run without it (p<0.05); all gaps but the 8.7- and 4.2-point ones clear the 10-point threshold.

llm.title_ja: fp32のマスターコピーを持たない全重みVLAファインチューニングは、大半の更新を密かに消去する
llm.tldr_ja: fp32のマスターコピーなしでbfloat16の訓練を行うとAdamWが更新を丸めてしまう問題を示し、fp32の重みを保持する簡単な修正によりLIBEROでの成功率が大幅に向上することを示した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルのファインチューニング時にbfloat16（bf16）のみで訓練すると、AdamWの更新が丸められて小さな更新が消去されてしまう。
llm.method: 学習中の訓練可能重みをfp32に保持する修正を導入し、複数のVLAコードベースやタスク（LIBERO等）で成功率を比較評価した。
llm.result: fp32のコピーを使用することで、SmolVLAおよびπ0.5の成功率が大幅に向上し（例：5.1%から80.9%への改善）、すべての比較でコピーありの実行がコピーなしを上回った。
keywords_ja: ファインチューニング

2610.31852.title: Multimodal MPC via Bayesian Set Optimization for Dynamic Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects
2610.31852.abstract: Dynamic manipulation of deformable linear objects (DLOs) remains challenging due to underactuated, high-dimensional dynamics, delayed deformation responses, and the presence of multiple feasible motions under obstacle constraints. This paper presents BM2PC, a Bayesian Multimodal MPC framework for agile manipulation of DLOs. Building on the control-as-inference posterior, BM2PC formulates multimodal planning as a set optimization problem that balances control quality and behavioral diversity. An efficient incremental update maintains multiple promising control modes with low additional computational overhead. For real-world deployment, BM2PC incorporates an execution dynamics model that predicts actual end-effector motion and compensates for execution mismatch during fast manipulation. We evaluate BM2PC on rope tracking and obstacle avoidance in simulation and hardware, and on simulated disturbance rejection. In trajectory tracking, BM2PC generalizes better to unseen trajectories than a learning-based baseline without task-specific policy training or fine-tuning. Real-world experiments demonstrate accurate long-horizon tracking, reducing RMSE by 44.0% on the longest task. In obstacle avoidance, BM2PC achieves comparable performance to existing multimodal MPC methods while reducing planning time by 29% to 66%. These results demonstrate accurate dynamic control and efficient multimodal planning within a unified MPC framework. The core implementation of BM2PC and supplementary videos are available at https://github.com/Longyouyuan/BM2PC.
2610.31852.tldr_en: BM2PC is presented, a Bayesian Multimodal MPC framework for agile manipulation of DLOs that formulates multimodal planning as a set optimization problem that balances control quality and behavioral diversity and achieves comparable performance to existing multimodal MPC methods.

llm.title_ja: 動的変形線状物操作のためのベイジアン集合最適化によるマルチモーダルMPC
llm.tldr_ja: 制御品質と行動の多様性のバランスをとる集合最適化問題としてマルチモーダル計画を定式化する、DLOの俊敏な操作のためのベイジアンマルチモーダルMPCフレームワーク（BM2PC）を提案する。
llm.problem: 変形線状物（DLO）の動的操作は、過小駆動、高次元ダイナミクス、変形応答の遅延、複数の実行可能な動作の存在により困難である。
llm.method: 制御推論事後分布に基づき、複数の有望な制御モードを効率的なインクリメンタル更新で維持し、実世界の実行誤差を補償する実行ダイナミクスモデルを組み込んだ。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよびハードウェアでのロープ追跡と障害物回避の実験において、学習ベースのベースラインや既存手法と比較して追跡誤差を低減し、計画時間を29%〜66%削減した。

2610.31845.title: EgoForesight: Effectively Scaling Policy Learning with Noisy Egocentric Actions
2610.31845.abstract: Scaling policy learning requires broad experience and reliable supervision. Robot demonstrations provide high-quality trajectory supervision but are costly to collect. Egocentric videos broaden task and environment coverage, yet motion reconstruction and retargeting introduce noisy action labels. To address this challenge, we introduce EgoForesight, a vision-language-action framework that learns jointly from both sources by reducing the influence of unreliable action labels and exploiting demonstrated outcomes as complementary supervision. A joint vision-action flow couples future visual representation prediction with action generation, unifying reliability-aware action learning with outcome-informed representation transfer. Specifically, reliability-conditioned corruption allocates action supervision across noise levels according to source reliability, while reliability-weighted regression regulates each source's contribution. Complementing this treatment of noisy labels, privileged-future representation distillation draws supervision from demonstrated outcomes. An exponential-moving-average teacher observes the current scene and clean future to encode action-relevant structure from the resulting scene change. Its deeper representations supervise an earlier student layer receiving a corrupted future, providing outcome-informed structure beyond noisy action annotations. Together, these mechanisms support effective scaling with noisy egocentric actions. Over the tested range, EgoForesight exhibits steeper scaling slopes than the baseline, reducing real-world open-loop action MSE by 20.5% and improving RoboCasa few-shot success by 8.1 percentage points at 30,000 hours of pretraining data. After post-training, it also achieves strong absolute performance in both simulated and real-world dexterous manipulation.
2610.31845.tldr_en: EgoForesight is introduced, a vision-language-action framework that learns jointly from both sources by reducing the influence of unreliable action labels and exploiting demonstrated outcomes as complementary supervision, unifying reliability-aware action learning with outcome-informed representation transfer.

llm.title_ja: EgoForesight：ノイズの多い自己中心行動を用いたポリシー学習の効果的スケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 信頼性の低い行動ラベルの影響を減らし、実証された成果を補完的監視として活用することで、両方のソースから共同で学習するVLAフレームワーク「EgoForesight」を提案する。
llm.problem: ポリシー学習のスケーリングには広範な経験と信頼性の高い監督が必要だが、ロボットデモンストレーションはコストが高く、自己中心動画は動作再構築によりノイズの多い行動ラベルが含まれる。
llm.method: 将来の視覚表現予測と行動生成を結合し、信頼度に応じた破損と信頼度加重回帰、および特権的将来表現蒸留を統合した共同ビジョン・アクションフローを構築した。
llm.result: ベースラインと比較して急峻なスケーリング傾斜を示し、実世界のオープンループ行動MSEを20.5%削減し、RoboCasaの少数例成功率を8.1ポイント向上させた。

2610.31841.title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
2610.31841.abstract: Coding agents can translate language instructions into robot programs. For contact-rich manipulation, a key challenge is to generate and refine control logic that responds to physical interaction. We present FORCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque (F/T) measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion. Between executions, the agent inspects force records alongside visual outcomes to diagnose failures and revise both motion and force-feedback control logic. FORCA requires no demonstrations, task-specific training, or simulation. Across five real-robot tasks, we demonstrate its effectiveness in three forms of contact-rich manipulation: improving manipulation accuracy, adapting to changes in object or surface properties, and regulating contact under surface variation and object motion. Compared with a vision-only variant of the same agent, FORCA improves grasp accuracy and task success and reduces contact loss in wiping and peeling.
2610.31841.tldr_en: ForCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion, improves grasp accuracy and task success and reduces contact loss in wiping and peeling.

llm.title_ja: FORCA：接触の多いロボット操作のための力認識型コーディングエージェント
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚観測と手首の力覚・トルク測定を入力として、接触探索と力応答運動のためのPythonプログラムを記述するコーディングエージェント「FORCA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 接触の多い操作において、物理的相互作用に応答する制御ロジックの生成と洗練が困難である。
llm.method: デモンストレーションやタスク特有の訓練を必要とせず、視覚情報とF/T測定値に基づいてエージェントがプログラムを記述し、実行間の力記録と視覚的成果を検査して失敗を診断・修正する。
llm.result: 5つの実ロボットタスクを用いた実験により、把持精度の向上、物体の性質の変化への適応、表面変動や物体運動下での接触の調整において有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: コーディングエージェント

2610.31835.title: SAGE: A hybrid vision-language and geometry framework for work-zone pathway prediction under temporary traffic control
2610.31835.abstract: Temporary traffic control redirects vehicles through work zones, requiring automated vehicles to connect an interpretation of the visible devices to a continuous passing path. Geometric predictors can provide several plausible paths, yet selecting the one consistent with the temporary control remains difficult. We propose SAGE (Semantic-to-Action Grounded Execution), a read-decide-execute-check framework that separates path construction, path preference, and control compliance within a shared candidate space. The central idea is to use a vision-language model's (VLM's) trajectory as a preference over intact geometric candidates. A role-decoupled generator constructs the candidates, and rank fusion combines each candidate's geometric score with its agreement with the VLM trajectory. Supervision structured around the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) trains SAGE-VLM to state the lane status and hazard side before its passage decision and trajectory. The predicted hazard side enters image-space predicates derived from MUTCD provisions, which support a final intervention bounded in score and displacement. On 2,306 real-world ROADWork validation episodes, the candidates include a path within 10 px of the human demonstration in 87% of episodes, yet selection regret accounts for 53% of the geometric ranker's error. SAGE reduces average and final displacement errors by 8.3% and 12.0% relative to the ranker, mostly in the far field, and hard-constraint violations by 37%. The trajectory opinion improves all four tested generator-selector combinations. SAGE is comparable to state-of-the-art VLM modules in accuracy, with a faster-responding VLM, and outperforms four other adapted driving VLMs in displacement error and safety measures. Project page: https://hhjj233.github.io/SAGE-page/.
2610.31835.comment: 26 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://hhjj233.github.io/SAGE-page/
2610.31835.tldr_en: This work proposes SAGE (Semantic-to-Action Grounded Execution), a read-decide-execute-check framework that separates path construction, path preference, and control compliance within a shared candidate space and is comparable to state-of-the-art VLM modules in accuracy, with a faster-responding VLM, and outperforms four other adapted driving VLMs in displacement error and safety measures.

llm.title_ja: SAGE：一時的な交通管理下での作業ゾーン経路予測のためのハイブリッドビジョン言語・幾何学フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 候補空間内で経路構築、経路選好、制御コンプライアンスを分離し、VLMの軌道を幾何学的候補への選好として利用するフレームワーク「SAGE」を提案する。
llm.problem: 一時的な交通管理は車両を作業ゾーンに誘導するため、自動運転車が可視デバイスの解釈と連続的な通過経路を結びつける必要がある。
llm.method: 役割分離型ジェネレーターが幾何学的候補を構築し、ランクフューズにより幾何学的スコアとVLM軌道との合意を組み合わせ、交通管理規則に基づく検証を行うリーダー・ディサイド・エグゼキュー・チェックフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 2,306の実世界ROADWorkエピソードにおいて、平均および最終変位誤差を8.3%および12.0%削減し、ハード制約違反を37%削減した。

2610.31834.title: WorldMirror: Agentic Real-to-Sim Generation of Interactive Worlds from In-the-Wild Robot Demonstrations
2610.31834.abstract: Existing approaches for robot learning in simulation often require substantial manual effort to construct scenes and specify tasks, limiting training scalability and data diversity. Meanwhile, in-the-wild robot demonstrations naturally provide diverse and realistic observations of real-world interactions. Leveraging these demonstrations for simulation requires both high-fidelity visual reconstruction and physically consistent interactions. General-purpose agents offer flexible adaptation to diverse scenarios and strong reasoning about 3D spatial relationships, while specialized generative models provide high-fidelity reconstruction of scene appearance and geometry. We introduce WorldMirror, an agentic real-to-sim framework that constructs interactive digital twins from in-the-wild robot demonstrations. Our central idea is to formulate real-to-sim construction as the iterative refinement of an executable world program. A coding agent decomposes the observed scene, plans reconstruction steps, and orchestrates specialized image and 3D generation tools, refining the program through verification feedback. A camera-pose-anchored scene representation organizes the world into static visual context, support geometry, and editable interactive assets while preserving spatial relationships among the scene, objects, and robot. The agent uses this representation to diagnose and correct reconstruction errors, enabling physically consistent interaction and trajectory replay. Experiments on DROID demonstrate that WorldMirror can reconstruct visually faithful and geometrically consistent interactive worlds while preserving the physical validity of recorded robot trajectories.
2610.31834.tldr_en: WorldMirror is introduced, an agentic real-to-sim framework that constructs interactive digital twins from in-the-wild robot demonstrations that can reconstruct visually faithful and geometrically consistent interactive worlds while preserving the physical validity of recorded robot trajectories.

llm.title_ja: WorldMirror：インザワイルドのロボットデモンストレーションからのインタラクティブな世界のAI駆動型Real-to-Sim生成
llm.tldr_ja: 実行可能なワールドプログラムの反復的洗練としてReal-to-Sim構築を定式化し、インザワイルドのロボットデモンストレーションからインタラクティブなデジタルツインを構築するAIエージェントフレームワーク「WorldMirror」を提案する。
llm.problem: シミュレーションでのロボット学習では、シーンの構築やタスクの指定に多大な手動作業が必要であり、拡張性やデータの多様性が制限されている。
llm.method: コーディングエージェントがシーンを分解し、再構築ステップを計画して専用の生成ツールをオーケストレーションし、カメラポーズで固定されたシーン表現を用いてエラーを診断・修正する。
llm.result: DROIDを用いた実験により、記録されたロボット軌道の物理的妥当性を維持しながら、視覚的に忠実で幾何学的に一貫性のあるインタラクティブな世界を再構築できることを示した。

2610.31829.title: SEVI: Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning
2610.31829.abstract: Real-world reinforcement learning has enabled contact-rich manipulation tasks to be trained directly on physical robots, but unsafe interactions during online learning remain a key barrier to practical deployment. We propose Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning (SEVI), a framework for reliability-aware safety intervention during real-world policy learning. SEVI introduces an Evidential Safety Critic that estimates both future constraint-violation risk and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. During online learning, SEVI evaluates each task-policy action before execution; if the action is predicted to be unsafe or the prediction is insufficiently supported by evidence, SEVI overrides it with an offline-trained recovery policy that guides the robot toward a lower-risk region. We evaluate SEVI on two simulated manipulation tasks and a real-world USB insertion task under in-distribution and distribution-shifted conditions. Across task-learning and safety-critic baselines, SEVI achieves the strongest trajectory-level safety prediction, the highest final task success, and the lowest unsafe-event counts. SEVI also reduces unsafe events by 13.4 to 57.1 percent relative to recovery-based safe RL while preserving low-latency execution-time filtering. The project page is available at: https://sevi-safe.github.io/
2610.31829.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), 2026. Project page: https://sevi-safe.github.io/
2610.31829.tldr_en: Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning (SEVI), a framework for reliability-aware safety intervention during real-world policy learning, is proposed and achieves the strongest trajectory-level safety prediction, the highest final task success, and the lowest unsafe-event counts.

llm.title_ja: SEVI：安全で確証的な実世界強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の制約違反リスクと認識的不確実性を単一のフォワードパスで推定するエビデンシャル安全性批評家（Evidential Safety Critic）を導入し、実世界ポリシー学習中の信頼性に応じた安全性介入を実現するフレームワーク「SEVI」を提案する。
llm.problem: 実世界強化学習では物理ロボットで直接訓練できる一方、オンライン学習中の安全でない相互作用が実用化への大きな障壁となっている。
llm.method: タスクポリシーの行動を実行前に評価し、安全でないと予測されたり証拠が不十分な場合に、オフラインで訓練されたリカバリーポリシーに置き換える仕組みを導入した。
llm.result: シミュレーションタスクおよび実世界のUSB挿入タスクにおいて、最も強力な軌道レベルの安全予測、最高の最終タスク成功率を達成し、安全でないイベントを13.4〜57.1%削減した。

2610.31812.title: PrefO2O: Zero-Shot Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning via Offline-to-Online Latent Preference Transfer
2610.31812.abstract: Preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for learning robot behaviors aligned with human intent. However, its scalability is fundamentally limited by the need to collect expensive human preference labels for every new task. In this work, we present PrefO2O, an offline-to-online latent preference transfer framework that enables zero-shot PbRL on unseen target tasks without requiring any human feedback. The core idea is to learn a task-invariant latent preference space from a small amount of offline preference data on source tasks, where transferable preference structures are disentangled from task-specific variations. This learned manifold allows PrefO2O to transfer preference structures and reward priors to new tasks under distribution shift, while confidence-weighted optimal transport alignment generates reliable pseudo-preference supervision for online reward adaptation. Extensive experiments on robotic manipulation and locomotion benchmarks demonstrate that PrefO2O substantially outperforms existing preference-transfer baselines and matches or exceeds PbRL methods trained with real human feedback, while generalizing across multi-to-one and one-to-one transfer settings as well as across different robot embodiments.
2610.31812.tldr_en: This work presents PrefO2O, an offline-to-online latent preference transfer framework that enables zero-shot PbRL on unseen target tasks without requiring any human feedback, and substantially outperforms existing preference-transfer baselines and matches or exceeds PbRL methods trained with real human feedback.

llm.title_ja: PrefO2O: オフライン・オンライン間潜在選好転移によるゼロショット選好ベース強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のフィードバックを一切必要とせずに未知のターゲットタスクでゼロショットPbRLを可能にするオフライン・オンライン潜在選好転移フレームワーク「PrefO2O」を提案する。
llm.problem: タスクごとに高価な人間の選好ラベルを収集する必要があり、選好ベース強化学習のスケーラビリティが根本的に制限されていること。
llm.method: 少量のオフライン選好データからタスク不変な潜在選好空間を学習し、信頼度加重最適輸送アライメントでオンライン適応を行う。
llm.result: 既存の選好転移ベースラインを大きく上回り、実世界の人間のフィードバックで訓練されたPbRL手法に匹敵またはそれを超える性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.31803.title: StackGen3D: Stable 3D Block Stack Generation from Multiview Silhouettes
2610.31803.abstract: Generating physically stable 3D structures from visual specifications requires resolving geometric ambiguity while accounting for physical interactions among objects. We present StackGen3D, a framework for generating stable block assemblies conditioned on a given block inventory and three orthographic silhouettes. Our approach consists of two stages. First, we develop a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) that models support relations between blocks and serves as a fast stability predictor for curating a diverse dataset of stable structures. Second, we train a conditional flow-matching model on this dataset to capture the multimodal distribution of block configurations consistent with the target silhouettes. At inference time, lightweight geometric selection and refinement reduce inter-block penetration without physics simulation. Preliminary experiments show that the PI-GNN generalizes from simple stacks to complex structures substantially better than a parameter-matched multilayer perceptron. For structure generation, Best-of-10 selection improves physical stability from 45.3% to 72.4% while achieving a silhouette IoU of 0.970. These results highlight the potential of combining relational physical reasoning, scalable data curation, and conditional generative modeling for creative 3D assembly. Project website: [https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/](https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/)
2610.31803.comment: A poster of this work is publicly available on the website of the Creativity in Assembly Workshop at IROS 2026 (non-archival)
2610.31803.tldr_en: StackGen3D is presented, a framework for generating stable block assemblies conditioned on a given block inventory and three orthographic silhouettes and develops a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) that models support relations between blocks and serves as a fast stability predictor for curating a diverse dataset of stable structures.

llm.title_ja: StackGen3D: マルチビューシルエットからの安定な3Dブロック積み上げ生成
llm.tldr_ja: 与えられたブロックの在庫と3つの直交シルエットを条件として安定したブロックアセンブリを生成するフレームワーク「StackGen3D」を提案する。
llm.problem: 視覚的仕様から物理的に安定した3D構造を生成する際、オブジェクト間の物理的相互作用を考慮しつつ幾何学的曖昧さを解決する必要があること。
llm.method: ブロック間の支持関係をモデル化する物理情報グラフニューラルネットワーク(PI-GNN)と条件付きフローマッチングモデルを組み合わせる。
llm.result: ベストオブ10選択により物理的安定性が45.3%から72.4%に向上し、シルエットIoU 0.970を達成した。
keywords_ja: グラフニューラルネットワーク

2610.31801.title: KiRoSe: Using Kinematic Data for Efficient Segmentation of Robot Demonstrations
2610.31801.abstract: Segmenting robot demonstration data into disjoint temporal and semantic subsegments is valuable for learning, cleaning, retrieval, and analysis. Segmentation is often performed manually in a tedious and error prone process. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have the potential for automating this process, but directly ingesting raw multi camera video streams into MLLMs can be costly and can quickly exhaust context windows. In this paper, we introduce KiRoSe (Kinematics for Robot Segmentation), a novel framework that focuses on the companion stream of robot kinematic data. Inspired by the principle of classical entropy coding, such as Huffman coding, where frequently occurring symbols are represented more compactly, we propose Sparse Motion Tokens (SMTs), a discrete kinematic vocabulary designed to compactly represent recurring, temporally localized motion patterns, which we refer to as kinematic events. SMTs are learned by encoding kinematic trajectories with temporal segment supervision and quantizing the resulting features. We use increasingly available robot demonstration subtask annotations to supervise an open language model to interpret the resulting token sequences. Evaluation against human labeled segmentation shows that KiRoSe can substantially outperform baseline segmentation methods in F1 quality and transfers zero shot to unseen robot embodiments and egocentric human motion, while preserving the language models open vocabulary knowledge. Beyond segmentation, KiRoSe tracks task progress on an unseen robot and detects when an action is being reversed.(website: https://berkeleyautomation.github.io/kirose/)
2610.31801.tldr_en: This paper introduces KiRoSe (Kinematics for Robot Segmentation), a novel framework that focuses on the companion stream of robot kinematic data and proposes Sparse Motion Tokens (SMTs), a discrete kinematic vocabulary designed to compactly represent recurring, temporally localized motion patterns.

llm.title_ja: KiRoSe: キネマティックデータを用いたロボットデモの効率的なセグメンテーション
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットのキネマティックデータに特化し、反復的な局所的モーションパターンのための離散的語彙である「Sparse Motion Tokens (SMTs)」を用いた新しいフレームワーク「KiRoSe」を導入する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデルに生のマルチカメラビデオストリームを直接入力すると、コストが高くなりコンテキストウィンドウを急速に枯渇させること。
llm.method: 古典的エントロピー符号化に着想を得たSparse Motion Tokens (SMTs)を学習し、言語モデルに解釈させる。
llm.result: 人間によるアノテーションとの比較において、F1品質でベースラインのセグメンテーション手法を大きく上回り、未知のロボットや一人称視点人間の動作へゼロショット転移できる。

2610.31797.title: PnP*: A certifiable solver for Perspective-n-Point
2610.31797.abstract: Estimating a camera pose from 3D-2D correspondences - Perspective-n-Point - is one of the most fundamental problems in computer vision. Existing methods either solve a minimal problem or replace the objective with an easier one. Surprisingly, no scalable certifiable solver for the actual Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) exists. We propose PnP*, the first practical solver that guarantees efficient computation and returns a certifiable globally optimal solution. We prove that the underlying convex relaxation is exact under moderate noise, which to our knowledge is the first stability guarantee for any relaxation for the MLE of PnP. Furthermore, we reduce the relaxation by exploiting chordal sparsity pattern and quotient ring reduction such that the relaxation is tractable and scalable. The stability and scalability results are verified numerically, as PnP* returns a provably correct camera pose at over 10 Hz.
2610.31797.tldr_en: It is proved that the underlying convex relaxation is exact under moderate noise, which to the knowledge is the first stability guarantee for any relaxation for the MLE of PnP.

llm.title_ja: PnP*: Perspective-n-Pointのための保証付きソルバー
llm.tldr_ja: 効率的な計算を保証し、証明可能な大域的最適解を返す、PnPの実際の最尤推定のための最初の実用的なソルバー「PnP*」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のPnP解法は最小問題を解くか、目的関数を簡単なものに置き換えており、実際の最尤推定に対するスケーラブルで証明可能なソルバーが存在しないこと。
llm.method: 背後にある凸緩和が中程度のノイズ下で厳密であることを証明し、弦スパース性と商環の縮小により緩和をスケーラブルにする。
llm.result: 数値検証により、PnP*は10 Hz以上で証明可能な正しいカメラ姿勢を返すことが示された。

2610.31779.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
2610.31779.abstract: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models. The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.
2610.31779.tldr_en: Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, is presented, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities and is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives.
2610.31779.hf_summary_en: Flora is an open-source industrial data engine for robotics foundation models that provides captioning, outcome and process reward labeling, and pretraining data curation at scale with high accuracy and low cost.

llm.title_ja: FLORA: ロボティクスデータエンジンのスケーリングのためのオープンモデルスイート
llm.tldr_ja: GR00Tモデルの訓練に使用される工業用品質のデータエンジン「Flora」を提案し、キャプションや報酬のベンチマークでSOTAを達成しつつAPIベースの代替手段よりも大幅に安価であることを示す。
llm.problem: ロボット基盤モデルのライフサイクルがデータラベルに深く依存しており、実世界展開の監視、強化学習、事前学習データのフィルタリングに多様な報酬やキャプションが必要であること。
llm.method: 512基のGB300を用いて毎日20万時間のデータをラベル付けする、工業用品質のマルチ機能データエンジンを構築・オープンソース化する。
llm.result: WGO-BenchやRoboRewardなどのベンチマークでSOTAスコアを達成し、GPT-6 Astraなどのフロンティアモデルに匹敵しつつ約125分の1のコストを実現した。

2610.31762.title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
2610.31762.abstract: What visual representation should a navigation policy act on? Navigation policies built on vision foundation models largely leave representation design to the encoders' pretraining objectives. We present RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model built on a self-constructed representation space: a visual representation constructed by the policy's own objectives from vision foundation models. RepresentNav builds this space with Representation Residuals, a compact three-layer transformer that attends over features spanning the full depth of multiple complementary vision foundation models, so that the policy learns to see what it needs for navigation. In the same space it dreams what it wants: before every action a latent chain-of-thought predicts the representation of the scene a moment ahead. The dream is trained end-to-end with the policy as a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), with a next-representation prediction loss and a regularizer on its targets. RepresentNav sets a new state of the art on VLNVerse, VLN-CE R2R, EVT-Bench, and two point-goal benchmarks, and its gains carry over to a physical robot amid clutter and moving people. On VLNVerse fine-grained, RepresentNav achieves 83.80% success, outperforming the previous state of the art by 20.05 percentage points, and on EVT-Bench distracted tracking it reaches 85.5% with a single camera (+10.1). With the same encoders, the self-constructed space clearly outperforms concatenating their outputs and learns to weight their layers unevenly, and a dream in it cuts collisions by a quarter. A single dreamed latent decodes into the depth, semantics, and 3D occupancy of the scene a moment ahead, more accurately than pretrained encoders applied to the real future frame, although occupancy is never supervised, and the rollout tracks the robot's own motion over the next second: the dream emerges as a compact latent world model.
2610.31762.tldr_en: RepresentNav is presented, a navigation foundation model built on a self-constructed representation space: a visual representation constructed by the policy's own objectives from vision foundation models, with a compact three-layer transformer that attends over features spanning the full depth of multiple complementary vision foundation models.

llm.title_ja: 見たいものを見、夢見るものを得る：自己構築表現空間上のナビゲーション基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 複数の補完的な視覚基盤モデルの深層特徴から自己構築された表現空間上に構築されたナビゲーション基盤モデル「RepresentNav」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の視覚基盤モデルに基づくナビゲーションポリシーは、表現の設計をエンコーダの事前学習目的に依存したままにしていること。
llm.method: Representation Residualsを用いたコンパクトなトランスフォーマーにより独自の目的で視覚表現空間を構築し、JEPAとしてエンドツーエンドで学習する。
llm.result: VLNVerseやEVT-Benchなどの複数のベンチマークで新たなSoTAを達成し、物理ロボットにおける雑然とした環境や移動中の人混みの中でも衝突を4分の1に削減した。

2610.31670.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
2610.31670.abstract: Robot foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, motivating low-cost offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To test this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to robotics and make sensorimotor alignment measurable, offering a low-cost, representation-level view of robot foundation models that closed-loop success rates alone cannot reveal.
2610.31670.comment: 28 pages. Project page and code available at https://yunfeixie233.github.io/s2/
2610.31670.tldr_en: Sensorimotor Alignment is proposed, a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion, offering a low-cost, representation-level view of robot foundation models that closed-loop success rates alone cannot reveal.
2610.31670.hf_summary_en: Sensorimotor alignment measures how sensory representations match physical motion geometry, serving as a low-cost offline predictor of robot model performance.

llm.title_ja: センサー運動アライメント：具現化ポリシーの成功のためのプラトン的プロキシ
llm.tldr_ja: モデルの感覚表現が物理的運動の幾何学とどれだけ一致するかを測定する、学習不要のオフライン指標「Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$)」を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボット基盤モデルの評価にはコストのかかる閉ループロールアウトが必要であり、モデル能力のための低コストなオフラインプロキシが求められていること。
llm.method: プラトン的表現仮説（PRH）をロボット工学に拡張し、感覚表現と物理的運動の幾何学の一致度を訓練不要で計測する指標を定義する。
llm.result: $S^2$は下流のロボットタスク成功率と正の相関を示し、閉ループ評価の前にモデルの優先順位付けを行う低コストなオフラインプロキシとして機能する。
keywords_ja: センサー運動アライメント

2610.31661.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
2610.31661.abstract: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io
2610.31661.comment: 14 pages, 14 figures. Project website, open-source hardware and software, and demonstration videos: https://opentac.github.io
2610.31661.tldr_en: A scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure and the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments is demonstrated.

llm.title_ja: OpenTac: カスタマイズ可能、スケーラブル、かつ転移可能な3D触覚センシングのためのオープンエコシステム
llm.tldr_ja: カスタマイズ可能でスケーラブル、かつ下流のロボット制御や学習に応用可能な触覚スキンのためのセンサおよびフルスタックエコシステム「OpenTac」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来の高精度な触覚センシングはカスタマイズやスケーラビリティ、多様なロボット形態への適用が困難であること。
llm.method: 接線方向の負荷を圧力に変換する構造化された変形可能なオーバーレイを持つ抵抗膜式触覚スキンを開発し、自動設計ツールを提供する。
llm.result: 30種類以上のセンサの設計・試作に成功し、4つの実ロボットにおいて接触を伴うフィードバック制御やマニピュレーションポリシーの学習に幅広く適用できることを示した。
keywords_ja: オープンソースハードウェア

2610.31625.title: Extending Harmonic Function Methods via Root Locus for Coordinated Path Generation
2610.31625.abstract: We consider the offline generation of coordinated paths for N interchangeable robots and N goals in planar environments with polygonal obstacles. After a conformal map to a circular domain, starts and goals become the poles and zeros of a rational function R, and the paths are the branches of its Generalized Root Locus (GRL), i.e. the streamlines of the logarithmic potential -log R. We show that, for every phase outside a finite set of critical phases and a set of boundary phases, the induced gradient motion drives each robot to a distinct goal along pairwise disjoint paths that never reach the obstacles; the robot-goal assignment is produced by the construction, and with the gain used as a clock all robots move as the closed-loop roots of the GRL and arrive together at a prescribed time. Obstacles become streamlines through successive Milne-Thomson reflections, and for a finite number of reflections a finite test certifies safety for the potential that is actually computed. Reciprocal root-locus planning is recovered as a special case. The method is illustrated on two polygonal workspaces, 100 random instances compared with independent harmonic planning and artificial potentials, and a scene with ten robots and ten obstacles.
2610.31625.comment: 16 pages, 6 figures. Extended version of a paper submitted to Automatica. Corresponding code: https://github.com/mfrascarelli/grl-certified-planning
2610.31625.tldr_en: It is shown that, for every phase outside a finite set of critical phases and a set of boundary phases, the induced gradient motion drives each robot to a distinct goal along pairwise disjoint paths that never reach the obstacles.

llm.title_ja: 協調的パス生成のための根軌跡による調和関数手法の拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 等角写像を利用して、多ロボットの衝突のない協調的パスを一般化根軌跡（GRL）の枝としてオフラインで生成する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 非線形システムの多ロボット協調は、制約付きの共同空間最適制御として定式化されるが、既存手法は中央集権的であるか安全性のみに特化していること。
llm.method: 円形領域への等角写像後、スタートとゴールを極と零点とし、一般化根軌跡の流線を利用して各ロボットを明確なゴールに誘導する。
llm.result: クリティカル位相等を除く任意の位相において、誘導された勾配運動が障害物を避けて各ロボットを異なるゴールへと駆動することを示した。

2610.31623.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
2610.31623.abstract: This paper studies category-level RGB-D object pose estimation, which recovers an object's 3D rotation and translation without instance-specific CAD models or reference views. This task is highly ambiguous due to intra-class variations, symmetries, and partial observations. Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at https://jrryzh.github.io/F2G-Pose/.
2610.31623.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 22 pages, including the complete technical appendix
2610.31623.tldr_en: F2G-Pose is a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference.
2610.31623.hf_summary_en: F2G-Pose is a real-time feed-forward framework that predicts category-level object pose, metric size, and completed shape from a single RGB-D image using dense visual features, DGCNN tokenization, and a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer.

llm.title_ja: F2G-Pose: 幾何学を考慮した基盤特徴リフティングによる直接的RGB-Dカテゴリレベル物体姿勢推定
llm.tldr_ja: 単一のRGB-D観測から1回のフィードフォワードパスでカテゴリレベルの姿勢、メトリックサイズ、完成した形状を予測するリアルタイムな直接的フレームワーク「F2G-Pose」を提案する。
llm.problem: カテゴリレベルのRGB-D物体姿勢推定において、従来の中間構造ベースの手法は誤差伝播しやすく、拡散モデルは推論遅延が大きいこと。
llm.method: 高密度な視覚基盤特徴を部分点群にリフティングし、DGCNNトークン化で局所幾何学をエンコードし、Mixture-of-Experts Transformerで統合する。
llm.result: SOPEおよびROPEデータセットでSoTAの精度を達成しつつ、姿勢のみの推論で28 FPSで動作した。

2610.31617.title: DiffDreamer: Coupling World Models with Differentiable Simulation for Agile Quadrotor Control
2610.31617.abstract: Tasks such as quadrotor dynamic-gate racing require agents to anticipate external motion while maintaining precise high-frequency control. World-model-based reinforcement learning provides a natural solution by learning latent dynamics for future imagination, yet it often entangles environmental evolution and the robot's own dynamics in a single learned rollout, where model bias can affect policy optimization efficiency. We propose DiffDreamer, a differentiable reinforcement learning framework that tightly couples a learned world model with differentiable simulation for actor optimization. In one optimization step, the learned world model propagates latent states that capture external dynamics and history-dependent features, while the differentiable simulator propagates the robot's explicit physical state. We further decompose the actor objective into a critic-driven pathway for non-differentiable task rewards and a simulator-driven pathway for differentiable motion rewards. Experiments on aggressive tracking and dynamic-gate racing show that DiffDreamer improves training convergence over the model-free, model-based, and differentiable-RL baselines, and final performance over these baselines and classical planning and control methods. Additional experiments assess reward decomposition and the odometry-conditioned relative-state representation through ablations. We also provide proof-of-concept real-world flight experiments for validation.
2610.31617.tldr_en: DiffDreamer is proposed, a differentiable reinforcement learning framework that tightly couples a learned world model with differentiable simulation for actor optimization and improves training convergence over the model-free, model-based, and differentiable-RL baselines, and final performance over classical planning and control methods.

llm.title_ja: DiffDreamer: 世界モデルと微分可能シミュレーションを結合した俊敏なクアドロプター制御
llm.tldr_ja: 学習された世界モデルと微分可能シミュレーションを密に結合し、アクター最適化を行う微分可能強化学習フレームワーク「DiffDreamer」を提案する。
llm.problem: 世界モデルベースの強化学習では、環境の進化とロボット自身の動力学が単一の学習済みロールアウトに絡み合い、モデルバイアスが最適化効率に影響を与えること。
llm.method: アクターの目的関数を、非微分可能なタスク報酬のための批評家駆動型経路と、微分可能なモーション報酬のためのシミュレーター駆動型経路に分解する。
llm.result: アグレッシブなトラッキングや動的ゲートレースにおいて、モデルフリー、モデルベース、微分可能RLのベースラインよりも訓練の収束性と最終性能が向上した。
keywords_ja: 微分可能シミュレーション

2610.31613.title: Progress Probes $P^2$: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.31613.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform diverse manipulation tasks directly from visual observations and natural language instructions, but they remain prone to mistakes and unpredictable failures. Deploying these policies without continuous human supervision will require robust runtime monitors that detect when the policy has gone off-course. Existing monitors use external foundation models, such as vision-language models (VLMs) to supervise the policy, introducing significant complexity and computational cost for monitoring at runtime. In this work, we investigate an alternate approach: \textit{can a VLA's own internal activations provide the information needed to monitor its execution?} Our method trains linear probes on policy activations from demonstrations to estimate progress, then flags executions that deviate from expected progress. In experiments with the open-source VLA $π_{0.5}$ and across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, this approach is competitive with or outperforms VLM-based monitors in task failure detection, as well as methods which require failure data for training. These findings suggest that simple probes of VLA internals can be used to develop reliable runtime monitors, opening a path toward building policies that can act reliably and monitor their execution without external foundation models.
2610.31613.tldr_en: It is suggested that simple probes of VLA internals can be used to develop reliable runtime monitors, opening a path toward building policies that can act reliably and monitor their execution without external foundation models.

llm.title_ja: Progress Probes $P^2$: ビジョン言語アクションモデルのための軽量ランタイム監視
llm.tldr_ja: VLAの内部活性化から進捗を推定し、期待される進捗から逸脱した実行にフラグを立てる線形プローブを訓練する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: ビジョン言語アクション（VLA）モデルは多様なタスクを実行できるが、失敗しやすく、継続的な人間監視なしでの展開には堅牢なランタイムモニターが必要であること。
llm.method: デモからのVLAポリシーの内部活性化に対して線形プローブを訓練し、実行の進捗を推定する。
llm.result: オープンソースVLA $\pi_{0.5}$ を用いた実験において、タスク失敗検知においてVLMベースのモニターに匹敵するかそれを上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2610.31608.title: Humanoid Mobility via Attention-based Contacts
2610.31608.abstract: Humanoid mobility over complex terrain requires accurate foot placement and coordinated whole-body motion capable of robust adaptation. Reinforcement learning (RL) policies trained without motion references generalize well across terrains, yet eliciting effective whole-body coordination through reward design and exploration alone remains challenging. In contrast, reference-based methods yield natural motions but struggle to adapt beyond the predefined trajectories in their training data. We introduce a learning framework that bridges these two approaches by using motion data strictly as a training prior. An explicit, self-supervised, attention-based contact planner predicts future body-environment contacts, while a contact-conditioned tracker translates these plans into coordinated whole-body motion. Together, they establish contact as an interface between sensory observations and control actions. This abstraction allows the policy to internalize the contact-aware structure of locomotion rather than directly replicating kinematics. Consequently, a single policy can exploit data-driven motion priors for natural whole-body coordination while retaining the flexibility to discover environment-dependent behaviors through reinforcement learning. Building on the learned contact planner and tracker, a subsequent fine-tuning stage bootstraps their acquired capabilities to explore environment variations beyond those covered by the original motion data. Operating entirely from onboard observations without any reference inputs at deployment, this framework enables versatile humanoid mobility in challenging environments.
2610.31608.tldr_en: This framework enables versatile humanoid mobility in challenging environments by using motion data strictly as a training prior for natural whole-body coordination while retaining the flexibility to discover environment-dependent behaviors through reinforcement learning.

llm.title_ja: アテンションベースの接触を介したヒノイドの移動
llm.tldr_ja: モーションデータを単なる訓練事前分布として使用し、環境に依存した行動を発見する柔軟性を維持しながら自然な全身協調を実現する学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 複雑な地形でのヒューマノイドの移動には正確な足の配置と協調された全身モーションが必要だが、報酬設計と探索のみで効果的な全身協調を引き出すことは困難であること。
llm.method: 明示的な自己教師ありアテンションベースの接触プランナーが将来の身体-環境間の接触を予測し、接触条件付きトラッカーがこれらを全身運動に変換する。
llm.result: 展開時に参照入力を必要とせず、オンボードの観測のみから動作し、挑戦的な環境における多様なヒューマノイドの移動を可能にした。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.31569.title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
2610.31569.abstract: Recognizing task completion and failure enables robots to stop upon success and initiate recovery or replanning after failure. Existing methods augment Vision Language Action (VLA) policies with task status signal prediction to support these execution decisions. However, learning and integrating these signals can require fine-grained supervision, external monitoring models, or complex architectural designs. Moreover, the potential of task status signals to directly guide action generation remains underexplored. We present Echo, a framework that combines task status signal learning without frame-level progress annotations with a compact design for status prediction and action generation within a single VLA. Specifically, Echo represents task status with stop and failure signals, added as two dimensions of each action chunk and denoised together with robot actions. Their combination distinguishes ongoing execution, successful completion, and failure. To learn these signals without fine-grained progress annotations, Echo constructs successful, failed, and recovery trajectories with complementary supervision properties. To enable status signal-guided action generation, Echo controls interactions between the signals and actions and denoises the signals faster than the actions. These allow later action denoising steps to condition on cleaner status estimates while preserving accurate signal prediction. Extensive real-world manipulation experiments show that Echo accurately predicts task status and consistently improves policy performance.
2610.31569.tldr_en: Echo is a framework that combines task status signal learning without frame-level progress annotations with a compact design for status prediction and action generation within a single VLA, and accurately predicts task status and consistently improves policy performance.
2610.31569.hf_summary_en: Echo integrates stop and failure signals into a vision-language-action model to guide robot execution and recovery without fine-grained progress labels.

llm.title_ja: Echo: ビジョン言語アクションモデルのための結合された行動およびタスクステータス信号のノイズ除去
llm.tldr_ja: フレームレベルの進捗アノテーションなしでタスクステータス信号の学習を行い、単一のVLA内でステータス予測と行動生成をコンパクトに統合するフレームワーク「Echo」を提案する。
llm.problem: タスクの完了や失敗の認識は重要だが、既存の手法はきめ細かいアノテーションや外部の監視モデル、複雑なアーキテクチャを必要とすること。
llm.method: タスクステータスを停止および失敗の信号として表現し、アクションチャンクの2つの次元として追加してロボットアクションとともにノイズ除去を行う。
llm.result: 広範な実世界のマニピュレーション実験により、Echoはタスクステータスを正確に予測し、ポリシーの性能を継続的に向上させることが示された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2610.31567.title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
2610.31567.abstract: Objective: Iontophoretic drug delivery has primarily relied on current modulation to regulate drug transport. Here, we investigate hydrogel geometry, microstructure, and local electric fields as alternative mechanisms for controlling transdermal delivery. Methods: Bovine serum albumin (BSA) was encapsulated in polypyrrole-polyvinyl alcohol (PPy-PVA) hydrogels. Five geometries, including Hilbert curve-based designs, were fabricated to vary pore architecture and local electric field distributions. We optimized PPy content, drug loading, and current density. Electric fields were evaluated using finite element analysis, and microstructures were characterized by scanning electron microscopy. Drug transport was assessed using Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes. Results: Hydrogel geometries exhibited distinct microstructures and electric field distributions. Iontophoresis substantially enhanced permeability compared with passive diffusion, while individual geometries produced different cumulative release, flux, and permeability profiles. The average iontophoretic permeability was (3.80 +/- 1.93) x 10^-5, exceeding previously reported values using artificial membranes. Conclusion: Geometry-driven fabrication of drug-loaded hydrogels enables tunable transport characteristics under both iontophoretic and passive conditions. Significance: Geometry-mediated control offers an alternative approach to regulating iontophoretic drug delivery without requiring individual current-density modulation.
2610.31567.tldr_en: Geometry-mediated control complements existing approaches for iontophoretic drug delivery without requiring individual current-density control and showed that the geometry-driven fabrication of drug-loaded hydrogel can achieve different delivery characteristics in both iontophoretic and passive transport using artificial membranes.

llm.title_ja: 物理的に架橋されたPPy-PVAハイドロゲルの幾何学的依存性特性に基づく調整可能なイオントフォレシス薬物送達
llm.tldr_ja: 個別電流密度変調を必要とせずにイオントフォレシス薬物送達を制御するための代替メカニズムとして、ハイドロゲルの幾何学形状、微細構造、局所電場を調査した。
llm.problem: イオントフォレシス薬物送達は主に電流変調に依存して薬物輸送を調整してきたこと。
llm.method: Hilbert曲線ベースのデザインを含む5つの幾何学形状でPPy-PVAハイドロゲルを作製し、有限要素解析とFranz拡散セルを用いて評価した。
llm.result: ハイドロゲルの幾何学形状が異なる微細構造と電場分布を示し、イオントフォレシスによって受動拡散と比較して透過性が大幅に向上した。

2610.31562.title: Decentralized Bi-Level Optimization for Cooperative Orbital Transportation of a Rigid Payload
2610.31562.abstract: The rapid growth of the space economy, alongside increasing orbital congestion and debris, is driving demand for reliable on-orbit transportation of large and non-cooperative objects. Performing such transportation with a swarm of small spacecraft distributes risk and removes the single point of failure inherent to monolithic architectures, but requires solving a non-convex trajectory optimization coupling every agent's cone-constrained thrust to the payload's rotational dynamics. Existing approaches span decentralized control laws with asymptotic guarantees but limited constraint enforcement, and centralized and partially centralized planners that reintroduce a single point of failure. In this work, we present a decentralized bi-level framework driven by exact gradients: the problem is split into an inner convex thrust allocation and an outer search over payload torque trajectories. This decomposition yields fuel-efficient solutions quickly, without requiring full NLP convergence, and at short timescales its performance scales with the number of agents. Theoretical convergence guarantees are established, and the method is validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulation, including closed-loop recovery from in-flight faults. These properties make the framework well suited to spacecraft swarm applications.

llm.title_ja: 剛体ペイロードの協調軌道輸送のための分散型二層最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 小宇宙機の群れによる大型かつ非協力的な物体の輸送には、各エージェントの推力とペイロードの回転ダイナミクスを結合した非凸軌道最適化を解く必要があること。
llm.method: 内側の凸推力配分と外側のペイロードトルク軌道の探索に問題を分割した、正確な勾配駆動型の分散型二層フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: NLPの完全な収束を必要とせずに燃料効率の高い解を素早く導き出し、飛行中の障害からの閉ループ回復を含むモンテカルロシミュレーションで検証された。

2610.31540.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination
2610.31540.abstract: Multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems is naturally formulated as joint-space optimal control subject to constraints over groups of robots. Existing methods that approach joint optimality remain largely centralized, offline, and confined to collision-free motion planning, while decentralized, real-time counterparts target safe navigation without pursuing the joint optimum. This paper develops a decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process. We extend a recent single-robot framework that searches dispersive trees of forward-propagated commands for differentially flat systems to coordinate a multi-robot team near-optimally. We first show that the inter-robot coupling can be effectively replaced by some local constraints, under which locally grown dispersive trees contain a near-optimal agreement. It is this structure that the robots pursue by decentralized column generation, negotiating rents on the shared space that guide the search of each robot's tree. The negotiation settles on an agreement whose near-optimality is certified at quiescence. Our protocol, WarpWeaver, implements this negotiation as an asynchronous real-time loop over a receding horizon, and demonstrates effective closure to quiesced agreements even when real-time deadlines cut the negotiation short. In simulation, WarpWeaver reduces total travel time by up to 22% against centralized offline planners on the Dynobench suite and by up to 37% against a decentralized real-time baseline, and nearly doubles the success rate of a task-specific planner on graph connectivity. Hardware experiments on six robots planning onboard demonstrate real-world implementability.
2610.31540.comment: 19 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics
2610.31540.tldr_en: A decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process, and runs the negotiation asynchronously over a receding horizon and closes on quiesced agreements even when deadlines cut it short.

llm.title_ja: 多ロボット協調のための分散木合意
llm.tldr_ja: 前方伝播されたコマンドの分散木を探索する単ロボットフレームワークを拡張し、いつでも停止可能なプロセスとして結合最適に近づく分散型リアルタイムプランナーを開発した。
llm.problem: 非線形システムの多ロボット協調は結合空間の最適制御として定式化されるが、既存の最適手法は主に中央集権的かつオフラインであること。
llm.method: ロボット間の結合を局所的制約に置き換え、分散型列生成を通じて共有空間のレンタルを交渉し、各ロボットの木を探索する「WarpWeaver」を実装する。
llm.result: Dynobenchスイートにおいて中央集権型オフラインプランナーと比較して総移動時間を最大22%削減し、分散型リアルタイムベースラインに対して最大37%削減した。

2610.31518.title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
2610.31518.abstract: Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) stands as a fundamental challenge in robotics, essential for enabling autonomous agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks in diverse environments. While Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce a new paradigm for TAMP by leveraging extensive common sense, their inherent reasoning limitations hinder direct application, and fine-tuning strategies to enhance these capabilities are currently bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing automated generation methods often suffer from homogeneity, limiting model generalization, and unsolvability, where hallucinated scene graphs create physical mismatches with task goals. To address these issues, we propose Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets. SCOPE incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios. Crucially, it introduces a Plan Feedback Error-correction pipeline that utilizes planner execution failures as feedback signals to retroactively rectify logical inconsistencies in scene graphs, ensuring physical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that SCOPE exhibits greater robustness to erroneous scene graphs and generates higher-quality data. When utilized for LLM fine-tuning, SCOPE-generated data yield a downstream TAMP model that achieves an absolute 12.33% gain in success rate over its counterpart fine-tuned with data generated by DELTA, a state-of-the-art PDDL-based planner.
2610.31518.comment: 8 pages. Accepted at IROS 2026. Project page: https://scope-page.github.io/
2610.31518.tldr_en: This work proposes Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets that incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios and introduces a Plan Feedback Error-correction pipeline.

llm.title_ja: SCOPE: ロボットの長期計画データセットのための計画エラー修正により最適化されたシーングラフ構築
llm.tldr_ja: 多様で実行可能なTAMPデータセットを生成するために、マルチレベルの多様性指標を取り入れ、計画の実行失敗をフィードバック信号としてシーングラフの論理的矛盾を遡及的に修正する自動フレームワーク「SCOPE」を提案する。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルを用いたTAMPのためのファインチューニング戦略が、高品質なデータセットの不足によってボトルネックになっていること。
llm.method: プランナーの実行失敗をフィードバック信号として利用し、シーングラフの論理的不整合を遡及的に修正するPlan Feedback Error-correctionパイプラインを組み込む。
llm.result: SCOPE生成的データを用いたLLMファインチューニングにより、既存のDELTAベースラインと比較して成功率が絶対値で12.33%向上した。
keywords_ja: タスク・モーション計画

2610.31494.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
2610.31494.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can perform a broad range of tasks across diverse settings, yet their performance in agentic contexts remains poorly understood. Although online evaluations in simulators and real-world environments are essential for measuring interactive agent performance, they are costly and challenging to scale. Complementary offline VQA benchmarks can enable faster and more reliable comparisons across agentic domains, yet existing benchmarks remain limited and fragmented. To address this gap, we introduce AgentVQA, an offline benchmark for evaluating VLMs on realistic agentic scenarios across five agent domains: Web Agents, Robotics, Egocentric Videos, Games, and Spatial Planning. We build AgentVQA by manually selecting 1000 challenging, real-world agent examples from 23 source datasets and adapting them for reliable offline evaluation. The resulting benchmark preserves realistic scenarios from interactive environments across diverse domains, and its model rankings track those from corresponding online evaluations. Across the 22 evaluated models, the best achieves only 58.5% accuracy. Our cross-domain analysis shows that errors are driven primarily by failures to ground and maintain accurate representations of the current and evolving visual state, including localizing relevant UI elements, interpreting motion, tracking state changes over time, and inferring 3D spatial relationships, rather than by task misinterpretation or downstream logical reasoning.
2610.31494.tldr_en: This work introduces AgentVQA, an offline benchmark for evaluating VLMs on realistic agentic scenarios across five agent domains: Web Agents, Robotics, Egocentric Videos, Games, and Spatial Planning, and shows that errors are driven primarily by failures to ground and maintain accurate representations of the current and evolving visual state.
2610.31494.hf_summary_en: AgentVQA is an offline benchmark assessing vision-language models on realistic agentic tasks across web, robotics, video, games, and spatial planning, revealing that visual grounding and state tracking errors are the primary failure modes.

llm.title_ja: AgentVQA: エージェント的視覚理解のための統合ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: Webエージェント、ロボット工学、一人称視点ビデオ、ゲーム、空間計画の5つのエージェントドメインにおける現実的なエージェントシナリオでVLMを評価するためのオフラインベンチマーク「AgentVQA」を導入する。
llm.problem: オンラインでのシミュレーターや実環境での評価は費用がかかりスケーリングが困難であり、既存のオフラインVQAベンチマークは限定的かつ断片的であること。
llm.method: 23のソースデータセットから1000の挑戦的な実世界のエージェント事例を手動で選択・適応させ、信頼性の高いオフライン評価のためのベンチマークを構築する。
llm.result: 評価された22モデルのうち最良のモデルでも正答率は58.5%に留まり、エラーの主な原因がタスクの誤解ではなく視覚状態のグラウンディングと維持の失敗であることを示した。

2610.31476.title: Point-Level Refinable Semantic Mapping for Spatial Understanding
2610.31476.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D semantic maps have emerged as a key spatial memory representation for long-horizon robot autonomy, enabling robots to reason about objects, their spatial relationships, and past observations across time. However, existing object-centric semantic maps are primarily designed for static environments and rely on an append-only point integration strategy, where newly observed points are accumulated but previously integrated points are rarely reevaluated. Consequently, perception errors accumulate over time, and outdated points persist after objects move or disappear. Although recent dynamic mapping methods update object-level representations in changing scenes, they do not explicitly revise noisy or obsolete points within each object. We propose an online refinable semantic mapping framework that continuously refines object representations through probabilistic point-level confidence updating. Each object point maintains a confidence score that is updated online using multi-view temporal evidence: consistent observations reinforce reliable points, while inconsistent segmentation masks, depth measurements, and visibility cues suppress spurious and outdated points. Combined with object tracking and re-identification to preserve instance identities under motion and relocation, our framework enables object-centric semantic maps to be continuously refined rather than monotonically accumulated. Experiments demonstrate improved mapping accuracy over the previous method by 3.46% on Replica and 2.55% on ScanNet, show robustness in dynamic environments and under perception noise, and provide an effective spatial memory for object navigation and embodied question-answering with success rates of 82.4% and 76.7%.
2610.31476.tldr_en: This work proposes an online refinable semantic mapping framework that continuously refines object representations through probabilistic point-level confidence updating, and enables object-centric semantic maps to be continuously refined rather than monotonically accumulated.

llm.title_ja: 空間理解のためのポイントレベル精緻化可能セマンティックマッピング
llm.tldr_ja: マルチビューの時間的証拠を用いて確率的ポイントレベルの信頼度更新によりオブジェクト表現を継続的に精緻化する、オンライン精緻化可能セマンティックマッピングフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のオブジェクト中心セマンティックマップは静的環境向けに設計されており、追加のみのポイント統合戦略を用いるため、時間の経過とともに誤差が蓄積すること。
llm.method: 各オブジェクトポイントがオンラインで更新される信頼度スコアを保持し、一貫した観測は信頼性を補強し、不一致なセグメンテーションなどは誤った古いポイントを抑制する。
llm.result: ReplicaおよびScanNetで従来法と比較してマッピング精度がそれぞれ3.46%および2.55%向上し、動的環境での堅牢性を示した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックマッピング
オープンボキャブラリー

2610.31474.title: Skeleton-Grounded Latent Action Model for Robot World Models
2610.31474.abstract: Robot world models simulate how environments evolve in response to robot actions. Latent action models enable learning dynamics from videos by encoding visual transitions as proxy actions. However, reconstruction-driven latent actions mix robot motion with object responses and other scene changes, complicating their correspondence with robot controls. We propose SkeLAM, a skeleton-guided latent action model for controllable robot world modeling. SkeLAM decomposes latent actions into a kinematic component grounded by robot skeleton supervision and a residual component retaining complementary visual dynamics. Cross-modal swap reconstruction encourages RGB-derived and skeleton-derived kinematic representations to be interchangeable during video reconstruction. The world model incorporates both components through separate conditioning pathways, while branch dropout reduces its dependence on future-derived residual information. A lightweight adapter maps robot actions to the kinematic space, and subsequent world-model fine-tuning adapts generation to these predicted conditions. At inference, the model generates future observations from the current observation and robot actions. On DROID, SkeLAM reduces end-effector ADE by 19.5% and LPIPS by 11.1% compared with DreamDojo. Motion probing supports kinematic specialization, while qualitative results demonstrate zero-shot human-to-robot motion transfer in generated rollouts. Policy evaluation shows agreement between predicted success rates and those measured in real robot executions.
2610.31474.tldr_en: SkeLAM is proposed, a skeleton-guided latent action model for controllable robot world modeling that decomposes latent actions into a kinematic component grounded by robot skeleton supervision and a residual component retaining complementary visual dynamics.
2610.31474.hf_summary_en: SkeLAM decomposes latent actions into skeleton-guided kinematic and residual components to improve controllable robot world modeling and motion transfer.

llm.title_ja: ロボット世界モデルのためのスケルトン接地型潜在行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットのスケルトン監視によって接地された運動学的コンポーネントと残差コンポーネントに潜在行動を分解し、制御可能なロボット世界モデルを実現する「SkeLAM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 再構築駆動型の潜在行動は、ロボットの動きと物体の応答やその他のシーンの変化を混同するため、ロボットの制御との対応付けが複雑になる。
llm.method: ロボットスケルトン監視による運動学的コンポーネントと補完的な視覚ダイナミクスを保持する残差コンポーネントに分解し、クロスモーダルスワップ再構築を用いてモデルを訓練した。
llm.result: DROIDにおいて、DreamDojoと比較してエンドエフェクターのADEを19.5%、LPIPSを11.1%削減し、ゼロショットでの人間からロボットへのモーション転移を実証した。

2610.31472.title: VecTile: A Low-Cost Flexible Tactile Array for 3-DoF Force Sensing
2610.31472.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with contact information difficult to obtain from vision alone. Shear force is particularly important for understanding tangential contact, guiding corrective motions, and maintaining grasp stability, yet flexible and low-cost tactile arrays often measure only normal force. We introduce VecTile, a low-cost, 6 mm thin, flexible tactile array capable of three-axis force sensing. VecTile combines a piezoresistive layer with passive silicone nubs that convert normal and shear forces into distinguishable pressure patterns. The sensor can be fabricated in-house without specialized equipment. The complete system costs less than 35 USD for a 4x4 array. We validate the sensing mechanism through finite element analysis and hardware experiments. In controlled single-taxel tests over 1-5 N normal force and up to 1.5 N shear force, VecTile achieves root-mean-square errors of 0.39 N and 0.16 N for normal and shear forces. A VecTile calibrated while flat retains accuracy when curved, while a five-minute manual calibration is sufficient for practical use. Two applications demonstrate its utility. First, shear readings are sensitive enough to stop a sharp scalpel from puncturing a balloon after contact. Second, the sensor substantially improves Diffusion Policy-guided power-plug insertion. All designs and code will be released upon paper acceptance. Project website: https://jiannnh.github.io/VecTile/.
2610.31472.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2027

llm.title_ja: VecTile: 3自由度力センシングのための低コストで柔軟な触覚アレイ
llm.tldr_ja: 法線力とせん断力を識別可能な圧力パターンに変換する、低コストで厚さ6mmの柔軟な3軸力センシング触覚アレイ「VecTile」を開発し、実験によりその性能を検証した。
llm.problem: 柔軟で低コストな触覚アレイは法線力のみを測定することが多く、接線方向の接触把握や把持安定性に不可欠なせん断力の測定が困難である。
llm.method: 圧電抵抗層と受動的なシリコン突起を組み合わせ、法線力とせん断力を圧力パターンとして識別する厚さ6mmの柔軟な触覚アレイを開発した。
llm.result: 1〜5Nの法線力と最大1.5Nのせん断力において、法線力0.39N、せん断力0.16NのRMSEを達成し、バルーンの穿刺防止やプラグ挿入を改善した。

2610.31432.title: A Sparse Topometric Graph for Scalable Cross-Session Indoor Navigation
2610.31432.abstract: A conventional embodied agent in an indoor environment builds a map by accumulating noisy real-world measurements and results from heavy inference to guide navigation. While the detailed measurements may differ due to scene changes or sensor settings, the unique topological structure of navigable passages or the connectivity between rooms may provide training-free guidance that complements local observations. We propose a sparse topometric graph as an efficient structural representation for robust indoor navigation, alleviating the need for fine-grained matching, which is computationally expensive, memory-intensive, and prone to real-world variations. The map consists of nodes that encode local 3D geometry and distance-weighted edges that capture traversable connectivity. A learned graph-matching network finds consistent subgraph structures across sessions by considering both node-level geometric descriptors and neighborhood connectivity. The holistic contextual matching is robust to local ambiguities caused by weak distinctiveness or repetitive structure, and establishes stable correspondences despite local scene changes, different sensor modalities, or limited spatial overlap. We analyze the practicality of the graph through cross-session point-goal navigation, where a goal specified in a prior reference map must be reached from an unknown initial pose in a later session. Experiments show that our method achieves the highest success rates (77.1% on Gibson and 40.0% under 3D-FRONT scene changes), while reducing memory by more than two orders of magnitude compared to point-level representations. The proposed approach further supports cross-session alignment and goal-directed navigation with strong scalability and robust real-world transfer.
2610.31432.tldr_en: A sparse topometric graph is proposed as an efficient structural representation for robust indoor navigation, alleviating the need for fine-grained matching, and supports cross-session alignment and goal-directed navigation with strong scalability and robust real-world transfer.

llm.title_ja: スケーラブルなセッション間屋内ナビゲーションのためのスパース・トポメトリック・グラフ
llm.tldr_ja: スパース・トポメトリック・グラフを効率的な構造表現として提案し、計算コストの高い微細なマッチングを不要にしながら、セッション間のアライメントとゴール指向ナビゲーションを高いスケーラビリティで実現した。
llm.problem: 従来の屋内ナビゲーションは、詳細な測定値の蓄積によるマップ構築に依存しており、シーンの変化やセンサ設定の違いに対して高コストで脆弱である。
llm.method: 局所的な3D幾何学と距離重み付きエッジを持つノードからなるスパース・トポメトリック・グラフを構築し、学習済みグラフマッチングネットワークでサブグラフ構造を照合する。
llm.result: Gibsonで77.1%、3D-FRONTで40.0%の最高成功率を達成し、ポイントレベル表現と比較してメモリを2桁以上削減した。

2610.31429.title: PhysTrace: Interpretable Temporal Evaluation of Physical Consistency in Video Generative Models
2610.31429.abstract: World action models increasingly rely on pretrained video models assumed to capture physical dynamics for prediction, planning, and action generation. Existing evaluations assess plausibility, probe representations, or measure predictive surprise, but rarely identify which history-conditioned physical expectations conflict with observations. We introduce PhysTrace, a training-free framework aligning MLLM-generated, history-conditioned expectations with observed video windows to temporally localize physical violations and provide interpretable descriptions without task-specific probes or classifiers. We also introduce IntPhys2-Timing, adding violation intervals to IntPhys2. PhysTrace achieves a Hit Rate of up to 70.7% across physical principles on IntPhys2-Timing and outperforms the compared methods in overall possible-impossible discrimination accuracy on IntPhys2. Applied to reconstructed videos along the trajectories of pretrained diffusion/flow-based video models, PhysTrace reveals attribute- and noise-dependent patterns in physical violation localization, enabling interpretable physical consistency analysis across timesteps.
2610.31429.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures (including supplementary material). Code: https://github.com/PhysTrace/PhysTrace
2610.31429.tldr_en: PhysTrace is introduced, a training-free framework that uses MLLMs to formulate history-conditioned physical expectations and tracks their agreement with observed video windows through temporal video--language alignment, rather than relying on direct plausibility judgments or task-specific probes.

llm.title_ja: PhysTrace: 動画生成モデルにおける物理的一貫性の解釈可能な時間的評価
llm.tldr_ja: トレーニング不要のフレームワーク「PhysTrace」を導入し、MLLMが生成した履歴条件付き期待値と観測された動画ウィンドウを整合させることで、タスク固有のプローブなしに物理的違反を時間的に特定し解釈可能な記述を提供する。
llm.problem: 既存の評価法は妥当性の評価や驚きの測定を行うが、履歴に依存した物理的期待値のどこが観測と矛盾しているかを特定することは稀である。
llm.method: MLLMが生成した履歴条件付き期待値と観測動画を整合させ、タスク固有のプローブや分類器なしに物理的違反を時間的にローカライズするトレーニング不要のフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: IntPhys2-Timingで物理原則にわたり最大70.7%のヒット率を達成し、IntPhys2での可能な・不可能な状況の識別精度において既存手法を上回った。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2610.31427.title: FastHarness: Experience-Driven Review Scheduling for Vision-Language-Action Policies
2610.31427.abstract: Agentic robot systems combine language-model reasoning with robot policies to monitor execution and recover from failures. However, reviewing every action chunk incurs substantial overhead, even in familiar situations. We introduce FastHarness, an experience-driven execution harness that adaptively schedules GPT-6 Astra supervision of a π0.5 policy. A fast path uses stage memory and reviewed outcomes to reduce review frequency as experience accumulates, while a complementary recovery path focuses supervision on correcting errors. Once recovery is verified, routine execution resumes, with failure experience retained to guide future interventions. The policy remains frozen and generates fresh actions from current observations. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, reviewer token use decreases by an average of 57.2% per task from the first evaluated episode to the mean of the final five episodes. Mean episode time decreases from 85.5 to 52.0 minutes over the same interval. On the same tasks, mean success increases from 80% for GPT-as-Policy (π0.5 + GPT-6 Astra) to 97.19% with FastHarness. These results highlight adaptive supervision as a practical route to more efficient agentic robotics without additional model training.
2610.31427.tldr_en: FastHarness, an experience-driven execution harness that adaptively schedules GPT-6 Astra supervision of a {\pi}0.5 policy, is introduced, highlighting adaptive supervision as a practical route to more efficient agentic robotics without additional model training.

llm.title_ja: FastHarness: 視覚言語行動ポリシーのための経験駆動型レビュー・スケジューリング
llm.tldr_ja: 経験駆動型の実行ハーネス「FastHarness」を導入し、追加のモデル学習なしでπ0.5ポリシーに対するGPT-6 Astraの監視を適応的にスケジューリングすることで、効率的なエージェント型ロボット工学を実現した。
llm.problem: すべての行動チャンクをレビューすることは、慣れた状況であっても多大なオーバーヘッドを発生させる。
llm.method: ステージメモリとレビュー済み結果を利用して経験の蓄積に伴いレビュー頻度を減らす高速パスと、エラー修正に焦点を当てるリカバリパスを組み合わせた実行ハーネスを導入する。
llm.result: シミュレーション化された4つの操作タスクにおいて、レビュートークン使用量が平均57.2%減少し、平均成功率が80%から97.19%に向上した。

2610.31423.title: FocusVLA: Future-Intent Guided Dynamic View Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.31423.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have become an important paradigm for robotic manipulation by unifying visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Since reliable manipulation requires sufficient observation of objects, end-effectors, and their spatial relationships, multi-view inputs are widely used to provide complementary spatial information. However, our experiments show that existing VLA models do not fully exploit such multi-view complementarity. The policy tends to persistently rely on the wrist view, lacking the ability to dynamically adjust global-local view dependency across manipulation stages, which limits stage adaptability and robustness. To address this issue, we propose FocusVLA, a stage-aware multi-view routing framework. FocusVLA predicts future interaction intent from historical actions and uses it to guide dynamic view routing during action generation. By adaptively coordinating global and local observations across different task stages, FocusVLA improves multi-view utilization. On RoboTwin 2.0, FocusVLA improves the average success rate over the strongest baseline $π_{0.5}$ by 10.10 pp. In real-world evaluation, FocusVLA improves the success rate from 71.7\% to 85.0\%, achieving a 13.3\% gain over $π_{0.5}$. Moreover, the intent prediction and dynamic routing modules of FocusVLA can be integrated into existing VLA frameworks without modifying their core architectures.
2610.31423.tldr_en: FocusVLA is proposed, a stage-aware multi-view routing framework that predicts future interaction intent from historical actions and uses it to guide dynamic view routing during action generation and improves multi-view utilization on RoboTwin 2.0.
2610.31423.hf_summary_en: FocusVLA improves robotic manipulation by dynamically routing between global and local camera views based on predicted interaction intent across task stages.

llm.title_ja: FocusVLA: 将来の意図に誘導された視覚言語行動モデルのための動的視点ルーティング
llm.tldr_ja: ステージ認識型のマルチビュー・ルーティングフレームワーク「FocusVLA」を提案し、過去の行動から将来の意図を予測して動的な視点ルーティングを誘導することでマルチビューの活用を改善した。
llm.problem: 既存のVLAモデルはマルチビューの相補性を十分に活用しておらず、手首視点に固執して操作ステージに応じた大域的・局所的視点の動的な調整能力を欠いている。
llm.method: 過去の行動から将来のインタラクション意図を予測し、行動生成中の動的視点ルーティングを誘導するステージ認識型のマルチビュー・ルーティングフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0において最強のベースラインπ0.5を10.10ポイント上回り、実世界評価では成功率を71.7%から85.0%に向上させた。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.31384.title: CoHelix: Event-Based Multi-Propeller Rotation-Rate Tracking with Shared Projective Geometry
2610.31384.abstract: Estimating propeller rates from a moving event camera requires separating blade rotation from the changing image geometry. Background activity mixes with blade events, while repeated blade appearances admit half- and double-rate ambiguities. We propose CoHelix, a recursive filter that estimates one shared homography and separate rotation states for four rigidly mounted, coplanar propellers. Each admitted event updates its assigned rotation state, and its accepted geometry measurements correct the shared homography used to interpret later events from every propeller. We report lock, the fraction of evaluated time for which an estimate remains within 2% of synchronized ground truth, because mean error alone does not show how long a tracker follows the true rate. With fixed-rate initialization, leave-one-recording-out evaluation on moving-camera data gives CoHelix 62.9% lock, compared with 39.8% for HelixTrack and 22.2% for EventPro. With other settings fixed, allowing four geometry contributors instead of one raises lock from 3.4% to 62.9%.
