On a private target-follower dataset with a different target quadcopter, CoHelix retains the measurement settings selected on moving-camera data and uses a fixed initial rate. It reaches 95.9% lock, compared with 56.2% for HelixTrack and 61.1% for EventPro.
2610.31384.tldr_en: This work proposes CoHelix, a recursive filter that estimates one shared homography and separate rotation states for four rigidly mounted, coplanar propellers, and reports lock, the fraction of evaluated time for which an estimate remains within 2% of synchronized ground truth.

llm.title_ja: CoHelix: 共有射影幾何を用いたイベントベースの複数プロペラ回転数追跡
llm.tldr_ja: 移動式イベントカメラを用いた複数プロペラの回転数推定のために、共有ホモグラフィと分離された回転状態を推定する再帰フィルタ「CoHelix」を提案した。
llm.problem: 移動中のイベントカメラからのプロペラ回転数の推定では、ブレードの回転と変化する画像幾何学の分離が必要であり、背景活動や半・倍率の曖昧さが課題となる。
llm.method: 4つの剛体マウントされた同一平面上のプロペラについて、1つの共有ホモグラフィと個別の回転状態を再帰的に推定するフィルタを提案する。
llm.result: 移動カメラデータにおいてHelixTrackの39.8%やEventProの22.2%を上回る62.9%のロック率を達成し、ターゲット追従データセットでは95.9%に達した。

2610.31371.title: Probabilistic Energy Modeling Unifies Versatile Swarm Control
2610.31371.abstract: Robotic swarms must coordinate across diverse missions, yet existing controllers often require redesign, retuning, or retraining when objectives change. Here we show that probabilistic energy modeling provides a unifying representation for versatile swarm control, in which diverse missions emerge from compositions of shared interaction principles rather than task-specific control formulations. By exploiting the correspondence between Gibbs random field energy minimization and structured reward maximization, we encode fundamental swarm behaviors as reusable energy terms within a unified probabilistic objective. Decentralized policies trained within this representation are composed into a single controller through lightweight policy gating, without retraining. An interpretable action-attention mechanism captures non-uniform local interactions, while dimensionless normalization supports transfer across swarm scales and platforms. Demonstrated on aerial swarms, the unified policy generalizes zero-shot across six mission classes, 10-100 agents, two hardware platforms, and indoor cluttered and GPS-denied woodland environments. Large-scale simulations achieve 0.96-1.00 task success rates with 1-10 ms per-agent inference latency, while physical deployments confirm zero-shot transfer to real platforms and unstructured environments. These results establish probabilistic energy modeling as a scalable and transferable framework for decentralized swarm control.
2610.31371.tldr_en: This work shows that probabilistic energy modeling provides a unifying representation for versatile swarm control, in which diverse missions emerge from compositions of shared interaction principles rather than task-specific control formulations.

llm.title_ja: 確率的エネルギーモデリングによる汎用的な群制御の統合
llm.tldr_ja: 確率的エネルギーモデリングが汎用的な群制御の統一的表現を提供することを示し、共有されるインタラクション原理の組み合わせにより多様なミッションを実現した。
llm.problem: ロボット群は多様なミッション間で協調する必要があるが、既存の制御器は目的が変わるたびに再設計、再チューニング、または再学習を必要とする。
llm.method: ギブス確率場のエネルギー最小化と報酬最大化の対応関係を利用し、基礎的な群行動を統一的な確率的目的に再利用可能なエネルギー項としてエンコードする。
llm.result: 6つのミッションクラス、10〜100機のマルチエージェント環境においてゼロショット汎化を実証し、大規模シミュレーションで0.96〜1.00の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 確率的エネルギーモデル

2610.31334.title: GelSlim 5.0: Unifying Vision and Touch with a Single Fingertip Camera
2610.31334.abstract: Vision and touch provide complementary cues for object pose and local contact geometry, but external cameras are often occluded at the contact site. We present GelSlim 5.0, a fingertip sensor that acquires visual and tactile observations with one fixed camera and a continuous UV-responsive contact layer. By switching illumination, the camera sequentially acquires through-membrane visual images and contact-sensitive tactile images from a shared viewpoint, avoiding inter-camera extrinsic calibration. To combine these observations, we introduce VisTacFusion, a multimodal transformer with separate prediction paths for planar object pose and contact geometry. Asymmetric bottleneck fusion incorporates visual context while preserving tactile spatial features for depth and surface-normal estimation. Modality dropout enables inference with paired inputs or either modality alone. On real validation data from 12 known objects, paired inputs reduce depth MSE, angular error, and translation $L_1$ by 61.2%, 72.3%, and 61.3%, respectively, relative to tactile-only inference with the same model. Relative to visual-only inference, the corresponding reductions are 93.7%, 6.1%, and 8.6%.
2610.31334.tldr_en: VisTacFusion, a multimodal transformer with separate prediction paths for planar object pose and contact geometry is introduced, a multimodal transformer with separate prediction paths for planar object pose and contact geometry that incorporates visual context while preserving tactile spatial features for depth and surface-normal estimation.

llm.title_ja: GelSlim 5.0: 単一の指先カメラによる視覚と触覚の統合
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚と触覚の観察を1台の固定カメラで取得する指先センサーGelSlim 5.0を提案し、平面物体の姿勢と接触形状の予測精度を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 外部カメラによる接触部位のオクルージョンや、複数カメラ間での外部キャリブレーションの難しさ。
llm.method: 照射を切り替えて視覚画像と触覚画像を順次取得し、マルチモーダルTransformer「VisTacFusion」で統合する。
llm.result: ペアの入力により、触覚のみの推論に比べて深度のMSE、角度誤差、位置のL1誤差がそれぞれ61.2%、72.3%、61.3%減少した。

2610.31302.title: Whole-Body Motion Guided Reference Generation for Uncertainty-Aware Compliant Assistance
2610.31302.abstract: Exoskeletons have shown great potential for augmenting human physical capabilities, yet generating reliable assistance remains challenging because human motion patterns and interaction requirements vary substantially in practice. To address this problem, a dual-loop assistance strategy is proposed to couple multimodal exoskeleton trajectory generation with variable admittance control, where trajectory variance links the outer-loop generator and the inner-loop controller. The generator synthesizes future exoskeleton trajectories through denoising, primarily using whole-body human motion and exoskeleton proprioception, with task descriptions as auxiliary semantic cues. To reduce cross-modal representation mismatch, a three-stage training pipeline is introduced to progressively optimize the human motion encoder, the exoskeleton proprioception encoder, and the trajectory generator. In the inner loop, multiple future trajectories are sampled from the generator to estimate the trajectory mean and variance. The mean is used as the control reference, while the variance provides an uncertainty measure for prediction reliability. This measure is further incorporated into a stiffness regulation law, enabling compliant assistance with input-to-state stability under bounded lumped interaction input. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces muscle activation levels compared with standard baselines, while also decreasing users' metabolic energy expenditure relative to the unassisted condition.
2610.31302.comment: Withdrawal requested because not all co-authors had consented to the submission of this manuscript to arXiv

llm.title_ja: 不確かさを考慮したコンプライアントな補助のための全身運動誘導型リファレンス生成
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダルな外骨格の軌道生成と可変アドミタンス制御を結合した二重ループ支援戦略により、筋肉の活動レベルと代謝エネルギー消費量を削減した。
llm.problem: 人間の動きのパターンやインタラクションの要件が実環境で大きく変動するため、信頼性の高い補助の生成が困難であること。
llm.method: デノイジングを用いて将来の外骨格軌道を合成する生成器と、予測の信頼性を不確かさ指標として利用する可変アドミタンス制御の組み合わせ。
llm.result: 提案手法により、標準的なベースラインと比較して筋肉の活性化レベルが大幅に低下し、未補助状態と比較してユーザーの代謝エネルギー消費量も減少した。

2610.31299.title: PiHand: Latent Hand-Object Interaction Priors for Physics-Based Policy Learning
2610.31299.abstract: Synthesizing physically grounded dexterous hand-object interactions is important for VR/AR, gaming, and robotics, yet remains challenging because subtle contact dynamics, diverse object geometries, and target trajectories must be jointly respected while maintaining natural grasps. Existing methods either track mocap trajectories with limited transfer to novel objects, or rely on hand-only generative priors that fail to capture coupled hand-object motion, sacrificing contact fidelity and sample efficiency. To tackle these challenges, we introduce PiHand, a Physically grounded Interaction-aware Hand motion synthesis framework. PiHand first trains expert policies that track mocap demonstrations in simulation, distills them into a unified hand-object interaction prior using a goal-conditioned VAE, and finally solve diverse dexterous manipulation tasks through bounded residual exploration in its latent space. With only a single reward and no complex curriculum training, this yields general tabletop manipulation policies that generalize to unseen objects and trajectories on GRAB and DexYCB. The same prior transfers to object catching and bimanual handover, two tasks that are rarely seen in its training data. Across all tasks, PiHand consistently outperforms baselines in all metrics. We will release the processed data and model checkpoints.
2610.31299.tldr_en: PiHand is introduced, a Physically grounded Interaction-aware Hand motion synthesis framework that trains expert policies that track mocap demonstrations in simulation, distills them into a unified hand-object interaction prior using a goal-conditioned VAE, and finally solve diverse dexterous manipulation tasks through bounded residual exploration in its latent space.

llm.title_ja: PiHand: 物理ベースのポリシー学習のための潜在的な手と物体の相互作用事前分布
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的に裏付けられたインタラクションを考慮したハンドモーション合成フレームワーク「PiHand」を導入し、多様な器用な操作タスクを解決した。
llm.problem: 自然な把握を維持しながら、微妙な接触ダイナミクス、多様な物体の形状、目標軌道を同時に満たす物理的に自然な器用な把持の合成が困難であること。
llm.method: シミュレーションでモーキャップデモンストレーションを追従するエキスパートポリシーを訓練し、条件付きVAEを用いて統合された手と物体の相互作用事前分布に蒸留する。
llm.result: GRABおよびDexYCBにおいて、未見の物体や軌道に汎化し、すべての指標でベースラインを一貫して上回る性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ハンド・オブジェクト相互作用

2610.31275.title: Learning Robot Behavior Priors from Non-Robotic Synthetic Data
2610.31275.abstract: Real robot data, rich across tasks and morphologies, is often treated as the bottleneck for training robot learning models, including embodied foundation models that aim for zero-shot physical transfer. In this paper, we investigate the degree to which such models can acquire necessary structure using data from systems without embodiment. To this end, we test if inexpensive, procedurally generated synthetic data can yield useful priors before a model observes any real-world behavior. We study this through robot action prediction, a natural pretraining objective and a direct test of whether structure learned from arbitrary synthetic tasks transfers to embodied settings. We introduce three data generation pipelines that model mathematical abstractions of robotic control, and use them as pretraining priors for a Transformer. We demonstrate that a model trained purely on this non-robotic data attains non-trivial zero-shot prediction performance on unseen physical robot tasks via an in-context learning mechanism, and that our specialized control priors notably improve upon generic causal priors. We also compare against a compute-matched baseline trained on real robot data, and find that it outperforms our model but only on the datasets it was trained on. These findings suggest that procedurally generated, mathematical abstractions can yield useful robotic priors, offering a potential complement to expensive embodied data collection.
2610.31275.tldr_en: It is demonstrated that a model trained purely on this non-robotic data attains non-trivial zero-shot prediction performance on unseen physical robot tasks via an in-context learning mechanism, and that the authors' specialized control priors notably improve upon generic causal priors.

llm.title_ja: 非ロボット系合成データからのロボット行動事前分布の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 非ロボット系タスクの合成データから学習した構造が、インコンテキスト学習メカニズムを通じて未見の物理ロボットタスクへのゼロショット予測性能を達成することを示した。
llm.problem: タスクや形態に富んだ実際のロボットデータの収集が高価であり、ロボット学習モデルの学習におけるボトルネックとなっていること。
llm.method: ロボット制御の数学的抽象化をモデル化する3つのデータ生成パイプラインを導入し、それらをTransformerの事前学習用事前分布として使用する。
llm.result: 非ロボットデータのみで訓練されたモデルが、インコンテキスト学習を通じて未見の物理ロボットタスクで非自明なゼロショット予測性能を達成することを示した。
keywords_ja: インコンテキスト学習

2610.31221.title: Consistent Distributed Invariant EKF SLAM with Point and Object Features
2610.31221.abstract: Multi-robot SLAM allows robots to improve their estimates by exchanging map information, but repeated exchanges create unknown correlations between local estimators. Covariance intersection (CI) can fuse estimates without tracking these correlations. In right-invariant extended Kalman filter (RI-EKF) SLAM, however, point features obtain their invariant errors through the robot rotation, so a neighbor's map estimate is expressed in its own error coordinates and is correlated with its pose, and cannot be fused by CI directly. This paper presents Joint-CI, a unified fusion method for distributed RI-EKF SLAM with point, object, and mixed point--object maps. Using a neighboring robot's local posterior and an inter-robot observation, a joint estimate of the receiving robot's pose and the common features is constructed in the receiving robot's error coordinates, retaining the robot--feature and feature--feature correlations. Partial-state CI then fuses this estimate with the receiving robot's local posterior. We show that the unified formulation and the fusion preserve the six unobservable directions associated with global rotation and translation, and that communication and fusion preserve first-order covariance consistency given consistent local posteriors. Monte Carlo simulations and a real-world dataset-derived experiment show that Joint-CI improves estimation accuracy while maintaining consistent, mildly conservative uncertainty.
2610.31221.comment: Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
2610.31221.tldr_en: Joint-CI is presented, a unified fusion method for distributed RI-EKF SLAM with point, object, and mixed point--object maps that improves estimation accuracy while maintaining consistent, mildly conservative uncertainty.

llm.title_ja: 点および物体特徴を用いた一貫した分散型不変EKF SLAM
llm.tldr_ja: 点地図、物体地図、およびその混合地図を持つ分散型RI-EKF SLAMのための統一された融合手法「Joint-CI」を提案し、推定精度を向上させた。
llm.problem: マルチロボットSLAMにおける地図情報の繰り返し交換が未知の相関を生み出し、共分散intersection（CI）による直接的な融合を妨げること。
llm.method: 受信ロボットの誤差座標系において、受信側の局所事後確率とロボット間観測を用いた姿勢と共通特徴の結合推定値を構築し、部分状態CIで融合する。
llm.result: モンテカルロシミュレーションおよび実世界データセット実験により、一貫した保守的な不確かさを維持しながら推定精度が向上することが示された。
keywords_ja: 拡張カルマンフィルタ

2610.31194.title: Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models
2610.31194.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models in latent space, enabling efficient planning but leaving their states opaque. We introduce Inside-JEPA, which places relational channels for ordered entity pairs inside the JEPA latent state and shows that an inverse-dynamics loss can ground these channels without relation labels when its head reads them, either alone or as part of the full state. On Something-Something V2, latent prediction alone performs no better than a random relation head, while inverse-dynamics supervision that recovers actions from channel changes improves relational AUROC by .065-.103 across ten settings with annotated boxes, by .081 on RH20T robot episodes with held-out tasks, and by .050-.061 across five relations using off-the-shelf detection and tracking. An inverse head on entity latents decodes actions more accurately but barely improves relational grounding; shuffled labels, two label-free objectives, and action labels on only 5% of the pairs also fail to ground the channels. Given an action, predicted relational changes approach the quality of observed future relations (AUROC .599 vs .621). For one-step relational goals, a supervised readout of the 16 channels ranks the correct action among the top five of 65 in 43% of cases, compared with 24% for prediction-only latents and 17% for a frequency prior.
2610.31194.tldr_en: Inside-JEPA is introduced, which places relational channels for ordered entity pairs inside the JEPA latent state and shows that an inverse-dynamics loss can ground these channels without relation labels when its head reads them, either alone or as part of the full state.

llm.title_ja: Inside-JEPA: 潜在世界モデルにおける予測から関係的グラウンディングへ
llm.tldr_ja: JEPAの潜在状態内に順序付きエンティティペアのリレーショナルチャネルを配置し、逆ダイナミクス損失が関係ラベルなしでこれらのチャネルをグラウンドできることを示した。
llm.problem: JEPAは潜在空間で世界モデルを学習し効率的な計画を可能にするが、その状態の内部が不透明であること。
llm.method: JEPAの潜在状態内に順序付きエンティティペアのためのリレーショナルチャネルを配置し、チャネルの変更から行動を復元する逆ダイナミクス損失による監督を行う。
llm.result: 逆ダイナミクス監督により、10個の設定でリレーショナルAUROCが0.065〜0.103向上し、行動が与えられた際に予測された関係的変化が観測された将来の関係の品質に近づいた。

2610.31186.title: RaSFNet: Ray-aligned and Scan-aware Fusion Network for LiDAR Semantic Segmentation
2610.31186.abstract: LiDAR point cloud semantic segmentation is a fundamental component of 3D perception for autonomous driving and robotics. Projection-based methods map 3D point clouds into 2D representations for feature extraction using 2D networks. However, aggregating multiple points during projection can obscure geometric differences within each frustum, while local feature extraction limits the modeling of spatial relationships across scanning regions. Moreover, proximity in the projected representation does not necessarily imply proximity in 3D space, and interactions between point and projected features may mix features from different ranges, reducing semantic discriminability. To address these challenges, we propose the Ray-aligned and Scan-aware Fusion Network (RaSFNet), which incorporates point cloud geometry and LiDAR scanning characteristics into projection-based semantic segmentation. Specifically, the Ray-Aligned Geometric Distribution Encoding (RAGDE) module characterizes point distributions within each frustum using a ray-aligned coordinate system. To model spatial context, a Scan-Topology-Aware Mamba (STAM) block organizes frustum features according to the LiDAR azimuth sampling pattern and captures long-range dependencies across scanning regions. In addition, a Range-Constrained Point-Frustum Fusion (RCPFF) mechanism uses shared range information to guide feature exchange between point and frustum representations while maintaining spatial correspondence. RaSFNet achieves mIoU scores of 70.2% and 77.7% on the SemanticKITTI and nuScenes validation sets, respectively, indicating competitive segmentation performance compared with the evaluated methods.
2610.31186.tldr_en: The Ray-aligned and Scan-aware Fusion Network (RaSFNet) is proposed, which incorporates point cloud geometry and LiDAR scanning characteristics into projection-based semantic segmentation and achieves competitive segmentation performance compared with the evaluated methods.

llm.title_ja: RaSFNet: LiDARセマンティックセグメンテーションのためのレイ整列およびスキャン認識型融合ネットワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 点群の幾何学特性とLiDARスキャン特性を投影ベースのセマンティックセグメンテーションに組み込んだRaSFNetを提案し、競合するセグメンテーション性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 3D点群を2D表現に投影する際、複数点の集約によって錐台内の幾何学的差異が隠されたり、投影表現上の近接が必ずしも3D空間上の近接を意味しないこと。
llm.method: レイ整列座標系を用いた錐台内の点分布符号化モジュール（RAGDE）、LiDAR方位サンプリングパターンに基づくスキャン・トポロジー認識Mambaブロック（STAM）等を導入する。
llm.result: SemanticKITTIおよびnuScenesの検証セットでそれぞれ70.2%および77.7%のmIoUスコアを達成し、競合手法と比較して優れたセグメンテーション性能を示した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックセグメンテーション

2610.31166.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2610.31166.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. We present WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. SAM3 tracks the task objects, and their events causally select key frames within an adaptive budget, which the action expert reads by cross-attention together with object tokens encoding appearance, geometry and time. We also contribute HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Keeping the right frames rather than more frames, WholeBodyMem surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines, raising its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on the real robot, while also improving the standard SIMPLE tasks (70.2% to 86.9%).
2610.31166.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Project page: https://memory-before-goal.github.io
2610.31166.tldr_en: W WholeBodyMem is presented, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal, which surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines and raises its base policy's success.

llm.title_ja: ゴール前の記憶: ヒューマノイドの移動・操作における事前履歴記憶の役割
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットがタスクを実行する前に目撃した物体イベントの事前履歴を保持する物体誘導型知覚記憶「WholeBodyMem」を提案し、ベースポリシーの成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 動的シーンにおけるヒューマノイドの移動・操作は非マルコフ的であり、対象が見えなくなったり視界から外れたりするにもかかわらず、従来のVLAポリシーは現在しか認識できないこと。
llm.method: SAM3でタスク対象を追跡し、適応型予算内でキーフレームを因果的に選択、行動エキスパートが外見・幾何学・時間をエンコードしたオブジェクトトークンと一緒にクロスアテンションで読み取る。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの成功率を29.1%から72.6%へ、実機ロボットで36.7%から88.3%へと向上させ、無記憶および一様記憶ベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.31162.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
2610.31162.abstract: Building virtual embodied agents that operate in open-ended games like human players is a long-standing goal requiring both long-horizon autonomy and reliable native-interface control. As a procedurally generated open world, Minecraft provides a natural testbed for studying the integration of these capabilities. Existing agents typically provide either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning executed through environment APIs or predefined skills. To bridge this gap, we propose HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness. At the orchestration level, we equip the harness with structured memory for tracking progress and a VLM planner for selecting subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. To reliably determine subtask completion, we further introduce a policy-coupled task completion state detector that conditions on VLA policy context to signal candidate completion. At the control level, a single VLA executes all subtasks with vision-only perception and native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between heterogeneous GUI and non-GUI interactions, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings. We also train the VLA through world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with environment feedback to improve reliability and recovery. HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, while also completing long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch like human players.
2610.31162.tldr_en: This work proposes HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness that achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, while also completing long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch like human players.
2610.31162.hf_summary_en: HiSTEVE is a hierarchical vision-language-action agent that combines long-horizon planning with native keyboard-and-mouse control to perform complex open-ended tasks in Minecraft.

llm.title_ja: HiSTEVE 1.0: オープンワールドゲームのためのヒューマンインタフェースVLAエージェントの活用
llm.tldr_ja: ケイパビリティ認識型のエージェントハーネスを備えた階層型VLAエージェント「HiSTEVE」を提案し、Minecraftにおいて高度な自律性と長期的タスクの遂行を達成した。
llm.problem: オープンエンドなゲームで人間のプレイヤーのように動作する仮想エージェントには、長期的自律性と信頼性の高いネイティブインターフェース制御の両方が必要であるが、既存のエージェントはどちらか一方しか提供していなかったこと。
llm.method: 進捗を追跡する構造化メモリとサブタスクを選択するVLMプランナーを持つハーネス、およびポリシー結合型タスク完了状態検出器とVLA制御の組み合わせ。
llm.result: MineStudio Benchで85.0%、OpenHAで37.4%の平均成功率を記録し、鉄のツルハシをゼロからクラフトするなどの長期的タスクを完了した。

2610.31156.title: Calibration-free IMU-based Relative Orientation Estimation under Dynamic Human Motion
2610.31156.abstract: Recent magnetometer-free inertial measurement unit (IMU) methods can reduce drift in joint motion estimation using rigid-body constraints, but they typically require pre-calibrated sensor locations, assumptions of specific joint models (e.g., hinge joints) or limited motion types, or an external reference for global orientation. Furthermore, challenges related to high-frequency impacts (e.g. at foot strikes during gait) and numerical differentiation of noisy measurements have not been explicitly addressed. We propose an extended Kalman filter that estimates relative IMU orientation and sensor location simultaneously, requiring neither offline sensor location calibration nor a global orientation anchor. A systematic simulation study shows that the quality of the relative orientation and the sensor location estimates depends on different motion-intensity sources: the joint center acceleration and the relative angular velocity, respectively. A low-pass filter (LPF) is used to mitigate real-signal outliers before applying the rigid-body constraint. When applied to the OpenSense dataset with real IMU measurements across four subjects with three lower-body joint types during walking and complex tasks including various motion types, the proposed method achieves an overall relative orientation error of 2.61°, compared with 10.40° for a baseline using offline-estimated sensor locations and 7.43° for a baseline using marker-derived sensor locations. These results show that the proposed calibration-free estimation framework handles real IMU data effectively and achieves accurate relative orientation without offline sensor location calibration.
2610.31156.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE Sensors Journal

llm.title_ja: 動的人体運動におけるキャリブレーション不要なIMUベースの相対方向推定
llm.tldr_ja: オフラインでのセンサー位置のキャリブレーションやグローバル方向アンカーを必要とせず、相対的なIMU方向とセンサー位置を同時に推定する拡張カルマンフィルタを提案した。
llm.problem: 最近の磁力計を用いないIMU手法は剛体制約を利用してドリフトを減らせるが、事前にキャリブレーションされたセンサー位置や特定関節モデルの仮定を必要とすること。
llm.method: 関節中心の加速度と相対角速度に基づく運動強度ソースを利用し、剛体制約を適用する前にローパスフィルタで実信号の外れ値を軽減する拡張カルマンフィルタ。
llm.result: 4被験者の下半身の歩行および複雑な動作のデータにおいて、全体的な相対方向誤差2.61°を達成し、従来ベースラインを大きく下回る誤差となった。
keywords_ja: 拡張カルマンフィルタ
センサーキャリブレーション

2610.31149.title: Navigating human-robot interaction challenges in private and residential aged care homes
2610.31149.abstract: This chapter explores how robotic systems and ambient intelligence can enhance care for older adults in residential aged care (RAC) homes and private homes. Although these settings differ, we frame both as extreme and challenging environments for human-robot interaction (HRI), characterised by cluttered and dynamic layouts, diverse resident needs, and limited on-site technical support. We review embodied and non-embodied systems that assist with daily living, safety monitoring, and social engagement, highlighting hybrid deployments where robots complement fixed and wearable sensors. To ensure these technologies are usable and effective, design considerations consider the cognitive, physical, and social needs of older adults. Interaction design prioritises accessibility for older adults with low digital literacy, using robust but simple voice interfaces, small sets of non-verbal cues, accessible screen-based companions, and safe object handovers. Privacy, trust, and acceptability are addressed via practical strategies such as on-device inference, data minimisation, visible consent controls, and transparent data handling aligned with emerging artificial intelligence (AI) and privacy regulation. Evaluation emphasises real-world metrics including false alarms per day, time to recover from faults, staff workload, and long-term system reliability. We close by outlining open research challenges and future directions for scalable, regulation-ready deployments that support aging with dignity, safety, and independence.
2610.31149.comment: Author-accepted manuscript of a book chapter published online in Elsevier's Reference Module in Materials Science and Materials Engineering (2026). Scheduled for inclusion in Comprehensive Robotics for Extreme and Challenging Environments (June 2027)
2610.31149.tldr_en: This chapter explores how robotic systems and ambient intelligence can enhance care for older adults in residential aged care (RAC) homes and private homes and outlines open research challenges and future directions for scalable, regulation-ready deployments that support aging with dignity, safety, and independence.

llm.title_ja: プライベートおよび高齢者居住ケア施設における人とロボットの相互作用の課題への対処
llm.tldr_ja: 居住型高齢者ケア施設や一般家庭における高齢者ケアを強化するためのロボットシステムやアンビエント知能の活用と、HRIの設計上の考慮事項について論じた。
llm.problem: 雑然とした動的なレイアウト、多様な居住者のニーズ、現場での限定的な技術サポートなど、過酷で挑戦的な環境でのHRIの実現。
llm.method: 高齢者の認知的・物理的・社会的ニーズを考慮した設計、音声インターフェースや安全なオブジェクト受渡しなどのインタラクション設計、デバイス上推論によるプライバシー保護。
llm.result: 尊厳、安全性、自立をサポートする、拡張可能で規制に対応した展開のためのオープンな研究課題と将来の方向性を提示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.31139.title: Pos4CHD: A Positive-Free Mask-Guided Counterfactual Synthesis Framework for Fetal Congenital Heart Defect Analysis
2610.31139.abstract: The scarcity of positive cases remains a major bottleneck in developing automated diagnostic systems for fetal Congenital Heart Defects~(CHDs), particularly for rare subtypes. Although normal cases are accessible with effort, positive cases are hard to collect due to low incidence rates and privacy concerns, causing severe class imbalance or absence of positive training samples. Existing works resort to synthesizing positives with conditional generative models, but they are task-specific and require positive training samples, hindering application for fetal CHDs. To this end, we propose a positive-free mask-guided counterfactual generation framework for fetal echocardiography, namely Pos4CHD, which enables realistic, high-quality synthesis of pseudo-positive samples from semantic masks, with only normal samples at hand. Technically, we first develop FE-Gen, a mask-guided generative model tailored for fetal heart ultrasound synthesis that mitigates histogram drift and enhances image-mask spatial alignment. Building on FE-Gen, Pos4CHD employs a mask-to-image generation paradigm for CHD synthesis. It first manipulates semantic masks to simulate fetal-heart structural anomalies and then renders anatomically consistent images. Extensive experiments on in-house datasets, together with expert evaluations, demonstrate the visual fidelity~($-12.97$ FID) and anatomical consistency~($+3.96\%$ DSC) of synthesized images. Further validations across diverse real-world CHD diagnosis tasks exhibit promising results and consistent increments, including zero-shot classification~(achieving $93.25\%$ ACC on EbA and $72.92\%$ ACC on TAPVC), lesion detection~($+6.95\%$ mAP50 on VSD), and anatomy segmentation~($+10.49\%$ DSC on fetal heart) compared with baselines. Codes and models are publicly available on \href{https://github.com/DREAMXFAR/Pos4CHD}{GitHub}.
2610.31139.comment: Submitted to IEEE TMI, under review
2610.31139.tldr_en: This work proposes a positive-free mask-guided counterfactual generation framework for fetal echocardiography, namely Pos4CHD, which enables realistic, high-quality synthesis of pseudo-positive samples from semantic masks, with only normal samples at hand.

llm.title_ja: Pos4CHD: 胎児先天性心疾患解析のためのポジティブサンプル不要のマスク誘導型反事実合成フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 正常なサンプルのみを手元に置き、セマンティックマスクから擬似陽性サンプルのリアルで高品質な合成を可能にするPos4CHDフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 胎児先天性心疾患（CHD）の自動診断システム開発において、正常例は入手可能である一方、陽性例は発生率の低さやプライバシーの懸念から収集が困難であること。
llm.method: ヒストグラムのドリフトを軽減し画像とマスクの空間的整合性を高める胎児ハート超音波合成向け生成モデルFE-Genを開発し、これを用いて構造異常をシミュレートする。
llm.result: 視覚的忠実度（-12.97 FID）と解剖学的一貫性（+3.96% DSC）が確認され、ゼロショット分類、病変検出、解剖学的セグメンテーションでベースラインを上回る結果を示した。

2610.31121.title: RGraph-Eval: Task-Grounded Scene Graphs for Evaluating Robot Video Generation
2610.31121.abstract: Generated robot videos can look convincing while depicting the wrong interaction: a different object is moved, a grasp disappears, or a placement ends outside its destination. We introduce RGraph-Eval, a reference-based framework that makes these discrepancies explicit through task-grounded temporal scene graphs. Unlike approaches that construct separate evidence representations for different evaluation dimensions, we organize task entities, interactions, and motion within a unified, interpretable scene graph representation. A foundation-model pipeline identifies manipulation roles, grounds persistent object masks, infers and verifies state transitions and action intervals, and reconstructs manipulated-object motion in three dimensions. Applying this representation to a generated video and a reference demonstration supports an interpretable RGraph-Eval score with visible-object, relation-change, and 3D path-shape components. We also introduce ShareRobot-SG, a collection of 1,000 manipulation scenes from ten ShareRobot sources annotated with the multimodal representation. Our evaluation separates graph-generation quality from agreement with human video judgments and includes comparisons with adapted SVG2 and SG-Ego, as well as a benchmark of three video generators. The framework connects robot-video assessment to the observable entities and interactions underlying a task while making the graph annotations reusable beyond evaluation. Code will be publicly available at https://github.com/SashaDance/rgraph-eval.
2610.31121.tldr_en: RGraph-Eval, a reference-based framework that connects robot-video assessment to the observable entities and interactions underlying a task while making the graph annotations reusable beyond evaluation, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: RGraph-Eval: ロボット動画生成評価のためのタスクグラウンド化シーングラフ
llm.tldr_ja: タスクのエンティティ、相互作用、モーションを統合された解釈可能なシーングラフ表現で整理し、生成されたロボット動画の評価を可能にするフレームワーク「RGraph-Eval」を提案した。
llm.problem: 生成されたロボット動画は、異なるオブジェクトが移動されたり把持が消えたりするなど、間違った相互作用を描写している場合でも説得力を持って見えてしまうこと。
llm.method: ファウンデーションモデルパイプラインにより、操作役割の特定、永続的オブジェクトマスクのグラウンド、状態遷移と行動間隔の推論・検証、3Dでの物体の動きの再構築を行う。
llm.result: 可視オブジェクト、関係の変化、3Dパス形状のコンポーネントを持つ解釈可能なスコアをサポートし、ヒューマンジャッジメントとの一致を確認した。
keywords_ja: タスクグラウンディング
ファウンデーションモデル

2610.31095.title: To Route or to Adapt? Multi-Expert Diffusion Planners in Unseen Regions
2610.31095.abstract: Diffusion trajectory planners with domain-specific experts face a practical question in unseen regions: can they rely on selecting among existing experts, or must the planner itself adapt? We study this question using a planner with a shared adapter and per-domain expert adapters. Across three real-world held-out maps, none of eight test-time routing schemes improves the fleet-mean lateral offset over the static default, which uses the same expert for every scene. Even an oracle that selects the best expert for each scene reduces the mean offset by only 0.9 m. In contrast, reward-based fine-tuning on just 20 target-region scenes yields substantially larger gains. On matched evaluation slices, joint replay achieves a fleet-mean offset of 6.9 m, compared with 12.4 m for the static default. Comparisons under the same target-region training budget show that target-region training drives the improvement, while replaying training scenes limits forgetting on the original ODDs. On nuPlan, fine-tuning across training cities also improves open-loop offsets, although closed-loop performance deteriorates. Further diagnostics reveal that two test-time adaptation baselines achieve low offsets by producing degenerate trajectories. These results show the limited headroom for selecting among existing experts and the greater open-loop gains available from adapting the planner.
2610.31095.comment: Accepted to the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). 36 pages. Code and weights: https://github.com/tlab-wide/RouteOrAdapt
2610.31095.tldr_en: Results show the limited headroom for selecting among existing experts and the greater open-loop gains available from adapting the planner, as well as the greater open-loop gains available from adapting the planner.

llm.title_ja: ルーティングか適応か？ 未見領域におけるマルチエキスパート拡散プランナー
llm.tldr_ja: ドメイン特化型エキスパートを持つ拡散軌道プランナーにおいて、既存のエキスパート選択には限界があり、プランナー自体の適応（ファインチューニング）がオープンループ性能の向上により大きく寄与することを示した。
llm.problem: 未見領域において、ドメイン特化型エキスパートを持つ拡散軌道プランナーが既存のエキスパートの中から選択に頼るべきか、プランナー自身が適応すべきかという疑問。
llm.method: 共有アダプターとドメイン別エキスパートアダプターを持つプランナーを用いて、テスト時のルーティング手法と報酬ベースのファインチューニングを比較する。
llm.result: 既存エキスパート選択のヘッドルームは限られている一方、目標領域のシーンでの報酬ベースのファインチューニングにより、平均オフセットが大幅に改善された。

2610.31080.title: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
2610.31080.abstract: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it. On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. Code: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent
2610.31080.tldr_en: The open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it, together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it.

llm.title_ja: nnInteractive Agent: 3D画像アノテーターとしての汎用AIエージェント
llm.tldr_ja: 汎用AIエージェントに空間プロンプトの指示やnnInteractiveツールの利用を組み込むことで、追加の訓練なしに自動で3D画像セグメンテーションのアノテーションを行えることを示した。
llm.problem: インタラクティブな3Dセグメンテーションモデルは正確なボリュメトリックマスクを生成できるが、構造の発見やプロンプトの配置などのアノテーション作業は依然として人間が行う必要があること。
llm.method: Model Context Protocol（MCP）を介してnnInteractiveをツールとして提供し、経験豊富なユーザーのプロンプト方法をエンコードしたスキルを持つオープンソースのnninteractive-agentを作成する。
llm.result: CT、MRI、PETなどの多様なベンチマークにおいて、Claude CodeやCodexが平均Dice 0.81〜0.84を達成し、プロンプトの配置を自動で行うことができた。
keywords_ja: ファウンデーションモデル

2610.31064.title: AstroBench: Benchmarking Free-Floating Capture and Space Robotic Manipulation
2610.31064.abstract: Capturing a loose object inside a spacecraft requires a robot to approach a target that can translate and rotate, and whose motion changes when contact is made. These conditions motivate evaluation beyond manipulation of supported objects. We introduce AstroBench, an open benchmark for free-floating capture and space robotic manipulation with a fixed-base arm. The task suite combines four initial-motion tracks with sample-storage operations based on MELFI hardware and cap and captive-screw servicing based on the Robotic Refueling Mission. The two workcells provide nine task definitions and 29 task-target combinations. A metadata-filtered Objaverse inventory supplies 8,414 object instances for asset expansion, alongside five cabin visual contexts and versioned task instructions. We report two acquisition-focused experiments using existing checkpoints. A frozen $π_{0.5}$ DROID joint-position policy captures 2 of 200 static targets and 4 of 200 moving targets across twenty object identities. A cube-specific ACT policy captures 8 of 10 static targets and 6 of 10 moving targets in a separate experiment. Each experiment retains its recorded observation, action and capture configuration. The results document difficult direct transfer for the tested generalist checkpoint and successful task-specific capture behavior, while identifying concrete settings for studying motion-aware perception and contact-sensitive control. Code, task definitions and editable workcell assets are available at https://github.com/AstroUpLab/AstroBench.
2610.31064.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Code and assets: https://github.com/AstroUpLab/AstroBench ; project website: https://astroup.com/astrobench/

llm.title_ja: AstroBench: 自由浮遊捕獲と宇宙ロボットマニピュレーションのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 固定ベースアームを用いた自由浮遊捕獲と宇宙ロボットマニピュレーションのためのオープンベンチマーク「AstroBench」を提案し、既存の汎用ポリシーとタスク特化ポリシーの性能を評価した。
llm.problem: 宇宙空間での物体の捕獲には、接触時に動きが変化する移動・回転するターゲットへのアプローチが必要であり、固定された物体の操作を超える評価の仕組みが必要であること。
llm.method: 初期モーショントラック、MELFIハードウェアに基づくサンプルストレージ操作、ロボット給油ミッションに基づくキャップおよびキャプティブスクリューの整備を組み合わせたワークセルとタスク定義を作成する。
llm.result: 汎用ジェネラリストチェックポイントの直接転送の難しさと、タスク特化型捕獲挙動の成功を実証し、動作認識知覚や接触感応制御の研究に向けた具体的な設定を特定した。

2610.31051.title: Tilt-Rotor Quadcopter with Learned Residual Control and Mode-Dependent State Estimation
2610.31051.abstract: Tilt-rotor quadcopters redirect thrust for translation without banking, but complicate modeling, state estimation, and disturbance rejection. This paper presents a simulation-based flight stack for a \SI{2.00}{\kilo\gram} tilt-rotor quadcopter. The system uses a six-degree-of-freedom nonlinear model with first-order motor dynamics and two-axis rotor tilt, parameterized using a 3D CAD model. A cascaded PD controller commands forward and lateral tilt angles. A 14-state EKF fuses sensor data across hover, early-transition, and transition modes using a hysteretic (Schmitt-trigger) classifier to prevent covariance discontinuities. Because the proportional position loop leaves a steady-state offset under constant wind, a small bounded neural residual is added on top of the unmodified PD controller. It is trained by behavioral cloning from a teacher with privileged access to the true wind, while the deployed network never observes wind. In simulation, the EKF achieves a post-settling position root mean square error (RMSE) of \SI{0.226}{\metre} (horizontal) and \SI{0.03}{\metre} (vertical) and an attitude RMSE below \SI{0.8}{\degree}, and it estimates a wind velocity of $(\num{2.0}, \num{-1.2})\,\unit{\metre\per\second}$ to within \SI{0.15}{\metre\per\second} per axis. The residual reduces steady-state station-keeping error under wind by approximately \SI{49}{\percent}, from \SI{0.117}{\metre} to \SI{0.060}{\metre} at \SI{1.5}{\metre\per\second} and from \SI{0.319}{\metre} to \SI{0.162}{\metre} at an out-of-distribution \SI{3.9}{\metre\per\second}. The framework provides a basis for hardware-in-the-loop and flight-test studies.
2610.31051.tldr_en: A simulation-based flight stack for a tilt-rotor quadcopter using a six-degree-of-freedom nonlinear model with first-order motor dynamics and two-axis rotor tilt, parameterized using a 3D CAD model provides a basis for hardware-in-the-loop and flight-test studies.

llm.title_ja: 学習型残差制御とモード依存の状態推定を備えたティルトロータークアッドコプター
llm.tldr_ja: 3D CADモデルでパラメータ化された非線形モデルを用いたシミュレーションベースのフライトスタックを提案し、風下での定常位置保持誤差を約49%削減した。
llm.problem: ティルトロータークアッドコプターはバンクなしで推力を偏向して平行移動できるが、モデリング、状態推定、および外乱除去が複雑になること。
llm.method: 6自由度非線形モデル、14状態のEKF（ヒステリシス分類器を使用）、風速を直接観測しない状態で風の知識を持つ教師から行動クローンで訓練された小さな有界ニューラル残差の組み合わせ。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて、EKFは水平方向位置RMSE 0.226m、姿勢RMSE 0.8°未満を達成し、風下での定常位置保持誤差を約49%削減した。

2610.31028.title: Multimodal Progress-Residual Fusion for Anticipating Navigation Retreat in Robotic Flexible Endoscopy
2610.31028.abstract: Flexible robotic endoscopes provide access through tortuous anatomy, where friction, deformation, and wall interaction separate commanded insertion from useful distal progress. Operators interpret this mismatch and retreat to recover a navigable configuration. Recognizing the approach to that decision requires relating motor intent to distal response and the local visual scene. We introduce Multimodal Progress-Residual Fusion (MPRF), a causal model that anticipates operator retreat from commands, electromagnetic (EM) tracking, and endoscopic video. A nominal-progress model predicts the response expected in normal or successful navigation; a temporal predictor combines its EM residual with all three observed modalities. In a 150-episode colon-phantom collection, MPRF achieves 0.580 +/- 0.007 AUPRC across three seeds, compared with 0.511 for the strongest reduced-modality control. Complete multimodal histories provide the principal ranking advantage, while the residual adds an explicit intent-response representation with a small, uncertain increment over raw fusion. Analysis of frozen alarms relates warning timing to the behavioral label and explains the increase in event recall under a longer matching window. These results establish a basis for behavioral assistance during operator-controlled navigation.
2610.31028.tldr_en: This work introduces Multimodal Progress-Residual Fusion (MPRF), a causal model that anticipates operator retreat from commands, electromagnetic (EM) tracking, and endoscopic video, and establishes a basis for behavioral assistance during operator-controlled navigation.

llm.title_ja: ロボットフレキシブル内視鏡におけるナビゲーション後退を予測するためのマルチモーダル進捗・残差融合
llm.tldr_ja: コマンド、電磁トラッキング、内視鏡ビデオから操作者の後退行動を予測する因果モデル「MPRF」を導入し、ナビゲーション時の行動支援の基礎を確立した。
llm.problem: フレキシブルロボット内視鏡による屈曲した解剖学的構造への侵入において、摩擦や変形、壁面との相互作用により指示された挿入と実際の先端の進捗にズレが生じること。
llm.method: 正常・成功時の応答を予測する公称進捗モデルと、その電磁残差をすべての観測モダリティと組み合わせる時間的予測因子を統合した因果モデル「MPRF」。
llm.result: 150エピソードの結腸ファントムデータにおいて、最も強力な縮小モダリティ制御の0.511を上回り、0.580のAUPRCを達成した。

2610.31020.title: Demonstration-Based Robotic Feeding Using Dynamic Movement Primitives
2610.31020.abstract: This paper presents a demonstration-based robotic feeding framework that integrates human demonstration, Dynamic Movement Primitive-based motion planning, vision-based scene perception, and robot control. A human operator first demonstrates the scooping and feeding motions while the position and Euler-angle orientation of the spoon are recorded using a motion-capture system. The recorded trajectory is segmented into scooping and feeding motions, which are encoded using separate Dynamic Movement Primitives. Before task execution, an RGB-D camera estimates the participant's mouth position, while two AprilTags are used for robot-frame registration and tray localization. The detected tray pose is used to position the scooping motion, whereas the detected mouth position defines the positional goal of the feeding motion. The approach, scooping, and feeding trajectories are then executed sequentially by a Kinova Gen3 manipulator through a ROS~2-based framework. A real-world experiment demonstrates the feasibility of the integrated pipeline and shows that the learned spoon motions can be reproduced within the detected experimental scene.
2610.31020.tldr_en: A demonstration-based robotic feeding framework that integrates human demonstration, Dynamic Movement Primitive-based motion planning, vision-based scene perception, and robot control is presented and it is shown that the learned spoon motions can be reproduced within the detected experimental scene.

llm.title_ja: 動的移動プリミティブを用いたデモンストレーションベースのロボット給餌
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のデモンストレーション、動的移動プリミティブベースのモーションプランニング、ビジョンベースのシーン知覚を統合した給餌フレームワークを提案し、実機での再現性を実証した。
llm.problem: 高齢者や身体障害者のための給餌を自動化する際、人間の自然なすくい上げや給餌の動作を柔軟かつ頑健にロボットに学習させることが難しいこと。
llm.method: モーションキャプチャシステムで記録されたスプーンの軌道をすくい上げと給餌の動作にセグメント化し、それぞれDynamic Movement Primitivesでエンコードして実行する。
llm.result: 実世界実験により統合パイプラインの実現可能性が示され、学習したスプーンの動きを検出された実験シーン内で再現できることが実証された。
keywords_ja: 動的移動プリミティブ
デモンストレーション学習
モーションプランニング

2610.31013.title: Multi-Tool Selection for Robotic Systems: Comparing Semantic Retrieval and LLM
2610.31013.abstract: Natural-language interfaces allow users to command robotic systems without interacting directly with mission planners or robotics middleware. Their reliable use depends on robot tool routing, defined here as the selection of the smallest complete subset of predefined executable capabilities required to satisfy a request. This task is particularly difficult for compound instructions, where incomplete selection may omit necessary sensing or monitoring capabilities, while excessive selection may expose irrelevant tools. We compare four routing strategies: three progressively refined ChromaDB-based methods - fixed-threshold retrieval, relative-distance retrieval, and clause-aware aggregated retrieval - and a cloud-hosted 120-billion-parameter language-model baseline. The methods are evaluated on 164 manually annotated prompts organised into three complexity levels, from direct single-tool requests to compound requests requiring at least three tools. Using exact-match accuracy, completeness, precision, a completeness-weighted composite score, and routing latency, CDB-v3 achieves the best macro-average score among the retrieval-only methods, with 0.7822, compared with 0.8869 for the large-model baseline. Although the LLM provides higher routing quality, CDB-v3 exhibits substantially lower latency and can be deployed locally without requiring cloud connectivity. These results identify a quality-latency trade-off between direct large-model selection and clause-aware semantic retrieval for privacy-sensitive, connectivity-constrained, and resource-constrained robotic systems.
2610.31013.tldr_en: A quality-latency trade-off between direct large-model selection and clause-aware semantic retrieval for privacy-sensitive, connectivity-constrained, and resource-constrained robotic systems is identified.

llm.title_ja: ロボットシステムのためのマルチツール選択：セマンティック検索とLLMの比較
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットシステムにおけるコマンドに応じたツールルーティングに関して、大規模言語モデルとセマンティック検索手法（CDB-v3）の品質とレイテンシのトレードオフを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 自然言語インターフェースによる指示、特に複合的な指示において、不完全なツール選択は必要なセンシング機能を欠落させ、過剰な選択は無関係なツールを露出させること。
llm.method: 3つの段階的に洗練されたChromaDBベースの手法と、クラウドホストされた120Bパラメータの言語モデルベースラインの計4つのルーティング戦略を比較・評価する。
llm.result: LLMベースラインはより高いルーティング品質を提供する一方で、CDB-v3はレイテンシが大幅に低く、クラウド接続なしでローカルに展開できることを示した。
keywords_ja: 自然言語インターフェース
ロボットミドルウェア

2610.31010.title: Revisiting Distribution Matching for State-to-Vision Policy Distillation in Laparoscopic Robotic Manipulation
2610.31010.abstract: End-to-end control policies trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL) have emerged as an alternative to conventional surgical robotic control approaches, with recent studies exploring state-based policies trained on privileged state observations. However, such approaches rely on precise physical states that are difficult to obtain reliably in surgical environments. Vision-based RL provides an alternative by learning manipulation policies directly from RGB observations, avoiding explicit state estimation and manually engineered perception pipelines while enabling policies to acquire task-relevant visual representations. Nevertheless, obtaining vision-based policies via pure RL methods for surgical manipulation remains challenging. Thus, imitation learning (IL) becomes another solution, yet it requires a large number of expert demonstrations, which are difficult to obtain in minimally invasive surgery. In this work, we propose a framework for state-to-vision policy distillation in laparoscopic robotic manipulation. Specifically, a state-based policy with privileged observations is employed as the teacher, and a vision-based policy learns from RGB observations and robot proprioceptive information, which requires less expert demonstrations than IL and introduces superior performance than RL methods. We conduct extensive experiments on various surgical manipulation tasks in the simulated environment. Experimental results show that, in the context of laparoscopic robotic manipulation, training vision-based policies with general-purpose RL methods is challenging, whereas our proposed state-to-vision policy distillation leads to more consistent and stable performance across tasks.
2610.31010.tldr_en: Experimental results show that, in the context of laparoscopic robotic manipulation, training vision-based policies with general-purpose RL methods is challenging, whereas the proposed state-to-vision policy distillation leads to more consistent and stable performance across tasks.

llm.title_ja: 腹腔鏡下ロボットマニピュレーションにおける状態から視覚へのポリシー蒸留のための分布マッチングの再検討
llm.tldr_ja: 実験結果から、腹腔鏡下ロボットマニピュレーションの文脈において、汎用強化学習法による視覚ベースポリシーの訓練は困難であるが、提案する状態から視覚へのポリシー蒸留により、タスク間でより一貫した安定した性能が得られることが示された。
llm.problem: 腹腔鏡下手術における正確な物理状態の取得や、純粋な強化学習・模倣学習による視覚ベースポリシーの訓練の困難さ。
llm.method: 特権的観察を持つ状態ベースポリシーを教師とし、RGB観測とロボット固有受容情報から学習する視覚ベースポリシー蒸留フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーション環境での多様な手術マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、提案手法は一貫して安定した性能を達成した。

2610.30994.title: TRACE: Traversability-aware Reactive Navigation via VLM-driven Adaptive Constraints Estimation
2610.30994.abstract: This paper presents TRACE, a traversability-aware reactive navigation framework designed for the autonomous operation of ground robots in unstructured forest environments. Unlike traditional approaches, TRACE leverages VLM-based confidence maps from positive and negative natural-language prompt sets and combines them through evidential fusion to produce a dense traversability map that prioritizes the terrain based on signs of previously traversed paths. Traversability-annotated points are then extracted and used to derive the left and right boundaries of the traversable path via percentile binning followed by spline or regularized polynomial fitting. These boundaries are then incorporated as soft barrier constraints within an NMPC formulation, enabling safe and adaptive path following in complex natural environments. Rigorous experimental trials carried out in real-life forest environments demonstrate TRACE ability for smooth navigation in cluttered, deformable, and visually ambiguous terrains.
2610.30994.tldr_en: TRACE leverages VLM-based confidence maps from positive and negative natural-language prompt sets and combines them through evidential fusion to produce a dense traversability map that prioritizes the terrain based on signs of previously traversed paths.

llm.title_ja: TRACE: VLM駆動型適応制約推定による走行可能性を考慮したリアクティブナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: TRACEは、ポジティブおよびネガティブな自然言語プロンプトセットからのVLMベースの信頼度マップを活用し、エビデンス融合によって統合することで、過去の走行跡の兆候に基づいて地形に優先順位を付けた高密度な走行可能性マップを生成する。
llm.problem: 非構造化森林環境における地上ロボットの自律走行の困難さと、従来の走行可能性推定の限界。
llm.method: VLMベースの信頼度マップとエビデンス融合による高密度走行可能性マップの作成、およびNMPC内でのソフトバリア制約としての経路境界の統合。
llm.result: 実際の森林環境における厳格な実験により、複雑で変形しやすく視覚的に曖昧な地形での円滑なナビゲーション能力が実証された。

2610.30991.title: UniFlowWAM: A Unified World-Action Model with Visual Semantics and 4D Geometry
2610.30991.abstract: Robot demonstrations record what the robot saw and what it did. They do not specify how the 3D world changed in between. Scene-level 3D flow describes it by tracking 3D scene points, providing the world representation with 4D geometry. Prior work has used flow to improve robot policies. Flow served as an intermediate prediction that a separate model converts into actions, as a prior injected at inference time, or as an extra output learned together with the action. In all of these designs, flow stays outside the policy, as a separate module or as an extra prediction head. We introduce UniFlowWAM, a Unified World-Action Model that makes 3D scene flow a third modality on par with vision and action. Its world representation therefore covers both visual semantics, through future visual features, and 4D geometry, through 3D flow, and flow receives its own supervision. UniFlowWAM is a diffusion transformer with one expert per modality, and the three experts exchange information through joint attention. We train UniFlowWAM under a ten-objective role grid, where each objective assigns every modality exactly one of three roles, namely target, condition, or absent. The same model thus serves as a policy, as forward and inverse dynamics, and as a predictor of future visual features or 3D flow. We evaluate UniFlowWAM on RoboCasa-GR1, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus in simulation, and on four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks. On RoboCasa-GR1, UniFlowWAM raises the success rate of its base model without flow from 52.1% to 56.4%. It preserves in-distribution success on LIBERO at 98.1% and reaches 87.7% zero-shot on LIBERO-Plus. On the real robot, it achieves 87.0% average success, compared with 68.5% for the strongest baseline.
2610.30991.tldr_en: UniFlowWAM, a Unified World-Action Model that makes 3D scene flow a third modality on par with vision and action, is introduced and evaluated on RoboCasa-GR1, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus in simulation, and on four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: UniFlowWAM: 視覚的セマンティクスと4Dジオメトリを備えた統合型世界・行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dシーンフローを視覚や行動と同等の第3のモダリティとする統合型世界・行動モデルであるUniFlowWAMが導入され、シミュレーションおよび4つの実世界両手マニピュレーションタスクで評価された。
llm.problem: 従来のロボットポリシーにおいて、3Dシーンフローがポリシーの外部の独立したモジュールや追加の予測ヘッドとして扱われていること。
llm.method: 3Dシーンフローをビジョンやアクションと同等の3番目のモダリティとし、マルチモダリティ間で共同アテンションを行う拡散トランスフォーマーを採用する。
llm.result: シミュレーション環境でのベースモデルの成功率向上、リベロ環境での性能維持、および実世界の両手操作タスクで平均87.0%の成功率を達成した。

2610.30988.title: In-Context Learning World Models for Robot Dual-Arm Manipulation of Soft Garment with Partial Observations
2610.30988.abstract: Robust manipulation of soft objects, such as garments, is a critical skill for service and household robots to adopt, but remains challenging due to its high-dimensional state space, and material-dependent deformations. Humans address this challenge by using mental world models that "imagine" the shape and material properties from partial observations, which enables them to predict how actions affect future states. As such, embedding such world models in robots allows for better generalization in manipulating a wide variety of garments in the real world. However, learned world models typically require large amounts of real world data that is strenuous to collect, and a mechanism to infer latent properties that govern dynamics. We present a Soft-Object World Model that performs generative full-state estimation and action-conditioned dynamics prediction using a transformer backbone trained on large-scale simulated soft object interactions, with measures to mitigate the sim-to-real gap. By learning to infer latent shape and material cues through in-context learning over a variable-length partial point-cloud history, the model generalizes across robot embodiments, material parameters, garment types and shapes, and manipulation coordination modes without weight updates. The world model is then integrated with a Goal-Conditioned action planner for motion synthesis. We validate the approach in simulation and real world for bimanual garment folding, reporting improvements in reconstruction fidelity, prediction accuracy, and task success. Project Website: https://1am5hy.github.io/ICL soft object world model/
2610.30988.tldr_en: A Soft-Object World Model that performs generative full-state estimation and action-conditioned dynamics prediction using a transformer backbone trained on large-scale simulated soft object interactions, with measures to mitigate the sim-to-real gap is presented.

llm.title_ja: 部分観測下での布製品のロボット両手操作に向けたインコンテキスト学習世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模なシミュレーション上の布の相互作用で訓練されたトランスフォーマーバックボーンを用い、シーム・トゥ・リアルギャップを軽減する対策を施して、生成的なフル状態推定と行動条件付きダイナミクス予測を行うソフトオブジェクト世界モデルが提案された。
llm.problem: 高次元な状態空間や材質依存の変形を持つ布などの柔軟物操作の難しさと、実世界データの収集の大変さ。
llm.method: 大規模なシミュレーションデータで訓練されたトランスフォーマーバックボーンを用い、可変長のポイントクラウド履歴に対するインコンテキスト学習により潜在的な形状や材質の手がかりを推論する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界の両手衣服折り畳みにおいて、再構成の忠実度、予測精度、タスク成功率の向上が報告された。
keywords_ja: インコンテキスト学習

2610.30979.title: LAST-V2X: Language-Driven Adaptive Scenario Synthesis and Testing for Communication-Induced Failures in V2X Safety Applications
2610.30979.abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication enables connected vehicles to make safety-critical decisions, but delayed, missing, or incorrect information can compromise driving safety. Systematically testing such failures is challenging because traffic interactions, communication conditions, and application responses must be jointly configured to produce meaningful scenarios. This paper presents LAST-V2X, a language-driven, adaptive framework for automated scenario synthesis and safety testing of V2X applications. LAST-V2X leverages large language models (LLMs) to translate natural-language test descriptions into executable scenarios grounded in roadway geometry, V2X communication semantics, and vehicle behavior. The framework integrates physical traffic simulation with spatially aware communication modeling and message-level fault injection to evaluate how information degradation affects vehicle decisions. To establish whether an observed safety failure is caused by communication rather than the underlying traffic conditions, LAST-V2X employs matched executions under degraded and ground-truth information. Furthermore, an execution-guided refinement mechanism combines parameter search and LLM self-reflection to identify ineffective test configurations, improve scenario effectiveness, and produce minimal reproducible failure cases. Experiments across diverse CARLA environments and V2X safety applications demonstrate the framework's ability to generate reliable scenarios, distinguish communication-induced failures from unrelated safety violations, and substantially improve failure discovery through adaptive refinement. These results establish LAST-V2X as a systematic approach to language-driven, causally verified, and adaptive safety testing for connected vehicle systems.
2610.30979.tldr_en: Experiments across diverse CARLA environments and V2X safety applications demonstrate the framework's ability to generate reliable scenarios, distinguish communication-induced failures from unrelated safety violations, and substantially improve failure discovery through adaptive refinement.

llm.title_ja: LAST-V2X: V2X安全アプリケーションにおける通信起因の故障のための言語駆動型適応型シナリオ合成とテスト
llm.tldr_ja: 多様なCARLA環境およびV2X安全アプリケーションにわたる実験により、信頼性の高いシナリオを生成し、通信起因の故障と無関係な安全違反を区別し、適応的洗練を通じて故障発見を大幅に改善するフレームワークの能力が実証された。
llm.problem: V2X通信の遅延・欠落・誤情報が駆動安全性を損なう問題に対する、交通状況や通信条件を統合した体系的なテストの困難さ。
llm.method: 大規模言語モデルを用いて自然言語の記述を実行可能なシナリオに翻訳し、物理交通シミュレーションと通信モデリング、故障注入、適応型洗練メカニズムを統合する。
llm.result: 信頼性の高いテストシナリオの生成や、通信起因の故障と他の安全違反の切り分け、および適応的洗練による故障発見の効率化を実現した。

2610.30969.title: IORA: Irregular Object Immobilization under Restricted Actuation
2610.30969.abstract: Stable grasping under task-specific disturbances is important for robotic manipulation. However, most dexterous grasp synthesis methods are developed for highly actuated hands in free space, and low-DoF hands may not be able to realize the contact topologies required by these grasps. Meanwhile, support surfaces can provide useful contact forces, but are often treated only as geometric constraints. We present a support-aware grasp synthesis framework for object immobilization with low-DoF coupled hands. Given irregular object geometry, our method represents both hand and object local surface regions as graphs and searches for kinematically feasible matchings between them. We then refine the wrist pose and motor state for geometric contact feasibility and validates the refined grasps through physical rollouts. Starting from the validated grasp pose, an optional task-guided local search explores nearby grasp configurations by varying the wrist pose and motor state, and selects one according to the specified task condition. Experiments on diverse objects show that our method generates various grasp configurations that achieve high grasp success and strong disturbance resistance. Real-world experiments further demonstrate physically executable grasps which enable object immobilization in cooking scenario.
2610.30969.tldr_en: This work presents a support-aware grasp synthesis framework for object immobilization with low-DoF coupled hands that represents both hand and object local surface regions as graphs and searches for kinematically feasible matchings between them.

llm.title_ja: IORA: 制限された駆動下での不規則な物体の固定化
llm.tldr_ja: 手と物体の局所表面領域をグラフとして表現し、それらの間で運動学的に実行可能なマッチングを探索する、低自由度結合ハンドのためのサポート対応型グラス合成フレームワークが提示された。
llm.problem: タスク特有の外乱下での安定した把持の必要性と、高自由度ハンド向けに開発された従来の器用な把持手法を低自由度ハンドに適用する際の困難さ。
llm.method: 手と物体の表面領域をグラフとして表現し、運動学的に実行可能なマッチングを探索した上で、手首姿勢とモータ状態を洗練し物理的ロールアウトで検証する。
llm.result: 多様なオブジェクトを用いた実験において、高い把持成功率と強力な外乱耐性を持つ多様な把持構成が生成され、調理シナリオでの実世界での物体固定が実証された。

2610.30955.title: A Transparent 3-DoF Assistive Device for Upper-Limb Tremor and Ataxia Compensation: Design and Experimental Validation
2610.30955.abstract: Assistive devices for patients with neurodegenerative movement disorders must combine high mechanical transparency with the ability to generate corrective interaction forces. Achieving both properties simultaneously remains challenging. This paper presents the completed iAssistADL platform, a 3-DoF assistive device for future tremor and ataxia compensation during activities of daily living. The system employs a transparency-oriented mechanical architecture with all actuators located at the base, resulting in low moving mass, decoupled kinematics, and high mechanical transparency. To compensate for friction-induced transparency limitations along the vertical axis, a hybrid control strategy is proposed that combines open-loop force rendering in the horizontal plane with closed-loop force control in the vertical direction. The platform is experimentally evaluated through transparency measurements and static and dynamic force-rendering experiments at representative configurations. Results demonstrate resistive torques below 0.1 Nm in the horizontal plane, end-effector forces of up to approximately 10 N throughout the workspace, and accurate horizontal force rendering up to 4 Hz. While the vertical axis remains limited by friction-induced dynamics at higher frequencies, the proposed system successfully combines high transparency with controlled force generation, establishing a promising hardware platform for future tremor and ataxia compensation.
2610.30955.tldr_en: The iAssistADL platform is presented, a 3-DoF assistive device for future tremor and ataxia compensation during activities of daily living that combines high transparency with controlled force generation, establishing a promising hardware platform for future tremor and ataxia compensation.

llm.title_ja: 上肢の振戦および運動失調補償のための透明な3自由度アシストデバイス：設計と実験的検証
llm.tldr_ja: 日常生活動作中の将来的な振戦および運動失調の補償に向けた3自由度アシストデバイスであるiAssistADLプラットフォームが提示され、高透明性と制御された力生成を両立し、将来の補償のための有望なハードウェアプラットフォームを確立した。
llm.problem: 神経変性運動障害患者向けのアシストデバイスにおいて、高い機械的透明性と矯正的相互作用力を生成する能力の両立の難しさ。
llm.method: すべての活性化装置をベースに配置した透明性志向の機械的アーキテクチャと、水平面のオープンループ力レンダリングおよび垂直方向のクローズドループ力制御を組み合わせたハイブリッド制御戦略の採用。
llm.result: 水平面の抵抗トルクが0.1 Nm未満、作業空間全体で最大約10 Nのエンドエフェクタ力、および4 Hzまでの正確な水平方向の力レンダリングが実証された。
keywords_ja: 上肢リハビリテーション

2610.30953.title: Measuring the Reasoning-Action Coupling in Driving Vision-Language-Action Models through Counterfactuals
2610.30953.abstract: Driving vision-language-action (VLA) models bring an appealing form of explainability to a safety-critical domain, since a system that can state the reasons for its maneuvers offers the transparency that deployment and public trust in autonomous driving demand. These models read the world into language before they act on it, describing the scene and reasoning over it in text that ranges from chain-of-thought to multi-stage question answering on the way to a trajectory. That framing quietly assumes two separable properties, namely that the trajectory follows the generated reasoning and that the generated reasoning tracks the causes that actually produce the trajectory. To thoroughly investigate these properties, we apply causal, counterfactual interventions to four driving VLAs across different benchmarks. First, we perturb the models' own reasoning and show that altering its meaning produces small trajectory changes relative to blanking the same models' camera inputs, a pattern that persists across benchmarks and model architectures. We then construct scene-level counterfactuals through photorealistic removal of key objects named in the models' reasoning and analyze whether the generated reasoning and trajectories track these changes. Overall, our findings indicate that the reasoning these models present to account for their resulting driving behavior is weakly coupled to that behavior itself, pointing to limits on the explainability these systems are intended to provide.
2610.30953.tldr_en: The findings indicate that the reasoning these models present to account for their resulting driving behavior is weakly coupled to that behavior itself, pointing to limits on the explainability these systems are intended to provide.

llm.title_ja: 反事実を用いた運転ビジョン・言語・行動モデルにおける推論と行動の結合の測定
llm.tldr_ja: 知見は、これらのモデルが自身の駆動行動を説明するために提示する推論が、その行動自体とは弱く結合していることを示しており、これらのシステムが提供することを意図している説明可能性に限界があることを指摘している。
llm.problem: 自動運転における安全クリティカルなドメインで説明可能性をもたらす運転VLAモデルにおいて、生成された推論と軌跡が因果関係で正しく結ばれているかという前提の未検証。
llm.method: 4つの運転VLAモデルに対し、モデル自身の推論の摂動や、モデルの推論で名付けられた主要オブジェクトのフォトリアルな削除によるシーンレベルの反事実的介入を適用する。
llm.result: 推論の意味を変更しても軌跡の変化は小さく、モデルが提示する推論は実際の駆動行動と弱くしか結合していないことが示された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.31718.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis
2610.31718.abstract: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges. Recently proposed multigraph neural network architectures leverage this structure explicitly to achieve a strong performance on anti-money laundering (AML) tasks. However, their robustness to adversaries that manipulate transaction structures to evade detection remains largely unexplored. We present the first scalable framework for structural attacks and adversarial training of multigraph neural networks using node-edge incidence matrices, adapting projected gradient descent and projected randomized block coordinate descent methods to optimize structural perturbations over such matrices. We further introduce a cycle-based regularizer that penalizes changes in the global counts of directed 2- and 3-cycles, providing a structural measure of attack plausibility. Experiments on synthetic pattern-detection and realistic AML datasets show that our learned attacks substantially outperform non-learnable perturbation baselines in reducing detection performance (PR-AUC), while adversarial training consistently improves robustness against these attacks. These results demonstrate that multigraph neural networks are vulnerable to learned structural attacks and that adversarial training provides an effective defense. Our code is available at https://github.com/denheijmans/robust_multignn.
2610.31718.comment: 20 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the Fifth Learning on Graphs Conference (LoG 2026). Code: https://github.com/denheijmans/robust_multignn
2610.31718.tldr_en: This work presents the first scalable framework for structural attacks and adversarial training of multigraph neural networks using node-edge incidence matrices, adapting projected gradient descent and projected randomized block coordinate descent methods to optimize structural perturbations over such matrices.

llm.title_ja: 金融犯罪分析に向けた敵対的ロバストマルチグラフニューラルネットワークに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: ノード・エッジの発生行列を用いたマルチグラフニューラルネットワークの構造的攻撃と敵対的訓練のための最初のスケーラブルなフレームワークが提示され、射影勾配降下法などの手法が構造的摂動の最適化に適応された。
llm.problem: 金融トランザクションネットワークをモデル化するマルチグラフニューラルネットワークの、検出を回避するための構造操作に対するロバスト性の未検討。
llm.method: ノード・エッジの発生行列を用いたスケーラブルな構造的攻撃・敵対的訓練フレームワークの構築と、攻撃の妥当性を測るサイクルベースの正則化の導入。
llm.result: 合成パターン検出および現実的なAMLデータセットを用いた実験により、学習された攻撃が検出性能を大幅に低下させること、および敵対的訓練がロバスト性を一貫して改善することが示された。
keywords_ja: グラフニューラルネットワーク

2610.30876.title: LocoManiLab: A Unified Testbed for Data, Policies, Controllers, and Deployment in Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2610.30876.abstract: Humanoid robots must coordinate locomotion and manipulation in everyday environments, yet progress is difficult to assess across differing policies, controllers, and task settings. LocoManiLab provides an integrated testbed spanning data collection and generation, policy training, evaluation, and physical deployment. Its task suite covers 234 atomic and compositional tasks across five household scene categories, supported by 51.5 hours of simulated teleoperation. The evaluation covers twelve policies with a shared controller across task and scene splits and perturbation levels, two policies across five controllers, and studies of demonstration scale and data-source mixtures. Success rates fall on unseen tasks and scenes and generally decline as visual perturbations increase, with differences in generalization and robustness across policies. For data generation, a humanoid motion generation model is fine-tuned for loco-manipulation to study the alignment of its outputs with task execution requirements and its integration into the data generation pipeline. Three simulated loco-manipulation tasks closely match real-world setups, enabling evaluation of three policies in both domains. Similar policy rankings support the reliability of simulation-based evaluation.
2610.30876.tldr_en: LocoManiLab provides an integrated testbed spanning data collection and generation, policy training, evaluation, and physical deployment, and a humanoid motion generation model is fine-tuned for loco-manipulation to study the alignment of its outputs with task execution requirements and its integration into the data generation pipeline.

llm.title_ja: LocoManiLab: ヒューマノイドの移動・マニピュレーションにおけるデータ、ポリシー、コントローラー、および実機展開のための統合テストベッド
llm.tldr_ja: LocoManiLabはデータ収集・生成、ポリシー訓練、評価、実機展開にわたる統合テストベッドを提供し、ヒューマノイド動作生成モデルが移動・マニピュレーション用にファインチューニングされてタスク実行要件との整合性が研究された。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットにおける移動とマニピュレーションの協調の必要性と、異なるポリシーやコントローラー、タスク設定間での進捗評価の難しさ。
llm.method: 5つの家庭シーンカテゴリにわたる原子・構成タスクを含むタスクスイートの提供、シミュレーション遠隔操作データの活用、および移動・マニピュレーション用のモーション生成モデルのファインチューニング。
llm.result: シミュレーションと実世界で同様のポリシーランキングが得られ、シミュレーションベースの評価の信頼性が支持された。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション
シミュレーション評価

2610.31716.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
2610.31716.abstract: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.
2610.31716.comment: 13 pages, 3 figures. Accepted as a poster at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations (NeurReps), Extended Abstract Track
2610.31716.tldr_en: These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.
2610.31716.hf_summary_en: Pretrained LeWorldModel's reproduction of small action effects is evaluated via Gram matrices across perturbation scales, showing scale-dependent sensitivity differences and higher errors than environment references.

llm.title_ja: LeWorldModelは局所の行動幾何学を保存しているか？
llm.tldr_ja: これらの発見は行動感度のスケール固有の評価を支持するものであり、制御に対するその影響は未解決の問題として残されている。
llm.problem: 事前訓練されたLeWorldModel（LeWM）が小さな行動変化の影響をどれほど正確に再現できるかの未解明。
llm.method: 一致させたシミュレータとモデルの応答を用いて、3つの摂動スケールにおけるグラム行列により行動感度を測定する。
llm.result: 最も感度の高い行動方向はスケールによって異なり、摂動を10倍に増やすと正規化されたグラムの不一致が減少することなどが判明した。

2610.30839.title: ProTrav: Probabilistic Traversability with Elevation Uncertainty Propagation for Risk-aware Off-road Navigation
2610.30839.abstract: Reliable traversability estimation is essential for autonomous navigation on unstructured terrain. State-of-the-art approaches typically evaluate traversability from deterministic terrain elevation, thereby overlooking spatial correlations in the terrain and failing to account for how elevation uncertainty propagates through nonlinear traversability mappings. We propose ProTrav, a probabilistic terrain representation that uses function-space sampling to generate spatially correlated terrain realizations and propagate elevation uncertainty to traversability cost. First, a Sparse Variational Gaussian Process (SVGP) reconstructs a probabilistic elevation field from observations. Then, posterior function-space sampling generates spatially correlated terrain realizations, preserving spatial dependencies between neighboring locations while propagating elevation uncertainty through geometric features into traversability cost. Consequently, a distribution of traversability cost at arbitrary location is established, where the mean and standard deviation quantify the expected traversability cost and associated uncertainty, respectively. A risk term is defined by moment-based Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) and incorporated into a Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controller for risk-aware navigation. Simulation experiments demonstrate navigation success rates exceeding 90\% on different terrains, compared with below 40\% for a baseline, while reducing attitude variations. Furthermore, the proposed approach is validated on a robot traversing real-world off-road terrain.
2610.30839.tldr_en: ProTrav is a probabilistic terrain representation that uses function-space sampling to generate spatially correlated terrain realizations and propagate elevation uncertainty to traversability cost, and is validated on a robot traversing real-world off-road terrain.

llm.title_ja: ProTrav: リスクを考慮したオフロードナビゲーションのための標高不確実性伝播を伴う確率的走行可能性
llm.tldr_ja: ProTravは、関数空間サンプリングを用いて空間的に相関した地形の実現を生成し、標高の不確実性を走行可能性コストに伝播する確率的地形表現であり、実際のオフロード地形を走行するロボットで検証された。
llm.problem: 非構造化地形における自律走行において、決定論的地形標高から走行可能性を評価する既存手法が空間相関や不確実性の伝播を見落としていること。
llm.method: スパース変分ガウス過程（SVGP）による確率的標高フィールドの再構成と、事後関数空間サンプリングによる空間的相関を持つ地形実現および不確実性の伝播。
llm.result: シミュレーション実験で90%を超えるナビゲーション成功率を達成し、実際のオフロード地形を走行するロボットでも検証された。
keywords_ja: オフロードナビゲーション

2610.30819.title: TEAR: Task-Evidence Authority Routing for Robotic Manipulation
2610.30819.abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation in field-deployed settings requires more than executing a capable controller. As the execution conditions change, the system must decide, online and on the robot side, which control source should hold authority. Human teleoperation adapts readily to contact-rich and semantically ambiguous situations but depends on a stable communication link. Local autonomy is executed without continuous human intervention, but may fail under semantic ambiguity, long-horizon drift, and unforeseen contingencies. These two control sources exhibit complementary reliability profiles. We formulate this complementarity as a control authority routing problem and present Task-Evidence Authority Routing for Robotic Manipulation (TEAR), an edge-deployable framework that allocates authority between human teleoperation and local autonomy. TEAR arbitrates on the robot side using network-state evidence, which governs the usability of teleoperation, and task-semantic evidence, which reflects whether autonomous execution remains consistent with the current task. A lightweight temporal arbitrator observes both forms of evidence together with robot state and current authority to time authority transfers.
