Across simulated and real-world trials under dynamic network conditions, TEAR achieves task success rates close to pure teleoperation while limiting teleoperation to 19.8-27.4% of control steps and improves success by 30-40% over autonomy-only execution in our settings. These results demonstrate the potential of complementary authority routing to sustain successful manipulation with substantially reduced dependence on continuous human control.
2610.30819.tldr_en: TEAR is an edge-deployable framework that allocates authority between human teleoperation and local autonomy and achieves task success rates close to pure teleoperation while limiting teleoperation to 19.8-27.8% of control steps.

llm.title_ja: TEAR: ロボットマニピュレーションのためのタスクエビデンス権限ルーティング
llm.tldr_ja: TEARは人間の遠隔操作とローカル自律性の間で権限を割り当てるエッジ展開可能なフレームワークであり、人間の遠隔操作への依存を大幅に削減しつつ、純粋な遠隔操作に近いタスク成功率を達成する。
llm.problem: 現場展開された設定における信頼性の高いロボットマニピュレーションにおいて、通信状態やタスクの曖昧さに応じてどの制御ソースに権限を持たせるべきか動的に決定する必要性。
llm.method: ネットワーク状態のエビデンスとタスク意味論のエビデンスをロボット側で監視し、軽量な時間的調停者によって人間遠隔操作とローカル自律性の間の権限移転のタイミングを制御する。
llm.result: 動的なネットワーク条件下でのシミュレーションおよび実世界の実証において、人間の制御ステップを19.8〜27.4%に制限しつつ、自律性単独実行に比べて成功率を30〜40%向上させた。
keywords_ja: エッジコンピューティング
ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.30817.title: Robot Motion Transition with a Human Motion Prior
2610.30817.abstract: Humanoid motion-tracking policies can reproduce diverse behaviors, yet connecting independently acquired motions into a continuous sequence remains challenging. Interpolation connects boundary poses without considering whether their relative position, heading, and timing provide suitable conditions for a transition. A generative motion prior can produce richer motion, but poorly arranged boundaries may cause it to generate excessive locomotion, turning, or another unintended action. We present Spatio-Temporal Alignment with a Motion Prior (STAMP), a framework for connecting independently acquired humanoid motions through a Robot-to-Human-to-Robot process. STAMP uses human motion space to draw on rich motion priors and reuse transition knowledge across robot embodiments. Its key component is a learned alignment model that determines the boundary conditions for motion inbetweening. Given the two motions retargeted to a human rig, the alignment model ranks candidate positions, headings, and transition durations for the following motion. A human motion prior generates the transition under the selected alignment. The completed sequence is retargeted to the robot and used as a reference to train a motion-tracking policy. We evaluate the tracking success of the generated transitions on Unitree~G1 and~ROBOTIS K1. Physical robot demonstrations further show that STAMP connects independently acquired motions into long-horizon sequences. Project page: https://childtoy.github.io/STAMP-project
2610.30817.tldr_en: Spatio-Temporal Alignment with a Motion Prior (STAMP), a framework for connecting independently acquired humanoid motions through a Robot-to-Human-to-Robot process, and physical robot demonstrations show that STAMP connects independently acquired motions into long-horizon sequences.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマンモーション事前知識を用いたロボット動作遷移
llm.tldr_ja: STAMPはロボットから人間、そしてロボットへのプロセスを通じて独立して取得されたヒューマンモーションを接続するフレームワークであり、物理ロボットのデモにより長期的なシーケンスに接続できることが示された。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの動作追跡ポリシーは多様な行動を再現できるが、独立して取得された複数のモーションを連続的なシーケンスに接続することの難しさ。
llm.method: 人間動作空間を利用して豊かな動作事前知識を引き出し、学習されたアライメントモデルによってモーション間の境界条件（位置、見出し、遷移時間）をランク付けして生成する。
llm.result: Unitree G1およびROBOTIS K1での追跡成功率の評価、および実機デモによる長期的な動作シーケンスの接続が示された。
keywords_ja: モーションキャプチャ

2610.30814.title: DRILL: Training World Models to Improve Policies, Not Predict Pixels
2610.30814.abstract: World models are increasingly used to reduce environment interaction when post-training vision-language-action (VLA) policies with reinforcement learning. Yet they are typically trained to predict pixels one step ahead, even though their role here is not merely to render visually faithful videos but to produce learning signals from imagined rollouts that improve the policy. We show that this mismatch is substantial: lower pixel MSE can produce worse policy gradients, and a world model trained for policy utility can yield better downstream policies despite 17% higher pixel MSE on the next frame. We propose the Downstream-Return Imagination Learning Loop (DRILL), a bilevel framework that updates the world model to maximize the policy's return after an inner GRPO update on imagined rollouts. DRILL has two instantiations. DRILL-VWI is a closed-form surrogate, requiring no additional simulator rollouts, that reweights prediction errors by policy visitation, the group-relative GRPO advantage, and model confidence. DRILL-IMG is a full meta-gradient method that differentiates through the inner update using truncated Hessian-vector products. We show that DRILL-VWI recovers the local one-step component of the DRILL-IMG meta-gradient under score-compatibility and small-residual assumptions. Across five manipulation simulators and two VLA backbones, DRILL-IMG raises mean success rate by 13.1 points over WMPO and 7.9 points over RLVR-World, and complements RLVR pretraining rather than competing with it. More broadly, we believe video world models for VLA reinforcement learning can be productively trained by the policy gradients they produce, not only by pixel-level prediction.
2610.30814.tldr_en: This work proposes the Downstream-Return Imagination Learning Loop (DRILL), a bilevel framework that updates the world model to maximize the policy's return after an inner GRPO update on imagined rollouts, and believes video world models for VLA reinforcement learning can be productively trained by the policy gradients they produce, not only by pixel-level prediction.

llm.title_ja: DRILL: ピクセル予測ではなくポリシーを改善するための世界モデルの訓練
llm.tldr_ja: DRILLは、想像上のロールアウトに対する内側のGRPO更新後にポリシーのリターンを最大化するように世界モデルを更新する二階層フレームワークであり、5つのマニピュレーションシミュレータと2つのVLAバックboneで性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 強化学習によるVLAポリシーのポストトレーニングにおいて、視覚的に忠実な動画ではなくポリシーを改善する学習信号を得る目的と、1ステップ先のピクセル予測を訓練する世界モデルの目的のミスマッチ。
llm.method: 想像上のロールアウト上の内側GRPO更新後のポリシーリターンを最大化するよう世界モデルを更新する二階層フレームワーク（DRILL-VWIおよびDRILL-IMG）の提案。
llm.result: 5つのマニピュレーションシミュレータと2つのVLAバックボーンにおいて、WMPOと比較して平均成功率を13.1ポイント向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.30810.title: Adaptive Aerial Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning via LLM-Assisted Proactive Task Generation
2610.30810.abstract: Loco-manipulation extends the workspace of conventional manipulation by combining mobility with physical interaction, while aerial loco-manipulation further expands this capability into three-dimensional space, enabling robots to reach environments inaccessible to ground-based systems. Moving to an aerial platform, however, gives rise to a demanding control problem, since the vehicle must track trajectories accurately in three dimensions while the motion of the arm and its interaction with the environment continuously shift the center of mass, alter the inertia, and impose force and moment disturbances on the body. Conventional controllers address these effects through explicit models and estimation, whereas learning-based controllers infer dynamics from experience, yet control rewards provide no direct target for the response information retained from history, and fixed task sampling can leave persistent tracking difficulties insufficiently explored. We present ALMA, an aerial loco-manipulation framework for adaptive flight control under external arm commands. ALMA employs a contextual flight policy that adapts from recent measurements and actions, using action-conditioned prediction of future measurement representations to train its context to retain response information relevant to flight control. To expand the experience available for this adaptation, an evolutionary process uses a large language model (LLM) to analyze observed control difficulties and propose new structures of arm motion for subsequent training. In simulation, ALMA reduces position root-mean-square error (RMSE) by up to 24.7% relative to the strongest baseline, while the same policy transfers zero-shot to the aerial manipulator and reduces hover position RMSE by 79.6% during periodic arm motion relative to the real-world baseline.
2610.30810.tldr_en: ALMA is presented, an aerial loco-manipulation framework for adaptive flight control under external arm commands that employs a contextual flight policy that adapts from recent measurements and actions, using action-conditioned prediction of future measurement representations to train its context to retain response information relevant to flight control.

llm.title_ja: LLM支援型プロアクティブタスク生成による適応型空中移動マニピュレーションポリシー学習
llm.tldr_ja: ALMAは外部アーム命令の下で適応的飛行制御を行う空中移動マニピュレーションフレームワークであり、最近の測定と行動から適応する文脈的飛行ポリシーを採用し、シミュレーションおよび実機で位置RMSEを削減した。
llm.problem: 空中移動マニピュレーションにおいて、アームの動きや環境との相互作用が重心、慣性、外乱を絶えず変化させるため、極めて困難な制御問題が生じること。
llm.method: 最近の測定と行動から適応する文脈的飛行ポリシーを用い、LLMを用いた進化型プロセスによって観察された制御困難を分析しアーム動作の新しい構造を提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーションで位置RMSEを最大24.7%削減し、実機の空中マニピュレータへゼロショット転移して周期的なアーム動作中のホバリング位置RMSEを79.6%削減した。
keywords_ja: 空中移動マニピュレーション

2610.30786.title: EBV-CAN: Vision--Language Grounding for Contact-Aided Endoscope Navigation
2610.30786.abstract: Flexible endoscopes exploit structural compliance to traverse narrow lumens, pipes, and cavities, where navigation involves distributed environmental contact. This compliance makes tip motion depend on the evolving support configuration. We present external bird's-eye-view contact-aided navigation (EBV-CAN), a vision-language policy that combines one initial global static bird's-eye image with evolving endoscopic observations and motor state. Three supervised semantic queries locate the tip, next waypoint, and instructed target on the cached global image; their residual representations predict bending and insertion commands. We introduce the Vision-Language Contact-Aided (VLCA) dataset, linking 517 demonstrations and 75k action samples to 958k spatial entries and 93k remaining-route records. On 50 held-out episodes, tip-coordinate and waypoint localization reach 97.5% and 94.8%. Swapping the target instruction under identical observations changes target attention and motor output across 17 dual-target episodes. Across 1,920 physical trials of eight policies trained under a shared protocol, EBV-CAN achieves 183/240 successes (76.25%) under automatic blue-area scoring. Gated recurrent unit behavior cloning (GRU-BC) achieves the lowest matched-task offline mean absolute error (MAE), 0.056, and 1/240 physical successes, establishing distinct rankings for action imitation and task completion. Successful multi-guide executions and representative failures connect spatial progress, steering transitions, and visibility to physical navigation.
2610.30786.tldr_en: This work presents external bird's-eye-view contact-aided navigation (EBV-CAN), a vision-language policy that combines one initial global static bird's-eye image with evolving endoscopic observations and motor state, and introduces the Vision-Language Contact-Aided dataset.

llm.title_ja: EBV-CAN: 接触を伴う内視鏡ナビゲーションのための視覚・言語グランディング
llm.tldr_ja: EBV-CANは、初期のグローバル静的鳥瞰図画像と進化する内視鏡観測およびモータ状態を組み合わせた視覚・言語ポリシーであり、 Vision-Language Contact-Aided（VLCA）データセットを導入した。
llm.problem: 狭い管腔や空洞を構造的コンプライアンスを利用して進む柔軟内視鏡のナビゲーションにおいて、先端の動きが変化する支持構成に依存する難しさ。
llm.method: 初期の大域的静的鳥瞰画像と、刻々と変化する内視鏡観測およびモータ状態を組み合わせ、スーパーバイズドセマンティッククエリによって先端、次のウェイポイント、指示されたターゲットを特定する。
llm.result: 先端座標とウェイポイントの局所化が97.5%と94.8%に達し、物理的試行において自動青色領域スコアリングの下で76.25%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 内視鏡ナビゲーション

2610.30781.title: DeXplicit: Making Physical State Explicit in Dexterous Manipulation World Models
2610.30781.abstract: Before acting on an object, a robot needs to anticipate how its hand motion will change the physical world and what the resulting scene will look like. Existing approaches typically entangle action-conditioned dynamics, camera motion, and visual synthesis within a video generation model, or represent dynamics as point trajectories without explicit object structure. We introduce DeXplicit, a dexterous manipulation world model that instead predicts how the world evolves explicitly in metric 3D before rendering its visual consequences. Given an initial scene and a future hand trajectory, a lightweight 3D dynamics network predicts object-centric motion and deformation, providing structured and geometrically grounded future world states. These predictions then serve as a strong scaffold for video generation: appearance is transported through the predicted 3D motion and projected into future views, allowing the renderer to focus on completing uncertain and newly visible content rather than implicitly learning world dynamics from pixels. This explicit-3D-first decomposition also enables efficient causal generation, requiring only two denoising steps per block while conditioning on generated history. Across HOT3D, OakInk2, and PhysTwin, DeXplicit reduces moved-point error by 27-40% relative to PointWorld and improves object fidelity IoU+ by 47% on HOT3D under a shared renderer. Our design with two-step causal generation achieves a 57x speedup from our 14B bi-directional configuration in video synthesis.
2610.30781.tldr_en: DeXplicit is introduced, a dexterous manipulation world model that predicts how the world evolves explicitly in metric 3D before rendering its visual consequences, and enables efficient causal generation, requiring only two denoising steps per block while conditioning on generated history.

llm.title_ja: DeXplicit: 器用な操作の世界モデルにおいて物理状態を明示的にする
llm.tldr_ja: DeXplicitは、視覚的結果をレンダリングする前に物理世界がメトリック3Dでどのように進化するかを明示的に予測する器用な操作の世界モデルであり、効率的な因果生成を可能にする。
llm.problem: 既存の動画生成モデルにおいて、行動条件付きダイナミクス、カメラモーション、視覚的合成が絡み合っているか、明示的な物体構造のない点軌跡としてダイナミクスが表現されていること。
llm.method: 初期シーンと将来の手の軌跡が与えられたとき、軽量な3Dダイナミクスネットワークが物体中心の動きと変形を予測し、それをビデオ生成の足場として使用する。
llm.result: HOT3D、OakInk2、PhysTwinにおいて移動点誤差を27〜40%削減し、オブジェクトの忠実度IoU+を47%改善するとともに、動画合成で57倍の高速化を実現した。

2610.30737.title: Causal Analysis of Failures of Cyber-Physical Systems with Continuous Inputs
2610.30737.abstract: Modern autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs), such as self-driving cars, operate in increasingly complex environments while expected to maintain high reliability. The black-box nature of many of these systems makes it impossible to fully verify their behavior prior to deployment. When a failure occurs, it is important to analyze it to guide improvements to system robustness. A recent work introduced the novel concept of leveraging the framework of actual causality for CPS failure explanation. However, that work considered only a discrete, binary causal model that cannot capture continuous changes in system inputs. In this paper, we address these limitations by extending the actual causality framework with the notion of distance to account for the continuous characteristics of the system. Specifically, we introduce the novel concepts of distance-weighted actual cause and distance-weighted degree of responsibility, enabling causal influence to account for the magnitude of changes required to avoid a failure, rather than only its cardinality. While motivated by the continuous nature of CPSs, this constitutes a general extension of the theory of actual causality and enables more fine-grained analysis of continuous inputs in any causal model. Building on these notions, we present an efficient, practical, system-agnostic explanation-derivation algorithm that uses distance-weighted responsibility to guide the explanation search. We experimentally evaluate our approach across a number of environments from two autonomous-driving simulators with black-box neural controllers. The results show that the proposed extension provides more effective guidance than the current discrete approach.
2610.30737.tldr_en: This paper introduces the novel concepts of distance-weighted actual cause and distance-weighted degree of responsibility, enabling causal influence to account for the magnitude of changes required to avoid a failure, rather than only its cardinality.

llm.title_ja: 連続的入力を持つサイバーフィジカルシステムの故障の因果分析
llm.tldr_ja: この論文では、システムの連続的特性を説明するために距離の概念で実際的因果関係のフレームワークを拡張し、距離加重実際的因果および距離加重責任度という新しい概念を導入した。
llm.problem: 複雑な環境で動作する自動運転車などの最新のサイバーフィジカルシステムにおける、離散的・バイナリな因果モデルではシステムの連続的な入力を捉えられないという限界。
llm.method: 実際的因果関係の枠組みに「距離」の概念を拡張し、距離加重実際的因果と距離加重責任度の新しい概念を導入して効率的な説明導出アルゴリズムを構築する。
llm.result: 2つの自動運転シミュレータのブラックボックスニューラルコントローラを用いた実験により、提案する拡張が従来の離散アプローチよりも効果的なガイダンスを提供することが示された。
keywords_ja: サイバーフィジカルシステム

2610.30735.title: When One Step Is Enough: An Empirical Study of Euler Integration in Flow-Matching Policies
2610.30735.abstract: Flow matching is now the dominant approach for vision-language action (VLA) robot policies, thanks to its expressiveness and simple training objective. However, inference for standard flow matching requires iteratively solving an ODE, limiting the control frequency at deployment. While several works have proposed novel methods to allow for single-shot action generation, we ask whether such additional objectives are actually necessary. We find that across six flow matching VLAs, one-step action generation largely matches multi-step sampling at scale: multi-step integration confers little to no consistent advantage at inference. We empirically find that this holds as long as models are sufficiently trained and have enough capacity. Practically, the implication is that for large VLAs, the single-step policy comes essentially for free from the multi-step model, enabling low-latency deployment without retraining, distillation, or auxiliary objectives.
2610.30735.comment: Accepted at the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026)
2610.30735.tldr_en: It is found that across six flow matching VLAs, one-step action generation largely matches multi-step sampling at scale: multi-step integration confers little to no consistent advantage at inference.

llm.title_ja: 1ステップで十分なとき：フローマッチングポリシーにおけるオイラー統合の実証的研究
llm.tldr_ja: 6つのフローマッチングVLA全体で、1ステップの行動生成はスケール上においてマルチステップサンプリング概ね匹敵し、推論時にマルチステップ統合が一貫した利点をほとんどもたらさないことが見出された。
llm.problem: 標準的なフローマッチングの推論にはODEを反復的に解く必要があるため、展開時の制御周波数が制限されるという課題と、シングルステップ行動生成のための追加の目的関数が実際に必要かという疑問。
llm.method: 十分に訓練され十分な容量を持つ6つのフローマッチングVLAモデルを用いて、1ステップとマルチステップの行動生成を実証的に比較する。
llm.result: 大規模なVLAにおいてシングルステップポリシーは追加の目的関数や蒸留なしでマルチステップモデルから実質的に得られ、再訓練なしでの低レイテンシ展開が可能になることが示された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2610.30732.title: SmolVLA-MoE: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
2610.30732.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in multi-task robotic manipulation by leveraging visual and language understanding for action generation. However, existing lightweight VLA models employ a single dense action expert to handle all tasks, which limits their multi-task capability under constrained computational budgets. To address this issue, we propose SmolVLA-MoE, a novel framework that introduces sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) into the FFN layers of the action expert in VLA models. SmolVLA-MoE replaces dense FFN layers with multiple parallel expert FFNs and a token-level router, enabling each token to adaptively select the most suitable expert for action generation. We further introduce a shared expert with a tunable weight parameter to balance the inheritance of pre-trained capabilities and task-specific expert specialization. Through sparse activation, SmolVLA-MoE activates only a single expert FFN during inference, with a total activated parameter count of approximately 500M including the frozen VLM backbone, while benefiting from approximately 800M total stored parameters. We evaluate our method on four task suites of the LIBERO benchmark. SmolVLA-MoE achieves an average success rate of 84.25%, outperforming SmolVLA (82.75%) and OpenVLA-7B (76.5%), while maintaining comparable inference efficiency. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/dudu435/smolvla-moe.
2610.30732.comment: 16 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables; conference paper prepared for IROS2027
2610.30732.tldr_en: SmolVLA-MoE is proposed, a novel framework that introduces sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) into the FFN layers of the action expert in VLA models, and introduces a shared expert with a tunable weight parameter to balance the inheritance of pre-trained capabilities and task-specific expert specialization.

llm.title_ja: SmolVLA-MoE: 効率的なマルチタスクロボットマニピュレーションのためのスパースMixture-of-Experts
llm.tldr_ja: SmolVLA-MoEは、VLAモデルのアクション専門家層にスパースMixture-of-Experts（MoE）を導入し、計算量を抑えつつマルチタスク性能を向上させる新しいフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存の軽量VLAモデルは単一の密なアクション専門家を使用しており、計算資源が限られた状況でのマルチタスク能力が制限される。
llm.method: VLAモデルのアクション専門家のFFN層にスパースMoEと重み調整可能な共有専門家を導入し、推論時に単一のエキスパートのみを活性化する。
llm.result: LIBEROベンチマークの4つのタスク群において平均成功率84.25%を達成し、SmolVLAやOpenVLA-7Bを上回る性能を示した。

2610.30694.title: Live Thread Reconstruction for Autonomous Manipulation
2610.30694.abstract: Autonomous robotic surgery has drawn increased attention in recent years due to its potential to relieve surgeons of time-consuming, mentally straining, and tedious tasks, particularly during prolonged operations. One suitable task for automation is suturing, which involves tracking the thread as it deforms during needle retrieval, de-tangling, knot tightening, and other tasks. Unlike rigid-object manipulation, deformable thread manipulation has no fixed pose to track and effectively infinite degrees of freedom, making its configuration difficult to predict and requiring the thread's state to be re-estimated rather than assumed. At the same time, thread manipulations involve sequential motions that depend on past and current thread contact points, which must be accurately and continuously tracked. This paper presents an image-to-manipulation pipeline that concurrently generates live thread reconstruction while conducting safe and optimized sequential manipulations to achieve long-horizon tasks.
2610.30694.tldr_en: This paper presents an image-to-manipulation pipeline that concurrently generates live thread reconstruction while conducting safe and optimized sequential manipulations to achieve long-horizon tasks.

llm.title_ja: 自律マニピュレーションのためのライブスレッド再構成
llm.tldr_ja: 本論文では、長期的タスクを達成するため、安全かつ最適化された順次マニピュレーションを実行しながらライブのスレッド再構成を同時に生成する画像からマニピュレーションへのパイプラインを提案する。
llm.problem: 変形可能な糸のマニピュレーションは固定された姿勢がなく自由度が高いため、状態の予測が難しく継続的な状態推定が必要となる。
llm.method: ライブのスレッド再構成を生成しつつ、安全で最適化された順次マニピュレーションを実行する画像・マニピュレーションパイプラインを構築する。
llm.result: 要旨に記載なし

2610.30671.title: Co^2Gen: Collaboratively Generating Task Plans for Decentralized Multi-Robot and Human Collaboration
2610.30671.abstract: Visual Language Action (VLA) models are designed to be generalist robot models that can be implemented across embodiments, tasks and environments. However, their ability to collaborate with other robots and humans remains underexplored. In this work, we propose a framework to automate the generation of multi-robot collaborative data for decentralized VLA training without requiring human teleoperation. Our framework first utilizes a decentralized collaborative planning approach to generate multi-robot collaborative robot plans in the form of an executable function. We then utilize the collaborative plan to produce collaborative demonstration data to finetune VLA models in a decentralized manner. We show that our approach produces demonstration data that when used to finetune VLA models on decentralized collaboration tasks matches the task performance of VLA models finetuned on human-teleoperated collaborative data.
2610.30671.tldr_en: This work proposes a framework to automate the generation of multi-robot collaborative data for decentralized VLA training without requiring human teleoperation, and produces demonstration data that when used to finetune VLA models on decentralized collaboration tasks matches the task performance of VLA models finetuned on human-teleoperated collaborative data.

llm.title_ja: Co^2Gen: 分散型マルチロボットおよび人間協調のための協調的タスク計画生成
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究では、人間のテレオペレーションを不要とし、分散型VLAトレーニング用のマルチロボット協調データを自動生成するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルは汎用ロボットモデルとして設計されているが、他のロボットや人間との協調能力については十分に検討されていない。
llm.method: 分散型協調計画アプローチを用いて実行可能な関数形式で計画を生成し、それを利用してVLAモデルを微調整するデモデータを自動生成する。
llm.result: 人間のテレオペレーションによる協調データで微調整されたVLAモデルと同等のタスク性能を達成することを示した。

2610.30607.title: Continuous-Time Motion Planning and Steering with Global Convergence
2610.30607.abstract: Motion planning is central to robotics, and it is increasingly used to correct the motions proposed by learned planners and policies. In both uses, constraints must hold at every instant of the motion, not only at sampled times. To our knowledge, no algorithm provably converges to a globally optimal motion once a smoothness cost is combined with such constraints. We cast planning and steering as a single continuous-time program: robots avoid one another and static or moving obstacles, and a learned proposal is steered by keeping the motion close to it. The program is elementary to state, yet nonconvex. We propose GlobMP (Global Motion Planning), a gradient projection method over piecewise-polynomial curves, on which each constraint is one polynomial per piece that must stay nonnegative over the whole motion; it alternates cost reduction with feasibility restoration. Under mild assumptions, we show that, from a fine grid start, its cost approaches the global optimum as the number of polynomial pieces grows, with every constraint met to any chosen tolerance, or exactly on stable instances. We demonstrate its superior performance over strong baselines in real and synthetic experiments, including teams of up to $200$ robots, multi-robot planning on the Robotarium testbed and an extended benchmark, maze navigation, and steering tactile-reactive policies on a bimanual humanoid.
2610.30607.tldr_en: GlobMP (Global Motion Planning), a gradient projection method over piecewise-polynomial curves, on which each constraint is one polynomial per piece that must stay nonnegative over the whole motion; it alternates cost reduction with feasibility restoration.

llm.title_ja: 大域的収束性を持つ連続時間モーションプランニングとステアリング
llm.tldr_ja: GlobMPという区分的多項式曲線上の勾配射影法に基づく連続時間プログラミング手法を提案し、制約を満たしつつ大域的最適性に近づく性能を示す。
llm.problem: 学習済みプランナーの修正において制約はサンプリング時点だけでなくあらゆる瞬間に成立する必要があるが、大域的最適性に収束するアルゴリズムは知られていない。
llm.method: プランニングとステアリングを単一の非凸な連続時間プログラムとして定式化し、コスト削減と実行可能性の復元を交互に行うGlobMPを提案する。
llm.result: 最大200台のロボットチームやロボットリウムなど、実機およびシミュレーション実験において強力なベースラインを上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.30606.title: CMAR-search: Commonsense and Memory Augmented Reasoning for Object Search in Dynamic Interactive Environments
2610.30606.abstract: Dynamic interactive object search in large-scale human environments presents substantial challenges for existing methods. Current scene representations like 3D Scene Graphs (3DSG) only provide coarse-grained spatial segmentation and cannot identify functional areas such as storage or leisure areas. Without functional area understanding, existing methods are constrained to exhaustive sequential exploration at large scales, resulting in inefficient search behaviors -- particularly in open-layout environments with numerous interactive objects such as drawers and cabinets. Moreover, these methods lack adaptability to environmental dynamics such as object relocations. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CMAR-search, a novel framework built upon Commonsense and Memory Augmented Reasoning (CMAR). Our approach leverages commonsense about area functionalities and aggregates environmental memory to construct a Functional 3D Scene Graph (F3DSG), which organizes the environment into functional areas with their associated containers. Through this structured representation, CMAR enables hierarchical action planning at both macro-area and micro-container levels, empowering the system to efficiently identify and inspect semantically relevant areas for effective object search. Notably, CMAR continuously integrates real-time perception, accumulated memory, and commonsense to dynamically relocalize objects in changing environments. Extensive experiments in simulation and real-world settings demonstrate that CMAR-search significantly surpasses state-of-the-art baselines in both success rate and search efficiency for object search in dynamic interactive environments.
2610.30606.journal_ref: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), pp. 18586-18593, 2026
2610.30606.tldr_en: CMAR-search is proposed, a novel framework built upon Commonsense and Memory Augmented Reasoning that significantly surpasses state-of-the-art baselines in both success rate and search efficiency for object search in dynamic interactive environments.
2610.30606.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation

llm.title_ja: CMAR-search: 動的インタラクティブ環境における物体探索のための常識およびメモリ拡張推論
llm.tldr_ja: CMAR-searchは、常識と環境メモリを統合して機能的3Dシーングラフを構築し、動的な環境における効率的な物体探索を実現する新しいフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 従来の3Dシーングラフ等のシーン表現は粗い空間分割しか提供できず、機能的エリアの理解がないため大規模な環境で効率的な探索ができない。
llm.method: エリアの機能に関する常識と環境メモリを活用して機能的3Dシーングラフを構築し、マクロおよびミクロレベルでの階層的アクション計画を可能にする。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界の実証実験において、動的インタラクティブ環境での物体探索の成功率と効率性で最先端のベースラインを大幅に上回った。

2610.30605.title: PATH: Preference-Aware Traversability Estimation for Robotic Teleoperation in Off-Road Navigation
2610.30605.abstract: Traversability estimation is critical for ground vehicle teleoperation, yet existing methods often neglect the human operator's preferences for speed and risk tolerance. To address this gap, we propose PATH-Net, a Preference-Aware Traversability estimation Hierarchical Network that adaptively generates preference-conditioned traversability cost maps and speed profiles for off-road teleoperation. Our framework integrates visual and geometric bird's-eye-view features with short-term historical vehicle states through a multi-head shared-backbone architecture. Our PATH-Net infers traversability cost maps while optimizing speed recommendations by using maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning and sparse speed supervision. Our method incorporates operator preference via an asymmetric feature aggregation mechanism, splitting inference into a cost branch that prioritizes high-risk traversability regions and a speed branch that outputs preference-adjusted recommended speeds. Experiments with 15 operators across 225 teleoperated trajectories show alignment with user-specific navigation strategies, achieving modified Hausdorff distance of 0.17 m (aggressive) and 0.15 m (conservative). In the questionnaire assessment, participants reported lower NASA-TLX workload scores with PATH-Net recommendations than without recommendations, decreasing from 34.7 to 22.2. These results support preference-conditioned trajectory and speed recommendation for off-road teleoperation.
2610.30605.tldr_en: The proposed PATH-Net, a Preference-Aware Traversability estimation Hierarchical Network that adaptively generates preference-conditioned traversability cost maps and speed profiles for off-road teleoperation, incorporates operator preference via an asymmetric feature aggregation mechanism.

llm.title_ja: PATH: オフロードナビゲーションのロボット遠隔操作における嗜好を考慮した通行性推定
llm.tldr_ja: PATH-Netは、人間のオペレーターの速度やリスク許容度の嗜好を適応的に反映した通行性コストマップと速度プロファイルを生成する階層型ネットワークである。
llm.problem: 車両の遠隔操作における通行性推定の既存手法は、速度やリスクに関する人間のオペレーターの嗜好をしばしば無視している。
llm.method: 視覚・幾何学的鳥瞰図特徴と短期の車両状態を統合し、逆強化学習とスパース速度監督を用いてコストマップと推奨速度を最適化する。
llm.result: 15名のオペレーターによる実験でユーザーのナビゲーション戦略との一致を示し、NASA-TLXのワークロードスコアを低下させた。
keywords_ja: オフロードナビゲーション

2610.30589.title: OASIS: Online Anchor-centric Scene Inference System for Open-Vocabulary Retrieval and Navigation in Dynamic Environments
2610.30589.abstract: Reliable robotic mapping in dynamic real-world environments is essential for embodied intelligence and long-term autonomy. However, existing methods often involve a trade-off: lightweight online mapping is efficient but captures limited semantic context, while dense mapping provides richer semantics at higher computational cost and is more vulnerable to distractors. They also struggle to relocalize objects after scene changes. To address these challenges, we propose the Online Anchor-centric Scene Inference System (OASIS), a unified system for online mapping, complex open-vocabulary retrieval, and navigation in dynamic environments. Motivated by the observation that indoor scenes are organized around stable semantic anchors, OASIS represents the environment using a sparse set of anchor nodes, each maintaining a unified multimodal representation that integrates semantic descriptions, visual features, and geometric states for reasoning, verification, and navigation. Its compact anchor-centric memory supports on-demand evidence extraction and hierarchical retrieval, reducing redundant storage while improving retrieval reliability. To handle scene dynamics, OASIS further reuses transient observations collected during navigation to relocalize moved objects. Experiments in both simulation and real-world environments, including standard retrieval benchmarks and navigation tasks under both static and dynamic settings, demonstrate that our system can perform complex open-vocabulary retrieval and navigation, while also enabling relocation of displaced objects after scene changes.
2610.30589.comment: Accepted for oral presentation at ACM Multimedia (ACM MM) 2026. 17 pages, 10 figures, including supplementary material
2610.30589.tldr_en: Experiments in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate that the proposed OASIS system can perform complex open-vocabulary retrieval and navigation, while also enabling relocation of displaced objects after scene changes.
2610.30589.venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia

llm.title_ja: OASIS: 動的環境におけるオープンボキャブラリ検索とナビゲーションのためのオンラインアンカー中心型シーン推論システム
llm.tldr_ja: OASISは、動的環境での効率的なオンラインマッピング、複雑なオープンボキャブラリ検索、ナビゲーションを統合的に行うアンカー中心型システムである。
llm.problem: 既存のロボットマッピング手法は、軽量なオンラインマッピングのセマンティック不足か、高コストな密なマッピングの二者択一であり、シーン変化後の物体再局所化に苦戦する。
llm.method: 環境を少数のアンカーノードで表現し、セマンティック記述・視覚的特徴・幾何学的状態を統合したコンパクトなマルチモーダル表現を維持して階層的検索を支える。
llm.result: シミュレーションと実世界の実験において、静的・動的設定での複雑なオープンボキャブラリ検索とナビゲーション、および移動した王の再局所化が可能であることを示した。
keywords_ja: オンラインマッピング
オープンボキャブラリ検索

2610.30587.title: Know When to Escalate: Critic-Guided Adaptive Execution for Cloud-Local Embodied Agents
2610.30587.abstract: Recent advances in foundation-model agents have enabled increasingly capable embodied systems for long-horizon planning and interaction. However, embodied agents require fast, closed-loop decisions as they continuously perceive and act on a changing environment. Deploying strong cloud agents leaves the platform idle for seconds between consecutive actions, while lightweight local models respond quickly but are more vulnerable to errors. Existing hierarchical architectures typically assign models fixed roles, whereas conventional model routers make stateless per-request decisions. We present CARE, a critic-guided adaptive execution framework that dynamically determines when to escalate control from a local executor to a stronger cloud model. A lightweight critic model monitors execution reliability and triggers escalation when local execution becomes unreliable; once escalated, control persists until the agent recovers, avoiding step-wise switching. To support such control transfer, a shared handoff memory maintains execution context and task-level progress across executors, enabling the model to intervene without restarting from scratch. Across diverse embodied benchmarks, CARE improves task success by 6.3-18.3 percentage points over the strongest evaluated collaboration baseline. CARE further approaches or exceeds Cloud-only success while reducing median time-between-action latency by 28.8-82.6%.
2610.30587.tldr_en: CARE is presented, a critic-guided adaptive execution framework that dynamically determines when to escalate control from a local executor to a stronger cloud model, and further approaches or exceeds Cloud-only success while reducing median time-between-action latency.

llm.title_ja: エスカレーションのタイミングを見極める：クラウド・ローカル協調型エージェントのための批評家誘導型適応実行
llm.tldr_ja: CAREは、ローカルエージェントの信頼性を監視し、必要に応じてより強力なクラウドモデルへの制御移行を動的に判断する批評家誘導型適応実行フレームワークである。
llm.problem: クラウドモデルは応答に時間がかかり、軽量なローカルモデルは高速だがエラーに脆弱であるというトレードオフが存在する。
llm.method: 軽量な批評家モデルが実行の信頼性を監視し、信頼性が低下した際に制御をクラウドモデルにエスカレートさせ、共有メモリによりコンテキストを維持する。
llm.result: 多様なembodiedベンチマークにおいて従来の協調ベースラインを上回る成功率を達成しつつ、アクション間の遅延を大幅に削減した。
keywords_ja: クラウド・ローカル協調

2610.30540.title: Motion Retargeting with Spatiotemporal Preferences for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2610.30540.abstract: Human motion retargeting bridges the embodiment gap between humans and humanoid robots by converting human demonstrations into reference trajectories for whole-body control and loco-manipulation. For object-interaction tasks, successful execution depends on accurately preserving body--object relations at critical stages. However, uniform per-frame iteration budgets do not account for these localized accuracy requirements, limiting the computational efficiency of retargeting. To address this limitation, we present Spatiotemporal Retargeting (STR), which uses keyframes and key body parts to allocate optimization effort. Specifically, a vision-language model selects relevant motion signals and body parts, and keyframes are identified from changes in the selected signals. Based on these selections, STR assigns additional solver iterations to keyframes and higher interaction weights to the selected parts. To further improve contact fidelity, we introduce Mechanics-Aware Contact Anchoring (MCA) to refine object-surface contact positions using an approximate object-wrench model while retaining the selected surface directions. Building on the resulting references, we develop Spatiotemporal Reinforcement Learning (STRL), which combines adaptive key-stage sampling with a contact-position reward based on target proximity for downstream control. Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 and real-world experiments on a Unitree R1 demonstrate that STR improves geometric contact coverage and continuity at lower computational cost, while the resulting references improve downstream task completion across diverse object-interaction motions.
2610.30540.tldr_en: Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 and real-world experiments on a Unitree R1 demonstrate that STR improves geometric contact coverage and continuity at lower computational cost, while the resulting references improve downstream task completion across diverse object-interaction motions.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマノイドの移動・操作のための時空間嗜好に基づくモーションリターゲット
llm.tldr_ja: STRは、VLAモデルを用いてキーフレームや身体部位を選択し、物体との接触精度と計算効率を向上させる時空間リターゲット手法である。
llm.problem: 均一なフレームごとの反復計算予算は局所的な精度要求を考慮しておらず、リターゲットの計算効率を制限している。
llm.method: VLAモデルでモーション信号と身体部位を選択し、キーフレームに多くの最適化反復を割り当て、接触の正確性を高めるために力学認識型接触アンカリングを導入する。
llm.result: Unitree G1でのシミュレーションおよびUnitree R1での実機実験により、低い計算コストで幾何学的接触の網羅性と連続性が改善されることを示した。
keywords_ja: モーションリターゲット
ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.30528.title: Decision Making and Ride Comfort Evaluation Based on Lane-Change Prediction for Autonomous Vehicles
2610.30528.abstract: Predicting surrounding vehicles' lane-change intentions enables autonomous vehicles to anticipate potential hazards and respond proactively rather than relying solely on reactive maneuvers. This study investigates the benefits of integrating lane-change prediction, based on knowledge graph embeddings and Bayesian inference, into autonomous vehicle decision-making. Three driving strategies are evaluated in risky merging scenarios simulated in CARLA: reactive driving, prediction-based longitudinal action, and prediction-based lateral action. The proposed prediction model anticipates the surrounding vehicle's lane change approximately 3-4 seconds before its occurrence, allowing the ego vehicle to adjust its behavior accordingly. In the representative simulation records, reactive driving results in a collision accompanied by aggressive deceleration. In contrast, prediction-based longitudinal action initiates early braking to establish a safe gap, while prediction-based lateral action performs a lane change when a safe adjacent lane is available. Both predictive strategies avoid collisions in the evaluated records. Compared with reactive driving, peak deceleration before impact is reduced by 31.5% with longitudinal action and 91.0% with lateral action. Additionally, an ISO 2631-1-based horizontal vibration estimate is used to provide a ride comfort assessment. Overall, the results highlight the potential of lane-change prediction to support safer and smoother driving through proactive decision-making, with additional insights into ride comfort provided by vibration-based estimates.
2610.30528.tldr_en: The results highlight the potential of lane-change prediction to support safer and smoother driving through proactive decision-making, with additional insights into ride comfort provided by vibration-based estimates.

llm.title_ja: 車線変更予測に基づく自動運転車の意思決定と乗り心地評価
llm.tldr_ja: 知識グラフ埋め込みとベイズ推論に基づく車線変更予測を自動運転車の意思決定に統合し、受動的な回避に比べて安全性と乗り心地が向上することを示した。
llm.problem: 周囲車両の車線変更意図の予測がない場合、自動運転車は受動的な操舵のみに依存し、危険な状況への対応が遅れるおそれがある。
llm.method: 周囲車両の車線変更意図を予測し、予測に基づく縦方向および横方向のアクション戦略をCARLAのシミュレーション環境で評価する。
llm.result: 予測ベースの戦略により衝突を回避し、衝突前の最大減速度を大幅に低減させ、振動に基づく評価で乗り心地の改善を示した。

2610.30500.title: PhysibleMDM: Enforcing Inference-Time Physical Feasibility Constraints on Motion Diffusion Models via Noise Optimization
2610.30500.abstract: Motion Diffusion Models (MDMs) can generate diverse and visually appealing human motion; yet, the resulting trajectories frequently violate physical constraints, limiting their downstream use in simulation and control. We present PhysibleMDM, a framework that promotes physical feasibility of MDM output by optimizing at inference time the diffusion noise without retraining the generative model. We introduce a set of surrogate feasibility constraints that can be evaluated without full trajectory simulation. These constraints combine kinematic checks (e.g., ground penetration, slip, and self-collision) with dynamic feasibility tests computed via an inverse-dynamics inner loop formulated as a cone program. We solve the resulting black-box noise optimization problem using the Separable Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (Sep-CMA-ES), thereby avoiding reliance on computationally expensive and discontinuous gradients. An autoregressive scheme then chains optimized segments to synthesize long motion sequences. Across 100 motion styles on an SMPL humanoid, PhysibleMDM reduces mean ground penetration, self-collision penetration, and ground slip by 75%, 92%, and 74%, respectively, relative to unoptimized diffusion output. Across 11 sequences for a custom bipedal robot, it achieves median reductions of 89.5% in per-sequence mean acceleration-reconstruction error and 79.5% in the mean inverse-dynamics residual.
2610.30500.tldr_en: PhysibleMDM is presented, a framework that promotes physical feasibility of MDM output by optimizing at inference time the diffusion noise without retraining the generative model, and introduces a set of surrogate feasibility constraints that can be evaluated without full trajectory simulation.

llm.title_ja: PhysibleMDM: ノイズ最適化を通じたモーション拡散モデルへの推論時物理的妥当性制約の強制
llm.tldr_ja: PhysibleMDMは、生成モデルを再学習させることなく推論時に拡散ノイズを最適化することで、モーション拡散モデルの出力における物理的妥当性を高めるフレームワークである。
llm.problem: モーション拡散モデルが生成する軌跡は多様で視覚的に優れているが、物理法則の制約に違反することが多くシミュレーションや制御での利用が制限される。
llm.method: 完全な軌跡シミュレーションなしで評価可能な一連の代理物理制約を導入し、ブラックボックスノイズ最適化問題を解くことで物理的妥当性を強制する。
llm.result: SMPLヒューマノイドやカスタム二足歩行ロボットにおいて、地面へのめり込みや滑り、逆動力学残差を大幅に削減した。
keywords_ja: モーション拡散モデル

2610.30478.title: Externalise the Memory: A Pre-Registered Study of Where an Embodied Agent's Experience Should Live
2610.30478.abstract: Should an embodied agent's experience be baked into its policy weights, or kept external and retrieved at inference? A memory-augmented teacher (a VLM that retrieves lessons, with their episode images, from its own past attempts) produces trajectories on a vision-conditioned reach task; from the same trajectories we distil LoRA student policies and evaluate them under matched protocols, including one that re-attaches the teacher's frozen retrieval buffer to a fixed set of student weights. We pre-registered the hypotheses, arms, tests, and analysis rules before training and before any p-value. Distilling the memory-augmented behaviour into weights beat an action-only control by +1 pp (n.s.); the registered test proves underpowered for its own minimum effect, so we withdraw - rather than refute - the memory-in-weights claim. Attaching retrieval to a fixed set of student weights added +34 pp (z=5.15), reaching the pooled memory-augmented teacher reference (49.3%); the pre-registered protocol contrast agrees (+23 pp, z=3.36); under a pre-registered auto-reset sensitivity count the two are +36 and +29 pp. An exploratory behavioural probe with pre-registered per-arm predictions is consistent with behavioural distillation transferring the marginal correction but not the conditional, situation-specific correction that retrieval supplies. The recipe that follows is to externalise the memory: in follow-up controls registered before they ran, the same frozen buffer lifts the base model with no adapter to 48% (sensitivity 48%) and the other three adapters from 19-26% to 53-55% (sensitivity 17-21% to 50-55%), and the adapter adds nothing detectable once the buffer is attached. On a second, harder task, the retrieval advantage points the same direction but falls short of significance (+6 pp, 95% CI [-4.5, +16.4]); exploratory diagnostics tie the attenuation to memory coverage.
2610.30478.comment: 28 pages. A 5-page version appears at the CL4FMAgents workshop, NeurIPS 2026 (non-archival). Code and pre-registration: https://github.com/TPEmist/AionGenos
2610.30478.tldr_en: An exploratory behavioural probe with pre-registered per-arm predictions is consistent with behavioural distillation transferring the marginal correction but not the conditional, situation-specific correction that retrieval supplies, and exploratory diagnostics tie the attenuation to memory coverage.

llm.title_ja: 記憶を外部化する：エージェントの経験はどこに置くべきかに関する事前登録済み研究
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントの経験をポリシーの重みに埋め込むのではなく外部に保持して推論時に検索させるアプローチが、タスク性能の向上に有効であることを検証した。
llm.problem: embodiedエージェントの過去の経験をポリシーの重みに焼き込むべきか、外部に保持して推論時に検索させるべきかという点が議論されている。
llm.method: 事前登録されたプロトコルに基づき、記憶を付加した教示者モデルの行動を学生ポリシーに蒸留する実験および検索バッファを再接続する実験を実施する。
llm.result: 固定された学生モデルの重みに検索バッファを再接続することで大幅な性能向上が得られ、行動の蒸留だけでは状況特異的な修正が不十分であることを示した。

2610.30452.title: Integrated Respiratory Sensing and Gated Control for Autonomous Needle Insertion Via CT Bore Robotic Arm
2610.30452.abstract: Currently, CT-guided lung biopsy is a highly manual procedure requiring patient breath-holding, iterative manual needle insertions, and repeated CT confirmation scans to accurately target a tumor. Automating this process within the CT bore--without relying on manual needle placement or patient breath-holding--has the potential to reduce procedure time, patient discomfort, and radiation exposure. In this work, we present an integrated sensing and control system capable of performing a gated needle insertion within the CT bore. The experiments demonstrate the system's ability to track and predict patient breath cycles, perform autonomous respiratory-gated needle insertion, and detect breath cycle anomalies.
2610.30452.tldr_en: An integrated sensing and control system capable of performing a gated needle insertion within the CT bore is presented, demonstrating the system's ability to track and predict patient breath cycles, perform autonomous respiratory-gated needle insertion, and detect breath cycle anomalies.

llm.title_ja: CTボア内ロボットアームを用いた自律的針穿刺のための呼吸センシングとゲート制御の統合
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究では、患者の呼吸サイクルを追跡・予測し、呼吸に同期してCTボア内で自律的に針穿刺を行う統合センシング・制御システムを提案する。
llm.problem: CTガイド下の肺生検は、患者の息止めや手動の針穿刺、確認スキャンを繰り返す手作業であり、時間や被曝の負担が大きい。
llm.method: 患者の呼吸サイクルを追跡・予測し、呼吸に同期した自律的な針穿刺や異常検出を行う統合システムを開発する。
llm.result: 実験により、呼吸サイクルの追跡・予測、呼吸同期による自律的な針穿刺、および異常検知が可能であることを実証した。

2610.30438.title: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives
2610.30438.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This paper reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing, and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision-language-action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.
2610.30438.comment: 30 pages. Author accepted manuscript. Posted with permission from the Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems, Volume 10; copyright 2027 the author(s), https://www.annualreviews.org. Published version: https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-control-032125-030330
2610.30438.tldr_en: This article first introduces the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action.
2610.30438.venue: Annual Review of Control Robotics and Autonomous Systems

llm.title_ja: 触覚に基づくロボットマニプリレーション：力学駆動型からデータ駆動型への展望
llm.tldr_ja: 本論文では、接触力学に基づく従来の力学駆動型アプローチと、データから直接学習するデータ駆動型アプローチの2つの視点から、触覚ロボットマニピュレーションの発展をレビューする。
llm.problem: 頑健で器用なマニピュレーションを実現するためには接触インターフェースにおける物理的相互作用への直接アクセスが必要だが、アプローチの変遷の整理が求められている。
llm.method: 触覚センシングの基礎を導入し、力学駆動型とデータ駆動型（模倣学習、強化学習、VLAモデルなど）の双方の観点から関連研究を体系的にレビューする。
llm.result: 触覚を活用したスケーラブルで汎用性、頑健性のあるロボットシステムに向けた今後の課題と機会について議論した。

2610.30437.title: Integrated Longitudinal and Lateral Control for High-Speed Platooning of Articulated Vehicles
2610.30437.abstract: This paper presents an integrated control framework for high-speed platooning of articulated vehicles, combining advanced longitudinal and lateral control strategies to address the challenges of safe and efficient autonomous driving. A novel proof of string stability for the proposed longitudinal control algorithm, based on a PID framework, ensures robust inter-vehicle distance regulation even under dynamic operating conditions. Additionally, an arc-length-based longitudinal error formulation enhances the applicability of the control system for curved roads, making it realistic for diverse driving scenarios. For lateral control, significant improvements to the clothoid-based path tracking algorithm are introduced to mitigate oscillations and enhance stability at high speeds. These enhancements include a tangential criterion for oscillation reduction, trajectory segment classification for adaptive lookahead distance tuning, a dual-adaptive mechanism for regulating the rate of lookahead distance adjustments based on both cross-track error (CTE) and anticipated road curvature, and extensions for articulated vehicle dynamics. The proposed integrated control framework is validated through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in maintaining stability, minimizing tracking errors, and ensuring robust performance in high-speed and challenging platooning scenarios.
2610.30437.comment: Original manuscript of an article published in Vehicle System Dynamics on September 20, 2026. Published version: https://doi.org/10.1080/00423114.2026.2733699

llm.title_ja: 関節車両の高速度プラトーニングに向けた縦横方向統合制御
llm.tldr_ja: 関節車両の安全かつ効率的な自動運転のため、先進的な縦方向と横方向の制御戦略を組み合わせた統合制御フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 関節車両の高速度プラトーニングにおいて、動的な運転条件下での安全な車間距離の維持や、カー路面での追従安定性の確保が課題となる。
llm.method: PIDフレームワークに基づく縦方向制御アルゴリズムのストリング安定性の証明と、クロソイド曲線をベースにした横方向の経路追従アルゴリズムの改良を統合する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにより、高速かつ困難なプラトーニングシナリオにおいて安定性を維持し追従誤差を最小化する有効性を示した。

2610.30411.title: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures
2610.30411.abstract: Recent work in additive manufacturing and neural inverse design enables the creation of complex three-dimensional structures to manipulate physical fields, yet these designs must also adhere to discrete, non-differentiable fabrication constraints. Current methods limit the design space by imposing differentiable soft manufacturability loss penalties, or by fixing structures through post-processing, causing a discrepancy between the geometry optimized by the physics model and the final fabricated result. Thus, we present AcoustiPrint, a physics-informed neural architecture for constrained inverse design that represents three-dimensional geometries with an implicit neural representation (INR) and passes each candidate through a printability operator before evaluating its final response. The printability operator executes layer-wise self-support, discrete material selection, and whole-body connectivity, assuring fabrication feasibility. To allow for backpropagation through the discrete non-differentiable operations, we use surrogate gradients for the backward pass and a self-supervised printability objective that progressively drives the INR toward a valid design domain. We demonstrate AcoustiPrint for personalized transcranial focused ultrasound, where inter-patient differences in acoustic properties and head geometry deform wave propagation and requires patient-specific acoustic focusing. AcoustiPrint jointly optimizes three-dimensional geometry and material composition through differentiable wave physics while ensuring manufacturability. Experiments show manufacturable acoustic structures with enhanced focal accuracy and over density-based and phase-based baselines, demonstrating a generalized methodology for neural design through non-differentiable manufacturing constraints and differentiable physics.

llm.title_ja: AcoustiPrint: 製造可能な音響構造の物理誘導型ニューラル設計
llm.tldr_ja: AcoustiPrintは、暗黙的ニューラル表現とプリンタビリティ演算子を用いて、製造不可能な制約を満たしながら3次元音響構造を物理誘導により逆設計するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 3次元構造のニューラル逆設計において、離散的な非微分可能な製造制約と物理モデルが最適化する幾何学形状との間に乖離が生じる。
llm.method: 暗黙的ニューラル表現で形状を表現し、レイヤーごとの自己支持や接続性などを保証するプリンタビリティ演算子を介して最適化を行う。
llm.result: 個人別頭蓋骨貫通型超音波の実験において、製造可能な音響構造が焦点の精度を向上させることを示した。

2610.30334.title: MPBRS: Multi-Potential-Based Reward Shaping for Unified Reward Configuration in Humanoid Locomotion
2610.30334.abstract: Designing and tuning reward functions remains one of the main challenges in building effective reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines for humanoid locomotion. While shaping rewards can accelerate learning, naively formulated terms often conflict with the desired behavior, overfit to a specific robot, or become unstable under small weight changes. Potential-Based Reward Shaping (PBRS) offers an alternative solution: shaping the reward via differences of a potential function to guide exploration without changing the optimal policy. In this paper, we study Multi-PBRS for humanoid locomotion and propose a unified reward configuration. We then evaluate the same reward structure and weights across nine humanoid robots, requiring only robot-specific metadata (joint/link mappings and default poses) rather than per-robot reward redesign. Our experiments show that, compared to standard shaping, MPBRS provides more consistent scaling behavior and reduced tuning sensitivity across robots, making it easier to tune without altering the optimal policy.
2610.30334.tldr_en: This paper studies Multi-PBRS for humanoid locomotion and proposes a unified reward configuration, showing that, compared to standard shaping, MPBRS provides more consistent scaling behavior and reduced tuning sensitivity across robots, making it easier to tune without altering the optimal policy.

llm.title_ja: MPBRS: ヒューマノイド歩行における報酬の統一的設定のためのマルチポテンシャルベース報酬シェーピング
llm.tldr_ja: MPBRSは、ヒューマノイド歩行の強化学習において報酬のチューニング感度を下げ、複数のロボット間で一貫したスケーリング動作を提供する統一的な報酬設定手法である。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイド歩行の強化学習における報酬関数の設計とチューニングは困難であり、報酬項が競合したりロボットに過剰適合したりしやすい。
llm.method: ポテンシャルベース報酬シェーピングを拡張したMulti-PBRSを研究し、ロボット固有のメタデータのみを用いて複数のヒューマノイド間で同一の報酬構造と重みを評価する。
llm.result: 標準的なシェーピングと比較して、より一貫したスケーリング動作と低いチューニング感度を示し、最適なポリシーを変更せずに容易に調整できることを示した。

2610.30320.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
2610.30320.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs. It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 19.4% for the best competing WAM.
2610.30320.tldr_en: Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer.
2610.30320.hf_summary_en: FRED improves single-step future video representations in world action models through self-distillation and temporal conditioning, boosting robot policy performance on long-horizon and unseen tasks.

llm.title_ja: ワールドアクションモデルのための将来ビデオ表現の自己蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: FREDは、単一のノイズ除去ステップで高品質な将来のビデオ表現を学習し、長期的タスクや人間からロボットへのスキル移転を大幅に改善するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: ビデオ拡散モデルを用いたワールドアクションモデルでは、アクション予測が中間的な将来ビデオ表現の品質に依存しているが、従来の反復的なノイズ除去は効率が悪い。
llm.method: 真の将来観測から抽出した表現をターゲットとして、ノイズから将来表現を予測する自己蒸留と、時間的文脈を与える履歴観測の条件付けを行う。
llm.result: 多様な実世界マニピュレーションシナリオにおいて競合するWAMを一貫して上回り、未学習の人間動画からのスキル移転で高い成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル

2610.30319.title: TerraTransfer++: Demonstration-Free End-to-End Planner
2610.30319.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks and real-world deployments. Its standard training recipe, however, is expensive across all existing paradigms: imitation learning requires fleet-scale driving logs whose behavior distribution only thinly covers the safety-critical tail; closed-loop reinforcement learning in a photorealistic simulator, while offering diverse behaviors, is bottlenecked by sample-efficiency, per-step cost of rendering, and a forward pass through a large vision backbone. Self-play in vectorized simulators changes the economics: at millions of rollout steps per second, one can obtain a state distribution with natural diversity in collisions, near-misses, and recoveries that no driving log contains, and a highly reactive policy emerges from a basic driving-quality reward. Our approach exploits this asymmetry. We pretrain a single policy by self-play, distill its rollouts into a flow-matching trajectory teacher that also plans, and train lightweight adapters on a frozen pretrained vision backbone to reproduce the latent space of either teacher through the action KL divergence, a batch-relational low-rank structural loss, and, for the planner, a trajectory-matching loss. Every target traces back to the self-play policy, so alignment never supervises against a logged trajectory: a paired dataset of (image, scene-state) frames suffices, with no need for the curated expert demonstrations that imitation pretraining is built on. From this one self-play teacher we obtain two end-to-end students: a closed-loop policy that outperforms every published imitation-based end-to-end method on the photorealistic 3D Gaussian splatting closed-loop benchmark HUGSim, and a planner that reaches 59.4 EPDMS on NAVSIM navhard, above every published method including DriveZero-Scale (57.1), and 95.5 PDMS on navtest, without human demonstrations.
2610.30319.tldr_en: This work pretrain a single policy by self-play, distill its rollouts into a flow-matching trajectory teacher that also plans, and train lightweight adapters on a frozen pretrained vision backbone to reproduce the latent space of either teacher through the action KL divergence, a batch-relational low-rank structural loss, and, for the planner, a trajectory-matching loss.

llm.title_ja: TerraTransfer++: デモ不要のエンド端プランナー
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、自己対戦を用いて事前学習した単一のポリシーから、デモデータを使用せずに高精度なクローズドイループポリシーとプランナーを効率的に蒸留する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンド自動運転の標準的な学習レシピは、模倣学習のための大規模な運転ログ収集や、シミュレータでの強化学習におけるサンプル効率の面でコストが高い。
llm.method: 自己対戦によりポリシーを事前学習し、そのロールアウトをフローマッチング軌跡教師に蒸留し、凍結した視覚バックボーン上に軽量なアダプターを学習させる。
llm.result: HUGSimクローズドイループベンチマークのすべての公開されている模倣ベース手法を上回り、NAVSIM navhardで高い性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド自動運転

2610.30136.title: Agentic World Action Models
2610.30136.abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.
2610.30136.tldr_en: AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction, is introduced and an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries is introduced.

llm.title_ja: エージェント型ワールドアクションモデル
llm.tldr_ja: AW-0は、コードベースの計画とビデオ・アクションの予測を統合し、言語追従や推論能力、タスク性能を向上させるエージェント型ワールドアクションモデルである。
llm.problem: 近年のワールドアクションモデルは視覚的予測を提供するが、構成的なスキルの再利用の明示的なメカニズムが欠けており、エージェント型ロボティクスは物理的動力学の予測的基盤が不足している。
llm.method: コード、将来ビデオ、ロボットアクションを結合生成ストリームとしてモデル化し、コード専門家がスキルのルーティンを生成するMixture-of-Transformersアーキテクチャを導入する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0および実世界の二足マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、VLAやWAMのベースラインを上回るタスク性能と頑健性を示した。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル
エージェント型ロボティクス

2610.30129.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
2610.30129.abstract: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression. We therefore ask how, where and how much a world model should compress. We build CADRE, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions. Its members differ only in a small bottleneck on frozen features and share a diffusion decoder self-distilled to one or a few steps. We train the same world model on each autoencoder in two domains, manipulation and navigation, with two environments each. CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera. Our study also leads to four findings. At strong compression, a diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression. In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the autoencoder than in the world model. Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions: temporal compression costs little when the camera is still, and spatial compression when it moves. Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt motion far more than image quality. Code, models and a live demo are at https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-10-21-cadre
2610.30129.tldr_en: Cadre is built, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions that forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera.

llm.title_ja: インタラクティブな世界モデルのためのビデオオートエンコーダーの再考
llm.tldr_ja: 複数の時空圧縮を持つ因果的拡散表現オートエンコーダーのオープンなファミリーであるCADREを構築し、特にカメラが動く場合にレイテンシと品質のフロンティアの大半を形成することを示した。
llm.problem: 世界モデルは既存のテキスト-ビデオ生成用のオートエンコーダーを再利用しているが、異なる圧縮率での再学習が困難である。
llm.method: 複数の時空圧縮を持つ因果的拡散表現オートエンコーダーのオープンなファミリー「CADRE」を構築した。
llm.result: CADREは特に動的カメラにおいてレイテンシと品質のフロンティアの大半を形成し、強い圧縮では拡散デコーダーが知覚的回帰よりも鮮明になる等の4つの知見を得た。

2610.30125.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
2610.30125.abstract: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. Without calibrating these physics factors for world models, predictions tend to regress toward an empirical prior and induce severe drift in novel test scenes. To this end, we propose PhysiCalWorld, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling. Our method encodes an exploratory interaction clip collected within the test scene into a compact physics descriptor token, which grounds subsequent predictions in the scene's actual physical behavior. PhysiCalWorld is trained end-to-end with the latent prediction loss alone, without physics labels. At inference time, the descriptor token is extracted once and can be reused across rollouts with negligible compute overhead. We evaluate PhysiCalWorld across four environments covering diverse physics variations and show that it substantially improves rollout prediction accuracy and visual planning success rate. The learned descriptors also form a physically structured latent space and generalize beyond the physics ranges seen during training.
2610.30125.tldr_en: PhysiCalWorld is proposed, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling, and substantially improves rollout prediction accuracy and visual planning success rate.

llm.title_ja: PhysiCalWorld: 世界モデルのための文脈内物理較正
llm.tldr_ja: ファインチューニングや解析的な物理モデリングを行わず、文脈内プロンプティングによってインスタンス固有のダイナミクスへと行動条件付き世界モデルを較正するPhysiCalWorldを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の世界モデルはシーンの物理特性を捉えきれず、新規のテストシーンで深刻なドリフトを引き起こす。
llm.method: 探索的なインタラクションクリップをコンパクトな物理ディスクリプタトークンにエンコードし、文脈内プロンプティングで世界モデルを較正するPhysiCalWorldを提案した。
llm.result: 4つの多様な物理環境の評価において、ロールアウト予測精度と視覚的計画の成功率が大幅に向上した。

2610.30117.title: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
2610.30117.abstract: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries. CW-WAM improves contact prediction and increases the insertion success rate from 25% to 70% for square pegs with 1-mm clearance per side and from 40% to 95% for power adapters, compared with WAM without wrench input. It also improves lifting-height accuracy across different loads. Our framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE from 4.8 to 2.7 N for peg insertion and from 2.0 to 1.3 N for wiping, respectively, with smaller force fluctuations during successful execution. Project website: https://cw-wam-project.github.io/
2610.30117.tldr_en: CW-WAM is presented, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench that contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references.

llm.title_ja: CW-WAM: 力覚を伴うマニピュレーションのための構造化接触レンチ世界行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ、モーション、接触レンチを共同で予測し、時間整合したモーション・レンチのチャンクを制御参照として予測する世界行動モデルCW-WAMを提案した。
llm.problem: 力覚を伴うマニピュレーションには視覚観測からは明示的に得られない接触および荷重情報が必要である。
llm.method: モーションと接触レンチをモデル化ターゲットとして扱い、時間整合したモーション・レンチのチャンクを制御参照として予測する統合インタラクションモジュールを持つCW-WAMを開発した。
llm.result: 角柱の挿入や電源アダプターの装着における成功率が大幅に向上し、力参照のRMSEと実行中の力変動が低減した。

2610.30108.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
2610.30108.abstract: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the current state, Anticipate action effects, Plan a feasible course, Act through an interface or body, and Verify the outcome. Defined by function rather than architecture, these capabilities let PAPAV identify what all three share and then compare MMEAs with MMAs and with RSs. Five physical constraints, from partial observability to unverifiable outcomes, leave fewer choices fixed in advance and less room to reverse errors. Across 64 benchmarks, explicit evaluation centers on Act; only 5 assess Anticipate and 3 assess Verify, leaving both largely hidden behind task success. These constraints also frame the open challenges we identify. PAPAV therefore provides a common basis for designing reliable physical agents and measuring progress across all five capabilities rather than task success alone.
2610.30108.tldr_en: PAPAV provides a common basis for designing reliable physical agents and measuring progress across all five capabilities rather than task success alone, and provides a common basis for designing reliable physical agents and measuring progress across all five capabilities rather than task success alone.
2610.30108.hf_summary_en: PAPAV defines five core capabilities for multimodal embodied agents and highlights gaps in evaluation and physical constraints when moving from digital to robotic settings.

llm.title_ja: マルチモーダル身体化エージェント: コンピュータ利用からロボット利用への統一された能力中心の視点
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダルなタスク推論と物理的行動を結合し、フィードバックから決定を修正する目標指向型システムとしてMMEAを定義し、再帰的な5つの機能からなる統一フレームワークPAPAVを導入した。
llm.problem: マルチモーダルエージェントがコンピュータ利用からロボット利用に移行する際に何が変わるのかという問いに答える共通の基準が不足している。
llm.method: 知覚、予測、計画、行動、検証の5つの再帰的機能からなる統一された能力中心のフレームワークPAPAVを導入した。
llm.result: 5つの物理的制約や既存ベンチマークの評価傾向を分析し、信頼性の高い物理エージェントを設計するための共通基盤を提供した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル身体化エージェント

2610.30105.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
2610.30105.abstract: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that a history-conditioned student can learn to do so when trained with on-policy contexts: the student first collects on-policy context under partial observability, and the privileged expert provides action labels conditioned on that context. By distilling expert actions directly conditioned on the student's on-policy history, the student learns to systematically resolve partial observability, i.e., search while uncertain and exploit once the hidden state is revealed. This enables efficient test-time exploration (similar to Bayesian posterior sampling) without incurring the impractical training-data costs of reinforcement learning. Across a diverse range of eleven different environments, including discrete exploration benchmarks, robotic manipulation, navigation, and Procgen environments, ASTEROID achieves ~2x higher returns under fixed exploration budgets, uses ~100x fewer interactions than RL baselines, and outperforms frontier models at exploration. Finally, our method transfers policies trained in simulation to vision-denied real-world robot manipulation, exhibiting efficient exploration and increasing success by +40% over standard distillation. Overall, it provides a simple yet surprisingly effective framework to learn efficient test-time exploration.
2610.30105.tldr_en: This work demonstrates that a history-conditioned student can learn to explore under partial observability when trained with on-policy contexts, and proposes ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration.

llm.title_ja: 非対称オンポリシー蒸留による文脈内探索の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 部分観測性のもとでテスト時探索を学習できるシンプルで効果的な教師あり学習フレームワークASTEROIDを提案し、強化学習ベースラインの約100分の1のインタラクションで効率的な探索を実現した。
llm.problem: 部分観測下での逐次意思決定では探索が必要だが、強化学習はサンプル効率が低く、模倣学習は探索を学習できない。
llm.method: 履歴条件付きスチューデントがオンポリシーコンテキストで収集を行い、特権を持つエキスパートが行動ラベルを提供する生徒-教師型の学習フレームワークASTEROIDを提案した。
llm.result: 11の多様な環境において固定探索予算で約2倍の報酬を達成し、ビジョンが制限された実機のロボットマニピュレーションでも成功率を40%向上させた。

2610.30102.title: Implementation of Dynamic Microsegmentation for a Multi-Robot Network
2610.30102.abstract: This report describes a laboratory instantiation of a dynamic microsegmentation function for an Internet-of-Things network, specifically a multi-robot network, using a commercial software-defined microsegmentation tool. Fine-grained dynamic segmentation policies are defined, where segments are adapted based on asset functional and health tags. Automated implementation of the dynamic policies in software is also undertaken. The microsegmentation solution is shown to automatically isolate an indicated threat in real time, while maintaining unaffected operations. The demonstration indicates that microsegmentation can be implemented in IoT networks, in a way that allows for robust operation in the face of threats and disruptions.

llm.title_ja: マルチロボットネットワークのための動的マイクロセグメンテーションの実装
llm.tldr_ja: IoTネットワーク（マルチロボットネットワーク）における動的マイクロセグメンテーション機能の実験室インスタンス化について説明し、脅威をリアルタイムで自動隔離しつつ通常動作を維持できることを示した。
llm.problem: IoTおよびマルチロボットネットワークにおいて、脅威や障害に対して堅牢な動作を維持しながら細粒度のセキュリティポリシーを適用する必要がある。
llm.method: 市販のソフトウェア定義マイクロセグメンテーションツールを用いて、資産の機能および健全性タグに基づいてセグメントを適応させる動的マイクロセグメンテーションを実装した。
llm.result: 提案するマイクロセグメンテーションソリューションが、影響を受けない動作を維持しながら指定された脅威をリアルタイムで自動的に隔離できることを示した。
keywords_ja: マイクロセグメンテーション
マルチロボットネットワーク

2610.30097.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
2610.30097.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.
2610.30097.tldr_en: AtomicRL is proposed, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration and a Real2Sim2Real pipeline is developed that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots.

llm.title_ja: AtomicRL: 長期ロボットマニピュレーションのためのアトミック強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: アトミックなタスク構造を活用して信用割当と適応的探索を行う強化学習ポストトレーニングフレームワークAtomicRLを提案し、実機への転送においてタスク性能を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: VLAモデルの模倣学習だけでは複雑な長期スキルを習得するのが難しく、既存のVLA-RL手法は遅延した報酬や偏った信用割当に悩まされている。
llm.method: セマンティック認識型ポリシー最適化（SAPO）とボトルネック適応型ターゲット探索（BATE）を導入するAtomicRLフレームワークとReal2Sim2Realパイプラインを開発した。
