llm.result: LIBERO-LONGやCALVINにおいてベースラインを上回る性能向上を達成し、実機ロボットのタスク性能を平均21.3%向上させた。

2610.30080.title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer
2610.30080.abstract: The Moon changes gravity, terrain, and soil at once. Learned locomotion has studied reduced gravity on rigid ground and granular terrain mostly at Earth gravity, but not humanoids under both, generalist-controller transfer, or the Earth cost of lunar adaptation. On a simulated Unitree G1, we train 12 policies with one recipe, varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact (rigid or three-dimensional resistive force theory, 3D RFT), and including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization. We test them at both gravities on rigid ground and 3D RFT, and at their training gravity on three held-out soil models. We also test the frozen SONIC, a released generalist humanoid controller, at both gravities on rigid ground only. Gravity transfer is asymmetric. Earth-trained policies keep 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground, Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies cannot stand at Earth, and SONIC survives at most 0.10 at the Moon. Rough training lifts combined-tile survival from 0.53 to 0.98 at Earth and 0.80 to 0.99 at the Moon. In 3D RFT, soil training helps on Earth sand, on tiles and for rough-trained policies also on flat sand. On the stiffer lunar soil it helps only flat-trained Earth policies at Earth and changes the survival of Moon-trained policies by at most a few hundredths. In the sampled rollouts of the held-out soil models, Moon-trained policies keep most of their rigid-ground progress on lunar regolith at the low G1 foot pressure, with per-seed progress ratios of 0.84 to 1.39 apart from one seed with a short rigid reference. A gravity-randomized policy trained on rough 3D RFT terrain has a seed-mean survival of at least 0.84 at Earth and 0.96 at the Moon on every key test cell up to 20 degrees. Lunar results are simulation predictions conditional on the contact model and soil stiffness.
2610.30080.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Supplementary material (13 pages) included as an ancillary file

llm.title_ja: 地球で訓練されたヒューマノイドコントローラーは月面で歩けるか？重力、地形、土壌の転移
llm.tldr_ja: 重力、地形、土壌が同時に変化する月面環境を想定し、シミュレーション上のUnitree G1を用いて多様な条件で学習したポリシーの汎化性能と重力転移の非対称性を検証した。
llm.problem: 学習された移動制御の研究は個別の条件下で行われており、ヒューマノイドにおける重力、地形、土壌の同時変化や一般化コントローラーの転移が十分に検証されていない。
llm.method: Unitree G1のシミュレーション上で、重力、地形形状、地面接触を変化させた12のポリシーを訓練し、地球・月面環境や土壌モデルでテストした。
llm.result: 重力転移は非対称であり、荒れた地形での訓練や重力ランダム化により地球と月の両方で生存率が大幅に向上することを示した。
llm.limitation: 月面の結果はシミュレーション予測である

2610.30061.title: Test-Time Motion Steering for Perceptive Humanoid Fall Recovery
2610.30061.abstract: Humanoid fall recovery requires selecting a motion that suits both the surrounding scene and the task. The same fallen pose can admit several ways to stand, with different routes, support transitions, and final headings. Yet reliable recovery alone does not provide control over which of these alternatives the robot executes. Steering this choice requires anticipating the physical consequences of a requested movement. We present RISE, an approach to perceptive humanoid recovery that lets task objectives steer how the robot returns to standing at inference time. It builds on two insights: diverse recoveries can be composed from shared movements, and anticipating how these movements unfold allows recovery to be steered toward a task objective. We learn a recovery vocabulary that connects intended movements to motor actions through sensory feedback. A visual diffusion planner learns from executions of this vocabulary to predict motion intent as future body states. Task costs guide this prediction toward a desired heading, rise speed, or path. The planner then generates motion latents conditioned on the steered intent, allowing the requested movement to shape its execution. Simulation experiments demonstrate diverse recoveries, terrain adaptation, and test-time steering without retraining, complemented by real-world demonstrations on a Unitree G1. Project page: https://osheraz.github.io/RISE/
2610.30061.tldr_en: RISE is presented, an approach to perceptive humanoid recovery that lets task objectives steer how the robot returns to standing at inference time and builds on two insights: diverse recoveries can be composed from shared movements, and anticipating how these movements unfold allows recovery to be steered toward a task objective.

llm.title_ja: 知覚的ヒューマノイドの転倒からの復帰に向けたテスト時モーションステアリング
llm.tldr_ja: タスク目的に応じてロボットが立ち上がる動きを推論時に誘導できる知覚的ヒューマノイド復帰アプローチRISEを提案し、シミュレーションと実機で実証した。
llm.problem: 転倒からの確実な復帰だけでは、ロボットが複数の選択肢のどれを実行するかを制御することができない。
llm.method: 知覚フィードバックから運動意図をモータ行動に接続する復帰ボキャブラリーを学習し、視覚拡散プランナーを用いてタスク目的に沿った動きの意図を予測するRISEを提案した。
llm.result: シミュレーション実験において多様な復帰動作や地形適応、再学習なしのテスト時ステアリングが実証され、Unitree G1を用いた実機デモも行われた。

2610.30051.title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
2610.30051.abstract: Recent advances in frontier AI models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, planning, and tool use, raising the possibility of using general-purpose AI models for robot manipulation without task-specific training. However, their manipulation capabilities have not been systematically evaluated on standardized robotics benchmarks. In this report, we present a unified closed-loop manipulation framework for evaluating frontier AI models on the LIBERO-10 benchmark. Our framework enables models to control a robot directly through visual observations, robot proprioception, and structured tool calls, primarily by specifying target end-effector poses and gripper commands, without task-specific fine-tuning or pretrained manipulation skills. We evaluate six frontier AI models, including GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini-4 Argon, across three reasoning effort levels, resulting in 18 configurations and 1,800 evaluation episodes. Our results show that GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest success rate of 44%, followed by Gemini-4 Argon at 43%. Increasing reasoning effort generally improves manipulation performance, but the benefits vary across models and come at additional inference cost. We also observe substantial differences across tasks, with models performing relatively well on object placement tasks but struggling with precise spatial arrangements and complex multi-step interactions. These findings demonstrate both the potential and limitations of frontier AI models for robot manipulation, highlighting the challenges of translating reasoning capabilities into reliable physical actions. We release our evaluation framework and experimental results to support reproducible benchmarking and future research on reasoning-based robot manipulation.
2610.30051.comment: 17 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. May Espinola and Qifan Zhang contributed equally. Project page: https://irvlutd.github.io/LLM-LIBERO/ Code: https://github.com/IRVLUTD/LLM_LIBERO
2610.30051.tldr_en: A unified closed-loop manipulation framework for evaluating frontier AI models on the LIBERO-10 benchmark, which enables models to control a robot directly through visual observations, robot proprioception, and structured tool calls, without task-specific fine-tuning or pretrained manipulation skills.

llm.title_ja: 推論から行動へ: LIBERO-10ロボットマニピュレーションタスクにおけるフロンティアAIモデルのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: タスク固有の訓練を行わずにフロンティアAIモデルを評価する統一された閉ループマニピュレーションフレームワークを提示し、LIBERO-10ベンチマークでの性能や課題を明らかにした。
llm.problem: フロンティアAIモデルの視覚理解や推論能力は優れているが、タスク特化の訓練なしでのマニピュレーション能力が標準化されたベンチマークで体系的に評価されていない。
llm.method: 視覚観測、ロボット固有知覚、構造化ツール呼び出しを通じてロボットを直接制御する統一された閉ループマニピュレーションフレームワークを構築し評価した。
llm.result: 最高成功率はGPT-6 Astraの44%であり、推論努力の増加は性能を向上させるがモデルごとに異なり推論コストが伴うこと、正確な空間配置等に課題があることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.30044.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2610.30044.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control. Existing interfaces typically rely on a single action representation for both task intent and whole-body coordination. This may burden the high-level policy or leave one aspect underspecified. We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control. Experiments in simulation and on a real humanoid robot demonstrate improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over existing approaches. Additional results and videos are available on our \href{https://sp-hlm.github.io/}{\textcolor{blue}{project page}}.
2610.30044.tldr_en: SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface that combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms, is presented.

llm.title_ja: SP-HLM: スパースポーズ駆動型モーション生成とヒューマノイドのロコモーション・マニピュレーションのための全身制御
llm.tldr_ja: 高レベルのタスク意図と全身協調を補完的な形式で表現するスパースポーズ駆動型インターフェースに基づくフレームワークSP-HLMを提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドのロコモーション・マニピュレーションでは、高レベルのタスクポリシーと全身制御の効果的なインターフェースが必要だが、既存手法は単一の行動表現に依存している。
llm.method: 5つのタスククリティカルな体勢と学習済み潜在モーション事前分布を組み合わせたインターフェースを構築し、VLAモデル、モーション生成モデル、汎用モーショントラッカーを統合したSP-HLMを提案した。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機ロボットの実験において、既存手法を上回るモーション追従、全身協調、ロコモーション・マニピュレーションの成功率を示した。

2610.30043.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
2610.30043.abstract: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue. An event-driven finite-state machine (FSM) uses completed actions and delivered information to update task states and evaluate outcomes. TARSphere-Harness, its embodied brain harness, lets a frozen multimodal large language model (MLLM) act through multi-level executable skills, using observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback to revise its decisions. On this foundation, agent-in-the-loop curation aligns task semantics, causal dependencies, and scene geometry to construct TARSphere-Bench: 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes. Five paired conditions assess perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task update, human coordination, and intent understanding for navigate-and-report and fetch-and-deliver tasks. Our evaluation of 8 MLLMs shows that general-purpose models can outperform embodied models, while task updates and human interaction remain difficult. Frequent collisions and falls further motivate evaluating execution safety alongside task success, even with a shared action interface and decision budget.
2610.30043.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://xuyicheng-zju.github.io/TARSphere/ Code: https://github.com/xuyicheng-zju/TARSphere
2610.30043.tldr_en: TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents, is introduced and an evaluation of 8 MLLMs shows that general-purpose models can outperform embodied models, while task updates and human interaction remain difficult.
2610.30043.hf_summary_en: TARSphere is a robot framework that integrates physics simulation, embodied NPCs, and a frozen multimodal language model to evaluate long-horizon embodied agents across diverse indoor tasks and social conditions.

llm.title_ja: TARSphere: 物理的・社会的環境が変化する中での長期身体化エージェント向けロボット指向フルスタックフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 環境の変化や人間のニーズに適応する、物理的および社会的に基盤付けられた長期身体化エージェント向けのロボット指向フルスタックフレームワークTARSphereを導入した。
llm.problem: 既存の身体化エージェントシステムは特定の目標に焦点を当てるか、抽象的な記号行動に落とし込むため、進化する世界での評価が制限されている。
llm.method: 物理シミュレータ内でロボットポリシーを実行するインフラ、マルチレベルの実行可能スキルを介して行動する脳ハーネス、タスクセマンティクスを調整するベンチマークを組み合わせたTARSphereを構築した。
llm.result: 8つのMLLMの評価により、汎用モデルが身体化モデルを凌駕する一方、タスクの更新や人間とのインタラクションがいまだに困難であることが示された。
keywords_ja: フルスタックフレームワーク
マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2610.29997.title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
2610.29997.abstract: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed. The scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging. Therefore, we present 1) DONIC, the first generalist bimanual tracker jointly trained across operation categories and human-motion sources, together with 2) BiHOI, a multi-view dataset of 1,575 sequences spanning 229 objects and emphasizing sustained bimanual interaction, where reconstructed interactions are retargeted into robot references. DONIC combines proximal policy optimization with behavioral cloning in a feedback loop that recycles verified successful executions into training demonstrations. An object-centered per-hand reward maintains object-motion feedback while supervising each hand according to its reference contact role. Clip-Centered Advantages remove reference-dependent advantage offsets while preserving within-trajectory differences. Together, these designs enable one single policy to learn coordinated manipulation across heterogeneous references. Without finetuning, a single checkpoint achieves 86.79% success on unseen trajectories of training objects and 57.32% on held-out objects, surpassing the state-of-the-art bimanual tracking baselines by 77.36 and 45.73 percentage points.
2610.29997.tldr_en: DonIC is presented, the first generalist bimanual tracker jointly trained across operation categories and human-motion sources, and BiHOI, a multi-view dataset of 1,575 sequences spanning 229 objects and emphasizing sustained bimanual interaction, where reconstructed interactions are retargeted into robot references.
2610.29997.hf_summary_en: DONIC is a generalist bimanual tracker trained on diverse human-motion data that uses reinforcement learning with recycled demonstrations and per-hand rewards to achieve high success on unseen objects without fine-tuning.

llm.title_ja: DONIC: 人間のデモンストレーションからの汎用器用両手追従制御
llm.tldr_ja: 操作カテゴリと人間のモーションソース全体で共同訓練された最初の汎用両手トラッカーDONICと、持続的な両手インタラクションを強調するマルチビューデータセットBiHOIを提案した。
llm.problem: 接触の豊富な両手マニピュレーションデータの不足と、接触調整の複雑さにより、汎用的な両手トラッカーの開発が困難である。
llm.method: 検証済みの成功した実行を訓練デモンストレーションにリサイクルするフィードバックループ内でPPOと行動クローンを組み合わせたDONICと、マルチビューデータセットBiHOIを開発した。
llm.result: ファインチューニングなしで、単一のチェックポイントが未見の軌道で86.79%、保持されたオブジェクトで57.32%の成功率を達成し、既存のベースラインを大幅に上回った。

2610.29964.title: Object- and Task-Aware Active Perception for Safe Navigation of Mobile Manipulators in Semi-Static Environments
2610.29964.abstract: Mobile manipulators must navigate safely in cluttered, partially unknown environments across logistics, manufacturing, and service applications. Semi-static changes between robot visits can lead to outdated scene knowledge and increased collision risk. We propose an active perception framework that enables a high degree-of-freedom (DoF) mobile manipulator to inspect uncertain or safety-critical regions with its hand camera during navigation. A probabilistic, object- and task-aware next-best-view (NBV) formulation prioritizes observations near the desired path and around uncertain or potentially changing objects. The perception objective is integrated into hierarchical-task model predictive control (HTMPC), exploiting kinematic redundancy for viewpoint adjustment while preserving the higher priority of base-trajectory tracking. The system unifies navigation, map maintenance, and active perception in a closed loop. Real-world tests show improved map consistency, reduced task-dependent map entropy, and lower navigation risk than passive or non-task-aware baselines. Additional simulation and real-world sequences demonstrate responses to controlled semi-static scene changes.
2610.29964.tldr_en: An active perception framework is proposed that enables a high degree-of-freedom (DoF) mobile manipulator to inspect uncertain or safety-critical regions with its hand camera during navigation and unifies navigation, map maintenance, and active perception in a closed loop.

llm.title_ja: 半静的環境におけるモバイルマニプータの安全なナビゲーションのためのオブジェクト・タスク認識型能動知覚
llm.tldr_ja: 高自由度モバイルマニピュレータがナビゲーション中にハンドカメラで不確実または安全上重要な領域を検査できる能動知覚フレームワークを提案し、閉ループで統合した。
llm.problem: 半静的環境の変化により、ロボットのシーン知識が古くなり衝突リスクが増加する。
llm.method: 目的の経路付近や不確実なオブジェクト周辺の観測を優先する確率的・オブジェクト/タスク認識型次善視点（NBV）定式化を階層型モデル予測制御（HTMPC）に統合した。
llm.result: 実世界テストにおいて、マップの一貫性向上、タスク依存のエントロピー低減、受動的ベースラインよりも低いナビゲーションリスクを実証した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレータ

2610.29936.title: DewHand: Direct Metric World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
2610.29936.abstract: Recovering metric world-space hand motion from egocentric video supports understanding human interactions and transferring them to embodied agents. Three challenges complicate this task: multi-stage pipelines propagate errors from independently estimated hand and camera motion; monocular observations leave physical scale ambiguous; and occlusion and out-of-view hands admit multiple plausible motion trajectories. We present DewHand, a unified model for direct joint reconstruction of world-space hand and camera motion. To avoid compounding errors from multi-stage estimation, DewHand jointly predicts hand and camera motion in a shared world coordinate system within a single-stage pipeline. To resolve metric-scale ambiguity, it combines scene-level geometric features from VGGT-$Ω$ with metric-space supervision, while hand-specific features preserve fine-grained articulation. To handle occlusion and out-of-view hands, we formulate reconstruction as conditional motion generation with flow matching. Under the same architecture, this generative formulation outperforms direct regression in both accuracy and temporal smoothness with only two sampling steps. Experiments on HOT3D and ARCTIC demonstrate improved world-space accuracy and temporal consistency over state-of-the-art methods. DewHand reduces rigid-aligned world-space error relative to StableHand from 32.9 to 28.4 mm on HOT3D and from 76.2 to 36.2 mm on ARCTIC. It also recovers camera scale within 10% on two thirds of HOT3D clips, versus about a quarter for SLAM. Moreover, in zero-shot evaluations on HoloAssist, H2O, and TACO, captured with different devices, DewHand achieves the lowest rigid-aligned world-space error (WA-MPJPE) on each dataset.
2610.29936.tldr_en: D DewHand, a unified model for direct joint reconstruction of world-space hand and camera motion, outperforms direct regression in both accuracy and temporal smoothness with only two sampling steps and achieves the lowest rigid-aligned world-space error (WA-MPJPE) on each dataset.

llm.title_ja: DewHand: エゴセントリックビデオからの直接的メトリック世界空間ハンドモーション再構築
llm.tldr_ja: エゴセントリックビデオから世界空間における手とカメラの動きを直接かつ同時に再構築する統一モデルDewHandを提案し、精度と時間的滑らかさを向上させた。
llm.problem: 多段階パイプラインによる誤差の伝播、単眼観測による物理スケールの曖昧さ、およびオクルージョンがハンドモーション再構築を困難にしている。
llm.method: 単一ステージのパイプライン内で手とカメラの動きを共有世界座標系で共同予測し、フローマッチングによる条件付きモーション生成として定式化したDewHandを提案した。
llm.result: HOT3DおよびARCTICにおいて従来法を上回る世界空間の精度と時間的一貫性を達成し、複数のデータセットでのゼロショット評価で最も低い誤差を記録した。
keywords_ja: ハンドモーション再構築
エゴセントリックビデオ

2610.29932.title: FrontierCS 2: A Benchmark for Computer Science R&D
2610.29932.abstract: Can LLM agents make contributions to frontier computer science R&D? We introduce FrontierCS 2, a benchmark of 48 open-ended tasks. We take a paper and the code its authors released and delete the paper's contribution. The deleted code becomes the human reference that sets the bar. Earlier open-ended benchmarks give each agent a problem statement and grade one program after the run. FrontierCS 2 places the agent inside a research environment. The agent inherits a working repository and may submit a patch at any point. For each patch, a judge returns a development-suite score but keeps the evaluator, the held-out final suite and the reference private, and grades the final submission on that suite against the reference. The tasks span 13 domains, from machine-learning systems and high-performance computing to databases, security and robotics. Beyond these 48 tasks, FrontierCS 2 keeps a private set of more than 100 tasks, to be announced in the future. We evaluate 12 agents. The best one is Claude Opus 5.5, passing 58% of its runs. No run passes on 16 tasks. A higher score is not the same as a pass: most runs that beat the reference on the combined final score still fall short on some metric or workload. On a shared capability scale for agents and tasks, the median task is roughly as difficult as what the strongest agent can handle.
2610.29932.tldr_en: FrontierCS 2, a benchmark of 48 open-ended tasks, is introduced, a benchmark of 48 open-ended tasks that takes a paper and the code its authors released and delete the paper's contribution, which becomes the human reference that sets the bar.
2610.29932.hf_summary_en: FrontierCS 2 evaluates LLM agents on open-ended computer science R&D tasks using hidden evaluation suites and reveals that even the best agents pass only about half of tasks.

llm.title_ja: FrontierCS 2: 計算機科学の研究開発のためのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 論文とそのコードから貢献部分を削除した48のオープンエンドタスクからなるベンチマークFrontierCS 2を導入し、エージェントを研究環境内に配置して評価を行った。
llm.problem: 従来のおおっぴらなベンチマークは問題文を与えて1つのプログラムを評価するだけであり、エージェントが最先端のコンピュータ科学R&Dに貢献できるかが十分に評価されていない。
llm.method: 動作するリポジトリを継承しパッチを提出できる研究環境内にエージェントを配置する、13ドメインからなる48のオープンエンドタスクベンチマークFrontierCS 2を構築した。
llm.result: 12のエージェントを評価した結果、最高性能のClaude Opus 5.5でも58%の実行通過率であり、多くの実行が完全には基準を満たさないことを示した。

2610.29915.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
2610.29915.abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can produce visually plausible videos, yet their camera ego-motion often drifts over long horizons. Camera ego-motion determines how the viewpoint changes between frames and is essential for maintaining consistent geometry and trajectories. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components. First, we diagnose how precise ego motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising. Second, we strengthen ego-motion state in VGM by aligning the representations at the identified layers to a 3D foundation model through delta-token space. This space encodes the changes between consecutive frames, allowing the alignment to focus on ego-motion dynamics rather than static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign can largely improve motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness, while preserving visual quality. For example, it improves geometric consistency by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, with the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves the success rate of world action models (WAMs) by 10 points on mobile manipulation tasks of RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.
2610.29915.tldr_en: This work proposes CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components that improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.
2610.29915.hf_summary_en: CausalAlign improves long-horizon camera ego-motion consistency in diffusion video generators by aligning internal representations to 3D dynamics via delta-token space.

llm.title_ja: CausalAlign: 一貫したエゴモーションのためのビデオ生成モデルの因果的アライメント
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ生成モデルにおけるカメラのエゴモーションのドリフトを解消するため、デノイジング中の表現の挙動を診断し、3D基盤モデルへのアライメントを行うフレームワークCausalAlignを提案した。
llm.problem: 拡散ベースのビデオ生成モデルは視覚的に自然なビデオを生成できるが、長時間のホライゾンではカメラのエゴモーションがドリフトしやすい。
llm.method: 線形プローブと因果的介入によってエゴモーションの表現を診断し、デルタトークン空間を介して3D基盤モデルと表現をアライメントする因果的アライメントフレームワークCausalAlignを提案した。
llm.result: モーション精度、幾何学的一貫性、時間的滑らかさが大幅に向上し、ロボットのモバイルマニピュレーションタスクにおける世界行動モデルの成功率を向上させた。

2610.29903.title: HuMiT: Low-Latency Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation via Compact Reference Tracking
2610.29903.abstract: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation remains challenging due to the computational latency introduced by optimization-based retargeting pipelines and future-frame conditioning. Existing motion tracking policies typically require dense reference targets including full joint positions, body-part transformations, and even future frames, which tightly couples the controller to expensive upstream modules. In this work, we present HuMiT, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states including complete joint positions, dense body-part transformations, and even future frames. Experiments show that our policy achieves a communication-to-inference latency of $\sim$20 ms measured between headset streaming and policy output and a video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms (median) across different motion types. We validate the system on a Unitree G1 humanoid, showcasing split-second reactive responses such as catching a tossed ball, as well as coordinated loco-manipulation capabilities. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/.
2610.29903.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/
2610.29903.tldr_en: HuMiT is presented, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states.

llm.title_ja: HuMiT: コンパクトなリファレンス追従による低レイテンシ全身ヒューマノイド遠隔操作
llm.tldr_ja: 現在のフレームにおける4つのスパースキーポイントの姿勢などのコンパクトなリファレンスターゲットのみを必要とする統一追従ポリシーに基づく全身遠隔操作システムHuMiTを提案した。
llm.problem: 最適化ベースのリファージングパイプラインや将来フレームの条件付けに起因する計算レイテンシが、リアルタイムの全身ヒューマノイド遠隔操作を困難にしている。
llm.method: ルートの高さ、速度、4つのスパースキーポイントのSE(3)姿勢というコンパクトな参照ターゲットのみを入力とする統一追従ポリシーを構築した。
llm.result: Unitree G1において約20msの通信から推論へのレイテンシを達成し、飛んできたボールをキャッチするなどの素早い反応動作やロコモーション・マニピュレーションを実証した。

2610.29866.title: GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.29866.abstract: Geometric structure is essential for robotic manipulation and understanding the 3D world. Most VLA models rely on 2D representations of current observations, while geometry-aware approaches often require additional 3D information. However, geometry inferred independently from individual observations is often discarded rather than accumulated into a persistent task representation. Our key insight is that action generation needs a compact, task-relevant geometric abstraction that can be continuously updated, rather than a complete, renderable 3D reconstruction at every step. We introduce GeoMem-VLA, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space. During training, a frozen geometry foundation model supervises learnable GeoPlan tokens through a geometric flow-matching objective over the current scene point map and future end-effector tracks. These tokens are integrated with the memory of observation representations, where historical information is retrieved, adaptively fused with current observations, and consolidated to retain event frames as the task progresses. At inference, the policy retrieves historical representations and fuses them with the current working representation to predict actions, without invoking the 3D teacher or explicitly reconstructing the scene. After benchmark-specific downstream adaptation, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9% average success on LIBERO and 91.10% / 91.24% on RoboTwin's clean/randomized settings. Across five real-world tasks, GeoMem-VLA achieves 78.0% average success. These results suggest that internalizing and remembering 3D scene understanding is a promising approach to robot control.
2610.29866.tldr_en: GeoMem-VLA is introduced, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space.

llm.title_ja: GeoMem-VLA: 3Dシーン理解をビジョン・言語・行動モデルの時間的メモリに内面化する
llm.tldr_ja: 明示的な3D教師信号を専用の幾何学的トークンに内面化し、行動生成のための時間的メモリとして維持するVLAフレームワークGeoMem-VLAを提案した。
llm.problem: 大半のVLAモデルは2D表現に依存しており、個別の観測から推論された幾何学情報は蓄積されずに破棄されてしまう。
llm.method: 幾何学的フローマッチング目的に基づいて学習可能なGeoPlanトークンを指導し、観測表現のメモリと統合して行動生成を行うGeoMem-VLAを導入した。
llm.result: LIBEROやRoboTwinのベンチマーク、および5つの実世界タスクにおいて高い平均成功率を達成した。

2610.29845.title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation
2610.29845.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced. Project website: https://rangenav.github.io/.
2610.29845.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Added project website to abstract and updated author affiliation; research content unchanged
2610.29845.tldr_en: RangeNav is presented, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data that demonstrates robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle.

llm.title_ja: RangeNav: ロボットナビゲーションのためのタスク整列型LiDARレンジ画像事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: 完全な合成データで事前学習されたコンパクトなLiDARレンジ画像エンコーダーRangeNavを提案し、混雑した環境や悪条件の現場で頑健なナビゲーションを実証した。
llm.problem: 全周LiDARは全方位のカバーを提供するが、強化学習における表現学習はサンプル効率が悪く、既存の3D事前学習済み点群エンコーダーは並列RLシミュレーションに対してメモリを消費しすぎる。
llm.method: 異方性畳み込みと円形パディングを使用し、レンジ再構​​築、セマンティックセグメンテーション、BEV予測を組み合わせたナビゲーション整列型目標で事前学習したコンパクトなエンコーダーRangeNavを開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの成功率が大幅に向上し、Unitree B2-W四足歩行ロボットによる混雑した群衆や低照度設定、建設現場でのゼロショット実機展開を成功させた。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2610.29839.title: Spacetime Splines for Adaptive Robot Motions
2610.29839.abstract: Movement primitives commonly represent robot mo- tions through basis functions indexed by time or phase. Inspired by spacetime representations employed in physics, we propose a spline-based formulation in which spatial geometry and temporal progression are represented within a common set of continuous variables. The proposed method jointly estimates a shared Bezier curve, while allowing spatial and temporal model complexity to be adapted independently (e.g., demonstration-specific phase modulation). As use case, we consider an alternating optimization process that simultaneously estimates path intervals observed in partial demonstrations. Simulation experiments demonstrate accurate joint recovery, refinement through modifications in model complexity and continuity, and improved robustness to variance in the demonstration set. Finally, we demonstrate online retiming and synchronization capabilities in a patient-turning task assisted by a robot, evaluated with a physical manikin.
2610.29839.tldr_en: A spline-based formulation in which spatial geometry and temporal progression are represented within a common set of continuous variables is proposed, which jointly estimates a shared Bezier curve while allowing spatial and temporal model complexity to be adapted independently.

llm.title_ja: 適応的なロボット動作のための時空スプライン
llm.tldr_ja: 空間幾何学と時間的進行を共通の連続変数で表現するスプラインベースの定式化を提案し、共有ベジェ曲線構造の空間・時間モデルの複雑さを独立して適応させる。
llm.problem: 運動プリミティブにおける空間および時間のモデル複雑さを独立して適応させることの難しさ
llm.method: 空間幾何学と時間的進行を共通の連続変数で表現し、共有ベジェ曲線群を共同推定するスプラインベースの定式化
llm.result: シミュレーション実験において正確な関節復元やモデル複雑性の変更による洗練、デモンストレーション分散に対する頑健性の向上が示された

2610.29829.title: Robot Generalization Beyond Volume: The Diversity Path via Zero-Shot Capabilities
2610.29829.abstract: General-purpose robots must handle tasks, objects and environments they were never trained on, yet zero-shot generalization remains one of the least solved problems in physical AI. In digital AI, zero-shot capability grew with the volume and, above all, the diversity of training data, much of it sourced from the crowd. Robotics instead relies on paid collection by a few well-funded teams, which yields volume without diversity. We formulate zero-shot generalization in physical AI as coverage of the deployment distribution, and show that more samples from the same collectors shrink the unseen region only slowly, while each new contributor can extend it. Building on this and on zero-shot learning, we propose a shared latent space for robot actions that combines multi-modal alignment, generative augmentation, and noisy-label learning. As a scalable source of diverse data, we propose a community of developers building applications on one standard, approachable robot, Origami. We close with a testable hypothesis and an evaluation protocol relating real-robot zero-shot success to the diversity of contributed data.
2610.29829.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables, including supplementary material
2610.29829.tldr_en: A shared latent space for robot actions that combines multi-modal alignment, generative augmentation, and noisy-label learning is proposed, and a community of developers building applications on one standard, approachable robot, Origami is proposed.

llm.title_ja: ボリュームを超えたロボットの汎化：ゼロショット性能を通じた多様性の道
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの行動に対する共有潜在空間を提案し、マルチモーダルアライメント、生成拡張、ノイズラベル学習を組み合わせるとともに、標準的なロボット「Origami」を用いた開発者コミュニティを提案した。
llm.problem: 物理AIにおけるゼロショット汎化の難しさと、既存のロボットデータ収集が多様性を欠く点
llm.method: マルチモーダルアライメント、生成拡張、ノイズラベル学習を組み合わせたロボット行動用の共有潜在空間の構築と、標準的なロボットによる開発者コミュニティの形成
llm.result: 実ロボットにおけるゼロショット成功率と貢献データの多様性を関連付ける評価プロトコルとテスト可能な仮説を提示した
keywords_ja: オープンソースロボット

2610.29768.title: UniRAP: Towards Unified Part-level Physical Affordance Reasoning and Actionable Perception
2610.29768.abstract: Vision-language perception has achieved impressive progress in aligning natural language with visual observations, yet grounding high-level semantics into part-level physical interaction remains challenging. To address this gap, we propose UniRAP, a unified model for inferring part-level physical affordances and mapping language instructions to actionable geometric representations. UniRAP formulates this problem as a conditional multimodal generation task, integrating visual inputs, textual instructions, and optional prompts into a shared spatiotemporal representation space through a unified interface token mechanism. To predict executable contact geometry, we introduce a Unified Affordance Decoder (UAD), which jointly performs object detection, part-level affordance segmentation, and 4-DoF interaction pose estimation by leveraging intermediate segmentation features. In addition, we propose a curriculum-based transfer training strategy that progressively adapts the model from general visual parsing to interaction-aware perception, improving data efficiency under limited textual annotations. Experiments show that UniRAP achieves state-of-the-art performance on referring expression segmentation, affordance grounding, and interaction pose estimation, while maintaining strong spatiotemporal consistency in dynamic video scenarios. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of UniRAP as a unified perception framework for language-guided physical manipulation.
2610.29768.tldr_en: Experiments show that UniRAP achieves state-of-the-art performance on referring expression segmentation, affordance grounding, and interaction pose estimation, while maintaining strong spatiotemporal consistency in dynamic video scenarios, demonstrating the effectiveness of UniRAP as a unified perception framework for language-guided physical manipulation.

llm.title_ja: UniRAP：統合されたパーツレベルの物理的アフォダンス推論と行動可能知覚に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: UniRAPは、視覚入力・テキスト指示・プロンプトを統合インターフェースを介して共有時空表現空間に統合し、パーツレベルの物理的アフォダンス推論と行動可能な幾何表現へのマッピングを行う統一モデルである。
llm.problem: 高レベルなセマンティクスをパーツレベルの物理インタラクションにグラウンディングすることの困難さ
llm.method: 視覚入力やテキスト指示を統合し、Unified Affordance Decoderを用いて物体検出、アフォダンスセグメンテーション、ポーズ推定を同時に行うUniRAPの提案
llm.result: 参照表現セグメンテーション、アフォダンスグラウンディング、インタラクションポーズ推定で最先端の性能を達成し、動的動画シナリオで時空の一貫性を維持した
keywords_ja: 物体セグメンテーション

2610.29761.title: OMAR: Open-World Multi-Attribute Reasoning for Scene-Conditioned Shelf Organization
2610.29761.abstract: With the advent of foundation models, robots are increasingly capable of understanding and executing explicitly specified human tasks. Extending these capabilities to open-ended tasks, however, requires robots to infer appropriate actions from the observed scene. Household organization exemplifies this challenge, as robots must often act without detailed instructions, predefined object vocabularies, or known object-receptacle associations. While robots may follow instructions or learn organization preferences from demonstrations, inferring the latent organization of an occasionally changing scene and placing a novel object consistently with it remains challenging. We propose an open-world multi-attribute reasoning pipeline that grounds unknown objects across views and constructs an instance-level 3D scene graph for placement reasoning. First, a vision-language model proposes labels together with attributes such as content and packaging type, which are grounded through segmentation, depth, and multi-view association. Then, an LLM reasons over this representation to infer the latent shelf organization and rank scene-consistent object placements without explicitly user-provided preferences. The resulting placement rankings guide subsequent geometric and kinematic feasibility checks for execution. Our experimental evaluation shows that our approach leads to improved instance mapping and placement coherence over single-view language-grounding and geometry-only baselines, enabling autonomous placement of previously unseen objects without predefined object-receptacle mappings or class-specific retraining.
2610.29761.tldr_en: This work proposes an open-world multi-attribute reasoning pipeline that grounds unknown objects across views and constructs an instance-level 3D scene graph for placement reasoning, enabling autonomous placement of previously unseen objects without predefined object-receptacle mappings or class-specific retraining.

llm.title_ja: OMAR：シーン条件付きシェルフ整理のためのオープンワールド多属性推論
llm.tldr_ja: 未知のオブジェクトをクロスビューでグラウンディングし配置推論のためのインスタンスレベル3Dシーングラフを構築するオープンワールド多属性推論パイプラインを提案し、事前定義されたマッピングなしで未見オブジェクトの自律配置を可能にした。
llm.problem: 詳細な指示や事前定義された語彙なしで、変化するシーンの潜在的な整理ルールを推論し新しいオブジェクトを配置することの困難さ
llm.method: VLMによるラベルと属性の提案、セグメンテーションやマルチビュー関連付けによるグラウンディング、LLMによるシーン整理の推論と配置の順位付けを行うパイプラインの構築
llm.result: 単一視点の言語グラウンディングおよび幾何学のみのベースラインと比較して、インスタンスマッピングと配置の一貫性が向上した

2610.29730.title: Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies
2610.29730.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies need to recognize gaps in their training knowledge to request useful demonstrations or assistance in new situations, especially when failures are costly. Disagreement within an ensemble of independently trained policies can guide these decisions, but requires training and running multiple policies. We propose post-hoc kernel-variance heads that estimate epistemic uncertainty from the embeddings of a single policy. Each head computes the conditional variance of a Gaussian process conditioned on embeddings from the training demonstrations. Fitting requires no regression targets or gradient updates and leaves the policy unchanged. In experiments with SmolVLA on LIBERO-10, the kernel variance heads perform competitively with two-policy ensemble scores in task-level correlation with task success, in demonstration acquisition during active learning, and in referral to a stronger supervisor policy as a proxy for human assistance. For SmolVLA, the head on the vision-language backbone reduces uncertainty-scoring time by up to approximately a factor of 50 compared with ensemble scores, while also substantially reducing setup costs. We also show that the established evaluation protocol on LIBERO-10 primarily rewards recognition of coverage differences between tasks, while execution variability weakens assessment of within-task rankings. Thus, controlled perturbations provide a complementary evaluation: modality-specific heads identify unfamiliar camera, instruction, or state inputs, while fused heads can detect unfamiliar combinations of individually familiar inputs. With a supervisor proxy trained on the evaluated perturbation families, the decoder head improves within-task referral over ensemble disagreement. These findings show that useful uncertainty estimates for adaptive robot learning can be obtained from a single policy.
2610.29730.tldr_en: Findings show that useful uncertainty estimates for adaptive robot learning can be obtained from a single policy, and post-hoc kernel-variance heads that estimate epistemic uncertainty from the embeddings of a single policy are proposed.

llm.title_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動ポリシーのための事後エピステミック不確実性
llm.tldr_ja: 単一ポリシーの埋め込みからエピステミック不確実性を推定する事後カーネル分散ヘッドを提案し、適応型ロボット学習において有用な不確実性推定を効率的に取得できることを示した。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーが新しい状況での失敗を防ぐため自身の知識のギャップを認識する必要があるが、アンサンブル法は計算コストが高い点
llm.method: 訓練デモンストレーションの埋め込みに基づくガウスプロセスの条件付き分散を計算する、単一ポリシー向け事後カーネル分散ヘッドの導入
llm.result: SmolVLAを用いたLIBERO-10での実験で、タスク成功との相関やアクティブラーニングにおいてアンサンブルと同等の性能を示しつつ、不確実性の計算時間を約50分の一に短縮した
keywords_ja: エピステミック不確実性

2610.29724.title: Sufficient and Necessary Causal Explanations for the Analysis of Autonomous Systems
2610.29724.abstract: Understanding failures of autonomous systems is challenging, particularly when their behavior depends on black-box components such as neural networks. In this work, we make a distinction between two objectives of failure analysis: reproduction, which seeks to identify conditions sufficient to reproduce an observed failure, and avoidance, which seeks to identify the changes required to prevent it. Previous work on causal explanations of system failures is based on the concept of sufficient explanations and naturally supports reproduction. Nevertheless, we observe that it does not address the problem of avoiding the failure. In this paper, we introduce and formalize the concept of necessary explanations for system analysis as the correct formalism for failure avoidance. We place necessary explanations in the framework of actual causality and show that, together with sufficient explanations, they provide a unified causal framework for addressing both objectives of failure analysis. We present an efficient approximation algorithm for generating necessary explanations based on the notion of causal responsibility. We evaluate the efficiency of our approach across multiple environments. We demonstrate the practical utility of necessary explanations for failure avoidance through counterfactual generation and show that it outperforms existing methods.
2610.29724.tldr_en: This work introduces and formalizes the concept of necessary explanations for system analysis as the correct formalism for failure avoidance and presents an efficient approximation algorithm for generating necessary explanations based on the notion of causal responsibility.

llm.title_ja: 自律システムの分析のための十分かつ必要な因果的説明
llm.tldr_ja: システム分析における「必要な説明」の概念を導入・定式化し、因果責任の概念に基づく効率的な近似アルゴリズムを提示して、十分な説明と合わせて統一された因果的枠組みを提供する。
llm.problem: ブラックボックス成分に依存する自律システムの失敗について、単に再現するだけでなく回避するための条件を分析することの難しさ
llm.method: 因果責任の概念に基づく「必要な説明」の形式化と、十分な説明と組み合わせた効率的な近似アルゴリズムの提示
llm.result: 複数環境での効率性の評価により、反事実生成を通じた失敗回避における実用的な有用性が示され、既存手法を上回った

2610.29716.title: Reconstruction-Augmented Visuomotor Pre-Training of 3D-Grounded Bimanual Dexterity from RGB-Only Human Videos
2610.29716.abstract: We present SpatialDex, a framework that learns 3D-grounded bimanual dexterity from RGB-only human videos through reconstruction-augmented visuomotor pre-training. The central idea is to learn human behavior together with its spatial context. From each video, we reconstruct the scene geometry and estimate the hand motion, align them at a shared video-level scale using the hand-size prior of 3D hand estimates. We retain the reconstructed geometry as both a policy input and a prediction target. The policy grounds the token grid of a pre-trained vision-language model in this geometry through gated residual fusion, is trained to predict future scene geometry alongside wrist and finger actions, and generates finger motion conditioned on the predicted trajectories of both wrists. Pre-trained on 1M human-video clips and fine-tuned with a small number of robot demonstrations, SpatialDex outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by 16.5 points on nine simulated dexterous tasks across two embodiments and by 38.3 points on six real-world bimanual dexterous tasks. Under a matched comparison, pre-training with reconstructed geometry improves success by 14.2 points over pre-training on hand motion alone.
2610.29716.tldr_en: SpatialDex, a framework that learns 3D-grounded bimanual dexterity from RGB-only human videos through reconstruction-augmented visuomotor pre-training, is presented, which outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

llm.title_ja: 再構築拡張された視覚運動事前学習によるRGB動画からの3Dグラウンドされた両手器用さ獲得
llm.tldr_ja: SpatialDexは再構築拡張された視覚運動事前学習によりRGBのみの人間動画から3Dグラウンドされた両手器用さを学習するフレームワークであり、最先端手法を大きく上回る性能を達成した。
llm.problem: RGBのみの人間動画から3D空間コンテキストを保持しつつ両手の器用な操作ポリシーを学習することの困難さ
llm.method: シーン幾何学の再構築と手の動きの推定を行い、手のサイズ事前知識を用いて共有動画レベルのスケールで整合させ、ゲート付き残差融合によりVLMのトークングリッドを幾何学にグラウンディングするSpatialDexの提案
llm.result: シミュレーションの器用なタスクで16.5ポイント、実世界のタスクで38.3ポイント既存手法を上回った

2610.29702.title: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning
2610.29702.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show promising reasoning capabilities, but reliable physical interaction requires planning that accounts for when actions are executable and how they change the world. These preconditions and effects are environment-dependent and often not captured by MLLMs, making adaptation challenging. Yet existing approaches either require costly environment-specific training or rely on unstructured interaction experience that is difficult to reuse. Therefore, we introduce CausGround, a non-parametric causal interaction grounding framework that distills interaction experience into reusable action-centered causal knowledge. CausGround identifies action preconditions and effects and organizes them in a factorized world-state representation capturing object attributes and inter-object relations. At planning time, task-relevant causal dependencies are grounded in current observations to support backward reasoning over preconditions and forward reasoning over effects for action selection and multi-step planning. We evaluate CausGround on simulated high-level planning, interaction reasoning, and real-world robot manipulation. On adapted VirtualHome and RoboCasa benchmarks, CausGround improves vision-based high-level planning across MLLM backbones, increasing average task success from 24.9% to 53.3% on VirtualHome and closed-loop planning success from 43.0% to 57.0% on RoboCasa. On SWITCH, average interaction reasoning accuracy increases from 25.8% to 31.9%, indicating improved action selection, recovery, and verification. Moreover, real-world experiments show that CausGround reasons backward from MLLM-interpreted goals to derive executable high-level action sequences for sequential manipulation. These results demonstrate that reusable action preconditions and effects support long-horizon embodied planning across diverse environments without parameter updates.
2610.29702.tldr_en: CusGround is introduced, a non-parametric causal interaction grounding framework that distills interaction experience into reusable action-centered causal knowledge and demonstrates that reusable action preconditions and effects support long-horizon embodied planning across diverse environments without parameter updates.
2610.29702.hf_summary_en: CausGround extracts reusable action preconditions and effects from interaction experience to improve embodied planning and reasoning across diverse environments without model retraining.

llm.title_ja: CausGround：適応型身についた計画のための因果的インタラクション・グラウンディング
llm.tldr_ja: CausGroundはインタラクション体験を再利用可能な行動中心の因果知識に要約するノンパラメトリックな因果的インタラクション・グラウンディングフレームワークであり、パラメータ更新なしで長期の身体化された計画を支援する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）が環境依存の行動の前提条件や結果を十分に捉えられず、適応が困難である点
llm.method: 行動の前提条件と効果を特定し、物体属性や関係を捉えた因果的表現に整理するノンパラメトリックフレームワークCausGroundの導入
llm.result: VirtualHomeおよびRoboCasaのベンチマークにおいてタスク成功率が向上し、実世界の連続的なマニピュレーションでも実行可能な高レベル行動シーケンスを導出した
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.29699.title: AirPlayground: Benchmarking Aerial Navigation across Diverse Reconstructed Environments
2610.29699.abstract: Large-scale aerial resources provide a foundation for learning navigation across diverse environments. However, existing resources remain limited in providing (1) densely sampled flight demonstrations for learning different policy formulations and (2) broad environment coverage for standardized closed-loop evaluation. To address these limitations, we introduce AirPlayground, a unified benchmark for training and evaluating aerial navigation policies across diverse environments. We first construct 94 photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) environments spanning indoor, urban outdoor, and vegetation settings, with aligned collision geometry. Building on these environments, we develop a scene-adaptive pipeline for automated expert flight collection, yielding 94K demonstrations and 46.5M synchronized observation-state-action samples at 50 Hz. We further provide an extensible API that supports training different policy formulations on this shared corpus and evaluating them under unified protocols in the corresponding environments. We benchmark seven baselines spanning four policy paradigms across three navigation settings in seen and unseen environments, and further examine scaling behavior with ACT. Scaling ACT's training corpus from 5 to 70 scenes raises median success rates on seen and unseen environments from 30.6% and 16.8% to 41.2% and 29.4%, respectively. Through this shared training and evaluation framework, AirPlayground supports analysis of how offline prediction errors relate to closed-loop outcomes. Our analyses highlight the roles of prediction errors, execution protocols, and scene interactions in closed-loop performance.
2610.29699.tldr_en: AirPlayground, a unified benchmark for training and evaluating aerial navigation policies across diverse environments, is introduced and analysis of how offline prediction errors relate to closed-loop outcomes is supported.

llm.title_ja: AirPlayground：多様な再構築環境にわたる空中ナビゲーションのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: AirPlaygroundは多様な環境で空中ナビゲーションポリシーを訓練・評価するための統一ベンチマークであり、オフライン予測誤差と閉ループ性能の関係の分析をサポートする。
llm.problem: 既存の空中ナビゲーションリソースが、多様な方策学習のための高密度な飛行デモンストレーションや標準化された閉ループ評価のための広い環境網羅性を欠いている点
llm.method: 94のフォトリアルな3Dガウススプラッティング（3DGS）環境の構築と、シーン適応型自動エキスパート飛行収集パイプラインによる大規模データの生成
llm.result: ACTの訓練シーンを5から70に増やすことで、見慣れた環境および未見環境での中央値成功率がそれぞれ大幅に向上した

2610.29692.title: FlowVLA: Learning Flow-Aware Physical Completion for Quantitative Robotic Pouring
2610.29692.abstract: During steady pouring, images and robot pose may remain nearly unchanged while transferred mass accumulates, making the return decision ambiguous for a whole-task vision-language-action (VLA) policy. We present FlowVLA, which separates motor generation from physical-completion estimation. A shared $π_{0.5}$ action expert learns approach, pour, and return with boundary-aware supervision. A target-independent estimator fuses visual, joint, wrist-wrench, and recurrent force-belief histories to maintain an estimate of transferred mass. The controller initiates return when this estimate plus predicted residual outflow reaches the requested mass. In coffee-pot/water experiments, FlowVLA achieves 13.1 g goal-balanced mean absolute error (MacroMAE), lower than all tested VLA baselines. Across all attempts, 53.7% both complete the task and finish within +/-10% of the requested mass. The same model interpolates to held-out 150/250-g targets without retraining. Independently trained models further evaluate the formulation in three additional container-fluid settings.
2610.29692.tldr_en: FlowVLA, which separates motor generation from physical-completion estimation, is presented, which achieves 13.1 g goal-balanced mean absolute error (MacroMAE), lower than all tested VLA baselines.

llm.title_ja: FlowVLA：定量的ロボットポアリングのための流れを意識した物理的完了の学習
llm.tldr_ja: FlowVLAはモーター生成と物理的完了推定を分離し、目標に応じた平均絶対誤差（MacroMAE）13.1gを達成して既存のVLAベースラインを上回った。
llm.problem: 安定したポアリング中、視覚やポーズがほぼ変化しないまま移動質量が蓄積するため、全タスク型VLAポリシーにとって復帰判断が曖昧になる点
llm.method: 行動専門家（$\pi_{0.5}$）によるアプローチ・ポアリング・復帰の学習と、視覚・関節・手首の力を統合して移送質量を推定する独立した推定量による分離設計
llm.result: コーヒーポット・水を用いた実験で、テストされたすべてのVLAベースラインよりも低い13.1gのMacroMAEを達成し、未訓練のターゲットにも補間可能であった

2610.29677.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
2610.29677.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. Recent digital agents test this idea by rewriting their own code and checking each version with executable tests. Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves. Gains carry forward only when feedback addresses remaining learning needs, the receiving component can use the change, its value survives changes in tasks or hardware, and continued practice remains safe and affordable. Existing studies, concentrated in manipulation, support behavioral improvement, benefits to later learning, and procedure improvement. Some systems also change the improver's knowledge or tools, but the physical studies reviewed here have yet to isolate gains attributable to recursion. We synthesize these findings into evaluation principles and research directions for machines that, trial by trial, safely improve the way they improve.
2610.29677.comment: 93 pages, 15 figures, 21 tables. Project page: https://physical2rsi.github.io/
2610.29677.tldr_en: This work examines how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves and synthesizes these findings into evaluation principles and research directions for machines that, trial by trial, safely improve the way they improve.

llm.title_ja: 物理AIにおける再帰的自己改善に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的経験が改善メカニズムをどのように強化できるか、またその結果得られる利点がメカニズム自体のさらなる自己改善をどのように支えられるかを検証し、試行錯誤を通じて自己改善の方法を安全に向上させるための研究方向を整理した。
llm.problem: デジタル世界の自己改善メカニズムを物理世界に持ち込む際に、部分観測からの学習、コストのかかる試行、変化する動作条件、不可逆的な結果を扱うことの難しさ
llm.method: ロボット学習内での再帰的自己改善（RSI）の位置づけ、行動改善から改善プロセス自体の向上への経路の分析、および評価原則の統合
llm.result: 既存のマニピュレーションにおける行動改善や手法改善の成果を整理し、安全に自己改善を行うための評価原則と研究方向を提示した

2610.29676.title: DriveMLP: When Training Strategy Outperforms Model Complexity in Autonomous Driving
2610.29676.abstract: Learning motion planning policies that remain reliable under closed-loop execution is a central challenge in Autonomous Driving (AD). Imitation Learning (IL) scales well to large AD datasets but suffers from distribution shift, causal confusion, and compounding errors under closed-loop execution. In contrast, Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically requires handcrafted rule-based rewards and massive simulation. We study a simple closed-loop IL framework that uses RL purely as an optimization tool, guided by a trajectory-distance reward derived from logged expert data. We refer to this training strategy as Expert-Guided RL (EGRL). Through a controlled empirical study we find evidence that the training procedure, rather than model size and complexity, accounts for a substantial part of the performance gains. We then introduce DriveMLP, a lightweight MLP policy trained with EGRL, as a simple instantiation of these findings. It achieves a score of 86.51 on the nuPlan Val14 Reactive benchmark, a +3.2 point improvement over the previous best IL planner (Flow Planner), with >15x faster inference. Code is available at: https://github.com/alessandro-canevaro/DriveMLP .
2610.29676.comment: Accepted at 2026 Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)
2610.29676.tldr_en: This work studies a simple closed-loop IL framework that uses RL purely as an optimization tool, guided by a trajectory-distance reward derived from logged expert data, and introduces DriveMLP, a lightweight MLP policy trained with EGRL, as a simple instantiation of these findings.

llm.title_ja: DriveMLP：自動運転において訓練戦略がモデル複雑性を上回る瞬間
llm.tldr_ja: ログに記録されたエキスパートデータから得られる報酬を用いた強化学習を最適化ツールとして利用する単純な閉ループ模倣学習フレームワーク（EGRL）を研究し、軽量なMLPポリシーであるDriveMLPを提案した。
llm.problem: 自動運転のモーションプランニングにおいて、模倣学習は分布のシフトや因果的混乱に悩まされ、強化学習は大規模なシミュレーションや報酬設計を必要とする点
llm.method: 軌道距離報酬を用いたエキスパート誘導型強化学習（EGRL）による訓練戦略の導入と、軽量MLPポリシーであるDriveMLPの構築
llm.result: nuPlan Val14 Reactiveベンチマークで86.51点を記録し、従来のベストなILプランナーを3.2点上回りつつ15倍以上高速な推論を実現した
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.29674.title: From Acceptance and Avoidance to Affective Viscosity: Designing Social Agents Intermediating in Human Relationships
2610.29674.abstract: As social agents become embedded in human relationships, they are expected not only to provide smooth assistance but also to handle rejection, discomfort, jealousy, persistence, and other forms of social tension. This paper connects two research directions: acceptance and avoidance in response to an agent's gaze, approach, and contact, and affective viscosity as a model of how negative affect accumulates, persists, is suppressed, and is expressed over time. We argue that avoidance should not be treated merely as a failure of interaction, but as a relational signal that indicates boundaries between humans and agents. Building on this view, affective viscosity provides a design perspective for agents that maintain, suppress, or express negative states depending on social relationships and interaction histories. We discuss several ongoing design cases, including triadic jealousy, discomfort suppression, patience timing, and spatiotemporal stickiness, and consider how these cases lead to broader questions of blame and accountable intervention. Rather than designing agents as simple scapegoats or artificial villains, we ask how agents can intermediate in problematic social situations while making their intervention traceable, limited, contestable, and repairable.
2610.29674.comment: The 2nd International Workshop on Trust and Blame in Multi-Person Multi-Agent Societies (TBSA_2nd) in conjunction with HAI 2026, 5 pages, 2 figures
2610.29674.tldr_en: This paper argues that avoidance should not be treated merely as a failure of interaction, but as a relational signal that indicates boundaries between humans and agents, and affective viscosity as a model of how negative affect accumulates, persists, is suppressed, and is expressed over time.

llm.title_ja: 受容・回避から情動的粘性へ：人間関係の仲介を行うソーシャルエージェントの設計
llm.tldr_ja: 回避をインタラクションの失敗としてではなく人間とエージェントの境界を示す関係的シグナルとして捉え、負の情動の蓄積や表現をモデル化する「情動的粘性」の設計視点を論じた。
llm.problem: ソーシャルエージェントが円滑な支援だけでなく拒絶や緊張などの社会的摩擦に対処する必要があるが、回避の扱いや負の情動のモデリングが課題である点
llm.method: 回避を関係的シグナルとみなし、負の情動の蓄積や抑制をモデル化する「情動的粘性」の設計視点の提示と、嫉妬や不快感抑制などのデザインケースの検討
llm.result: エージェントが追跡可能・限定的・修正可能な形で社会的緊張に介入するための幅広い問いと設計原則を導出した
keywords_ja: ソーシャルエージェント

2610.29647.title: Reading the Room: Scale-ambiguous Semantic Registration of Sparse VSLAM Maps to Floor Plans in Partially Built Environments
2610.29647.abstract: Many robotic construction applications, such as progress tracking, require registering a sensor trajectory to a prior 2D floor plan. Visual capture is attractive for its low cost and availability, but aligning a visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) map to a floor plan is difficult; VSLAM recovers geometry only up to an unknown similarity transform, the sparse point cloud is cross-modal to the symbolic floor plan, sites are only partially built during capture, and construction sites are visually repetitive, degrading map quality while removing distinctive features. Existing methods address at most two of these challenges. We thus introduce Reading the Room(RR), a global-local approach to register scale-ambiguous, sparse, semantic VSLAM maps to partially built floor plans. Our key idea is to define a single robust, differentiable, class-balanced semantic-geometric energy function that governs all stages of the pipeline. We develop two global initialization schemes, leveraging a single inaccurate user-provided correspondence if provided, or estimating the initialization globally using a cross-modal matching network. Both schemes are designed to find initial candidates with respect to the energy function, which is then directly optimized for local refinement. We evaluate RR on 33 sequences across three active construction sites against classical and learning-based baselines, achieving a 4.5x improvement in mean absolute trajectory error over the strongest baseline in the general unconstrained setting, which increases to 7.6x when an anchor is provided.
2610.29647.tldr_en: Reading the Room (RR), a global-local approach to register scale-ambiguous, sparse, semantic VSLAM maps to partially built floor plans, is introduced, to define a single robust, differentiable, class-balanced semantic-geometric energy function that governs all stages of the pipeline.

llm.title_ja: 部屋を読む：部分的に構築された環境におけるスパースなVSLAMマップのフロアプランへのスケール曖昧な意味論的登録
llm.tldr_ja: Reading the Room (RR)は、すべてのパイプラインを支配する単一でロバストかつ微分可能なクラスバランス型意味論的幾何学的エネルギー関数を定義することにより、スケール曖昧なスパースVSLAMマップを部分構築フロアプランに登録するグローバル・ローカル手法である。
llm.problem: VSLAMマップのスケールの曖昧さ、クロスモダリティ、および建設現場が部分的にしか構築されておらず視覚的に反復的である点に起因するフロアプランへの位置合わせの困難さ
llm.method: ロバストで微分可能な意味論的・幾何学的エネルギー関数を定義し、ユーザー提供の対応関係やクロスモダリティマッチングネットワークを用いてグローバル初期化を行ってから局所最適化を行う手法の提案
llm.result: 33の建設現場のシーケンスを用いた評価において、一般的な制約のない設定で最強のベースラインの4.5倍、アンカー提供時には7.6倍の平均絶対軌跡誤差の改善を達成した
keywords_ja: セマンティックマップ

2610.29646.title: From Association to Decision Value: Testing Paired Instruction Dependence for VLA Corpus Selection
2610.29646.abstract: Choosing among robot demonstration corpora is a ranking problem: an upstream diagnostic must preserve which candidates produce better downstream policies, not merely correlate with average performance. We study paired instruction dependence, the rate at which a demonstrator changes its first decision when only the goal changes. Across 136 independently seeded quadruped-navigation corpora, predictions developed on 56 corpora are evaluated prospectively on 80 held-out corpora. The audit is reliable and associated with downstream paired correctness, and lowers mean absolute prediction error when added to a correctness-aware baseline, but the primary proper-log-score increment is +0.059 nats (95% corpus-bootstrap CI [-0.027, 0.133]) and the prespecified top-20% comparison does not establish an incremental selection gain. An exploratory response decomposition suggests a structural source of this predictive-ranking mismatch: under the tested predictor specification, separating both-correct and both-wrong responses yields larger held-out gains than their unsigned switch statistic. Seed-to-seed agreement indicates that the held-out endpoint retains recoverable rank signal. These results show that counterfactual response structure can be reliable and predictive while providing limited incremental decision value in this setting when compressed into an unsigned statistic, motivating diagnostics that preserve outcome-relevant structure and are validated against the decisions they are intended to support.
2610.29646.tldr_en: Results show that counterfactual response structure can be reliable and predictive while providing limited incremental decision value in this setting when compressed into an unsigned statistic, motivating diagnostics that preserve outcome-relevant structure and are validated against the decisions they are intended to support.

llm.title_ja: 関連付けから決定価値へ：VLAコーパス選択のためのペア命令依存性の検証
llm.tldr_ja: 反事実的応答構造が信頼性と予測可能性を持ちつつも、非符号化統計量に圧縮された場合には限定的なインクリメンタル決定価値しか提供しないことを示した。
llm.problem: ロボットデモンストレーションコーパスの選択において、上流の診断がダウンストリームの方策性能を確実に予測し保持する必要がある点
llm.method: 136の四足歩行ナビゲーションコーパスを用い、デモンストレータがゴール変更時に最初の決定を変更する割合である「ペア命令依存性」を検証する診断手法の評価
llm.result: 予測構造の改善により正確性が向上する一方で、単純な非符号化統計量への圧縮では追加の決定価値が限られることが示された

2610.29612.title: Watch Your Step: Anticipated Perception for Humanoid Locomotion
2610.29612.abstract: Perceptive locomotion policies typically observe a dense robot-centric elevation map, although only the terrain beneath and around the next footsteps informs the control decision. Learned encoders compress the whole visual input, leaving the policy to work out which inputs matter while learning the baseline locomotion task. Learning both at once slows training and, without computationally expensive attention mechanisms, makes generalization to new terrain harder. We instead remove redundant inputs from the elevation map before the policy sees it. A lightweight foothold prediction model (FPM) predicts future footholds from proprioception and the velocity command alone, and we sample the elevation map only in small patches around these predicted footholds. We train the prediction model alongside the locomotion policy, periodically retraining it on new policy rollouts as the robot's gait matures. This allows the perception to anticipate where the policy will step, while the policy learns to leverage terrain information around those steps. With the proposed lightweight preprocessing, the policy reaches a given terrain difficulty in roughly a third of the training iterations required with the complete map. It outperforms policies that observe the complete map where footholds are sparse, including in narrow walled corridors, and on unseen terrain, and it matches an attention-based encoder trained at several times the cost. The policy transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid traversing various obstacles, stairs, gaps, and step-downs beyond the training distribution in both indoor and outdoor environments.
2610.29612.tldr_en: A lightweight foothold prediction model (FPM) predicts future footholds from proprioception and the velocity command alone, and the model is trained alongside the locomotion policy, allowing the perception to anticipate where the policy will step, while the policy learns to leverage terrain information around those steps.

llm.title_ja: 足元にご注意を：ヒューマノイド歩行のための予見的知覚
llm.tldr_ja: 軽量な足場予測モデル（FPM）により、固有受容感覚と速度指令のみから将来の足場を予測し、その予測足場周辺の小さなパッチの標高マップのみを観測することで、歩行ポリシーの学習と一般化を効率化する。
llm.problem: 知覚的歩行ポリシーがロボット中心の高密度な標高マップ全体を処理するため学習が遅くなり、一般化が困難になる点
llm.method: 固有受容感覚と速度指令から将来の足場を予測する軽量な足場予測モデル（FPM）を導入し、予測された足場周辺のみの標高マップをポリシーに入力する仕組みの構築
llm.result: 完全なマップを用いる手法に比べ約3分の1の学習イテレーションで同等の困難な地形に到達し、Unitree G1ヒューマノイドでのゼロショット実機転移に成功した
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.29586.title: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Jumping in Lunar Gravity
2610.29586.abstract: Legged robots can extend planetary exploration to rugged and discontinuous terrain that is inaccessible to conventional rovers. In lunar gravity, jumping further expands this mobility by enabling robots to cross obstacles and gaps that cannot be traversed by walking alone. We present a multistage reinforcement-learning approach that produces a single end-to-end control policy for commanded point-to-point jumping under lunar gravity. The resulting policy has a simple architecture and relies exclusively on mission-compatible onboard sensing, making its deployment on a real lunar mission plausible. In simulation, the learned policy performs accurate point-to-point jumps with landing errors smaller than the robot's body size. We analyze the torque and power demands of lunar jumping and characterize performance degradation under extreme outlier events, including control-update freezes of up to \SI{1}{s} during flight. Hardware transfer demonstrates that the policy can successfully execute a vertical jump under lunar-gravity offloading. Furthermore, the measured torque and power profiles are consistent with the simulation results and remain within the robot's hardware limits.

llm.title_ja: 月面重力下における四足歩行ロボットの跳躍のためのエンドツーエンド強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 月面重力下でのコマンド指示による点間跳躍を行う単一のエンドツーエンド制御ポリシーを生成する多段階強化学習アプローチを提案し、実機での検証を行った。
llm.problem: 月面の起伏の激しい不連続な地形において、従来の車輪型ローバーではアクセスできない領域を脚ロボットの跳躍によって踏破することの難しさ
llm.method: ミッション互換性のあるオンボードセンシングのみに依存し、月面重力下での点間跳躍を行う多段階強化学習によるエンドツーエンド制御ポリシーの構築
llm.result: シミュレーションで体サイズ以下の着地誤差での正確な跳躍を実現し、月面重力オフロード下でのハードウェア実機転移により垂直跳躍の実行に成功した

2610.29570.title: Joint-Angle Invariance of Jacobian-Based Performance Indices for Serial Robotic Manipulators
2610.29570.abstract: This article investigates the joint-angle invariance (JAI) of Jacobian-based performance indices for serial robotic manipulators. We identify kinematic conditions under which representative performance indices, including manipulability, stiffness, and other Jacobian-derived indices, remain independent of the first and last joint angles. This property allows a systematic reduction in the effective configuration-space dimensionality, thereby simplifying the performance evaluation. The utility of JAI is demonstrated through two application scenarios: workspace performance map construction and task layout optimization. Comparative results show that the proposed JAI-based strategy reduces computational effort and storage requirements without compromising the effectiveness.
2610.29570.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at the 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026)

llm.title_ja: 直動型ロボットマニピュレータのヤコビアンに基づく性能指標の関節角不変性
llm.tldr_ja: 直列型ロボットマニピュレータのヤコビアンに基づく性能指標における関節角不変性（JAI）の運動学的条件を特定し、構成空間の次元を削減して性能評価を単純化する。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレータの作業空間性能や stiffness などの性能指標評価において計算負荷が高くなる点
llm.method: 可操作性や剛性などの性能指標が最初と最後の関節角に依存しない運動学的条件の特定と、それを利用した構成空間の次元削減
llm.result: ワークスペース性能マップの構築やタスクレイアウト最適化の応用シナリオにおいて、効率と保存要件の削減が示された

2610.29568.title: Mixture of Flow Matching and Particle Filter for Proprioception-Based Online Contact Estimation
2610.29568.abstract: In this article, we propose ContactFlowFilter, a novel approach for contact estimation that determines the number of active contacts, their locations, and the associated force vectors. We consider a robot manipulator equipped with joint torque sensors and a base force/torque sensor; such a proprioceptive-only setup presents a challenging inverse problem characterized by (i) multi-modality from non-unique solutions, (ii) temporal dependencies in state evolution, and (iii) discrete contact events involving contact addition/removal. Existing approaches, such as particle filters (PFs) and learning-based methods, often struggle to address these challenges simultaneously. To overcome this, ContactFlowFilter integrates a generative model into the PF framework. The recursive structure of the PF captures temporal dependencies, while the flow matching model serves as an auxiliary proposal distribution to track multi-modal beliefs and detect contact events. Extensive validation in both simulation and real-world experiments confirms the effectiveness of the proposed method. In real-world settings, ContactFlowFilter achieves the lowest dissimilarity from the target distribution, with errors of only 0.36 cm and 0.88 cm for single- and dual-contact scenarios, respectively, while operating at 0.69 ms and 2.69 ms.
2610.29568.comment: Author accepted manuscript; 21 pages (including a cover page), 21 figures, 5 tables
2610.29568.journal_ref: IEEE Transactions on Robotics, vol. 42, pp. 3646-3665, 2026
2610.29568.tldr_en: A novel approach for contact estimation that determines the number of active contacts, their locations, and the associated force vectors using a generative model into the PF framework, which achieves the lowest dissimilarity from the target distribution.

llm.title_ja: 固有受容感覚ベースのオンライン接触推定のためのフローマッチングと粒子フィルタの混合モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ContactFlowFilterは、生成モデルを粒子フィルタ（PF）フレームワークに統合することで、アクティブな接触数、その位置、関連する力ベクトルを同時に推定する新しいアプローチである。
llm.problem: 関節トルクセンサとベースF/Tセンサのみの固有受容感覚を用いた接触推定が、非一意な解による多峰性や離散的接触イベントなどの逆問題として困難である点
llm.method: 時間的依存性を捉える粒子フィルタの再帰構造に、多峰性信念の追跡と接触検知のための補助提案分布としてフローマッチングモデルを統合したContactFlowFilterの提案
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界実験において、単一および二重接触シナリオでそれぞれ0.36cmおよび0.88cmという非常に低い誤差で目標分布を追跡できることが確認された

2610.29565.title: Preserving Operator Intent Under Actuation Constraints: Teleoperation of Manipulators with Coupled Transmissions
2610.29565.abstract: Teleoperation enables intuitive control of remote engineering robots for precision tasks. Existing direct joint-mapping methods have two limitations: independent motor saturation disrupts pitch-roll coordination in differential wrists, while fixed mappings struggle with abrupt tracking changes caused by gravitational loads and actuation constraints. We propose an actuator-constraint-aware leader-follower teleoperation method that jointly models leader gravity compensation, leader-follower joint mapping, and follower differential-wrist control. Specifically, we perform coordinated saturation in motor space according to the available gravity margin and integrate continuous angle unwrapping, feedback-state monitoring, and feasible-reference updates. This preserves the operator's motion direction, reduces coordination distortion, and suppresses recovery transients during saturation or brief communication failures. Real-robot experiments demonstrate smoother wrist trajectories and more continuous recovery than direct mapping.
2610.29565.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Contribution to the IROS 2026 workshop "5th Sensorimotor-Augmented Teleoperation: Human-Interaction-Oriented Paradigm and Real-World Concerns"
2610.29565.tldr_en: This work proposes an actuator-constraint-aware leader-follower teleoperation method that jointly models leader gravity compensation, leader-follower joint mapping, and follower differential-wrist control and performs coordinated saturation in motor space according to the available gravity margin.

llm.title_ja: 作動制約下でのオペレーター意図の維持：結合トランスミッションを持つマニピュレータのテレオペレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 利用可能な重力マージンに応じてモーター空間で協調飽和を行う、アクチュエータ制約を考慮したリーダー・フォロワー型テレオペレーション手法を提案し、操作の連続性と復帰性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 結合トランスミッションを持つマニピュレータのテレオペレーションにおいて、独立したモーターの飽和が差動手首の協調を乱し、重力や制約による追従異常を引き起こす点
llm.method: リーダーの重力補償、リーダー・フォロワー間関節マッピング、フォロワーの差動手首制御を結合し、重力マージンに合わせたモーター空間での協調飽和を行う手法の提案
llm.result: 実ロボット実験により、直接マッピングと比較して滑らかな手首軌道と、飽和や通信途絶からの連続的な復帰が実証された

2610.29560.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
2610.29560.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. Existing work has begun to address these challenges by augmenting foundation-model policies with memory and by introducing hierarchical architectures that separate high-level planning from low-level execution. We organize the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience. We instantiate this approach as SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), with a fixed VLA executor providing low-level control. The harness maintains and updates task context using observations and execution feedback to guide subsequent planning. Self-evolution uses environment rollouts to propose and evaluate harness revisions, with the selected configuration fixed before held-out testing. On RoboMME, SERA achieves 51.38% overall success with autonomous selection, compared with 44.38% without self-evolution. Our exploration suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.
2610.29560.tldr_en: This work organizes the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience, and suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.
2610.29560.hf_summary_en: SERA improves long-horizon robotic manipulation by using an editable harness to maintain task context and evolve planning through execution feedback, paired with a fixed low-level VLA executor.

2610.29555.title: WRDO: Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization in Aligned Language Models
2610.29555.abstract: Aligned large language models are trained to comply with benign requests while refusing harmful ones. However, recent work shows that this refusal behavior is fragile and can often be disrupted by simple activation- or weight-space interventions. In particular, refusal has been shown to be largely mediated by a single residual-stream direction, typically computed as a difference-of-means vector between harmful and harmless prompts. However, this standard construction aggregates heterogeneous harmful prompts into one uniform average, potentially conflating distinct refusal-related phenomena.
