In this work, we study whether refusal interventions can be strengthened by learning how to combine prompt-specific refusal directions. We propose Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization (WRDO), a procedure that constructs a composite refusal direction from a bank of per-prompt directions using learned aggregation weights. This approach allows different harmful prompts to contribute unequally to the final intervention direction. We evaluate WRDO against prior single-direction methods on three open-weight language models using three guard judges and HarmBench as an external evaluator. We further measure the effect of the intervention on general model capability through standard utility benchmarks. Finally, we investigate a defense-oriented setting in which the same optimization machinery is used in reverse to restore refusal behavior in an abliterated model checkpoint. Our results show that weighted aggregation provides a more effective and flexible mechanism for manipulating refusal representations.
2610.29555.tldr_en: This work proposes Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization (WRDO), a procedure that constructs a composite refusal direction from a bank of per-prompt directions using learned aggregation weights and shows that weighted aggregation provides a more effective and flexible mechanism for manipulating refusal representations.
2610.29555.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

badges.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natur 2026

llm.title_ja: WRDO：アライメント済み言語モデルにおける加重拒絶方向最適化
llm.tldr_ja: プロンプトごとの拒絶方向を学習済み集約ウェイトで組み合わせて複合的な拒絶方向を構築する手順（WRDO）を提案し、拒絶表現の操作においてより効果的で柔軟なメカニズムを提供することを示す。
llm.problem: アライメント済み大規模言語モデルの拒絶動作は脆弱であり、標準的な構築法では異質な有害プロンプトが均一に集約される。
llm.method: プロンプト固有の拒絶方向のバンクから、学習された集約ウェイトを用いて複合的な拒絶方向を構築するWeighted Refusal Direction Optimization (WRDO)を提案する。
llm.result: 重み付き集約により、拒絶表現を操作するためのより効果的で柔軟なメカニズムが提供されることを示した。

2610.29517.title: AutoPhyX: Automatic Text-Condition Physics Property Generation
2610.29517.abstract: High-fidelity 4D physical simulation requires accurate physical parameter assignments that align with diverse material properties. Previous methods struggle with critical bottlenecks: they either rely on computationally intensive per-scene optimization or predict parameters from purely visual inputs. The latter suffers from inherent ambiguity, e.g., the inability to distinguish the stiffness of rubber from its appearance alone. To bridge this gap, we propose AutoPhyX, a text-conditioned framework for predicting spatially-varying physical properties. Since training robust feed-forward models requires fine-grained supervision, we first introduce a novel part-controllable data generation pipeline that decomposes complex 3D assets into semantically distinct components and pairs them with physically plausible, diverse parameters and corresponding text descriptions. Leveraging this dataset, AutoPhyX employs a cross-modal modulation mechanism where text features dynamically modulate visual features for precise physical grounding. By formulating property prediction within a voxel field, AutoPhyX ensures compatibility with diverse 3D representations, including meshes, point clouds, Gaussian Splatting, and NeRF. Experiments demonstrate that our method enables physically plausible, text-driven parameter assignment in a single forward pass. It achieves high accuracy and robust generalization to in-the-wild objects, paving the way for future physics-intensive embodied and robotic applications.
2610.29517.tldr_en: This work proposes AutoPhyX, a text-conditioned framework for predicting spatially-varying physical properties that achieves high accuracy and robust generalization to in-the-wild objects, paving the way for future physics-intensive embodied and robotic applications.

llm.title_ja: AutoPhyX：テキスト条件付けによる物理特性の自動生成
llm.tldr_ja: テキスト条件に基づいて空間的に変動する物理特性を高精度かつロバストに予測するフレームワークAutoPhyXを提案し、多様な3D表現と互換性を持つ単一フォワードパスでのパラメータ割り当てを実現する。
llm.problem: 従来の物理パラメータ予測は、計算負荷の高いシーンごとの最適化に依存するか、視覚入力のみから予測するため曖昧さが生じる。
llm.method: 複雑な3Dアセットを意味論的に分離された部品に分解し物理的パラメータと対にしたデータ生成パイプラインを構築し、テキスト特徴が視覚特徴を変調するクロスモーダル変調メカニズムを用いる。
llm.result: 単一のフォワードパスで物理的に妥当なテキスト駆動型パラメータ割り当てを可能にし、現場のオブジェクトに対して高い精度とロバストな汎化性能を実現した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2610.29505.title: Make it Walk: Computational Design of LEGO Walkers
2610.29505.abstract: LEGO walkers are walking automata constructed from modular LEGO Technic bricks. They exhibit intriguing locomotion and are also highly reconfigurable through the modular Technic bricks, making them widely applicable in education, recreation, and robotics research. However, existing LEGO walkers are designed mostly by reusing existing single-actuator walking mechanisms. Although the locomotion is stable, their fixed walking gaits limit their adaptability and versatility. This paper presents the first computational solution capable of designing LEGO walkers that not only walk stably, but also support a variety of walking gaits. Our idea is twofold. First, we control the foot motion trajectory of each leg mechanically via a specifically-designed gear-linkage mechanism, in which we incorporate a pair of 3D-printed non-circular gears to work with a LEGO Technic mechanism. Second, we drive each leg by an independent motor and synchronize the timings of multiple leg motions via a simple yet adaptable control algorithm, enabling stable and versatile locomotion. Importantly, we take this modeling as a foundation to co-design the morphology and control of the LEGO walkers to meet the target locomotion and appearance. Leveraging our approach, we created a variety of LEGO walkers, demonstrating various walking gaits and appearances, and fabricated some of them to show their locomotion capability in the real world.
2610.29505.tldr_en: This paper presents the first computational solution capable of designing LEGO walkers that not only walk stably, but also support a variety of walking gaits, and takes this modeling as a foundation to co-design the morphology and control of the LEGO walkers to meet the target locomotion and appearance.

llm.title_ja: 歩かせる：レゴ製歩行機械の計算機による設計
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dプリント製の非円形歯車と適応可能な制御アルゴリズムを組み合わせることで、安定した歩行と多様な歩行動作の両方をサポートするレゴ製歩行機械の初の計算機による設計手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のレゴ製歩行機械は単一アクチュエータの機構を再利用して設計されることが多く、固定された歩行動作が適応性と汎用性を制限している。
llm.method: 非円形歯車を組み込んだ歯車連動機構により各脚の足の動作軌道を機械的に制御し、独立したモーターと適応可能な制御アルゴリズムで同期させる共設計手法を用いる。
llm.result: 多様な歩行動作や外観を持つレゴ製歩行機械を作成し、実世界での歩行能力を示した。

2610.29478.title: S-Rolling: Steerable Rolling Gaits for Twistable Snake Robots in Low-Clearance Environments
2610.29478.abstract: Snake robots can traverse complex environments with limbless locomotion, but maneuvering in low-clearance environments remains challenging because a gait must maintain a small swept height while also providing planar steering. Existing rolling gaits preserve a low swept height body configuration but generally provide limited steering, whereas steering gaits often introduce vertical undulation and require additional clearance. With that in mind, this paper develops S-rolling, a steerable rolling gait that combines low swept height locomotion with planar maneuverability for twistable snake robots. S-rolling is designed using an S-shaped planar backbone curve, whose head and tail segments roll with independently controlled angular velocities, producing different motion modes. We derive its joint space gait equation, in which a central twist joint realizes the relative rotation between the two segments. We also develop a quasi-static kinematic model relating the segment rolling speeds to the linear and angular velocities of the robot. Real-robot experiments demonstrate the various motion modes, traversal through a 10 cm clearance test track, and maneuvering tasks beneath a large workpiece and a car chassis. In these low-clearance scenarios, S-rolling successfully performs approximately 90$^\circ$ and 180$^\circ$ heading changes, whereas the baseline rolling arc gait cannot change the robot heading.

llm.title_ja: S-Rolling：低クリアランス環境におけるねじれ可能なヘビ型ロボットのための操舵可能なローリング歩容
llm.tldr_ja: S字型の骨格曲線を用いた低クリアランス環境向けの新ローリング歩容「S-rolling」を開発し、実機実験において高さ10cmの障害物通過や狭小地での方向転換を実証した。
llm.problem: 低クリアランス環境では小さなスイープ高さを維持しつつ平面的な操舵を行う必要があり、従来の歩容では制限があった。
llm.method: 頭部と尾部を独立して制御された角速度で回転させるS字型平面バックボーン曲線を用いた操舵可能ローリング歩容（S-rolling）を設計し、準静的運動学モデルを構築した。
llm.result: 実機実験により様々な動作モード、10cmのクリアランス通過、およびワークピースや車のシャシー下での約90度・180度の方向転換に成功した。

2610.29474.title: Extending Affordance Segmentation for Wearable Robots to Multi-Object Images
2610.29474.abstract: This paper proposes a refinement to existing vision-based portable pipelines for the recognition of graspable object parts. Such pipelines can effectively support automatic grasp selection and preshaping in upper-limb prosthetic devices. However, realistic scenarios in which multiple objects are present still represent a challenge. The proposed method exploits a minor modification to the conventional hardware setup and a custom training approach to extend the applicability of vision-based pipelines. A laser pointer is introduced in the setup as an effective mechanism for object disambiguation. Accordingly, a suitable retraining of the deep convolutional neural networks supporting recognition of graspable parts is implemented. A mixed reality strategy allows the reuse of available high-quality segmentation masks to generate realistic images procedurally, extending the range of scenarios supported by the final device. Experimental results confirm that the proposed pipeline improves target disambiguation accuracy by up to 9% compared with existing solutions, while preserving the computational cost.
2610.29474.tldr_en: Experimental results confirm that the proposed pipeline improves target disambiguation accuracy by up to 9% compared with existing solutions, while preserving the computational cost.

llm.title_ja: ウェアラブルロボット向けアフォーダンスセグメンテーションの複数オブジェクト画像への拡張
llm.tldr_ja: レーザーポインタを用いたハードウェアの改良とカスタムトレーニングアプローチにより、複数オブジェクトが存在する現実的なシナリオにおける把持可能部位の認識精度を向上させる。
llm.problem: 複数のオブジェクトが存在する現実的なシナリオでは、把持可能部位を認識するビジョンベースのパイプラインの適用が課題となる。
llm.method: オブジェクトの曖昧さを解消するためのメカニズムとしてレーザーポインタを導入し、認識をサポートする深層畳み込みニューラルネットワークの再学習と、MR戦略による画像生成を行う。
llm.result: 計算コストを維持しながら、ターゲットの曖昧さ解消精度を既存の解決策と比較して最大9%向上させた。
keywords_ja: ウェアラブルロボット

2610.29461.title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains
2610.29461.abstract: Sidewinding is an efficient gait for snake robots to locomote on various terrains, by undulating the backbone curve and shifting the contact segments along it. However, relying solely on undulatory motion limits the locomotive capability of snake robots, and combining it with twisting motion can improve their speed and robustness. This hypothesis has recently been verified by the rolling vector approach, which locomotes the robot like a differential-drive car. Yet its twisting is concentrated in a short buffer segment, imposing most of the workload on the two twist joints in the middle, which can often overburden the motors and limit its locomotion. With that in mind, this paper develops a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits that distribute the workload over the entire body with our proposed linear twisting function. Under matched turning speed and total output power, our gaits reduce the peak output power of a single twist joint by 42%. Real-robot experiments show that, with the reduced workload, our new gaits can locomote the robot in various terrains that the existing rolling vector approach cannot. Besides, our new gaits can move up to 49% faster than conventional sidewinding without twisting.

llm.title_ja: 複雑な地形におけるねじれ可能なヘビ型ロボットのモーションプランニングのための線形ねじれ側方移動歩容
llm.tldr_ja: 全身にワークロードを分散させる線形ねじれ関数を用いた新しいねじれ側方移動歩容を開発し、単一のねじれ関節のピーク出力を42%削減しつつ、従来手法が適用できない多様な地形での移動を実現した。
llm.problem: 従来のローリングベクターアプローチでは、ねじれが中央の短いバッファセグメントに集中し、モーターに過度な負担をかける。
llm.method: 提案する線形ねじれ関数を使用して、出力パワーを全身に分散させる新しいねじれ側方移動歩容を開発した。
llm.result: 実機実験において、ワークロードが軽減されたことで従来手法が不可能な多様な地形での移動が可能になり、ねじれなしの側方移動より最大49%高速に移動した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.33079.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access
2610.33079.abstract: Large-scale AI training increasingly relies on massive video datasets with random temporal sampling patterns. However, existing video storage paradigms are optimized for sequential playback and employ sophisticated inter-frame reference structures to maximize compression efficiency. When applied to the random-sampling workloads of AI training, these paradigms face substantial decoding-efficiency bottlenecks. Workarounds such as independent JPEG frames and short groups of pictures (GOPs) reduce decoding work at the cost of larger storage and transfer volumes. In this paper, we identify two sources of decode amplification: sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reconstruction of the reference chains required by sampled targets. We address both sources by co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure. Dependency-aware sparse decoding reconstructs only requested frames and their required references, skipping unrelated reconstruction without transcoding the source videos. Optional offline Dependency-Decoupled Random Access (DDRA) encoding further reduces reference reconstruction by restricting each interior frame to two bounding intra-coded anchors. Together, sparse decoding and DDRA retain inter-frame prediction while bounding reconstruction to at most three frames per requested target, independent of the intra period. Experiments on a large-scale robotics corpus show that, at comparable reconstruction quality, our method achieves $1.45\times$ the loading throughput of LeRobot v3 with 58.7% less media payload.
2610.33079.comment: 18 pages, including supplementary material. Project page: https://skywalker-yqz.github.io/codec4AI/ Code: https://github.com/kaname-madoka18/codec4AI
2610.33079.tldr_en: This paper identifies two sources of decode amplification: sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reconstruction of the reference chains required by sampled targets by co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure and co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure.
2610.33079.hf_summary_en: Co-designed sparse decoding and dependency-decoupled encoding reduce video decode overhead for random AI training sampling by bounding reconstruction per target.

2610.29452.title: Distance Field Driven Reinforcement Learning for Reactive and Robust Collision Avoidance
2610.29452.abstract: Robust and reactive collision avoidance remains a central challenge for deploying Reinforcement Learning (RL) policies on real robotic manipulators, particularly when transferring behaviours learned in simulation to the physical world. This paper presents an RL framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field (EDF) directly into the observation space, providing the agent with continuous geometric cues that support stable and responsive avoidance behaviours. By leveraging the rich spatial information encoded in the EDF, the method enables a streamlined reward formulation that achieves effective obstacle avoidance both with and without Artificial Potential Field guidance. The proposed approach is validated on a 7-DoF redundant manipulator, demonstrating zero-shot transfer from simulation to real hardware. Despite being trained exclusively with randomised static objects, the deployed policy generalizes to previously unseen real environments and exhibits robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles. These results highlight the potential of EDF-based representations to mitigate the sim-to-real gap and support reliable and real-time collision-aware behaviour in complex and changing environments.
2610.29452.comment: Accepted to 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
2610.29452.tldr_en: An RL framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field directly into the observation space, providing the agent with continuous geometric cues that support stable and responsive avoidance behaviours, and demonstrates zero-shot transfer from simulation to real hardware.

llm.title_ja: 反応的かつロバストな衝突回避のための距離場駆動型強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: ユークリッド距離場（EDF）を観測空間に直接統合した強化学習フレームワークを提案し、シミュレーションから実機へのゼロショット移行によるロバストな衝突回避を実現する。
llm.problem: 強化学習ポリシーを実ロボットのマニピュレータにデプロイする際、ロバストかつ反応的な衝突回避とシム2リアル移行が課題となる。
llm.method: 空間情報をエンコードしたユークリッド距離場（EDF）を観測空間に統合し、連続的な幾何学的手がかりをエージェントに提供する強化学習フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 7自由度の冗長マニピュレータを用いた実機実験により、シミュレーションから実機へのゼロショット移行と未知の動的障害物に対するロバストなオンライン回避を実証した。

2610.29442.title: Beyond Shortcut Learning: Hierarchical Spatial Prototype Regularization for Face Forgery Detection
2610.29442.abstract: Recent advances in generative models have enabled highly realistic face forgeries, yet generalizing deepfake detectors to unseen manipulation pipelines remains a major challenge. One critical yet underexplored issue is that the learned forensic representation itself may fail to remain stable across different manipulation sources. In this paper, we provide new evidence that naively fine-tuned vision models suffer from severe \textit{forensic representation collapse}: their extracted cues are often entangled with unstable, dataset-specific artifacts, resulting in structurally fragile representations and poor cross-domain generalization. Leveraging this insight, we propose \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{S}patial \textbf{P}rototype (\textbf{HSP}) regularization, which explicitly models the forgery manifold by learning a structured prototype subspace over spatial features. We further introduce prototype orthogonality and second-order assignment balance, which jointly preserve the geometric independence of latent forgery factors and promote high-effective-rank utilization of the forensic representation, thereby reducing reliance on dataset-specific shortcuts. Empirical results demonstrate that our method substantially improves generalizability, yielding average frame-level AUC gains of 5.6\% and 5.3\% in the cross-dataset and cross-manipulation settings, respectively. Moreover, when used as a plug-in module, HSP boosts the average video-level AUC of existing state-of-the-art detectors to 95.3\% (+1.8\%). These results demonstrate the practical value of HSP as an easy-to-adopt regularization module for enhancing deepfake detectors.
2610.29442.tldr_en: This paper proposes HSP regularization, which explicitly models the forgery manifold by learning a structured prototype subspace over spatial features, and introduces prototype orthogonality and second-order assignment balance, which jointly preserve the geometric independence of latent forgery factors and promote high-effective-rank utilization of the forensic representation, thereby reducing reliance on dataset-specific shortcuts.

llm.title_ja: ショートカット学習を超えて：顔偽造検出のための階層的空間プロトタイプ正則化
llm.tldr_ja: 空間的特徴上に構造化されたプロトタイプ部分空間を学習することで偽造マニフォールドを明示的にモデル化するHSP正則化を提案し、クロスデータセットおよびクロスレイアウト設定での汎化性能を大幅に向上させる。
llm.problem: 微調整されたビジョンモデルは、データセット固有の人工物に起因するフォレンジック表現の崩壊を起こし、クロスドメイン汎化性能が低い。
llm.method: 空間的特徴上の構造化プロトタイプ部分空間を学習する階層的空間プロトタイプ（HSP）正則化を提案し、プロトタイプ直交性と2次割り当てバランスを導入する。
llm.result: クロスデータセットおよびクロス操縦設定でそれぞれ平均フレームレベルAUCが5.6%および5.3%向上し、既存検出器の性能を底上げした。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出
コンピュータビジョン

2610.29438.title: A2I-Calib++: A Kinematics-Driven Anti-noise Active Calibration Framework for Whole-Body Multi-IMU Systems on Legged Robots
2610.29438.abstract: Recently, multi-node inertial measurement unit (multi-IMU) systems have shown promise for robust odometry in legged robots. Multi-IMU fusion can improve legged robot odometry but requires accurate spatiotemporal calibration among the sensors. Existing multi-IMU calibration methods, designed for aerial or handheld platforms, face challenges on legged robots because routine locomotion may provide insufficient excitation, while foot slips, impacts, and vibrations introduce measurement disturbances. To address these challenges, we propose A2I-Calib++, a kinematics-driven anti-noise active calibration framework for body-mounted IMUs covered by the robot kinematic model. It estimates temporal offsets, extrinsic rotations and translations, and inertial biases through temporal correlation search followed by analytic spatial and bias estimation, without artificial calibration targets or complex parameter tuning for the target IMU. A2I-Calib++ comprises three core modules: 1) a Noise-Isotropy-Inspired Trajectory supported by a finite-horizon conditioning proposition that generates sufficient excitation to limit noise sensitivity; 2) a constraint-aware Adversarial Motion Priors controller that combines the anti-noise excitation with a rolling-contact reward for contact-aware execution; and 3) a contact-constrained virtual IMU that fuses pre-calibrated calf IMUs and joint kinematics under a rolling-contact model to construct the calibration reference. Furthermore, evaluations on both simulation and real-world quadruped platforms demonstrate notably reduced noise sensitivity and simulation calibration errors compared to conventional methods, together with repeatable real-world calibration and improved proprioceptive odometry accuracy for legged robots.
2610.29438.tldr_en: A2I-Calib++ is proposed, a kinematics-driven anti-noise active calibration framework for body-mounted IMUs covered by the robot kinematic model that demonstrates notably reduced noise sensitivity and simulation calibration errors compared to conventional methods, together with repeatable real-world calibration and improved proprioceptive odometry accuracy for legged robots.

llm.title_ja: A2I-Calib++：脚式ロボット上の全身マルチIMUシステムに向けた運動学駆動型ノイズ耐性アクティブキャリブレーションフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット運動学モデルを活用した運動学駆動型ノイズ耐性アクティブキャリブレーションフレームワーク「A2I-Calib++」を提案し、脚式ロボットにおけるマルチIMUシステムのキャリブレーション誤差とノイズ感度を大幅に低減する。
llm.problem: 脚式ロボットの日常的な歩行では十分な励起が得られず、足の滑りや衝撃、振動が外乱となり従来のマルチIMUキャリブレーションが困難となる。
llm.method: ノイズ耐性軌跡生成モジュール、制約を考慮した敵対的モーションプライアコントローラ、および接触制約付き仮想IMUを組み合わせたA2I-Calib++を構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび四足歩行実機プラットフォームでの評価により、従来手法に比べてノイズ感度と較正誤差が顕著に低減され、プロプリオセプティブオドメトリの精度が向上した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2610.29432.title: PRISM: Learning Realistic Depth via Physics-Grounded Noise Disentanglement with Semantic-Geometric Collaboration
2610.29432.abstract: Real-world physical sensing exhibits complex, heterogeneous noise patterns that deviate significantly from idealized simulation, posing a fundamental bottleneck for sim-to-real transfer. Existing sensor modelings typically treat depth noise as a monolithic black-box process, overlooking the distinct physical mechanisms that govern different error modalities. In this work, we introduce a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: \textbf{sensing invalidation} and \textbf{measurement inaccuracy}, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{PRISM}, a tripartite framework that distills 3D Visual Foundation Model features as rich spatial-semantic priors for physics-based reasoning. To address the inherent sparsity and class imbalance of invalidation regions, we develop Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision, integrating multi-scale positive-weighted objectives with a positive-preserving dynamic hard mining strategy to enforce precise artifact delineation. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves state-of-the-art fidelity in noisy depth synthesis. Furthermore, downstream robotic experiments show that PRISM facilitates a \textbf{92.1\%} average success rate in the real world, marking a significant improvement over monolithic baselines. Our project page is available at: \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}.}
2610.29432.tldr_en: This work introduces a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: sensing invalidation and measurement inaccuracy, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins.

llm.title_ja: PRISM：意味論的・幾何学的協調を伴う物理的根拠に基づくノイズ分離を通じた現実的な深度学習
llm.tldr_ja: モノリスな深度ノイズを「センシング無効化」と「測定不正確さ」の2つの物理的モダリティに分離する物理的根拠に基づくパラダイム「PRISM」を提案し、シム2リアル転移のボトルネックを解消する。
llm.problem: 現実世界の物理的センシングは理想化されたシミュレーションから大きく逸脱する複雑で異質なノイズパターンを示し、シム2リアル転移の障害となる。
llm.method: 3Dビジョン基盤モデルの特徴を空間意味論的プライアとして蒸留する三部構成フレームワークPRISMを提案し、階層的ポジティブ優先監督を開発する。
llm.result: ノイズの多い深度合成において最先端の忠実度を達成し、ダウンストリームのロボット実験では現実世界で92.1%の平均成功率を記録した。

2610.29408.title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
2610.29408.abstract: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We study multi-agent video world modeling, where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents while interpreting heterogeneous controls ranging from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. This task presents two complementary challenges. First, every agent-indexed action stream must control its intended visual entity independently. Second, the model must adapt the meaning of each control variable across different tasks, where the same tensor dimension may denote an attack, steering command, or robot command. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. Across games and robot manipulation, LiveAct reaches 0.898 and 0.942 agent-attribution accuracy without agent locations or identity crops, and the causal generator attains 17.70 FPS at $512\times 448$.
2610.29408.tldr_en: This work introduces LiveAct, a Heterogeneous Action Interface centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface whose two components mirror this decomposition, and instantiates the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluates visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency.

llm.title_ja: LiveAct：異種アクションインターフェースを備えたリアルタイムマルチエージェント世界モデルに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: ゲームのボタンからロボットの連続指令まで多様な制御を解釈しつつ複数エージェントの将来の視覚情報を共同で生成する異種アクションインターフェース（HAI）を備えた「LiveAct」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の対話型ビデオ世界モデルは単一の制御エージェントとタスク固有のアクションインターフェースを前提としており、マルチエージェントや多様な制御に対応できない。
llm.method: 言語駆動型空間ゲートとエージェント固有の注意機構による「エージェント認識型空間変調」と、制御変数を言語で記述し数値と変調する「スキーマ誘導型アクション適応」を統合したLiveActを構築する。
llm.result: ゲームとロボットマニピュレーションにわたる6つのマルチエージェントソースにおいて、エージェントの位置や切り抜きなしで高いエージェント帰属精度（0.898および0.942）を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション
アクションインターフェース

2610.29377.title: Integrating Flow Matching and Model Predictive Control for Safe Robot Navigation
2610.29377.abstract: Learning-based path planners based on diffusion and flow matching can generate diverse trajectories from demonstrations but typically lack mechanisms for constraint satisfaction and collision avoidance during deployment. This work proposes a framework that combines flow-matching-based path planning with model predictive path-following control to integrate data-driven path generation with real-time, constraint-aware execution. The flow-matching model captures multimodal path distributions, while the predictive controller adapts motion online to satisfy state and input constraints and avoid obstacles using updated local sensor information. An event-triggered re-planning scheme incorporates predictive control solutions into subsequent path generation, promoting collision-free navigation in environments with previously unseen obstacles. Simulation results for mobile robot navigation demonstrate robust performance across cluttered environments. The framework provides a systematic approach to combining flow matching with predictive control for adaptive, data-driven navigation.
2610.29377.tldr_en: This work proposes a framework that combines flow-matching-based path planning with model predictive path-following control to integrate data-driven path generation with real-time, constraint-aware execution to integrate data-driven path generation with real-time, constraint-aware execution.

llm.title_ja: フローマッチングとモデル予測制御の統合による安全なロボットナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: フローマッチングに基づく経路計画とモデル予測追従制御を組み合わせたフレームワークを提案し、多様なデータ駆動型経路生成とリアルタイムの制約考慮型実行を統合して安全なナビゲーションを実現する。
llm.problem: 拡散やフローマッチングに基づく学習済みパスプランナーは多様な軌道を生成できるが、展開時の制約充足や衝突回避のメカニズムを欠いている。
llm.method: マルチモーダルな経路分布を捉えるフローマッチングモデルと、センサー情報に基づいて状態・入力制約をオンラインで満たす予測コントローラをイベントトリガー型再計画スキームで統合する。
llm.result: 雑然とした環境でのモバイルロボットナビゲーションのシミュレーションにおいてロバストなパフォーマンスを示した。

2610.29374.title: AOV-GS: Active Open-Vocabulary Semantic Mapping with 3D Gaussian Splatting
2610.29374.abstract: Robots deployed in human-centered environments need maps that support both geometric navigation and open-vocabulary semantic queries beyond a fixed label set. A key challenge is enriching such maps with semantic information without relying on manually annotated segmentation masks or closed-set semantic categories. Existing geometry-driven active mapping maximizes coverage but treats semantics as a passive by-product of the collected trajectory, whereas active semantic mapping typically depends on supervised semantic segmentation. We present AOV-GS, an active 3D Gaussian mapping system that guides exploration using frozen foundation models. During coarse exploration, AOV-GS re-ranks geometrically promising candidate views according to CLIP mask-embedding novelty computed from SAM instance segmentation, biasing exploration toward semantically informative regions. Frozen SAM and CLIP provide instance masks and language-aligned embeddings throughout mapping, while a lightweight scene-specific language field is fitted offline directly to the collected CLIP embeddings rather than manually annotated masks, enabling open-vocabulary text-query segmentation on novel views. In a controlled comparison using the same SAM-CLIP perception stack, AOV-GS improves average language-field mIoU over geometry-only active planning by 1.3 percentage points on Replica (34.6% on eight scenes) and by 1.8 points on Matterport3D (23.1% on five scenes). With CorrCLIP, AOV-GS reaches 35.6% on Replica, 2.0 points above the matched Geometry-based + CorrCLIP baseline. Novel-view PSNR remains comparable to the geometry-only baseline on both datasets while depth L1 improves on Replica. Code is available at https://github.com/OptimusFaber/AOV-GS.
2610.29374.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables. Published at AIST 2026
2610.29374.journal_ref: AIST 2026, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16795, pp. 312-328, Springer, Cham (2027)
2610.29374.tldr_en: AOV-GS is presented, an active 3D Gaussian mapping system that guides exploration using frozen foundation models that improves average language-field mIoU over geometry-only active planning over geometry-only active planning on Replica.
2610.29374.venue: International Joint Conference on the Analysis of Images, Social Networks and Texts

badges.venue: AIST 2026, Lecture Notes in Computer Sci

llm.title_ja: AOV-GS：3D Gaussian Splattingを用いた能動的オープンボキャブラリー意味論的マッピング
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された基盤モデルを活用して探索を誘導する能動的3Dガウス分布マッピングシステム「AOV-GS」を提案し、手動アノテーションなしで新規ビューに対するオープンボキャブラリーのテキストクエリセグメンテーションを可能にする。
llm.problem: 人間中心の環境に配属されるロボットには幾何学的ナビゲーションと固定ラベルセットを超えたオープンボキャブラリーセマンティクスが必要だが、手動アノテーションや教師ありセグメンテーションに依存している。
llm.method: SAMインスタンスセグメンテーションから計算されたCLIPマスク埋め込みの新規性に基づいて幾何学的に有望な候補ビューを再ランク付けし、探索を意味論的領域に誘導するAOV-GSを提案する。
llm.result: ReplicaおよびMatterport3Dデータセットにおいて、幾何学のみの能動的プランニングと比較して平均言語フィールドmIoUがそれぞれ1.3ポイントおよび1.8ポイント向上した。
keywords_ja: オープンボキャブラリー

2610.29356.title: Payload generalization on feedforward control actions for trajectory tracking in robots with rigid and elastic joints
2610.29356.abstract: Industries employ robots for repetitive tasks due to their high precision and performance, typically achieved through feedforward control actions based on an accurate robot description. However, an exact dynamic model can be difficult to obtain, especially for robots with elastic elements or when the payload changes. Learning-based feedforward approaches are promising for trajectory tracking under model uncertainties, but typically face generalization issues when task parameters vary. This paper proposes a novel method to generalize the feedforward control action with respect to payload parameters, independently of the underlying controller. Firstly, the minimal number of example objects needed for payload generalization is derived. Then, an algorithm is proposed to execute the same trajectory with a new payload, given only its parameters, without knowledge of the robot's dynamic model and even in the presence of elastic joints. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated in simulations and experiments on tracking tasks with different robots and controllers. Two sets of experiments are performed: on a standard Franka Emika Panda robot, and on a Franka Emika Panda robot equipped with an elastic wrist.
2610.29356.comment: 18 pages, 17 figures. Accepted for publication in Control Engineering Practice
2610.29356.tldr_en: A novel method to generalize the feedforward control action with respect to payload parameters, independently of the underlying controller is proposed, and the minimal number of example objects needed for payload generalization is derived.

llm.title_ja: 剛体および弾性関節を持つロボットの軌跡追従におけるフィードフォワード制御アクションのペイロード汎化
llm.tldr_ja: 基底のコントローラから独立して、ペイロードパラメータに関するフィードフォワード制御アクションを汎化するための新しい手法を提案し、ロボットの動力学モデルの知識なしでの軌跡追従を実現する。
llm.problem: 正確な動的モデルの取得が困難な場合、特に弾性要素を持つロボットやペイロードが変化する場合、学習済みフィードフォワード手法は汎化の課題に直面する。
llm.method: ペイロード汎化に必要な最小限のサンプルオブジェクト数を導出し、動力学モデルの知識なしに新しいペイロードで同じ軌跡を実行するアルゴリズムを提案する。
llm.result: 標準のFranka Emika Pandaロボットと弾性手首を備えたFranka Emika Pandaロボットを用いたシミュレーションと実機実験により有効性を検証した。
keywords_ja: フィードフォワード制御

2610.29355.title: GaP-MoE : Explicit Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts via Orthogonal Gradient Accumulation and Projection
2610.29355.abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) models improve scalability by routing input tokens to only a subset of expert networks, but they often suffer from representation collapse, in which multiple experts converge toward similar functions and lose their intended diversity. Prior work has addressed this limitation either by improving router architectures or by introducing auxiliary loss terms that implicitly penalize similarity among experts. However, router-based approaches remain vulnerable to routing collapses, and loss-based approaches can conflict with the task's original objective during optimization. In this work, we propose GaP-MoE (Gradient Accumulation and Projection in MoE), which induces expert specialization by directly manipulating expert output gradients rather than modifying the loss function. At each training step, GaP-MoE stochastically selects one of the $TopK$ routed experts as a leader based on normalized routing scores, and projects the gradients of the remaining follower experts onto the orthogonal complement of the subspace spanned by the leader's recent gradients. This removes directional overlap between expert gradients without altering the task loss, allowing specialization to emerge as a direct consequence of the optimization dynamics rather than an externally imposed constraint. We evaluate GaP-MoE in both fine-tuning settings (BERT-based, on GLUE) and from-scratch pretraining settings (GPT-2-based, on WikiText-103, enwik8, and text8), and further confirm its compatibility as a drop-in module for existing SMoE architectures. Experimental results show that GaP-MoE achieves performance comparable to or better than standard SMoE.
2610.29355.tldr_en: This work proposes GaP-MoE (Gradient Accumulation and Projection in MoE), which induces expert specialization by directly manipulating expert output gradients rather than modifying the loss function, allowing specialization to emerge as a direct consequence of the optimization dynamics rather than an externally imposed constraint.

llm.title_ja: GaP-MoE：直交勾配の蓄積と投影によるMixture-of-Expertsにおける明示的なエキスパート特化
llm.tldr_ja: 損失関数を変更する代わりにエキスパートの出力勾配を直接操作して方向の重複を排除する「GaP-MoE」を提案し、タスク損失を損なうことなく最適化ダイナミクスからエキスパート特化を自発的に引き出す。
llm.problem: スパースMixture-of-Expertsモデルは表現の崩壊（複数のエキスパートが類似の機能に収束する現象）に悩まされがちである。
llm.method: 上位K人のエキスパートからリーダーを確率的に選択し、残りのフォロワーの勾配をリーダーの最近の勾配部分空間の直交補空間に投影するGaP-MoEを提案する。
llm.result: ファインチューニングおよびゼロからの事前学習設定において、標準的なSMoEと同等以上の性能を達成した。

2610.29329.title: Plan First, Act Later: Streaming Reasoning for Executable Memory in Robot Control
2610.29329.abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires a robot to remember task-relevant information beyond its short observation window. Existing memory-augmented policies typically retrieve relevant information from history and reason over it at execution time, placing a heavy reasoning burden on the high-level model. To address this challenge, we propose PAL (\textbf{P}lan first, \textbf{A}ct \textbf{L}ater), a hierarchical memory framework for vision-language robot manipulation. It maintains a short-term visual buffer, a semantic-event memory, and an executable \texttt{subtask\_list}. A high-level vision-language model (VLM) converts streaming visual observations into the \texttt{subtask\_list}. At execution time, the VLM selects the currently relevant subtask from the \texttt{subtask\_list} and passes it to a low-level vision-language-action (VLA) policy. To teach the model what to write to memory and when to update it, we introduce a two-stage data generation procedure that first expands sparse update supervision and then uses self-labeling with task-grounded verification to generate training data that better match the state distribution encountered during execution. We evaluate our approach on memory-dependent benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks. On RoboMME, PAL achieves a \textbf{56.05\%} success rate, outperforming the strongest baseline, FrameSamp-Modul, at 44.51\%. In real-world experiments across four manipulation tasks, \pal{} reaches \textbf{60.83\%} overall success, surpassing MemER (45.00\%) and FrameSamp-Modul (28.33\%). These results show that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control. Code and videos can be found on our website: https://qinghangliu.github.io/pal-webpage/
2610.29329.tldr_en: Results show that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control.

llm.title_ja: 最初に計画し、後で実行する：ロボット制御における実行可能な記憶のためのストリーミング推論
llm.tldr_ja: 短期視覚バッファ、意味イベント記憶、実行可能なサブタスクリストを維持する階層的記憶フレームワーク「PAL」を提案し、長期的な視覚推論とロボット制御の性能を大幅に向上させる。
llm.problem: 長期的なロボットマニピュレーションでは短期的な観察ウィンドウを超えたタスク関連情報の記憶が必要であり、既存の手法は高レベルモデルに大きな推論負担を課す。
llm.method: 視覚的観察をサブタスクリストに変換する高レベルVLMと、それを低レベルVLAポリシーに渡す実行メカニズムを備えた階層的記憶フレームワークPALを提案し、2段階のデータ生成手順で学習させる。
llm.result: RoboMMEで56.05%の成功率を達成し、実世界の4つのマニピュレーションタスクでも60.83%の総合成功率を記録して既存手法を上回った。
keywords_ja: 長期マニピュレーション

2610.30197.title: Alpha: Systematic Fault Injection and Robustness Evaluation for LLM-Driven Embodied Manipulation
2610.30197.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into embodied robotic planning, yet standard benchmarks primarily evaluate end-to-end task completion in nominal environments, obscuring failure origins across the execution stack. We present Alpha, a systematic fault-injection and robustness-evaluation framework for LLM-driven manipulation in simulation. Alpha injects calibrated faults across perception (sensor lag), actuation (grip slip), kinematics (unreachable targets), and planning (planner-output corruption), alongside concurrent conditions. To separate physical vulnerabilities from planner sensitivities, we introduce a matched methodology pairing an LLM agent (Llama-3 via Ollama) against a deterministic Scripted Oracle planner across a balanced 150-episode matrix under identical seeds, geometries, and safety criteria. Across the matrix, the Oracle achieves 64.0% (48/75) success while the LLM achieves 44.0% (33/75) (paired McNemar p = 3.01 x 10^-4). Crucially, excluding planner-output corruption, performance across all physical and kinematic conditions is identical: 55.0% (33/60) for both planners with zero discordant pairs (McNemar p = 1.00). This demonstrates that physical actuator slip, kinematic reach boundaries, and perceptual staleness affect deterministic controllers and LLM planners equivalently. The performance gap is driven entirely by planner-output corruption (100% Oracle vs. 0% LLM), isolating the prompt-to-JSON serialization and validation interface rather than a cognitive reasoning deficit. We also audit 169 historical pilot attempts for transparency.
2610.30197.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Code and reproduction artifacts: https://github.com/jonajoy142/embodied-agent-chaos
2610.30197.tldr_en: Alpha, a systematic fault-injection and robustness-evaluation framework for LLM-driven manipulation in simulation, and a matched methodology pairing an LLM agent against a deterministic Scripted Oracle planner across a balanced 150-episode matrix under identical seeds, geometries, and safety criteria are presented.

llm.title_ja: Alpha：LLM駆動型ロボットマニピュレーションのための体系的な障害注入とロバスト性評価
llm.tldr_ja: 知覚、動作、運動学、計画にわたる較正された障害を体系的に注入する評価フレームワーク「Alpha」を提案し、LLMプランナーと決定論的オラクルプランナーの比較を通じて性能ギャップの原因を切り分ける。
llm.problem: 標準的なベンチマークは名目環境でのタスク完了度を評価するのみであり、実行スタック全体の障害の起因が不明確である。
llm.method: センサー遅延、グリップの滑り、到達不能ターゲット、プランナー出力破損などの障害を注入し、LLMエージェントとスクリプト化されたオラクルプランナーを同一の条件で比較する評価フレームワークAlphaを構築する。
llm.result: 物理的条件および運動学的条件では両プランナーの性能は同等であり、性能格差は推論能力の欠如ではなくプロンプトからJSONへのシリアライズと検証インターフェースの破損に起因することを実証した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.29302.title: Compressing Onboard Language Models for Space Robots under a Behavioral-Fidelity Requirement
2610.29302.abstract: Language models are being explored as the interface through which space robots interpret operator commands and select among verified skills. Running them onboard calls for low-bit compression, and flight use adds requirements that generic post-training quantization leaves implicit: a fixed memory budget and storage format, a static artifact under configuration control, and behavior close to the full-precision model validated on the ground. We treat compression as a ground-segment step and study QSelect, which composes one static low-bit model from compatible AWQ, GPTQ, and AutoRound checkpoints by assigning each linear module to one quantizer family and scoring every substitution at the final next-token distribution. The default fidelity mode needs no labels or tuned thresholds and accepts a substitution only when the forward KL divergence from the BF16 reference decreases; an optional target-adapted mode adds answer likelihood on a small labeled set. On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Llama-3.2-3B at 3 and 4 bits, composed models reach lower mean held-out perplexity than every single-family model in all six settings, and the fidelity mode lowers perplexity and KL further. In a matched scaffold, final-output scoring gives lower held-out KL than representation-similarity scoring in all 12 paired runs. With labels from training or development splits of the evaluated task families, the target-adapted mode raises 3-bit pooled accuracy on the two Llama models by 4.3 and 4.5 points over the best single-family model. At 3 bits, unquantized embedding and output layers make up 43-46% of the packed artifact. All evaluations use general-domain benchmarks on a ground GPU; space-domain tasks and flight hardware are left to future work.
2610.29302.tldr_en: This work treats compression as a ground-segment step and study QSelect, which composes one static low-bit model from compatible AWQ, GPTQ, and AutoRound checkpoints by assigning each linear module to one quantizer family and scoring every substitution at the final next-token distribution.

llm.title_ja: 動作忠実度要件に基づく宇宙ロボット向けオンボード言語モデルの圧縮
llm.tldr_ja: 互換性のある量子化チェックポイントから単一の静的低ビットモデルを構成する「QSelect」を提案し、宇宙ロボット向けに固定メモリ予算や動作忠実度を維持したオンボード言語モデルの圧縮を実現する。
llm.problem: 宇宙ロボットに言語モデルをオンボードで実行するには低ビット圧縮が必要だが、一般の事後量子化では固定メモリ予算や静的アーティファクトなどの飛行要件が満たされない。
llm.method: 線形モジュールごとに量子化器ファミリを割り当て、最終的な次トークン分布で置換をスコアリングすることにより、AWQ、GPTQ、AutoRoundチェックポイントから単一の静的低ビットモデルを構成するQSelectを提案する。
llm.result: 複数のモデルと設定において、単一ファミリモデルよりも低い保持パープレキシティを達成し、ターゲット適応モードによって3ビットでのpooled精度が向上することを示した。

2610.29282.title: Relational Geometry Forcing for World Action Models
2610.29282.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have shown strong potential for robot manipulation by jointly learning visual dynamics and executable actions. However, their video and action objectives do not explicitly constrain the 3D geometry that is crucial for precise manipulation. Recently, geometry-aware WAMs introduce depth or 4D prediction branches, whereas representation alignment methods supervise intermediate WAM features with pretrained 3D foundation models. Yet we find that such pointwise alignment benefits the video features but degrades action learning, since dense geometric feature targets overly restrict compact action features. To address this limitation, we propose Relational Geometry Forcing (RGF), which transfers geometric priors from a frozen 3D foundation model by aligning pairwise feature relations instead of pointwise features. Specifically, RGF applies three complementary relational objectives, where intra-frame and cross-view relations transfer scene geometry and multi-view correspondence to the video features, while action-temporal relations couple action dynamics to geometric scene evolution. Applied only during training, RGF requires no explicit geometry branch or extra inference module. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate the effectiveness of Relational Geometry Forcing, showing consistent gains across diverse manipulation scenarios and WAM paradigms.
2610.29282.tldr_en: Relational Geometry Forcing (RGF), which transfers geometric priors from a frozen 3D foundation model by aligning pairwise feature relations instead of pointwise features, is proposed, showing consistent gains across diverse manipulation scenarios and WAM paradigms.

llm.title_ja: ワールドアクションモデルのための関係幾何学的強制
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された3D基盤モデルから幾何学的事前分布を転移する「Relational Geometry Forcing（RGF）」を提案し、多様なマニピュレーションシナリオとWAMパラダイムで一貫した性能向上を示した。
llm.problem: 既存の幾何学対応型WAMは点ごとの特徴アライメントを行っており、密な幾何学的特徴ターゲットがコンパクトなアクション特徴を過度に制限し、アクション学習を低下させる。
llm.method: 凍結された3D基盤モデルからの幾何学的事前分布を、点ごとではなくペアごとの特徴関係のアライメントによって転移するRGFを提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界での広範な実験により、多様なマニピュレーションシナリオとWAMパラダイムにわたって一貫した性能向上が示された。

2610.33074.title: AGQ: Action-Guided Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.33074.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform tasks specified through natural-language instructions, but their large weight footprint challenges deployment on memory-constrained onboard platforms. Ultra-low-bit quantization reduces this footprint, yet preserving task performance and controlling weight recovery costs remain challenging. We propose Action-Guided Quantization, which combines action sensitivity with a measured proxy for weight recovery cost to allocate matrix bitwidths under storage budgets. Per-channel calibration compensates for quantization error, while a uniform bitwidth within each matrix preserves regular layouts. Bit-dependent grouped lossless coding reduces resident weight storage, and block-wise recovery limits temporary buffers. On LIBERO, AGQ achieves 92.7% task success at W3, exceeding AWQ and GPTQ by 1.2 and 3.7 percentage points, respectively, and retains 70.5% success at W2.5. An asymmetric configuration, denoted W1.5$^{*}$, uses W4 vision weights and a parameter-weighted average of 1.5 bits for language weights. With lossless coding, it achieves $6.10\times$ complete-model compression relative to BF16 while retaining 25.5% task success. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/Qiuxu00/AGQ
2610.33074.comment: 3 figures, 3 tables. Code and experimental results: https://github.com/Qiuxu00/AGQ
2610.33074.tldr_en: Action-Guided Quantization is proposed, which combines action sensitivity with a measured proxy for weight recovery cost to allocate matrix bitwidths under storage budgets to allocate matrix bitwidths under storage budgets.

llm.title_ja: ビジョン・言語・アクションモデルのためのアクション誘導型超低ビット量子化
llm.tldr_ja: アクション感度と重み復元コストの測定プロキシを組み合わせ、ストレージ予算内でマトリクスビット幅を割り当てるアクション誘導型量子化を提案した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルの大きな重みフットプリントが、メモリ制約のあるオンボードプラットフォームへの展開を困難にしている。
llm.method: アクション感度と重み復元コストの測定プロキシを組み合わせてストレージ予算内でマトリクスビット幅を割り当てるアクション誘導型量子化を提案する。
llm.result: LIBEROにおいてW3で92.7%のタスク成功率を達成し、AWQやGPTQを上回り、W2.5でも70.5%の成功率を維持した。

2610.29264.title: Training in Deployment: Human-in-the-loop Online Post-Training for Robot Manipulation
2610.29264.abstract: Large pretrained robot foundation models provide strong priors for manipulation, yet adapting them to target tasks with offline teleoperated demonstrations often fails to cover the contact-rich, recovery, and precision-critical states encountered during deployment. Existing methods mitigate this issue by augmenting offline demonstrations with human-in-the-loop data or online reinforcement learning. Despite this, offline post-training adapts slowly because it cannot immediately absorb deployment experience, while online RL typically relies on value functions or auxiliary actor-critic models, increasing both training complexity and instability. We present TIDE (Training In DEployment), a human-in-the-loop online post-training system. TIDE introduces a provenance-conditioned supervised learning framework that updates the policy online from human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer. Across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, TIDE improves milestone-normalized task progress and binary full-task completion over the warm-start policy and matched additional offline demonstrations, and performs comparably to the fixed-policy collection baseline while making updated checkpoints available during deployment. Each task-specific online post-training session, from the start of deployment rollouts until the final checkpoint is available, completes in less than one hour while learning and checkpoint handling run asynchronously.
2610.29264.tldr_en: TIDE (Training In DEployment), a human-in-the-loop online post-training system that updates the policy online from human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer is introduced.

llm.title_ja: デプロイ中トレーニング：ロボットマニピュレーションのためのヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ型オンラインポストトレーニング
llm.tldr_ja: 学習済み批評家や報酬モデルなしで、デプロイ中に収集された人間の介入とポリシー生成ロールアウトからポリシーをオンラインで更新するヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ型オンラインポストトレーニングシステム「TIDE」を提案した。
llm.problem: オフラインのデモンストレーションで適応させたロボット基盤モデルは、デプロイ時に遭遇する接触リッチでリカバリや精度が要求される状態をカバーしきれない。
llm.method: 学習済みの批評家、報酬モデル、アクションスコアラーを使用せず、デプロイ中の人間の介入やロールアウトからオンラインでポリシーを更新するフレームワーク「TIDE」を導入する。
llm.result: 4つの実世界双腕マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、ウォームスタートポリシーや追加のオフラインデモンストレーションと比較してタスクの進捗と完了率が向上した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ
ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.29246.title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation
2610.29246.abstract: Predictive representations for robot manipulation should connect scene geometry with the state changes induced by actions. Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes. Guided by this intuition, we introduce DepState-JEPA, a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, DepState. Built on V-JEPA~2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding. Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features. Robot-state readouts provide recursive proprioceptive inputs; object-trajectory supervision and calibrated forward kinematics shape state learning through motion targets and joint--TCP consistency. Comparisons show stronger RGB-encoder transfer after RGB-D adaptation, feature completion, conditioned visual forecasting, and manipulation success. Within-model ablations identify contributions from depth content, metric coordinates, and future-state matching, with additional control gains from FK regularization. The project page is available at https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/depstate-jepa/.
2610.29246.tldr_en: DepState-JEPA is a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, DepState, built on V-JEPA~2.1.

llm.title_ja: DepState-JEPA：視覚的知覚とマニピュレーションのための深度グラウンド化状態表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: V-JEPA 2.1をベースにし、共有潜在状態「DepState」を通じて空間理解とアクション条件付き予測を結びつけるデュアルストリームRGB-深度共同埋め込み予測アーキテクチャ「DepState-JEPA」を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーションのための予測表現は、シーンの幾何学とアクションによって引き起こされた状態変化を結びつける必要がある。
llm.method: 深度を補足的な観測ストリームとして使用し、両方のモダリティをメトリック3D空間にグラウンド化するデュアルストリームRGB-深度共同埋め込み予測アーキテクチャ「DepState-JEPA」を導入する。
llm.result: RGB-D適応後のRGBエンコーダの転移、特徴補完、条件付き視覚予測、マニピュレーション成功率の向上が示された。

2610.29244.title: Failure Modes of Vision-Language Models for Human Activity Understanding in Thermal HRI
2610.29244.abstract: Thermal cameras enable robots to perceive human activities in darkness while revealing less personally identifiable appearance information and fewer details of the surrounding environment than RGB cameras. As vision-language models (VLMs), originally developed for RGB imagery, are increasingly integrated into embodied systems for scene understanding and high-level planning, thermal sensing offers a promising way to extend activity perception to low-light and privacy-sensitive settings. However, the failure modes of VLMs in thermal human activity understanding for human-robot interaction (HRI) remain underexplored. We fill this gap by evaluating seven locally deployable VLMs, including models developed for physical AI and robotics, on two person-centric thermal datasets. Our diagnostic tasks examine fine-grained action recognition, activity timeline reconstruction, and the ability to withhold unsupported answers. Paired RGB recordings serve as a performance reference, while controlled variations in frame sampling, thermal input presentation, and reasoning are used to assess whether the observed errors can be mitigated. Our results show that models can recognize broad activity categories but struggle with fine-grained actions such as coughing, sneezing, and yawning. They also produce inaccurate event timelines and hallucinate actions involving objects. Simple thermal input preprocessing and additional reasoning offer only limited, model-dependent gains. Abstention behavior also varies across models even under explicit instructions, limiting their reliability for practical robotic use.
2610.29244.tldr_en: This work evaluates seven locally deployable VLMs, including models developed for physical AI and robotics, on two person-centric thermal datasets and shows that models can recognize broad activity categories but struggle with fine-grained actions such as coughing, sneezing, and yawning.

llm.title_ja: サーマルHRIにおける人間活動理解のためのビジョン・言語モデルの失敗モード
llm.tldr_ja: フィジカルAIやロボット工学向けモデルを含む7つのローカル展開可能なVLMを2つの人物中心のサーマルデータセットで評価し、モデルが広範な活動カテゴリを認識できる一方で咳やくしゃみなどの微細な行動に苦戦することを示した。
llm.problem: HRIにおけるサーマル画像を用いた人間活動理解において、VLMの失敗モードが十分に探求されていない。
llm.method: 物理AIやロボット工学向けに開発されたモデルを含む7つのローカル展開可能なVLMを2つの人物中心サーマルデータセットで評価する。
llm.result: モデルは広い活動カテゴリを認識できるものの、咳やくしゃみ、あくびといった微細な行動の認識、正確なタイムライン再構築、オブジェクトを伴う行動のハルシネーションに苦戦することが示された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語モデル

2610.29203.title: NavBind: Diagnosing Instruction-Action Binding at Route Forks in Navigation VLAs
2610.29203.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) navigation models translate visual observations and instructions into actions. Navigation success assesses whether an agent reaches the goal. However, reaching the goal successfully does not establish whether the model genuinely follows the instructions or relies on visual cues or navigation history. We introduce NavBind to diagnose instruction-action binding: whether changing the instruction influences the probabilistic distribution of the actions, with the navigation context fixed. We construct 3,252 route-fork contexts by recombining route-aligned instruction segments from R2R-CE and RxR-CE. Each context pairs full instructions that share the description of the route already traveled but specify different branches. Both are evaluated under the same agent state and navigation history. We compare generated local action sequences, the likelihoods of fixed reference action sequences under both instructions, and changes in visual attention and attribution. Across the evaluated models, higher reported navigation success does not imply that the model more faithfully follows the instructions.
2610.29203.tldr_en: Across the evaluated models, higher reported navigation success does not imply that the model more faithfully follows the instructions, and across the evaluated models, higher reported navigation success does not imply that the model more faithfully follows the instructions.

llm.title_ja: NavBind：ナビゲーションVLAのルート分岐における指示と行動の結合の診断
llm.tldr_ja: ナビゲーションコンテキストを固定した状態で指示を変更することが行動の確率分布に影響を与えるかを診断する「NavBind」を提案し、報告される高いナビゲーション成功率が必ずしも指示への忠実な追従を意味しないことを示した。
llm.problem: ナビゲーションの成功は目標到達を示すが、モデルが本当に指示に従っているのか、それとも視覚的手がかりやナビゲーション履歴に依存しているのかが不明確である。
llm.method: ナビゲーションコンテキストを固定して指示を変更した際のアクションの確率的分布への影響を診断するため「NavBind」を構築する。
llm.result: 評価されたモデル全体において、報告されるナビゲーション成功率が高いことが、モデルがより忠実に指示に従っていることを意味するわけではないことが示された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・アクション

2610.29200.title: NeuralSRender: G-Buffer Guided Video Diffusion for Sim-to-Real Rendering
2610.29200.abstract: The scarcity of high-quality annotated visual data remains a critical bottleneck for autonomous-driving perception. Simulators provide training data at scale, but the limited realism of synthetic videos compromises perception performance in real-world applications. To address this limitation, we propose NeuralSRender, a sim-to-real video translation framework that enhances the photorealism of synthetic videos while maintaining geometric consistency with the source scenes. Built on a pretrained video diffusion transformer (DiT), NeuralSRender uses a lightweight projector to inject geometric and material priors from G-buffers, and LoRA enables parameter-efficient adaptation. The model is trained in two stages: it first learns G-buffer conditioning from synthetic videos with accurate G-buffers, then adapts to real-world appearance using real videos with estimated G-buffers. During the second stage, an additional LoRA module is trained while the projector and first-stage LoRA remain frozen to reduce interference from estimation noise. NeuralSRender introduces only 1.45\% parameter overhead and can be trained on consumer-grade GPUs with 24 GB of memory. To support training and evaluation, we introduce GenReal, a large-scale driving video dataset comprising synthetic and real-world videos with corresponding G-buffers. Experiments demonstrate improved photorealism with competitive geometric consistency. Training perception models on our translated videos instead of raw simulator renders improves detection $\mathrm{AP}_{50}$ on nuImages from 35.1 to 40.6 and segmentation mIoU on Cityscapes from 32.4 to 40.8. Our code, data, and model weights are available at: https://github.com/WHU-USI3DV/NeuralSRender.
2610.29200.tldr_en: NeuralSRender is a sim-to-real video translation framework that enhances the photorealism of synthetic videos while maintaining geometric consistency with the source scenes, and GenReal, a large-scale driving video dataset comprising synthetic and real-world videos with corresponding G-buffers is introduced.

llm.title_ja: NeuralSRender：Gバッファ誘導型ビデオ拡散によるSim-to-Realレンダリング
llm.tldr_ja: Gバッファからの幾何学的・素材的事前情報を注入することで、ソースシーンとの幾何学的一貫性を維持しながら合成ビデオの写実性を高めるSim-to-Realビデオ変換フレームワーク「NeuralSRender」を提案した。
llm.problem: 高品質な注釈付き視覚データの不足が自動運転知覚のボトルネックとなっており、シミュレータの合成ビデオは現実世界での知覚性能を損なう。
llm.method: 事前学習済みビデオ拡散Transformerをベースに、Gバッファからの幾何学的・素材的事前情報を軽量プロジェクタで注入するSim-to-Realビデオ変換フレームワーク「NeuralSRender」を提案する。
llm.result: 写実性が向上し、nuImagesの検出AP50が35.1から40.6へ、CityscapesのセグメンテーションmIoUが32.4から40.8へ向上した。

2610.29169.title: SMR: Learning streaming motion retargeting for humanoids from human semantic
2610.29169.abstract: Retargeting human motion to humanoids requires preserving motion semantics while accounting for the robot's physical constraints. Kinematic pipelines prescribe a robot trajectory through geometric matching, without establishing whether it can be executed under the robot's dynamics. Prior physics-supervised neural methods train bidirectional full-sequence models on physics-refined kinematic trajectories, remaining tied to prescribed kinematic solutions and requiring noncausal context. We propose SMR, a streaming neural motion retargeter learned from semantic-conditioned physics experts. We convert human motion into robot-aware task-space targets for body landmark positions, orientations, and velocities. Physics experts track these targets directly in simulation under contact, dynamics, and actuator constraints. We train a single strictly causal Transformer on their executed state trajectories that complete the motion and pass semantic and physical validity checks. At each incoming frame, the student uses only current and past human observations to generate a robot motion reference for a downstream whole-body controller. Experiments demonstrate that semantic-conditioned physics experts generate motion with higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than direct optimization-based retargeting, while the resulting streaming retargeter achieves improved closed-loop performance over kinematic and physics-refined baselines under a common whole-body controller.
2610.29169.tldr_en: Experiments demonstrate that semantic-conditioned physics experts generate motion with higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than direct optimization-based retargeting, while the resulting streaming retargeter achieves improved closed-loop performance over kinematic and physics-refined baselines under a common whole-body controller.

llm.title_ja: SMR：人間のセマンティクスからのヒューノイド向けストリーミング動作リターゲティングの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 意味条件付き物理エキスパートから学習するストリーミング型ニューラル動作リターゲティング手法「SMR」を提案し、従来の運動学ベースや物理洗練ベースのベースラインを上回るクローズドール性能を実現した。
llm.problem: 人間の動きをヒューノイドにリターゲティングする際、運動学パイプラインはロボットの物理的ダイナミクス下で実行可能かを確認せずに幾何学的マッチングを行っている。
llm.method: 人間の動きをロボット対応のタスク空間ターゲットに変換し、物理エキスパートによって追従させ、その実行状態軌跡から厳密に因果的なTransformerを訓練する。
llm.result: セマンティック条件付き物理エキスパートがより高いセマンティック忠実度と物理的妥当性を持つ動きを生成し、SMRは優れたクローズドループ性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 動作リターゲティング
物理シミュレーション

2610.29168.title: How Representational Priors Shape Generalization in World Action Models
2610.29168.abstract: World action models (WAMs) are shown to substantially diverge under generalization performance based on their generative backbones. We investigate this gap through the representational geometry that WAMs inherit from their backbones and how policy training reorganizes it. Our central hypothesis is that a useful representational prior would structure geometry that separates nuisance information from the in-distribution manifold in advance of training as a policy. We quantify this with nuisance orthogonality; orthogonality of the feature under visual variation outside the empirical in-distribution manifold. Across various image and video backbones, we show that a higher orthogonality from the representational prior is associated with stronger robustness to visual variations after WAM training, enabling policy generalization measurable prospectively for world models. In addition, analyzing the resulting robust WAMs reveals nuisance suppression; relative suppression of feature displacement caused by such variations and robust action generation of the policy. Together, these findings provide a geometric perspective on how the representational prior of the world model shapes the generalization performance of WAMs.
2610.29168.tldr_en: It is shown that a higher orthogonality from the representational prior is associated with stronger robustness to visual variations after WAM training, enabling policy generalization measurable prospectively for world models.

llm.title_ja: 表現事前分布がワールドアクションモデルの汎化性能をどのように形作るか
llm.tldr_ja: 表現事前分布からの高い直交性がWAM訓練後の視覚的変動に対する頑健性の強さと相関しており、ワールドモデルの汎化性能を事前に測定可能にすることを示した。
llm.problem: ワールドアクションモデル（WAM）は、生成バックボーンに基づいて汎化性能に大きな乖離が生じる。
llm.method: バックボーンから継承する表現幾何学とポリシー訓練によるその再編成に着目し、分布外の視覚的変動に対する特徴の直交性（妨害直交性）を定量化して調査する。
llm.result: 表現事前分布からの高い直交性がWAM訓練後の視覚的変動に対する強い頑健性と関連しており、ポリシー汎化を予測可能にすることを示した。

2610.29161.title: SimPT: An Automated Simulation Framework for Intervention-Based VLA Post-Training
2610.29161.abstract: Human-in-the-loop (HIL) post-training improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies through expert corrections, but costly human supervision and repeated real-robot evaluation limit algorithm exploration and development. We introduce SimPT (Simulation-based Post-Training), a simulation framework that automates intervention-based VLA post-training by integrating policy rollouts, corrective data collection, policy training, and standalone evaluation. To automatically determine intervention timing and recovery strategies, we develop an Agent-Compiled Progress Graph that tracks task progress using privileged simulator state and retains stable snapshots during policy execution. After a rollout fails, a CuRobo-based expert attempts recovery from these snapshots, starting at more advanced task stages and falling back to earlier ones as needed to generate corrective trajectories. We implement and compare four post-training methods, RECAP, HG-DAgger, DPO+SFT, and FlowPRO, across seven RoboTwin manipulation tasks. Relative to a fixed-interval snapshot baseline, the Progress Graph reduces recovery attempts by 75.0% and increases recovery success from 93.4% to 98.9%. Using SimPT, we develop RECAP-CF-LPF, a refinement of RECAP that combines cross-fitting and low-pass filtering of value predictions. This refinement increases the overall success rate from 76.50% to 79.36% in held-out simulation trials. In real-robot HIL post-training, it increases the success rate from 72% to 96% across 25 scenarios of an Ethernet cable-insertion task. These results demonstrate the utility of SimPT for exploring and developing VLA post-training algorithms.
2610.29161.tldr_en: SimPT (Simulation-based Post-Training), a simulation framework that automates intervention-based VLA post-training by integrating policy rollouts, corrective data collection, policy training, and standalone evaluation, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: SimPT：介入ベースのVLAポストトレーニングのための自動化シミュレーションフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシーのロールアウト、修正データの収集、ポリシー訓練、評価を統合し、介入ベースのVLAポストトレーニングを自動化するシミュレーションフレームワーク「SimPT」を提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループのポストトレーニングは専門家の修正を必要とするが、コストのかかる人間の監督と繰り返しの実機評価がアルゴリズムの探索を制限している。
llm.method: 特権的なシミュレータ状態を使用してタスクの進捗を追跡するエージェントコンパイル進捗グラフを開発し、リカバリ戦略と介入タイミングを自動的に決定するシミュレーションフレームワーク「SimPT」を導入する。
llm.result: プログレスグラフによりリカバリ試行が75.0%削減され、実機実験においてイーサネットケーブル挿入タスクの成功率が72%から96%に向上した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマン・イン・ザ・ループ

2610.29142.title: State-Dependent Objective Coordination for End-to-End Balance and Navigation
2610.29142.abstract: Traditional robotic navigation systems separate mapping, planning, and low-level control through cascaded modules, introducing computational overhead and accumulated latency. End-to-end reinforcement learning offers a compact unified policy that maps onboard observations directly to control actions. However, on inherently unstable platforms such as two-wheeled inverted-pendulum robots, navigation progress and obstacle avoidance can conflict with attitude stabilization in a strongly state-dependent manner. We propose a lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for integrated navigation and control. A pitch-conditioned scalarization coefficient $β(s)\in[0,1]$ adjusts the relative contributions of balance stabilization and navigation objectives during training, without extra control hierarchies or auxiliary attitude-stabilization controllers, such as proportional-integral-derivative (PID) or linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) controllers. To support zero-shot deployment, simulation training models execution delay, action hold, asynchronous and noisy observations, and dynamics uncertainty. Gradient analysis reveals persistent directional interference and state-dependent variation in the objectives' relative scales. Comparisons with alternative reward-weighting, constraint, training, and control-structure strategies show that PPO+$β(s)$, where PPO denotes proximal policy optimization, achieves 98% and 95% success rates with small attitude excursions on the fixed obstacle map and the randomly generated high-obstacle-density map, respectively. Zero-shot hardware experiments further demonstrate bounded attitude behavior and consistent obstacle avoidance using only onboard observations. Training and evaluation code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.
2610.29142.tldr_en: A lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for integrated navigation and control is proposed, where PPO+ achieves 98% and 95% success rates with small attitude excursions on the fixed obstacle map and the randomly generated high-obstacle-density map, respectively.

llm.title_ja: エンドツーエンドのバランスとナビゲーションのための状態依存型目的調整
llm.tldr_ja: 追加の制御階層や補助コントローラを使用せず、ピッチ条件付きスカラー化係数によってバランス安定化とナビゲーションの目的の相対的寄与を調整する軽量な状態依存型目的調整手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 不安定な二輪倒立振子ロボットにおいて、ナビゲーションや障害物回避の進行が姿勢安定化と状態依存的に強く競合する。
llm.method: ピッチ条件付きスカラー化係数を用いて訓練中にバランス安定化とナビゲーションの目的の相対的寄与を調整する軽量な状態依存型目的調整手法を提案する。
llm.result: PPO+β(s)は固定障害物マップおよびランダム障害物マップにおいてそれぞれ98%および95%の成功率を達成し、ゼロショット実機実験でも一貫した障害物回避を示した。

2610.29117.title: Learning to Absorb Corrections: Critic-Weighted Residual Flow for Vision-Based Insertion
2610.29117.abstract: Vision-based insertion requires correcting alignment errors while retaining useful behavior learned from demonstrations. We present ACT--Flow, an online learning framework that couples an adaptive Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) with a conditional residual flow policy. Following anchor-guided warmup, ACT absorbs successful executed actions through behavioral cloning, while residual targets are recomputed relative to the updated prior. A chunk-level critic learns from successful and failed interactions and evaluates final composed actions. Its estimates weight generated residual candidates for flow matching, complemented by supervision from successful real executions. Candidate scoring is confined to training; deployment uses RGB observations and samples one residual per action chunk. We evaluate the framework on power-plug, USB, and key insertion, together with cable routing and needle threading. Results show a five-task mean success rate of 66% at 20,000 post-initialization interaction steps, exceeding the strongest baseline by 18 percentage points at this checkpoint. Evaluations at matched checkpoints with the residual disabled show ACT's mean success increasing from 16% to 76%. Component ablations further support the complementary roles of behavior absorption, value weighting, and successful-action supervision.
2610.29117.tldr_en: ACT--Flow is presented, an online learning framework that couples an adaptive Action Chunking Transformer with a conditional residual flow policy and shows a five-task mean success rate of 66% at 20,000 post-initialization interaction steps, exceeding the strongest baseline by 18 percentage points at this checkpoint.

llm.title_ja: 修正の吸収学習：視覚ベースの挿入に向けた批評家加重型残差フロー
llm.tldr_ja: 適応型ACTと条件付き残差フローポリシーを組み合わせたオンライン学習フレームワーク「ACT-Flow」を提案し、5つのタスクで平均成功率66%を達成した。
llm.problem: 視覚ベースの挿入では、デモンストレーションから学習した有用な行動を維持しながら、アライメントの誤差を修正する必要がある。
llm.method: 適応型Action Chunking Transformer（ACT）と条件付き残差フローポリシーを組み合わせたオンライン学習フレームワーク「ACT-Flow」を提案する。
llm.result: 20,000ステップ後の5タスク平均成功率が66%に達し、最強のベースラインを18ポイント上回った。

2610.29088.title: Causal world models under physical parameter shifts
2610.29088.abstract: World models predict how embodied systems evolve under actions, but their accuracy can degrade when physical conditions move outside the training distribution. We study two components of causal modeling: which inputs a predictor may use, and how its mechanism computes their effects. In a synthetic benchmark with shortcut features, a frozen dependency mask derived from paired interventions reduces mean out-of-distribution (OOD) RMSE from 1.769 for a fully connected predictor to 0.697, close to the generator-oracle mask (0.694). For robot link-mass extrapolation in CausalWorld, with disjoint training and test mass ranges, we develop finger-local world models in which link masses enter inertia and dynamics-bias terms through explicit affine coefficients, actions act through either a learned torque network or the known PD controller, and learned residuals capture contact-related effects. Compared with a separately trained control whose mass inputs are fixed at training means, the known-PD model turns out-of-range masses into a consistent predictive gain: median time-averaged joint R2 over 150-step rollouts rises from 0.609 to 0.727, with improvement in all ten task-seed runs (exact two-sided sign test, p = 0.002). In a shared 100-step forecast, the learned-torque model is competitive with the strongest recurrent robotic world model (RWM) configuration (median joint R2 of 0.755 - 0.768 versus 0.752), whereas supplying out-of-range masses sharply degrades the MLP and recurrent predictors. These results indicate that how a physical parameter enters the dynamics mechanism determines whether its out-of-range value helps or harms prediction.
2610.29088.tldr_en: Results indicate that how a physical parameter enters the dynamics mechanism determines whether its out-of-range value helps or harms prediction, whereas supplying out-of-range masses sharply degrades the MLP and recurrent predictors.

llm.title_ja: 物理的パラメータ変動下での因果ワールドモデル
llm.tldr_ja: 物理パラメータがダイナミクス機構にどのように入るかによって、分布外の値が予測を助けるか害するか決まることを示し、リンク質量外挿において既知のPDモデルが予測性能を向上させることを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 物理条件が訓練分布外に移行すると、ロボットの行動に対するワールドモデルの予測精度が低下する。
llm.method: リンク質量が慣性やダイナミクスバイアス項にアフィン係数として入る指単位のワールドモデルを開発し、予測への影響を分析する。
llm.result: 既知のPDモデルを使用することで、範囲外の質量が予測ゲインとなり、中央値の時系列平均結合R2が0.609から0.727に向上した。

2610.37692.title: Bouba Beats Kiki, and Other Regularities in the Subjective Preferences of LLMs
2610.37692.abstract: Users engage with large language models on tasks that are purely objective ("When was Netflix founded?"), purely subjective ("What should I name my child?") or anywhere in-between. We have rich tools for evaluating model accuracy with respect to objective criteria. However, when it comes to subjective aspects of a task, we do not have similarly developed methodology at hand. In this paper, we take some early steps towards framing the question of subjective evaluation. Rather than measure how often a model is right or wrong on a question, we instead ask, how do models make choices among multiple viable responses without a clear winner? To study this question, we restrict our focus to short-form content, and consider comparison tasks among three such content types: numbers, baby names, and fictional cities. We identify 29 aspects of these short-form examples covering many areas of syntax and semantics (length, alphabetic order, popularity, vowel mix, spoken sound, etc.). We show first that models tend to have strong and reproducible preferences for or against some of these aspects. Second, we show that variations in how the model is asked to express a preference may cause some of these aspects to activate or deactivate in the model's selection. Third, we show that overall preference distributions among pairs may vary radically based on seemingly-unimportant variations in the nature of the question posed to the model, raising new questions about manipulation. And finally, we show that, if models are used both to create lists of alternatives and to rank them, there are unexpected interactions between the two stages that may also drive the models' stated preferences.
2610.37692.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures in main text; 27 pages, 13 figures in supplement. To appear at NeurIPS 2026
2610.37692.tldr_en: This paper restricts its focus to short-form content, and considers comparison tasks among three such content types: numbers, baby names, and fictional cities, showing that models tend to have strong and reproducible preferences for or against some of these aspects.

llm.title_ja: 「ブーバはキキを打ち負かす」およびLLMの主観的選好におけるその他の規則性
llm.tldr_ja: 数、赤ちゃんの名前、架空の都市という3つの短形式コンテンツを用いてLLMの選好を調査し、モデルが特定の側面に対して強くて再現性のある選好を持つことを示した。
llm.problem: 正解のない主観的なタスクにおいて、大規模言語モデルがどのように複数の中から選択を行うかについての評価手法が十分に確立されていない。
llm.method: 数、赤ちゃんの名前、架空の都市という3種類の短形式コンテンツを対象に、構文や意味論に関する29の側面を特定してモデルの選好を分析する。
llm.result: モデルは特定の側面に対して強く再現性のある選好を示し、質問の表現方法のわずかな変化によって選好分布が大きく変動することが示された。

2610.29030.title: PHD-Hand: A Printable Humanoid Dexterous Hand with Linkage-Driven 3-DOA Digits
2610.29030.abstract: Currently, dexterous humanoid robot hands are widely considered the final hardware bottleneck that hampers generalist robots from physically assisting people at home and work. As conventional tendon-driven designs suffer from high cost, demanding maintenance, poor reliability, and short durability, alternative linkage-driven designs have increasingly gained attention. Despite their potential to avoid the weaknesses of tendon-driven hands, integrating multiple degrees of actuation (DOA) in a single digit with linkage drivetrains is a challenge for design and fabrication. Only a few studies have managed to present functional humanoid hands that are completely linkage-driven and have at least three DOAs per digit without compromising actuator placement and other design preferences. Our work introduces a new linkage-driven hand featuring a unique flexure hinge. Together with elastic drive rods made of spring steel, the linkage drivetrains are significantly simplified. Unlike other linkage-driven designs of similar dexterity, our design does not require many miniature moving parts. As a result, the hand can be fabricated easily with a budget 3D printer. This not only significantly lowers the barrier to entry for using and developing dexterous humanoid robot hand functions, but also allows the hands to be sized much closer to regular human hands. The design offers desirable kinematic advantages as well. A prototype is evaluated for grasping and object manipulation. In addition, this paper presents our latest findings on kinematics and control of the hand.
2610.29030.comment: Submitted and Accepted at IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids 2026). 8 pages. Supplementary video: https://lnkd.in/p/er-NRfMn
