llm.title_ja: PHD-Hand：リンク駆動型3DOA指を持つ印刷可能なヒューノイド器用ハンド
llm.tldr_ja: ばね鋼製の弾性駆動ロッドと独自の屈曲ヒンジを備えた、安価な3Dプリンタで製作可能なリンク駆動型ヒューマノイドハンドを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の腱駆動型設計は、高コスト、困難なメンテナンス、低い信頼性、短い耐久性に苦しんでいる。
llm.method: 独自の屈曲ヒンジとばね鋼製の弾性駆動ロッドを採用し、多数の微小な可動部品を必要としないリンク駆動型ハンドの設計と製作を行う。
llm.result: 手頃な3Dプリンタで容易に製作可能でありながら、人間の手に近いサイズを実現し、把持とオブジェクト操作の評価を行った。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドハンド

2610.29014.title: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development
2610.29014.abstract: Coding agents are rapidly advancing from single-file generation to long-horizon repository-scale engineering, yet the evaluation of their capabilities to author interactive extended reality (XR) applications remains an open challenge. Unlike traditional software, XR applications operate within dynamic 3D physical environments where runtime robustness depends jointly on continuous user motion, spatial input, and environmental sensing. We introduce GenXR-Bench, the first benchmark for the end-to-end evaluation of coding agents in XR software development. GenXR-Bench contains 112 expert-authored tasks spanning 24 feature implementations, 21 bug repairs, and 67 application generation tasks. Held-out tests combine scripted and adaptive interactions with programmatic and visual assertions to evaluate core functionality and runtime behavior. GenXR-Bench's testing suite achieves 96.5% accuracy against blinded expert judgments of 124 candidate applications executed on consumer XR hardware. Evaluating 10 models on GenXR-Bench, we find that the strongest configuration achieves only 50.9% overall Pass@1. Failure analysis identifies recurring misunderstandings in asynchronous sensor lifecycles, physical grounding, and embodied interaction semantics. GenXR-Bench establishes a reproducible testbed for evaluating coding agents in the interactive and physically situated conditions of spatial computing.
2610.29014.comment: 37 pages, 10 figures. Code available at https://github.com/whuang37/genxr-bench
2610.29014.tldr_en: GenXR-Bench establishes a reproducible testbed for evaluating coding agents in the interactive and physically situated conditions of spatial computing and identifies recurring misunderstandings in asynchronous sensor lifecycles, physical grounding, and embodied interaction semantics.

llm.title_ja: GenXR-Bench：インタラクティブXR開発のためのコーディングエージェントのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: インタラクティブなXRアプリケーションの開発におけるコーディングエージェントのエンドツーエンド評価を行う最初のベンチマーク「GenXR-Bench」を構築し、モデルの成功率がまだ低いことを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 動的な3D物理環境で動作するインタラクティブなXRアプリケーションのオーサリングにおけるコーディングエージェントの評価手法が不足している。
llm.method: 機能実装、バグ修正、アプリケーション生成のタスクを含む112のエキスパート作成タスクからなるベンチマーク「GenXR-Bench」を提案する。
llm.result: 最強の構成でもPass@1が50.9%に留まり、非同期センサーライフサイクルや物理的グラウンディングにおける理解不足が特定された。
keywords_ja: コーディングエージェント

2610.28994.title: The Optimal Sampler for Diverse TSP Solutions: Characterization, Limits, and Learning
2610.28994.abstract: We address the Diverse Traveling Salesman Problem (D-TSP) that seeks a set of $k$ distinct TSP tours. Each selected tour must not exceed a prescribed multiple of the optimal tour length, while the maximum pairwise Jaccard similarity within the selected set is minimized. This formulation is important for applications requiring both solution quality and fault tolerance, such as logistics planning, robotics, and strategic patrolling. We propose a novel hybrid framework that decomposes D-TSP into a sampling stage and a selection stage. The selection stage is a max-min dispersion problem, for which any approximation better than a factor of two is NP-hard; we therefore focus on the sampling stage. Our contributions are both theoretical and empirical. Theoretically, we give two end-to-end guarantees for the optimal sampling distribution, from two perspectives: including an optimal set in the sampled pool, or having at least $k$ mutually distant tours in the pool. The second reduces the number of samples from exponential to linear in $k$, at the cost of weakening the benchmark from the best $k$ tours to the best $βk$ for some $β> 1$. For practical use, we prove that a pipeline that samples spanning trees and then converts to tours does not hurt the quality of the pool in principle. Empirically, both objectives are learnable, and our experiments not only validate the analysis but also outperform the baselines on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, by a single trained model with no fine-tuning.
2610.28994.tldr_en: It is proved that a pipeline that samples spanning trees and then converts to tours does not hurt the quality of the pool in principle, and it is proposed that a pipeline that samples spanning trees and then converts to tours does not hurt the quality of the pool in principle.

llm.title_ja: 多様なTSP解のための最適サンプラー：特徴付け、限界、および学習
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な巡回セールスマン問題（D-TSP）に対し、スパニングツリーをサンプリングしてツアーに変換するパイプラインがプールの質を損なわないことを理論的・実証的に証明した。
llm.problem: 解の品質とフォールトトレランスの両方を必要とする用途において、多様な複数のTSPツアーを効率的に見つける必要がある。
llm.method: D-TSPをサンプリング段階と選択段階に分解し、最適サンプリング分布に対する理論的保証と、スパニングツリーをサンプリングしてツアーに変換するパイプラインの有効性を証明する。
llm.result: 単一の訓練されたモデルにより、追加のファインチューニングなしで、分布内および分布外のインスタンスにおいてベースラインを上回る性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 巡回セールスマン問題

2610.28990.title: Doob-Based Generative Policy Optimization
2610.28990.abstract: Diffusion and flow models provide expressive policy classes for robotic and sequential decision-making systems. However, their action likelihoods are generally intractable, limiting the direct use of widely adopted policy optimization methods such as PPO and GRPO. We propose Doob Policy Optimization (DoobPO), a framework that leverages Doob's $h$-transform for likelihood-free reinforcement learning fine-tuning of generative policies. DoobPO separates policy improvement from generative policy learning. It first learns a lightweight ratio model that represents the desired policy update, and then distills the resulting ratio-tilted target policy into the generative policy via conditional drift matching. This formulation applies uniformly to both diffusion and flow policies and supports a broad family of policy improvement rules, including PPO and GRPO. We prove that the practical conditional drift matching objective is gradient-equivalent to the ideal Doob drift matching objective. We further show that the induced diffusion process solves an endpoint-constrained stochastic optimal control problem. This establishes that it achieves the minimum-energy modification required to realize the desired policy tilt. Across MuJoCo continuous-control benchmarks, DoobPO achieves strong performance against competitive diffusion- and flow-policy baselines, showing a principled and practical route to RL fine-tuning for generative policies.
2610.28990.tldr_en: Doob Policy Optimization (DoobPO), a framework that leverages Doob's $h$-transform for likelihood-free reinforcement learning fine-tuning of generative policies, is proposed, showing a principled and practical route to RL fine-tuning for generative policies.

llm.title_ja: Doobベースの生成ポリシー最適化
llm.tldr_ja: Doobのh-transformを活用して、生成ポリシーの尤度不要な強化学習ファインチューニングを行うフレームワーク「DoobPO」を提案した。
llm.problem: 拡散モデルやフローモデルは強力なポリシー表現を提供するが、アクションの尤度が一般に計算困難であり、PPOやGRPOなどのポリシー最適化手法の直接適用が制限される。
llm.method: Doobのh-transformを利用して尤度不要な強化学習ファインチューニングを行うフレームワーク「DoobPO」を提案する。
llm.result: MuJoCoの連続制御ベンチマークにおいて、競合する拡散およびフローポリシーのベースラインに対して優れた性能を達成した。

2610.28962.title: RoPT: Robust 6DoF Object Pose Tracking in Video
2610.28962.abstract: Accurate 6-DoF object pose tracking is essential for robotic interaction, yet conventional monocular pipelines frequently suffer from catastrophic divergence under rapid object motion. We present RoPT, a robust tracking framework engineered to overcome this limitation by unifying visual perception, temporal kinematics, and global re-localization into a tightly coupled closed loop. Unlike existing open-loop trackers, RoPT delivers three critical capabilities that fundamentally alter system resilience. First, the visual perception component tracks object masks to robustly handle partial and severe occlusions. Second, a kinematic factor graph regularizes frame-to-frame updates, forecasts forward pose predictions, and drives a parallel multi-hypothesis verification scheme to bypass local minima. Finally, an active re-localization module transforms the pipeline into a closed-loop system, making it failure-aware and capable of deterministic self-recovery. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework across challenging benchmarks alongside real-world robotic demonstrations, achieving significantly higher tracking survivability under rapid motion.
2610.28962.tldr_en: RoPT, a robust tracking framework engineered to overcome this limitation by unifying visual perception, temporal kinematics, and global re-localization into a tightly coupled closed loop, is presented.

llm.title_ja: RoPT：ビデオにおける頑健な6自由度オブジェクト姿勢追跡
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚知覚、時間的運動学、グローバル再局所化を緊密に統合したクローズドループの頑健なオブジェクト姿勢追跡フレームワーク「RoPT」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の単眼パイプラインは、急速なオブジェクトの動きに対して破滅的な発散を起こすことが多い。
llm.method: オブジェクトマスクを追跡する視覚知覚、フレーム間更新を正則化する運動学ファクターグラフ、およびアクティブな再局所化モジュールを統合したクローズドループ追跡フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 困難なベンチマークや実世界のロボットデモンストレーションにおいて、急速な動きに対する追跡の生存率が大幅に向上した。

2610.28955.title: SLoSa: Small, Low-Power, and Safe Foundation Models for Robotic Task Planning
2610.28955.abstract: Safe robotic task planning requires planners that can reliably achieve task goals while satisfying safety constraints. Classical planners search over explicit symbolic task representations and can provide formal guarantees with respect to encoded safety constraints, but require rigid input formats. Their computational cost also increases rapidly with the search space. In contrast, large language models (LLMs) offer flexible task interfaces and strong generalization capabilities, but they are large, power-hungry, and pre-trained with little robot-specific safety data and knowledge. Thus, they can be difficult to deploy locally on robotic systems with limited resources. To address these limitations, we present SLoSa, a neuro-symbolic compression and fine-tuning framework for training foundation-model-based robotic task planners with Small size, Low power demand, and Safety awareness. The framework first constructs a safety-aware dataset using classical planners, an advanced teacher LLM, and formal verifiers, followed by two training stages: supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning guided by a verification-based reward machine to enforce safety alignment. We evaluate SLoSa across four Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) domains, two household simulation environments, local edge platforms, and a desktop robotic arm. Across the PDDL tasks, verifier-guided post-training raises the success rate of compact 4B-14B planners to 70.5-76.0%, while INT4 deployment on a Jetson Orin requires 17.85-26.41 W of average power. Results in household simulators and on the physical robot further demonstrate the applicability of SLoSa across diverse robotic task settings.
2610.28955.tldr_en: This work presents SLoSa, a neuro-symbolic compression and fine-tuning framework for training foundation-model-based robotic task planners with Small size, Low power demand, and Safety awareness, and evaluates its applicability across diverse robotic task settings.

llm.title_ja: SLoSa：ロボットタスク計画のための小型・低電力・安全な基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 古典的プランナーと検証ベースの報酬機械を用いた教師ありファインチューニングおよび強化学習フレームワーク「SLoSa」を提案し、コンパクトな4B〜14Bプランナーの成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルは柔軟なインターフェースを持つが、サイズが大きく、電力消費が多く、ロボット固有の安全データが不足しているため、リソースの限られたオンボードでの展開が困難である。
llm.method: 古典的プランナー、教師LLM、および形式検証器を用いて安全意識の高いデータセットを構築し、検証ベースの強化学習ファインチューニングを行う「SLoSa」を提案する。
llm.result: PDDLタスクにおいて、4B〜14Bサイズのプランナーの成功率が70.5〜76.0%に向上し、Jetson Orin上で効率的な電力消費で動作することを確認した。
keywords_ja: ニューロ・シンボリック

2610.28953.title: GGraph: A GPU-Accelerated Library for Graph-Based Robot Deployment and Learning
2610.28953.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots require spatial representations that capture geometry and semantics while staying sparse enough for planning in large, unknown environments. Graphs provide a natural representation for this purpose and underpin both classical planning methods and a growing class of reinforcement-learning (RL) policies. However, RL training needs hundreds to thousands of parallel environments, each constructing and updating its own graph. Existing graph libraries are typically designed for either single-robot deployment or fixed graphs, and CPU-based graph construction limits scalable training to only a few dozen environments. We introduce GGraph, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library for both robot deployment and large-scale learning. GGraph supports real robots through ROS 2 interfaces and vectorized GPU-based policy training, with built-in support for tasks including 3-D navigation, exploration, and loop-closure integration. For single-robot operation, GGraph updates graphs in milliseconds. At scale, it enables graph-based exploration policies to train across hundreds of parallel robots, reducing wall-clock training time by one order of magnitude. Across simulation and real-world experiments, these results establish GGraph as a unified graph infrastructure for both large-scale robot learning and deployment.
2610.28953.tldr_en: GGraph is introduced, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library for both robot deployment and large-scale learning, with built-in support for tasks including 3-D navigation, exploration, and loop-closure integration.

llm.title_ja: GGraph: グラフベースのロボット展開と学習のためのGPUアクセラレーテッドライブラリ
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの展開と大規模学習の両方に対応し、ROS 2インターフェースとベクトル化されたGPUポリシー学習をサポートするオープンソースのGPU加速グラフライブラリGGraphを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のグラフライブラリは単一ロボットや固定グラフ向けであり、CPUベースのグラフ構築では数十環境での学習に限定される。
llm.method: ROS 2インターフェースとベクトル化されたGPUベースのポリシー学習をサポートし、3次元ナビゲーションや探索を統合したGPU加速グラフライブラリを構築する。
llm.result: 数パロレルロボットでのグラフベース探索ポリシーの学習を可能にし、壁時計の学習時間を1桁削減する。

2610.28950.title: HyperDrone: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer at Millions of Frames per Second
2610.28950.abstract: We present HyperDrone, an extremely fast quadrotor simulator focused on high-performance batch rendering that is more than 20x faster than existing state-of-the-art batch quadrotor simulators. HyperDrone combines highly optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new ray-tracing engine that supports Nvidia OptiX, Vulkan, Apple Metal and WebGPU backends that takes full advantage of modern ray-tracing hardware, capable of running both components entirely on the GPU. HyperLux renders RGB, depth, semantic/instance segmentation, surface normals and optical flow observations at configurable levels of fidelity, including reflections, realistic lighting, motion blur, anti-aliasing, and Physically Based Rendering (PBR). Even in the highest-fidelity settings, HyperLux achieves millions of Frames Per Second (FPS) on consumer-grade GPUs while rendering realistic 3D scenes. We demonstrate the merits of HyperDrone by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and transferring it to a real small-scale quadrotor (Crazyflie) with a camera, running completely onboard.
2610.28950.comment: Accepted at Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026)
2610.28950.tldr_en: The merits of HyperDrone are demonstrated by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and transferring it to a real small-scale quadrotor (Crazyflie) with a camera, running completely onboard.
2610.28950.hf_summary_en: HyperDrone is a GPU-accelerated quadrotor simulator using a ray-tracing engine to render high-fidelity observations at high speed, enabling vision-based policy training and real-world transfer.

llm.title_ja: HyperDrone: 毎秒数百万フレームでのシミュレーションから現実への移行
llm.tldr_ja: 既存の最先端バッチクアッドロータシミュレータより20倍以上高速な、高性能バッチレンダリングに特化した超高速クアッドロータシミュレータ「HyperDrone」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のクアッドロータシミュレータは速度やレンダリングの忠実度が低く、実機へのスムーズなSim-to-Real移行が困難である。
llm.method: 最適化されたマルチロータダイナミクスと、最新のレイトレーシングハードウェアを活用する新しいレイトレーシングエンジン「HyperLux」を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 民生用GPUで数百万FPSを達成し、シミュレーションで学習した視覚ベースのヨー制御ポリシーを実機の小型クアッドロータに完全オンボードで移行できた。

2610.28948.title: COWBOY: A Scalable Sim-to-Real Framework for Learning Contextual Whole-Body Manipulation
2610.28948.abstract: Mobile manipulators must adapt not only to objects, but also to the spatial context in which they appear: where to position the base, how to manipulate, and where to look while navigating surrounding scene geometry. To address this, we present COWBOY, a scalable sim-to-real framework for learning such contextual whole-body manipulation. On whole-body dexterous grasping, COWBOY transfers zero-shot to hundreds of objects and diverse in-the-wild scenes, spanning cluttered tabletops, shelves, drawers, and other unstructured settings. Rather than learning scene adaptation directly with RL in simulation, a vectorized environment-aware whole-body controller (WBC) handles reaching in thousands of scenes by coordinating base-arm motion, collision avoidance, and active vision. Then, local RL experts are trained in local scenes for object interaction and can be reused across thousands of full-scene layouts. We distill these composed WBC-RL teachers into a single vision policy that controls the mobile base, arm, dexterous hand, and actuated camera from point-cloud observations. The resulting policy exhibits contextual whole-body behavior, automatically adapting base placement, camera viewpoint, arm trajectory, and grasp strategy to observed scene and object geometry. Videos are available at https://cowboy-manip.com
2610.28948.tldr_en: COWBOY, a scalable sim-to-real framework for learning contextual whole-body manipulation, automatically adapting base placement, camera viewpoint, arm trajectory, and grasp strategy to observed scene and object geometry.

llm.title_ja: COWBOY: コンテキストに基づく全身マニピュレーション学習のためのスケーラブルなSim-to-Realフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 物体の配置や周囲のシーン幾何学に合わせて、ベースの配置、カメラ視点、アーム軌道を自動適応させる、コンテキストに基づく全身マニピュレーション学習のスケーラブルなフレームワークCOWBOYを提案する。
llm.problem: モバイルマニピュレータは、オブジェクトだけでなく、周囲の空間コンテキスト（ベースの位置、操作方法、視線）にも適応する必要がある。
llm.method: 環境認識型全身コントローラ（WBC）とローカルシーンで訓練されたローカルRLエキスパートを組み合わせ、単一のビジョンポリシーに蒸留する。
llm.result: 数百のオブジェクトや多様な未調整のシーンに対してゼロショットで移行し、コンテキストに応じた全身動作を実現した。
keywords_ja: 全身マニピュレーション
モバイルマニピュレータ

2610.28940.title: StyleStream 2.0: Fast and Controllable Streaming Voice Style Conversion
2610.28940.abstract: Voice style conversion (VSC) aims to transform a source utterance to match the timbre, accent, and emotion of a target voice while preserving linguistic content. StyleStream 1.0 introduced the first streamable zero-shot VSC system with state-of-the-art conversion quality, but remained limited in two ways: approximately 1s end-to-end latency on consumer hardware, and the lack of a text-based interface for designing or editing target voices. We present StyleStream 2.0, a fast and controllable streaming VSC framework that addresses these limitations. To reduce latency, we train a few-step pixel MeanFlow model and further fine-tune it with autoregressive feedback inspired by Self Forcing, improving robustness under streaming inference. This reduces end-to-end latency to 520~ms on a consumer GPU, a 2x speedup over StyleStream 1.0, while maintaining conversion quality. To enable controllable style manipulation, we remove the mel-spectrogram context and instead route target style information through a compact style embedding. In this embedding space, we train a unified text-conditioned flow matching model that supports both text-based voice design, which maps natural language prompts to voice styles, and instruction-based voice editing, which modifies a specific attribute of a source utterance while preserving the rest. Experiments show that StyleStream 2.0 achieves the strongest target style fidelity on VSC, voice design, and voice editing, while remaining competitive on intelligibility and non-edited attribute preservation.
2610.28940.tldr_en: Experiments show that StyleStream 2.0 achieves the strongest target style fidelity on VSC, voice design, and voice editing, while remaining competitive on intelligibility and non-edited attribute preservation.
2610.28940.hf_summary_en: StyleStream 2.0 improves streaming voice conversion with lower latency via a few-step MeanFlow model and enables text-based voice design and editing through a unified flow matching model.

llm.title_ja: StyleStream 2.0: 高速かつ制御可能なストリーミング音声スタイル変換
llm.tldr_ja: エンドツーエンドのレイテンシを削減し、テキストベースのインターフェースによるターゲット音声のデザインや編集を可能にした、高速かつ制御可能なストリーミング音声スタイル変換フレームワークStyleStream 2.0を提案する。
llm.problem: StyleStream 1.0は約1秒のレイテンシがあり、ターゲット音声をデザイン・編集するためのテキストベースのインターフェースが欠けていた。
llm.method: 数ステップのpixel MeanFlowモデルを学習しSelf Forcingに着想を得た自己回帰フィードバックで微調整するとともに、テキスト条件付きフローマッチングモデルを導入する。
llm.result: 民生用GPUで520msのレイテンシを実現し、VSC・音声デザイン・音声編集において最も強力なターゲットスタイル忠実度を達成した。

2610.28925.title: One Policy, Many Styles: Where to Aggregate Preferences for Steerable Humanoid Control?
2610.28925.abstract: Modern robotic agents are increasingly expected to support steerable control, where a single policy can adjust its behavioral style at runtime under changing user preferences. Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning provides this interface, but conditioning alone does not ensure that a requested behavior change is strong, does not leak into unrelated behaviors, and does not compromise task performance. Our evaluation combines Preference Reward Responsiveness (PRR) with coverage and utility metrics. We use these measures to compare reward-level, advantage-level, loss-level, and PCGrad-based aggregation across two humanoid-control frameworks. No aggregation level performs best across all environments and criteria. Experiments show that aggregating objectives early produces a wider range of behavioral responses but greater unintended changes in other objectives, while aggregating them later improves control precision at some cost to responsiveness.
2610.28925.tldr_en: This evaluation combines Preference Reward Responsiveness (PRR) with coverage and utility metrics to compare reward-level, advantage-level, loss-level, and PCGrad-based aggregation across two humanoid-control frameworks.

llm.title_ja: 1つのポリシー、多様なスタイル: 操縦可能なヒューマノイド制御のための選好集約はどこで行うべきか？
llm.tldr_ja: 選好報酬応答性（PRR）とカバレッジ・ユーティリティ指標を組み合わせ、2つのヒューマノイド制御フレームワークにおける報酬、アドバンテージ、損失、PCGradベースの集約を評価した。
llm.problem: 選好条件付き強化学習において、単なる条件付けだけでは意図した動作変更が十分に強くならず、無関係な動作への漏洩やタスク性能の低下を引き起こすことがある。
llm.method: PRR、カバレッジ、ユーティリティ指標を用いて、報酬レベル、アドバンテージレベル、損失レベル、PCGradベースの集約手法を比較評価する。
llm.result: 目的を早期に集約すると幅広い行動反応が得られるが他への予期せぬ変化が増え、後発の集約は応答性を犠牲にしつつ制御精度を向上させることが示された。
keywords_ja: 選好条件付き強化学習

2610.28920.title: Navigation Explainability for Object Avoidance with LLMs for Assistive Robots
2610.28920.abstract: Blind and visually impaired individuals face uncertainty when navigating unfamiliar areas. Whether a cane or a guide dog is used for navigation, this may prove to be challenging. To mitigate this challenge, we present the Context-Aware Navigation Explanation framework that explains guide dog movements for obstacle avoidance and navigation using a large language model. This system integrates perceptual context with planned future trajectories to generate natural-language explanations of robot movement. We deploy the system on a Unitree Go2 platform in indoor navigation scenarios and evaluate how different explanation context configurations affect user trust and explanation satisfaction. Results show a strong positive relationship between explanation satisfaction and trust, and suggest that combining obstacle information with future trajectory leads to the most effective explanations. These findings highlight the potential of context-aware language explanations to improve transparency and trust in assistive robot navigation.
2610.28920.tldr_en: The ContextAware Navigation Explanation framework that explains guide dog movements for obstacle avoidance and navigation using a large language model is presented and it is suggested that combining obstacle information with future trajectory leads to the most effective explanations.
2610.28920.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Robot and Human Interactive Communication

badges.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Robot an

llm.title_ja: 支援ロボットのためのLLMを用いた障害物回避のためのナビゲーション説明可能性
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデルを使用して、障害物回避やナビゲーションのための盲導犬の動きを説明するコンテキストアウェア・ナビゲーション説明フレームワークを提案し、障害物情報と将来の軌跡の組み合わせが最も効果的な説明につながることを示した。
llm.problem: 視覚障害者が不慣れな場所を移動する際、移動の不確実性が高く、既存の手段では困難を伴うことがある。
llm.method: 知覚コンテキストと計画された将来の軌跡を統合し、大規模言語モデルを用いてロボットの動きに対する自然言語の説明を生成する。
llm.result: 説明への満足感と信頼感の間に強い正の相関が見られ、障害物情報と将来の軌跡を組み合わせることで最も効果的な説明が生成されることが示された。

2610.28901.title: Learning Dynamic Games for Cooperative Iterative Tasks
2610.28901.abstract: We consider cooperative and iterative tasks involving multiple agents whose interactions are modeled as a dynamic game with shared constraints. We propose a general learning framework applicable to nonlinear and nonconvex dynamic games that uses previously executed feasible trajectories to construct a sampled joint safe set and player-specific cost-to-go functions. At each time step, the agents jointly select a previously sampled terminal state and a Generalized Nash equilibrium used to reach it. A new solution is adopted only if it satisfies a cooperative acceptance rule agreed upon by the players. The framework accommodates individual non-degradation requirements and selection criteria such as weighted costs and Nash bargaining. We show that the proposed framework guarantees recursive feasibility and characterize conditions under which each player's cost is non-increasing across iterations.
2610.28901.tldr_en: A general learning framework applicable to nonlinear and nonconvex dynamic games that uses previously executed feasible trajectories to construct a sampled joint safe set and player-specific cost-to-go functions and guarantees recursive feasibility and characterize conditions under which each player's cost is non-increasing across iterations.

llm.title_ja: 協調的反復タスクのための動的ゲームの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 過去に実行された実現可能な軌跡を用いて、再帰的実行可能性を保証しつつ非線形・非凸の動的ゲームを解くための一般的な学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 共有制約を持つ複数のエージェント間の相互作用を伴う協調的かつ反復的なタスクにおいて、非線形・非凸な動的ゲームを効率的に解く必要がある。
llm.method: 過去の実行軌跡からサンプルされた結合安全集合とプレイヤー固有のコストゴーフ関数を構築し、協調的受容ルールに基づいて平衡点を選択する。
llm.result: 提案フレームワークが再帰的実行可能性を保証し、各プレイヤーのコストが反復ごとに非増加となる条件を明らかに示した。

2610.28893.title: Flexible Language-Guided Representation Editing for Adaptive Robot Behavior
2610.28893.abstract: Trajectory demonstrations show robots how to behave but not why, leaving them to guess which features of the task actually matter. Incorrect guesses produce misaligned internal representations and lead to incorrect robot behaviors. Because task features are often semantically defined, we argue that natural language is better suited for specifying features rather than relying on demonstrations. Although existing representation editing methods have proposed using language to specify new features, only allowing additive edits produces feature sets that are often over-specified or too narrowly scoped, especially in sequential editing tasks. We propose the Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline (FLEX), which uses language models to iteratively refine a robot's internal representation of task features from natural language corrections via three complementary operations: Add missing features, Generalize existing specific features, and Mask irrelevant features. We evaluate FLEX on 2D navigation scenarios, 7DoF Franka tabletop manipulation tasks, and a real-world study using naturalistic human language corrections and real-robot demonstrations. Comparisons against single-operation and unscaffolded baselines show that all three operations are necessary in interactive scenarios, and that FLEX achieves consistently higher normalized reward compared to other feature editing approaches while maintaining compact, transferable representations. Project available at https://mit-clear-lab.github.io/FLEX/
2610.28893.comment: Accepted to the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026), Austin, TX. 25 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables
2610.28893.tldr_en: The Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline (FLEX) is proposed, which uses language models to iteratively refine a robot's internal representation of task features from natural language corrections via three complementary operations: Add missing features, Generalize existing specific features, and Mask irrelevant features.

llm.title_ja: 適応的ロボット行動のための柔軟な言語誘導型表現編集
llm.tldr_ja: 言語モデルを用いて、自然言語の修正からタスク特徴のロボットの内部表現を反復的に洗練させる「Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline (FLEX)」を提案する。
llm.problem: デモンストレーションのみではタスクのどの特徴が重要か推測しにくく、誤った内部表現が不適切なロボットの行動を招く。
llm.method: 「欠落特徴の追加」「既存特定特徴の一般化」「無関係な特徴のマスク」という3つの補完的操作を言語モデルで行うFLEXを提案する。
llm.result: FLEXは他の特徴編集アプローチと比較して一貫して高い正規化報酬を達成し、コンパクトで転移可能な表現を維持できることが示された。

2610.28882.title: inr2action: Encoding Robot Episodes as Neural Implicit Representations for Recall and Action
2610.28882.abstract: Long-horizon robotic operation requires memory that scales with essential information rather than execution time. We present a parameter-space memory framework where each episode is stored as a separable object. A neural implicit representation is fitted to episode video from a shared, meta-learned initialization; the resulting weight delta constitutes the memory. Crucially, this delta remains a fixed size regardless of whether the episode spans a hundred or a hundred thousand frames. A learned projector maps the weight delta into token embeddings, conditioning a language model for question answering and a decoder for joint command regression, without frame retrieval at query time. On RoboMME, the language model exceeds chance across all question types, and the decoder achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.51. Replacing the delta with matched noise drops performance by 11.4 points, while random-origin weights are non-decodable, proving the meta-learned initialization is essential for embedding episode content. By representing individual experiences as fixed-size weight deltas in a common parameter space, this approach decouples memory cost from time horizon and provides a basis for scalable streaming memory.
2610.28882.tldr_en: A parameter-space memory framework where each episode is stored as a separable object, representing individual experiences as fixed-size weight deltas in a common parameter space and providing a basis for scalable streaming memory is presented.

llm.title_ja: inr2action: リコールと行動のためのニューラル暗黙的表現としてのロボットエピソードのエンコード
llm.tldr_ja: 各エピソードを分離されたオブジェクトとして保存し、メモリコストを時間水平線から切り離すパラメータ空間メモリフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 長期的なロボットの操作には、実行時間ではなく本質的な情報に応じてスケーリングするメモリが必要である。
llm.method: 共有されたメタ学習初期化からエピソードビデオにニューラル暗黙的表現（INR）をフィッティングし、得られた重みデルタをメモリとする。
llm.result: 言語モデルがすべての質問タイプで偶然を大きく上回り、デコーダは0.51の平均R^2を達成し、スケーリング可能なストリーミングメモリの基礎を提供した。
keywords_ja: ニューラル暗黙的表現

2610.28880.title: Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration
2610.28880.abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. We present Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category. R2Sem2R tracks the SE(3) pose of each object with DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats, outperforming existing methods and FoundationPose with estimated metric depth. R2Sem2R then aligns digital cousins, each generated from one or a few photographs, to the demonstrated objects with a semantic alignment. This alignment matches whole objects and the functional regions of target objects, such as a coffee machine's tray. R2Sem2R maps the human hand to a feasible robot grasp that extends to the cousins. Robot demonstrations are generated either in IsaacSim, for photorealistic rendering, or MuJoCo, for contact physics, and R2Sem2R can generate over 2,000 episodes in about two hours. On two real robots and four tasks, we train a vision-language-action policy on data from one human video per task, and policies trained on our data match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances. The project page is available at https://real2sem2real.github.io/.
2610.28880.comment: Matthew Strong and Ankush K. Dhawan contributed equally. Project page: https://real2sem2real.github.io/
2610.28880.tldr_en: Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category.

llm.title_ja: Real2Sem2Real: 単一の人間RGBデモンストレーションからのロボット学習のための3Dセマンティック拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の単眼RGBビデオから、カテゴリのセマンティックなオブジェクトインスタンスにわたる数千のロボットデモンストレーションを生成するパイプライン「Real2Sem2Real」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の人間ビデオを用いたロボット学習手法は、深度センサを必要とするか、2Dビデオ上にロボットを重ねるか、実演されたオブジェクトのみのデータ生成に限定される。
llm.method: DINOv3で蒸留されたGaussian splatsを用いて各オブジェクトのSE(3)ポーズを追跡し、デジタルカズンをセマンティックに整列させてロボットの把持を生成する。
llm.result: 2つの実ロボットと4つのタスクにおいて、1人当たりのビデオデータから訓練されたポリシーが、テレオペレーションで訓練されたポリシーと同等以上の性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 人間デモンストレーション
ビジョン言語アクション

2610.28814.title: T-WLA: Bridging Slow Vision and Fast Touch
2610.28814.abstract: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Recomputing the plan through the visual policy adds latency, while tactile feedback alone does not specify how the ongoing motion should be revised for the task. We introduce T-WLA, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction. At each visual update, the visual branch integrates the current image, task instruction, and retrieved history into a visual memory that conditions base-action generation. The same memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor, which combines it with the active action chunk and incoming touch to predict residual corrections to unexecuted actions without rerunning the visual branch. Future-image and future-pressure prediction provide training-only supervision, encouraging the visual memory and tactile features to capture interaction dynamics relevant to action generation and correction. We evaluate T-WLA on tactile-conditioned hand-motion prediction using EgoTouch and Tachin, and on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. T-WLA reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% relative to the strongest reported baseline and achieves an average success rate of approximately 50.0% across real-robot manipulation tasks. Videos and code are available at https://anonymous-submission-20.github.io/T-WLA.github.io/.
2610.28814.tldr_en: T-WLA is introduced, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction and reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% relative to the strongest reported baseline and achieves an average success rate of approximately 50.0% across real-robot manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: T-WLA: 遅い視覚と速い触覚の架け橋
llm.tldr_ja: 共有ビジュアルメモリを使用してアクション生成と触覚補正の両方をガイドし、実世界の器用なマニピュレーションタスクで高い成功率を達成する世界・言語・アクションアーキテクチャ「T-WLA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 接触が豊富なマニピュレーションでは視覚ポリシーの更新前に接触条件が変化し、視覚ポリシーの再計算は遅延を生じ、触覚フィードバック単体では動作の修正方法が定まらない。
llm.method: 視覚ブランチで統合されたビジュアルメモリを構築し、軽量な触覚エディタがアクションチャンクと入ってくる触覚を組み合わせて未実行アクションの残差補正を予測する。
llm.result: 指関節のMPJPEを最も強力なベースラインから30%削減し、実ロボットマニピュレーションタスクで平均約50.0%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.28810.title: Combining Long-Term Memory and LLMs Comes at a High Cost: From Prompt Injection to Persistent Compromise
2610.28810.abstract: The widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence in recent years has brought a parallel rise in prompt injection and jailbreak attacks. By embedding malicious instructions, these exploits manipulate language models to bypass intended behavior and operational boundaries. In traditional chatbots, such attacks are confined to a single session because state memory is not preserved across conversations. However, persistent memory features in modern conversational interfaces enable cross-session attack propagation, establishing a threat vector known as memory injection. This work explores this emerging vulnerability in leading LLM-as-a-service platforms, highlighting its real-world severity and the need for countermeasures. While existing literature focuses on violations tailored to specific platform features, we present a general threat model. We demonstrate that all NIST attack goals are collectively achievable across ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash under this model. We also show that memory injections can exploit multiple attack vectors, including personal memories, projects, skills, organization instructions, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-connected resources. Our findings reveal that all evaluated services can be manipulated to persistently spread disinformation, generate harmful content, or simulate offline unresponsiveness, even in fresh sessions. In the particular case of Claude, shared-memory features allow an attacker to compromise multiple users within an organization and also exfiltrate user prompts. To address these vulnerabilities, we derive defense mechanisms from our proposed threat model and foundational cybersecurity principles. Our analysis indicates that nearly half of these mitigations remain unimplemented across the target services. Datasets and attack artifacts are available at https://github.com/PedroBarcha/Memory-injection.
2610.28810.tldr_en: This work explores this emerging vulnerability in leading LLM-as-a-service platforms, highlighting its real-world severity and the need for countermeasures, and presents a general threat model that demonstrates that all NIST attack goals are collectively achievable across ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash under this model.

llm.title_ja: 長期記憶とLLMの組み合わせには高い代償が伴う: プロンプトインジェクションから永続的な侵害まで
llm.tldr_ja: 主要なLLMプラットフォームにおける持続的メモリ機能が引き起こすクロスセッション攻撃（メモリインジェクション）の脆弱性を探求し、一般的な脅威モデルを提示する。
llm.problem: 近年の会話型インターフェースにおける持続的メモリ機能は、会話をまたいだ攻撃の伝播（メモリインジェクション）という新たな脅威ベクトルを生み出している。
llm.method: 一般的な脅威モデルを定義し、ChatGPT Instant 5.3、Claude Sonnet 4.6、Gemini 3 Flashを対象にNISTの攻撃目標が達成可能かを検証する。
llm.result: 評価されたすべてのサービスが悪意ある操作に対して脆弱であり、組織内での複数ユーザの侵害や機密情報の流出が可能であることが示された。
keywords_ja: プロンプトインジェクション

2610.28791.title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
2610.28791.abstract: Target-based extrinsic calibration estimates the rigid transform between sensors from a few observations of a known target, and its result is commonly assessed by the root-mean-square error of the fitted residuals. However, this scalar error is computed on the same observations and therefore cannot indicate whether to accept the result, re-extract, recollect or add observations. This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state. The key insight is a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism, in which the extrinsic compensates the rigid part of each observation error at the residual level, and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level. Consequently, the fitted residual can reveal neither an inconsistency between the observations and the model nor whether the estimated extrinsic is reliable in every direction. Accordingly, we assess the calibration through a structured covariance that jointly propagates the uncertainty of the camera and LiDAR board features with a known-geometry prior, and estimate its scale as a variance component from the residuals. On this covariance, we decouple rotation and translation to resolve the precision along each direction and guide data collection toward the weakest one. Since this precision presumes consistent observations, we further develop within-view and cross-view checks that examine the internal residual and the rigid discrepancy between observations, respectively, with thresholds that hold their significance level under an unknown noise level. We also extend the minimal detectable bias to the extrinsic to bound the smallest detectable fault along each direction. These criteria form a calibration state that indicates whether to accept the result or how to collect the data...
2610.28791.tldr_en: This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state through a structured covariance that jointly propagates the uncertainty of the camera and LiDAR board features with a known-geometry prior.

llm.title_ja: VeriCalib: 検証可能なターゲットベースのLiDAR・カメラキャリブレーション
llm.tldr_ja: カメラとLiDARボード特徴量の不確実性を既知の幾何学事前分布とともに共同伝播させる構造化共分散を用いて、外部パラメータの較正を検証可能な推定問題として定式化するVeriCalibを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のターゲットベースの外部較正は、適合された残差の二乗平均平方根誤差に依存しているが、これは同じ観測値から計算されるため結果の採否やデータ追加の判断ができない。
llm.method: 残差レベルでの剛体誤差補償とパラメータレベルでの回転・並進の相互補償を行う2レベル外部補償メカニズムと構造化共分散を用いた較正状態の報告を導入する。
llm.result: 各方向の精度を解決してデータ収集を最も弱い方向に誘導できる較正状態を形成し、一貫性をチェックする仕組みを実現した。
keywords_ja: LiDAR・カメラキャリブレーション

2610.28788.title: ArcFlow: Training Flow Policies for Multiple Solver Budgets
2610.28788.abstract: Flow-matching policies adjust inference cost through the number of solver steps, but reinforcement learning at a single fixed solver budget can hide degradation at cheaper deployment budgets and even erase useful one-step behavior present in a pretrained policy. We introduce Action-Ratio-Clip Flow (ArcFlow), a deployment-aware algorithm for training one flow policy across a specified range of solver budgets. ArcFlow combines action-aligned supervision, budget exposure, and worst-budget checkpoint selection. For reconstruction objectives, its bridge aggregates temporal probes into one surrogate ratio and one PPO-style clip per action, with a boundary residual exactly equal to deployed one-step reconstruction error. Cycling exposes the shared field to the deployment range, and selection optimizes its performance floor. For native velocity objectives, multi-budget endpoint supervision applies the same principle without replacing the native update. Both realizations preserve the architecture and deployment-time cost. Across DM Control, manipulation, and locomotion, ArcFlow attains the highest mean one-step return among five flow-policy baselines on 25 of 30 tasks under each method's reported training settings. Component studies identify complementary improvements from boundary supervision, the fixed-grid bridge, budget exposure, and deployment selection. These results establish deployment-budget-aware training as an effective route to strong low-step control with one policy serving multiple inference costs.
2610.28788.tldr_en: These results establish deployment-budget-aware training as an effective route to strong low-step control with one policy serving multiple inference costs.

llm.title_ja: ArcFlow: 複数のソルバーバジェットに向けたフローポリシーの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 複数の推論コストに対応する1つのフローポリシーを訓練するための展開バジェット考慮型アルゴリズム「ArcFlow」を提案する。
llm.problem: フローマッチングポリシーはソルバーのステップ数で推論コストを調整できるが、単一の固定予算での強化学習は安価な予算での性能劣化を隠してしまう。
llm.method: アクション整合監視、予算露出、ワースト予算チェックポイント選択を組み合わせたデプロイメント対応アルゴリズム「ArcFlow」を適用する。
llm.result: DM Control、マニピュレーション、移動タスクの大部分で、複数のフローポリシーベースラインの中で最高の平均1ステップ報酬を達成した。

2610.28769.title: Learning-Enhanced Observer for Sensorless Task-Null-Space Compliant Control
2610.28769.abstract: This paper presents a novel framework integrating a robust wrench observer with a hybrid pose and force controller for physical Human-Robot Interaction (pHRI). In pHRI tasks, robots are expected to perform task-space motions robustly while remaining compliance with human disturbance, which proposes distinct control objectives. Most existing approaches focus mainly on either robustness or compliance and rely on force sensors for real-time tracking. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework with the following key contributions. Firstly, a neural network (NN) is trained to improve the observer performance by compensating for system friction and unmodeled dynamics. Secondly, a task-null-space decomposition is applied to separate the joint velocity and reduce the effect of the human disturbance on the observer. Finally, a hybrid pose and force controller is introduced to achieve the end-effector pose and force tracking. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides robust and accurate wrench estimation while maintaining reliable pose and force tracking performance. The proposed approach offers an effective solution and framework for pHRI without the need of force/torque sensor measurements which can be applied to many robotic manipulator platforms which do not have force/torque sensors.
2610.28769.tldr_en: The proposed approach offers an effective solution and framework for pHRI without the need of force/torque sensor measurements which can be applied to many robotic manipulator platforms which do not have force/torque sensors.

llm.title_ja: センサレスなタスクヌル空間コンプライアント制御のための学習強化型オブザーバ
llm.tldr_ja: システム摩擦や未モデル化ダイナミクスを補償するニューラルネットワークとハイブリッド姿勢・力コントローラを統合し、力/トルクセンサなしで頑健な物理的ヒューマンロボットインタラクション（pHRI）を実現するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のpHRIアプローチの多くはロバスト性かコンプライアンスのどちらかに偏り、リアルタイム追従に力センサを必要とする。
llm.method: ニューラルネットワークによるオブザーバの性能向上、関節速度を分離するタスクヌル空間分解、およびエンドエフェクタの姿勢・力追従のためのハイブリッドコントローラを統合する。
llm.result: 力/トルクセンサの測定値なしで、頑健かつ正確なレンチ推定と信頼性の高い姿勢・力追従性能を実現できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: コンプライアント制御

2610.28761.title: Human-Robot Interaction via Meta-Learning Based Mode Recognition and Adaptive Control
2610.28761.abstract: In human-robot interaction (HRI) tasks, humans may interact with the robot in either an active guiding or passive following state, resulting in distinct control objectives for each interaction mode. Most existing approaches rely on predefined switching thresholds to distinguish interaction modes, but their performance can be sensitive to measurement noise. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework with the following key contributions. First, a neural network (NN) trained via meta-learning is developed to recognize human intention without manually defined thresholds. By successfully incorporating force-dependent parameters from the controller, the recognition rates are improved from 90.1\% to 99.1\% for the passive mode and from 79.8\% to 97.1\% for the active mode. Second, an adaptive meta-learning controller is introduced to compensate for human disturbances and enable online adaptation to varying interaction forces. Third, a multiple-trajectory meta-learning algorithm is designed to jointly learn an environment-basis representation and force-dependent parameters, allowing the controller to deal with unmodeled dynamics efficiently. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves robust and accurate control performance, while providing reliable mode recognition for safe and adaptive physical HRI.
2610.28761.tldr_en: A neural network trained via meta-learning is developed to recognize human intention without manually defined thresholds, and an adaptive meta-learning controller is introduced to compensate for human disturbances and enable online adaptation to varying interaction forces.

llm.title_ja: メタ学習に基づくモード認識と適応制御によるヒューマンロボットインタラクション
llm.tldr_ja: 手動で定義された閾値なしで人間の意図を認識するメタ学習ベースのニューラルネットワークと、人間の外乱を補償する適応型メタ学習コントローラを提案する。
llm.problem: HRIタスクにおいて、人間の能動的誘導または受動的追従のモードを識別するために既存手法が用いる事前定義された切り替え閾値は、測定ノイズに敏感である。
llm.method: 力依存パラメータを組み込んだメタ学習によるニューラルネットワークによるモード認識と、複数の軌跡を用いた環境基底表現の適応制御アルゴリズムを開発する。
llm.result: 受動モードの認識率を99.1%に、能動モードを97.1%に向上させ、安全で適応的なpHRIのための頑健な制御性能を実現した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.28632.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
2610.28632.abstract: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.
2610.28632.tldr_en: A model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion is presented.
2610.28632.hf_summary_en: The model co-generates video and 3D motion for arbitrary skeletons via cross-attention with a pretrained video generator, enabling scene-registered animation and bidirectional video-motion conversion.

llm.title_ja: 関節、カメラ、アクション! 任意のRigに向けた3Dモーションとビデオの同時生成
llm.tldr_ja: 任意のスケルトン（Rig）に対応する3Dモーションとビデオを、シーンに登録するカメラとともに直接同時生成し、3Dモーションのキーフレーム制御を可能にするモデルを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のビデオ・モーションモデルは人間の骨格のみを対象にするか、2Dポーズマップから3Dモーションを三角測量するため、特定の3Dアセットやシーンへの適用が困難である。
llm.method: 3Dモーションを任意のスケルトンをサポートする別個のモデルに保持し、少数のクロスアテンション層を介して事前学習済みビデオモデルに接続する。
llm.result: テキストから多様なRigを忠実にアニメーション化でき、ビデオからRigのモーションへの変換やキーフレームベースの制御が可能であることを示した。
keywords_ja: スケルトンアニメーション

2610.28628.title: Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills via Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking
2610.28628.abstract: Dexterous multi-finger hands hold promise to unlock diverse skills like functional grasps, in-hand reorientation, and dynamic handover that the human-designed world assumes, yet existing learning recipes force a trade-off. Goal-reaching reinforcement learning generalizes to arbitrary object poses but, lacking any human prior, converges to unnatural and unreliable finger strategies; motion tracking reproduces human-like behavior from a single clip but cannot deviate from it. We present AdaDex, a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill. At the core of AdaDex is Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking: a shared policy is trained on two populations of massively parallel environments: motion tracking environments trained with dense motion tracking objective, which instill the human prior from human motion; and generalization environments with noised initial states and goals and a sparse object-success reward, which force the skill to work far off the reference. From seconds of human motion per skill, the resulting policies can learn diverse adaptable dexterous skills, such as functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and dynamic behaviors like throw-and-catch. Our method outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality, and we demonstrate transfer across simulators and to the real world. Project page: https://yuxuank.com/AdaDex/.
2610.28628.tldr_en: AdaDex is a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill, and outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality.

llm.title_ja: ハイブリッド器用模倣を通じた適応可能な器用スキルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 数秒間の単一の手とオブジェクトの軌跡を、多様な環境や未調整のシーンにゼロショットで適応可能な器用なスキルへと変換するゴール条件付き強化学習フレームワーク「AdaDex」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のゴール指向型RLは人間の事前知識がなく不自然な戦略に収束し、モーション追跡は人間の行動を再現できるがそこから逸脱できない。
llm.method: 高密度モーション追跡環境（人間の事前知識を注入）と一般化環境（初期状態やゴールにノイズを加え疎な成功報酬を与える）の2つの並列環境集団で共有ポリシーを訓練する。
llm.result: 機能的な把持やインハンド再配向などの多様な器用スキルを獲得でき、シミュレータ間や実世界への転移においてベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2610.28626.title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
2610.28626.abstract: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).
2610.28626.tldr_en: UniWALM is introduced, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target and can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior.

llm.title_ja: UniWALM: ロボット制御のための統合型世界・アクション・言語モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ、アクション、言語を単一の共有表現で学習し、各モダリティが条件付け信号と監視ターゲットの両方として機能する統合型世界・アクション・言語モデル「UniWALM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のアプローチは、推論やビジョン言語モデルをビデオ・アクションのバックボーンに個別段階として接続しており、メモリ依存の動作やタスク計画の統合が不十分である。
llm.method: すべてのモダリティを単一の混合トランスフォーマーバックボーン内に統合し、アクションと同等のパスでサブタスクとテキストメモリをデコードするとともに、摂乱からの回復を教えるFMC（Flow Matching with Correction）を導入する。
llm.result: MolmoSpacesやRMBenchのメモリ依存サブセットでベースラインを上回り、実世界のアイテム探索タスクにおいてテキストメモリの生成により成功率を大幅に向上させた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2610.28624.title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
2610.28624.abstract: Warehouse robot fleets continuously observe operational conditions, but preserving these observations as reusable semantic memory incurs substantial computation, communication, and storage costs. For example, explaining recurring aisle blockages can require reviewing video from multiple robots across several shifts. We present IndustrialRemembr, a shared spatiotemporal memory system that extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR to robot fleets and reduces server-side computation by generating scene descriptions only on demand. On each robot, an NVIDIA Jetson encodes video clips into retrieval embeddings with Cosmos-Embed1, vision tokens with Cosmos3-Edge, and reconstruction latents with the Wan2.2 VAE, without uploading raw camera frames. The encoding models are re-used to detect people in image patches, zeroing them out to support PII abstraction for GDPR-compliant deployments. We split Cosmos3-Edge at its vision-language boundary, placing the vision encoder on the robot and the language decoder on an on-premises server. A Nemotron agent retrieves memories by content, position, and time and queries the decoder using cached vision tokens. This design eliminates caption generation at write time, while cached-token decoding reproduces the unsplit model's output in all 450 tested decodes.
2610.28624.tldr_en: IndustrialRemembr, a shared spatiotemporal memory system that extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR to robot fleets and reduces server-side computation by generating scene descriptions only on demand, is presented.

llm.title_ja: Industrial ReMEmbR: ロボット艦隊への時空メモリのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット艦隊における共有時空メモリシステムとしてNVIDIA ReMEmbRを拡張し、オンデマンドでのみシーン記述を生成することでサーバ側の計算量を削減する「IndustrialRemembr」を提案する。
llm.problem: 倉庫のロボット艦隊が継続的に観測する運用条件を再利用可能なセマンティックメモリとして保持するには、膨大な計算、通信、ストレージコストがかかる。
llm.method: 各ロボット上でNVIDIA Jetsonを用いてビデオクリップをエンコードし、ビジョンエンコーダと言語デコーダを分割し、オンデマンドでシーン記述を生成する。
llm.result: 書き込み時のキャプション生成を排除しつつ、キャッシュトークンデコードにより未分割モデルの出力をすべてのテストされたデコードで再現可能にした。
keywords_ja: セマンティックメモリ

2610.28623.title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
2610.28623.abstract: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. At the highest tested noise level in 4D, PUN achieves 10.7-60.6% relative gains in success rate over other methods while running 3.29-32.15 times faster.
2610.28623.tldr_en: This work introduces Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example.

llm.title_ja: ニューラルオペレータを用いたノイズ下での計画
llm.tldr_ja: ノイズのあるモンテカルロラベルから幾何学から場への写像を学習することで、未知の形状での計画に向けたノイズ適応型価値場を学習するニューラルオペレータ「PUN」を提案する。
llm.problem: 制御実行ノイズが存在する環境において、未知の形状に対する信頼性の高いフィードバック方策を得ること。
llm.method: 境界条件にノイマン条件を課し、拡張モンテカルロソルバー（Walk on Stars）を用いてPDEを解くニューラルオペレータ「PUN」の学習を行う。
llm.result: 4次元再計画ベンチマークで95〜100%の成功率を達成し、他の手法と比較して最小の実行時間を維持しつつ最高60.6%の相対的利得を実現した。
keywords_ja: ニューラルオペレータ

2610.28613.title: Physical Canvas: A Vision Tactile World Model For Robot Policy Evaluation And Learning
2610.28613.abstract: Evaluating and post-training robot policies through physical interaction is costly and difficult to scale, motivating action-conditioned world models as interactive simulators. However, visually plausible predictions can misrepresent contact dynamics, providing unreliable feedback for policy evaluation and learning. We introduce PhysCanvas, a state-consistent visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich robot manipulation. PhysCanvas unifies multi-view RGB, tactile images, marker displacement, task state, and actions within a unified vision space. All modalities share a video VAE and pretrained generative backbone, allowing optical touch to reuse visual and temporal priors. Motion images derived through forward kinematics and camera projection provide spatially aligned action conditioning, while an initial RGB anchor and updated reference observations guide sequential generation. Our consistency-aware post-training uses the frozen Scene Reward Model, Modality Reward Model, and State Reward Model to supervise scene preservation, visual-tactile compatibility, and agreement with real task outcomes. The resulting world model supports closed-loop policy rollouts for evaluation and provides imagined interactions and rewards for GRPO policy updates. Across four real-world manipulation tasks, when policies are rolled out in the world model, State Reward Model supervision increases the arithmetic mean of task-wise Pearson correlations between world-model and real-world success rates from 0.602 to 0.885. Policy post-training in the reward-guided world model further increases $π_{0.5}$'s mean real-world success rate from a 59.1% SFT baseline to 70.8%. These results demonstrate the value of unified multimodal modeling and consistency-aware post-training for robot policy evaluation and learning. Project page: https://zebinx.github.io/PhysCanvas_HomePage/.
2610.28613.tldr_en: PhysCanvas is introduced, a state-consistent visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich robot manipulation that supports closed-loop policy rollouts for evaluation and provides imagined interactions and rewards for GRPO policy updates.

llm.title_ja: Physical Canvas: ロボット方針の評価と学習のための視覚触覚世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 接触の多いロボットマニピュレーション向けの状態整合的な視覚触覚世界モデル「PhysCanvas」を導入し、評価のための閉ループ方策ロールアウトやGRPO方策更新のための想像上の相互作用と報酬を提供する。
llm.problem: 物理的な相互作用を通じたロボット方策の評価や事後学習は費用がかかり、拡張が困難であること。
llm.method: マルチビューRGB、触覚画像、マーカー変位、タスク状態、行動を統一されたビジョン空間内で統合し、一貫性を意識した事後学習を行う。
llm.result: 世界モデルと実世界の成功率の相関が向上し、報酬誘導型世界モデルでの方策の事後学習により実世界の平均成功率が59.1%から70.8%に向上した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.28594.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
2610.28594.abstract: Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene. To this end, we introduce Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. We extend a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing that integrates complementary observations across cameras, and add a trajectory head that predicts how physical points move through time. Each trajectory tracks a single point across all views, and supervising these trajectories alongside video generation therefore anchors appearance changes in every camera to a shared description of 3D motion. To support training and evaluation, we build VPM-Data, a simulation corpus pairing synchronized multi-view videos with persistent point trajectories, and VP-WorldBench, a forecasting benchmark spanning simulated and real environments. We further extend VPM to robot control by adding robot actions as a token modality in the generator. Action tokens share the point-supervised backbone and are denoised jointly with future videos, thereby grounding the policy in the same 3D-aware representation. On VP-WorldBench and existing 4D generation benchmarks, point supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D motion accuracy over a video-only counterpart, and in simulated and real-robot experiments, it also raises the manipulation success of the action-enabled model.
2610.28594.tldr_en: Video-Point Model (VPM) is introduced, a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points that extends a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing.
2610.28594.hf_summary_en: Video-Point Model predicts future multi-view videos and 3D point trajectories from video histories and instructions, improving forecasting and robot control through shared 3D-aware representations.

llm.title_ja: 点軌跡予測を通じた4次元世界の学習
llm.tldr_ja: マルチビュー映像履歴と言語指示を条件として、視点からの将来映像と永続的シーンポイントの3D軌跡を共同予測する世界モデル「Video-Point Model (VPM)」を提案する。
llm.problem: 信頼性の異なるカメラからのビデオが同じ進化する3Dシーンを記述するようにマルチビュー予測を行うこと。
llm.method: 事前学習済みの世界モデルにカメラ条件付きマルチビュー処理と、物理的ポイントの時間を経た動きを予測する軌跡ヘッドを追加する。
llm.result: ポイント指導により、ビデオ専用の従来手法と比較してビデオの忠実度と3Dモーションの精度が向上し、シミュレーションおよび実機ロボット実験でのマニピュレーション成功率が向上した。

2610.28712.title: Warping the Workspace: Expanding Visual Access with Adjustable Reach Mapping for Humanoid Teleoperation
2610.28712.abstract: First-person humanoid teleoperation ties access to side and rear targets to operator rotation. We present coupled visual--motor remapping, pairing a panoramic azimuth warp with its inverse upper-limb yaw transform. A working prototype implements Global Zoom (GZ) and Focus+Context (F+C). In a within-subject study (N=8); 72 trials), GZ had the largest completion count (23/24; Fixed: 20/24; F+C: 21/24), whereas F+C was preferred by 6/8 participants. Therefore, completion and preference favored different mappings in this sample.
2610.28712.tldr_en: C coupled visual--motor remapping is presented, pairing a panoramic azimuth warp with its inverse upper-limb yaw transform, pairing a panoramic azimuth warp with its inverse upper-limb yaw transform.

llm.title_ja: ワークスペースのワープ：ヒューマノイド遠隔操作のための調整可能なリーチマッピングによる視覚アクセスの拡張
llm.tldr_ja: パノラマのアジマوثワープとそれの逆である上肢のヨー変換を組み合わせた、結合型視覚運動リマッピングを提案する。
llm.problem: 一次元のヒューマノイド遠隔操作において、側面や背面のターゲットへのアクセスがオペレータの回転に縛られること。
llm.method: パノラマアジマワープと逆の上肢ヨー変換をペアにした結合型視覚運動リマッピングを実装する。
llm.result: GZは最大の完了回数を記録し、F+Cは参加者の過半数に好まれるなど、サンプルにおいて完了数と選好が異なるマッピングに分かれた。
keywords_ja: 視覚運動リマッピング

2610.28589.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
2610.28589.abstract: Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks. Recent work improves these systems through better harnesses and external memory, but relies on powerful closed-source models as planners and does not improve the planners' own capabilities. In contrast, coding agents have improved substantially by post-training the model itself. We therefore investigate whether post-training can also improve robot planners. However, applying it across robot harnesses requires accommodating different execution mechanisms, including VLA skill invocation and control-code generation. To this end, we introduce AgenticRoboRL, a framework for post-training robot planners across different harnesses. The training recipe combines supervised fine-tuning with multi-turn reinforcement learning. To accommodate different execution mechanisms, harness-specific adapters connect recorded planner interactions with task outcomes, enabling a common RL training pipeline while keeping execution components fixed. On LIBERO-PRO, AgenticRoboRL raises the success rate of a 9B-parameter planner from 18.1% to 71.0% without external memory, approaching the 72.1% achieved by Codex (GPT-5.5) with external memory. These results demonstrate post-training as an effective approach for improving robot planners. We will release the framework and trained planner checkpoints.
2610.28589.tldr_en: Post-training as an effective approach for improving robot planners is demonstrated by introducing AgenticRoboRL, a framework for post-training robot planners across different harnesses, which combines supervised fine-tuning with multi-turn reinforcement learning.
2610.28589.hf_summary_en: AgenticRoboRL improves robot planners via supervised fine-tuning and multi-turn reinforcement learning across diverse harnesses, significantly boosting success rates without external memory.

llm.title_ja: AgenticRoboRL: コーディングエージェントの事後学習をエージェント型ロボティクスへ応用する
llm.tldr_ja: さまざまなハーネス間でロボットプランナーの事後学習を行うフレームワーク「AgenticRoboRL」を提案し、教師あり微調整と多ラウンド強化学習を組み合わせる。
llm.problem: 既存のエージェント型ロボットシステムは強力な閉ソースモデルをプランナーとして依存しており、プランナー自体の能力が向上しないこと。
llm.method: ハーネス固有のアダプターを使用して記録されたプランナーの相互作用とタスク結果を接続し、共通の強化学習パイプラインを有効にする。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROにおいて、外部メモリなしで9Bパラメータのプランナーの成功率を18.1%から71.0%に向上させた。

2610.28585.title: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
2610.28585.abstract: Simulation is a powerful tool for robotics, but building diverse, simulation-ready scenes at scale remains difficult. Reconstructing scenes from single images is a promising alternative, but visual similarity alone is insufficient: objects must also be recovered, accurately placed, and physically grounded. Existing methods that rely on post-hoc physics settling often misplace objects, producing scenes that look correct but behave poorly under manipulation. We present SceneRig, an agentic system that turns a single image into an editable, simulation-ready scene. SceneRig combines geometric, visual, and physical tools to reconstruct a faithful 3D scene. An agent then performs edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to achieve physical stability. Across diverse inputs, SceneRig improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement while keeping the reconstructed scenes physically stable. Furthermore, SceneRig is effective for downstream robotics: its scenes predict real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than the baseline method and more reliably support replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.
2610.28585.comment: Accepted at CoRL 2026 Agentic Robotics Workshop. Project page: https://red-fairy.github.io/SceneRig/
2610.28585.tldr_en: SceneRig is an agentic system that turns a single image into an editable, simulation-ready scene, and its scenes predict real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than the baseline method and more reliably support replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.

llm.title_ja: SceneRig: 単一画像からのシミュレーション対応3Dシーン再構築のためのエージェントシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 単一画像から編集可能でシミュレーション対応の3Dシーンを構築するエージェントシステム「SceneRig」を提案し、物理シミュレータ内で編集と検証のループを実行して物理的安定性を実現する。
llm.problem: 多様でシミュレーションに対応したシーンを大規模に構築することが難しく、単一画像からの再構築ではオブジェクトが不適切に配置され物理的に不安定になること。
llm.method: 幾何学的、視覚的、物理的ツールを組み合わせ、物理シミュレータ内でエージェントが編集と検証のループを行って物理的安定性を達成する。
llm.result: インスタンスセグメンテーションや3D配置が改善され、再構築されたシーンは物理的に安定し、実ロボットの方策結果をより正確に予測できるようになった。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション
エージェントシステム

2610.28580.title: Continuous-Time Policy Gradient from Discrete Data: Convergence Analysis and Model-Free Algorithms
2610.28580.abstract: Continuous-time reinforcement learning seeks an optimal policy under unknown dynamics driven by stochastic differential equations using observations collected at discrete times. We develop a policy gradient framework that combines rigorous convergence analysis with learning from discrete data. We first establish a performance difference lemma and derive policy gradient formulas for randomized and parametrized policies. We then prove exponential convergence of an entropy-regularized policy flow to the regularized optimum. For discrete parametrized updates, we derive a convergence bound that explicitly separates the contributions of critic error, policy-regression error, and the learning step size. To enable learning under unknown dynamics, we integrate this framework with PhiBE, which constructs a continuous-time surrogate generator from discrete transition data. The resulting on-policy and off-policy model-free actor-critic algorithms preserve the continuous-time structure of the control problem. Numerical experiments on an entropy-regularized linear-quadratic regulator and a nonlinear wheeled robot demonstrate the performance and stability of the proposed methods with both known and data-driven dynamics.
2610.28580.tldr_en: This work develops a policy gradient framework that combines rigorous convergence analysis with learning from discrete data and integrates this framework with PhiBE, which constructs a continuous-time surrogate generator from discrete transition data.

llm.title_ja: 離散データからの連続時間方策勾配：収束解析とモデルフリーアルゴリズム
llm.tldr_ja: 厳密な収束解析と離散データからの学習を組み合わせた方策勾配フレームワークを開発し、未知のダイナミクス下での連続時間強化学習を行う。
llm.problem: 確率微分方程式に従う未知のダイナミクス下で、離散的な時刻で収集された観測を用いて最適な方策を求めること。
llm.method: 性能差補題を確立し、ランダム化およびパラメータ化された方策の方策勾配公式を導出し、連続時間サロゲートジェネレータを構築するPhiBEと統合する。
llm.result: エントロピー正則化線形二次レギュレータおよび非線形車輪型ロボットを用いた数値実験により、提案手法の性能と安定性が実証された。

2610.28566.title: MAPLE: Mondrian-Anchored Prior for Learning-free Indoor Exploration
2610.28566.abstract: Robots exploring unknown indoor environments must decide where to move while much of the environment remains unseen. Predicting the occupancy of unseen space beyond the current sensor range can improve these decisions, but recent approaches commonly rely on learned models that require offline training and repeated inference during exploration. We introduce the Mondrian-Anchored Prior for Learning-free Indoor Exploration (MAPLE), a training-free predictive approach that adapts the Mondrian process into an online generative prior conditioned on observed geometric cues in the current partial map. MAPLE generates multiple plausible map hypotheses and evaluates visibility separately within each to estimate frontier gain, preserving differences in predicted visibility across hypotheses. Across KTH floor-plans and real-SLAM environments at multiple sensor ranges, MAPLE consistently improves over non-predictive exploration and remains competitive with learned predictive approaches. Its lightweight procedural construction enables predictive exploration with limited computational resources. Experimental results further show that more accurate map prediction does not necessarily produce better exploration, highlighting the importance of how predictions are represented and used in exploration decisions.
2610.28566.tldr_en: The Mondrian-Anchored Prior for Learning-free Indoor Exploration (MAPLE), a training-free predictive approach that adapts the Mondrian process into an online generative prior conditioned on observed geometric cues in the current partial map, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: MAPLE: 学習不要な室内探索のためのモンドリアン型アンカー事前分布
llm.tldr_ja: モンドリアン過程を現在の部分地図の幾何学的手がかりに条件付けられたオンライン生成事前分布に適応させた、学習不要の予測型アプローチ「MAPLE」を導入する。
llm.problem: 未知の室内環境を探索するロボットにおいて、センサー範囲外の占有状態予測にオフライン訓練や推論が必要な学習モデルが使われていること。
llm.method: モンドリアン過程を拡張し、観測された幾何学的手がかりに基づいて複数の妥当な地図仮説をオンラインで生成・評価してフロンティアゲインを推定する。
llm.result: KTHフロアプランおよび実SLAM環境の複数のセンサー範囲において、非予測型探索を一貫して改善し、学習済み予測アプローチと同等の性能を維持した。

2610.28555.title: Learning Computational Structure for Sample-Efficient Prediction
2610.28555.abstract: Statistical learning in high dimensions suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Fortunately, many functions of practical interest are compositionally sparse, meaning they admit a composition of local functions, each depending on only a few variables, allowing sample complexity to depend on local arity rather than ambient dimension. Yet realizing this benefit requires exploiting hidden compositional structure, which theory does not establish for practical gradient-based training. We study this gap with CSFRBench, a controlled benchmark that hides the target's compositional computation during training but retains it for diagnosis, and find that dense networks and sparsity-based baselines leave much of that benefit unrealized. Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, we introduce Learned Wiring (LeWi): each neuron has a learned low-dimensional embedding, only nearby neurons connect, and embeddings and weights are trained jointly. LeWi improves sample efficiency on targets with hierarchical structure, intermediate reuse, or independent modules. Across 32 additional targets generated by independently sampled computation graphs, LeWi is the most sample-efficient method not given the target graph, with 27% lower mean learning-curve area than dense networks. Dense networks perform better on targets with a single high-arity function. LeWi's representations and connectivity align with the target computation. On 17 world-model prediction tasks spanning control, navigation, and manipulation, LeWi beats the dense baseline on 16 and wins 99/119 baseline comparisons. These results show that jointly learning connectivity and weights can exploit computational structure to improve sample efficiency.
2610.28555.tldr_en: Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, LeWi is introduced: each neuron has a learned low-dimensional embedding, only nearby neurons connect, and embeddings and weights are trained jointly, showing that jointly learning connectivity and weights can exploit computational structure to improve sample efficiency.

llm.title_ja: サンプル効率の高い予測のための計算構造の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 生物学的神経回路の空間組織に着想を得て、ニューロンが学習された低次元埋め込みを持ち近接するニューロンのみが結合する「LeWi」を提案し、サンプル効率を向上させる。
llm.problem: 高次元の統計学習における次元の呪いを克服し、隠れた構成的構造を実用的な勾配ベースの訓練で活用すること。
llm.method: 各ニューロンに学習された低次元埋め込みを付与し、近接するニューロン間でのみ結合させ、埋め込みと重みを共同で訓練する。
llm.result: 階層構造などのターゲットにおいてサンプル効率が向上し、17の世界モデル予測タスクのうち16で高密度ベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: ニューラルネットワーク

2610.28530.title: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding
2610.28530.abstract: Collaborative perception enables agents to retrieve the scene semantics and geometry beyond the field of view of any individual agent. This broader scene understanding enhances transportation safety and improves efficiency in multi-robot systems. However, existing collaborative semantic occupancy methods rely on dense 3D voxel annotations and are limited to recognizing objects within a predefined set of semantic classes. To overcome these limitations, we present CoGaussian, an open-vocabulary Gaussian-based collaborative semantic occupancy prediction framework. CoGaussian represents a scene as a set of foundation model-aligned sparse 3D Gaussians, which serve as a compact representation for communicating and fusing geometric and semantic information across multiple agents. On the Semantic-OPV2V benchmark, our method outperforms existing open-vocabulary single-agent approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of open-vocabulary collaborative scene understanding.
2610.28530.tldr_en: CoGaussian is presented, an open-vocabulary Gaussian-based collaborative semantic occupancy prediction framework that outperforms existing open-vocabulary single-agent approaches on the Semantic-OPV2V benchmark, highlighting the effectiveness of open-vocabulary collaborative scene understanding.

llm.title_ja: CoGaussian: オープンボキャブラリーガウスベースの協調型3Dシーン理解
llm.tldr_ja: 基盤モデルに整列したスパースな3Dガウスのセットとしてシーンを表現し、複数エージェント間で幾何学的および意味的情報を通信・融合するオープンボキャブラリー協調型意味占有予測フレームワーク「CoGaussian」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の協調型意味占有手法は、高密度な3Dボクセル注釈に依存し、あらかじめ定義されたセマンティッククラスのセットに限定されていること。
llm.method: シーンを基盤モデルに整合したスパース3Dガウスの集合として表現し、エージェント間で幾何・意味情報を共有・融合する。
llm.result: Semantic-OPV2Vベンチマークにおいて、既存のオープンボキャブラリー単一エージェント手法を上回る性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: オープンボキャブラリー

2610.28523.title: VLM-Guided Contact Retargeting and Generative Partner Modeling for Humanoid-Human Interaction
2610.28523.abstract: Humanoid-human interaction requires robots to operate under severe partial observability: during close physical contact, the human partner is occluded, truncated, or outside the robot's field of view, causing pose estimation to fail and often necessitating external tracking or privileged human state.
