At the same time, heavy mutual occlusions introduce errors into the human-human motion-capture data used for learning. We present REACT, a framework for learning deployable humanoid-human interaction policies from human-human demonstrations. REACT treats semantic contact structure as the key supervisory signal connecting demonstration processing, interaction learning, and onboard control. First, a VLM-guided contact modeling and retargeting pipeline identifies semantically meaningful contacts and transfers them onto humanoid-human geometry while preserving interaction structure. Using these annotations, privileged interaction policies learn physically grounded behaviors through interaction-aware contact rewards and are then distilled into deployable egocentric depth policies trained entirely from onboard sensing using photorealistic human depth rendering. To address severe partial observability, we introduce generative partner-state modeling objectives that predict partner motion from occluded egocentric views. We evaluate REACT in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid across five contact-rich interactions. Semantic contact modeling substantially improves preservation of demonstrated interactions, while generative partner-state modeling improves contact recall on four of five interactions, most under heavy occlusion. On real hardware, REACT performs all five interactions using onboard sensing alone.
2610.28523.tldr_en: Generative partner-state modeling objectives that predict partner motion from occluded egocentric views are introduced and substantially improves preservation of demonstrated interactions, while generative partner-state modeling improves contact recall on four of five interactions.

llm.title_ja: VLMガイド付き接触再ターゲットとヒューマノイド・人間相互作用のための生成型パートナーモデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 人間同士のデモから展開可能なヒューマノイド・人間相互作用方策を学習するフレームワーク「REACT」を提案し、意味的な接触構造を主要な指導信号として利用する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドと人間の相互作用において、近接した物理的接触時に人間のパートナーがオクルージョンや切り捨てにより見えなくなり、ポーズ推定が失敗すること。
llm.method: VLMガイド付き接触モデリングパイプラインにより意味のある接触を特定してヒューマノイド・人間ジオメトリに転送し、生成型パートナー状態モデリング目的を導入する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機のUnitree G1ヒューマノイドにおいて、オンボードセンシングのみを用いた5つのインタラクションの実行に成功した。
keywords_ja: 人間とロボットの協調

2610.28519.title: Touch-JEPA: Tactile Representation Learning from Hand-Object Video with Limited Tactile Supervision
2610.28519.abstract: Understanding contact and tactile magnitude in hand-object interaction is a key step toward physically intelligent systems, yet learning such representations is limited by the cost and restricted coverage of tactile measurements. We present Touch-JEPA, a framework for learning tactile representations from hand-object videos with limited tactile supervision. We first introduce a self-supervised pretraining objective that learns from video alone without tactile supervision. Using video-derived hand geometry, Touch-JEPA predicts masked visual features at corresponding hand-surface locations from spatial and temporal context, encouraging the representation to capture latent contact dynamics. We then extend this formulation to joint representation learning, where masked prediction is applied to all videos while tactile supervision is available only for a labeled subset, grounding the shared representation in measured contact and magnitude. With self-supervised pretraining alone, simple supervised readouts on frozen Touch-JEPA features outperform supervised baselines in contact discrimination and tactile magnitude estimation across three human-hand benchmarks, and transfer to robotic hands without robot tactile training data. Joint learning with limited tactile supervision further improves contact and magnitude estimation on the human-hand benchmarks. Together, these results show that hand-object video can provide scalable self-supervision for tactile representation learning, while limited tactile measurements provide complementary physical grounding.
2610.28519.tldr_en: The results show that hand-object video can provide scalable self-supervision for tactile representation learning, while limited tactile measurements provide complementary physical grounding.

llm.title_ja: Touch-JEPA: 限られた触覚指導を用いた手と物体のビデオからの触覚表現学習
llm.tldr_ja: 限られた触覚指導の下で手と物体のビデオから触覚表現を学習するフレームワーク「Touch-JEPA」を提案し、ビデオベースの自己教師あり事前学習を行う。
llm.problem: 接触や触覚の大きさを理解するための表現学習が、触覚計測のコストや限られた網羅性によって制限されていること。
llm.method: ビデオから得られた手の幾何学情報を用いて、空間および時間的文脈から対応する手表面位置のマスクされた視覚特徴を予測し、潜在的な接触ダイナミクスを捉える自己教師あり事前学習を行う。
llm.result: 教師あり事前学習のみの単純な読み出しで、3つの人間の手のベンチマークにおける接触識別や触覚の大きさ推定でベースラインを上回り、ロボットハンドへ転移した。

2610.28483.title: Exploring Temporal Context-Aware Physical Grounding in Latent World Models
2610.28483.abstract: Learning latent dynamics is fundamental to building action-conditioned world models for planning. Among existing families, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) offer a natural framework by modeling transitions directly in latent space rather than at the pixel level. However, two issues remain in JEPA-based world models: (i) physical grounding lacks explicit aggregation of temporal context and (ii) action planning always overly relies on generic sampling distributions. To this end, we propose $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, which incorporates temporal context into physical grounding for latent world models and couples the learned models with prior-guided action planning. Specifically, during learning, we incorporate a shared causal temporal module that aggregates temporal context within observation and prediction sequences under physical state supervision, grounding both in task-relevant physical states. When planning, we further introduce action inference through stepwise conditioning of a generative action distribution on the current and goal latent representations together with their evolving discrepancy, yielding anchored proposals that guide model-based online refinement. Together, physical state supervision guides temporal representation learning, while the action prior guides search through the learned world model. Experiments demonstrate improved planning performance on manipulation tasks, including tasks with increasing temporal separation between initial and goal observations. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/myl11045/G-JEPA.
2610.28483.tldr_en: This work proposes $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, which incorporates temporal context into physical grounding for latent world models and couples the learned models with prior-guided action planning, and demonstrates improved planning performance on manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: 潜在世界モデルにおける時間的文脈を意識した物理的接地性の探索
llm.tldr_ja: 潜在世界モデルに時間的文脈を組み込み、学習したモデルと事前分布誘導型行動計画を組み合わせた「$\mathcal{G}$-JEPA」を提案する。
llm.problem: JEPAベースの世界モデルにおいて、物理的接地が時間的文脈の明示的な集約を欠いており、行動計画が汎用的なサンプリング分布に過度に依存していること。
llm.method: 物理的状態の監視のもとで観測・予測シーケンス内の時間的文脈を集約する共有因果時間モジュールを組み込み、生成行動分布を条件付ける行動推論を導入する。
llm.result: 初期観測と目標観測の時間的分離が増加したタスクを含むマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、計画性能の向上が実証された。

2610.28480.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
2610.28480.abstract: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.
2610.28480.comment: Accepted at CoRL 2026 (Oral). Project website: https://supermimic.github.io
2610.28480.tldr_en: SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws, and transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions.

llm.title_ja: SuperMimic: 1つの微分可能な世界モデルによるヒューマノイド全身制御のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 標準的な剛体シミュレータのログから適合させた共有ダイナミクスの1つの微分可能な世界モデルを用いて、すべてのモーションにわたる学習を効率化する「SuperMimic」を提案する。
llm.problem: 大規模な人間モーションデータセットの追従によるヒューマノイド全身制御のスケーリングコストが高いこと。
llm.method: 世界モデルと追跡方策を1つのループで同時に訓練し、短い想像ロールアウトに対する時間方向の逆伝播によって解析的勾配を方策に与える。
llm.result: 単一GPUで3時間以内に128GPUで7日間訓練したベースラインの報酬を上回り、Unitree G1ヒューマノイドにおいて多様かつアクロバティックな動きへ転移した。
keywords_ja: 微分可能な世界モデル

2610.28476.title: CLOSER: Evidence-Aware Active Visual Verification for Embodied Object-Goal Navigation
2610.28476.abstract: Object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) requires an embodied agent to find an instance of a specified category in an unseen environment and stop near it. The agent typically relies on an object detector but must judge online from a limited egocentric video stream, sometimes a single frame, whether a detected candidate is the target. Detectors often confidently mistake similar objects, such as a sofa for a bed, and stopping at a false positive fails the episode. Prevailing systems also approach candidates greedily, leaving them occluded or partially observed. We present CLOSER, an evidence-aware active verification framework that treats stopping as closed-loop evidence acquisition, coupling vision-language model (VLM) verification with active perception. CLOSER fine-tunes an open-source VLM to label each view of a candidate tracked across frames as target, non-target, or uncertain, selects complementary views with an embedding-based diversity gate, and fuses their per-view probabilities with a lightweight network. If the fused judgment remains uncertain, a diffusion policy drives the agent toward the candidate using only the tracked mask and depth until the decision becomes decisive. CLOSER runs locally and plugs into existing ObjectNav systems without retraining them. On Gibson and Habitat-Matterport 3D, it raises average success rate by 3.6 points and success weighted by path length by 2.0 points, showing that verifying evidence before committing improves embodied navigation.
2610.28476.tldr_en: CLOSER is presented, an evidence-aware active verification framework that treats stopping as closed-loop evidence acquisition, coupling vision-language model (VLM) verification with active perception, and shows that verifying evidence before committing improves embodied navigation.

llm.title_ja: CLOSER: 具現化されたオブジェクト目標ナビゲーションのための証拠認識型アクティブ視覚検証
llm.tldr_ja: 停止を閉ループの証拠収集と見なし、VLM検証と能動的知覚を結合した証拠認識型のアクティブ検証フレームワーク「CLOSER」を提案する。
llm.problem: オブジェクト目標ナビゲーション（ObjectNav）において、限られたエゴセントリック映像から検出された候補がターゲットであるかをオンラインで正確に判断することが困難であること。
llm.method: オープンソースのVLMを微調整して各ビューをラベル付けし、埋め込みベースの多様性ゲートで相補的なビューを選択し、拡散方策を用いて候補に向かってエージェントを駆動する。
llm.result: GibsonおよびHabitat-Matterport 3Dにおいて平均成功率と経路長加重成功率が向上し、コミット前の証拠検証がナビゲーションを改善することを示した。

2610.28470.title: Fast Motion Retargeting Pipeline for Scalable Humanoid Robot Learning
2610.28470.abstract: While large-scale human motion capture datasets provide a rich source of demonstrations for humanoid robot learning, retargeting the diverse motions to different humanoid robots remains a nontrivial challenge. Existing kinodynamic trajectory optimization pipelines are computationally expensive and often require manual adjustments per motion. We present FRDV (Fast Retargeting with Dynamics Validation), a scalable framework consisting of rapid constrained kinematic retargeting and an additional dynamics validation pipeline. Its kinematic stage integrates a custom Sequential Quadratic Programming solver, Real-Time Iteration, and parallel chunk-based processing, achieving up to 9,156 frames per second, approximately up to 136 times faster than GMR and ProtoMotions, while robot-specific constraints are incorporated into the optimization to reduce common retargeting artifacts, such as ground penetration and self-collision. For motions requiring additional verification, a contact implicit iLQR controller is utilized to test the retargeted reference under full rigid body dynamics. This dynamics-based validation identifies dynamically infeasible motions and refines contact-related artifacts such as foot floating and foot skating. We evaluate retargeting quality by training motion tracking reinforcement learning policies using several state-of-the-art pipelines and comparing their tracking fidelity and success rates. Furthermore, sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated on a Unitree G1 humanoid. Videos and code are available at: https://daroslab.github.io/frdv/.
2610.28470.tldr_en: FRDV (Fast Retargeting with Dynamics Validation), a scalable framework consisting of rapid constrained kinematic retargeting and an additional dynamics validation pipeline, and sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated on a Unitree G1 humanoid.

llm.title_ja: スケーラブルなヒューマノイドロボット学習のための高速モーションリターゲットパイプライン
llm.tldr_ja: 迅速な制約付き運動学的リターゲットと追加のダイナミクス検証パイプラインからなるスケーラブルなフレームワーク「FRDV」を提案する。
llm.problem: 大規模な人間モーションデータセットからのデモンストレーションを異なるヒューマノイドロボットへリターゲットする際、従来の最適化パイプラインが計算コストを要すること。
llm.method: カスタムの逐次二次計画法ソルバー、リアルタイム反復、および並列チャンクベース処理を統合した運動学ステージと、接触暗黙的iLQRコントローラを用いたダイナミクス検証を行う。
llm.result: GMRやProtoMotionsよりも最大約136倍高速（最大9,156 fps）なリターゲットを実現し、Unitree G1ヒューマノイドでのシムツーリアル転移を実証した。
keywords_ja: モーションリターゲット

2610.28465.title: MARE: An Open-Source Lunar Rover Simulator with Shadow Ground Truth for Perception and Autonomy
2610.28465.abstract: Lunar surface exploration increasingly relies on autonomous rovers that must perceive and traverse unstructured terrain under extreme illumination conditions. Near the lunar poles, low sun elevations produce long, high-contrast shadows that challenge stereo vision, terrain segmentation, and localization. Developing perception and navigation algorithms for these conditions requires large amounts of sensor data with accurate ground truth, which field campaigns and analog facilities can only provide at high cost and with limited variety. This paper presents MARE (Modular Autonomy and Rendering Environment), an open-source simulation suite for lunar rover perception and autonomy built on Unreal Engine 5 and ROS 2. MARE consists of three integrated components. Terrain Studio generates cratered and rocky lunar Digital Elevation Maps (DEMs) to build simulation scenes. A dedicated Unreal Engine project hosts two physics-based rovers with plugins for stereo, lidar, event, and Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) cameras, streaming time-stamped sensor data and pixel-accurate ground truth. Lastly, a Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) stack provides web-based mission control. Validation shows a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.79 between predicted and rendered shadows at low sun elevations, and stereo depth analysis verifies decreased pixel coverage in shadowed regions relative to sunlit terrain.
2610.28465.comment: 10 pages, 16 figures, 3 tables. v2: adds a dataset with segmentation and depth baselines. Code: https://github.com/raulcastar/MARE-Lunar-Simulator. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/raulcastar/mare-lunar-rover-dataset. Video: https://youtu.be/EI4HgbMFbBE
2610.28465.tldr_en: MARE (Modular Autonomy and Rendering Environment), an open-source simulation suite for lunar rover perception and autonomy built on Unreal Engine 5 and ROS 2, is presented.

llm.title_ja: MARE: 知覚と自律性のためのシャドウグラウンド真値を持つオープンソース月面ローバシミュレータ
llm.tldr_ja: Unreal Engine 5とROS 2を基に構築された、月面ローバーの知覚と自律性のためのオープンソースシミュレーションスイート「MARE」を提示する。
llm.problem: 月面極付近の低太陽高度による長くてコントラストの高い影が、ステレオビジョン、地形セグメンテーション、およびローカリゼーションを困難にしていること。
llm.method: 地形スタジオによるDEM生成、物理ベースのローバーと各種センサープラグインを搭載したUnreal Engineプロジェクト、およびWebベースのGNCスタックを統合する。
llm.result: 予測された影とレンダリングされた影の間で平均IoU 0.79を達成し、影領域でのピクセルカバレッジの低下をステレオ深度分析により検証した。

2610.28457.title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
2610.28457.abstract: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.
2610.28457.tldr_en: This work examines tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability of general-purpose multimodal models, using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed and presents GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action.

llm.title_ja: GPT-6-Astraは触覚を理解し、視覚・触覚・言語・行動モデルを凌駕する
llm.tldr_ja: 専門家のデモンストレーションをタスク指導と触覚リファレンスに要約し、接触評価と是正措置を行う「GPT-as-Tactile-Policy」を提案する。
llm.problem: 接触リッチなマニピュレーションにおいて、触覚フィードバックの解釈や障害物回避後の行動調整には、専門的な事前学習と高いデータ・訓練コストが必要であること。
llm.method: 専門家のデモンストレーションから得たタスク指導と触覚リファレンスを、マルチモデル観測やインタラクション履歴と組み合わせて制御コマンドを生成する。
llm.result: 追加のロボティクス特化の事前学習やタスクごとの微調整なしで、5つのUniVTACタスクで平均93.8%の成功率を達成し、「穴への挿入」タスクでは成功率が31%から99%に向上した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルモデル
接触リッチマニピュレーション

2610.28432.title: Physical AI for Intralogistics: Benchmarking the NVIDIA Sim-to-Real Ecosystem for Cosmos-Enhanced COMPASS Navigation on Industrial Mobile Robots
2610.28432.abstract: Classical robot navigation stacks are reliable but often require re-engineering for each new robot type and site. Learning-based navigation shifts this effort from hand-tuned parameters to data generation and training, where a policy adapts to each new embodiment or facility by fine-tuning in simulation. Whether policies adapted this way stay reliable on real industrial robots has seen little systematic testing. We study this for NVIDIA's X-Mobility and COMPASS workflow for training learned navigation policies on Idealworks robots. In simulation, we extend the COMPASS benchmark with two embodiments, the differential-drive iw$\mkern-1.5mu.\mkern-1.5mu$hub and an omnidirectional Humanoid Mobile Platform (HMP), and with a digital twin of the Idealworks R&D center. For the real world, we fine-tune X-Mobility on data from this digital twin, with and without sim-to-real variants generated by NVIDIA Cosmos, train COMPASS on top of it from scratch in the digital twin, deploy the resulting policies on the iw$\mkern-1.5mu.\mkern-1.5mu$hub's onboard Jetson AGX Xavier, and benchmark them in the Idealworks R&D center against COMPASS trained only on NVIDIA's environments and the existing Idealworks navigation stack on task success, efficiency, safety, smoothness and onboard compute. Running every static scenario both in a digital-twin replica and in the real facility measures the sim-to-real gap and how far Cosmos-augmented data closes it. Training in the digital twin with Cosmos sim-to-real augmentation raises the real-world success rate of learned navigation from 65.3% to 91.7% across four scenarios and nearly halves its weighted travel time compared with simulation-only training, bringing it within 8.3 points of the production navigation stack, fully onboard; with an integrated global planner, it also reaches far, occluded goals in every trial.
2610.28432.tldr_en: This work studies NVIDIA's X-Mobility and COMPASS workflow for training learned navigation policies on Idealworks robots, and benchmarks them against COMPASS trained only on NVIDIA's environments and the existing Idealworks navigation stack on task success, efficiency, safety, smoothness and onboard compute.

llm.title_ja: イントラロジスティクス向けPhysical AI: NVIDIAのSim-to-Realエコシステムによる産業用移動ロボット向けCosmos強化COMPASSナビゲーションのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: NVIDIAのX-MobilityとCOMPASSワークフローを用いてIdealworksロボット向けに学習されたナビゲーション方策を訓練し、シムツーリアルギャップを検証する。
llm.problem: 従来のロボットナビゲーションスタックは信頼性が高いものの新しいロボットやサイトごとに再エンジニアリングが必要であり、学習ベースのナビゲーションが実世界で信頼性を保てるか十分に検証されていないこと。
llm.method: IdealworksのR&Dセンターのデジタルツインを構築し、NVIDIA Cosmosによって生成されたシムツーリアルバリアントの有無にかかわらずX-Mobilityを微調整する。
llm.result: Cosmosによるシムツーリアル拡張を用いたデジタルツインでの訓練により、実世界のナビゲーション成功率が65.3%から91.7%に向上し、移動時間が大幅に短縮された。
keywords_ja: イントラロジスティクス

2610.28431.title: Plausible Future, Wrong Choice: Steering World-Action Models toward Intended Future
2610.28431.abstract: World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied generalist policies by jointly modeling future world evolution and robot actions across diverse manipulation tasks. However, representing diverse futures is only the first step: a capable WAM must also generate futures that match the requirements of the current task and execution progress. In long-horizon manipulation where similar observation-action segments occur across different tasks and stages, existing approaches may generate locally plausible yet misdirected rollouts to drift toward wrong task stage, i.e., a phenomenon we term Stage Confusion. To address this problem, we propose TaskWAM, a closed-loop, stage-aware framework that represents fine-grained task requirements with Mode Tokens and tracks execution progress with State Tokens, forming a structured task state to steer world--action generation toward intended future. We further introduce StageBench, a controlled multi-stage manipulation benchmark with parameterized stage variations and automated evaluation.Extensive experiments on both simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks demonstrate that TaskWAM effectively reduces confusion and achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, TaskWAM provides strong plug-and-play transfer across heterogeneous WAM architectures and robot embodiments, including single-arm robots, dual-arm grippers, dexterous hands, and humanoid robots.
2610.28431.tldr_en: This work proposes TaskWAM, a closed-loop, stage-aware framework that represents fine-grained task requirements with Mode Tokens and tracks execution progress with State Tokens, forming a structured task state to steer world--action generation toward intended future.

llm.title_ja: もっともらしい未来、誤った選択：意図した未来へと世界行動モデルを誘導する
llm.tldr_ja: 細かなタスク要件をモードトークンで表現し実行進捗を状態トークンで追跡して、世界・行動生成を意図した未来へ誘導する閉ループのステージ認識型フレームワーク「TaskWAM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 長期的なマニピュレーションにおいて、類似した観測行動セグメントが異なるタスクや段階で発生し、モデルが誤ったタスク段階へ漂流する「ステージ混同」を引き起こすこと。
llm.method: モードトークンと状態トークンを用いて構造化されたタスク状態を形成し、もっともらしいが誤った軌道の生成を防ぎながら世界行動の生成を誘導する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界タスクにおける実験により、TaskWAMが混同を効果的に軽減し、最先端手法と競合する性能を達成することが示された。

2610.28411.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
2610.28411.abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonstrate improved final accuracy and faster convergence compared to random initialization. Additionally, its frozen embeddings outperform anatomically defined volumetric features on four of five downstream classification tasks and perform competitively with a state-of-the-art foundation model pre-trained on substantially more data. Lastly, we show that Brain2Vec encodes information primarily from a spatially localized and neuroanatomically meaningful set of brain regions, and that manipulating a subset of latent features produces monotonic, region-specific effects on the reconstructed anatomy. Brain2Vec code and trained models are available as an open-source package on https://github.com/CBICA/Brain2Vec. Users can apply Brain2Vec locally by installing the package, or directly through the NiChart cloud platform https://cloud.neuroimagingchart.com, where Brain2Vec features can be derived without requiring local installation or specialized infrastructure.
2610.28411.tldr_en: Brain2Vec is introduced, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies that can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor.

llm.title_ja: Brain2Vec: 構造的脳MRIのための自己教師あり3D基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: Brain2Vecは複数研究から集めた74,425件のT1強調MRIスキャンで事前学習された基盤モデルであり、ダウンストリームタスクの重み初期化バックボーンや単体の特徴抽出器として機能する。
llm.problem: 医療画像における深層学習モデルの訓練は、ラベル付きデータの不足と計算上の制約により多様なタスクのエンドツーエンド訓練が困難であること。
llm.method: 複数研究から集めた74,425件のT1強調MRIスキャンを用いた自己教師あり学習による3D基盤モデルの構築。
llm.result: ランダム初期化と比較して脳年齢予測タスクでの最終精度向上と収束の高速化を実現し、固定埋め込みは多くのダウンストリーム分類タスクで解剖学的特徴を上回る性能を示した。

2610.28397.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
2610.28397.abstract: Agentic AI extends large language models (LLMs) from generating responses to planning and executing complex workflows, substantially expanding their utility while exposing applications to unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation. Multi-agent systems further expand these capabilities through specialization and collaboration, but distributed authority, heterogeneous roles, and opaque or potentially compromised participants make safeguarding even more challenging. Existing defenses address important individual threats but provide fragmented coverage across local execution, system-level interactions, and enforcement mechanisms. We introduce MAS-Guard, a unified framework that closes this gap for safeguarding single- and multi-agent AI applications containing both instrumentable and opaque agents. Within instrumentable agents, the proposed local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) layer applies task-specific experts to assess agentic events. At the system level, developer-owned Agent Charters and a Control Plane combine deterministic structural checks of routes, agent capabilities, and message formats with semantic assessments of roles and message content. These complementary layers enable enforcement through a shared set of interventions: allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. Evaluated across six benchmarks covering diverse single- and multi-agent scenarios with three agent LLMs from different providers, MAS-Guard reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5-86.3% relative to unguarded agents, while meeting the utility reference criterion on benign tasks.
2610.28397.tldr_en: MAS-Guard is introduced, a unified framework that closes the gap for safeguarding single- and multi-agent AI applications containing both instrumentable and opaque agents and reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5-86.3% relative to unguarded agents.

llm.title_ja: MAS-Guard: 個別エージェントからマルチエージェントLLMシステムまでの統合ガードレール
llm.tldr_ja: MAS-Guardは、インストルメント可能および不透明なエージェントを含む単一・マルチエージェントAIアプリケーションを保護するための統合フレームワークであり、攻撃成功率を71.5〜86.3%削減する。
llm.problem: エージェント型AIは効用を大幅に拡大する一方で、安全でないアクション、情報漏洩、敵対的操作にアプリケーションを晒していること。
llm.method: ローカルのA-Guard層、開発者所有のエージェントチャーター、コントロールプレーンを組み合わせた統合フレームワークの導入。
llm.result: 保護されていないエージェントと比較して全体の攻撃成功率を71.5〜86.3%削減しつつ、良性タスクの有用性基準を満たした。

2610.28381.title: CAPSafe: A Benchmark for Contextual Action and Plan Safety Reasoning in Embodied Agents
2610.28381.abstract: Reasoning about safety is essential for embodied agents powered by large language models (LLMs). We introduce the Contextual Action and Plan Safety benchmark (CAPSafe), designed to evaluate safety reasoning at two levels: (1) an action-level dataset that tests whether a single action is safe given its environmental context, and (2) a plan-level dataset that evaluates whether agents can generate safe long-horizon plans for complex hazardous household tasks. CAPSafe models safety conditions where hazards are situational (inferred from object properties), multiple hazards can co-occur within the same environment, and each is annotated with a relative severity level for fine-grained analysis. Evaluating nine closed and open-source LLMs reveals a substantial gap between hazard recognition and safe long-horizon planning. Several models achieve high accuracy in recognizing unsafe actions (exceeding 90% in the best cases), yet safe long-horizon planning remains substantially harder. Gemini-3-pro achieves the highest safe success rate (78.19%), while other models remain below 65%. These results highlight that robust safety reasoning over long action sequences remains an open challenge.
2610.28381.tldr_en: The Contextual Action and Plan Safety benchmark (CAPSafe) is introduced, designed to evaluate safety reasoning at two levels: an action-level dataset that tests whether a single action is safe given its environmental context, and a plan-level dataset that evaluates whether agents can generate safe long-horizon plans for complex hazardous household tasks.
2610.28381.venue: Proceedings of the Second Workshop for REsearch on Agent Language Models (REALM 2026)

llm.title_ja: CAPSafe: 身体性エージェントにおける文脈的アクションおよび計画の安全性推論のためのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: CAPSafeは、単一アクションの安全性と長期的な複雑な危険家事タスクに対する安全な計画生成能力を2つのレベルで評価するために設計されたベンチマークである。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）によって駆動される身体性エージェントにとって、安全性に関する推論は不可欠であるにもかかわらず、その評価が十分に整備されていないこと。
llm.method: 環境文脈に応じた単一アクションの安全性をテストするアクションレベルのデータセットと、安全な長期計画を評価するプランレベルのデータセットからなるCAPSafeベンチマークの導入。
llm.result: 9つのLLMの評価により、危険認識において高い精度を達成する一方で、安全な長期計画の生成は依然として大幅に困難であることが明らかになった。

2610.28362.title: SPAR: Search-trained Push Action Ranker for Efficient Navigation Among Movable Obstacles
2610.28362.abstract: Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) requires a robot to rearrange objects that block access to its goal. For a pushing robot, progress may depend on a setup push that enables a later opening without itself clearing a passage. The number of candidate sequences can grow exponentially with sequence length, making physics-based search costly. We introduce the Search-trained Push Action Ranker (SPAR), which learns to prioritize push primitives from simulated search outcomes. Searches over sequences of up to two pushes per object provide supervision that distinguishes immediate openings from setup pushes. A transformer trained with regression and ranking losses scores primitives using contact tokens conditioned on scene geometry and reachability regions. The same model guides simulator evaluations in SPAR Search and selects actions for direct execution in SPAR Policy. Both modes solve successive keyhole problems that open access to neighboring free-space regions within a NAMO planner. Across successful runs on $300$ simulated two-push keyhole problems, SPAR Search reduces median simulator calls by $7.0\times$, leading to a $3.8\times$ reduction in planning time relative to Random Search. Without retraining, the same ranker guides search on $600$ keyhole problems which have no solution within two pushes. At a depth limit of five pushes, SPAR Search achieves $50.7\%$ success within $100$ simulator calls, compared with $20.2\%$ for Random Search. These gains carry over to NAMO planning: on hard simulated scenes, SPAR Search achieves $47\%$ success within $100$ simulator calls, compared with $21\%$ for Random Search. In real-robot experiments, SPAR Policy succeeds in $37/40$ trials without a physics-based digital twin, compared with $33/40$ for SPAR Search and $27/40$ for Random Search.
2610.28362.tldr_en: The Search-trained Push Action Ranker (SPAR), which learns to prioritize push primitives from simulated search outcomes, is introduced, which helps NAMO planning and succeeds in real-robot experiments without a physics-based digital twin.

llm.title_ja: SPAR: 可動障害物間の効率的なナビゲーションのための探索訓練済みプッシュアクションランカー
llm.tldr_ja: SPARはシミュレーション探索結果からプッシュプリミティブの優先順位付けを学習し、NAMO計画を助け、物理ベースのデジタルツインなしで実機実験に成功する。
llm.problem: 可動障害物間ナビゲーション（NAMO）において、物理ベースの探索は候補シーケンスが長さに伴い指数関数的に増加するため費用がかかること。
llm.method: シミュレーションされた探索結果からプッシュプリミティブを優先順位付けすることを学習し、接触トークンを用いてプリミティブをスコアリングするTransformerベースのSPARの導入。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの計画時間を大幅に削減し、実機実験において物理ベースのデジタルツインなしで40中37回の試行に成功した。

2610.28329.title: Reinforced Iterative Learning Control for elastic joint arms: Guaranteed cross-trajectory generalization under model uncertainties
2610.28329.abstract: Trajectory tracking for compliant robots is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and modeling uncertainties, often requiring learning-based methods to avoid explicit parameter identification. Iterative Learning Control (ILC) ensures theoretically high precision and preserves the passive compliance of the robot. However, traditional ILC requires a separate learning phase for each new trajectory. Conversely, Reinforcement Learning (RL) generalizes to new trajectories, but practically suffers from high sample complexity and limited tracking precision. This work proposes Reinforced Iterative Learning Control (RILC) that combines the strengths of both approaches to achieve fast adaptation and guaranteed tracking convergence across diverse trajectories. By establishing a concurrent coupling between the two controllers, RILC overcomes the high initial errors and slow adaptation of traditional ILC, enabling high-performance tracking from the very first trials. In this architecture, ILC provides high-quality samples, while RL contributes as a generalizing best-effort policy across iterations. Additionally, a theoretical proof is presented to show that the RL component preserves ILC stability and, under specific conditions, can also reduce the error bound asymptotically. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated through simulation and experiments on an underactuated 4-degree-of-freedom serial elastic robot using different trajectories and modeling mismatches.
2610.28329.comment: Accepted for publication in Control Engineering Practice, 2026. 16 pages, 10 figures
2610.28329.tldr_en: By establishing a concurrent coupling between the two controllers, RILC overcomes the high initial errors and slow adaptation of traditional ILC, enabling high-performance tracking from the very first trials.

llm.title_ja: 弾性関節アームのための強化学習反復学習制御：モデル不確実性下での保証されたクロストラジェクトリ汎化
llm.tldr_ja: RILCは2つのコントローラー間の同時結合を確立することにより、従来のILCの高い初期初期誤差と遅い適応を克服し、最初の試行から高性能な追従を可能にする。
llm.problem: コンプライアントロボットの軌道追従は、非線形ダイナミクスとモデリングの不確実性のために困難であり、従来のILCは新しい軌道ごとに別個の学習フェーズを必要とすること。
llm.method: ILCと強化学習（RL）の強みを組み合わせて高速適応と追従収束を達成する強化学習反復学習制御（RILC）の提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび4自由度の直列弾性ロボットを用いた実機実験により、異なる軌道とモデリングの不一致の下で有効性を示した。

2610.28290.title: Distributed Platoon Control for Safe and Smooth Crossing at an Unsignalized Intersection-Part I: Stability Analysis
2610.28290.abstract: We propose a distributed platoon controller that guarantees safe and smooth crossing of multi-vehicle systems at an unsignalized intersection. To support the stability analysis, we consider a multi-vehicle platoon maneuvering along a closed path with a single unsignalized intersection. Unlike traditional bi-level decoupled designs on open paths, which primarily focus on intersection control while neglecting its coupling with platoon convergence, and thus hindering rigorous convergence analysis, the closed-path setting allows us to analyze the asymptotic behavior of the platoon. The local exponential convergence analysis of the switched closed-loop system, induced by repeated vehicle switching at the intersection, is presented. Under some mild conditions on the controller gains, we show that safe intersection crossing is ensured during the transient phase and smooth crossing is achieved in steady state, where all vehicles travel at a common constant speed while avoiding collisions at the intersection. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed distributed controller is demonstrated in a high-fidelity CARLA simulator using multiple commercial vehicle models.
2610.28290.tldr_en: A distributed platoon controller that guarantees safe and smooth crossing of multi-vehicle systems at an unsignalized intersection is proposed and the effectiveness of the proposed distributed controller is demonstrated in a high-fidelity CARLA simulator using multiple commercial vehicle models.

llm.title_ja: 信号機のない交差点での安全かつ円滑な交差のための分散プラトゥーン制御―パートI：安定性解析
llm.tldr_ja: 信号機のない交差点における多車両システムの安全かつ円滑な交差を保証する分散プラトゥーンコントローラを提案し、高精度なCARLAシミュレータで有効性を実証した。
llm.problem: 従来のオープンパス上の二レベル分離設計では交差点制御に重点が置かれる一方でプラトゥーン収束との結合が軽視され、厳密な収束解析が妨げられていること。
llm.method: 閉路設定の下で交差点での繰り返しの車両切り替えによって誘導される、切り替え閉系システムの局所的指数収束解析の提示。
llm.result: コントローラゲインの穏やかな条件の下で、遷移フェーズ中の安全な交差と、定常状態での円滑な交差が達成されることを示した。

2610.28286.title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
2610.28286.abstract: Teams of large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to complex tasks, but their collaboration protocols are mostly designed empirically, without convergence guarantees. We formalize collaborative problem solving as block optimization: each agent improves one part of a shared solution, guided by its local objective plus a correction for how its changes affect the other parts. A coordinator checks every proposal against the global objective and merges proposals that do not interfere with each other. We prove linear convergence up to an error floor that vanishes when the corrections are exact. Interfering proposals can also be merged once their combination has been checked; the rate then depends on how well the proposals actually combine, not on worst-case interactions. With GPT-OSS-120B agents on robot routing, a three-agent team finds collision-free plans in every run, better than those of a single agent that controls all robots. On a larger routing task, a six-agent team completes its search about twice as fast as the single agent (in median). Merging the best checked combination of proposals, rather than only proposals that do not interfere, cuts the team's search time by about 30%. With constants measured on the runs, our convergence bound holds in every round and follows the observed progress. We also test the theory on query planning in SQLite and on a synthetic task.
2610.28286.tldr_en: This work formalizes collaborative problem solving as block optimization as block optimization: each agent improves one part of a shared solution, guided by its local objective plus a correction for how its changes affect the other parts.

llm.title_ja: ローカル作業、グローバルな進展：AIエージェント協調の収束理論
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、共同問題解決をブロック最適化として定式化し、各エージェントが局所的目的に従って共有ソリューションの一部を改善し、コーディネーターが提案を統合する。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）エージェントのチームは複雑なタスクにますます適用されているが、その協調プロトコルは主に経験的に設計されており、収束保証がないこと。
llm.method: 共同問題解決をブロック最適化として定式化し、各エージェントが局所的目的に基づいて改善を行い、コーディネーターがグローバル目的に対して確認・統合を行う手法の提案。
llm.result: 全ての実行において衝突のないプランを見つけ、単一エージェントよりも優れた結果を示し、誤差上限が収束することを確認した。

2610.28259.title: Large Multimodal Models for Direct Robot Control: GPT-6 as a Beginning
2610.28259.abstract: Recent advances in visuospatial understanding and agentic reasoning enable direct robotic manipulation with general-purpose multimodal models, but their embodied capabilities remain poorly understood. This paper systematically evaluate GPT-6 Astra for closed-loop robotic manipulation using a lightweight agent execution framework. We first probe three fundamental embodied capabilities-depth perception, embodied in-context learning, and tactile understanding-and demonstrate that the model can exploit depth information, acquire simple manipulation strategies from contextual demonstrations, and use tactile feedback to correct its actions. We then evaluate GPT-6 Astra across five established manipulation benchmarks along six capability dimensions. Despite competitive performance on several benchmarks-26.92\% success on RoboDojo and 76.0\% on RoboTwin 2.0-our analysis reveals a pronounced gap between semantic reasoning and physical execution, particularly in consequence-aware action planning, precision, and complex motion coordination. To further examine these limitations, we introduce LIBERO-GeoMotion, a new benchmark of geometry-constrained tasks that require precise pose alignment, coordinated translation and rotation, and anticipation of physical action consequences. GPT-6 Astra achieves only 11.1\% zero-shot success, exposing the difficulty of translating spatial understanding into physically feasible motion. Real-world experiments corroborate these findings: zero-shot execution is feasible for simple tasks, yet persistent deficits remain in motion feasibility, precise control, and physical safety, while substantial inference latency further hinders practical deployment. Overall, our results characterize the emerging embodied capabilities of general-purpose multimodal models and delineate the key challenges toward safe, efficient, and reliable robotic manipulation.
2610.28259.tldr_en: This paper systematically evaluates GPT-6 Astra for closed-loop robotic manipulation using a lightweight agent execution framework and characterize the emerging embodied capabilities of general-purpose multimodal models and delineate the key challenges toward safe, efficient, and reliable robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: 直接的ロボット制御のための大規模マルチモーダルモデル：始まりとしてのGPT-6
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、軽量なエージェント実行フレームワークを用いて閉ループロボットマニピュレーションにおけるGPT-6 Astraを体系的に評価し、汎用マルチモーダルモデルの持つ身体化された能力を特徴づけた。
llm.problem: 視空間理解やエージェント推論の最近の進歩により汎用マルチモーダルモデルを用いた直接的なロボット操作が可能になったが、その身体的能力は十分に理解されていないこと。
llm.method: 軽量なエージェント実行フレームワークを用いた閉ループロボットマニピュレーションに対するGPT-6 Astraの体系的な評価と新しいベンチマーク（LIBERO-GeoMotion）の導入。
llm.result: いくつかのベンチマークで競争力のある性能を示した一方で、意味論的推論と物理的実行の間に顕著なギャップがあることが明らかになった。
llm.limitation: 実機におけるゼロショット実行は単純なタスクでは可能だが、モーションの実現可能性、精密な制御、物理的安全性の面で課題が残る。
keywords_ja: 大規模マルチモーダルモデル

2610.28251.title: Safe Multi-Robot Collaboration With Uniform Exclusion Using Trust
2610.28251.abstract: Robot swarms coordinate through directed, time-varying local communication links, some of which may be compromised to allow the transmission of arbitrary malicious data. We provide an algorithm that acts as a wrapper around robot communication---when a robot seeks to update its state using data from some incoming links, our wrapper provides a subset of trusted links whose data can be safely incorporated. It selects these links by testing a stream of trust values---data collected from an anomaly detector on each robot---using Safe Anytime-Valid Inference. We require only that the detector be better than chance. This wrapper ensures safe and performant autonomy by providing two powerful statistical guarantees: it uniformly excludes all compromised links for all time with high user-chosen probability, but nevertheless quickly learns to trust legitimate links. Both guarantees are vital to secure generic tasks, but no previous work provides them simultaneously without restrictive assumptions on connectivity structure or the number of compromised links that are not guaranteed in practice. We study our Safe Wrapper's performance in hardware for two contrasting tasks---neural implicit mapping and heading consensus---deploying on 3 LoCoBots and 8 GoPiGos, respectively. We provide simulations using trust values sampled from hardware to validate that our approach scales well to swarms of hundreds of robots.
2610.28251.comment: 44 pages (30 main text + 14 supplementary); 10 figures, 6 tables
2610.28251.tldr_en: The Safe Wrapper is provided, an algorithm that acts as a wrapper around robot communication that uniformly excludes all compromised links for all time with high user-chosen probability, but nevertheless quickly learns to trust legitimate links.

llm.title_ja: 信頼を用いた一様排除による安全なマルチロボット協調
llm.tldr_ja: セーフ・ラッパーは、ロボット間通信のラッパーとして機能し、悪意あるデータを送信する可能性のあるリンクを一様に排除しつつ、正当なリンクを素早く信頼することを学習するアルゴリズムである。
llm.problem: ロボット群は時間変動する局所通信リンクを通じて協調するが、一部のリンクが侵害され任意の悪意あるデータが送信される可能性があること。
llm.method: 各ロボットの異常検知器からの信頼値のストリームを Safe Anytime-Valid Inference を用いてテストし、安全に組み込める信頼されたリンクのサブセットを提供するアルゴリズムの提案。
llm.result: ハードウェアおよびシミュレーションにおいて、侵害されたリンクを確実に排除しつつ正当なリンクを学習し、数百台のロボット群へ拡張可能であることを示した。

2610.28184.title: Perceives but Doesn't Brake: A Perception-Action Binding Gap in Reasoning Driving VLAs
2610.28184.abstract: Reasoning-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) driving models can perceive and reason about safety-critical hazards yet fail to translate that evidence into safe actions. We characterize this failure as a perception-action binding gap: hazard information is available inside the model but exerts insufficient control over trajectory generation. Using matched simulated counterfactuals and logged driving replay, we show that in-path hazards are actually encoded in the visual representation, but longitudinal plans are dominated by ego-speed history and respond only weakly to hazard proximity or the model's own reasoning trace. Further analysis shows that the trajectory generator is capable of braking but sometimes fails to do so due to the perception-action binding gap. Without retraining or modifying any weights, we inject a hazard-conditioned energy into the frozen flow-matching sampler of Alpamayo-1.5, restoring the missing coupling at generation time. With exact obstacle geometry, guidance cuts footprint intrusion from 58.1% to 14.5% and recovers safe braking whenever sufficient stopping distance remains, eliminating collisions entirely in our braking-relevant closed-loop battery. It also reverses the diagnosed dependence of the plan, from tracking ego speed to responding to obstacle range. These results separate hazard perception from hazard control in driving VLAs, show that unsafe behavior can arise even when the model has both the evidence and the ability to act on it, and propose a simple fix for bridging this binding gap.
2610.28184.tldr_en: The results separate hazard perception from hazard control in driving VLAs, show that unsafe behavior can arise even when the model has both the evidence and the ability to act on it, and propose a simple fix for bridging this binding gap.

llm.title_ja: 知覚するがブレーキを踏まない：推論駆動型VLAにおける知覚・行動結合のギャップ
llm.tldr_ja: 推論駆動型の視覚言語行動（VLA）駆動モデルは安全上の危険を知覚・推論できるがその証拠を安全な行動に翻訳できず、本研究ではこれを知覚・行動結合のギャップとして特徴づけた。
llm.problem: 推論拡張型VLA駆動モデルが安全上の危険を知覚し推論できるにもかかわらず、その証拠を安全な行動にうまく翻訳できないこと。
llm.method: シミュレートされた反事実とログに記録された運転リプレイを用いて、モデル内部での障害物のエンコードとトラジェクトリ生成の間の不整合を分析し、ハザード条件付きエネルギーをサンプラーに注入する手法の提案。
llm.result: 厳密な障害物幾何学を用いた誘導により、フットプリント侵入を大幅に削減し、ブレーキ関連の閉ループ評価において衝突を完全に排除した。

2610.28166.title: Reasoning as a Distribution: Generative Plan Latents for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.28166.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies increasingly reason before acting, but existing reasoning models compress this intermediate decision into a single representation. When several plans are valid, this commitment hides alternatives that could otherwise be selected or revised. We introduce the Generative Plan Latent (GPL), which represents the reasoning state as a low-dimensional conditional distribution over plans, such as which object, grasp, or route to use. This makes the reasoning state addressable: without retraining the VLA, plans can be sampled (coverage), selected on request (steering), and reweighted by deployment outcomes (outcome adaptation). We test all three on SimplerEnv manipulation with $π_0$, and extend the analysis to RoboCasa, LIBERO, and a maze domain. Steering the plan raises the fraction of executions that follow the request from 0.48 to 0.94, while the same guidance on the native action distribution shows no reliable gain. Finally, we show that an explicit plan is most useful when it carries decision information not already determined by the observation.
2610.28166.tldr_en: The Generative Plan Latent (GPL) is introduced, which represents the reasoning state as a low-dimensional conditional distribution over plans, such as which object, grasp, or route to use, and shows that an explicit plan is most useful when it carries decision information not already determined by the observation.

llm.title_ja: 分布としての推論：視覚言語行動モデルのための生成型プラン潜在変数
llm.tldr_ja: 生成型プラン潜在変数（GPL）は、推論状態をプランに関する低次元の条件付き分布として表現し、VLAを再学習することなくプランのサンプリング、選択、結果適応を可能にする。
llm.problem: 既存の推論モデルは中間決定を単一の表現に圧縮するため、複数のプランが有効な場合に他の代替案が隠されてしまうこと。
llm.method: オブジェクト、把持、ルートなどのプランに関する低次元条件付き分布として推論状態を表現する生成型プラン潜在変数（GPL）の提案。
llm.result: プランのステアリングにより、リクエストに従う実行の割合が向上し、オブザベーションだけで決定されない場合に明示的プランが有用であることを示した。

2610.28164.title: From Predictive Geometry to Action: Learning Complementary Predictive Representations for Embodied Manipulation
2610.28164.abstract: Effective manipulation requires a policy to capture not only about the current scene geometry, but also about how that geometry will evolve under interaction. Existing approaches either augment policies with geometric information from current observations or introduce future prediction as auxiliary supervision, leaving open how predictive geometry should be represented for action generation. Therefore, we propose a two-stage framework, which learns complementary predictive representations from multi-view video clips. During pretraining, a frozen 3D foundation model provides dense geometric features that are compressed into predictive geometric representations and optimized to preserve scene structure and its temporal evolution. Action supervision is then applied to geometric transitions to extract a complementary motor representation that emphasizes action-relevant transitions. During downstream post-training, predictive geometry is transferred through geometry queries, while the motor representation guides intermediate features along the action-generation pathway. Future observations are used only as privileged supervision during training and are not required at inference time. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, SimplerEnv, and real-world bimanual and single-arm tasks, our approach consistently improves downstream policies, including an absolute gain of 10.4 percentage points on the WidowX evaluation. We further demonstrate transfer across multiple VLA architectures and WAMs, with improvements in both future-world and action prediction. The code will be available at https://github.com/xuxiaoxxxx/CPR.
2610.28164.tldr_en: A two-stage framework, which learns complementary predictive representations from multi-view video clips and consistently improves downstream policies, with improvements in both future-world and action prediction.

llm.title_ja: 予測幾何学から行動へ：身体性マニピュレーションのための補完的予測表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、マルチビュービデオクリップから補完的な予測表現を学習する2段階のフレームワークを提案し、ダウンストリームポリシーの性能を継続的に向上させる。
llm.problem: 既存のアプローチでは、現在の観測からの幾何学情報の追加や将来予測の補助的監督にとどまり、行動生成のための予測幾何学をどのように表現すべきか未解決であること。
llm.method: マルチビュービデオクリップから予測幾何表現と行動関連の遷移を強調するモーター表現を学習する2段階フレームワークの提案。
llm.result: LIBEROや実世界のタスクを含む複数のダウンストリームポリシーを改善し、WidowXの評価で10.4ポイントの絶対的向上を達成した。
llm.limitation: 将来の観測は訓練時の特権的監督としてのみ使用され、推論時には必要とされないが、データ依存性などの詳細な限界は本文に委ねられる。

2610.28127.title: Design and implementation of thermal control strategy for micro-size lunar exploration rover hakuto
2610.28127.abstract: The research focuses on the thermal interface design of the HAKUTO Rover Flight Model (FM) and its evaluation using the final thermal vacuum experiment. Initially, an analytical thermal model was developed, dividing the rover into six distinct radiating surfaces. The surface temperature of the rover was then determined based on its orientation relative to the solar radiative flux, as well as other thermal factors such as lunar radiation, solar albedo, and conduction from the lunar regolith. By considering the impact of these heat sources, suitable mounting locations for the avionics and the angle of the solar panels were determined to optimize the rover's thermal performance and power generation while ensuring the rover's mass remained under 4 kg. After the preliminary thermal analysis, numerical computational simulations were conducted to further elaborate on the thermal response of the final HAKUTO Rover FM design, which was then verified through a thermal balance test in a vacuum environment.
2610.28127.comment: 69th International Astronautical Congress (IAC), Bremen, Germany, 1-5 October 2018

llm.title_ja: マイクロサイズ月面探査ローバーHAKUTOのための熱制御システムの設計と実装
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、HAKUTOローバーフライトモデルの熱インターフェース設計に焦点を当て、最終的な熱真空実験を用いてその評価を行ったものである。
llm.problem: 質量を4kg未満に抑えつつ、太陽放射流や月面放射などの熱的要因に対してローバーの熱性能と発電を最適化する必要があること。
llm.method: ローバーを6つの放射面に分割した解析的熱モデルの開発、および真空環境での熱バランス試験による数値計算シミュレーションと検証。
llm.result: 予備熱解析の後、数値計算シミュレーションを実施し、真空環境での熱バランス試験によって設計の検証を行った。

2610.28122.title: De-Diffusing WAMs: Action-Sufficient Direct Prediction for Robot Control
2610.28122.abstract: Cascade world-action models (WAMs) use predicted visual futures to condition robot actions, but inherit costly iterative inference from diffusion-pretrained experts. We ask what a single-step predicted future must preserve to support accurate single-step action prediction. In the evaluated WAM, resampling video noise has little effect on downstream actions, yet naively truncating both streams to one step substantially reduces task success. Video-space supervision only partially closes this gap, and a local sensitivity analysis shows that vision prediction errors have highly unequal consequences for action accuracy. These findings motivate DirectWAM, which converts pretrained video and action experts into single-step predictors without stochastic sampling through action-sufficient distillation, while retaining the explicit future-to-action cascade. After learning a one-step action model, we train the future predictor by decoding actions from its own predicted futures and backpropagating demonstration action error through the expert, with an optional future-latent reconstruction loss. The resulting objective evaluates the student-generated future through its downstream control consequences rather than relying on representation matching alone. DirectWAM achieves 97.1% average success across four LIBERO suites and 85.4% on RoboTwin 2.0, outperforming Flash-WAM at the same one-evaluation-per-stream budget. This advantage has also extended to three real-world tasks that we designed. Compared with the full iterative teacher, it reduces inference latency by $28.0\times$.
2610.28122.tldr_en: DirectWAM, which converts pretrained video and action experts into single-step predictors without stochastic sampling through action-sufficient distillation, while retaining the explicit future-to-action cascade, achieves 97.1% average success across four LIBERO suites and 85.4% on RoboTwin 2.0.

llm.title_ja: De-Diffusing WAMs: ロボット制御のための行動十分な直接予測
llm.tldr_ja: DirectWAMは、確率的サンプリングを伴わずに事前学習されたビデオおよびアクション専門家を1ステップ予測器に変換し、LIBEROスイート全体で平均97.1%の成功率を達成する。
llm.problem: カスケード型世界・行動モデル（WAMs）は予測された視覚的未来を用いてロボット行動を条件付けるが、拡散モデルに基づく専門家による高コストな反復推論を受け継いでしまうこと。
llm.method: 行動十分な蒸留を通じて確率的サンプリングなしで事前学習されたビデオおよびアクションの専門家を1ステップ予測器に変換するDirectWAMの提案。
llm.result: 4つのLIBEROスイートで平均97.1%の成功率を達成し、完全な反復的教師モデルと比較して推論レイテンシを28.0倍に削減した。

2610.28121.title: Interruption-Aware Recurrent Reinforcement Learning for UAS Navigation Under Temporary Overrides
2610.28121.abstract: Safe autonomous navigation of UASs requires tactical deconfliction to address conflicts that strategic coordination cannot prevent. This task is challenging under partial observability, when sensor or traffic data are missing, delayed, or degraded. Geometry-based methods can offer separation assurances but face limitations in dense encounters. Recurrent reinforcement learning has therefore been proposed to learn navigation policies that integrate observation-action histories to optimise long-term safety-efficiency trade-offs. However, operational safeguards may require a remote pilot, onboard detect-and-avoid system, or runtime assurance mechanism to temporarily override the learned policy. A research gap remains in understanding how these interruptions affect recurrent policies when the agent regains authority. Benchmark evidence shows that interruptions make task variables less decodable from the recurrent hidden state and increase post-interruption collision risk. The findings suggest that altered recurrent context prolongs post-handback degradation through an action-observation feedback loop, in which changed actions alter the flight path and subsequent recurrent updates. To address this vulnerability, we propose three interruption-aware architectures that condition recurrent processing on interruption context through separate feature streams, dedicated interruption memory, or gated environmental features. Across simulations, all three architectures preserve more decodable task information than a standard recurrent policy. Moreover, the strongest architecture reduces post-interruption collisions by 74% and interruption-induced mission failures by 69% relative to the recurrent baseline, without degrading interruption-free performance. These results show that safe interruption does not guarantee safe handback, and support interruption-aware recurrent design for resilient UAS autonomy.
2610.28121.comment: This work has been submitted to IEEE for possible publication
2610.28121.tldr_en: The results show that safe interruption does not guarantee safe handback, and support interruption-aware recurrent design for resilient UAS autonomy, and propose three interruption-aware architectures that condition recurrent processing on interruption context through separate feature streams, dedicated interruption memory, or gated environmental features.

llm.title_ja: 一時的なオーバーライド下におけるUASナビゲーションのための割り込み認識型反復強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、割り込みが反復ポリシーに与える悪影響を分析し、別個の特性ストリームや専用の割り込みメモリを用いた3つの割り込み認識型アーキテクチャを提案する。
llm.problem: 運用上の安全保障としてリモートパイロット等による学習済みポリシーの一時的なオーバーライドが必要となる場合があり、その割り込みが反復ポリシーに与える影響が十分に理解されていないこと。
llm.method: 割り込みコンテキストに基づいて反復処理を条件付ける3つの割り込み認識型アーキテクチャ（別個の特性ストリーム、専用の割り込みメモリ、またはゲート付き環境特性）の提案。
llm.result: 全ての提案アーキテクチャが標準的な反復ポリシーと比較してタスク情報をより多く保持し、最強のアーキテクチャはポスト中断衝突を74%削減した。

2610.28109.title: FIT-MAC: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Robust Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.28109.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong performance on standard robotic manipulation benchmarks. However, their reliability can degrade substantially when task conditions deviate from the nominal setting. Perturbations in object positions and task instructions may lead to complete task failure. Existing VLA policies generally lack an explicit runtime mechanism for distinguishing these failure modes and selecting an appropriate recovery strategy. To systematically mitigate this issue, we propose FIT-MAC, a failure-aware, closed-loop multi-agent control framework for improving the robustness of VLA policies at inference time. FIT-MAC augments a VLA policy with an inference-time control layer. First, the Planner Agent parses the language instruction into a structured task specification that captures the manipulation goal and spatial constraints, and the Grounder Agent resolves each instruction-level reference to a visual target. Next, the Verifier Agent tracks phase-specific execution progress, distinguishes target-binding errors from local execution failures, and determines whether intervention is warranted. The Correction Agent then routes permitted interventions to target rebinding or bounded grasping or placement recovery, depending on the failure type. When no intervention is required, the pretrained VLA remains the default action generator. Extensive experiments on LIBERO-PRO demonstrate that FIT-MAC improves robustness across multiple VLA backbones, consistently increasing success rates and achieving state-of-the-art performance under diverse perturbations.
2610.28109.tldr_en: FIT-MAC is proposed, a failure-aware, closed-loop multi-agent control framework for improving the robustness of VLA policies at inference time, and it is demonstrated that FIT-MAC improves robustness across multiple VLA backbones, consistently increasing success rates and achieving state-of-the-art performance under diverse perturbations.

llm.title_ja: FIT-MAC: 堅牢な視覚言語行動モデルのための閉ループ型マルチエージェントフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: FIT-MACは、VLAポリシーの推論時における堅牢性を向上させるための失敗認識型閉ループマルチエージェント制御フレームワークであり、多様な摂動下で成功率を向上させる。
llm.problem: 視覚言語行動（VLA）モデルは標準的なロボットマニピュレーションで高い性能を達成しているが、オブジェクトの位置や指示の摂動により信頼性が大幅に低下すること。
llm.method: プランナーエージェント、グラウンダーエージェント、ベリファイアエージェント、および補正エージェントから構成される推論時制御レイヤーを用いたFIT-MACフレームワークの提案。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROを用いた広範な実験により、複数のVLAバックボーンにおける堅牢性が向上し、多様な摂動下で最先端の性能を達成した。

2610.28106.title: Temporal Difference Learning of Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Value Functions
2610.28106.abstract: Reach-avoid sets, defining the states from which a task can be completed while avoiding unsafe regions, are fundamental tools for deploying robots in environments subject to disturbances and uncertainty, as well as for runtime task-feasibility monitoring, allowing prediction of whether a state is safe and will lead to successful task completion. Classical Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability (HJR) and its recent neural extensions (e.g., Lipschitz Continuous Reachability Learning, DeepReach) treat disturbances adversarially, computing the reach-avoid set under worst-case disturbances from a bounded set. This guarantees safety but can yield overly conservative sets when disturbances are stochastic rather than adversarial, and additionally requires the disturbance set to be known or specified in advance. We propose Probabilistic reach-avoid Value Function (PVF), a self-supervised method, applicable to black-box systems, for computing reach-avoid sets as the states with a certain reach-avoid probability under stochastic, potentially unbounded disturbances. We evaluate our approach against HJR-based baselines on systems of increasing complexity, up to a Hopper locomotion task, and show that our probabilistic sets are less conservative and more accurate than adversarial HJR sets when disturbances are non-adversarial.
2610.28106.tldr_en: Probabilistic reach-avoid Value Function (PVF), a self-supervised method, applicable to black-box systems, for computing reach-avoid sets as the states with a certain reach-avoid probability under stochastic, potentially unbounded disturbances is proposed.

llm.title_ja: 確率的到達回避バリュー関数の時間差学習
llm.tldr_ja: PVFは、ブラックボックスシステムに適用可能な自己教師あり学習手法であり、確率的かつ非有界な外乱の下での到達回避セットを計算する。
llm.problem: 古典的なハミルトン・ジャコビ到達可能性（HJR）とそのニューラル拡張は外乱を敵対的に扱うため、外乱が確率的である場合に過度に保守的なセットになってしまうこと。
llm.method: 確率的かつ潜在的に非有界な外乱の下で特定の到達回避確率を持つ状態として到達回避セットを計算する自己教師あり手法「PVF」の提案。
llm.result: Hopper歩行タスクに至るまでの複雑なシステムにおいて、非敵対的外乱の下でHJRベースのベースラインよりも保守的でなく正確な確率的セットが得られることを示した。

2610.28092.title: BAIT: Can LLMs Find What Biases a Reader? A Benchmark for Cognitive Bias Triggers in News
2610.28092.abstract: Persuasive writing exploits cognitive biases, recruiting a reader's mental shortcuts to shape belief, often without the reader noticing. We call the linguistic features exploiting such mental shortcuts cognitive bias triggers. As large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people encounter news, summarizing it, ranking it, and answering questions over it, a natural question is whether they can recognize the features of a text that bias a human reader. We introduce BAIT (Bias Annotation In Text), a resource for detecting cognitive bias triggers in news. BAIT pairs a schema of nine triggers, each specified in an annotator codebook, with 50 English news articles annotated by trained annotators at the article and span levels and adjudicated into a gold standard. On this data we define two tasks, detecting which triggers a text contains and locating the spans that carry them. We then benchmark six frontier LLMs zero-shot and with three or ten in-context examples. The models approach human agreement on which triggers an article contains, but rarely recover its full set of triggers, and they reach less than half of human agreement in locating the passages that carry them. Moreover, they over-predict triggers that come with easy surface cues, and most of the passages they mark for these triggers are not triggers, yet carry the trigger's surface cue far more often than random text. These findings suggest that the evaluated LLMs respond to surface cues rather than to the mechanisms that make a passage manipulative. We release the schema, the codebook, standoff annotations, and the evaluation pipeline.
2610.28092.tldr_en: It is suggested that the evaluated LLMs respond to surface cues rather than to the mechanisms that make a passage manipulative, which would suggest that the evaluated LLMs respond to surface cues rather than to the mechanisms that make a passage manipulative.

llm.title_ja: BAIT：LLMは読者のバイアスを見つけられるか？ニュースにおける認知的バイアートリガーのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: BAITはニュース記事内の認知的バイアートリガーを検出するためのリソースであり、LLMが操作的なメカニズムではなく表面的な手がかりに応答していることを示している。
llm.problem: 説得的な文章は認知的バイアスを利用して読者の信念を形成するが、大規模言語モデルが人間の読者にバイアスを与えるテキストの特徴を認識できるかどうかは不明であること。
llm.method: 9種類のトリガーからなるスキーマと、専門家によりアノテーションされた50の英語ニュース記事からなるデータセット「BAIT」の構築と、フロンティアLLMのゼロショット・インコンテキスト学習評価。
llm.result: モデルは記事に含まれるトリガーの検知において人間の合意に近づくものの、パスワードの正確な位置特定には至らず、表面的な手がかりに過剰反応することが示された。

2610.28074.title: Slot-JEPA: Object-Structured Prediction Interfaces for Latent World Models
2610.28074.abstract: As a prototypical latent world model, Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) provide strong semantic representations. However, dense patch representations expose a redundant interface to downstream predictors, which must implicitly infer spatial organization and temporal correspondence, presenting three challenges. First, object information is distributed across patches, forcing each downstream predictor to redundantly recover object structure that could otherwise be reused across tasks before modeling interactions. Second, the lack of explicit entity correspondence across time makes historical transitions expensive, restricting the predictor's flexibility in utilizing context. Third, without explicit transport structure, existing JEPA models typically use pointwise l1/l2 distances, which are insensitive to spatial displacement when predicted and goal supports are largely disjoint. We propose the Slot-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Slot-JEPA), which decomposes dense representations into stable semantic slots and time-varying spatial masks. Pretrained once and frozen downstream, this decomposition exposes a reusable object-structured interface. Building on it, our Transition Memory Predictor (TMP) stores visual transitions as compact masks and retrieves useful context using statistics of corresponding slots. Its two branches separate slot-specific dynamics from shared cross-slot dynamics. We further use Unbalanced Optimal Transport (UOT) to supervise mask prediction and evaluate candidate plans by transporting mass between aligned predicted and goal masks, providing a signal better aligned with spatial progress. Across seven visual-understanding benchmarks, the slot-reconstructed features remain transferable. Slot-JEPA also improves goal-conditioned planning across six planar environments and four robotic arm planning tasks on the REALM-JEPA benchmark.
2610.28074.tldr_en: The Slot-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Slot-JEPA) is proposed, which decomposes dense representations into stable semantic slots and time-varying spatial masks and improves goal-conditioned planning across six planar environments and four robotic arm planning tasks on the REALM-JEPA benchmark.
2610.28074.hf_summary_en: Slot-JEPA decomposes dense representations into reusable semantic slots and spatial masks to improve predictive modeling, planning, and transfer across visual tasks.

llm.title_ja: Slot-JEPA: 潜在的世界モデルのためのオブジェクト構造化予測インターフェース
llm.tldr_ja: Slot-JEPAは、密な表現を安定したセマンティック・スロットと時間変動する空間マスクに分解し、計画性能を向上させるオブジェクト構造化インターフェースを提供する。
llm.problem: 潜在的世界モデルとしてのJEPAの密なパッチ表現は、ダウンストリームの予測器に対して冗長なインターフェースを露出させ、空間組織と時間的対応関係の推論を困難にしていること。
llm.method: 密な表現を安定したセマンティック・スロットと時間変動する空間マスクに分解し、遷移メモリ予測器（TMP）と非平衡最適輸送を用いるSlot-JEPAの提案。
llm.result: 7つの視覚理解ベンチマークにおいて特徴の転移性を維持し、複数の平面環境やロボットアームの計画タスクでゴール条件付き計画性能を向上させた。

2610.28701.title: Real-Time Ground Normal Vector Estimation for Spherical Mobile 3D Mapping using LiDAR-Inertial Odometry
2610.28701.abstract: Accurate ground plane normal estimation is essential for odometry in spherical mobile mapping systems (SMMS), which face challenges from rapid rotations and limited ground coverage. We propose two RANSAC-based approaches: single-scan estimation with normal vector scoring and multi-step validation, and LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO)-based estimation using a global 3D map. Evaluated across diverse real-world datasets against terrestrial laser scanner ground truth, results show that LIO-based estimation significantly outperforms single-scan methods in accuracy and robustness. Integrating ground normal estimates into the motion model improves pose estimation, supporting autonomous navigation in challenging and hazardous environments.
2610.28701.comment: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Automation in Space (i-SAIRAS 26)
2610.28701.tldr_en: Two RANSAC-based approaches are proposed: single-scan estimation with normal vector scoring and multi-step validation, and LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO)-based estimation using a global 3D map, which shows that LIO-based estimation significantly outperforms single-scan methods in accuracy and robustness.

llm.title_ja: LiDAR慣性オドメトリを用いた球面移動3Dマッピングのためのリアルタイム地表面法線ベクトル推定
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、2つのRANSACベースのアプローチを提案し、LIOベースの推定が単一スキャン法と比較して精度と堅牢性において大幅に優れていることを示した。
llm.problem: 球面移動マッピングシステム（SMMS）におけるオドメトリは、急速な回転と限定された地面カバレッジのために正確な地面平面法線推定が困難であること。
llm.method: 正規ベクトルスコアリングと多段階検証を行う単一スキャン推定と、グローバル3Dマップを使用するLiDAR慣性オドメトリ（LIO）ベースの推定という2つのRANSACベースアプローチの提案。
llm.result: 多様な実世界データセットでの評価により、LIOベースの推定が単一スキャン法よりも精度と堅牢性において大幅に優れていることが示された。

2610.28699.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
2610.28699.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.
2610.28699.tldr_en: This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications, and identifies recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems.

2610.28698.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
2610.28698.abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. Our results show: (1) more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity improves transfer to related worlds with limited gains in distant worlds, and model size improves data efficiency but generalizes worse to distant worlds under single-world training; (2) we observe an early interface phase with broad cross-world benefits and a later world phase with gains narrowed to in-corpus and related worlds, and fit an empirical scaling law relating validation loss to data volume, diversity and model size; and (3) our models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds, and perform best in real-time settings. However, the limits of imitation and persistent gaps in distant worlds suggest that building generalist embodied agents requires richer training stages beyond continued pre-training.
2610.28698.tldr_en: The limits of imitation and persistent gaps in distant worlds suggest that building generalist embodied agents requires richer training stages beyond continued pre-training, and the authors' models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds, and perform best in real-time settings.
2610.28698.hf_summary_en: Continued pre-training across data scale, diversity, and model size improves embodied learning in virtual worlds but reveals limits in distant-world generalization, motivating richer training beyond imitation.

llm.title_ja: ゲームにおけるスケーリング: 多様な仮想世界における身体性エージェントのための継続的事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: 継続的事前学習におけるデータ量、多様性、モデルサイズの3つの軸に関する制御された研究を行い、一般化性能とスケーリング則を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 物理環境における身体性学習の向上のゲインが、異なる視覚スタイルやダイナミクスを持つ仮想世界にも拡張できるかどうかは不明確である。
llm.method: 0.8Bから27Bまでの4つのモデルサイズ、50〜1,600時間の6つのデータ予算、5つの混合データを用いた120の訓練設定による継続的事前学習（CPT）の制御スタディを実施する。
llm.result: データ量の増加はインコーパス性能を向上させ、多様性は関連する世界への転移を改善することを示し、検証損失に関する経験的スケーリング則を導出した。

2610.28019.title: PACT-VLA: Speculative Action-Chunk Verification with Pre-Commit Observations
2610.28019.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are commonly deployed with asynchronous inference in real-world settings, where the next action chunk is generated while the robot is still executing the previous one. By the time the new chunk is committed, the robot and scene have changed, so the chunk is conditioned on a stale observation and task success drops sharply as this inference delay grows. Generating multiple candidate chunks could let newer observations inform the final choice, but existing multi-candidate methods either rank candidates with the stale inference-start observation or repeatedly switch between candidates during execution, which can make the executed action sequence discontinuous. Our key insight is that inference delay can be used as decision time. While candidate generation is still underway, candidate selection can reuse the VLA itself to choose the complete action chunk that best fits a later observation. We propose PACT-VLA, a training-free framework that generates candidates from the inference-start observation and selects one using this pre-commit observation. Its scoring function, FlowRes, measures the residual between each candidate's implied flow direction and the velocity predicted by the frozen policy under the pre-commit observation, requiring no separate verifier. A pipelined implementation overlaps observation processing with candidate generation and batches scoring, so selection adds no control-step delay on the evaluated hardware. At a four-step delay, PACT-VLA improves average success by 15.0 percentage points over RTC on Kinetix and by 5.2 points over single-candidate asynchronous execution with GR00T N1.7 on LIBERO, and it further improves existing delay-robust methods. On three real-robot tasks, it raises average success from 60% to 82% over naive asynchronous execution with the same frozen $π_{0.5}$ checkpoint.
2610.28019.tldr_en: PACT-VLA is a training-free framework that generates candidates from the inference-start observation and selects one using this pre-commit observation, requiring no separate verifier, and improves existing delay-robust methods.

llm.title_ja: PACT-VLA: プレコミット観測を用いた推論的アクションチャンク検証
llm.tldr_ja: 推論遅延を意思決定時間として活用し、追加の検証器なしで事後観測に最も適合する完全なアクションチャンクを選択するトレーニング不要のフレームワーク「PACT-VLA」を提案した。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーを非同期推論でデプロイする場合、推論遅延の間にロボットやシーンが変化するため、古い観測に条件付けられたチャンクにより成功率が急激に低下する。
llm.method: 推論開始時の観測から複数の候補を生成し、事前コミット観測下の凍結ポリシーが予測する速度との残差を測るスコアリング関数を用いて最適なチャンクを選択する。
llm.result: 4ステップの遅延において、KinetixでRTCを15.0ポイント、LIBEROでGR00T N1.7を用いた非同期実行を5.2ポイント上回り、実ロボットでも成功率を向上させた。

2610.28011.title: Knowing When to Stop Thinking: A Dissection of Expected Free Energy as a Test-Time Compute Controller for Latent World-Model Planning
2610.28011.abstract: A planner using a learned world model can improve its predicted outcome while choosing a worse action. We study when expected free energy (EFE) can help decide how much computation to spend on a plan. An EFE-inspired objective combines goal distance with disagreement among stochastic predictions. We test candidate scoring, stopping, and online predictor updates separately. Stopping when elite cost stalls reduces refinement on tasks whose success plateaus with depth, with mean success close to fixed-depth references. At the larger tested weights, rewarding disagreement lowers success with a frozen model. Penalizing it helps at some task and weight settings but harms others. When training data omit a region needed to reach the goal, online updates recover part of the resulting loss. The tested cost-stall rule can fail when further optimization exploits model errors, because predicted cost keeps falling after task success peaks.
