Cost progress can guide computation on a plateau, but protecting performance after a peak requires information about the consequences of the chosen actions.
2610.28011.tldr_en: This work studies when expected free energy (EFE) can help decide how much computation to spend on a plan, and an EFE-inspired objective combines goal distance with disagreement among stochastic predictions.

llm.title_ja: 思考を停止すべきタイミングを知る: 潜在世界モデル計画におけるテスト時計算量コントローラとしての期待自由エネルギーの分析
llm.tldr_ja: 期待自由エネルギー（EFE）に基づく目的関数を用いて、計画にどの程度の計算量を費やすべきかを決定する方法を検討し、停止ルールや不確実性報酬の影響を分析した。
llm.method: ゴール距離と確率的予測間の不一致を組み合わせたEFEインスパイアの目的関数を用い、候補のスコアリング、停止、オンライン予測器の更新を個別にテストする。
llm.result: エリートコストの停滞時に停止することで、深さに対する成功率がプラトーに達するタスクにおいて計算量を削減しつつ、固定深度の参照値に近い成功率を維持した。

2610.27998.title: LocoPilot: Single-Operator Bilateral Teleoperation for Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning
2610.27998.abstract: Learning loco-manipulation policies requires demonstrations that capture coordinated base and arm motion on the target embodiment. Robot-free interfaces allow demonstrations to be collected independently of the target robot, increasing flexibility but without directly capturing platform-specific commands, proprioception, and body-mounted observations. On-robot teleoperation allows to capture these signals directly, but requires an interface capable of commanding the complete system concurrently. This paper presents LocoPilot, a single-operator bilateral teleoperation and data-collection framework implemented on a 12-DoF Unitree Go2 quadruped equipped with a 6-DoF AgileX Piper L manipulator, an Intel RealSense D435 wrist camera, and an Intel RealSense D405 head camera. A second 6-DoF Piper L arm, used as the leader and two handheld controllers provide simultaneous control of the base, body posture, manipulator, and gripper. The follower arm interaction forces are estimated without a dedicated force/torque sensor and rendered to the operator through a passivity-constrained haptic channel. A ROS~2 pipeline records synchronized multimodal observations together with a unified 11D action shared by teleoperation and policy deployment. Compared to prior work, LocoPilot uniquely unifies robot-in-the-loop legged data collection, force feedback without motion-capture instrumentation, and the same action interface at deployment. We evaluate the interface across multiple loco-manipulation tasks and validate the complete collection-to-deployment pipeline by fine-tuning MolmoAct2 \cite{MOLMO} on pick-and-place demonstrations and deploying on the physical robot without action retargeting or additional inverse kinematics. Code available at: https://github.com/iit-DLSLab/LocoPilot
2610.27998.tldr_en: LocoPilot uniquely unifies robot-in-the-loop legged data collection, force feedback without motion-capture instrumentation, and the same action interface at deployment and evaluates the interface across multiple loco-manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: LocoPilot: ロコマニピュレーションポリシー学習のための単一オペレータ双方向テレオペレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 4足歩行ロボットとマニピュレータを同時に制御し、力フィードバックとロボット内蔵データ収集を統合した単一オペレータ向けの双方向テレオペレーションフレームワーク「LocoPilot」を提案した。
llm.problem: ロコマニピュレーションポリシーの学習には、対象のロボットにおける協調的なベースとアームの動きを捉えたデモンストレーションが必要となる。
llm.method: 2つの6軸マニピュレータ（1つをリーダー、もう1つをフォロワーとして利用）とハンドヘルドコントローラを組み合わせ、受動性制約付きハプティックチャネルを介して力フィードバックを提示する。
llm.result: 複数のロコマニピュレーションタスクでインターフェースを評価し、追加の逆運動学や再ターゲットなしでMolmoAct2を実機に直接デプロイすることに成功した。
keywords_ja: ロコマニピュレーション

2610.27995.title: Learning Tactile-Aware Hand Representations from Human Hand-Object Interaction Data
2610.27995.abstract: Tactile representation learning for dexterous manipulation often requires substantial robot-side data collection, limiting its scalability across different hands and sensors. We explore whether large-scale human hand-object interaction (HOI) data can provide a useful prior for robotic tactile learning. To this end, we propose HuTact, a framework that pretrains tactile-aware hand representations from human HOI data without requiring real tactile signals during pretraining. HuTact transfers the interaction structure learned from human hand motions to robotic tactile observations and can be further adapted with a small amount of unlabeled robot interaction data. We evaluate HuTact on tactile perception and manipulation tasks, including grasp prediction, slip detection, object classification, and tactile-conditioned policy learning. Across these tasks, human HOI pretraining improves data efficiency and provides a strong initialization for downstream learning. Notably, with HOI pretraining followed by midtraining on unlabeled robot play data, HuTact achieves 88.26% Macro-F1 on grasp prediction using only 25\% of the labeled downstream data, comparable to training from scratch on the full labeled dataset (88.23%). These results suggest that human interaction data can serve as a scalable complementary source for robotic tactile representation learning.
2610.27995.tldr_en: The proposed HuTact framework, a framework that pretrains tactile-aware hand representations from human HOI data without requiring real tactile signals during pretraining, suggests that human interaction data can serve as a scalable complementary source for robotic tactile representation learning.

llm.title_ja: 人間手・物体インタラクションデータからの触覚認識手表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 実際の触覚信号を必要とせずに人間の手・物体インタラクション（HOI）データから触覚認識手表現を事前学習するフレームワーク「HuTact」を提案し、データ効率の向上を示した。
llm.problem: 器用な操作のための触覚表現学習はロボット側での多大なデータ収集を必要とし、異なる手やセンサへのスケーラビリティが制限される。
llm.method: 人間の手動作から学習したインタラクション構造をロボットの触覚観測に転移し、少量の未ラベルのロボットインタラクションデータで適応させる「HuTact」フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: ロボットプレイデータのミッドトレーニングを伴うHOI事前学習により、全ラベル付きデータの25%のみを使用して、完全なデータセットでゼロから訓練した場合に匹敵する88.26%のマクロF1を達成した。
keywords_ja: 人間の手・物体インタラクション

2610.27974.title: Media Intelligence Platform: Multimodal Detection of Synthetic and Manipulated Content
2610.27974.abstract: The rapid progress of generative artificial intelligence has led to a significant increase in manipulated multimedia content, including synthetic faces, forged videos, AI-generated images, fake audio, and locally edited images. Existing detection approaches are typically designed for a single manipulation type, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios involving heterogeneous media sources. In this work, we present the Media Intelligence Platform (MIP), a unified web-based framework for multimodal media forensics integrating specialized modules for fake video detection, face morphing detection, AI-generated image detection, audio deepfake detection, localized image manipulation detection, and text analysis. Its modular architecture enables flexible integration of heterogeneous models and supports future extensions for emerging manipulation techniques. Experimental results on representative benchmark datasets demonstrate reliable detection performance across multiple media modalities while providing a practical and user-friendly interface for forensic investigations. The platform highlights the potential of unified multimodal systems for comprehensive deepfake detection in real-world environments, and is accompanied by a public demonstrator released with this workshop submission to support reproducibility and community evaluation.
2610.27974.comment: ECCV 2026, Workshop on AI for Multimedia Forensics & Disinformation Detection (AI4MFDD2026)
2610.27974.tldr_en: The Media Intelligence Platform is presented, a unified web-based framework for multimodal media forensics integrating specialized modules for fake video detection, face morphing detection, AI-generated image detection, audio deepfake detection, localized image manipulation detection, and text analysis.

llm.title_ja: メディアインテリジェンスプラットフォーム: 合成・操作コンテンツのマルチモーダル検出
llm.tldr_ja: フェイク動画検出、顔モーフ検出、AI生成画像検出、音声ディープフェイク検出などを統合した統一されたウェブベースのマルチモーダルメディアフォレンジックフレームワーク「Media Intelligence Platform（MIP）」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の検出アプローチは単一の操作タイプ向けに設計されていることが多く、異種メディアソースが関わる実世界のシナリオでの適用性が制限される。
llm.method: 偽動画、顔モーフ、AI生成画像、音声ディープフェイク、局所的画像操作、テキスト分析の各専門モジュールを統合したモジュラー型のウェブベースのフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 代表的なベンチマークデータセットにおける実験により、複数のメディアモダリティにわたって信頼性の高い検出性能を示した。
keywords_ja: メディアフォレンジック
ディープフェイク検出

2610.28696.title: PCLA-Bridge: A Framework for Cross-Domain Deployment of CARLA Agents
2610.28696.abstract: Most high-performing end-to-end autonomous driving agents (ADAs) are developed for the CARLA Leaderboard, tightly coupling them to CARLA's APIs, sensor layouts, coordinate systems, and internal clock. Reusing these models on real datasets, alternative simulators, or physical platforms necessitates substantial manual re-engineering. We present PCLA-Bridge, a deployable tool that runs unmodified CARLA Leaderboard agents from any sensor source to any control destination without an active CARLA server. With PCLA-Bridge handling dependency isolation, tensor marshalling, routing, and synthetic timing, integrators only need to provide a minimal interface. We validate the tool across two operational paradigms: offline replay on in-domain CARLA recordings and real-world nuScenes logs, and live closed-loop control across three diverse simulation engines: MetaDrive, AWSIM, and AlpaSim. We analyze the lightweight integration requirements for each platform, highlighting output translation (such as converting agent actions into target trajectory formats) and coordinate-frame transformations, showing that integration requires minimal glue code rather than structural changes. All eight evaluated agents execute across all three simulators without modification, confirming the reliability of PCLA-Bridge and establishing a foundation for systematic sim-to-real, cross-sim, and security testing.
2610.28696.tldr_en: PCLA-Bridge is presented, a deployable tool that runs unmodified CARLA Leaderboard agents from any sensor source to any control destination without an active CARLA server, establishing a foundation for systematic sim-to-real, cross-sim, and security testing.

llm.title_ja: PCLA-Bridge: CARLAエージェントのクロスドメインデプロイメントのためのフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: アクティブなCARLAサーバなしで任意のセンサソースから任意の制御先へ未変更のCARLAエージェントを実行できるツール「PCLA-Bridge」を提案し、シム2レアル等のテストの基盤を確立した。
llm.problem: 高性能なエンドツーエンド自動運転エージェントはCARLAリーダーボード用に開発されており、CARLAのAPIや内部クロックに強く結びついているため、再利用には手動での再エンジニアリングが必要となる。
llm.method: 依存関係の分離、テンソルマーシャリング、ルーティング、合成タイミングを処理し、最小限のインターフェースを提供するデプロイ可能なツールを実装する。
llm.result: オフライン再生およびMetaDrive、AWSIM、AlpaSimの3つのシミュレータでのライブ閉ループ制御を通じて、すべての評価エージェントが修正なしで実行できることを確認した。
keywords_ja: エージェントデプロイ

2610.27946.title: Decoupling Action from Egocentric Observation for World Simulation
2610.27946.abstract: Egocentric action transfer aims to decouple the semantic action from egocentric observations and reproduce them in new visual contexts, enabling scalable world simulation, embodied policy learning, and robotic data generation. Existing approaches to transferring actions rely on condition-guided video generation, which converts the observation video into explicit geometric controls (e.g., hand poses or meshes) to drive synthesis. However, these methods introduce geometric estimation errors, making it difficult to preserve physically plausible interactions when transferred to new scenes. Alternatively, motion transfer methods directly extract motion patterns from the observation video, yet motion-level features alone cannot encode rich contact dynamics, frequently leading to severe hand structural collapse and implausible contact layout. To address both limitations, we present EgoACT, a test-time framework for egocentric action transfer that operates directly on the denoising process of video diffusion models without requiring additional geometric estimators. EgoACT uses Velocity-guided Structure Anchoring to stabilize reference-consistent hand-object structure in the early denoising stage, and Sparse Correspondence Calibration to refine reliable local correspondences in the mid-to-late denoising stages. Together, these two components preserve transferable action semantics while improving temporal coherence and interaction realism. We further establish EgoActionBench, a benchmark for evaluating action preservation, visual quality, and hand-object plausibility across diverse egocentric manipulation scenarios. Experiments show that EgoACT generates more coherent and physically plausible interaction videos than strong baselines.
2610.27946.comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026, Project page: https://ego-act.github.io/, Code: https://github.com/mayuelala/EgoACT
2610.27946.tldr_en: EgoACT is presented, a test-time framework for egocentric action transfer that operates directly on the denoising process of video diffusion models without requiring additional geometric estimators, and establishes EgoActionBench, a benchmark for evaluating action preservation, visual quality, and hand-object plausibility across diverse egocentric manipulation scenarios.

llm.title_ja: ワールドシミュレーションに向けたエゴセントリック観測からのアクションの分離
llm.tldr_ja: 幾何学的推定器を必要とせず、動画拡散モデルのノイズ除去プロセス上で直接動作するエゴセントリックアクション転移のためのテスト時フレームワーク「EgoACT」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のアクション転移手法は幾何学的推定エラーを持ち物理的に妥当なインタラクションの保持が困難であるか、モーション特徴だけで豊かな接触ダイナミクスをエンコードできない。
llm.method: 初期ノイズ除去段階で参照一貫性のある手・物体構造を安定させる「速度誘導構造アンカリング」と、中後期段階で局所的対応を洗練する「スパース対応キャリブレーション」を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 新たに確立したベンチマーク「EgoActionBench」において、従来の手口よりも一貫性があり物理的に妥当なインタラクション動画を生成することを実証した。
keywords_ja: ワールドシミュレーション
エゴセントリック視点

2610.27917.title: EventSync: Event-Driven Memory Updates for History-Dependent Manipulation
2610.27917.abstract: History-dependent robotic manipulation requires task context and interaction history, as the current observation alone is insufficient to determine the next action. Hierarchical frameworks use task memory for high-level subgoal reasoning and low-level policies for execution. However, memory updates require accurate completion assessment: similar observations may correspond to different execution phases, and prematurely recording completion can mislead subsequent subgoal reasoning. We present EventSync, a hierarchical framework that coordinates task reasoning and action execution through event-driven memory updates. A vision-language model generates subgoals from task plans and interaction history, while a vision-language-action model executes them. A lightweight Event Monitor combines visual observations with end-effector trajectories to determine whether the current subgoal is complete. The framework records the current subgoal in its completed-subgoal history and triggers subsequent reasoning only after obtaining completion evidence. With visual history in the executor, EventSync achieves 64.5% overall success on RoboMME, exceeding the best baseline reported in the benchmark by 20.0 percentage points. Further analysis shows that this update mechanism helps build a reliable completed-subgoal history. Experiments on four real-robot tasks with different memory requirements validate the framework's effectiveness in real-world robotic manipulation.
2610.27917.tldr_en: This work presents EventSync, a hierarchical framework that coordinates task reasoning and action execution through event-driven memory updates and shows that this update mechanism helps build a reliable completed-subgoal history.

llm.title_ja: EventSync: 履歴依存操作のためのイベント駆動型メモリ更新
llm.tldr_ja: イベント駆動型のメモリ更新を通じてタスク推論と行動実行を調整する階層型フレームワーク「EventSync」を提案し、信頼性の高い完了済みサブゴール履歴の構築を実証した。
llm.problem: 履歴依存ロボット操作において、類似した観測が異なる実行フェーズに対応する場合があり、早すぎる完了記録は後続のサブゴール推論を誤導する。
llm.method: VLMがタスクプランからサブゴールを生成し、VLAがそれを実行する中で、視覚観測とエンドエフェクタ軌跡を組み合わせてサブゴールの完了を判断する軽量なイベントモニタを導入する。
llm.result: RoboMMEにおいて全体成功率64.5%を達成し、ベンチマークの最高ベースラインを20.0ポイント上回り、4つの実ロボットタスクで有効性を検証した。
keywords_ja: 階層型フレームワーク

2610.27907.title: What Novice Operators See Changes What the Policy Learns: A User Study of Keypoint Hand Visual Representation for Teleoperated Demonstration
2610.27907.abstract: Imitation learning increasingly relies on novice operators, whose demonstrations fall short of experts' in number and inter-trial consistency. Operators act on what they are shown, yet how the rendering of the robot affects their demonstrations, and the policies trained on them, has not been examined. We study this question with PointHand, a teleoperation interface that renders a multi-fingered robot hand as sparse keypoints at its fingertips and joints, the same keypoints a policy can observe. In a simulated mug-in-box task, 18 novices and 4 experts collected 2,200 trials under three renderings: the real shape of the hand, all keypoints emphasized, or the thumb and index finger alone emphasized. The novices shown the thumb and index finger emphasized collected 441 successful demonstrations from 600 trials, against 320 for those shown the real shape. We then trained diffusion policies on these demonstrations, replacing the scene point cloud and proprioceptive state they observe with the hand keypoints and two object keypoints. Within 400 steps these demonstrations went from the weakest of the three novice conditions under the point-cloud policy (46.3%) to the strongest under the keypoint policy (57.3%), a gain of +11.0 percentage points in all five seeds. Those collected with all keypoints emphasized changed by at most +0.7 percentage points, and in no more than three seeds. The value of a demonstration therefore depends on the rendering shown during collection and on what the policy observes together. A shared representation can pay off on both sides, in the number of successful demonstrations and in the success rate of the policy trained on them. Project page: https://omron-sinicx.github.io/point-hand/
2610.27907.tldr_en: The value of a demonstration depends on the rendering shown during collection and on what the policy observes together, and a shared representation can pay off on both sides, in the number of successful demonstrations and in the success rate of the policy trained on them.

llm.title_ja: 初心者のオペレータが見るものがポリシーの学習内容を変える: テテレポテーションデモンストレーションのためのキーポイント手視覚表現のユーザー調査
llm.tldr_ja: 親指と人差し指を強調してレンダリングするポイントハンドインターフェースを用いて、デモンストレーションの収集数と学習されたポリシーの成功率の両方を向上させられることを示した。
llm.problem: 模倣学習は初心者のオペレータに依存することが増えているが、ロボットのレンダリングがデモンストレーションや訓練されたポリシーに与える影響は検討されていない。
llm.method: ロボットの手を指先や関節のスパースキーポイントとしてレンダリングするポイントハンドインターフェースを用い、異なるレンダリング条件下での初心者のデモンストレーション収集と拡散ポリシーの訓練を行う。
llm.result: 親指と人差し指を強調した条件で収集されたデモンストレーションは、キーポイントポリシー下で57.3%の成功率（+11.0ポイントの向上）を達成した。

2610.27905.title: High-Precision RCM Motion for Ophthalmic Robotics via Hierarchical QP Control and Authority-Guided Recovery Planning
2610.27905.abstract: General-purpose manipulators can position ophthalmic instruments under a software Remote Centre of Motion (RCM). However, at some reachable configurations that are nonsingular for the tip task alone, the RCM and tip-tracking objectives conflict and the servo oscillates. We formalise this failure as a constraint-induced task singularity: the RCM-projected tip Jacobian loses rank while the unprojected tip Jacobian stays well conditioned. Thus, the effective tip authority collapses although the target remains reachable. We present a high-precision RCM servo architecture with built-in singularity recovery: for each commanded target, an authority-guided planner selects a well-conditioned arm configuration that reaches it and plans an RCM-consistent route, executed by a fixed hierarchical-QP controller. On a 200-scenario kinematic benchmark, the complete nominal-and-recovery protocol reaches 128/128 near-singular targets and 71/72 near-joint-limit targets (100% and 99%, respectively), with the software-RCM residual below 0.142 mm. On a physical 6-DOF arm it executes across four RCM entry points, with a worst-case kinematically reconstructed RCM residual of 178 μm and a median tip-regulation error of 32μm, within the 200μm control requirement adopted for the ophthalmic task.
2610.27905.tldr_en: This work presents a high-precision RCM servo architecture with built-in singularity recovery: for each commanded target, an authority-guided planner selects a well-conditioned arm configuration that reaches it and plans an RCM-consistent route, executed by a fixed hierarchical-QP controller.

llm.title_ja: 階層型QP制御と信頼度誘導型リカバリ計画を用いた眼科ロボットのための高精度RCM動作
llm.tldr_ja: 階層型QP制御と信頼度誘導型リカバリ計画を組み合わせた高精度RCMサーボアーキテクチャを提案し、特異点回避と高精度な追従を実現した。
llm.problem: RCMと先端追従の目的が競合し、特定の位置でサーボが振動する制約起因のタスク特異点が発生すること。
llm.method: 権限誘導型プランナーと固定された階層型QPコントローラーを組み合わせた、特異点リカバリ機能付き高精度RCMサーボアーキテクチャの提案。
llm.result: 200シナリオの運動学的ベンチマークで特異点ターゲットを100%近く達成し、実機の6自由度アームで中央値32μmの先端制御誤差を達成した。

2610.27894.title: Testing Associative Creativity in Humans and Multimodal LLMs with Difficult-to-Name Visual Stimuli
2610.27894.abstract: We investigate associative creativity in descriptions of abstract visual stimuli by humans and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). While conceptual association is central to human communication, it remains unclear how humans and models adapt when visual stimuli become increasingly difficult to map onto familiar semantic concepts. We evaluate several state-of-the-art MLLMs and human participants along two dimensions of creativity, originality and effectiveness, using two datasets with controlled manipulations of difficulty. SilCC varies naming difficulty through progressively more complex combinations of abstract shapes, and PixCC varies difficulty through increasing levels of random visual noise. Results show that humans produce more diverse associative descriptions than MLLMs, including greater semantic distance, higher entropy, and more novel expressions relative to reference lexica. As difficulty increases, effectiveness declines in SilCC, and humans increasingly shift from holistic associations to descriptions of low-level visual properties in PixCC.
2610.27894.tldr_en: Results show that humans produce more diverse associative descriptions than MLLMs, including greater semantic distance, higher entropy, and more novel expressions relative to reference lexica, as difficulty increases.

llm.title_ja: 困難な視覚刺激を用いた人間とマルチモーダルLLMにおける連想的創造性のテスト
llm.tldr_ja: 抽象的な視覚刺激の記述における人間とマルチモーダルLLMの連想的創造性を、命名の難易度を制御した2つのデータセットを用いて調査した。
llm.problem: 視覚刺激が馴染みのある意味概念へのマッピングが困難になった際、人間やモデルがどのように適応するか不明であること。
llm.method: 抽象的な形状の組み合わせやランダムな視覚的ノイズにより難易度を変化させた2つのデータセットを用い、複数の最先端MLLMと人間の参加者を評価する。
llm.result: 人間はMLLMと比較して、より多様な連想的記述、大きな意味的距離、高エントロピー、より斬新な表現を生み出すことが示された。

2610.27890.title: EndoWorld-JEPA: Motion-Guided Global-Local Latent World Modeling for Endoscopic Video Representation Learning
2610.27890.abstract: Endoscopic video contains state transitions induced by camera displacement, deformable tissue, and instrument interaction, yet existing pre-training methods treat dynamics implicitly. Inspired by action-conditioned joint-embedding predictive world models and by the observation that endoscopic optical flow contains both shared image-plane displacement and localized residual motion, we reformulate passive endoscopic video pre-training as causal motion-guided latent-state prediction. We present EndoWorld-JEPA, to our knowledge the first latent world-model pre-training framework designed for general-purpose endoscopic video representation learning. In place of recorded actions, calibrated poses, or robot kinematics, the model conditions prediction of the next latent state on motion observed up to the current state. Its Optical Motion-guided module separates dominant displacement from residual motion and converts the resulting evidence into an ordered temporal motion condition and spatial local-motion weights. Complementary global and motion-local predictors use these outputs: the temporal condition modulates both latent transitions, whereas the local weights define an auxiliary motion-local state that extends prediction from scene-level evolution to spatially selective dynamics. Patch-wise motion weighting emphasizes localized change while retaining anatomical context, and past-motion-window dropout randomly withholds the complete motion condition to reduce dependence on unreliable motion. This global--local formulation learns predictable visual--motion dynamics in representation space without reconstructing stochastic appearance artifacts. Evaluation shows that a common pre-trained checkpoint achieves strong transfer across four downstream benchmarks, supporting motion-guided global--local latent prediction as an effective pre-training paradigm for endoscopic video.
2610.27890.tldr_en: This work reformulates passive endoscopic video pre-training as causal motion-guided latent-state prediction as an effective pre-training paradigm for endoscopic video, and presents EndoWorld-JEPA, to their knowledge the first latent world-model pre-training framework designed for general-purpose endoscopic video representation learning.

llm.title_ja: EndoWorld-JEPA：内視鏡映像表現学習のための動き誘導型グローバル・ローカル潜在世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 内視鏡映像の受動的な事前学習を因果関係に基づく動き誘導型潜在状態予測として再定式化し、汎用的な EndoWorld-JEPA を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の事前学習方法は動的変化を暗黙的に扱っており、カメラの変位や組織の変形による状態遷移を明示的に捉えきれていないこと。
llm.method: 現在までの動きに基づいて次の潜在状態の予測を条件付けし、オプティカルフローから大域的変位と局所的残差を分離して処理する EndoWorld-JEPA の提案。
llm.result: 一般的な事前学習済みチェックポイントが、4つの下流ベンチマークにわたって強力な転移性能を達成することを示した。

2610.27877.title: Gaze2HOI: Gaze-Aware Intention Disambiguation for Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Forecasting
2610.27877.abstract: Anticipating how users will interact with their surroundings is essential for proactive systems that provide timely assistance in AR, VR, and embodied applications. Prior work typically forecasts hand-object interactions directly from historical observations, leaving intention and contact geometry implicit. However, similar observation histories can precede semantically or geometrically distinct futures. Inspired by behavioral evidence that gaze can provide early cues for underlying intention, we propose Gaze2HOI, a gaze-aware framework that formulates hand-object interaction forecasting as a hierarchical problem comprising intention inference, contact grounding, and coupled hand-object motion generation. Specifically, Gaze2HOI first weights gaze cues by fixation strength and recency, and uses them to modulate the visual representations of a vision-language model (VLM) through Temporal Gaze Saliency Modulation (TGSM), thereby reducing semantic ambiguity in intention inference. Subsequently, an Anticipatory Contact Grounding (ACG) module maps these structured intentions into explicit contact, support, and placement fields, effectively mitigating geometric ambiguity. Driven by these explicit conditions, a diffusion-based model jointly generates the 6-DoF object trajectories and future articulated motion of both hands. To evaluate Gaze2HOI, we further introduce EgoAIM, a phase-aware benchmark that organizes egocentric hand-object interactions into four phases defined by evolving hand-object relations and provides fine-grained intention annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Gaze2HOI achieves state-of-the-art performance in both intention inference and motion forecasting, even approaching oracle-level end-to-end performance in specific interaction phases. Project page: https://gaze2hoi.github.io/.
2610.27877.tldr_en: Gaze2HOI is proposed, a gaze-aware framework that formulates hand-object interaction forecasting as a hierarchical problem comprising intention inference, contact grounding, and coupled hand-object motion generation and achieves state-of-the-art performance in both intention inference and motion forecasting.

llm.title_ja: Gaze2HOI：一次視点の手・物体インタラクション予測のための視線認識型意図曖昧性解消
llm.tldr_ja: 視線を活用した階層的フレームワーク Gaze2HOI を提案し、意図の推論、接触のグラウンディング、手と物体の動作生成を統合して最先端の性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 従来のハンド・オブジェクト・インタラクション予測では意図や接触幾何学が暗黙的であり、類似した履歴から異なる未来が生じうる点。
llm.method: 視線の手がかりを固定強度と直近性で重み付けし、VLMの視覚表現を変調する時間的視線サルイディティ変調（TGSM）などの階層的モジュールを導入する。
llm.result: Gaze2HOIは意図推論と動作予測の両方で最先端の性能を達成し、特定のインタラクションフェーズではオラクル級の性能に近づいた。
keywords_ja: 人・物体インタラクション

2610.27870.title: Enumeration-Guided Training of Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Safety Certificates
2610.27870.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis offers formal safety guarantees for control systems, but training accurate neural certificates remains difficult, particularly when unsafe regions are hard to characterize. We propose a verification-guided training framework that addresses this by using probabilistic enumeration of safety constraints to detect forward-invariance violations, i.e., states where the learned certificate incorrectly classifies unsafe behavior. This produces a compact, targeted set of counterexamples that more precisely captures the failure boundary than inputs generated by standard adversarial attack methods. Crucially, using this representation to fine-tune a pretrained HJ value function yields larger certified regions and reduces certification time across all tested benchmarks. We further introduce a shielding mechanism based on the refined certificates to enforce safety constraints at deployment time. We evaluate the proposed safety filter in a realistic, physics-based Isaac Sim environment and through real-world autonomous racing experiments, achieving zero safety constraint violations compared to a nominal controller and a backup policy based on Linear Quadratic Regulation (LQR). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed shielding mechanism in ensuring safe operation under high-speed, safety-critical conditions.
2610.27870.tldr_en: This work proposes a verification-guided training framework that addresses forward-invariance violations by using probabilistic enumeration of safety constraints to detect forward-invariance violations, and introduces a shielding mechanism based on the refined certificates to enforce safety constraints at deployment time.

llm.title_ja: ニューラルハミルトン・ジャコビ安全証明書の列挙誘導型トレーニング
llm.tldr_ja: 安全性制約の確率的列挙を用いて前方不変性違反を検出し、安全証明書を洗練させる検証誘導型トレーニングフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: ハミルトン・ジャコビ（HJ）到達可能性解析は形式的な安全性を保証するが、特に不安全領域の特性把握が難しい場合に正確なニューラル証明書の訓練が困難であること。
llm.method: 安全性制約の確率的列挙により前方不変性違反を検出し、精密な反例セットを得て事前学習済みのHJ価値関数をファインチューニングする。
llm.result: シミュレーション環境および実世界の自動レーシング実験において、安全制約違反ゼロを達成し、高速な安全性確保に有効であることを示した。
keywords_ja: ハミルトン・ジャコビ

2610.27865.title: Frontier LLMs Enter the World of Robotics: A Cross-Model Evaluation on RoboColiseum
2610.27865.abstract: Recent studies have explored the potential of multimodal large language models for robot control, yet the models' embodied capabilities remain insufficiently characterized across models, tasks, and execution settings. We conduct a multidimensional comparative evaluation on RoboColiseum across four tracks: Instruction Following, Spatial Reasoning, General Manipulation, and Robustness. We implement Agent2Act, a control harness that integrates GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini 4 Argon into the evaluation environment through shared observation, action execution, and feedback interfaces. Under common task settings and scoring criteria, all four models exhibit a consistent capability profile: high instruction-following scores, with three approaching perfect performance; strong spatial reasoning; and general manipulation scores below those of the other three tracks. Within the evaluated configurations, Astra leads instruction following and robustness, while Opus leads spatial reasoning, general manipulation, and overall performance. These results reveal complementary strengths across models and a persistent gap between task understanding and reliable physical execution. Component comparisons on selected tasks further show that harness design affects task success, planning cost, and execution time. Additionally, case studies with Astra examine whole-body coordination, manipulation across robot embodiments, precision manipulation, dexterous-hand manipulation, and real-robot tasks, providing further insight into the model's capabilities and limitations across embodied tasks.
2610.27865.tldr_en: A multidimensional comparative evaluation on RoboColiseum across four tracks reveals complementary strengths across models and a persistent gap between task understanding and reliable physical execution.

llm.title_ja: 最先端LLMのロボット工学への進出：RoboColiseumにおけるクロスモデル評価
llm.tldr_ja: RoboColiseumを用いて複数の最先端マルチモーダル大規模言語モデルを多次元的に比較評価し、モデル間の相補的な強みと課題を明らかにした。
llm.problem: ロボット制御におけるマルチモーダル大規模言語モデルの潜在能力は探求されているが、モデル、タスク、実行設定にわたる実証的な評価が不十分であること。
llm.method: 共通の観測・実行インターフェースを統合する制御ハーネス「Agent2Act」を用いて4つのモデルを4つのトラックで多次元比較評価する。
llm.result: 全モデルが指示追従や空間推論で高い性能を示した一方で一般マプリケーションスコアは低く、タスク理解と信頼性の高い物理的実行との間に乖離があることを示した。

2610.27861.title: RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation
2610.27861.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks. We introduce \textbf{RoboCasa-Shift}, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlying settings and differs only in the target shift, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics. We evaluate GR00T N1.5 on four long-horizon tasks that pass a predefined clean-performance gate under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, including conditions that drive the evaluated policy to complete task failure, totaling 1,040 formal rollouts. Robustness responses vary substantially across factors and tasks, and increasing severity does not always produce monotonic degradation. For example, one camera condition yields $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0$ despite 8 of 80 matched episodes changing outcome. Stage-aware analysis further shows that the same end-to-end degradation can correspond to different execution-depth profiles. Camera $L_2$ and Gaussian blur $L_1$ both yield $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0.188$, yet their first-stage failure rates are 19.0\% and 36.4\%, respectively. Our findings suggest that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaochengWang23/RoboCasa-Shift.
2610.27861.tldr_en: It is suggested that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression.
2610.27861.hf_summary_en: RoboCasa-Shift evaluates vision-language-action robustness through paired rollouts and stage-aware diagnostics, revealing that failure patterns vary by shift factor and task rather than degrading uniformly.

llm.title_ja: RoboCasa-Shift：長期的家庭内マニピュレーションにおけるVLAポリシーの段階認識型ロバストネス評価
llm.tldr_ja: 制御された単一要因のシフトや段階認識型診断を組み合わせた診断用ロバストネスベンチマーク「RoboCasa-Shift」を提案した。
llm.problem: VLAのロバストネスは総合的なタスク成功率のみで要約されることが多く、分布シフト下での個々の実行の変化や長期タスクでの失敗の発生箇所が不明確であること。
llm.method: 単一因子のシフト、ペアになったクリーン・摂動ロールアウト、シミュレータベースの段階認識型診断を組み合わせたベンチマークを構築して評価する。
llm.result: ロバストネスの応答は要因やタスクによって大きく異なり、VLAのロバストネスは単一の指標ではなく多次元的な実行特性として評価すべきであることを示した。

2610.27851.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
2610.27851.abstract: This paper shows that JEPA-style latent world models (LWMs) can learn across diverse domains and data sources by adopting the language-conditioned interface of video generation models. We establish this approach as an effective and efficient basis for planning with imagination and downstream policy fine-tuning. To this end, we introduce LaLa-World, a Language-conditioned Latent World model that learns from simulation and robot trajectories together with broader image and video data. Two designs make this work. First, we describe both numerical actions and visual changes in language, enabling joint training of a single future predictor across heterogeneous datasets. Second, we build the predictor on a language model, allowing it to interpret language conditions while predicting future latent states. The resulting predictor achieves higher average MPC planning performance than existing LWMs trained separately for each domain or task. Adding image and video data further improves average planning performance and robustness to action phrasing. In a matched comparison with an RAEv2-based video generation model baseline, LaLa-World reaches comparable planning performance with $6\times$ less training cost and $13.9\times$ faster planning. Beyond planning, the pretrained LaLa-World serves as an initialization for LaLa-Policy, which jointly predicts actions and future visual representations. LaLa-Policy performs competitively with Cosmos Policy on LIBERO and RoboCasa, with up to $5.5\times$ faster inference.
2610.27851.tldr_en: This paper shows that JEPA-style latent world models (LWMs) can learn across diverse domains and data sources by adopting the language-conditioned interface of video generation models by introducing LaLa-World, a Language-conditioned Latent World model that learns from simulation and robot trajectories together with broader image and video data.
2610.27851.hf_summary_en: LaLa-World is a language-conditioned latent world model that jointly learns from diverse simulation, robot, and video data to enable efficient model-predictive planning and policy initialization.

llm.title_ja: LaLa-World：自然言語アクションを用いた潜在世界モデルのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 動画生成モデルの言語条件付きインターフェースを採用し、多様なドメインやデータソースで学習可能な言語条件付き潜在世界モデル「LaLa-World」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の潜在世界モデルはドメインやタスクごとに個別に訓練されており、異種データセット間でのスケーリングや汎化が困難であること。
llm.method: 数値アクションと視覚的変化の両方を言語で記述することで異種データセットの共同学習を可能にし、言語モデルベースの予測器を構築する。
llm.result: 既存の潜在世界モデルと比較して平均MPC計画性能が向上し、訓練コストと計画速度の大幅な改善を実現した。

2610.27836.title: Agentic discovery of interpretable car-following laws from multi-source trajectory data
2610.27836.abstract: Car-following (CF) models is a fundamental component of microscopic traffic simulation and underpin the analysis of collective traffic dynamics, while its modeling becomes more challenging due to diverse human driving behaviors and the increasing presence of automated vehicle. Analytical CF models offer interpretable representations of longitudinal vehicle interactions, but their prescribed functional structures may limit the representation of heterogeneous driving behavior. This study proposes an agent-centered, physics-aware framework for the empirical discovery of CF laws from multi-source trajectory data. The framework iteratively combines agent-guided hypothesis generation, informed by traffic flow knowledge and state-dependent reconstruction errors, with evolutionary symbolic search and physics-aware multi-objective evaluation. Using NGSIM US-101, highD, and exiD, the framework discovers the Adaptive Equilibrium Response Model (AERM), which couples state-dependent relative-speed response with spacing-dependent equilibrium-speed restoration. AERM admits analytical equilibrium speed-spacing and flow-density relationships; its stability conditions are derived for the zero-delay formulation, and platoon simulations examine disturbance propagation. Evaluated against seven classical CF models on Shanghai naturalistic driving data, NGSIM I-80, and Waymo trajectories, AERM attains the lowest spacing and speed reconstruction errors under trajectory-specific calibration, reducing spacing RMSE by 9.11%, 7.59%, and 21.73% relative to the strongest baselines, and remains competitive under dataset-level shared parameters. These results demonstrate the fitting flexibility and analytical tractability of the discovered CF law, providing an interpretable basis for microscopic traffic simulation.
2610.27836.tldr_en: An agent-centered, physics-aware framework for the empirical discovery of CF laws from multi-source trajectory data is proposed, which discovers the Adaptive Equilibrium Response Model (AERM), which couples state-dependent relative-speed response with spacing-dependent equilibrium-speed restoration.

llm.title_ja: マルチソース軌跡データからの解釈可能な追従法則のエージェント型発見
llm.tldr_ja: 交通流の知識と状態依存の再構成誤差に基づくエージェント中心の物理認識フレームワークにより、適応平衡応答モデル（AERM）を発見した。
llm.problem: 多様な人間の運転行動や自動運転車の増加により、追従モデルのモデリングがますます困難になっていること。
llm.method: エージェント誘導型仮説生成と進化型記号探索、物理認識型多目的評価を反復的に組み合わせるフレームワークの提案。
llm.result: 複数データの較正において最も低い間隔および速度の再構成誤差を達成し、従来ベースラインに対して間隔RMSEを大幅に削減した。
keywords_ja: 交通流シミュレーション

2610.27794.title: Multi-View Latent Action Pretraining for Cross-Embodiment Robot Learning from Videos
2610.27794.abstract: Action-free videos are an appealing substitute for costly teleoperated data. Latent action models (LAMs) turn videos into a supervision signal by inferring abstract actions between frames. Existing LAMs observe a single camera view, which resolves 6D robot actions only ambiguously missing out-of-plane movements and potential occlusions. We propose a LAM that ingests synchronized multi-camera views using cross-attention to resolve depth and occlusions before compressing them into latent actions. The latent actions are fed into a policy in which a latent expert and an action expert are coupled by sequential flow matching around a frozen VLM backbone. We further evaluate in strict cross-embodiment settings where task-specific demonstrations come from other embodiments. We show that dual-view LAM pretraining improves the decodability of ground-truth 6D actions by 17% compared to single-view, while scaling single-view data by two orders of magnitude is not sufficient to fully recover out-of-plane motions. The downstream policy improves success rate by +13.5% compared to +6.2% for single-view LAM. A single cross-embodiment is sufficient for skill transfer, and adding a second viewpoint outperforms adding up to four further embodiments. The results transfer to hardware where demonstrations come from a human hand improving success rate by +20% over action-only policies in 850 rollouts. We show that video and robot data are complementary, and that benefits of learning from video are task-dependent. Website: https://learnsyslab.github.io/multiview_latent_action_pretraining/
2610.27794.tldr_en: It is shown that video and robot data are complementary, and that benefits of learning from video are task-dependent, and that video and robot data are complementary, and that benefits of learning from video are task-dependent.

llm.title_ja: 動画からのクロスエンボディメント・ロボット学習のための多視点潜在アクション事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: 同期された複数カメラの視点をクロスアテンションで処理し、深度とオクルージョンを解消して潜在アクションを抽出する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 単一カメラ視点に基づく従来の潜在アクションモデルでは、視野外の動きやオクルージョンにより6次元のロボット動作が曖昧になること。
llm.method: 複数視点の映像を入力としてクロスアテンションで統合し、フリーズされたVLMバックボーン周辺でシーケンシャル・フローマッチングを行うポリシーに接続する。
llm.result: デュアルビュー事前学習により、真の6Dアクションの復元精度が10%以上向上し、人間の手によるデモンストレーションからの実機タスク成功率が向上した。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント

2610.27782.title: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation
2610.27782.abstract: Video generation models are promising foundations for embodied world models, but only if their generated rollouts are physically valid and faithful to task instructions. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to judge these properties, yet their agreement with human judgments on embodied videos has not been systematically evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as judges of embodied video generation. The benchmark measures two fundamental dimensions, Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, across 800 human-annotated videos from 8 source corpora and 10 video generators, spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Experiments reveal uneven alignment between existing judges and human ratings: general-purpose MLLMs show lower agreement on physical adherence, while specialized video judges designed for general-domain physical reasoning do not consistently transfer to embodied scenarios. Motivated by these findings, we construct RoboJudge-Train, comprising 12K videos annotated with 25K human-verified scores and model-assisted rationales for Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment. We fine-tune a 9B MLLM on this dataset with supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, yielding RoboJudge-9B. Among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench, RoboJudge-9B achieves the highest overall agreement, reaching a Pearson correlation of 0.719 with a statistically significant 0.089 gain over Gemini-3.7-Flash, the best-performing proprietary baseline in our evaluation. Training on RoboJudge-Train also yields gains on external benchmarks, including VideoPhy2 and Physion-Eval. We further use RoboJudge-9B as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment.
2610.27782.tldr_en: RoboJudge-9B is used as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, and achieves the highest overall agreement among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench.
2610.27782.hf_summary_en: Researchers introduce a benchmark and training dataset to evaluate multimodal language models as judges of physically valid, instruction-aligned embodied video generation, yielding a fine-tuned 9B judge with high human agreement.

llm.title_ja: RoboJudge：身体性動画生成の評価者としてのマルチモーダル言語モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 身体性動画生成の評価を行うためのベンチマークを構築し、教師あり学習と強化学習でファインチューニングした RoboJudge-9B により人間との高い合意度を達成した。
llm.problem: 動画生成モデルの生成結果が物理的に妥当でタスク指示に忠実であるかを判定するため、マルチモーダルLLMが使われているが、人間との判断の一致度が体系的に評価されていないこと。
llm.method: 800本の人間注釈付き動画からなるベンチマーク「RoboJudge-Bench」を構築し、12Kの動画データセットでファインチューニングした「RoboJudge-9B」を提案する。
llm.result: RoboJudge-9BはRoboJudge-Bench上で他の評価モデルの中で最も高い人間との一致度（ピアソン相関0.719）を達成した。

2610.27756.title: Give the Model a Finger: Developmentally Aligned Evaluation of Counting in Vision-Language Models
2610.27756.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are exact on small sets and drift into estimation on larger ones, a profile reminiscent of children before they master counting. Children cross the barrier with epistemic actions: pointing at each item while reciting number words, moving counted items aside, partitioning the array. We give VLMs the same actions as dumb image tools with no visual intelligence of their own in a training-free agent loop. Our central claim is about measurement, not intervention: a model that counts by marking leaves a normally hidden serial procedure on the image, and the developmental principles of counting turn those marks into an interpretable audit of serial visual reasoning: every tag is classified against point-level ground truth as on-target, duplicate, phantom, or omitted, the answer is checked against the number of tags, and order irrelevance is tested by forcing opposite traversal orders. Across 9 models, 682 images, and 7 harness conditions we find that (i) the exact-counting range is a model-specific signature spanning nearly two orders of magnitude (R80 from 3 to 150 dots); (ii) as an intervention the finger mostly fails: tags help 4 of 9 models on small-count photographs, hurt imprecise pointers, and rarely beat a verbal routine or a blind point list; what the loop buys is an auditable trace, not accuracy; (iii) as measurement it succeeds: a tag-perturbation probe shows that precise pointers read their answers off the tags, pointing precision tracks which models benefit, dense scenes fail by omission, and models rarely revise after seeing their own tags; and (iv) the capacities dissociate: models follow an instructed traversal order yet often change their answer when it reverses, and children's regular-over-scattered advantage appears only under the routine and survives lattices that defeat a rows-times-columns shortcut.
2610.27756.tldr_en: This work gives VLMs the same actions as dumb image tools with no visual intelligence of their own in a training-free agent loop and claims that a model that counts by marking leaves a normally hidden serial procedure on the image, and the developmental principles of counting turn those marks into an interpretable audit of serial visual reasoning.

llm.title_ja: モデルに指を与えよ：ビジョン・言語モデルにおける発達的整列に基づく数え上げ評価
llm.tldr_ja: 訓練不要のエージェントループ内でVLMに画像ツールとしての「指」のアクションを与え、数え上げの段階的原則に基づいて直列的な視覚推論を監査する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語モデルは少数の集合では正確だが多数になると推定になり、数え上げをマスターする前の子供のような状態になること。
llm.method: 数え上げるときにタグを残す訓練不要のエージェントループを構築し、タグ付けされた結果の正確性や順序不変性を監査する。
llm.result: 正確な数え上げの範囲がモデル固有のシグネチャであることや、ポインタによる明示的な監査トレースの取得に成功したことを示した。

2610.27736.title: AWLS: Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering for One-Step Generative Robotic Manipulation Policies
2610.27736.abstract: Human-collected real-world robotic manipulation demonstrations often contain mixed-quality trajectories, including hesitant, indirect, or inefficient action segments. While diffusion- and flow-based policies can model such multimodal data, standard behavior cloning (BC) assigns equal likelihood to all demonstrated actions and may therefore reproduce suboptimal modes. Offline RL value estimates offer a natural signal for biasing policies toward higher-value behavioral modes, but directly fine-tuning the generative policy or using critic gradients for policy steering can amplify critic errors and induce prior drift. We propose Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering (AWLS), an offline post-training method for improving frozen one-step generative manipulation policies without updating their decoders. AWLS learns a residual noise shaper, an observation-conditioned residual correction to the policy's latent noise, and trains it with an advantage-weighted action reconstruction objective. The advantages are detached, scale-normalized, and used only as supervised weights on demonstrated actions, avoiding critic-gradient policy updates while preserving fast single-step inference. We further introduce a rollout-free decoder-sensitivity criterion for selecting pretrained checkpoints that remain responsive to latent-noise perturbations. Experiments on simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks with clean and mixed-quality demonstrations show that AWLS improves over the frozen base policy while limiting drift from the pretrained behavior prior. Project page: https://awls-corl2026.github.io/
2610.27736.tldr_en: Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering (AWLS) is proposed, an offline post-training method for improving frozen one-step generative manipulation policies without updating their decoders, and a rollout-free decoder-sensitivity criterion for selecting pretrained checkpoints that remain responsive to latent-noise perturbations.

llm.title_ja: AWLS：1ステップ生成型ロボットマニプリュケーションポリシーのためのアドバンテージ重み付き潜在ステアリング
llm.tldr_ja: デコーダーを更新せずにフリーズされた1ステップ生成ポリシーを改善するオフライン後学習手法「AWLS」を提案した。
llm.problem: 実世界のデモンストレーションには多様な品質の軌跡が含まれており、標準的な行動クローンでは最適でないモードを再現してしまうこと。
llm.method: 観測条件付きの残差補正を行う残差ノイズシェーパーを学習し、切り離されたスケーリング済みのアドバンテージを重みとしてアクション再構成目的関数で訓練する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界のロボットマニプリュケーションタスクにおいて、事前学習済みの動作事前分布からのドリフトを抑えつつベースポリシーを改善した。
keywords_ja: マニプリュケーション

2610.27732.title: Prescribed Performance Guided Safe Reinforcement Learning for Roundabout Navigation of Autonomous Vehicles
2610.27732.abstract: Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) face significant challenges in roundabout navigation due to dense traffic interactions and unpredictable agent behaviors, necessitating high levels of adaptability and safety. While the combination of Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Model Predictive Control (MPC) offers a promising approach, existing frameworks suffer from a structural mismatch where pointwise RL decisions fail to align with MPC's trajectory level optimization, and often lack rigorous safety guarantees. This work proposes RLTrajGen-PPMPC-CBF, a hierarchical framework for safe, smooth and comfort roundabout navigation, which regulates the coupling between RL-based planning and MPC-based control. We employ Prescribed Performance Constraints (PPC) to enforce a gradual, stable convergence between reference trajectories and control outputs, ensuring MPC tracking performance remains consistent with intended behavior from RL. Additionally, a Control Barrier Function (CBF) layer provides real-time safety corrections that are fed back into the RL process. Simulation results in the MetaDrive environment demonstrate that our method achieves a 6.25\% increase in average success rate and a 65.87\% reduction in Motion Sickness Dose Value (MSDV) compared to the optimal baseline, meanwhile accelerating training convergence.
2610.27732.tldr_en: This work proposes RLTrajGen-PPMPC-CBF, a hierarchical framework for safe, smooth and comfort roundabout navigation, which regulates the coupling between RL-based planning and MPC-based control, and employs Prescribed Performance Constraints (PPC) to enforce a gradual, stable convergence between reference trajectories and control outputs.

llm.title_ja: 自律走行車のラウンドアバウト走行に向けた規定性能誘導型安全強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 強化学習ベースの計画とMPCベースの制御の結合を規制する階層型フレームワークを提案し、安全でスムーズなラウンドアバウト走行を実現した。
llm.problem: 接続・自律車両（CAV）は、密集した交通環境や予測不可能なエージェントの挙動により、ラウンドアバウト走行で大きな課題に直面していること。
llm.method: 規定性能制約（PPC）を用いて参照軌道と制御出力の間の漸進的な収束を強制し、制御バリア関数（CBF）層でリアルタイムの安全性補正を行う階層型フレームワーク。
llm.result: MetaDrive環境でのシミュレーションにより、最適ベースラインと比較して平均成功率の向上とモーションシックネスの著しい削減を達成した。
keywords_ja: 交通シミュレーション

2610.27725.title: World2HOSI: A Multi-Expert Harness for Long-Horizon Human-Object-Scene Interaction Generation
2610.27725.abstract: Long-horizon human-object-scene interaction (HOSI) is central to embodied AI, animation, and game development. Existing human-object interaction (HOI) and human-scene interaction (HSI) models excel in their respective domains, but none alone covers tasks requiring multiple interaction skills. Training unified HOSI models is hindered by scarce and costly data. We introduce World2HOSI, a multi-expert orchestration harness that generates continuous HOSI data from 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scenes and natural language instructions. Our key insight is that long-horizon HOSI hinges not on a stronger single model but on orchestration. Given a shared, structured scene state and an orchestration harness grounded in it, existing experts can jointly accomplish tasks beyond the reach of any of them alone. World2HOSI realizes this insight as a closed loop around a persistent scene state built from decoupled background and object assets. A harness plans action stages over this state, invokes experts via their native conditioning interfaces, and writes each action's effects back, so that every invocation is grounded in the evolving world. To reduce physical artifacts, bounded residual optimization and contact-driven physics simulation further ensure the physical plausibility of human motion and object manipulation, respectively, while preserving interaction intent. Experiments and a perceptual user study show that World2HOSI achieves the best task completion and interaction quality on the evaluated HOSI tasks, while generating more diverse data.
2610.27725.tldr_en: World2HOSI is introduced, a multi-expert orchestration harness that generates continuous HOSI data from 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes and natural language instructions and achieves the best task completion and interaction quality on the evaluated HOSI tasks, while generating more diverse data.

llm.title_ja: World2HOSI：長期的人間・物体・シーンインタラクション生成のためのマルチエキスパートハーネス
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dガウススプラッティングシーンと自然言語指示から連続的なHOSIデータを生成するマルチエキスパートオーケストレーションハーネス「World2HOSI」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の人間・物体インタラクションモデルはそれぞれの領域に優れているが、複数のインタラクションスキルを必要とするタスクを単体でカバーできないこと。
llm.method: 背景と物体の資産から構築された構造化されたシーン状態の周りに閉ループを形成し、シーンの変化に合せて複数のエキスパートを呼び出すハーネスを構築する。
llm.result: 評価されたHOSIタスクにおいて、最高のタスク完了率とインタラクション品質を達成し、より多様なデータを生成できることを示した。
keywords_ja: 人間・物体インタラクション

2610.27714.title: When Does Experience Memory Help Closed-Loop LLM Driving Agents? A Controlled Evaluation with Resampled Warmup Pools, Token-Matched Fillers, and Audited Baselines
2610.27714.abstract: When does experience memory help a closed-loop LLM driving agent? Published gains cannot say, because the two factors we find to matter most, which warmup experiences the pool contains and what any injected tokens do to the prompt, are controlled in none of them. We answer with a controlled evaluation on one audited HighwayEnv testbed (1Hz, gpt-4o-mini for the decisive contrasts). We treat the warmup pool as a resampled random factor (ten disjoint pools) and add token-matched irrelevant-filler controls, oracle-certified diagnostics, caution-pricing metrics, and quantified audits of the baseline ports. The probe suite spans flat-text retrieval (a DiLu port), a single-frame grid port (RESPOND-inspired), our episodic temporal-graph memory, a retrieval-free consolidated rulebook, and a flat K-step observation-history baseline. Four findings follow, each a property of this testbed. (1) Headline memory gains belong to the warmup draw. The reported pool is the best of ten for both retrieval memories, which beat No-Memory in only one pool of ten (sign test p=0.011), and even the rulebook's apparent pool-immunity collapsed on five fresh draws. (2) No retrieval design tested exceeds token-matched filler. The collision-only merge ceiling is reached by a single 15-token caution instruction, and metrics that price caution erase the rulebook's lead. (3) Representational sophistication is nowhere robustly operative. (4) Baseline port quality silently inverts conclusions. On this testbed, a single-pool comparison without filler controls would have reported memory gains that these controls reverse. We release the testbed, audited ports, seeds, and caches.
2610.27714.tldr_en: This work treats the warmup pool as a resampled random factor and adds token-matched irrelevant-filler controls, oracle-certified diagnostics, caution-pricing metrics, and quantified audits of the baseline ports to answer the question when does experience memory help a closed-loop LLM driving agent.

llm.title_ja: 経験メモリは閉ループLLM運転エージェントの役にいつ立つのか？
llm.tldr_ja: ウォームアッププールの再サンプリングやトークン一致のフィラーコントロールを導入した制御された評価を通じて、LLM運転エージェントにおける経験メモリの効果を検証した。
llm.problem: 経験メモリが閉ループLLM運転エージェントにいつ役立つのかについて、ウォームアッププールの影響やプロンプトへのトークンの影響が従来の公開研究では制御されていなかったこと。
llm.method: ウォームアッププールを再サンプリングされたランダム因子として扱い、トークン一致の無関係なフィラーコントロール、オラクル診断、慎重度評価指標を導入した検証を行う。
llm.result: 見出しのメモリ利益はウォームアップのドローに依存しており、検証されたどの検索デザインもトークン一致フィラーを超えるものではないことを示した。

2610.27704.title: VEOcc++: Learning Persistent Voxel Feature Maps for Embodied Online Semantic Occupancy Mapping and Offline Refinement
2610.27704.abstract: Semantic occupancy mapping supports embodied perception during exploration and detailed scene understanding afterward, giving rise to two complementary requirements: online incremental mapping for maintaining an up-to-date global map under causal constraints, and offline global map refinement for improving the completed scene representation with additional computation. We present VEOcc++, a unified voxel-centric framework that connects both stages through a persistent sparse voxel feature map. During exploration, the map expands with newly observed regions and integrates aligned local features through reliability-guided updates, while context-aware decoding produces the current semantic occupancy map. After exploration, cached local features are consolidated as complementary evidence and combined with the completed online representation for multi-scale spatial refinement. On EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet, VEOcc++ achieves 67.12\% IoU and 58.40\% mIoU, establishing new state-of-the-art performance for online incremental mapping. With the local predictor fixed, our online mapping pipeline outperforms VEOcc fusion by 3.70 IoU and 3.74 mIoU points, demonstrating substantial gains from the proposed global mapping design. Offline global map refinement further improves the completed map to 67.79% IoU and 59.37% mIoU using only the observations acquired during exploration. Zero-shot deployment on a mobile robot further demonstrates transferability to unseen environments, onboard feasibility, and scalability to large-scale indoor mapping. Project page: https://wryzju.github.io/VEOccpp/.
2610.27704.tldr_en: VEOcc++, a unified voxel-centric framework that connects both stages through a persistent sparse voxel feature map, is presented, a unified voxel-centric framework that connects both stages through a persistent sparse voxel feature map.

llm.title_ja: VEOcc++：身体性オンライン意味論的占有マッピングとオフライン洗練のための持続的ボクセル特徴マップの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 持続的なスパースボクセル特徴マップを介してオンライン増分マッピングとオフライン大域マップ洗練を接続する統一ボクセル中心フレームワーク「VEOcc++」を提案した。
llm.problem: 意味論的占有マッピングにおいて、因果的制約下でのオンライン増分マッピングと、追加計算によるオフライン大域マップ洗練という2つの要件を同時に満たす必要があること。
llm.method: 探索中に信頼度誘導型アップデートによって局所特徴を統合し、探索後にキャッシュされた特徴を組み合わせてマルチスケール空間洗練を行うボクセル中心のフレームワーク。
llm.result: EmbodiedOcc-ScanNetにおいて67.12%のIoUを達成し、オンライン増分マッピングの新たな最高性能を確立するとともに、移動ロボットでのゼロショット展開を示した。

2610.27698.title: VLA-Retain: Benchmarking Cross-Dimension Effects of Vision Tuning in VLAs
2610.27698.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer knowledge from large-scale pretraining into robot control, but their manipulation performance remains sensitive to changes in observation conditions, which recent work addresses by fine-tuning the visual module on target-domain data. However, it remains unclear how such adaptation affects robustness beyond the target condition, as existing robustness benchmarks only evaluate models without fine-tuning and adaptation studies only report the target gain. Measuring this cross-dimension effect requires separating target gains from off-target changes, isolating adaptation effects from architectural differences, ruling out generic forgetting, and comparing tuning choices. Therefore, we introduce VLA-Retain, a benchmark that compares five open VLA models, tuned on Camera-view or Sensor-noise data, with their own base checkpoints on LIBERO-Plus dataset spanning seven perturbation dimensions. Our study reveals four findings. First, targeted vision tuning is not local, and its target gain does not predict retention. Mean off-target gain is negative in 8 of 10 model--domain configurations. Under Camera-view tuning, X-VLA gains $69.4$ percentage points on the target but loses $4.6$ points on average elsewhere, whereas OpenVLA-OFT gains $39.3$ and $1.4$ points, respectively. Second, these regressions are not explained only by performance loss on the same tasks without perturbations. Third, broader training coverage raises overall gain over target-specific training but does not eliminate dimension-level regressions. Fourth, tuning strategies are model-dependent, as DELTA-style feature preservation raises X-VLA's mean off-target gain to $+1.2$ points but lowers OpenVLA-OFT's to $-23.1$. Overall, these findings show that target-domain success alone is insufficient and highlight cross-dimensional retention as a key criterion for targeted VLA adaptation.
2610.27698.tldr_en: VLA-Retain is introduced, a benchmark that compares five open VLA models, tuned on Camera-view or Sensor-noise data, with their own base checkpoints on LIBERO-Plus dataset spanning seven perturbation dimensions, and shows that target-domain success alone is insufficient and highlight cross-dimensional retention as a key criterion for targeted VLA adaptation.

llm.title_ja: VLA-Retain：VLAにおけるビジョンチューニングのクロス次元効果のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な摂動次元にわたる5つのオープンVLAモデルを比較するベンチマーク「VLA-Retain」を導入し、ターゲットドメインの成功だけでは不十分であることを示した。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語・アクション（VLA）モデルの視覚モジュールをファインチューニングした際、ターゲット条件以外のロバストネスにどのような影響を与えるかが不明確であること。
llm.method: カメラビューやセンサーノイズのデータでチューニングされた5つのオープンVLAモデルを、LIBERO-Plusデータセットの7つの摂動次元でベースチェックポイントと比較する。
llm.result: ターゲットのビジョンチューニングは局所的ではなく、平均的なオフサイドのゲインが多くのモデルで負になるなど、クロス次元の保持が重要であることを示した。
keywords_ja: ファインチューニング

2610.27696.title: PanoGraphGS: Unifying Panoptic Segmentation and Hierarchical 3D Scene Graphs with Gaussian Splatting
2610.27696.abstract: 3D scene graphs support language-guided navigation by organizing physical entities and their containment and spatial relations into hierarchical maps. Building such structured maps requires a scene representation that consistently distinguishes semantic regions and object instances across viewpoints. To this end, we present PanoGraphGS, a unified framework that integrates panoptic 3D Gaussian representation learning with hierarchical 3D scene graph construction. The framework learns semantic and instance features on shared Gaussian geometry. Prototype-based semantic learning and association-based instance learning produce consistent panoptic predictions across viewpoints. The learned representation supports novel-view panoptic segmentation and direct Gaussian-level panoptic decoding. A semantic-aware scene graph module further recovers a floor-room-stuff-object hierarchy with containment and spatial relations. We further release NaviGS, a real-world dataset for panoramic scene understanding. The dataset provides 3DGS, mesh, RGB, semantic, and depth data. For 3D scene graph identification, PanoGraphGS outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline in object-node accuracy by more than 50\% points on average across Replica and NaviGS. PanoGraphGS also achieves state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods in 2D panoptic segmentation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of PanoGraphGS in both hierarchical 3D scene understanding and 2D panoptic segmentation. The project website is available at: https://github.com/gaojh0333/PanoGraphGS.
2610.27696.tldr_en: PanoGraphGS, a unified framework that integrates panoptic 3D Gaussian representation learning with hierarchical 3D scene graph construction with state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods in 2D panoptic segmentation, is presented.

llm.title_ja: PanoGraphGS：ガウススプラッティングを用いたパノラマセグメンテーションと階層型3Dシーングラフの統合
llm.tldr_ja: パノラマ3Dガウス表現学習と階層型3Dシーングラフ構築を統合した統一フレームワーク「PanoGraphGS」を提案した。
llm.problem: 言語誘導型ナビゲーションをサポートする構造化されたマップの構築には、視点間でセ意味領域とインスタンスを整合的に区別するシーン表現が必要であること。
llm.method: 共有されたガウス幾何学上でセマンティックおよびインスタンス特徴を学習し、意味論的アウェアなシーングラフモジュールで階層を復元するフレームワーク。
llm.result: Replicaおよび新しく公開した NaviGS データセットにおいて、オブジェクトノードの精度でベースラインを大幅に上回り、最先端の性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ガウススプラッティング
パノラマセグメンテーション

2610.27690.title: NeoWorld-3: From Pixels to Code-Defined Physical Worlds
2610.27690.abstract: Simulation-ready world reconstruction demands physical interactivity beyond visual realism, which existing black-box 3D generation fails to deliver. We present NeoWorld-3, a coding-agent framework that reconstructs interactive 3D worlds from visual observations via tunable, executable programs. At its core, NeoSDK provides the underlying computational engine for low-level geometries, part composition, differentiable parameter refinement, and physics validation. At the same time, NeoMCP exposes these capabilities as structured, tool-callable APIs for vision-language agents to visually inspect, edit code, and iteratively refine programs. Through a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture, the framework scales seamlessly from standalone articulated objects to complex compositional scenes. Evaluations across object-level and scene-level reconstruction benchmarks demonstrate that NeoWorld-3 achieves state-of-the-art geometric fidelity and physical readiness. Crucially, manipulation trajectories planned within our reconstructed twins achieve successful zero-shot execution on a physical dual-arm robot, completing the Real-Sim-Real loop.
2610.27690.tldr_en: This work presents NeoWorld-3, a coding-agent framework that reconstructs interactive 3D worlds from visual observations via tunable, executable programs, and achieves state-of-the-art geometric fidelity and physical readiness.

llm.title_ja: NeoWorld-3：ピクセルからコードで定義された物理世界へ
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的観測から調整可能で実行可能なプログラムを介してインタラクティブな3D世界を再構築するコーディングエージェントフレームワーク「NeoWorld-3」を提案した。
llm.problem: シミュレーション用の世界再構築には視覚的リアリズムだけでなく物理的インタラクティビティが必要であるが、既存のブラックボックス型3D生成ではそれが実現できないこと。
llm.method: 低レベル幾何学や物理検証を行う計算エンジンと、ビジョン言語エージェントがプログラムを視覚的に検査・編集するためのツール呼び出しAPIを組み合わせる。
llm.result: 最先端の幾何学的忠実度と物理的即応性を達成し、再構築したツイン内で計画したマニピュレーション軌跡が物理的な双腕ロボットでゼロショット実行を完了した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション
コーディングエージェント

2610.27688.title: Adaptive Traversal Tubes for Posture-Aware Navigation of Bipedal Humanoids
2610.27688.abstract: Bipedal humanoids can change their effective footprint by adjusting body yaw, enabling both narrow-passage traversal and socially aware yielding. This paper presents a posture-aware navigation framework centered on \emph{Adaptive Traversal Tubes} (ATT), \emph{Interval Velocity--Heading} (IVH) control, and a sidestep-enhanced AMP locomotion prior. ATT represents a behavior-feasible corridor width field along a reference path, unifying geometric clearance and social comfort into a continuous signal. IVH maps this width to a continuous frontal-to-sidestep posture schedule and omnidirectional velocity commands. A velocity-conditioned AMP policy, trained with GVHMR-retargeted frontal/sidestep motions and coupled \((v_x,v_y)\) tracking rewards, is designed to improve transition stability over a generic locomotion controller while remaining interchangeable with the default onboard policy. This preprint presents the full method; a planned evaluation protocol on a Unitree G1 is outlined, with quantitative results to follow. Demo videos of MuJoCo simulation and real-robot deployment are available at: github.com/lborogzj997/Humanoid-Navigation-in-Crowds-and-Narrow-Spaces.
2610.27688.tldr_en: A velocity-conditioned AMP policy, trained with GVHMR-retargeted frontal/sidestep motions and coupled \((v_x,v_y)\) tracking rewards, is designed to improve transition stability over a generic locomotion controller while remaining interchangeable with the default onboard policy.

llm.title_ja: 二足ヒューマノイドの姿勢認識型ナビゲーションに向けた適応型トラバーサル・チューブ
llm.tldr_ja: 速度条件付けされたAMPポリシーが、汎用ロコモーションコントローラーと比較して遷移の安定性を向上させるように設計されている。
llm.problem: 狭い通路の移動や配慮を伴う譲り合いにおいて、二足ヒューマノイドの効果的なフットプリント調整と姿勢認識型ナビゲーションの実現。
llm.method: 適応型トラバーサル・チューブ（ATT）、区間速度見出し（IVH）制御、およびサイドステップ強化型AMPロコモーションプライアンスを統合したフレームワーク。
llm.result: MuJoCoシミュレーションおよび実機でのデモビデオが利用可能であり、Unitree G1での評価プロトコルが計画されている。

2610.27677.title: CovNav: Conformal Prediction-Guided Adaptive Inference for Object Goal Navigation
2610.27677.abstract: In object goal navigation (ObjectNav), an embodied agent must find a target object (e.g., "find a bed") in a previously unseen environment, relying on spatial commonsense such as object co-occurrence. Large Language Models (LLMs) encode this commonsense, but deploying them on robots exposes a trade-off between reasoning quality and efficiency: cloud-based models incur latency and privacy risks, whereas small on-device LLMs are fast but prone to hallucinated spatial judgments. Hybrid reasoning LLMs offer both a fast non-thinking mode and a slow thinking mode, which raises a key question for embodied agents: when is slow thinking worth its cost? We propose CovNav, a training-free framework that answers this question with Conformal Prediction (CP), turning dual-process (System 1 / System 2) inference into an uncertainty-aware decision. Much like recent decision models such as Jev, CovNav casts each spatial query as a structured binary decision rather than free-form generation: a local LLM in fast mode judges whether the target is likely near an observed object, CP converts its token probabilities into a prediction set, and only ambiguous queries are escalated to slow chain-of-thought reasoning. The object-pair formulation keeps calibration tractable and supports open-set objects through off-the-shelf detectors. Experiments on Gibson and HM3D show that CovNav surpasses the strongest zero-shot baseline by 0.8 and 1.7 percentage points in success rate on HM3D v1 and v2, while invoking slow reasoning for only 12.4% of queries and retaining most of the gain of always-on thinking at a fraction of its latency. Real-robot experiments on a TurtleBot 4 further validate the approach. CovNav shows how calibrated uncertainty can decide when an embodied agent should think slowly, offering a principled form of adaptive test-time reasoning for LLM-based robots.
2610.27677.tldr_en: CovNav shows how calibrated uncertainty can decide when an embodied agent should think slowly, offering a principled form of adaptive test-time reasoning for LLM-based robots.

llm.title_ja: CovNav：物体目標ナビゲーションのためのコンフォーマル予測誘導型適応推論
llm.tldr_ja: 較正された不確実性を利用して、LLMベースのロボットがいつゆっくり思考すべきかを決定する方法を示している。
llm.problem: LLMをロボットに導入する際、推論品質と効率のトレードオフ（クラウド型の遅延・プライバシーリスク、車載型モデルのハルシネーション）が存在する点。
llm.method: コンフォーマル予測（CP）を用いて、二重プロセス（システム1/システム2）推論を不確実性認識型決定に変換する訓練不要のフレームワーク「CovNav」の提案。
llm.result: GibsonおよびHM3Dでの実験において、HM3D v1およびv2の成功率で最強のゼロショットベースラインをそれぞれ0.8および1.7ポイント上回った。
keywords_ja: 物体目標ナビゲーション

2610.27672.title: Reusing Assurance Evidence in AI Pipelines: Validity Conditions, a Fail-Closed Release Gate, and a Replay of 714 Public Data Version Control Pipelines
2610.27672.abstract: Rerunning every governance control after every change to an artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline is expensive, so teams reuse earlier results. Reuse is safe only if each control's declared dependencies cover everything that can change its outcome, and only if the release gate checks that reused evidence describes the candidate being released. This article makes both conditions explicit and measures how often the first fails in practice. It defines when a signed evidence record is valid for a candidate and gives sufficient conditions under which change-local re-execution reaches the same release decision as rerunning every control. A reference gate implementing these checks with Ed25519 digital signatures blocks eight of nine manipulation scenarios, against one for a gate that trusts the planner and three for a gate that only verifies signatures; a dependency the policy never declared passes every gate. A replay of 38,083 commits from 714 public Data Version Control (DVC) pipelines measures that failure mode. Reusing stage results according to declared dependencies avoids 83.4% of stage executions, but in 3.3% of commits it reuses a stage whose imported code or referenced configuration changed, and 31% of pipelines are affected. A manual audit confirms the undeclared dependency in 36 of 40 sampled events. Evaluation stages, whose outputs are the evidence, are the most exposed. Adding each stage's static import closure lowers stale reuse to 0.4% while still avoiding 81.6% of executions; sampled shadow re-execution removes far less, and rerunning everything after unexplained changes avoids only 45.3%.
2610.27672.tldr_en: This article defines when a signed evidence record is valid for a candidate and gives sufficient conditions under which change-local re-execution reaches the same release decision as rerunning every control, and measures how often the first fails in practice.

2610.27657.title: PLaCA: Learning Patch-Level Future Latent Change for Action Generation
2610.27657.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but effective manipulation also requires anticipating how the environment will change. Existing world-action models explore future image prediction and latent dynamics modeling. However, generating complete future images can be computationally expensive, while highly compressed latent representations may obscure local changes. To address these challenges, we propose PLaCA, a world-to-action framework built around future latent change. PLaCA directly predicts spatially structured patch-level future latent change from the current multimodal input, preserving local information about expected environmental changes. We introduce patch-level change-aware supervision to emphasize regions undergoing larger changes and a future-to-action interface that explicitly incorporates predicted future latent change into action generation. Experiments on LIBERO-Long show that PLaCA achieves a 79.0% success rate, improving upon the Action-only baseline by 5.0 percentage points. On CALVIN, PLaCA improves the average sequence length from 2.784 to 3.564. These improvements are achieved while updating only 2.95% of the model parameters during the second training stage, demonstrating the effectiveness of future latent change modeling for downstream robotic manipulation.
2610.27657.tldr_en: PLaCA introduces patch-level change-aware supervision to emphasize regions undergoing larger changes and a future-to-action interface that explicitly incorporates predicted future latent change into action generation, demonstrating the effectiveness of future latent change modeling for downstream robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: PLaCA：行動生成のためのパッチレベル将来潜在的変化の学習
llm.tldr_ja: パッチレベルの変化認識型教師あり学習と、将来の潜在的変化を行動生成に明示的に統合するインターフェースを導入し、ロボットマニピュレーションにおける将来の潜在的変化モデリングの有効性を示した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルにおいて環境変化を予測する必要があるが、完全な将来画像の生成は計算コストが高く、高度に圧縮された潜在表現は局所的な変化を隠してしまう点。
llm.method: 現在のマルチモーダル入力から空間的に構造化されたパッチレベルの将来潜在的変化を直接予測する「PLaCA」フレームワークの提案。
llm.result: LIBERO-Longにおいて79.0%の成功率を達成し、行動のみのベースラインを5.0ポイント向上させ、CALVINでも平均シーケンス長を向上させた。

2610.27629.title: Minimum-Time Escape from the Conic Field of View of a Reeds-Shepp Pursuer: Classification and Game Value for a Slower or Equally Fast Evader
2610.27629.abstract: We study minimum-time escape of an omnidirectional evader from the forward conic field of view of a Reeds-Shepp pursuer with minimum turning radius $r$. For speed ratio $ν$ and cone half-angle $0<α<π/2$, we prove a global escape/holding classification: straight reversal holds the whole cone for $ν\le\sinα$, escape is confined to a barrier-bounded dart for $\sinα<ν\le1$, and escape is possible from every state for $ν>1$. For the slower or equally fast evader, $\sinα<ν\le1$, we construct the solution with Isaacs' characteristics and verify it in feedback form, using a Filippov pursuer relay and a one-sided evader branch. The finite escape time is the first root of one scalar equation, and the holding region is bounded by the nonusable parts of the rays and a barrier that closes with a convex corner on the front axis. Sample-and-hold counter-controls show that this escape time is the value of the game in nonanticipative strategies at every state except the corner. There the two strategy values differ: the pursuer's is infinite, whereas an evader that chooses which barrier branch to cross from the initial germ of the pursuer's control escapes before the barrier time $τ_I$, which is the evader's exact strategy value. An independent level-set solver, refined on fixed comparison points, agrees with the closed-form escape time and reproduces the holding region at the tested parameters.

llm.title_ja: リード・シェップ追跡者の円錐状視野からの最短時間脱出：速度の遅いあるいは等速の逃走者に対する分類とゲーム価値
llm.tldr_ja: 要旨に記載なし
llm.problem: 最小旋回半径を持つリード・シェップ追跡者の前方円錐状視野からの全方位逃走者の最短時間脱出問題の解析。
llm.method: 速度比と円錐半角に基づく大域的な脱出・保持の分類の証明、およびアイザックスの特性曲線を用いた解の構成とフィードバック形式での検証。
llm.result: 速度比に応じた大域的な脱出・保持の分類を証明し、有限の脱出時間が1つのスカラー方程式の最初の根であることを示した。

2610.27622.title: A Head Camera Is (Almost) All You Need: An Electronics-Free UMI Glove Labelled and Observed by One Moving Camera
2610.27622.abstract: Handheld demonstration devices decouple data collection from the robot, but conventional designs burden the hand with a wrist camera, cables and a pose tracker (SLAM, an IMU, a VR controller, or a fixed external camera that the collector's body occludes), and burden the pipeline with as many data streams to timestamp, synchronise and cross-calibrate. We show that a single egocentric camera (USD 122) worn on the collector's head replaces the wrist camera, the pose tracker and their separate streams with one. It reads printed fiducials on an electronics-free glove (USD 22) against paper tiles taped around the workspace, giving the 6-DoF gripper pose and the jaw width from the same frames the policy will see; at deployment the same camera rides a low-cost (USD 120) arm beside the robot that mimics the collector's head from the robot's joint state. Against the robot's encoders the labels are accurate to 6.5 mm and 1.6 degrees median with 93-100% frame coverage, and a policy trained on them instead of encoders pays 3% in validation loss.
