Adding 194 glove demonstrations to 48 teleoperated episodes lifts rollout success from 10/25 to 17/25, level with 172 teleoperated episodes alone (18/25), and the full co-trained head-camera policy succeeds in 20/25 against 15/25 for the wrist-camera recipe, whose policies drop the object when the goal leaves their view, and 12/25 for a fixed camera.
2610.27622.tldr_en: It is shown that a single egocentric camera worn on the collector's head replaces the wrist camera, the pose tracker and their separate streams with one, and the full co-trained head-camera policy succeeds in 20/25 against 15/25 for the wrist-camera recipe, and 12/25 for a fixed camera.

llm.title_ja: ヘッドカメラが（ほぼ）すべて：単一の動くカメラによってラベル付けおよび観測される電子部品不要のUMIグローブ
llm.tldr_ja: 収集者の頭部に装着された単一の独占的カメラが手首カメラ、ポーズトラッカー、およびそれらの別々のストリームを置き換え、共訓練されたヘッドカメラポリシーが優れた成功率を達成することを示した。
llm.problem: 従来のハンドヘルドデモンストレーションデバイスは、手首カメラ、ケーブル、ポーズトラッカーなどの負担を手にかけ、タイムスタンプや同期、クロスキャリブレーションのパイプラインを複雑にする点。
llm.method: 収集者の頭部に装着した単一のヘッドカメラを用い、ワークスペース周辺に貼られたペーパータイルに対して電子部品不要のグローブ上の印刷された基準マークを読み取る手法の提案。
llm.result: フル共訓練されたヘッドカメラポリシーは25回中20回成功し、手首カメラ方式（15/25）や固定カメラ（12/25）を上回った。

2610.27618.title: JARVIS: From Visual Manuals to Autonomous Robotic Assembly
2610.27618.abstract: Visual manuals communicate procedural knowledge through stepwise diagrams, but translating these instructions into reliable long-horizon robotic execution remains challenging. We introduce JARVIS, a method-agnostic benchmark for autonomous visual-manual-guided execution without additional language instructions. JARVIS comprises 236,679 LEGO assembly tasks across 8,987 scenes, with a carefully curated JARVIS-v1 suite of 50 tasks for interactive robotic evaluation. Tasks span varying initial structural complexities and assembly horizons, requiring agents to interpret manuals, ground actions in an evolving workspace, and execute the intended procedure. A structure-aware evaluation protocol captures geometric accuracy, structural relations, construction order, partial progress, and completion. We further introduce JARVIS-agentic, a tool-grounded embodied agent that composes robot primitives into executable programs and uses execution feedback for verification and recovery, without task-specific action trajectories or model parameter updates. Across nine multimodal and reasoning models, task-oriented primitives increase the average assembly score. Performance nevertheless declines sharply with assembly horizon, and execution errors remain difficult to correct. Prior-task experience improves initial performance, while repeated reflection provides inconsistent benefits, highlighting persistent limitations in connecting visual procedural reasoning with reliable physical execution.
2610.27618.tldr_en: JARVIS is introduced, a method-agnostic benchmark for autonomous visual-manual-guided execution without additional language instructions, and JARVIS-agentic, a tool-grounded embodied agent that composes robot primitives into executable programs and uses execution feedback for verification and recovery, without task-specific action trajectories or model parameter updates.

llm.title_ja: JARVIS：ビジュアルマニュアルから自律型ロボット組立へ
llm.tldr_ja: 追加の言語指示なしで自律的なビジュアルマニュアル誘導実行を行うための手法非依存型ベンチマーク「JARVIS」と、ツール基盤型具現化エージェント「JARVIS-agentic」を導入した。
llm.problem: ビジュアルマニュアルの段階的図解による手続き的知識を、信頼性の高い長期的なロボット実行に翻訳することが困難である点。
llm.method: 多様な初期構造の複雑さと組立ホスizonを持つ数万のLEGO組立タスクを含むベンチマークJARVISの構築、およびロボットプリミティブをプログラムに構成して実行フィードバックを利用するJARVIS-agenticの導入。
llm.result: タスク指向のプリミティブにより平均組立スコアが向上したが、組立ホライズンの増大に伴い性能が急激に低下し、実行エラーの修正が依然として困難であることが示された。
llm.limitation: 組立ホライズンの増大に伴い性能が急激に低下し、実行エラーの修正が困難であること。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルマニュアル
ロボットエージェント

2610.27616.title: EchoNav: Evidential BEV Completion from Historical Observations for Visual Navigation
2610.27616.abstract: Visual navigation in cluttered environments requires robots to recover previously observed structure and infer obstacles and free space that remain occluded. We present a framework that combines temporal aggregation and occupancy completion in an evidential bird's-eye-view (BEV) representation predicted from short RGB sequences. A decoder adapts frozen VGGT-Omega features and combines historical residual proposals using cellwise weights and a learned no-update option. The BEV predictor produces a local map in the latest ego frame without depth or camera-pose inputs or explicit geometric warping. The evidential model treats observed free space separately and predicts occupancy with associated confidence across the remaining supported region. We train the predictor on simulated RGB sequences paired with complete and visibility-masked occupancy annotations. Our experiments evaluate navigation in simulation and on a wheeled robot, with additional demonstrations on quadruped and humanoid robots. In simulated sequential two-goal navigation, our system achieves 89.6% success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 32.5 percentage points. Across 60 wheeled-robot trials in 20 scenes, it achieves 73.3% success, compared with 33.3% for the strongest evaluated baseline.
2610.27616.tldr_en: This work presents a framework that combines temporal aggregation and occupancy completion in an evidential bird's-eye-view (BEV) representation predicted from short RGB sequences, and trains the predictor on simulated RGB sequences paired with complete and visibility-masked occupancy annotations.

llm.title_ja: EchoNav：ビジュアルナビゲーションのための過去の観測に基づくエビデンシャルBEV補完
llm.tldr_ja: 短いRGBシーケンスから予測されるエビデンシャルな鳥瞰図（BEV）表現において時間的集約と占有補完を組み合わせたフレームワークを提示し、シミュレーションおよび実ロボット実験で高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 雑然とした環境でのビジュアルナビゲーションにおいて、ロボットが以前に観測された構造を復元し、隠された障害物や自由空間を推論する必要がある点。
llm.method: フリーズした特徴量を適応させ、セルごとの重みと学習された更新なしオプションを使用して過去の残差提案を組み合わせるデコーダーを持つ、エビデンシャルBEV表現に基づくフレームワークの構築。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの連続2ゴールナビゲーションで89.6%の成功率を達成し、最強のベースラインを32.5ポイント上回り、車輪型ロボットの実機試験でも73.3%の成功率を記録した。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルナビゲーション

2610.27613.title: Embodied Task Agents Can Perform Fine Manipulation through Tactile In-Context Learning
2610.27613.abstract: Can embodied task agents use tactile experience to perform fine manipulation without task-specific model training? We investigate this capability through Tactile-ETA, a system that incorporates tactile experience into an embodied task agent through in-context learning. Successful expert demonstrations show how contact changes during manipulation. We pair each recorded robot movement with its camera views and bilateral tactile observations. We keep tactile observations at the start and end of each movement and add two neighboring time points when the tactile images change markedly in between. The agent combines these demonstrations with current vision, tactile observations, and proprioception to select actions through general-purpose robot tools, without updating model parameters. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, adding tactile observations to the same two expert demonstrations increases average success from 15.75% to 24.00%, with current sensing and execution interfaces held fixed. Further experiments show that performance depends on the sensory content and representation of demonstrations, while comparing agent models on Lift Bottle reveals substantial differences under the same system configuration. On the real-robot tasks, demonstrations with aligned visual and tactile observations increase the task success rate from 0% to 60%. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using tactile experience in context for fine manipulation and suggest a path toward extending embodied task agents to additional sensory inputs.
2610.27613.tldr_en: The feasibility of using tactile experience in context for fine manipulation is demonstrated and a path toward extending embodied task agents to additional sensory inputs is suggested.

llm.title_ja: 具現化タスクエージェントは触覚インコンテキスト学習を通じて微細なマニピュレーションを実行できる
llm.tldr_ja: 触覚経験をインコンテキスト学習によって具現化タスクエージェントに組み込むシステム「Tactile-ETA」により、モデルパラメータを更新することなく微細なマニピュレーションが可能であることを実証した。
llm.problem: 具現化タスクエージェントがタスク固有のモデル訓練なしで触覚経験を使用して微細なマニピュレーションを行えるかどうかという点。
llm.method: 運動の開始と終了、および触覚画像が著しく変化する時点の触覚観測をカメラビューや固有受容感覚とペアにし、モデルパラメータを更新せずにインコンテキストで行動を選択する「Tactile-ETA」の提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションタスクにおいて触覚観測の追加により平均成功率が15.75%から24.00%に向上し、実機タスクでは成功率が0%から60%に向上した。
keywords_ja: インコンテキスト学習
ロボットエージェント

2610.27586.title: Sensitivity-Orthogonal Residual Learning for Adaptive Sideslip and Cornering Stiffness Estimation
2610.27586.abstract: Online adaptation of the cornering stiffness keeps a model-based sideslip estimator valid as tires change, but competes with learned model correction for the same filter innovation. A corrector with enough parameters can absorb the innovation pattern that a stiffness change produces, and adaptation is suppressed while the fit improves. We propagate the stiffness sensitivities of the predicted measurements through the vehicle states and construct a corrector orthogonal to them. A null-space parameterization enforces the constraint without a penalty coefficient and preserves the static least-squares stiffness estimate on each identification segment. In full-vehicle simulation, the stiffness response of the unconstrained corrector declines as its parameter count grows, whereas the orthogonal corrector responds at least as fully as the uncorrected filter at all sizes and lowers sideslip error by 12.7% to 22.0%. In a simulated drive with a stiffness step, the orthogonal corrector adapts as quickly as the uncorrected filter and lowers sideslip error during and after the transient. On public real-vehicle data, the 430-parameter unconstrained corrector loses most of its response to deliberate offsets of the filter's nominal stiffness, whereas the orthogonal corrector of the same size retains most of it, with a sideslip error slightly above the uncorrected filter's.
2610.27586.comment: 25 pages, 15 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to Vehicle System Dynamics
2610.27586.tldr_en: This work propagates the stiffness sensitivities of the predicted measurements through the vehicle states and construct a corrector orthogonal to them, which enforces the constraint without a penalty coefficient and preserves the static least-squares stiffness estimate on each identification segment.

llm.title_ja: 適応型横滑り角およびコーナリング剛性推定のための感度直交残差学習
llm.tldr_ja: 予測測定値の剛性感度を車両状態を通じて伝播させ、それらに直交する補正器を構築することで、ペナルティ係数なしで制約を強制し、各識別セグメントで静的最小二乗剛性推定値を保持することを示した。
llm.problem: コーナリング剛性のオンライン適応において、タイヤの変化に対応してモデルベースの横滑り推定器を有効に保とうとする際、学習されたモデル補正とフィルターのイノベーションが競合してしまう点。
llm.method: 予測測定値の剛性感度を車両状態を通じて伝播させ、その感度に直交する補正器をヌル空間パラメータ化により構築する手法の提案。
llm.result: 完全車両シミュレーションにおいて、直交補正器は横滑り誤差を12.7%から22.0%低下させ、実車データでも名目剛性の意図的なオフセットに対する応答性を維持した。

2610.27574.title: The Show-Up Attack: When Subagents Win Over Their Supervisor
2610.27574.abstract: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed to coordinate multiple large language model (LLM) agents. However, this also creates new attack surfaces: malicious agents may have chances to exploit the coordination. In this paper, we propose and study the \textit{show-up attack}, in which a malicious subagent manipulates the supervisor into involving it in tasks beyond its assigned scope. To evaluate this risk, we propose SUA-Arena, which implements 6 attack strategies and contains 188 test cases. Then, we evaluate 6 frontier LLMs and find that all of them are vulnerable to show-up attacks. For example, GPT-5.6-Sol as a supervisor suffers an ASR of up to 0.93. Mitigation strategies such as prompting and restricted communication fail to reduce the risk consistently. These results show that multi-agent systems need explicit mechanisms for enforcing authority boundaries.
2610.27574.tldr_en: The proposed SUA-Arena, which implements 6 attack strategies and contains 188 test cases, finds that all of them are vulnerable to show-up attacks and shows that multi-agent systems need explicit mechanisms for enforcing authority boundaries.

llm.title_ja: ショーアップ攻撃：サブエージェントがスーパーバイザーを打ち負かすとき
llm.tldr_ja: 悪意のあるサブエージェントが割り当てられたスコープを超えたタスクにスーパーバイザーを関与させる「ショーアップ攻撃」を提案・研究し、すべてのフロンティアLLMが脆弱であることを示した。
llm.problem: 複数の大規模言語モデル（LLM）エージェントを調整するマルチエージェントシステムの普及に伴い、悪意のあるエージェントが協調プロセスを悪用する新しい攻撃サーフェスが生まれている点。
llm.method: 6つの攻撃戦略と188のテストケースを含む「SUA-Arena」を実装し、6つのフロンティアLLMを評価するアプローチ。
llm.result: 評価されたすべてのLLMがショーアップ攻撃に対して脆弱であり、例えばGPT-5.6-Solは最大0.93の攻撃成功率（ASR）を示した。

2610.27573.title: When LLMs Manipulate: Measuring Behavioral, Social, and Temporal Effects
2610.27573.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can influence user trust and decision-making through subtle linguistic cues, yet the behavioral effects of manipulative outputs remain poorly quantified. We introduce a behavioral computing framework for measuring \textit{behavioral vulnerability}, defined as users' susceptibility to manipulative AI responses. Building on DarkPatterns-LLM benchmark, we generate controlled manipulative stimuli using Manipulation Gradient Descent (MGD), targeting biases associated with authority, urgency, and social proof. We analyze participant responses using the Multi-Stakeholder Impact Assessment Network (MSIAN) to model cross-user influence and the Temporal Harm Propagation Model (THPM) to characterize the persistence of behavioral effects over time. In a study involving 120 participants, manipulative framing produced significant changes in trust calibration and compliance ($p < 0.01$), with effects also propagating across social contexts. These findings highlight the need to extend LLM safety evaluation beyond model outputs to measurable behavioral consequences and provide a computational framework for quantifying individual, social, and temporal risks arising from manipulative AI interactions.
2610.27573.tldr_en: The need to extend LLM safety evaluation beyond model outputs to measurable behavioral consequences and provide a computational framework for quantifying individual, social, and temporal risks arising from manipulative AI interactions is highlighted.

2610.27562.title: Velocity Optimization via Thermal Imaging Enhances Autonomous Tumor Resection
2610.27562.abstract: Objective: To demonstrate and evaluate THERMO, a thermal-velocity optimization algorithm for autonomous electrosurgery, in ex vivo porcine tissue using the UR10e-based ASTR system. Methods: Thermography for Electrosurgical Rate Modulation via Optimization (ThERMO), a closed-loop algorithm that uses real-time thermal imaging data to minimize thermal injury while ensuring accurate cut margins, was tested on ex vivo porcine tissue. Histological analysis was performed to detect thermal injury extent at a cellular level, and 3D photogrammetric measurement was used to verify margin accuracy. ThERMO's performance was compared against two previously used fixed velocity methods. Results: ThERMO outperformed both fixed velocity comparison methods without requiring data-driven training or iterative tuning, reducing thermal injury by up to 52%, improving cut accuracy by up to 59%, and maintaining task completion speed. Conclusions: Closed-loop thermal feedback via ThERMO improves autonomous robotic electrosurgery by simultaneously reducing thermal injury and improving margin accuracy, reinforcing its value over fixed velocity approaches for tumor resection applications. Significance: This work advances autonomous robotic tumor resection by demonstrating that real-time closed-loop thermal feedback control can substantially reduce collateral tissue damage and improve surgical margin accuracy.
2610.27562.tldr_en: Close-loop thermal feedback via ThERMO improves autonomous robotic electrosurgery by simultaneously reducing thermal injury and improving margin accuracy, reinforcing its value over fixed velocity approaches for tumor resection applications.

llm.title_ja: サーマルイメージングによる速度最適化が自律型腫瘍切除を強化する
llm.tldr_ja: リアルタイムの熱画像データを使用して熱損傷を最小限に抑えつつ正確な切除マージンを確保する閉ループアルゴリズム「ThERMO」が、データ駆動型の訓練や反復的なチューニングなしに、固定速度手法と比較して熱損傷を低減し切除精度を向上させたことを示した。
llm.problem: 自律型電気手術において、熱損傷を最小限に抑えながら正確な切除マージンを確保することが課題である点。
llm.method: リアルタイムの熱画像データを用いて熱損傷を最小化し切除マージンの精度を保証する閉ループアルゴリズム「ThERMO」を実装し、離体ブタ組織で評価する手法。
llm.result: ThERMOは、データ駆動型の訓練や反復チューニングなしで、固定速度の比較手法に対して熱損傷を最大52%削減し、切除精度を最大59%向上させ、タスク完了速度を維持した。

2610.27547.title: SynCalib: Breaking Dataset Shortcuts in LiDAR-Camera Calibration via Extrinsic-Controllable Synthesis
2610.27547.abstract: Online LiDAR-camera calibration remains a fundamental yet challenging task in the field of robotics. Recently, deep learning-based data-driven approaches have emerged, offering high-precision, targetless calibration capabilities. However, existing methods often suffer from a critical dataset shortcut phenomenon due to the lack of extrinsic diversity in their training data. Networks tend to overfit to fixed nominal extrinsic configurations, leading to severe performance degradation and poor generalization in real-world deployments. To address this limitation, we propose a highly generalizable data generation framework tailored for training LiDAR-camera calibration networks. Our framework leverages existing omnidirectional image datasets annotated with depth ground truth to synthesize multi-modal calibration data under rigorous extrinsic constraints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the data generated by our pipeline significantly enhances the generalization and robustness of typical learning-based calibration networks. Furthermore, we conduct comprehensive real-world evaluations across various camera-LiDAR configurations, validating the zero-shot transfer capability of models trained exclusively on our synthetic data. To facilitate future research and community use, the code for data generation, the pre-trained models, and online benchmark datasets will be made publicly available.
2610.27547.tldr_en: This work proposes a highly generalizable data generation framework tailored for training LiDAR-camera calibration networks, and leverages existing omnidirectional image datasets annotated with depth ground truth to synthesize multi-modal calibration data under rigorous extrinsic constraints.

llm.title_ja: SynCalib：外因的制御可能な合成によるLiDAR-カメラキャリブレーションにおけるデータセットのショートカットの打破
llm.tldr_ja: 既存のオムニidirectional画像データセットを活用して厳格な外因的制約の下でマルチモーダルなキャリブレーションデータを合成する汎用的なデータ生成フレームワークを提案し、学習ベースのキャリブレーションネットワークの汎化性能と頑健性を高めた。
llm.problem: オンラインでのLiDAR-カメラキャリブレーションにおいて、訓練データにおける外因的多様性の欠如によるデータセットのショートカット現象が発生し、実世界での汎化性能が低下する点。
llm.method: 深度グランド真値がアノテーションされた既存のオムニidirectional画像データセットを利用し、厳格な外因的制約の下でマルチモーダルなキャリブレーションデータを合成するデータ生成フレームワーク「SynCalib」の提案。
llm.result: 提案手法により生成されたデータが、典型的な学習ベースのキャリブレーションネットワークの汎化性能と頑健性を大幅に向上させ、ゼロショット転移能力を実証した。
keywords_ja: LiDAR-カメラキャリブレーション
センサーフュージョン

2610.27533.title: Adversarial Benchmarks and BenchDoor Attacks: Exploiting Benchmark Incentives for Backdoor Attacks
2610.27533.abstract: Machine learning benchmarks act as guideposts for model development and spur the creation of training datasets intended to improve benchmark scores. We introduce BenchDoor, a family of data poisoning attacks that exploits this incentive. Beyond preserving benign performance, BenchDoor requires benchmark gains that encourage adoption of data that also implants a backdoor. The adversary either manipulates a benchmark's training or test data, creating an adversarial benchmark, or supplies an independent training dataset while leaving the benchmark unchanged. We formalize five attack scenarios, including training on rewritten test examples and applying similarity-based decontamination. Across multiple-choice Q&A, text classification, and open-ended Q&A with Qwen and Gemma models, BenchDoor achieves positive benchmark gains for all 30 evaluated configurations, with held-out attack success rates of 82.33% to 100.00% at poisoning rates of 2% to 10%. Both objectives remain achievable after synthetic data generation and similarity-based decontamination, with attack success rates of at least 90.33%. These findings show how benchmarks can serve as attack vectors both through their own data and through training resources that deliver improvements on them.
2610.27533.tldr_en: benchDoor, a family of data poisoning attacks that exploits this incentive to serve as attack vectors both through their own data and through training resources that deliver improvements on them, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: 敵対的ベンチマークとBenchDoor攻撃：バックドア攻撃のためのベンチマークインセンティブの悪用
llm.tldr_ja: モデル開発のインセンティブを利用してバックドアを埋め込むデータポイズニング攻撃ファミリ「BenchDoor」を提案し、評価されたすべての構成で正のベンチマーク向上と高いバックドア攻撃成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 機械学習ベンチマークがモデル開発のガイドポストとして機能する一方、そのインセンティブがデータポイズニング攻撃などの悪用に利用される可能性がある点。
llm.method: ベンチマークの訓練・テストデータを操作するか独立した訓練データセットを供給してバックドアを埋め込むデータポイズニング攻撃「BenchDoor」の形式化と評価。
llm.result: QwenおよびGemmaモデルを用いた30の評価構成すべてで正のベンチマーク向上が達成され、保持された攻撃成功率は82.33%から100.00%に達した。
keywords_ja: 機械学習ベンチマーク

2610.27522.title: OmniVLoc: Topo-metric Visual Localization for Omnidirectional Cameras
2610.27522.abstract: Omnidirectional cameras provide surround-view information, significantly overcoming the field-of-view constraints for traditional visual localization systems. However, existing localization systems fail to fully exploit the characteristics of omnidirectional cameras, struggling to deliver accurate and robust localization performance amidst scene content variations and illumination-induced appearance changes. In this work, we propose OmniVLoc, a surround-view localization system based on a topo-metric framework. By integrating state-of-the-art global place recognition and monocular depth estimation methods, we introduce a multi-constrained visual localization paradigm. By solving a scale-aware pose graph and performing precise spherical bundle adjustment, we accurately recover the metric-level pose for each query frame.Furthermore, a hierarchical verification mechanism is designed to filter out erroneous outputs across different stages, effectively bolstering the overall system robustness. Extensive experiments on both public and our custom datasets validate the superior accuracy and reliability of OmniVLoc. To benefit the community, our source code and dataset will be made publicly available upon publication.
2610.27522.tldr_en: Omnidirectional cameras provide surround-view information, significantly overcoming the field-of-view constraints for traditional visual localization systems, and OmniVLoc, a surround-view localization system based on a topo-metric framework, is proposed, introducing a multi-constrained visual localization paradigm.

llm.title_ja: OmniVLoc：全方位カメラのためのトポ・メトリック視覚的ローカリゼーション
llm.tldr_ja: 大域的場所認識と単眼深度推定を統合し、スケール認識型ポーズグラフの求解と球面バンドル調整を行う全方位カメラ向けトポ・メトリック視覚的ローカリゼーションシステム「OmniVLoc」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の視覚的ローカリゼーションシステムにおける視野制約や、シーンの内容変動・照明変化に対する不十分な頑健性。
llm.method: 大域的場所認識と単眼深度推定手法を統合したマルチ制約視覚的ローカリゼーションパラダイム、および階層的検証メカニズムを持つ「OmniVLoc」システムの構築。
llm.result: 公開データセットおよび独自データセットを用いた大規模な実験により、OmniVLocの優れた精度と信頼性が検証された。
keywords_ja: 視覚的ローカリゼーション

2610.27504.title: Robot-Task Suitability in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Task Allocation
2610.27504.abstract: Heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation depends on estimates of how suitable individual robots are for candidate tasks, yet suitability can be defined in substantially different ways. We compare ten deterministic methods and two LLM-based variants spanning rule-based, similarity-based, requirement-oriented, fuzzy, and semantic approaches. Using common robot and task profiles, we compare how the methods score and rank candidate robots, identify feasibility, and select a top robot, while examining how these outcomes change with team composition, scale, spatial context, capability uncertainty, and task representation. The methods frequently disagree despite operating on identical scenarios. Generic similarity measures can violate properties expected under a one-sided requirement-satisfaction interpretation of suitability, while LLM-based scoring introduces additional stochastic and linguistic sensitivity. These results show that robot--task suitability should be treated as an explicit modeling choice whose assumptions, robustness, and decision-level consequences should be considered before allocation.
2610.27504.comment: Accepted at Workshop on Foundation Models for Multi-Robot Systems (FM-MRS), IROS 2026
2610.27504.tldr_en: The results show that robot--task suitability should be treated as an explicit modeling choice whose assumptions, robustness, and decision-level consequences should be considered before allocation.

llm.title_ja: 異種マルチロボットタスク割り当てにおけるロボットとタスクの適合性
llm.tldr_ja: 異種マルチロボットのタスク割り当てにおける適合性の定義方法の違いを比較し、適合性を明示的なモデリング上の選択肢として扱うべきであることを示した。
llm.problem: 異種マルチロボットのタスク割り当ては個別ロボットのタスク適合性見積もりに依存するが、適合性の定義が手法によって大きく異なる点。
llm.method: ルールベース、類似度ベース、要件指向、ファジー、意味論的アプローチにわたる10の決定的手法と2つのLLMベースのバリアントを比較し、チーム構成やスケールを変えて評価する手法。
llm.result: 同一のシナリオで動作しているにもかかわらず手法間で不一致が頻発し、一般の類似度尺度は要件充足解釈の性質に違反する場合があり、LLMベースのスコアリングには確率的・言語的感度があることが示された。

2610.27496.title: Evaluating Social Reasoning in Embodied Vision-Language Models
2610.27496.abstract: Foundation models now serve as reasoning layers for robot teams, but it remains unclear whether embodiment-specialized vision-language models (VLMs) preserve the social-reasoning capabilities of general-purpose VLMs. We evaluate Gemini Robotics-ER on SHREC, a benchmark of real human-robot social interactions, and compare it with published general-purpose VLM baselines. Robotics-ER outperforms GPT-4o-mini on error/competence detection but performs worse on detailed social-attribute judgments; adding a visual frame helps one task while hurting the other. These results suggest embodiment-specialized models may perform differently on social judgments that can be read more directly from observable interaction cues versus those requiring more inference about a person's internal state. Because the comparison spans model families, these differences cannot be attributed to embodiment specialization alone. This matters for multi-robot systems, where a shared foundation model could cause systematic social-perception errors to influence multiple coordination decisions. This work presents an initial evaluation, with broader cross-context and video-based analyses left for future work.
2610.27496.comment: Accepted at Workshop on Foundation Models for Multi-Robot Systems (FM-MRS), IROS 2026
2610.27496.tldr_en: Evaluated Gemini Robotics-ER on SHREC, a benchmark of real human-robot social interactions, and a comparison with general-purpose VLM baselines suggest embodiment-specialized models may perform differently on social judgments that can be read more directly from observable interaction cues versus those requiring more inference about a person's internal state.

llm.title_ja: 具現化視覚言語モデルにおける社会的推論の評価
llm.tldr_ja: 具現化特化型VLMであるGemini Robotics-ERを実世界の社会的相互作用ベンチマークSHRECで評価し、汎用VLMベースラインと比較した結果、観察可能な相互作用の手がかりから直接読み取れる社会的判断と内面状態の推論が必要な判断で性能が異なることが示唆された。
llm.problem: 基盤モデルがロボットチームの推論層として機能する中で、具現化特化型の視覚言語モデル（VLM）が汎用VLMの社会的推論能力を保持しているかどうかが不明である点。
llm.method: Gemini Robotics-ERを実世界の人間とロボットの社会的相互作用のベンチマークであるSHRECで評価し、公開されている汎用VLMベースラインと比較する手法。
llm.result: Robotics-ERはエラー/有能さの検出でGPT-4o-miniを上回ったが、詳細な社会的属性の判断では劣り、視覚フレームの追加がタスクによってプラスチックにもマイナスにも働くことが分かった。
llm.limitation: モデルファミリーの比較であるため、違いを具現化特化のみに起因させることができない点、およびビデオベースの分析が今後の課題であること。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.27485.title: HATCH: Hardware-Attested Task Chains for Verifiable Manipulation
2610.27485.abstract: Capability claims in robot manipulation are unverifiable, and existing leaderboards are each closed, simulated, or gameable. We propose HATCH, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark. Tasks span five skill categories at three difficulty levels and are chained so that the sensor confirming one task's completion unlocks the next, turning a room into a single long-horizon evaluation. Success is confirmed by instrumentation rather than human judgment, scoring is embodiment-agnostic, and object placements are randomized by a run-day seed. Entrants submit attested self-runs (uncut video, sensor logs, and the seed), with occasional organized events for calibration. Task specifications, build guide, bill of materials, and scoring rubrics are released under an open license.
2610.27485.comment: 2 pages, 1 table. Accepted at the 5th Workshop on Open Robotics Software, IROS 2026, Pittsburgh, PA, USA. Benchmark repository: https://github.com/shizacharania/hatch-benchmark
2610.27485.tldr_en: HATCH, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark, is proposed, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark.

llm.title_ja: HATCH：検証可能なマニピュレーションのためのハードウェア証明付きタスクチェーン
llm.tldr_ja: オープンに仕様化され、物理的に複製可能で、センサーによってスコアリングされるリハーサル不可能なロボットベンチマーク「HATCH」を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーションにおける能力の主張が検証可能ではなく、既存のリーダーボードがそれぞれ閉じた環境、シミュレーション、またはゲーム化されたものである点。
llm.method: センサーの確認によって次のタスクのロックを解除する、3つの難易度レベルの5つのスキルカテゴリにわたるチェーン構造を持つオープンなロボットエスケープルーム「HATCH」の提案。
llm.result: 人間の判断ではなく計測器によって成功が確認され、実施日ごとのシードによってオブジェクトの配置がランダム化される評価システムが構築された。
keywords_ja: ロボットエスケープルーム

2610.27472.title: Towards Autonomous Bricklaying Using Boston Dynamics Spot
2610.27472.abstract: Mobile legged robots offer unique advantages for on-site construction, including the ability to traverse unstructured terrain, climb stairs, and operate independently between spatially separated work zones. This paper presents a proof-of-concept system for autonomous brick stacking using a Boston Dynamics Spot quadrupedal robot equipped with a manipulator arm. The system operates between a supply area and an assembly area, using AprilTag fiducials for localization and autowalk missions for navigation. Target brick positions and orientations are specified in CAD software and exported directly for robotic execution. We evaluate placement accuracy through ten repeated assemblies of a curved four-layer wall comprising 14 wooden bricks. Results show mean translation errors below 10 mm and mean yaw errors below 1.5 degrees, while the overall RMSE across all runs is 27.72 mm (translation) and 2.06 degrees (rotation). The system was also tested outdoors with stairs between the two areas. The workflow is modular and easily extendable to different wall geometries.
2610.27472.comment: 8 pages. Published in the Proceedings of the 43rd International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction (ISARC 2026), Singapore
2610.27472.journal_ref: Proc. 43rd Int. Symp. Automation and Robotics in Construction (ISARC 2026), Singapore, 2026, pp. 398-405
2610.27472.tldr_en: A proof-of-concept system for autonomous brick stacking using a Boston Dynamics Spot quadrupedal robot equipped with a manipulator arm that operates between a supply area and an assembly area, using AprilTag fiducials for localization and autowalk missions for navigation.
2610.27472.venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction (IAARC)

badges.venue: Proc. 43rd Int. Symp. Automation and Rob 2026

llm.title_ja: Boston Dynamics Spotを用いた自律型レンガ積みに向けた取り組み
llm.tldr_ja: マニピュレータアームを装備した四足歩行ロボットBoston Dynamics Spotを用いて、供給エリアと組立エリアの間で自律的にレンガを積み上げる実証システムを提案し、その配置精度を評価した。
llm.problem: 移動型脚式ロボットが、非構造化地形の横断、階段の昇降、作業ゾーン間での独立した動作といった建設現場での利点を活かして自律作業を行う必要がある点。
llm.method: AprilTag基準マークによるローカライゼーションとautowalkミッションによるナビゲーションを使用し、CADで指定された目標位置に基づいてロボットアームでレンガを配置するシステムの構築。
llm.result: 4層の曲面壁の10回の繰り返し組立において、平均並進誤差が10 mm未満、平均ヨー誤差が1.5度未満であり、全体のRMSEが並進27.72 mm、回転2.06度であることが示された。

2610.27417.title: KPHarness: Co-Evolving Knowledge and Probing for Long-Horizon Gaming Harnesses
2610.27417.abstract: A failed gaming trajectory reveals that an agent needs intervention, but not necessarily how its execution harness should change. Effective harness adaptation therefore requires gathering diagnostic evidence, rather than merely proposing alternative recovery rules. We present KPHarness, a framework that adapts the external execution harness of a frozen vision-language-action model through knowledge-probing co-evolution. Recovery knowledge supplies context-specific intervention hypotheses that guide active probing; probe outcomes reveal when these hypotheses apply and provide evidence for refining both recovery knowledge and later probe selection. This reciprocal process allows the harness to improve not only which interventions it applies, but also how it investigates failures. KPHarness separates fast policy execution from a slow research loop that translates accumulated knowledge and probing evidence into bounded harness revisions. Each revision is compared with the incumbent under matched sandbox conditions and accepted only when the paired evaluation shows improvement. Recoveries supported by further validation are retained for cross-task reuse, while immediate interaction feedback and delayed episode-success credit update action- and knowledge-probing policies during adaptation. Experiments on Minecraft tasks spanning mining, combat, and crafting show improved task coverage over bare policy execution, a manually specified fixed harness, and knowledge-only harness evolution with non-adaptive probing. Evaluation on previously unseen tasks further shows improved task completion with the evolved harness, knowledge bank, and probing policies held fixed,
2610.27417.tldr_en: KPHarness is presented, a framework that adapts the external execution harness of a frozen vision-language-action model through knowledge-probing co-evolution through knowledge-probing co-evolution and separates fast policy execution from a slow research loop that translates accumulated knowledge and probing evidence into bounded harness revisions.

llm.title_ja: KPHarness：長期ゲームハーネスのための知識とプロービングの共進化
llm.tldr_ja: KPHarnessは、知識とプロービングの共進化を通じて凍結されたビジョン・言語・行動モデルの外部実行ハーネスを適応させるフレームワークであり、高速なポリシー実行と低速なリサーチループを分離する。
llm.problem: 失敗したゲームの軌跡からエージェントに介入が必要なことは分かるが、実行ハーネスをどう変更すべきかは自明ではない。
llm.method: 回復知識を用いた能動的なプロービングの誘導と、プローブ結果に基づく知識・プローブ選択の洗練を共進化させる。
llm.result: マインクラフトのタスクにおいて、生ポリシー、手動の固定ハーネス、非適応型プロービングを持つ知識のみのハーネスよりもタスクカバレッジが向上した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2610.27414.title: Real-Time Disturbance-Aware Koopman Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors in Spatially Varying Winds
2610.27414.abstract: Reliable quadrotor flight in disturbed environments requires predictive models that remain accurate as unmodeled aerodynamic effects change during deployment. We introduce a disturbance-aware Koopman Control Family (DA-KCF) framework that preserves an offline-identified nominal model while learning only a disturbance-induced correction online. A reference-dependent KCF is first learned from simulation data and calibrated using limited hardware data. During deployment, the nominal KCF remains fixed while a lightweight residual ensemble learns a low-dimensional disturbance correction from causal state-command-state transitions. The Adaptive DA-KCF model is incorporated into MPC, where disturbance corrections are evaluated along the prediction horizon to optimize position and yaw references sent to the onboard stabilizing controller. Hardware experiments on a nano-quadrotor under uniform wind and a spatially varying wake demonstrate that online adaptation improves multi-step prediction and trajectory tracking as disturbance-induced model mismatch increases, while satisfying real-time control requirements.

llm.title_ja: 空間変動風中でのクアッドコプターに向けたリアルタイム外乱適応型Koopmanモデル予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: オフラインで同定された公称モデルを維持しつつオンラインで外乱による補正のみを学習する外乱適応型Koopman制御ファミリー（DA-KCF）フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 未モデル化の空力効果が変化する外乱環境において、クアッドコプターが正確な予測モデルを維持し信頼性高く飛行することが困難である。
llm.method: シミュレーションデータから基準依存のKCFを学習し、デプロイ時に軽量な残差アンサンブルを用いて低次元の外乱補正をオンライン学習してMPCに組み込む。
llm.result: ナノ・クアッドコプターを用いたハードウェア実験により、外乱モデルの不一致が増加する中でもリアルタイム制御要件を満たしつつ追従性が向上することを示した。

2610.27387.title: Training Controllable World Models via Action Influence Maximization
2610.27387.abstract: Action-conditioned video generative models trained on successful, goal-directed demonstrations tend to ignore the commanded action, rendering a plausible expert-like future regardless of what is asked of them. We trace this failure to training data that lack sufficient action influence. We analyze this metric and prove that it upper bounds the action influence that any model trained on that data can express. Expert demonstrations, whose narrow action distributions let next states be predicted without attending to the action, set a low ceiling that no amount of model capacity alone can raise. Raising it requires collecting different data. We introduce Action Influence Maximization (AIM), an algorithm for actively collecting training data for improving dataset action influence. We compare the performance and data-efficiency of AIM against exploration heuristics and intrinsic-motivation methods on simulated navigation and manipulation tasks. In pixel-based manipulation, AIM is the only method that consistently improves controllability: 500 actively collected episodes added to 3k demonstrations match a world model trained on 300k expert episodes on end-effector controllability, an $85\times$ reduction in data.
2610.27387.tldr_en: This work introduces Action Influence Maximization (AIM), an algorithm for actively collecting training data for improving dataset action influence, and compares the performance and data-efficiency of AIM against exploration heuristics and intrinsic-motivation methods on simulated navigation and manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: 行動影響最大化を通じた制御可能な世界モデルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: データセットの行動影響を向上させるための能動的データ収集アルゴリズムであるAction Influence Maximization (AIM)を提案し、シミュレーション上のナビゲーションおよびマニピュレーションタスクで評価する。
llm.problem: 成功したデモに基づいて学習された行動条件付きビデオ生成モデルは、指示された行動を無視しがちである。
llm.method: データセットの行動影響度を向上させるために能動的にトレーニングデータを収集するアルゴリズム（AIM）を導入する。
llm.result: ピクセルベースのマニピュレーションにおいて、専門家のデモと比較して85分の1のデータ量で同等のエンドエフェクタ制御性を達成した。

2610.27373.title: Fundamental Impossibility Results in AI Safety: Trading Off between Desiderata
2610.27373.abstract: Is there a fundamental tradeoff between desiderata for safe AI systems, such as harmlessness and helpfulness? We answer by formalizing the interaction between AI systems and users as a game with three players: a defender and an attacker that are computationally or informationally bounded, and an AI that provides public advice and is less constrained. Our main result shows that there is a fundamental tradeoff in providing advice that helps the defender while advice remains public. We also consider whether the information that the AI shares can be manipulated to benefit only the defender and conclude with a discussion of how we can use these results in designing safer AI systems.
2610.27373.tldr_en: This work formalizes the interaction between AI systems and users as a game with three players: a defender and an attacker that are computationally or informationally bounded, and an AI that provides public advice and is less constrained.

2610.27357.title: LiBRA: Logit Fingerprints for Byzantine-Robust Client Selection in Federated Learning
2610.27357.abstract: Byzantine-robust aggregation shields federated learning from malicious updates, but the rules that filter out suspect updates do so by comparing clients' parameter vectors. That comparison requires access to every client's update, which secure aggregation exists to withhold, costs $O(n^2 d)$ in the parameter dimension $d$, and is defined only between clients that share an architecture. We propose LiBRA, which compares clients on what their models compute rather than on the parameters that compute them, using a fingerprint of $C^2$ values for $C$ classes, the class-conditional logit response of each client's model to pseudo-patterns optimised against it. We instantiate LiBRA as variants of Krum, Multi-Krum and Bulyan that change only what the dissimilarity score is computed on. On Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 with three architectures and four backdoor and label-manipulation attacks under i.i.d. partitions, each variant holds every attack its parent holds, and on identical client updates under a backdoor attack the fingerprint ranks malicious clients within 0.006 AUC of the full parameter vector. The variants thus match the robustness of the rules they extend, while their trust decision reads no client parameter, compares up to 49,090 times fewer values, and can by construction compare clients whose architectures differ, at the cost of one pattern optimisation per client per round.
2610.27357.tldr_en: LiBRA is proposed, which compares clients on what their models compute rather than on the parameters that compute them, using a fingerprint of C^2 values for C$ classes, the class-conditional logit response of each client's model to pseudo-patterns optimised against it.

llm.title_ja: LiBRA：フェデレーテッドラーニングにおけるByzantineロバストなクライアント選択のためのロジット指紋
llm.tldr_ja: モデルが計算するものに基づいてクライアントを比較するLiBRAを提案し、パラメータそのものではなく最適化された擬似パターンに対するクラス条件付きロジット応答を用いる。
llm.problem: Byzantineロバストな集約手法はクライアントのパラメータベクトルを比較する必要があるが、セキュアアグリゲーションの制約や計算コストの課題がある。
llm.method: 各クライアントモデルのクラス条件付きロジット応答からなる「ロジット指紋」を用いて、パラメータにアクセスせずにクライアントを比較する。
llm.result: パラメータを読まずに従来のルールと同等のロバスト性を維持しつつ、比較する値を最大49,090倍削減できることを示した。
keywords_ja: フェデレーテッドラーニング

2610.27350.title: Refuses When Asked, Complies When Acting: A Runtime Safety Check for Robot Control Loops
2610.27350.abstract: Frontier models can control robots through agent harnesses that loop on one question: what motion comes next toward the user's goal? We show that this default loop carries out harmful instructions. With GPT-6 Astra controlling a low-cost SO-101 arm through the Inspect Robots harness on three household tasks whose hazard is common knowledge, such as "put the knife in the toy basket", the policy refused 0% of 15 trials, attempted the harm every time, and completed it in 27%. Its one exit, give_up, is meant for goals that cannot be achieved, and it never cited the hazard. We add an optional runtime safety check to the loop: before the first motion, the model is asked whether it would carry out the instruction, given the same camera frames. The check would have stopped all 15 hazardous instructions, including the 4 that completed the harm, and flagged none of the 15 harmless controls. Code and data: https://github.com/Arnav-Gr0ver/Refuses-When-Asked-Complies-When-Acting.
2610.27350.comment: 4 pages plus references. Submitted to the Science of Physical AI Safety (SPAIS) workshop at CoRL 2026
2610.27350.tldr_en: An optional runtime safety check is added to the loop: before the first motion, the model is asked whether it would carry out the instruction, given the same camera frames, and the check would have stopped all 15 hazardous instructions, including the 4 that completed the harm, and flagged none of the 15 harmless controls.

llm.title_ja: 質問には拒否し、行動時には従う：ロボット制御ループのためのランタイム安全性チェック
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットのエージェントループの最初の動作の前に、同じカメラ画像を与えて指示を実行するかどうかをモデルに問うオプションのランタイム安全性チェックを追加する。
llm.problem: フロンティアモデルをロボット制御に用いるデフォルトのループでは、有害な指示が無条件に実行されてしまう。
llm.method: 最初の動作の前に、モデルに指示を実行するかどうかを自己問答させるランタイム安全性チェックをループに組み込む。
llm.result: 15件の危険な指示すべてを阻止し、15件の無害な制御は誤検知しなかったことを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2610.27336.title: Determination of the Human-Robot Interaction Workspace for Robot Assisted Head Stabilization Control
2610.27336.abstract: Accurate head immobilization is critical for medical procedures such as neuroimaging and intracranial radiation therapy, where even minor motion can compromise precision. Traditional methods, such as rigid stereotactic frames and thermoplastic face masks, are invasive, uncomfortable for patients, and require a time-consuming setup. To overcome these limitations, a novel approach employs a 6-degree-of-freedom (6DoF) robotic head holder that is integrated with real-time optical motion tracking, enabling dynamic compensation for head movements without physical restraint. However, implementing this system requires a detailed biomechanical understanding of skull-cervical spine interactions to define safe and effective motion limits. In this study, we conduct a human volunteer investigation using a 6DoF Stewart platform robot to characterize biokinematic workspace of the head-neck system and establish foundational data for human-robot interaction in precision head stabilization.
2610.27336.tldr_en: A human volunteer investigation using a 6DoF Stewart platform robot is conducted to characterize biokinematic workspace of the head-neck system and establish foundational data for human-robot interaction in precision head stabilization.

llm.title_ja: ロボット支援頭部安定化制御に向けたヒューマン・ロボット相互作用ワークスペースの決定
llm.tldr_ja: 6自由度Stewartプラットフォームロボットを用いた人間のボランティア調査を実施し、頭部・頸部システムの生物運動学的ワークスペースを特徴付ける。
llm.problem: 頭部の正確な固定が必要な医療処置において、従来の固定フレームやマスクは侵襲的で患者の負担が大きい。
llm.method: 6自由度のロボット式頭部ホルダーと光学式モーション追跡を統合し、人間のボランティアを対象とした実験により頭頸部システムの生物運動学的ワークスペースを調査する。
llm.result: 精密な頭部安定化における人間とロボットの相互作用のための基礎データを確立した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.27315.title: Design and Control of a Multimodal Legged-Aerial Robot Through Separate Control Contraction Metrics
2610.27315.abstract: The integration of dynamic legged locomotion and aerial mobility offers versatility that is deterred by challenges in payload distribution, actuation, and the contrasting requirements of both domains. In this paper, we present the design and operation of a multimodal quadrupedal aerial-legged robot. The presence of legged aerial systems also allows for thruster-assisted legged locomotion, which we make possible with a unified control framework using Control Contraction Metrics (CCM). We search for separate domain-specific contraction metrics for walking and flight independently offline and unify them using an online energy-based Control Lyapunov Function Quadratic Program (CLF QP). This enables optimal, cross-domain control allocation, which we show using simulations. We also show experimental results that validate the mechanical viability of our hardware and the paradigm of thruster-assisted trotting. The stability of said experiments motivates the deployment of the control framework for multimodal operations.
2610.27315.comment: Presented at 2026 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems, Pittsburgh PA

llm.title_ja: 分離された制御収縮指標を用いたマルチモーダル脚・空中ロボットの設計と制御
llm.tldr_ja: オフラインで別々に求めた歩行と飛行のドメイン固有の収縮指標を、オンラインのエネルギーベースCLF-QPを用いて統合し、最適でクロスドメインな制御割り当てを実現する。
llm.problem: 動的な脚式移動と空中モビリティの統合は、ペイロード分散、駆動系、および両ドメインの相反する要件によって困難である。
llm.method: 制御収縮指標（CCM）を用いた統一制御フレームワークを提案し、オフラインの指標探索とオンラインのCLF-QPによる統合を行う。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよびハードウェアの実験により、ハードウェアの機械的妥当性とスラスタ補助歩行のパラダイムを検証した。

2610.27310.title: RadGeoLoc: Radar Geolocalization via Particle Filtering
2610.27310.abstract: In real-time autonomous field applications, GNSS is often unreliable and inaccurate. A possible solution is localizing against a prebuilt map like a satellite image, as it is georeferenced and already surveyed. In this work, we localize a spinning radar measurement against overhead RGB imagery with a learned observation model. We use a radar representation pretrained by masked reconstruction and align it to features from a satellite image. A particle filter propagated by radar odometry proposes candidate poses, and our observation model provides a likelihood over these poses. We evaluate our method over 31 distinct routes, over 8 datasets spanning both urban and offroad conditions using only ground radar and a coarse local prior. We also examine the robustness over changing weather using repeated traversals over the same route over 13 months, in both urban and offroad conditions.
2610.27310.tldr_en: This work localizes a spinning radar measurement against overhead RGB imagery with a learned observation model that uses a radar representation pretrained by masked reconstruction and aligns it to features from a satellite image.

llm.title_ja: RadGeoLoc：パーティクルフィルタによるレーダー位置特定
llm.tldr_ja: マスク再構築により事前学習されたレーダー表現を用い、回転レーダー測定値を衛星画像の俯瞰特徴量に位置合わせする手法を提案する。
llm.problem: リアルタイムの自律型フィールドアプリケーションにおいて、GNSSはしばしば信頼性が低く不正確である。
llm.method: レーダーオドメトリによって伝播されるパーティクルフィルタで候補ポーズを提案し、学習済み観測モデルで尤度を提供する。
llm.result: 都市およびオフロード条件を含む31の異なるルート、8つのデータセット、さらに天候変化に対する頑健性を実証した。
keywords_ja: ジオローカライゼーション
パーティクルフィルタ

2610.27279.title: A latent control model for realistic rodent motion
2610.27279.abstract: The development of embodied models of animal behavior is a major goal of the neuro-AI community. Embodied models will enhance our ability to make direct comparisons between biological and artificial agents. To make such comparisons effective, though, we need embodied models that actually move like animals. Previous work has developed virtual animal bodies and techniques for training realistic motion through imitation. However, to date, there is no system for embodied animal modeling that produces natural movements both during trained goal-directed behavior, and during exploration driven by random generation. Here, we introduce Simulated Control via Augmented Motor Priors for Embodied Reinforcement learning (SCAMPER), a system for training an embodied virtual rat model, enabling natural movements during both goal-directed behavior and random exploration. SCAMPER uses a variational architecture with two distinct priors, a motion prior for control and a behavior prior for exploration. We show that combining both of these priors allows SCAMPER to generate realistic behavior during exploration and exploit the task structure effectively. SCAMPER can also learn from sparse rewards as a result of the diverse movements induced by the behavior prior, allowing the system to model realistic sparse-reward tasks from experimental neuroscience. Altogether, SCAMPER provides the neuro-AI community with an effective new system for training embodied models of rodents on realistic tasks.
2610.27279.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 10 pages, 13 figures. Project page with supplementary videos: https://aidansirbu.com/SCAMPER-site/
2610.27279.tldr_en: Simulated Control via Augmented Motor Priors for Embodied Reinforcement learning (SCAMPER), a system for training an embodied virtual rat model, enabling natural movements during both goal-directed behavior and random exploration, is introduced.

llm.title_ja: 現実的なげっ歯類の動きのための潜在制御モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 制御用のモーション事前分布と探索用の行動事前分布という2つの異なる事前分布を持つ変分アーキテクチャにより、目標指向的行動とランダム探索の両方で自然な動きを生成するSCAMPERシステムを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の仮想動物モデルは、目標指向的行動とランダム探索の両方で自然な動きを生成することができなかった。
llm.method: 2つの異なる事前分布（モーション事前分布と行動事前分布）を持つ変分アーキテクチャを用いたSCAMPERシステムを開発した。
llm.result: SCAMPERにより、探索中の現実的な行動生成、タスク構造の効果的活用、および神経科学実験におけるスパース報酬タスクのモデル化が可能になった。
keywords_ja: げっ歯類シミュレーション

2610.27277.title: What Would Removing This Corruption Change? Failure Attribution for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.27277.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are sensitive to visual corruptions, but knowing that a corruption is typically harmful does not establish whether removing it would benefit the current episode. Furthermore, when several corruptions co-occur, deciding what to correct requires understanding which ones contribute to failure risk and how much their removal would help. We define this problem as failure attribution. Detecting corruption presence alone cannot answer this question, as corruptions can be present but relatively harmless, while directly measuring removal benefits requires costly paired policy rollouts with and without the corruption present. To address this, we introduce a factorized risk model that learns separate representations of the scene and corruptions, allowing us to estimate removal benefits through latent intervention from the current image and task instruction, without paired clean images or additional counterfactual rollouts. We evaluate our approach on OpenVLA and $π_{0.5}$ in simulation and $π_{0.5}$-DROID on a Franka robot. Our method outperforms monolithic and vision-language-model (VLM) baselines, including achieving approximately 3x lower attribution error than frontier VLMs. We also demonstrate our method adapts to execution context and corruption intensity, and can be used for online failure monitoring on hardware.
2610.27277.tldr_en: A factorized risk model is introduced that learns separate representations of the scene and corruptions, allowing us to estimate removal benefits through latent intervention from the current image and task instruction, without paired clean images or additional counterfactual rollouts.

llm.title_ja: この破損を除去すると何が変わるか？ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのための失敗起因特定
llm.tldr_ja: シーンと破損の表現を別々に学習する因子化リスクモデルを導入し、ペアのクリーン画像や追加の反実仮想ロールアウトなしで潜在介入により破損除去の効果を推定する。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語・行動（VLA）モデルは視覚的破損に敏感であるが、どの破損が失敗リスクに寄与しているかを特定することが難しい。
llm.method: シーンと破損の別々の表現を学習する因子化リスクモデルを構築し、現在の画像とタスク指示から潜在介入により除去メリットを推定する。
llm.result: OpenVLAやπ0.5等のシミュレーションおよびFrankaロボットを用いた実機実験において、既存のベースラインを大幅に上回る低い起因特定誤差を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2610.27275.title: On Maximum Clique and Maximum Consensus Formulations in Point Cloud Registration
2610.27275.abstract: Maximum clique and maximum consensus are widely used formulations for robust point cloud registration in robotics. Maximum consensus seeks one transformation that aligns as many matches as possible, while maximum clique selects matches through pairwise distance tests. Maximum clique is often used as a substitute for or an approximation to maximum consensus, with empirical evidence suggesting a close relationship. However, how closely the two formulations agree is not fully understood. We study this relationship theoretically. We show that a maximum clique can have arbitrarily large alignment error and be arbitrarily larger than the maximum consensus set at any fixed positive tolerance, and derive geometric conditions that bound this error. When rotation is fixed, we derive sharp error bounds and tests that exactly characterize maximum consensus for the translation subproblem. Finally, we study group-$k$ consistency, which tests groups of $k$ matches, and determine the smallest group sizes that guarantee alignment error bounds independent of point cloud scale and geometry. These are $d+1$ for rotations and translations and $d+2$ when reflections are allowed, in dimensions $d\ge 2$. Interactive examples and proof verification using the Lean theorem prover are available at https://ariarobotics.github.io/mc-vs-mc-registration/.
2610.27275.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Interactive examples and Lean proof verification: https://ariarobotics.github.io/mc-vs-mc-registration/
2610.27275.tldr_en: It is shown that a maximum clique can have arbitrarily large alignment error and be arbitrarily larger than the maximum consensus set at any fixed positive tolerance, and derive geometric conditions that bound this error.

llm.title_ja: 点群登録における最大クリーク定式化と最大コンセンサス定式化について
llm.tldr_ja: 最大クリークが任意の正の許容値において任意の大きな整列誤差を持ち、最大コンセンサスセットよりも大きくなり得ることを理論的に示し、幾何学的条件を導出する。
llm.problem: ロボット工学の点群登録において広く使われている最大クリークと最大コンセンサスの間の関係が完全に理解されていない。
llm.method: 最大クリークと最大コンセンサスの関係性を理論的に解析し、整列誤差を制限する幾何学的条件やグループk一貫性を導出する。
llm.result: 最大クリークが持つ誤差の限界を証明し、平行移動サブ問題の最大コンセンサスを正確に特徴付けるテストを導出した。

2610.27271.title: XoNav: An Exoskeleton as a Personalized Haptic Interface for Assisted Navigation
2610.27271.abstract: Walking without vision requires timely, unambiguous guidance, yet many wearable aids encode directions as audio or vibrotactile signals that users must translate into movement. We present XoNav, a four-actuator hip exoskeleton that renders guidance cues directly at the hip joints. It renders an Advance cue and two-level Braking cues through sagittal-plane actuators and two-level Steering cues through frontal-plane actuators. A bilateral LSTM-based gait-state classifier uses two thigh-mounted IMUs to identify gait states, enabling haptic cues to be delivered in coordination with the wearer's gait while suppressing them during standing. The classifier generalized to unseen users with recalls of 95.2-97.9%, with mean detection delays of 38.6 and 63.1 ms for stance-to-swing and swing-to-stance transitions, respectively. Constrained human-in-the-loop Bayesian optimization personalized Braking for minimum resistance and Steering for maximum comfort while ensuring detectability and safety. All participants reliably distinguished between grades of their personalized cues and the firmest Braking cue remained below 53% of the safety limit. In blindfolded Wizard-of-Oz navigation trials along three paths, the participants kept 98.8% of the walked distance within a 0.75 m wide passage, with a 4.9% increase in mean progression speed per trial. A body-worn camera, RTAB-Map and Nav2 further enabled a feasibility study of autonomous navigation and detours around previously unmapped obstacles.
2610.27271.comment: A supplementary video illustrating the XoNav hardware, haptic cues, Wizard-of-Oz trials and autonomous navigation is available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.34701648
2610.27271.tldr_en: XoNav, a four-actuator hip exoskeleton that renders guidance cues directly at the hip joints is presented, a four-actuator hip exoskeleton that renders an Advance cue and two-level Braking cues through sagittal-plane actuators and two-level Steering cues through frontal-plane actuators.

llm.title_ja: XoNav：補助ナビゲーションのためのパーソナライズされた触覚インターフェースとしての外骨格
llm.tldr_ja: 股関節で直接ガイダンスキューをレンダリングする4アクチュエータの股関節外骨格XoNavを提案し、歩行状態分類器と組み合わせて視覚障害者のナビゲーションを支援する。
llm.problem: 視覚なしでの歩行には適時で明確な指導が必要であるが、多くのウェアラブル補助具は音声や振動触覚信号によるためユーザーが動きに変換する必要がある。
llm.method: 矢状面アクチュエータによる進行・制動キューと前額面アクチュエータによる操舵キューを備えた4アクチュエータの股関節外骨格を開発し、IMUベースの歩行状態分類器と統合する。
llm.result: ブラインドフォードでのナビゲーション実験において、参加者は歩行距離の98.8%を0.75m幅の通路内に維持し、自律ナビゲーションの可能性を示した。
keywords_ja: 触覚インターフェース

2610.27242.title: EmbodyHOI: Embodiment-Aware Generation of Hand-Object Interactions for Humanoid Dexterous Manipulation
2610.27242.abstract: Humanoid dexterous manipulation needs reference motions that are both semantically rich and kinematically feasible for the target robot. Text-conditioned hand-object interaction (HOI) generators supply diverse, language-specified demonstrations, but they synthesize motion in human (MANO) space. The embodiment gap is therefore deferred to post-hoc retargeting, where trajectories deployed on the robot can fail to maintain contact with objects and also degrade policy learning. Our key idea is that robot reachability should constrain the interaction trajectories while they are being generated. We present EmbodyHOI, which runs a differentiable inverse-kinematics (IK) solver for a specific humanoid embodiment inside the sampling loop of a frozen flow-matching HOI trajectory generator. We feed back gradients from the embodiment-aware IK solver into the HOI sampler and jointly optimize the position of the humanoid with respect to the object. Because guidance acts only at inference, one HOI trajectory generator trained on human hand poses transfers across humanoid embodiments without retraining. On ARCTIC trajectories with two contrasting humanoids (Unitree G1 and H1-2), our proposed guidance-based method cuts the retargeted wrist error from 8.9 cm to 0.6 cm while leaving text-to-HOI generation quality intact, and raises task success from 68% to 79% on 50 random G1 tasks and from 62% to 76% on a four-task H1-2 suite. Critically, cheaper alternatives for bridging the embodiment gap fail to beat EmbodyHOI. Post-hoc wrist refinement and compute-matched best-of-N selection both reach lower IK energy than our guidance yet train worse policies. For simulation results, see our website: https://embodyhoi.github.io/
2610.27242.tldr_en: EmbodyHOI is presented, which runs a differentiable inverse-kinematics solver for a specific humanoid embodiment inside the sampling loop of a frozen flow-matching HOI trajectory generator, and feeds back gradients from the embodiment-aware IK solver into the HOI sampler and jointly optimize the position of the humanoid with respect to the object.

llm.title_ja: EmbodyHOI：ヒューマノイド器用マニピュレーションのための身体性認識型手・物体相互作用生成
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結されたフローマッチングHOI軌跡生成器のサンプリングループ内で特定のヒューマノイドの微分可能逆運動学ソルバーを実行し、ロボットのリーチ可能性を考慮した相互作用軌跡を生成するEmbodyHOIを提案する。
llm.problem: 人間の手・物体相互作用（HOI）生成器は人間空間で動作するため、ロボットへの後処理的な逆運動学適用では接触が維持できずポリシー学習が劣化する。
llm.method: 身体性を考慮した微分可能逆運動学ソルバーからの勾配をHOIサンプラーにフィードバックし、ヒューマノイドの位置と物体を共同最適化する。
llm.result: Unitree G1およびH1-2を用いた評価において、手首の誤差を大幅に削減し、タスク成功率を向上させた。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2610.27199.title: Which Depth Estimator for Jetson AGX Orin? A 2026 Benchmark of Monocular and Stereo Methods
2610.27199.abstract: The Jetson AGX Orin is a common computer for robots and vehicles, yet measured accuracy, speed and energy of current depth estimators on it are hard to find. We benchmark nine model families as of October 2026: the monocular Depth Anything V2 and 3, Depth Pro, MoGe-2, Metric3D v2 and UniDepth V2, and the stereo methods libSGM, NVIDIA ESS and Fast-FoundationStereo. Every method runs on the Orin as a TensorRT FP16 engine or native CUDA code at up to three input sizes, up to the full 5.7 MP, and is scored for metric accuracy against Middlebury 2014 ground truth (non-occluded pixels of the 10 scenes whose disparity stays below 256 px), GPU time, energy and licence. Stereo is far more accurate. At 30 fps, NVIDIA's ESS reaches 0.70% AbsRel in 8.6 ms and libSGM 0.73% in 25 ms; with more compute, Fast-FoundationStereo reaches 0.33%. The best monocular models reach 12% with the true focal length (Depth Anything 3 Metric-L in 33 ms, Depth Pro in 803 ms), and 3.8-4.0% only with an oracle per-image scale (MoGe-2-L, UniDepth V2-B, Metric3D v2-L). Stereo error falls as the input resolution grows; no monocular model improves, and the metric scale of most drifts away from the truth outside their training resolution. At depth discontinuities, which AbsRel barely registers, the monocular models scatter 17-46% of the edge points between foreground and background, learned stereo 2-9% and libSGM at full resolution 1%. We give recommendations per frame-rate budget and release all code, per-scene results and engine build scripts.
2610.27199.comment: 18 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables. Code and per-scene results: https://github.com/nodarhub/orin-depth-benchmark
2610.27199.tldr_en: No monocular model improves, and the metric scale of most drifts away from the truth outside their training resolution as the input resolution grows; no monocular model improves, and the metric scale of most drifts away from the truth outside their training resolution.

llm.title_ja: Jetson AGX Orinに最適な深度推定器は何か？単眼およびステレオ手法の2026年ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: Jetson AGX Orin上における9つの単眼およびステレオ深度推定モデルの精度、速度、エネルギー効率をベンチマーク評価し、ステレオ手法が優れた精度とスケーラビリティを持つことを示す。
llm.problem: Jetson AGX Orinにおける現在の深度推定器の測定精度、速度、エネルギー消費量が明確ではない。
llm.method: 9つのモデルファミリー（単眼6種、ステレオ3種）をTensorRT FP16エンジンまたはネイティブCUDAコードとして実装し、Middlebury 2014データセットを基準に評価する。
llm.result: ステレオ手法（NVIDIA ESSなど）がより高い精度と解像度スケーラビリティを示した一方、単眼モデルは解像度変化に対してスケールがドリフトする傾向があることを明らかにした。

2610.27194.title: Learning to Be Different: Component Specialization for Compositional Diffusion Policies
2610.27194.abstract: Diffusion policies with linearly composed scores have emerged as a promising approach to multitask robotic learning by combining separate factors to enable modular, task-wise adaptation, compositional generalization, and interpretable functional decomposition. However, current training objectives do not encourage factor specialization, often resulting in uninterpretable denoisers whose composed prediction is an average over identical copies, undermining their architectural premise. To address this, we propose a drop-in score-decorrelation auxiliary loss, motivated by projective composition theory. Our approach encourages specialization by penalizing overlap directly between component noise predictions, with little architectural change or computational overhead. We demonstrate across multiple benchmarks that our decorrelation loss consistently reduces measurable double-counting between components, improves task decomposition, and produces behaviorally meaningful specialization without compromising multitask performance. Website: https://al3cl1.github.io/robotics-score-decorrelation.
2610.27194.tldr_en: This work demonstrates across multiple benchmarks that the proposed drop-in score-decorrelation auxiliary loss consistently reduces measurable double-counting between components, improves task decomposition, and produces behaviorally meaningful specialization without compromising multitask performance.

llm.title_ja: 違いを学ぶこと：構成的拡散ポリシーのためのコンポーネント特殊化
llm.tldr_ja: 射影的構成理論に基づくドロップインのスコア非相関化補助損失を提案し、コンポーネント間の重複をペナルティすることで特殊化を促し、マルチタスク性能を損なわずにタスク分解を改善する。
llm.problem: 線形構成されたスコアを持つ拡散ポリシーはマルチタスク学習に有効だが、現在の訓練目的関数は因子の特殊化を促さず、解釈不可能なデノイザーになってしまう。
llm.method: コンポーネントのノイズ予測間の重複を直接ペナルティする、スコア非相関化のためのドロップイン補助損失関数を導入する。
llm.result: 複数のベンチマークにおいて、提案手法はコンポーネント間の二重カウントを削減し、タスク分解を改善しつつマルチタスク性能を維持することを示した。
keywords_ja: モジュール型ロボット工学

2610.27190.title: On the Fragility of Tasks under Composition: Implicit Budgeting in Language Models
2610.27190.abstract: Modern language models are increasingly asked to handle several tasks within a single prompt. Doing so requires solving each task correctly while integrating the resulting answers into a coherent response. In this paper, we identify a fundamental limitation in this process, where models make substantially more errors when tasks are composed, even when they can solve every constituent task reliably in isolation. This degradation cannot be fully explained by the accumulation of independent errors. Across both open-weight models and the frontier model Claude Opus 5, our findings instead point to an implicit thinking budget underlying this effect. In particular, under composition, models use substantially fewer tokens per task than in isolation, even when the full sequence remains well within the context window. Tasks that require longer solution traces in isolation are consequently more $\textit{fragile}$ under composition, i.e., models make more errors on prompts containing these tasks. In isolation, non-fragile tasks receive more reasoning than they need and waste compute. However, by grouping tasks according to their fragility, the implicit budgeting can be manipulated to reduce token usage by $43$\% across a range of math and linguistic tasks while also preserving accuracy.
2610.27190.tldr_en: By grouping tasks according to their fragility, the implicit budgeting can be manipulated to reduce token usage by $43$\% across a range of math and linguistic tasks while also preserving accuracy.

llm.title_ja: 構成下におけるタスクの脆弱性について：言語モデルにおける暗黙の予算配分
llm.tldr_ja: 言語モデルが複数のタスクを統合する際、個別に解ける場合でもエラーが大幅に増加する現象を識別し、モデルがコンポーネントごとに割り当てるトークン数が減少する暗黙の思考予算が原因であることを示す。
llm.problem: モダンな言語モデルは単一プロンプト内で複数のタスクを処理する際にエラーが著しく増加するが、単なる個別エラーの蓄積では説明がつかない。
llm.method: オープンウェイトモデルおよびClaude Opus 5を用いて、タスク構成時のトークン消費量とエラー率の関係を分析する。
llm.result: タスクの脆弱性に基づいてグループ化を行うことで、精度を維持しながらトークン使用量を43%削減できることを示した。

2610.27162.title: Visual Task Modeling and Automated Planning for Humanoid Robots in Education of Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder
2610.27162.abstract: In robot-assisted education, a robot must understand how to complete a task in order to effectively guide a student through it. We present a novel method that enables a semi-autonomous, camera-equipped robot to recognise the task goal and plan actions to achieve it. Our work focuses on Shoebox Tasks, an activity commonly used in the education of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). These tasks are designed so that the goal can be inferred directly from their visual structure. We have developed a solver that uses a vision-based Large Language Model to convert photos of a Shoebox Task into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) representation and generate action plans for solving it. We have also implemented a robotic interface that enables a Nao robot to autonomously execute various Shoebox Tasks and assist a student by suggesting next steps or signalling detected failures through action demonstrations, voice commands, or gestures. With an adapted robotic interface, the solver can be integrated into a variety of educational robots. No programming expertise is required from teachers, and the solver operates exclusively on captured images as input. Research in special educational needs indicates that students with ASD can benefit substantially from robot-assisted teaching, and our system aims to strengthen these learning opportunities while also fostering interest in robotics among individuals with ASD.
2610.27162.comment: 6 pages, presented at conference AICCONF 2026 in Prague, Czech Republic
2610.27162.tldr_en: A novel method is presented that enables a semi-autonomous, camera-equipped robot to recognise the task goal and plan actions to achieve it, and a solver is developed that uses a vision-based Large Language Model to convert photos of a Shoebox Task into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) representation and generate action plans for solving it.
2610.27162.venue: 2026 4th Cognitive Models and Artificial Intelligence Conference (AICCONF)

llm.title_ja: 自閉症スペクトラム障害児教育におけるヒューマノイドロボットのための視覚的タスクモデリングと自動プランニング
llm.tldr_ja: ビジョンベースの大規模言語モデルを用いてシューボックスタスクの写真からPDDL表現への変換と行動計画の生成を行う、セミアクサスロボット向けの新しい手法を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボット支援教育において、ロボットが学生を効果的に誘導するためにはタスクの達成方法を理解する必要がある。
llm.method: 視覚ベースの大規模言語モデルを用いたソルバーを開発し、シューボックスタスクの画像をPDDL表現に変換して計画を生成し、Naoロボットに統合する。
llm.result: 教師のプログラミング専門知識を不要にし、画像を入力として自閉症スペクトラム障害児向けタスクの自律実行と支援を実現した。
keywords_ja: 自閉症スペクトラム障害
ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.27141.title: Towards Interaction State Recognition in Sensorized Gecko-Inspired Adhesive Interfaces for Orbital Servicing
2610.27141.abstract: Reliable contact establishment remains a critical challenge for autonomous on-orbit servicing (OOS), particularly when interacting with non-cooperative targets. Gecko-inspired dry adhesives provide a lightweight, passive, and residue-free solution for robotic capture in space, yet current systems operate in open loop, without the ability to estimate their own contact or adhesion state during interaction. This paper presents a real-time interaction-awareness framework that enables sensorized gecko-inspired adhesive interfaces to estimate their contact state throughout the adhesion lifecycle using embedded capacitive sensing. Five discrete interaction states (idle, proximity, contact, engaged, and disengaged) are classified using experimentally collected and augmented sensor data, enabling a comparative evaluation of six lightweight machine learning models suitable for embedded deployment. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest achieved the highest offline classification accuracy of 95.65%. For online deployment, combining Random Forest with a rule-based state machine improved accuracy from 78.02% to 93.14%, achieving a macro F1-score of 0.9343 while maintaining a 53 ms inference cycle. These results demonstrate that incorporating physics-consistent state constraints significantly improves robustness during realtime inference, representing a step toward interaction-aware capture in future autonomous orbital servicing missions.

llm.title_ja: 軌道上サービス向けセンサー付きヤモリ風接着インターフェースにおけるインタラクション状態認識に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: 埋め込み型容量性センシングを用いてヤモリ風ドライ接着インターフェースが接着ライフサイクル全体で接触状態を推定できるようにするリアルタイムのインタラクション認識フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 非協調ターゲットとの自律的軌道上サービス（OOS）において、接着システムが自身の接触や接着状態を推定する機能を持たずオープンループで動作していること。
llm.method: 埋め込み型容量性センシングを用いた5つの離散的なインタラクション状態の分類を行い、ランダムフォレストとルールベースの状態機械を組み合わせたリアルタイム推定フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 物理的一貫性のある状態制約を組み込むことで、推論の頑健性が大幅に向上し、93.14%の精度と53msの推論サイクルを実現した。

2610.27132.title: Glass-Box Deep Reinforcement Learning for High-Speed Flow Control
2610.27132.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is challenging long-held assumptions in active flow control. By learning directly from interaction with a flow, DRL agents can find actuation strategies for nonlinear, unsteady flows without explicit models, often exploiting mechanisms that classical control would not anticipate. High-speed flows are a demanding test of this promise: shocks, shock/boundary-layer interactions, transition, aerothermal loading and microsecond-scale dynamics strain both algorithms and hardware. Yet most demonstrations remain idealized, low-speed simulations with limited evidence of robustness, interpretability, transferability or experimental deployment. In this perspective, we examine what constrains DRL-based high-speed flow control, including compressible simulation cost and fidelity, data efficiency, sensing in extreme environments, reward design, explainability, and generalization across Mach and Reynolds number. We argue that these limits reflect a tension between data-driven optimization and the structured physics, constraints and uncertainties of real flows. We then highlight where DRL may go beyond conventional approaches: adaptive control of shock-induced separation and turbulent boundary layers, coordination of distributed actuators, and discovery of unconventional flow-manipulation mechanisms.The central challenge, however, is translating these capabilities into reliable technology, which will require validated compressible simulation environments, physics- and constraint-aware learning, robustness to off-design conditions and sensor degradation, real-time operation, hardware-in-the-loop and wind-tunnel validation, and credible pathways to safety and certification.
2610.27132.tldr_en: What constrains DRL-based high-speed flow control, including compressible simulation cost and fidelity, data efficiency, sensing in extreme environments, reward design, explainability, and generalization across Mach and Reynolds number is examined.

llm.title_ja: 高速度流れ制御のためのグラスボックス深層強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 非線形かつ非定常な流れに対するアクチュエーション戦略を発見する深層強化学習（DRL）を用いた高速度流れ制御における課題と展望について包括的に検討する。
llm.problem: 高速度流れ（衝撃波、乱流境界層など）の制御は、圧縮性シミュレーションのコスト、データ効率、極限環境でのセンシングなどの観点からアルゴリズムとハードウェアの双方に大きな負担をかける。
llm.method: データ駆動型最適化と実流体の物理的制約・不確実性との間の緊張関係を分析し、DRLベースの高速度流れ制御における制約と将来の方向性を体系的に検証する。
llm.result: 検証済みの圧縮性シミュレーション環境、物理制約を考慮した学習、実時間動作、風洞検証に向けた課題とアプローチを提示した。

2610.27114.title: Joint Constraint Aggregation for Qualifier-Sensitive Retrieval-Augmented QA
2610.27114.abstract: Retrieval-augmented QA can fail even when the correct answer is in the retrieved evidence. This can happen when a competing answer satisfies some, but not all, of the question's requirements and is mentioned frequently in the retrieved documents, which can make it appear to be the best-supported answer. To test whether this retrieval skew actually affects the decision, we manipulate it directly: increasing the prevalence of passages that favor the competing answer makes the model more likely to select it. This points to a decision problem that candidate-level support alone cannot resolve. We therefore introduce Joint Constraint Aggregation (JCA), which compares candidates against the same question-derived requirements using the retrieved evidence. Across three evaluation settings and three instruction-tuned backbones, JCA improves overall accuracy, and its advantage grows when retrieval favors a competing answer. Together, these results suggest that when partial matches and retrieval prominence pull models toward a competing answer, comparing candidates against the question's full requirements can make selection more reliable.
2610.27114.tldr_en: JCA is introduced, which compares candidates against the same question-derived requirements using the retrieved evidence and improves overall accuracy, and its advantage grows when retrieval favors a competing answer.
2610.27114.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

badges.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Em

llm.title_ja: 資格条件に敏感な検索拡張QAのための結合制約集約
llm.tldr_ja: JCAは検索された証拠を用いて候補を質問由来の要件に対して比較し、全体の精度を向上させ、検索が競合する回答に有利な場合にその優位性が増す。
llm.problem: 検索拡張QAにおいて、競合する回答が質問の一部要件を満たし頻出する場合、最適な回答のように見えて誤答につながる課題。
llm.method: 質問から導出された同一の要件に対して、検索された証拠を用いて候補を比較する結合制約集約（JCA）の導入。
llm.result: 3つの評価設定と3つのバックボーンにおいて全体的な精度が向上し、検索が競合回答に有利な状況で優位性が拡大した。

2610.27104.title: LVMem: Image-Augmented Memory for Long-Horizon Question Answering
2610.27104.abstract: Reliable language-guided perception is essential for embodied agents, where questions about objects, events, and their locations must be answered from long observation histories. Unlike conventional visual question answering, realistic robotic settings require reasoning over extended temporal horizons and persistent scene memory. We build upon the view-based memory paradigm and propose an efficient framework for long-horizon spatio-temporal question answering. While existing view-based systems typically store either text captions or visual embeddings, we extend the ReMEmbR-style memory with image paths that link each stored description to its original visual content. To make the stored annotations more informative, we replace uniform sampling during memory construction with an optical-flow-based frame selection strategy (PSFR) and store an object-centric descriptive scene representation instead of plain captions. We further equip a VLM-based agent with an adaptive retrieval tool that returns the image associated with the most relevant caption, allowing the agent to decide when visual inspection is needed. On the OC-NaVQA benchmark, LVMem outperforms ReMEmbR on binary and positional metrics with both backbones and matches or exceeds a 4D scene graph DAAAM baseline on binary accuracy, while operating on a lightweight view-based memory that requires no explicit graph construction.
2610.27104.tldr_en: LVMem builds upon the view-based memory paradigm and proposes an efficient framework for long-horizon spatio-temporal question answering, and extends the ReMEmbR-style memory with image paths that link each stored description to its original visual content.

llm.title_ja: LVMem：長期視空間質問応答のための画像拡張メモリ
llm.tldr_ja: LVMemは長期の視空間質問応答のための効率的なフレームワークであり、ReMEmbRスタイルのメモリを拡張して各保存された説明を元の視覚コンテンツにリンクする画像パスを持たせる。
llm.problem: 具象エージェントにおいて、長時間の観測履歴にわたるオブジェクトやイベントに関する質問に信頼性高く答える必要がある課題。
llm.method: 光学的フローベースのフレーム選択戦略（PSFR）を用いた画像拡張メモリと、必要に応じて画像検査を行う適応型検索ツールの導入。
llm.result: OC-NaVQAベンチマークにおいて、バイナリおよび位置指標でベースラインを上回り、明示的なグラフ構築なしで同等以上の性能を達成した。

2610.27103.title: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
2610.27103.abstract: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and strong cross-architecture generalization of OWP. Using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B as the backbone, OWP improves performance by 12.9 and 8.6 points on CMM and AVHBench, respectively, while consistently achieving gains of 0.67-2.25 points across four general OLLM reasoning benchmarks. Furthermore, OWP generalizes effectively to VideoLLaMA2-AV, improving performance by 4.6 and 3.9 points on the same benchmarks. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZiiJianLiu/Omni-Woodpecker
2610.27103.tldr_en: OWP is proposed, a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing and adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding.
2610.27103.hf_summary_en: Omni-Woodpecker is a training-free framework that reduces cross-modal hallucinations in omni LLMs by identifying modality conflicts and rebalancing hidden representations to suppress misleading priors.

llm.title_ja: Omni-Woodpecker：オムニLLMのための証拠・事前分布リバランスを通じたハルシネーション修正
llm.tldr_ja: OWPは、出力レベルのマニピュレーションから競合条件付き表現のリバランスへとハルシネーションの軽減を移行させ、デコード前に隠れ状態の表現を適応的に再調整するフレームワークである。
