llm.problem: オムニLLMにおける音声・視覚の共同推論において、クロスモーダルなハルシネーションが主要な課題となっている点。
llm.method: クロスモーダルな矛盾を特定し、直交分解を用いて隠れ状態から根拠の証拠と競合する事前分布を分離し、適応的に再バランスするトレーニング不要のフレームワークOWPの提案。
llm.result: CMMやAVHBenchなどのベンチマークで大幅な性能向上を達成し、他の汎用オムニLLM推論ベンチマークでも一貫した改善を示した。
keywords_ja: ハルシネーション修正

2610.27066.title: BUMP: Body-driven Unified Multi-object Physics for HOI Synthesis
2610.27066.abstract: Generating human-object interactions (HOIs) with multiple objects is challenging because the resulting motions arise from different underlying causes. Human motion reflects semantic intent, intentionally manipulated objects must remain coordinated with the human, while surrounding objects move primarily as physical consequences of contact and collision. We present BUMP, a text-driven framework for multi-object HOI generation based on a simple principle: learn intentional motion and simulate physical consequences. Our method first generates full-body human motion from text and scene context, then predicts trajectories for a small number of intentionally manipulated driver objects conditioned on the human motion. We then obtain responder object motions through physics simulation, allowing the framework to handle varying numbers and configurations of surrounding objects without expanding the learned trajectory output space. To address the scarcity of paired full-body multi-object HOI data, we combine heterogeneous supervision from human-only motion, full-body HOI, and hand-centric manipulation data augmented with plausible body motion. We further introduce outcome-conditioned interaction editing, which infers a local modification of the causal driver object trajectory from a desired responder object behavior without requiring an explicit target driver object trajectory. Experiments demonstrate strong performance on both single-object and multi-object HOI benchmarks. Qualitative results showcase diverse scenarios involving inter-object relationships and edits, highlighting the advantage of our unified model formulation.
2610.27066.tldr_en: BUMP is presented, a text-driven framework for multi-object HOI generation based on a simple principle: learn intentional motion and simulate physical consequences, and outcome-conditioned interaction editing is introduced, which infers a local modification of the causal driver object trajectory from a desired responder object behavior without requiring an explicit target driver object trajectory.

llm.title_ja: BUMP：ヒューマン・オブジェクト相互作用合成のための身体駆動型統合マルチオブジェクト物理
llm.tldr_ja: BUMPは意図的なモーションの学習と物理的結果のシミュレーションという原則に基づいたテキスト駆動型マルチオブジェクトHOI生成フレームワークであり、結果条件付き相互作用編集を導入している。
llm.problem: 人間と複数のオブジェクトとの相互作用（HOI）生成は、動作の起因が異なるため困難であるという課題。
llm.method: テキストとシーンから全身の人間動作を生成し、ドライバーオブジェクトの軌跡を予測した上で、レスポンダーオブジェクトの動きを物理シミュレーションで得るフレームワークの提案。
llm.result: 単一および複数のオブジェクトのHOIベンチマークの両方において強力なパフォーマンスを発揮し、多様な相互作用シナリオを実証した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマン・オブジェクト相互作用
物理シミュレーション

2610.26855.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
2610.26855.abstract: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.
2610.26855.tldr_en: Ropedia W0 is presented, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments, and Xp-Data, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data, is introduced.
2610.26855.hf_summary_en: Ropedia W0 is a world foundation model for cross-embodiment loco-manipulation that unifies human and robot data via kinematic representations and achieves state-of-the-art results across diverse benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: Ropedia W0：人間の経験を用いた多様な身体性における位置・操作ワールドモデルのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: Ropedia W0は、人間と多様な身体性を持つロボットにまたがる最初のエゴセントリックな位置・操作ワールド基盤モデルであり、高品質な器用なヒューマノイド遠隔操作データに基づくXp-Dataを導入している。
llm.problem: 異質な行動空間と限られたマルチモーダル監督信号のため、多様な身体性における移動と操作を共同でモデル化することが困難である点。
llm.method: カメラポーズによる移動と投影スケルトンによる操作をエンコードする統一された運動学的表現を用いたワールドモデルと、大規模なエゴセントリックデータセットの構築。
llm.result: 5つのクロス身体性ベンチマークおよび未見のエゴセントリック動画において、ゼロショットからフルデータのポストトレーニングまで最先端の性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: エゴセントリックデータ

2610.26854.title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
2610.26854.abstract: Multimodal reasoning provides robotic foundation models with predictive context needed for reliable action generation. However, language-based reasoning captures task semantics but struggles to express fine-grained physical dynamics, while latent reasoning models future state evolution but offers limited structure for organizing these dynamics into reusable reasoning primitives. To bridge this gap, we introduce PhysWord, a reasoning-before-acting foundation model built on Physical Words, which use atomic action verbs as shared semantic anchors for continuous representations of physical dynamics. Specifically, PhysWord predicts upcoming atomic action words and directly aligns their contextual hidden states with latent targets derived from the corresponding future observations. Building on these primitives, we construct a temporally structured PhysWord space with visual and optional tactile variants of each action word. Autoregressively predicting Physical Words across future timesteps captures transitions between execution stages, providing structured multimodal context for action generation. PhysWord achieves state-of-the-art success rates of 90.3\% on visuotactile UniVTAC and 99.6\% on vision-based LIBERO-Long, and outperforms competing methods on real-world tasks using bimanual grippers and dexterous hands. Further evaluations demonstrate that our structured latent reasoning framework generalizes to unseen scenarios and enables long-horizon manipulation. Project page: https://nvidia-isaac.github.io/video_to_data/physicalword/
2610.26854.tldr_en: PhysWord, a reasoning-before-acting foundation model built on Physical Words, which predicts upcoming atomic action words and directly aligns their contextual hidden states with latent targets derived from the corresponding future observations to bridge the gap between language-based and latent reasoning.

llm.title_ja: Physical Words：ロボット操作における潜在的推論を構造化するための語彙
llm.tldr_ja: PhysWordは、物理的動的表現の共有意味的アンカーとして原子行動動詞を使用する物理的言葉に基づいて構築された、行動前推論基盤モデルである。
llm.problem: 言語ベースの推論はタスクの意味論を捉えるが微細な物理的動的表現を捉えるのが難しく、潜在的推論は将来の状態変化をモデル化する一方で動的表現を整理する構造が限られている点。
llm.method: 今後の原子行動単語を予測し、その文脈的隠れ状態を将来の観測から得られた潜在的ターゲットに直接アライメントするPhysWordフレームワークの導入。
llm.result: ビジオタクタイルのUniVTACで90.3%、ビジョンベースのLIBERO-Longで99.6%という最高水準の成功率を達成し、実世界のタスクでも優れた性能を示した。

2610.26852.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
2610.26852.abstract: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. Leveraging cooperation effectively for both prediction and navigation remains a major challenge. We propose CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making. CoopUQ predicts future occupancy grid maps through cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion and further leverages forecasts and their uncertainty to guide policy via constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the cost penalizes navigation through regions predicted to be occupied or highly uncertain. This design enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts. Experimental results across multiple Unity3D-based simulation environments with both in-distribution and OOD settings, including diverse layouts, pedestrian densities, and rushing behavior, demonstrate improved prediction performance and safety over representative baselines. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate its robustness across various scenes. Our code and videos are available at https://coopuq.github.io/.
2610.26852.comment: Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026); Project Website: https://coopuq.github.io/
2610.26852.tldr_en: CoopUQ is proposed, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making and enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts.

llm.title_ja: CoopUQ：不確実性を考慮した協調的予測を通じた堅牢なマルチロボット社会ナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: CoopUQは、不確実性を考慮した協調的占有予測と堅牢な意思決定を橋渡しし、ポリシーが分布シフトに対するリスク感度を適応できるようにするマルチロボット社会ナビゲーションフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 単ロボット向けの手法をそのままマルチロボット環境に拡張すると、特にオクルージョンやOODシナリオにおいて安全性と効率性を確保できないという課題。
llm.method: クロスロボットの時空間特徴フュージョンによる将来の占有グリッドマップの予測と、予測・不確実性を制約付きマルチエージェント強化学習に組み込んでポリシーを誘導する手法の提案。
llm.result: 多様なシミュレーション環境での予測性能と安全性の向上が示され、実ロボット実験でも様々なシーンで堅牢性が実証された。

2610.26848.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
2610.26848.abstract: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. We introduce PhysRSI-eval to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure. Different VLMs are evaluated on 18 manipulation tasks under a fixed interaction budget. The analysis of experimental results motivates the Physical Barrel Hypothesis: different capabilities may constrain different parts of improvement. The five-axis metrics also distinguish systems with close public benchmark averages and show that high scores need not come with early or efficient gains. We study observational scaling from two perspectives: predicting the relative performance of VLM agents from their public capabilities, and forecasting later progress from early physical feedback. Together, these analyses ask how quickly and how far an agent can improve. Moreover, we conduct workspace interventions and then analyze what improvement leaves behind. Removing history reduces late-round success, frozen workspaces remain useful on unseen layouts, and three cross-task cases achieve success earlier. The results suggest that scene-specific adaptation and reusable experience can coexist.
2610.26848.tldr_en: PhysRSI-eval is introduced to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure, and the results suggest that scene-specific adaptation and reusable experience can coexist.
2610.26848.hf_summary_en: Physical recursive self-improvement in vision-language agents is evaluated via multi-axis metrics, scaling analysis, and workspace interventions to assess improvement speed, limits, and reusable experience.

llm.title_ja: 物理的RSI能力はどこから来るのか？LLMをポリシーとする場合の観測的スケーリング則
llm.tldr_ja: PhysRSI-evalを導入して5軸の指標で物理的RSIを定量化し、その結果からシーン特化型適応と再利用可能な経験が共存できることが示唆された。
llm.problem: 物理的再帰的自己改善（RSI）のメカニズム、スケーリング動作、および汎化性能を体系的に調査する必要がある課題。
llm.method: 初試行パフォーマンス、効率、成功率、予算、失敗からの改善という5軸の指標からなるPhysRSI-evalを導入し、18の操作タスクで多様なVLMを評価。
llm.result: 5軸指標によりシステムの違いが明確になり、シーン固有の適応と再利用可能な経験が共存できることが示された。

2610.26846.title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
2610.26846.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal models have enabled GPT-6 Astra to perform robotic manipulation through in-context learning. Yet contact-rich control and tactile perception are often regarded as strengths of specialist policies, leaving open whether Astra can directly understand and use tactile observations. We provide, to our knowledge, the first demonstration that Astra directly interprets vision-based tactile images and uses their contact cues for manipulation. Tactile RGB images enter through its existing visual interface, enabling few-shot closed-loop control on nineteen simulated UniVTAC and OpenViTac tasks with 210 sampled scene seeds per setting. With visuo-tactile input, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% and 81.8%, exceeding the strongest reported specialist baselines in our comparison by 22.9 and 13.1 percentage points, respectively. Vision-only performance also leads these baselines, reaching 76.3% and 80.6%. Trajectory analysis reveals active probing, cautious grasping, contact-guided alignment, and recovery, alongside difficulties with tangential loading and corrective execution. Our findings challenge the exclusivity of specialist policies in contact-rich manipulation and show that fine-grained vision can partially compensate for missing touch. They also identify vision-based tactile sensing as an interface for scaling contact understanding with foundation models and reveal signs of benchmark saturation. These results motivate joint visual-tactile pretraining, harder contact-rich evaluations, and physical-robot validation.
2610.26846.comment: 22 pages, 19 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://tactalent.github.io/
2610.26846.tldr_en: These findings challenge the exclusivity of specialist policies in contact-rich manipulation and show that fine-grained vision can partially compensate for missing touch, and identify vision-based tactile sensing as an interface for scaling contact understanding with foundation models and reveal signs of benchmark saturation.

llm.title_ja: GPT-6 Astraは接触リッチな操作のためのネイティブな視覚触覚ポリシーである
llm.tldr_ja: GPT-6 Astraが視覚ベースの触覚画像を直接解釈し、その接触の手がかりを操作に利用できることを示し、微細な視覚が不足している触覚を部分的に補うことができることを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 接触リッチな制御や触覚知覚は専門特化したポリシーの強みとされ、Astraが触覚観測を直接理解して使用できるかは不明であった課題。
llm.method: 触覚RGB画像を既存の視覚インターフェースに入力し、シミュレートされた19のタスクで少数ショットの閉ループ制御を行う手法の検証。
llm.result: ビジオタクタイルの入力により、専門特化型のベースラインを大きく上回る平均成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルモデル

2610.26813.title: PICA-WAM: Visual Perturbation Invariance via Cross-Appearance Self-Alignment in World Action Models
2610.26813.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future video and generate actions, yet remain sensitive to task-irrelevant visual perturbations, i.e., changes in visual appearance that should not affect robot behavior. We identify a gap in conventional WAM training: video prediction encourages representations to preserve appearance information, while action generation does not explicitly enforce invariance to task-irrelevant appearance. Data augmentation exposes WAMs to such perturbations but does not require perturbed and nominal observations to produce consistent action representations, and alignment with external pretrained features does not guarantee the desired invariance. To address this gap, we propose PICA-WAM, a self-supervised training framework that casts perturbation invariance as an auxiliary cross-appearance self-alignment task for WAMs. An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher processes the nominal observation to provide a deeper-layer target, while the online WAM processes a perturbed observation and aligns its shallower-layer action representation to this target through a lightweight projection head. Across four strong WAMs evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO-Plus, EBench, and a real robot, PICA-WAM consistently improves robustness under visual perturbations, preserves nominal performance in simulation, and raises the real robot success rate. PICA-WAM further reduces the sensitivity of video features to task-irrelevant appearance and its propagation into actions, as shown by paired layer-wise diagnostics. Code: https://github.com/YudeZou/PICA-WAM-release
2610.26813.tldr_en: PICA-WAM, a self-supervised training framework that casts perturbation invariance as an auxiliary cross-appearance self-alignment task for WAMs, consistently improves robustness under visual perturbations, preserves nominal performance in simulation, and raises the real robot success rate.

llm.title_ja: PICA-WAM：ワールド行動モデルにおけるクロス外見自己アライメントを通じた視覚的摂動不変性
llm.tldr_ja: PICA-WAMは、摂動不変性をWAMの補助的なクロス外見自己アライメントタスクとして定式化する自己教師あり学習フレームワークであり、視覚的摂動に対する堅牢性を一貫して向上させ、実ロボットの成功率を高める。
llm.problem: ワールド行動モデル（WAM）は将来の動画予測と行動生成を共同で行うが、ロボットの行動に影響を与えるべきではないタスクに無関係な視覚的摂動に対して敏感である点。
llm.method: EMA教師モデルが公称観測を処理してターゲットを提供し、オンラインWAMが摂動された観測を処理して浅い層の行動表現をそのターゲットにアライメントする自己教師ありフレームワークPICA-WAMの提案。
llm.result: 複数のシミュレーションベンチマークおよび実ロボットにおいて、視覚的摂動に対する堅牢性が向上し、公称性能が維持または向上した。

2610.27045.title: Physical AI: Concepts, Techniques, and Challenges
2610.27045.abstract: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. However, the field has yet to reach consensus on its definition, technical landscape, and core challenges. To address this gap, this monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth. In doing so, it establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. Further, this monograph distinguishes physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins. It develops the foundations of physical AI across physics, control, cognition, learning, and reasoning. It reviews key methodologies, including multimodal perception, physical data and simulation, world models, embodied foundation models, motor-control systems, multi-agent coordination, and hardware-software co-design. Furthermore, it examines applications spanning robotics, manufacturing, infrastructure, scientific experimentation, and autonomous services. Particular attention is given to sim-to-real transfer, reliability, real-time execution, evaluation, safety, governance, and long-term deployment. By connecting perception, prediction, decision-making, action, and adaptation in a closed loop, this monograph identifies the technical challenges and research directions required to advance from narrow automation toward more generalizable physical AI and, ultimately, physical artificial general intelligence (Physical AGI).
2610.27045.tldr_en: This monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth, and establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints.

llm.title_ja: Physical AI：概念、技術、および課題
llm.tldr_ja: 本モノグラフはPhysical AIを定義し、その技術的ランドスケープを提示し、実世界の制約下で連続的なフィードバックを通じて物理世界を知覚し、モデル化し、行動する人工システムとしての統一されたフレームワークを確立する。
llm.problem: Physical AIが急速に発展している一方で、その定義、技術的ランドスケープ、および核心的課題について合意に達していない点。
llm.method: 物理学、制御、認知、学習、推論にわたるPhysical AIの基礎を発展させ、マルチモーダル知覚、シミュレーション、ワールドモデル、基盤モデル等の主要な方法論をレビューする。
llm.result: 知覚、予測、意思決定、行動、適応を閉ループで接続し、狭義の自動化からより汎用的なPhysical AIへの移行に必要な研究方向を特定した。

2610.26810.title: Bio-inspired Thrust-Assisted Trotting on a legged-Aerial Robot via Real-Time QP-MPC
2610.26810.abstract: This paper presents the hardware implementation of a quadratic program-based controller on Harpy: thruster-assisted bipedal robot to perform thruster-assisted trotting. This is inspired by wing-assisted locomotion observed in birds such as the chukar partridge, which employ thrust vectoring to manipulate the ground reaction force. The proposed controller formulates the thruster-assisted spring-loaded inverted pendulum dynamics as a condensed QP-based model predictive control problem, enabling simultaneous regulation of ground contact force and active thrust vectoring at 500 Hz. A decoupled control architecture is used, where the robot's sagittal dynamics are controlled using QP-MPC while the frontal dynamics is regulated using a cascade orientation stabilization controller. Two experiments were conducted with different forward reference velocities of 0 m/s and 0.1 m/s. While the instantaneous velocity oscillates, the mean velocities can track their respective reference. Additionally, joint tracking error remains within 1 deg while tracking the desired leg length given by the leg trajectory controller and desired swing trajectory given by Raibert's heuristic. The QP-MPC problem is consistently solved with 0.18ms, which is well within the 2ms computation budget while satisfying the GRF friction cone constraint.
2610.26810.comment: To be published in IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026)
2610.26810.tldr_en: The hardware implementation of a quadratic program-based controller on Harpy: thruster-assisted bipedal robot to perform thruster-assisted trotting is presented, inspired by wing-assisted locomotion observed in birds such as the chukar partridge.

llm.title_ja: 生体模倣スラスター補助型QP-MPCによる脚空中ロボットのトロッティング
llm.tldr_ja: 本論文は、鳥類に見られる翼補助型移動にインスパイアされた、ハーピー（スラスター補助型二足歩行ロボット）における二次計画法ベースのコントローラーのハードウェア実装を提案する。
llm.problem: 脚ロボットにおけるスラスターを用いた移動において、接地力と能動的な推力ベクトルを同時にかつリアルタイムに制御する必要がある課題。
llm.method: スラスター補助型ばね負荷逆子振り子ダイナミクスを圧縮QPベースのモデル予測制御問題として定式化し、500Hzで制御する手法の採用。
llm.result: 平均速度がそれぞれの参照速度に追従し、関節追跡誤差が1度以内に収まり、計算予算内（0.18ms）でQP-MPC問題が継続的に解かれることを実証した。

2610.26780.title: V-JEPA Hand: Simple, Accurate and Fast 3D Hand and Camera Trajectory Recovery from Egocentric Videos
2610.26780.abstract: Egocentric video supports diverse applications, including robot learning, augmented reality, and human activity understanding. Recovering metric 3D hand trajectories from such video requires estimating both hand motion and camera egomotion to express the hands in a consistent reference frame. Many existing pipelines recover hand and camera motion in separate stages, combining hand detection, hand reconstruction, camera tracking, and trajectory refinement. We present V-JEPA Hand, a simple feed-forward video model that jointly reconstructs bilateral hand motion and camera motion from egocentric clips. It uses a self-supervised V-JEPA 2.1 encoder to extract spatio-temporal features from full-frame video and a query-based predictor to decode these features into per-frame hand poses, hand presence, and camera motion. We use the predicted camera motion to express the hand trajectories in a common world frame. The model accepts known focal lengths or predicts them when unavailable. It reconstructs each clip in a single forward pass. We train both components end to end in a single stage on a mixture of diverse pseudo-labelled videos and high-precision 3D annotations. A single model achieves the lowest coverage-aware mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) among comparable baselines on ARCTIC, HOT3D, and EgoStandard. It also yields lower world-frame trajectory errors than the compared SLAM-based pipelines. Ablations support the benefits of video pretraining, temporal context, and mixed supervision. V-JEPA Hand achieves a forward-pass throughput of 93.4 FPS on a single RTX A6000. Project page: https://qft-333.github.io/V-JEPA-Hand-Page/.
2610.26780.tldr_en: V-JEPA Hand is presented, a simple feed-forward video model that jointly reconstructs bilateral hand motion and camera motion from egocentric clips and achieves the lowest coverage-aware mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) among comparable baselines on ARCTIC, HOT3D, and EgoStandard.

llm.title_ja: V-JEPA Hand：エゴセントリック動画からのシンプルで正確かつ高速な3D手・カメラ軌跡復元
llm.tldr_ja: V-JEPA Handは、自己教師ありV-JEPA 2.1エンコーダーを用いてエゴセントリッククリップから両手のモーションとカメラモーションを共同で再構築するシンプルなフィードフォワード動画モデルである。
llm.problem: エゴセントリック動画からメトリックな3D手軌跡を復元する際、手とカメラの動きを別々の段階で推定する従来手法の複雑さという課題。
llm.method: フルフレーム動画から時空間特徴を抽出し、クエリベースの予測子でフレームごとの手のポーズやカメラモーションにデコードする単一ステージのエンドツーエンドモデルの提案。
llm.result: ARCTIC、HOT3D、EgoStandardにおいて同等のベースラインの中で最も低いMPJPEを達成し、RTX A6000で93.4 FPSのスループットを実現した。
keywords_ja: エゴセントリック動画

2610.27040.title: ACE-Brain-0.6: Scaling Spatial Grounding for Physical Foundation Models
2610.27040.abstract: General-purpose multimodal models, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, demonstrate broad capabilities in embodied manipulation. Our analysis indicates that this generality is accompanied by strong spatial perception, as Astra can determine where to interact with task-relevant entities amid visual distractors. Because spatial perception connects high-level reasoning to the physical scene, we investigate scaling visual grounding to strengthen the perceptual foundation of general embodied operation. We develop a unified data pipeline that combines robot manipulation recordings with complementary visual data from diverse sources. After automatically annotating the robot recordings, the pipeline converts the collected data into verifiable grounding supervision. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on approximately 1.5 million samples produced by this pipeline yields ACE-Brain-0.6. The model outperforms GPT-6 Astra on four of seven public grounding benchmarks, with an overall average score of 75.41 compared with Astra's 73.68. Under a fixed Qwen3.5-9B fine-tuning setup, aggregate grounding performance improves steadily as successive data releases expand the training collection to cover a broader range of grounding scenarios. These results show that scaling verifiable grounding supervision from diverse sources can strengthen the spatial perception of an open 9B model for general embodied operation.
2610.27040.tldr_en: Results show that scaling verifiable grounding supervision from diverse sources can strengthen the spatial perception of an open 9B model for general embodied operation, and investigate scaling visual grounding to strengthen the perceptual foundation of general embodied operation.
2610.27040.hf_summary_en: Scaling diverse verifiable visual grounding data improves spatial perception and embodied manipulation performance in open multimodal models.

llm.title_ja: ACE-Brain-0.6：物理基盤モデルのための空間グラウンディングのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット操作記録と多様なソースからの視覚データを組み合わせた統一されたデータパイプラインにより、検証可能なグラウンディング監督信号をスケーリングし、汎用的な空間知覚を強化することを示す。
llm.problem: 汎用マルチモーダルモデルが持つ高度な空間知覚の基盤をさらに強化するために、視覚的グラウンディングのスケーリングが必要とされる点。
llm.method: ロボット操作記録を自動注釈し、検証可能なグラウンディング監督データに変換するパイプラインを構築し、Qwen3.5-9Bをファインチューニングする手法。
llm.result: 4つのパブリックグラウンディングベンチマークでGPT-6 Astraを上回り、全体的な平均スコアで75.41を達成した。
keywords_ja: 空間グラウンディング
マルチモーダルモデル

2610.27039.title: Embodied Playground: A Long-Horizon Agentic Robotics Benchmark for Physical, Strategic, and Spatial Reasoning
2610.27039.abstract: Foundation models offer a promising basis for robotic agents, but long-horizon tasks require them to sustain coherent reasoning and reliable physical execution across interdependent stages. We introduce Embodied Playground, a benchmark for evaluating how foundation-model agents coordinate physical, strategic, and spatial reasoning throughout such tasks. Agents must track task progress, satisfy intermediate constraints, and revise their plans using execution feedback as earlier actions shape subsequent decisions. The playground comprises 410 task environments spanning basic manipulation, sequential puzzles, and multi-stage household activities, with variations in planning depth, geometric constraints, and physical execution demands. We curate EP-100, a representative selection of 100 tasks across five suites and 16 task types, together with the EP-Easy and EP-Hard difficulty splits and the compact EP-20 selection. A shared protocol specifies observation and tool access, resource budgets, repeated trials, and independent checks of goal completion, task-rule compliance, and physical validity. Embodied Playground provides a unified framework for studying whether foundation-model agents can sustain effective reasoning and action over extended task horizons. https://winniechen2002.github.io/Agent-bench-website/
2610.27039.tldr_en: Embodied Playground is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating how foundation-model agents coordinate physical, strategic, and spatial reasoning throughout long-horizon tasks, and a unified framework for studying whether foundation-model agents can sustain effective reasoning and action over extended task horizons.

llm.title_ja: Embodied Playground：物理的・戦略的・空間的推論のための長期エージェント型ロボット工学ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: Embodied Playgroundは、基盤モデルエージェントが長期的なタスク全体で物理的・戦略的・空間的推論をどのように調整するかを評価するためのベンチマークである。
llm.problem: 基盤モデルに基づくロボットエージェントにおいて、長期タスクを遂行するために一貫した推論と信頼性の高い物理実行を維持する必要がある点。
llm.method: 基本的な操作、シーケンシャルパズル、多段階の家事活動にわたる410のタスク環境と、観測・ツールアクセスの仕様などを定める共通プロトコルの導入。
llm.result: 基盤モデルエージェントが拡張されたタスクホライゾンにわたって効果的な推論と行動を維持できるかを研究するための統一された枠組みを提供した。
keywords_ja: ロボットエージェント

2610.26765.title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
2610.26765.abstract: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. Across diffusion, vision-language-action, world-action, and prompted VLM-based methods, the best trained multi-task policy achieves 29.1% Core-50 success. Without benchmark finetuning, GPT-6 using move_eef for palm-and-finger control achieves 5.2% on Core-50 and 1.9% on Transfer-16 over 660 trials. Trained-policy stage diagnostics expose failures in contact establishment, action coordination, and maintaining achieved goals, with additional sequencing errors in composed tasks. HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction.
2610.26765.tldr_en: HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction and is introduced, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation.
2610.26765.hf_summary_en: HandsOn is a cross-embodiment simulation benchmark and platform for dexterous manipulation that evaluates generalization across robotic arms, hands, objects, and composed tasks, revealing substantial gaps in current multi-task policies and foundation-model-based control.

llm.title_ja: HandsOn：汎用的な器用な操作のための大規模シミュレーションベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: HandsOnは、クロス身体性の器用なマニピュレーションに向けた構成可能なシミュレーションプラットフォームおよびベンチマークを提供し、操作の汎化性と物理的相互作用の限界を検証するための共通基盤となる。
llm.problem: 汎用的な操作には、多様な身体性、オブジェクト、タスク要件にわたる信頼性の高い動作が必要であるが、その評価基盤が限られている点。
llm.method: 5つのロボットアーム、6つの器用なハンド、約200の資産をサポートし、18,000の人間のデモンストレーションと66のタスクを組み合わせたシミュレーションプラットフォームの構築。
llm.result: トレーニング済みマルチタスクポリシーの成功率や、学習済みポリシーの段階別診断における接触確立や行動調整の課題を明らかにした。

2610.26762.title: DexOAK: Object-Aware Kinematic Retargeting
2610.26762.abstract: We introduce DexOAK, a learning-based object-aware kinematic retargeting framework for generating contact-consistent robot hand references from human motion-capture data. DexOAK first minimizes an interaction-graph Laplacian objective over a joint hand-object graph, so the robot reproduces the demonstrated object-relative interaction geometry rather than the human hand pose alone. These per-frame solutions form seed retargeted references, from which a feed-forward network conditioned on human keypoints and object point clouds learns the retargeting function. Object-aware finetuning then refines the network under contact, non-penetration, and self-collision losses that position the fingers on the demonstrated contacts and reduce artifacts destabilizing physics-based refinement. Once trained, the network transfers to unseen data by inference alone, without per-frame optimization. DexOAK references improve dynamic retargeting over the state-of-the-art across bimanual tasks with rigid and articulated objects. On the Inspire hand, success rises from 39.5% to 48.4% on OakInk-v2, and ADD-AUC rises from 62.7% to 77.9% on ARCTIC. Ablations trace the gains to object-aware kinematic retargeting and the amortized network refined with contact losses. Trained on OakInk-v2, it transfers to ARCTIC zero-shot and nears in-domain performance after fine-tuning. On hardware, 46/56 open-loop replays succeed across five tasks, enabling dexterous robot data generation from human data. Visualizations and interactive results are at: https://fspinola.github.io/dexoak/.
2610.26762.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 11 tables. Project page: https://fspinola.github.io/dexoak/

llm.title_ja: DexOAK：オブジェクト認識型運動学的リターゲティング
llm.tldr_ja: DexOAKは、人間からロボットハンドへの接触整合性のあるリターゲティング参照を生成するための学習ベースのオブジェクト認識型運動学的リターゲティングフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 人間のモーションキャプチャデータからロボットハンドの参照動作を生成する際、単なる手のポーズだけでなくオブジェクトとの相対的な相互作用ジオメトリを再現する必要がある点。
llm.method: 相互作用グラフのラプラシアン最適化によるシード参照の生成と、人間キーポイントとオブジェクト点群を条件とするフィードフォワードネットワークによるリターゲティングの学習。
llm.result: 多様な把持タスクや把持デバイスにおいて動的リターゲティングが向上し、ゼロショットでの転移や実機でのオープンループ再生の成功を確認した。
keywords_ja: モーションキャプチャ
オブジェクト相互作用

2610.26759.title: Tactile In-Hand Object Rotation: A Comparative Study of Hand Morphology in Simulation and Hardware
2610.26759.abstract: Continuous in-hand rotation requires coordinated contact maintenance and renewal, linking manipulation performance to both hand geometry and tactile feedback. We investigate these relationships through rotational progress, finger participation, and fingertip loading on two versions of the low-cost LEAP Hand with anthropomorphic and symmetric finger arrangements. Both hands are integrated with TacTip vision-based tactile sensors and use a shared reinforcement learning framework. Simulation evaluates full tactile, binary touch, and proprioception-only observations on 12 unseen objects; hardware experiments evaluate full tactile policies on ten objects under multiple hand orientations. In simulation, full tactile observations increase mean normalized rotation per episode over proprioception alone by 94.8% for the anthropomorphic hand and 66.9% for the symmetric hand, with longer mean episode durations and lower mean total fingertip loads. Hardware contact measurements reveal more differentiated finger participation in the anthropomorphic hand, while cumulative loading is more evenly distributed across the symmetric hand's fingers. Overall, the symmetric hand achieves a 32.0% higher mean rotation count and a 25.8% higher aggregate rotation rate, together with longer manipulation duration. Additional hardware force recordings show a 19.9% lower mean total fingertip load for this layout. These findings relate finger arrangement to contact organization and load sharing, and show that richer tactile information supports greater task progress at lower mean loading in both simulated embodiments.

llm.title_ja: 触覚による手内オブジェクト回転：シミュレーションおよびハードウェアにおけるハンド形態の比較研究
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究は、2バージョンのLEAPハンドを用いて、指の配置が接触組織や負荷分散に与える影響を調査し、より豊かな触覚情報がより低い平均負荷でのタスク進行をサポートすることを示した。
llm.problem: 連続的な手内回転には接触の維持と更新の調整が必要であり、操作性能がハンドのジオメトリと触覚フィードバックの両方に依存している点。
llm.method: 解剖学的および対称的な指の配置を持つLEAPハンドにTacTip視覚触覚センサを統合し、共通の強化学習フレームワークを用いてシミュレーションと実機で評価。
llm.result: フル触覚観測により回転量が大幅に増加し、対称的なハンドがより高い回転数と回転率、および低い指先負荷を達成することを実証した。

2610.26757.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing
2610.26757.abstract: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. We introduce Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that uses structured simulation priors for rapid adaptation. PIA pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it with limited target-domain interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. Rather than requiring an accurate simulator for policy transfer, PIA treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected during online adaptation. We evaluate PIA in autonomous racing using high-fidelity simulation and on a real full-size autonomous race car. In simulation, PIA adapts faster across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, achieving lower lap times and fewer failures. On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.
2610.26757.tldr_en: This work introduces Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that uses structured simulation priors for rapid adaptation that achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.

llm.title_ja: 自動運転レースのためのモデルベース強化学習における迅速な適応のためのシミュレーション事前分布
llm.tldr_ja: PIAは、構造化されたシミュレーション事前分布を使用して迅速に適応するオフラインからオンラインへのモデルベース強化学習フレームワークであり、1時間未満の車載インタラクションで信頼性の高い少数ショット適応を実現する。
llm.problem: 強化学習における高パフォーマンス制御ポリシーの学習はデータ収集コストと安全性の問題から実システムへの展開が制限されるという課題。
llm.method: 低・高忠実度のシミュレーション軌跡でワールドモデルを事前学習し、不確実性正則化計画を用いて限定的なターゲットドメインインタラクションで適応させる手法。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいてベースラインよりも速く適応し、実車においても1時間未満のインタラクションで信頼性の高い少数ショット適応を実現した。
keywords_ja: モデルベース強化学習
シミュレーション事前分布

2610.26751.title: Beyond Omni: A Unified MLLM for Embodied Sensory Understanding
2610.26751.abstract: Recent embodied systems increasingly build on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for their pretrained understanding and reasoning capabilities, but their perception of the physical world remains largely limited to basic modalities such as vision and audio. However, broadening MLLMs to more diverse sensory modalities from the physical environment is challenging: their representations are often weakly connected to the MLLM and vary substantially in structure and statistics, while their interpretation still requires shared high-level understanding and reasoning. We therefore propose Unisense, a unified embodied MLLM framework that supports diverse physical sensory modalities within a shared multimodal architecture. Unisense follows a two-stage training process: (i) aligning sensory representations with language to establish a language-accessible interface; and (ii) tuning modality-specific experts within the shared LLM to provide specialized processing for different sensory modalities. To support broad sensory learning, we curate Unisense-1M, a large-scale embodied sensory training corpus comprising 1M samples across 8 sensory modalities. We further evaluate Unisense on 12 benchmarks spanning depth, point cloud, IMU, tactile, thermal, radar, motion, and smell understanding. Across these heterogeneous sensing tasks, Unisense achieves strong performance and outperforms both generalist and specialized models on most benchmarks, demonstrating the potential of pretrained MLLMs as unified models for embodied sensory understanding.
2610.26751.tldr_en: Unisense is proposed, a unified embodied MLLM framework that supports diverse physical sensory modalities within a shared multimodal architecture and achieves strong performance and outperforms both generalist and specialized models on most benchmarks, demonstrating the potential of pretrained MLLMs as unified models for embodied sensory understanding.

llm.title_ja: オムニを超えて：具象的感覚理解のための統合型MLLM
llm.tldr_ja: Unisenseは、共有マルチモーダルアーキテクチャ内で多様な物理的感覚モダリティをサポートする統合型具象MLLMフレームワークであり、ほとんどのベンチマークで汎用・特化型モデルを上回る。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）を物理環境の多様な感覚モダリティに拡張する際、表現の構造や統計が大きく異なり、共通の推論が必要である点。
llm.method: 感覚表現を言語とアライメントする第1段階と、共有LLM内でモダリティ固有のエキスパートをチューニングする第2段階からなる2段階トレーニングプロセスの提案。
llm.result: 深さ、点群、IMU、触覚、熱画像などの8つのモダリティにわたる12のベンチマークにおいて優れた性能を達成し、具象的感覚理解のための統一モデルとしての可能性を示した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2610.26717.title: Robot Learning with Vision-Language-Action Models for Agricultural Manipulation
2610.26717.abstract: Robotic manipulation in agricultural environments remains challenging due to variations in plant geometry, occlusion, and camera viewpoints. Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) and generalist robot policies offer a promising approach to addressing these challenges by learning manipulation behaviors from multimodal observations and language instructions. However, adapting these policies to agricultural tasks requires domain-specific demonstrations, which are costly and time-consuming to collect on physical robots. In this work, we develop a simulation-to-real robot-learning framework for agricultural reaching and grasping that integrates task-specific demonstration collection and pretrained policy adaptation. A MuJoCo-based agricultural environment is developed with diverse tomato plant structures to support demonstration collection and controlled evaluation. Expert demonstrations are collected through joystick teleoperation, with a low-level controller used to execute robot actions. Two pretrained generalist robot policies, Octo and $π_{0.5}$, are adapted using simulated demonstrations, followed by further fine-tuning on a physical Franka Research 3 manipulator using real-robot demonstrations. The adapted policies are evaluated under in-distribution, viewpoint/spatial-shift, and out-of-distribution conditions in simulation, followed by physical-robot experiments. The influence of proprioceptive information on policy performance is also investigated. Results show that $π_{0.5}$ achieves higher task-performance scores than Octo and exhibits less degradation under distribution shifts. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating pretrained generalist policies with task-specific demonstration learning for agricultural manipulation.
2610.26717.tldr_en: A simulation-to-real robot-learning framework for agricultural reaching and grasping that integrates task-specific demonstration collection and pretrained policy adaptation is developed and results show that $\pi_{0.5}$ achieves higher task-performance scores than Octo and exhibits less degradation under distribution shifts.

llm.title_ja: 農業用マニピュレーションのためのVision-Language-Actionモデルを用いたロボット学習
llm.tldr_ja: 農業環境における到達・把持タスクのためのSim-to-Realロボット学習フレームワークを開発し、$\pi_{0.5}$がOctoよりも高いタスク性能スコアを達成し分布シフトに対して劣化が少ないことを示した。
llm.problem: 農業環境におけるロボットマニピュレーションは、植物の形状の変化、オクルージョン、視点の違いにより困難であり、物理ロボットでのデモンストレーション収集にはコストとかかる。
llm.method: MuJoCoベースの農業環境を構築し、ジョイスティックによる専門家のデモンストレーション収集と、Octoおよび$\pi_{0.5}$の事前学習済みポリシーの適応・ファインチューニングを行う。
llm.result: $\pi_{0.5}$はOctoと比較して高いタスク性能スコアを達成し、分布シフト下でも性能低下が少なかった。

2610.26711.title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
2610.26711.abstract: Recent video generation models produce visually compelling outputs, yet their physical plausibility remains poorly measured. Physical plausibility asks whether generated objects obey geometry, kinematics, dynamics, and conservation laws. Existing benchmarks rely on coarse visual-language model judgments or target embodied world models rather than video generation itself. We introduce PVBench, a physical video benchmark that quantitatively measures the plausibility of generated videos across 46 dimensions organized into seven domains, spanning: i) instruction and semantic fidelity, ii) behavioral and causal consistency, iii) perceptual and temporal quality, iv) geometric and spatial consistency, v) material properties and field states, vi) kinematic and spatiotemporal persistence, vii) and mechanical plausibility with conservation laws. PVBench comprises 600 carefully crafted prompts, of which 30% involve physical embodied agents such as robot arms, humanoids, quadrupeds, and multi-agent systems. For challenging physically tractable dimensions, it pairs each with specialized vision models that derive verifiable, physically grounded measurements, such as object-level 6D pose, metric scale, surface normals, kinematics, and numerical conservation-law residuals. It thus avoids relying solely on subjective scoring, while supporting both text-to-video and image-to-video generation. Finally, we validate the agreement between automatic metrics and human judgments through human evaluation. Meanwhile, we evaluate mainstream open-source and closed-source models and present several insights. By releasing the benchmark, prompts, and calibration protocol, we aim to foster physically grounded video generation.
2610.26711.tldr_en: PVBench is introduced, a physical video benchmark that quantitatively measures the plausibility of generated videos across 46 dimensions organized into seven domains, and validate the agreement between automatic metrics and human judgments through human evaluation.
2610.26711.hf_summary_en: PVBench introduces a quantitative benchmark with 46 physical dimensions to evaluate the plausibility of generated videos using specialized vision models and human-aligned metrics.

llm.title_ja: PVBench：物体レベルの物理測定を用いた動画生成における物理的妥当性の定量化
llm.tldr_ja: 生成された動画の妥当性を7つのドメインにわたる46の次元で定量的に測定する物理動画ベンチマーク「PVBench」を提案し、自動指標と人間の判断の一致性を検証した。
llm.problem: 近年の動画生成モデルは視覚的に説得力のある出力を生成するが、その物理的妥当性（幾何学、運動学、力学、保存則に従っているか）が十分に測定されていない。
llm.method: ロボットアームなどの物理的エージェントを含む600のプロンプトと7つのドメイン（46次元）からなる物理動画ベンチマーク「PVBench」を構築し、専門の視覚モデルによる検証可能な物理測定を行う。
llm.result: 自動指標と人間の評価の間で高い合意が得られ、主流のオープンソースおよびクローズドソースモデルの評価から多くのインサイトが提示された。

2610.26690.title: Foundation Model Driven Optical Flow
2610.26690.abstract: We investigate how frozen pretrained visual and depth representations support dense optical flow when coupled with a supervised matching network. Building on TTSFlow, this paper studies Dense Prediction Transformer (DPT) feature decoding and one coarse-to-fine refinement stage. Our method fuses features from frozen DINOv2 and Depth Anything V2 models and estimates optical flow through a trainable transformer-based matching pipeline. After optical-flow training on FlyingChairs and FlyingThings3D, it achieves 2.37 endpoint error (EPE) on the Sintel training split, Final pass, compared with 2.52 for the FlowSeek (T) configuration reported here. Our RoCo-Spring 2026 entry, RoCo-29.VSAI, obtains a robustness-balanced score of 1.1038, Spring EPE of 1.411, and RobustSpring proxy EPE of 4.739, with a lower balanced score than seven of the twelve listed reference baselines. These results characterize the complete pipeline, which reuses frozen foundation backbones and performs one refinement stage. Code is available at: \url{https://github.com/Visual-and-Spatial-AI-Lab/FFlow}
2610.26690.comment: 19-pages, 5 figures, 16 tables. Accepted for publication at 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: RoCo-Spring: The Robust Correspondence Challenge
2610.26690.tldr_en: This paper studies Dense Prediction Transformer feature decoding and one coarse-to-fine refinement stage, which fuses features from frozen DINOv2 and Depth Anything V2 models and estimates optical flow through a trainable transformer-based matching pipeline.

llm.title_ja: 基盤モデル駆動型オプティカルフロー
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された事前学習済み視覚・深度表現を教師ありマッチングネットワークと組み合わせ、密なオプティカルフローを効率的に推定する手法を研究した。
llm.problem: 凍結された事前学習済みビジュアル・深度表現を、教師ありマッチングネットワークと組み合わせて密なオプティカルフロー推定に活用する方法の検証が求められている。
llm.method: 凍結されたDINOv2およびDepth Anything V2モデルからの特徴を融合し、学習可能なTransformerベースのマッチングパイプラインを通じてオプティカルフローを推定する。
llm.result: FlyingChairsおよびFlyingThings3Dでの訓練後、Sintelの訓練スプリット（Final pass）で2.37のEPEを達成し、RoCo-Spring 2026において優れたロバスト性スコアを獲得した。

2610.26680.title: Robotic Physical Comparison of Biologically Motivated and Counterfactual Sensory Arrangements using Biomimetic Skin
2610.26680.abstract: Human skin contains diverse mechanoreceptors, including Merkel cells and Pacinian corpuscles, each localized in specific regions. Although their spatial organization is known to be shaped by molecular signaling and neural induction during development, experimentally examining its functional significance under controlled conditions in living systems remains challenging. In particular, physically comparing alternative receptor arrangements that do not occur biologically is difficult. In this study, we developed a layered biomimetic robotic skin designed to mimic key structural features of human skin tissue by embedding receptor-analog sensors within compliant soft media. Using this platform, we implemented both biologically motivated and counterfactual sensory arrangements and quantitatively evaluated their performance across three passive tactile tasks: detection of weak contacts, a two-point discrimination-like assessment, and texture identification. Arrangements reflecting key features of the biologically motivated sensory organization exhibited higher performance than the alternative configurations examined. This study addresses a biological question concerning how spatial organization influences tactile function by presenting a biomimetic robotic approach that enables physical and empirical comparison of biologically motivated and counterfactual sensory arrangements that are difficult to investigate in living systems.
2610.26680.comment: Published in Bioinspiration & Biomimetics (IOP Publishing). Project page: https://poyotamu000.github.io/biomimetic-skin-sensory-arrangements/ Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=25HPwOTodQ8

llm.title_ja: 生体模倣スキンを用いた生物学的動機付け感覚配置と反事実的感覚配置のロボット工学的物理比較
llm.tldr_ja: 生体模倣スキンを用いて受容器アナログセンサーを埋め込んだ層状ロボットスキンを開発し、受容器の空間配置が受動的触覚タスクの性能に与える影響を検証した。
llm.problem: 生体の皮膚における多様な受容器の空間組織化の機能的意義を生きたシステムで制御された条件下で実験的に検証することは困難である。
llm.method: 受容器アナログセンサーを柔らかいメディアに埋め込んだ層状の生体模倣ロボットスキンを開発し、生物学的配置と反事実的配置を実装して3つの受動的触覚タスクで評価する。
llm.result: 生物学的動機付けに基づく感覚配置を反映した構成は、検証された他の代替構成よりも高い性能を示した。

2610.26663.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
2610.26663.abstract: Robotic value models assess task execution from visual observations and instructions, providing feedback for policy learning and execution monitoring. However, existing evaluations cover only selected aspects of execution understanding, leaving the reliability of value feedback insufficiently tested. We introduce RoboValue, a fine-grained sim-and-real benchmark for unified evaluation of robotic value models. Its framework evaluates four complementary capability dimensions through shared interfaces: task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure and recovery reasoning, and value consistency. Diagnostic trajectories and instruction variations test whether value judgments accurately reflect task requirements and changes throughout execution. RoboValue-Dataset covers 15 simulation and 20 real-world manipulation tasks, providing expert demonstrations for training and annotated trajectories for fine-grained evaluation. We evaluate representative robotic value models in zero-shot and one-shot settings under standard conditions and separate shifts in robot embodiment and environment. Our results reveal errors in fine-grained instruction grounding, history-dependent progress tracking, and recovery assessment, even in models with strong outcome and forward-progress scores. The same semantic subtask can also receive substantially different value gains across valid execution orders. These findings identify concrete targets for value supervision, while the dataset and public leaderboard support continued assessment of feedback reliability. The website is available at https://robovalue-benchmark.github.io/.
2610.26663.hf_summary_en: RoboValue introduces a benchmark to evaluate robotic value models across task-state understanding, progress tracking, failure recovery, and consistency in both simulated and real-world settings.

llm.title_ja: RoboValue：ロボット価値モデルの統一評価のための高粒度Sim-and-Realベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット価値モデルをタスク状態理解、時間的進捗モニタリング、失敗・リカバリー推論、価値の一貫性の4つの側面からシミュレーションと現実世界で評価するベンチマーク「RoboValue」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のロボット価値モデルの評価は実行理解の一部側面のみをカバーしており、価値フィードバックの信頼性が十分に検証されていない。
llm.method: タスク状態理解、時間的進捗、失敗リカバリー、価値一貫性の4つの次元で評価するシミュレーションおよび現実世界のマニピュレーションタスクを含むベンチマーク「RoboValue」を構築した。
llm.result: 既存のモデルであっても細かな指示の接地や履歴依存の進捗追跡、リカバリー評価においてエラーがあることが明らかになった。

2610.26641.title: EgoRayFormer: Ray-Space Stereo Refinement for Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
2610.26641.abstract: Head-mounted stereo fisheye cameras provide a compact view of the wearer's body, but strong distortion, partial visibility and a short baseline make 3D pose estimation difficult. Existing refinement decoders sample image features independently in each view, without requiring the samples to correspond to a common 3D hypothesis. We introduce EgoRayFormer, a causal pose estimator that couples stereo feature sampling and geometric refinement in ray space. For each joint, the decoder projects shared 3D hypotheses along and around its viewing ray into both images. A geometric branch then corrects the projected joint locations and intersects the resulting rays; a learned gate blends this geometric estimate with a learned pose update. This formulation introduces an explicit stereo constraint while retaining flexibility when the rays provide weak depth constraints. In local evaluations on the official device-relative test splits, EgoRayFormer achieves three-seed mean MPJPEs of 17.64 mm on UnrealEgo2 and 49.55 mm on UnrealEgo-RW, improving to 47.57 mm with UnrealEgo2 pre-training. In paired validation ablations, removing the geometric branch increases MPJPE in all three seeds at both input resolutions. With a common ResNet-18 encoder and input resolution, our system reduces RW test MPJPE by 9.09 mm relative to the device-relative EgoPoseFormer baseline. A separate protocol analysis quantifies the difference between device-relative and oracle-root evaluation.
2610.26641.tldr_en: EgoRayFormer, a causal pose estimator that couples stereo feature sampling and geometric refinement in ray space, is introduced, a causal pose estimator that introduces an explicit stereo constraint while retaining flexibility when the rays provide weak depth constraints.

llm.title_ja: EgoRayFormer：一人称視点3D人体姿勢推定のためのレイ空間ステレオ洗練
llm.tldr_ja: 視線に沿ったステレオ特徴量サンプリングと幾何学的洗練を結合した因果的姿勢推定器「EgoRayFormer」を提案し、一人称視点フィッシュアイカメラでの3D姿勢推定精度を向上させた。
llm.problem: ヘッド装着型ステレオフィッシュアイカメラは装着者の体のコンパクトなビューを提供するが、強い歪み、部分的な可視性、短いベースラインのため3D姿勢推定が困難である。
llm.method: ステレオ特徴量サンプリングと幾何学的洗練をレイ空間で結合し、各関節の共有3D仮説を両方の画像に投影して幾何学的推定と姿勢更新をブレンドする因果的姿勢推定器を設計する。
llm.result: UnrealEgo2およびUnrealEgo-RWデータセットにおいて従来のベースラインと比較してMPJPE（平均関節位置誤差）を大幅に削減した。

2610.26633.title: CAOS-SLAM: Class-Agnostic Object-Aware Real-Time vSLAM for Dynamic Environments
2610.26633.abstract: Robust visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (vSLAM) in dynamic environments faces challenges due to the presence of moving objects that may introduce erroneous observations, corrupt the map reconstruction and overall degrade localization accuracy. Existing vSLAM approaches often rely on predefined semantic classes or costly pixel-wise classification, limiting their robustness or applicability in real-world scenarios. This paper presents CAOS-SLAM, a dynamic vSLAM framework that extends ORB-SLAM3 with a hybrid perception pipeline to detect, track, and filter both semantically known and previously unseen moving objects in real-time. On-demand panoptic segmentation is performed for object discovery, with candidate unknown objects instantiated through depth-based clustering of unclassified regions. Between panoptic updates, persistent object tracks are updated using lightweight detection when available or temporal mask propagation based on world-frame Kalman prediction, depth consistency, and appearance similarity. The estimated object motion is then used to reject dynamic features from the SLAM pipeline. Experimental results on multiple dynamic RGB-D datasets and real-world experiments demonstrate improved localization accuracy over state-of-the-art dynamic vSLAM approaches, achieving up to 59% lower localization error in scenes characterized by unknown dynamic objects and up to 88% lower error in heavily occluded scenes, while achieving a median processing rate of 30 FPS on a laptop. Furthermore, the tracking module provides estimates of object trajectories and velocities, supporting potential future applications in perception, navigation, and motion-planning tasks in dynamic environments. Code and dataset will be released upon acceptance.
2610.26633.tldr_en: CAOS-SLAM is presented, a dynamic vSLAM framework that extends ORB-SLAM3 with a hybrid perception pipeline to detect, track, and filter both semantically known and previously unseen moving objects in real-time, achieving improved localization accuracy over state-of-the-art dynamic vSLAM approaches.

llm.title_ja: CAOS-SLAM：動的環境のためのクラス非依存・オブジェクト認識型リアルタイムvSLAM
llm.tldr_ja: ORB-SLAM3を拡張し、動的環境において既知および未知の移動オブジェクトをリアルタイムで検出し、追跡・フィルタリングして位置推定精度を向上させるハイブリッド知覚パイプライン「CAOS-SLAM」を提案した。
llm.problem: 動的環境におけるロバストなvSLAMは、誤った観測をもたらし地図再構築を破損させて位置推定精度を低下させる移動オブジェクトの存在により困難である。
llm.method: ORB-SLAM3をベースに、オンデマンドのパノプティックセグメンテーションと未知オブジェクトの深度ベースクラスタリングを組み合わせ、動的特徴をSLAMパイプラインから排除するハイブリッド知覚パイプラインを構築する。
llm.result: 未知の動的オブジェクトや激しいオクルージョンが存在するシーンにおいて、最先端の動的vSLAM手法と比較して最大59%〜88%低い位置推定誤差を達成した。
keywords_ja: パノプティックセグメンテーション

2610.26629.title: VaDar: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation
2610.26629.abstract: Long-horizon tasks are important for modern AI and robotics, yet pose a challenge for reinforcement learning. Historically, a popular approach has been to decompose a task into subgoals, and learn a subgoal-conditioned policy to execute each subtask in sequence. We introduce an alternative called Value Disaggregation (VaDar), which trains a single subgoal-independent policy to maximize a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values. Because subgoal information is needed only at training-time, VaDar removes the need for possibly costly or cumbersome subgoal-selection during policy deployment. Moreover, through careful experiments, we show that VaDar (1) is always competitive with, and frequently outperforms, natural baselines like goal-conditioning and (2) succeeds on tasks with non-sequential goal structure and multiple optimization objectives. In particular, VaDar is the first algorithm to solve challenging, long-horizon tasks in the RoboCasa suite, even when starting from a policy pretrained from behavior cloning with near-zero initial task success. Taken together, VaDar's successes suggest that subgoal information benefits actor-critic reinforcement learning by enhancing the efficacy of critic learning, whereas policy goal-conditioning is often unnecessary.
2610.26629.tldr_en: Value Disaggregation (VaDar), which trains a single subgoal-independent policy to maximize a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values, is introduced, suggesting that subgoal information benefits actor-critic reinforcement learning by enhancing the efficacy of critic learning, whereas policy goal-conditioning is often unnecessary.

llm.title_ja: VaDar：価値分解を通じた暗黙的ゴール条件付け
llm.tldr_ja: サブゴール情報に依存しない単一のポリシーを訓練し、サブゴールごとのクリティック値の線形結合を最大化することで、展開時のサブゴール選択の手間を不要にする「VaDar」を提案した。
llm.problem: 強化学習において長期タスクは課題であり、従来はタスクをサブゴールに分解してサブゴール条件付きポリシーを学習していたが、展開時にコストがかかる。
llm.method: サブゴールの情報を使用せず、サブゴールごとのクリティック値の線形結合を最大化するように単一のポリシーを訓練する価値分解手法（VaDar）を導入する。
llm.result: RoboCasaスイートの困難な長期タスクを解決し、行動クローンから事前学習されたポリシーでも競合手法を上回る成功率を示した。

2610.26625.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
2610.26625.abstract: Reconstructing human activity from egocentric video requires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, and hand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world. Achieving this coherence requires both joint reconstruction and aligned supervision, yet existing methods and datasets offer limited support for either. We present EgoXperience, a full-stack paradigm that addresses these needs through data collection, automatic annotation, unified modeling, and benchmarking. Central to EgoXperience is an automatic annotation engine, EgoX-Engine, that couples geometrically verified object tracking with SLAM-based world alignment, yielding consistent supervision for the camera, scene, hands, and objects. This yields EgoX-Data-6M, a 50-hour dataset of task-driven manipulation and locomotion within and across indoor and outdoor environments, with second-level task captions. We carefully select one hour across these activity categories as EgoX-Bench to evaluate joint reconstruction. To translate this supervision into reconstruction, we introduce EgoX, trained with EgoX-Data-6M and complementary annotations from additional public datasets. Given monocular egocentric video and first-frame object masks, our model achieves joint metric reconstruction of the camera, scene, hands, and objects in a shared world coordinate frame with a single forward pass. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across scene estimation and world-space hand-object pose recovery. Against the strongest evaluated baselines, EgoX reduces camera, hand, and depth errors by 68.9%, 65.6%, and 42.9%, and improves object pose scores by 28.0%.
2610.26625.hf_summary_en: EgoXperience introduces a unified framework for joint reconstruction of camera motion, scene geometry, hands, and objects from egocentric video using automatically annotated large-scale data and a single-pass model.

llm.title_ja: EgoXperience：人間の経験から世界に接地された一人称視点表現を学習する
llm.tldr_ja: 一人称視点映像からカメラ、シーン、手、オブジェクトを共通のワールド座標系で一括して幾何学的再構築を行うフルスタックパラダイム「EgoXperience」を提案した。
llm.problem: 一人称視点映像からの人間活動の再構築には、観察者の動き、周囲の幾何学、手とオブジェクトの相互作用が一貫した世界に適合する必要があるが、既存手法やデータセットは十分なサポートを提供していない。
llm.method: 幾何学的に検証されたオブジェクト追跡とSLAMベースのワールドアライメントを組み合わせた自動アノテーションエンジン（EgoX-Engine）と、単一のフォワードパスで同時メトリック再構築を行うモデル（EgoX）を開発する。
llm.result: EgoX-Data-6Mデータセットを用いた実験において、カメラ、手、深度のエラーを大幅に削減し、オブジェクト姿勢のスコアを28.0%改善した。
keywords_ja: ハンド・オブジェクト相互作用

2610.26605.title: A Probabilistic, Rotation-Preserving Kernel Operator Surrogate for Continuum-Robot Design Spaces
2610.26605.abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware, operator-learning-based surrogate for tendon-driven continuum robots (TDCRs) that generalizes across robot design and actuation while predicting the complete equilibrium configuration. Our central idea is a nonstationary Gaussian-process (GP) kernel whose metric is learned by a shallow neural network from mechanics-aware design coordinates. The network learns how similarity changes across design space, while the resulting kernel defines the design-to-pose operator, its posterior uncertainty, and a criterion for sequential simulator acquisition. We represent backbone position and rotational strain with spatial kernels and reconstruct orientation directly on SO(3), preserving valid material frames and tendon geometry. We use ASkotch with Nystrom preconditioning for scalable kernel operator solves and a separate Nystrom approximation for posterior covariance. Experiments show that kernel-coverage acquisition reduces mean trajectory error by approximately 15% relative to IID sampling, while posterior variance increases for increasingly unsupported designs. Compared with prior neural-operator TDCR models, the method is 30-50% more accurate using approximately 5x fewer training designs while additionally providing posterior uncertainty estimates.
2610.26605.comment: Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

llm.title_ja: 連続体ロボットの設計空間のための確率的・回転保存型カーネル演算子サロゲート
llm.tldr_ja: 力学考慮型設計座標からニューラルネットワークによって計量を学習する非定常ガウス過程カーネルを用い、連続体ロボットの平衡構成を予測する不確実性考慮型サロゲートモデルを開発した。
llm.problem: テンドン駆動型連続体ロボット（TDCRs）の設計と駆動に一般化しつつ完全な平衡構成を予測することは困難である。
llm.method: 力学を考慮した設計座標から計量を学習する非定常ガウス過程（GP）カーネルを構築し、空間カーネルを用いて背骨の位置と回転ひずみを表現してSO(3)上で直接向きを再構築する。
llm.result: カーネルカバレッジ獲得により、IIDサンプリングと比較して平均軌道誤差を約15%削減し、従来のニューラル演算子モデルよりも5倍少ない訓練設計で30〜50%高い精度を実現した。

2610.26584.title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control
2610.26584.abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. We propose HAF-VLA, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control. Built upon a pretrained flow-matching VLA, HAF-VLA inherits the vision-language prefix encoder and action expert weights, and adapts them to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with learnable stage embeddings and cross-stage KV-cache conditioning. Instead of generating the full action chunk in a single pass, HAF-VLA progressively denoises a shared whole-body action space: first locomotion and head commands, then waist refinement, and finally full-body manipulation. To preserve structural dependencies across stages, we introduce a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism, enabling subsequent action generation stages to refine and augment their outputs based on the action representations from preceding stages. Experimental results across six real-world tasks demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, demonstrating an effective pathway for adapting strong mobile-manipulation VLAs to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.
2610.26584.tldr_en: HAF-VLA is proposed, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control that significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, and introduces a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism to preserve structural dependencies across stages.

llm.title_ja: HAF-VLA：ヒューマノイドビジョン・言語・行動制御のための階層型アクションフローフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ヒューマノイドの全身移動マニピュレーションのために、学習可能なステージ埋め込みとステージ間KVキャッシュ条件付けを用いて全身アクションスペースを段階的にノイズ除去する階層型フレームワーク「HAF-VLA」を提案した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットは高次元の全身アクションスペースにおいて移動、姿勢、視線、双腕マニピュレーションを協調させる必要があり、不正確なベースの動きが上半体の不安定性を引き起こしやすい。
llm.method: 事前学習済みのフローマッチングVLAを基盤とし、移動・頭部コマンド、ウエストの洗練、全身マニピュレーションへと段階的にアクションを生成する階層型アクションフローフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 6つの実世界タスクにおける実験により、既存モデルのヒューマノイド移動マニピュレーション性能が大幅に向上することが示された。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション
階層型フレームワーク

2610.26583.title: DenseHap: Dense Hand Haptic Estimation from Monocular Images
2610.26583.abstract: As dexterous robotic manipulation advances, scalable annotations of human hand-object interactions are becoming increasingly important. Furthermore, previous hand contact estimation methods suffered from issues such as dorsal-side misclassifications and insufficient precision, while lacking a unified framework for integrating multiple hand to environment interaction modalities, including distance fields, contact thresholds, and pressure. To address that, we present DenseHap, a unified end-to-end approach to estimate hand distance field recognition, comprehensive hand contact detection, hand pressure analysis, and hand reconstruction from a single monocular image. By incorporating three distinctly defined heads, along with a pretrained 3D reconstructed skeleton and an enhanced dataset, DenseHap outperforms previous state of the art models on four evaluation datasets, improving the F1 score by 8.5 percentage points (a 16% relative improvement) on untrained datasets and by 3 percentage points (5% relative improvement) on in-distribution datasets. Furthermore, DenseHap has effectively improved short-range hand estimate and pressure evaluation. Code and models will be publicly available upon the paper's acceptance.
2610.26583.tldr_en: DenseHap is presented, a unified end-to-end approach to estimate hand distance field recognition, comprehensive hand contact detection, hand pressure analysis, and hand reconstruction from a single monocular image that outperforms previous state of the art models on four evaluation datasets.

llm.title_ja: DenseHap：単一画像からの高密度ハンド触覚推定
llm.tldr_ja: 単一の単眼画像からハンドの距離場認識、接触検出、圧力解析、3D再構築を統合的に推定するエンドツーエンドの手法「DenseHap」を提案し、複数の評価データセットで従来手法を上回る性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 従来の手法は、背側の誤分類や精度不足といった課題を抱えており、距離場、接触閾値、圧力などの複数のインタラクションモダリティを統合する統一されたフレームワークが欠けていた。
llm.method: 3D再構築されたスケルトンと拡張されたデータセットに加え、3つの異なるヘッドを組み込んだエンドツーエンドのニューラルネットワークアーキテクチャを構築する。
llm.result: 4つの評価データセットにおいて、未訓練データセットでF1スコアを8.5ポイント（16%の相対的改善）向上させ、近距離のハンド推定と圧力評価を効果的に改善した。
keywords_ja: ハンド・オブジェクト相互作用

2610.26564.title: PrismWAM: Decoupling State Representations in World Action Models
2610.26564.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) typically represent the world through latent embeddings from pretrained video models, which entangle heterogeneous aspects of the world, from how it looks (e.g., texture and color) to how it is physically configured (e.g., occupancy and pose). This raises an underexplored question: $\textbf{what should constitute the state of a WAM?}$ We argue that the world state should separate how the world appears from how the world evolves under action: the former captures semantic context, while the latter is governed by physical state. To this end, we propose $\textbf{PrismWAM}$, which decouples physics from semantics while jointly modeling state and action. PrismWAM factorizes an embodied task into a $\mathrm{Semantic\ Planning}\rightarrow\mathrm{Physical\ Rollout}\rightarrow\mathrm{Executable\ Action}$ pipeline: given only the initial RGB observation, semantic planning learns to predict the final goal image, while physical rollout predicts the fine-grained evolution toward this goal in depth space; executable actions are then generated from the depth rollout. Without any embodied action pretraining or additional data augmentation, PrismWAM achieves strong manipulation performance in both simulation and the real world. Notably, PrismWAM even surpasses a broad range of models with large-scale embodied action pretraining (e.g., OpenWAM-$α$). More broadly, we reframe World Action Models from modeling how the world looks to how it responds to action, paving the way for action-centric world models grounded in occupancy, flow, tactile sensing, proprioception, and beyond.
2610.26564.tldr_en: PrismWAM is proposed, which decouples physics from semantics while jointly modeling state and action, and reframe World Action Models from modeling how the world looks to how it responds to action, paving the way for action-centric world models grounded in occupancy, flow, tactile sensing, proprioception, and beyond.

llm.title_ja: PrismWAM：ワールド・アクション・モデルにおける状態表現の分離
llm.tldr_ja: 見た目（セマンティクス）と物理的状態（ダイナミクス）を分離し、意味的計画→物理的ロールアウト→実行可能アクションのパイプラインとしてモデル化する「PrismWAM」を提案した。
llm.problem: ワールド・アクション・モデル（WAMs）は事前学習済み動画モデルの潜在表現を用いて世界を表現するが、見た目と物理的構成がもつれ合っており、WAMの状態として何を構成すべきかという問いが未開拓であった。
llm.method: セマンティック計画によって最終目標画像を予測し、物理的ロールアウトによって深度空間での詳細な進化を予測し、最終的にアクションを生成する因数分解パイプライン「PrismWAM」を提案する。
llm.result: 大規模なembodiedアクション事前学習なしで、シミュレーションと実世界の両方で強力なマニピュレーション性能を達成し、多くの事前学習モデルを上回った。

2610.26554.title: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
2610.26554.abstract: Long-horizon embodied agents face temporal confusion and incomplete or distorted records, recurring errors from fixed memory rules, and growing storage and retrieval costs. We present BetaMem, a framework for building and evolving traceable long-term memory through six linked layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural memory. A dual-level write contract constrains operation executability and source support for content: supervised fine-tuning learns compliant memory operations, while reinforcement learning combines repeated sampling with teacher verification of the original observations to reward complete, accurate records and penalize omissions, distortion, and unsupported content. We formulate failure-driven policy recursive self-improvement through diagnosis along the causal sequence of memory operations and local rule repairs gated by independent replay. Atomic tools frame storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting as cost-utility allocation under storage and read budgets. Using the open-source Qwen3.5-9B model for memory generation, BetaMem achieves overall scores of 48.08% on M3-Bench-robot, 92.08% on LoCoMo, 72.6% on OpenEQA EM-EQA, and 62.4% on EgoLifeQA, the highest among the listed memory methods under their respective evaluation protocols. Training the model for memory generation raises the contract pass rate from 50.9% to 86.2% while reducing output tokens per stored action by 47.3%. A separate Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on EMem-Bench achieves an average success rate of 38.4% and an average error recurrence rate of 24.9%. We perform best among evaluated methods using comparably sized open-source models. Category results show that we have advantages in integrating information across observations, recalling events over long histories, and inferring personal habits.

llm.title_ja: BetaMem：エージェントのための変化する世界を記憶する学習
llm.tldr_ja: 作業、空間、エンティティ、エピソード、経験的、手続き的記憶の6つの連動レイヤーを通じて、トレーサブルな長期記憶を構築・進化させるフレームワーク「BetaMem」を提案した。
llm.problem: 長期的なエージェントは、時間的混乱、不完全または歪んだ記録、固定された記憶ルールによる繰り返しのエラー、ストレージと検索コストの増大に直面している。
llm.method: 二段階の書き込み契約を用いて記憶操作を制約し、教師あり微調整と強化学習を組み合わせて完全で正確な記録を促し、コスト・ユーティリティ配分としてストレージや検索を管理するフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: M3-Bench-robotやLoCoMoなどの複数のベンチマークで最高スコアを達成し、コントラクトの合格率を高めつつトークン消費量を削減した。
keywords_ja: ロボットエージェント

2610.26550.title: Learning Wheel Motion Uncertainty for Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry on Quadrupedal Wheel-Legged Robots
2610.26550.abstract: Wheel kinematics can support odometry for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots when LiDAR geometry provides weak motion constraints. However, slip and contact loss make rolling predictions unreliable, and contact state alone cannot determine their reliability across motion directions. We propose a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework that retains analytical rolling predictions and learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history. The estimator maintains moving wheel-center states, allowing the learned uncertainty to regulate the influence of rolling predictions through forward-kinematic corrections. Degeneracy-aware projection (DAP) complements this mechanism by suppressing LiDAR constraints along geometrically weak directions. The learned covariance network (CovNet) is trained through a differentiable filter using simulated velocity supervision and deployed on the real robot without fine-tuning. On the six room sequences with the highest degeneracy ratios in our indoor dataset, the method reduces mean per-sequence position root mean square error (RMSE) by 66.2% relative to FAST-LIO2 and by 31.0% relative to a fixed-covariance variant. In a severely degenerate corridor run, it achieves an endpoint position error of 0.198 m, compared with 7.531 m for FAST-LIO2. These results demonstrate robust odometry under challenging geometric and wheel-motion conditions. We plan to publicly release our code and multimodal dataset. Project website: https://weihairuo.github.io/wheel-motion-uncertainty/
2610.26550.tldr_en: A tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework that retains analytical rolling predictions and learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history, and demonstrates robust odometry under challenging geometric and wheel-motion conditions.

llm.title_ja: 車輪付き四足ロボットの退化耐性LiDAR-慣性オドメトリのための車輪運動不確実性の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 解析的な転がり予測を維持しつつ固有受容の履歴から車輪ごとの方向依存のプロセス共分散を学習する、密に結合されたLiDAR-慣性-運動学オドメトリフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: LiDAR幾何学が弱い運動制約しか提供しない場合、車輪運動学がオドメトリを支援できるが、スリップや接触喪失によりローリング予測が信頼できなくなる。
llm.method: 動的な車輪中心状態を維持し、前方運動学補正を介して学習された不確実性がローリング予測の影響を調整する仕組みと、幾何学的に弱い方向のLiDAR制約を抑制する退化耐性プロジェクションを組み合わせる。
llm.result: 屋内データセットの退化率の高いシーケンスにおいて、FAST-LIO2と比較して平均位置RMSEを66.2%削減し、困難な幾何学および車輪運動条件下でロバストなオドメトリを実現した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2610.26545.title: ReInsVLN: Revisiting Historical Evidence for Training-Free Vision-and-Language Navigation
2610.26545.abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) relies on retaining and using relevant observations. Yet growing histories introduce redundancy, and retained information may remain underused. We introduce ReInsBench, a diagnostic benchmark that examines history utilization through controlled continuation trials. Its results show that history-review reinstruction can recover navigation failures using the existing task context. Motivated by this finding, we propose ReInsVLN, a training-free framework supporting memory construction and utilization in frozen navigators. Coverage- and Instruction-Aware Compression constructs compact visual context through temporal redundancy reduction, coverage-aware protection, and instruction-guided token selection. Forgetting-Inspired History Reminders guide navigators to revisit retained observations according to a predefined schedule, without additional model calls. On R2R Val-Unseen, ReInsVLN improves success rates by 8.48 and 3.37 percentage points over the native StreamVLN and InternVLA-N1, reaching 64.27% and 64.44%, respectively. Visual compression largely preserves navigation performance while reducing prefill latency and KV cache memory by up to 21.77% and 32.25%, respectively, on matched observation workloads. Real-world trials on humanoid and quadruped robots further support the applicability of ReInsVLN to sequential instruction following and ordinal navigation.
2610.26545.tldr_en: This work proposes ReInsVLN, a training-free framework supporting memory construction and utilization in frozen navigators and introduces ReInsBench, a diagnostic benchmark that examines history utilization through controlled continuation trials that shows that history-review reinstruction can recover navigation failures using the existing task context.

llm.title_ja: ReInsVLN：トレーニング不要の視覚言語ナビゲーションのための過去の証拠の再訪
llm.tldr_ja: 履歴レビュー再指示によってナビゲーションの失敗を回復できることを示し、凍結されたナビゲーターにおいてメモリ構築と利用をサポートするトレーニング不要のフレームワーク「ReInsVLN」を提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚言語ナビゲーション（VLN）は関連する観察の保持と利用に依存するが、履歴の増大は冗長性をもたらし、保持された情報が十分に活用されない。
llm.method: 冗長性の削減や指示誘導型トークン選択によってコンパクトな視覚文脈を構築する圧縮技術と、事前定義されたスケジュールに従って保持された観察を再訪するリマインダーを組み合わせたトレーニング不要のフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: R2R Val-Unseenにおいて、成功率を従来のベースライン（StreamVLNやInternVLA-N1）と比較して大幅に向上させ、KVキャッシュメモリとレイテンシを削減した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション
ロボットナビゲーション

2610.26508.title: Learning Geometry-Aware Planning Representations for Monocular Flight with Cross-Modal Supervision
2610.26508.abstract: Existing high-speed navigation systems for micro aerial vehicles (MAVs) commonly rely on depth cameras, stereo vision, or LiDAR to obtain explicit geometric information, while monocular cameras offer a lighter and lower-cost alternative. However, monocular flight remains challenging because RGB images offer no direct metric cues and visual appearance varies considerably across environments.
