We propose a geometry-aware monocular visual planning framework that predicts trajectories from two image frames, their relative pose, and the MAV state. Without explicitly reconstructing depth, the proposed method complements the downstream planning objective with feature-level geometric supervision by transferring the planning-relevant representation learned by a privileged depth expert to the RGB planner through cross-modal distillation. The framework first trains a depth-based geometric expert, then distills its planning features into a monocular branch using paired RGB-D observations, and finally adapts the planner to the downstream trajectory planning objective. This design encourages the policy to learn planning-relevant geometric features, enabling collision avoidance. We further use a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) simulator to render visual observations for data collection, paired RGB-D supervision, and simulation evaluation. The planner trained in simulation is then deployed in real-world environments without real-world fine-tuning, achieving obstacle avoidance at speeds of up to 6.5 m/s.
2610.26508.tldr_en: A geometry-aware monocular visual planning framework that predicts trajectories from two image frames, their relative pose, and the MAV state by transferring the planning-relevant representation learned by a privileged depth expert to the RGB planner through cross-modal distillation is proposed.

llm.title_ja: クロスモダリティ指導を用いた単眼飛行のための幾何学認識型プランニング表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 特権的深度エージェントが学習したプランニング関連表現をクロスモダリティ蒸留によってRGBプランナーに転写し、深度を明示的に再構築することなく軌道を予測する幾何学認識型単眼視覚プランニングフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: マイクロ空中車両（MAVs）の高速ナビゲーションは深度カメラ等に依存することが多く、単眼カメラは軽量かつ低コストである一方、直接的なメトリックの手がかりがなく困難である。
llm.method: 特権的な深度ベースの幾何学的エージェントを訓練し、ペアとなるRGB-D観察を用いてそのプランニング特徴を単眼ブランチに蒸留し、障害物回避のためのプランニング目標に適応させる。
llm.result: シミュレーション環境で訓練されたプランナーを実世界環境にそのままデプロイし、実世界での微調整なしで最大6.5 m/sの速度での障害物回避を実現した。

2610.26507.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
2610.26507.abstract: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%. With $π_{0.5}$ on an Independent task, a 4 s pause transfers 2.56 s of delay to the opposite arm under the Concurrent schedule distribution, but only 0.25 s with CTR. On real robots, CTR violates task constraints in only 0--4% of trials, versus 36--98% for narrow-schedule baselines. Code will be released at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/CTR.
2610.26507.tldr_en: Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints is introduced.

llm.title_ja: タスクを学び、スケジュールを学ぶな：双腕模倣学習における偽のクロスアーム結合の削減
llm.tldr_ja: 記録されたアームごとのセンサーモータコンテンツを保持しつつ、タスクに必要なクロスアーム制約を維持する許容スケジュールに再タイミングするデータ介入手法「CTR」を提案した。
llm.problem: 双腕デモンストレーションはタスク内容と特定のアーム動作のタイミングを同時に指定するため、標準的な模倣学習は誤ったクロスアーム結合を作り出す可能性がある。
llm.method: 記録されたアームごとのセンサーモータ内容を保持し、タスクに必要なクロスアーム制約を満たすように対応するセグメントを再タイミングする訓練時データ介入手法（CTR）を導入する。
llm.result: 6つの実世界の双腕タスクにおいて、CTRは最強のベースラインと比較して最悪状態の成功率を56%から76%に向上させ、スケジュール違反を大幅に削減した。

2610.26487.title: SPAR: Structural Pruning and Action Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.26487.abstract: The limited onboard computing resources of robots make the inference demands of vision-language-action (VLA) models costly to accommodate. Reducing these demands through aggressive compression, however, can degrade manipulation performance beyond what supervised fine-tuning alone recovers. We present SPAR (Structural Pruning and Action Recovery), which simultaneously prunes the hidden and feed-forward intermediate dimensions of the large language model (LLM) backbone through pruning-aware tuning, then applies reinforcement learning (RL) to recover policy performance. Applied to $π_{0.5}$, SPAR reduces the language backbone from 2.34B to 0.09B parameters and the full model from 3.37B to 1.12B, removing approximately 96% and 67% of their parameters, respectively. At this compression level, RL raises average success across the four LIBERO suites from 84.55% to 93.45%, an 8.90-percentage-point gain. The compressed policy achieves a $1.98\times$ full-policy inference speedup over the unpruned model. These results identify substantial intermediate-dimension redundancy and show that post-pruning RL can recover manipulation performance in compact policies.
2610.26487.tldr_en: SPAR (Structural Pruning and Action Recovery), which simultaneously prunes the hidden and feed-forward intermediate dimensions of the large language model (LLM) backbone through pruning-aware tuning, then applies reinforcement learning (RL) to recover policy performance, identifies substantial intermediate-dimension redundancy and shows that post-pruning RL can recover manipulation performance in compact policies.

llm.title_ja: SPAR：ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのための構造的プルーニングとアクション回復
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデルバックボーンの隠れ層およびフィードフォワード中間次元をプルーニング認識型チューニングによって同時にプルーニングし、強化学習を用いてポリシー性能を回復させる手法「SPAR」を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットの限られたオンボード計算資源にとってVLAモデルの推論要求はコストが高く、大幅な圧縮はマニピュレーション性能を低下させる。
llm.method: プルーニング認識型チューニングによってLLMバックボーンの隠れ層・中間次元をプルーニングし、その後強化学習（RL）を適用してポリシー性能を回復させるフレームワーク（SPAR）を構築する。
llm.result: $0.5$に適用した場合、パラメータを大幅に削減しつつLIBEROスイート全体の平均成功率を向上させ、1.98倍の推論速度向上を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2610.26455.title: ALIGN: Aligning Condition Estimation and Expression in Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning
2610.26455.abstract: Human-collected robot manipulation data often mix successful behavior with retries, pauses, recoveries, and failures. Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning (AC-BC) can exploit such mixed-quality data, but only if the conditioning signal is both accurately constructed from offline trajectories and effectively incorporated into the policy's action-vector-field prediction. Existing pipelines can weaken this signal by thresholding estimator-derived advantage scores into noisy conditions, and by routing conditions through prompts that weakly affect the action vector field. We introduce ALIGN, a condition-aligned AC-BC framework for vision-language-action policies. ALIGN directly predicts categorical pairwise conditions in the policy-facing label space and injects them into a DiT action expert through AdaRMS modulation fused with flow time. We evaluate ALIGN on deliberately mixed real-robot datasets for ARX X5 bowl stacking and Franka key hanging, each combining standard demonstrations with retry-heavy trajectories. ALIGN improves condition fidelity, strengthens conditional vector-field separability, and achieves 90.0% and 56.7% closed-loop success, compared with 56.7% and 33.3% for the strongest AC-BC baseline. These results indicate that aligning conditions from estimation to action prediction is an effective way to extract robust manipulation policies from data in which success, recovery and error coexist.
2610.26455.tldr_en: ALIGN, a condition-aligned AC-BC framework for vision-language-action policies, is introduced, a condition-aligned AC-BC framework for vision-language-action policies that aligning conditions from estimation to action prediction is an effective way to extract robust manipulation policies from data in which success, recovery and error coexist.

llm.title_ja: ALIGN：アドバンテージ条件付き行動クローンにおける条件推定と表現のアライメント
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシー側のラベル空間でカテゴリカルなペアワイズ条件を直接予測し、フロー時間と変調されたDiTアクションエキスパートにそれらを注入する条件アライン型AC-BCフレームワーク「ALIGN」を提案した。
llm.problem: 人間の収集したロボットマニピュレーションデータは成功と失敗・再試行が混在しており、アドバンテージ条件付き行動クローン（AC-BC）を活用するには条件付け信号を正確に組み込む必要があるが、従来の手法ではシグナルが弱まる。
llm.method: ポリシー側のラベル空間でカテゴリカルなペアワイズ条件を直接予測し、AdaRMSモジュレーションとフロー時間を介してDiTアクションエキスパートに注入するフレームワーク（ALIGN）を導入する。
llm.result: 意図的に混在させた実世界データセットでの実験において、条件の忠実度を高め、最強のAC-BCベースラインと比較して高い閉ループ成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: アドバンテージ条件付け

2610.26445.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Comparison of Proportional Control and Adaptive Gravity Compensation in Elbow EMG-Driven Exoskeletons
2610.26445.abstract: Electromyography (EMG)-driven control enables wearable robots to assist users based on their neuromuscular activity. Upper-limb exoskeletons typically rely on proportional myoelectric control (PMC), which amplifies user effort but may compromise stability at high assistance levels. EMG-driven adaptive gravity compensation (AGC) offers a promising alternative, counterbalancing gravitational torques while continuously adapting to neuromuscular activity. However, these approaches have not been systematically compared in a human-in-the-loop setting. This study evaluates five control algorithms: two PMC strategies at different assistance levels, a purely integral AGC (AGC-PI), a kinematics- and acceleration-aware model-based (MB) AGC (AGC-AW), and a novel MB AGC approach based on Recursive Least Squares (AGC-RLS) for online payload estimation. Fourteen healthy participants performed target-reaching tasks using an active elbow exoskeleton under 0 kg and 2 kg loading conditions. Performance metrics included muscular activity, movement accuracy, task efficiency, and subjective workload. PMC exhibited a trade-off between physical effort and task performance: low assistance levels required greater physical effort under load, whereas high gains impaired task execution. AGC-PI reduced agonist activity but induced antagonist activation. In contrast, both model-based AGC approaches effectively compensated for external payloads, reducing physical and cognitive demands while improving movement accuracy and completion time.

llm.title_ja: 肘EMG駆動型外骨格における比例制御と適応型重力補償の人手による比較
llm.tldr_ja: 肘EMG駆動型外骨格において、モデルベースの適応型重力補償は外部ペイロードを効果的に補償し、身体的・認知的負荷を軽減しつつ動作精度と完了時間を改善することを示した。
llm.problem: 比例筋電制御（PMC）は物理的負荷とタスク性能の間でトレードオフがあり、適応型重力補償（AGC）は人間参加型（HITL）設定で体系的に比較されていなかった。
llm.method: 5つの制御アルゴリズム（2種類のPMC、積分型AGC、運動学・加速度認識モデルベースAGC、オンラインペイロード推定のための再帰最小二乗法モデルベースAGC）を14名の被験者によるターゲット到達課題で評価した。
llm.result: モデルベースのAGCアプローチは外部負荷を効果的に補償し、物理的・認知的要求を軽減しつつ、動作精度と完了時間を改善した。

2610.26414.title: RoboMMT: Learning Stable Tracking of Modulated Expressive and Interactive Robot Motion
2610.26414.abstract: Expressive robot motion can improve naturalness, effectiveness, and perceived likability in human-robot interaction. When deployed on dynamically unstable platforms, however, reactive execution of expressive body motion may bring the robot to its stability limits, especially when expressivity is decoupled from physical control. In this paper, we present RoboMMT (Robot Modulated Motion Tracking), a modular control architecture that couples parameterized expressive motion synthesis, physics-based character control, and reactive adaptation to spatial interaction goals. Our approach trains a reference-conditioned tracking policy across a broad domain of expressivity, enabling it to faithfully realize the commanded motions while maintaining dynamic stability. Goal reactivity is achieved by training lightweight, task-specific interaction policies that modulate the reference generator's spatial goal-attraction point, with the stabilizing tracking policy kept in the loop. Evaluations on a quadruped and two humanoid robots show that the learned tracker remains stable and accurate across the entire modulation domain, whereas trackers trained without this coverage lose balance, tracking accuracy, or both. We show that layering closed-loop goal adaptation over this foundation enables interactive facing and pointing behaviors, while maintaining stable execution and comparable reference-tracking fidelity. The robot learns to proactively redistribute its weight and take corrective steps. Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated through real-robot experiments on a quadruped under heavy disturbances.

llm.title_ja: RoboMMT：変調された表現力豊かでインタラクティブなロボットモーションの安定した追従学習
llm.tldr_ja: 表現力豊かなモーション合成、物理ベースのキャラクタ制御、空間的インタラクション目標への反応的適応を結合するモジュール型制御アーキテクチャ「RoboMMT」を提案し、四足歩行および2体のヒューマノイドロボットで動的安定性と追従精度を実証した。
llm.problem: 動的に不安定なプラットフォームにおいて、物理制御から切り離された表現力豊かなボディモーションの反応的実行は、ロボットを安定限界に追い込む可能性がある。
llm.method: パラメータ化された表現力豊かなモーション合成、物理ベースのキャラクタ制御、および空間的インタラクション目標への反応的適応を結合するモジュール型制御アーキテクチャ「RoboMMT」を提案し、参照条件付き追従ポリシーを訓練した。
llm.result: 四足歩行および2体のヒューマノイドロボットを用いた評価において、学習されたトラッカーは変調ドメイン全体で安定かつ正確を維持し、ゼロショットでのSim-to-Real転移も実証された。

2610.26404.title: LaMER: Language-Conditioned Multi-Expert Routing for Weakly Supervised Referring Expression Comprehension
2610.26404.abstract: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) localizes the image region described by a natural language expression, underpinning applications such as autonomous navigation, human-robot interaction, and medical image analysis. Under weak supervision, REC is challenged by the visual-linguistic semantic gap and the difficulty of inferring region-text correspondences from coarse image-level signals alone. Moreover, no single visual encoder captures all complementary properties---semantic alignment, fine-grained texture, and boundary awareness---while naively fusing multiple pretrained encoders yields heterogeneous, hard-to-reconcile representations. We propose LaMER, a weakly supervised REC framework that dynamically aggregates four frozen expert encoders through a language-conditioned Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module, adapting expert selection to each referring expression without instance-level bounding-box supervision. A Cell-Text Matching Head with Negative Anchor Augmentation, trained with a multi-objective loss combining contrastive, reconstruction, alignment, and load-balancing terms, further stabilizes optimization. LaMER achieves 77.67\%, 62.81\%, and 69.49\% Acc@IoU\(\geq 0.5\) on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg, surpassing DViN and WeakMCN by up to 16.49 and 14.49 points, with ablations validating each component.
2610.26404.tldr_en: LaMER is proposed, a weakly supervised REC framework that dynamically aggregates four frozen expert encoders through a language-conditioned Cross-Modal Routing Fusion module, adapting expert selection to each referring expression without instance-level bounding-box supervision.

llm.title_ja: LaMER：弱教師あり参照表現理解のための言語条件付きマルチエキスパートルーティング
llm.tldr_ja: LaMERは、インスタンスレベルのバウンディングボックスの教師なしで、言語条件付きクロスモーダルルーティング融合モジュールを介して4つの凍結されたエキスパートエンコーダを動的に集約する、弱教師あり参照表現理解（REC）フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 弱教師あり学習におけるRECは、視覚・言語間の意味的ギャップや、粗い画像レベルの信号のみから領域とテキストの対応関係を推論することの難しさに直面している。
llm.method: 言語条件付きクロスモーダルルーティング融合モジュールを通じて4つの凍結エキスパートエンコーダを動的に集約し、負のアンカー拡張を備えたセル・テキストマッチングヘッドを用いる「LaMER」を提案した。
llm.result: RefCOCO、RefCOCO+、RefCOCOgにおいてAcc@IoU≧0.5でそれぞれ77.67%、62.81%、69.49%を達成し、既存手法を大幅に上回った。

2610.26395.title: ForagerSim: Evaluating Embodied Map-Based Reasoning in Large-Scale Dynamic Worlds
2610.26395.abstract: Animals build cognitive maps of vast environments, use them to perform map-based navigation, and might even be reusing the same circuitry used in spatial reasoning for creating and using maps of arbitrary task-spaces. In contrast, current embodied AI systems either rely on hand-engineered mapping pipelines, which break in the presence of unmodeled dynamics and are restricted to metric space, or on learned policies that rarely form map-like representations at all. Developing architectures that could learn to build and use map-like representations as flexibly as animals is, however, difficult because few embodied AI benchmarks actually require map-based reasoning. To address this, we present ForagerSim --- an interdisciplinary research platform and simulation environment focused on embodied tasks that require map-based reasoning, with scenarios ranging from mobile-robot search and rescue to animal foraging in both complex mazes and vast, potentially infinite open areas. ForagerSim is highly modular and allows modifying independent axes of difficulty related to perception (abstract 2D sensing to full RGB or LiDAR), scale (room-scale to multi-km scale), topology (open-fields to complex mazes), dynamics (smoke, debris, sensorimotor failures and others) and tasks (from simple 2D coverage to foraging-inspired well-alternation tasks). We compare reinforcement learning baselines with a simple engineered robotics stack and a human player on 8 example worlds which show how different difficulty axes affect existing methods. Our results show that, when sensing is simplified to 2D, learned policies can perform multi-object search and well-alternation tasks surprisingly well in simple topologies, but they fall short of human performance in larger or more complex-topology environments where map-based baselines perform well, suggesting that map-based reasoning is the bottleneck in these scenarios.
2610.26395.tldr_en: The results show that, when sensing is simplified to 2D, learned policies can perform multi-object search and well-alternation tasks surprisingly well in simple topologies, but they fall short of human performance in larger or more complex-topology environments where map-based baselines perform well, suggesting that map-based reasoning is the bottleneck in these scenarios.

llm.title_ja: ForagerSim：大規模動的世界における具現化されたマップベース推論の評価
llm.tldr_ja: マップベースの推論を必要とする具現化されたタスクに焦点を当てた異分野融合型研究プラットフォームおよびシミュレーション環境「ForagerSim」を提案し、大規模環境においてマップベース推論がボトルネックであることを示した。
llm.problem: 現在の具現化されたAIシステムは、手動構築のマップパイプラインか、マップ状表現をほとんど形成しない学習済みポリシーに依存しており、動物のように柔軟にマップ状表現を構築・利用するアーキテクチャの開発が困難である。
llm.method: 知覚、スケール、トポロジ、ダイナミクス、タスクの難易度軸を独立に変更可能な、マップベース推論に特化したシミュレーション環境「ForagerSim」を構築し、強化学習ベースラインと従来の手法や人間プレイヤーを比較した。
llm.result: 単純なトポロジでは学習済みポリシーがマルチオブジェクト探索や交互探索タスクを良好にこなす一方、より大規模または複雑なトポロジの環境では人間のパフォーマンスに及ばず、マップベース推論がボトルネックであることが示された。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション環境

2610.26390.title: Cartender: Verifiable Language-Conditioned Driving by Learning the Drives Not Taken
2610.26390.abstract: Every driving scene is logged once, but driving is one-to-many: the scene determines which behaviors are feasible, while an instruction selects among them. A log records only the action taken, leaving no direct supervision for alternative feasible actions or instructions the scene cannot support. Consequently, a policy that ignores language and one that follows it without regard to scene constraints can fit the same data. We present Cartender, which learns from the drives not taken. Counterfactual Branching constructs matched and mismatched instruction-action pairs from real recordings without a simulator: a vision-language model proposes alternative futures and their selecting instructions, while unsupported instructions provide negative labels. A learned scene-language compatibility score regulates language conditioning in trajectory generation, and a reward-trained language residual re-ranks generated candidates over a scene-based score. The branches are used for training; instruction following is evaluated by swapping instructions under identical recorded inputs and measuring behavior rather than agreement with generated targets. On WOD-E2E, the best of four proposals achieves an RFS of 8.642 across 3,603 feasible instruction conditions. Across 8,974 admitted proposals, mean RFS is 8.203 versus 7.906 for matched logged trajectories, and 67% score higher than their logged counterpart. Compared with matched-only imitation using the same backbone, Cartender improves same-scene paired instruction success from 23.67% to 57.00% and RFS from 6.32 to 7.10; its gate reduces infeasible-instruction execution from 53.36% to 14.18%.
2610.26390.tldr_en: Cartender is presented, which learns from the drives not taken, which improves same-scene paired instruction success and reduces infeasible-instruction execution from 53.36% to 14.18% on WOD-E2E.

llm.title_ja: Cartender：取られなかった走行からの学習による検証可能な言語条件付き自動運転
llm.tldr_ja: Cartenderは、実記録から対となる命令と行動のペアを構築する反実仮想分岐手法を用いて、言語条件付き自動運転の不可能な命令の実行を削減し、性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 運転シーンは一対多であり、記録されたデータには選択されなかった代替行動や指示に対する直接的な教師信号が存在しないため、言語を無視するポリシーと無視しないポリシーが同じデータに適合してしまう。
llm.method: 反実仮想分岐により実記録から一致・不一致の指示・行動ペアを構築し、シーンと言語の互換性スコアや報酬学習された言語残差を用いて軌道生成時の言語条件付けを調整する「Cartender」を提案した。
llm.result: WOD-E2Eにおいて、同一シーンでのペア指示成功率を23.67%から57.00%に改善し、不可能な指示の実行を53.36%から14.18%に削減した。

2610.26287.title: Robotic Photography System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
2610.26287.abstract: Modern robotic photography requires understanding photographic intent, planning camera motions, and producing aesthetically pleasing images in complex environments. We present RoboPhoto-VLA, a unified Vision-Language-Action framework that jointly models perception, reasoning, and camera control for autonomous robotic photography. RoboPhoto-VLA incorporates PhotoCoT for structured action planning and Aesthetic Direct Preference Optimization (ADPO) to align camera behaviors with human aesthetic preferences. To facilitate training and evaluation, we construct OpenPhotography, a robotic photography dataset with language-guided demonstrations. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that RoboPhoto-VLA produces photographs better aligned with human aesthetic preferences while generalizing effectively to unseen subjects, viewpoints, poses, and complex photographic instructions.
2610.26287.tldr_en: RoboPhoto-VLA is presented, a unified Vision-Language-Action framework that jointly models perception, reasoning, and camera control for autonomous robotic photography that incorporates PhotoCoT for structured action planning and Aesthetic Direct Preference Optimization to align camera behaviors with human aesthetic preferences.

llm.title_ja: ビジョン・言語・アクションモデルに基づくロボット写真撮影システム
llm.tldr_ja: RoboPhoto-VLAは、構造化されたアクション計画のためのPhotoCoTと美的嗜好に合わせた選好最適化を統合し、人間の美的嗜好に合致した写真を撮影する統一されたVLAフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 現代のロボット写真撮影には、複雑な環境において写真の意図を理解し、カメラの動きを計画し、美しい画像を生成することが求められている。
llm.method: 構造化された行動計画のためのPhotoCoTと、カメラの動作を人間の美的嗜好に合わせる美的直接選好最適化（ADPO）を統合した統一VLAフレームワーク「RoboPhoto-VLA」を提案した。
llm.result: 実世界実験により、RoboPhoto-VLAは人間の美的嗜好により一致した写真を生成し、未知の被写体や視点、複雑な指示に対しても効果的に汎化することが示された。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語アクションモデル

2610.26210.title: AnchorFlow-VIO: Fixed-Template Monocular Visual-Inertial Odometry on LaMAria
2610.26210.abstract: We present AnchorFlow-VIO, an open-source Basalt-derived monocular visual-inertial odometry system, and evaluate a uniform configuration on LaMAria. The system uses one grayscale camera and one IMU, combining factory IMU correction, a fixed timing adjustment, windowed initialization and fixed-template patch tracking. Server evaluation of all 63 test recordings yields control-point scores of 47.2, 37.1, 24.8, 35.1 and 15.6 for Short, Medium, Long, Low light and Moving platform. Test pose recalls at 5 m are 84.6%, 69.1%, 53.9% and 62.9% for the four categories reporting dense recall. On ten training recordings, mean control-point score is 41.38 and all 265,694 image timestamps receive poses, including 204 filled poses. One training platform recording diverges and scores zero. A paired four-record comparison favors fixed over rolling templates on three recordings, while reversing that ranking on the fourth. Increasing feature density also yields mixed results. Ten fresh runs at prospectively fixed 30 s and 120 s offsets expose substantial start sensitivity: a low-light recording scores 6.14 at the earlier start and 42.00 at the later start. These results characterize the limits of the frozen system and show why complete output, feature counts and selected successful runs are insufficient evidence of robust localization. Source code, frozen configuration and reproducible submission tools are publicly available; training ablations are reported separately from the submitted test evaluation.
2610.26210.tldr_en: The limits of the frozen AnchorFlow-VIO are characterized and it is shown why complete output, feature counts and selected successful runs are insufficient evidence of robust localization.

llm.title_ja: AnchorFlow-VIO：LaMAriaにおける固定テンプレート単眼視覚慣性オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: AnchorFlow-VIOは、LaMAriaデータセット上で評価されたBasalt由来のオープンソース単眼視覚慣性オドメトリシステムであり、固定テンプレートパッチトラッキングやウィンドウ初期化などを活用している。
llm.problem: 完全な出力や特徴量数、選択された成功事例だけでは、頑健なローカライゼーションの証拠としては不十分である。
llm.method: 1台のグレースケールカメラと1台のIMUを使用し、工場出荷時のIMU補正、固定タイミング調整、ウィンドウ化された初期化、固定テンプレートパッチトラッキングを組み合わせたシステム「AnchorFlow-VIO」を評価した。
llm.result: 63のテスト記録のサーバー評価において制御点スコアや姿勢リコールを算出し、固定テンプレートとローリングテンプレートの比較や開始感度の限界を明らかにした。
keywords_ja: ローカライゼーション

2610.26201.title: K-AoI: A Spatio-Temporal Synchronization Metric for Digital Twin-based Teleoperation in Dynamic Network Environments
2610.26201.abstract: Synchronization between a digital twin (DT) and its physical robot is critical for effective teleoperation, as mismatches directly degrade operator awareness and task performance. Existing synchronization metrics are predominantly time-based and rarely capture the spatial consequences of delayed information during motion. In this paper, we introduce Kinematic Age of Information (K-AoI), a spatio-temporal metric that weights AoI by instantaneous Cartesian velocity, translating temporal staleness into physically meaningful spatial divergence. We implement and evaluate K-AoI on a DT teleoperation testbed comprising a six-degrees-of-freedom (6-DOF) manipulator, a Unity-based twin, and controlled network impairments using tc netem across seven network conditions. Per-sample analysis shows that K-AoI exhibits rank-correlations with AoI at $ρ\leq 0.65$ across all networks, dropping to $ρ= 0.22$ under satellite connections. This shows that K-AoI is not a simple transformation of AoI, but instead captures velocity-dependent degradation effects that time-only metrics cannot resolve. We further analyze AoI tail behavior using Ultra-Low AoI (ULAoI) and find that the commonly assumed Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD) model is rejected. This reflects the impact of deterministic forwarding and bounded jitter, which violate standard extreme-value assumptions. Overall, K-AoI provides a complementary and physically grounded synchronization metric, linking network delay to task-relevant spatial error in digital-twin teleoperation systems. The dataset and testbed software are publicly available at: https://github.com/luziyaotian/kaoi-testbed.
2610.26201.comment: 4 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Accepted as a short paper at IEEE Smart World Congress (SWC 2026)
2610.26201.tldr_en: Kinematic Age of Information (K-AoI), a spatio-temporal metric that weights AoI by instantaneous Cartesian velocity, translating temporal staleness into physically meaningful spatial divergence, provides a complementary and physically grounded synchronization metric in digital-twin teleoperation systems.

llm.title_ja: K-AoI：動的ネットワーク環境におけるデジタルツインベースの遠隔操作のための時空間同期指標
llm.tldr_ja: Kinematic Age of Information (K-AoI) は、時間的古さを物理的に意味のある空間的乖離に変換する、瞬間的なカルテシアン速度によってAoIに重み付けを行う時空間同期指標である。
llm.problem: 既存の同期指標は主に時間ベースであり、移動中の遅延情報の空間的影響を捉えきれていない。
llm.method: AoIに瞬間的なデカルト速度を重み付けし、時間的古さを空間的乖離に翻訳する時空間指標「K-AoI」を提案し、6自由度マニピュレータとUnityベースのツインからなるデジタルツイン遠隔操作テストベッドで評価した。
llm.result: K-AoIはAoIの単純な変換ではなく、時間のみの指標では解決できない速度依存の劣化効果を捉えることが示された。

2610.26174.title: PhantomTac: Hijacking Robotic Tactile Systems with Deploy-and-forget Tags
2610.26174.abstract: Tactile perception is crucial for precise robotic manipulation, providing an important foundation for dexterous, closed-loop force control. Among various tactile sensing techniques, magnetic tactile sensors stand out thanks to their fine-grained, three-dimensional force perception capability and strong robustness against visual occlusion. In this study, we discover a physical loophole called PhantomTac in magnetic tactile sensors. The attacker can alter the magnetic field, thus spoofing the force interpreted by magnetic tactile sensors. The attacker can stealthily deploy such an attack by simply attaching a thin (the thickness is around 0.5 mm), battery-free magnetic tag to the surface of an object. Hence, the attack tag can be easily concealed by a barcode sticker. Such an attack scheme is "deploy-and-forget" -- the attacker can deploy the tag and leave. When a robotic hand is picking up an object, it may severely damage the object. Specifically, spoofing the normal force can crush the object, whereas spoofing the shear force can lead to a loose grip, thus dropping the object. Compared with directly sabotaging the robotic hand, PhantomTac is much more concealed as the attacker does not need access to the device. We performed extensive reverse-engineering efforts to characterize the sensing mechanism of commercial-off-the-shelf tactile sensors and proposed a practical tag design. End-to-end evaluations conducted on real robots and robotic arms demonstrate that our attack can bypass existing anti-interference mechanisms and effectively hijack their closed-loop control processes, achieving an attack success rate exceeding 95% when the grasping-position offset is bounded within 8 mm. Finally, based on the limitations of existing anti-magnetic interference mechanisms, we propose a multimodal-consistency defense mechanism to mitigate such physical-layer security threats.
2610.26174.comment: Accepted at ACM CCS 2026. Project page: https://phantomtac.org

llm.title_ja: PhantomTac：デプロイ・アンド・フォゲット型タグによるロボット触覚システムのハイジャック
llm.tldr_ja: PhantomTacは、薄いバッテリー不要の磁気タグを対象物の表面に貼り付けるだけで磁気触覚センサーの力解釈を偽装し、ロボットの閉ループ制御プロセスを乗っ取る物理的脆弱性である。
llm.problem: 磁気触覚センサーは高精度な3次元力知覚とオクルージョンに対する頑健性を持つが、攻撃者が物理的な磁場を変化させて力をスプーフィングする脆弱性が存在する。
llm.method: 市販の触覚センサーのセンシングメカニズムをリバースエンジニアリングし、バーコードステッカーなどで容易に隠蔽できる薄さ約0.5mmのバッテリー不要な磁気タグを設計・実証した。
llm.result: ロボットアームを用いたエンドツーエンドの評価において、既存の干渉防止メカニズムを回避し、把持位置のオフセットが8mm以内の場合に95%を超える攻撃成功率で閉ループ制御をハイジャックできることを示した。

2610.26170.title: Data-Efficient Learning from Demonstration for Humanoid Robots via Feature-Level Perception and Prompt-Based Object Detection
2610.26170.abstract: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) allows robots to learn new skills from human examples; however, many vision-based methods require large datasets and resource-intensive end-to-end training. This paper introduces a data-efficient LfD framework for humanoid robots that learns manipulation skills from compact, task-specific features instead of raw images. The proposed approach integrates layered visual preprocessing, Kinect-based human joint estimation, prompt-based object detection, and depth information to extract human motion features and three-dimensional object locations from demonstration videos. These features are used to train a temporal deep learning model that predicts robot joint-angle trajectories for execution. The framework is implemented on a NAO humanoid robot, evaluated quantitatively in simulation, and demonstrated on physical hardware. In simulation, the robot achieves a 78% success rate on a pick-and-place task using only 16 demonstrations, which increases to 86% when trained with 100 demonstrations. The framework also achieves a 71% success rate on a pushing task using eight demonstrations, highlighting its effectiveness for data-efficient humanoid skill acquisition.
2610.26170.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Presented at IEEE ISAIA 2026
2610.26170.tldr_en: A data-efficient LfD framework for humanoid robots that learns manipulation skills from compact, task-specific features instead of raw images to extract human motion features and three-dimensional object locations from demonstration videos is introduced.

llm.title_ja: 特徴量レベルの知覚とプロンプトベースの物体検出によるヒューマノイドロボットのためのデータ効率の高いデモンストレーションからの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 生画像ではなくコンパクトでタスク特化型の特徴量を用いてデモンストレーションから操作スキルを学習する、ヒューマノイドロボット向けのデータ効率の高いLfDフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 多くのビジョンベースの手法は、大規模なデータセットとリソースを大量に消費するエンドツーエンドの訓練を必要とする。
llm.method: 階層的な視覚前処理、Kinectベースの人体関節推定、プロンプトベースの物体検出、深度情報を統合して特徴量を抽出し、ロボットの関節角度軌道を予測する時間的ディープラーニングモデルを訓練するフレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: NAOヒューマノイドロボットを用いたシミュレーションおよび実機実験において、わずか16デモンストレーションでピック＆プレースタスクで78%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーションからの学習

2610.26169.title: Compositional Humanoid Manipulation through Isomorphic Teleoperation and Independent Skill Routing
2610.26169.abstract: Humanoid manipulation requires reusable arm skills, yet demonstrating every possible skill combination is impractical. We present Humanoid Semantic Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Policy (HS-MoDP), which composes separately demonstrated arm skills through independent semantic routing over a shared expert pool. This design preserves arm-specific skill control while sharing action-generation parameters across arms. A semantic scheduler integrates the learned policy with an existing locomotion controller through alternating manipulation and repositioning stages, extending the effective workspace and enabling skill reuse across location changes. To acquire demonstrations of whole-body contact manipulation, we develop G1Exo, an isomorphic exoskeleton that provides direct joint-level control of arm configurations. Experiments on a Unitree G1 show stronger skill composition than the baselines. G1Exo enables more reliable contact teleoperation than end-effector VR-IK, and its demonstrations improve contact-skill learning across four policy architectures. For HS-MoDP, switching from VR-IK to G1Exo demonstrations raises full cabinet workflow success from 35% to 65%. All project hardware designs and source code will be released as open source after the review process.
2610.26169.tldr_en: G1Exo is developed, an isomorphic exoskeleton that provides direct joint-level control of arm configurations that enables more reliable contact teleoperation than end-effector VR-IK, and its demonstrations improve contact-skill learning across four policy architectures.

llm.title_ja: 同型遠隔操作と独立したスキルルーティングを通じた構成的ヒューマノイドマニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: HS-MoDPは、共有されたエキスパートプールに対する独立したセマンティックルーティングを通じて、個別に実演された腕のスキルを構成し、位置変更にわたるスキルの再利用を可能にする。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドのマニピュレーションには再利用可能な腕のスキルが必要だが、考えられるすべてのスキルの組み合わせを実演することは非実用的である。
llm.method: 腕の構成を直接関節レベルで制御する同型エクソスケルトン「G1Exo」を開発し、共有エキスパートプールに対する独立したセマンティックルーティングを通じて別々に実演された腕のスキルを構成する「HS-MoDP」を提案した。
llm.result: Unitree G1を用いた実験において、ベースラインよりも強力なスキル構成を示し、G1Exoのデモンストレーションによりキャビネット操作のワークフロー成功率が35%から65%に向上した。

2610.26106.title: A GPU-Resident Pipeline for Multi-Robot 3D Inspection with Limited Perception
2610.26106.abstract: We present a complete, GPU-resident pipeline for multi-robot 3D inspection of underwater structures. Given a triangle mesh and a fleet of $K$ robots, each carrying a short-range, limited field-of-view camera, the pipeline computes 6-DOF trajectories that jointly cover a target fraction of the surface while minimizing a linearly interpolated makespan/total-cost objective. The joint problem is NP-hard, so we decompose it into five core stages - candidate viewpoint generation, visibility computation, set cover, min-max vehicle routing solved as a mixed integer program (MIP) with lifted Miller-Tucker-Zemlin subtour elimination, and priority-based multi-agent path finding with continuous-time inter-robot conflict checking - flanked by mesh loading and surface sampling as preprocessing and by trajectory smoothing as postprocessing. Our contributions are: an end-to-end GPU-accelerated integration of the five stages, with its kernel design documented; a GPU batch adaptation of Lien's $\varepsilon$-visibility with four custom CUDA kernels; a $β$-aware per-vehicle tour upper bound derived from the interpolated objective, supplementing the Desrochers-Laporte coefficient lift with forbidden-pair cuts; a 4D space-time extension of Zhou and Zeng's GPU parallel-frontier A*; and an experimental evaluation on 14 meshes (up to $7.2$M faces) that ablates the routing cuts and the parallel-frontier search, audits collision freedom and waypoint attainment \emph{after} trajectory smoothing, and measures the end-to-end gap against analytical and LP-relaxation lower bounds. Code and raw results are publicly available.
2610.26106.tldr_en: This work presents a complete, GPU-resident pipeline for multi-robot 3D inspection of underwater structures that computes 6-DOF trajectories that jointly cover a target fraction of the surface while minimizing a linearly interpolated makespan/total-cost objective.

llm.title_ja: 限られた知覚を持つマルチロボット3D検査のためのGPU常駐型パイプライン
llm.tldr_ja: 水中構造物のマルチロボット3D検査に向けて、候補視点生成や視覚計算、セット被覆、MIPルーティング、多エージェント経路探索を統合した完全なGPU常駐型パイプラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 三角形メッシュと限られた視野を持つ複数の短距離カメラを用いた共同での6自由度軌道生成問題はNP困難である。
llm.method: 候補視点生成、視覚計算、セット被覆、混合整数計画法として解かれる最小最大車両ルーティング、および連続時間競合チェックを伴う優先度ベースの多エージェント経路探索の5つのステージをGPU上で完全に統合したパイプラインを構築した。
llm.result: 最大720万面の14のメッシュを用いた実験において、ルーティングカットや並列フロンティア探索の性能評価、衝突回避の検証が行われた。

2610.26091.title: GeoNaviDiff: Transferring Disentangled Semantic Controls to Diffusion Features via Local Riemannian Navigation
2610.26091.abstract: Disentangled real-image manipulation requires factor-specific semantic control while preserving image fidelity and non-target content. StyleSpace $S$ provides interpretable controls but is limited by GAN inversion, whereas diffusion models offer stronger image realization without an explicit factorized control basis. We introduce GeoNaviDiff, an unsupervised cross-space framework that transfers disentangled StyleSpace interventions to local Riemannian trajectories in diffusion $h$-space. GeoNaviDiff constructs reconstruction-decoupled supervision by extracting a spherical Log-map tangent from a matched StyleGAN reconstruction-edit pair and parallel-transporting it to the real-image diffusion state. A shared, factor-conditioned Navigator predicts this tangent at inference, while norm-preserving geodesic realization and source-anchored rollout stabilize the reverse process without edited references or factor-specific models. Experiments across multiple datasets show that GeoNaviDiff outperforms the compared methods in fidelity, factor selectivity, edit locality, and trajectory smoothness.

llm.title_ja: GeoNaviDiff：局所リーマンナビゲーションによる拡散特徴量への絡み合いのないセマンティック制御の転移
llm.tldr_ja: GeoNaviDiffは、絡み合いのないStyleSpaceの介入を拡散h空間の局所リーマン軌道に転移させる、教師なしのクロス空間フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 絡み合いのない実画像操作には因子特異的なセマンティック制御が必要だが、StyleSpaceはGAN反転に制限され、拡散モデルは明示的な因数分解された制御基底を持たない。
llm.method: StyleGANの再構成・編集ペアから球面Log写像接線を抽出し、それを実画像の拡散状態に平行移動させる、再構成分解された教師信号を構築するフレームワーク「GeoNaviDiff」を提案した。
llm.result: 複数のデータセットを用いた実験において、忠実度、因子選択性、編集の局所性、軌道の滑らかさの点で従来手法を上回った。

2610.27003.title: Replan for Error Recovery: Training Embodied VLMs through Verifiable Interaction with Action-Grouped Turn-GSPO
2610.27003.abstract: Embodied VLMs can execute increasingly complex manipulation tasks, yet execution errors can leave the environment in states that require replanning for recovery. Existing recovery methods either rely on inference-time mechanisms with fixed policies or learn from failure examples and reference corrections rather than verified action outcomes. To enable recovery learning through verifiable interaction, we introduce the Embodied Replanning for Recovery Environment (ERR-Env), which provides feedback on task progress and execution errors. We further construct ERR-Bench, a benchmark with held-out tasks spanning nominal, intermediate, and error states for evaluating recovery capability and execution reliability. We then propose Action-Grouped Turn-GSPO (AGT-GSPO), an online reinforcement learning method combining turn-level rewards for task progress and error states with action-grouped advantage estimation, and use it to train ERR-VLM, a compact 2B embodied VLM. Evaluation on ERR-Bench reveals a mismatch between task progress and execution reliability across diverse VLMs. AGT-GSPO improves ERR-VLM by 10.25 percentage points in Strict Success Rate for error-free completion and 22.95 percentage points in Recovery Rate, while ablations and zero-shot transfer further validate the effectiveness of our method.
2610.27003.tldr_en: This work introduces the Embodied Replanning for Recovery Environment (ERR-Env), which provides feedback on task progress and execution errors, and proposes Action-Grouped Turn-GSPO (AGT-GSPO), an online reinforcement learning method combining turn-level rewards for task progress and error states with action-grouped advantage estimation.

llm.title_ja: エラー回復のための再計画：検証可能なインタラクションとアクション単位のTurn-GSPOを通じた具現化VLMの訓練
llm.tldr_ja: ERR-Env環境とAction-Grouped Turn-GSPO（AGT-GSPO）オンライン強化学習手法を導入し、コンパクトな2B具現化VLMのタスク進行とエラー回復能力を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 既存の回復方法は、推論時の固定ポリシーに依存するか、検証された行動結果ではなく失敗例や修正から学習している。
llm.method: タスクの進捗と実行エラーに関するフィードバックを提供する「ERR-Env」、およびターンレベルの報酬とアクション単位の利得推定を組み合わせたオンライン強化学習手法「AGT-GSPO」を提案した。
llm.result: ERR-Benchでの評価において、AGT-GSPOはERR-VLMのエラーフリー完了の厳格な成功率を10.25ポイント、回復率を22.95ポイント向上させた。

2610.26043.title: OmniInteract: Towards Unified Whole-Body Interaction Control for Dual Humanoids
2610.26043.abstract: Physical interaction is a key capability for humanoid collaboration, requiring coordinated whole-body motion and precise contact. However, learning diverse dual-humanoid interactions faces two major challenges: (1) human-robot morphological differences disrupt contact interfaces and spatial relationships during retargeting, and (2) jointly learning motor skills and partner coordination makes it difficult to retain control fidelity as interaction diversity grows. In this paper, we propose OmniInteract to address these challenges through surface-aware modeling and scalable residual policy learning. First, we introduce Surface Contact-Aware Retargeting, which leverages dense human-robot surface correspondences to jointly retarget both humanoids, preserving explicit interaction contact interfaces and their near-field geometric context. Second, we propose a Scalable Flow-based Interaction Policy for partner-conditioned residual generation. It factorizes dual-humanoid control into a reusable motor foundation and interaction-specific adaptations: partner-aware experts learn corrections over a frozen whole-body motion prior, while conditional flow matching unifies them in a shared residual action space. This enables scalable skill consolidation while retaining pretrained motor capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OmniInteract improves retargeting fidelity and dual-humanoid coordination while better retaining interaction performance as skill diversity grows. Real-world deployment further demonstrates successful contact establishment, stable whole-body coordination, and recovery from external perturbations.
2610.26043.comment: 30 pages including appendix, 11 figures. Project page: https://calvinyhli.github.io/omniinteract.github.io/
2610.26043.tldr_en: OmniInteract improves retargeting fidelity and dual-humanoid coordination while better retaining interaction performance as skill diversity grows, and factorizes dual-humanoid control into a reusable motor foundation and interaction-specific adaptations.

llm.title_ja: OmniInteract：デュアルヒューマノイドに向けた統合された全身インタラクション制御の実現
llm.tldr_ja: OmniInteractは、表面接触を意識したリターゲットと拡張可能なフローベースのインタラクションポリシーを組み合わせることで、デュアルヒューマノイドの協調性と接触制御を向上させる。
llm.problem: 多様なデュアルヒューマノイドのインタラクション学習は、形態の違いによる接触インターフェースの混乱と、モータースキル・パートナー協調の同時学習による制御忠実度の低下という課題に直面している。
llm.method: 高密度な人間とロボットの表面対応関係を利用する「表面接触対応リターゲット」と、凍結された全身モーション事前分布上でパートナー対応の専門家が修正を学習する「拡張可能なフローベースインタラクションポリシー」を提案した。
llm.result: 実験において、スキル多様性の増加に伴うパフォーマンス維持やリターゲット忠実度の向上が示され、実機での安定した全身協調と外乱からの回復が実証された。
keywords_ja: 物理インタラクション

2610.26027.title: A Spiking Ring-Attractor Architecture for Representation and Control of Revolute Robot Joints
2610.26027.abstract: Robotic systems with revolute joints evolve on circular state spaces, yet most control architectures represent these states using Euclidean variables that ignore this underlying geometry. We propose a fully spiking neural control architecture in which ring attractors encode joint states, enforcing representations consistent with the topology of revolute systems. Homeostatic regulation computes goal-state mismatch directly over these distributed representations, and opponent gain-modulated populations convert this mismatch into controlled phase shifts of the activity bump, implementing set-point regulation as motion on the ring. We show that the bump dynamics follow an SO(2) geometry, and that gain asymmetries induce a signed phase velocity on the ring. To interface distributed activity with scalar regulation signals, we derive an analytic Fourier phase decoder and implement its signed components using push-pull spiking populations. For multi-joint systems, we demonstrate that local ring-based Fourier features compose into product representations that linearly decode SO(3) orientations through forward kinematics. Experiments in NEST validate the full SO(2) regulation mechanism and the spiking product-feature decoder for lift, pitch, and yaw. Robot experiments on a Tiago arm show that decoded ring dynamics generate joint velocity commands, producing directed motion with joint-dependent accuracy. Together, these results establish a neuromorphic control framework in which representation, regulation, and action are unified within a ring-attractor substrate aligned with the geometry of revolute systems.

llm.title_ja: 回転ロボット関節の表現と制御のためのスパイキング・リングアトラクタ・アーキテクチャ
llm.tldr_ja: リングアトラクタが関節状態をエンコードする完全なスパイキング神経制御アーキテクチャを提案し、回転システムの幾何学に一致した表現と制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 回転関節を持つロボットシステムは円形の状態空間で進化するが、ほとんどの制御アーキテクチャはこの基礎となる幾何学を無視したユークリッド変数を使用している。
llm.method: リングアトラクタが関節状態をエンコードし、ホームオスタティック調整によって目標状態の不一致を計算し、位相シフトに変換する完全なスパイキング神経制御アーキテクチャを提案した。
llm.result: NESTを用いたシミュレーションおよびTiagoアームを用いた実機実験において、デコードされたリングダイナミクスが関節速度コマンドを生成し、関節依存の精度で方向性のある動作を生み出すことが示された。
keywords_ja: スパイキングニューラルネットワーク

2610.26003.title: Curvature as a Baseline: Monocular Pose Measurement of Cylindrical Objects with Dual Colour Stripe Markers
2610.26003.abstract: Thin cylindrical objects offer little space for planar markers. We propose a dual-colour-stripe marker that uses the known curvature of an object to improve pose measurement with a single camera. The boundary between two colours provides a long centre line, while dots and printed edges supply features at different depths. We analyse how this depth separation improves the estimation of rotation about the cylinder axis, or roll. For a camera-facing marker at 15 cm, the Cramér-Rao lower bound on roll standard deviation is 2.00°for a flat marker, 0.38°for a single curved marker and 0.21°for a wrap-around marker. Monte Carlo roll RMS errors are within about 10% of the corresponding standard-deviation bounds. A first-order relation connects the sagitta of the curved marker to the roll sensitivity provided by a stereo baseline. The analytical and simulation results explain how curvature improves monocular measurement and provide a basis for designing marker geometry.

llm.title_ja: ベースラインとしての曲率：二色ストライプマーカーを用いた円筒形小物の単眼姿勢計測
llm.tldr_ja: 物体の既知の曲率を利用して単眼カメラでの姿勢計測を改善する二色ストライプマーカーを提案し、曲率がロール角の推定精度を向上させることを解析とシミュレーションで示した。
llm.problem: 薄い円筒形の物体には平面マーカーを貼るスペースがほとんどない。
llm.method: 物体の既知の曲率を利用して単眼カメラでの姿勢計測を改善する「二色ストライプマーカー」を提案し、Cramér-Rao下限やモンテカルロ法によるロールRMS誤差を分析した。
llm.result: 平坦なマーカーと比較して、単一の曲面マーカーやラップアラウンドマーカーを使用することでロール標準偏差の下限が大幅に改善され、曲率が単眼計測を向上させる仕組みが示された。
keywords_ja: コンピュータビジョン

2610.25988.title: SSIO: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry
2610.25988.abstract: Learning inertial odometry for a new platform usually requires ground-truth trajectories. We show that an inertial odometry model can instead be trained from scratch by a myopic teacher that integrates the IMU over each short window independently, a scheme we call integration self-supervision. Interestingly, although supervised only by short-window velocity changes, the student learns to directly predict velocity, and does so more accurately than its integration teacher. Pose graph distillation then refines the model with sequence-consistent targets from a pose graph over many windows. Training on a new platform therefore no longer requires collecting ground-truth trajectories, but only calibrating the IMU and recording data during normal operation. Across six datasets spanning pedestrians, drones, quadrupeds, and a humanoid, the same recipe with no velocity or position labels trains models that come within 0.07~m/s average velocity error of a same-architecture supervised baseline.
2610.25988.tldr_en: It is shown that an inertial odometry model can be trained from scratch by a myopic teacher that integrates the IMU over each short window independently, a scheme the authors call integration self-supervision, and although supervised only by short-window velocity changes, the student learns to directly predict velocity, and does so more accurately than its integration teacher.

llm.title_ja: SSIO：自己教師あり慣性オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 各短ウィンドウ上でIMUを独立して統合する近視眼的な教師によって慣性オドメトリモデルをゼロから訓練できる「統合自己教師あり学習」手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 新しいプラットフォーム向けの慣性オドメトリの学習には通常、グランドトュース軌道が必要となる。
llm.method: 各短ウィンドウ上でIMUを独立して統合する近視眼的な教師によってモデルをゼロから訓練する「統合自己教師あり学習（SSIO）」を提案し、ポーズグラフ蒸留によりシーケンス全体の一貫したターゲットでモデルを洗練させた。
llm.result: 歩行者、ドローン、四足歩行、ヒューマノイドにわたる6つのデータセットにおいて、速度や位置のラベルなしで、教師ありベースラインと平均速度誤差0.07 m/s以内のモデルを訓練できることが示された。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2610.25981.title: FR-VLA: Implicit Force Reasoning VLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation
2610.25981.abstract: Integrating force awareness into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models involves not merely encoding wrench measurements as an additional modality, but determining when and how strongly physical interaction should influence robot action generation. Existing VLAs that use force typically inject it through a fixed pathway, without explicitly determining when it is relevant to the current action. This calls for an intermediate force relevance mechanism inside the VLA, in which visual-language context estimates the relevance of physical feedback to the current task before force enters the action pathway. FR-VLA addresses this gap with a Vision-Language Force-Reasoning Model that uses learnable force query tokens to derive a force admission signal grounded in visual-language context, and uses this signal to modulate an external tokenized force pathway for action generation. In real-world experiments on five contact-rich tasks across two robotic platforms, FR-VLA achieves the highest mean success rate over six evaluated stages, and trajectory visualizations show that its force admission varies with the interaction phase.
2610.25981.tldr_en: FR-VLA is a Vision-Language Force-Reasoning Model that uses learnable force query tokens to derive a force admission signal grounded in visual-language context, and uses this signal to modulate an external tokenized force pathway for action generation.

llm.title_ja: FR-VLA：接触リッチなマニピュレーションのための暗黙的力推論VLA
llm.tldr_ja: FR-VLAは、学習可能な力クエリトークンを使用して視覚・言語コンテキストに根ざした力受入信号を導出し、それを用いて行動生成のための外部トークン化された力経路を変調するビジョン・言語・力推論モデルである。
llm.problem: VLAモデルに力認識を統合する際、単にレンチ測定値をモダリティとして追加するだけでなく、いつ、どの程度物理的インタラクションが行動生成に影響を与えるべきかを決定する必要があるが、既存手法は固定的な経路を使用している。
llm.method: 学習可能な力クエリトークンを用いて視覚・言語コンテキストに基づいた力受入信号を導出し、トークン化された力経路を変調して行動を生成する「FR-VLA」を提案した。
llm.result: 2つのロボットプラットフォームにおける5つの接触リッチなタスクの実機実験において、6つの評価ステージ全体で最も高い平均成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 接触リッチマニピュレーション

2610.25967.title: Reconstruction and Discrete-Event Simulation Assessment of an Analytical
2610.25967.abstract: This article presents an analytical-DES benchmark for intra-aisle robotic picking in automated warehousing. The investigated cycle combines horizontal shuttle travel, tote handling and item picking at storage locations. Simulation results are compared with the analytical formulation of Lerher et al. under the same rack geometry, shuttle-motion, handling and picking conditions, and the same definitions of cycle time and derived item throughput. Reproducing the published analytical tables requires the distance interpretation dES = 1.5 m and dTB = 0 m. The analytical-DES benchmark comprises 180 scenarios formed from three rack lengths, two paired motion profiles and n = 1 to 30 visited picking locations, with ten simulation replications per scenario. The six n = 1 cases are reported separately because no travel-between component is present. Across the remaining 174 scenarios, the mean absolute relative cycle-time discrepancy is 0.8655%, the median is 0.6758%, and the maximum is 7.0370%. The mean absolute error is 2.411 s and the RMSE is 2.744 s. The simulated scenario-mean cycle time is below the analytical value in all 174 principal scenarios. The results therefore show close numerical correspondence under the tested conditions, but not exact agreement, formal statistical equivalence, or validation against an operating warehouse.

llm.title_ja: 自動倉庫における通路内ロボットピッキングのための解析的・離散事象シミュレーション評価の再構築
llm.tldr_ja: 自動倉庫の通路内ロボットピッキングにおける水平シャトル移動、トート処理、アイテムピッキングを組み合わせたサイクルについて、解析的定式化と離散事象シミュレーション（DES）の比較評価を行った。
llm.problem: 自動倉庫における解析モデルとシミュレーション結果の間で、正確な数値的対応や厳密な統計的同等性が検証されている必要がある。
llm.method: ラックの長さ、移動プロファイル、訪問するピッキングロケーションの数からなる180のシナリオを構築し、シミュレーション結果とLerherらの解析的定式化を比較した。
llm.result: 174の主要シナリオにおいて、サイクルタイムの平均絶対相対誤差は0.8655%、中央値は0.6758%、最大は7.0370%であり、テスト条件下で密接な数値的対応を示す一方で完全な一致ではないことが分かった。
keywords_ja: 離散事象シミュレーション

2610.25962.title: SkateNav: Learning Energy-Efficient Navigation through Adaptive Skating on Passive-Wheel Quadrupedal Robots
2610.25962.abstract: Passive-wheel quadrupedal robots offer energy-efficient locomotion through leg-driven propulsion and momentum-driven gliding. However, navigation requires coordinating steering with intermittent propulsion and adapting push-glide timing to task demands. Velocity-tracking objectives may suppress the speed variations inherent in skating, discouraging efficient gliding. To address these challenges, we propose SkateNav, a unified skating-navigation framework based on reinforcement learning. A time-budgeted goal-reaching objective allows the policy to jointly learn steering, propulsion, and their temporal allocation. An adaptive skating cycle structures gliding, pushing, and recovery, while frequency modulation at every control step adjusts phase durations to navigation demands. Simulation experiments demonstrate higher average success rates and lower cost of transport than the evaluated planner-controller baselines, with ablations confirming the contributions of cycle structure and frequency adaptation. Real-world experiments demonstrate zero-shot transfer from simulation to a passive-wheel Mini Cheetah across cluttered indoor spaces, slopes, and paved outdoor surfaces. Supplementary videos are available on the project page: https://ktw1404.github.io/SkateNav/
2610.25962.comment: 8 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables. Project page: https://ktw1404.github.io/SkateNav/

llm.title_ja: SkateNav：受動車輪付き四足歩行ロボットにおける適応型スケーティングを通じたエネルギー効率の高いナビゲーションの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 強化学習に基づく統合スケーティング・ナビゲーションフレームワーク「SkateNav」を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機のMini Cheetahにおいてゼロショットでの省電力な移動を実現した。
llm.problem: 速度追従目的はスケーティング特有の速度変動を抑制し、効率的な滑走を妨げるという課題がある。
llm.method: 時間予算付きの目標到達目的を用いて、操舵、推進、およびその時間配分を強化学習で共同学習する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験において、ベースラインと比較して高い成功率と低い輸送コストを達成した。
keywords_ja: 省電力ナビゲーション

2610.25961.title: PaceVLA: Adaptive Temporal Action Quantization in Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.25961.abstract: Fast and reliable manipulation is crucial for practical robot deployment. Although Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently shown remarkable progress as generalist robot policies, their execution often remains temporally inefficient. A key source of this inefficiency is that policies learn fine-grained temporal patterns from teleoperated demonstrations, requiring many low-level action steps. Temporal action quantization offers a simple way to accelerate execution by aggregating consecutive low-level actions into temporally coarser actions. However, applying action quantization without considering when fine-grained control is required introduces a speed-accuracy trade-off: accelerated actions may efficiently reduce redundant steps in some phases, while discarding critical motion details in precision-sensitive interactions. To address this, we propose PaceVLA, a unified framework for adaptive temporal execution in VLAs that integrates two coupled components: (1) mode-specific action decoders built on a shared action expert, supporting multiple temporal granularities and prediction horizons, and (2) a quantizability-guided mode selection scheme which decides whether coarse execution is appropriate, and a context-conditioned router that selects an execution mode at each inference step. Experiments across three multi-task simulation benchmarks and six real-world tasks show that PaceVLA improves execution efficiency while maintaining task success rate across multiple embodiments, including long-horizon and dexterous manipulation.
2610.25961.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, 10 tables. Project page: https://pacevla.github.io/
2610.25961.tldr_en: PaceVLA is proposed, a unified framework for adaptive temporal execution in VLAs that integrates two coupled components: mode-specific action decoders built on a shared action expert, supporting multiple temporal granularities and prediction horizons, and a quantizability-guided mode selection scheme which decides whether coarse execution is appropriate.

llm.title_ja: PaceVLA：ビジョン・言語・行動モデルにおける適応的時間行動量子化
llm.tldr_ja: PaceVLAは、共有アクションエキスパートに基づくモード特異的アクションデコーダーと量子化ガイド付きモード選択スキームを統合し、タスク成功率を維持しながら実行効率を向上させるVLAのフレームワークである。
llm.problem: きめ細かな時間的パターンの学習に起因するVLAモデルの時間的な非効率さと、一様な行動量子化による速度・精度のトレードオフ。
llm.method: 複数の時間的粒度をサポートするモード特異的アクションデコーダーと、コンテキスト条件付きルーターによる量子化ガイド付きモード選択を統合する。
llm.result: 3つのマルチタスクシミュレーションベンチマークおよび6つの実世界タスクにおいて、タスク成功率を維持しつつ実行効率が向上した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.25959.title: EmbodiedWorld-200K: Toward Embodied World Agents via Embodied-Planning Dataset and Interactive World Models
2610.25959.abstract: Building embodied agents that can perceive, reason, and act across diverse 3D worlds is a central research direction toward artificial general intelligence. Yet most existing work remains confined to specific tasks in a single scene and transfers poorly to new environments, leaving general embodied agents for open-world settings under-explored. We refer to such agents as Embodied World Agents (EWAs), whose defining property is the ability to understand diverse visual environments and execute general actions in open-world conditions. To advance EWA research, we study open-world embodied navigation-planning and release EmbodiedWorld-200K, a large-scale dataset of over 200K samples spanning diverse scenes. Each example is equipped with multi-level annotations, ranging from low-level camera-motion trajectories to high-level semantic instructions. The dataset also provides unified evaluation splits and task-specific metrics, supporting offline pretraining and fair evaluation of EWAs. Beyond offline supervision, a defining characteristic of an EWA is its interaction with the environment; training solely on offline data is therefore insufficient, especially for generalizing to scenes not covered in the training distribution. Building dedicated real interactive environments, however, is often prohibitively expensive. To address this, we propose a novel training scheme that employs a video world model as a low-cost environment proxy and performs interactive reinforcement-learning (RL) post-training of the EWA within it. Empirically, pretraining on EmbodiedWorld-200K substantially improves the open-world embodied planning ability of the EWA, and further RL post-training inside a world model yields clear gains on out-of-distribution scenes. The dataset, baseline checkpoints, and training and evaluation code are available at https://xiaokunfeng.github.io/EmbodiedWorld-200K/.
2610.25959.tldr_en: A novel training scheme is proposed that employs a video world model as a low-cost environment proxy and performs interactive reinforcement-learning post-training of the EWA within it, and performs interactive reinforcement-learning post-training of the EWA within it.

llm.title_ja: EmbodiedWorld-200K：体現型プランニングデータセットとインタラクティブ世界モデルを通じた体現型ワールドエージェントに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ世界モデルを低コストの環境プロキシとして用いてインタラクティブな強化学習の事後訓練を行うことで、オープンワールドでの体現型計画能力を向上させる新しい訓練スキームを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の体現型エージェントは特定の単一シーンに留まりがちで、オープンワールドの新しい環境への汎化が不十分である。
llm.method: 20K以上のサンプルを含む大規模データセットEmbodiedWorld-200Kによる事前学習と、ビデオ世界モデルを用いたインタラクティブな強化学習の事後訓練を行う。
llm.result: EmbodiedWorld-200Kでの事前学習と世界モデル内での強化学習事後訓練により、分布外のシーンに対する体現型プランニング能力が大幅に向上した。

2610.25946.title: Policy Search in Code Space for Multi-Agent Pathfinding
2610.25946.abstract: Developing coordination policies for complex multi-agent systems relies on either labor-intensive algorithm design or opaque task-specific reinforcement learning. With recent advances in autonomous coding agents, we show that policy search directly in code space offers a compelling third path that combines automated optimization with explicit interpretability. We investigate a human-directed workflow in which coding agents iteratively propose, implement, evaluate, diagnose, and eventually refine algorithms guided by simulation feedback and explicit correctness verification. We conducted two case studies and found that this workflow robustly outperformed any manually engineered solutions. On a challenging map in the 2024 League of Robot Runners competition, a two-day search discovered a policy that exceeds the stronger locally reproduced competition entry by 35.0% on the densest instance and generalizes to unseen map instances. In simulated real-world warehouses with irregular lanes, continuous robot geometry, and asynchronous motion, a week-long search discovered an entirely new class of multi-agent pathfinding algorithm that outperforms a calibrated proprietary solution in throughput by 58.9%. Under stated assumptions, we further prove that the new algorithm is collision-free and completes, in finite time, every accepted goal that is not withdrawn or replaced. Together, the studies show that policy search in code space powered by state-of-the-art coding agents offers a highly competitive path to building real engineering solutions that are both effective and analytically tractable.
2610.25946.tldr_en: This work investigates a human-directed workflow in which coding agents iteratively propose, implement, evaluate, diagnose, and eventually refine algorithms guided by simulation feedback and explicit correctness verification and shows that this workflow robustly outperformed any manually engineered solutions.

llm.title_ja: マルチエージェント経路探索のためのコード空間におけるポリシー探索
llm.tldr_ja: 自動化された最適化と明示的な解釈可能性を組み合わせるため、最先端のコーディングエージェントを活用してコード空間で直接ポリシー探索を行う人間誘導型ワークフローを調査し、手動設計を凌駕することを示した。
llm.problem: 複雑なマルチエージェントシステムの協調ポリシー開発は、労力のかかるアルゴリズム設計か不透明なタスク特化型強化学習に依存している。
llm.method: コーディングエージェントがシミュレーションフィードバックと正確性検証に導かれてアルゴリズムを反復的に提案・評価・洗練する人間誘導型ワークフローを用いる。
llm.result: 競技のベストエントリや従来型プロプライエタリソリューションをスループットや汎化性能で大きく上回るアルゴリズムを発見した。

2610.25930.title: TESS: LLM-guided Translation, Exploration, Simulation, and Search for Embodied Task Planning
2610.25930.abstract: In this work we focus on the problem of embodied task planning, which requires an agent to accomplish a complex task by separating it into atomic actions. Recent studies have developed LLM-based methods to address this problem. However, the executability and correctness of the generated plans remain suboptimal in complex environments and tasks. On the other hand, classical search algorithms have the potential to solve the planning problems perfectly, yet they require fully observable environments, known state transitions and goal state, which are often unattainable in general task domains. Therefore, we propose to implement an LLM-guided search algorithm that makes the search process possible and efficient by incorporating LLMs' commonsense knowledge. Our method leverages LLMs to (1) translate natural language instructions into formatted goal conditions, (2) facilitate efficient exploration in partially observable environments, (3) implement a rule-based world simulator, and (4) prune the space of candidate actions to improve search efficiency. Experimental results on VirtualHome and ALFWorld demonstrate its superior performance.
2610.25930.comment: EMNLP 2026 findings. Code will be released at https://github.com/woyut/TESS_EMNLP26
2610.25930.tldr_en: This work proposes to implement an LLM-guided search algorithm that makes the search process possible and efficient by incorporating LLM'commonsense knowledge, and leverages LLMs to translate natural language instructions into formatted goal conditions and facilitate efficient exploration in partially observable environments.
2610.25930.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

badges.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natur 2026

llm.title_ja: TESS：体現型タスク計画のためのLLM誘導型翻訳、探索、シミュレーション、探索
llm.tldr_ja: LLMの常識的知識を組み込むことで探索プロセスを可能かつ効率的にするLLM誘導型探索アルゴリズムを提案し、VirtualHomeやALFWorldでの優れた性能を示した。
llm.problem: 複雑な環境においてLLMベースの計画手法の生成されたプランの実行可能性や正確性が最適ではないこと、また古典的探索が完全観測等を要求するため一般ドメインで困難であること。
llm.method: LLMを利用して自然言語指示を目標条件に翻訳し、部分観測環境での探索を促進し、ルールベースの世界シミュレータを実装し、候補行動空間を枝刈りする。
llm.result: VirtualHomeおよびALFWorldを用いた実験により、優れた性能を発揮することが実証された。

2610.25927.title: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
2610.25927.abstract: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. We propose CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding. Given a sequence of cached per-frame features from the VLM backbone, CondenseVLA distills observation history into a fixed set of slot tokens using learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention. Simple auxiliary regularization penalizes overlap among slot attention maps and decorrelates slot embeddings, encouraging complementary attention and reducing slot redundancy. Across the evaluated tasks, CondenseVLA improves Simpler-WidowX success from 58.7% to 69.8% (+11.1 percentage points), achieves 97.2% on LIBERO, and reaches 52.8% on real-world tasks. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA
2610.25927.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 39 pages, including supplementary material and the NeurIPS paper checklist. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA
2610.25927.tldr_en: CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding, supports selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window.

llm.title_ja: CondenseVLA：効率的なマルチフレームVLAのための学習可能な履歴凝縮
llm.tldr_ja: CondenseVLAは、学習可能なデコーダ側の履歴凝縮モジュールを備えたマルチフレームVLAポリシーであり、短期間の視覚的文脈を利用して計算コストを抑えつつタスク性能を向上させる。
llm.problem: 単一フレームでは曖昧な短期的手掛かりを処理するために単に履歴ウィンドウを拡大すると、膨大な冗長性と柔軟性のないサンプリングにより計算コストが高くなる。
llm.method: VLMバックボーンからのキャッシュされた特徴のシーケンスを、学習可能なクエリとマルチヘッドクロスアテンションを用いてスロットトークンに蒸留する。
llm.result: Simpler-WidowX、LIBERO、実世界タスクにおいて成功率が大幅に向上した。
llm.limitation: より困難なマルチ観測タスクにおいて、有限な履歴ウィンドウの限界が露呈した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.25874.title: Vision-Language-Delta-Action: Learning Compact Deltas as Actionable Transition Interfaces for Robotic Manipulation
2610.25874.abstract: Robotic manipulation is not merely observation-to-action generation, but the realization of task-specified state changes in the physical world. Existing vision-language-action (VLA) methods directly learn observation-to-action mappings, imposing a substantial learning burden due to the gap between semantic understanding and action execution. Although world-action models (WAMs) improve control through future prediction, modeling complete future states wastes capacity on static appearance and action-irrelevant changes. We propose Vision-Language-Delta-Action (VLDA), a paradigm that reformulates full future prediction as compact actionable transition modeling. Its core is a compact Delta variable that captures latent world-state changes, serving as an interface between vision-language understanding and action generation. VLDA learns Delta through a unified objective composed of the Local Transition Filter (LT-Filter) and Global Transition Anchor (GT-Anchor). LT-Filter captures task-relevant manipulation-centric changes while suppressing static reconstruction biases. GT-Anchor provides coarse future-level regularization to preserve the overall direction of state changes. Delta-Driven Action Refinement (DDAR) further grounds Delta in the action manifold and injects it as a structured seed to guide action denoising. We implement VLDA within LoongForge, an open-source training framework for large-scale foundation and embodied models, using its modular and distributed infrastructure for unified two-stage optimization. Experiments show that VLDA improves long-horizon consistency, robustness, and generalization, validating actionable Delta as an alternative to direct action prediction and full future-state modeling.
2610.25874.tldr_en: Experiments show that VLDA improves long-horizon consistency, robustness, and generalization, validating actionable Delta as an alternative to direct action prediction and full future-state modeling.
2610.25874.hf_summary_en: VLDA reformulates robotic control as compact transition modeling via a Delta variable that bridges vision-language understanding and action generation, improving long-horizon consistency and generalization.

llm.title_ja: Vision-Language-Delta-Action：ロボット操作のための行動可能な移行インターフェースとしてのコンパクトなデルタの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 完全な将来予測をコンパクトな行動可能移行モデリングに再定義するVLDAパラダイムを提案し、長期の一貫性、ロバスト性、汎化性能を向上させることを示した。
llm.problem: 直接的な行動予測は大きな学習負担を強め、世界・行動モデルにおける完全な将来状態のモデリングは静的な外見や無関係な変化に容量を浪費する。
llm.method: 潜在的な世界状態の変化を捉えるコンパクトなDelta変数を導入し、ローカル移行フィルタとグローバル移行アンカーによる統一目的で学習する。
llm.result: VLDAにより、長期の一貫性、ロバスト性、汎化性能が向上することが実験で示された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動

2610.25869.title: AeroIntent: A Synchronized Multimodal Benchmark for UAV Mission Intent Recognition
2610.25869.abstract: Reliable recognition of mission-level UAV intent from multimodal observations is essential for low-altitude airspace surveillance and security. Existing multimodal UAV datasets primarily support detection, tracking, and localization, leaving limited support for evaluating mission-intent recognition across held-out trajectory programs and incomplete radar histories. We introduce AeroIntent, a simulation-based benchmark comprising 990 synchronized multimodal sequences generated by 22 trajectory programs across five mission intents. The benchmark provides radar, RGB, infrared, and depth observations, together with program-disjoint, radar-gap, and observation-prefix evaluation protocols. Building on this benchmark, we propose AeroMIR, a structured Multimodal Intent Reasoner that integrates radar trajectories, derived behavioral features, selected visual evidence, and task knowledge for candidate-based UAV intent recognition. Under a strict program-disjoint protocol evaluating unseen tactical realizations, AeroMIR achieves a mean accuracy of 71.56% and a mean Macro-F1 of 69.84% across three seeds, outperforming the strongest trajectory-only baseline by 7.79 Macro-F1 points and a conventional radar-RGB late-fusion baseline by 19.32 points. AeroMIR also demonstrates strong performance under controlled radar gaps and early intent recognition settings. AeroIntent and AeroMIR provide a reproducible foundation for multimodal UAV intent recognition. The benchmark is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/AeroIntent

llm.title_ja: AeroIntent：UAVミッション意図認識のための同期型マルチモーダルベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: UAVのミッション意図認識を評価するためのシミュレーションベースのマルチモーダルベンチマーク「AeroIntent」と、それに基づく構造化マルチモーダル意図推論器「AeroMIR」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のマルチモーダルUAVデータセットは検出や追跡を主にサポートしており、非表示の軌跡プログラムや不完全なレーダー履歴にわたるミッション意図認識の評価への対応が限られている。
llm.method: 5つのミッション意図と22の軌跡プログラムによる990の同期マルチモーダルシーケンスを生成し、レーダー軌跡や視覚的証拠を統合するAeroMIRを構築する。
llm.result: 厳格なプログラム非依存プロトコルにおいて、AeroMIRは従来のベースラインを大きく上回る平均精度とMacro-F1を達成した。

2610.25840.title: OV-PEAR: Observation-Verified Pose-Scale Estimation and Reconstruction for Unknown Industrial Manipulation Objects
2610.25840.abstract: Fine industrial robotic manipulation requires 6D pose, scale, and an operation-ready 3D model. Existing industrial pose estimation relies on CAD models, object-specific training data, or stable workcells, limiting use with unseen objects; zero-shot methods suffer from single-view occlusion, generative bias, and scale uncertainty. We present OV-PEAR, an observation-verified framework for 3D reconstruction and pose-scale estimation of unknown industrial objects. Its three-stage object-centric pipeline: (1) segments RGB-D instances and generates object-level 3D hypotheses; (2) anchors them to the robot frame via appearance-aware view retrieval, explicit scale search, and visibility-sensitive registration; (3) back-projects multi-view RGB-D evidence into the object-canonical frame to verify voxel occupancy, suppress hallucinations, and produce reusable trusted object models. On BOP-Industrial, OV-PEAR achieves 0.657 average AR and improves pose and voxel-level geometric consistency in real scenes; real-robot connector assembly reaches 99.67% grasp and 84.00% assembly success. The model library and pose-scale log enable short-term object-level state maintenance at 0.02 ms/frame.
2610.25840.tldr_en: OV-PEAR is presented, an observation-verified framework for 3D reconstruction and pose-scale estimation of unknown industrial objects and back-projects multi-view RGB-D evidence into the object-canonical frame to verify voxel occupancy, suppress hallucinations, and produce reusable trusted object models.

llm.title_ja: OV-PEAR：未知の産業用操作対象物に対する観測検証済み姿勢・スケール推定と再構築
llm.tldr_ja: OV-PEARは、RGB-Dインスタンスのセグメンテーション、ビュー取得によるロボットフレームへのアンカリング、オブジェクト正準フレームへのマルチビュー逆投影を通じて未知の工業用オブジェクトの3D再構築と姿勢・スケール推定を行うフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存の産業用姿勢推定はCADモデル等に依存しており未見のオブジェクトに限界があり、ゼロショット手法は単一視点オクルージョンや生成バイアス、スケール不確実性に悩まされる。
llm.method: RGB-Dインスタンスのセグメンテーション、外観を考慮したビュー取得・スケール探索によるアンカリング、およびマルチビュー証拠の逆投影によるボクセル占有の検証を行う。
llm.result: BOP-Industrialにおいて平均0.657 ARを達成し、実環境での幾何学的一貫性を改善、実ロボットでのコネクタ組み立てで高成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 産業用マニピュレーション

2610.25785.title: Long-Horizon Multi-Object Rearrangement via Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions
2610.25785.abstract: Despite recent advances in policy learning, long-horizon manipulation remains difficult because learned policies must avoid compounding errors while preserving future feasibility. While search-based planning can explicitly reason over such future consequences, it quickly becomes expensive in high-dimensional continuous action spaces. This raises a central question: how can long-horizon reasoning from search be transferred into policies in continuous action spaces? To this end, we propose DISCO: Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions. DISCO uses progressive-widening MCTS in physics simulation to generate long-horizon plans. During search, a learned policy proposes continuous actions, while a learned value function scores actions by their expected progress toward task completion. Using GPU-parallelized simulation, DISCO periodically distills MCTS-generated plans into the policy-value model, improving the action proposals and value estimates used in subsequent searches. Finally, the learned policy-value model can be directly deployed without the need for simulator-based search at test time. Across simulated and real-world rearrangement tasks, DISCO outperforms behavior cloning, reinforcement learning, and search-based baselines.
2610.25785.comment: Accepted at CoRL 2026 (Oral). Project page: https://distilled-search.github.io
2610.25785.tldr_en: Across simulated and real-world rearrangement tasks, DISCO outperforms behavior cloning, reinforcement learning, and search-based baselines.

llm.title_ja: 連続行動に対する蒸留木探索を通じた長期マルチオブジェクト再配置
llm.tldr_ja: 物理シミュレーションにおけるプログレッシブ・ワイドニングMCTSを用いて長期計画を生成し、それをポリシー・バリューモデルに蒸留するDISCOを提案し、行動クローニングや強化学習のベースラインを上回った。
llm.problem: 学習済みポリシーが誤りの蓄積を避けつつ将来の実行可能性を維持しなければならないため、長期マニピュレーションは困難であり、探索ベースの計画は高次元連続行動空間で非常に高コストになる。
llm.method: GPU並列シミュレーションを用いてMCTSプランをポリシー・バリューモデルに定期的に蒸留するDISCO（Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions）を提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界の再配置タスクにおいて、行動クローニングや強化学習ベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2610.25763.title: TrajWAM: An Efficient Trajectory-Guided World Action Model for Dynamic Robotic Manipulation
2610.25763.abstract: Dynamic object manipulation requires robots to anticipate target motion while replanning fast enough to avoid executing outdated actions. Existing approaches either rely on fast reactive control without an explicit future target state or encode anticipated motion only implicitly. World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising alternative by coupling future visual prediction with action generation, but scene-level video objectives may underrepresent target dynamics that are critical for manipulation, while iterative video-action denoising introduces substantial latency. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-guided world action model for efficient dynamic robotic manipulation. Our key insight is to explicitly ground future visual imagination in predicted target-object motion and use the resulting future representation to condition action generation, while preserving this anticipation pathway after acceleration. Given a short history of object masks, a history-conditioned motion predictor forecasts future masks encoding the target object's trajectory. A lightweight Trajectory ControlNet then steers a pretrained video model toward trajectory-consistent futures. The resulting future representation conditions an action expert to predict executable action chunks. To enable one-step inference without breaking this interface, we introduce a decoupled distillation scheme that combines distribution matching for the video backbone, Trajectory ControlNet realignment, and action rollout distillation to support accurate one-step action prediction conditioned on the compressed future representation. Comprehensive evaluations in simulation and the real world show that TrajWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on dynamic object manipulation tasks while enabling efficient one-step video-action inference. Project page: https://kevingeng3.github.io/TrajWAM/.
2610.25763.tldr_en: Comprehensive evaluations in simulation and the real world show that TrajWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on dynamic object manipulation tasks while enabling efficient one-step video-action inference.

llm.title_ja: TrajWAM：動的ロボット操作のための効率的な軌跡誘導型世界行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の視覚的想像を予測されたターゲット物体の動きに明示的にグラウンドし、行動生成の条件付けに用いることで、動的オブジェクト操作において高効率な1ステップ推論を実現するTrajWAMを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存手法は将来のターゲット状態なしのリアクティブ制御に頼るか、動的予測が暗黙的であり、世界行動モデルのシーンレベルビデオ目的は操作に重要なターゲットダイナミクスを十分に表現できない。
llm.method: オブジェクトマスクから将来のマスクを予測する履歴条件付きモーション予測器と、軽量な Trajectory ControlNet により事前学習済みビデオモデルを誘導し、デカップルド蒸留によって1ステップ行動予測を実現する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界における動的オブジェクト操作タスクで最先端の性能を達成し、効率的な1ステップビデオ行動推論が可能であることを示した。
keywords_ja: 動的マニピュレーション

2610.25736.title: Learning from Fleet Experience: Collective Experience Learning Across 96 Robots
