2610.25736.abstract: Robot deployment generates experience that can support policy improvement, but continued reliance on expert corrective actions makes learning difficult to scale across growing fleets. We propose learning from fleet experience: using deployed robots' own executions as a source of supervision for further policy improvement. We call this paradigm Collective Experience Learning (CEL), in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet. Following expert-supervised initialization, we realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT). FERT uses failure contexts to retrieve relevant segments from successful trajectories and prioritizes their recorded actions for supervised updates, without collecting additional expert demonstrations or corrective actions. Operators provide binary episode-outcome labels and environment resets. A fault-tolerant asynchronous training system (FATS) coordinates robot execution, cloud inference and policy optimization despite local interruptions. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and generally improve performance across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots raises success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment.
2610.25736.tldr_en: Results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment, in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet.
2610.25736.hf_summary_en: Robots share execution experience across fleets to improve policies via failure-guided retrieval and asynchronous training, achieving high success without extra expert corrections.

llm.title_ja: フリート経験からの学習：96台のロボットにわたる集合経験学習
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット群が自身の実行経験をプールして共有ポリシーを更新する集合経験学習（CEL）を提案し、専門家の追加デモンストレーションなしでポリシーの信頼性を高めることを実証した。
llm.problem: ロボットの展開により得られる経験をポリシー改善に活用できるが、専門家の修正行動への継続的依存により、成長するフリート全体でのスケーリングが困難である。
llm.method: 失敗コンテキストを使用して成功した軌跡から関連セグメントを検索し、教師あり更新用の行動を優先順位付けする失敗誘導経験検索ファインチューニング（FERT）を用いる。
llm.result: 5つの実世界マニピュレーションタスクにおいて93.3〜99.2%の成功率を達成し、96台のロボットを用いた学習により多段階の携帯電話包装タスクの成功率が向上した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.25734.title: Think Densely, Act Sparsely: Latent Expert Cognitive Chains for Vision-Language-Action Autonomous Driving
2610.25734.abstract: Autonomous driving fundamentally demands dense understanding of visual, semantic, and geometric information, yet existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are typically trained with sparse supervision such as language instructions or trajectory signals. This direct mapping from dense visual observations to sparse representations forces the model to compress or even discard critical scene information essential for safe driving. We argue that this limitation does not stem from insufficient model capacity, but from the lack of explicit mechanisms that encourage the formation of dense world representations in the latent space. In this spirit, we propose a novel paradigm for driving intelligence, Think Densely, Act Sparsely, and instantiate it with an efficient and interpretable framework, LECDrive (Latent Expert Cognitive Chains for Vision-Language-Action autonomous Driving). The core idea is to mimic the hierarchical perception process of humans by embedding a progressive chain of latent expert cognition within the VLA model. Concretely, we inject a compact set of task-specific latent tokens as carriers, enabling the model to internalize dense knowledge from foundational vision models, including visual representations (DINOv3), semantic structures (SAM3), and spatial geometry (DepthAnything3), while maintaining efficient inference. This interdependent cognitive chain follows a curriculum learning principle, where supervision is progressively structured from representation to semantics and geometry. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LECDrive consistently improves the performance of base VLMs across multiple autonomous driving benchmarks, covering key tasks such as object perception, state prediction, and trajectory planning. These findings suggest that constructing dense world models through structured latent expert chains is a promising direction for VLA-based autonomous driving.
2610.25734.tldr_en: The core idea is to mimic the hierarchical perception process of humans by embedding a progressive chain of latent expert cognition within the VLA model, enabling the model to internalize dense knowledge from foundational vision models, including visual representations, semantic structures, and spatial geometry, while maintaining efficient inference.

llm.title_ja: 密に考え、疎に行動する：ビジョン・言語・行動自動運転のための潜在エキスパート認知チェーン
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の階層的知覚プロセスを模倣し、VLAモデル内にタスク特異的潜在トークンのプログレッシブチェーンを埋め込むことで、効率的な推論を維持しつつ基盤ビジョンモデルからの密な知識を内面化するLECDriveを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のVLAモデルは言語指示や軌跡信号などの疎な監督で訓練されており、密な視覚的・意味的・幾何学的情報の直接マッピングが安全な運転に不可欠なシーン情報の圧縮や破棄を強いる。
llm.method: 表現から意味論、幾何学へと段階的に監督が構造化されるカリキュラム学習の原則に従い、表現・意味構造・空間幾何学の密な知識を埋め込む潜在エキスパート認知チェーン（LECDrive）をVLAモデルに組み込む。
llm.result: オブジェクト認識、状態予測、軌跡計画などの主要な自動運転ベンチマークにおいて、ベースとなるVLMの性能が一貫して向上した。

2610.25720.title: Enhancing Lunar PNT Performance Through Surface Station Enabled Radiometric Observables
2610.25720.abstract: Future lunar surface missions require reliable positioning for autonomous rover operations. Lunar navigation satellite systems may provide limited vertical positioning accuracy due to satellite availability and observation geometry, particularly during early deployment. This study investigates a radiometric navigation architecture in which a lunar surface station (SS) improves rover positioning through double-differenced satellite observations and additional surface-to-surface ranging. Pseudorange and Doppler measurements from lunar navigation satellites are used for relative positioning between the SS and rover, while dual one-way ranging (DOWR) provides an additional range observable. The radiometric solution is integrated with rover dead-reckoning information. Monte Carlo simulations were conducted using five satellites representative of NASA's Lunar Communications Relay and Navigation Systems (LCRNS) constellation and a rover trajectory near Connecting Ridge at the lunar south pole. The results show that the SS improves horizontal and vertical relative positioning, with further gains from DOWR. In the simulated scenario, the mean 99.7% vertical positioning error decreased from 29.9 m without the SS to 5.5 m with double-differenced pseudorange and Doppler processing, and to 4.8 m with DOWR. An uncorrected DOWR hardware bias significantly degraded positioning, whereas the proposed bias-estimation method achieved a final estimation error of 0.058 +/- 0.057 m. The benefit of DOWR also depended on observation geometry. These results demonstrate the potential of a lunar surface station to improve vertical relative positioning through direct radiometric ranging, complementing its communication and navigation support roles.

llm.title_ja: 月面局を用いた放射測定観測量による月面PNT性能の向上
llm.tldr_ja: 月面局（SS）が二重差分衛星観測と追加の表面間測距を通じてローバーの測位精度を向上させる放射測定ナビゲーションアーキテクチャを調査し、シミュレーションにより垂直位置誤差の低減効果を示した。
llm.problem: 将来の月面ミッションにおいて、衛星の可用性と観測幾何学の制約により、月ナビゲーション衛星システムは限定的な垂直測位精度しか提供できない場合がある。
llm.method: 月面ナビゲーション衛星からの疑似距離・ドップラー測定値を用いた月面局とローバー間の相対測位、およびデュアル一方向測距（DOWR）をローバーのデッドレコニング情報と統合する。
llm.result: モンテカルロシミュレーションにおいて、月面局の導入とDOWRの活用により、平均99.7%の垂直測位誤差が大幅に減少した。

2610.25711.title: SWAP: Test-Time Steerable Humanoid Whole-Body Collision Avoidance
2610.25711.abstract: Humanoid robots operating in human-centric environments must coordinate the entire body to traverse tight, cluttered spaces while maintaining balance. Existing methods often struggle to jointly consider dynamic stability and collision avoidance from high-dimensional perceptual inputs. Moreover, for humanoids, safe behavior is inherently multimodal: the same obstacle may admit multiple valid traversals, which is difficult to represent with a single deterministic policy. To address these challenges, we propose SWAP (Steerable Whole-body Avoidance Policy), a hierarchical framework that separates collision-aware decision making from stabilization. A high-level, perception-conditioned diffusion policy generates multimodal, collision-aware motion proposals, while a low-level whole-body RL controller tracks these proposals and maintains dynamic balance. To efficiently train the high-level policy, we obtain scalable supervision via hindsight labeling: we roll out the low-level policy under randomized commands, place obstacles only in the space that each executed motion did not sweep, so the motion is collision-free by construction, and re-render the perception the robot would have seen. At deployment, Monte Carlo sampling with simple cost signals steers the diffusion model toward safe, task-aligned behaviors without heavy reward tuning. Experiments in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid show reliable avoidance with static and dynamic obstacles. Test-time steering further enables customization, improving targeted rewards (e.g., speed, orientation, or posture) by 34% on average while maintaining a high collision avoidance rate. Together, these results support a practical solution to humanoid whole-body collision avoidance with test-time steerability. Project website: https://iscoyizj.github.io/SWAP-steerable-humanoid-oa-website/

llm.title_ja: SWAP：テスト時に制御可能なヒューマノイド全身衝突回避
llm.tldr_ja: 高レベルの知覚条件付き拡散ポリシーによるマルチモーダルな衝突回避プラン生成と、低レベルの全身強化学習コントローラーによる動的バランス維持を分離した階層型フレームワーク「SWAP」を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機で実証した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットは、狭く雑然とした空間を移動する際、動的安定性と衝突回避を高次元知覚入力から同時に考慮することや、単一の決定論的ポリシーで多様な障害物回避を表すことが困難である。
llm.method: 事後ラベリングによるスケーラブルな監督を用いて高レベルの拡散ポリシーを訓練し、テスト時にシンプルなコスト信号を用いたモンテカルロサンプリングにより安全な行動へ誘導する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよびUnitree G1ヒューマノイドの実機実験において、静的・動的障害物の信頼性の高い回避とテスト時ステアリングによるタスク報酬の改善が示された。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.25710.title: Evidence Sufficiency and Model Comparisons in MexRegQA: An Item-Level Audit of Mexican-Spanish Regulatory QA
2610.25710.abstract: Similarity-gated coverage does not establish that retrieved evidence contains the facts needed to answer a question. We audit Mexican-Spanish financial-regulatory QA and find that 35 of 135 covered items lack some or all load-bearing facts. On the post-hoc full-evidence slice (n=98), eleven prompt-matched models score 95-98/98 and none differs significantly from the anchor; this does not establish equivalence. Removing evidence-defective items changes the nominal significance status of 14 of 55 pairwise comparisons. On 56 zero-evidence items, accuracy spans 33.9%-89.3%. Removing evidence from the audited items under an abstention-permitting prompt reduces accuracy by 63-81 percentage points in all ten tested legs, with no recovered items. Building on sufficient-context research, we contribute MexRegQA v1.0: 192 items with provenance and evidence-status labels, frozen retrieval evidence for 191 evaluated items, predictions, judge outputs and offline checks. The audit was outcome-aware, the later model/panel sweep reused the same questions, and all reported scores and labels rely on machine evaluation without independent human validation. We propose releasing evidence-status labels alongside grounded QA benchmarks so that model comparisons can be examined separately from evidence availability.
2610.25710.comment: 26 pages. Companion artifacts are prepared but not yet publicly available

2610.25701.title: Validation of Human Motor Development Scales with Humanoid Robots
2610.25701.abstract: We investigate how humanoid robots can learn a series of motor skills defined by human infant motor development scales, and we evaluate which scales are comprehensive enough to serve as self-contained guides for developing gross motor skills up to standing and walking. We represent each motor development scale as a developmental graph that guides the training of a humanoid robot. We then apply this graph within a reinforcement learning framework so that the robot learns skills following the natural phases of human motor development described by the scale. Our work demonstrates that graphs derived from three out of four popular pediatric motor scales can successfully guide humanoid robots to develop these skills. The fourth scale misses some intermediate milestones that the other scales have, which causes some failures. After adding a missing milestone in its graph, it also enables the robot to develop those skills successfully.
2610.25701.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to ICRA 2027. Video available at https://youtu.be/SR3LUVhohV4
2610.25701.tldr_en: This work demonstrates that graphs derived from three out of four popular pediatric motor scales can successfully guide humanoid robots to develop gross motor skills up to standing and walking.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマノイドロボットによる人間運動発達スケールの検証
llm.tldr_ja: ヒューマノイドロボットが乳児の運動発達スケールで定義された一連の運動スキルをどのように学習できるかを調査し、小児運動スケールから導出されたグラフが立位や歩行までの粗大運動スキルの発達を成功裡に誘導できることを実証した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットにおいて、どの小児運動発達スケールが自立的な粗大運動スキル発達のガイドとして十分に包括的であるかが不明確であること。
llm.method: 各運動発達スケールを発達グラフとして表現し、強化学習フレームワーク内で適用してロボットに自然な発達段階に沿ったスキルを学習させる。
llm.result: 4つ中3つの小児運動スケールから導出されたグラフがヒューマノイドロボットのスキル発達を成功裡に誘導でき、不足していたマイルストーンの追加により4つ目のスケールでも成功させられることを示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2610.25692.title: Progress-Guided Preference Generation for Aligning Generative Control Policies
2610.25692.abstract: Generative policies have achieved strong performance in imitation learning tasks, but their success is often constrained by the limited availability of expert demonstrations. Although preference-based fine-tuning can leverage suboptimal rollouts to improve performance, existing approaches heavily rely on expensive human annotations. In this work, we introduce Progress-Guided Preference Generation (PGPG), an unsupervised preference alignment framework that eliminates the need for human-in-the-loop supervision. Our method leverages ordered coverage alignment to measure sequential progress relative to a small set of expert demonstrations, enabling the automatic extraction of pseudo-preference labels from autonomously collected rollouts. Furthermore, we introduce key enhancements to improve the reliability of these progress-guided preferences, enabling effective fine-tuning of pretrained generative policies without requiring manually designed reward functions. Extensive experiments across a suite of challenging long-horizon manipulation tasks demonstrate that PGPG outperforms standard supervised fine-tuning baselines. Moreover, our conceptually simple framework is broadly applicable across multiple classes of generative policies, demonstrating strong versatility when integrated with both diffusion and flow-matching policies.
2610.25692.tldr_en: Progress-Guided Preference Generation is introduced, an unsupervised preference alignment framework that eliminates the need for human-in-the-loop supervision and is broadly applicable across multiple classes of generative policies, demonstrating strong versatility when integrated with both diffusion and flow-matching policies.

llm.title_ja: 生成的制御ポリシーのアライメントに向けた進捗誘導型選好生成
llm.tldr_ja: 人間参加型監督の必要性を排除した教師なし選好アライメントフレームワーク「PGPG」を提案し、少数の専門家デモンストレーションに対する順次進捗を測定することで自動的に擬似選好ラベルを抽出して汎用的にファインチューニングできることを示した。
llm.problem: 生成的ポリシーの模倣学習における成功は限定的な専門家デモンストレーションに制約されており、既存の選好ベースのファインチューニングは高価な人間のアノテーションに大きく依存している。
llm.method: 順序付きカバレッジアライメントを活用して少数の専門家デモンストレーションに対する進捗を測定し、自律的に収集されたロールアウトから擬似選好ラベルを自動抽出するProgress-Guided Preference Generation（PGPG）を導入する。
llm.result: 長期マニピュレーションタスクを用いた実験により、拡散ポリシーおよびフローマッチングポリシーの両方において標準的な教師ありファインチューニングベースラインを上回る性能を実証した。

2610.25691.title: ReDOA: Real-World Distillation via Observation Alignment for Image-Based Manipulation Policy Learning
2610.25691.abstract: Data-driven learning for general-purpose robotic manipulation presents a fundamental trade-off between data-collection cost and adaptability to real-world environments. Imitation learning (IL) requires costly human demonstrations, whereas simulation-based learning is vulnerable to sim-to-real gaps in dynamics and sensor observations. We propose ReDOA (Real-World Distillation via Observation Alignment), a framework that decouples control learning from perception learning to learn image-based policies in the real world. A state-based teacher policy trained in simulation is executed on a real robot, and its control knowledge is distilled into an image-based student policy using the collected trajectories. Observation Alignment resolves observation mismatches between data collection and deployment. This framework collects successful, efficiently executed trajectories paired with real-world visual observations, without requiring demonstrations from human experts. In real-robot experiments on three non-prehensile manipulation tasks, including bimanual manipulation, our method achieves better overall performance when jointly considering task success and execution efficiency than both IL based on human demonstrations and policy distillation in simulation. https://isri-aist.github.io/redoa-project-page/
2610.25691.tldr_en: ReDOA (Real-World Distillation via Observation Alignment), a framework that decouples control learning from perception learning to learn image-based policies in the real world, achieves better overall performance when jointly considering task success and execution efficiency.

llm.title_ja: ReDOA：画像ベースのマニピュレーションポリシー学習のための観測アライメントを介した実世界蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: 制御学習と知覚学習を分離し、シミュレーションで訓練された状態ベースの教師ポリシーの知識を観測アライメントを用いて画像ベースの学生ポリシーに実世界で蒸留するフレームワーク「ReDOA」を提案した。
llm.problem: 汎用ロボットマニピュレーションのデータ駆動型学習には、データ収集コストと実世界の環境適応性との間にトレードオフがあり、模倣学習はコストが高く、シミュレーション学習はシム・ツー・リアルギャップに脆弱である。
llm.method: シミュレーションで訓練された状態ベースの教師ポリシーを実ロボットで実行し、収集された軌跡を用いて観測アライメントにより画像ベースの学生ポリシーに知識を蒸留する。
llm.result: 3つの非把持マニピュレーションタスクにおける実ロボット実験で、人間のデモンストレーションやシミュレーション蒸留ベースラインよりも優れたタスク成功率と実行効率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2610.25690.title: ScaleNav: Scalable Internet Video Pretraining for Language-Conditioned Local Navigation
2610.25690.abstract: We study language-conditioned local navigation, where a robot must navigate to a text-specified target visible in its initial observation and stop at the described location. End-to-end navigation policies require diverse training data to generalize across scenes, yet real-robot data is costly to collect and simulated data leaves a sim-to-real gap. Internet egocentric videos offer a scalable source of real-world navigation experience. Our key insight is to learn goal-directed visual dynamics from Internet egocentric videos, and use these dynamics to support robot action generation. To this end, we propose ScaleNav, a unified world-action framework with three-stage training. We first perform instruction-conditioned video pretraining on these videos to learn how observations evolve as the camera approaches instructed targets across diverse real-world scenes. Action alignment then uses action-labeled simulated data to train the model to predict executable action chunks. Joint fine-tuning subsequently optimizes all trainable components together for navigation. ScaleNav achieves success rates of 86.5% on a single-view adaptation of Short-Horizon OVON and 94.9% on our HabitatGS-LN benchmark, outperforming the evaluated baselines on both benchmarks. We further deploy and evaluate ScaleNav on a real quadruped robot, with results supporting the model's ability to generalize to real-world navigation. Code and videos are available at https://zju3dv.github.io/ScaleNav/
2610.25690.hf_summary_en: ScaleNav learns goal-directed visual dynamics from internet egocentric videos to generate robot actions for language-conditioned local navigation, achieving high success rates in simulation and real-world deployment.

llm.title_ja: ScaleNav：言語条件付きローカルナビゲーションのためのスケーラブルなインターネット動画事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: インターネットの主観視点動画からゴール指向の視覚的ダイナミクスを学習し、それを利用してロボットの行動生成をサポートする統一世界行動フレームワーク「ScaleNav」を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機の四足ロボットで高い成功率を実証した。
llm.problem: 言語条件付きローカルナビゲーションポリシーのエンドツーエンド訓練には多様なデータが必要だが、実ロボットデータの収集はコストが高く、シミュレーションデータはシム・ツー・リアルギャップを残す。
llm.method: インターネット主観視点動画を用いた命令条件付き動画事前学習により多様な実世界シーンでの観察の進展を学び、行動ラベル付きシミュレーションデータによる行動アライメントと共同ファインチューニングを行う。
llm.result: Short-Horizon OVONやHabitatGS-LNベンチマーク、および実世界の四足歩行ロボットへの展開において、ベースラインを上回る高い成功率を達成した。

2610.25688.title: Vehicle-State-Aware Confidence Estimation for Direct Wind Sensing on a Multirotor
2610.25688.abstract: Direct wind sensing from a multi-rotor UAV enables localized atmospheric measurements, but the reliability of the anemometer depends on vehicle motion. This work presents a vehicle-state-aware confidence method that uses horizontal and vertical vehicle speed to quantify the acquisition of each wind observation. The resulting confidence score is used to adapt measurement influence to a two-dimensional vector estimator. Experiments were conducted during horizontal translation, vertical motion, and held-out autonomous waypoint flight. The proposed two-feature formulation achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.995, with 98.84% of translation observations identified as unreliable. The confidence-aware adaptation reduced median estimator gain during translation from 0.207 to 0.064 while retaining median gain of 0.151 during hover. The results show that vehicle state provides useful proprioceptive context for regulating the influence of direct airborne wind observations.

llm.title_ja: マルチローターにおける直接風センシングのための車両状態を考慮した信頼度推定
llm.tldr_ja: 車両の速度を用いて風観測の信頼度を定量化し、その信頼度スコアに基づいて2次元ベクトル推定器への測定の影響を適応的に調整する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 風速計の信頼性が車両の運動に依存する課題がある。
llm.method: 水平および垂直方向の車両速度を利用して各風観測の信頼度スコアを計算し、推定器のゲインを適応的に調整する。
llm.result: ROC-AUC 0.995を達成し、翻訳時の誤った観測を98.84%特定しつつホバリング時のゲインを維持した。

2610.25687.title: Revealing and Bridging the Physical Executability Gap in Vision-Language Navigation
2610.25687.abstract: Continuous vision-and-language navigation (VLN) is typically evaluated by goal-reaching success, assuming it reflects an agent's ability to execute language-grounded behavior. We show that this assumption can fail: permissive contact models in current simulators may mask physically infeasible actions, creating a physical executability gap between semantic competence and embodied realization. To bridge this gap, we introduce Visual-Semantic Traversability Alignment (VeSTA), a framework that aligns VLN policies with physically executable futures. We define visual-semantic traversability as the ability to predict instruction-conditioned trajectories that are semantically valid, geometrically feasible, and physically robust. VeSTA addresses this misalignment through two complementary mechanisms: improving executable support in trajectory generation and risk-aware selection among multimodal futures. Specifically, Trajectory Relative Group Policy Optimization uses strict-contact feedback to reshape the candidate distribution toward executable regions, while the Traversability Risk Critic learns a risk-adjusted scalar utility for candidate-wise future selection. Experiments on R2R and RxR reveal substantial dependence of existing VLN agents on simulator contact semantics. Under strict-contact evaluation, VeSTA substantially reduces collision-induced failures while preserving or improving goal-reaching performance, and controlled real-world robot experiments provide evidence that the learned preference transfers beyond simulation.
2610.25687.tldr_en: Under strict-contact evaluation, VeSTA substantially reduces collision-induced failures while preserving or improving goal-reaching performance, and controlled real-world robot experiments provide evidence that the learned preference transfers beyond simulation.

llm.title_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーションにおける物理的実行可能性のギャップの解明と橋渡し
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレータの接触モデルがもたらす物理的実行可能性のギャップを解消するため、ポリシーを物理的に実行可能な未来に適合させるVeSTAフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: シミュレータの過剰な接触モデルが物理的に不可能な行動を隠蔽し、意味的能力と具現化の間にギャップを生む課題がある。
llm.method: 厳密な接触フィードバックを用いた軌跡相対グループポリシー最適化と、動的リスク評価を行うリスク批評家を導入した。
llm.result: 厳密な接触評価において衝突による失敗を大幅に減らしつつ、ゴール到達性能を維持または向上させた。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2610.25666.title: Frechet Forcing: Training Long-Horizon Streaming World Models from Short Clips
2610.25666.abstract: Streaming video world models generate the future chunk by chunk, conditioned on their own past and a stream of actions. Trained on short clips, they drift once a rollout exceeds the training horizon, as prediction errors re-enter the context and compound. A common remedy is to train the model on its own rollouts via distribution matching distillation (DMD). For action-conditioned world models, the teacher becomes a bottleneck: an external video model is agnostic to the actions, whereas the model's own pretrained network drifts in the same manner as the student. We observe that a long rollout need not match a teacher, provided it remains a realistic continuation of its own scene that follows the commanded actions. Realism and scene fidelity can be measured against real-data statistics, which remain valid at any horizon, while action following is preserved by the model's conditional generation loss. We propose Fréchet Forcing, which fine-tunes a world model together with its deployed multi-step sampler under three constraints. Generative anchoring applies the flow-matching loss after a self-generated history ending on real data. Context fidelity, a Fréchet distance (FD) on latent statistics of the free rollout centred on each clip's own ground truth, keeps every rollout faithful to its scene. Reality matching, an FD to real frames in a frozen perceptual space, keeps the generated frames realistic. Because all three targets are derived from short real clips without comparing a rollout against a long recorded future, training requires no teacher, no online critic and no long videos. Fine-tuning MiniWorld-1B, pretrained on 253-frame clips, for at most 36 GPU-hours on 381-frame clips yields rollouts that remain stable beyond 4,000 frames and continue to follow their actions in both robot manipulation and camera-controlled exploration.
2610.25666.tldr_en: It is observed that a long rollout need not match a teacher, provided it remains a realistic continuation of its own scene that follows the commanded actions, and Fr\'echet Forcing is proposed, which fine-tunes a world model together with its deployed multi-step sampler under three constraints.
2610.25666.hf_summary_en: Fréchet Forcing fine-tunes streaming video world models using self-generated rollouts and real-data statistics to prevent long-horizon drift without requiring teachers or long videos.

llm.title_ja: Frechet Forcing：短いクリップからの長期ストリーミング世界モデルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 教師モデルや長期ビデオを必要とせず、実データ統計に基づく3つの制約を用いて世界モデルとそのサンプラーを微調整するFréchet Forcingを提案した。
llm.problem: 短いクリップで学習されたストリーミング世界モデルは、ロールアウトが訓練地平を超えると予測誤差が蓄積してドリフトを起こす。
llm.method: 生成アンカリング、コンテキスト忠実度、現実一致という3つの制約の下で世界モデルを微調整する。
llm.result: 4000フレームを超えても安定して動作し、行動追従を維持するロールアウト生成を実現した。

2610.25665.title: SpaRV: Sparse Radiance Voxels for Scalable Geometrically Consistent LiDAR-Visual Mapping and Rendering
2610.25665.abstract: Robotic simulation, navigation, and inspection need photorealistic and geometrically accurate maps. Radiance fields achieve photorealism, but building them from robot data raises three challenges. A robot's trajectory serves its task, not reconstruction, so images from few viewpoints leave the geometry under-constrained. Residual errors in camera poses and intrinsics blur the map. The map's GPU memory grows with scene size, which limits its level of detail in large scenes. We present \textbf{SpaRV}, a \textbf{Spa}rse \textbf{R}adiance \textbf{V}oxel map rendered by differentiable ray marching, which lets irregular LiDAR scans supervise it alongside images. LiDAR depth and occupancy anchor the under-constrained geometry, and normal and smoothness regularizers keep it smooth between LiDAR points. To correct camera errors, SpaRV alternates map training with photometric optimization of the camera poses and focal lengths. To bound GPU memory in training and rendering, SpaRV holds one submap at a time at full resolution and the rest at coarser octree levels. Experiments show that SpaRV keeps the geometry consistent away from the captured trajectory and sharpens textures by optimizing the camera parameters. On one 24\,GB GPU, SpaRV reconstructs a university campus captured in 63{,}582 images and simulates other cameras and LiDARs. Our code will be released at \url{https://github.com/hku-mars/SpaRV}.
2610.25665.tldr_en: Experiments show that SpaRV keeps the geometry consistent away from the captured trajectory and sharpens textures by optimizing the camera parameters, which means that SpaRV keeps the geometry consistent away from the captured trajectory and sharpens textures by optimizing the camera parameters.

llm.title_ja: SpaRV：スケーラブルで幾何学的に一貫性のあるLiDAR・視覚マッピングおよびレンダリングのためのスパース放射ボクセル
llm.tldr_ja: LiDARスキャンと画像を組み合わせて微分可能なレイマーチングでレンダリングするスパース放射ボクセルマップSpaRVを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットの軌跡が再構成に最適化されておらず、カメラの誤差や大規模シーンにおけるGPUメモリの増大が課題である。
llm.method: LiDARの深さと占有情報でジオメトリをアンカーし、カメラパラメータの光度最適化とマップ学習を交互に行う。
llm.result: 幾何学的整合性を保ちながらテクスチャを鮮鋭化し、単一GPUで大規模キャンパスの再構成とシミュレーションを可能にした。

2610.26979.title: Latent Projection for Latent Planning
2610.26979.abstract: Latent world models let an agent plan in latent space. The planner searches for an action sequence that minimizes a cost, and that cost is often the $\ell_2$ distance between the predicted terminal latent and the goal latent. The latent, however, is partly noise: the regularizer that prevents collapse during world model training promotes variance in the directions carrying no signal. We show that the same regularizer also supplies the structure to prune that noise in the latent. SIGReg drives the latent marginal to a standard Gaussian at every step, and assuming further that the latent sequence is a Gauss-Markov process, the transition is linear with its covariance pinned by the map itself, $z' \mid z \sim \mathcal{N}(Az,\, I - AA^\top)$. Fitting the state dynamics $A$ therefore yields the covariance at no additional cost, and in its eigenbasis each latent direction carries its own uncertainty. Furthermore, constraining $A$ to be a normal matrix fixes that basis across timesteps, so one eigenbasis measures the uncertainty over an arbitrary number of steps and serves as a stable basis to compute the planning cost on. We then restrict the $\ell_2$ cost to the $k$-dimensional subspace the state dynamics carry forward with the least uncertainty. The correction is post hoc: the encoder, the predictor, the rollout, and the planner are all left untouched, and only a single constrained matrix, $A$, is fit. We evaluate across six environments and show large gains on the 2D navigation tasks, TwoRoom and PointMaze, raising success rate over the plain $\ell_2$ cost by up to $+54.7$ points under a harder planning setting. Code is available at https://github.com/yjang43/lp2.
2610.26979.comment: Accepted to the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Modeling Uncertainty in Robotic World Models
2610.26979.tldr_en: This work evaluates across six environments and shows large gains on the 2D navigation tasks, TwoRoom and PointMaze, raising success rate over the plain $\ell_2$ cost by up to $+54.7$ points under a harder planning setting.

llm.title_ja: 潜在的計画のための潜在空間射影
llm.tldr_ja: 世界モデルの学習時の正則化に起因する潜在空間のノイズを固有基底で削減し、計画コストの精度を向上させる事後補正手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 世界モデルの正則化により、シグネチャーを持たない方向に分散が生じ、潜在空間の計画におけるノイズとなる課題がある。
llm.method: 状態ダイナミクスを当てはめて不確実性の共分散を求め、最も不確実性の低いk次元部分空間にコストを制限する。
llm.result: 2次元ナビゲーション課題（TwoRoom、PointMaze）において、従来のL2コストと比較して成功率を最大54.7ポイント向上させた。

2610.25649.title: InteractAgent: Agentic Human Motion Interaction with Memory-Augmented Reflection
2610.25649.abstract: Long-horizon human-scene interaction requires coordinated spatial reasoning, physical feasibility, and the ability to recover from compounding execution errors. Text-driven motion models are largely scene-agnostic and lack closed-loop correction, while geometry-conditioned approaches depend on paired scene-motion training or explicit 3D preprocessing that limits generalization to novel layouts and open-vocabulary goals. We present InteractAgent, an agentic multimodal LLM system for long-horizon human-scene interaction that plans, executes, observes, and reflects in a closed loop, using a single MLLM as both planner and evaluator and a frozen MotionLLM as the executor. InteractAgent integrates Online Observation for step-wise recovery decisions (continue/redo/replan) and Memory-Augmented Reflection for multi-round plan refinement with adaptive stopping. On UniHSI, InteractAgent improves task success and reduces penetration compared with training-free baselines. Code: https://github.com/AIGeeksGroup/InteractAgent.
2610.25649.tldr_en: InteractAgent is an agentic multimodal LLM system for long-horizon human-scene interaction that plans, executes, observes, and reflects in a closed loop, using a single MLLM as both planner and evaluator and a frozen MotionLLM as the executor.

llm.title_ja: InteractAgent：メモリ拡張リフレクションを用いたエージェント型ヒューマンモーションインタラクション
llm.tldr_ja: 単一のマルチモーダルLLMをプランナーおよび評価者として、凍結されたMotionLLMを実行者として活用する閉ループ型のエージェントシステムを提案した。
llm.problem: 長期的な人間とシーンのインタラクションにおいて、既存のテキスト駆動型モデルはシーン非依存であり、幾何学条件付きモデルは一般化が制限される。
llm.method: オンライン観察によるステップごとのリカバリ決定と、メモリ拡張リフレクションによる多ラウンドの計画洗練を統合した。
llm.result: UniHSIにおいて、訓練不要なベースラインと比較してタスク成功率を向上させ、貫通を削減した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンシーンインタラクション

2610.25637.title: TNVD-SC: Diagnosing Scan Context Failures in Forests with Terrain-Normalized Vertical Distributions
2610.25637.abstract: Long-term LiDAR place recognition in forests is difficult because repetitive vegetation and uneven terrain create severe structural aliasing. We diagnose Scan Context (SC) by separating candidate retrieval from fine matching: on the standardized TreeLoc++ Wild-Places protocol, a TNVD support key places a valid location in the top-25 set for approximately 99% of queries, while conventional SC matching on those candidates reaches only 61.84% mean R@1. With an identical raw-SC candidate set, terrain normalization improves max-height cells by only 1.21 points but vertical-distribution cells by 19.72 points. These observations motivate Terrain-Normalized Vertical Distribution Scan Context (TNVD-SC), which preserves the SC ring-sector topology while encoding terrain-relative vertical probability distributions. Under the standardized TreeLoc++ protocol, TNVD-SC reaches 91.83% mean R@1 and attains the highest R@1 mean and R@1 stability among the compared methods, while TreeLoc++ remains stronger in mean MR, MF1, and AUC. The unchanged method reaches 85.14% mean R@1 on the four-session CVTNet-style NCLT evaluation. A lossless count-coded implementation with exact hierarchical Jensen-Shannon search reduces descriptor payload by 3.86x and compute latency by 23.8% without changing the audited retrieval outputs.
2610.25637.tldr_en: Terrain-Normalized Vertical Distribution Scan Context (TNVD-SC), which preserves the SC ring-sector topology while encoding terrain-relative vertical probability distributions, is motivated.

llm.title_ja: TNVD-SC：地形正規化垂直分布を用いた森林環境におけるScan Contextの失敗診断
llm.tldr_ja: SCのリングセクター位相を保持しつつ地形相対の垂直確率分布をエンコードするTNVD-SCを提案し、森林環境での場所認識精度を向上させた。
llm.problem: 森林環境における長期的なLiDAR場所認識では、反復的な植生と起伏のある地形により深刻な構造的エイリアシングが発生する。
llm.method: 候補検索と詳細マッチングを分離し、地形正規化された垂直分布をエンコードする記述子を構築した。
llm.result: TreeLoc++プロトコルにおいて91.83%の平均R@1を達成し、データ量と計算遅延を削減しつつ高い安定性を示した。

2610.25632.title: SteerAct: Unlocking Action Models through Few-Shot Temporal Steering
2610.25632.abstract: Improving pretrained robot action models at test time from only a few rollouts remains challenging. Activation steering offers a lightweight approach by modifying feature activations while keeping model weights fixed. However, effective steering requires identifying which features to modify and determining the timing and strength of modification. We introduce SteerAct, a few-shot temporal steering framework that uses a shared temporal descriptor of sparse-feature dynamics for offline feature selection and online control. A pretrained sparse autoencoder provides candidate features, and our temporal descriptor summarizes the distribution of local activation-order patterns for each feature, enabling comparisons across rollouts without requiring timestep alignment. Before steering begins (offline), we use successful and failed reference rollouts to select a single task-specific feature whose temporal descriptors best distinguish the two outcomes and construct its reference banks. During each new execution (online), we compare the feature's evolving temporal descriptor with these references to determine when to intervene and how strongly to increase or decrease its activation via a steering coefficient. Using only 24 outcome-labeled rollouts per task, SteerAct improves task success by approximately 10% relative to unsteered models in evaluations spanning $π_{0.5}$, Fast-WAM, RoboTwin 2.0, DexJoCo, and real-world manipulation, without updating action-model weights. Code and demos are available at: https://steeract.github.io/.
2610.25632.tldr_en: SteerAct is introduced, a few-shot temporal steering framework that uses a shared temporal descriptor of sparse-feature dynamics for offline feature selection and online control that improves task success by approximately 10% relative to unsteered models in evaluations spanning $\pi_{0.5}$, Fast-WAM, RoboTwin 2.0, DexJoCo, and real-world manipulation, without updating action-model weights.

llm.title_ja: SteerAct：少数例の時間的ステアリングによるアクションモデルの解放
llm.tldr_ja: 重みを更新せずに少数のロールアウトから特徴活性化を動的に修飾する少数例の時間的ステアリングフレームワークSteerActを提案した。
llm.problem: 少数のロールアウトからテスト時に既存の事前学習済みロボットアクションモデルを改善することは困難である。
llm.method: スパース特徴のダイナミクスの時間的記述子を用いてオフラインでの特徴選択とオンラインでの活性化調整を行う。
llm.result: モデルの重みを更新することなく、複数のシミュレーションおよび実世界操作タスクでタスク成功率を約10%向上させた。

2610.25631.title: Where Do the Gaussians Go? Foreground Attraction for Camera-Based Weakly Supervised 3D Occupancy
2610.25631.abstract: Camera-based 3D semantic occupancy models can be trained without 3D labels by rendering their predictions into the images and supervising them with 2D pseudo labels. In sparse Gaussian representations trained this way, Gaussian positions are learned only through pixel-wise rendering losses, which we hypothesize give small foreground objects little weight. In trained GaussianFlowOcc models, the Gaussian density on foreground voxels is on average only 1.62 times that on background voxels. We propose a training-only foreground attraction loss that back-projects foreground pseudo-label pixels with pseudo depth and pulls nearby Gaussians toward these 3D points, favoring Gaussians that already predict the target class; the inference network is unchanged. On Occ3D-nuScenes, the loss raises this concentration to 2.40 over three seeds. Over three seeds, the mean foreground IoU increases from 6.29 to 6.96 and is higher for each seed, whereas the change in mean mIoU (13.53 to 13.82) is within the seed-to-seed variation of the baseline. Single-run ablations further indicate that pseudo-label targets outperform targets placed at ground-truth voxels and that acting on the Gaussian positions alone is not sufficient, and a single-seed test shows that the model degrades less when fewer Gaussians are kept at inference.
2610.25631.tldr_en: Single-run ablations indicate that pseudo-label targets outperform targets placed at ground-truth voxels and that acting on the Gaussian positions alone is not sufficient, and a single-seed test shows that the model degrades less when fewer Gaussians are kept at inference.

llm.title_ja: ガウス分布はどこへ向かうのか：カメラベースの弱教師あり3D占有のための前景アトラクション
llm.tldr_ja: 前景の疑似ラベルピクセルを3D点に逆投影し、近くのガウス分布を引き付けることで前景の集中度を高める学習用損失関数を提案した。
llm.problem: スパースガウス表現を用いたカメラベースの3Dセマンティック占有モデルでは、ピクセル単位のレンダリング損失により小さな前景オブジェクトに十分な重みが与えられない。
llm.method: 疑似深度を用いて前景疑似ラベルピクセルを逆投影し、ターゲットクラスを予測するガウス分布をその3D点に引き寄せる損失関数を導入した。
llm.result: Occ3D-nuScenesにおいて前景の集中度が向上し、平均前景IoUが6.29から6.96に増加した。
keywords_ja: ガウスプラッティング
セマンティックセグメンテーション

2610.25628.title: Humanoid SRL: Augmenting Humanoids with Supernumerary Limbs for Coordinated Loco-Manipulation
2610.25628.abstract: Humanoid robots are envisioned to perform diverse human-level tasks through their anthropomorphic morphology. Their dual-arm configuration enables a broad range of everyday actions. Yet, as in humans, this morphology can constrain loco-manipulation when both arms are occupied or additional contacts are required beyond their reach. Supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) offer a way to extend these capabilities, but their integration requires the added limb to be coordinated with whole-body motion and balance. In this study, we develop and integrate a supernumerary arm into a humanoid platform to investigate how morphological augmentation reshapes its feasible action space. Through quantitative analysis and hardware experiments across two configurations, we show how the additional limb expands whole-body interaction capabilities by enabling manipulation and support to be coordinated beyond the constraints of the native dual-arm configuration. To control this augmented morphology, we leverage model-based trajectory optimization (TO) to generate dynamically feasible motions for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL) controllers. The controllers are trained in simulation and transferred to hardware in a zero-shot manner, enabling coordinated whole-body skills for contact-rich tri-arm loco-manipulation. We further show vision-guided autonomous execution on selected tasks using diffusion policies trained from hardware demonstrations. Our findings suggest that humanoid morphology need not be restricted to human-like forms, but can be reimagined as an extensible design space for robotic augmentation.
2610.25628.tldr_en: The findings suggest that humanoid morphology need not be restricted to human-like forms, but can be reimagined as an extensible design space for robotic augmentation, to investigate how morphological augmentation reshapes its feasible action space.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマンoid SRL：協調的な移動・マニピュレーションのための超多数肢によるヒューマノイドの拡張
llm.tldr_ja: モデルベースの軌跡最適化と強化学習を用いて、超多数肢（SRL）を追加したヒューマノイドロボットの接触豊かな移動・マニピュレーションを実現した。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの生来の二腕構成では、両手がふさがっている場合やリーチ外の接触が必要な場合に移動・マニピュレーションが制限される。
llm.method: 追加の腕を統合し、動的に実行可能なモーションを生成する軌跡最適化とゼロショットでハードウェアに移行する強化学習コントローラーを開発した。
llm.result: 追加の腕により全体のインタラクション能力が拡張され、三腕による接触豊かな移動・マニピュレーションを実証した。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション

2610.25600.title: Vector-Quantized World Model: Latent Feedback Motion Planning for Robot Manipulation
2610.25600.abstract: Visual world models have shown strong potential for robot planning, yet long-horizon manipulation remains challenging due to compounding prediction errors, large search complexity, and latent plans that the low-level controller cannot reliably reach. In this work, we introduce Vector-Quantized World Model (VQ-WM), a latent feedback motion planning framework that integrates discrete long-horizon search with continuous visual feedback control: a discrete latent predictor models transitions between vector-quantized latent states, allowing the planner to look far ahead and find a shortest path to the goal through discrete search and a continuous learned controller sequentially reaches the planned states through visual feedback, correcting deviations to mitigate compounding errors. Whereas most vector quantization uses Euclidean distance, we use a novel estimator of the first-passage-time as a quasi-metric, which aligns the planning abstraction with the controller's capabilities. We evaluate on the physical robot manipulation of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle: whereas existing state-of-the-art foundation models (VLAs, WAMs) only succeed when the solution trace in their training dataset, our method achieves 100\% success rate with only short-play data, demonstrate its ability to compose long-horizon solutions beyond the short demonstrated trajectories and execute them reliably. Our solution also outperforms strongest world-models by 13.3--85.3 percentage points on simulation benchmarks spanning manipulation and locomotion, demonstrating consistent progress and new capabilities.
2610.25600.tldr_en: Vector-Quantized World Model (VQ-WM), a latent feedback motion planning framework that integrates discrete long-horizon search with continuous visual feedback control, is introduced, allowing the planner to look far ahead and find a shortest path to the goal through discrete search and a continuous learned controller sequentially reaches the planned states through visual feedback.

llm.title_ja: ベクトル量子化世界モデル：ロボットマニピュレーションのための潜在フィードバックモーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 離散的な長期探索と連続的な視覚フィードバック制御を統合したベクトル量子化世界モデル（VQ-WM）を提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚世界モデルを用いた長期マニピュレーションでは、予測誤差の蓄積や大きな探索複雑性が課題となる。
llm.method: ベクトル量子化された潜在状態間の遷移をモデル化する離散潜在予測子と、視覚フィードバックで状態に到達する連続コントローラーを組み合わせた。
llm.result: ハノイの塔パズルやシミュレーションベンチマークにおいて、短いプレイデータのみで100%の成功率と優れた性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2610.25596.title: Cognitive Maps in Large Language Models
2610.25596.abstract: It has long been proposed that animals construct cognitive maps to support flexible behavior in novel environments. We tested whether large language models form similar representations using relational reasoning tasks and causal "mosaic experiments" that manipulate internal activations in open-weight language models. Models beyond the ten-billion-parameter scale successfully inferred unstated relationships between entities and generalized to synthetic entity names. Across model and task families, models generated abstract representations of relational structure and combined them additively with representations of entity identity, binding entities to roles within that structure. Models stored observed relationships as pairwise links that they composed retrospectively when queried, rather than prospectively positioning each entity in a global coordinate system. Binding was mediated by a sparse, distributed set of key--value pairs; by perturbing these pairs, we implanted "false memories" that altered model behavior in predictable ways. Overall, our findings reveal an internal organization analogous to a cognitive map that explains how language models reason with limited information.
2610.25596.tldr_en: Across models and tasks, models formed abstract representations of relational structure, additively combining them with representations of entity identity, revealing a conserved organization analogous to a cognitive map supporting flexible and systematic reasoning in language models.

llm.title_ja: 大規模言語モデルにおける認知地図
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデルが関係推論タスクと内部活性化操作を通じて、柔軟な行動を支える構造化された内部表現（認知地図）を形成していることを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 動物が新しい環境で柔軟な行動を支える認知地図を構築するように、大規模言語モデルが同様の表現を形成しているかの検証が求められていた。
llm.method: 関係推論タスクや内部活性化を操作する因果的モザイク実験を用いて、モデルの内部表現を分析した。
llm.result: モデルは関係構造の抽象的表現を生成し、エンティティのアイデンティティと加算的に結合させて記憶していることを示した。

2610.25585.title: Adaptive Bendpoint Formation in Octopus-Inspired Soft Continuum Arms
2610.25585.abstract: Octopuses exhibit a powerful form of embodied intelligence from a highly adaptable soft body. One key mechanism is the ability to instantiate bending points at any location along the arm, which enables performant and dexterous behaviours. Taking inspiration from the octopus for its dexterity, this study focuses on changing the curvature of a tendon-actuated arm by adaptively changing the anchoring end-point along the arm. An array of inflatable shells is integrated into the arm, where inflating a shell causes an increase in friction at the location, jamming the tendon and creating a temporary new anchoring point. The novel soft actuator does not break the continuity of the arm between the actuated segment and the loose segment. Experiments show that the actuated segment has a non-constant bell-shaped curvature which is comparable to that of a real octopus arm during a reaching motion. Compared to conventional single-tendon continuum manipulators, the proposed design offers an expanded workspace and enhanced dexterity through the ability to independently shape different regions of the arm through selective curvature tuning. At the same time, it avoids the mechanical complexity typically associated with multi-segment, multi-actuator systems.

llm.title_ja: タコに着想を得たソフト連続体アームにおける適応型曲げ点形成
llm.tldr_ja: アーム内のシェルを膨らませて摩擦を増加させ、一時的なアンカーポイントを形成することで柔軟に曲率を変更するソフトアクチュエータを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の連続体マニピュレータは、マルチセグメント・マルチアクチュエータシステムの機械的複雑性が高い課題がある。
llm.method: アームに膨張式シェルアレイを統合し、特定位置で腱をジャミングして一時的なアンカーポイントを適応的に生成する。
llm.result: 実際のタコのアームに匹敵する釣鐘状の非定常曲率を実現し、ワークスペースと器用さを拡張した。

2610.25534.title: AQUAACT: A Joystick-Level Underwater Teleoperation Dataset and Closed-Loop Benchmark
2610.25534.abstract: Underwater robots support a growing range of work, from inspecting offshore structures and pipelines to surveying reefs and accompanying divers. Most of these tasks, however, are still flown by hand by a pilot, which raises the question of whether they can be carried out autonomously instead. On land, vision-language-action (VLA) models already let robots carry out tasks autonomously from language instructions, which makes them a natural candidate for taking the pilot's place. Underwater, however, there is little data to train such models. We take inspiration from how these tasks are flown today: the pilot watches the camera image and steers with a joystick, whose commands the flight controller turns into motion. We therefore record the pilots and introduce AQUAACT, to our knowledge the first publicly available language-annotated underwater dataset pairing camera images with human joystick commands. It comprises 1.9 hours of real-world and 17.9 hours of simulated demonstrations, both flown by human pilots, together with the vehicle's inertial measurements. Experiments with AQUAACT show that its simulated demonstrations transfer to real data and greatly reduce the real demonstrations a policy needs. A closed-loop benchmark of seven policies in simulation, from imitation-learning baselines to VLA models, each trained with its default recipe, shows that these tasks remain far from solved: no policy completes more than a fifth of the episodes. Pretraining on land data gives large VLA models no advantage over small policies trained from scratch, a gap that land-trained models have yet to close underwater.
2610.25534.tldr_en: This work introduces AQUAACT, to its knowledge the first publicly available language-annotated underwater dataset pairing camera images with human joystick commands, and records the pilots and introduces AQUAACT, to its knowledge the first publicly available language-annotated underwater dataset pairing camera images with human joystick commands.

llm.title_ja: AQUAACT：ジョイスティックレベルの水中テレオペレーションデータセットと閉ループベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: カメラ画像と人間のジョイスティック操作をペアにした水中データセットAQUAACTを構築し、複数のポリシーの性能を評価した。
llm.problem: 水中環境において、ビジョン・言語・アクション（VLA）モデルを学習するためのデータが十分に存在しない課題がある。
llm.method: 人間パイロットによる実世界およびシミュレーション上の水中デモンストレーションを記録し、言語アノテーション付きのデータセットを構築した。
llm.result: シミュレーションでのデモンストレーションが実データへの転移に有効であり、既存ポリシーの多くがタスクを達成できていないことを示した。

2610.25476.title: CusADi2: Latency-Optimized Batch Computation of Robot Kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians on the GPU
2610.25476.abstract: Trajectory optimization methods, from sampling-based zero-order to gradient-based first- and second-order approaches, require many evaluations of dynamical system functions, i.e., functions derived from a robot's dynamical model, such as forward kinematics and their Jacobians and Hessians. These evaluations are largely independent, e.g., across sampled trajectories or time steps, and can thus be evaluated in parallel as a batch. When used to make decisions online, these methods require low latency, i.e., each batch must complete in as little wall-clock time as possible. Existing frameworks utilize modern GPU hardware primarily to parallelize across batch instances, thereby optimizing throughput but not latency. We present CusADi2, a software library that reduces the batch evaluation latency by additionally parallelizing computation within each batch instance. We benchmark forward kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians for all 67~robots in the MuJoCo Menagerie, including arms, hands, quadrupeds, humanoids, and biomechanical models, against MuJoCo XLA, MuJoCo Warp, frax, CusADi, and CasADi. CusADi2 achieves lower latency than all baselines at batch sizes of 64 to 4096, while matching them at larger batch sizes. We also demonstrate the performance advantage of CusADi2 in a sampling-based control application. All code is open-source at: https://github.com/johnviljoen/cusadi2
2610.25476.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Code: https://github.com/johnviljoen/cusadi2

llm.title_ja: CusADi2：GPU上におけるロボット運動学、ヤコビアン、ヘッシアンの遅延最適化バッチ計算
llm.tldr_ja: バッチインスタンス内並列化によりロボットの動力学関数のバッチ評価遅延を削減するソフトウェアライブラリCusADi2を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のフレームワークはGPUの並列性をスループットの最適化に用いており、オンライン決定に必要な低遅延に対応できていない課題がある。
llm.method: 各バッチインスタンス内の計算をさらに並列化することでバッチ評価遅延を削減するソフトウェアライブラリを設計した。
llm.result: MuJoCo Menagerieの67体のロボットにおいて、バッチサイズ64から4096で既存のベースラインよりも低い遅延を達成した。

2610.25459.title: BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks
2610.25459.abstract: Bimanual manipulation with dexterous hands has attracted growing attention in research on robotic action models. However, few studies have developed benchmarks specifically tailored for dexterous manipulation, leaving the dexterous manipulation capabilities of existing models insufficiently characterized. In this paper, we present BiDex-100, a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation that combines broad task coverage, multi-dimensional evaluation, and high-DoF hand embodiments. Concretely, the benchmark comprises 106 tasks organized along five capability axes: generalization, instruction following, limited demonstrations, long horizon, and memory. Each task is paired with an out-of-domain variant featuring controlled visual and spatial changes, allowing systematic assessment of robustness. In addition, the benchmark supports two embodiments and provides 8,080 success-validated teleoperated demonstrations, totaling 6.25 million frames. We evaluate seven recent Vision-Language-Action models under a unified protocol, establishing baselines for capability-specific performance, robustness, and data efficiency. The website is available at https://robbyant-research.github.io/BiDex-100/.
2610.25459.tldr_en: This paper presents BiDex-100, a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation that combines broad task coverage, multi-dimensional evaluation, and high-DoF hand embodiments, and evaluates seven recent Vision-Language-Action models under a unified protocol.
2610.25459.hf_summary_en: BiDex-100 is a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation that evaluates vision-language-action models across diverse tasks, robustness variants, and demonstration scales.

llm.title_ja: BiDex-100：100以上のシミュレーションタスクにわたる両手器用操作のための包括的ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 多様なタスクと高自由度ハンドを備えた両手器用操作のためのシミュレーションベンチマークBiDex-100を構築し、最近のVLAモデルを評価した。
llm.problem: 両手による器用な操作に特化したベンチマークが少なく、既存モデルの器用な操作能力が十分に特徴づけられていない課題がある。
llm.method: 5つの能力軸に沿った106のタスクと、成功検証済みの8,080件のテロップ操作デモンストレーションを含むベンチマークを開発した。
llm.result: 7つのVLAモデルを統一プロトコルで評価し、能力別のパフォーマンス、頑健性、データ効率のベースラインを確立した。

2610.25455.title: Self-Crystallizing Behavior Trees: Amortizing Foundation-Model Reasoning into Deterministic Control for Autonomous Drones
2610.25455.abstract: Classical robot control, Finite State Machines and Behavior Trees (BTs), is deterministic and inspectable but fixed at design time: it fails on situations its designers did not anticipate. Foundation models can synthesize new control logic at runtime, at a cost in latency and non-determinism hard to accept in safety-critical aerial systems. Existing LLM-driven approaches keep the model in the loop permanently and discard what it produces. We propose Self-Crystallizing Behavior Trees (SCBT), in which the foundation model is a compiler rather than a runtime. When a BT node fails, an LLM proposes a minimal, mission-agnostic subtree patch; CMA-ES tunes its parameters in simulation; a contextual bandit decides whether a stored patch or a new LLM call is worth its cost; and a three-stage admission pipeline (static check, invariant-monitored replays, an empirical margin over the unpatched tree) admits only patches that demonstrably recover. Admitted patches are stored in a fleet library and, once the LLM call rate decays, crystallized into a deterministic BT that no human wrote. We implement SCBT on Microsoft Project AirSim with a schema-constrained LLM pipeline (Gemini 3.1 Pro) and a lockstep simulator. Over three seeds of a 20-episode learning phase with wind-gust and battery failures, SCBT used $11\pm1.4$ LLM calls against 26 for whole-tree regeneration and 22 without a library, with 0.33 calls per episode in the second half. The crystallized trees, 28 and 33 nodes with two patches each, reached $97\pm2\%$ mission success with no learning running, against 12\% for the unpatched tree and 98\% for a hand-coded expert tree, and reproduce decision traces exactly when re-ticked offline. Two negative results: replay admission rejected useful wind recoveries by attributing wind-induced geofence excursions to the patch, and a static-only ablation generalized better to held-out failures.
2610.25455.tldr_en: Self-Crystallizing Behavior Trees is proposed, in which the foundation model is a compiler rather than a runtime, and two negative results are implemented: replay admission rejected useful wind recoveries by attributing wind-induced geofence excursions to the patch, and a static-only ablation generalized better to held-out failures.

llm.title_ja: 自己結晶化行動ツリー：基礎モデルの推論を自律ドローンのための決定論的制御に落とし込む手法
llm.tldr_ja: 基礎モデルをランタイムではなくコンパイラとして機能させ、障害時にパッチを生成・検証して決定論的な行動ツリーに結晶化するSCBTを提案した。
llm.problem: 古典的制御は決定論的だが未対応の状況に弱く、基礎モデルによる実行時生成は安全性・遅延の面で問題がある。
llm.method: LLMによる最小限のサブツリーパッチ提案、シミュレーションでのパラメータ調整、厳格な承認パイプラインを経てツリーに結晶化する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて少ないLLM呼び出し回数で97%のミッション成功率を達成し、決定論的な動作を再現した。
llm.limitation: 再生承認が風による軌道逸脱を誤って排除する等の負の結果が観測された

2610.25436.title: Intent-Informed Model Predictive Control for Shared Autonomy in Remote Manipulation Tasks
2610.25436.abstract: Shared autonomy is a control paradigm that combines human cognitive abilities with robot precision to enable effective remote manipulation in complex environments. A key challenge is how to adapt the level of autonomy using information extracted from the human, task, and/or environment. In this paper, we propose a novel arbitration strategy that dynamically adjusts the level of autonomy in the system using the entropy of a belief distribution derived from a multimodal intent inference. Human intent is modeled with a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN), which updates beliefs over goals given real-time operator gaze data and robot arm motion during teleoperation. We then formulate the blending of human input and autonomous control as a Model Predictive Control (MPC) problem, where the system's autonomous behavior is guided by the belief distribution. This approach enables continuous, gradual transitions across the full spectrum of autonomy levels, from direct teleoperation to full autonomy. To validate our approach, we conducted experiments to compare the performance of our proposed algorithm against two MPC-based shared autonomy methods. Compared to the baselines, our approach achieved reductions of at least 61% in object retrieval time, 44% in trajectory length, and 60% in human control input. Participants reported high perceived control, predictability, intent recognition, and responsiveness, along with low workload.

llm.title_ja: リモートマニピュレーションにおける協調自律のための意図を考慮したモデル予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: 視線データとアーム動作から人間の意図を動的ベイジアンネットワークで推定し、モデル予測制御により自律レベルを動的に調整する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 複雑な環境でのリモートマニピュレーションにおいて、人間とロボットの協調のための自律レベルを適切に動的調整することが難しい。
llm.method: マルチモーダルな意図推論に基づく信念分布の不entropyを利用して、MPC問題として人間の入力と自律制御をブレンドする。
llm.result: オブジェクト取得時間を61%以上、軌跡長を44%以上、人間の制御入力を60%削減した。
keywords_ja: リモートマニピュレーション

2610.25426.title: SurGPT: A Multi-Task Foundation Model for Robotic Surgical Skills Assessment and Gesture Recognition
2610.25426.abstract: The assessment of surgical skills in robotic surgery training has traditionally relied on subjective evaluations by human experts, creating bottlenecks in surgical education and limiting scalability. We present a novel foundation model that automatically analyzes robotic surgical videos to provide comprehensive skill assessment and gesture understanding. Combining a visual encoder with a transformer architecture, the model performs three key tasks simultaneously: 1) surgical task classification (knot tying, needle passing, suturing), 2) skill level assessment on a standardized scale, and 3) natural language generation of surgical gesture descriptions. The model processes video sequences from the da Vinci surgical robot and generates human-readable text descriptions of surgical actions, similar to how language models generate text from prompts, using a multi-task learning framework with adaptive uncertainty weighting to optimize performance across all objectives. Our transformer-based architecture incorporates positional encoding for temporal understanding and attention mechanisms for spatiotemporal feature integration. Evaluated on the da Vinci Skills Simulator dataset, the proposed framework demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in surgical task recognition and provides interpretable skill assessments that correlate with expert evaluations, with the model's ability to generate natural language descriptions of surgical gestures opening new possibilities for automated surgical education, real-time feedback systems, and objective skill assessment in surgical training and certification programs.

llm.title_ja: SurGPT：ロボット手術のスキル評価とジェスチャー認識のためのマルチタスク基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ビジュアルエンコーダとトランスフォーマーアーキテクチャを組み合わせ、手術タスク分類、スキル評価、自然言語によるジェスチャー記述を同時に行う基盤モデルを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボット手術のスキル評価は従来専門家による主観的評価に依存しており、教育のボトルネックやスケーラビリティの限界があった。
llm.method: da Vinci手術ロボットの動画シーケンスを入力とし、マルチタスク学習フレームワークと適応的不確実性重み付けを用いて処理する。
llm.result: 手術タスク認識において最先端の性能を示し、専門家の評価と相関する解釈可能なスキル評価と自然言語記述を生成した。

2610.25419.title: Learning When to Adapt: Reactivity-Conditioned Residual Adaptation under Human-Robot Distribution Shift
2610.25419.abstract: Pedestrians differ in whether they respond to a robot, yet many RL policies assume all are non-reactive to prioritize safety. Policies trained without conditioning on local pedestrians' reactivity may therefore be unnecessarily conservative or rely on cooperation that does not occur. We propose RCRA, an online adaptation framework that modulates a learned residual around a frozen conservative navigation policy according to estimated pedestrian reactivity. A Transformer-based estimator infers latent pedestrian reactivity from motion histories and robot context, providing a more accurate signal for navigation adaptation and improving scenario-averaged simulation accuracy by $12.62$ percentage points over the Bayesian baseline, which assumes known pedestrian goals. These estimates are spatially aggregated into an adaptation scale that gates LoRA modules, enabling cooperative behavior near reactive pedestrians and conservative behavior near non-reactive pedestrians. Among baselines achieving SR above $90\%$ in every scenario, RCRA reduces scenario-averaged path length by $16.7\%$ relative to the conservative backbone and by $7.3\%$ relative to randomized-training baselines. It improves mean SR by $14.88$ percentage points over the reactive-trained policy.
2610.25419.tldr_en: RCRA, an online adaptation framework that modulates a learned residual around a frozen conservative navigation policy according to estimated pedestrian reactivity, is proposed, an online adaptation framework that modulates a learned residual around a frozen conservative navigation policy according to estimated pedestrian reactivity.

llm.title_ja: 適応タイミングの学習：歩行者・ロボット間の分布シフト下における反応性を条件とした残差適応
llm.tldr_ja: 歩行者の反応性を推定し、保守的なナビゲーションポリシー周囲の学習済み残差をオンラインで変調する適応フレームワークRCRAを提案した。
llm.problem: 多くの強化学習ポリシーは歩行者が非反応的であると仮定するため、過度に保守的になったり協力関係を活用できなくなったりする課題がある。
llm.method: トランスフォーマーベースの推定器で移動履歴から潜在的な歩行者反応性を推論し、LoRAモジュールを制御する適応スケールに統合した。
llm.result: 保守的なバックボーンと比較してパス長を16.7%削減し、平均成功率を14.88ポイント向上させた。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2610.25410.title: T(R,O) Grasp++: Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping in Cluttered Environments at Scale
2610.25410.abstract: Dexterous grasping in cluttered scenes remains a central challenge in robotic manipulation, as it requires high-dimensional hand coordination under complex object-environment constraints. To address this problem, we introduce one of the largest simulation benchmarks to date, comprising around 0.5B grasp annotations across eight dexterous hands and approximately 50K objects. Furthermore, we propose T(R,O) Grasp++, a scalable diffusion-based framework for cross-embodiment dexterous grasp synthesis in cluttered environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving an average success rate of 88% across eight dexterous embodiments. Meanwhile, our pipeline achieves only 0.3s inference latency while improving inference sample efficiency by over 10 times.
2610.25410.tldr_en: One of the largest simulation benchmarks to date, comprising around 0.5B grasp annotations across eight dexterous hands and approximately 50K objects, is introduced and T(R,O) Grasp++ is proposed, a scalable diffusion-based framework for cross-embodiment dexterous grasp synthesis in cluttered environments.

llm.title_ja: T(R,O) Grasp++: 複雑環境における大規模なクロスエンボディメント器用把持
llm.tldr_ja: 8種の器用な手と約5万個のオブジェクトにわたる約5億件の把持アノテーションを含む最大級のシミュレーションベンチマークを導入し、複雑環境でのクロスエンボディメント器用把持合成のためのスケーラブルな拡散ベースのフレームワークであるT(R,O) Grasp++を提案する。
llm.problem: 複雑な物体と環境の制約のもとで高次元の手の協調が必要となるため、複雑なシーンでの器用な把持は依然としてロボットマニピュレーションにおける中心的な課題である。
llm.method: 8種の器用な手と約5万個のオブジェクトにわたる約5億件の把持アノテーションを含む大規模シミュレーションベンチマークと、スケーラブルな拡散ベースのクロスエンボディメント把持合成フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 既存のベースラインを大幅に上回り、8種の器用なエンボディメントで平均成功率88%を達成し、推論レイテンシはわずか0.3秒でサンプル効率が10倍以上向上した。
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント
シミュレーションベンチマーク

2610.25407.title: AeroDASH: Asynchronous Vision-Language-Action Control for Continuous UAV Flight
2610.25407.abstract: Onboard inference latency creates a mismatch between the trajectories predicted by vision-language-action (VLA) policies and the ongoing motion of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). We present AeroDASH, an asynchronous VLA framework for continuous language-conditioned flight. A B-spline policy is initialized through supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations, providing continuous trajectory references in position and yaw. During execution, trajectory fusion removes the expired prediction prefix and connects the remaining segment to the active reference with derivative continuity while limiting trajectory deformation. To account for deviations induced by asynchronous execution, execution-aware group relative policy optimization (GRPO) further adapts the policy using trajectory-level rewards. On the UAV-Flow test set, AeroDASH achieves a success rate of 76.56%, exceeding OpenVLA-UAV and AeroDASH w/o GRPO by 38.1 and 20.1 percentage points, respectively. Execution experiments show that AeroDASH sustains motion during inference and reduces acceleration, jerk, and speed fluctuations relative to asynchronous tracking of waypoint sequences. We further demonstrate language-conditioned flight with onboard inference and asynchronous trajectory execution. The code will be released upon acceptance.

llm.title_ja: AeroDASH: 連続的なUAV飛行のための非同期ビジョン・言語・行動制御
llm.tldr_ja: UAV飛行におけるVLAポリシーの予測軌跡と実際の動きの不整合を解消するため、連続的な言語条件付き飛行を実現する非同期VLAフレームワーク「AeroDASH」を提案する。
llm.problem: オンボード推論のレイテンシにより、VLAポリシーが予測した軌跡とUAVの実際の動きとの間に不整合が生じる。
llm.method: エキスパートデモによる教師ありファインチューニングで初期化されたBスプラインポリシーを用い、実行時には軌跡融合と実行を考慮したGRPOによる適応を行う非同期VLAフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: UAV-Flowテストセットで76.56%の成功率を達成し、OpenVLA-UAVなどを大きく上回るとともに、推論中の動きの持続と加速度・ジャーク・速度の変動抑制を実現した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2610.25401.title: Energy-Score Stabilized Attentive Mixture-Density Policy: A Lightweight Approach to Multimodal Robot Motion
2610.25401.abstract: For practical motion generation, it is essential to handle multimodality (multiple actions can be correct for the same observation) while maintaining low inference cost and strong generalization from limited demonstrations. We introduce an attentive mixture-density policy trained with the Energy Score that represents future visuomotor trajectories as explicit probability distributions with a single forward pass. Concretely, we output Gaussian mixture parameters for joint commands (and optionally attention points) and optimize them with the Energy Score (computed as a sum of 1D CRPS under a diagonal covariance assumption) instead of the negative log-likelihood (NLL) to avoid MDN singularities and gradient-scale instabilities. Our architecture couples explicit spatial attention with mixture-density outputs, enabling robust multimodal behavior selection under visual noise and small-data regimes. On an 8-DOF manipulator, the method generates distinct avoidance trajectories and stabilizes learning in obstacle avoidance. Moreover, in a randomized moving-object grasping task, where spatiotemporal multimodality and fast timing decisions are required, the proposed model outperforms Diffusion Policy by 15-25% under several unseen conditions, demonstrating superior generalization and real-time feasibility.
2610.25401.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Accepted to IROS 2026
2610.25401.tldr_en: An attentive mixture-density policy trained with the Energy Score is introduced that represents future visuomotor trajectories as explicit probability distributions with a single forward pass, enabling robust multimodal behavior selection under visual noise and small-data regimes.

llm.title_ja: エネルギー・スコア安定化アテンティブ混合密度ポリシー：マルチモーダルなロボットモーションのための軽量アプローチ
llm.tldr_ja: エネルギー・スコアを用いて訓練され、単一のフォワードパスで将来の視覚運動軌跡を明示的な確率分布として表現するアテンティブ混合密度ポリシーを導入し、視覚的ノイズや小規模データ環境下でのロバストなマルチモーダル行動選択を実現する。
llm.problem: 限られたデモンストレーションからの強力な汎化性能と低い推論コストを維持しつつ、マルチモダリティ（同一の観測に対して複数の正しい行動が存在する状況）に対処することが求められる。
llm.method: ガウス混合パラメータを出力し、NLLの代わりにエネルギー・スコアで最適化を行う明示的な空間アテンションと混合密度出力を組み合わせたポリシーを提案する。
llm.result: 8自由度マニピュレータにおいて異なる回避軌跡を生成し、未見の条件下においてDiffusion Policyを15〜25%上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: 混合密度ネットワーク

2610.25397.title: Visual-Inertial Odometry for Ground Robots with Dynamic Camera-IMU Extrinsic Calibration
2610.25397.abstract: Visual-inertial odometry systems are often constrained by the assumption that sensors are rigidly mounted, which limits their adaptability in practical scenarios involving structural motion. To address this limitation, this paper investigates time-varying camera-IMU extrinsic calibration. First, a dynamic camera-IMU extrinsic calibration method based on the Denavit-Hartenberg convention is proposed by incorporating the robot kinematic model. Second, a two-step initialization strategy is developed to efficiently estimate the initial joint angles, providing a reliable starting point for subsequent extrinsic parameter optimization and enabling online estimation of timevarying camera-IMU extrinsic parameters. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively accommodate variations in camera-IMU extrinsic parameters while maintaining competitive localization accuracy.
2610.25397.tldr_en: A dynamic camera-IMU extrinsic calibration method based on the Denavit-Hartenberg convention is proposed by incorporating the robot kinematic model, providing a reliable starting point for subsequent extrinsic parameter optimization and enabling online estimation of timevarying camera-IMU extrinsic parameters.

llm.title_ja: 動的カメラ-IMU外因的キャリブレーションを用いた地上ロボットのための視覚慣性オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの運動モデルを組み込んだDH条約に基づく動的カメラ-IMU外因的キャリブレーション手法を提案し、時間変化する外因的パラメータのオンライン推定と優れた測位精度の維持を実現する。
llm.problem: 視覚慣性オドメトリシステムは、センサーが剛体として固定されているという仮定に制約されており、構造的な動きを含む実際のシナリオでの適応性が制限される。
llm.method: ロボットの運動モデルを組み込んだDenavit-Hartenberg条約に基づく動的カメラ-IMU外因的キャリブレーション手法と、初期関節角を効率的に推定する2段階初期化戦略を開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーション実験により、提案フレームワークは競争力のある測位精度を維持しながら、カメラ-IMUの外因的パラメータの変化に効果的に対応できることが示された。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2610.25376.title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models
2610.25376.abstract: Large-scale action pretraining equips Embodied Foundation Models (EFMs) with strong manipulation capabilities, with particular strengths in generalization and closed-loop robustness, but reproducing such pretraining requires substantial robot data and computation. To transfer these capabilities from pretrained EFMs to policies without action pretraining, we introduce TILDE (Teacher-In-the-Loop Distillation from EFMs), which synergizes on-policy distillation at student-induced states with learning from teacher-executed recovery trajectories. We further propose AutoDAgger, an autonomous data aggregation pipeline in which a robotic reward model is utilized to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, thereby collecting recovery experience without human monitoring or manual control. AutoDAgger accelerates recovery-trajectory collection by more than $2\times$ compared with the human-in-the-loop method. By unifying learning from demonstrations, on-policy teacher supervision, and teacher's corrective behavior, TILDE improves task performance by up to $4.1\times$ over behavior cloning across three real-world tasks and supports effective cross-architecture distillation.
2610.25376.tldr_en: TILDE (Teacher-In-the-Loop Distillation from EFMs), which synergizes on-policy distillation at student-induced states with learning from teacher-executed recovery trajectories, and proposes AutoDAgger, an autonomous data aggregation pipeline in which a robotic reward model is utilized to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, thereby collecting recovery experience without human monitoring or manual control.
2610.25376.hf_summary_en: TILDE distills embodied foundation model capabilities into robot policies via on-policy teacher supervision and autonomous recovery data collection, improving real-world task performance without large-scale action pretraining.

llm.title_ja: TILDE: 体現型基盤モデルからのティーチャーインザループ蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントが誘発する状態でのオンポリシー蒸留と、教師が実行したリカバリ軌跡からの学習を統合し、人間による監視なしでリカバリ経験を収集するデータ集約パイプラインを提案することで、タスク性能を大幅に向上させる。
llm.problem: 体現型基盤モデル（EFM）の強力なマニピュレーション能力をアクション事前学習のないポリシーに移行するには、膨大なロボットデータと計算が必要となる。
llm.method: 学生の状態におけるオンポリシー蒸留と教師のリカバリ軌跡からの学習を統合し、報酬モデルを用いて教師の介入をトリガーする自律データ集約パイプライン「AutoDAgger」を提案する。
llm.result: 人間の介入を必要とせずにリカバリデータの収集を2倍以上加速し、3つの実世界タスクにおいて行動クローンと比較して最大4.1倍のタスク性能向上を達成した。

2610.25358.title: LateMatch: Breaking the Interaction Bottleneck via Cacheable Matching for Efficient Visual Localization
2610.25358.abstract: Visual localization is critical for embodied agents, but deploying state-of-the-art deep feature matchers on edge devices is fundamentally limited by their massive computational cost. Standard deep matchers tightly interleave intra-image context building and inter-image matching at every layer, creating a severe interaction bottleneck. Localizing a single query against K database images forces the system to execute the full network K independent times with no capacity for caching. To break this bottleneck, we advocate for a paradigm shift toward cacheable image matching. We realize this paradigm with LateMatch, a versatile approach that restructures existing matchers by deferring inter-image interaction to their final layers. By isolating intra-image processing into offline-cacheable Context Blocks, only a small set of Interaction Blocks must be executed online. To further optimize LateMatch, we introduce E-SToRE (Entropy-guided Spatial Token Reduction and Expansion). E-SToRE leverages the decreasing Shannon entropy of the late Interaction Blocks to dynamically reduce token counts just prior to cross-image interaction. Evaluated across HPatches, ScanNet, MegaDepth, ETH-3D, and Aachen, LateMatch reduces effective computational cost by over 2x compared to standard deep matchers, while E-SToRE yields an additional 10% to 14% savings with negligible degradation in accuracy.
2610.25358.tldr_en: This work proposes LateMatch, a versatile approach that restructures existing matchers by deferring inter-image interaction to their final layers by isolating intra-image processing into offline-cacheable Context Blocks, and introduces E-SToRE (Entropy-guided Spatial Token Reduction and Expansion).

llm.title_ja: LateMatch: キャッシュ可能なマッチングによるインタラクションのボトルネックの打破と効率的な視覚的ローカライゼーション
llm.tldr_ja: 画像間インタラクションを最終層に遅延させ、画像内処理をオフラインキャッシュ可能なコンテキストブロックに分離することで、標準的なディープマッチャの計算コストを削減する汎用アプローチ「LateMatch」を提案する。
llm.problem: 最先端のディープ特徴量マッチャをエッジデバイスに展開することは、その莫大な計算コストによって根本的に制限されている。
llm.method: 画像間インタラクションを最終層に遅延させ、画像内処理をオフラインキャッシュ可能なコンテキストブロックに分離するLateMatchと、エントロピー誘導型空間トークン削減・拡張（E-SToRE）を導入する。
llm.result: 標準的なディープマッチャと比較して実効計算コストを2倍以上削減し、精度低下を無視できるレベルに抑えながら追加で10%〜14%の削減を実現した。
keywords_ja: 視覚的ローカライゼーション
コンピュータビジョン

2610.25301.title: Shared-Private Cross-Modal Discrepancy Learning for Imbalanced Multi-Source Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection
2610.25301.abstract: Audio-visual deepfake detectors are often trained under a single dataset or manipulation regime, but multi-source training collections may contain heterogeneous attacks and uneven source distributions. Training separate detectors for each source is inefficient, while a single shared detector may be biased toward dominant source-specific patterns. We study known-source imbalanced multi-source audio-visual deepfake detection using FakeAVCeleb and LAV-DF, where source identity is supplied during training and inference. To address this setting, we build on the Multi-Scale Cross-Modal Transformer Encoder (MSCT) and propose Pre-MSCT Shared-Private Feature Fusion. Our method routes \texttt{[CLS]}-augmented audio and visual tokens into a shared stream and source-specific private streams before the first MSCT block, while retaining its internal multi-scale self-attention (MSSA), differential cross-modal attention (DCA), and feed-forward operations. The shared stream models cross-source reusable evidence, while the private streams retain source-dependent residual variations. A domain-aware gated residual fusion module injects selected private evidence into the shared representation for the main fused prediction. Experiments under two controlled source-composition protocols show improved macro and worst-source AUC compared with the MRDF and MSCT baselines. These results support shared-private cross-modal discrepancy learning in the evaluated two-source setting with known source identity.
2610.25301.tldr_en: This work builds on the Multi-Scale Cross-Modal Transformer Encoder (MSCT) and proposes Pre-MSCT Shared-Private Feature Fusion, which supports shared-private cross-modal discrepancy learning in the evaluated two-source setting with known source identity.

llm.title_ja: 不均衡なマルチソース音声・映像ディープフェイク検出のための共有・プライベートクロスモーダル不一致学習
llm.tldr_ja: マルチスケールクロスモーダルTransformerエンコーダー（MSCT）を基盤として、MSCTブロックの前に音声・映像トークンを共有ストリームとソース固有のプライベートストリームにルーティングする共有・プライベート特徴量融合手法を提案する。
llm.problem: マルチソースのトレーニングコレクションには異種攻撃や偏ったソース分布が含まれる可能性があり、単一の共有検出器では優勢なソース固有パターンに偏るという課題がある。
llm.method: MSCTを拡張し、[CLS]で拡張されたオーディオおよびビジュアルトークンを共有ストリームとソース固有のプライベートストリームに分岐させる事前MSCT共有・プライベート特徴量融合を提案する。
llm.result: 制御された2つのソース構成プロトコルを用いた実験において、MRDFおよびMSCTベースラインと比較してマクロおよび最悪ソースのAUCが改善された。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2610.25288.title: Vision as Proprioception: Estimating Humanoid Robot Pose from Video
2610.25288.abstract: Estimating a humanoid robot's internal state from video has a wide range of real-world applications but remains unexplored.
